entry.summary: This paper shows that strong LLMs fail to preserve predictions across logically equivalent inputs and generalize poorly to unseen logical forms, indicating reliance on shallow semantic cues rather than logical structure. It proposes LoGIST, a framework that guides LLM reasoning using explicit logical structure to build logic-invariant behavior. The evaluation uses systematically curated logically equivalent data.

entry.title: Symbolic Constraint Agents: Mining Formal Tool-Call Constraints to Prevent Agent Errors

author.name: Jinu Lee, Shraddha Barke

entry.summary: Symbolic Constraint Agents (SCA) mine symbolic constraints on tool calls from API documentation, refine them against execution traces, and check agent tool calls at runtime with an SMT solver, issuing warnings or deterministic fixes on violation. Unlike prior work enforcing predefined safety policies, this mines tool-dependency constraints from environments and tests whether they improve end-to-end task performance. It combines neural agents with deterministic verification to prevent tool-use errors.

entry.title: When Retrieval Partially Conflicts with Skills: Understanding Procedural Hallucination in Language Models

author.name: Guanqun Jiang, Pengfei Cao, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: The paper defines procedural hallucination — models producing retrieval-supported but skill-invalid answers when retrieved context conflicts with a selected skill — and introduces SourceClash, a matched benchmark with 1,271 bundles and 6,355 prompts across ten procedural domains. Each bundle varies retrieved cues while fixing task, skill specification, and answer space to isolate the failure mode.

entry.title: GLOBE: Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit via Unit-Sphere Trajectories

author.name: Xinyue Peng, Zhenlin Liang, Meng Cai, Hua Wang

entry.summary: GLOBE is a training-free method that terminates chain-of-thought reasoning early by embedding completed reasoning segments on a unit sphere and analyzing the semantic trajectory shape, combining a trial-answer phase with trajectory analysis. This cuts serving costs and prevents correct intermediate answers from being overwritten.

entry.title: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards

author.name: Zhizhou Wang, Yaxi Lu, Zhong Zhang, Zikun Hu, Xin Cong, Yankai Lin, Fangming Liu

entry.summary: VeriCUA learns when and what to verify for computer-use agents whose RL training relies on proactive reward agents interacting with post-execution GUI environments. It shows prompted judges from 4B to GPT-5.4 all plateau at 68-70 percent macro-average agreement regardless of scale or few-shot examples, because check value depends on the environment and only becomes apparent through execution, and learns verification decisions from execution feedback instead.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Forgetting and Transfer in Unified Multimodal Post-Training

author.name: Francesco Colasurdo, Ivan Slobozhan, Joaquin Vanschoren, Anna Vettoruzzo

entry.summary: The authors measure cross-modal forgetting when LoRA post-training Janus-Pro-7B on weak capabilities, finding that a single fine-tuning run appears safe on benchmarks but chaining three runs reveals degradation in untrained capabilities across modalities. The study carefully designs interventions where the base model is genuinely weak to test real retention risk.

entry.title: On the Selectivity of Generative Models in Structure-Based Drug Design

author.name: Ella Miray Rajaonson, Jungyoon Lee, William Chau, Alan Aspuru-Guzik, Benjamin Sanchez-Lengeling, Dominique Beaini, Kirill Neklyudov, Marta Skreta

entry.summary: The paper introduces SELECTBENCH, a benchmark evaluating whether generative structure-based drug design models produce molecules selective for a target protein while avoiding off-target binding, with three tasks covering literature case studies, safety screening, and additional real-world scenarios. It addresses the common neglect of selectivity in SBDD generative modeling.

entry.title: GazeAct: A Human-Gaze-Annotated Manipulation Dataset for Attention-Regularized Policies

author.name: Anupam Pani, Wang Yuan, Qifan Wang, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces GazeAct, a real-robot manipulation dataset pairing 12,000 demonstrations across 40 tasks and five domains with 300 Hz operator gaze recorded directly on the robot camera feed during screen-based teleoperation. The dataset enables training multi-view vision-language-action policies regularized by human attention signals to better ground instructions in objects and contact points.

entry.title: EG-GRPO: Evidence-Guided Step-level Credit Assignment for Deep Search Agents

author.name: Sijia Luo, Mengjie Gao, Yuxiao He, Mengshu Sun, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: EG-GRPO improves RL training of LLM search agents by deriving step-level supervision from evidence annotations in synthetic deep search data, identifying the first supporting citation for each required evidence item rather than relying solely on trajectory-level outcome rewards. This grounds step credit assignment in the actual search and reasoning process.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers

author.name: Sravanth Kodavanti, Manjunath Arveti

entry.summary: MOSAIC applies multi-objective neural architecture search to learn per-layer KV-cache budgets for token-eviction methods, instead of the uniform budgets used by methods like SnapKV, H2O, and AdaKV. One search yields a budget-score trade-off that transfers across target budgets, beating uniform allocation in 146 of 154 tested settings on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Shiao Xie, Siyu Chen, Jianwei Lv, Xiandong Li, Yujin Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes privileged-correction contamination in multimodal RL with verifiable rewards: token-level teacher corrections may conflate visual evidence with linguistic priors, style, or the privileged view itself. The method makes on-policy self-distillation corrections visually attributable before distillation, improving error localization in visual reasoning. Combines RLVR with dense teacher supervision in a principled way.

entry.title: Continual Test-Time Learning with Evolution Strategies

author.name: Guangya Hao, Yiting Duan, Longyan Tan, Yunbo Long, Hao Wu, Ge Zheng, Alexandra Brintrup, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: This paper proposes Evolution Strategy Reinforcement, a test-time adaptation method for LLMs in open-ended environments that derives supervision from a population rather than the single drifting policy, mitigating policy collapse and catastrophic forgetting. It removes dependence on external labeled data or reward signals during continual adaptation.

entry.title: fxBench: Evaluating and Understanding Formula Suggestions in Spreadsheets

author.name: Sanket Mhatre, Sumit Gulwani, Vu Le, Yasharth Bajpai, Gust Verbruggen

entry.summary: fxBench is the first public benchmark for proactive formula suggestions on real spreadsheets, from a Microsoft research team including Gulwani, Le, and Verbruggen. It addresses the challenges of context collection and representation, formula correctness, and latency/cost constraints needed for per-keystroke suggestions in Excel-like tools. Given that formula suggestions ship in Excel and Google Sheets, a public benchmark is a meaningful community contribution.

entry.title: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training

author.name: Dongyang Li, Mingsong Yan, Zheng Zhang, Sui Tang

entry.summary: T-MUON generalizes the Muon optimizer using t-SVD tensor decompositions, grouping structurally related Transformer gradients into third-order tensors and defining Muon-style updates via the M-transform. The authors prove the exact update is a steepest-descent direction under the star-M spectral norm with convergence guarantees, and evaluate on GPT-2-style and LLaMA-style models from 51M parameters up. This extends the rapidly growing orthogonalized-optimizer line for LLM pretraining.

entry.title: Memory as Belief: Bayesian Evolution of Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Yiming Xu, Qian Yang, Zihan Chen, Yuefei Wu, Wenhan Zeng, Bin Shi, Bo Dong

entry.summary: BEAM reformulates memory value evaluation for LLM agents as a parameterized cognitive process inspired by the Bayesian brain hypothesis, treating memory as evolving belief rather than relying on historical retrieval success rates. It accounts for context-dependency of memory usefulness and varying reliability of estimates under different amounts of evidence. The goal is more accurate reuse of accumulated experience for continual agent adaptation.

entry.title: Distributionally-Robust Policy Learning with Observational Data

author.name: Debmalya Mandal

entry.summary: This paper studies policy learning from observational data that maximizes worst-case policy value over an f-divergence ball around the data-generating distribution, targeting applications like personalized medicine and welfare targeting where deployment distributions may shift. The estimator combines cross-fitted doubly-robust scores for conditional treatment effects with DRO solvers handling KL, chi-squared, and CVaR ambiguity sets, with convergence guarantees provided. It bridges causal inference and robust optimization.

entry.title: Statistical Learning Theory for Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Joel Wills, Yuanfan Li, Yiming Ying, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: This paper provides a statistical learning theory for DPO, characterizing structural approximation error through the triangle-curl of preference log-odds, which vanishes exactly when preferences admit a Bradley-Terry representation. It establishes upper and lower bounds on excess logistic risk separating structural misspecification from model capacity and finite-sample effects.

entry.title: Copying Under Repetition: From Prefix Matching to Position Hashing

author.name: Anxin Guo, Tianlong Huang, Chenxiao Yang, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: The paper explains why frontier LLMs fail to copy long repeated-character blocks and proves that a two-layer transformer with logarithmic-bit precision and modest width can copy any string up to a horizon N and terminate correctly under arbitrary repetition. The construction uses RoPE-style VO-rotations with small prime periods and the Chinese Remainder Theorem to encode distances modulo primes.

entry.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check

author.name: Ruqiya Bin Safi

entry.summary: Holding target model, prompts, and responses fixed while varying only the LLM grader, the author shows that several 8-9B parameter graders collapse compliant responses into the neighboring evasion class, with one assigning the compliance label zero times in 900 responses. This class collapse distorts reported jailbreak attack success rates and reproduces across model families and harmful request types. The paper proposes per-class label counting as a free, label-free diagnostic check.

entry.title: DeGMatch: Target-Aware Reasoning Data Selection via Deconfounded Gradient Matching

author.name: Changho Lee, Janghoon Han, Rajdeep Mukherjee, Yeda Song, Lening Nick Cui, Xinya Du, Honglak Lee

entry.summary: Studies target-aware data selection for LLM reasoning post-training, finding that existing gradient-matching methods suffer from limited target discrimination on long reasoning trajectories due to dominant population-level gradient structure. DeGMatch constructs a target-relevance-adjusted gradient space before matching, improving selection quality for capability specialization.

entry.title: Dual-Slot: From Serial Loops to Parallel Slots in Language Models

author.name: Yiqin Hao, Zitong Wang, Boyi Zeng, He Li, Shixiang Song, Feichen Song, Yifan Liu, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Dual-Slot reorganizes serial looped language model computation into parallel latent and prediction slots, shifting the latent dependency across adjacent tokens so that prediction does not wait on latent computation. This replaces two sequential module invocations with a single paired invocation, reducing autoregressive decoding latency while preserving depth.

entry.title: Arbitrary-Scale Anisotropic 3D MRI Super-Resolution with Gaussian Prototypes

author.name: Aditya Rastogi, Ramon Leiser, Prateek Singh, Martha Foltyn-Dumitru, Martin Bendszus, Fabian Bamberg, Klaus Maier-Hein, Kai Schlamp, Alexander Radbruch, Gianluca Brugnara, Philipp Vollmuth

entry.summary: Presents GSMR3D, a continuous volumetric super-resolution model that reconstructs arbitrary isotropic and anisotropic MRI resolutions from a single checkpoint per contrast. It combines a learned dictionary of anisotropic 3D Gaussian prototypes with scale-conditioned frequency encoding and exact measurement-consistency projection, targeting reduced scan times across heterogeneous clinical protocols.

entry.title: Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation

author.name: Junwei Wen, Deshui Miao, Guangming Lu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Xin Li, Wenjie Pei

entry.summary: Proposes TCoVP, a spatiotemporally grounded form of video chain-of-thought that organizes query-relevant observations into a chronological reasoning chain, with each primitive linking an entity reference to temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence. This targets the video reference gap in text-only CoT for reasoning video segmentation, where linguistic inference is not made visually explicit.

entry.title: Tricking Synthetic Image Detectors with Amortized Generative Attacks

author.name: Mohamed Awad, Khaled Elhady, Yasser Rohaim, Samuele Poppi, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates transferability of attacks against synthetic-image detectors, introducing a two-axis protocol that independently varies surrogate detector and source generator across four detectors and five generators. Comparing iterative perturbation attacks (MIG, MuMoDIG) with the amortized generative attack Tricker, it exposes underexplored failure modes of AI-image detection.

entry.title: RoAR-VAE: Improving Latent Diffusability through Robust Prediction

author.name: Yang Yue, Fangyun Wei, Yitong Wang, Jinjing Zhao, Henry Zheng, Dong Chen, Gao Huang

entry.summary: RoAR-VAE revisits REPA-E and shows that removing its diffusion objective while retaining semantic prediction from corrupted latents matches downstream generation performance, motivating a general robust-prediction principle for visual tokenizers. It instantiates this with RobustAlign and a complementary objective to make generation-relevant information recoverable from corrupted latents. This informs how to design better tokenizers for latent diffusion.

entry.title: AutoPruner: Agentic Depth Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Tao Lin, Yikeng Chen, Qiwei Liang, Zinan Xie, Zhengtu Liang, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: Introduces AutoPruner, an LLM-agent-driven framework that jointly searches layer-pruning structures and recovery recipes for vision-language-action models via closed-loop experimentation. Offline layer interventions supply functional evidence about action-output sensitivity, which the agent combines with evaluation history to propose deletion sets under a search budget. It addresses the practical need to deploy large VLA models cheaply.

entry.title: Humanoid SRL: Augmenting Humanoids with Supernumerary Limbs for Coordinated Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Fukang Liu, Feiyang Wu, Paul Barsa, Jaehwi Jang, Akshat Jain, Zhigen Zhao, Yipu Chen, Zhaoyuan Gu, Nikhil Vemuri, Anshul Chandaliya, Kaijie Zhu, Sean Lublinsky, Matthew Zhu, Tony G. Chen, Ye Zhao

entry.summary: This study physically integrates a supernumerary robotic arm onto a humanoid platform to explore how morphological augmentation reshapes the feasible action space for loco-manipulation, including cases where both standard arms are occupied. The added limb must be coordinated with whole-body motion and balance, and the authors provide quantitative analysis and hardware experiments across two configurations. This extends humanoid capability beyond anthropomorphic constraints.

entry.title: Cartender: Verifiable Language-Conditioned Driving by Learning the Drives Not Taken

author.name: Zhiwen Chen, Benjin Zhu, Yan Xie, Jun Ma

entry.summary: Cartender learns language-conditioned driving from counterfactual alternatives: a Counterfactual Branching scheme uses a vision-language model to propose alternative futures and their selecting instructions from single logged recordings, while unsupported instructions yield negative labels, all without a simulator. This addresses the one-to-many nature of driving where logs record only the action taken.

entry.title: What Social Media Teaches Us About Accumulative AI Risks

author.name: Dawei Li, Bohan Jiang, Huan Liu

entry.summary: This position paper argues AI safety research over-focuses on catastrophic existential risks while neglecting accumulative harms that build through repeated use, feedback loops, and interconnected deployments, analogous to harms observed with social media. It proposes that safety assessments must capture gradual effects like selective exposure, recurring decision biases, and exploitable personal profiles.

entry.title: WAQS: Weight Absorption for Quadratic Probing and Affine Steering

author.name: Ding Zhu, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili

entry.summary: WAQS is an activation steering framework that achieves input-dependent, state-dependent steering of LLM behavior with no additional inference-time computation. It models a concept with a quadratic probe whose gradient yields an affine, activation-dependent steering direction, resolving the usual trade-off between fixed steering vectors and costly nonlinear interventions. This advances lightweight model control as an alternative to fine-tuning.

entry.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations

author.name: Meng-Chen Wu, Umesh Bodhwani

entry.summary: This paper organizes the pluralistic alignment literature around a two-layer taxonomy separating Overton, Steerable, and Distributional pluralism, and distinguishing whose preferences define the reference from what evidence demonstrates success. It clarifies how existing work conflates distinct questions about desired behavior, reference populations, and evaluation. As a survey/position paper it should help structure a growing research area.

entry.title: HSPR: Recovering Software-Agent Benchmark Scores via Hierarchical Posterior Inference

author.name: Wanyi Chen, Wanqin Shen, Yuanchen Shi, Zhensu Sun, Fang Kong

entry.summary: HSPR reduces the cost of evaluating software agents on full benchmarks by combining source-fitted response factors with uncertain group success rates, updating posteriors as observed outcomes arrive. Its acquisition criterion provably equals the expected one-step reduction in full-score posterior variance, enabling cheap subset-based score recovery.

entry.title: Teaching Code Agents to Ask Without Leaking Private Code

author.name: Wenjia Jiang, Jieke Shi, Zhensu Sun, Chengran Yang, Shidong Pan, Peixin Zhang, Yifan Jia, James Hoang, Xiwei Xu, Zhenchang Xing, David Lo, Zhou Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes utility-verified abstraction (UVA), which teaches local coding agents to describe private entities by role and type when consulting stronger cloud models, avoiding exposure of identifiers, paths, and source. Rewrites are kept only if they disclose fewer private entities and still yield successful repairs in replayed trajectories.

entry.title: MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yiming Zong, Shiyuan Piao, Jiashuo Jiang, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: Introduces MemPrice, which treats an agent's active context window as a shared resource and allocates it across memories and representation levels using an adaptive price that rises with memory pressure. Detail is retained only when its estimated retention value justifies the context footprint, with pressure persisting across refreshes for long-run control.

entry.title: DAGLoop: Aligning Method Design with Experimental Feedback in Automated AI Research

author.name: Dengyuxing Wang, Yonggang Zhang, Qianshu Cai, Huajiang Zheng, Jun Song, Yangqiu Song, Yike Guo

entry.summary: DAGLoop improves automated AI research agents by applying ablation-style analysis to candidate method revisions, testing each design decision in isolation rather than relying only on overall evaluation outcomes. This lets the loop determine which decisions actually produced expected effects and should be retained or revised. The approach addresses credit-assignment ambiguity in iterative machine learning method discovery.

entry.title: Stepwise Reasoning Verification: Don't Generate, Classify!

author.name: Yifei Shi, Michalis Korakakis, Rami Aly, Eric Chamoun, Lukasz Szpruch, Andreas Vlachos

entry.summary: The paper recasts stepwise verification of LLM reasoning as natural language inference, with the problem and partial solution prefix as premise and the next reasoning step as a hypothesis to classify as entailed or non-entailed. This enables error localization at individual steps and controlled comparison of encoder classification, decoder classification, and decoder generation paradigms. The title's conclusion suggests classification outperforms generation for verification.

entry.title: P(Yes): 15$\times$ Improvements via Test-Time Scaling of Decision Models

author.name: Lev Stambler

entry.summary: This work adds training-free test-time search to frozen decision models by reading the model's probability of endorsing a proposed answer and iteratively editing or jointly optimizing answers to raise that probability. Accuracy improves across all tested models and datasets, with the largest gains on logic puzzles requiring exact correctness, where Qwen3.8-27B improves from 2 to 30 fully correct puzzles. It demonstrates that decision-model probabilities can serve as an effective search signal.

entry.title: ActTime: Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series

author.name: Xinxing Zhou, Xiaojie Yuan, Yanlong Wen, Ming Jin

entry.summary: ActTime is an action-conditioned world model for time series that updates variable-specific latent states via action-conditioned transitions and rolls them forward under candidate actions to compare counterfactual plans. Training uses only factual trajectories, enabling counterfactual prediction for controlled systems without action-diverse data.

entry.title: CODA: Cohort- and Drift-aware Foundation Model for Multimodal Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Changshuo Liu, Jiaqi Zhu, Wenqiao Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: CODA is a multimodal clinical foundation model that explicitly integrates population-level cohort structure and patient-specific deviation from group prototypes, motivated by how clinicians reason over similar patient cohorts. It also addresses drift awareness, aiming to reflect real-world clinical reasoning beyond individual-sample prediction.

entry.title: EmbodiedWorld-200K: Toward Embodied World Agents via Embodied-Planning Dataset and Interactive World Models

author.name: X. Feng, J. Tang, Z. Lin, L. Chen, S. Shao, Q. Lu, K. Huang

entry.summary: Defines Embodied World Agents (EWAs) for open-world navigation and planning, and releases EmbodiedWorld-200K, a 200K+ sample dataset spanning diverse 3D scenes with multi-level supervision, alongside interactive world models. The goal is to move beyond single-scene, task-specific embodied systems.

entry.title: The Scheduler Is a Hidden Retriever: How Asynchrony Shapes Evidence Acquisition in Search Agents

author.name: Ruiyang Ren, Yuhao Wang, Yinan Zhang, Chunyan Miao

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that in language-model agents performing parallel reasoning and asynchronous search, delivery timing alone redirects search decisions even with identical initial evidence, with acquisition disagreement up to 24 percentage points above repeat variation. The dependence persists across repeated searches, and the authors prove an acquisition-regret bound showing that invariance at fixed early arrival counts can limit use of already-received evidence.

entry.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts

author.name: Heejeong Nam, Divyat Mahajan, Quentin Le Lidec, Randall Balestriero, David Klindt

entry.summary: AnyGoal is a benchmark of goal-shifted task variants built from widely used world model environments, studying compositional generalization: whether world models can recombine familiar state and action factors into valid dynamics beyond expert rollout coverage. It connects data coverage, dynamics generalization, and downstream planning performance.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Bi-Approximate CHC Solving

author.name: Baiting Jiang

entry.summary: This work proposes Derivation Power Under-approximations (DPUs), where an LLM proposes solver-certified under-approximations of multi-step constrained Horn clause derivations, validated via SMT with symbolic witnesses. Validated DPUs can be soundly composed and reused, helping CHC solvers find deep counterexamples that require extensive rule unfolding.

entry.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jiakun Fan, Min Xiao, Qiang Wang, Neiwen Ling, Zhichao Liu, Zhihao Jia, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos, Zijun Wei

entry.summary: DScout observes that higher mean accepted tokens in diffusion-drafted speculative decoding need not yield higher throughput due to prefix-acceptance and latency effects, and introduces two factorizations guiding drafter training (inclusion, weighting, prediction losses) and inference for throughput. This better aligns diffusion drafters with the actual acceptance dynamics of verification.

entry.title: How Much Can We Prune? Exploring the Performance Limits of Visual Token Pruning

author.name: Janghoon Cho, Shubhankar Borse, Reza Pourreza, Juntae Lee, Jihwan Bang, Munawar Hayat, Fatih Porikli

entry.summary: This work reframes visual token pruning for vision-language models as selecting one shared visual-token subset under a fixed budget across a broad question distribution, using offline search to establish upper bounds on achievable performance. It aims to distinguish intrinsic pruning limits from limitations of current selection algorithms.

entry.title: Agentic Interpretation: Harness-Governed Evidence Construction for Software Agents

author.name: Yifeng He, Yanjun Wang, Siwei Cui, Aritra Sengupta, Murali Krishna Ramanathan

entry.summary: AgInt is a framework in which software agents answer behavioral questions about code by proposing typed evidence records that a deterministic harness admits, grades, and persists, licensing answers only under task-specific rules. Append-only certificate states provide auditable decision records and persistent external state.

entry.title: Which Long Documents Matter? A Controlled Study of Data Selection for Context Extension

author.name: Junlong Jia, Jiang Zhou, Xing Wu, Chaochen Gao Tinghao Yu, Feng Zhang, Lilin Wang

entry.summary: A controlled study of training-data selection for extending Qwen2.5-3B context to 128K under matched 6B-token budgets, finding that random long-document sampling beats repacking and that LongPPL-based key-token density selection yields further gains where generic-quality and LLM-judge selectors do not. Introduces truncLongPPL, scoring only a truncated prefix with measured cost savings and near-equal downstream performance.

entry.title: CasePlay: Self-Play Reinforcement Learning from Case Reports for Medical Reasoning

author.name: Hao Wang, Zihan Wang, Kai Wu, Jian Yao, Yiwen Ye, Yongcan Luo, Dapeng Wu, Jiale Chen, Haihua Yang

entry.summary: CasePlay converts unlabeled clinical case reports into RL training signals for medical reasoning via document-grounded self-play, addressing failure modes such as knowledge-point fixation and difficulty drift found in existing self-play methods. It reduces reliance on expert-labeled questions and costly synthetic data generation for clinical LLM training.

entry.title: Auto-MD-bench: Evaluating Autoresearch Agents for Real-World Medical Tasks

author.name: Shenqi Zhou (National University of Singapore, Zhejiang University), Qiran Zou (National University of Singapore), Wenhao Zhao (National University of Singapore), Zhenyu Liao (Amazon), Dianbo Liu (National University of Singapore)

entry.summary: Auto-MD-bench evaluates autonomous ML development agents on 15 real-world medical tasks, testing whether optimizing simple discrimination metrics like AUROC produces models suitable for clinical use. The benchmark additionally measures calibration and robustness across patient populations, revealing gaps between target-metric performance and real-world medical requirements.

entry.title: Vision as Proprioception: Estimating Humanoid Robot Pose from Video

author.name: Jiaxi Jiang, Matthias Heyrman, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Marco Hutter, Christian Holz

entry.summary: HumanoidPose recovers full-body joint configurations of humanoid robots in world space from video alone, treating vision as proprioception when onboard state information is unavailable due to privacy, ownership, or communication constraints. The unified model combines pretrained human-pose features with robot kinematics to predict joint configurations for each embodiment, also enabling use of online and AI-generated robot videos lacking joint labels.

entry.title: Enhanced Masked Diffusion Unlearning

author.name: Tomer Garber, Tom Tirer

entry.summary: This paper improves machine unlearning for masked diffusion language models, which generate text by iterative token unmasking with bidirectional context. Building on the first MDLM-specific unlearning method that matches a frozen prompt-masked anchor via KL divergence, the authors identify limitations of the anchor-based approach and propose an enhanced method balancing forget-set removal with capability preservation.

entry.title: When Better Opportunities Backfire: Service Worker Responses to Parallel AI Deployment in Customer Acquisition

author.name: Xinyu Fu, Shulong Luo, Narayan Ramasubbu, Peng Shen, Xincheng Wang, Yucheng Wang

entry.summary: Using over half a million customer outreach records around an AI voice-agent deployment at a Chinese health-insurance brokerage, this study applies regression-discontinuity-in-time to show that AI-driven lead routing enriches human workers' opportunities but raises their reservation value, reducing persistence on leads in hand. It offers rare field evidence on how parallel AI deployment reshapes human work behavior.

entry.title: A Calibrated Instrument for Detecting Disposition Drift in Language Models

author.name: Jerry Kaplan

entry.summary: Adapts a calibrated measurement methodology to detect degradation of certified safe behaviors (deception, power seeking, sycophancy) as models undergo fine-tuning or setting changes, applying it to two open-weight models. Unlike summary rates scored by another AI, the instrument quantifies precision and error analysis, enabling trustworthy detection of disposition drift before deployment.

entry.title: VEILED-SH: Vulnerability Expression through Indirect Language Evaluation Dataset (Self-Harm)

author.name: Leanne Tan, Keith Chua, Shaun Khoo, Onno P. Kampman, Lim Ruling Charmaine, Hazirah Hoosainsah, Kellie Yu Hui Sim, Kai He, Kenny Tsu Wei Choo, Roy Ka-Wei Lee

entry.summary: VEILED-SH is a 10,003-prompt benchmark evaluating single-turn AI responses to indirect expressions of suicide, self-harm, and distress, spanning counselor chat, forums, platform search, and triage contexts, with Singapore-grounded sources and an expert-validated multi-label taxonomy. It uniquely addresses cultural variation, application context, and practitioner disagreement. Automated judge profiles are calibrated to practitioners and clinicians.

entry.title: Large-Scale Biomedical RAG: Corpus Scaling, Document Representation, and Efficiency Trade-offs

author.name: Adri\'an S\'anchez-Freire, Gonzalo P\'erez-G\'omez, Aitziber Atutxa, Ander Barrena

entry.summary: This paper presents a controlled, large-scale evaluation of how corpus scale, document representation (abstract, flat full-text, hierarchical full-text), and reranking affect biomedical RAG effectiveness and efficiency. Configurations are evaluated on five external benchmarks plus a held-out test set, with retrieval latency and index storage measured to quantify operational cost. It provides practical guidance for building biomedical RAG systems at scale.

entry.title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation

author.name: Shashwat Saxena, Mehul Goel, Sreyas Venkataraman, Sarvesh Patil, Max Simchowitz

entry.summary: VaDar (Value Disaggregation) trains a single subgoal-independent policy that maximizes a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values, requiring subgoal information only at training time and removing costly subgoal selection at deployment for long-horizon tasks. Experiments show it is consistently competitive with and frequently outperforms goal- and subgoal-conditioned baselines. It offers an alternative to the classic decompose-then-condition recipe for long-horizon RL.

entry.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models

author.name: Huawei Lin, Jinting Liu, Tan Yu, Weijie Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a latent communication interface where a frozen encoder LLM compresses context once into a fixed-size package that a receiver LLM selectively reads per question, avoiding reprocessing full text for each query. It satisfies compactness, reusability, and cross-model readability simultaneously, which prior compression methods only partially achieve. Targets efficiency of multi-LLM systems.

entry.title: DISCERN: Identifiable Disease Evidence for Generalizable Medical Multimodal Learning

author.name: Xiaoguang Zhu, Pengyi Jiang, Juncen Guo, Jingyi Wu, Lianlong Sun, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Models clinical multimodal data with a latent structural causal model where disease state and background factors generate physiology, while cohorts differ in selection and measurement. It identifies conditional disease evidence without disease-state labels, removing enrollment shortcuts via a minimal selection statistic and yielding an identifiable reference posterior under specified shift families. Targets the common failure of clinical models that break on new cohorts.

entry.title: Inside the Loop: A Mechanistic Study of Weight-Tied Transformers on Depth-Bound Algorithmic Tasks

author.name: Magnus Sesodia, Juil Sock, Philip Torr, Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: Using directed permutation traversal with per-hop ground truth, this mechanistic study examines what each iteration of a looped (weight-tied) transformer computes on multi-hop algorithmic tasks. The findings clarify whether looping merely simulates a deeper untied stack and establish that a minimum effective depth is necessary to solve the task.

entry.title: Transformers as Adaptive Kernel Learners across Tasks for In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhaiming Shen, Alexander Cloninger, Rongjie Lai, Wenjing Liao

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows transformers can act as adaptive kernel learners for in-context learning, extending prior analyses that assumed fixed kernel functions. Because query and key matrices are trained, attention implements a kernel that adapts across tasks, and the paper establishes statistical guarantees for this adaptive-kernel view of ICL. Authors include established researchers in the theory of ICL.

entry.title: FlowMaker: From Tasks to Cost-Efficient Generative AI Workflow Deployments

author.name: Dimitrios Liakopoulos, Prasoon Sinha, Neeraja J. Yadwadkar

entry.summary: FlowMaker is a system for serving generative AI workflows that jointly optimizes workflow structure, model assignments, and deployment configurations under dynamic workloads, rather than fixing these decisions early or optimizing them in isolation. It emphasizes joint exploration of all combinations and reuse of deployed LLMs to reduce cost. This addresses real cost-efficiency challenges as LLM pipelines move into production at scale.

entry.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Pointwise Replicable Agnostic Learning

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: The paper determines the optimal sample complexity for pointwise replicable agnostic learning on finite and countable domains, where two predictors trained with a shared seed must agree at each fixed query with high probability. For any binary class of VC dimension d, the required sample size is characterized up to constants as Theta(d/(rho^2 alpha^2) + log(1/beta)/alpha^2) across accuracy, failure, and replicability parameters. The learner is improper, uses shared randomness, and covers zero-mass queries.

entry.title: Follow the Mixed Groups: Ridge-Tracking Gaussian Sampling for Zero-Variance Web Rollouts

author.name: Tomas Duncun, Jonah Ellison, Owen Pell, Mateo Ruiz, Hanae Fujita, Ingrid Solberg, Caleb Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper addresses the zero-variance group problem in group relative policy optimization for web-based agents, where groups that are all-correct or all-wrong waste already-spent search and fetch budgets. The proposed RIDGE method keeps a Gaussian curriculum but replaces the sampling coordinate with a Beta-posterior-based ridge-tracking scheme that targets prompts whose pass rates can still produce mixed groups. This is a targeted efficiency improvement for RL training of web agents.

entry.title: FTFM: Factorized Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Josif Grabocka

entry.summary: FTFM introduces a factorized attention scheme for tabular foundation models that preserves cell-level representations while computing each cell update through the interaction of a contextual latent per row and one per column, avoiding both expensive full row-column attention and information loss from collapsing rows into fixed embeddings. This addresses the efficiency-expressiveness trade-off in in-context tabular learning. The design parallels factorization ideas from matrix methods.

entry.title: LOOP: Recovery-Aligned Iterative Layer Pruning via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Liang Xu, Shufan Shen, Zhongni Hou, Yufei Zhang, Wei Lin, Guojun Yin, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: LOOP rethinks LLM layer pruning by interleaving layer selection with capability recovery instead of one-shot removal followed by retraining. It uses on-policy distillation signals from recovery to guide which layers to prune, aiming to better preserve reasoning capabilities under a fixed training budget.

entry.title: Provable Adversarial Detection: Prime Quantization meets Gromov--Wasserstein

author.name: Manohar Kaul, Sadbhavana Babar, Aditya Ramesh, Aditya Saibewar, Fumiyoshi Kasahara, Maki Inui, Hiroaki Kurihara

entry.summary: The authors develop a theoretically grounded adversarial example detector based on comparing sample geometry across two complementary metric spaces: a standard CNN embedding and a novel prime-quantized space that absorbs small perturbations, using Gromov-Wasserstein comparisons. The key insight is that adversarial perturbations cannot preserve geometric structure across spaces with fundamentally different properties.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Learning of Heterogeneous Survival Treatment Effects under Time-Varying Treatments

author.name: Tom\`as Garriga, Munib Mesinovic, Luke De Bretton-Gordon, Gerard Sanz, Axel Brando, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a doubly robust learner for heterogeneous survival treatment effects under time-varying treatments and censoring, a setting where existing survival learners handle only baseline treatments and longitudinal effect learners assume uncensored outcomes. It sequentially adjusts for both treatment and censoring to estimate which treatment sequences maximize survival probability.

entry.title: Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay

author.name: Wen-Zhi Li, Sainyam Galhotra, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: Analyzes how RLVR reduces reasoning diversity in LLMs, showing from finite-sample learning dynamics that limited on-policy rollouts progressively suppress semantically distinct but equally rewarded reasoning modes, which standard RL rarely recovers. The proposed TAR framework replays a compact memory bank of diverse base-model solutions to preserve correct reasoning diversity.

entry.title: Denoising Implicit Variational Inference

author.name: Zitong Wang, Zekun Wu, Longlin Yu, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: DIVI addresses the intractable marginal score problem in semi-implicit variational inference by learning the score directly through denoising score matching, replacing costlier reverse-conditional sampling or approximation approaches used in UIVI-style methods. The learned score serves as a plug-in estimator in path-gradient ELBO estimates. This offers a more stable and efficient route to training expressive implicit variational families.

entry.title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic API Use

author.name: Tianhe Lu, Sakuna Harinda Jayasundara, Eric Spero, Ewan Tempero, Robert Biddle, Giovanni Russello

entry.summary: The authors study whether internal representation changes associated with different cryptographic API repairs in LLM-generated code share a common direction that can be used for intervention. Building a dataset of 48,000 matched program pairs across four languages and ten misuse categories, they extract repair vectors by subtracting misuse from secure program representations and find consistency across five models, enabling activation steering for safer code generation.

entry.title: SPLASH: Contrastive Audit Pressure for Detecting and Localizing Security Hallucinations in Generated Code

author.name: Mirza Masfiqur Rahman, MD Ajwad Akil, Imtiaz Karim, Ashish Kundu, Ramana Kompella, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: SPLASH detects and localizes security hallucinations in LLM-generated code that passes functional tests but is insecure, using a training-free measure called audit pressure that contrasts teacher-forced log-probabilities under a security review versus a style review. Grounded in a probabilistic model of competing edits, it can select the secure candidate program and pinpoint vulnerable statements without training or CWE-specific rules.

entry.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression

author.name: Andreea-Alexandra Musat, Nicolas Boumal

entry.summary: The authors prove that gradient descent with sufficiently large step size achieves an epsilon optimality gap on multiclass logistic regression in a number of iterations independent of epsilon, depending only on data properties such as number of points and margin. The proof connects rescaled gradient descent in the large-step limit to the perceptron algorithm.

entry.title: Ask Less, Ask Better: Allocating User Attention in Proactive LLM Agents with Interruption Budgets

author.name: Xuanming Zhang, Amir H. Rezaeian, Miguel Ballesteros, Weiyi Sun, Werner Geyer, Lydia B. Chilton, Zhou Yu, Yassine Benajiba, Dan Roth

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation protocol for proactive LLM agents that separates how often an agent asks clarifying questions from how well it asks them, using an interruption budget plus a user-attention cost that penalizes hard-to-read or low-value questions via a human-validated LLM judge. Human annotators agreed with the cost metric about which of two conversations demanded more effort 75% of the time.

entry.title: Beyond Factual Accuracy: A Benchmark for Evaluating Perspective Alignment in LLMs

author.name: Sunghoon Kim, Sangyeop Kim

entry.summary: PerspectiveBench quantifies how well LLMs adhere to user-requested perspectives in scenarios where multiple valid reasoning paths coexist, using a Perspective Alignment Score. Experiments show state-of-the-art models include target content but fail to exclude non-requested perspectives, and RAG improves grounding without fixing this control failure.

entry.title: From Unverifiable Domain Text to Cross-Lingual RLVR via Code-Switched Task Synthesis

author.name: Cheonbok Park, Jihwan Kim, Shinyoung Joo, Joosung Lee, Hwiyeol Jo, Jeonghoon Kim, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: The paper introduces code-switched task synthesis to derive target-language and code-switched RLVR task variants from otherwise unverifiable English domain text, using fill-in-the-middle multiple-choice QA as a seed format. This addresses data scarcity for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards in non-English specialized domains.

entry.title: LEAPS: Long-context Evaluation of Adaptive Pattern Learning and State Tracking

author.name: Howard Yen, Nitya Mani, Alex Renda, Christopher S. Hardin

entry.summary: Introduces LEAPS, a benchmark of 12 novel tasks targeting three long-context capabilities: recall, state tracking, and pattern learning. Unlike existing long-context benchmarks that mostly test recall, LEAPS evaluates whether long-context language models can track evolving states and infer distributions from many in-context observations, capabilities needed by agents over long trajectories.

entry.title: AfriGuard: Safety and Robust Refusal For African Languages

author.name: Israel Abebe Azime, Jesujoba O. Alabi, Iffat Maab, Alexander D. Cai, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Atnafu Lambebo Tonja, Jonas Kgomo, Folasade Alabi, Salomey Osei, Saminu Muhammad Aliyu, Nkechinyere Faith Aguobi, Bontu Fufa Balcha, Blessing Sibanda, Davis David, Mouhamadane Mboup, Daud Abolade, Neo Putini, Louis Powell, Kiant'e Brantley, Philipp Slusallek, Dietrich Klakow, Julia Kreutzer

entry.summary: Introduces AfriGuard, a culturally grounded multilingual dataset for studying harmful intent detection, safety-category understanding, and refusal behavior across 10 African languages and English. It reveals how safety behaviors vary with linguistic and cultural context and provides resources for building culturally appropriate refusal systems.

entry.title: Beyond Generator-Specific Shortcuts: Open-World AI-Generated Video Detection via Adversarial Training

author.name: Qi Zhou, Yuanfan Li, Huiqi Deng, Hongbin Pei, Yazhe Tang

entry.summary: Analyzing AI-generated video detectors under cross-generator out-of-distribution shifts, the authors find detector representations heavily encode generator-specific cues, and naive perturbation of generator-sensitive tokens can even hurt OOD performance. They propose an adversarial training approach to suppress generator shortcuts and improve open-world generalization to unseen video generators.

entry.title: Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series

author.name: Shenyi Li, Ziyang Zhang, Wen Wu, Ming Liu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Time-JEPA fine-tunes video world models using low-dimensional, temporally aligned physical time series as auxiliary supervision, connecting video representations with physical state at corresponding time positions. This avoids domain-specific physical laws while giving more sustained attention to temporal physical-state evolution than frame- or pair-level supervision.

entry.title: IntriAdapt: Generalizable Intrinsic-Guided Test-Time Adaptation for Metric Geometry Estimation

author.name: Jiaxing Chen, Zizheng Yan, Jingyu Zhuang, Jinwei Chen, Shuguang Cui, Guanying Chen, Qingnan Fan

entry.summary: IntriAdapt uses camera intrinsics as an output-side geometric verifier for test-time adaptation, minimizing a closed-form residual between the predicted point cloud's viewing rays and those implied by known intrinsics. It optimizes a lightweight LoRA adapter on a frozen geometry foundation model, avoiding dependence on external depth measurements used by prior TTA approaches.

entry.title: CorrCLIPv2: Harnessing Unlabeled Images for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Dengke Zhang, Fagui Liu, Quan Tang, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: Proposes CorrCLIPv2, a training-free framework for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation that fixes noisy inter-class patch interactions in CLIP-based models. It combines class-agnostic mask generation to disentangle patch correlations, self-supervised spatially coherent features, and output regularization, leveraging unlabeled images without task-specific training.

entry.title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats

author.name: Hyebin Kim, Hwasik Jeong, Joonhyuk Park, Gyeongjin Kang, Jungwoo Kim, Younghyun Kim, Eunbyung Park

entry.summary: Introduces FineSplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework built around fine-grained image patches, with a dual-grouping strategy combining view-wise grouping for efficient neighboring-view interaction and 3D spatial grouping that reconnects geometrically related tokens. This addresses the prohibitive cost of global multi-view attention at high token resolutions while improving fine-grained geometry and appearance.

entry.title: A New Hope for PRNU on Modern Smartphones? Evidence That Device-Specific Fingerprints Survive Computational Photography

author.name: Benjamin Loison (Agence Minist\'erielle pour l'IA de D\'efense, France, ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France), Quentin Bammey (T\'el\'ecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, LTCI, Palaiseau, France), Thibaud Ehret (Agence Minist\'erielle pour l'IA de D\'efense, France), Rafael Grompone von Gioi (ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France), Pablo Mus\'e (ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France, IIE, Facultad de Ingenier\'ia, Universidad de la Rep\'ublica, Uruguay), Marina Gardella (ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France)

entry.summary: This forensic study investigates whether Photo Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) remains a reliable source-camera identifier on modern smartphones, where reported cross-device correlations have cast doubt. Using 30 controlled devices, the authors identify a model-shared component inflating the standard sPCE metric and propose Delta-sPCE, which restores discriminative fingerprint matching.

entry.title: Think Densely, Act Sparsely: Latent Expert Cognitive Chains for Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jie Wang, Guang Li, Zhijian Huang, Jinlong Li, Chenxu Dang, Hangjun Ye, Yahong Han, Long Chen

entry.summary: This paper argues that VLA driving models trained with sparse supervision (instructions, trajectories) discard dense scene information needed for safe driving, proposing a Think Densely, Act Sparsely paradigm. It instantiates latent expert cognitive chains that encourage explicit dense world representations in latent space before sparse action decoding.

entry.title: ActionRoPE: action as coordinates for spatially consistent control in planar-camera game world models

author.name: Zhiyang Deng, Yuzhe Wu, Zijun Lin, Yeying Jin

entry.summary: ActionRoPE is a parameter-free action interface for game world models that converts action-driven camera displacement into world-coordinate representations, rather than relying on generic feature conditioning. This exploits the well-defined planar geometry of top-down and isometric game worlds to achieve spatially consistent control during interactive generation.

entry.title: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning

author.name: Yuanhang Lei, Baofei Liu, Xingxuan Li, Tao Cheng, Zixuan Wang, Boming Zhao, Yujun Shen, Siyuan Huang, Ruizhen Hu, Peter Yichen Chen, Hujun Bao, Zhaopeng Cui

entry.summary: PhysSkin++ learns continuous neural skinning fields from static geometries to build compact deformation subspaces for real-time physics-based animation, generalizing across shapes and discretizations without per-object training. A physics-informed self-supervised strategy with conflict-aware gradient correction removes the need for simulation trajectories.

entry.title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents

author.name: Fuyao Zhang, Wenwen He, Jiaming Zhang, Yurong Hao, Xuan Wang, Guowei Guan, Che Wang, Longtao Huang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: FocusGUI tackles the problem that GUI agents receiving full streaming omni-modal context (screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, device states) at every step suffer from Sequential Distraction and irreversible trajectory drift. It introduces Focused Perception, realized as a lightweight adapter that dynamically prioritizes multimodal channels per action. This is relevant as GUI agents become a major application area.

entry.title: One Fact, Many Places: Redundant Evidence in Long Visual Documents Breaks Single-Gold Evaluation of Retrieval, Citation and Attribution

author.name: Xiaokang Yuan, Binhui Yao, Luwei Yang, Ruimin Chen, Zeng Wang

entry.summary: This evaluation study shows that facts in long visual documents often appear in multiple places, often cross-modally, breaking single-gold-location evaluation of retrieval, citation, and attribution. Annotating 420 questions from MMLongBench-Doc and MMDocRAG, they find 19.5-28% of questions have valid non-gold evidence locations. This exposes systematic mismeasurement in document understanding benchmarks.

entry.title: Drive2Gauss: FeedForward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction from Multimodal Generative Driving Videos

author.name: Tong Zhao, Zhiyuan Han, Lin Chen, Bowen Xie, Yunxi Qiao, Bohan Li, Weiqing Xiao, Gen Li, Shu Han, Xuyang Dai, Cheng Bi, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li

entry.summary: Drive2Gauss converts jointly generated RGB, metric depth, and dynamic flow from a multimodal video generator into dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes in a feedforward manner, avoiding per-sequence optimization. A Gaussian Query Decoder uses depth to initialize sparse 3D queries and flow to associate them over time. This enables reusable, view-controllable driving environments for simulation and autonomous driving research.

entry.title: Generative Priors for Total-Body PET Reconstruction

author.name: Movindu Dassanayake, George Webber, Denis Prokopenko, Julia A. Schnabel, Andrew J. Reader

entry.summary: TB-PET-DDS combines a CT-conditioned generative prior with patient-specific list-mode PET data for total-body PET reconstruction at low dose counts, enforcing PET consistency via a closed-form 3D MAP-EM fusion update during reverse diffusion. This is the first demonstration of explicit PET measurement conditioning at total-body scale. It could enable faster, lower-dose clinical imaging.

entry.title: A Spiking Ring-Attractor Architecture for Representation and Control of Revolute Robot Joints

author.name: Aung Htet, Alejandro Rodriguez Jimenez, Ruidong Ma, Alessandro Di Nuovo

entry.summary: Proposes a fully spiking neural control architecture where ring attractors encode revolute joint states on circular topologies, matching the true SO(2) geometry of such joints. Homeostatic regulation computes goal mismatch over distributed representations, and opponent gain-modulated populations convert mismatch into controlled phase shifts of the activity bump. This is an elegant marriage of neuroscientific circuit motifs with robot joint control.

entry.title: ContactKernels: Adaptive Proposals using Geometry-COnditioned Wrenches for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Aditya Kamireddypalli, Mat\'ias Mattamala, Jo\~ao Moura, Sethu Vijayakumar, Steve Tonneau, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: Introduces ContactKernels, a contact-adaptive proposal kernel for sampling-based MPC that uses geometry-conditioned wrench measurements to estimate contact location and local geometry, steering future sampling toward corrective motion. This exploits incidental contact as information rather than treating it as failure in contact-rich insertion tasks. A principled improvement over generic proposal distributions in SMPC.

entry.title: RoMo-GS: Efficient Online 3D Gaussian Splatting for Robot Mapping via Exposure-Integrated Motion Blur

author.name: Sangwoo Jung, Di Deng, Jiahui Fu, Laura Herlant, Ayoung Kim, Yafei Hu

entry.summary: RoMo-GS is an online 3D Gaussian Splatting system for robot mapping that analytically integrates each projected Gaussian over the camera exposure interval to handle motion blur at O(1) complexity per Gaussian, rather than averaging discrete sub-frames. It also bounds Gaussian growth during continuous online mapping.

entry.title: Learning Waypoints and Passage Events for Decentralized Multi-Quadrotor Trajectory Planning

author.name: Yunhan Shi, Jia Deng, Zehao Jia, Lin Cheng, Shengping Gong

entry.summary: The authors propose a learning-optimization framework for multi-quadrotor passage planning that predicts spatial waypoints and ordered passage events, which are then fed to independently solved per-vehicle trajectory planners. A common time grid aligns vehicles, and differentiable sequential convex programming incorporates rigid-body dynamics and thrust bounds. This decouples the joint spatiotemporal optimization problem while preserving coordination.

entry.title: FR-VLA: Implicit Force Reasoning VLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Jiaju He, Zhiyuan Yang, Ruyang Han, Jiahong Tang, Zhiping Lin, Haiyue Zhu

entry.summary: FR-VLA adds a force-relevance mechanism to vision-language-action models: visual-language context drives learnable force query tokens that produce an admission signal deciding when and how strongly force feedback should influence action generation, rather than injecting force through a fixed pathway. This targets contact-rich manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots

author.name: Hairuo Wei, Yunfan Ren, Renda Yang, Qiangsheng Huang, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: The authors propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework for wheel-legged quadrupeds that learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history to handle wheel slip and contact loss. A degeneracy-aware projection suppresses unreliable LiDAR constraints, improving localization robustness when geometric constraints are weak.

entry.title: From SEC Filings to Financial Signals: Evaluating LLMs on Stock Market Reactions and Analyst Forecasts

author.name: Shengkun Wang, Taoran Ji, Linhan Wang, Sattar Mansi, Chang-Tien Lu, Yinlin Chen

entry.summary: The study evaluates 13 general-purpose and finance-specialized LLMs on 45,964 Form 10-Q filing events (2001-2024), linking MD&A narrative text to fundamental ranks, analyst forecasts, and realized abnormal returns. It goes beyond QA-style financial benchmarks to test whether LLM outputs align with market and analyst outcomes across controlled information views and EPS forecasting interfaces.

entry.title: Is This Your Agent? Identity Watermarking for Agent Systems in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Yuwei Zhong, Yu Cheng, Jiuan Zhou, Weizhi Liu, Yi Xie, Yongkang Hu, Yuan Xie, Zhaoxia Yin

entry.summary: DASMark is an identity watermarking framework for LLM agent systems whose memories, skills, and configurations evolve in dynamic environments. It introduces Action-Preserving Embedding to learn semantically similar but distinguishable decision-expression channels for stable watermark embedding despite environmental changes. This addresses agent provenance and authentication, an emerging security concern as agents proliferate.

entry.title: ReTRACE: Feedback-Guided LLM Agent in a Chemistry Harness for Retrosynthesis Planning

author.name: Jinxiang Xie, Yijian Zhang, Qingyuan Yi, Jianyi Wang, Hao Dong

entry.summary: ReTRACE places an LLM agent in a chemistry harness integrating molecular tools, single-step prediction engines, a purchasable starting-material library, route memory, and a multi-criterion route evaluator for whole-route retrosynthesis planning. It introduces a route-quality metric combining programmatic checks with advisory scoring over stereochemistry, compatibility, cost, and greenness.

entry.title: Outcome-Anchored Credit Reallocation for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Yucheng Li, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: OACR addresses the trajectory-to-operation mismatch in outcome-supervised RL for agentic KGQA, where a rollout's outcome-level advantage is uniformly assigned to all tokens. It trains a KG-state outcome model that estimates outcome-reward changes between adjacent search states and converts these into per-operation credit. This provides finer-grained, verifiable credit assignment for multi-turn KG interactions.

entry.title: From Trace to Fix: Residual Task State in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Zile Huang, Ser-nam Lim

entry.summary: TRACE-FIX is a unified recovery framework for long-horizon stateful language agents built around a versioned residual task state: Trace converts execution logs into a dependency-linked ledger prioritizing unresolved requirements, and Fix formulates recovery as budgeted planning with outcome forecasting and explicit repair reserves. It addresses the gap where the action causing a defect, its symptom, and the state needing repair diverge.

entry.title: Productive State-Space Exploration for Multi-turn RL in LLM Agents

author.name: Mohammed Haroon Dupty, Yong Liang Goh, Song Guo, Wee Sun Lee

entry.summary: Diagnoses why LLM agents in multi-turn RL get stuck in loops of invalid or repetitive high-confidence actions, attributing this to mismatches between the agent's internal state representation and environment dynamics. Proposes methods to encourage productive state-space exploration for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Selective Transfer through Sequence Distillation: From Benchmark Knowledge to Backdoor Behaviour

author.name: Jonibek Mansurov, Sholpan Bolatzhanova, Filbert Aurelian Tjiaranta, Vallerie Alexandara Putra, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: The paper studies which teacher properties survive distillation, comparing benchmark knowledge and refusal backdoors across four distillation channels. Benchmark knowledge transfers reliably through all channels, including students trained only on teacher-generated number sequences with no natural language, while refusal backdoors do not transfer the same way. This reveals that distillation selectively transmits different kinds of hidden model properties.

entry.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhen Li, Mingfa Feng, Yiming Zhang, Yang Yu, Changhai Zhou, Pengxiang Li, Dongkuan Wu, Congkai Xie, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: miniTE shows that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient for consistent policy evaluation across separate training and sampling engines in native 4-bit RL for LLMs, and provides execution diagnostics plus cross-engine numerical alignment with native W4A4 GEMM. It improves consistency without altering the RL objective.

entry.title: Unbounded Losses, Unchecked Inputs: Measuring the Safeguards of LLM Options-Trading Agents

author.name: Mengxiao Wang, Nitesh Saxena

entry.summary: This is the first measurement of safeguards in real deployed LLM options-trading agents, screening 765 GitHub repositories and broker documentation to score 26 systems including all broker-native interfaces by enforced safeguards and worst-case loss of documented order paths. It moves beyond academic equities decision-flipping attacks to financial harm potential in shipped systems. The findings expose significant real-world risk in an unregulated agent ecosystem.

entry.title: UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop

author.name: Tieyuan Chen, Huabin Liu, Yingtao Zhang, Shijie Li, Tengyu Pan, Weiyao Lin, Jianguo Li

entry.summary: UpLoop is a post-training recipe that upcycles pretrained non-looped LLMs into looped (recurrent-depth) models by looping each selected layer locally, preserving the pretrained depth hierarchy, with hidden-wise gates on attention and MLP residual branches so later loops act as progressive refinements. This avoids the expense of pretraining looped models from scratch and reportedly breaks a commonly observed failure pattern.

entry.title: CHSM8: A Chess Transformer that Follows Natural-Language Style Prompts

author.name: Ilia Badanin

entry.summary: CHSM8 is a 210M-parameter chess Transformer trained without search on 1.07B Lichess games that reaches 1837 Elo against strength-limited Stockfish and beats larger search-free public models. It is then fine-tuned on synthetic data generated with Gemma-4-31B (an existing model) to follow free-text style prompts such as requesting a specific opening or playing style.

entry.title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation

author.name: Yanjin He, Cuifeng Shen, Wanzhou Lei, Maohua Li, Tao Lan, Kan Liu, Hanlin Tang, Qing Qu

entry.summary: Introduces Swift, a training method in which a frozen weak denoiser (e.g., an early checkpoint) guides a stronger diffusion model by extrapolating the regression target away from the weak prediction, amplifying underfit components at no extra inference cost. The weak guide requires no backpropagation during training and is discarded afterward, preserving the original sampler and conditional/unconditional modes.

entry.title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction

author.name: Moritz Wagner, Christophe Roux, Max Zimmer, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: KV-Surgeon addresses offline KV-cache compaction by accounting for the nonlinear coupling that softmax attention creates between deletion decisions, using calibration data and a tractable quadratic surrogate with closed-form solutions. Existing methods score candidates independently, ignoring these interactions. This could improve long-context serving efficiency where a fixed context is queried repeatedly.

entry.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing

author.name: Jianqiang Xia, Han Xu, Dianxi Shi

entry.summary: The paper identifies Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence in rubric-based RL, where as total rubric score rises, certain sub-dimension scores systematically decrease, indicating the policy sacrifices specific quality aspects to optimize the aggregate. The authors diagnose dimension imbalance and dimension absence, then propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation, which makes generations compete within each dimension separately. This mitigates rubric hacking and improves training robustness.

entry.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory

author.name: Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun, Di Wu, Sibo Peng, Mingyang Zhang, Zhen Yang, Ruiyi Zhang, Nanyun Peng, Zhe Gan, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness with a capability layer for tool interfaces plus persistent multimodal memory, motivated by a controlled study over 22 benchmarks showing that larger inference budgets alone give only modest gains. It enables grounded perception, external knowledge access, and interpretable tool outputs retained across reasoning steps. A systems contribution for visual agentic tool use.

entry.title: Muon Operates Beyond the Edge of Stability

author.name: Niko Covic, Baraq Lipshitz, Alexander Padula, Stefan Visnjic

entry.summary: This study provides the first empirical evidence that the Flat Minima Hypothesis extends to the Muon optimizer, showing sharpness strongly correlates with generalization gap on CIFAR-10 within each optimizer family. Notably, Muon operates stably above the sharpness-based Adaptive Edge of Stability threshold that bounds diagonally-preconditioned optimizers like Adam, suggesting it occupies a fundamentally different optimization regime.

entry.title: The Certification Exponent: Instance-Optimal Sequential Certification of Policy Improvement from History Dependent Logs

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: The paper addresses how many logged episodes are needed to certify that a new policy improves on a deployed one when the logging policy is history-dependent. It characterizes the answer via an exponent K-star, the smallest KL divergence to a non-improving law matching logged action probabilities, proving any sound certifier needs at least log(1/delta)/K-star episodes and that a plug-in Kelly certifier attains this rate to first order. This provides instance-optimal guarantees for sequential policy certification from offline data.

entry.title: Uncovering Semantic Hierarchies in Text-Attributed Graphs via Variational EM-based LLM-GNN Synergy

author.name: Yunhui Liu, Xudong Jin, Qizhuo Xie, Chunhui Zhao, Xiao Luo, Tao Zheng, Bin Chong, Tieke He

entry.summary: SHiFT combines LLM reasoning with GNN structural representation in a variational EM framework to learn hierarchical (rather than flat) semantic spaces on text-attributed graphs. The E-step uses LLMs as expert taxonomists to induce a semantic tree with a lightweight Mapping and Diagnosis strategy for cost-efficient hierarchical updates, while the M-step aligns the GNN encoder to the induced hierarchy. This addresses an important gap in capturing coarse-to-fine granularity in graph representation learning.

entry.title: Trust Your Targets: Is Target Propagation Block-Diagonal Gauss-Newton?

author.name: Giuseppe Castiglione, Christopher Buckley, Ivor Simpson

entry.summary: The paper rederives target propagation as trust-region optimization under a previously unexamined norm, clarifying when TP corresponds to Gauss-Newton updates, and introduces CGTP, which solves layer-local subproblems in parallel with conjugate gradients. A single adaptive parameter jointly controls the trust region and a matching bound on weight updates.

entry.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows

author.name: Qian Xie, Wenyue Hua, Yueli He, Sripad Karne, Armaan Agrawal, Nikos Pagonas, Eugene Wu, Kostis Kaffes, Tianyi Peng, Nairen Cao

entry.summary: The paper introduces Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of cost-aware Gittins search for recommending model-to-role assignments in LLM agentic workflows along the quality-cost (and latency) Pareto frontier. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs so each evaluation informs both quality and cost searches.

entry.title: Tilted Mondrian: Triage and Mitigation of Fine-grained Disparities in Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ziang Gao, Pengqi Liu, Archer Yi Yang, Mouloud Belbahri, Jesse C. Cresswell, Masoud Asgharian

entry.summary: The paper shows that Mondrian conformal prediction's group-wise coverage guarantees are coarse, allowing substantial disparities within finer strata, and introduces propensity standardization to assess how group composition drives disagreement between aggregate and fine-grained fairness comparisons. For mitigation, Tilted Mondrian improves fairness relative to group-wise calibration. This addresses a real gap in fair uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Yuxiang Lu, Yantong Liu, Jinghua Hou, Xueli Sun, Ruihua Han, Zhe Liu, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: TILDE transfers capabilities from large action-pretrained embodied foundation models to smaller policies via on-policy distillation at student-induced states combined with teacher-executed recovery trajectories. Its AutoDAgger pipeline uses a robotic reward model to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, reducing the data and compute needed to reproduce foundation-model pretraining benefits.

entry.title: A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models

author.name: George Panagopoulos, Saman Omidi, Tsz Pan Tong, Jun Pang

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard evaluation practices for gene perturbation prediction models are unstable: varying the number of top differentially-expressed genes flips the winning method 86.7% of the time under precision-based rankings across eight methods and six datasets. It further exposes that repeating a single predicted profile across cell-level rows, a common practice, can inflate metric scores.

entry.title: Toward a Universal Local Speech Feature Extractor Through Distillation

author.name: Jessica Yang, Marcelo Beramendi Caballero, Ju-Chieh Chou, Karen Livescu

entry.summary: Shows that the computationally heavy CNN feature extractors at the front of self-supervised speech models like HuBERT, WavLM, and data2vec can be replaced by a single small distilled two-layer extractor. The universal extractor retains most teacher performance on SUPERB(-SG), transfers to unseen models such as wav2vec 2.0, and needs only about 3% of the original MACs.

entry.title: A Thousand Faces: A Persuasion Benchmark with Experience-Grounded Persuadees Informed by Psychology and Pragmatics

author.name: Ziqing Zhuang, Dingyi Zhang, Deyu Zhou

entry.summary: ATF-Persu is a persuasion benchmark with 1,000 personas across 200 topics and nine domains, where personas are grounded in the experiences that shaped their beliefs and draw on attitude theory and conversational implicature. It evaluates whether persuasive arguments address a person's actual reasons rather than merely matching a belief description.

entry.title: Representations in Motion: Layer-wise Rotation and Trajectory Divergence in LLMs

author.name: Zhuonan Yang, Yik Siu Chan, Wannan Yang, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: Studies the layer-wise evolution of factuality representations and finds that factuality directions extracted under lying versus honest prompting conditions rotate away from each other across layers. A similar rotation appears in a 3D visual perspective-taking task, suggesting activation-trajectory divergence may be a general signature of controlled internal state manipulation.

entry.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression

author.name: Ziqing Man, Di Wu, Jia-Chen Gu, Junyi Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Introduces KEEP-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark with 4,102 cases directly assessing whether context compression preserves critical evidence for plausible references, explicit qualifiers, and minority perspectives, beyond what QA metrics capture. Even the strongest long-context models prove unreliable despite compression inputs averaging only 3.1K tokens in windows exceeding 100K.

entry.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks

author.name: Rohan Menon, Chih-Hong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces ASR_STEP, a metric that penalizes jailbreak attacks for repeated victim-model calls while retaining binary success judgments, reflecting the added detection opportunities each call gives deployed systems. Evaluations on JailBreakBench across GCG, PAIR, and PAP show meaningful score reductions for iterative attacks, changing relative attack rankings.

entry.title: Hierarchical and Query-Aware Visual Token Pruning for High-Resolution LVLMs

author.name: Luther Wei, Ling Zou, Kang-Yang Huang, Yu-Syuan Xu, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free, hierarchical visual token pruning framework for high-resolution large vision-language models that applies query-aware relevance computation before any LLM blocks execute, operating on the thumbnail-plus-local-crops token structure. This addresses the computational bottleneck of thousands of vision tokens while improving on prior query-agnostic or late, crop-level query-aware pruning.

entry.title: Visual Sufficiency Landscapes: Understanding Query-Conditioned Reliability in Visual Token Pruning

author.name: Zhenghan Li, Kexin Sun, Wei Zheng, Peng Hu, Xiao Wei, Anbo Huang

entry.summary: Introduces visual sufficiency landscapes to characterize how many visual token subsets preserve a vision-language model's behavior at a given layer and budget, measured across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL2-8B, and LLaVA-v1.5-7B on GQA and TextVQA. The analysis reveals that sufficiency abundance varies by query beyond estimation noise, offering a principled view of when token pruning is reliable.

entry.title: PoSTCache: From Forecasting to Postdictive Smoothing for Revisable Diffusion Caching

author.name: Liwei Lan, Hui Chen, Jungong Han, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: PoSTCache reformulates diffusion caching as revisable trajectory inference, allowing approximations from skipped evaluations to be corrected using feedback from later full-computation steps, unlike prior forward-only caching schemes. The training-free, plug-and-play framework adds postdictive smoothing to existing caching methods for diffusion and flow matching acceleration.

entry.title: HORIA: 4D Human and Object Reconstruction from a Monocular Video with Interaction-Aware Re-Rendering

author.name: Hyeongjin Nam, Taeryung Lee, Daniel Sungho Jung, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: HORIA performs joint 4D reconstruction of humans and objects from monocular video, handling composite interaction phases and occlusion-induced geometric inconsistency via interaction-aware decomposition and re-rendering. It aims to reconstruct how people physically interact with their environment from a single camera.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention for Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion

author.name: Yuanyu He, Zhuokun Chen, Yefei He, Zhiwei Tang, Jiasheng Tang, Yinghao Yu, Jianfei Cai, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: DASA shifts autoregressive diffusion transformers from dense spatiotemporal computation to sparse, motion-driven generation, decoupling video into regions analogous to video codecs to eliminate storage and compute redundancy. This targets the prohibitive memory and compute costs of long video generation. Video-codec-inspired sparsity is a pragmatic efficiency lever.

entry.title: CheckDistill: Adaptive Checklist Distillation for Efficient Distributional Reward Modeling in Image Editing

author.name: Yaqi Cai, Zuan Gao, Mengting Chen, Wei Li, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: CheckDistill is a pointwise reward modeling framework for RL-based instruction-guided image editing that decomposes editing conditions into atomic, independently verifiable requirements distilled into internalized instruction-adaptive checklists, producing four-dimensional scoring labels efficiently. This avoids the cost of long generative reasoning trajectories during online RL while retaining explicit, decomposed judgment. Reward model quality and cost are key bottlenecks for RLHF in image editing.

entry.title: SpaRV: Sparse Radiance Voxels for Scalable Geometrically Consistent LiDAR-Visual Mapping and Rendering

author.name: Jianheng Liu, Yunfei Wan, Fangming Cheng, Xiangyu Hong, Zuhao Zou, Haotian Li, Longji Yin, Chunran Zheng, Jiarong Lin, Fu Zhang
