author.name: Harikrishna Kuttivelil, Katia Obraczka

entry.summary: This paper introduces SPADE-KD, a peer-to-peer distributed deep learning method that removes the need for a central aggregator while supporting clients with heterogeneous model architectures via knowledge distillation rather than parameter averaging. It also targets personalized solutions when client data distributions differ, avoiding the one-size-fits-all global model assumption.

entry.title: PAC Learning with Query Feedback

author.name: Chase Hutton, Adam Melrod, Han Shao

entry.summary: The paper studies multiclass PAC learning where each example provides a binary response indicating whether its label lies in a chosen subset from a query family, introducing the query dimension as a combinatorial parameter capturing hypothesis-class structure and query discriminating power. It recovers the bandit DS dimension for singleton queries and proves sample-complexity lower bounds of Omega(D/eps) and upper bounds of O-tilde(D^2/eps), with tighter results for stronger query families.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Regret for Semi-Bandit Learning of Monotone Stochastic Problems

author.name: Zhengjia Zhuo, Viswanath Nagarajan

entry.summary: The paper studies learning approximately optimal policies for stochastic optimization problems with semi-bandit feedback, where only samples of chosen random variables are observed. The proposed algorithm achieves near-optimal regret for a broad class of monotone problems including prophet inequality, Pandora's box, stochastic knapsack, and stochastic matching. Bounds are O(sqrt(nkT)) for weakly monotone and O(sqrt(nT)) for strongly monotone settings.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations

author.name: Weibo Huang, Qing Feng, Ruihao Zhu, Cheng Hua

entry.summary: AI-GPB is a variance-reduction method for Bayesian optimization that combines an offline estimate of an auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations, exploiting correlation between paired observation errors. It provides finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. This matters for expensive black-box optimization where low-cost auxiliary data exist beforehand.

entry.title: A Symmetry-Matching Approach to Blind-Spot Reduction in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Csaba Balogh

entry.summary: The paper studies SAE blind spots — where language models treat semantically distinct inputs as representationally interchangeable — as a feature-basis orientation problem, adding a differentiable Gini-based regularizer to SAE training that penalizes uneven perturbation response. Evaluated frozen across GPT-2, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5, the regularization reduces blind spots relevant to safety-critical extraction tasks. This is interpretability research with a safety motivation.

entry.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimator for High-Dimensional Quantities of Interest

author.name: Zhibo Dai, Hamdi A. Tchelepi, Daniel M. Tartakovsky

entry.summary: This work extends multifidelity Monte Carlo estimation to vector-valued quantities of interest by replacing scalar control-variate coefficients with matrices, minimizing a weighted mean-squared error. Closed-form optimal full-matrix coefficients are derived, with an effective correlation replacing the Pearson correlation in the design rule, and block-diagonal, diagonal, and scalar restrictions form a nested estimator hierarchy. Applications target expensive high-fidelity simulations in areas like reservoir modeling.

entry.title: Predicted Class Correction: Conformal Thresholds for Classes with No Calibration Data

author.name: One Octadion, Novanto Yudistira, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: This paper tackles class-conditional conformal prediction in long-tailed settings where rare classes have few or no labelled calibration examples. Predicted Class Correction (PCC) regresses the offset between per-class and marginal conformal quantiles from label-free geometric descriptors of the classifier head, with a shrinkage scalar tuned on labelled classes. This extends rigorous prediction sets to classes that previously had undefined or degraded coverage.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning on the EPRI AI-ccelerating Unit Commitment benchmark: diagnosing over-commitment and guiding MILP with learned policies

author.name: Maharani Devira Pramita, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: This is the first study applying reinforcement learning to the 51-generator, 72-hour EPRI AI-ccelerating Unit Commitment benchmark, tracing why standalone RL agents underperform MILP: PPO and action-branching DQN commit roughly twice the units at 39-64% higher cost due to exploration-driven over-commitment. The authors close most of this gap and show the learned policy can accelerate an exact MILP solver. The work connects RL speed with exact optimization reliability for grid operations.

entry.title: FinHopper: A Progressive Multi-Hop Benchmark for Complex Financial Agents with Step-wise Evaluation

author.name: Yuxuan Wu, Miaopei Lin, Qiufang Ying, Lin Dan, Hao Zhao, Qirui Liu, Yuteng Shen, Shaohui Wu, Weihong Luo, Xiku Du, Xing Tang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: FinHopper is a benchmark for financial agents performing multi-hop open-search QA, with controlled reasoning depth from 1 to 6 hops and gold intermediate answers enabling process-level evaluation. A state-transition synthesis framework generates data at scale across stocks, funds, and macroeconomic facts, capturing how exact typed constraints chain queries in finance.

entry.title: A Simple and Unified Method for Gradient-Variation Regret

author.name: Hang Yu, Peng Zhao

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified method for gradient-variation online learning, based on surrogate losses with quadratic penalties on decision movement, that yields gradient-variation regret bounds in both non-stationary and universal online learning settings. It also induces an optimistic-to-gradient-variation reduction enabling many existing algorithms to obtain improved bounds.

entry.title: Cross-Fitting for Neural Posterior Estimation

author.name: Jeffrey Regier

entry.summary: This paper identifies extreme overconfidence in neural posterior estimation caused by the log-likelihood objective and flexible density estimators, showing early stopping selects along an unfavorable trajectory where posterior means are underfit. It proposes cross-fitting for NPE to ameliorate this degeneracy in simulation-based inference.

entry.title: Rethinking weakly supervised localization on chest radiographs: position nulls, protocol dependence, and PACE

author.name: Shixin Qiu

entry.summary: This critical evaluation shows that weakly supervised localization results on chest radiographs are heavily protocol-dependent and often fail against position-null controls that keep a readout's box but move only its position. CAM-based methods beat the null on only a minority of findings, while radiologists clear it broadly, and three rarely stated protocol choices each move results more than most reported method effects. It proposes PACE and calls for better evaluation standards in medical weak supervision.

entry.title: Location, Location, Generation: Where You Ask Matters for Generative Engine Optimization

author.name: Mahe Chen, Nick Koudas

entry.summary: A controlled audit of 31,200 answers showing that user location substantially changes which sources generative engines like ChatGPT and Gemini cite, with ChatGPT following declared application-level location down to the city and localizing its search backend. The findings complicate generative engine optimization practices that monitor citations from a single location.

entry.title: Training with Ciphers to Enhance In-Context Terminology Learning For Translation from Rare Languages

author.name: Deevyanshu Malu, Deeptanshu Malu, Sunita Sarawagi

entry.summary: The authors formalize in-context term learning (ICTL), showing that standard in-context training fine-tuning only weakly teaches LLMs to translate rare terms from examples. Their RareCipherFT method replaces rare terms with character-shuffled ciphers in paired in-context examples, forcing the model to recover terms by copying from context, with the ciphered fraction annealed during training. This improves translation of rare languages without lexical resources.

entry.title: Measuring Data Diversity with Embeddings: A Taxonomy and Benchmark for Diversity Measures

author.name: Cantao Su, Anna Wegmann, Esther Ploeger, Dong Nguyen

entry.summary: The authors provide a taxonomy of 21 embedding-based text diversity measures organized into four computational families, plus EmbDivBench, a benchmark evaluating the measures along three conceptually distinct components. This addresses a real fragmentation problem, as existing measures yield substantially different scores on identical data. The work supports better data curation, test-set design, and generalization analysis.

entry.title: Breaking the 1/3 Barrier for Approximate Nash Equilibria in Symmetric Bimatrix Games

author.name: Ashkan Soleymani, Patrick Jaillet, Gabriele Farina

entry.summary: The authors give the first unconditional family of polynomial-time algorithms computing symmetric approximate Nash equilibria in symmetric bimatrix games with approximation factor better than 1/3, achieving roughly 1 - 1/sqrt(2) + delta for any fixed delta. This improves the previous best guarantee from 2011 after more than a decade of no progress.

entry.title: Knowledge Manifold Optimization for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Shigeru Obayashi, Yoshiaki Kawagoe, Kazuhiko Komatsu, Tomonaga Okabe

entry.summary: The paper introduces Knowledge Manifold Optimization, a framework that treats scientific discovery as multiobjective search over a continuous literature-derived knowledge space. Candidate hypotheses are scored on boundary strength, white-space novelty, semantic-gradient magnitude, and evidential support, with Pareto-optimal Supported Knowledge Gaps identified rather than collapsing criteria into one score. This targets the problem of locating where new supportable knowledge may emerge in rapidly growing literature.

entry.title: Beyond Clean Accuracy: The Practical Challenges and Benefits of Pixel-Based Language Models

author.name: Haowen Tang, Wei Xia, Raoyuan Zhao, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Yihong Liu

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates pixel-based language models that process rendered text without a fixed vocabulary, examining fine-tuning behavior, robustness to typographical noise, and zero-shot crosslingual transfer. It finds these models need more training data and time than text-based counterparts, with delayed learning and learning-rate-dependent failures, though they retain promise for noisy and multilingual inputs.

entry.title: MisleadQA: Diagnosing LLM Failures under Misleading Context

author.name: Hui Wang, Bohao Chu, Qianli Wang, Shuning Zhang, Norbert Fuhr

entry.summary: Introduces MisleadQA, a diagnostic multiple-choice dataset with abstention options that contrasts factually true but out-of-scope context with false but in-scope context to test which misleads LLMs more, and whether adding gold context prevents being misled. The study isolates a failure mode prior work on false or irrelevant context had overlooked.

entry.title: A Measurement Perspective on Benchmarking LLM-Generated Text Detectors using Item Response Theory

author.name: Yanbin Zhao, Zhipeng Chen, Guangsheng Bao, Guandong Zhang, Yan Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a measurement-based benchmarking framework for LLM-generated text detectors using multidimensional item response theory, treating benchmark texts as measurement items and detectors as respondents. It estimates text-level discrimination and difficulty parameters, offering richer insight than aggregate metrics like accuracy, F1, or AUC.

entry.title: DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia

author.name: Jiuzhou Han, Abhishek Bijay Mishra, Trevor Cohn, Shubham Mittal

entry.summary: Introduces DeepSEA, a benchmark professionally translated into 12 Southeast Asian languages spanning high-resource (Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese) and low-resource (Burmese, Khmer, Lao) tiers across five tasks including mathematical and scientific reasoning. It addresses the acute underrepresentation of the region's 700 million people and linguistic diversity in existing evaluations.

entry.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting

author.name: Sanghyun Lee, Wonjin Nam, Seungho Jang, Jaeho Lee, Jiho Park, Jaewoon Lee, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Proposes ReAnchor, a training-free method for speculative decoding with block diffusion drafters that reuses verifier hidden states computed beyond the first rejection point as anchors for new parallel draft blocks. This extends draft coverage and improves predictions, with the largest gains at temperature zero.

entry.title: Dual Task Vector Merging: Leveraging Emotion and ASR Knowledge for Low-Resource Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Yuan-Chao Li, Yin-Long Liu, Liu He, Sizhe Liu, Ji-Xuan Deng, Yin Zhang, Zhen-Hua Ling, Jiahong Yuan

entry.summary: The authors propose a parameter-efficient method that adapts a frozen wav2vec 2.0 backbone for Alzheimer's detection from speech by injecting task vectors derived from emotion- and ASR-fine-tuned models, training only merging coefficients and a classification head. This avoids overfitting on limited AD data while transferring relevant paralinguistic and linguistic knowledge.

entry.title: Grounding Confusable Movie Moments

author.name: Dong-Hee Kim, Seonwoo Choi, Changbeen Kim, Juyeon Ko, Youngju Choi, Il Hyeon Mun, Hyunwoo J. Kim, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: CoM2-Bench is a temporal movie grounding benchmark built from confusable query pairs that share most attributes but differ in a single distinguishing detail across a full-length movie. The paper also analyzes where retrieve-then-localize pipelines break down on these fine-grained cases, exposing weaknesses of existing temporal grounding approaches.

entry.title: Trimodal Context-Aware Micro-Expression Recognition in Real-World Conversations: A Dataset and a Hierarchical Fusion Network

author.name: Junbo Wang, Yan Zhao, Shigang Wang, Jian Wei, Qiming Zhang, Yu Wu

entry.summary: This work introduces a dataset and hierarchical fusion network for recognizing micro-expressions in real conversations, incorporating visual, semantic, and acoustic context that prior de-contextualized clip-based methods ignore. Grounded in psychological findings about how social context shapes both interpretation and intensity of facial expressions, the work moves micro-expression recognition toward realistic conversational settings.

entry.title: BiNar: Bitstream Native Restorer for Bitstream-corrupted Image Restoration

author.name: Fangcheng Li, Zhen Yu, Kejun Wu, Tianyi Liu

entry.summary: BiNar tackles bitstream-corrupted image restoration, where corruption in compressed bitstreams causes unpredictable pixel-domain error propagation and can render images undecodable by standard decoders. The framework uses bitstream semantic modeling to extract robust semantics directly from corrupted bitstreams, guiding a generative restoration process that operates in the bitstream domain rather than the pixel domain.

entry.title: BodyBridge: Grounded Body Layers for Sim-to-Real Translation of Vulnerable Road Users

author.name: Mark Azer, Fabian B. Flohr

entry.summary: BodyBridge introduces Grounded Body Layers, a simulator-derived, pixel-aligned representation combining scene geometry, canonical per-pixel body correspondence, and exact VRU masks to give video diffusion models explicit articulation control over pedestrians and cyclists. This enables safer sim-to-real generation of driving scenarios involving vulnerable road users, with per-joint evaluation support.

entry.title: Design Anything, Design at Scale

author.name: Xuchao Ren, Siyuan Feng, Jing Huang, Yanhua Yao, Jing Wang, Lingyu Alina Wang, Anan Chen, Hangjie Yuan, Tao Feng, Qiong Wu, Sai Ma

entry.summary: Introduces a graph-based harness that preserves design intent outside the model for agentic AI design workflows, binding deliverables to workflow steps through an intent-execution graph and task contracts that retain constraints and decisions. The goal is to keep agentic AI aligned with design briefs over long-horizon, multi-artifact projects across domains.

entry.title: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control

author.name: Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Zhen Xing, Bojia Zi, Xiaoling Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Map2Vid, a new task that frames embodied navigation video generation as bird's-eye-view (BEV) map-to-video synthesis, addressing the spatial ambiguity of text prompts and the unintuitiveness of camera-trajectory controls. The authors also contribute a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation.

entry.title: Preserving the Manifold: Frozen Expert Alignment for Label-Efficient SAR Scene Understanding

author.name: Eli A. Underwood, I. Taylor McKechnie, Leslie M. Collins

entry.summary: This paper addresses cross-modal alignment of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery with natural language, identifying two failure modes: modality mismatch from optical-pretrained text encoders and physical forgetting when SAR encoders are fine-tuned on small caption datasets. It proposes a frozen expert alignment approach that preserves the learned semantic manifold and radar physics without requiring large caption corpora.

entry.title: After the Federation: Benchmarking Knowledge Portability to Heterogeneous Newcomers

author.name: Xinyuan Zhao

entry.summary: FEDNBO is a seven-dataset benchmark studying how much federated learning knowledge remains usable by new clients with different architectures after original clients leave, separating knowledge supply, policy identification, and private-model compilation. Controlled studies reveal inflated oracle gains, architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and strong performance from plain public-response distillation.

entry.title: GeoNaviDiff: Transferring Disentangled Semantic Controls to Diffusion Features via Local Riemannian Navigation

author.name: Tao Sun, Huanting Guo, Baao Xie, Zhou Fang, Qiuyu Chen, Hao Zheng, Wenjun Zeng

entry.summary: GeoNaviDiff transfers interpretable StyleSpace semantic edits into diffusion models by constructing local Riemannian trajectories in the diffusion h-space, using tangent maps from StyleGAN reconstruction-edit pairs parallel-transported to real-image diffusion states. This enables unsupervised disentangled real-image manipulation combining GAN interpretability with diffusion fidelity.

entry.title: 3D Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging

author.name: Frank-Peter Schilling, Daniel Barco, Philipp Denzel, Marc Stadelmann

entry.summary: This paper surveys and develops 3D diffusion models for medical imaging tasks across CT, MRI, and PET, covering use cases such as data augmentation, domain transfer, reconstruction, inpainting, and artifact correction. It situates diffusion models against VAEs and GANs for 3D medical image synthesis. The work matters because volumetric generative modeling underpins synthetic data and reconstruction in clinical imaging.

entry.title: Dual-Scale Condition-Shift Editing for Robust Real-World Image Demoir\'eing

author.name: Shiyang Zhou, Haijin Zeng, Congpei Qiu, Zhengcen Li, Ping Chen, Xiangming Wang, Zheng Li, Yongyong Chen, Jingyong Su

entry.summary: This paper introduces DemoiréEdit, a framework that repurposes a pretrained flow-matching image editor for removing moiré patterns from screen-captured photos, addressing the diversity of moiré artifacts across different display-camera pairs. The method combines an endpoint-supervised training objective (pixel, perceptual, and frequency-domain losses alongside velocity matching) with a dual-scale condition-shift strategy that corrects low-frequency color banding globally at low resolution and refines high-frequency stripes at higher resolution. It matters because it shows how generative editing priors can be adapted for content-preserving restoration tasks where traditional restoration networks trained on limited paired data struggle to generalize.

entry.title: Open-Form Geometric Style Transfer

author.name: Adar Elad, Gal Metzer, Omer Dahari, Min Lu, Daniel Cohen-Or

entry.summary: This paper introduces Open-Form Geometric Style Transfer, which learns a geometric design language from a stylized shape family (e.g., a Latin alphabet) and applies it to entirely different forms such as Greek glyphs or human poses. The key technical challenge is disentangling style from the source shape family, using structural sketches as representations of target forms. This opens style transfer beyond same-family shapes, with implications for generative design and graphics.

entry.title: ProtoGTX: Prototype-Aligned Graph Transformer for Explainable Whole-Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Iori Azuma, Hiroyuki Kusuhara, Tadahaya Mizuno

entry.summary: ProtoGTX is a graph-based framework for explainable whole-slide image analysis that combines spatial contextualization with a flexible morphological prototype vocabulary, separating reference prototypes (from unsupervised clustering or external sources) from the predictive model. This lets explanations identify morphological patterns, not just important regions, bridging patch-level evidence and slide-level pathological interpretation. Interpretability with clinically meaningful concepts is the core contribution.

entry.title: When to Make a Decision: Task-Sufficient Active Perception for Mobile Manipulator Robots

author.name: Mariana da Silva Barros, Matthias Kerzel, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid neuro-symbolic framework for task-sufficient active perception, in which a robot generates an initial plan and iteratively reevaluates whether it has enough information, choosing to gather viewpoints, inspect or manipulate objects, ask the user, or act. Neural perception updates an object-centric belief state while a symbolic layer decides sufficiency. It addresses the often-overlooked question of when to stop perceiving and commit.

entry.title: Multimodal Interaction Estimation for Contact-Aware Adaptive Impedance Control

author.name: Mateusz Jaszczuk, Paris Perdikaris, Nadia Figueroa

entry.summary: The paper proposes a task-agnostic framework that fuses force history and 3D point clouds via a transformer-based classifier to distinguish payloads from human interaction, enabling adaptive impedance control in human-centric environments. Training uses modality dropout for occlusion resilience, addressing weaknesses of single-modality sensing.

entry.title: Learning When to Adapt: Reactivity-Conditioned Residual Adaptation under Human-Robot Distribution Shift

author.name: Immanuel R. Santjoko, Benedictus C. G. Cinun, Jing Chen, Bin Hu

entry.summary: RCRA is an online adaptation framework for social robot navigation that modulates a learned residual around a frozen conservative policy based on estimated pedestrian reactivity. A Transformer-based estimator infers latent reactivity from motion histories and robot context, improving scenario-averaged simulation accuracy by 12.62 percentage points over a Bayesian baseline with known reactivity. This addresses distribution shift when pedestrians vary in whether they respond to the robot.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry

author.name: Yuheng Qiu, Yutian Chen, Carlton Cort, Weison Huang, Shibo Zhao, Pieter Abbeel, Rocky Duan, Koushil Sreenath, C. Karen Liu, Carmelo Sferrazza, Junyi Geng, Sebastian Scherer, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: This work trains an inertial odometry model from scratch without ground-truth trajectories, using integration self-supervision where a myopic teacher integrates the IMU over short windows. Surprisingly, the student learns to predict velocity more accurately than its teacher, and pose graph distillation further refines sequence-consistent targets, enabling platform adaptation with only IMU calibration.

entry.title: ReInsVLN: Revisiting Historical Evidence for Training-Free Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Siwei Cheng, Hao Wu, Zitong Qi, Xinming Zhang, Haoyu Xi, Peiran Yin, Haozhe Hu, Xudong Wang, Xiaoyu Shen, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces ReInsBench, a diagnostic benchmark showing that vision-and-language navigation agents often underuse their observation histories, and demonstrates that simply reinstructing the agent to review history can recover navigation failures. Building on this finding, ReInsVLN is a training-free framework that compresses visual history via coverage-aware and instruction-guided token selection while working with frozen navigator models.

entry.title: Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL

author.name: Youbing Yin, Xujun Peng, Muhammad S. Uddin, Erin Babinsky, Daben Liu, Anoop Kumar

entry.summary: AIR is a training-free multi-agent framework for text-to-SQL that resolves ambiguous natural-language queries by constructing competing interpretations, verifying via SQL execution that they yield different results, and generating grounded clarification questions. It shows strong performance and cross-benchmark robustness on ambiguity-focused text-to-SQL benchmarks.

entry.title: Cortex: A Fixed-Point Theory of Governed Coding Agents - Technical Report

author.name: Marius-Constantin Dinu, Florian Zeba

entry.summary: This technical report formalizes supervisory governance for LLM-based coding agents via a layer called Cortex that handles pre-execution governance, requirement tracking, and iterative validation and repair. The authors prove that with a fixed requirement set and a sound, monotone validation rule with persistent evidence, exhaustive or fairly-scheduled iteration converges to the least fixed point of requirement closure on a finite lattice, with bounded iteration counts.

entry.title: Learning to Compose: Recursive Self-Improvement of Shared Executable Stacks for Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yangzhi Chen, Feiran Liu, Zishuo Wang, Zijian Jin, Xin Zhu, Lecheng Ruan, Wenjuan Han

entry.summary: Recursia is a recursive self-improvement framework for robot manipulation that treats the shared executable stack—tools, skills with execution contracts, handoffs, and verifiers—as the unit of improvement rather than individual task programs. Source-side execution traces guide failure attribution and generation of missing tools, with generality checks and regression gates controlling which changes persist. It targets zero-shot long-horizon manipulation where composed skills fail.

entry.title: Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator with Multi-scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling

author.name: Yiqiang Ye, Yichi Wang, Haodi Zhang, Jiawei Wen, Jiahui Jiang, Zhaoyu Zhong, Jiangjian Yu, Chunxia Xiao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a spherical physics-informed neural operator for meteorological downscaling that uses Spherical Laplacian Decomposition to partition atmospheric fields into hierarchical frequency components, plus a localized spherical integral operator for evaluation at arbitrary locations. It addresses geometric distortion, multi-scale coupling, and missing atmospheric physics constraints in existing neural operators.

entry.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework

author.name: Savan Doshi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a risk-sensitive evaluation framework for patient-facing medical LLMs that scores responses on six categories of risk-bearing language (e.g., treatment directives, dosage expressions, overconfident assertions) using a three-judge LLM ensemble anchored on clinical harm taxonomies. Applied to medical fine-tuning, it finds fine-tuning reshapes rather than reduces risk profiles.

entry.title: HyperTaxa: Multiscale Genome Representations for Generalized Microbial Taxonomic Inference

author.name: Akash Rao, Sushim Gupta, Vishalini Ramnath, Akhilesh Ramachandran, Sathyanarayanan Aakur

entry.summary: HyperTaxa is a taxonomy-aligned representation learning framework for open-set microbial taxonomic inference, encoding whole genomes as multiscale hyperspectral k-mer transition fields and aligning them to a taxonomy-derived semantic space via a Node2Vec-to-MDS procedure. It targets inference over species absent from genome-level training, addressing the limits of alignment- and database-driven tools as sequencing outpaces reference coverage. The learned space supports generalized taxonomic prediction.

entry.title: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants: Enhancing LLM Agents for Automated Fact-Checking with Human Expert Skills

author.name: Xinwen Chen, Haorui He, Yupeng Li

entry.summary: SkillCheck distills publicly available AFP Fact Check guidelines into a modular Professional Fact-Checking Skill and gives LLM agents dynamic inference-time access to it for evidence retrieval and claim verification. This transfers professional expertise without costly post-training or human-in-the-loop feedback.

entry.title: EvoSkill v2: Fully Agentic Skill Evolution from Benchmark Adaptation to a Stateful Evolver

author.name: Dastin Huang, Baran Nama, Salaheddin Alzubi

entry.summary: EvoSkill v2 is a three-agent system that improves an agent's instructions (skills) without touching the model or harness, using a single stateful coding agent as the evolver across a whole run rather than per-round fresh agents or one-shot model calls. It also analyzes rollout variability in solver attempts.

entry.title: BOSS: Token-Budgeted Online Sampling and Selection for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yupeng Chang, Yahan Li, Chenlu Guo, Diana Inkpen, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: BOSS is a training-free policy for test-time compute allocation that makes a three-way online decision under a hard shared token budget: stop generating, sample another candidate, or spend residual tokens adjudicating existing candidates, with worst-case budget checks before every generation and judge call. Across two Llama-3.1 models and four reasoning benchmarks, it achieves the highest accuracy in 22 of 24 model-task-budget cells.

entry.title: SOMA: Continuous Monitoring and Intervention for System Two Reasoning with System One Models

author.name: Ruizhi Qian, Lei Shi, Tianyu Hu, Bo Yan, Song Wang, Yu Tian

entry.summary: SOMA uses a fast System One decision model (returning calibrated probabilities from natural-language questions) to continuously monitor a System Two reasoning model during execution and intervene when problems appear, mirroring human metacognition. This extends S1 models beyond their typical role as pre-reasoning gates.

entry.title: EgoVine: Post-Training with Branching Experience Compiled from Real-World Videos

author.name: Qinchuan Cheng, Bowen Lyu, Zhantao Gong, Angela Yao, Cheston Tan, Shijie Li

entry.summary: EgoVine converts fixed egocentric video demonstrations into interactive branching experience in executable symbolic environments, letting agents explore alternative actions and recover from their own mistakes under partial observation and delayed consequences. It jointly trains action generation and consequence prediction in one model for long-horizon manipulation planning.

entry.title: SituHOI: Scalable Capture of Scene-Situated Full-Body Human-Object Interaction

author.name: Qifan Wang, Qihang Fang, Boao Shi, Yushi Du, Pei Zhou, Siyan Dong, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: SituHOI is a large-scale RGB-D dataset of scene-situated human-object interaction with 18,429 annotated clips across 16 indoor rooms and roughly 86 hours of activity, pairing moving-camera recordings with static scene scans, object geometry, language descriptions, and estimated trajectories. A pipeline combining camera localization, depth alignment, mesh recovery, and tracking yields structured supervision.

entry.title: Bootstrap Stochastic Interpolant Tree for Inference-time Search Under Sparse Reward

author.name: Binglin Ji, Anindya Sarkar, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: The paper identifies that tree-based inference-time samplers using learned DDPM-like transitions couple neighboring states, restricting exploration under sparse rewards. It proposes a Bootstrap Stochastic Interpolant Tree that breaks this coupling to broaden coverage of the target distribution while avoiding per-step reward and gradient dependencies of SMC-style methods. This is relevant to improving compute-efficient test-time search for generative and policy models.

entry.title: VERAS: Verification-Guided Adaptive Search for Reliable Operations Research

author.name: Minbo Ma, Honglin Zhang, Bangtao Zhou, Chunguang Yu, Dasheng Ju, Yichen Shen, Fengli Xu, Yong Li

entry.summary: VERAS is a verification-guided adaptive search harness for LLM agents solving operations research problems, addressing the gap that passing self-authored verification does not guarantee task constraints are met due to correlated specification errors between programs and their checks. It uses verification evidence to prioritize feasibility repair, constraint-coverage review, and solution-quality improvement. The correlated-error observation is a sharp diagnosis of a widespread failure mode in agent self-verification.

entry.title: SENTRY: A Streaming Edge Network Trust Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Chirantan Banerjee, Soumita Chatterjee, Bhargab B. Bhattacharya, Hafizur Rahaman

entry.summary: Presents SENTRY, a hardware-oriented streaming engine for inline audio deepfake detection at the network edge, using an integer lifting-wavelet front end and multiplier-free transforms so analysis requires only add, shift, compare, and bitwise operations. It targets real-time voice-cloning attacks like vishing that defeat buffered, GPU-based NDR post-processing.

entry.title: First-Order LoRA Training with Phone NPUs

author.name: Xu Zheng, Wei Cheng, Zhuomin Chen, Dongkuan Xu, Mo Sha, Jingchao Ni, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: The paper presents a system for on-device LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs using phone NPUs, which normally only support inference and lack input-gradient computation. It runs all frozen-weight products on the NPU while keeping the training graph, adapters, and optimizer on the CPU, reusing resident weight tiles for input-gradient kernels, enabling privacy-preserving learning from user data.

entry.title: BatchParScale: Sparse Batch-Mixing for Sequence Models

author.name: Hans Peter Lyngs{\o}e Raaschou-jensen (University of Copenhagen), M. Onurcan Kaya (Technical University of Denmark), Desmond Elliott (University of Copenhagen)

entry.summary: BatchParScale extends parallel test-time scaling by introducing sparse mixing between parallel reasoning streams during inference, addressing the limitation of ParScale where streams do not exchange information mid-sequence. This allows discoveries made in one rollout to influence others, going beyond independent streams aggregated post hoc by voting or verification.

entry.title: Multimodal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Models for Spatiotemporal Brain MRI Forecasting

author.name: Antonio Scardace, Silvia Ingala, Sebastiano Battiato, Daniele Rav\`i

entry.summary: MC-LDM is a latent diffusion model for forecasting patient-specific 3D brain MRI changes in Alzheimer's disease, conditioned during training on MRI, tau-PET, CDR, and APOE4 but requiring only baseline MRI, APOE4, and metadata at inference to match realistic clinical availability. The framework uses LoRA fine-tuning of the diffusion backbone and multimodal biomarker conditioning.

entry.title: Auditor-Assisted Summary-Channel Verification for Hosted LLM Identity Substitution

author.name: Ziyi Zhang, Ziyao Wang, Guoheng Sun, Ang Li, Jian Li

entry.summary: SUMMARK is a watermarking framework that lets a trusted auditor verify which model configuration served a request through user-visible reasoning summaries, without runtime access to model internals, logs, or provider metadata. It targets the problem of model identity substitution by hosted LLM providers. This addresses an emerging transparency and accountability issue in commercial LLM serving.

entry.title: PhyPro-FM: A Physics and Prompt-Guided Graph Foundation Model for Contingency Analysis

author.name: Xu Yang, Zhanyuan Sheng, Chenhui Lin, Haotian Liu, Qi Wang, Yue Yang, Wenchuan Wu

entry.summary: PhyPro-FM is a physics and prompt-guided graph foundation model for power-grid contingency analysis, designed to remain generalizable and engineering-viable under high renewable penetration and dynamic topology changes. It integrates physical grid constraints and prompting beyond pure regression formulations of N-1/N-2 contingency screening. The goal is faster, more scalable and interpretable grid reliability analysis.

entry.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding

author.name: Junchao Yang

entry.summary: Presents a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels enabling CUDA Graph replay under adaptive speculative decoding, where batch size and draft length change per step. By capturing one maximum-grid graph and writing the active shape to GPU memory (only 28 bytes per update), it avoids shape pre-capture, on-the-fly capture, or padding. Demonstrated on an H800 with trace-driven prototype.

entry.title: Hidden Trajectories Don't Lie: Correcting Corruption Drift for Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Amirhossein Sabour, Amir Khasahmadi, Mengliu Zhao

entry.summary: Drift-TTA improves test-time adaptation by exploiting hidden trajectories — ordered sequences of intermediate representations across a network — which separate cleanly from corrupted trajectories as corruption severity increases. The method trains zero-initialized low-rank adapters on a frozen backbone to align corrupted trajectories with cleaner ones, in source-dependent and source-free variants.

entry.title: What "Form'' of Uncertainty Does Conformal Prediction Quantify?

author.name: Soroush H. Zargarbashi, Mohammad Sadegh Akhondzadeh, Rebekka Burkholz, Aleksandar Bojchevski

entry.summary: This paper shows that the set-size difference between full and split conformal prediction connects directly to Bayesian posterior variance, i.e., the model's epistemic uncertainty. The difference aggregates two opposing effects: accuracy gains from extra calibration points and a formability effect toward every possible label that vanishes with stronger models or more data. This clarifies the epistemic interpretation of conformal prediction set sizes.

entry.title: DeliMF: Gated Cross-Attention Fusion of Structured Time Series and Clinical Text for Early Intensive Care Delirium Prediction

author.name: Yibo Yang, Zerui Huang, Haomiao Yang, Zixia Wang

entry.summary: DeliMF is a multimodal framework for early ICU delirium prediction that fuses structured EHR time series (encoded by a temporal Transformer) with free-text clinical notes using gated cross-attention. Delirium affects many ICU patients and predicts worse outcomes, so first-day prediction gives clinicians an intervention window. The work matters because prior state-of-the-art predictors ignored clinical text that carries information vital signs and labs cannot encode.

entry.title: Emergent Sparsity: How Many Effective Variables Survive Coarse-Graining in AlphaEarth Embeddings?

author.name: Johannes Hirn

entry.summary: The paper asks how many effective variables of AlphaEarth's 64-component per-pixel land embeddings suffice at a given reconstruction tolerance, and whether that count decreases with spatial scale. It frames effective dimension as a surface over tolerance and spatial scale, using beta-VAE scans with common architecture to produce rank-distortion envelopes at each scale. This connects representation learning with coarse-graining ideas from physics.

entry.title: Divergence based Ranked Preference Alignment for LLMs

author.name: Rajdeep Haldar, Yue Xing, Qifan Song

entry.summary: f-RPO unifies two perspectives on LLM alignment: using ranked (listwise) preference feedback rather than pairwise comparisons, and interpreting alignment objectives as f-divergence estimators between preferred and less-preferred response distributions. The framework provides interpretable theoretical grounding for ranked-preference alignment with a family of divergence-based objectives. This extends the alignment toolbox beyond pairwise RLHF-style methods.

entry.title: Detection Augmented Learning In Non-Stationary Bandit Environments

author.name: Argyrios Gerogiannis, Yu-Han Huang, Subhonmesh Bose, Venugopal V. Veeravalli

entry.summary: DAL is a modular black-box paradigm for non-stationary bandits combining a bandit algorithm, change detector, and forced exploration schedule. A single regret bound shows it transfers the regret of the stationary input algorithm to piecewise-stationary settings, attaining or improving best known bounds across classical and structured bandit problems.

entry.title: Graph-to-Table Interfaces Control Relational Generalisation

author.name: Alessandro Cagiano, Lorenzo Molfetta, Gianluca Moro, Matteo Zignani, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: The authors decompose graph-to-table systems (encoder, context constructor, tabular decoder) and evaluate components independently via matched comparisons across CLUTRR, GraphLog worlds, and knowledge graphs. They find conclusions about one component can flip depending on the others, e.g., absolute positional encodings fit short paths well but generalize worse than relational alternatives.

entry.title: TaQFormer: A Treatment-as-Query Transformer with Data-Fusion for Multidimensional Treatment Modeling in Coupon Allocation

author.name: Jiahong Li, Zeqin Yang, Yu Xiang, Zhifan Jiang, Jingqi Ma, Enzheng Hua, Jixing Xu, Jun Wu, Fei Wang, Enyun Yu, Jiecheng Guo

entry.summary: TaQFormer is a Transformer that represents each category-specific discount (treatment coordinate) as a query token, using cross-attention to estimate responses to full treatment vectors for coupon allocation across multiple marketplace categories. It fuses large policy-biased observational logs with small RCT data via observational pretraining followed by LoRA fine-tuning with request-specific fusion.

entry.title: PACT: Plan-Augmented Coordination via Trace-Graphs for Dynamic Multi-Agent Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Xiao Zhou, Alex Schutz, Victor-Alexandru Darvariu, Nick Hawes

entry.summary: PACT addresses multi-agent reinforcement learning for neural combinatorial optimization under dynamic settings where problem information is progressively revealed as agents act. It augments the environment graph with auxiliary nodes representing plans and trace information to coordinate exploration and exploitation of newly revealed constraints.

entry.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles

author.name: C\'elian Vasson, Daniil Ognev, Kentaro Inui, Benjamin Heinzerling

entry.summary: Uses Sajaniemi's taxonomy of eleven variable roles (accumulation, traversal, best-so-far, etc.) to probe whether large language models encode semantic code structure, introducing annotation rules and a 126,926-file corpus across five languages. Residual probes outperform individual sparse autoencoder features and lexical baselines, and combining SAE features closes much of the gap.

entry.title: Can Agents Keep Secrets They Were Never Told? Benchmarking Latent Privacy Risks Across Sessions with MemJoin

author.name: Qishun Yang, Shu Yang, Difei Xu, Di Wang, Meng Ding

entry.summary: Introduces MemJoin, a privacy benchmark of 288 synthetic cases where combining an agent's long-term memory across sessions reveals a sensitive relation that no individual session exposes, testing whether agents avoid leaking such latent relations during ordinary tasks. Evaluation of six memory systems against full-history and no-history controls quantifies this previously unmeasured cross-session privacy risk.

entry.title: From Seeing to Reporting: A Theory of Reliable Visual Set Generation in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junzhe Shi, Yuan Gan, Shida Jiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes From Seeing to Reporting (FSR), a theory modeling VLM visual reporting as a chain from responses to decoded records, constructed sets, and task answers, with inference-time procedures that improve reports of frozen models. Motivated by failures such as a model listing 173 shapes correctly while stating counts summing to 188, it treats reporting as part of the visual task rather than mere formatting, with applications to counting, grounding, and GUI tasks.

entry.title: RECAP: Reciprocal Sparse Attention and Hierarchical Caching for Efficient Video Diffusion

author.name: Tiange Xu, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: RECAP is a training-free method for video diffusion transformers that composes sparse attention with temporal caching, observing that errors from sparsified predictions propagate through cache reuse and that sparsification errors are directionally aligned across nearby steps. It exploits this to share correction information across steps, recovering fidelity without changing the reuse schedule.

entry.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings

author.name: Riccardo Molteni, Minjun Jeon, Paolo Braccia, Abhinav Deshpande, Vedran Dunjko, Liang Jiang, Su-un Lee, Swarnadeep Majumder, Javier Robledo Moreno, Parthasarathy Suryanarayanan, Kunal Sharma

entry.summary: The paper introduces quantum Hamiltonian embeddings, a supervised learning framework where training data is encoded into a single parameterized Hamiltonian whose approximate ground state defines the classifier. Once the ground state is approximated on quantum hardware, inference can proceed either classically or quantumly, and the authors provide guarantees on performance, trainability, and inference cost.

entry.title: Ask, Don't Guess: Targeted Clarification for Speech Recognition Errors

author.name: Sankalp Parashar, Preethi Jyothi, Sunita Sarawagi

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for online error localization in streaming ASR that identifies spans likely to benefit from asking the speaker to repeat under better acoustic conditions. Supervision derives from aligning noisy and clean decodes with a pair-HMM to train a counterfactual gain scorer using acoustic and language features.

entry.title: Design Considerations in Low-Resource Archival OCR: A Case Study in Lakota

author.name: T\'ea Wright, Laura X. Ma, Claudia Iron Hawk, Hannah J. Haynie, Alexis Palmer, Alane Suhr, Abteen Ebrahimi, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: This case study adapts small (at most 3B) vision-language models as OCR tools for Lakota, a North American Indigenous language, benchmarking modeling approaches alongside practical facets like constrained budgets, segmentation noise, scan degradation, and orthographic variance. It is grounded in community conversations and supports language reclamation from archival documents.

entry.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang, Kewei Fu, Yongqi Tong, Chenzhi Zheng, Wei Wu, Jiang-Ming Yang, Jianshe Li

entry.summary: Introduces Heartbeat Thinking for tool-using realtime voice agents: periodic Thinker invocations read the latest partial transcript and a shared record of completed reasoning and tool results, while allowing ongoing invocations and dispatched tools to finish rather than truncating them on input updates. This enables speculative reasoning and tool execution during speech, reducing post-speech latency.

entry.title: RESIN: Multi-Chain Reasoning with Entity-Structured Indexing

author.name: Xuanyu Meng, Jash Rajesh Parekh, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Introduces RESIN, which decomposes multi-chain reasoning questions into focused one-hop needs, retrieves source-grounded evidence per hop via entity-structured indexing, and maintains a compact reasoning buffer rather than relying on flat retrieval or premature single-path selection. This keeps reasoning grounded in original sources while locating dispersed evidence.

entry.title: ContraSafe-VL: A Contrastive Safety Preference Dataset for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Di Wu, Yanyan Zhao, Xin Lu, Hao Yang, Taotao Zhang, Yunzhen Zhao

entry.summary: ContraSafe-VL is a multimodal safety alignment dataset using a contrastive preference format that supervises how visual context should inform safety judgments, addressing the gap where response-preference datasets teach what to say but not how to weigh visual evidence. The dataset targets the tension between unsafe responses and over-refusal in VLMs.

entry.title: Learning When to Trust and Reobserve Sparse-Frame VideoQA from Temporal Sampling Perturbations

author.name: Shujia Liu

entry.summary: The paper shows that sparse-frame video-language models can flip answers when only sampling timestamps shift, and proposes PhaseGuard+, which probes a frozen VLM at controlled temporal offsets to separately predict answer reliability and the expected correctness gain of a rescue action such as denser sampling or a stronger model. Lightweight predictors route only examples expected to benefit from additional observation.

entry.title: RiSE: Residual Subspace Expert for Generalizable Text-Centric Image Forgery Localization

author.name: Kahim Wong, Kemou Li, Yiming Chen, Haiwei Wu, Jiantao Zhou

entry.summary: RiSE targets text-centric image forgery localization for financial and legal documents, showing that full-parameter fine-tuning causes low-rank feature collapse and overfitting to training artifacts. It freezes principal SVD components of pre-trained features and adapts only residual subspaces with lightweight experts to preserve priors and improve generalization to unseen forgery types.

entry.title: From Views to Worlds: Active Exploration over 3D Worlds for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Qijian Tian, Jiayu Ying, Ke Fan, Lizhuang Ma, Xin Tan

entry.summary: V2W is an active exploration framework that lets vision-language models actively acquire spatial evidence in 3D worlds - camera poses and cross-view relationships - beyond passively given 2D views, lifting VLM 3D spatial reasoning. It addresses the limitation that existing methods either lack active exploration or only add views at inference without explicit spatial evidence acquisition.

entry.title: SL-Ground: Sentence-Level Grounding for Fine-Grained Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Yang-Syu Li, Cheng-Huan Yang, Chia-Yung Jui, Peggy Joy Lu

entry.summary: Observes that token-level scoring in grounding-based open-vocabulary detectors bottlenecks fine-grained detection where categories are defined by complete compositional descriptions. SL-Ground reformulates grounding at the sentence level, encoding each category description as a whole sentence rather than scoring against fragmented token evidence.

entry.title: MT Forcing: Towards Stable and Consistent Multi-Turn Image Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion

author.name: Houyuan Chen, Fanzhou Wang, Xiangyu Fan, Zesong Qiu, Yukun Wei, Songlin Yang, Zhitao Yang, Lvmin Zhang, Pei Yang, Hao Zhao, Lei Yang, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: Proposes MT Forcing, a training paradigm for multi-turn image editing in unified multimodal autoregressive diffusion models, using Single-Turn Distribution Matching Distillation to combat quality drift and unintended content changes across sequential editing instructions. Includes Lvmin Zhang among the authors.

entry.title: ViMoLa: Discrete Motion Tokens for Language-Guided Video Generation

author.name: Bishoy Galoaa, Sarah Ostadabbas

entry.summary: ViMoLa improves motion fidelity in language-guided video generation by predicting a discrete motion prior from text (64 tokens from a 512-entry codebook via a 28M-parameter transformer) and injecting it into a frozen Wan 2.2 DiT backbone through zero-gated cross-attention adapters. Trained on 462K videos, it raises directional motion accuracy from 0.287 to 0.442 while maintaining generative quality.

entry.title: Learning Goal-Conditioned Subgoals through Frozen Hierarchical World Models

author.name: Xiang Kaibo, Liu Qingfeng

entry.summary: This work replaces expensive search-based subgoal selection in hierarchical world models with a lightweight goal-conditioned network trained through the frozen high-level predictor using hindsight goals and state-prediction losses on offline trajectories. Inference avoids high-level candidate optimization entirely. This makes long-horizon planning with world models substantially cheaper.

entry.title: Foundation Model Driven Optical Flow

author.name: Praroop Chanda, Suryansh Kumar

entry.summary: Building on TTSFlow, this paper fuses frozen DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 features through a trainable DPT-based matching pipeline with coarse-to-fine refinement to estimate dense optical flow, achieving 2.37 EPE on Sintel Final and competitive RoboFlow/Spring 2026 challenge results. It demonstrates that frozen foundation representations support state-of-the-art flow with limited trainable machinery. The frozen-features recipe is efficient and broadly applicable.

entry.title: ChairNav: Cross-Embodiment Pre-training and Personalization for Long-Horizon Wheelchair Navigation

author.name: Junhua Huang, Zhizheng Liu, Honglin He, Xiang Zhang, Bolei Zhou

entry.summary: ChairNav adapts general visual navigation foundation models into personalized electric wheelchair navigation for long-horizon outdoor sidewalk navigation using a three-stage data pyramid: pre-training on large-scale navigation datasets, then in-domain adaptation, then personalization. It targets accessibility-critical mobility with lightweight hardware rather than expensive sensor stacks. This addresses an underserved, socially important application of embodied AI.

entry.title: Stress-Query and Temporal Reliability of Vision-Language Models as copilots in Autonomous UAV Navigation

author.name: Hiago Sodre, Sebastian Barcelona, Vincent Sandin, Pablo Moraes, Andre S. Kelbouscas, Ricardo B. Grando

entry.summary: Benchmarks vision-language models as copilots for autonomous UAV navigation, systematically stress-testing model scale and hardware constraints from workstations to constrained laptops. It isolates the kinetic impact of inference latency against reasoning accuracy and finds a dichotomy: lightweight models suffer structural hallucinations that break state machines, while heavyweight models cause trajectory overshoot from latency. A useful empirical guide for deploying VLMs in real-time control.

entry.title: MicroSplat: Towards Automating 3D Small-Scale Reconstruction

author.name: Roman Mineyev, Robert Azarcon, Suvrat Jain, Chuizheng Kong, Shreyas Kousik

entry.summary: Presents MicroSplat, a system producing 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions of sub-millimeter objects using a low-cost consumer microscope on a manipulator rig, handling the extreme field-of-view and depth-of-field constraints of macro optics that violate standard 3DGS assumptions. It automates capture and processing that previously required human-in-the-loop photogrammetry. Applications include circuit-board inspection and specimen digitization.

entry.title: Touch Where It Matters: Learning Local Tactile Policies for Fine-Grained Gripper Control

author.name: Mingyuan Ba, Yanan Zhou, James Zhao, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: ContactPolicy is a learned local controller that takes over gripper control during contact-rich task stages while a visual base policy continues to control the arm, combining tactile and force histories with robot state to predict gripper increments. An Intent policy manages the control handover between the visual policy and the tactile local controller.

entry.title: Intent-Informed Model Predictive Control for Shared Autonomy in Remote Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Lorena Maria Genua, Camilla Tabasso, Mya Schroder, Joshua Migdal, Tye Brady, Taskin Padir

entry.summary: The paper proposes a shared-autonomy arbitration strategy that dynamically adjusts autonomy level using the entropy of a belief distribution from multimodal intent inference. Human intent is modeled with a Dynamic Bayesian Network over goals given real-time gaze data and arm motion during teleoperation, and human-autonomy blending is formulated as a model predictive control problem. The inclusion of industry authors (Tye Brady, Amazon Robotics) hints at practical deployment interest.

entry.title: LogicVal:A Logic-Formalized Benchmark for Constraint Satisfaction in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Savitha Sam Abraham, Marjan Alirezaie, Hossein Rahnama

entry.summary: LogicVal recasts text-to-image evaluation as a constraint-satisfaction problem, using a logical framework to formally specify objects, attributes, relations, and constraints that generated images must satisfy. Four state-of-the-art T2I models are evaluated across nine classes of constraints from single attributes to multi-object relationships.

entry.title: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jie Mao, Pingchen Lu, Zikun Qu, Jiahang Sun, Xiangyi Wang, Zhiwei Shang, Zhiyong Wang, Guojun Xiong, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: IF-MAP is an influence-function-inspired method for identifying which agent in an LLM multi-agent system should be prioritized for improvement under resource constraints. It measures end-to-end loss changes under controlled semantic prompt perturbations and fits a regularized local response model in a low-dimensional prompt-embedding subspace. This moves beyond failure attribution toward estimating improvement potential, a useful resource-allocation lens.

entry.title: MM-LeJEPA: Correlated Gaussian Regularization for Multimodal Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Haowen Bai, Rui Gong$, Meichen Liu, Ming-Xuan Weng, Bihan Wen, Kim-Hui Yap

entry.summary: MM-LeJEPA extends LeJEPA, a decoder-free self-supervised learning method with isotropic Gaussian embedding targets, to multimodal settings by modeling tasks as strength-weighted combinations of modality-independent and shared-content components. This yields correlated Gaussian regularization that respects cross-modal task structure.

entry.title: Bridging Concepts: Multi-Agent Reasoning over Scientific Concept Graphs for High-Impact Research Prediction

author.name: Donggyu Yoon, Minsung Hwang, Juneha Baek, Donghyuk Shin, Joyce Jiyoung Whang

entry.summary: The authors construct scientific concept graphs with LLM-extracted fine-grained concepts as nodes and paper co-occurrence as edges, then forecast currently unconnected concept pairs that will become high-impact when connected. They release benchmark datasets from CIKM, KDD, and SIGIR papers with settings including emerging concepts unseen during training, and propose MiroGraph, a multi-agent reasoning framework for the task.

entry.title: Bud ContextCompact 2.0: Context Compaction for Agent Success and Accuracy with Small Language Models and Constrained Context Windows

author.name: Jithin VG, Ditto PS

entry.summary: This industry paper describes Bud ContextCompact 2.0, a context compaction mechanism for multi-turn agents running on small language models with constrained windows, replacing older turns with summaries. Evaluations show compaction to a 16K budget improves recall accuracy for a 1.2B model (0.176 with full history to 0.335) and a 9B model on SWE tasks versus truncation. It demonstrates that well-timed compaction can outperform both truncation and full-context for small models.

entry.title: Learning Which Device to Call: Online Tool Grounding for LLM Agents in IoT

author.name: Yichen Liu, Xiaochong Jiang, Haoran Yu, Lifei Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies online tool grounding for LLM agents in IoT: binding an already-specified tool call to a specific physical device when multiple endpoints offer the same capability, under service cost and participation constraints. The proposed framework formulates device selection as a contextual bandit problem combining adaptive context partitions with hierarchical endpoint selection. This addresses a real gap where prior work retrieves tools but never learns which eligible device returns useful observations.

entry.title: ABACUS: Program-Guided Multistep Reasoning over Frozen Judgment Models

author.name: Yuhao Wang, Zelin Zang

entry.summary: ABACUS composes saved programs with frozen judgment models that score candidate outcomes, letting a generative teacher design judgment schemas and composition procedures offline while the judgment model resolves local semantic questions online. Nine independently constructed programs solve all 450 executions of selected BIG-Bench Hard tasks.

entry.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching

author.name: Yitong Li, Jiang Bian, Jingling Wang, Pan Ding, Chengying Gu

entry.summary: MoveBench is the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching, assessing dimensions general benchmarks miss such as exercise safety, physiological appropriateness, personalization, and actionable coaching quality, using a rubric-based framework. Incorrect recommendations in this domain risk physical harm, making evaluation safety-critical.

entry.title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Capability-Focused Evaluation with Structural Diversity for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Hongyin Zhang, Mingyi Xiang, Rongzhao Chen, Yankai Wang, Jialin Qiao, Xiangdong Huang, Xiaoou Ding, Chen Wang, Zhongyi Pei, Jianmin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes CaFE, a refreshable evaluation extension for time series foundation models that enriches static benchmarks with structural diversity and replaces single-score evaluation with multi-dimensional, capability-oriented assessment. It profiles original benchmark data to generate diverse test distributions, countering benchmark-specific tuning. This addresses a growing problem as TSFMs become popular.

entry.title: Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints

author.name: Guannan Lai, Zi-Yang Bai, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: The paper shows that under tight generation, interaction, and memory budgets, existing lifelong-memory methods often offer little advantage over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents, because retrieving a relevant but ineffective memory consumes scarce context and hinders execution. It proposes learning the value of memories, i.e., deciding what is worth retaining and reusing when resources are scarce.

entry.title: Toward Structured Financial Foundation Models

author.name: Natraj Raman, Saumitra Mishra, Vamsi Potluru, Sumitra Ganesh

entry.summary: A position/research-agenda paper from a JPMorgan-affiliated team arguing that financial foundation models require structured-data-first, modular architectures to handle partial observability, asynchronous events, regime changes, and rare high-consequence states. It critiques both incompatible specialist models and monolithic multi-domain alternatives on governance and representation grounds.

entry.title: StebBench: Diagnosing Real-World Procedural Understanding in AI Agents

author.name: Hossein A. Rahmani, Bin Wu, Chaeeun Lee, Fanghua Ye, Sahan Bulathwela, Sujay Kumar Jauhar, Marzieh Fadaee, Nick Craswell, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: StepBench is a benchmark of 6,885 verified wikiHow procedures across 81 open-domain categories, with five diagnostic task types (withheld, incorrect, shuffled steps, next-step generation, full-plan generation) that distinguish error types rather than scoring only final plans. It examines how diagnostic performance correlates with end-to-end plan validity.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Tabular Learning via Hypergraph Reasoning with LLMs

author.name: Geon Lee, Kyungho Kim, Dongwon Choi, Juyeon Kim, Shinhwan Kang, Kijung Shin

entry.summary: TABHGR+ uses LLM-generated rules to weakly label and group table rows, then refines noisy labels via hypergraph-based label propagation, enabling efficient zero-shot tabular prediction that exploits inter-row dependencies. This improves on row-wise prompting approaches in both cost and accuracy for healthcare and finance-style data.

entry.title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs

author.name: Lei Tian, Chunzheng Zhu, Kai Wu, Yifan Zhang, Haihua Yang

entry.summary: PACE targets ViT-free native multimodal LLMs that tokenize pixel patches directly, showing empirically that unlike ViT-based models they tolerate aggressive visual token compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. The paper proposes an analysis pipeline and Pareto-adaptive compression tailored to this setting.

entry.title: Does AI-Assisted Development Homogenize Software? An Empirical Study of Code Similarity, Quality, and Evolution

author.name: Luciano Marchezan, Romain Lefeuvre, Kevin Delcourt, Benoit Combemale, Houari Sahraoui

entry.summary: The study analyzes 50 long-lived Java and Python open-source projects across pre-LLM, LLM-assisted, and detected agentic development eras using Software Heritage snapshots, measuring semantic and syntactic code similarity, SonarQube quality metrics, and evolution characteristics. It empirically investigates whether AI-assisted development reduces code diversity or degrades quality.

entry.title: Analyzing Repetition and Interference Effects in Memory-Constrained User Simulators

author.name: Cara Su-Yi Leong, Nicholas Tomlin, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: This study evaluates memory-constrained user simulators against two well-documented human memory phenomena: repetition improving retention and interference from competing information. While some simulators match human overall accuracy and replicate effect magnitudes, none match human error patterns at the question level: humans misremember facts whereas models forget them. The released benchmark gives future simulator work a behavioral-parity target.

entry.title: Towards Reinforcement Learning for Space Robotics: Fast Training and Reliable Real-World Transfer

author.name: Abhishek Naik, Michael Wu, Michael O'Sullivan, Colin Bellinger, Yunli Wang

entry.summary: This work demonstrates a fast simulation-based RL training framework with minimal hardware requirements whose learned policies transfer reliably to real robots. A quadruped learned to traverse diverse real-world terrains, including at a lunar-analog facility, after under 20 minutes of training on a single consumer GPU. It showcases practical sim-to-real RL for space robotics applications.

entry.title: Cooperation Without Shared Rewards via Reciprocal Q-Augmentation

author.name: Francesco Morri, Adel Abusitta, Quentin Cappart, Margarida Carvalho

entry.summary: This multi-agent RL paper introduces Reciprocal Q-Augmentation (RQA), which uses a latent-variable opponent model to augment an agent's Q-function with estimates of how its actions affect others, enabling sustained cooperation in general-sum games without access to other agents' rewards or internal states. It targets the well-known failure mode where a single defection collapses agents into welfare-suboptimal Nash equilibria.

entry.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis

author.name: Xiaoyu Wu, Zhaoxin Yu, Xinglin Xiao, Nan Xu

entry.summary: TIRE is a framework for scalable synthesis of physics reasoning training data that instantiates problems top-down from reusable physical formulas and their applicability conditions, with reliable execution producing verifiable numerical answers. This avoids hallucination risks of pure LLM text-based synthesis while retaining expert-style control over laws, conditions, and scenarios.

entry.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research

author.name: Wei Xiong, Jiangtong Li, Han Zhao, Linxiao Yang, Jie Li, Changjun Jiang

entry.summary: NeuroAct is an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis and decoding that runs dual loops over EEG foundation models, task-specific predictors, and model combinations. An inner loop of research, development, and review roles uses evidence on signal structure, representations, and training dynamics to test hypotheses and select interventions, aimed at explaining performance and generalization gaps rather than blind search.

entry.title: When Interpretations Persist: Downstream Influence in Gaze-Aware Assistants

author.name: Mingcong Ding, Chenyan Zhang, Zhuojiang Cai, Dongyang Guo, Babette B\"uhler, Enkelejda Kasneci

entry.summary: This controlled study examines whether interpretation records carried in an AI assistant's memory influence later predictions in gaze-aware streaming assistance. Findings show free-form interpretations amplify historical influence in both helpful and harmful directions, while evidence-bounded interpretation formats preserve distinguishing behavior and reduce harmful influence of wrong histories.

entry.title: A "feature ODE" describing the learning behavior of shallow MLPs on simple functions

author.name: Joseph Turnbull, Berkan Ottlik, Jamie Simon

entry.summary: Proposes a simplified ordinary differential equation, the feature ODE, meant to describe the gradient-flow learning dynamics of two-layer MLPs on anisotropic Gaussian data, and shows empirically that real MLPs learning Hermite polynomials and staircases roughly follow its loss trajectories. The surprisingly close agreement despite large simplifications is discussed and speculated upon.

entry.title: AirMPA: A Meteorology-to-Pollution Adapter for Global Air Quality Forecasting

author.name: Yiheng Wang, Kai Zheng, Yuetan Lin, Fanglu Fan, Chenliang Tao, Guochao Chen, Hongliang Zhang, Hao Li

entry.summary: Presents AirMPA, a decoupled autoregressive deep learning framework that forecasts 13 atmospheric pollutants globally at 0.4-degree resolution by adapting meteorological fields and emission priors to pollution prediction, rather than entangling meteorology and pollutants in one model. It aims to overcome the cost and parameterization limits of numerical forecasting systems.

entry.title: Keep the Lineages Alive: Diversity-Preserving SMC for Diffusion LLM Decoding

author.name: Minoo Ahmadi, Seyedarmin Azizi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: This work improves sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding for masked diffusion language models by preserving particle lineage diversity during resampling, avoiding the duplication-and-discard failure of multinomial resampling. It works with both internal confidence rewards and external process reward models and requires no post-training. It matters because diffusion LLM inference is an emerging area needing better decoding methods.

entry.title: Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization

author.name: Suwan Yoon, Seongryong Jung, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: APSD improves self-distillation policy optimization for LLM post-training by mixing student and self-teacher distributions asymmetrically based on rollout correctness: interpolation preserves successful behaviors on correct rollouts, while extrapolation beyond the self-teacher strengthens correction on incorrect ones. The paper supports the design with divergence decomposition and gradient analysis. It targets a real failure mode of naive self-teacher matching.

entry.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness

author.name: Caixin Kang, Sitong Gong, Tianyu Yan, Kaipeng Zhang, Yoichi Sato, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: ZhenhuanBench is a 1,592-item benchmark for detecting mock politeness (polite form, hostile intent), built from expert commentary on a Chinese drama, covering speaker intent, emotion-language mismatch, and listener uptake. GPT-6 Astra, an existing OpenAI model released in September 2026, leads at 73.48% overall with weaker listener-reaction performance at 58.37%. With 338 gold traces, an 8B model beat teacher distillation, and subsequent RL saturated, with chance correction shrinking the estimated recoverable gap substantially.

entry.title: ALIGN: Aligning Condition Estimation and Expression in Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning

author.name: Zechen Wang, Zhenqi Qiu, Houlong Xiong, Suohang Zhang, Yiyu Ren, Wanting Xu, Hongfei Niu, Chengyang He, Ge Sun, Ran Cheng, Qian Zhu

entry.summary: ALIGN improves Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning for vision-language-action policies trained on mixed-quality human demonstration data by directly predicting categorical pairwise conditions in the policy-facing label space rather than routing noisy thresholded advantage scores through prompts. This strengthens the conditioning signal in both construction and incorporation into the action vector field. The result is better exploitation of retries, recoveries, and failures in manipulation datasets.

entry.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction

author.name: Murat Guney Kemal, Robert Lieck

entry.summary: This work studies whether meaningful hierarchical structure can emerge from compression alone, introducing a hierarchical token-merging autoencoder that recursively composes sequences into multi-level representations. Using unsupervised grammar induction as a testbed where hierarchies can be explicitly evaluated, the authors probe whether reconstruction objectives favor compositional structure. It speaks to a core representation-learning question about emergent hierarchy without structural supervision.

entry.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting

author.name: Zehao Wang, Jianpeng Yao, Yuping Wang, Yiping Li, Jiaqi Li, Zhixu Li, Kanghoon Lee, Jinfeng Wang, Cong Liu, Zhaowei Tan, Jinkyoo Park, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-robot social navigation framework combining uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting across robots with robust decision making, targeting safety under occlusions and out-of-distribution scenarios. Cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion predicts future occupancy grids to improve coordination. Addresses a known weakness of naively extending single-robot RL navigation to multi-robot settings.

entry.title: SAGE-CP: When Marginal Coverage Hides Route-Conditional Failures in Adaptive VLM Ensembles

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: Shows that adaptive VLM ensembles with early exits can satisfy marginal conformal coverage while failing badly on individual computational routes, quantifying the worst-case conditional coverage given route prevalence. SAGE-CP freezes routing and applies Mondrian split conformal calibration separately to early-exit and escalated groups to restore route-conditional guarantees. A useful theoretical and practical contribution to uncertainty-aware ensembles.

entry.title: LatLM: Line-Parallel Language Models with Deferred Commitment

author.name: Shaorong Zhang, Shiyuan Li, Longxuan Yu, Greg Ver Steeg

entry.summary: Introduces LatLM, which makes commitment schedules an adaptive decoding-time choice for line-parallel language models, scoring eligible frontier tokens on a 2D lattice and committing confident candidates while deferring unready ones. This avoids premature commitments and cascading errors caused by fixed schedules like LCLM. One forward pass supervises entire sampled trajectories, supporting training.

entry.title: Inducing Fourier Geometry: A Smoothness Prior Imposes Approximate Translation Equivariance in Multimodal Stellar Embeddings

author.name: Ilay Kamai, Alex M. Bronstein, Hagai B. Perets

entry.summary: The authors introduce a graph-Laplacian smoothness prior that encourages learned representations to vary smoothly over a known physical parameter space, which in the continuum limit selects Laplacian eigenfunctions and predicts Fourier-like geometry corresponding to approximate translation symmetry. Applied to multimodal stellar embeddings across six astronomical surveys, the prior induces Toeplitz Gram structure and sinusoidal modes along stellar parameters.

entry.title: Revisiting Smoothed Online Learning: Competitive Ratio, Dynamic Regret with Switching Cost, and Best of Both Worlds

author.name: Lijun Zhang, Linzhe He, Wei Jiang, Shiyin Lu

entry.summary: This paper develops improved algorithms for smoothed online learning with better competitive ratios, optimal dynamic regret with switching costs, and best-of-both-worlds guarantees. It shows naive hitting-cost minimization achieves surprisingly strong competitive ratios for polyhedral and quadratic-growth functions, with matching lower bounds in some cases. The results unify competitive analysis and regret minimization for a broad class of costs.

entry.title: TideKV: Delayed KV Eviction via Layer-Wise Chunked Prefill for Memory-Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Yu Wang, Zhu Wang, Ning Hu, Yifan Guo, Xiu Ma, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: TideKV is an on-GPU cache-construction architecture for long-context LLM inference that performs layer-major delayed KV eviction, processing all prompt chunks per Transformer layer and retaining full-prompt KV only for the active layer. This lowers peak prefill memory without the degradation risk of chunk-level eviction that selects before observing the full prompt. It addresses a real bottleneck in long-context serving systems.

entry.title: CARTA: Self-Supervised Reusable Transaction Embeddings via Heterogeneous Tokenization and Cross-Attention

author.name: Shreyas K. Chandrahas, Jose Munoz, Satish Babu Bellapu

entry.summary: CARTA is a self-supervised encoder producing compact 16-dimensional transaction embeddings without fraud labels, using type-specific projections and learned embedding tables for high-cardinality identifiers, trained with token excision and InfoNCE contrastive loss. The frozen embedding supports label-efficient fraud probing — at 1% of labels on IEEE-CIS it beats raw features at 100% — and unsupervised risk stratification. Practical relevance to payment fraud detection where labels are scarce and expensive.

entry.title: Polynomial Learning of Positive ReLU Networks under Gaussian Inputs

author.name: Zhijie Zheng

entry.summary: The paper gives a learning guarantee for one-hidden-layer bias-free ReLU networks with nonnegative output weights under Gaussian inputs, allowing hidden directions to be arbitrarily close or linearly dependent. A width-k target can be approximated to squared error epsilon by a network of width at most k + min(k, d) with polynomial sample and computation cost in d, k, 1/epsilon, and log(1/delta). The argument combines implicit high-order moments with a direction cover robust to heavy noise atoms.

entry.title: FracTS: Hierarchical and Autoregressive Time Series Generation

author.name: Jiayu Li, Umair Afzal, Zilong Zhao, Milad Abdollahzadeh, Uzair Javaid, Biplab Sikdar

entry.summary: FracTS adapts fractal generative modeling from 2D images to 1D multivariate time series, learning a hierarchical coarse-to-fine autoregressive model that captures global trajectory structure at coarse scales and local dynamics at fine scales.
