On 512 fresh objects with a pre-registered held-out confirmation and sealed models, the memory reduces 1-second feature-forecast error. This mirrors how people learn object dynamics by poking them.

entry.title: FrameScout: Scouting Query-Relevant Frames for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Haonan Hu, Shuhao Chen, Weisen Jiang, Lizhao Gao, James Kwok, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: FrameScout is a keyframe selection method for long video understanding that uses a streaming selector with sliding-window KV cache and successor aggregation to produce temporally contextualized frame scores, avoiding the limitations of independent frame encoders or hard-to-optimize chunk ranking. It enables VideoLLMs to answer queries about videos spanning tens of minutes to hours within token budgets. This targets a key bottleneck for video LLMs.

entry.title: Recording-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal OT Intrusion Detection

author.name: Mustafa Umut Ozbek, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: Shows that benchmark intrusion-detection datasets for operational technology, where normal and attack data come from separate recordings, inflate reported performance because models exploit recording-associated artifacts. The paper introduces a recording-aware evaluation procedure with same-recording comparisons, prior-only fitting, randomized event schedules, and event-coverage and alarm-burden metrics, demonstrating strong leakage on the ProvICS dataset.

entry.title: Conditional Weight of Evidence for Gradient-Boosted Credit Models: Estimation, Additivity and Its Relation to Adverse Action Reasons

author.name: Agus Sudjianto, Denis Burakov

entry.summary: The paper introduces conditional weight of evidence for credit risk models, measuring how an individual characteristic changes default log-odds after the applicant's remaining credit information is known, enabling per-applicant rather than population-level assessment. The authors develop estimation methods and connect the measure to adverse action reason generation for gradient-boosted credit models. This supports regulatory interpretability requirements in lending.

entry.title: Integrable building blocks for symplectic neural networks: learned-type layers, fiber-preserving layers, and what a single layer can do

author.name: Andrew Qing He

entry.summary: This work expands the design space of exactly symplectic neural network layers, which are traditionally built from shear maps and gain expressivity only through depth. Observing that existing layers are flows of Hamiltonians of commuting integrals, the author derives three new layer families including learned-type layers and fiber-preserving layers, and characterizes what a single symplectic layer can express.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation with User Dropouts in Federated Learning

author.name: Jinbao Zhu, Kai Wan, Giuseppe Caire

entry.summary: This paper characterizes fundamental communication limits of information-theoretic secure aggregation in federated learning under user dropouts, across key distribution, masked-gradient upload, and mask-elimination phases. It shows that existing schemes designed for a prescribed dropout threshold cannot adapt communication to actual dropout, and derives tighter bounds and phase-adaptive designs.

entry.title: LaMER: Language-Conditioned Multi-Expert Routing for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Comprehension

author.name: Yu Yu Chang, Tzu-Hsuan Weng, Youssef Mohamed Amin, Mohaned Ahmed Elsayed, Hung-Hsuan Chen, Min-Te Sun, Sherine Shawky

entry.summary: LaMER is a weakly supervised framework for referring expression comprehension that dynamically routes among four frozen pretrained visual encoders to combine semantic alignment, fine texture, and boundary awareness without full encoder fusion. It targets the visual-linguistic gap under image-level supervision only.

entry.title: Discuss More, Comment Less: Boosting Automated Research via Multi-Perspective Collaborative Review

author.name: Junkai Zhou, Jiajia Wu, Zhaoyi Zhang, Shiting Guan, Chuanguang Yang

entry.summary: RoundtableReview is a deliberative multi-agent framework for automated peer review that structures papers into eight semantic slots and coordinates six reviewers with complementary roles to enable cross-examination and more reliable quality control of AI-generated research. It goes beyond single-model feedback or simple aggregation.

entry.title: Beyond Recall Saturation: Scaling Hard-Negative Reranker Training for Industrial Legal Retrieval

author.name: Yunhan Li, Mingjie Xie, Zeyang Shi, Gengshen Wu, Min Yang

entry.summary: Studies Chinese legal retrieval, showing that enlarging embedding candidate pools yields diminishing recall returns once top-300 reaches a high-recall operating region, shifting attention to reranker quality. It compares embedding-mined, self-mined, and dynamic hard-negative strategies under aligned protocols, finding an embedding-to-self-mined staged configuration effective.

entry.title: Towards Figurative Language Understanding in Moroccan Darija: An Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Jihad R'baiti, Youssef Hmamouche, Emmanuele Chersoni, Chu-Ren Huang, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni

entry.summary: The authors introduce MDFC, a benchmark for idioms, metaphors, and proverbs in Moroccan Darija covering machine translation and multiple-choice selection, and evaluate 19 open and closed models under zero-shot and six-shot settings. The work also includes layer-level analysis, addressing scarce resources for this low-resource dialect.

entry.title: Quality-Controlled Reply and Summary Data for Post-Training Small Language Models in AI Call-Screening Agents

author.name: Jiaqi Gan, Tsang Ng, Ankit Raj, Tommy Duong, Xingyu Shen, Kidus Zewde, Huaiyu Guo, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: The paper constructs quality-controlled synthetic supervision for on-device call-screening small language models, covering in-call replies within the owner's authority and post-call summaries, since real calls provide no reference data. It targets failure modes such as unwarranted alarms and summaries that report caller claims as fact.

entry.title: Truncated Reasoning Under a Budget: Evaluating System-1 Models as Decision-makers

author.name: Zhongyin Wang, Zhaoqian Xue, Junting Mu, Haozheng Liu, Ye Yuan, Haolun Wu, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Evaluates a System-1 decision model as a reader of truncated reasoning traces from LLM reasoners across seven reasoners and five multiple-choice benchmarks. Reading truncated traces yields higher accuracy than forced answering at tested token budgets, improving accuracy by 4.1 points overall at a 1,500-token budget including reasoning and answering costs.

entry.title: Balance-Aware Pivot Selection for Parallel Diffusion LLM Decoding

author.name: Yejin Lee, Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Proposes Balance-Aware Pivot Decoding (BPD) for diffusion language models, which selects central pivots within contiguous masked intervals for parallel token commitment instead of relying solely on predictive confidence. By considering how token positions shape the remaining decoding schedule and inter-token dependencies, BPD accelerates parallel decoding while preserving quality.

entry.title: SNO-PI: Label-Scarce SNOMED CT Entity Linking with Pre-trained Encoders and Curated Terminology Knowledge

author.name: Piyawoot Songsiritat

entry.summary: Presents SNO-PI, the top-performing submission on SNOMED International's SNOMED CT Entity Linking Benchmark as of October 2026, achieving a macro character IoU of 0.5387 versus the reference system's 0.4582. The approach combines high-recall span proposal, SapBERT retrieval, listwise reranking, and curated terminology knowledge to handle a label space of roughly 219,000 concepts with very sparse annotation.

entry.title: Information Theory of Random Composition Trees

author.name: Doron Sivan, Weishun Zhong, Tankut Can, Mikhail Katkov, Misha Tsodyks

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes random composition trees, a stochastic model of hierarchical semantic text structure, proving that entropy grows linearly with root size and deriving an analytical expression for entropy rate as a function of branching factor. The work formalizes empirical observations that different text types exhibit distinct branching factors and matching entropy-rate behavior.

entry.title: Label Authority in Speech Emotion Recognition: Intended and Perceived Ground Truth in Emozionalmente

author.name: Marco Giordano, Stefano Giacomelli, Claudia Rinaldi, Fabio Graziosi

entry.summary: Using the Emozionalmente acted Italian corpus with both elicited production labels and five listener judgments per clip, the authors compare three label authorities for speech emotion recognition with frozen XLS-R, HuBERT, and WavLM probes. They find recovering the expressed condition is easier than predicting tie-broken listener plurality, highlighting that these represent different construct questions rather than a strict difficulty ranking.

entry.title: Toward AI-Driven Phytoplankton Event Detection from Image Classification: Temporal Aggregation Under Domain Shift

author.name: Ali Rohan, Hassan Shayan, Han-Gue Jo, Colin Moffat

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether image-level AI classifications from Imaging FlowCytobot systems can produce ecologically meaningful temporal occurrence patterns for phytoplankton monitoring, evaluating across realistic sampling and cross-domain transfer from MedPlanktonSet to an independent Swedish dataset. It develops a monitoring-oriented framework with biologically meaningful event aggregation under domain shift.

entry.title: Spatons: Spatiotonally Localized Building Blocks for Efficient XR Predistortion

author.name: Mohammadjavad Maheronnaghsh, Sushant Kondguli, Steve Mann, Andreas Moshovos

entry.summary: Spatons are compositional, spatially localized neural operators combining tiny MLPs with fixed-function interpolation for efficient XR display predistortion, compensating geometric and color distortions on untethered, battery-powered headsets. The design targets low energy and latency while remaining programmable across different projection systems and manufacturing tolerances.

entry.title: Predicting Individual Differences in Lipreading From Eye-Tracking and Pupillometry During Silent Visual Speech

author.name: Puneet Kumar, Satyarth Malik, Gao Zheng, Guoying Zhao, Xiaobai Li

entry.summary: Introduces the LiPS dataset and a tracker-independent pipeline to study whether lipreading ability can be inferred from viewing behavior, quantifying contributions of gaze dynamics, pupil-linked signals, and spatial viewing allocation in 24 adults during silent speech. The work aims to explain individual differences in speechreading, particularly relevant to people who are hard of hearing.

entry.title: GeoART: Geometry-Aware Refinement via Test-Time Scaling for Camera-Conditioned Video Diffusion

author.name: Liudi Yang, Ziyuan Liu

entry.summary: GeoART is a training-free self-refinement framework that improves camera controllability in video diffusion through geometry-aware test-time scaling, generating multiple candidates during denoising and selecting them with a geometry prior, including confidence gating of unreliable geometric evidence.

entry.title: Only Means Only: what a harmonization benchmark score averages over

author.name: Imad Bulji\'c, Delaida Muminovi\'c

entry.summary: Audits a standard image harmonization benchmark and finds 1,399 photographs appear in both training and test splits, accounting for a quarter of the test set, producing two-to-five-times lower measured error that mostly reflects composition artifacts rather than method quality.

entry.title: From Label Priors to Task Evidence: Efficient Long-Video Frame Selection via Bayesian GRPO

author.name: Shuochen Chang, Bingjie Gao, Qingyang Liu, Qianli Ma, Yibo Miao, Haonan Zhao, Zhaohe Liao, Xiaofeng Zhang, Jiangtong Li, Li Niu

entry.summary: Reformulates long-video frame selection for MLLMs as latent-variable inference, initializing a lightweight policy with supervised learning and then refining it with a frozen MLLM acting as task evidence via a Bayesian variant of GRPO reinforcement learning, aligning frame selection with downstream reasoning needs.

entry.title: Where Do the Gaussians Go? Foreground Attraction for Camera-Based Weakly Supervised 3D Occupancy

author.name: Jeagon Song, Jhonghyun An

entry.summary: The paper shows that sparse Gaussian representations for camera-based 3D occupancy trained with rendering losses under-weight foreground objects, with foreground Gaussian density only 1.62x background. It proposes a training-only foreground attraction loss that back-projects pseudo-labeled pixels into 3D and pulls class-consistent Gaussians toward them, leaving inference unchanged.

entry.title: See the Future, Classify the Present: Stochastic Latent World Modeling for Hyperspectral Images

author.name: Muhammad Ahmad, Gemine Vivone, Ronny H\"ansch, Ahmed Sohaib, Manuel Mazzara, Danfeng Hong

entry.summary: This work proposes LWM, a trajectory-based representation learning framework for hyperspectral image classification that uses stochastic latent-state prediction to model structured dependencies in latent space. It tokenizes spectral and spatial information with separate transformer branches, fuses them, and organizes the result into an environment state capturing center, neighborhood, spectral, and global context.

entry.title: Multi-scale Fusion of Fast Vision Mamba and Foundation Model Features for Patch-Level Gleason Grading in Computational Pathology

author.name: Zihe Zhang, Weimiao Yu, Piumi Don Simonge

entry.summary: The authors build a multi-scale classifier using state-space models (Vision Mamba) fused with pathology foundation model features for patch-level Gleason grading of prostate whole slide images. The approach targets subtle morphological differences, severe class imbalance, and multi-scale diagnostic context under limited data and compute budgets.

entry.title: DCR-TSF: Dual-Level Compositional Reasoning with Triadic Spherical Fusion for Training-Free Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Gwang-Ho Na, Ho-Joong Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: DCR-TSF is a training-free framework for zero-shot composed image retrieval that uses dual-level compositional reasoning and triadic spherical fusion to combine reference image, text modification, and generated descriptions, mitigating appearance-biased retrieval caused by over-reliance on MLLM-generated target descriptions.

entry.title: RGB--Event Object Detection Across Operating Frequencies via Reliability-Supervised Routing and Asymmetric-Resolution Fusion

author.name: Peijun Shi, Jiannan Zhao, Xiujin Zhu, Zhenguo Lao, Chee-Onn Chow, Wei Ru Wong

entry.summary: This paper targets object detection with RGB and event cameras at decision rates far above the camera frame rate, where event windows become sparse and reliability varies. It proposes reliability-supervised routing that assigns per-location fusion weights supervised by single-modality classifier losses during training. Relevant to autonomous vehicle perception between frames.

entry.title: From Legacy to Contemporary: Scalable Color Modernization for Long Video

author.name: Dongyun Kim, Jiwoo Choi, Jaeseong Lee, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: This paper formulates long-video color modernization, updating chromatic and tonal appearance of legacy footage while preserving content and cross-shot coherence, and proposes a training-free framework that jointly modernizes grids of adjacent keyframes with a pretrained text-guided image editing model, needing no paired supervision. It addresses a task that currently relies on expert colorists and scales poorly.

entry.title: CaptionFuse: Training-Free Composed Product Retrieval Via VLM Intent Captioning and Weighted Embedding Fusion

author.name: Zhao Gao, Mina Metias, Mohamed Noordeen Alaudeen, Bassel Saleh

entry.summary: CaptionFuse is a training-free composed image retrieval method for eCommerce that uses a VLM to caption the user intent grounded in the reference image, filling in attributes the sparse modification text omits, then fuses embeddings with weighting. It identifies a fundamental limitation of arithmetic CLIP fusion when user text specifies changes but not what to preserve. The approach is practical and directly deployable for product search.

entry.title: An Anatomy-Aware Staged Pipeline for Vessel-Specific Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation in CT and MR Angiography

author.name: Gniewosz Drwiega, Wojciech Szymanski, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: This work tackles the TopAneu 2026 challenge with a six-stage anatomy-aware pipeline for voxel-level, vessel-specific intracranial aneurysm segmentation across CT and MR angiography, including modality routing, vessel segmentation, candidate localization, lesion segmentation, instancing, and anatomical classification. The staged design handles a 50+ class taxonomy that a single network could not manage. It demonstrates rigorous engineering for a clinical challenge.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Models for Direct Multi-Shell Diffusion MRI Signal Estimation

author.name: Sanna Persson, Fabian Leander Sinzinger, Christoffer Ohlsson, Rodrigo Moreno

entry.summary: This paper represents the entire diffusion MRI signal with an implicit neural representation using wavelet activations, Fourier features, and spherical harmonics, enabling q-space super-resolution and interpolation despite acquisition-time limits. A group-template pretraining strategy enables faster per-patient fitting. It addresses a fundamental acquisition-efficiency problem in neuroimaging.

entry.title: Progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory for incomplete multimodal brain tumor segmentation

author.name: Milad Rostamian, Mohammadreza Mohammadi, Mohsen Soryani

entry.summary: Presents PMTM, a network that segments brain tumors from any non-empty subset of four MRI sequences by maintaining a progressive tumor-state memory across encoder stages. Assignment maps pool spatial features into ordered evidence vectors that are retained and updated to guide later-stage fusion. This addresses the practical problem of missing MRI modalities in clinical settings.

entry.title: Evaluating Lightweight Contact Feedback in Dual-Operator Collaborative Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Austin Graves, Chuizheng Kong, Yunho Cho, Yuanshao Yang, Advaith Nidumukkala, Shreyas Kousik, Mohsen Moghaddam

entry.summary: This paper presents XRT, an extended-reality teleoperation framework returning fingertip contact information through lightweight vibrotactile and auditory feedback, plus a synchronized dual-humanoid testbed. A 16-dyad within-subject study of a collaborative crate lift-and-flip under four feedback conditions yields findings on how feedback channels affect collaborative teleoperation performance.

entry.title: Scalable, Intuitive, Mixed Reality-Based Semi-Autonomous Robotic Telemanipulation for the Execution of a Fine-Grained Bimanual Task

author.name: Shifei Duan, Zhe Wang, Francesco De Pace, Minas Liarokapis

entry.summary: This paper presents a mixed-reality semi-autonomous telemanipulation system for fine-grained bimanual tasks, aimed at reducing operator fatigue during large-scale demonstration collection. By blending autonomy with human control, the system improves the scalability and quality of demonstration data used for robot learning. The work targets the bottleneck that manual teleoperation imposes on dataset creation.

entry.title: OmniInteract: Towards Unified Whole-Body Interaction Control for Dual Humanoids

author.name: Yinghao Li, Tianyu Zhang, Zhuohao Li, Yi-Lin Wei, Fa-Ting Hong, Qing Zhang, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: OmniInteract addresses dual-humanoid whole-body interaction through Surface Contact-Aware Retargeting, which uses dense human-robot surface correspondences to preserve contact relationships during motion retargeting, plus scalable residual policy learning to retain control fidelity as interaction diversity grows.

entry.title: Robot Learning with Vision-Language-Action Models for Agricultural Manipulation

author.name: Hamid Hafezi, Javad Mohammadpour Velni, Mohammadreza Davoodi

entry.summary: This work develops a simulation-to-real robot-learning framework for agricultural reaching and grasping that combines task-specific demonstration collection with adaptation of pretrained vision-language-action policies, using a MuJoCo-based agricultural environment. It targets challenges such as plant geometry variation, occlusion, and camera viewpoint changes while reducing costly real-robot demonstrations.

entry.title: Human vs AI in Go in 2026: Lessons for superintelligence?

author.name: Haoxing Du

entry.summary: The author analyzes Shin Jin-seo's July 2026 match victory over KataGo with only a 2-stone handicap, probing what this surprising result implies about AI superhuman claims in Go and about superintelligence forecasts generally. The post surveys possible interpretations and their implications for how much we should trust domain-level superhuman benchmarks as evidence of general AI superiority.

entry.title: Twitch Plays: AI Interpretability of Bonsai-8B

author.name: moridinamael

entry.summary: The author launches a Twitch livestream where an audience collaborates with Claude to semi-autonomously interpret neurons, connections, and circuits in the Bonsai-8B LLM, with an evolving interpretability map that contributors can extend via pull requests. The project explores large-scale crowd-agent hybrid interpretability of a full model.

entry.title: Capital Ownership Will Make You Go Crazy First

author.name: Jan_Kulveit

entry.summary: Jan Kulveit argues that in AI-driven disempowerment scenarios, large capital owners may be disempowered sooner than the jobless masses, via a mechanism of epistemic corruption: growing numbers of people and organizations optimizing against the billionaire's beliefs and values to capture their resources. The post analyzes why staying sane and value-coherent becomes harder as one's capital grows.

entry.title: Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter issue centered on his Per Jacobsson lecture at the October IMF meeting in Bangkok, arguing that AI is beginning to operate at the frontier of human science and that policymakers should expect rapid transformative change. It focuses on how humanity can share AI's benefits through foresight and restraint.

entry.title: SAR: Learning Global Item-Space Matching and Geometry-Aware Placement Ranking for Buffered Online 3D Bin Packing

author.name: Xinpeng Lei, Jin Zhang, Yizhe Yang, Yihong Duan, Fucheng Wan

entry.summary: SAR is a learning-based framework for online 3D bin packing with a bounded buffer that coordinates global item-space matching with geometry-aware placement ranking, using a voxel-token spatial encoder to represent container occupancy. It addresses how to allocate spatial reasoning between item selection and placement evaluation under irreversible decisions with limited future knowledge.

entry.title: AuDQ: Auditable Data Quality through Agentic Rule Discovery

author.name: Jacopo Biggiogera, Nicolas Colombo, Krati Saxena, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

entry.summary: Presents a vision for an ontology-grounded data quality layer where quality rules are first-class artifacts, versioned, linked to governance texts, and re-playable via immutable execution traces, with an agentic rule-discovery core offering Full-Agentic and Guided modes plus human-in-the-loop review. An evaluation framework and initial experiments validate the core.

entry.title: UtoMe: Observation-Uncertainty-Guided Token Merging for Weather Foundation Models

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Xi Xiao, Jihun Hamm, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: UtoMe is a token-merging framework for weather transformers that combines dynamics saliency with ensemble data assimilation spread as an input-reliability proxy, protecting high-value tokens as anchors during bipartite matching. On ERA5 72-hour forecasting at two resolutions, it improves efficiency while accounting for heterogeneous observation uncertainty across variables and weather regimes.

entry.title: Reflection-Guided Dynamics Rectification for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Shuo Xu, Hanrui Ying, Debin Liu, Jianjun Li, Zhiyuan Ma

entry.summary: RGDR converts reflections on completed text-to-image generations into corrective interventions on the sampling dynamics during inference, addressing the execution gap where prior test-time optimization methods identify residual errors but cannot ensure the model acts on the feedback. The method operates under a limited additional budget at test time.

entry.title: OV-PEAR: Observation-Verified Pose-Scale Estimation and Reconstruction for Unknown Industrial Manipulation Objects

author.name: Guoqin Tang, Qingxuan Jia, Yichen Tan, Zihang Lv, Ruiquan Wang, Zeyuan Huang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Presents OV-PEAR, a three-stage pipeline combining RGB-D segmentation, appearance-aware view retrieval, explicit scale search, and multi-view RGB-D verification to estimate 6D pose, scale, and reconstruct operation-ready 3D models of unseen industrial objects without CAD models. It targets limitations of zero-shot methods such as occlusion, generative bias, and scale uncertainty.

entry.title: CIS-Transolver: A Cross-Layer Incremental-State Neural Operator for Fine-Scale Automotive Aerodynamic Flow Prediction

author.name: Jianglong Liu, Zhicheng Zhu, Jia Hao, Liangyue Jia

entry.summary: CIS-Transolver proposes a cross-layer incremental-state neural operator that carries fine-scale local flow information extracted near complex geometries through subsequent operator layers, addressing spectral bias in neural operator predictions of automotive aerodynamics. This extends fine-scale modeling from one-off local extraction to continuous use across the network. The aim is more accurate rapid prediction of complex flow fields.

entry.title: Fast Construction of Inner Sphere Trees Using Machine Learning

author.name: Jianneng Huang, Wenjia Rao

entry.summary: Reformulates inner sphere tree construction for collision detection as single-shot set prediction: a network predicts inscribed sphere candidates from voxel geometry, refined via differentiable coverage feedback and a geometric projection for validity. This accelerates IST construction that is otherwise sequential and expensive, benefiting physics simulation, VR, and robotics. Practical ML acceleration of a geometry bottleneck.

entry.title: Torch-DPhys: A Torch-Native, MOOSE-Compatible Framework for Differentiable Physics Simulation and Hybrid Machine Learning Integration

author.name: Akzhol Almukhametov, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Torch-DPhys is a PyTorch-native framework for differentiable physics simulation implementing thermal-hydraulics concepts from MOOSE's Thermal Hydraulics Module and SAM, with sensitivity computation via automatic differentiation or discrete adjoints. It supports CPU and GPU execution, sparse direct solves, and is verified against analytical solutions and reference codes.

entry.title: CVTA: Cross-Variable Temporal Attention for Multivariate Irregular Time Series Prediction

author.name: Ankitkumar Joshi, Milos Hauskrecht

entry.summary: CVTA is a continuous-time forecasting framework for irregularly sampled multivariate time series that uses Variable-Conditioned Embeddings to project heterogeneous variables into variable-specific latent spaces and temporal attention over a compact interpretable state to capture cross-variable dependencies. Targeted domains include healthcare, climate, and monitoring systems. The framework emphasizes short-term prediction from recent dynamics with interpretability.

entry.title: OceanTensorCube and ST-MMT: A Multimodal Data and Transformer System for Seven-Day Forecasting of Pyropia Bleaching

author.name: Gwangjin Kim, Cheolyoung Jang, Yosep Jo

entry.summary: The paper presents a system forecasting bleaching of cultured Pyropia (laver) seven days ahead for Korean seaweed farm clusters, aligning 32 marine, meteorological, and satellite channels on a 30 m grid and applying a 9.2M-parameter spatiotemporal transformer with hub-style cross-attention. A six-seed ensemble detects all reported positives with at most 3.5% false alarms on validation data.

entry.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks

author.name: Wanjie Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes FLICKER, a federated gradient-based power iteration that recovers targeted singular directions of a horizontally partitioned matrix using only local matrix-vector products, with non-asymptotic convergence guarantees. Building on it, BiFLICKER performs federated community detection in bipartite networks under a sparse model, with a projected variant for nearby or repeated singular directions.

entry.title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity

author.name: Youran Dong, Junfeng Yang, Wei Yao, Jin Zhang

entry.summary: The authors develop two Newton-based bilevel optimization algorithms, Newton-based GALET and Newton-based BAMM, that handle nonunique lower-level solutions and singular lower-level Hessians without requiring strong convexity. This extends the applicability of second-order bilevel methods used in hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning.

entry.title: Pronouncing Hard Words: Phoneme Adaptation of a Pretrained Conversational Text to Speech Model

author.name: Yashish M. Siriwardena, Dinesh K. Gnanasekaran, Tanmay Laud, Shinji Watanabe, Subhabrata Mukherjee, Shanil Puri

entry.summary: The paper retrofits phoneme controllability onto a pretrained conversational TTS model without retraining from scratch, using an ARPAbet vocabulary extension, continued phoneme-augmented SFT, and training-free inference mechanisms. This targets accurate pronunciation of rare, trust-critical entities like drug names in streaming voice-agent pipelines.

entry.title: I$^2$-Med: Interpretable Medical Inference through Visual-Guided Dynamic Logits Calibration

author.name: Md Sajid, Shreeyut Maheshwari, Akshat Mishra, Ritik Mishra, Mohammad Tanveer

entry.summary: Proposes I2-Med, a framework for medical vision-language models that improves visual grounding and clinical explanation coherence via visual-guided dynamic logits calibration, targeting visual hallucination under scarce expert annotations. It aims to make medical inference more interpretable and clinically reliable.

entry.title: Pseudo-Label Foreground Quality Weighting for Domain-Generalized Fundus Image Segmentation

author.name: Lucas Gabriel Telesco, Jos\'e Ignacio Orlando

entry.summary: The paper extends Noisy Student semi-supervised training for optic disc and cup segmentation in fundus images by weighting pseudo-label supervision with a mask-derived reliability estimate from a multitask Dice predictor. This targeted quality weighting improves robustness under domain shift for automated glaucoma assessment.

entry.title: Cross-polarization pairing for label-free few-shot thin-section classification

author.name: Bingchen Yan

entry.summary: This work studies few-shot classification of unseen rock types with no labeled slides, exploiting the fact that polarized-light microscopy naturally records paired PPL and XPL images of the same material. The authors show these physically grounded positive pairs avoid the failure modes of generic unsupervised pseudo-tasks, which produce either wrong positives or near-duplicates that teach the model little.

entry.title: MoCKEFA: Model-Conditioned Keyframe Extraction and Fair Attribution for Video Model Explanation

author.name: Lahiru Wijayasingha

entry.summary: Presents a method that extracts video keyframes conditioned on a model's prediction so that a few frames preserve the model's belief about the video, then fairly distributes frame importance using Shapley values. The author shows keyframe attribution outperforms traditional per-frame attribution for explainable video models and explores differences between adjacent keyframes.

entry.title: LC-TSRNet: A Land-Cover-Guided Two-Stage Network for Annual MODIS Surface Reflectance Time Series Reconstruction

author.name: Wenjuan Zhang, Xuesong Ma, Zhen Li, Meixiang Wang, Caimeng Yi, Jie Pan, Nan Su, Bing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage network that reconstructs seamless annual MODIS surface reflectance time series by using annual land cover maps as prior knowledge in the first stage, avoiding reliance on scarce cloud-free references or spatially mismatched SAR data. This addresses data gaps from cloud contamination and sensor malfunctions that limit long-term, large-scale satellite studies.

entry.title: Visual Memory and Textual Alignment for Cross-Modal Few-Shot Segmentation

author.name: Tianqi Wei, Zhi Chen, Xin Yu, Scott Chapman, Zi Huang

entry.summary: ViTA-SAM builds on SAM 3 for few-shot segmentation in specialized domains where text prompts and visual representations are poorly aligned. It adds a visual memory module encoding support features with their masks for support-aware guidance, combined with cross-modal alignment between visual memory and textual features.

entry.title: HP-PnP-Flow: Hybrid Time Scheduling and Projection for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration via Flow Matching

author.name: Yong Li, Xiaojie Wang, Xiaoyan Zhang

entry.summary: HP-PnP-Flow improves plug-and-play image restoration by combining flow-matching-based denoisers with a different time schedule and a pixel-space projection operator, yielding rigorous convergence guarantees and better efficiency over prior PnP-Flow methods (building on ICLR 2025 work by Martin et al.). It matters for inverse problems in imaging.

entry.title: DinoMUSE: A DINOv2-guided Framework for Unsupervised Lateral Motion Estimation in Ultrasound Elastography

author.name: Xiyao Meng, Xingyue Wei, Baihua Luo, Bo Peng, Jianwen Luo

entry.summary: DinoMUSE incorporates DINOv2's high-level visual representations into a mixture-of-experts framework for unsupervised lateral motion estimation in quasi-static ultrasound elastography, addressing the low-resolution, phase-poor lateral direction problem. Global semantic context from foundation-model features supplements local image matching and physical constraints. This could improve non-invasive tissue stiffness assessment.

entry.title: Beyond Human-Derived Motion: Exploring Robot-Specific Execution for Construction Humanoids

author.name: MinJun Chang, Taehyung Kim, Yong K. Cho, Francis Baek

entry.summary: This study examines whether humanoid robots in construction settings should exploit robot-specific motions that depart from human demonstrations once task-relevant motion information has been transferred. It explores robot-specific motion execution as a complement to human motion retargeting for construction workspaces and tools.

entry.title: Bio-inspired Thrust-Assisted Trotting on a legged-Aerial Robot via Real-Time QP-MPC

author.name: Shreyansh Pitroda, Eric Sihite, Alireza Ramezani, Morteza Gharib

entry.summary: The paper presents hardware implementation of a QP-based model predictive controller on Harpy, a thruster-assisted bipedal robot, inspired by wing-assisted locomotion in birds like the chukar partridge. The condensed QP-MPC regulates ground contact force and thrust vectoring at 500 Hz with a decoupled sagittal/frontal control architecture.

entry.title: Decision4Rec: A Jev-Inspired Framework of Decision Models on Knowledge and Active Graphs for Multi-Agent Recommender Systems

author.name: Marco Polignano, Het Darshan Mehta, Pasquale Lops, Ernesto William De Luca, Giovanni Semeraro

entry.summary: Decision4Rec is an open modular framework applying scoring-based decision models to recommendation: a knowledge graph renders logs as short statements, agent pools propose candidates, a residual ranker keeps the top 30, and a decision model scores them through typed questions with a fusion step. It works with any decision model sharing the interface, demonstrated with commercial and open models.

entry.title: Stable Signer V3: 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting Is All You Need for Sign Language Production

author.name: Sen Fang, Liwei Che, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Stable Signer V3 is a high-resolution interactive sign language avatar system built on 4D deformable primitive splatting, adding transferable facial primitives for expression, a test-time identity-specific virtual muscle layer for body deformation, and a super-resolution module for signer-specific detail. Both test-time modules optimize once per signer identity, after which inference runs from stored parameters.

entry.title: Margin-Based Generalization for Quantum Machine Learning with Classical Data Encoding

author.name: Ju-Young Ryu, Tak Hur, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: Develops a margin-based generalization theory for quantum models operating on classically encoded data, treating the data encoding as part of the hypothesis class. For fixed encodings the existing margin bound transfers unchanged, while for trainable encodings a two-scale covering argument adds an encoding-capacity term of order O~(sqrt(L/m)) to the bound.

entry.title: TriScore: Post-Hoc Out-of-Distribution Detection with Energy, Boundary Probes, and Transform Consistency

author.name: Ege Gursoy, Nicolas Mansard

entry.summary: TriScore is a post-hoc out-of-distribution detector that fuses three complementary ID-calibrated signals from a frozen classifier: an energy prior, a boundary-fragility score, and a transform-consistency score. It targets the failure mode where adversarial classifier-level shift preserves the cue a single-signal detector relies on while changing model behavior, and fuses standardized signals via an ensemble.

entry.title: Image Dehazing as In-Context Tabular Inference

author.name: Le-Anh Tran

entry.summary: Reformulates single-image dehazing as an in-context tabular regression problem solved by tabular foundation models, introducing DehazeTab, which estimates atmospheric transmission from structured image-patch representations without task-specific training. This offers an alternative to handcrafted physical priors or dedicated deep architectures for dehazing.

entry.title: A Two-Stage Hybrid Framework for Inferring Air Trips from Mobile Location-based Service (LBS) Data under Incomplete Airport Sightings

author.name: Hsuan-Chih Wang, Xianfeng Terry Yang

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage hybrid framework for inferring U.S. domestic air travel from large-scale mobile location-based service (LBS) data, even when airport sightings before or after flights are missing. Stage 1 applies heuristic rules to flag high-confidence air trips with endpoints observed at two airports, while Stage 2 uses a probabilistic model leveraging spatial proximity, temporal compatibility, and historical flight schedules to infer latent air trips. It matters because it offers airport planners a more complete picture of traveler mobility patterns than rule-based detection alone.

entry.title: Frequency-Domain Membership Inference Does Not Beat Confidence Thresholding: A Band-Resolved Analysis of Why

author.name: Mohammad Zare, Pirooz Shmamsinejadbabaki

entry.summary: This negative-result paper tests the widely repeated claim that degrading input resolution exposes model memorization in membership inference attacks. Using a monotone family of low-pass filters and a dozen decay-scoring schemes on two federated ResNet-18 targets, the authors find frequency-domain profiles fail to beat a simple confidence threshold, with best AUC of 0.513 versus 0.537.

entry.title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations

author.name: Yuanhao Gong

entry.summary: Proposes a wavelet-inspired neural Poisson solver with only 24 trainable scalars organized in four 5x5 kernels, combining the efficiency of learned methods with the robustness of traditional numerical solvers. The extreme compactness enables deployment in settings where heavy neural PDE solvers are impractical.

entry.title: Dialogue Generation for Conversational Recommendation Using User Search Interactions and Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Minsung Hwang, Donggyu Yoon, Gowoon Hwang, Kwanghee Jang, Joyce Jiyoung Whang

entry.summary: SearCl automatically generates conversational recommendation dialogues from real user search and click logs, avoiding costly manual annotation. It segments interactions into query sessions, uses a probabilistic state machine for dialogue flow, employs two LLM agents as seeker and recommender, and grounds recommendations in knowledge graphs built from content metadata.

entry.title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing

author.name: Jiayan Yang, Ad Feelders, Arno Siebes

entry.summary: This study bridges clinical risk prediction and operational planning with an uncertainty-aware anticipatory staffing framework that translates probabilistic deterioration estimates into ICU staffing decisions under real-world constraints like shift rigidity and hiring delays. It explicitly addresses the gap between discrimination metrics and downstream operational value. The framework links short-term patient risk prediction to staff planning without modifying the upstream predictive model.

entry.title: Minimum-Cost Robust Evidence Certificates for Horn Reasoning under Correlated Source Failures

author.name: Yukun Yang

entry.summary: The paper studies minimum-cost certificates that preserve Horn-rule conclusions under withdrawal of up to k source domains, accounting for correlated failures and replicated attestations. It characterizes robustness via transversals of minimal-support footprints, gives an exact algorithm alternating weighted evidence selection with a source-failure oracle, and derives a globally valid selection cut from a rule-closed counterinterpretation.

entry.title: On the Benefits of Uncertainty Estimation for Species Classification: A Case Study on Optimizing Expert re-Annotation

author.name: Kamenan N'Gadi (LORIA, BISCUIT), Martin Laviale (LIEC, LTSER-ZAM), C{\'e}dric Pradalier (LORIA, BISCUIT), J{\'e}r{\'e}my Fix (LORIA, BISCUIT)

entry.summary: Builds a ResNet-18 classifier for a 759-class diatom biomonitoring dataset and shows that temperature scaling improves calibration (ECE from 0.117 to 0.055), enabling selective classification that triages which images need expert re-annotation. This reduces expert workload while preserving taxonomic integrity in freshwater monitoring.

entry.title: CoRS: Fast Neural Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling via Composite Interval State Reuse

author.name: Jiang Sutong, Zhao Peng, Wu Xuan, Wang Yan, Wang Jiaqi, Zhang Rui, Jiang Yuan, Zhou You, Wang Di

entry.summary: CoRS accelerates neural solvers for the Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem by decoupling expensive graph representation updates from cheap feasibility updates: the graph encoding is reused across multiple decisions while exact feasibility state is refreshed at every step. This two-timescale design amortizes encoding cost without parallelizing action generation or relaxing constraints, plus a feasibility-preserving composite-interval decoding scheme.

entry.title: From Outcomes to Components: A Counterfactual Evaluation Framework for LLM-Proposed Repairs

author.name: Hengyu Ye, Songhua Hu

entry.summary: A counterfactual evaluation framework that decomposes LLM-proposed repair actions into target-set and numerical-update components, executing each pairing from the same initial state against a reference action. In traffic networks and database repair, it finds many actions show super-additive gains only when both components are corrected together.

entry.title: Transformer-based segmentation of prosodic boundaries in Brazilian Portuguese

author.name: Rodrigo de Freitas Lima, Julio Cesar Galdino, Marcos Vinicius Treviso

entry.summary: The authors present SAMPA, a fine-tuned Whisper large-v3 model that transcribes Brazilian Portuguese speech while inserting explicit markers for prosodic boundaries, using manually segmented NURC-SP recordings. It achieves competitive boundary detection including out-of-distribution tests on the MuPe-Diversidades dataset.

entry.title: CARVS: A Congestion-Aware Algorithm for Online Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery in Human-Collaborative Warehouses

author.name: Chaoran Li, Zeyuan Zhao, Shao Zhang

entry.summary: Formalizes MAPDwHC, an extension of multi-agent pickup-and-delivery incorporating human unpredictability such as dynamic obstacles from robot-human interactions, and presents CARVS, a congestion-aware online algorithm for warehouse settings. The work targets realistic human-robot collaboration constraints largely ignored by classical MAPD formulations.

entry.title: Pair-Aware Optimization: Coordinating Exploration and Refinement for Jailbreaking LLM Agents

author.name: Juanyang Xu, Zheng Wang, Xingyu Zhao, Siddartha Khastgir, Andi Zhang

entry.summary: This attack paper systematically studies combinations of zeroth-order and first-order optimization for jailbreaking LLM agents, proposing a ZO-FO framework that explores adversarial prefixes with ZO methods and refines suffixes with gradient-based FO methods, coordinated by pair-aware optimization. It aims to expose vulnerabilities in LLM agents facing adversarial inputs.

entry.title: World Models, Trees and Foundation Models for Retail Forecasting: Evidence from Four Public Data Sets

author.name: Karthik Iyer, Madan Dabbeeru

entry.summary: This paper compares forecasting models including a state-carrying world model, tree methods, and foundation models across four grains of the retail product-store-time hierarchy on four public datasets (M5, Dominick's, Breakfast at the Frat, Corporacion Favorita), using rolling origins with paired tests and model confidence sets. The central message is that the right forecasting model depends on the decision grain, from store orders to chain-level financial planning.

entry.title: DiaLong: Benchmarking Reminiscence in Long-Context Dialogues

author.name: Owen Bianchi, Samer Aslan, Ryunosuke Saito

entry.summary: DiaLong is a benchmark of 100 long human-created, LLM-augmented conversations with a fact-recall memory task: classify 40 candidate facts about a dialogue as true or false. It standardizes quantitative evaluation of how well LLMs retain and retrieve long-range factual information within dialogue contexts.

entry.title: Beyond Leaderboards: A Method for Application-Specific Capability Profiling of Large Language Models

author.name: Oleg Grynets, Vasyl Lyashkevych, Andrii Salyk, Dmytro Koziuberda, Dmytro Kostetskyi, Oleh Kaskun, Olena Pochernina, Alona Seletska, Oleksii Ilchuk, Viktoriia Tsymbal, Daryna Tukalo, Bohdan Saukh, Ivan Fedorchuk, Hryhorii Petrenko

entry.summary: Presents a methodology and containerized testbed for profiling LLM capabilities per application, treating each application (migration agents, chatbots, support automation) as an extension unit with its own dataset, evaluator, and dashboards. Measurements accumulate in a versioned metamodel to support model selection against application, architecture, and cost constraints.

entry.title: Behavioral Probes for Information Flow in LLM Swarms

author.name: Junhui Chen, Yu Zhang, Lantian Li, Dong Wang

entry.summary: This paper repurposes hallucination-analysis metrics (External Context Score and Parametric Knowledge Score) as behavioral probes to quantify information flow in LLM swarms, examining how nodes rely on external context versus parametric knowledge. It reveals consistent patterns linking context dependence to input relevance. It moves beyond utility-only views of multi-LLM systems.

entry.title: Physics-anchored residual quantum neural networks for cloud-cover parameterization

author.name: Zhuo Wang, Ce Yu, Bin Yang

entry.summary: This paper evaluates quantum neural networks for cloud-cover parameterization in climate models using an offline residual formulation, where the network learns a correction to a fitted classical estimate in logit space. Using ICON/DYAMOND-derived data, the authors compare ten model variants under a matched, controlled protocol with replicates. The work matters because it grounds speculative quantum ML claims in careful physics-informed benchmarking.

entry.title: Announced Breaks Separate Conformal Reliability from Frequency Calibration

author.name: Karl Li (Columbia University)

entry.summary: Analyzes announced distributional breaks and reset rules, distinguishing per-time conformal reliability from frequency calibration in adaptive forecasting. Shows a reset rule based on the post-boundary empirical quantile attains minimax per-time rates for independent scores, and derives frequency gap bounds for bounded scores, outperforming five adaptive methods in synthetic experiments. Single-author Columbia theory paper.

entry.title: DS-Net: A Dynamic Split Network for Edge-Cloud Collaborative Inference

author.name: Xinyun Zhang, Li Wang, Lei Jin, Lianming Xu, Zhu Han

entry.summary: Proposes DS-Net, which enables flexible switching among multiple split points within one network for edge-cloud collaborative inference, avoiding the need to load separate models per split point. This reduces switching time and edge storage overhead while improving speed and accuracy across changing communication and device conditions. Addresses practical deployment constraints in edge intelligence.

entry.title: Power-Law Correlations Without Apparent Temperature-Tuned Criticality in Fixed-Tree Hierarchical Languages

author.name: Marcel K\"uhn, Bernd Rosenow

entry.summary: This paper studies whether temperature-induced changes in long-range correlations of autoregressive generation reflect genuine phase transitions or smooth statistical shifts. Using a controlled analogue: a finite-depth probabilistic context-free grammar on a fixed tree with belief-propagation-computed conditionals rescaled by softmax temperature, the authors find mutual information between tokens follows a power-law envelope across temperatures. This suggests apparent criticality-like behavior can arise without temperature-tuned phase transitions.

entry.title: Paired-Outcome Learning for Selective Spacecraft Attitude Capture under Torque Limits

author.name: Donghe Chen, Jia Deng, Zehao Jia, Lin Cheng, Shengping Gong

entry.summary: This paper develops a paired-outcome learning method for torque-limited spacecraft attitude capture, learning when to selectively modify a baseline controller's maneuver speed based on uncertain braking authority. It combines interpretable continuation policies, separate prediction of task failure and tracking gains, and context-dependent rejection that falls back to the baseline, with calibration separated by context and Basilisk simulation experiments. This is a careful application of baseline-relative learning to a high-stakes aerospace control problem.

entry.title: EasyResearch: Honest Regression, Forecasting and Signal Classification for Researchers Who Do Not Program

author.name: Ahmad B. A. Hassanat, Ghada A. Altarawneh

entry.summary: EasyResearch extends the EasyClassifier idea to regression, time-series forecasting, and signal classification, providing open-source analysis cores plus a Windows desktop app requiring no programming. All tasks enforce honest evaluation: everything learned from data is learned on training data only, published defaults with fixed seeds, and separate final evaluation of the selected model. This aims to reduce methodological errors by non-programmer researchers.

entry.title: Simulating Infant Senses with Age-Tuned Networks

author.name: Somesh Mohapatra

entry.summary: This paper consolidates developmental psychology measurements of infant vision, hearing, and touch across the first two years of life into age-indexed input filters paired with small prediction networks, producing an inspectable simulation of sensory perception by age. The filters reproduce the known maturation order of the senses by construction, while the networks capture nonlinear deficits such as newborns extracting far less than their sensory input permits. This bridges cognitive science measurements with computational modeling.

entry.title: Stochastic Tracking of Drifting Affine Fixed Points

author.name: Sajad Khodadadian

entry.summary: This paper analyzes linear stochastic approximation with time-varying affine operators, where fixed points drift over time and noise may be correlated. It derives bounds on cumulative squared tracking error for constant-stepsize updates and matching lower bounds for scalar Gaussian models showing constant stepsizes are near-optimal for tracking.

entry.title: Scenario Generalization and Sector Transfer in Real Surface Irrigation Surrogate Modelling with Tabular Models

author.name: Alessandro Cagiano, M. Aybars Seyhan, Fabiola Gangi, Matteo Zignani, Daniele Masseroni

entry.summary: This applied study evaluates tabular surrogates (gradient boosting, neural tabular models, AutoML, tabular foundation models) for replacing expensive shallow-water simulations in surface irrigation planning. It assesses same-sector scenario generalization versus sector-out transfer using drone-derived field morphology and hydrological descriptors.

entry.title: Nested Shared-Operator Recursion on ARC-AGI-1: An Empirical Study of HRM, TRM and URM

author.name: Sara Neri, Eugenio Gaeta, Andrea Ceschini, Andrea Facchinetti, Giuseppe Fico

entry.summary: The paper empirically tests whether adding a persistent intermediate state that integrates repeated updates of a faster state, applied uniformly to HRM, TRM, and URM recursive reasoning architectures, improves performance on ARC-AGI-1 at matched parameter counts. The results are evaluated on held-out queries using the official codebases.

entry.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Maria-Eleni Sfyraki, Jun-Kun Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets that mix ground-truth labels with potentially noisy labels produced by an ML predictor. This targets the practical scenario where human annotation is too expensive for large datasets. The work provides convergence-oriented algorithms for a realistic weak-supervision setting.

entry.title: VERDICT: Visual Extraction-Result Decoder with Integrated Confidence and Traceable Evidence

author.name: Harikrishnan P M, Goutham Vignesh, Siva Prasad, Zishan Ahmad, Mahesh Basveshwar Deshmukhe, Varun V, Rohit Agrawal, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: VERDICT is a plug-in framework that attaches to existing document field extractors, using a small vision-language model to localize grounding evidence per document and calibrate confidence in both values and their evidence. It leaves the base extractor untouched while adding traceability. This addresses enterprise needs for auditable, trustworthy structured extraction from documents.

entry.title: Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems

author.name: Davood Damircheli

entry.summary: Derives guaranteed a posteriori error bounds for neural network approximations of parabolic obstacle problems, bounding flux and energy errors of the feasible projection via constitutive residual, initial mismatch, complementarity defect, and PDE residual. The result extends the Apushkinskaya-Repin majorant for the heat operator to general coefficients, free multipliers, and a flux bound.

entry.title: Scalable and Adaptive Distribution Regression via Random Features

author.name: Yinsong Wang, Xiao Liu, Yu Ding

entry.summary: The paper develops Random Feature Distribution Regression with finite-sample guarantees under two-stage sampling, using perturbation analysis to separate distribution-level sampling, finite within-bag sampling, and random feature approximation errors. It establishes sufficient feature-budget conditions for convergence and enables adaptive, scalable alternatives to kernel-based distribution regression. This unifies kernel methods, multi-instance learning, and set-valued learning settings.

entry.title: Normalizing Flow for Neural-Enhanced Track-Before-Detect

author.name: Shaoxiu Wei, Bhaskar Rao, Florian Meyer

entry.summary: The authors propose a neural-enhanced track-before-detect framework for multiobject tracking that operates directly on complex-valued raw signals, using an environment-dependent latent intensity variable represented by a normalizing flow. The flow density is trained online and unsupervised within a sequential Bayesian inference procedure, enabling adaptation to unmodeled propagation effects in radar, sonar, and 6G sensing applications.

entry.title: RAIL-5G: A Challenging Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for AI-Based 5G Indoor Localization

author.name: Jonas Pirkl, Andreas Eidloth, Maximilian Kasparek, Tobias Feigl, Christopher Mutschler

entry.summary: RAIL-5G is a public real-world 5G channel impulse response benchmark recorded in an operational railway maintenance facility, covering an 811 square meter indoor area with distributed radio units, robot-mounted receiver trajectories, and high-accuracy reference positions under severe multipath and non-line-of-sight conditions. It enables rigorous evaluation of how geometric, unsupervised, and semi-supervised localization methods generalize to realistic industrial settings.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Gated SHAP-Dirichlet Refinement for MRI-Based Depression Classification

author.name: Phuc Truong Loc Nguyen, Nguyen Truong Toan To, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Hoang-Loc Cao, Hung Cao

entry.summary: This work introduces a post-hoc reliability layer for MRI-based major depressive disorder classification that retrieves similar SHAP explanations, constructs Dirichlet class evidence, and selectively refines uncertain predictions while deferring unreliable cases to experts. Evaluated on 504 SRPBS subjects with five classifiers under nested cross-validation, refinement consistently improved accuracy without retraining.

entry.title: FLMNet: Self-Ensemble Distillation from Masks to Seeds for Single-Tower CTR Prediction

author.name: Yifan Wang, Yifei Du

entry.summary: The paper explains why self-distillation helps recent CTR models like FinalNet and QNN, proving that as the number of dropout patterns grows the objective reduces exactly to label loss on logit-averaged prediction plus a disagreement penalty among dropout copies. It builds on this analysis to design FLMNet, a single-tower architecture with self-ensemble distillation that removes the need for random sampling.

entry.title: R2-GP: Variance-Calibrated Priors for Additive Gaussian Processes

author.name: Javier Enrique Aguilar, Soham Mukherjee, David Kohns

entry.summary: R2-GP introduces an R2D2-type prior for Gaussian process additive models that directly calibrates each component's contribution to explained variance under Matern kernels. By rescaling components by length scale and inputs, it avoids variance overestimation that plagues independent amplitude priors, especially in high dimensions.

entry.title: Translating in style: An open-weight alternative to GPT-4 for culturally aligned machine translation

author.name: Thomas Rietman, Hadi Mohammadi, Robert A. Bagheri

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether the open-weight Hunyuan-MT-7B translation model, in base, LoRA fine-tuned, and GRPO-steered variants, can replace closed GPT-4 in the RASTA retrieval-augmented stylistic alignment framework across formality, politeness, and intimacy in twelve language pairs. It targets the systematic flattening of style in translation into non-Western languages.

entry.title: Inside the Scorer: Mechanistic Evidence on Rubric Control in LLM-Based Automated Essay Scoring from 25 Base Models

author.name: Chungche Huang, Po-Ya Angela Wang, Shu-Kai Hsieh

entry.summary: Probes and steers 25 open-weight LLMs (0.13B-10.31B parameters, 14 families) to determine whether essay-scoring rubrics form distinct, independently controllable internal representations on human-scored English writing data. Holistic scores are decodable from activations for longer tasks, and rubric representations are partly separable, enabling steering.

entry.title: Rethinking BPE: Merge Selection as Model Selection

author.name: Vijini Liyanage, Fran\c{c}ois Yvon

entry.summary: Reframes choosing the BPE merge budget as a statistical model selection problem and derives information-theoretic criteria for computing optimal merge sets directly from corpus statistics. It further augments BPE training corpora with synthetic texts to improve merge selection under limited data, targeting compact yet effective token inventories.

entry.title: Expert L2 English Speech Evaluation on a Gaming PC: Accuracy, Fluency, and Prosody with XLS-R, XEUS, and PhoneticXeus

author.name: Richard Rose (Hankuk University of Foreign Studies)

entry.summary: Presents oollim, a locally executable system for evaluating L2 English pronunciation accuracy, fluency, and prosody using pretrained speech representations and ridge regressions on consumer hardware. It outperforms archived Azure API scores on 305 expert-rated recordings across all three constructs.

entry.title: Path-Conditioned Attention Mobility: From Depth to Execution Hubs in SegFormer

author.name: Aleksandr Druzhinin

entry.summary: This single-author study examines whether attention heads in hierarchical vision transformers are locally mobile across depth, finding that task-relevant heads in SegFormer-B5 can be relocated to nearby depths only when computational context, including normalization and spatial-reduction preprocessing, is jointly adapted. The technique is applied toward transformer compression.

entry.title: Automatic Cause Determination in Road Scene Understanding Using Qualitative Reasoning and Four-Valued Logic

author.name: Nassim Belmecheri, Arnaud Gotlieb, Nadjib Lazaar, Helge Spieker

entry.summary: The paper presents a method for automatic cause determination in road scenes from video, identifying relevant actors and the causes of ego-car actions using qualitative reasoning and four-valued logic to handle multiple, contradictory causes in complex urban environments. The approach supports explainability and acceptance in automated driving by providing explicit causal explanations.

entry.title: CRISP: Progressive Illumination Curriculum for Recurrent Low-Light Video Enhancement with Semantic Priors

author.name: Ruirui Lin, Xin Yan Lim, Yini Li, Zhiming Liu, Nantheera Anantrasirichai

entry.summary: CRISP is a recurrent two-frame framework for low-light video enhancement that propagates temporal context across frames and uses a progressive illumination curriculum during training, transitioning supervision from interpolated targets to full references. Semantic priors help preserve structure while balancing brightness, color, and temporal coherence recovery.

entry.title: Sufficient Frame Subsets for Video Understanding

author.name: Lahiru Wijayasingha

entry.summary: Introduces Sufficient Frame Subsets: compact frame sets that, when all other frames are masked, each independently preserve a video model's prediction, addressing the tendency of attribution methods to spread evidence across near-duplicate frames. Evaluated on UCF101 and Something-Something v2 across CNN and transformer architectures, finding that models relying on more sufficient subsets behave differently.

entry.title: MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes

author.name: Yifei Wang, Wei Tian, Wenhua Bao, Jia Zhou, Hanshi Wang, Fudong Ge, Jianhua Wu, Shuai Yuan, Zhipeng Zhang, Xingliang Liu, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Bingzhao Gao

entry.summary: Addresses cross-camera photometric inconsistency and unreliable geometric supervision in feed-forward Gaussian splatting for driving scenes, constructing a canonical appearance space from depth-guided correspondences and using a Bilateral Grid Transformer for multi-scale appearance restoration.

entry.title: DiffGround: Semantic Difference-Guided Zero-Shot Video Question Grounding

author.name: Cheng-Han Lee, Amir Salimi, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Che-Chun Su, Min Sun, Cheng-Hao Kuo

entry.summary: DiffGround is a zero-shot framework for Video Question Grounding built on frozen multimodal LLMs, using a predicted action cue to convert reasoning-oriented questions into action-centric retrieval targets. A VLM then selects informative temporal segments, avoiding costly supervised temporal annotations.

entry.title: Do We Need Learned Targets? Classical Gradients as Supervision for 2D Gaussian Initialization

author.name: Kyungjune Baek

entry.summary: This paper shows that costly per-image optimization targets used by learning-based Gaussian image initializers can be replaced with classical image gradients (normalized Sobel maps). It presents a training-free analytic initializer producing parameters in about 0.32 seconds and a neural initializer trained with online Sobel supervision that scales to 10,000 images, both achieving competitive reconstruction quality on Kodak and DIV2K.

entry.title: Toolkit for Facial Deidentification

author.name: Esteban Leiva-Montenegro, Matthieu Pillot, Manfred Gonzalez-Hernandez, Vitomir Struc, Peter Peer, Bla\v{z} Meden

entry.summary: An open-source toolkit providing a complete evaluation pipeline for face deidentification techniques, covering preprocessing, deidentification, and assessment across data utility, image quality, and identity-protection metrics on multiple datasets. It aims to standardize benchmarking of privacy-enhancing facial biometrics methods.

entry.title: TIM: Temporal Decoupling with Iterative Mutual-Refinement Model for Longitudinal Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Yiheng Dong, Yi Lin, Shilong Huang, Xiyan Yang, Xin Yang

entry.summary: TIM is a two-stage framework for longitudinal radiology report generation that decouples spatial pathology from temporal progression and uses iterative mutual refinement, avoiding the semantic blur from merging multi-timepoint images in one representation space. It addresses an underexplored but clinically important temporal dimension of report generation.

entry.title: Long-form Video-to-Text Summarization using Recursive Language Models

author.name: Alessia Intini, Lorenzo Vaiani, Enrico Chen, Luca Cagliero

entry.summary: RVLSM recursively decomposes long videos into semantically coherent segments and delegates chunk-level reasoning to VideoLLM sub-models and external tools, using Semantic Temporal Decomposition to preserve temporal continuity. It targets long-form video summarization where VideoLLMs degrade due to long-context prompts. First recursive approach tailored to video-to-text summarization.

entry.title: From Short Clips to Real-Time Streams: Identity-Aware Supervision and Context-Efficient Generation for Video Face Swapping

author.name: Zekai Luo, Yuwei Liang, Ruiqi Ma, Haoyu Huang, Xuehao Wang, Huanyi Zheng, Mingyu Liu, Linhao Zhong, Chenchen Jing, Yuling Xi, Hao Chen

entry.summary: This work improves reference-guided video face swapping by introducing Joint Rec-ID Loss balancing identity supervision and latent reconstruction by noise level, plus context-efficient generation enabling real-time streaming from short training clips. It targets faithful identity transfer, fidelity, and real-time long-video performance simultaneously. Face swapping advances here also raise dual-use deepfake considerations.

entry.title: Flow Matching-Based Semantic Communication With Time-Aware Structural Residual Injection

author.name: Chengyang Liang, Dong Li

entry.summary: This letter proposes a dual-information-flow semantic communication framework based on flow matching, transmitting a matched text prompt plus an ultra-low-dimensional structural residual velocity vector extracted from the inversion trajectory of the original image. At the receiver, a Time-Aware Recursive Residual Injection network progressively restores structure during generation. The approach reduces bandwidth while improving structural fidelity over text-only semantic communication.

entry.title: LUMINR: Intensity-conditioned Meta-learned INRs for Accelerated Medical Image Registration

author.name: Damian Rynczak, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: LUMINR accelerates implicit-neural-representation-based deformable image registration by meta-learning an initialization and conditioning the INR locally per coordinate via intensity features rather than globally. This speeds per-pair fitting at test time while allowing the deformation field to vary across the domain. It targets faster registration for clinical image analysis workflows.

entry.title: Adaptive Question Generation for Ambiguous Robot Instructions Based on Information Gain and Human Cognitive Characteristics

author.name: Ryo Terashima, Yuga Yano, Hakaru Tamukoh

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive question-generation mechanism for service robots facing ambiguous natural-language instructions, balancing probabilistic discrimination efficiency with the user's ease of response. By accounting for human cognitive characteristics, the robot reduces incorrect or uncertain answers and extra clarification turns. It improves practical human-robot dialogue efficiency.

entry.title: Rollbot 2: Agile Locomotion by a Single-Actuator Spherical Robot

author.name: Jingxian Wang*, Chen Yu*, Sam Kriegman, Michael Rubenstein

entry.summary: Rollbot 2 improves on the original single-actuator spherical robot with a redesigned mass distribution enabling near-straight rolling, plus onboard inertial and ultra-wideband sensing for learned steering, beacon seeking, and waypoint following using only one motor-velocity command. It demonstrates autonomous beacon approach without motion capture and completes a 468 m indoor route at 0.87 m/s.

entry.title: SkateNav: Learning Energy-Efficient Navigation through Adaptive Skating on Passive-Wheel Quadrupedal Robots

author.name: Jeil Jeong, Taeyun Kim, Sangjin Kim, Jinyoung Choi, Sung-Eui Yoon

entry.summary: SkateNav is an RL framework for energy-efficient skating navigation on passive-wheel quadrupeds, using a time-budgeted goal-reaching objective so the policy learns steering, propulsion, and gliding timing jointly. An adaptive skating cycle with per-step frequency modulation structures push-glide-recovery phases.

entry.title: Finite-Time Capture by a Dubins Pursuer Against Unknown Evader Strategies

author.name: Dinesh Patra, Bhargav Jha, Ashish R. Hota

entry.summary: This theoretical work considers planar pursuit-evasion where a Dubins (car-like) pursuer captures a slower evader that can change heading instantaneously. The authors derive a turn-rate feedback law with an explicit gain interval guaranteeing finite-time capture against any admissible evader strategy, plus explicit capture-time bounds and a speed ceiling computable from pursuer parameters alone.

entry.title: How is "prosaic aligned AI" supposed to work?

author.name: MichaelDickens

entry.summary: The author examines the prosaic vision of aligned AI — superintelligence that keeps society recognizable while boosting growth and ending scarcity — and argues that thinking it through surfaces major unresolved issues, such as how a single ASI design handles conflicting requests from rival governments. The post probes whether the Star Trek-style outcome that AI companies publicly endorse is actually coherent.

entry.title: RoboMMT: Learning Stable Tracking of Modulated Expressive and Interactive Robot Motion

author.name: Till Hielscher, Kai O. Arras

entry.summary: RoboMMT is a modular control architecture coupling parameterized expressive motion synthesis with physics-based character control and reactive adaptation, training a reference-conditioned tracking policy across a broad expressivity domain. This lets unstable platforms execute expressive, socially meaningful motion without being pushed to instability.

entry.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache

author.name: Syed Usama Khalid Bukhari, Syed Safwan Khalid, Muhammad Aamir

entry.summary: System X extends an LLM-as-Judge-style decision model with a text-reply option: when the reply option wins or confidence is low, the same model continues generation from the decision's KV cache, avoiding repeated prompt prefill. Built on LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B, it preserves decision accuracy while reducing expected calibration error from 0.292 to 0.169 and saving 15-37% latency via cache reuse on an Apple M4 Pro.

entry.title: The Forward/Inverse Duality of Controlled Emergence:A Computational Design Program from Explanation to Engineering

author.name: Hao Li, Minghui Ren, Shaowen Lu

entry.summary: This position-style paper proposes a unified research program for controlled emergence in systems of many simple interacting units, restating the tension between adaptability and control as dual problems: a forward problem explaining macroscopic behavior from local rules and an inverse problem solving for controllable rules and readout mechanisms. It formalizes the shared object as an augmented quintuple and decomposes engineering into steps connecting explanation to design. The program aims to give designers formal tools for managing emergent behavior.

entry.title: Benefit-Targeted Routing and Bounded Revision for LLM-Based Evidence Screening in Manufacturing Supplier Discovery

author.name: Yijiashun Qi, Hanzhe Guo, Yuxuan Li

entry.summary: This paper studies when to allocate additional LLM judgments in an evidence-review system for manufacturing supplier discovery, proposing benefit-targeted routing that learns recovered agreement minus newly introduced disagreement. Notably, on independently double-annotated fresh cases without retraining, the advantage over a logistic-risk router becomes inconclusive, an unusually honest negative-flavored result.

entry.title: A Generic On-Board AI Processing Chain for Earth Observation: From Application Development to Embedded Deployment and Mission-Level Orchestration

author.name: Michel-Fran{\c c}ois Foulon (TAS), Liz Ramos Medina (TAS), Thomas Goudemant (TAS), Clotilde Szywala (TAS), Virgile Robles (TAS), Cl{\'e}ment Petitjean (TAS), Ad{\`e}le Hankache (TAS), Omar Hlimi

entry.summary: The paper presents a complete on-board AI processing chain for Earth observation satellites that downlink compact products like segmentation masks instead of full scenes. It covers model tuning, int8 quantization, and deployment on an AMD Versal VCK190 with preserved segmentation performance, demonstrated via wildfire segmentation alongside ship detection and cloud segmentation, plus mission-level orchestration.

entry.title: Answer Delivery Under a Shared Token Budget: An Audited Study of Stopping and Finalization

author.name: Yupeng Chang, Linyuan Gao, Zhiyuan Li, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: This study examines a fixed-budget inference policy combining first-valid-box stopping with a charged finalization cue, evaluated on independently audited GSM8K test sets per model. It improves delivered endpoint accuracy by 8.0 and 7.0 percentage points for two reasoning models over first-box stopping, with a prelocked repeat confirming gains and ablations separating stopping from cue recovery and extraction effects.

entry.title: SECURE-AI: Multi-Signal Uncertainty Quantification for Trustworthy Acoustic Cough Detection

author.name: Sejal Solkhan, Feiya Xiang, Mayur Sanap, Geet Khatri, Edgar Lobaton

entry.summary: SECURE-AI wraps a frozen MobileNetV3 cough classifier with multi-signal uncertainty quantification combining Monte Carlo Dropout, Temperature Scaling, and Mahalanobis distance in embedding space to flag when predictions should not be trusted. On held-out Coswara recordings it evaluates which uncertainty signals best detect confident misclassifications under distribution shift.

entry.title: Graph-Regularized Synthetic Control for Stable Counterfactual Estimation under Donor Redundancy

author.name: Yanlin Zhang, Sungyong Chung, Alireza Talebpour

entry.summary: Graph-SC augments synthetic control estimation with a graph Laplacian penalty over donor-similarity structure to stabilize donor weights when the donor pool is large, highly correlated, and short in pre-treatment history. The paper provides theory on bias-variance trade-offs alongside the convex estimator.

entry.title: lepidoptera: A Domain-Agnostic Engine for Causal Simulation with Mixed Variable Types, Vine Copula Dependence, and Individual-Level Counterfactual Propagation

author.name: Danilo Augusto Sarti

entry.summary: lepidoptera is an open-source R/Python package for simulating data from structural causal models with heterogeneous variable types, using a typed mechanism architecture that separates causal graphs from node-level generating rules. It includes a pre-built mechanism library covering all nine continuous/categorical/ordinal parent-child combinations, vine copula dependence estimation, and individual-level counterfactual propagation. It is useful infrastructure for causal inference benchmarking and evaluation.

entry.title: ASR Personalization in Pathological Voice: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Duration Effects

author.name: Giuseppe Giaimis, Sergei Katkov, Muhammad Azfar Yaqub, Antonio Liotta

entry.summary: A component-level study of LoRA adaptation in Whisper for single-speaker pathological speech, examining how adapter placement interacts with model size, training efficiency, and utterance duration. Findings include that scaling reduces but does not eliminate speaker mismatch, and full-attention LoRA provides the best accuracy and time-accuracy trade-off, with gains varying by utterance length.

entry.title: RAFT: Redundancy-Aware Input Filtering for Temporal Graph Neural Network Training

author.name: Yue Dai, Sarah Zhou, Youtao Zhang

entry.summary: RAFT analyzes whether all events in temporal graph neural network training are necessary, distinguishing events needed as prediction targets from those needed as historical context, and filters redundant events and their dependency-induced serialization constraints. This improves training throughput for dynamic graph learning as interaction volumes grow.

entry.title: MT-CC: Multi-Group Temperature Scaling for Asymmetric Calibration Behavior in Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Sungjun Yun, Yonghee Choi, Dong-Jun Han

entry.summary: Introduces MT-CC, a post-hoc multi-group temperature scaling method that addresses asymmetric calibration in class-incremental learning, where confidence changes do not track accuracy changes across groups. It extends static temperature scaling, which has rarely been examined in continual settings, to evolving data distributions.

entry.title: How Robust Are Prognostic Radiomic Features? Comparing Selection Techniques on Pooled Glioblastoma Cohorts

author.name: Yannick Sodonougbo, Marlene Schnieders, Alexia Rizoudis, Santiago Cepeda, Frank Kramer, Dominik M\"uller
