entry.summary: This study compares three feature-selection techniques (log-rank test, univariate Cox regression, XGBoost with SHAP) over 463 radiomic, anatomical, and clinical features across 705 IDH-wildtype glioblastoma patients from three public cohorts. Only five features were selected by all methods, revealing substantial method-driven heterogeneity in radiomic prognostic literature. It is a caution about reproducibility in medical AI biomarker research.

entry.title: Data-Driven Resource Aggregation for Scalable Digital Twin and Simulation Model Generation

author.name: Yucheng Wu, Alp Akcay

entry.summary: The paper proposes automatically selecting and aggregating resources to simplify simulation models built from production event logs for digital twins of manufacturing systems, using ideas from inverse reinforcement learning to learn behavioral value representations. This addresses the growing complexity of maintaining digital twins under frequent system reconfiguration.

entry.title: Transport What Shares the Conduction Pathway: Normal-Anchored SPD Geometric Transport for Source-Free Patient Adaptation of Holter and Patch ECG

author.name: JinKook Kim

entry.summary: This work addresses ECG beat classifier degradation on new patients and devices with a source-free adaptation method, Normal-Anchored Geometric Transport (NAGT). It exploits the fact that label-free recordings are overwhelmingly normal beats, estimating a closed-form SPD congruence map from normal anchors in the first five minutes and applying it selectively to normal and supraventricular prototypes only. Evaluation spans multiple ECG databases including Holter and patch recordings.

entry.title: VBO-MI: A Differentiable Black-Box Optimization Framework via Variational Mutual Information Estimation

author.name: Farhad Mirkarimi

entry.summary: VBO-MI is a fully gradient-based Bayesian optimization framework that avoids Gaussian-process scalability limits and expensive posterior sampling by using variational mutual information estimation. It requires no assumptions on a Gaussian prior or a specific variational posterior family and trains internal action and information-estimation components via gradient updates. This targets expensive noisy black-box optimization in high dimensions.

entry.title: Theory-Guided Instance-Dependent Early Stopping via Second-Order Loss Dynamics

author.name: Ahad Bin Islam Shoeb, Jamal Uddin Tanvin, Kamrul Hasan, Alve Reduan, Imtiaz Ahmed

entry.summary: TG-IES provides theoretical justification for instance-dependent early stopping, which skips backpropagation for examples whose losses have stabilized. The authors analyze the second-order loss-difference criterion, deriving a noise-calibrated mastery threshold and conditional stability bounds, and show second-order differencing has favorable bias-variance trade-off in a specific signal-to-noise regime. This turns an empirical efficiency heuristic into a principled method.

entry.title: Process-Aware Event Log Augmentation for Process Prediction under Labeled Data Scarcity

author.name: Sjoerd van Straten, Alessandro Padella, Marwan Hassani

entry.summary: SiamSA-PPM is a self-supervised framework for predictive process monitoring combining Siamese learning with statistically grounded data augmentation that leverages control-flow semantics to generate realistic trace variants. This addresses labeled-data scarcity and low variability in real-world event logs, evaluated with exhaustive tuning across logs of wide variability. The approach enables generalizable prefix representations without labels.

entry.title: A discrete-continuous-time stochastic framework for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptom modeling and pharmacological intervention via methylphenidate

author.name: Oana-Maria-Catalina Crisan

entry.summary: The paper formalizes ADHD neural dynamics as stochastic processes converging toward stable dysfunctional trajectories, with methylphenidate treatment modeled as an external control signal that redirects trajectories toward neurotypical regimes. Latent representations are inferred from empirical clinical data via a novel deterministic hybrid approach, bridging optimal-control theory with clinical modeling. The aim is a mathematical framework for evaluating pharmacological intervention efficacy.

entry.title: Semi-supervised learning on singular data sets

author.name: Guillaume Valette

entry.summary: This theoretical work models singular data clouds using subanalytic sets and develops a semi-supervised learning approach based on a Morrey-type embedding of Sobolev spaces relative to measures with singular support. The authors provide a greedy algorithm using Monte Carlo approximation of Sobolev norms and demonstrate it on point clouds from real algebraic varieties and downsampled MNIST. It extends the mathematical foundations of semi-supervised learning to genuinely singular supports.

entry.title: Evidence Sufficiency and Model Comparisons in MexRegQA: An Item-Level Audit of Mexican-Spanish Regulatory QA

author.name: Fred Hu (Huawei Technologies de M\'exico, Mexico), Yeqi Wang (Huawei Technologies de M\'exico, Mexico), Xing Zhou (Northeastern University, USA)

entry.summary: This audit of Mexican-Spanish financial-regulatory QA shows that 35 of 135 similarity-covered items lack load-bearing facts, and that removing evidence-defective items changes significance conclusions in 14 of 55 pairwise model comparisons. It highlights that retrieval coverage does not imply evidence sufficiency and that model comparisons can be artifacts of defective items.

entry.title: Optimal Multi-Kernel Combination for Online Multi-Label Classification

author.name: Tingting Zhai, Wei Liu, Renjian Yu

entry.summary: The paper introduces an online multi-kernel combination method for large-scale multi-label classification, addressing the limits of single preselected kernels and the kernel-selection curse of prior methods like OKS-OMC. It aims to exploit complementary information across multiple kernels in streaming settings.

entry.title: Two hidden layer suffice: the caterpillar net

author.name: Jakob Paul Zimmermann

entry.summary: This theory paper gives a nonrecursive construction, the Caterpillar Net, showing the maximum of N inputs can be represented by ReLU networks with two hidden layers, with widths O(N^2) and 2^{O(N log N)}, building on recent work proving two hidden layers suffice for CPWL functions. It carries direct geometric interpretation. This resolves questions in the expressivity theory of deep networks regarding depth for maxima computation.

entry.title: Learning to Refer: Inference-Time Collaboration in Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Yuheng Ma, Chendi Wang, Qiong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates inference-time collaboration in decentralized federated learning as budgeted local expert referral, where queries move only between neighboring clients and only visited clients contribute predictions. EdgeDRM learns density-based routing potentials per client to select referrals while aggregating local model predictions along the route. This exploits heterogeneous client expertise without global coordination.

entry.title: InJePA: Intention-First Latent Planning with Coupled JEPA World Models for Visual Navigation

author.name: Siming Zhou, Bowen Ma, Ruiran Du, Pengcheng Zheng, Sheng Zheng, Dongshen Han, Zhijie Li, Wei Dong, Fan Mo, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: InJePA proposes an intention-first planning paradigm for visual navigation in which a goal-conditioned JEPA proposes latent intentions and an action-conditioned JEPA predicts future latent states, sharing a latent space so predicted consequences guide stepwise intention construction. This inverts typical propose-then-evaluate world-model pipelines. It targets more efficient goal-directed planning directly in latent space.

entry.title: Candidate-dependent residual routing trades top-of-list accuracy for recall in sequential recommendation

author.name: Han Chen, Yingrui Li

entry.summary: Tests candidate-dependent routing in sequential recommenders with carefully controlled paired-seed experiments on the REES46 dataset, finding that average NDCG@10 is essentially unchanged while two opposing effects cancel: candidate-dependent routing trades top-of-list accuracy for recall. The paper is a model of careful ablation and honest reporting of null/negative results.

entry.title: Prototype-Guided Optimization of Quantum Data Embeddings with Linear Cost

author.name: Seokhoon Jeong, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: Proposes a prototype-guided framework for data-adaptive quantum data embeddings that replaces O(B^2) pairwise fidelity evaluations with an O(B) prototype-based objective using class-prototype separation and compactness, including a measurable lower certificate for class distinguishability. This removes a key computational bottleneck in iterative embedding optimization for quantum machine learning.

entry.title: LastWords: Boring Problems Revisited

author.name: Huayang Li, Richard Sproat

entry.summary: Revisiting a 2022 Computational Linguistics Last Words piece on deceptively simple NLP problems like number name reading in text normalization, the authors document that recent frontier models have essentially solved this subproblem. The paper reflects on which classical hard-but-boring problems the LLM era has resolved and what this implies about the nature of remaining linguistic challenges. It offers a valuable longitudinal perspective on LLM capabilities.

entry.title: DF-PALM: Dynamic Fusion Prompt Learning for Audio--Language Models

author.name: Yulin Sun, Shenghua Li, Yong Dou, Xinwang Liu, Cheng Yang, Kele Xu

entry.summary: DF-PALM improves few-shot audio classification with audio-language models by conditioning class representations on the input audio after text encoding and using asymmetric cross-attention for audio refinement, while keeping pretrained encoders frozen. It fixes PALM's limitation of input-independent class representations and lack of class-conditioned refinement. This targets better acoustic event discrimination from limited labeled data.

entry.title: An Information-Geometric Framework for OCS-Reconfigurable Interconnect Topology in Large-Scale AI Clusters

author.name: Shintaro Yoshizawa

entry.summary: This paper provides a unified information-geometric framework for designing programmable wiring topologies in AI datacenter clusters using optical circuit switches. It models wiring as a point in a probability simplex, measures departure from a symmetric Fat-Tree prior via KL divergence, and proves well-posedness and adaptation bounds for a free-energy objective whose gradient is computed via forward-backward recursion.

entry.title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement

author.name: Reza T Batley, Sourav Saha

entry.summary: This work presents a two-scale topology optimization framework for printable bone scaffolds in which a conditional rectified flow generates periodic lattice microstructures that are then refined in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities. On a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all refinements yield printable cells with under 1% error across six prescribed moduli, jointly optimizing geometry and spatial assignment under mechanical constraints.

entry.title: Physics-Driven Framework for QoS-Constrained Satellite System with Non-Linear PA Distortion

author.name: Hamza Ahmed Qureshi, Abuzar Babikir Mohammad Adam, Vu Nguyen Ha, Konstantinos Ntontin, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: The paper develops a self-supervised graph learning framework that jointly designs distortion-aware precoders and admission control for a downlink MISO satellite system under nonlinear power amplifier distortion, minimizing PA power subject to QoS constraints. It uses a GNN optimized end-to-end self-supervised via a differentiable Ito-Hermite model, avoiding expensive optimizer-generated labels.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books

author.name: Skander Lejmi

entry.summary: A single-author study trains cooperative multi-agent RL market makers on Polymarket, reconstructing order-level LOBSTER-format data from thin prediction-market order books and simulating training on 417 real markets in JaxMARL-HFT. It addresses adverse selection, delayed feedback, and data sparsity challenges specific to prediction markets.

entry.title: BanglaBBQ: A Bias Benchmark for Question Answering in the Bangladeshi Context

author.name: Sumit Anthony Gomes, Yasin Rahman, Taeeba Tasnia, Faiza Nooren Suhita

entry.summary: Adapts the BBQ bias benchmark to the Bangladeshi context in both Bangla and English, classifying original templates as directly translated, context-modified, or removed, and adding five newly authored categories reflecting local stereotypes such as marital status and regional origin. The result is 140 templates spanning eleven categories for evaluating social bias in QA.

entry.title: Behave Like Experts: Fusing Data with Semantic Knowledge for Effective and Efficient Semantic Map Construction

author.name: Zhu Liu, Zhen Hu, Yuxuan Liu, Ying Liu

entry.summary: The paper fuses distributional semantic knowledge from language model internal representations into a top-down algorithm for constructing semantic map models, which capture cross-lingual form-meaning mappings. This expert-like guidance re-sorts candidates in a huge graph search space, improving both accuracy and efficiency over purely data-driven methods.

entry.title: Reading Time Modeling with Pixel-Based Language Models

author.name: Junlin Li, Sara Alhajeri, Tatsuki Kuribayashi

entry.summary: Integrates tokenization-free pixel-based language models into computational psycholinguistics, using them to estimate next-word predictability for modeling naturalistic human reading times. Pixel-based models avoid tokenizer-induced bias in surprisal estimates and can incorporate bottom-up visual orthographic features normally excluded from token-based approaches.

entry.title: Training Negatives Still Matter After Calibrating Answerability Readouts

author.name: Jinchen Zhang, Zheyuan Liu, Yihan Zhu, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: Presents a controlled study comparing native training, which retains negative passages, against empty training, which removes them, for calibrated answerability readouts in open-book QA. Native-trained readouts achieve lower Brier loss and better downstream answer retention on SQuAD 2.0 and RepLiQA across two model families.

entry.title: BERT Is Already a Denoiser: Cheaply Unlocking Iterative Generation in Masked Language Models

author.name: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez

entry.summary: Tests whether frozen MLMs like BERT can perform conditional generation via iterative masked-token prediction with confidence-based commitment, without diffusion training. Frozen BERT shows substantial denoising capability but generation quality collapses with heavy corruption and task-directed generation remains very weak.

entry.title: Unifying Amplitude-Phase Coupling and Reliable Endogenous Priors for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Tongshun Zhang, Zixuan Zhong, Pingping Liu, Jin Kuang, Yubing Lu, Dong Liu, Qiuzhan Zhou

entry.summary: This paper proposes a frequency-spatial framework for low-light image enhancement that jointly models amplitude-phase spectral coupling rather than treating them independently, via an Amplitude-Phase Adaptive Compensation Fusion module. Reliable endogenous priors provide additional guidance to avoid structural distortion from artificial spectral decoupling.

entry.title: Multi-Speed Field Evaluation of a Semi-Autonomous Precision Sprayer for Weed Control in Vegetable Crops

author.name: Md Khairul Islam, Boyang Deng, Yuzhen Lu, Daniel Brainard, Ajit Srivastava

entry.summary: Evaluates a tractor-based, machine-vision-guided precision sprayer for weed control in radish across three operating speeds, curating a five-season dataset of 10,599 images with 84,311 annotated instances. The system integrates a YOLOv11-medium detector with ByteTrack tracking and custom actuation, quantifying how speed affects the integrated detection-tracking-actuation pipeline under real field conditions.

entry.title: MotionShift: Environment-Compatible Motion Transfer via Planner-Evaluator Synergistic Adaptation

author.name: Yanchen Liu, Junyao Gao, Yanan Sun, Wensheng Chen, Guangming Lu, Wenjie Pei

entry.summary: MotionShift transfers motion from reference videos to target scenes while ensuring physical compatibility, using an iterative planner-evaluator mechanism where an LLM generates motion trajectories and a VLM evaluates and corrects them against the target environment.

entry.title: PolarVis: A Dataset and Diffusion Framework for RGB-to-Polarization Perception in Adverse Driving Scenes

author.name: Ruilin Huang, Jue Wang, Zhen Tian, Xia Hua, F. Richard Yu

entry.summary: Introduces RGB-P Wild, a 10,000-image paired RGB and four-angle linear-polarization dataset for driving scenes, plus PolarVis, a diffusion-based framework with hierarchical features and angle-specific decoders to recover polarization representations from a single RGB image.

entry.title: TNVD-SC: Diagnosing Scan Context Failures in Forests with Terrain-Normalized Vertical Distributions

author.name: Jineon Kim, Jhonghyun An

entry.summary: This work diagnoses why Scan Context-based LiDAR place recognition fails in forests due to structural aliasing from repetitive vegetation and uneven terrain. It shows terrain normalization mainly helps vertical-distribution cells and proposes TNVD-SC, which preserves the SC ring-sector topology while adding terrain-normalized vertical distributions, achieving roughly 99% top-25 retrieval on the TreeLoc++ Wild-Places protocol.

entry.title: Auditing Semantic and Relational Reliability in Open-Vocabulary Human-Object Interaction Evaluation

author.name: S M Asif Hossain, Ruksat Khan Shayoni, Md Kishor Morol

entry.summary: The authors present a diagnostic protocol for evaluating open-vocabulary human-object interaction detectors, holding predictions fixed and scoring them under five evaluation views ranging from official category scoring to strict propositional equivalence. The protocol separates the effect of the matching engine from semantic credit and uses controlled meaning-preserving and meaning-breaking transformations with a blinded audit.

entry.title: Context-Aware Topological Distillation Graph Network for Asymmetric EEG-Eye Movement Emotion Recognition

author.name: Peijun Shi, Xiujin Zhu, Zhenguo Lao, Chee-Onn Chow, Wei Ru Wong, Zhen Liu, Xiaobing Jiang

entry.summary: CTD-GNet fuses EEG and eye-movement signals for emotion recognition by forming an electrode graph whose nodes and edges are modulated by eye movements and prior context, with bidirectional distillation into a single-window EEG-only student. This supports mental-health monitoring when eye data are unavailable. It reports strong leave-one-subject-out results on SEED and SEED-IV.

entry.title: CARNet: End-to-End Coupled Association-Recognition Network for Fine-Grained Multi-Drone Collaborative Detection

author.name: Zhao Zhang, Ruigang Fu, Yu Zhang, Jiajun Xiang, Zixuan Xiao, Ping Zhong

entry.summary: CARNet jointly optimizes cross-view target association and recognition fusion for multi-drone collaborative detection through a shared target-pair representation, replacing error-prone two-stage pipelines with inconsistent objectives and error propagation. This improves fine-grained detection from overlapping aerial viewpoints.

entry.title: HGASurv: Hierarchical Granularity-Aware Integration for Multimodal Survival Prediction

author.name: Peike Yu, Wuchao Liu, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: HGASurv integrates histopathology whole-slide images, genomic profiles, and clinical variables for survival prediction using a hierarchical WSI encoding module with spatial-grid convolutions and clinical-guided graph propagation, explicitly accounting for granularity differences across modalities. Aims to improve patient risk stratification in cancer.

entry.title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets

author.name: Luciano Ambrosini

entry.summary: Proposes two hybrid metaheuristics, a CMA-ES enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors and an adaptive particle swarm with DE injection and local refinement, for architectural design optimization under tight budgets of roughly a thousand expensive evaluations. Also introduces a budget-aware delay of population-size reduction in adaptive DE. The CMA-ES hybrid ranks first across seven shared evaluation problems.

entry.title: Tension Tells the Tail: Cable-Obstacle Interaction Sensing for Tethered Mobile Robot Navigation

author.name: Ryuki Shimada, Koki Suzuki, Genya Ishigami

entry.summary: The paper investigates cable tension as a sensing modality for tethered mobile robots to estimate whether a contacted obstacle is movable or non-movable, using systematic experiments varying velocity, contact angle, obstacle mass, and material. This enables risk assessment of cable-obstacle contacts that could otherwise cause snagging or mission failure.

entry.title: AeroIntent: A Synchronized Multimodal Benchmark for UAV Mission Intent Recognition

author.name: Yutong Chen, Jingxin Mao, Zhiwei Wei, Bing Li, Jianzhong Ni, Rongqing Zhang

entry.summary: AeroIntent is a simulation-based benchmark of 990 synchronized multimodal UAV sequences with radar, RGB, infrared, and depth data across five mission intents, featuring program-disjoint and radar-gap evaluation protocols. The accompanying AeroMIR model targets mission-level intent recognition for low-altitude airspace surveillance.

entry.title: CROPS: Cosserat-Rod-Based Co-Design of Soft Slender Programmable Material Systems for Biomedical Applications

author.name: Aaditya Chandrasekhar, Dex Doksoo Lee, Hyunwoo Kwon, Shicheng Li, Wei Chen

entry.summary: CROPS is a computational co-design framework, built on Cosserat rod mechanics, for stimuli-responsive slender structures that jointly optimizes material layout and actuation to meet patient-specific biomedical requirements. It addresses the nonintuitive, computationally demanding structure-actuation-response relationship of such programmable material systems.

entry.title: Using AI to find good Manifund projects

author.name: Caroline Ellison

entry.summary: The authors test using Claude Opus 5.5, an existing frontier model, to review 530 Manifund grant proposals from July 2026, producing quality scores and predictions of funding outcomes. They conclude AI is not yet a replacement for human grantmaking judgment but is promising for surfacing proposals worth human attention.

entry.title: Examining AI Swarm Efficiency with the AI Futures Model

author.name: Julian Bradshaw

entry.summary: The author explores the AI Futures Model (which informed AI 2027) to analyze how the parallelizability parameter lambda, borrowed from Toby Ord's swarm scaling analysis, affects how AI agent swarms could accelerate AI progress and shorten timelines. It quantifies the diminishing returns of adding parallel agents to a task.

entry.title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications article on machine learning analysis of antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China's food chain, with projections to 2050. The supplied content field is empty, so only the title and venue are available for assessment.

entry.title: Prosodic Structure as a Critical Component in Phonemic Language Modelling at BabyLM Scale

author.name: Bill K. S. Ku, Janet B. Pierrehumbert

entry.summary: The study trains BERT MLMs on 10M and 100M words comparing orthographic input against a ladder of increasingly phonologically rich conditions that include estimates of prosody, asking whether the prosodic cues infants exploit improve phonemic language modeling. The authors also introduce ecologically valid small-data evaluation tasks including a lexical decision task.

entry.title: Learning Geometry-Aware Planning Representations for Monocular Flight with Cross-Modal Supervision

author.name: Wencan Feng, Bailing Tian, Yulin Hui, Zhiyu Li, Junjie Lu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a monocular MAV navigation framework that predicts trajectories from two image frames, relative pose, and vehicle state without explicit depth reconstruction. Feature-level geometric supervision transfers planning-relevant representation knowledge from depth- or LiDAR-based teachers to make the RGB-only representation geometry aware.

entry.title: Can Compact Open-Weight Large Language Models Recover Mobility Events from Incomplete Trajectories? A Controlled Evaluation Using Air Trips

author.name: Hsuan-Chih Wang, Xianfeng Terry Yang

entry.summary: This controlled study evaluates whether compact locally deployed LLMs can recover missing mobility events from incomplete GPS trajectories, using 30 high-confidence US air trips under three incompleteness conditions, four prompt variants, and two LLMs. It tests whether more explicit prompting can compensate for lost endpoint evidence.

entry.title: $M^2Net$: Unifying Scale-Specific Structures and Prototype Decomposition for Spatial-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Chengyang Zhou, Zijian Zhang, Hao Miao, Chunxu Zhang, Ziming Liu, Chao Tang, Juncheng Hu, Irwin King

entry.summary: M2Net is a spatial-temporal forecasting framework combining multi-scale masked attention to capture granularity-dependent spatial correlations with prototype decomposition to separate global patterns from node-specific disturbances. It targets urban management applications where existing methods overlook scale shifts and signal entanglement. The design addresses two identified fundamental data characteristics.

entry.title: Can AI agents make law? Evaluating AI legal relevance and creativity

author.name: Benjamin Ricaud, Artem Galushko

entry.summary: The authors simulate constitutional assemblies in which a single LLM plays multiple debating characters to draft a hypothetical constitution for a community of AI agents. The assemblies converge on a robust floor of legal provisions while producing novel AI-specific provisions absent from human law, which the authors then analyze for legal relevance and creativity.

entry.title: Motor compound fault diagnosis using an attention-based cross-talk architecture

author.name: Wonjun Yi, Wonho Jung, Junho Kim, Rismaya Kumar Mishra, Yong-Hwa Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes an attention-based cross-talk multi-task learning architecture for motor compound fault diagnosis, jointly classifying multiple fault components and their severities from vibration signals while avoiding negative transfer from forced shared-trunk representations. It is motivated by physical AI's need for reliable condition monitoring of increasingly complex industrial machinery.

entry.title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions

author.name: Saad Naja, Nasser Odtallah, Jake Van-Praag, Sarah May

entry.summary: This empirical study tested whether four AI trading agents followed their declared strategies and risk rules across 2,627 closed positions from February to August 2026, mostly simulated against live prices with some real Hyperliquid orders. The fleet finished net positive after fees with high rule adherence including for unprofitable agents, and the paper offers an evaluation toolkit for separating luck from rule-following before granting agents autonomy or capital.

entry.title: Local data augmentation for imbalanced binary classification

author.name: Harold Gu{\'e}neau (SAMM), Alain Celisse (LPP, MODAL), Pascal Delange

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes rebalancing strategies for imbalanced binary classification, proving that merely rebalancing class proportions cannot change classification performance, while a proposed local data augmentation scheme based on subsampled anchor points and local perturbation provably does affect results. The analysis targets maximizing minority-class recall while limiting false detections.

entry.title: Can the Quantum Fisher Effective Dimension Judge a Hybrid Quantum Neural Network?

author.name: Md Masum Mia, Amith Khandakar, Mohamed Arselene Ayari

entry.summary: This paper critically examines whether the effective dimension of a quantum Fisher information matrix, commonly used to assess hybrid quantum neural networks, actually predicts trainability or accuracy. Through controlled experiments varying datasets, backbones, circuit depths, and seeds, the authors clarify what this widely used scalar metric genuinely measures.

entry.title: Leveraging Mental Models for Human-Centered Explanations: A Systematic Design Approach Illustrated by Explainable Fake Review Identification

author.name: Sidra Naveed (University of Siegen, Germany), Md Shajalal (University of Siegen, Germany), Gunnar Stevens (University of Siegen, Germany, Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg), Alexander Boden (Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg)

entry.summary: The paper proposes MIND-X, a human-centered explainability design method that aligns AI explanations with users' mental models and judgment heuristics, illustrated through fake review detection. It contributes a qualitative study eliciting credibility cues, design principles linking cues to LLM-generated adaptive explanations, and a quantitative evaluation.

entry.title: Reranking Answers of Large Language Models with Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Mikhail Salnikov, Hai Le, Olga Tsymboi, Ivan Lazichny, Dmitrii Iarosh, Egor Cheremiskin, Andrey Savchenko, Dmitry Simakov, Alexander Panchenko

entry.summary: The paper presents a method for knowledge-graph question answering that extracts query-related subgraphs via shortest paths between LLM-inferred candidate entities, then extracts subgraph features to train reranking models that select the most probable answers. Experiments are conducted on Wikidata-based benchmarks.

entry.title: Multimodal Decoupling for Diversified Recommendation through Semantic and Structural Shaping

author.name: Changran He, Jiaming Wei, Jianghong Ma, Tianjun Wei, Haijun Zhang, Xiaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why accuracy-optimized recommenders become over-concentrated and proposes decoupling multimodal signals from ID embeddings, shaping both the structural properties of representations and optimization dynamics to improve diversity. It addresses persistent semantic underutilization and the accuracy-diversity trade-off. Relevant to industrial recommendation systems.

entry.title: Pack and Extract: An Effective Graph-Based Approach for Feature Selection

author.name: Faisal N. Abu-Khzam, Joseph R. Barr, Cynthia Chaaya, Nadim Obeid, Peter Shaw

entry.summary: Improves combinatorial feature selection based on Independent Dominating Sets by favoring diverse features and generalizing to a node packing model, targeting high-dimensional molecular biology datasets like single-cell omics. Makes an overlooked combinatorial approach more tractable and effective. Classic combinatorial optimization meets modern high-dimensional data.

entry.title: From Score to Diagnosis: Search-Independent Post-Diagnosis for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Qian Li, Yuxiao Hu, Juncheng Liu, Yanhao Jia, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: PostDiag is a search-independent feedback mechanism for symbolic regression that diagnoses why a candidate expression skeleton fails, using Patch-wise Feature Profiling to capture local behavior. Unlike prior enhanced-feedback methods tied to specific solvers, PostDiag can be shared across diverse SR solvers facing the same low-information fitness bottleneck. This improves the modularity and reusability of SR diagnostics.

entry.title: MLFont: Machine Learning-Driven Font Subsetting and Range-Compact Unicode-Range Slicing for Low-Latency Web Typography

author.name: Quan Wang, Yiran Mao

entry.summary: MLFont learns font slicing strategies for web typography, combining a Zipfian high-frequency tier with latent co-occurrence topic tiers (Online LDA or a neural topic model with entropy-difference and Sinkhorn-based losses) to minimize unused-glyph downloads for CJK and Pan-European fonts. This addresses concrete web performance problems (multi-megabyte fonts, HTTP round trips, CSS bloat). An applied ML systems contribution to web infrastructure.

entry.title: Structured Relevance Determination and Channel Additive Gaussian Processes for Image Data

author.name: Harald Ro{\ss}els, Ludovico Scarton

entry.summary: This paper proposes structured hyperparameter sharing for RBF kernels in Gaussian processes applied to images, tying lengthscale parameters across groups of adjacent pixels and within color channels to reduce overfitting and improve uncertainty calibration with limited data. It also introduces channel-additive Gaussian processes for multi-channel inputs. The work addresses the hyperparameter explosion of fully anisotropic kernels on high-dimensional data.

entry.title: Which Answers Agree? Evaluating Self-Consistency from Incomplete Logs

author.name: Zhengtao Gui, Zexi Chen, Weining Shen

entry.summary: This paper derives sharp accuracy bounds for evaluating self-consistency voting using only correctness labels and partial agreement information from incomplete logs, leveraging stochastic majorization. It also introduces Plurality-U, a dynamic program that exactly averages voting accuracy when answer-category counts are available.

entry.title: Declarative Explanations for Graph Neural Networks: A Demonstration

author.name: Cibo Yu, Haitong Tang, Yinghui Wu, Arijit Khan, Tingting Zhu, Tingyang Chen, Xiangyu Ke

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates SliceGXQ, an end-to-end interactive system for querying layer-wise explanations of graph neural networks on large graphs, combining a GUI, a SPARQL-like query parser, and an execution/visualization workflow built on the SliceGX explanation engine. It targets making GNN behavior more transparent and explorable at scale.

entry.title: GeoSplit: Selective Edge--Server Map Acquisition for Cross-User Travel-Mode Recognition

author.name: Zepu Wang (Xuegang), Luyao Niu (Xuegang), Ruolin Li (Xuegang), Jeff (Xuegang), Ban

entry.summary: GeoSplit is an edge-server framework for travel-mode recognition that separates map-evidence utility, training-time transfer, and selective runtime acquisition, using entropy gating to decide when querying geospatial context is worthwhile. It improves macro-F1 for unseen users substantially while querying only 39.5 percent of trajectories and reducing application-layer costs.

entry.title: Super-resolution as Spatial Downscaling: Coherence, Structure and Task Utility in Earth Observation

author.name: Bright Wiredu Nuakoh, Ebenezer Afrifa-Yamoah

entry.summary: This study reframes satellite super-resolution as spatial downscaling and evaluates four lightweight networks, including a compact 0.36M-parameter model, using variograms, codispersion, spectral correlation, and observation coherence rather than only pixel fidelity. Networks beat bicubic by about 1.4 dB at x2 yet recover only roughly 30 percent of spectral power above observed resolution, questioning whether reconstructions support downstream analysis. It argues for structure-aware evaluation in earth observation super-resolution.

entry.title: Learning from the Right Regions: Class-Conditioned Explanation Guidance for Medical Imaging

author.name: Zubair Faruqui, Rahul Dubey

entry.summary: Proposes a class-conditioned explanation-guided learning framework for multi-label medical imaging that builds a separate Grad-CAM explanation per positive class and penalizes evidence outside its class-specific annotated regions, handling co-occurring abnormalities. It is evaluated on 14 abnormalities across EfficientNet and ViT backbones.

entry.title: Decision-Target Reversal under Informative Label Missingness

author.name: Farinborz Setoudehtazangi, Geoffrey J. McLachlan

entry.summary: The paper shows that informative label missingness, which can improve classification efficiency, may help under one deployment loss but hurt under another, a phenomenon the authors call decision-target reversal. Through a cost-sensitive excess-risk analysis of binary Gaussian discrimination, they derive explicit critical cost ratios where the risk ordering flips, with implications for how missing-data advantages should be evaluated across deployment objectives.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Interpretable Ranking for Sector Rotation

author.name: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Ziling Liu, Xinyang Li, Shuowei Feng, Ruoyu Liang, Mathieu Giroux, Eugene Y. Wen, Xuan Yao, Ke-Wei Huang, Hugo Lamarre

entry.summary: RegimeRank formulates sector rotation in portfolio management as an interpretable ranking task conditioned on learned macroeconomic regimes, using expert-defined temporal signal characteristics and forward Sharpe ratios as targets. It aims to preserve temporal structure and capture cross-sector dependencies in economically familiar terms.

entry.title: Modeling bilingual naming performance through laterally-connected SOMs

author.name: Divya Prabhakaran, Uli Grasemann, Erie Shivers, Marissa Russell-Meill, Swathi Kiran, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: Extends the BiLex computational model of the bilingual lexicon by adding excitatory and inhibitory lateral connections to its self-organizing-map architecture, increasing biological realism. The extension lets the model fit individual patient data more accurately, accounting for response times and characteristic naming errors in bilingual speakers.

entry.title: Morpheus: a fully local, defense-in-depth de-identification engine for Greek clinical text - a benchmark evaluation

author.name: Filippos-Paschalis Rorris (Onassis Hospital, Athens, Greece, Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children, London, United Kingdom), Nikoleta Stanitsa (Evangelismos General Hospital, Athens, Greece), Tatiana Rorri (Onassis Hospital, Athens, Greece), Foteini Rorri (Universita della Svizzera italiana, Lugano, Switzerland), Constantine N. Antonopoulos (Attikon University Hospital, University of Athens Medical School, Athens, Greece)

entry.summary: The authors evaluate Morpheus, a fully local de-identification pipeline for Greek clinical documents, on 500 clinician-reviewed synthetic discharge summaries generated with Gemini 3.1 Pro under authentic hospital layouts. They report recall over must-redact identifiers and over-redaction rates, filling a gap since no Greek clinical de-identification benchmark existed.

entry.title: Flattening Fantasies: Analyzing Stereotypes in Pornographic Discourse

author.name: Sarmad Chandio, Osama Khalid, Sharaf Zia, Ethan Kutlu

entry.summary: A large-scale computational sociolinguistic analysis of 5.4 million adult video titles examining how nationalities, ethnic groups, and gender identities are portrayed, finding American content functions as the industry norm and identifying persistent ethnic stereotypes tied to colonial power dynamics and fetishization. Demonstrates NLP methods applied to a sensitive, understudied discourse domain.

entry.title: Modal Sense Disambiguation in Language Models: The Role of Context, Training Domain, and Input Frequency

author.name: Ezgi Ba\c{s}ar, Yevgen Matusevych, Annemarie van Dooren, Arianna Bisazza

entry.summary: Evaluates seven language models on distinguishing root versus epistemic senses of modals like may and must, using vector similarity and surprisal across four datasets. The study examines whether models use context for modal disambiguation and how performance relates to training-data sense distributions, echoing known difficulties in child language acquisition.

entry.title: The Geometry of Agent Memory: Forecasting Retrieval-Bound Memory Failures, and Characterizing Its Limits

author.name: Iliya Zhechev, Radoslav Ralev, Chris Coleman, Srijith Rajamohan, Jen Agarwal, Tyler Hutcherson, Simba Khadder

entry.summary: Investigates whether geometric relationships among conversation turns, memory texts, and queries can predict answer correctness before generation in agent memory systems. On LongMemEval-small, pooled AUROC reaches only 0.640, below a question-difficulty baseline, with geometry adding limited value after controlling for difficulty and question-type identity.

entry.title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition

author.name: Vincenzo Perri, Ciro Cattuto, Daniela Paolotti

entry.summary: Presents EpiLens, an open-source RAG package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to a corpus of 2,297 epidemiological papers, linking outputs to source passages. Its classifier matches or exceeds supervised and zero-shot baselines on 214 manually labeled papers without task-specific training data.

entry.title: Hexagonal Basis Projectors for Model-Based Iterative CT Reconstruction

author.name: Ke Chen, Alireza Entezari

entry.summary: This work develops constant and linear hexagonal basis projectors for 2D fan-beam CT reconstruction using box spline calculus, exploiting the superior sampling efficiency and isotropy of the hexagonal lattice over Cartesian grids. The authors derive analytic ray footprints, implement GPU-accelerated projection, and validate on simulated FORBILD data.

entry.title: Learning Lane-Structured Conditioning Fields for Online HD Mapping

author.name: Andrea Bertogalli, Anthony Dell'Eva, Marcello Ceresini, Federico Pirazzoli, Lorenzo Cipelli, Filippo D'Addeo, Nicola Marinello, Massimo Bertozzi

entry.summary: Proposes the Lane Field, a dense BEV-aligned structural representation for online high-definition map construction that combines the integrability of dense rasters with the geometric fidelity of sparse vectors, providing learnable geometric guidance for autonomous driving downstream tasks.

entry.title: DragonMoCap: Monocular Video-based Motion Capture for Diverse Dragon Topologies

author.name: Zhongfei Qing, Xiaoxiang Zhao, Ling-Hao Chen, Zhongang Cai, Wenjia Wang, Yifan Wu, Qianying Liu, Wei Zeng, Bo Hu, Songnan Li

entry.summary: DragonMoCap tackles monocular motion capture for dragon-type characters, where extreme topological diversity in joint counts and naming conventions defeats fixed-template regressors. The framework treats the target rig as a dynamic input using language-grounded joint query tokens, targeting prevalent production topologies for high-fidelity animation results.

entry.title: ExMR: Extremity Motion Refinement for Monocular Human Motion Capture

author.name: Tom Wehrbein, Bodo Rosenhahn

entry.summary: ExMR extends prior foot-refinement work to hands, adding modules that refine ankle rotations from foot keypoints and elbow, wrist, and finger rotations using pretrained hand-reconstruction features plus initial arm poses. This improves detailed extremity articulation in monocular human motion capture. Relevant to animation and motion analysis.

entry.title: A Configurable ETC2 Encoder with Learned Search

author.name: Ziyu Guo, Haomiao Jiang, Sergey Makeev, Angelo Pesce

entry.summary: This paper presents a configurable CPU encoder for the ETC2 texture format in which rules or small neural networks allocate conventional searches, spanning configurations from fast-encoder output to broad mode and endpoint searches. Learned action ranking and second-search allocation yield measurable PSNR gains at equal search cost, and high-quality configurations beat reference encoders with large speedups. Authors include recognized texture-compression experts.

entry.title: Peer-Relative Trust-Guided Update Screening for Robust Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning under Label-Flipping Attacks

author.name: Ajay Kumar Shrestha, Sandhya Joshi

entry.summary: Extends a prior semi-decentralized federated learning framework with peer-relative update screening that combines robust validation-utility scores with direction- and norm-based update quality to resist label-flipping attacks under non-IID data. Evaluated on 50 MNIST clients with 20 percent persistent attackers across Dirichlet heterogeneity levels and multiple seeds. It tackles the known problem that strict filtering penalizes honest non-IID updates.

entry.title: Visual-Inertial Odometry for Ground Robots with Dynamic Camera-IMU Extrinsic Calibration

author.name: Bo Dong

entry.summary: This paper relaxes the rigid-mount assumption in visual-inertial odometry by proposing dynamic camera-IMU extrinsic calibration based on the Denavit-Hartenberg convention combined with the robot kinematic model. A two-step initialization strategy estimates initial joint angles, enabling online estimation of time-varying extrinsics for sensors mounted on moving structures. Simulation experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

entry.title: Validation of Human Motor Development Scales with Humanoid Robots

author.name: Fanxing Meng, Jing Xiao

entry.summary: The paper encodes pediatric infant motor development scales as developmental graphs and uses them to structure reinforcement learning training of humanoid robots acquiring gross motor skills up to standing and walking. Three of four popular scales successfully guided skill development, while one was found incomplete.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning is Probably Inconsistent with Ethics

author.name: Our Critical Point

entry.summary: The author argues, beyond the standard reward-hacking critique, that reinforcement learning's reward hypothesis embeds assumptions about ethics (that the best action in any scenario is well-defined and commensurable) that are likely false, implying every RL-trained AI would be misaligned regardless of reward specification. The post frames this as a more fundamental objection than proxy-gaming.

entry.title: IECLA: Interpretable Emotion Contribution Learning for Affective Image Editing

author.name: Yijie Guo, Dexiang Hong, Weidong Chen, Xinyan Liu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: IECLA is a framework for affective image editing that separates source-emotion attribution from target-aware editing, using counterfactual interventions to build signed object-level supervision and a context-conditioned contribution predictor to localize regions supporting or opposing the source emotion. This tells the editor which regions to change and which to preserve when evoking a target emotion.

entry.title: ChronoChart: Setup-Agnostic Channel Charting for Label-Free Indoor Localization

author.name: Majid Sharghi Foroushani, Jonas Pirkl, Jonathan Ott, Maximilian Stahlke, George Yammine, Tobias Feigl, Christopher Mutschler

entry.summary: ChronoChart is a channel charting method for radio-based indoor localization that removes dependence on setup-specific dissimilarity metrics and precomputed quadratic-size distance matrices, improving scalability across deployments. It learns low-dimensional CSI representations without position labels, addressing the costly recalibration requirements of supervised fingerprinting in dynamic indoor environments.

entry.title: Injection of Space Radiation Errors on Low-power NVM using Generative Deep Learning

author.name: Eleonora Giudici, Antonio Miele, Luca Mottola

entry.summary: Using bit-error data from an actual CubeSat mission in low Earth orbit, the authors characterize spatial patterns of radiation-induced faults in FRAM memory and train a generative deep learning model to synthesize realistic additional error patterns. This enables better-grounded testing of error-mitigation strategies for space hardware.

entry.title: SAP-Depth: Scene-Adaptive Probability Framework for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Bowen He, Li Zhang, Yujie Chen, Chang Cheng

entry.summary: SAP-Depth introduces a Dynamic Bins mechanism with a Learnable Parameter Predictor that estimates scene-specific depth distributions conditioned on image context, plus a Bin-wise Probability Distribution Decoder for fusing multi-scale features. This improves boundary sharpness and structural recovery in self-supervised monocular depth estimation.

entry.title: Multi-View Structural Representations for Physically-Consistent TeX Generation

author.name: Daoheng Li, Jianjun Qian*, Mengkai Yan, Jian Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes MVR-MoE, a physics-based framework for low-light image generation that fuses infrared and visible imagery without paired data, using multi-view hyper connections and hierarchical routing over mixture-of-experts. It mines intrinsic structural cues from both modalities to build physically consistent representations.

entry.title: Interpretable Face Contrast Modeling for Smartphone Portrait Rendering

author.name: Yujin Cho, Beno\^{i}t Pochon, Jean-Michel Morel, Gabriele Facciolo

entry.summary: The authors propose an interpretable framework that decomposes facial contrast in smartphone portrait photography into three components: overall tonal separation, eye-region contrast, and micro-contrast of skin details, with dedicated metrics for each. This helps characterize why the same portrait renders differently across manufacturers. The work is relevant to perceptual quality evaluation and computational photography pipeline design.

entry.title: A GPU-Resident Pipeline for Multi-Robot 3D Inspection with Limited Perception

author.name: Kry\v{s}tof P\v{s}eni\v{c}ka, Stefan Edelkamp

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully GPU-resident pipeline for multi-robot underwater 3D inspection that decomposes the NP-hard joint coverage problem into viewpoint generation, visibility computation, set cover, min-max vehicle routing as a MIP with lifted MTZ constraints, and priority-based multi-agent path finding with continuous-time conflict checking.

entry.title: Rethinking EEG Spatial Super-Resolution as Dynamic State Decomposition and Filtering

author.name: Hongjun Liu, Leyu Zhou, Chang Ge, Shitong Duan, Chao Yao

entry.summary: This paper reformulates streaming EEG spatial super-resolution as a sequential state filtering problem, proposing Dynamic State Filtering (DSF) that explicitly separates predictable state evolution from newly emerging changes in the current observation. DSF combines a hierarchical decomposition with filtering rather than a single temporal reconstruction pathway. This offers a principled reframing for recovering high-density neural signals from sparse electrodes.

entry.title: Improving Fake Profile Detection Through Multimodal Learning and Research-Guided Feature Integration

author.name: Jean Claude Hirwa, Jamiu Dahunsi, Candide Giramata, Lowami Uwimana, Thierry Henry Ishimwe

entry.summary: This study evaluates bot detection on a TwiBot-22 subsample by combining XLM-RoBERTa textual, CLIP visual, and account metadata features with CatBoost and an R-GCN. Findings indicate metadata alone is highly predictive, tempering claims that multimodal learning provides large gains over strong baselines.

entry.title: TrustAgent-RFF: Agentic Diagnostic Planning for Reliable RF Fingerprinting under Domain Shift

author.name: Chuan Liu, Tianya Zhao, Xuyu Wang

entry.summary: TrustAgent-RFF is a prediction-level reliability framework for radio frequency fingerprinting under domain shift, combining counterfactual stability, prototype consistency, acquisition-domain similarity, and signal quality into a source-calibrated trust estimator, without needing target-domain labels. It addresses the failure of softmax confidence thresholding when receiver, distance, or environment changes.

entry.title: Optimizing Marketing Budgets for Social Influence: A Generalized Fractional Incentives Framework

author.name: Abhishek K. Umrawal, Akhil Bhimaraju, Eliot W. Robson, Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Formulates Budgeted Generalized Fractional Influence Maximization, where continuous marketing spend is allocated across users with heterogeneous response functions and network spillovers, and proposes a scalable discrete greedy algorithm with provable approximation guarantees. The framework captures variable per-user incentive costs and baseline propensities.

entry.title: Residual-Guided Adaptive Tucker Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient MCI Conversion Prediction

author.name: Guanghua He, Hancan Zhu, Gaohang Yu, An Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a PEFT method for 3D networks that jointly selects Tucker input- and output-channel ranks per convolutional layer under a fixed adapter-parameter budget, guided by learned proxy updates and a perturbation analysis linking output discrepancy to layerwise reconstruction residuals. It is applied to predicting MCI-to-Alzheimer's conversion from imaging data.

entry.title: Vocabulary-Incomplete Unsupervised Vision-Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Si Qin, Jiawei Tang, Yaxin Hou, Yan Chen, Yutong Xie, Chen Li, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: The paper introduces VI-UVA, an unsupervised adaptation setting for vision-language models where only a subset of class names is available, since unlabeled data may contain overlooked or out-of-scope classes. The method adapts VLMs via pseudo-labeling while handling the incomplete vocabulary. This relaxes an unrealistic assumption in prior unsupervised VLM adaptation work.

entry.title: SafeWall: A Risk-Aware Job Walltime Recommendation for HPC Scheduling

author.name: Kanglin Xu, Michael Papka, Zhiling Lan

entry.summary: SafeWall is a risk-aware method for recommending HPC job walltimes that augments learned predictions with an explicit nonnegative safety margin to avoid premature job termination. It shifts focus from pure prediction accuracy to recommendation risk, addressing systematic user overestimation of walltime.

entry.title: S3D-Mosaic: Subgradient-Guided Cross-Band Structure Transfer for Spectral Demosaicing

author.name: Weiqiang Zhao, Xian Li, Yuzhe Gui, Tianzhu Liu, Yanfeng Gu

entry.summary: S3D-Mosaic is a model-based spectral demosaicing method that transfers spatial structure across spectral bands via a subgradient-guided regularization framework with a magnitude-invariant cosine-similarity interpretation. It avoids the layout-specific training and per-image tuning required by prior model-based and learning-based approaches to multispectral filter array imaging.

entry.title: Spectral-Aware Proposal Enhancement for Diffusion-Based Multispectral UAV Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Xu Lin, Tingfa Xu, Tianhao Li, Haolin Qin, Huawei Gao, Jichuan Xing, Jianan Li

entry.summary: DSATrack is a diffusion-guided, spectral-aware tracking framework for multispectral UAV multi-object tracking with oriented boxes, injecting multispectral cues into the RPN branch via a lightweight spectral encoder for better proposal initialization and confidence calibration. It targets small targets and cluttered backgrounds typical of UAV scenarios.

entry.title: CASE: Complementary Articulation-Aware Speech Encoder to Enhance Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation

author.name: Jaehong Myung, Seungho Eum, Taegon Kim, Hyunjung Chung, Unsang Park

entry.summary: CASE adapts a speech encoder via contrastive alignment with 3D lip-mesh VQ-VAE latents to better capture articulatory dynamics, then fuses the audio-only representation with baseline SSL features through residual cross-attention, reducing mean lip vertex error by 2.8-6.0% across VOCASET baselines.

entry.title: Confidence-Guided Pseudo-Label Refinement for Unsupervised Cross-Domain Person Re-Identification

author.name: Sundas Iqbal, Danish Ali, Qing Tian, Yuhui Zheng, Jianping Gou, Weihua Ou

entry.summary: CGPLR refines noisy pseudo-labels in unsupervised cross-domain person re-identification by estimating sample reliability from centroid compatibility, neighborhood consistency, competing-cluster separation, and temporal assignment stability. The confidence distribution softens hard identity supervision on ambiguous target samples during iterative adaptation.

entry.title: Continuous Ontology Assurance through External Resources -- An Ontology Engineering Method with a Case Study in Software Language Engineering

author.name: Ralf L\"ammel

entry.summary: COATER is a method for continuously assuring domain ontologies against evolving external resources using executable review components called arrows that report support or challenges to axioms. Challenges become triage tasks for humans or agents, illustrated with an LLM-assisted case study in software language engineering. It offers a structured approach to keeping ontologies current, a persistent engineering problem.

entry.title: On Counting Graphs for Modal Logic with Counting

author.name: Avijeet Ghosh, Fran\c{c}ois Schwarzentruber

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies the computational complexity of counting trees and graphs that are classified positively by graph neural networks, equivalently those satisfying formulas of modal logic with counting. It also examines convergence properties of these counts. The work connects GNN expressivity with modal logic, providing formal tools for understanding what GNN classifications imply about the underlying graph structure.

entry.title: Autonomous intelligence for mining productivity: a multi-agent AI approach to operational value creation

author.name: N Guerin (CGS i3), A Dehoux (ERAMET), M Nakhla (CGS i3)

entry.summary: The paper proposes an integrated agentic architecture for mining Integrated Remote Operation Centres that orchestrates SCADA systems, digital twins, predictive analytics, and human-machine interfaces under safety-critical constraints. It also introduces an evaluation framework covering real-time, health-safety-environment, regulatory-auditability, and cost-per-decision requirements for industrial agentic deployments.

entry.title: A Semantic Knowledge Graph Construction Pipeline for Vehicle Intention Prediction in nuScenes

author.name: Khaled Nowara, Mohamed Manzour, Catherine Elias

entry.summary: Presents NIKG, an OWL-based semantic knowledge graph pipeline over nuScenes scenes that makes ego-relative motion, spatial configuration, and time-to-collision risk first-class properties for vehicle intention prediction. It fills a gap by targeting intention context rather than general scene understanding or trajectory forecasting.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Power Outage Detection Task with Limited Training Data

author.name: Olukunle Owolabi

entry.summary: This paper investigates zero-shot and few-shot transfer learning with language models for detecting power outages from social media tweets using limited labeled data. Results show classical baselines beat zero-shot LLMs, but few-shot fine-tuning substantially closes the gap and enables generalization to unseen outage classes.

entry.title: Severity-Channel Conditioning: An Injection-Level Study for Consumer-Device Deblurring

author.name: Abdullah Al Shafi, Kazi Saeed Alam, Sumaiya Rahim Suma, Sk. Imran Hossain

entry.summary: Studies how severity descriptors condition motion-deblurring models adapted from professional cameras to smartphone imagery on the iPhoneBlur benchmark, comparing input concatenation, global and spatial feature modulation, and a tier-contrastive output objective under a shared fine-tuning budget. Notably, the primary experiment is framed as an oracle diagnostic supplying target-derived severity information at inference.

entry.title: Same Data, Different Bytes: Serialization-Invariant Integrity Checks for Agent-Published Datasets

author.name: Jin Gao, Maura Clark

entry.summary: This paper proposes a serialization-invariant identification method for agent networks so that data representations equivalent under explicit rules receive the same identifier, addressing false mismatches when checksums differ only due to serialization. It uses DataFacts as a case study, retaining existing checksums alongside the proposed identifier.

entry.title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval

author.name: Pranav Singh, Prashant Singh

entry.summary: This theory paper studies how an agent can pre-retain information beside an immutable binary archive before knowing a future query, with worst-case limits on bit or word reads at retrieval time. The authors characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells, construct encoders partitioning the complete record space, and show that supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query.

entry.title: AdaFedXplain: Adaptive Federated Learning with Explainable AI for Ransomware Detection

author.name: Md. Emran Biswas, Md. Delowar Hossain, Mst. Tanbin Yasmin Tanny, Muhammad Aminur Rahaman, Md Al Amin, Tangina Sultana

entry.summary: AdaFedXplain combines adaptive federated learning with explainable AI for ransomware detection, using progressive XGBoost complexity, a decaying learning rate schedule, and techniques to handle non-IID data and communication costs. The goal is collaborative detection without sharing sensitive security data across institutions.

entry.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics

author.name: Omid Shams Solari

entry.summary: Rebuilds the block generalized-power method for sparse spectral optimization from first principles, showing the standard formulation conflates two nonequivalent objectives and providing exact identities, explicit conventions for degenerate cases, and finite identification results. It demonstrates a two-component instance where the commonly used objectives disagree.

entry.title: Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machines as Unsupervised Encoders for Biomechanical Movement Sequences

author.name: Wafi Sharif, Nicholas LaHaye

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machine, an energy-based model, into an unsupervised encoder producing fixed-length embeddings of windows of continuous biomechanical movement data, testing what its recurrent structure contributes. It addresses the limitation that most unsupervised pipelines treat frames independently and discard temporal structure. The work is a niche revival of energy-based temporal models for a specific application domain.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Domain Generalization in Edge Networks via Dynamic Prototype Regulation

author.name: Yuankun Xia, Hui Wang, Ling Yuan, Ziyu Hong, Di Yin, Yufeng Zhou

entry.summary: DPGR-GCAM is a communication-efficient federated domain generalization framework for deploying vision-language models over wireless edge networks, addressing uplink latency, Non-IID client drift, and straggler dropouts. It uses dynamic prototype regulation to avoid auxiliary computations that consume wireless transmission time slots.

entry.title: Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility: A Theoretical Framework for Multi-Agent Task Obstructions

author.name: Steven Motta, Davide Mambelli, Alessandro Rozza

entry.summary: This theoretical work introduces a sheaf-theoretic framework, Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility, that separates task-level compatibility obstructions from system capability in multi-agent systems, using cohomological signatures over interaction complexes. Registered interventions test capability, and cochain realization is solvable exactly when the cohomology class vanishes. It offers a formal language for why identically capable multi-agent systems can still fail on certain joint tasks.

entry.title: Measuring the Influence of Modality-Specific Node Representations on Graphs

author.name: Xu Wang, Xunkai Li, Yinlin Zhu, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: This paper defines and studies influence measurement for modality-specific node representations (text and image) in multimodal attributed graphs, scoring each candidate representation by replacing it with a counterpart and measuring the distributed change in predictions. It outputs separate text and image influence rankings, revealing which modality a trained graph predictor relies on. This aids interpretability of multimodal graph models in recommendation and multimedia.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Detection of Photovoltaic Systems on Industrial Building Rooftops Using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning

author.name: Frederick Bruch, Christian Knoth, Florian Detsch, Edzer Pebesma, Hanna Meyer

entry.summary: This paper develops an ML framework using open-access multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery combined with OpenStreetMap building geometries to detect industrial rooftop solar photovoltaic installations over time. It addresses the gap between rapid PV deployment and lagging administrative registries, providing scalable monitoring for grid operators and policymakers. Open data usage makes the approach reproducible and widely applicable.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Interpolation for Inverse Problems

author.name: Pourya Shamsolmoali, Masoumeh Zareapoor

entry.summary: GAIN is a VAE-based framework that replaces conventional linear or bilinear interpolation in Spatial Transformer Networks with geometry-aware interpolation for image reconstruction from degraded or incomplete inputs. The approach aims to better capture geometric characteristics of image data and stabilize gradient propagation during optimization. It targets improved inverse problem performance on complex image structures.

entry.title: HullProbe: Measuring Interventional Part Reliance in Maritime Vessel Classifiers

author.name: Faisal Mohammad, Mohamed Younis

entry.summary: HullProbe is a method for directly measuring how much a vessel classifier relies on specific anatomical parts, such as the generic hull versus the distinctive superstructure, by swapping registered parts between same-class vessel images and observing decision changes. This provides an interventional alternative to worst-group accuracy proxies for certifying debiasing methods in maritime surveillance applications.

entry.title: Sampling of Signals on Multigraphs: From Removable and Uniqueness sets to Spectral Proxies

author.name: Alejandro Parada-Mayorga

entry.summary: This paper develops a theory of sampling bandlimited signals on multigraphs, where multiple non-commuting shift operators act on the same nodes and frequencies become matrices rather than scalars. It extends removable and uniqueness sets to the multigraph setting and proves sampling-set optimality is determined solely by the common Fourier basis and its invariant subspaces.

entry.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions

author.name: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav

entry.summary: The paper develops hybrid variational-collocation physics-informed neural networks with multiscale Fourier features and residual-based adaptive refinement for singular elliptic PDEs on cracked or nonconvex domains with mixed boundary conditions. The variational term requires only first derivatives, easing training near re-entrant corners and crack tips.

entry.title: Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation

author.name: Nizar Yahya Habash

entry.summary: This dissertation presents Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation (GHHT), an approach for source-poor and target-rich language pairs that exploits symbolic and statistical target-language resources instead of requiring symmetric parallel resources. It addresses a persistent bottleneck in MT system development across transfer, interlingua, symbolic, and statistical paradigms.

entry.title: Conditional information Retrieval for Longitudinal Survey Harmonisation

author.name: Wing Yan Li, Zeqiang Wang, Michelle Lin, Jon Johnson, Suparna De

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional information retrieval framework for matching conceptually equivalent survey questions across longitudinal studies, decomposing the task into concept extraction with a fine-tuned generative model and concept-aware retrieval that conditions on the extracted sociological concept. This handles cases where lexical similarity misleads about conceptual equivalence.

entry.title: WenSight-Decision-1 for Direct Decisions under E-commerce Rules

author.name: Mingwen Liu (WenSight AI Lab), Jun Sun (TooChuang), Sichen Wang (WenSight AI Lab)

entry.summary: Introduces WenSight-Decision-1, a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B that scores supplied options directly from natural-language rules and case evidence across six multilingual e-commerce operational tasks. Accuracy rises from 61.60 percent to 92.92 percent on 1,440 held-out synthetic cases under identical inputs.

entry.title: Dynamic self-ensemble on multi-exit residual vision transformer for small-data image classification

author.name: Stephen Ekaputra Limantoro, Yan-Kai Wang, Ching-Chun Huang, Hong-Han Shuai, Wen-Huang Cheng, Jungwoo Huh, Sanghoon Lee

entry.summary: ReSEViT is a multi-stage residual vision transformer with multiple exits and a dynamic self-ensemble method that leverages intermediate features to improve small-data image classification, motivated by medical imaging scenarios where datasets are limited. Multiple classifiers mitigate error from complex decision boundaries that a single classifier handles poorly.

entry.title: Evaluating Cloud and Self-Hosted OCR Systems for Arabic, English, and French Documents: Bounding Box Detection, Text Recognition, and Mathematical Expression Recognition

author.name: Jumana Alsubhi, Ahmed Alhusayni, Abdulrahman Gharawi, Israa Hamdine, Khadija Alansari, Alshaymaa Allahim, Lamees Alhumaid, Ahmad Shabana

entry.summary: A benchmark study comparing cloud and self-hosted OCR systems across Arabic, English, and French documents on detection, text recognition, and math expression recognition, with statistical rigor (95% intervals, paired comparisons). Google Document AI and Surya lead detection at 98% and 96% page-level accuracy.

entry.title: RAHF-Net: Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion for LiDAR-Assisted RGB Semantic Segmentation

author.name: R. D. Lin, Pengcheng Weng, Ge Wang, Han Ding, Fei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a fusion network for LiDAR-assisted RGB segmentation with a Cylindrical-to-Perspective module projecting pretrained voxel features into the image plane and a range-aware fusion module using soft depth-derived masks to weight LiDAR guidance by reliability.

entry.title: Curvature as a Baseline: Monocular Pose Measurement of Cylindrical Objects with Dual Colour Stripe Markers

author.name: Jaesung Hong, Dong Won Lee

entry.summary: This work proposes a dual-colour-stripe fiducial marker that exploits the known curvature of cylindrical objects for monocular pose estimation, using the colour boundary and depth-separated features to improve roll estimation. It provides Cramer-Rao bound analysis showing large precision gains over flat markers and validates with Monte Carlo experiments.

entry.title: YUTELA: A Scalable Edge Cloud AIoT System for Multi-Site Video Anomaly Detection with Scene Specific Adaptation

author.name: Shanle Yao, Babak Rahimi Ardabili, Amir Kimiyaie, Hamed Tabkhi

entry.summary: YUTELA is an edge-server-cloud AIoT system for long-term multi-site video anomaly detection, using NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge devices with camera batching, shared memory, task integration, and TensorRT acceleration, plus per-camera anomaly models retrained centrally on pseudo-normal data. TensorRT roughly doubles throughput (14.17 to 29.94 FPS with eight cameras). This is a systems paper building on the authors' prior Ancilia framework.

entry.title: A Heterogeneous UAV UGV Methodology for Aerial Tracking of Mini Autonomous Cars

author.name: Santiago Fernandez, Angel da Silva, Hiago Sodre, Pablo Moraes, Bruna Gutterres, Ricardo B. Grando

entry.summary: Presents a ROS 2 and Gazebo-based methodology for aerial tracking of small autonomous ground vehicles using a Tello-like UAV with an RGB camera. Three approaches are compared: a training-free color-marker baseline, a YOLO-based visual baseline, and a third method addressing occlusions and field-of-view limits. It provides situational awareness where fixed perception infrastructure is unavailable.

entry.title: Vehicle-State-Aware Confidence Estimation for Direct Wind Sensing on a Multirotor

author.name: Sri Arjun Senthil Kumar, April Zi Qian Chan, Chen-Hua Yeow

entry.summary: The authors present a confidence-scoring method for UAV-mounted anemometers that weights wind observations by horizontal and vertical vehicle speed, reflecting how motion corrupts direct wind measurements. A two-feature model achieves ROC-AUC of 0.995 in identifying unreliable measurements and feeds a confidence-adapted 2D vector estimator validated on waypoint flights.

entry.title: AI as a Normal Technology should be a vision

author.name: June Jimenez

entry.summary: The author argues that Narayanan and Kapoor's AI as a Normal Technology framework, released in April 2025, functions better as a prescriptive vision than as a descriptive or predictive claim, and proposes unbundling its descriptive, predictive, and normative components. The critique is that conflating these weakens the framework's communication and modeling.

entry.title: When AI Advice Shapes the Evidence It Later Interprets

author.name: rozenn@post.bgu.ac.il

entry.summary: A conceptual post arguing that AI assistants can create self-fulfilling loops: advice given to a user shapes outcomes that the assistant later interprets as independent confirmation of its original assumption. The author proposes evaluating whether assistants weight such downstream evidence appropriately given the user's actions.

entry.title: Agentic Orchestration of EDC Data Space Retrieval and Natural Language Driven Data Processing

author.name: Marla Grunewald, Fin Gentzen, Iulisloi Zacarias, Admela Jukan

entry.summary: A multi-agent architecture built on LangGraph over Eclipse Dataspace Components that automates Dataspace Protocol negotiation flows from natural language requests, with an orchestrator, a data extraction agent exposing catalog discovery, contract negotiation, and download as tools, and credential-gated negotiations. Downstream ML and visualization agents process the retrieved data.

entry.title: How Well Can LLMs Verbalize Mathematical Formulas? A Multi-Domain Evaluation

author.name: Peter Volbach, Tim Schlippe

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates five frontier LLMs on verbalizing LaTeX math formulas for text-to-speech use cases such as audio learning and accessibility, and introduces Read-Aloud Math, a multi-domain corpus with manually validated transcriptions. GPT-5.2, an existing OpenAI model, achieved the best simple-transcription score (75.9% multi-reference BLEU without context).

entry.title: Federated Learning for Malware Image Classification under Data Heterogeneity

author.name: Victor Taiwo, Cemal Nisan, Muhammad Athallah, M. Emre Gursoy, Oznur Ozkasap

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies federated malware image classification under non-IID data heterogeneity across three datasets (MalImg, Virus-MNIST, MalNet), and contributes mitigation techniques plus an extended evaluation framework. It addresses an understudied intersection of privacy-preserving collaborative training and security applications.

entry.title: Multi-author style detection with stylistic embeddings

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, Chak Fai Li, Damianos Karakos, Fred Bernardin, Brian Ulicny

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a Mistral-7B embedding model for authorship verification and combine it with DeBERTa embeddings via cross-domain transfer learning for the PAN-25 multi-author style change detection challenge. The two models excel in complementary text scenarios, and their combination yields more effective style change detection.

entry.title: Ben-Misandry: A Bengali Dataset and Late-Fusion Transformer Framework for Detecting Anti-Male Gender Hate

author.name: Md Mehedi Hasan Nipu, Chinmoy Mitra, Tarannum Ahmed Nowshin, Israt Moyeen Noumi

entry.summary: Introduces Ben-Misandry, the first dataset for detecting anti-male gendered hate speech in Bengali, comprising 5,000 comments across six taxonomy classes including a novel category for mocking male emotional vulnerability. The corpus is synthetic, generated with GPT-4.1 and spot-checked by four human reviewers on a 500-comment sample, paired with a late-fusion transformer detection framework.

entry.title: MPIG: Multi-angle Polarization Image Generation from a Single Polarization Observation

author.name: Jue Wang, Ruilin Huang, Liquan Shen, Zhen Tian, Xia Hua

entry.summary: Proposes a Swin Transformer-based framework that predicts missing 45, 90, and 135 degree polarization views from a single 0-degree observation, using cross-angle feature interaction and residual decoding, reducing the need for specialized multi-angle polarization hardware.

entry.title: K-AoI: A Spatio-Temporal Synchronization Metric for Digital Twin-based Teleoperation in Dynamic Network Environments

author.name: Lu Tian, Zhenhui Yuan, Zexin Deng, Wenjuan Zhang

entry.summary: K-AoI (Kinematic Age of Information) is a spatio-temporal synchronization metric that weights temporal staleness by instantaneous Cartesian velocity, translating network delay into physically meaningful spatial divergence between a digital twin and its physical robot. It is evaluated on a 6-DOF manipulator teleoperation testbed under controlled network impairments.

entry.title: Suffering Risks Belong in AI Prospectuses

author.name: James_Miller

entry.summary: The author argues that Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus should disclose s-risk (risks of AI-inflicted mass suffering) alongside extinction risks, invoking Regulation S-K Item 105 and the Basic v. Levinson materiality standard. The legal argument is that even a small credible risk of catastrophic suffering could materially affect investor decisions and company valuation.

entry.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Comparison of Proportional Control and Adaptive Gravity Compensation in Elbow EMG-Driven Exoskeletons

author.name: Francesco Pascucci (University of Verona, Italy), Eldison Dimo (University of Verona, Italy), Davide Costanzi (University of Verona, Italy), Mario Sedilesu (University of Verona, Italy), Andrea Calanca (University of Verona, Italy)

entry.summary: This study systematically compares five EMG-driven elbow exoskeleton control algorithms in human-in-the-loop experiments: two proportional myoelectric control variants at different assistance levels, integral adaptive gravity compensation, and kinematics-aware model-based adaptive gravity compensation. It addresses the stability-versus-assistance trade-off of PMC at high assistance.

entry.title: Screening LLM Judges Without Ground Truth: A Preliminary Evaluation of an AI Dental Hygiene Coach

author.name: William DeShong, Barath Kannan, Auberon Palma, Brenda Bradshaw, James F. Leathrum, Jr., Yuzhong Shen

entry.summary: This paper presents a staged pipeline for screening candidate LLM judges and fine-tuned student models before costly expert review, using decision rules around judge audits, similarity checks, bias checks, and robustness. It is demonstrated on an AI dental hygiene coach with synthetic data using Granite-4.1-8B and Qwen3-8B models. The authors are explicit that clinical performance is not established.
