entry.summary: The paper uses machine learning to predict the failing RED4 spectral channel of the HiRISE Mars camera, which since 2023 has intermittently created gaps and halved the instrument's color-imaging capability. The approach restores synthetic color-infrared imagery beyond the existing SYN4 pipeline. This is a practical ML application maintaining the science return of an aging planetary instrument.

entry.title: Regularized free deconvolution for spectral repair of resampling distortion in high-dimensional particle filters

author.name: Deming Song, Chi-Kin Lam, Kefeng Li, Hui Yu, Xilin Li, Huagang Lin

entry.summary: This paper studies how resampling in high-dimensional particle filters distorts the ensemble covariance spectrum and constructs a regularized free-deconvolution estimator to recover the pre-resampling spectrum from observed weights alone. It proves consistency with an explicit error budget and certifies model mismatch. This is a sophisticated statistical contribution to sequential Monte Carlo methods.

entry.title: GRAFT-EEG: Gauge-Aware Physical Field Transport for Cross-Dataset Motor-Imagery EEG

author.name: Ying Zhou, Mengting Liu

entry.summary: This paper reframes cross-dataset EEG decoding by treating changes in montage, reference, and active sensors as changes to the observation operator rather than mere representation shift. The method removes the active-set common-reference gauge and transports signals through a template leadfield with a source-fitted spectral classifier, evaluated target-statistics-blind across five leave-one-dataset-out targets covering 253 participants, reaching about 60.9% accuracy. It includes identifiability and perturbation bounds.

entry.title: Logic-Guided Graph Denoising Diffusion Models

author.name: Samuel Cognolato, Luciano Serafini, Alessandro Sperduti, Andrea Cavallaro

entry.summary: The authors propose grounding graph diffusion models in First Order Logic constraints via classifier guidance, steering the generative process to satisfy strict structural constraints that diffusion models otherwise violate. This combines the expressiveness of FOL with the flexibility of diffusion-based graph generation. It addresses the practical failure mode of invalid graph samples under hard constraints.

entry.title: Physics-Transfer Learning: A Physics-Constrained Theory for Zero-Shot Generalization Along the Ladder of Complexity

author.name: Yingjie Zhao, Zhiping Xu

entry.summary: This work proposes physics-transfer learning, a theory for zero-shot out-of-distribution generalization built on chains of anchor domains that progress from tractable physical idealizations to high-fidelity mechanisms. Rather than distribution alignment or invariance assumptions, it leverages progressively incorporated physical mechanisms to bridge domain shifts.

entry.title: Source-Aware Dynamic Pricing with Strategic Buyers

author.name: Jinjiang Zou, Yang Li, Zemin Zheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a source-aware contextual dynamic pricing framework that distinguishes verified seller-record features from strategically manipulable self-reported buyer features in a high-dimensional semiparametric setting. The SALE policy combines localized exploration and calibrated exploitation, with theoretical guarantees under sparse linear valuations and unknown noise.

entry.title: Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation

author.name: Zhenwei Tang, Jintao Liu, Di Bai, Xidong Wu, Xinwu Cheng

entry.summary: Builds ReRankID, a controlled testbed for LLM-based reasoning rerankers that rank candidate slates represented only as compact Semantic IDs rather than item text, probing whether generative-recommender training transfers behavioral signal into SID token embeddings. The work tests shorter prompts and SID-embedded behavioral cues as replacements for full metadata in reranking.

entry.title: What Shapes Brain Alignment of Large Language Models during Dialogue? Insights from Language Production and Comprehension

author.name: Yuko Nakagi, Yuya Chiba, Yasue Kishino

entry.summary: Uses fMRI data collected during natural dialogue to examine LLM-brain alignment in both language production and comprehension, across LLM layers and brain regions. It links alignment patterns to the intrinsic dimension of LLM representations and interpretable linguistic and communicative features, extending beyond prior passive-comprehension studies.

entry.title: CIIR - Class-Indexed Interface Representation Learning

author.name: Doo Yon Kim, Christian Wallraven

entry.summary: CIIR is a modular encoder-decoder framework that aligns heterogeneous, independently collected datasets through a class-indexed address space, without paired or synchronized samples. The authors demonstrate learning a shared address space across handwritten digits, clothing images, spoken-digit spectrograms, and hand signs, with label-free receivers recovering addresses at about 94.7% accuracy.

entry.title: From Parallels to Divergence: Language Models' Learning of Action Nominal Constructions

author.name: Iskar Deng, Shane Steinert-Threlkeld

entry.summary: Using grammar-engineered synthetic corpora spanning 96 target languages varying in word order, alignment, complement systems, and action-nominal strategies, the authors train GPT-2-small models from scratch to study how grammatical configuration affects learning of action nominal constructions. They compare model learning preferences with typological distributions in natural languages.

entry.title: ToMStories: Interpreting Theory-of-Mind in Synthetic Narratives

author.name: Melanie Subbiah, Chia-En Jacklyn Tsai, Kathleen McKeown

entry.summary: Introduces ToMStories, ~6,000 synthetic narrative vignettes probing whether models can infer characters' emotions, fears, motivations, and emotional wounds from implicit versus explicit cues or dialogue-description conflicts. Evaluating thirteen open-weight models (1B-72B), the largest models match humans on multiple choice but not open-ended questions.

entry.title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory For Long-Horizon Embodied Agents

author.name: Chloe Su, Jiahan Li, Zhenting Qi, Chaoran Cheng, Haoyu Chen, Sejoon Jun, Weirui Ye, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Proposes MFM, a multimodal filesystem memory architecture for long-horizon embodied agents that maintains episodic, spatial, semantic, procedural, and working memory types in complementary filesystem stores. The design preserves visual and spatial details that summarization-based memory compression loses, enabling experience reuse across long interactions.

entry.title: Recognizing Atari and Assessing Sente: Controlled Evaluation Tasks for Language-Based Go Agents

author.name: Taiyi Chen, Iskar Deng, Amandalynne Paullada

entry.summary: The paper builds controlled evaluation tasks for language-based Go agents around the concepts of atari and sente, testing whether a fine-tuned Go language model (LoGos) can recognize board-state terminology and relate it to move evaluation. The model struggles to track atari changes and its terminology predictions are decoupled from sound move preferences, exposing shallow understanding of strategic concepts.

entry.title: Who Pays for Efficient Inference? Confidence-Based Small-to-Large LLM Routing Across Tasks and Languages

author.name: Md Sabbir Hossen, Anichur Rahman, Pabon Shaha, Airin Afroj Aishi, Andrew H. Sung, Md Shohel Rana

entry.summary: This is a systematic evaluation of confidence-based small-to-large model routing across three model families, four languages, three task types, 72 configurations, and over 42,000 predictions, comparing against random, equal-quota, and oracle baselines. It finds confidence reliably identifies beneficial escalations on some tasks but its reliability across multilingual settings is uneven. The paper clarifies when cheap routing strategies actually pay off.

entry.title: Revealing the Impact of Visual Text Style on Attribute-based Descriptions Produced by Large Visual Language Models

author.name: Xiaomeng Wang, Martha Larson, Zhengyu Zhao

entry.summary: This study investigates whether the visual style of rendered text (functional readability-oriented styles versus decorative display-oriented styles) changes how Large Visual Language Models describe the referenced concept. The findings show style can perturb LVLM attribute descriptions even though word meaning should be style-invariant, revealing a robustness gap.

entry.title: Can AI interview? Comparing AI-led to Human-led Chat Interviews

author.name: Semra Guven, Tobias G{\aa}rdhus, Andreas Bjerre-Nielsen, Anna Rogers, Hjalmar Bang Carlsen

entry.summary: In a randomized experiment (N=41), the authors compare qualitative data quality from AI-led versus human-led synchronous text chat interviews with university students, measuring exposure, specificity, and relevance. AI interviewers asked more than twice as many questions and elicited roughly 65 percent more of some quality metrics, offering the first direct empirical comparison for AI as qualitative interviewer.

entry.title: Enhancing RAG-based Medical VQA with Gated Multimodal Representations

author.name: Daniela Jimenez-Pano, Hugo Jair Escalante, Delia Iraz\'u Hern\'andez-Far\'ias

entry.summary: This work proposes a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation framework for medical visual question answering in which a Gated Multimodal Unit fuses medical images and clinical questions into a joint query representation for evidence retrieval. Because the underlying medical LVLM stays frozen, the approach is parameter-efficient and avoids costly fine-tuning. Benchmark evaluations show that multimodally guided retrieval outperforms single-modality retrieval in grounding medical VQA responses.

entry.title: PresenceBench: An Exploratory Evaluation of Large Language Model Adaptation to User State

author.name: Pe\~na Arroyo Gallego, Mauro Ruiz Moreno, Alejandro Acien, Sergio Romero-Tapiador, Teresa Arroyo-Gallego

entry.summary: PresenceBench measures presence-aware intelligence: an LLM's ability to adapt responses to a user's functional state such as readiness, flow, and stability while preserving task quality and safety. It tests two properties — receptivity (does the state improve responses?) and specificity (does the improvement depend on the correct state?) — while leaving cross-state adaptation as future work. The benchmark evaluates use of a supplied state rather than sensing it.

entry.title: KFS$^4$LAM: Adaptive KeyFrame Selection with Structure-Aware Mapping for Endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Xinwei Ju, Zhehua Mao, Tianyi Song, Danail Stoyanov, Sophia Bano, Francisco Vasconcelos

entry.summary: This paper presents KFS4LAM, an adaptive keyframe selection method for Gaussian-splatting SLAM in colonoscopy, where non-uniform motion, repetitive anatomy, and specularities break fixed-interval or simple pose-based selection criteria. Structure-aware mapping selects informative keyframes, improving localization, reconstruction, and rendering quality. The work targets surgical robotics and medical imaging applications.

entry.title: HilbertGen-3D:Hilbert--Multifractal Conditioning for Topology-Aware 3D Generation

author.name: Ziyi Zhang, Shixuan Li, Yorie Nakahira, Paul Bogdan, Guannan Qu

entry.summary: HilbertGen-3D introduces Hilbert-Multifractal Conditioning for conditional diffusion-based point cloud generation, serializing multi-scale voxel measures along a 3D Hilbert curve to capture global structural organization. This targets the common weakness of local voxel/patch features missing topology in 3D generative modeling for games, medical imaging, and VR/AR.

entry.title: Frame-Consistent Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Unposed Images

author.name: Viruthshaan Vinasirajan, Ranga Rodrigo

entry.summary: The authors analyze two-stage feed-forward Gaussian splatting pipelines that pair a frozen pose estimator with a frozen reconstruction backbone, challenging the common attribution of quality degradation to noisy poses. Their findings clarify the true source of degradation in such pipelines and inform how to build faster, more reliable novel view synthesis from sparse unposed images. This contributes to the rapid field of instantaneous 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds

author.name: Ching-Heng Cheng, Chia-Ming Lee, Ming-Ching Chang, Xin Li, Yu-Lun Liu, Chih-Chung Hsu

entry.summary: FlashReFocus enables interactive post-capture refocusing by observing that recovering an all-in-focus image is ill-posed and needs a generative prior, while rendering blur is largely determined by depth and focal plane. It runs a one-step diffusion deblurrer once per photograph, then renders every subsequent focal or blur edit with a lightweight network, achieving second-scale interactivity. This design avoids rerunning large diffusion models per edit.

entry.title: From Adult Renal Masses to Pediatric Wilms Tumors: Evaluating Cross-Domain Generalization of Kidney Lesion Segmentation on MRI

author.name: Sarah de Boer, Myrthe A. D. Buser, Hartmut H\"antze, Jawed Nawabi, Lisa C. Adams, Alida F. W. van der Steeg, Marry M. van den Heuvel-Eibrink, Annemieke S. Littooij, Keno K. Bressem, Mathias Prokop, Alessa Hering

entry.summary: Evaluates whether kidney lesion segmentation models trained on large adult renal MRI datasets generalize to rare pediatric Wilms tumors, comparing against a pediatric-specific nnU-Net using Dice and Hausdorff metrics. The study provides empirical evidence on cross-domain, cross-population transfer in a clinically important low-data setting.

entry.title: FedRAPP: Federated Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models with Reliability-Aware Prompt Personalization

author.name: Syed Md. Ahnaf Hasan, Md Akil Raihan Iftee, Sajib Mistry, Amin Ahsan Ali, AKM Mahbubur Rahman

entry.summary: Explores source-free federated test-time prompt tuning for CLIP-style VLMs, where clients adapt prompts on unlabeled non-IID target data without sharing raw data. FedRAPP adds reliability-aware prompt personalization to counter prompt drift caused by heterogeneous client distributions during federated aggregation.

entry.title: An Agentic ENF Framework for Forensic Video Authentication Against Generative AI

author.name: Ryan Wyton (Southampton Solent University), Bacha Rehman (Southampton Solent University)

entry.summary: Develops a forensic framework authenticating video via the electric network frequency (ENF) signal in audio and rolling-shutter video flicker, a signal generative models do not control. It uses a unified two-channel detector, synthetic-injection training based on an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model, and reference matching to verify claimed recording times.

entry.title: LGGS: Longitudinal MRI Reconstruction via Guided Group Sparsity

author.name: Nikola Janju\v{s}evi\'{c}, Hersh Chandarana, Yao Wang, Li Feng

entry.summary: Proposes an interpretable deep-learning framework that exploits prior MRI scans of the same patient to accelerate current-exam reconstruction, addressing inter-visit misregistration, pathological changes, and phase variation through longitudinal guided group sparsity. Accelerated MRI reconstruction has broad clinical relevance given scan-time costs.

entry.title: FCTS: Failure-Guided Curriculum Tree Search Over Generated Terrain for Legged Parkour

author.name: Narayanan Palghat Parameswaran (Carnegie Mellon University), Dong-Ki Kim (FieldAI), Jay Patrikar (FieldAI), Santiago Gutierrez (FieldAI), Harshad Zade (FieldAI), Shayegan Omidshafiei (FieldAI), Harmish Khambhaita (FieldAI)

entry.summary: FCTS is a failure-conditioned terrain curriculum framework for quadruped parkour that uses localized traversal failures to automatically generate the terrains a policy should train on next, addressing the gap between canonical training obstacles and irregular industrial or disaster-site geometry. It improves on hand-designed curricula and LLM-generated curricula that offer little control over targeted weaknesses.

entry.title: FLoTS-SLAM: Optical Flow-Derived Uncertainty for Monocular Dynamic SLAM with Two-Stage Optimization

author.name: Haorui Du, Lipu Zhou

entry.summary: FLoTS-SLAM estimates motion uncertainty directly from optical flow rather than rendering residuals or multiview inconsistency, providing direct motion evidence for dynamic-object identification in monocular RGB SLAM. A two-stage optimization prevents inaccurate uncertainty from corrupting pose estimation and reconstruction during bundle adjustment.

entry.title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline

author.name: Muhammad Usman Altaf

entry.summary: This paper argues that rank-based characterizations of fine-tuning weight updates require baselines, comparing measures against random matrices, pretrained weights, and matched non-alignment fine-tunes across thirteen released model pairs up to 8B parameters. It shows low-rank counts sit barely below noise while stable rank sits far below, both correct since updates have a few strong directions atop a long tail, and that instruction tuning is not distinctive from Wikipedia or code under fixed training.

entry.title: Noise-Robust Forced Alignment for Spontaneous Speech

author.name: Laurin Wagner, Mario Zusag

entry.summary: The paper shows that forced aligners degrade on spontaneous, noisy speech where fillers, laughter, and disfluencies corrupt word boundaries, and rebuilds a GMM-HMM aligner using upsampled WavLM features, explicit units for non-lexical vocal events, and a discriminative projection trained on clean/noisy feature pairs. The self-bootstrapped pipeline (149h of audio) achieves word-boundary MAEs of 20.6 and 76.9 ms on Buckeye and FluencyBank, 19 and 17 percent better than the strongest alternatives.

entry.title: Learning to Be Guided: Shaping Latent Geometry for Classifier-Free Guidance

author.name: Haoming Liu, Junhao Zhu, Shaoyi Zheng, Yuanhe Guo, Jinnuo Liu, Shenji Wan, Hongyi Wen

entry.summary: This paper studies how class arrangement in latent space (class geometry) affects classifier-free guidance in latent diffusion models, showing under a Gaussian class model that shifting variance from intra- to inter-class makes classes more distinguishable under noise. It derives conditions for latent spaces that work well with CFG, connecting latent-space learning to guided generation quality.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware AI-enabled framework for predicting hydrogen dispersion in confined spaces to enhance operator situational awareness

author.name: Niclas Flehmig, Mary Ann Lundteigen, Shen Yin

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-stage AI framework for maritime hydrogen bunkering safety: it first estimates leakage rate from early sensor readings, then forecasts hydrogen cloud dispersion with confidence bounds to support operator decisions. The system is designed as a decision-support tool enabling preventive safety barriers before hazardous concentrations form. It applies uncertainty-aware AI to an emerging energy-safety application.

entry.title: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tianmeng Hu, Biao Luo, Ke Li

entry.summary: CocoRNA is a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for RNA inverse design, decomposing the task of designing sequences that fold into target secondary structures into sub-problems solved collaboratively by multiple agents with a centralized critic using global structural information. The approach reduces problem complexity and improves exploration, generalizing effectively to unseen targets. It applies MARL to an important computational biology problem.

entry.title: How Murky Before a VLM Knows It Cannot See? Accuracy, Confidence and Abstention on a Physical Visibility Axis

author.name: Mochamad Rizal Fauzan, Irgi Surya

entry.summary: Evaluates accuracy, token-probability confidence, verbalized confidence, and abstention for five small open VLMs on a physically grounded visibility axis, using Koschmieder fog and underwater absorption models with metric depth maps swept over eight log-spaced visibility levels. The study tests whether model confidence tracks genuine loss of visibility on COCO object identification.

entry.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning

author.name: Ashray Saxena, Sharad Shrivastava

entry.summary: The authors map the folded transonic flutter boundary of Isogai's case A aerofoil using coupled unsteady Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate trained via batch active learning, and split conformal prediction to produce stability calls with distribution-free error guarantees. They also document failure modes of time-domain damping labels and provide a physical explanation via shock energy transfer.

entry.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups

author.name: Markus Fischer, Jens Meiler, Matthias Elgeti

entry.summary: Munin is an open-source, self-hosted scientific assistant that indexes a research group's corpus and citation graph and wraps any servable open-weight model in an agent harness with reading, search, and computation tools, keeping unpublished data local. On 199 paired literature questions the harness more than compensates for weaker models, supporting the claim that the harness rather than the model drives usefulness. It ships with its evaluation suite.

entry.title: VTrajEmbed: Aligning Text with Video Object Trajectories via Spatiotemporal Embeddings

author.name: Ruizhi Chen, Zining Fan, Yudi Guo, Jiang Liu, Zhiyu Lin, Zhongjiang He, Shouqian Shi, Hao Sun

entry.summary: VTrajEmbed decomposes video into object trajectories and aligns each trajectory embedding with text for object-level grounding via retrieval, using a Slow-Fast dual-branch trajectory encoder combining dense low-resolution sampling for motion and sparse high-resolution frames. This overcomes the entanglement of global video embeddings for fine-grained trajectory-text alignment.

entry.title: UniPolar: Joint Image and Polarimetric Restoration under Compound Degradations via Physical Consistency Learning

author.name: Yang Jin, Guangyu Guo, Linghao Shen, Binglu Wang

entry.summary: UniPolar addresses polarimetric image restoration when device- and environment-induced degradations coexist, as in color polarization filter array imaging. The key observation is that improved image fidelity alone does not guarantee accurate recovery of polarimetric quantities like Stokes vector, DoLP, and AoLP, so the method enforces physical consistency during restoration. This couples image and polarimetric restoration under realistic compound degradations.

entry.title: CLEAR: Cooperative Latent Flow for Visual Counterfactual Explanations with Accurate Region Preservation

author.name: Yan Zeng, Changlu Guo, Oskar Kristoffersen, Anders Nymark Christensen, Morten Rieger Hannemose, Anders Bjorholm Dahl

entry.summary: Identifies two failure sources in latent-space visual counterfactual explanations — opposing update directions between generative and classifier guidance, and VAE reconstruction altering irrelevant regions — and proposes CLEAR, a latent Flow Matching framework using explicit instantaneous velocity to produce faithful, region-preserving counterfactuals efficiently.

entry.title: InstAgent: A Recursively Self-Improving Agent Operating System for Heterogeneous Robot Collaboration

author.name: Haoyang Luo, Junhao Qin, Jingyan Cao, Yi Huang, Guangjie Yang, Xiaoyu Chen, Haotao Lu, Tianxiang Gui, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: InstAgent is an agent operating system for heterogeneous robot teams that organizes behaviors as agentic behavior trees with explicit capability assignment, inter-robot dependencies, and handoff checks, while retaining execution-time corrections as reusable experience and maintaining task-relevant context memory across space and time. It aims at recursively self-improving multi-robot collaboration for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Multi-Terrain Adaptive Whole-Body Control for a Quadruped Manipulator

author.name: Yanzhou Jin, Fei Suo, Chang Liu, Yasuhisa Hasegawa, Liming Chen, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Yaonan Zhu

entry.summary: This paper presents an RL whole-body control framework for quadruped loco-manipulation on complex terrain, combining a hybrid task representation with task-prioritized learning to keep end-effector behavior task-consistent despite locomotion-manipulation coupling. A lightweight quadruped manipulator platform supports real-world validation.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting

author.name: Kamil Faber, Katarzyna Filus, {\L}ukasz Pawela

entry.summary: The authors introduce SAGA, which converts a sparse autoencoder trained at each task boundary into local, low-rank constraints on representation drift to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in continual learning. Replay examples determine where constraints apply, and leading right singular directions of the encoder Jacobian determine which changes are penalized, yielding input-dependent geometry that need not retain the SAE afterward.

entry.title: Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?

author.name: Bangji Yang, Hongbo Ma, Ruihan Guo, Jiajun Fan, Xi Zhu, Ge Liu

entry.summary: This paper tackles the cost of long rollout windows in RLVR by proposing Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement, which packs three independently verifiable problems into one capped completion so correct answers completed before truncation retain credit. A shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without explicit length penalties, with analysis connecting the mechanism to conditional reward- and update-variance.

entry.title: Deconstructing Multi-Task Active Learning: The Paradox of Gradient Conflict and Orthogonal Decomposition

author.name: Juho Jung, Seongjae Kang, Jinyoung Han

entry.summary: The authors argue that multi-task active learning methods rely too heavily on linear scalarization of heterogeneous objectives and propose a framework that deconstructs the problem along three orthogonal dimensions. They identify a Conflict Paradox: penalizing gradient conflict when ranking candidate samples is measurably worse than ignoring it entirely, contradicting optimization intuition. This reframing could improve active learning method design.

entry.title: Controlling the Diversity-Quality Trade-Off of LLMs by Merging Models Before and After Alignment

author.name: Yasuaki Sumita, Tomoharu Iwata, Toshiyuki Tanaka

entry.summary: Proposes a depth-aware FrankenMerging approach that combines lower layers of an aligned model with higher layers of its base model to control the diversity-quality trade-off without additional training. It rests on the hypothesis that lexical diversity is associated with certain depths, addressing limits of temperature sampling which mostly shifts lexical rather than semantic diversity.

entry.title: Interpreting SSL Representations for Spoof Detection: a WavLM Study

author.name: Mohamed Mallat, Michele Panariello, Massimiliano Todisco, Nicholas Evans, Anthony Larcher

entry.summary: This is a layer-wise interpretability study of WavLM for audio anti-spoofing on ASVspoof 5, combining per-layer linear probing across synthesis, voice conversion, and adversarial attacks, canonical correlation analysis linking layers to acoustic features, and a grid search over layer subsets. It finds that selecting five layers outperforms full thirteen-layer pooling.

entry.title: When Does Uncertainty Measure RAG Hallucination Risk?

author.name: Rajeel Ahmad Ansari, Tautik Agrahari

entry.summary: Analyzes when uncertainty signals such as perplexity actually indicate hallucination risk in RAG, showing they work only when retrieved evidence constrains the answer. Across four models on HotpotQA and SQuAD, perplexity reaches 0.81-0.91 AUROC on targeted unsupported edits, and detection quality varies non-monotonically with retrieval depth.

entry.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents

author.name: Ravil Mussabayev, Saveliy Zavertyaev, Dmitriy Parpulov, Andrey Savchenko

entry.summary: SIT-Eval is an adjustable framework for evaluating conversational agents through situation-based, interactive turn-by-turn dialogues, addressing the safety gap that static benchmarks underrepresent rare situations that become frequent failures at production scale. It navigates the trade-off between natural-dialogue realism and adaptive situation sampling for statistical coverage. It targets multi-criteria assessment appropriate to context.

entry.title: High prevalence of antagonizing rhetoric in trending topics on Twitter/X

author.name: Armin Pournaki, Eckehard Olbrich

entry.summary: This computational social science study distinguishes antagonization (portraying opponents as enemies) from legitimate criticism in political discourse and finds a high prevalence of antagonizing rhetoric in trending topics on Twitter/X. The work refines prior research that treated political negativity as a single dimension, with implications for understanding platform discourse health.

entry.title: UniField++: A Unified Agentic Framework with Loop Reasoning for MRI Field-Strength Enhancement

author.name: Yiyang Lin, Chenhui Wang, Tianliang Yao, Shuaibo Li, Zijun Sun, Yiming Deng, Yixuan Yuan

entry.summary: UniField++ is a two-agent framework unifying MRI field-strength enhancement across multiple transitions (64mT-to-3T and 3T-to-7T), pairing a VLM-based planner with a flow-matching enhancer and loop reasoning to reduce anatomical hallucinations in difficult brain regions. Unified learning lets both components exploit field-dependent image characteristics across tasks.

entry.title: FlexPart: Text-Controlled Semantics-Aware 3D Part Segmentation at Flexible Granularity

author.name: Yiqun Zhao, Jiachen Xu, Yihao Zhi, Yunfei Zhao, Zibo Zhao, Xintong Han, Chunchao Guo, Shenghua Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a unified framework for text-controlled 3D mesh part segmentation where users specify desired part names with location and shape clauses, achieving what-you-ask-is-what-you-get granularity. It overcomes the lack of multi-granularity training data via an automated VLM pipeline for generating supervision.

entry.title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning

author.name: Zhe Zhou

entry.summary: This work asks whether a model that previously learned a specific fact-binding retains a relearning advantage later, beyond mere familiarity with the entity, vocabulary, or format. Using matched counterbalanced histories (LEARNED, CONTROL, WRONG) in Qwen2.5-1.5B under rehearsal-free continual finetuning, it shows that prior specific learning measurably shapes later updates, which standard output-accuracy evaluation misses.

entry.title: Flat Loss, Evolving Features: Grokking in Modular Addition

author.name: Akash Kumar, Karthik Sankaranarayanan

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that ReLU networks on modular addition can maintain near-flat training cross-entropy at a positive level while hidden features keep evolving and held-out accuracy rises from zero to above 90 percent. It proves this coexistence via two finite-window theorems for one-hidden-layer networks, showing constant gains in Fourier fraction of hidden features under specific training modifications including weight decay and normalized output updates.

entry.title: Understanding Stability of Outer Nesterov Momentum on Stochastic Pseudo-Gradients

author.name: Nishant Sharma, Laura Gomezjurado Gonzalez, Ganesh Talluri, Sarath Chandar, Hiroki Naganuma

entry.summary: This work derives an exact mean-square stability criterion for Nesterov momentum outer optimizers in distributed training where workers take multiple local steps and send pseudo-gradients. Analysis on random quadratics reveals how batch size determines whether more local steps stabilize or destabilize outer iterations.

entry.title: Spectral Limits of Polynomial Graph Filters on the Long-Range Ising Model Benchmark

author.name: Amin Najafgholizadeh, Mohsen Afsharchi

entry.summary: The authors prove that polynomial graph filters, the linear core of isotropic message passing and spectral GNNs, leave an irreducible error floor on the Long-Range Ising Model benchmark because targets vary along spectral level sets where such filters are constant. Their exact predictions match adapted spectral network errors to within a tenth of a decade.

entry.title: OrderFlowDiT: Transport-Regularized Diffusion Transformer for Probabilistic Limit-Order Supply Forecasting

author.name: Jung Hun Phee, Tucker Balch

entry.summary: OrderFlowDiT is a conditional Diffusion Transformer for forecasting joint bid/ask volume-at-price fields over five-minute horizons, trained with an unbalanced optimal-transport auxiliary loss to capture price placement, total volume, and uncertainty simultaneously. It also proposes a full-field evaluation framework for distributional fidelity beyond summary statistics.

entry.title: Non-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems

author.name: Mohsen Amidzadeh, Lauri Viitasaari, Mario Di Francesco

entry.summary: The paper develops a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus yielding non-parametric optimality conditions for time-varying stochastic optimization with stochastic decisions. It supports a scalable deep-learning algorithm whose design is insensitive to parameterization dimension.

entry.title: Untrained CNN and coefficient-space regularization for joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography

author.name: Alfio Bozi, Anwesa Dey, Souvik Roy

entry.summary: This paper proposes a regularized data-driven framework for jointly reconstructing initial pressure and spatially varying sound speed in photoacoustic tomography, using frozen untrained CNN features with Tikhonov-regularized least squares plus a learned coefficient-space prior. It shows accurate reconstruction on held-out data and generalization to unseen phantom geometries. The approach avoids full network training while retaining data-driven priors.

entry.title: Boundary Detection for High-Dimensional Point Clouds

author.name: Abigail Hickok, Valerio Galanti, Osama Al Dalahmah, Andrew J. Blumberg

entry.summary: This paper proposes two methods for detecting boundaries in high-dimensional point cloud data under non-uniform density, high ambient dimension, and noise: one based on separating hyperplanes after local dimension reduction, and one measuring directional uniformity of local neighborhoods. The algorithms also output estimated normal vectors at boundary points and are validated on synthetic data plus real applications including spatial transcriptomics.

entry.title: Neural Expansion: A Unified Mechanism for How Deep Neural Networks Generalize

author.name: Chashi Mahiul Islam, Samuel Jacob Chacko, Mao Nishino, Canlin Zhang, Xiuwen Liu

entry.summary: The authors introduce Neural Expansion, a geometric framework characterizing generalization through expansion of directionally-selective ray coverage in input space, quantified by Generalization Intervals around training samples where predictions remain stable. They present extensive empirical studies across architectures claiming a unified mechanistic account of generalization. This aims to explain why over-parameterized networks generalize, a long-standing puzzle.

entry.title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling

author.name: Ying Cao, Yifan Yang, Junqiang Xia, Julia C. Mullarney, M\'ario J. Franca

entry.summary: The paper introduces AH-GNO, an adaptive-horizon graph neural operator that predicts bed elevation increments directly on unstructured meshes to surrogate expensive morphodynamic simulations coupling hydrodynamics, sediment transport, and bed updating. It adaptively selects history length and update interval based on evolving flow conditions.

entry.title: Upper bounds on the number of causal pieces in spiking neural networks

author.name: Dominik Dold, Dennis Elbr\"achter, Philipp Petersen

entry.summary: The paper derives two complementary upper bounds on the number of causal pieces in feedforward single-spike spiking neural networks, complementing prior lower bounds on approximation error. One combinatorial bound via poly-Bernoulli numbers applies broadly across spiking neuron models, of order exp(2(L-1)N log N), while a second bound exploits network structure.

entry.title: Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning

author.name: Yanming Zhou, Yuchen Liu, Ahmed H. Qureshi

entry.summary: Introduces a physics-informed neural framework that learns a reusable travel-time (cost-to-go) field for rigid-body motion that explicitly separates geometric constraints on translation and rotation. The learned field is paired with a sampling-based planner balancing goal progress with local motion difficulty for manipulation in cluttered environments.

entry.title: FederatedBytes: Tokenizer-Free, Byte-Level Small Language Models for Efficient Multimodal Federated Learning

author.name: Ali Sarabadani, Massimo Piccardi, Mehran Abolhasan, Farzad Tofigh, Ian Zhou, Justin Lipman

entry.summary: Presents FederatedBytes, a tokenizer-free byte-level small language model with linear attention that handles text and multimodal data (including images) with reduced compute and communication cost for federated learning. The design aims to make FL tractable for contemporary NLP and multimodal workloads while preserving client data privacy.

entry.title: Sentence-Level Topic Modeling with Lexical and Contextual Evidence

author.name: Federica Granese, Serena Villata, Charles Bouveyron

entry.summary: SentenceETM is a neural topic model that assigns topics at the sentence level, combining lexical evidence (word distributions via embeddings) with contextual evidence (Gaussians over sentence embeddings in topic-specific subspaces). This resolves the granularity dilemma between word-level probabilistic models and document-level transformer methods.

entry.title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces

author.name: Valeria Repetto, Stefano Melchionna, Romina D'Aurizio

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical characterization of the function class represented by IQP (Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial) quantum kernels, deriving a Fourier representation of the RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions. This connects feature-map and hyperparameter choices to the learning behavior of quantum kernels.

entry.title: Parametric Resonance in Primal-Dual Learning for Slowly Non-Stationary Constrained MDPs

author.name: Maxime Baelde

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes primal-dual methods for constrained MDPs under slowly non-stationary constraints entering through additive and parametric channels. It shows dual oscillation saturates at a floor in the additive case, while in the parametric case instability arises from a mismatch between primal and dual constraint estimates producing a parametric resonance.

entry.title: Literal Lock-In: How Test Language Shifts Literal Attraction in Typed Decision Models on Bengali Idioms

author.name: Adib Sakhawat, Syed Rifat Raiyan

entry.summary: Audits three non-generative decision models (encoder scorer, decoder scorer, closed API) on expert-annotated Bengali idioms via input interventions, showing that inserting an idiom's literal gloss as an option captures 65-96% of remaining errors. A model-by-language matrix reveals that this literal attraction is 1.9-6.4x stronger depending on the test language.

entry.title: Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries

author.name: Anna Mazhar, Seiji Maekawa, Nikita Bhutani

entry.summary: Presents BRIA (Branch-Inspect-Adopt), an agent that isolates candidate tool investigations in separate execution branches, then selectively adopts useful results into the main trajectory, avoiding failed attempts contaminating subsequent reasoning. The method targets tool discovery from libraries with thousands of tools where execution is needed to disambiguate candidates.

entry.title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Gokhan Ceyhan

entry.summary: ParetoChat is an LLM-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization that translates natural-language preferences into scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, and iteratively elicits feedback on candidate solutions via a multi-agent architecture. It eases the burden of stakeholders specifying numerical weights for conflicting criteria.

entry.title: AMEND: Constraint-Guided Multi-Agent Text Detoxification with Isolated Critics

author.name: Tianyu Wang

entry.summary: AMEND is an inference-time framework for text detoxification that decouples the task into role-conditioned proposal generation, isolated multidimensional criticism, and constraint-first selection to balance toxicity removal with semantic preservation. A lighter variant, AMEND Lite, limits search to at most one targeted repair round. It addresses the known problem where unconstrained scalar objectives let safety scores mask semantic loss.

entry.title: The Italian lawmaking process: a unified and structured dataset

author.name: Matilde Contestabile, Chiara Ferrara, Giovanni Parrillo, Lorenzo Emer, Andrea Vandin

entry.summary: The authors apply an LLM-based extraction pipeline validated against manual annotations to convert unstructured Italian parliamentary records into a structured dataset covering all 5,346 laws enacted between 1985 and 2026, totaling 101,413 dated procedural events. This resource enables systematic computational study of legislative processes.

entry.title: Star Light, Star Bright: Can Multimodal Models Parse an Astronomy Visual Question Answering Dataset Right?

author.name: J. P. Naiman

entry.summary: This paper builds a domain-specific astronomy VQA dataset of 2,001 partially synthetic figures — contour plots, real telescope images from NASA SkyView, and controlled fake sky images — with 47,357 questions, including realistic page-aging degradations. It evaluates several low-cost large multimodal models on these scientific figure understanding tasks. The controlled synthetic design allows precise diagnosis of what models actually parse.

entry.title: Input- and Feature-Space Correction for Cross-Hospital IHC Grading

author.name: Jongwoon Lee, Jhair Gallardo, Christopher Kanan

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks label-free correction methods for cross-hospital immunohistochemistry grading using frozen pathology foundation models UNI and Virchow2 across three markers and six directed hospital transfers. The proposed FIX input-space correction achieves the largest macro-F1 improvements over no correction and established alternatives.

entry.title: MaskMerge: Structure-aware Token Merging for Efficient Instance Segmentation

author.name: Bavesh Balaji, Letian Jiang, Alexander Wong, David Clausi, Sirisha Rambhatla

entry.summary: MaskMerge identifies cross-instance token fusion as a failure mode of feature-similarity-based token merging in instance segmentation, where same-class adjacent objects have similar features. It constrains merging using coarse intermediate mask predictions to preserve instance boundaries, evaluated on PanNuke and iSAID.

entry.title: TAN: A Size- and Form-Adaptive Masked-Convolution Encoder for Tissue Graphs

author.name: Jan Herschel, Anselm von Gladiss

entry.summary: Proposes an encoder for tissue graphs in computational histology that avoids bounding-box cropping and padding of superpixels, preventing background or fill-value leakage into node features. The paper shows that merely changing mask fill values shifts frozen-encoder accuracy on BACH by up to six percentage points, motivating the adaptive masked-convolution design.

entry.title: PreciseEdit: Strong Yet Stable Semantic Transport for One-Step Image Editing

author.name: Jingyi Wang, Xiao Lu

entry.summary: Addresses instability in one-step text-to-image editing, where global transport fields built from vector operations between conditional predictions can distort structure and drift the background. PreciseEdit revisits the transport formulation to keep strong semantic movement within edited regions while avoiding unreliable directions and over-conservative smoothing.

entry.title: Erase the Mark, Preserve the Motion: Temporally Consistent Removal of Video Watermarks

author.name: Yifan Liao, Zhen Sun, Zhicong Huang, Jiaming He, Zongmin Zhang, Xi Ai, Cheng Hong, Xinhu Zheng, Xinlei He

entry.summary: Proposes PoseRegen, a pose-consistent reconstruction attack for evaluating video watermark robustness, addressing flickering from signal-optimization removal and structural inconsistency from diffusion resynthesis. The work highlights underexplored robustness of video watermarks against temporally consistent removal attacks.

entry.title: Micro-Localization: High-Precision Mobile Robot Localization Using Microscopic Ground Texture

author.name: Aaron Wilhelm, Marina de Albuquerque Marcon, Emith Uyanwatte, Nils Napp

entry.summary: Demonstrates global localization of mobile robots at tens-of-micrometers precision using natural ground texture viewed through microscope optics, relating optical magnification to localization uncertainty. The system handles calibration, camera modeling, and focus challenges, achieving low translation RMSE across 1,007 held-out queries per surface.

entry.title: Expand-and-Prune: Test-Time Candidate-Space Adaptation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Fabian Schmidt, Karol Fedurko, Markus Enzweiler, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: Introduces a test-time framework for candidate-based end-to-end driving planners that expands the trajectory candidate set using semantic intent and temporal propagation, then adaptively prunes based on uncertainty in intermediate trajectory scores, all without updating learned parameters. It improves results across four planners and multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: DriveWorld3D Evidence Constrained 3D World Modeling and Generative Simulation for Real-World Autonomous Driving

author.name: Wei Wang (Robostreet research team Cambridge, MA, USA), Yiru Veronika Wang (Robostreet research team Cambridge, MA, USA), Yihan Wang (Robostreet research team Cambridge, MA, USA), Zihao Li (Robostreet research team Cambridge, MA, USA), Xiaohui Liang (Robostreet research team Cambridge, MA, USA)

entry.summary: DriveWorld3D combines temporal video learning, multi-sensor measurement constraints, and offline generative simulation to maintain a unified 3D world state for autonomous driving, including road surfaces, occupancy, and uncertainty. It addresses the key criticism that visually realistic generative world models can hallucinate content not supported by measurements.

entry.title: Spatial Memory by Agents, for Agents

author.name: Qianwei Wang, Ce Zhang, Zhanpeng Luo, Pengpeng Su, Shuo Yang, Hao Xu

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether coding agents can automatically design spatial memory systems for robots, with a Designer Agent writing and revising memory construction and retrieval code using feedback from a fixed Query Agent under a fixed development budget. Implementations are frozen before evaluation on held-out observation histories across five task tracks, avoiding contamination from downstream questions.

entry.title: F-LIVO: A Feature-Level Geometric Measurement Framework for LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry

author.name: Xinye Dai, Yapeng Wang, Shujie Zhou, Zihao Wang, Shiqi Zheng, Jiayu Hu, Yusheng Wang, Weiwei Song, Weiming Tang

entry.summary: F-LIVO is a filter-based LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry framework coupling visual-inertial and LiDAR-inertial subsystems through feature-level point-to-plane constraints, avoiding the storage and update costs of dense photometric map attachments. It recovers visual feature depth from the LiDAR map via local plane fitting and ray-plane intersection to preserve cross-modal coupling when triangulation is weak.

entry.title: MOSS: Multimodal Origami Swamp Robot System

author.name: T. Lan, A. Babgei, L. Romanello, M. Kovac, S. F. Armanini

entry.summary: Presents an amphibious robot for wetland monitoring that uses 3D-printed origami wheels capable of switching between contracted and expanded configurations via a crank mechanism. The wheel geometry adapts to terrain, with contracted wheels for firm ground and expanded wheels for soft surfaces. It matters for environmental monitoring applications where fixed-geometry wheels perform poorly.

entry.title: SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Sai Sandeep Damera, Ryan Matheu, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: Proposes lower approximations of min and max operators based on sparsemax projections for signal temporal logic robustness, proving both soundness and horizon-independent nonzero gradient allocation on violating samples. Existing smooth approximations such as log-sum-exp fail to satisfy both properties simultaneously. This improves gradient-based trajectory optimization for safety-critical systems.

entry.title: Cointegrated Regressors: Where Folded Concave Penalties Go Beyond LASSO

author.name: Hongqi Chen, Chengwang Liao, Ziwei Mei, Zhentao Shi

entry.summary: Shows that LASSO's convex penalty inconsistently estimates coefficients in high-dimensional predictive regressions with cointegrated regressors, and demonstrates that folded concave penalties like SCAD and MCP achieve both local and global oracle properties under suitable penalty-level constraints. This provides theoretical guarantees for sparse cointegration analysis. Relevant to economics and any field using high-dimensional predictive regression.

entry.title: Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients

author.name: Xiaoli Li, Qianqian Lei, Ziyang Wei, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: Derives exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear constant-stepsize SGD under infinite-variance gradient noise, showing how large gradient shocks transported through the local Hessian flow determine accuracy. The analysis connects to central stable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limits and applies for every available gradient moment above one. This quantifies when SGD behaves badly even when most iterates appear near the optimum.

entry.title: Coverage Cliffs in Off-Policy Quantile Certification

author.name: Pauline Bourigault, Emmanuelle Bourigault

entry.summary: The paper studies when logged contextual-bandit data can certify an upper-tail quantile for a policy selected from the same sample, constructing a PAC-Bayes Bernstein lower-confidence envelope simultaneous over a threshold grid and data-dependent posteriors. The TailCert procedure returns atom-safe upper confidence bounds on quantiles or an inconclusive verdict, and its main theoretical contribution is a matched finite-class certification boundary comparing full logs with subsamples.

entry.title: Diagnosing GNN Failure Modes with Layer-Wise Probe Entropy

author.name: Shanzi Bao, Mar Gonz\`alez I Catal\`a, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: This work introduces a post-hoc diagnostic for GNNs that freezes a trained model, fits a linear probe per layer, and tracks probe accuracy alongside normalized predictive entropy during message passing. Layer-wise probe entropy distinguishes beneficial, neutral, and harmful smoothing, and separates the two main GNN failure modes: structural mismatch under heterophily versus over-smoothing in deep models.

entry.title: Acquisition Function-Guided Generation for Bayesian Optimization over Discrete Spaces

author.name: Tommaso Ancilli, Thomas Wedenig, Henry Moss, Robert Peharz

entry.summary: The paper combines a pretrained generative model with a surrogate defined directly in data space for discrete Bayesian optimization, sampling candidates from the generative model under a distribution tilted by the acquisition function rather than maximizing it. This enables incorporating domain knowledge like structured kernels while avoiding expensive discrete search.

entry.title: LagNet: Lag-Structured Operators for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Zhenan Yu, Guangxin Jiang, Jiuyun Jiang, Jin Yang

entry.summary: The authors observe that sensitivity matrices across many forecasting model families exhibit recurring diagonal patterns corresponding to relative temporal lags, and build LagNet, a direct multi-step forecasting architecture whose LagLayer constructs Toeplitz matrices tying history-to-future connections with equal lags. This is a structural inductive bias derived empirically from existing models. It targets the long-term time series forecasting benchmark space.

entry.title: Distinguishability and Recovery for a Doubly Sparse Spiked Wigner Model

author.name: Ioana Dumitriu, JD Flynn, Zhichao Wang

entry.summary: Studies detection and recovery of a sparse rank-one signal in a spiked Wigner model with independently sparse noise, providing algorithms and theory across parameter regimes at constant SNR. Contributions include a leave-one-out quadratic thresholding procedure for support identification, exact recovery for Rademacher spikes via sign synchronization, and strong recovery via spectral refinement.

entry.title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits

author.name: Felix Frohnert, Adri\'an P\'erez-Salinas, Sebastian Lange, Marcus Schwaebisch, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Vedran Dunjko

entry.summary: The authors show that in data reuploading quantum circuits, encoding a fixed task-defined spectral query can change the hypothesis class over the varying signal by modulating how existing signal frequencies combine, without adding new sample-dependent information. They connect this mechanism to tasks based on nonuniform Fourier transforms.

entry.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making

author.name: Qiang Yan (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: Chinese Decision is a family of Chinese-language models that produce probability distributions over candidate decisions in a single forward pass by reading final-position candidate-letter logits and normalizing over valid options, supporting Boolean, categorical, and ordinal judgments without autoregressive generation. A completed 0.8B model was trained with distribution cross-entropy on 13 million decisions, with preliminary 2B RLCD checkpoints evaluated on CJ-Bench of 307,900 decisions.

entry.title: LiveSync: Iterative Self-Training for Lip-Sync Generation

author.name: Huaishao Luo, Huan Zhang, Guanbo Bao, Yinglu Liu, Youzheng Wu, Xiaodong He

entry.summary: Presents an iterative self-training framework for audio-driven lip synchronization in which a mask-based model generates pseudo training pairs and is progressively refined, closing the gap between random-reference training inputs and the aligned self-reference used at inference. The method preserves identity, head pose, and facial context while matching target speech.

entry.title: When the implementation matters more than the algorithm: NSGA-II and other multi-objective optimizers in engineering design tools

author.name: Luciano Ambrosini

entry.summary: Tests whether the name of a multi-objective optimization algorithm predicts results in engineering design tools, exposing a deterministic black-box building-performance problem to native optimizers in three Grasshopper plug-ins, canonical library implementations, and RBFMOpt. Four NSGA-II implementations differed by up to 5 percent in hypervolume, showing implementation details can matter more than algorithm choice.

entry.title: PCDFusion: Proposal-Context-Detail Bayesian Rendering for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion

author.name: Rui Liu, Lin Gu, Hesong Li, Ying Fu

entry.summary: Reformulates infrared-visible image fusion as local Bayesian posterior rendering, where fusion is governed by posterior action weights deciding when visible appearance should dominate versus thermal responses. PCDFusion provides an explicit local rule for modality contribution rather than direct mixing.

entry.title: GR-VIP: Geometric representation conditioning for precise visuomotor policy

author.name: Chanhwi Lee, Jiwon Seong, Eunje Choi, Hohyung Lee, Jongsoo Lee, Junyeong Bae, Inveom Kwak, Woosang Shin, Soohee Han

entry.summary: GR-VIP is a goal-conditioned visuomotor policy that conditions on geometric representations to achieve millimeter-scale terminal position and heading alignment, arguing that general-purpose pretrained visual encoders do not capture the fine-grained spatial differences between current and goal views needed for precise control. It targets zero-shot transfer across environments combined with precise docking-style control.

entry.title: Deterministic Bounds on Accuracy and Stability of Metric-Space Regression and Classification

author.name: Nina Maria Gottschling, Jakob Gawlikowski, Michele Caprio

entry.summary: The paper introduces a geometric framework that quantifies input-target ambiguity through average kernel size computed from data-dependent, model-independent feasible sets derived from worst-case noise. It yields computable, deterministic, non-asymptotic bounds on best achievable empirical error and accuracy for finite datasets, independent of the learning algorithm, covering metric-space regression and classification.

entry.title: Alert-List Concordance for Evaluating Imputation Strategies in ICU Sepsis Prediction

author.name: Priyanka Siddappa, Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma

entry.summary: This paper introduces alert-list concordance, an evaluation metric measuring whether different imputation pipelines flag the same high-risk ICU patients via Jaccard similarity of top-k% alert sets. It shows that pipelines with similar AUROC can produce materially different patient alert lists, exposing an under-measured reliability risk in clinical prediction preprocessing.

entry.title: Next Token or Vector? Learning How Far to Decode

author.name: Sai Sreenivas Chintha, Chidera Biringa, Rishab Sharma, Anusha Agrawal, Prachi Badarayani, Gemma Zhang, Nigel Boachie Kumankumah, Marco Ayala, Sulaiman Vesal

entry.summary: CADENCE is a decoding method that learns both what to draft and how far ahead to draft, using Gaussian prediction heads to represent future spans as latent vectors and a learned router to adapt prediction length to context with single-token fallback. The backbone verifies proposals and retains matching prefixes, aiming to accelerate autoregressive generation.

entry.title: TALLOP: Joint Optimization of Local Training and Communication Compression for Time-Constrained Federated Learning

author.name: Honoka Anada, Yafei Ou, Shinya Takamaeda-Yamazaki

entry.summary: TALLOP jointly optimizes local training workload and communication compression under per-round time constraints in federated learning, targeting straggler-induced delays in heterogeneous environments. Unlike prior work focused only on local computation, it treats communication as a co-equal bottleneck in communication-limited settings.

entry.title: SETAREH Transform: A Sorting-Assisted Haar-Wavelet Sparsification Method for Approximate Inner-Product Computation

author.name: Seyed Kamaledin Setarehdan

entry.summary: SETAREH is a Haar-wavelet-based sparsification transform that concentrates energy to enable approximate inner-product computation, targeting the memory-traffic and communication costs of repeatedly processing high-dimensional vectors in distributed and edge settings. It complements model-compression techniques by reducing the cost of the vectors themselves. The single-author paper is an efficiency contribution at the systems level.

entry.title: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding

author.name: Ying Zhou, Yaoxin, Mengting Liu

entry.summary: TriRouter is a routing framework for EEG motor-imagery decoding that handles sparse or corrupted electrode montages via three paths: discriminative preservation, mask robustness, and latent compensation, with a validation-calibrated router allocating contributions based on channel availability. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68 to 6.46 percentage points under increasing missingness on BNCI2014-001. This addresses a practical robustness gap for real-world brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations

author.name: Rafael Florencio D\'iaz, Julio Guerrero Garc\'ia, Elvira Romera Guti\'errez

entry.summary: The authors propose a variational quantum-classical framework for solving Lindblad master equations, representing the density matrix via purification to guarantee positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace, with exact gradients via the parameter-shift rule. They also derive an upper bound on the covering number of the compositional model class.

entry.title: Unifying Embodied Foundation Models via a Model-to-Policy Formulation

author.name: Xinyi Hong, Mingyang Ren

entry.summary: Offers a unified, architecture-agnostic probabilistic formulation for embodied foundation models, including vision-language-action models and world-action models, based on stochastic kernels. It characterizes these models via conditional output distributions and action-realization kernels that induce task-conditioned policies, and connects pretraining, post-training, and deployment in one framework.

entry.title: Beyond Latent Personalization: Integrating HRV-Conditioned Personalization via LLM for Interpretable Stress Detection

author.name: Wei-Hsiang Ma, Ya-Tse Wu, Hsing-Hang Chou, Chi-Chun Lee

entry.summary: The authors propose an LLM-enhanced stress detection framework that combines heart rate variability features with personal attributes through LLM-based semantic interpretation rather than latent representations, yielding human-readable descriptions of physiological responses. It reports a 29.9% relative MCC improvement over the strongest baseline on the TILES-2018 dataset.

entry.title: Cultural (In)Competence: Investigating Culture-Specific Stereotype Detection Capabilities of LLMs

author.name: Maximilian Splieth\"over, Jannes L\"otfering, Dominik Bachmann, Alexander Espig, Willem Zuidema, Katrin Schulz, Henning Wachsmuth

entry.summary: Systematically investigates whether LLMs can detect culture-specific stereotypes across languages, cultural contexts, and model factors, motivated by the fact that stereotypes are culturally mediated. The study finds disparities in detection capability tied to cultural knowledge availability, particularly for non-English and non-US contexts.

entry.title: Bengali Hallucination Detection with Retrieval and Programs: A System Study

author.name: Shamim Hasan, Samiya Ahmed Chowdhury

entry.summary: A system study of inference-only Bengali hallucination detection combining response-conditioned query rewriting, six hybrid retrieval routes, and task-specific model judging, with a router directing examples to a 27B judge or a 14B program-generating agent. It reports a high private macro-F1 on the Olikbochon Kaggle challenge and releases versioned code, predictions, and traces.

entry.title: Inferring L1 Backgrounds from L2 English with LLM Token Probabilities

author.name: Ahmet Yavuz Uluslu, Mark Gales, Kate Knill, Gerold Schneider

entry.summary: The paper approaches native language identification by scoring texts as continuations of prompt prefixes specifying candidate L1s using token probabilities from Llama 3.1 8B and 70B, evaluated on TOEFL9, WriQ 2024, and BULATS-L1. Token-probability scoring substantially improves on direct classification, especially for the 8B model, with the 70B model achieving state-of-the-art results. This shows LLM token probabilities encode subtle traces of a writer's linguistic background.

entry.title: HAPACT: A Benchmark For Human-Centric Physical Impact Localization in Movies

author.name: Youngrae Kim, Yejin Jang, Eunho Kim, Youjin Sung, Kun-Woo Song, Sangpil Kim, Sang Ho Yoon

entry.summary: HAPACT introduces human-centric impact localization, a new task localizing physical impacts temporally in video and spatially on the human body, with a movie-based dataset of over 2.8K video-query pairs and 20K+ annotated frames. It extends physical reasoning about humans beyond everyday contact interactions toward abrupt forceful events.

entry.title: ShadowCast: On-the-Fly Context-Aware Shadow Augmentation for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

author.name: Yechan Kim, Dongho Yoon, Jongmin Joo, JongHyun Park, Moongu Jeon

entry.summary: Instead of detecting and removing shadows in remote sensing imagery, ShadowCast synthesizes realistic shadows from segmentation labels of elevated objects and injects them during training to improve robustness of segmentation models. It infers image-specific cast-shadow directions by probing brightness around buildings and trees.

entry.title: Beyond Multi-Stage Pipelines: A Label-Correlation Ensemble for Multi-Label Retinal Fundus Disease Classification

author.name: Md Asif Uddin, Jannatul Ferdous, Asif Islam, Zobaer Mahmud Zisan, Promit Ghosh, Shah Ahafik Arman, Niloy Farhan, Rafeed Rahman

entry.summary: Performs a controlled comparison of three architectures — a three-stage gated cascade of eight models, a flat 39-output model, and a label-correlation model with learned label queries and a transformer decoder — on a unified 39-target retinal disease label space built from RFMiD and ODIR-K datasets. The study questions whether clinical-triage-style hierarchical pipelines earn their complexity.

entry.title: mmPencil: Toward Writing-Style-Independent In-Air Handwriting Recognition via mmWave Radar and Large Vision-Language Model

author.name: Yifan Guo, Zhu Wang, Qian Qin, Yangqian Lei, Qiwen Gan, Zhuo Sun, Chao Chen, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: Develops mmPencil, a system recognizing 3D in-air handwriting from mmWave radar by reconstructing trajectories with a multi-stage algorithm and mapping them to visual representations so large vision-language models can read them. It targets independence from predefined writing planes, styles, and small vocabularies in RF-based handwriting recognition.

entry.title: Hardware-as-Regularization: Enhancing Data Consistency in Imitation Learning via an Adjustable Passive Compliant Leader Arm

author.name: Hideyuki Ichiwara, Yushi Kaida, Hirokazu Ishida

entry.summary: This work addresses inconsistent joint-space trajectories from low-cost passive leader arms used for imitation learning data collection by adding a cheap passive joint module with a mechanical clutch and 3D-printed spiral spring that pulls joints toward a neutral posture. The restoring force acts as a physical prior equivalent to joint-space L2 regularization, reducing variance and improving kinematic consistency while preserving movement smoothness.

entry.title: TransNav: Transformer-Based End-to-End Navigation Method for Static and Dynamic Quadrotor Obstacle Avoidance

author.name: Jianghan Zhu, Zhuo Li, Yanjun Zhang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: TransNav is a transformer-based end-to-end navigation method for quadrotors that handles both dense static and moving obstacles using a patch-based point-cloud encoder combining local feature extraction with global context. A single integrated perception-navigation architecture directly predicts avoidance actions across diverse environments.

entry.title: Foundation Models for Autonomous Space Robotics: Architectures, Physical Adaptation, and Validation

author.name: Zizhe Wang, Jia Deng, Xin Lu, Zehao Jia, Yi Huang, Yao Zhu, Jianing Li

entry.summary: This critical review follows space-specific requirements through perception, prediction, planning, action, deployment, and validation for space robotics, emphasizing orbital manipulation and proximity operations. It argues that terrestrial foundation model benefits transfer poorly to space dynamics and constrained onboard operation, highlighting event cameras and physical adaptation as underexplored levers.

entry.title: Initiating Removal from Operational Symptoms in Federated Vehicular Networks

author.name: Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Qiang Duan

entry.summary: The paper addresses federated unlearning when a removal request is only a delayed on-road symptom that names no vehicle or round, proposing ATONE, which makes unlearning part of the FL aggregation rule. It projects driving errors and reported symptoms onto a subspace spanned by recent global increments and propagates contribution effects with curvature estimates, applied to connected-vehicle driving models.

entry.title: Network-Wide Freeway Speed Nowcasting and Forecasting from Sparse Fixed Sensors with a Probe-Supervised Graph Convolutional Recurrent Network

author.name: Ran Tu, Zihao Li, Arash Mirzaei

entry.summary: The paper introduces GCRN+, a graph convolutional recurrent network for nowcasting and hour-ahead forecasting of speeds across all 4,127 Dallas-Fort Worth freeway links using sensors covering only 15.6% of them, with a probe-supervised sparse sensing training scheme. It combines direction-aware kernel interpolation with diffusion-convolution to predict deviations from historical speed profiles.

entry.title: Towards a GraphNARX model for structural dynamics

author.name: George Tsialiamanis, Keith Worden

entry.summary: The paper introduces GraphNARX, a graph-based nonlinear autoregressive exogenous model for structural dynamics that encodes past displacements and forces as nodal attributes to predict next-timestep displacements. The graph formulation enables generalization across structures of different dimensions and inference of displacements at unmeasured nodes.

entry.title: Replay Pruning and Few-Bit Integer Inference for Hardware-Efficient Speed-Sign Recognition

author.name: Se Un Park, Kyungkeon Chung, Huigeol Kim, Junyoung Park

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage automotive speed-sign recognizer optimized for camera SoC budgets, using channel replay pruning (recording and replaying channel deletions on a parent YOLOv5n network followed by knowledge distillation) plus few-bit integer quantized inference. Replay removes 60.3 percent of parameters at parent accuracy and beats iterative pruning and from-scratch baselines across seeds.

entry.title: Who Do Perspectivist Models Predict Well? Annotator Agreement, Sparsity, and Performance

author.name: London Lowmanstone IV, Vaagishwaran Sivakumar, Anwesha Samaddar, Akul Mundada, Harnoor Kaur, Maria Gini

entry.summary: Studies how perspectivist NLP algorithms perform for annotators who are idiosyncratic or sparse in their labeling, curating the largest collection to date of perspectivist datasets with ordinal annotations. The work models the relationship between individual annotator divergence and algorithmic performance.

entry.title: Broad and Efficient PII Detection with Unified Labels

author.name: Andy Hsu, Konstantin Berlin

entry.summary: Trains a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based PII detector on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, addressing taxonomy conflicts and label inconsistency through relabeling under a unified schema. The system targets high-volume traffic with low false-positive rates at low deployment cost.

entry.title: Variational and Decomposed method for Mitigating Bimodal Bias in Robust Visual Question Answering

author.name: Yihan Zhao, Yuncheng Jiang

entry.summary: The paper investigates multimodal bias in VQA, showing counting and non-counting questions exhibit distinct bias mechanisms, and proposes that quantity information stems from the magnitude of multimodal features in specific dimensions. It then introduces variational and decomposed methods to mitigate this bimodal bias for more robust VQA.

entry.title: MLLM Frame Subset Ensembling for Audio-Visual Video QA and MLLM-based Reranking for Ad-hoc Video Search in TRECVID 2025

author.name: Andreas Goulas, Damianos Galanopoulos, Ioannis Patras, Vasileios Mezaris

entry.summary: This system paper describes the CERTH-ITI team's runs for the TRECVID 2025 Ad-hoc Video Search and Video QA tracks. The pipeline uses multiple vision-language models with LLM-augmented query rephrasing for initial retrieval, followed by a multimodal-LLM reranking stage that scores semantic alignment between candidate shots and the query. It demonstrates effective engineering patterns for combining foundation models in video retrieval benchmarks.

entry.title: STC-MGNet: Spatial-Temporal-Channel Attention-Enhanced Multimodal Graph Network for Pedestrian Intention Prediction

author.name: Yuanzhe Li, Meng Wang

entry.summary: STC-MGNet predicts pedestrian crossing intentions for autonomous driving using a spatial-temporal-channel attention-enhanced pose graph encoder over pedestrian pose sequences. Three parallel attention branches emphasize informative skeletal joints, observations, and ego-vehicle motion cues. The work targets safety in pedestrian-vehicle interactions by better capturing subtle spatiotemporal patterns.

entry.title: ADA 2025: A Multimodal Dataset for Water-Deficit Stress Detection in Sugar Beets

author.name: Piper Powell, Robert Franz, Amos Smith, Isaak Ihorst, Joachim Hertzberg, Martin Atzmueller

entry.summary: Releases a multimodal public dataset for detecting water-deficit stress in sugar beets, addressing the scarcity of public datasets for crop stress detection relative to disease and pest detection. The dataset includes multiple modalities, accurate metadata, many plants, and fine-grained sampling intervals to enable multimodal early-stress-detection research.

entry.title: The Collection of a Real-World, Large-Scale Dataset for Automated Skill Evaluation in Central Line Dressing Change

author.name: Ummey Tanin (Pam), Shannan K. Hamlin (Pam), Hsin-Mei Chen (Pam), Peizhu (Pam), Qian

entry.summary: Collects a large-scale real-world dataset for AI-assisted evaluation of the central line dressing change clinical procedure, motivated by the limitations of manual observation by educators. The work targets objective, scalable, and consistent assessment of clinical skills to help reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections.

entry.title: PASS-VLN: Passability-Aware Local-Command Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Cong Zou, Xiangsheng Shi, Xuanhui Wang, Fubin Wang, Guangjun Ge, Chao Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: PASS-VLN targets body-dependent local execution in vision-and-language navigation, grounding local navigation commands in physically executable motion under environmental and robot-body constraints, including passability and collision-free execution. It isolates these factors from long-horizon task planning to make navigation failures easier to attribute, addressing a blind spot in existing VLN benchmarks.

entry.title: PASS: A Trustworthy Precision Approach Simulation System for CAT III Integrity Algorithm Development

author.name: Lang Zhu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China), Xin Zhang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China), Yulong Sun (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China), Nan Liu (Flight Automatic Control Research Institute, Xi'an, China), Jiahe Shen (Flight Automatic Control Research Institute, Xi'an, China), Xiaodong Zhang (Flight Automatic Control Research Institute, Xi'an, China), Xingqun Zhan (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China)

entry.summary: PASS is a precision approach simulation system for developing CAT III navigation integrity algorithms, integrating configurable airport environments, prescribed trajectories, inertial simulation, calibrated stereo images, and continuous runway-relative ground truth in a unified temporal and geometric framework. It enables safe reproduction of visual errors and failures that are costly or impossible to collect in real approach flights.

entry.title: Online Constraint Optimization-Based Indirect-Adaptive Robust Control for Autonomous Vehicles with Unknown Friction

author.name: Yupeng Zhou, I-Chia Chang, Ziran Wang, Bin Yao

entry.summary: Introduces a two-layer control framework for autonomous vehicles under large friction uncertainty, combining an upper-layer constrained optimal trajectory planner with a lower-layer indirect adaptive robust controller that estimates unknown friction parameters. An estimation monitor guards against unreliable parameter adaptation. The goal is reliable tracking performance despite uncertain road conditions.

entry.title: Computing Fr\'echet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Ian McPherson, Mauro Maggioni

entry.summary: Studies computation of intrinsic Frechet means for data on an unknown compact Riemannian submanifold, assuming only a local sampler and an observation metric without knowledge of intrinsic geometry. The authors propose a graph-based iterative algorithm and analyze its convergence. This extends a fundamental statistical primitive to non-Euclidean settings such as Wasserstein spaces.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Spatial Kernels for Gaussian Process Distributed Port-Hamiltonian Systems

author.name: Tianyi Yang, Thomas Beckers

entry.summary: The authors improve Gaussian process distributed port-Hamiltonian systems with a structure-aware kernel design that removes irrelevant state coordinates and decouples state and spatial dependencies through a tensor-product covariance. This lets practitioners inject qualitative knowledge of spatial heterogeneity via kernel choice without an analytical model of the underlying physics.

entry.title: Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations

author.name: Xu Cao, Wenxuan Xiao

entry.summary: This paper studies how much of a scale-calibration update learned for one representation of a pretrained model can be transferred to another (e.g., floating-point to GPTQ-quantized) without recipient-side optimization. For a Qwen3-1.7B pair, bidirectional transfer retains 76.9-90.5% of recipient-specific calibration gains, with shuffled gains confirming learned structure.

entry.title: What Accuracy Hides In Learned Transformer Programs

author.name: Jonathan Lee, Narmeen Oozeer, Philip Quirke

entry.summary: Using Transformer Programs, which constrain transformers so learned computation can be extracted as readable Python code, this paper shows token accuracy can hide incorrect complete answers and missed failure modes. Program inspection and failure analysis also guide training-data improvements, yielding sequence-accuracy gains on several of nine algorithmic tasks.

entry.title: A Label Noise Robust Algorithm for Graph Data using Neighborhood Label Distribution

author.name: Pintu Kumar, Nandyala Hemachandra

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how label noise smooths neighborhood label distributions in graph-structured data, increasing entropy and reducing interclass distinguishability for GCNs. It proposes a Leave-one-out Entropy Node Scoring-based algorithm to achieve robustness to noisy labels on graphs.
