The paper formalizes Multi-Session Agentic RL, shows that broadcasting trajectory-level advantages across sessions is suboptimal, and proposes methods that distinguish per-session contributions.

entry.title: AbridgeKV: Compressing Long Reasoning into the KV Cache of Learned Pause Tokens

author.name: Jack Cai, Lijie Yang, Vasilis Kontonis, Dimitris Papailiopoulos, Shivam Garg

entry.summary: AbridgeKV addresses the memory growth of long chain-of-thought decoding by training models to compress each completed generated block into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens, then evicting the original block cache. Three design choices make the compression trainable and effective, allowing subsequent tokens to attend to the compacted representation instead.

entry.title: Perception or Reasoning? Diagnosing and Tackling Reinforcement Learning Bottlenecks in VLMs

author.name: Zeyuan Yang, Zhuohao Chen, Jiaben Chen, Yao Zhang, Maohao Shen, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: The paper introduces PARA, a method that attributes visual-task failures in VLMs to perception versus reasoning by measuring how many errors are recovered with better visual information versus a stronger reasoner. Across 4 VLMs and 17 multimodal benchmarks, it reveals model-specific bottlenecks and informs targeted RL interventions.

entry.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock

author.name: Ningxin Pan, Hanyu Li, Yeqing Shen, Ning Ding, Yehui Tang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces RealtimeBench, a benchmark of 180 tasks across six game types where the environment keeps running during agent inference, exposing failures of otherwise-correct actions that arrive too late. It also proposes TORSI, a two-timescale self-improvement scheme in which a slow teacher analyzes paused replays and writes reusable instructions for a fast student that acts without teacher calls during live gameplay.

entry.title: MSP: Modality Self-Play for Training Multimodal LLMs Without Paired Cross-Modal Data

author.name: Robert Moseley, Md Kaykobad Reza, Ameya Patil, Edward Ayrapetian, Salman Asif

entry.summary: Proposes Modality Self-Play, a training framework where multimodal models generate proxy textual descriptions of unseen modalities as semantic bridges, removing the need for expensive aligned cross-modal training data. This addresses a key scaling bottleneck for multimodal foundation models. If validated, it could substantially lower the data curation barrier for new modality combinations.

entry.title: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows

author.name: Shirley Anugrah Hayati, Patricia Anugrah Setiani, Ruizi Wang, Zhouyi Li, Khanh Chi Le, Young-Jun Lee, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Introduces Kolab, a dataset of 115+ hours of screen recordings of 50 professionals from 40 occupations collaborating with AI agents on realistic long-horizon problems, emphasizing interaction quality (e.g., plan revision) over single-shot automation. It addresses the gap between agentic benchmark performance and real-world collaborative effectiveness. A rich, ecologically valid resource for human-AI collaboration research.

entry.title: Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure

author.name: Pradipta Ghosh, Gaurav Mitra, Shripad Nadgowda, Akshil Shah, Junyu Liu, Canturk Isci, Syamla Bandla, Xinyao Hu, Onkar Deshpande, Anik Dasgupta

entry.summary: Diviner is an agentic root-cause analysis system deployed at Meta for incident navigation across large-scale distributed systems, organized around a four-stage reliability lifecycle. It addresses failure modes of generic LLM agents such as stale context, misinterpreting failed queries, and overloading observability services, using human-governed adaptation. It matters because it reports production-scale deployment of agentic RCA rather than a purely academic evaluation.

entry.title: QREF: Improving DeepSearch Agents by Aligning Search with Reasoning via Query Refinement and Evidence Filtering

author.name: Yujia Chen, Yuhui Wang, Junzhe Wang, Shihan Dou, Di Liang, Yujiong Shen, Yuhao Zhou, Zhiheng Xi, Ming Zhang, Senjie Jin, Jiayi Chen, Dingwei Zhu, Yajie Yang, Yuan Hua, Chenyao Lu, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: QREF is a plug-and-play framework for DeepSearch agents that addresses misaligned, under-constrained, and redundant search queries by adding a Query Refiner, which rewrites queries to match the current reasoning intent with complementary coverage, and an Evidence Filter, which retains only evidence relevant to the batch and overall reasoning objective. The refiner is initialized with supervised fine-tuning. This directly targets a well-known failure mode of retrieval-augmented reasoning agents and should improve evidence quality in deep search pipelines.

entry.title: AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations

author.name: Yuanjian Xu, Jinyi Han, Jianing Hao, Yuxuan Sun, Fanyang Lu, Richeng Xuan, Guang Zhang, Zhichao Hu

entry.summary: AgentPerturb introduces a systematic two-dimensional framework (perturbation targets and types) for evaluating LLM agent robustness in noisy real-world conditions. Evaluations on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon show perturbations consistently degrade frontier model performance, with trajectory analysis revealing agents rarely detect corrupted inputs and propagate errors.

entry.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Weijian Luo, Yujian Chen, Hao Jiang, Guang Cheng, Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: The authors systematically study Transformer architecture choices for continuous diffusion language models, which existing work has served with architectures borrowed from causal LLMs or image DiTs. They introduce LangDiT with feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing, and confidence-gated self-conditioning, reducing generation perplexity and setting a new state of the art in matched comparisons.

entry.title: Wrong Votes, Right Gradients: Why Majority-Vote Rewards Track Verifiable RL

author.name: Dylan P. Wilson, Chengsong Huang, Jiaxin Huang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper explains the puzzle of why majority-vote self-labeling recovers most of the gains of verifiable-reward RL despite wrong labels. The authors show the relevant unit is the batch-level update: a prompt's own gradient accounts for less than 1% of the change in its output at practical batch sizes, so label errors only harm when misdirection is shared across prompts. They decompose the majority-vote update into shrinkage and misdirection relative to the gold update.

entry.title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Jianchang Su, Dawei Xiang, Yifan Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces DIB-Bench, a benchmark of 7,560 scored examples across six tamper types showing that LLM-agent evaluation pipelines cannot detect tampered deployment stacks that preserve evaluated outputs. Counterintuitively, stronger LLM judges accept more tampered outputs (rising from 88.6% for rule-based scorers to 94.1% for GPT-5-nano), and a PAC-style bound formalizes that zero-output-shift tampers are fundamentally undetectable from outputs alone.

entry.title: Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense

author.name: Yushu Li, Jiin Woo, Xiaoxiao Li, Youngsuk Park

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how combining a primary reward with auxiliary rewards during LLM post-training can cause aggregate reward to rise while primary-task performance degrades when symmetric aggregation is used. The authors formalize the failure in a one-step multi-reward decision framework, prove convergence results for conditional-mean GRPO under symmetric aggregation, and propose a trust-anchored defense. It matters because reward hacking is a central alignment concern for RLHF-style training pipelines.

entry.title: In the Guise of Correction: How Framing and Cultural Adaptation Erode LLM Safety on Real-World Criminal Cases

author.name: Mohsinul Kabir, Md. Tariquzzaman, Karam S. R. Elradie, Polydoros Giannouris, Yuechen Jiang, Shaoxiong Ji, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: Introduces GUISE, a benchmark of criminal-assistance scenarios built from real-world cases organized under the UNODC ICCS taxonomy, evaluated across framings and five cultures. It finds unsafe compliance jumps from 28.9% for direct requests to 66.4% for correction-seeking framings, showing that benign framing alone can bypass safety training on serious crime categories.

entry.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos

author.name: Zhuoming Liu, Jinhong Lin, Lin Zhang, Yiwu Zhong, Yin Li

entry.summary: Proposes MaLoW, a streaming memory framework for vision-language models that internalizes historical video context into fixed-size LoRA weight updates via a recurrent HyperNetwork, instead of caching or retrieving past observations into the context window. This avoids competition between memory and current observations for limited context, enabling continuous video understanding without revisiting the full stream.

entry.title: Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning

author.name: Arnav Chavan, Kusha Sareen, Rishabh Tiwari, Abhranil Chandra, Johan Obando-Ceron, Kurt Keutzer, Scott Niekum, Inderjit S Dhillon, Devvrit Khatri

entry.summary: Introduces Subspace Tuning (SST), which restricts LLM weight updates to the bottom singular subspace of weight matrices, avoiding changes along principal directions and thereby reducing catastrophic forgetting. The work builds on the observation that on-policy methods naturally avoid principal singular directions while SFT concentrates updates there and forgets.

entry.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play

author.name: Botao He, Yiming Dou, Yiannis Aloimonos, Jitendra Malik, Akash Sharma, Ruoshi Liu

entry.summary: Presents DSP, a robot learning framework where a play policy is behavior-cloned from minutes of human play, then autonomously deployed to collect hours of interaction data for training a world model used in model-predictive control. The same play policy proposes candidate actions for MPC, and a closed-loop goal-conditioned policy is distilled via self-play within the world model. Evaluated on contact-rich tasks like pushing and in-hand pose reorientation.

entry.title: Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL

author.name: Skylar Zhai, Haonan Wang, Zhining Liu, Linxin Song, Xuwei Ding, Jingcheng Liang, Jian Kang

entry.summary: This paper proposes MRTPO, a method for multi-reward reinforcement learning of language models that assigns each verifiable reward's advantage only to the tokens relevant to that reward, rather than spreading it across the whole response. It builds on reward-decoupled normalization (GDPO) and requires no auxiliary models or token-level annotations, replaying responses with and without each verifier's information to localize credit.

entry.title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret

author.name: Mohammad Pedramfar, Siamak Ravanbakhsh

entry.summary: The authors formalize tilted sampling, an online learning problem where the learner must sample from the Gibbs distribution induced by an unknown reward, covering settings like entropy-regularized RL, RLHF, and reward-guided generation. They define sampling regret via temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence and show the problem unifies bandit and RL sampling formulations, achieving logarithmic regret results. This provides a principled theoretical foundation for diverse generative sampling systems.

entry.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories

author.name: Jiachen Yao, Xiyuan Zhang, Annan Yu, Boran Han, Abdul Fatir Ansari, Shuai Zhang, Michael Bohlke-Schneider, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: PathFM is a trajectory-level time-series forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths rather than marginal quantiles, preserving dependence structure needed for quantities like cumulative demand and peak load. It is distilled to one or two steps with shared attention caching, generating multiple paths in roughly the time of a single large-model query.

entry.title: A Phenomenology of Neural Geometry in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mozes Jacobs, Aiden Swann, Mathilde Papillon, Siddharth Boppana, Fenil R. Doshi, Usha Bhalla, Thomas Icard, Matt Feiszli, Thomas McGrath, Vasudev Shyam, Demba Ba, Leon Bergen, Nina Miolane, Owen Lewis, Jack Merullo, Ekdeep Singh Lubana, Atticus Geiger, Matthew Kowal, Thomas Fel

entry.summary: This paper studies the internal geometric structure of vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies, showing that task-relevant concepts are encoded as multi-dimensional, curved manifolds rather than single linear directions, shaped by physical constraints such as joint limits. Using probes, interventions, and controlled rollouts across seven concept types, it builds a taxonomy of how representational geometry relates to policy behavior. This matters for interpretability of embodied AI systems beyond simple linear probing.

entry.title: VisualTrust: Video Reasoning under On-Screen Claim Framing

author.name: Huachao Zhu, Junjielong Xu, Sicheng Li, Liang Yang, Mingtao Chen, Zhichao Hu, Li Jiang, Pinjia He

entry.summary: VisualTrust is a counterfactual benchmark of 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes that tests claim deference: multimodal LLMs letting on-screen text claims override conflicting visual evidence. Each video appears in no-claim, accurate-claim, and misleading-claim versions, and evaluation across seven open-weight and four proprietary models reveals systematic vulnerability to misleading framing.

entry.title: FeaTok: Feature-Loss Tokenization for Image Generation

author.name: Zhang Xiaofeng, Samuel Lavoie, Nicolas Beltran-Velez, Jianhao Yuan, Felix Friedrich, Jakob Verbeek, Aaron Courville, Michal Drozdzal, Adriana Romero-Soriano

entry.summary: FeaTok trains discrete image tokenizers by reconstructing pretrained self-supervised features instead of pixels, arguing that tokens should be easy for generators to model rather than merely enable faithful reconstruction. Motivated by feature-predictive self-supervised learning, it shows consistent improvements across SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINOv2, and DINOv3 feature targets. In class-conditional generation, FeaTok advances the quality-compute Pareto frontier.

entry.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient

author.name: Qiuhong Shen, Shizun Wang, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Velox is a training-free attention router for chunked video diffusion world models that selects region-level historical context using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry instead of ever-growing KV caches. This keeps long visual rollouts coherent while preventing the progressive slowdown of later chunks. It addresses a core bottleneck for interactive video-based simulation and world models.

entry.title: Fast-VLA: You Only Think Once for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Kehong Gong, Guanli Hou, Xiaoxu Zheng, Qi Wang, Mingxi Xu, Anbang Zhai, Xiaoyu He, Mingyuan Zhang, Michael Bi Mi

entry.summary: Fast-VLA accelerates vision-language-action policies by invoking a frozen 4B VLM only once per episode, caching its outputs as a fixed multi-layer key-value task memory, while a lightweight online actor fuses current visual and proprioceptive feedback to predict action chunks. Reported success rates around 92% on benchmarks suggest large inference savings with minimal loss of task performance, challenging the assumption that a large model must sit in the control loop.

entry.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Tianxing Chen, Wenwei Lin, Chuqiao Lyu, Peicheng Xiang, Junyuan Tang, Tian Nian, Zijian Cai, Kehe Ye, Chenze Yu, Wenxuan Zhu, Eric J. Chen, Yan Qin, Yue Chen, Tongyu Wu, Junhao Gong, Kai-Chong Lei, Jiahao Zhang, Kailun Su, Qiwei Liang, Renjing Xu, Ping Luo, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: Spark-0 is a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action model that uses tactile glove-derived contact maps and a frozen 3D geometry teacher to supervise visual tokens during pretraining, plus a tactile pathway encoding regional force histories and 3D taxel states to condition the action expert. A single checkpoint supports both vision-only and tactile-conditioned deployment, scaled via a large data collection effort.

entry.title: Who May Release an Agent's Promise? Standing over Commitments in Multi-Party Chat

author.name: Lan Wei, Bingyu Shen, Jiaqi Tang, Qing Lu, Kuan Huang, Meng Xu, Miles Q. Li, Bin Hu, Boyang Li

entry.summary: Defines standing in multi-party agent interactions: only the creditor or authorized parties may release an agent's commitment, and tests six models in a controlled chat environment separating unauthorized release from override errors. Results show large models drop promises on a peer's word (e.g., Qwen3.8-27B at 89%, gpt-6.1-sol at 83%) and nearly all comply with bystanders. Highlights a systematic, safety-relevant gap in multi-party agent behavior involving currently deployed frontier models.

entry.title: Open Benchmark of AI Impact on Humans (ImpactBench): an expert-guided, open platform for the holistic evaluation of AI impact on humans

author.name: Chayapatr Archiwaranguprok, Krystal Kirkland, Rachel Poonsiriwong, Stanley Huang, Constanze Albrecht, Jackson Trager, Emillie de Keulenaar, Sheer Karny, Peter Baxter, Nikos Bellos, Andre Luiz Freire de Carvalho Kato, Yuning Liu, Valdemar Danry, Auren Liu, Jennifer Pfister, Pattie Maes, Nathanael J. Fast, Ravi Iyer, Juliana Schroeder, Pat Pataranutaporn

entry.summary: ImpactBench is an open, iterable platform for measuring the multi-dimensional impact of generative AI on user wellbeing across psychological, physical, and social domains, translating expert-defined constructs and existing benchmarks into behavior-grounded metrics evaluated in simulated multi-turn conversations. It includes a notably large and interdisciplinary author team spanning MIT-affiliated researchers and social scientists.

entry.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards

author.name: Hasan Demirkiran, Jens Ernstberger

entry.summary: Builds LinguaGuardBench from TS-Bench AgentDojo-Traj, translating only user instructions into five languages while keeping tool calls and labels byte-identical, isolating language as the cause of guard verdict changes. The study tests six managed guards and finds that agent safety guards' decisions depend on request language, exposing a security vulnerability in English-centric guard design.

entry.title: Same Answer, New Box: How Much of RLVR's Out-of-Domain Gain Is Answer Format?

author.name: Zongye Lyu

entry.summary: Critically examines out-of-domain gains credited to RLVR (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards), showing that answer extractors copied from public code can inflate scores when models learn to place answers where the extractor looks rather than answering better. Using an extractor that reads stated answers anywhere in the text, the author finds roughly 82 percent of reported out-of-domain gains on 7B SimpleRL base-RL pairs may be format artifacts. This challenges a common narrative about RLVR generalization.

entry.title: Close Enough is Nowhere Near: Fidelity-Consumability Decoupling in KV Caches

author.name: Adam Deng, Shicheng Liu, Yada Zhu

entry.summary: This paper studies training-free substitution of one frozen LLM's KV cache for another in multi-agent communication and shows it fundamentally fails: a frozen transformer only accepts caches within a narrow tolerable set close to its own, and geometric similarity to its own cache does not predict usability. The key insight is a decoupling between cache fidelity and consumability, meaning more faithful substitutes are not the remedy they appear to be. This is an important negative result for the KV-cache-sharing direction in multi-agent LLM systems.

entry.title: Recursive Reward Improvement via Adversarial Meta-Prompt Evolution

author.name: Wei Dai, Qianchu Liu, Guanghui Qin, Xing Han, Tristan Naumann, Paul Pu Liang, Sheng Zhang

entry.summary: Extends proposer-solver recursive self-improvement loops to open-ended expert tasks like clinical report generation, where the proposer must also write rubrics. It addresses rubric exploitation by solvers through adversarial meta-prompt evolution. This tackles a real gap in applying self-improvement beyond verifiable domains.

entry.title: RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary

author.name: Johannes Knittel, Alec Helbling, Hanspeter Pfister

entry.summary: RoleQ is a quantization framework that places scales by the functional roles of Transformer units — readers from versus writers to the residual stream — rather than by weight-matrix layout, enabling ternary conversion without search, calibration, or stored state. In a rotated basis it matches per-layer axis search at half the solver cost, addressing the loss of factual knowledge and task accuracy typical of sub-4-bit quantization.

entry.title: Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Discussions

author.name: Liangjie Huang, Henry Peng Zou, Wei-Chieh Huang, Wooseong Yang, Yuwei Han, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: This study shows that multi-agent LLM discussion, assumed to catch individual errors, is highly vulnerable to conformity: in ten-agent factual QA discussions, a single adversarial agent repeatedly asserting a false answer raises the rate of benign agents privately holding the false belief from 0.6% to 44.8%, and three attackers to 60.5%. It separates private belief from public stance via hidden probes across six models.

entry.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?

author.name: Trizal Garg, Sibayan Mitra, Arya Karanjkar, Advait Singh, Jagat Sesh Challa, Yash Sinha, Siddharth Mehrotra, Dhruv Kumar, Pratham Yogish Maliya

entry.summary: This study tests whether evaluation awareness, in which LLMs behave more cautiously when they detect they are being tested, extends beyond English by probing four instruction-tuned models across five Indic languages plus English. Models refuse harmful requests more often when told they are being monitored as a safety test, with implications for the validity of non-English safety evaluations serving over a billion speakers.

entry.title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization

author.name: Sai Varun Kodathala, Prashanth Pollishetty, Jaylen Cargill

entry.summary: This security paper defines twelve attacks on agent approval paths, including decoy recipients, label spoofing, and threshold splitting, and tests them against the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), Microsoft's action-bound approval design, and MCP elicitation. An audit of ten agent runtimes finds no third-party verifiable approval records and no flood limits. The paper argues approval is a real second factor only when compromise cannot produce it and it names exactly what it approves.

entry.title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?

author.name: Subigya Nepal, Ruth Heo, Emma M Parrish, Colin A Depp

entry.summary: A cross-sectional audit of 2,550 scripted multi-turn conversations (September 2026) testing how five chatbots respond when users repeatedly refuse suicide-prevention referrals, finding near-universal initial redirection but widely varying persistence (0.01 to 9.94 refusals) and suggesting newer versions of all five tested chatbots persist differently. The study extends safety evaluation beyond the first referral response.

entry.title: Decentralized LLM Workflows via Sequential Auctions

author.name: Ian Gemp, Shubhendu Trivedi, Adam Fisch, Fantine Huot, Michael Kaisers, Mirella Lapata, William W. Cohen, Alekh Agarwal, Kate Larson, Jacob Eisenstein

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for multi-step LLM task solving via a decentralized market of self-interested agents organized through sequential auctions. It relaxes the restrictive perfect-clone assumption of prior theory, empirically showing that both excessive and absent competition cause market failure, and studies how heterogeneous agents survive between these extremes.

entry.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents

author.name: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li, Zhoumianze Liu, Kanzhi Cheng, Fangzhi Xu, Yanan Sun, Qiushi Sun, Yu Qiao

entry.summary: Presents OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space, motivated by findings that naively adding a code tool degrades GUI agents. Introduces application-artifact composition to generate hybrid supervision pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts for training native GUI/code routing.

entry.title: Lethe: Link Inference Attacks For Evaluation of Edge Unlearning Methods

author.name: Andrea D'Angelo, Francesco Gullo, Davide Mottin, Sayan Ranu, Giovanni Stilo

entry.summary: The authors introduce Lethe, a link inference attack designed to evaluate whether edge unlearning methods in graph neural networks truly remove the influence of forgotten edges. They identify systematic flaws in existing edge unlearning evaluations, including cases where dedicated methods are slower than retraining and where accuracy metrics are uninformative. This provides a much-needed adversarial benchmark for the graph unlearning field.

entry.title: CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty

author.name: Yuan-Chen Chang, Niklas Herbster, Gauthier Gidel, Tommaso Tosato

entry.summary: CATCH is a continuous adversarial training method that improves LLM honesty by training models toward honest answers and away from dishonest ones while preserving general capabilities. Using only hundreds of self-reporting scenario targets, the method transfers across Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and Qwen-class models and reduces contradictions with knowledge or context.

entry.title: Intern Lumina U2: A Multi-Codebook Diffusion Large Language Model for Omni-Visual Understanding and Image Generation

author.name: Qian Yu, Zongyang Qiu, Juncheng Yan, Hongliang Li, Qi Qin, Keqi Wang, Siqi Luo, Junkui Ju, Yapeng Mi, Tiantian Lu, Tian Liu, Pengyu Xie, Chenhao Ji, Minghui Zhang, Yiang Zhao, Siyu Yan, Haiying Xu, Yanbo Wang, Jianghan Shen, Yuandong Pu, Jiayi Lei, Borui Zhang, Jinxin Shi, Bo Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Shenglong Ye, Lixin Gu, Hongjie Zhang, Linghan Liu, Xinyuan Chen, Yuewen Cao, Lihe Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Junjun He, Qiangwei Liu, Qi Zhang, Yu Cheng, Tianfan Xue, Hui Xiong, Chang Xu, Yu Qiao, Yihao Liu, Bin Fu

entry.summary: Intern Lumina U2 is presented as the first diffusion language model using multi-codebook visual tokenizers to unify understanding and image generation in a single backbone, claiming to balance the representational capacity of continuous approaches with the text-modeling alignment of discrete ones. It addresses optimization conflicts from heterogeneous modality spaces by sharing one optimization space. Backed by a large team from the Shanghai AI Lab / Intern ecosystem.

entry.title: Can World and Action Modeling Benefit Each Other under Unified Causal Training?

author.name: Yue Su, Bokai Lin, Xinkai Wang, Chubin Zhang, Xiangnan Wu, Kuan Zhang, Weiyang Jin, Jiwen Yu, Yiming Li, Cewu Lu, Lixin Yang, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: OneWM is a unified causal training framework that treats actions as both conditions for world-model video prediction and targets for policy learning in a shared architecture. The authors systematically test whether forward-dynamics learning improves policy learning and vice versa, evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, and real-world robot experiments.

entry.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Hyunwook Choi, Seungryong Kim, Dongyoon Han, Sangdoo Yun

entry.summary: Speculative Forcing accelerates few-step autoregressive video generators by treating intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicting when individual tokens can be safely accepted early and frozen without further denoising. This exploits the observation that many tokens converge well before the final denoising steps. The approach transfers speculative-execution ideas from LLM decoding to video diffusion inference.

entry.title: Proof-based general-purpose computing with Magnetar

author.name: Srinath Setty

entry.summary: Microsoft Research introduces Magnetar, a zero-knowledge proof system that proves correct execution of programs written in Rust, Go, or C, running 10 to 39 times faster on average than the prior fastest comparable systems while relying only on standard hash functions for long-term cryptographic security. The post frames it as progress on the three grand challenges of practical proof-based computing: speed, accessibility, and durable trust assumptions.

entry.title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yixuan Xie, Xueqiang Xu, Xinyi Fan, Xinxi Lyu, Tao Feng, Xing Fan, Chenlei Guo, Jie Hao, Shaowen Wang, Jiashuo Sun, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Proposes a learned memory composer that jointly decides which retrieved experiences to include, how many, and in what order, trained via Experience Policy Optimization (ExPO), a GRPO-based framework using task-success feedback from complete agent interactions. Evaluated across three tau-bench domains with frozen agents. Moves agent memory beyond similarity-based retrieval toward utility-optimized assembly.

entry.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch

author.name: Zhanli Li, Zeyuan Xu, Chaoxu Pang, Zeyuan Liu, Anyang Ji, Te Sun, Kongcheng Zhang, Wenbo Xu, Xubin Yue, Shipeng Luo, Junjie Zhao, Yingfan Hua, Jingqing Ruan, Zhongda Su, Feng Hong, Zhizhao Zeng, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai, Hanjia Ye

entry.summary: Data World is a multi-agent engine that synthesizes training environments, tasks, and rubrics for data agents by first specifying the generative world behind files, then generating files from it — sidestepping privacy, IP, and verification problems. Independent audits check target recoverability, and the approach yields DataWorld-Bench (100 tasks, 50 held-out worlds, 16 domains) plus RL training rewards.

entry.title: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems

author.name: Thuy Dung Nguyen, Jingyi Guo, Rana Seda Dubauskas, Sreepriya Damuluru, Taylor T. Johnson, Kevin Leach

entry.summary: INFUSE is an end-to-end benchmark for indirect prompt injection across the full lifecycle of long-horizon agent workflows, comprising 40 realistic tasks and a taxonomy of 56 attack scenarios across five threat categories. It addresses the limitations of prior evaluations that test only isolated malicious strings, single tool calls, or narrow agent configurations.

entry.title: Router Drift Control: Mitigating Off-Policy Degradation in Mixture-of-Experts Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Liangyao Jin, Zhixin Wang, Liming Liu, Mingjun Zhang, Zhengzhou Zhu, Fangcheng Fu, Jinlong Hou, Yuan Cheng, Xiaohe Hu, Ping Zhang, Siyuan Feng

entry.summary: The paper analyzes router drift in MoE models under RL, where rollout-training mismatches change expert routing decisions, and shows that the existing Rollout Routing Replay fix introduces gradient bias by dropping contributions from experts selected only by the training router. It proposes Router Drift Control, which uses rollout-training routing disagreement as a staleness signal to selectively correct the bias. This is directly relevant to frontier MoE post-training reliability.

entry.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models

author.name: Chenyuan Zhou, Yining Hong, Huang Huang, Yunfan Jiang, Wenlong Huang, David Held, Vitor Campagnolo Guizilini, Yue Wang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Leonidas Guibas, Yejin Choi

entry.summary: Augments robotic world models with a learnable environment latent capturing unobserved factors such as friction, mass, and human-defined environmental rules, optimized at test time without supervision of what those factors are. Training alternates between world-model optimization with fixed latents and latent optimization. This lets predictions account for environmental variation that is neither visible nor specified.

entry.title: ReFlow: Replay-Driven Decoupling for Efficient RL Post-Training

author.name: Yukun Tian, Junwei Su, Haofeng Xu, Lansong Diao, Zhengping Qian, Weibo Zhao, Wenchao Zhou, Ruiting Zhou, Chuan Wu

entry.summary: ReFlow addresses efficiency bottlenecks in LLM RL post-training by replacing static asynchronous rollout-optimization overlap with a replay-driven decoupled design that adapts to shifting resource demands in multi-turn agentic workloads. The system mitigates the staleness-quality tradeoff that limits existing asynchronous RL infrastructure.

entry.title: Interfaces and Modules: A Scalable Representation for Weight-Space Learning across Architectures

author.name: Micha{\l} Kozyra, Michael Bronstein

entry.summary: The authors introduce a typed graph representation for weight-space learning built around interfaces (coordinate spaces with joint permutation constraints) and modules (operation occurrences as typed hyperedges), compiled automatically from PyTorch models. The Universal Weight Encoder combines local equivariant updates for scalable cross-architecture weight-space processing. This addresses a key scalability and generality bottleneck in learning over neural network parameters.

entry.title: On the Stability and Convergence of Flow Map Training

author.name: Ishan Nath, Tom Stanic, Avishek Joey Bose, Gauthier Gidel, Quentin Bertrand

entry.summary: This work provides theoretical analysis of flow map training for one-step generative samplers, explaining why stop-gradient operators and adaptive weighting heuristics, which are ubiquitous empirically, matter for training dynamics and convergence. The authors derive conditions under which these heuristics stabilize flow map learning.

entry.title: VELD-QA: A Large-Scale Dataset for Visual Evidence Grounding and Question Answering in Long Documents

author.name: Zhivar Sourati, Marianne Menglin Liu, Rongguang Wang, Zheng Wang, Yazhe Hu, Lan Guo, Yuying Wang, Mengqing Guo, Bhavesh Dnyaneshwar Gore, Shubham Pathak, Ramapriya Ranganath, Sandeep Sharma, Tao Sheng, Sujith Ravi, Dan Roth

entry.summary: VELD-QA provides 15,000 fully human-authored QA pairs over 5,859 real-world PDFs spanning 372,445 pages, with page-level and element-level visual evidence annotations covering charts, tables, and complex layouts. The annotations enable separate evaluation of retrieval and interpretation, and the authors benchmark nine vision-language models under four evidence settings. It fills a real gap in long-document multimodal QA evaluation.

entry.title: Compliant GMT: Making General Motion Tracking Compliant via Residual Reference Adaptation

author.name: Venki Parsuram, Michelle Wang, Jin-Hyuk Hong, Pulkit Agrawal

entry.summary: Compliant GMT adds full-body compliant responses to general motion tracking policies for humanoids, whose existing trackers rigidly imitate mocap data and behave unsafely under disturbance. The residual reference adaptation approach avoids the trade-off between compliance and generality seen in prior single-reference curated policies.

entry.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments

author.name: Panrong Tong, Quyu Kong, Pengxiang Li, Tianyu Xia, Hanzhang Zhou, Lei Wang, Chenglin Cai, Long Li, Long Chen, Jianan Zhang, Zhengwen Zeng, Xu Zhang, Gongjie Zhang, Yue Wang, Steven Hoi

entry.summary: Introduces MAI-Gym, an open platform unifying GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online RL training across mobile, computer, and web environments, with a shared rollout pipeline, support for ten benchmarks, and scaling to 20,000 parallel environment instances. It also enables automated synthesis of diverse GUI applications and training tasks.

entry.title: Sci$\Pi$vot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents

author.name: Youran Sun, Xingyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Kejia Zhang, Di Wu, Yingkang Cao, Allen Zhou, Jianping Ye, Suying Liu, Jiaxuan Guo, Jianda Du, Weicheng Ye, Kecheng Liu, Hefan Zhang, Haixin Wang, Jie Xiao, Eric Yang, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: A 248-case benchmark of scientific judgment built from six months of records in which senior researchers corrected LLM research agents across 26 projects and six fields; the agent must choose between its original plan and the human-corrected alternative using only the project record. It targets the hard-to-evaluate capability of PI-level research judgment. A novel and grounded evaluation approach for autonomous research.

entry.title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Shuoran Jiang, Wentao Zhu, Yang Xiang, Dongfeng Li, Yunan Zhang, Mengchen Zhao, Yuhui Guo, Kai Chen, Youcheng Pan, Xiangping Wu, Qingcai Chen

entry.summary: Inspired by localized plasticity in biological brains, this work uses gradient-attribution profiling to identify functionally specialized, low-overlap subnetworks in LLMs and proposes CiMEO, a continual learning framework that routes each training example to its corresponding subnetwork, restricting parameter updates to mitigate catastrophic forgetting while remaining memory-efficient. This tackles one of the central open problems in keeping deployed LLMs up to date without degrading existing capabilities.

entry.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research

author.name: Yijia Mao, Song Dai, Tao Chen, Xiangyu Lu, Linqian Zeng, Chenxi Hu, Sitong Zhou, Dongyang He, Xiaodan Mao, Linxuan Zhang, Tong Zhu, Yafu Li, Fangchen Yu, Peng Ye, Feng He, Yu Cheng, Yun Luo

entry.summary: PhysClosureBench evaluates whether AI agents can organize scientific investigations leading to well-supported conclusions, using 50 expert-verified physics research tasks across strong-field, attosecond, and adjacent areas. It introduces a 20-criterion Atomic Score for local accomplishments and a Research Closure scale (RC0-RC4) measuring whether investigations fully resolve their research questions.

entry.title: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection

author.name: Dixi Yao, Tahseen Rabbani, Tian Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight privacy mechanism for retrieval-augmented generation that applies the same random projection to both datastore and query embeddings. The method provably preserves semantic similarity while mitigating data extraction attacks, and empirically outperforms prior formal-privacy approaches on retrieval and generation quality across multiple RAG architectures and datasets.

entry.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Matteo He, William F. Shen, Alex Iacob, Andrej Jovanovic, Xinchi Qiu, Nicholas D. Lane

entry.summary: The paper shows that a language model's hidden states can encode task information before its unembedding (readout) matrix expresses it, meaning capability timelines read from outputs conflate encoding with expression. The authors introduce parameter-trajectory crosscoding, fitting a sparse dictionary to every token's readout row across checkpoints, requiring only checkpoint weights. They use this to locate a narrow early training window in readout development.

entry.title: System1-Arena: Which Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?

author.name: Tianyu Chen, Xinyang Liu, Ruyi An, Zhendong Wang, Mingyuan Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces System1-Arena, a large-scale benchmark (92k questions, 105 tasks, 268 sources, plus 138 closed-loop environments) that compares fast single-forward-pass decision models against generative System-2 reasoning approaches on identical discrete decision requests. It maps which decision types fast probability-output models can handle and which require costly reasoning.

entry.title: V-SHARE: Provable Convergence Guarantees for Advantage-based Algorithms

author.name: Kintan Saha, Hamed Masoudi, Xinyi Sheng, Dominik Baumann, Joni Pajarinen, Arsenii Mustafin

entry.summary: V-SHARE is an advantage-based value-learning algorithm combining cross-action value sharing with an importance-weighted Bellman-residual correction. The authors claim the first complete theoretical characterization of an advantage-based algorithm, providing both asymptotic convergence and non-asymptotic finite-sample guarantees. This fills a notable gap since advantage decomposition is widely used in deep RL but poorly understood theoretically.

entry.title: Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence

author.name: Owen Walters, Lihu Chen, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: Investigates why search-augmented LLMs produce outdated answers even when relevant evidence is retrieved, using temporal facts that changed after training cutoffs. The study finds models often answer from snippets without opening source pages, and layer-wise analysis reveals a gap between evidence availability and its effective internal use, with implications for citation faithfulness.

entry.title: Causal Integrated Gradients: Scalable Feature Attribution Along Causal Paths

author.name: Joran Michiels, Anis Ismail, Maarten De Vos, Alejandro Sifrim

entry.summary: Extends integrated gradients with causal integrated gradients (CIG) and causal expected gradients (CEG), which incorporate known causal structure among input features while retaining computational efficiency and, under graph conditions, axiomatic guarantees. This prevents attribution methods from crediting downstream effects over true upstream causes, as demonstrated with gene-regulation examples.

entry.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms

author.name: Guowei Xu, Zhenting Qi, Amani Kiruga, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Introduces market-based post-training (MPT), a framework where agents in a decentralized swarm jointly learn action policies and bidding behavior, so individual capabilities and collective coordination adapt together without a central orchestrator. Bids determine which agent acts and how collective outcomes generate local training credit. This addresses a key gap in multi-agent systems where orchestration structures are typically fixed during training.

entry.title: Resisting Harmful Instructions through Training-Free Weight Editing

author.name: Ali Ebrahimpour-Boroojeny, Xiaocong Yang, Samuel Schapiro, Zahra Borhani, Francisco R. Ortega, Yujia Zheng, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: This work introduces a training-free weight-editing method that reduces a language model's compliance with targeted harmful instructions, such as instructed falsehood and instructed sexism, using only forward passes on a small set of prompt pairs. Because the edit is stored in the weights, it cannot be undone by prompt-level changes, and it improves honest response rates by up to 6.2 percentage points across five instruction-tuned models.

entry.title: Finite-Time Guarantees for Constrained Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability

author.name: Valentina Zaccaria, Philip Jordan, Tingting Ni, Gian Antonio Susto, Maryam Kamgarpour

entry.summary: The paper develops the first non-asymptotic guarantees for constrained partially observable MDPs (CPOMDPs), where agents maximize reward under cost constraints with incomplete state information. By representing finite history windows as states of a constrained MDP and applying a primal-dual algorithm, the authors jointly bound average-reward suboptimality and constraint violation in the original problem.

entry.title: Learning Lean Feedback for Efficient Proof-Candidate Evaluation on GPUs

author.name: Lazar Milikic, Etienne Bamas, Emmanuel Abbe, Viktor Kun\v{c}ak

entry.summary: This work trains neural evaluators to predict Lean 4 theorem-prover verdicts and compiler feedback directly on GPUs, using 4.84M labeled programs to avoid slow verifier calls during RL training of theorem-proving models. A two-stage evaluator combining a validity classifier with a feedback model reaches 87.8% accuracy on a 68,932-program benchmark. It matters because verifier bottlenecks are a key constraint in scaling formal reasoning systems.

entry.title: Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation

author.name: Shuo Han, Ziqing Hu

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes policy gradient estimation for RLHF-style post-training of LLMs under regularized importance sampling, which arises from off-policy training due to mismatch or staleness. The authors show that importance-weighted policy gradients lose invariance to constant reward shifts under truncation/clipping, and recover this invariance by using the covariance between reward and importance-weighted score as the estimand.

entry.title: ContextLift: Breaking the Spurious Correlation Behind Conditional Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Florian Mai, David Kacz\'er

entry.summary: The paper reframes conditional emergent misalignment (misalignment that returns when prompts resemble the finetuning context) as a spurious correlation: in the training mix, the finetuning context co-occurs only with misaligned answers. ContextLift, a counterfactual augmentation that lifts context sentences into interleaved safety rows, breaks this correlation without any model, labels, or domain knowledge, improving on standard safety-data interleaving.

entry.title: REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs

author.name: Juliette Marrie, Paul Pacaud, Adrien Ramanana Rahary, Shizhe Chen, Moritz B\"ohle

entry.summary: REKI is a 2.4B vision-language-action model pretrained entirely on public data, pairing a VLM with a flow-matching action expert and setting a new Pareto frontier between size and performance on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand, and RoboCasa365. It adds a lightweight memory via register tokens in the action expert that summarize each frame's VLM output and persist in the expert cache, improving simulated and real success rates.

entry.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas

author.name: Manya Wadhwa, Pranav Narayanan Venkit, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yu Li, Tuhin Chakrabarty, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: This work trains reasoning models with a set-level reinforcement learning objective to generate K structured, document-grounded scientific ideas that are simultaneously high-quality and mutually distinct. Prior LLM ideation work optimized individual idea quality while neglecting diversity. The authors include researchers from a major industrial lab (Amazon-style team), giving it credibility in the AI-for-science space.

entry.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?

author.name: Dongyue Lu, Guian Fang, Hur Lim, Yonggang Wu, Yanrong Wang, Hongshan Chen, Shengju Qian, Yue Liao, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Tianxin Huang, Yu Yang, Hongji Yang, Junchao Huang, Ao Liang, Yihao Wang, Zihan Wang, Rong Li, Hanlin Chen, Xin Wang, Wei Tsang Ooi, Mike Zheng Shou, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: Orbia is the first benchmark dedicated to systematically evaluating 3D consistency in interactive world models, organized around input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency via controlled exploration and revisit protocols. It uses registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors rather than relying on VLM judges. This addresses a critical blind spot as video generators are increasingly marketed as world simulators.

entry.title: Do VLAs Really Follow Instructions? Diagnosing How-Level Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Sangwu Park, Wonjoong Kim, Yeonjun In, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: This diagnostic study shows that vision-language-action models largely fail to follow How-level instructions specifying how to perform a task, as opposed to What-level task specifications. The authors show single-instruction-per-episode training limits this capability, introduce segment-level enriched instruction training, and release SIMPLER-IN, a benchmark requiring conditional success criteria.

entry.title: Seeing is Believing: Benchmarking and Mitigating the Interference of Language Priors on Visual Perception in MLLMs

author.name: Li Ma, Yan Zhuang, Jiawen Deng, Fuji Ren

entry.summary: This work introduces ViSiP-Bench, a benchmark of rare-but-real scenarios across six prior categories for measuring how language priors override visual evidence in multimodal LLMs. It identifies flaws in prior benchmarks, such as items answerable without images, and adds a model-aware dynamic prior induction protocol with three continuous metrics. Evaluation of 24 models shows pervasive prior adherence that does not improve with scale, plus mitigation analysis.

entry.title: Dense4D: Pixel-Level 4D Human Correspondence

author.name: R{\i}za Alp G\"uler

entry.summary: Dense4D is the first feed-forward model for dense 4D correspondence of humans across body, clothing, and hair from monocular RGB images without requiring a body template. It predicts Human Point Maps that assign each pixel a 3D position at a common reference time, enabling amodal correspondence for occluded points. This matters for human motion reconstruction, virtual try-on, and avatar applications.

entry.title: KODA: Kinematics--Observation Data Alignment for Humanoid Learning from Human Egocentric Demonstration

author.name: Zibo Zhou, Yueru Chen, Junsong Wu, Weiji Xie, Qingyao Xu, Sheng Yin, Shiqing Wang, Jiyuan Shi, Siheng Chen, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: KODA converts egocentric human RGB demonstrations into whole-body VLA training data for humanoids, using a reusable canonical trajectory to guide robot-view synthesis and generate controller-compatible state-action labels. This reduces dependence on costly robot demonstrations for training humanoid whole-body policies.

entry.title: Towards bio-inspired visual navigation: a neuromorphic navigation paradigm for MAVs

author.name: Junjie Jiang, Ankang Zhou, Zheng Fang

entry.summary: This paper presents the first end-to-end event-driven neuromorphic paradigm for micro aerial vehicle visual navigation, combining neuromorphic vision sensors, spiking neural networks, and neuromorphic processors. It targets the robustness and extreme power efficiency that biological visual navigation achieves but frame-based neural systems lack, which is critical for energy-constrained MAVs in complex environments.

entry.title: MOSS: Mode-Oriented Source Shaping for Robot Flow Matching Policies

author.name: Zirun Ma, Jindou Jia, Tuo An, Jiaqi Bai, Jiahua Dong, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: MOSS makes behavior mode selection an explicit choice in flow-matching robot policies by showing theoretically and empirically that distinct behavioral modes have distinct source-space preimages under deterministic transport. It then shapes the generation source to control which mode is executed instead of relying on random sampling.

entry.title: A Simpler and Better Debate Protocol for Scalable Oversight

author.name: Zhiyang Xun

entry.summary: A linkpost to an arXiv paper introducing FBS Debate, a new AI-debate protocol for problems with stable subproblem decompositions. It improves on prior work by giving worst-case rather than average-case correctness guarantees under a stronger equilibrium concept, and proves that no protocol treating human judgment as a black box can do better on this problem class.

entry.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery

author.name: Dongxu Yang, Hongda Yan, Renxin Wang, Baoli Zhang, Haojia Zuo, Ying Zhao, Youmin Chen, Xiaojian Liao, Congming Gao, Tianyang Jiang, Yixiao Chen, Qing Wang, Zhiguo Yu, Xiaqing Li, Yuhao Zhang, Jiawen Sun, Renzhe Xu, De Mi, Tiancheng Wu, Xianya Fu, Xuanlu Zhao, Bo Feng, Meixuan Ren, Guanming Lin, Ziheng Zhou, Xinhua Wang

entry.summary: FDE-Gym is a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks drawn from 20 real customer scenarios across 18 sectors, where agents must clarify ambiguous requirements, interact with scripted stakeholders, and operate production-like systems as forward-deployed engineers would. Scoring is based on actual improvement to the customer's system, moving beyond well-specified issue-and-ticket style agent benchmarks.

entry.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?

author.name: Wenkai Li, Wenyi Hong, Zhuoyi Yang, Jie Tang

entry.summary: The paper asks whether image-generation training can add knowledge to unified multimodal models that is accessible through text-only QA. It introduces Knowledge Transfer Probing, a controlled protocol showing direct but uneven transfer from visual generation supervision to language across seven categories and three models, then proposes Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image-Text Alignment methods to strengthen the connection. This is a novel empirical question at the intersection of generation and knowledge acquisition.

entry.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Leyang Shen, Yaxin Gong, Yang Zhang, Chenxiao Fan, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Fuli Feng, Chun Kai Ling, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Addresses goal drift in LLM agent and multi-agent execution with a learned steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and intervenes when drift occurs, choosing between a low-cost fast path and a high-cost slow path. The steering agent is trained to jointly assess drift and generate effective interventions.

entry.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility

author.name: Sambit Ghosh, Madelyn Mathai, R. Venkatesh Babu, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: Systematically studies how much activation data sparse autoencoders need by training four SAE architectures on three language models with budgets from 5M to 500M tokens. Functional behavior converges at much smaller budgets than one-to-one feature reproducibility, which keeps improving with data, meaning standard evaluations can hide instability in the learned feature sets. For Gemma-2-2B BatchTopK, strictly matched feature fractions remain far below the full-data reference.

entry.title: Learn Only Where You Can't Compute: Structured Corrections to Gaussian Process Posteriors

author.name: Tobias Weber, Carla Sagebiel, Philipp Hennig

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid framework combining tractable physics-informed Gaussian processes with diffusion-model corrections, where the diffusion model learns only the structured residual that the Gaussian reference cannot capture. This addresses the complementary weaknesses of GPs (poor scaling to nonlinear information) and diffusion models (data scarcity in scientific settings). It is a notable step toward principled fusion of classical probabilistic inference with generative deep learning for scientific applications.

entry.title: Spurious Attention Heads in Vision Transformers: Mechanistic Identification of Annotation-Driven Bias in Medical Chest X-Ray Analysis

author.name: Joshua Muhumuza, Cornelius Kalenzi

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability, the authors identify a single attention head (L8H10) in ViT-Base 16 that reads corner annotation text instead of lung pathology on chest X-rays, attending to text in 62% of COVID-19 images. Causal inpainting validation and replication across NIH ChestX-ray14, DeiT-Base, and ViT-Large establish annotation-attention as a reproducible spurious mechanism. This matters because it makes a known dataset-bias problem locatable and potentially fixable.

entry.title: CarryOn: A Dual-Loop Harness for Personalized and Reliable Robot Assistance

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Yuqi Liu, Yuxin Chen, Sengqiao Yang, Jinhui Ye, Pengguang Chen, Changsheng Lu, Shu Liu, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: CarryOn augments a frozen vision-language-action policy with a dual-loop harness: a planning loop maintains persistent user-level and scene-level context for personalized subtask decomposition, while an execution loop provides explainable safety assurance, proactive hazard prevention, and recovery from physical failures. It targets real-world robot assistance gaps like reliably executing open-ended instructions such as making a sandwich. Strong author group (CUHK and collaborators).

entry.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies

author.name: Wenye Yu, Yijin Chen, Kaiyi Xiong, Wenbo Han, Wendi Chen, Yang Jin, Han Xue, Jun Lv, Cewu Lu, Chuan Wen

entry.summary: VaM enables online real-world post-training of generalist robot policies by caching value predictions as task-progress memory to disambiguate action selection under partial observability. It combines offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation, transitioning from offline RL warmup to autonomous online learning with sparse rewards.

entry.title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation

author.name: Morio Hamada, Jehyeok Yeon, Matteo Migliarini, Justin Olive, Magda Dubois

entry.summary: Investigates whether full solution transcripts from saturated benchmarks can still differentiate model capabilities once scores reach ceiling, using retrospective simulation with historical benchmark and model releases. The work aims to preserve the utility of benchmarks for safety cases and frontier policy decisions even after top-line scores lose discriminative power.

entry.title: OmicsBench: a long-horizon multi-turn benchmark of AI agents on research-study-scale bioinformatics

author.name: Gideon Shaked, Siddharth Nagisetty

entry.summary: Introduces a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark with 97 tasks structured as DAGs of 662 deterministically graded subtasks, evaluated across 12 models and three harnesses. No configuration comes close to saturating it, with mean scores of 0.43-0.5 and some tasks taking 3.6 hours per agent run. It fills a real gap left by single-shot bioinformatics benchmarks.

entry.title: Mine, Sample, Render: Test-Time Diversity Alignment Of Generative Models

author.name: Kostas Triaridis, Morris E. Sharp, Nebojsa Jojic

entry.summary: Introduces MSR, a test-time method that externalizes diversity into an explicit corpus-derived procedure: mine an interpretable categorical schema from real artifacts, sample attribute configurations from corpus statistics, and use the generative model purely as a conditional renderer. Evaluated across weather reports, user simulation, webpage design, text-to-image, and 3D assets. Addresses the persistent failure of generative models to sample diversely even when instructed.

entry.title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally

author.name: Zhizhuo Kou, Jian Yang, Pengfei Hao, Junyu Luo, Jingshu Peng, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Shows that increasing test-time thinking makes reasoning models cancel everyday scalar and logical implicatures (reading some as not-all-canceling, or as inclusive), while improving context-driven inferences such as indirect answers, holding weights fixed and varying only thinking budget. Uses reasoning truncation to localize where readings change. An interesting dissociation between logical and pragmatic competence as a function of compute.

entry.title: Auditing Escalation Reliability in Healthcare LLM Agents: A Perturbation-Controlled Benchmark of Workflow-State Failures

author.name: Zihao Zheng (Washington University in St. Louis), Junyi Yao (Washington University in St. Louis), Baichuan Li (Southern Methodist University), Jiayu Long (Washington University in St. Louis)

entry.summary: Presents a 400-episode perturbation-controlled benchmark of healthcare workflow decisions scored on answer/clarify/abstain/escalate actions, finding that while clean decision accuracy reaches 0.97 across five open-weight configurations, uncertainty-prompted models miss 32-97% of required escalations. It exposes that high static accuracy masks severe failures under missing, stale, or conflicting evidence. Highly safety-relevant for clinical agent deployment.

entry.title: SCRIBE: Scalable Contextual Representations of Interpretable Brain-Grounded Semantics

author.name: Camila Kolling, Omer Moussa, Emin \c{C}elik, Mariya Toneva

entry.summary: This paper introduces SCRIBE, a framework that uses an ensemble of open-source large language models to build interpretable, word-level semantic representations for studying how the human brain constructs contextual meaning from natural language. A behavioral study with 921 participants shows that human semantic judgments shift systematically with context, and SCRIBE captures these shifts at 75-81% of the estimated human noise ceiling, with supporting brain-activity evidence from participants listening to naturalistic stories. The work matters because it bridges LLM-based representations and cognitive neuroscience, offering a scalable tool for connective research on language understanding in the brain.

entry.title: Evaluating Inquiry Learning in LLM-Based Agents: Hypothesizing, Reasoning, and Exploration

author.name: Marta Kne\v{z}evi\'c, Seyed Parsa Neshaei, Jibril Frej, Vinitra Swamy, Tanja K\"aser

entry.summary: The authors introduce a unified interactive framework for evaluating LLM agents' full scientific inquiry cycle - exploration, hypothesis generation, and reasoning over observations - by extending the Countdown task into a mathematical environment where agents probe a system by manipulating variables and inferring hidden relationships. Prior work typically evaluated these abilities in isolation, so this fills an evaluation gap for integrated scientific reasoning. It matters for assessing progress toward AI-assisted scientific discovery.

entry.title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models

author.name: Jiamin Shi, Yuanhong Zhang, Zhiyang Liu, Jiawei Sun, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: This paper studies how to learn world model representations that preserve intrinsic dynamics (the action-consequence relationship) despite distracting visual variation. It proposes that action predictability — reconstructing an action from consecutive latent states — serves as a signal that prevents representations from discarding dynamics-relevant distinctions, supported by both theoretical lower bounds and empirical evidence.

entry.title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction

author.name: Aozhong Zhang, Selcuk Gurses, Yanxia Deng, Naigang Wang, Chi-Chun Liu, Davis Wertheimer, Derrick Liu, Xin Li, Zi Yang, Felix X. -F. Ye, Penghang Yin

entry.summary: DropKV reframes KV-cache eviction, a key bottleneck for long-context LLM serving, by decoupling the NP-hard joint eviction decision into independent per-token scoring under a Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation framework. This yields principled near-optimal eviction that is kernelizable, avoiding ad hoc heuristics.

entry.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents

author.name: Siqi Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Yuchen Yan, Xingyu Wu, Qipeng Chen, Xin Zhang, Aiting Liu, Chao Deng, Jie Liu, Jin Ma, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: KnowGPO is a reinforcement learning framework for deep search agents that assigns credit by the task-relevant knowledge trajectories acquire rather than by surface trajectory states or model-internal signals, addressing the limits of outcome-only rewards and noisy process supervision. This knowledge-grouped alignment targets long-horizon, multi-turn search where observations are heterogeneous and retrieved contexts are long and noisy.

entry.title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs

author.name: Anita Kriz, Antonin Berthon, Nicol\'as Astorga, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: The authors train reasoning LLMs to perform adaptive sequential Bayesian experimental design by using information-gain rewards, with the experimental generative model specified independently of the LLM's own beliefs. The paper systematically studies amortization design choices including reward estimation, hypothesis-space specification, and multi-step objectives. This connects LLM reasoning to principled scientific decision-making, an important step toward LLMs that actively gather information rather than merely answer.

entry.title: When Judges Agree and Are Wrong: Consistency-Accuracy Dissociation as a Blind Spot for Label-Free Evaluation

author.name: Xiang Zhang, Lovedeep Gondara, Jekaterina Novikova

entry.summary: This paper directly tests the assumption that consistency is a proxy for correctness in label-free evaluation, using four financial QA datasets, ten consistency dimensions, and two frontier model families at the example level. It finds 60% of incorrect answers fall in the high-consistency region (consistency >= 0.8), with 77.7% of those showing complete answer collapse. This is a significant cautionary result for self-consistency filtering, majority-vote aggregation, and LLM-as-judge reliability methods.

entry.title: Judging the Judges: Confidence and Disagreement in Rubrics as Rewards

author.name: Michael Tian-Yue Liu, Anne Harrington, Trevor Darrell, Yutong Bai

entry.summary: Examines how judge identity affects Rubrics-as-Rewards RL training, showing substantial score spread across five frontier and open-weight judges when training Qwen3-4B-Base on medical and science rubrics. Proposes RaRE, a judge ensemble strategy using logprob-weighted soft-Likert rewards that emphasize confident judges and handle disagreement.

entry.title: TRACER: A Multimodal Harness for Patient Care in Hospitals

author.name: Zane Durante, Paul Tang, Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Amit Kaushal, Shrinidhi Kowshika Lakshmikanth, Feolu Kolawole, Yu Jun Zheng, Yifan Geng, Shobhit Agarwal, Kevin Schulman, Juan Carlos Niebles, Ehsan Adeli, Arnold Milstein, Li Fei-Fei

entry.summary: Presents a training-free multimodal harness that builds minute-level action records from continuous hospital video, combines them with clinical records into hourly reports, and equips an LLM agent with tools to query the hierarchy and inspect evidence. Evaluated on two new benchmarks including 397 annotated clips and 144 clinician-informed multi-step questions, with a strong author team including Li Fei-Fei and clinical collaborators.

entry.title: Full-Duplex Interaction with Speech, Expressions and Gestures

author.name: Siyin Wang, Wenyi Yu, Terumi Chiba, Xianzhao Chen, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Lu Lu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: ELLSA 2 is an end-to-end full-duplex dialogue model that jointly optimizes speech interaction and streaming gesture-expression generation. An autoregressive chunk-wise synthesizer blends pretrained acoustic features with distinct listening and speaking states, enabling continuous non-verbal generation even during verbal silence, with contextual semantic gesture calls guided by templates. This pushes toward embodied, human-like conversational agents beyond text-only chat.

entry.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It

author.name: Faridoun Mehri, Hinrich Sch\"utze

entry.summary: Distinguishes active facts, which support generalization to new relations, from inert facts that can be recalled but do not aid learning, using constructed relabeling experiments where models infer new relations for held-out subjects. The central finding is that facts represented linearly prior to fine-tuning generalize after it.

entry.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Bingcong Li, Hao Ma, Michael Muehlebach, Niao He, Yi Ma

entry.summary: Analyzes an exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts architectures that combine fine-grained expert segmentation with shared experts: shared experts reduce variability of token representations, dampening the exploration needed to navigate the combinatorially enlarged routing space created by fine-grained segmentation. The paper diagnoses this tension and presumably proposes routing modifications to restore exploration benefits.

entry.title: Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Xuanchang Zhang, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GGPO, an off-policy RL method for training LLMs with verifiable rewards that avoids high-variance learner-to-behavior importance weights by minimizing a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards per prompt. Derives guarantees connecting the population loss to the KL-regularized optimality gap and bounds single-response reward relative to best-of-K behavior.

entry.title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval

author.name: Charalampos Koilakos, Kimon-Antonios Provatas, Michail Patsakis, Candace SY Chan, Georgios A. Pavlopoulos, Ilias Georgakopoulos-Soares

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates two data-only poisoning attacks against protein foundation models: one targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models (ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants at 300M parameters) and another targeting the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. By injecting trigger-payload sequences, the authors show models reliably acquire trigger-dependent generation behavior. The work exposes a security gap in biotechnology-adjacent AI systems that rely on large public biological datasets, with implications for biosecurity and trustworthy generative biology.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: Curse of Dimensionality and Structural Bias

author.name: Yunhao Ni, Yuxin Guo, Jie Luo, Wenjun Wu, Lei Huang

entry.summary: This theoretical work asks whether the favorable dimension-independent approximation rates claimed for Kolmogorov-Arnold networks stem from the architecture or from assumptions about the target function class. The authors prove worst-case exponential coefficient growth for deep spline-KANs on isotropic Sobolev balls below an accuracy threshold, show comparable guarantees exist for composition-matched MLPs, and find empirical gaps in scaling-law benchmarks.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference

author.name: Vlad Alexandru S\u{a}nduleac, Shahariya Rasheed Rayamarakkarveettil Puthanpurayil, Noman Khan, Remus Teodorescu

entry.summary: This paper distills a 20.1M-parameter grid foundation model for power-flow prediction into a 0.62M-parameter student model, a 32.5x reduction, using a combined objective of masked power-flow loss, physics residuals, latent-state, and attention transfer. The goal is real-time edge inference for low-inertia power grids at batch size one within a single PMU reporting frame. It matters because it addresses the practical deployment gap between data-center-scale foundation models and edge hardware in critical infrastructure.

entry.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion

author.name: Shiyuan Zhang, Xuheng Li, Qiwei Di, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: SIRS corrects the bias of parallel token unmasking in masked diffusion models with a rejection sampler that estimates log acceptance probability from a single score query per step rather than one per token, using a Bernoulli factory for accept/reject decisions. This substantially reduces the query cost of unbiased parallel sampling from MDMs. It matters for making masked diffusion generation both fast and statistically correct.

entry.title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving

author.name: Yihan Xu, Jia-Chen Gu, Junyi Zhang, Di Wu, Haikang Deng, Po-Nien Kung, Kai-Wei Chang, Amit Sahai, Wei Wang, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: LeanGraphSearch improves lemma retrieval for Lean 4 theorem proving by building a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traversing multi-hop dependency chains to find supporting lemmas that are not lexically similar to the target. The strong author team from UCLA spans ML and cryptography expertise, and retrieval of relevant declarations is a known bottleneck for neural provers.

entry.title: Clean Data Can Still Carry Backdoors: Support-Persistent Backdoors for Model Reuse

author.name: Junhoo Lee, Baekseung Kim, Seungyeon Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: The paper introduces DAR (Discover-and-Relabel), a backdoor attack that survives clean-data knowledge distillation by exploiting naturally abundant patterns in low-dimensional feature subspaces rather than artificial triggers, poisoning only label-only samples that already satisfy the discovered rule. This challenges the common belief that KD acts as an effective backdoor purification defense.

entry.title: Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta's End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Arshad Rahman, Adnan Aziz, Ajith Prabhudev, Amin Farmahini, Ben Rhoads, Benson Ma, Brian Shi, Cen Zhao, CK Luk, Dingming Wu, Emad El-Haraty, Eric Chen, Frank Li, Gary Huang, Gefei Zuo, Haoran Zhang, Hiwot Kassa, Hongyi Zeng, Jack Taylor, Jeremy Hadidjojo, John Donati, Jonathan Sheffield, Julio Machado Silva, Karthik Ganesan, Kent Russell, KR Kishore, Lei Tian, Liu Ke, Muhammad Osama, Peng Chen, Rakesh Hemnani, Ryan Swann, Saleel Kudchadker, Shankar Yanamandram, Shobhit Kanaujia, Shucai Xiao, Srinath Bayareddy, Srinivas Vaidyanathan, Sudharssun Subramanian, Supadchaya Puangpontip, Taylor Robie, Tianhao Huang, Tyler Hart, Viswesh Sankaran, Weijun Jiang, Wenkai Du, Xiaodong Wang, Xiaohu Guo, Yao Rong, Yinbin Ma, Yue Dong, Yuzhen Huang, Yvonne Liu, Zhan Shu, Dan Rabinovitsj, Ajit Mathews, Chunqiang Tang

entry.summary: Meta details its methods for optimizing AI training on non-NVIDIA accelerators, using recommendation model training on AMD Instinct MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 as a case study within its heterogeneous fleet of NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and MTIA. The paper distills reusable principles including hardware-model co-design that revises model structures and software recipes rather than directly porting, and analytic performance modeling.

entry.title: Behavioral Forgetting Is Not Privacy in Machine Unlearning

author.name: Tyler Lizzo, Larry Heck

entry.summary: The paper argues that machine unlearning evaluations measuring forgetting on a single benchmark distribution are insufficient for privacy, demonstrating via cross-lingual querying that forgetting varies substantially when semantically equivalent information is queried in different languages and scripts across multilingual model families. One alternative access path can expose real privacy leakage. This is an important critique of current unlearning evaluation standards.

entry.title: Multi-Target Few-Shot Prompting with Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Anton Xue, Alan Li, Rahul Saha

entry.summary: This paper introduces multi-target few-shot prompting with diffusion language models, where in-context examples guide infilling of multiple masked regions on a shared canvas, addressing edit-by-example tasks like formatting changes or API migrations that require both left and right context. A likelihood-ratio reward via selective masking helps the model reliably follow demonstrations. This matters because it showcases a natural strength of diffusion LMs over autoregressive models for multi-site editing.

entry.title: Mind the Tail: Data Selection Through Sparse Concepts

author.name: Ziheng Zhang, Neha Hulkund, Colin Lee, Zheda Mai, Hui Shen, Ying Ding, Tanya Berger-Wolf, Sara Beery, Wei-Lun Chao, Jianyang Gu

entry.summary: This work uses sparse autoencoders to extract concept-level activations from images and studies how data selection reallocates training support across concepts, with particular attention to tail concepts supported by few samples. It evaluates allocation strategies across fine-grained classification, spurious-correlation settings, general classification, and multimodal pretraining.

entry.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World

author.name: Yijiang Li, Bingyang Wang, Nuno Vasconcelos

entry.summary: Trains VLMs to actively explore 3D environments through their native single-image encoding, treating the 3D scene as an environment the model interacts with via actions and rendered observations. After trajectory-supervised finetuning, reinforcement learning with correctness-driven rewards teaches the model to reason, navigate, and reorient its viewpoint before answering visual questions.

entry.title: FALCON: FPGA-Accelerated Latency-Certifiable Occupancy Networks for Camera-Based Autonomous Driving

author.name: Haohua Que, Mingkai Liu, Handong Yao

entry.summary: FALCON is a camera-based 3D occupancy perception front-end deployed on an embedded AMD Kria KR260 FPGA, designed to guarantee per-frame latency deadlines rather than low average latency. It layers the guarantee into analytically cycle-bounded programmable-logic compute, a measured inference envelope over 100k-frame traces, and a watchdog that publishes fallback outputs. The system targets safety-critical autonomous driving where worst-case bounds are mandatory.

entry.title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Han Su, Meng Tian, Tianyu Huang, Mingyu Gao, Lennox Wei, Dongxu Li, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Xiaohe Wu, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: DK-VLM introduces Dual-Kernel Attention, computing attention from both a token's input position and its estimated 3D geometric position, so a geometric kernel modulates attention via point displacements and camera poses while a semantic kernel preserves pretrained behavior. This targets persistent weaknesses of VLMs in cross-view 3D spatial reasoning. It offers an alternative to fusing 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens.

entry.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers

author.name: Yitong Xia, Zeren Jiang, Chuanxia Zheng

entry.summary: Gen4P repurposes a pretrained video generator as a feed-forward 4D perceiver, processing clean video latents in a single encoder pass with on-demand and continuous-time queries to recover 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. A frozen pretrained video-depth LoRA serves as a plug-in geometry prior. This supports the thesis that generative video models contain reusable geometric knowledge.

entry.title: MoCaP: Mobile Code-as-Policies for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation from Passive Human Videos

author.name: Yiyang Cai, Tatsuya Kamijo, Ninghao Lu, Zijin Hu, Sherry Yang

entry.summary: MoCaP is an agentic framework that converts passive human videos into guidance for an end-to-end mobile manipulation policy, extracting spatial memory and human interaction cues to inform navigation and manipulation-ready configuration search. It enables zero-shot mobile manipulation without per-task demonstrations via closed-loop code-as-policy execution.

entry.title: Comfortably Stuck: Evaluation Pitfalls in Bench2Drive's Closed-Loop Protocol
