entry.summary: Shows that multimodal document RAG answers underuse visual evidence even when retrieval is perfect, and characterizes generator needs via two requirements: Loud (fully using visual token capacity) and Clear (feeding focused evidence). Experiments on SciEGEGA show raising page-only budgets from 1K to 32K visual tokens improves accuracy by 15.22 points, and adding ground-truth crops at fixed budget adds 3.75 points.

entry.title: Can LLMs Tell Stories Out of Order? A Corpus and Benchmark for Nonlinear Narrative Generation

author.name: Syed Rifat Raiyan, Md. Tariquzzaman, Md Farhan Ishmam, Tenghao Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark of 83 published works annotated with chronological and told-order event lists, causal dependency graphs, character knowledge, and question structure, to test whether language models can generate nonlinear narratives. Across 19 models, stories told from chronological inputs default to chronology and only about half of structure-targeted attempts land within the human range. It exposes a systematic weakness in long-range narrative control.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Tool Graph Memory in Multi-Turn Tool Use

author.name: Uiji Hwang, Richeng Xuan, Taeuk Kim

entry.summary: The paper critically evaluates tool graph memory, which stores past experience as tool transitions to guide LLM agent tool selection, across nine models and two benchmarks. It finds the memory seldom improves significantly over baselines, its guidance is often incorrect, and random or no guidance retains most of the apparent gain, implying benefits come from extra computation rather than memory content. This is a valuable negative result for the agent-memory literature.

entry.title: Harmful Partial Interventions and Benign Leakage in Concept-based Models

author.name: Gregory Verghese, Christopher J. Soelistyo, Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga, Alessandro Barp, Christopher R. S. Banerji

entry.summary: Formalizes intervention harm in concept-based models, showing that concept interventions can counterintuitively worsen downstream predictions, especially under partial interventions which are the realistic oversight scenario. The paper examines how information leakage in concept representations interacts with intervention safety, refining claims that leakage is benign.

entry.title: EMO: A Closed-Loop Test-Time Computation Framework via Alternating Context Optimization and Logits Steering

author.name: Wei Xia, Yehui Tang, Zhi-Hong Deng

entry.summary: Introduces EMO, a training-free test-time framework inspired by expectation-maximization that alternates question-specific context estimation using textual gradients from an external judge, with a distribution refinement step that applies confidence-constrained logit corrections. This closed loop gives separate control over the strength of distributional changes induced by context updates.

entry.title: Feature Elicitation for SAE Steering of Deceptive Behaviour in Small LLMs

author.name: J Koorndijk

entry.summary: Tests whether steering sparse autoencoder features associated with deontological ethics can mitigate alignment-faking behavior in small LLMs, using a bag-of-words feature elicitation pipeline to find concept-level steering directions. Reports reducing the compliance gap to non-significance in Gemma-3-27B-class models. This extends mechanistic interpretability interventions to deceptive alignment, an understudied regime in smaller models.

entry.title: Do Emergent Misalignment Models Share a Circuit?

author.name: Muhammad Haseeb, Muhammad Tahir

entry.summary: Investigates whether models exhibiting emergent misalignment from narrow harmful fine-tuning share common computational circuitry, using three LoRA fine-tunes of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct on medical, financial, and extreme-sports harm. Direction-based activation tracing finds three attention-head locations shared among all three models, and replacing head contributions with base-model values reduces misalignment, suggesting a common mechanism.

entry.title: Recursive Offline Distillation via Entropy Gain Sampling and Answer Mixing

author.name: Andrey Goncharov, Daniil Vyazhev, Simon Epanov, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: The authors propose a recursive offline distillation method for transferring reasoning ability from LLMs to smaller 3-4B models without full access to teacher internals. The approach uses entropy-based weighted sampling of reasoning chains relative to an auxiliary 70-72B model and mixes thinking traces with ground-truth answer tokens. It consistently outperforms naive distillation at comparable data budgets, which matters for building capable small models under restricted API access.

entry.title: Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Stanley Wei, Jiin Woo, Kaan Ozkara, Youngsuk Park

entry.summary: The authors theoretically explore what makes a teacher compatible with a student in on-policy distillation, where supervision is applied at the token level during rollouts. Building on this theory, they derive empirical heuristics for token-level teacher selection, capturing desiderata such as compatible reasoning patterns, teacher competence, and induced learning signal.

entry.title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment

author.name: Nikita Tsoy

entry.summary: This game-theoretic analysis models safety investment in an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and competing downstream firms, comparing market-driven safety levels with welfare- and industry-profit-maximizing levels. The key finding is that downstream competition induces over-investment relative to the industry-profit optimum while upstream incentives diverge, suggesting safety requires intervention at the supply-chain level.

entry.title: P2TPO: Structure-Aligned Page-to-Token Credit Assignment for Full-Page Document Parsing

author.name: Yong Zu, Ninghua Yang, Zezhong Tan, Xinhong Ma, Ziqiang Dong, Yang Yang

entry.summary: P2TPO is a structure-aligned credit assignment framework for end-to-end full-page document parsing that associates block-level quality contrasts with generated token spans rather than using a single page-level advantage. It includes reference-element alignment and Unified Anchor Pricing to handle matched and missing elements relative to a fixed quality ceiling. This improves on coarse-grained RLHF-style rewards for structured document generation.

entry.title: Explore Once, Evaluate Many: Multiple Policy Evaluation for Stochastic Linear Bandits

author.name: Spyros Dragazis, Yilei Chen, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: PRISMA estimates the values of K target policies simultaneously in stochastic linear contextual bandits using reward-free access to policy queries, with sample complexity depending logarithmically on K and an instance-dependent difficulty term bounded by the dimension. The key idea is designing a single shared sampling distribution regularized for information sharing across policies. This improves the sample efficiency of off-policy evaluation at scale.

entry.title: A polylogarithmic bound for list replicability

author.name: Ari Blondal, Hamed Hatami, Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov, Sivan Tretiak

entry.summary: This note provides a short, self-contained proof of a recently announced result by Zhang that the list-replicability number of concept classes is O(log^2 M log N), the first polylogarithmic upper bound. The authors follow the high-level approach of the original manuscript with considerably simpler arguments.

entry.title: Planning to Learn: Real-Time Robust Adaptive Control on the GPU with Guaranteed Future Learning

author.name: Anutam Srinivasan, Siddhant Panse, Glen Chou

entry.summary: A-SLS is a learning-aware robust adaptive MPC framework based on system-level synthesis that forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to build tight reachable sets accounting for guaranteed future learning. A GPU-accelerated solver enables real-time performance on high-dimensional robotic systems. This makes robust adaptive control less conservative while retaining safety guarantees.

entry.title: Score Mismatch and Set-Constrained Sampling in Zero-Shot Conditional Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Renxiang Huang, Yuchen Liang, Yingbin Liang, Ness Shroff, Lifeng Lai

entry.summary: The paper provides the first theoretical analysis of score-mismatched discrete diffusion models, deriving a general KL divergence upper bound that isolates the additional error from reusing a model trained on an unconditional distribution for zero-shot conditional sampling. It also analyzes set-constrained sampling in this regime. This addresses the common practical situation where training and target distributions differ.

entry.title: Two Sample Sizes in Test-Time LLM Ensembling: Buffered ERM and Minimax Theory

author.name: Zhi Zhang, Arash A. Amini

entry.summary: This work provides minimax theory for weighted test-time ensembles of LLMs, characterizing how two sample sizes interact: Q labeled questions and N generations per question. Under a margin condition, ERM with a calibrated margin buffer achieves excess risk on the order of Q^-1/2 plus N^(-beta/2) for the ensemble's infinite-generation voting risk, with matching lower bounds implied by the framing.

entry.title: Conditional Mean Flows: Few-Step Densities for Simulation-Based Inference

author.name: Jonas Arruda, Jan Hasenauer, Stefan T. Radev

entry.summary: This work develops conditional mean flows for simulation-based inference that combine few-step sampling with tractable density evaluation, showing the mean flow objective identifies conditional flow maps and that masking enables direct marginal likelihood estimation. This makes MCMC with learned posteriors practical, since repeated density evaluations no longer require numerical ODE integration.

entry.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics

author.name: Jian Gu, Hongyu Zhang, Chunyang Chen, Aldeida Aleti

entry.summary: The authors propose interpreting language model residual stream states through lexical reference frames induced by the model's own remaining layers, using rounds of attention and typical attention outputs rather than fixed lenses or point-cloud methods. They argue no fixed-direction lens can exceed a squared-radius bound, and approximate each state's native, context-adaptive reference frame.

entry.title: Making every stage of medical device document assessment with large language models deterministic

author.name: Ryosuke Suzuki

entry.summary: This empirical study sends identical regulatory-assessment requests to fourteen commercial LLM deployments under deterministic sampling settings and finds every deployment returned differing assessments for at least one request, with label changes in twelve. Reduced reasoning and rephrased prompts did not eliminate the variation, raising reliability concerns for compliance-critical LLM use.

entry.title: Enhancing Multimodal RLVR with Pairwise Token Contrast and Adaptive Trajectory Confidence

author.name: Yiran Zhang, Hanbo Huang, Jielan Li, Zhen Zhao, Shiyu Liang, Hongxia Hao

entry.summary: PACE improves multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by addressing two weaknesses of group-relative policy optimization: token-agnostic advantages and unreliable teacher-student credit signals that may reflect language shortcuts rather than image grounding. It scores responses under four teacher views crossing answer hints with image presence, applying confidence adaptively. This targets better credit assignment and visual grounding in multimodal reasoning RL.

entry.title: MagiC: Evaluating Multimodal Cognition Toward Grounded Visual Reasoning

author.name: Chengfei Wu, Ronald Seoh, Bingxuan Li, Liqiang Zhang, Fengrong Han, Dan Goldwasser

entry.summary: MagiC is a benchmark evaluating grounded multimodal cognition, assessing answer accuracy alongside reasoning quality and alignment with visual evidence. It contains roughly 5,500 weakly supervised QA examples plus 900 human-curated examples annotated with answers, rationales, and bounding boxes. It probes whether vision-language models genuinely ground their reasoning or exploit dataset biases.

entry.title: VoteGEO-Bench: Measuring the Impact of Generative Engine Optimization on Electoral Visibility

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao

entry.summary: VoteGEO-Bench studies how generative engine optimization (GEO) - rewriting web content to boost visibility in LLM-generated responses - could distort electoral information, covering the 2024 U.S. presidential and 2026 Japanese House of Representatives elections. The analysis finds many generative-engine citations come from lower-cost owned and open-platform sources, raising manipulation risks. This is a timely examination of information integrity in AI-mediated search.

entry.title: UltraDiff: Transferring High-Fidelity Priors to Compressed Latent Spaces for High-Resolution Image Generation

author.name: Jingjing Ren, Haitian Zheng, Haoyu Chen, Connelly Barnes, Zhifei Zhang, Yuqian Zhou, Zhe Lin, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: UltraDiff tackles the fidelity-efficiency trade-off in high-resolution latent diffusion by learning a joint f8-f32 latent distribution with a dual-branch DiT (MixTeacher) that uses shared attention to resolve ambiguity in heavily compressed f32 latents using f8 priors. It reformulates the problem as joint latent learning followed by marginal score distillation.

entry.title: GRASE: Geometry-native Real-to-sim Agentic Scene Modeling from Video

author.name: Zhaorui Lin, Haohan Liu, Zhen Chen, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: Presents an agentic real-to-sim framework that converts multi-view video into editable 3D scenes by keeping the capture as a standing reference throughout modeling, revising intermediate hypotheses when rendered evidence disagrees with observations. This closed-loop approach reduces the error propagation typical of one-pass pipelines.

entry.title: The Dormant Spiking Neuron: A State-Driven Mechanism for Efficient Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Ruichen Ma, Yicai Chen, Pujun Zhou, Yue Zuo, Chongyang Li, Shuang Liu, Shaogang Hu, Guanchao Qiao

entry.summary: Identifies an overlooked source of overhead in spiking neural networks: the continuous subthreshold dynamics of postsynaptic neurons, with up to 44% of ImageNet-trained ResNet-18 SNN neurons in deeply inhibited states that rarely fire. The proposed Dormant Spiking Neuron model uses a state-driven dynamic gate to let neurons enter a dormant state, cutting computation while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation

author.name: Yiqun Zhao, Binbin Huang, Haobin Duan, Zibo Zhao, Shenghua Gao

entry.summary: STRUCTPARTS addresses image-conditioned 3D generation with explicit part decomposition by introducing a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism, where each shape latent is interpreted in both part-local and object-global reference frames. A global-local interleaved transformer lets the model inherit geometric detail and structural coherence from holistic structured 3D priors. This enables generating editable, decomposable 3D assets rather than single fused meshes.

entry.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents

author.name: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao, Mugeng Liu, Ru Peng, Lang Mei, Xiaohan Yu, Liyan Liu, Chong Chen, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: MMSearch-OPD addresses training of long-horizon multimodal search agents via controllable data refinement plus joint reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation. A Refine pipeline expands reasoning chains from simple multimodal questions with parameterized control over search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements, reusing existing image-question pairs. Answer rewards with behavior penalties guide RL while the reward gap modulates token-level distillation.

entry.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Shimon Malnick, Nadav Orenstein, Ohad Fried, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: SoftCache improves training-free caching acceleration for diffusion transformers by using the staleness signal's headroom below the refresh threshold to modulate step size, replacing hard binary refresh/reuse decisions with soft, error-aware adjustments. This exploits information that existing dynamic caching methods discard. It reduces generation cost while controlling reuse-induced error.

entry.title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Yanchen Ding, Jiayi Chen, Jianfeng Xu, Wei Zhao, Li Yi, He Wang

entry.summary: CQDC-Warp is a GPU-accelerated differentiable quasi-dynamic simulator enabling batched model predictive control for contact-rich manipulation, with soft costs encouraging intended contacts while dynamics determine geometry and frictional response. Across 17,408 trials on 17 tasks it demonstrates contact-guided trajectory optimization at high throughput.

entry.title: From Optical Flow to Safety: Visual Safety Certification via Scale-Free Relative Motion

author.name: Bazeela Banday, Jishnu Keshavan

entry.summary: The authors propose a visual safety-certification paradigm for monocular autonomous navigation that encodes collision-cone geometry and safety constraints in a scale-free, depth-normalized relative-motion representation derived from optical flow, without reconstructing obstacle states or a metric world model. An online Concurrent Learning observer estimates normalized relative velocity to certify collision risk in real time.

entry.title: SPEAR: Selective Preference Elicitation with Adaptive Rewards for VLM-Guided Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zewen Wu, Ruizhe Liu, Pei Zhou, Feng Chen, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: SPEAR turns vision-language models into efficient preference oracles for robot manipulation by selecting only informative and distinguishable comparisons to reduce abstention, and by bootstrapping exploration with VLM-synthesized rewards before transitioning to preference-based refinement. It achieves 88.9% average success on manipulation benchmarks while cutting costly VLM inference.

entry.title: TS-WAM: Temporal Latent Actions and World-Action Coupling for Vision-Language Robot Control

author.name: Menghao Yin, Jiaju Yin, Xiyue Dong, Lixin Xu, Zhenhui Zhang, Ke Zhang, Yating Feng, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: TS-WAM is a lightweight teacher-student world-action model that learns from heterogeneous data including action-free human videos via a vlm-jepa framework with an EMA target branch, and couples it with a delta latent world model to predict temporal latent actions and future visual states. This addresses the lack of explicit future prediction in action-labeled VLA policies and improves generalization beyond demonstration conditions.

entry.title: Onboard Lightweight LLM Reasoning for Human-Aware Safe UAV Navigation

author.name: Siwei Cai, Yuwei Wu, Vijay Kumar, Lifeng Zhou

entry.summary: The authors present a fully onboard UAV pipeline that uses a shared BLIP encoder for scene captioning and text-conditioned segmentation fused with depth, plus a lightweight LLM (Qwen-2.5-0.5B) to infer obstacle-specific risk. This closes the human-aware safety gap where conventional planners treat pedestrians, cars, and walls as identical occupied geometry.

entry.title: A One-Sided McDiarmid-Type Inequality for Heavy Tails via Reverse KL Tensorization

author.name: Hanuka Eshima, Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Andrea Paudice

entry.summary: The paper derives a one-sided McDiarmid-type concentration inequality for functions of independent variables that are almost surely bounded above with a conditional moment condition of order p in (1, 2], applicable even with infinite variance. The proof introduces a reverse KL tensorization inequality with applications to sample means, median-of-means, and uniform risk bounds for unbounded losses.

entry.title: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Avishree Khare, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Rajeev Alur

entry.summary: Introduces Temporal Specification Guidance (TSG), a training-free inference-time framework that represents ordering, timing, and persistence requirements as temporal logic specifications and converts them into differentiable objectives to steer video generation during sampling. It scores visual concept evidence traces and uses gradient-based guidance with efficient differentiable semantics for metric temporal logic.

entry.title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models

author.name: Dingjie Song, Zhiling Yan, Yuxuan Zhang, Lichao Sun

entry.summary: Presents LEV, a decision model that adapts its computation depth by rerunning layers in a loop rather than generating tokens, reading options at every loop step and training all steps jointly so one checkpoint answers at any depth. Built on language models pretrained as loops, accuracy rises with additional depth, mimicking dual-process thinking without token-generation costs.

entry.title: GRADS: Graph-Regulated Agentic Data Synthesis with Controllable Difficulty

author.name: Gaocheng Yang, Ruijie Tao, Kai Ye, Senhua Zhang, Zhengqin Zhu, Ziyang Li

entry.summary: Introduces GRADS, a graph-guided agentic data synthesis framework for deep research agents that runs a closed loop of seed selection, evidence expansion, QA construction, and difficulty verification, ensuring synthesized multi-hop questions have difficulty that is empirically rather than only apparently deeper. It tackles the mismatch between intended and actual reasoning difficulty in synthetic data. Useful for training retrieval-heavy agents.

entry.title: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows

author.name: Kaixiang Wang, Zhaijiacheng Zhou, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: Profiling three multi-agent frameworks shows routing and review consume 31.7-43.5% of generative-LLM tokens, motivating replacement by low-cost decision models. Jev-LiteMAS bridges the planning gap (structured execution plans) and review gap (actionable repair feedback) that bounded decisions alone cannot fill. This yields significant cost savings in multi-agent LLM systems.

entry.title: Learning from Interaction Experience via Localized Context Distillation

author.name: Zhezheng Hao, Yongkang Yang, Xilin Xia, Jiarui Yu, Yi Liu, Fanjunduo Wei, Peijie Dong, Tianfu Wang, Qiang Lin, Can Wang, Hande Dong, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes Localized Context Distillation to resolve a dilemma in learning from interaction experience: off-policy distillation suffers exposure bias while on-policy distillation has uninformative states. The method selectively applies privileged teacher information at localized points, combining benefits of both. This supports continual improvement of LLMs during deployment.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond

author.name: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan, Haowen Xu, Liangliang Zhao, Ruixun Liu, Yuhan Wang, Yuwei Zhang, Liang Feng, Junhao Xiao, Kaiyan Zhang, Xuekai Zhu, Daizong Liu, Biqing Qi, Yihao Liu, Ganqu Cui, Ning Ding, Linfeng Zhang, Jianjun Li, Kun He, Xiang Bai, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive survey of reinforcement learning as a post-training mechanism for diffusion models, arguing that reward-driven trajectory optimization can address diffusion models' limitations in reasoning, exploration, and alignment with human objectives, analogous to RLHF's role for LLMs. The paper reviews methods across language, vision, and other modalities and includes an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion generation process. Its value lies in consolidating a fast-moving research area into a unified framework with an experience-centric, goal-driven perspective.

entry.title: RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent

author.name: Huan Zhang, Mingju Chen, Dongxu Zhou, Can Lv, Sen Cui, Faguo Wu, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: RSIFlow is a recursive self-improvement framework combining adaptive workflow orchestration with a meta-agent that evolves the improvement mechanisms themselves. It targets adapting self-improvement workflows to shifting performance bottlenecks using execution feedback across tasks like code generation and multi-hop QA.

entry.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations

author.name: Hasan Demirkiran, Jens Ernstberger

entry.summary: The paper audits agent-safety evaluation datasets for shortcut cues that make safety labels predictable without measuring the intended construct, introducing a three-level shortcut-auditing framework applied to LinuxArena trajectories and TS-Bench-derived datasets. Findings include shell-command length strongly predicting labels and guard performance collapsing from F1 0.901 to 0.495 under domain holdout.

entry.title: Same Context, Different Agents: A Behavioral Study of Semantic Layers, Orchestration and Compaction in Data Agents

author.name: Zhivar Sourati, Marianne Menglin Liu, Zheng Wang, Rongguang Wang, Sai Ashish Somayajula, Tao Sheng, Kyu J. Han, Sujith Ravi, Dan Roth

entry.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive empirical study of three context-engineering techniques (semantic layers, orchestration, compaction) for data agents, evaluated alone and combined across seven LLMs and 1,514 long-horizon tasks on five benchmarks, covering behavior, accuracy, and cost. Agents without these techniques cluster into behavioral groups such as investigators and premature answerers. The results inform how agent behavior mediates the effectiveness of context engineering.

entry.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Ziye Mei, Haotian Ma

entry.summary: Introduces the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS) to identify SAE feature responses that recur consistently under prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request, evaluated across 27 pretrained SAEs on eight language models. The work clarifies that feature changes observed on one transformed prompt need not recur or affect downstream computation, separating reproducible redistribution from incidental variation.

entry.title: LTM: Latent Transition Based In-Context Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qixin Sun, WenLong Gao, Xiansheng Chen, Zhongyuan Wang, Si Liu, Pengwei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Transition Memory, which stores robot manipulation history as compact latent transitions between consecutive observations, instantiated on the pi-0.5 VLA model with a frozen latent action encoder, lightweight adapter, and causal KV caching. Achieves 58.54% success on RoboMME and 80.5% on LIBERO-Mem without memory-specific annotations or external reasoning-model calls.

entry.title: X-Fly: Learning to Reach and Stop in Full-Chunk Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Ruibin Ju, Ruifeng Cai, Min Xu, Lin Wang

entry.summary: X-Fly is a staged training framework for aerial vision-language navigation that executes full predicted action chunks to amortize expensive VLM queries, cutting inference from 195 to 42 ms per waypoint. It introduces Recovery DAgger to relabel learner-visited states and address the fact that no-stop failures account for nearly half of full-chunk behavior cloning outcomes on OpenFly. The work tackles real deployment constraints of VLM-based drone navigation.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification

author.name: Mohamed Karim Belaid, Maximilian Rabus, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: The paper proposes a classification variant of pairwise difference learning, which trains on instance pairs to predict outcome differences, together with a meta-learning technique for the task. It further addresses faithful uncertainty quantification by building on decompositions of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. This extends a promising low-data regime method with calibrated confidence estimates.

entry.title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection

author.name: Kajaree Das, Oliver B\"ose, Subarnaduti Paul, Gabriel Storch, Martin Mundt

entry.summary: Analyzes how continual learning methods for deepfake detection, trained on a chronological sequence of 11 real-world generation methods, affect fairness across demographics over time. It shows that mitigating accuracy forgetting is insufficient: CL methods produce non-trivial, worsening fairness dynamics, making deepfake detection a societal as well as technical concern.

entry.title: Change the Number, Change the Answer: Assessing Rating Scale Sensitivity in LLM-Based Text Scoring

author.name: Wonjeong Jo, Gyuwan Kim, Ming Shan Hee

entry.summary: Systematically defines and investigates scale sensitivity in LLM-based text scoring, distinguishing numerical sensitivity from semantic sensitivity. Crossing formats, ranges, and sign conventions across three social-science tasks shows that LLM scores shift substantially with rating scale design, questioning cross-study comparability.

entry.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code

author.name: Yipeng Gao, Ziyao Zeng, Jinfa Huang, Yijiang Li, Haolin Xiong, Wang Qin, Xinlei Yu, Youheng Yao, Jie Zhang, Kun-Yu Lin, Rong Liu, Yinyuan Zhao, Yajie Zhao, Meiqi Guo, Jiebo Luo, Lei Shu, Yunhao Ge, Xinyu Hu, Laurent Itti

entry.summary: Introduces an ecosystem for coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content, including a 2M-program dataset of standalone executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical 3D coding guidance. Programs are packaged with execution environments, assets, and verification records. This extends the code-as-world-representation paradigm to 3D content creation at scale.

entry.title: Hard Way, The Only Way: Provable Merits of Training on Hardest Examples

author.name: Elvis Dohmatob

entry.summary: The paper develops a high-dimensional theory of data pruning via weighted empirical risk minimization, precisely characterizing limiting test error curves when input dimension and sample size grow with a fixed ratio. The analysis shows provable merits of training on the hardest examples and recovers several recent empirical and theoretical results as special cases.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery

author.name: Xudong Zhang, Jianzhe Li, Yitong Tang, Peijie Zhou

entry.summary: TDAL formulates budgeted genetic and drug perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem and learns the acquisition policy with temporal difference learning, instead of using a fixed acquisition function with model updates. Experimental feedback is used as a training signal for the selection policy itself, enabling adaptation to different response landscapes. This could improve experimental design efficiency in biology and drug screening.

entry.title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows

author.name: Claudio Bonanno, Andrea Bulgarelli, Elia Cellini, Alessandro Nada, Dario Panfalone, Davide Vadacchino, Lorenzo Verzichelli

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate numerically that topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills lattice gauge theory can be mitigated by combining open boundary conditions with Stochastic Normalizing Flows, showing controlled autocorrelation times for the topological charge down to lattice spacings of 0.03 fm. This marks progress toward ML-assisted ergodic sampling in the continuum limit.

entry.title: Acceleration and its Limits in Gaussian Variational Inference

author.name: Jaesung R. Park, Uijeong Jang, Yifan Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows that classical momentum acceleration achieving sqrt-kappa convergence extends to Gaussian variational inference when exact Gaussian expectations are available, but proves that with only pointwise derivatives, any randomized algorithm requires kappa^1-o(1) queries for a family of strongly log-concave targets. This identifies curvature information as the fundamental barrier to acceleration in GVI. The lower bound is a sharp separation result.

entry.title: Dimension-Free PAC-Bayes Generalization for Deep Neural Networks via Dirichlet Processes

author.name: Sumit Vashishtha

entry.summary: The paper addresses the vacuity of classical PAC-Bayes bounds for overparameterized networks by placing the prior over the nonparametric space of data distributions via a Dirichlet Process, inducing parameter distributions through push-forward measures. The data processing inequality then yields relative entropy terms independent of parameter dimension, avoiding bounds that scale with network size.

entry.title: Designing Experiments for External Decision Makers

author.name: Sahel Iqbal, Tom Rainforth

entry.summary: The paper introduces usage-aware experimental design, extending Bayesian experimental design to settings where collected data is acted upon by external parties whose decision procedures are unknown or non-Bayesian. An adaptive design policy is trained to minimize usage risk, handling multiple external rules via averaging or worst-case formulations.

entry.title: MARS - A foundational map auto-regressor

author.name: Qi Zhang, Suvam Bag, Rupanjali Kukal, Lucas Thai, Jacob Kovarskiy, Mike Bianco, Xiaojie Guo, Raphael Tang, Mikael Figueroa, Rishi Madhok, Nikolaos Karianakis, Fuxun Yu

entry.summary: MARS is claimed to be the first map foundation model, an autoregressive model that generates both multi-polyline road networks and polygon buildings in a unified manner, avoiding multi-stage pixel-segmentation-plus-vectorization pipelines. It was trained on what the authors report as the largest multi-class map extraction dataset, totaling 3.4M examples. This applies autoregressive language-modeling ideas to structured vector map generation.

entry.title: VLA-$\Delta$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qi Lu, Jiarun Li, Ce Zhang, Miao Pan, Yi Pan, Xu Wang, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: VLA-Delta proposes supervising VLA models on explicit physical state changes between current and future states rather than only observation-action mappings, addressing overfitting to demonstrated correspondences. Unlike methods that use language, visual, or latent reasoning as indirect guidance, it makes the physical transition itself the learning target.

entry.title: Hear, Localize, and Reason: Spatially Aware Scene Understanding for Audio-Visual LLMs

author.name: Kim Sung-Bin, Lee Jung-Mok, Jinwoo Jung, Oh Hyun-Bin, Hyeonggon Ryu, David Harwath, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: Introduces HLR-AVSceneQA, a benchmark with a hear-localize-reason hierarchy testing whether audio-visual LLMs can recognize sounds, localize their sources in egocentric and allocentric views, and reason about how those sources relate to the visual scene. This targets a key limitation of current AV-LLMs that treat audio as monaural semantics without spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Teaching DINOv3 About Partial 3D Geometry: A Self-Supervised Geometry-Aware Approach

author.name: Viktoria Ehm, Dongliang Cao, Riccardo Marin, Daniel Scholz, Weikang Wang, Florian Bernard, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Refines DINOv3 features via LoRA-based self-supervised learning to produce descriptors robust to partial shape observations, targeting the underexplored partial shape matching problem where existing features struggle with boundaries and spatial position dependence. The resulting features substantially improve partial matching performance.

entry.title: Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones

author.name: Madhav Iyengar, Andreas Geiger, Hilde K\"uhne

entry.summary: This paper adapts depth-recurrence retrofitting to vision-language models, pruning layers from the language backbone and looping over a subset of remaining layers with linear adapters that fuse and re-project token representations at each loop step. A three-stage recovery training procedure first restores language backbone quality, then recovers the full VLM. The approach reduces parameter footprint of pretrained VLMs while retaining capability.

entry.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture

author.name: Chen Yang, Jiemin Fang, Fanpeng Meng, Zihao Huang, Jichen Pang, Guanjun Wu, Zhikuan Bao, Qi Tian

entry.summary: SUPRA-Tex addresses single-image 3D texture generation by decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion, including an MLLM-based image editing model that predicts lighting-dependent materials. This avoids multi-view fusion artifacts and preserves fine details of the reference image. Author list includes Qi Tian, indicating an industrial research pedigree.

entry.title: Line-Augmented cuVSLAM: Robust Visual Odometry in Low-Texture Environments

author.name: Dara Molloy, Terry Wu, Wonju Lee, Abhilash Nand Kumar, David Adley, Conor Ferguson, Hesam Rabeti

entry.summary: This work extends NVIDIA's CUDA-accelerated cuVSLAM with line features parameterized via Plucker coordinates and a minimal 4-DOF orthonormal representation, using Cauchy-robust point-to-line residuals. Lines from rack uprights, door frames, and wall junctions provide stable signals where point features fail in warehouse and factory environments. It directly improves deployable robot visual odometry.

entry.title: BubbleCBF: Constructive Safety for Second-Order Systems and Application to Autonomous Robot Navigation in Unknown Environments

author.name: Mani Amani, Mohammed Alyaseen, Zhirui Dai, Ki Myung Brian Lee, Nikolay Atanasov, Jorge Cortes

entry.summary: BubbleCBF provides a constructive method for designing feasible control barrier functions for second-order systems by building collision-free spheres in position space from signed distance functions and deriving velocity-dependent safety constraints from their geometry. The approach addresses feasibility challenges of higher-order CBFs and is applied to navigation in unknown environments.

entry.title: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Lichao Ni, Yuhan Liu, Pengfei Li, Guanghuan Fang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-level on-policy distillation framework that consolidates multiple frozen domain-specialist flow-based VLA policies into a single student, supervising both environment observations and intermediate action-flow trajectories with teacher velocity supervision on student-generated inputs. The student continually collects new environment data after each update, mitigating distribution mismatch at deployment.

entry.title: Preface to the Computational Agent Theory and ASI Alignment Sequence

author.name: Vanessa Kosoy

entry.summary: Vanessa Kosoy opens a research sequence laying out her Computational Agent Theory program for making superintelligence safe, framing the theoretical gaps in computer science and decision theory that must be closed and the unprecedented reliability standards any solution must meet. The preface situates her long-running formal alignment agenda in the current landscape where leading labs openly pursue ASI.

entry.title: Preface to the Computational Agent Theory and ASI Alignment Sequence

author.name: Vanessa Kosoy

entry.summary: This is the AI Alignment Forum crosspost of Vanessa Kosoy's preface to her Computational Agent Theory and ASI Alignment sequence, framing the existential risk posed by openly pursued superintelligence and the theoretical gaps in computer science and decision theory that any reliable solution must close. It introduces a formal research agenda intended to meet unprecedented standards of robustness.

entry.title: Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields: Evidence-Grounded Selective Safety for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Tianshi Wang, Jingsong Wang, Fengling Li, Jingjing Li, Xin Li, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces CNRF, a framework for selective safety in vision-language models that builds context-matched benign-harmful counterfactual pairs and uses their representation differences as risk directions, estimating neighborhood support separately from risk. This prevents unfamiliar inputs from being conflated with harmful ones and enables selective intervention rather than blanket refusal.

entry.title: RAC: A Relational Agent Contract for Constraint-Governed Engineering Tasks

author.name: Kaiyuan Zheng, Fengqing Jiang, Yichen Feng, Zubin Aaron Assadian, Yuetai Li, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Basel Alomair, Luyao Niu, Radha Poovendran

entry.summary: Proposes RAC, a harness-agnostic contract for engineering agents that separates the agent's semantic decisions from tool-based realization of precise consequences, specifying authoritative observations, independent verification, and repair evidence. On PCB placement, routing, and repair tasks it achieves the highest clean-pass rates, showing strong results on constraint-governed engineering.

entry.title: Money-Mule Detection as a Relational Learning Problem: A Study on the RBIH NFPC Dataset

author.name: Owais Ahmad, Anirudh Deodhar

entry.summary: The paper reframes money-mule detection as direct account-level scoring over a bank's relational schema modeled as a heterogeneous graph, using per-column encoders, relative-time encoding, and HeteroGraphSAGE on the RBIH NFPC dataset. Unlike rule-based production systems and transaction-level research, it captures counterparty and temporal network structure. This is relevant to financial crime detection where individual transfers look benign.

entry.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine

author.name: Junyao Yang, Zongxia Li, Yucheng Shi, Zhongzhi Li, Ruhan Wang, Ruiwen Zhou, Haitao Mi, Shuicheng Yan, Leowei Liang

entry.summary: Terminal-RSI trains terminal agents via alternating recursive self-rewrite of verified trajectories and critic-inheriting policy refinement, supported by technical components like Turn-Boundary Skip-Observation GAE, Family Dense Reward, and Success-Prioritized Reward. It implements a five-stage training sequence starting from Qwen3.8, an established model rather than a new release.

entry.title: CoTS: Competitive Token Selection for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Jie Yu, Yuxi Sun, Zhaoxu Li, Chunxiao Liu, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: CoTS proposes continuously adapting the strength of latent reasoning at each decoding step, replacing the typical all-or-nothing approach of global soft activation or hard uncertainty-threshold switching in chain-of-thought alternatives. Confident steps commit to discrete tokens while ambiguous steps preserve multiple plausible alternatives as competing soft candidates.

entry.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?

author.name: Zhengxin Zhang, Maosen Tang, Ning Wang, Changhao Li, Jingren Zhou, Bo Dai, Sainyam Galhotra, Alex Townsend, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: Introduces STOPD, which accelerates on-policy distillation by randomly truncating student rollouts and correcting the resulting sampling bias with blockwise inverse-probability weighting, sampling stopping positions before generation. This avoids computing teacher feedback over full rollouts while preserving distillation quality.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents

author.name: Hanzhen Wang, Boxiang Lyu, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Dake Zhang, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: Develops provably efficient algorithms for offline risk-sensitive RL using optimized certainty equivalents, a general class of risk measures, covering both dynamic and static OCE formulations. Under the tabular setting, the paper provides theoretical guarantees for learning risk-averse policies from fixed datasets without environment interaction.

entry.title: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation

author.name: Junho Moon, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, a topology-aware, prediction-adaptive loss for segmenting thin elongated structures, which for each required connection identifies the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction and supervises its bottleneck jointly with the skeleton point. This adapts supervision to the evolving prediction rather than fixed centerlines, improving connectivity.

entry.title: Can Capability Enhancement be Localized?

author.name: Anh Tuan Nguyen, Anna Bair, Zico Kolter

entry.summary: Complementing prior work showing some attention heads are critical for task performance, this paper asks whether there exist small sets of heads whose removal improves task performance, a notion called Capability Enhancement Localization. The authors study this empirically across model families and find such heads do exist.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models as Open Quantum Systems

author.name: Akinori Tanaka, Yukinao Akamatsu, Takuki Tomita, Yuji Hirono

entry.summary: The authors show that the continuous-time forward and reverse dynamics of diffusion language models can be embedded in the open quantum systems framework, enabling sampling over superpositions of sentence states. They construct a tau-leaping unraveling scheme that updates multiple token positions per step, supporting generation conditioned on superposed prompts and thoughts.

entry.title: ABNAT: Attention-Based Noise-Aware Training for Robust Transformers on Analog Compute-in-Memory Systems

author.name: Wenshuai Yao, Wenyong Zhou, Hanyong Shao, Zhiyuan Ning, Yizhe Chen, Yuannuo Feng, Kechao Tang, Ru Huang

entry.summary: ABNAT analyzes how analog compute-in-memory hardware noise reshapes attention maps in Transformers, finding that divergence between clean and noisy attention grows in deeper layers, and proposes an attention-aware noise injection training method to build robustness. This targets the energy-efficiency promise of analog CIM hardware without the usual performance degradation. It addresses a key gap in prior noise-aware training that ignored attention dynamics.

entry.title: Graph Additive Models disentangling feature, topology, and interactions

author.name: Clara Alvarez-Rodriguez, Steve Azzolin, Vincenzo Marco De Luca, Filippo Maria Bianchi, Andrea Passerini, Antonio Longa

entry.summary: The paper introduces AMIGA, an interpretable graph neural network that fixes three limitations of Graph Neural Additive Networks: spurious relevance inheritance by irrelevant nodes, topology represented only via shortest-path distances, and entanglement of feature, distance, and interaction effects. It explicitly disentangles these components for more faithful interpretability.

entry.title: Policy-Aligned Predictive Verification for Adaptive VLA Action-Chunk Execution

author.name: Minkyu Kim, Junhoo Lee, Seungyeon Kim, Suhyun Jeon, Baekseung Kim, Donghoon Han, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: The paper introduces a policy-aligned predictive verifier (PAV) for vision-language-action policies that evaluates candidate action-chunk prefixes in the policy's internal task-conditioned representation space, predicting whether execution preserves the ability to complete the task. This improves on existing adaptive-execution signals like generation stability or prediction agreement.

entry.title: Stop Training Against Soft Users: Mentalized Adversarial Self-Play for Proactive Dialogue

author.name: Zanwu Liu, Dan Zhang, Xiaodi Wang, Yongbo Mao, Xiaoyang Guo, Yonglin Wu, Peiyue Jiang, Yangyang Wei, Zecheng Lin

entry.summary: MASP frames proactive dialogue as a partially observable game between a system and a rationally resisting user, representing the user's evolving mental state with a BDI-based latent state and separating teacher mentalization from policy learning in adversarial self-play. It addresses the problem that planners trained against fixed or overly compliant simulators achieve inflated success reflecting soft-user bias.

entry.title: OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Yuechen Luo, Zhiyi Lai, Miao Ziqi, Zihang Xu, Jingxuan Xu, Songwei Yu, Wenqiang Zhu, Weihao Li, Junhao Fan, Haoyang Huang, Yanan Wu, Ken Deng

entry.summary: OPRD targets a diagnosed failure mode of repository-level coding agents: ignoring relevant information already in context, with only sparse Pass/Fail supervision available. It combines multi-scope reminder supervision with outcome-based routing, using self-imitation on successful rollouts and teacher reverse-KL supervision on failed ones. This addresses process supervision for long-horizon agent reliability.

entry.title: ZoomCap: Evidence-Routed Visual Zooming for Recoverable Visual Information Transfer

author.name: Hao Shi, Jiafeng Wang, Yuzhuo Fu, Tao Zhang, Jian Bai, Juelu Zhang, Qing Cui, Chao Huang

entry.summary: ZoomCap reformulates fine-grained captioning as recoverable visual information transfer, where a teacher acquires missing evidence under a finite observation budget. It routes conditional knowledge retrieval, OCR-sensitive reading, coverage-gap recovery, and adaptive visual zooming based on a draft caption, applying deeper crops only to complex regions. This targets the conflation of caption quality with caption length.

entry.title: PiCo: Physics-Informed Concept Probing for Geo-Foundation Models

author.name: Yihang She, Andrew Blake, Jianbo Qi, Srinivasan Keshav

entry.summary: PiCo is a post-hoc interpretability framework for geo-foundation models that identifies concept vectors in embedding spaces using synthetic multispectral satellite observations generated by coupling a 3D radiative transfer model with a game engine. Projecting embeddings onto these vectors reveals which physical sensitivities drive predictions, informing hypotheses about downstream performance. This brings concept-probing interpretability to geospatial foundation models.

entry.title: Decoupled Safety Control: A Safety-Control Algorithm for Training-Free Safety Guidance

author.name: Huilin Zhou, Ruoxi Cheng, Yuhang Wang, Yuming Liu, Minghao Sun, Ruolong Ma, Lan Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes the coupled safety-control chain in training-free safety guidance for text-to-image diffusion models, where one unsafe condition simultaneously determines what to avoid, when to intervene, and how. The proposed decoupled safety control separates these roles, improving robustness when harmful and benign semantics are entangled during sampling.

entry.title: Beyond Generation: Using Multimodal LLMs as Detectors of LLM-Generated Deepfake Facial Images

author.name: Olivia Salamon, Virginia N. L. Franqueira, Shujun Li

entry.summary: Benchmarks six MLLMs (including GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5, Gemini 3, and Seed 1.6) on detecting synthetic facial images from a 400-image dataset spanning seven leading image generators, investigating whether models rely on physical inconsistencies or digital artifacts such as watermarks. The study probes whether MLLMs can serve as practical forensic tools as traditional detection struggles.

entry.title: SCOPE: Semantic Bounded Credit Optimization for Prompt Engineering in Text-to-image Generation

author.name: Yufei Jiao, Jinfa Huang, Zeyue Xue, Tianyu Xie, Yuexiao Ma, Rongrong Ji, Xiawu Zheng, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: SCOPE improves RL-based prompt rewriting for frozen text-to-image generators by aligning credit assignment with semantic structure. The rewriter jointly generates an enhanced prompt and its semantic partition, and SCOPE pools policy log-probability shifts within each object, count, attribute, or relation span to derive shared token coefficients under GRPO, without needing separate span rewards or extra annotations. This matches updates to coherent semantic units rather than individual subwords.

entry.title: Complementary Future Token Pruning for World Action Models

author.name: Baekseung Kim, Junhoo Lee, Sohyeon Hong, Suhyun Jeon, Minkyu Kim, Seungyeon Kim, Donghoon Han, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: CF-Prune is a training-free method that prunes future-frame tokens in world action models by exploiting the insight that predicted visual frames need not retain full synthesis fidelity since they mainly support action generation. It uses instruction and action attention plus entropy-based phase identification to keep dense computation only during precision-critical denoising phases. This cuts inference latency for robot-focused WAMs.

entry.title: MuSTMM: Learning Sound-Triggered Mobile Manipulation across Multiple Scenes

author.name: Hao Ju, Feng Yan, Zhihao Zhong, Heng Yang, Shaofei Huang, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: MuSTMM is a large dataset for Sound-Triggered Mobile Manipulation spanning 31 scenes, combining spatial audio rendering with physical interaction, including 14.36 million precomputed binaural room impulse responses and scene-disjoint splits for unseen-scene evaluation. The resource enables systematic study of audio-driven navigation and manipulation generalization beyond limited object-layout variations.

entry.title: Mem4Act: Learning Effective Latent Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yun Zhang, Zhiyu Huang, Tianhui Cai, Chen Tang, Wei Wang, Jiaqi Ma

entry.summary: Mem4Act learns a fixed-size latent memory representation explicitly optimized for long-horizon robotic control, addressing how to efficiently cover long histories, what to retain, and how to use it, instead of relying on raw histories, compressed visual tokens, or language summaries. The aim is to keep task-relevant temporal, semantic, and perceptual information without unbounded context growth.

entry.title: When Reasoning Traces Conflict with Evidence: How Answer Configuration Shapes Evidence Following

author.name: Shaoang Li, Yanhang Shi, Jian Li

entry.summary: Studies how retained reasoning traces interact with new evidence, finding that answering in a separate call rather than continuing the model's own thinking raises evidence-following by 29.9 to 60.6 points across three model families on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, while removing the trace lowers accuracy similarly. Continuation tends to repeat stale conclusions when traces and evidence conflict.

entry.title: FedSkillGit: Federated Skill Evolution via Version Control

author.name: Boxun Lan, Jiamei Li, Weijian Li, Chengyu Yang, Zhuang Qi, Chengcheng Wan, Xiaohong Chen, Ming Hu

entry.summary: FedSkillGit tackles federated evolution of natural-language agent skills across data owners who cannot pool raw data, replacing whole-document aggregation with a version-control-inspired mechanism that transmits only client-specific deltas. It identifies three flaws of naive whole-document federated skill evolution: privacy leakage in evolved documents, wasted communication, and buried client contributions. This connects the agent-skills trend with federated learning constraints.

entry.title: Are You Sure Your LLM Is Sure? Repairing and Auditing Confidence

author.name: Arijit Dey, Bhartendu Kumar, Ramya Hebbalaguppe, Khuushi Maheshwari

entry.summary: RADAR is a reliability framework that separates confidence repair from deployment decisions and residual-error auditing, decomposing prediction risk into outcome noise, information hidden by the score, and mapping error. It proposes Probe-Anchored Isotonic Calibration, which learns a monotone map from correctness-probe predictions on unlabeled target prompts without requiring labels.

entry.title: Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing

author.name: Sima Noorani, Shayan Kiyani, George Pappas, Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: The paper revisits weak-to-strong routing, where small edge-deployed models escalate to stronger models, and characterizes the optimal routing policy using disagreement signals rather than ground-truth correctness supervision. This enables cost-effective routing for open-ended and agentic tasks where correctness signals are hard to obtain.

entry.title: SHRED: Self-Play for Heterogeneous Road-Users without Expert Demonstrations

author.name: Wei-Jer Chang, Zhouchonghao Wu, Akshay Rangesh, Weixin Li, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: SHRED is a framework that jointly trains vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists through large-scale heterogeneous self-play from random initialization, without human driving demonstrations. It combines type-specific dynamics and objectives with procedural scenario generation to enable diverse interaction behaviors to emerge. This challenges the assumption that realistic traffic simulation requires large-scale logged trajectories, with implications for autonomous driving planning and simulation.

entry.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations

author.name: Haotian Ma, Ziye Mei, Frederic Sala

entry.summary: Introduces SAE Additivity Residuals (SAR) to quantify behavioral variation unexplained by low-order feature interactions, showing under independent subset sampling that population SAR equals the normalized energy of higher-order interactions. Comparisons with sum-preserving random rotations distinguish compositionality inherent to SAE representations from that induced by downstream computation.

entry.title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework

author.name: Yanyang Xiao

entry.summary: Develops an orthogonal polynomial dynamics framework explaining spectral bias (F-principle) asymptotically: why networks learn low-frequency, sinusoidal components first, under general activations including ReLU and sigmoid, with weak data assumptions and avoidance of aliasing effects. It extends theoretical understanding of frequency-order learning to arbitrary network structures.

entry.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning

author.name: Sara Dorfman, Nir Goren, Gal Barak, Daniel Cohen-Or, Or Patashnik

entry.summary: Identifies that multi-turn image editing degrades because small distribution shifts accumulate across turns, creating a train-inference gap. The authors adapt the Self-Forcing principle to image editing, forcing the editor to train on its own previous-turn outputs, with a training scheme (asymmetric conditioning) to handle deviations of self-generated trajectories from ground truth. This should improve the reliability of iterative editing workflows.

entry.title: Imperfect Is Perfect: Learned Column Prefilling for Branch-Price-and-Cut

author.name: Haoran Liu, Yu Yang

entry.summary: Shows that preloading a branch-price-and-cut solver with imperfect, non-optimal columns held outside the master and priced at smoothed duals speeds up the root LP, whereas even optimal columns can hurt. Trains a neural edge scorer and a dual-center predictor to generate these pools in seconds, turning warm-starting into a learning problem.

entry.title: Isolating a Language Model's Judgment with a Label-Free Subspace

author.name: Chaemin Jang, Donggyu Lee, Jeesoo Kim, Dongman Lee, Jihee Kim

entry.summary: This work shows that differences in hidden states of a language model judging the same input under different instruction formats concentrate in a low-dimensional expression subspace. The subspace is identified without benchmark labels and removed from a linear predictor to isolate the model's internal judgment, improving reliability of correctness, entailment, and safety judgments.

entry.title: Ranking and Partitioning of Attention Heads for Sparse and Continual Reinforcement Learning Fine-tuning

author.name: Ruizhe Shi, Zaiwen Yang, Qiubo Wang, Banghua Zhu, Maryam Fazel

entry.summary: The authors rank attention heads by gradient norm to select a small trainable subset for sparse RL fine-tuning of language models, and partition heads across tasks to reduce interference in continual learning. They provide theory linking gradient norm to training effectiveness and show empirically that tuning higher-ranked heads often matches dense baselines on math, instruction-following, and coding tasks.

entry.title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Bingxi Hou, Guochao Jiang, Guofeng Quan, Weiqing Li, Wenfeng Feng, Guohua Liu, Yuewei Zhang

entry.summary: Waypoint-OPD improves policy-shift distillation by comparing a teacher's early and late RL policy shifts using an intermediate checkpoint, gating which shifts are transferred to a student on student-visited trajectories. This addresses the problem that endpoint-only shifts can hide canceling or contradictory preference changes during teacher training.

entry.title: LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training

author.name: Max Zhu, Bohang Sun, Pietro Lio, Jialin Yu

entry.summary: LCT is a GPU execution framework for losslessly compressing weights, activations, and optimizer states during training, using optimized Huffman coding kernels with precomputed codebooks designed for the repeated encode-decode regime of training. It achieves up to 1.455x compression with low overhead, demonstrated on training and finetuning including a 162M-parameter model. This offers exact rather than lossy memory savings for LLM training.

entry.title: Iterative Neural Variational Solver of Committor Function in Under-damped Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Tiejun Li, Zhaoqi Liu, Xiang Zhou

entry.summary: This paper tackles the open problem of computing committor functions for under-damped Langevin dynamics, where the backward Kolmogorov equation lacks a variational structure. The authors develop an iterative neural variational solver enabling quantitative transition path theory analysis in the under-damped regime.

entry.title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost

author.name: Felix Parker, Danielle A. Ripsman, Emmett Springer, Kimia Ghobadi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why learned warm starts for the simplex method reduce iteration counts far more than wall-clock time, finding on 25 LP classes that a supervised predictor removes two-thirds of iterations but only a third of time. The authors prove that starts with equal overlap with an optimal basis can differ in linear-algebra cost, explaining the gap. They propose learning from measured solver cost rather than iteration proxies.

entry.title: Coordination-Free Workload Regularization for Variable-Cost Distributed Training

author.name: Tao Huang, Chen Zhu, Antonio Alonso, Daming Li, Adarsh Goura, Jaideep Ray, Yitong Zhou

entry.summary: Batch Cost Lookahead (BCL) is a coordination-free data-loading policy that buffers a bounded local window and repacks records into fixed-cardinality batches with balanced estimated cost, addressing idle time when per-record costs vary widely in synchronous data-parallel training. It preserves the trainer contract without cross-rank communication, reducing per-rank batch-cost variability by up to 82.8 percent in simulation and improving throughput across 13 NeMo-based training runs.

entry.title: International Multi-Centre Validation of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Precise Discrimination between Normal and Abnormal Retinal Development

author.name: Zhanhan Tu, Nikhil Reddy, Helen J. Kuht, Ha-Jun Yoon, Gail D. E. Maconachie, Ravi Purohit, Prateek Pani, Line Kessel, Jinu Han, Jing Jin, Shui-Hua Wang, Karthik Bharadwaj, Viral Sheth, Michael Hisaund, Rebecca J. McLean, George Garratt, Chetan Kantibhai Patel, Kanmin Xue, Callum Hunt, Zisen Zhou, Ian De Silva, Seema Teli, Sonal Shah, Vanessa Rodwell, Aarti Patel, Irene Gottlob, Yu-Dong Zhang, Zedong Zheng, Girish Varma, Mervyn G. Thomas

entry.summary: A retrospective multicentre study validating a ResNet50-based domain adversarial network for classifying normal versus abnormal retinal development in OCT scans across five centres in four countries, four OCT devices, and the UK Biobank. It compares six source-to-target domain adaptation pairings against clinician graders, addressing device variability in paediatric retinal imaging.

entry.title: Multimodal AI Detection for Math-Heavy Scientific Text

author.name: Yixuan Huang, Danish Pruthi, Bhuwan Dhingra

entry.summary: The authors build coupled human-AI pairs by regenerating human-written proofs and prose from pre-2022 arXiv LaTeX sources using 15 modern LLMs, then show that detectors using only PDF-extracted text miss the visual formatting signals of math-heavy scientific content. They propose a multimodal detection approach exploiting this rendering information.

entry.title: Data Strategies for Large Language Models: A Unified Perspective on the Training Lifecycle

author.name: Yuanjian Xu, Jianing Hao, Tianze Sun, Yongyao Duan, Sam Chen, Jinyi Han, Wanbo Zhang, Yuxuan Sun, Guang Zhang, Zhong Li

entry.summary: This survey unifies data-strategy research across pretraining and post-training by framing data selection, weighting, and scheduling as policies that allocate a training budget over candidate examples, with utility depending on the model and its training state. It organizes methods by decision granularity and model dependence, addressing inconsistent terminology in the field. A useful reference for anyone doing data-centric LLM training.

entry.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?

author.name: Zixiang Xu, Zirui Song, Wanrong Zheng, Chiyu Zhang, Yue Huang, Yuyang Peng, Kexin Zhang, Jinkun Chen, Xiuying Chen, Xiangliang Zhang, Yan Liu, Laurent Itti, Frank Shyu, Xiaoqiang Luo, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Luke Simon, Xiyang Hu, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: Grid-Bench is an executable benchmark testing whether LLMs can predict final states of discrete grid worlds after sequences of spatial operations, with rules given as text and every prediction checkable via reference execution. It spans 2D, 3D, and 4D grids and eight operation families. Evaluation of six LLMs probes a largely untested capability: compositional spatial state tracking.

entry.title: RoboCloth: A Large-Scale Real Cloth Material Dataset for Neural Reflectance Reconstruction

author.name: Zhen Li (Simon Fraser University), Haoran Qin (Westlake University), Francesco Di Sario (University of Torino, Simon Fraser University), Daniel Rebain (University of British Columbia, Wayve), Andrea Tagliasacchi (Simon Fraser University, Wayve, University of Toronto)

entry.summary: RoboCloth provides 500 real cloth materials captured with robotically controlled calibrated cameras and lighting, with roughly 580 HDR frames per material and sparse surface geometry aligned to the robot frame. The authors demonstrate a two-stage neural reconstruction pipeline that learns cloth material priors and then fits high-resolution latent material representations.

entry.title: A Decision-Aware Evaluation Protocol for Uncertainty in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Saket Maganti, Shreyank N Gowda

entry.summary: Proposes a decision-aware protocol that separates uncertainty estimation from deferral policy and evaluates their combination under fixed review budgets in medical segmentation, reporting fixed-budget error reduction and risk-coverage behavior. Demonstrated across retinal vessel, skin lesion, and polyp segmentation with multiple backbones.

entry.title: Visual Sanad: Auditing Vision-Language Models for False Acceptance of Qur'anic Citations

author.name: Niaz Mohaiman Abtahi, Reyana Shahid, Evan Maksud

entry.summary: Visual Sanad is a controlled benchmark of 2,400 rendered images testing whether VLMs falsely accept incorrect Quranic verse attributions depending on visual framing, from plain text to decorative and authority-framed layouts. It covers 100 English verses with four factual states and six visual conditions, all human-audited before rendering. Across 24 model-prompt runs, the authors observe sharp failure patterns in citation verification.

entry.title: FPG-Seg: Annotation-free Retinal Vessel Topology Segmentation

author.name: James Willoughby, Irina Voiculescu

entry.summary: FPG-Seg is an annotation-free pipeline for retinal vessel segmentation combining classical vesselness filtering, Bayesian deep learning, and topology-aware graph reconstruction, requiring no manual labels for training or hyperparameter tuning. Across four benchmark datasets it achieves a clDice of 0.74-0.78, reaching 86-98 percent of a fully-supervised baseline. The work also releases what the authors believe is the largest resource of its kind for this task.

entry.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation

author.name: SeungJu Cha, Ye-Chan Kim, HyunGee Kim, Sungho Koh, Dong-Jin Kim

entry.summary: DaTMe is a training-free token merging framework for diffusion models that grounds merging decisions in diffusion dynamics rather than text relevance, preserving background objects and unmentioned local details that prompt-aligned criteria degrade. It addresses the key question of which tokens can be safely merged during generation. The result is faster image generation with better structural coherence.

entry.title: When to Ask for Help: A Decision-Theoretic Account and Measurement Standard for Slow-Module Scheduling in Dual-System Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shilin Zhang (North China University of Technology)

entry.summary: This paper formalizes when a dual-system VLA model should invoke its slow, expensive module, unifying fixed-ratio, fixed-budget, and history-gated schedules as degenerate cases of a Value of Intervention quantity. It proves optimal periodic scheduling under a renewal baseline and provides measured cost ratios across published systems, plus a measurement standard separating schedule quality from module quality.

entry.title: Diffeomorphic Hidden-State Steering: Improving Imitation Learning Policy Robustness through Expert Hidden-State Geometry

author.name: KwangBin Lee

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a trained imitation-learning policy and finds expert hidden-state variation concentrated in few dimensions, then proposes DHS: learning an invertible nonlinear coordinate map from expert hidden states to attenuate low-expert-variation coordinates at test time, improving closed-loop robustness without extra demonstrations or retraining.

entry.title: CF-Splat: Closed-Form Triangle Splatting with Mesh Priors

author.name: Yixin Fang, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: CF-Splat reformulates triangle-splatting radiance-field estimation over a known mesh as a closed-form problem, avoiding the iterative nonlinear optimization over millions of coupled parameters used in existing splatting methods. This yields faster scene appearance estimation with lower GPU memory and reduced susceptibility to local minima for robotic perception.

entry.title: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multi-Stream Quickest Change Detection

author.name: Wuxia Chen, Arman Adibi, Taposh Banerjee, Vahid Tarokh

entry.summary: The authors propose a mixture-of-experts framework for quickest change detection where a weighted sum of expert statistics crosses a threshold to declare a change, applied to multi-stream settings where an unknown subset of streams changes distribution. The resulting algorithms outperform best-known methods while avoiding the expense of generalized likelihood ratio approaches.

entry.title: Value-Informed Schedule Trimming for Accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo Guidance in Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Jaehyeon Kim, Ziseok Lee, Siyoung Choi, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: Proposes VISTA, a training-free method that automatically selects which denoising timesteps to guide in reward-guided discrete diffusion, replacing fixed heuristic sparse-guidance schedules. It formulates sparse guidance as approximating the full-guidance probability path and derives an estimable bound to allocate a fixed compute budget.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for HPC Job Scheduling: A Statistical Evaluation

author.name: Justin M. Cheney, Clement N. Nyirenda

entry.summary: A rigorous statistical comparison of six deep RL treatments (PPO, A2C, DQN, with and without action masking) against heuristics and a masked random control on two real Slurm workload traces across ten seeds. The finding that masked DRL treatments show no significant advantage on the homogeneous trace is a valuable skeptical result. It cautions against overclaiming RL value in HPC scheduling beyond masking effects.

entry.title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent

author.name: Xuanyi Liu, Ruiqi Li, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: Mallea is a system where a coding agent constructs explicit code world models from text, planning object structure, properties, and behavioral rules, with user steering and text-based world editing that preserves unaffected state. It also introduces texture memory for reusable appearance of whitebox-defined objects. This contributes to world-model research by coordinating object representations, rule revision, and visual memory in an executable framework.

entry.title: ISW-Agent: Integrating LLM-Driven Dialogue with n8n Workflow for Internal Solitary Wave Remote Sensing Image Processing

author.name: Hao Zhang (First Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, Qingdao, China), Hengrui Liu (First Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, Qingdao, China), Lina Sun (First Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, Qingdao, China), Junmin Meng (First Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, Qingdao, China)

entry.summary: The authors present ISW-Agent, a domain-specific agentic system that combines LLM dialogue interpretation with n8n workflow orchestration and independent scientific models to process internal solitary wave remote sensing imagery, from acquisition through detection to propagation prediction. In tests with 120 Chinese instructions per backend, both GPT-5.6 Sol and DeepSeek achieved a 94.2% strict task-match rate, with Sentinel-1 case studies demonstrating end-to-end processing. The work matters as a concrete example of LLM agents orchestrating scientific pipelines in oceanography.

entry.title: In-Context Preference-Conditioned Pareto Set Learning from Limited Offline Data

author.name: Yiming Yao, Liang Zhao, Qingfu Zhang

entry.summary: ICPSL introduces in-context learning for multi-objective optimization, mapping a specified preference directly to a Pareto-optimal solution using only limited offline data, avoiding per-preference retraining or repeated search. This enables adapting to new preferences and problems without further objective evaluations.

entry.title: CARA: Causally Guided Retrieval Agent for Question Answering

author.name: Weicheng Liu, Xiangcheng Wu, Depeng Xu, Haopeng Zhang, Xi Niu

entry.summary: CARA is a training-free retrieval agent for question answering over text-rich knowledge graphs that evaluates causal relevance of evidence using two criteria: consequentiality (does adding evidence help answerability) and essentiality (does removing it hurt). It combines these with path consistency to guide graph exploration, moving beyond pure textual-similarity retrieval.

entry.title: Exploring the Design Space of Permutation Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Zhe Xu, Mingfu Liang, Kavosh Asadi, Jean-Pascal Billaud, Tianyi Chen, Yanhui Guo, Christina Huang, Baekjin Kim, Jimmy Kim, Yufei Li, Daqi Sun, Jiachen Sun, Dian Yu, Zaiwei Zhang, Kaushik Rangadurai, Frank Shyu, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Luke Simon

entry.summary: This paper studies text-conditioned permutation generation with diffusion LMs through three parameterizations: hard assignment over shuffled candidate indices, soft assignment over doubly stochastic matrices, and direct ordering-score prediction with sorting. Evaluating on recommendation reranking with candidate sets of size 10 and 20 across three Amazon domains, it maps how the placement of permutation constraints shapes training objectives and sampling procedures.

entry.title: CoTranslator: Reverse to Forward Chain-of-Thought Translator for Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Zinan Tang, Zhuoshi Pan, Kairui Chen, Ze Yan, Shaomian Zheng, Yukun Zhang, Gang Wang, Biqing Huang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the cost-accuracy tradeoff in reasoning distillation by proposing CoTranslator, a model that learns to translate cheap reverse chain-of-thought responses (conditioned on known answers) into the distribution of verified forward responses obtained via rejection sampling. Trained on a small set of paired examples, it enables large-scale distillation data generation without expensive teacher calls. This matters because CoT data quality is a key bottleneck for training smaller reasoning models.

entry.title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Jongann Lee, Sun Woo Park, Yun Young Choi

entry.summary: The paper proves a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks, showing standard masking forces models to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. SIEVE resolves this with an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework using a spherical projection mask that preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics. Experiments confirm the predicted collapse and downstream gains on point cloud tasks.

entry.title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models

author.name: Yingzhuo Deng, Chong Li, Bingxin Liu, Yi Shu, Tianyu Peng, Can Xie, Siyao Song, Shuo Ren, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CoSTA, a post-hoc framework that decouples generation and synthesis token spaces in spoken dialogue models using compressed tokens, avoiding costly tokenizer replacement by extending the generation vocabulary with mean-initialized extensions and adapting pronunciation and dialogue behavior. It preserves the original speech tokenizer and decoder while shortening autoregressive sequences for cheaper inference.

entry.title: When Is Muon Optimal? Radial Fragility and Minimax Geometry

author.name: Ao Xu

entry.summary: The paper examines the theoretical justification for the Muon optimizer, which replaces matrix gradients with approximate polar factors, by extending the Isotropic Curvature Model to general radial laws via a Random-Radius ICM and a Polar-Factor Admissibility Set. It derives an exact geometric characterization of when scaled-polar updates are optimal and shows fragility of prior curvature-based explanations. This sharpens understanding of a rapidly adopted optimizer.

entry.title: Encoded but Exposed: Language Embeddings can Reveal More Than They Should in Recommender Systems

author.name: Linda Bekov\'a, Rodrigo Alves

entry.summary: The paper shows that item embeddings used in recommender systems can leak item identities: a simple cosine-similarity attack recovers identities with high mean reciprocal rank when an adversary holds auxiliary item text, persisting even through independently sourced descriptions. Leakage further propagates to user re-identification from sparse ratings. This exposes underappreciated privacy risks of embedding-based recommendation.

entry.title: FIRM: Fisher-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning
