author.name: Reeyansh Shah, Maram Hasan, Subhasis Chaudhuri, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: Proposes FIRM, a single-round server-side aggregation method for federated LLM unlearning that uses client-local Fisher statistics to normalize merged updates. It addresses a magnitude explosion failure mode where unnormalized aggregation of locally trained adapters degrades retained utility, offering a stable way to remove knowledge when forget and retain data stay distributed across private clients.

entry.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization

author.name: Sekh Mainul Islam, Pepa Atanasova, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: The authors shift LLM personalization research from dense models, whose polysemantic neurons obscure which components drive personalization, to Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, where sparse token routing enables localizing personalized behavior. They fine-tune three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of personalized and base models to learn interpretable latents that identify which experts encode user-specific traits. This provides both a practical personalization recipe and mechanistic interpretability into how MoE experts specialize.

entry.title: Specification Gaming and a Constrained Reinforcement Learning Mitigation in a Cleaning Gridworld

author.name: Hilda Adwubi Osei

entry.summary: Constructs a minimal gridworld where a cleaning robot can genuinely remove dirt or conceal it from a cheap sensor, showing a standard deep Q-network trained on the proxy reward games the sensor. The work pairs a deliberately constructed proxy/true objective gap with a constrained RL mitigation carrying a verifiable guarantee, moving beyond observational evidence of specification gaming.

entry.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning

author.name: Hedi Zisling, Liran Nochumsohn, Ilan Naiman, Mihir Parmar, Omri Azencot

entry.summary: Proposes a design principle for time-series language models based on combining complementary visual representations: line plots that preserve absolute measurements plus normalized delay embeddings that factor out amplitude scaling while exposing temporal structure. Dedicated visual encoders process both views before the language model reasons over them. This challenges the single-representation inductive bias common in existing TSLMs.

entry.title: Selection-Safe Conformal Early Exit: Distribution-Free Coverage under Adaptive Depth

author.name: Adria Binte Habib, Ibne Farabi Shihab

entry.summary: Shows that calibrating conformal prediction sets at each early-exit layer breaks coverage when the exit is chosen in a data-dependent way, and proposes a pathwise score based on prefix maxima with a single calibrated quantile. The resulting guarantee holds simultaneously for any post-calibration label-free stopping policy, and experiments show large coverage improvements over naive layerwise selection.

entry.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation

author.name: Haotian Ma, Ruqi Yang, Philip Townsend

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a post-hoc explainability method for multispectral image models that produces a full attribution matrix over position-channel pairs rather than a single spatial heatmap or global channel ranking. It works by defining a conditional game over the channels at each spatial position, fixing surrounding context, and computing Shapley values for that local game. This matters because channel relevance in multispectral data is often spatially localized and physically meaningful, a structure that existing explanation approaches fail to capture.

entry.title: TimeCap: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Captioning Wearable Health Time-Series Data

author.name: Max Rosenblattl, Milana Gurbanova, Karl Aurel Deck, Narayan Schuetz, Thomas Kaar, Manuel Milling, Nicolas Zumarraga, Ning Wang, Kelly W. Zhang, Anders Johnson, Robert Jakob, Bj\"orn W. Schuller, Elgar Fleisch, Daniel Seung Kim, Allan Lawrie, Patrick Langer, Maxwell A. Xu, Euan Ashley, Paul Schmiedmayer

entry.summary: TimeCap is an open-source pipeline for generating text captions of wearable health time-series data to address the scarcity of signal-grounded, reproducible text-time-series pairs that bottleneck time-series language models. Unlike LLM-based annotation, its outputs are exactly regenerable, enabling re-derivation, extension, and auditing of the resulting corpora.

entry.title: Activation-Adjacent Layer Normalization: Effects on Approximation Power

author.name: Yunhao Ni, Yuxin Guo, Jie Luo, Wenjun Wu, Lei Huang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how inserting layer normalization or RMSNorm next to activations changes the functions a network can represent, studying when activation-normalized and preactivation-normalized shallow networks can approximate a reference MLP. Using width augmentation to locally linearize normalization, the authors derive tight width requirements depending on activation range and affine parameters.

entry.title: Graph Dirichlet Energy for Fitting-Free Bivariate Causal Inference

author.name: Povilas Daniu\v{s}is

entry.summary: The paper proposes GDECI, a causal discovery criterion for bivariate cause-effect identification based on the Dirichlet energy of a graph signal on a kernel similarity graph, choosing the direction with lower energy. The method requires no regression fitting or independence testing, is invariant to strictly monotone transformations after a probability integral transform, and runs in O(n log n) time. It offers a fast, assumption-light alternative to classical causal inference methods.

entry.title: Topology-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Wind-Field Super-Resolution

author.name: Arjun Dadhwal, Brian Summa

entry.summary: This paper studies super-resolution models for wind fields, showing that pointwise reconstruction metrics and topological descriptors (persistence diagrams, merge trees) can disagree on whether CNN or GAN models are better. The authors fine-tune pretrained models with differentiable topology-inspired auxiliary losses on scalar speed, gradients, and level sets to better preserve scientifically meaningful structure.

entry.title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree

author.name: Xiaotian Chang, Yacoub Hendi

entry.summary: The authors prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella using deformations of rational curves and Riemann-Roch arguments. As a consequence, they establish identifiability of neural networks with general polynomial activation functions of sufficiently large degree.

entry.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks

author.name: Wentao Yu, Vincent W. S. Wong

entry.summary: The authors propose using analog radio-frequency computing to let base stations multicast neural network weights encoded in waveforms, enabling extremely low-power AI inference on constrained edge devices via passive mixers performing matrix-vector multiplications. The work addresses practical challenges of integrating AI and data flows over wireless networks. This could enable telecom operators to serve AI inference to devices too weak to run models locally.

entry.title: Flexible Doubly Robust Proximal Causal Inference for Censored Outcomes

author.name: Dhanajit Brahma, Ruolin Meng, Lawrence Carin, Ricardo Henao

entry.summary: This paper introduces Proximal Survival Bridge learning (PSB), a flexible doubly robust framework for estimating causal effects on right-censored time-to-event outcomes when unmeasured confounding is present. It extends proximal causal inference beyond restrictive parametric bridge models by providing outcome-bridge, treatment-bridge, and doubly robust estimators, instantiated with a kernel-based learner (PSB-K) using low-rank time decomposition and a neural learner (PSB-N) trained via projected maximization. This matters because survival analysis with hidden confounders is central to medicine, epidemiology, and policy evaluation.

entry.title: MIDI-REPA: Improving Text-to-Music Generation with Symbolic Representation Alignment

author.name: Song-Ze Yu, Fang-Duo Tsai, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: MIDI-REPA aligns intermediate representations of a flow-matching diffusion transformer with symbolic MIDI supervision derived from automatic music transcription, improving musical structure in text-to-music generation without extra inference cost. Building on the 122M-parameter FluxAudio-S baseline, the authors systematically study what, where, and when to align, finding early-layer piano-roll alignment over the full trajectory works best. This injects compact symbolic structure into audio generation.

entry.title: L2GSSL: Label-Efficient Local-to-Global Self-Supervised Learning for Volumetric Healthcare Data

author.name: Po-Cheng Cheng, Hung-Hsuan Chen

entry.summary: L2GSSL decomposes CT volume pretraining into intra-slice local features and inter-slice global context, using a stop-gradient to isolate the two spaces and a memory-efficient three-phase schedule. On LIDC-IDRI lung nodule malignancy classification it reaches 0.9229 AUROC with only 10 percent of labels, demonstrating strong label efficiency for medical imaging.

entry.title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance for TI2I Flow Matching

author.name: Andreas Floros, Elena Koritska, Teofilo de Campos, Christoph Vogel, Chu-Tak Li, Anuj Sharma, Alexandros Neophytou

entry.summary: The paper shows that classifier-free guidance is implicitly harmful during the noisy early phase of text-and-image-to-image flow matching for editing, hindering instruction following and controllability. A simple correction in early flow steps improves the alignment-preservation tradeoff at no extra cost, demonstrated on both pixel-space and latent TI2I flows.

entry.title: Stateful Testing for Deep Learning Compilers

author.name: Jiatao Ge, Ruixiang Qian, Yibo Hu, Yanzhou Mu, Yinglong Zou, Jiawei Liu, Zhenyu Chen, Chunrong Fang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a neglected failure class in deep learning compilers where retained compiler state (lazy compilation caches) makes later invocations incorrect even when correct in isolation, documented across PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow issue trackers. The proposed Rondo system generates model-plus-invocation-sequence test cases using MCMC sampling guided by compilation behavior and a three-way differential oracle.

entry.title: PRISM: Transfer and Limits of Activation Interventions in Tool-Calling Language Models

author.name: Giovana Kerche Bon\'as, Thales Sales Almeida, Marcelo da Silva Reis, Rodrigo Nogueira, Marcos Meideiros Raimundo

entry.summary: PRISM studies activation interventions for unsafe tool calls in tool-calling LLMs, showing that behavioral labels from quantized NF4 copies and cross-lingual transfer provide a low-resource path to estimate and improve alignment directions. Intervention directions supervised on five languages transfer to held-out Arabic, demonstrating robustness of cheaply obtained alignment signals.

entry.title: Beyond Retrieval Failure: Understanding Why LLMs Miss Evidence in Multi-Hop RAG

author.name: Jiaqi Wei, Wenxuan Huang, Chengdong Xu, Xiang Zhang, Wanli Ouyang

entry.summary: The paper disentangles two causes of missing evidence in multi-hop RAG: passages inaccessible to the retriever versus search drift where the agent stops tracking unanswered sub-questions. It introduces ExecutionRAG, a training-free requirement register recording open sub-questions and their evidence, which changes search guidance without changing evidence access to isolate the causes.

entry.title: Translation Circuit Discovery and Targeted Optimization for Low-Resource Multilingual Translation

author.name: Atai Waris Khan, Abdullah Mazhar, Raghu Kumar, Md Shad Akhtar

entry.summary: TITAN is a mechanistic framework combining causal intervention, sparse feature decomposition, and targeted preference optimization to identify and optimize translation circuits in decoder-only multilingual LLMs, studied on Hindi-to-Urdu and Hindi-to-Sindhi. It updates fewer than 5% of parameters, restricting tuning to causally important circuits. This offers a parameter-efficient path for low-resource translation adaptation.

entry.title: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing

author.name: Tianxiang Fei, Jiazheng Kang, Mao Zheng, Xingyan He, Xiang Yu

entry.summary: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B is a compact specialized model for the memory-write path in external-memory systems, trained across Mem0, MemOS, and Hy-Memory protocols using memory on-policy distillation plus attributed reinforcement learning. This addresses serving cost and non-transferable prompt-based writers by producing a unified writer across frameworks. It targets a critical but underexplored component of agent memory stacks.

entry.title: Decision-FLIP: Budget-Free Structured Pruning for Gaussian Occupancy Models

author.name: Jingxing Li, Anurag Paul, Subhasis Das, Cindy Xu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Decision-FLIP, a framework for pruning the large banks of Gaussians or learned queries used in occupancy prediction models for autonomous driving and 3D perception. Instead of hand-tuned budgets or proxies like opacity, it scores each row by how many voxel argmax decisions change when it is removed (Exact Mean-FLIP), uses a guarded Otsu split to automatically pick the survivor count, and abstains when the split is not statistically supported. The approach requires only unlabeled calibration data, making it practical for deployment where labels are scarce.

entry.title: FocusOPD: Structure-Guided On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models

author.name: Xinrui Lin, Shumin Wang, Suqi Song, Fan Li, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: FocusOPD analyzes teacher-student feature mismatch across transformer blocks and denoising timesteps in multi-teacher on-policy distillation of rectified-flow DiT models, finding mismatch concentrated in deeper blocks during early denoising. It augments OPD with token-wise directional feature supervision targeted at where and when it helps most.

entry.title: PET Quantification-Preserving Registration for Longitudinal Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT

author.name: Fryderyk K\"ogl, Anna Reithmeir, Daniel M. Lang, Emily Chan, Rickmer Braren, Julia A. Schnabel

entry.summary: Adapts the LapIRN diffeomorphic registration architecture for longitudinal whole-body PSMA PET/CT in the Learn2Reg 2026 challenge, adding biomarker preservation losses for metabolic tumor volume and total lesion glycolysis plus rigidity constraints for bones. Achieves strong results (81.0% DSC, 3.3% biomarker error) with code released.

entry.title: Bridging the Markerless Tracking Validation Gap: Intraoperative X-ray Workflow Integration

author.name: Connor Daly, Salvatore Russo, Jinendra Ekanayake, Daniel S. Elson, Ferdinando Rodriguez y Baena

entry.summary: Develops a clinically viable pipeline that derives per-vertebra 6-DoF ground truth from routine intraoperative C-arm fluoroscopy co-registered to an RGB-D camera, enabling validation of markerless spinal tracking without extra radiation, instrumentation, or workflow changes. This fills a key gap: no prior clinical dataset provides independent subsurface ground truth for such tracking.

entry.title: SurgStreamer: proactive, request-driven monitoring of surgical video streams with structured state and a reusable reasoning layer

author.name: Bowen Xiang, Jon S. Heiselman, Michael I. Miga

entry.summary: SurgStreamer formalizes request-driven event detection over surgical video, separating procedure-specific perception that converts a 1-FPS stream into structured state over tools, actions, and phases from a procedure-agnostic reasoning layer that evaluates formal monitoring conditions with causal alert semantics. The reasoning layer uses exact rules or a small pointer-based controller with an event memory. This design enables reusable surgical assistants that alert teams to requested events.

entry.title: Grounded Human-Attributed Description and Activity Recognition in Videos

author.name: Jay N. Paranjape, Jurijs Nazarovs, Rohan Sarkar, Yue Guo, Lipeng Ke, Sankar Venkataraman, Vishal M. Patel, Nataraj Jammalamadaka

entry.summary: This paper introduces GHADAR, a new task of describing characteristics and activities of every person in a video given their location, moving beyond grounded group activity and closed-set recognition simplifications. The authors derive a new dataset from existing resources to support per-person open-vocabulary attributed description and activity recognition. The task is more practical for real-world multi-person video understanding applications.

entry.title: ARC-SORT: Adaptive, Robust, Compensated Multi-Object Tracking with Interacting Multiple Models

author.name: Girish Kumar Adari

entry.summary: ARC-SORT is a training-free, real-time multi-object tracker for sports broadcasts that couples an Interacting Multiple Model Kalman filter with an uncertainty-adaptive expansion IoU matching rule. The tracker measures its own predictive uncertainty and uses it to size per-track search regions, handling fast athlete motion and simultaneous camera pan/zoom. It matters because it shows uncertainty estimation alone can yield strong tracking without any learned components.

entry.title: LEAP: Gradient Flow Augmented Lagrangian Trajectory Optimization for Contact Constrained Robots

author.name: C\'esar E. Ramos Chuquiure, Ryan Tsai, Yutong Zhou, Zihang Huang, Vansh Thakur, Akshunn Trivedi, Zachary Lin, Pearl Lin, Ruikai Yang, Challen Enninful Adu, Ram Vasudevan

entry.summary: LEAP transcribes contact-constrained optimal control problems for legged and manipulating robots using pseudospectral collocation, then solves them by integrating a primal-dual gradient flow of a Powell-Hestenes-Rockafellar augmented Lagrangian with a custom linearly implicit integrator. This improves robustness to initial guesses and scaling with joint count compared to Newton/SQP solvers.

entry.title: TRACE: Typed Reference-Aware Conversational Editing for Humanoid Motion Diffusion

author.name: Zejian Kang, Yifu Luo, Boyang Shen, Jingxuan Li, Zekai Chen, Zekun Shi, Yongxue Xu, Zhenyu Hou, Bingqian Wu, Shaolei Zhang, Wentao Yang, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: TRACE is a generation-and-editing framework for the Unitree G1 humanoid in which a language model predicts typed, measurable kinematic events (support, root, hand) grounded in motion-derived supervision, feeding time-aligned encodings into a diffusion generator. This enables users to iteratively refine robot movements conversationally relative to an accepted reference motion, bridging underspecified language requests and concrete motion structure.

entry.title: VP-EVT: Active Visibility Preservation for Embodied Visual Tracking

author.name: Yanci Wen, Tianle Zeng, Jianwei Peng, Weixi Situ, Hanjing Ye, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: VP-EVT treats target visibility as an explicit motion control objective for embodied visual tracking, actively reasoning about occluders and how robot motion can restore view rather than reacting to occlusions after the fact. This addresses prolonged target loss in dynamic pedestrian environments relevant to human-robot collaboration.

entry.title: You Should Specify Your Code Unambiguously (and Prove That You Did)

author.name: Simon Henniger

entry.summary: The author presents a workflow where humans write formal specifications and an LLM (the Djinn) generates Rust implementations verified to provably satisfy them, eliminating the need to read the code. The post discusses why this LLM-plus-verifier combination is harder in practice than in theory and argues for unambiguous specification as a safety and reliability pattern.

entry.title: Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements

author.name: Jianyu Zhang, L\'eon Bottou

entry.summary: A position/theory paper by Zhang and Bottou arguing that open-world AI requires inference-time learning, rich representations beyond what iid generalization needs, and predictive disentanglement aligning inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. It derives these requirements by modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective.

entry.title: SkillNEO: Non-Elitist Evolutionary Optimization of Agent Skills

author.name: Enze Ma, Chunyu Miao, Yankai Chen, Jie Yang, Liancheng Fang, Kening Zheng, Hanrong Zhang, Muyao Xu, Xinle Yu, Chengze Li, Wei-Chieh Huang, Ziwei Ren, Yunhao Du, Zhixiang Shen, Xue Liu, Philip S. Yu, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: Introduces SkillNEO, which applies non-elitist evolutionary optimization to agent skill libraries, separately selecting which skill version to use versus which to develop next. This allows low-reward intermediate versions with interdependent pending edits to be preserved and repaired rather than discarded for lacking immediate reward gains.

entry.title: Tool-Augmented Large Language Models for Reliable Medical Calculation from Patient Notes

author.name: Yang Zhong, Ling Luo, Xuanlyu Zhu, Yanhua Wang, Yuanyuan Sun, Jian Wang, Hongfei Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a tool-augmented LLM framework for applying medical calculators to free-form patient notes, separating variable extraction from exact formula execution by retrieving calculator specifications, generating reusable executable tools, and decoupling arithmetic from generation. Direct LLM prompting is unreliable when rule recall, extraction, arithmetic, and formatting are entangled. This improves clinical reliability of LLM-derived scores.

entry.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Bingxiang He, Pengqi Sun, Shihao Peng, Shaoxuan Li, Huiyu Xiao, Hongjian Shi, Zixuan Fu, Ziqing Qiao, Yuxin Zuo, Cheng Qian, Xinqiang Yu, Jiayi Li, Xiusi Chen, Yizhen Song, Xiangyang Wang, Iofai Lei, Yudong Wang, Ning Ding, Zhiyuan Liu, Xiaozhi Wang, Chaojun Xiao

entry.summary: AutoSFT automates the full range of data-engineering actions, adjusting proportions, pruning, repairing, replacing, and synthesizing training data, within supervised fine-tuning pipelines. The paper analyzes why single-agent loops fail by exhausting context and settles on a structured system design to support the full data action space.

entry.title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation

author.name: Weilin Ruan, Bohan Zhou, Jinghao Li, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li, Peiran Dong, Yingjie Xu, Leyi Wu, Haojian Huang, Binghui Xie, Han Yang, Kaiwen Zhou, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen, James Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces Anvil, a unified framework spanning data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence, including Anvil-Gen (a data flywheel across 11 Ground-Relation-Act forms with consistency verification and failure-driven recollection) and Anvil-Ben (scene-aligned supervision). It targets models that localize entities, reason about spatial relations, and express knowledge in action-relevant forms.

entry.title: Do As I Do, Not As I Say: On-Policy Distillation Inherits the Teacher in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Frank F. Yang, Kefei Yan, Yiren Wang, Yiyang Wang

entry.summary: Controlled comparison of on-policy distillation versus filtered SFT for training VLMs across data budgets and teacher reliability levels, analyzing how teacher supervision at each student state shapes learned behavior. Finds OPD can inherit teacher behavior in ways that matter for downstream reliability, informing post-training method choice.

entry.title: CausalEvo: Causal Skill Self-Evolution for Health LLM Agents

author.name: Yuchen Zhang

entry.summary: CausalEvo is a method for LLM health agents to autonomously decide which reusable textual skills (rules, criteria, formulas) to keep or discard during self-evolution, using causal estimation of skill effects while holding model weights and context fixed. A frozen LLM proposes candidate rules that compete with incumbent skills in paired replacement evaluations. This matters because faulty skill generalizations can propagate errors in safety-sensitive health applications.

entry.title: Online Quantile Omniprediction for Proper Losses

author.name: Hyunsuk Kim, Isaac Gibbs, Michael W. Mahoney, Ryan J. Tibshirani

entry.summary: This paper develops sample-efficient online algorithms for omniprediction with quantile-based forecasts that are simultaneously accurate across all proper losses under mild regularity conditions. It extends omniprediction beyond the largely binary-focused prior literature to multiclass and continuous outcomes with better error rates.

entry.title: Local Epochs as Optimal Stopping: Theory and Evidence in Federated Learning

author.name: Ke Xiao, Qiyuan Wang, Christos Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: This paper recasts the choice of local epochs in federated learning as a finite-horizon optimal stopping problem, where a client trains while the next epoch's expected loss reduction exceeds its priced squared drift. The authors prove a one-stage look-ahead threshold is optimal under nested stopping, derive closed forms, and validate the model's structure empirically, revealing a simple decision rule.

entry.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Machine Learning for Fracture Prediction in Heterogeneous Materials

author.name: Muhamad Alim, Xiaolong He, Mei-Na Tsao, Chi-Hua Yu, J. S. Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces tLaSDI, a thermodynamically consistent latent-dynamics method using GENERIC formalism-informed neural networks to predict fracture evolution in heterogeneous materials as a surrogate for expensive physics simulations. Embedding thermodynamic constraints in a reduced latent space improves generalization and physical fidelity over black-box surrogates.

entry.title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Utku Cicek, Mahip Singh, Ziyao Shang, Kimathi Kaai, C Thomas, Pedro Pablo Guerrero Vela, Alexander Wong, Sirisha Rambhatla

entry.summary: TEAL is the first pixel-level active learning framework built on frozen ViT token representations, performing diversity-based selection directly in token space to support very low annotation budgets such as a single queried pixel per image. This addresses the challenge of identifying informative locations and training decoder heads from extremely sparse signals. It reduces the heavy pixel-labeling costs of segmentation annotation.

entry.title: Efficient Agnostic Learning of Univariate Densities Under Local Differential Privacy

author.name: Mohammad Afzali, Hassan Ashtiani, Sivan Sabato

entry.summary: The paper proposes a general non-interactive locally differentially private (LDP) learning framework for univariate distributions approximable by piecewise polynomials, yielding the first sample-efficient LDP learners for classes including Gaussian mixtures. It also proves an improved lower bound for LDP learning of GMMs and contributes an efficient LDP synthetic-data generation algorithm over large domains. The results carry agnostic guarantees and are computationally efficient.

entry.title: ManiFusion: Unlocking the High-Throughput Generation via Superposition in Manifold Space

author.name: Minkyu Kim, Baekseung Kim, Junhoo Lee, Jangho Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: ManiFusion accelerates diffusion image generation along an orthogonal throughput axis by processing multiple samples in a single denoising evaluation: samples are fused before the denoising backbone and separated afterward via unfusion, with a geometric argument for when fused representations remain separable. The framework is backbone-agnostic and complements per-sample latency optimizations.

entry.title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Kelvin J. L. Koa, Yuncong Liu, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a within-event timing leakage problem in financial NLP benchmarks where prediction targets can begin before model inputs (text, audio) are complete, which chronological splits do not prevent. It proposes an Availability Contract specifying input boundaries, evidence of availability, outcome start, and supported claims, applied to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms.

entry.title: PRISM: PRIvileged Sibling-guided Multi-Agent Topology Design

author.name: Phuong Tuan Dat, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: PRISM improves post-training of topology generators for LLM-based multi-agent systems by addressing the limitation that execution-verified graph corpora are unranked, leaving SFT with no per-query preference. It uses privileged sibling guidance to extract preference signals among candidate topologies so the generator fits topologies suited to each query rather than those most common in the corpus.

entry.title: Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches

author.name: Wanyang Hong, Zhaoning Zhang

entry.summary: This work studies how gaps left by evicted tokens distort RoPE-based query-key matching in sparse KV cache compression, and proposes RoPERelay, which assigns compact order-preserving coordinates to retained states via inverse rotation and re-rotation. The approach improves use of retained evidence and answer quality in long-context inference.

entry.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling

author.name: Tong Zhu, Zhe Xu, Zefeng He, Yunkai Chai, Xuyang Hu, Dehong Zheng, Yun Luo, Yafu Li, Qi Zhang, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Intern-Decision is a family of 0.8B, 2B, and 4B multimodal models that return structured choices and candidate probabilities from text and optional images in a single forward pass, using a decision-placeholder objective in a complete JSON skeleton. The 4B model reaches 90.02% unweighted average accuracy, reducing latency versus free-form generation for agentic decision points. It targets efficient, interface-friendly agent decisions.

entry.title: EVA-Cap: Optimizing Audiovisual Video Captioning via Event-Centric Alignment

author.name: Jiapeng Shi, Qiuxia Hou, Jiaqi Leng, Junke Wang, Yanhao Zhang, Haonan Lu, Ziyi Ye, Zuxuan Wu

entry.summary: EVA-Cap decomposes video captions into atomic audiovisual events and trains omni language models via SFT and GRPO on a self-curated event-centric dataset, EVA-Data. During the RL phase, the model receives explicit alignment signals to improve fine-grained audiovisual correspondence. This moves video captioning beyond unstructured text generation toward structured semantic supervision.

entry.title: MYOPIA: Understanding the Limits of Tree-Based Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Islam Mesabah, Sary Elmansoury, Gerrit Gro{\ss}mann, Peter Neigel, Sebastian J. Vollmer

entry.summary: Introduces MYOPIA, a benchmark of four LLM-generated, human-refined decision trees over standard datasets to test whether interpretable root-to-leaf question chains can replace direct VLM classification. Across GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA-3.2 Vision in all 12 dataset-model pairs, tree traversal underperforms zero-shot prompting, with diagnostics characterizing the failure modes.

entry.title: SCCL-DT: Semantic-Conflict-Aware Contrastive Learning with Dual-Rule Teacher Distillation for Zero-Shot Chest X-Ray Diagnosis

author.name: Ting Liu, Haoran Lai, HaobinChen, Ming Liu, S Kevin Zhou

entry.summary: SCCL-DT tackles false-negative supervision in contrastive vision-language pre-training for zero-shot chest X-ray diagnosis, where recurring findings across patients make batch negatives semantically compatible, a problem the authors term semantic conflict. The method uses semantic-conflict-aware objectives with dual-rule teacher distillation to avoid miscalibrated fixed thresholds and residual repulsive gradients from soft reweighting. The result is improved zero-shot radiology diagnosis.

entry.title: First Mathematical Runtime Analyses of Evolutionary Multitask Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Danyang Zhang, Weijie Zheng

entry.summary: This paper provides the first rigorous mathematical runtime analyses of evolutionary multitask optimization for multi-objective problems, analyzing how the MO-MFEA algorithm covers Pareto fronts of two bi-objective benchmarks (OMM and OJZJ). It proves expected runtime bounds, including cases where cross-task knowledge transfer yields the same runtime as optimizing the easier task alone. It fills a recognized gap between empirical evidence and theory.

entry.title: LIN-SLAM: Lightweight LiDAR--Inertial Neural SLAM for Real-Time Onboard Navigation

author.name: Shiqi Che, Yijie Liu, Shuo Wang, Wenxin Liu

entry.summary: LIN-SLAM is a hybrid SLAM system coupling high-rate geometric LiDAR-inertial odometry with neural implicit tracking, continual mapping, and global refinement for accurate real-time onboard operation. Experiments across twelve sequences and three datasets with 32-, 64-, and 128-channel LiDAR show the lowest overall trajectory error.

entry.title: MAGMA: Multiplier-Augmented Geometric Motion Algorithm

author.name: C\'esar E. Ramos Chuquiure, Vansh Thakur, Challen Enninful Adu, Ram Vasudevan

entry.summary: MAGMA is a trajectory optimizer based on Affine Geometric Heat Flow that incorporates an augmented Lagrangian framework solved via primal-dual flow, with theoretical characterization showing it is a gradient flow on a defined energy. It handles constraints from obstacles, state limits, and actuation limits, and compares favorably against state-of-the-art trajectory solvers.

entry.title: Inertially Significant Humanoid Teleoperation via Whole Body Model Predictive Control and Online Parameter Estimation

author.name: James Foster, Beomyeong Park, Luigi Penco, Robert Griffin

entry.summary: This paper integrates whole-body model predictive control with an extended Kalman filter for online estimation of time-varying inertial parameters, enabling humanoid teleoperation during heavy tool use or significant payload carrying. The estimates feed the full rigid body dynamics model to improve feedforward accuracy where feedback control alone is insufficient.

entry.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate via Model-Agnostic Importance Measures

author.name: Mengtao Wen, Haojie Ren, Changliang Zou

entry.summary: The paper introduces MAS, a model-agnostic variable selection method with FDR control that uses sample splitting and a novel agent-X importance measure to bypass distributional assumptions on covariates, complementing Model-X knockoffs. It targets interpretable scientific discovery with complex machine learning models.

entry.title: A Self-Improving Agent that Grows its Own DSL: Oracle-Free Operator Induction for Exact Question Answering

author.name: Yun-Shiuan Chuang, Yirou Ge, Yixi Li, Yiming Bian, Zijie Pan, Jenna L. Ballard, Uma Kona, Linsey Pang, Prakhar Mehrotra

entry.summary: Describes a self-improving agent that expands its own domain-specific language with no reward model, judge, or answer key, using a frozen model in two nested loops: an inner loop only accepts answers when two independently written expressions agree on every record, and an outer loop discovers missing capabilities and authors operators admitted under agreement-based criteria.

entry.title: AgentEval: Evidence-Bounded Assessment of Stateful Agents

author.name: Ruiqi Gao (Alibaba Cloud, Alibaba Group)

entry.summary: Presents AgentEval, a system that maintains a contract-bound assessment record through tool execution and state capture, separating what an agent did, what the evidence establishes, and whether conclusions remain supported. Evaluated on 32 tool-world administrations plus controlled interventions on 48 evidence views. Addresses auditability of stateful agents beyond mere task completion.

entry.title: Self-Guided LLM Reasoning for Error Diagnosis in Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Ni Zhang, Jianan Zhou, Yue-Jiao Gong, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies LLMs' ability to detect and correct errors in VRP instances, finding key limitations on complex instances and high-reasoning-burden errors. It proposes a self-guided framework where LLMs generate code that provides structured insights to aid their own diagnosis. This extends LLM-for-optimization work to the neglected realistic case of faulty inputs.

entry.title: Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models

author.name: Xiuhui Zhang, Ning Gao, Xingyu Jiang, Yihui Chen, Yuheng Pan, Mohan Zhang, Yue Deng

entry.summary: PRM4RL integrates LLM-based task planning with dense reward generation to handle long-horizon RL tasks with sparse rewards. Complex tasks are decomposed into simpler subtasks, with a progress reward model providing incremental learning signals, addressing limitations of both skill-library planning and human-feedback-heavy reward methods.

entry.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction

author.name: Wenhao Yan, Haodong Li, Xiaotong Li, Yaxin Luo, Zhengrong Yue, Jialv Zou, Xu Huang, Haojin Yang, Nan Jia, Yan Feng, Peng Pei, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: WorldCast organizes multimodal generative capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and focuses on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level underexplored task requiring models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and references. The work, with authors including Meituan-affiliated researchers, highlights that entangled understanding and generation remains a bottleneck despite recent progress.

entry.title: How to Train Your Little Dragon: Teaching a Small Language Model to Construct and Refine GPU Optimization Scripts

author.name: Annabelle Sujun Tang, Wei Tang, Songyao Jiang, Tianhui Li, Shengzhe Xu, Jiin Woo, Kaan Ozkara, Youngsuk Park, Zhen Jia, Hadi Esmaeilzadeh

entry.summary: The paper trains a small language model to generate compiler optimization scripts (rather than kernel code) for GPU kernel tuning, using a compact lossless representation whose deterministic decoding reconstructs the exact TVM MetaSchedule compiler trace. Training data spans 54,116 distinct workloads with 108,594 examples. This is a notable application of LLMs to systems performance, showing small models can handle structured optimization search.

entry.title: A Jury, Not an Electorate: Label-Free Reliability Estimation for Ensembles of Language Models

author.name: Alessandro Rozza, Davide Mambelli, Steven Motta, Juri Taresch

entry.summary: The paper models LLM ensembles as juries with per-question latent true answers and per-expert reliabilities estimated via expectation maximization from unlabelled answer configurations alone, deriving a log-odds weighted linear decision rule. This contrasts with fixed-reputation or majority-vote ensemble methods. The framing that credibility, not majority, is the right question offers a cleaner statistical basis for label-free ensembling.

entry.title: Where, How, and When: Query-Guided Grounding for Video Understanding

author.name: Yogesh Kumar

entry.summary: A thesis covering three query-guided video grounding tasks: object localization, relationship grounding, and moment localization. It introduces QDETRv, a query-guided Detection Transformer extension with query-context fusion, temporal memory, and unsupervised pretraining on synthetic trajectories, plus related temporal object-aware components. The work consolidates video understanding contributions into a coherent multi-level framework.

entry.title: AVALON: Zero-Shot Indoor Navigation with Human-Seeded Topological Memory

author.name: Jing Xia, Changyan Li, Yuduo Wang, Guiyin Tian, Bo Wang, Yifan Liao, Mingjun Li, Shiyan Hu

entry.summary: AVALON is a topological navigation framework for service robots entering unmapped buildings, using human-seeded layered spatial memory, node-verified topological execution, and evidence-gated human-robot memory co-updating. Deployment needs only a floor plan, place clues, and an initial topology-odometry alignment, with visual depth point-goal navigation enabling re-anchoring without a robot-built global SLAM map. It targets the practical human-familiar, robot-unseen setting.

entry.title: Cross-Embodiment Causal Transfer from Human Videos to Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xingyu Zhang, Yingchao Li, Peizheng Guo, Jie Hu, Changwen Zheng, Wenwen Qiang

entry.summary: Studies what knowledge from abundant human manipulation videos can transfer to robot manipulation despite morphology and action-space differences, analyzing subtask transfer via causal beams that identify which contextual conditions and dependencies to retain. The approach aims to reduce dependence on costly real-robot interaction data.

entry.title: Decoding Naturalistic Speech from fMRI with Temporal Modeling and Multimodal Alignment

author.name: Corentin Caris, Louis Jalouzot, Nona Rajabi, G\'eraud Ilinca, Ahmed Hassayoune, Asilbek Muminov, Thadd\'ee Delebarre, Clara Fonteneau, Charles Maussion, Bertrand Thirion, Alexis Thual, Antoine Collas

entry.summary: Introduces NOEMA, a temporal convolutional decoder aligning consecutive fMRI windows with multimodal text, audio, and speech embeddings of stimuli, enabling retrieval of heard speech segments from brain activity. On two naturalistic speech datasets it retrieves the correct segment among 2,000 candidates, advancing naturalistic neural decoding despite fMRI's temporal smearing.

entry.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling

author.name: Hongchang Liu, Jian Liu, Yujuan Ding, Liang Peng, Xun Jiang, Fei Ma, Xing Xu, Yi Bin

entry.summary: Proposes GeoState, which decouples view-dependent features from geometry foundation models so that scene-state evolution can be predicted separately from camera-induced variation. A scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled state, queried by camera rays via a geometry decoder, while an autoregressive model predicts future states and camera motion is modeled independently. This makes 3D world model dynamics easier to learn.

entry.title: CogDrift-4D: Hierarchical Multimodal Modeling of Temporal Behavioral Decay for MCI Detection

author.name: Sankalp Vaish, Sumukh Veeramalla, Rishank Singh, Caroline Summerour, John A. Batsis, Xiaohui Liang

entry.summary: Introduces an 18-month multimodal behavioral dataset of unscripted interactions and CogDrift-4D, a hierarchical 4D Transformer that models Batch x Session x Time x Feature structure to capture both local dynamics and long-term cognitive decline for mild cognitive impairment detection. The longitudinal design addresses a key gap in snapshot-based screening.

entry.title: Noise-Space Reward Alignment for Few-Step Generative Models

author.name: Woocheol Shin, Taeyoung Yun, Jiwon Sung, Hyeongyu Kang, Jeongmin Park, Jaewoo Lee, Kyuil Sim, Dohyun Kim, Yutong He, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: Proposes Noise Policy Optimization, which learns an amortized flow policy over the input noise space to align few-step generative models with black-box rewards, avoiding the reward over-optimization of direct RL fine-tuning and the efficiency loss of test-time scaling. Targets a practical gap where standard alignment tools transfer poorly to few-step regimes.

entry.title: Does Compression Imply Generalization? A Minimum Description Length Perspective

author.name: Lincen Yang, Jiayang Shi, Nan Pu, Dani\"el M. Pelt, Matthijs van Leeuwen, Zhong Li, Shujian Yu

entry.summary: This work approaches the compression-generalization question via the MDL principle, proposing prequential regret as a signal computable from the training trajectory alone, avoiding held-out data and high-dimensional mutual information estimation. It establishes connections between expected prequential regret and generalization in the nearly interpolating regime.

entry.title: Transfer Learning in Bandits from Unknown Adaptive Policies: Problem-Dependent Lower and Upper Bounds

author.name: Adrien Prevost, Timothee Mathieu, Waris Radji, Odalric-Ambrym Maillard

entry.summary: The paper studies transfer learning in stochastic multi-armed bandits when historical observations come from an unknown, possibly data-dependent adaptive source policy, with bounded distribution shifts between source and target means. The authors derive an asymptotic problem-dependent lower bound and propose KL-UCB-Transfer with matching matching guarantees.

entry.title: A Closed Form Depth-Width Law for Neural Collapse in Deep Linear Networks

author.name: Pankhil Gawade, Kirsten Fischer, Guy Wolf, Ewa Szczurek

entry.summary: Using neural collapse as a probe, the authors derive closed-form expressions for NC1-NC3 in terms of the learned feature kernel, extending known identities to the angular part of NC2 and NC3 under ridge readout. For deep linear networks with exchangeable class structure, they obtain a geometric law where accumulated within-class compression becomes a function of the depth-to-width ratio L/N.

entry.title: Not All Unlabeled Data Are Equal: Unlabeled Data Selection for Semi-Supervised QSAR Modeling with Large Chemical Repositories

author.name: Oliver Majer, Saso Dzeroski, Jurica Levatic

entry.summary: The paper studies how to select unlabeled molecules from large repositories like ChEMBL for semi-supervised QSAR modeling, where activity labels require costly wet-lab experiments. It addresses how unlabeled data selection behaves in realistic SSL settings with genuine unlabeled distributions rather than curated benchmarks. This is a practical contribution at the intersection of SSL and drug discovery.

entry.title: Latent Annealed Posterior Sampling with a Variance-Preserving Bridge for Sparsely Observed Random Fields

author.name: Jiankun Lei, Tian Qi

entry.summary: LAPS performs posterior inference for random fields from sparse observations by mapping fields into a low-dimensional latent space with Branch and Trunk decoder networks, learning the latent prior via flow matching, and running annealed posterior sampling entirely in latent space with progressive likelihood incorporation. This controls the cost growth that typically accompanies grid refinement.

entry.title: Two-Stage Score Estimation for Group-Specific Diffusion Models

author.name: Huitao Yang, Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla

entry.summary: The paper develops a statistical theory of diffusion transfer: learning a shared pooled score plus a target-specific offset to generate from a target distribution with limited observations. Under Besov regularity assumptions, the authors derive convergence rates separating the costs of learning each component and identify when a simpler offset yields faster risk rates than separate fitting. This formalizes when shared structure across related distributions benefits diffusion generative modeling.

entry.title: On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped Gradient Methods

author.name: Zijian Liu

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes last-iterate convergence guarantees for clipped stochastic gradient methods in stochastic strongly convex optimization under heavy-tailed gradient noise, conditions under which unclipped SGD fails. Prior last-iterate results required strong assumptions like exponentially decaying noise tails. Clipping is shown to restore convergence guarantees under realistic noise models.

entry.title: When Should a Low-Light Pipeline Generate? Auditable Risk Control for Selective Generative Enhancement

author.name: Qiyi Xie, Wei Chen Ng, Suyang Xi, Xicheng Wang, Ziyao Li, Bohong Xu, Wenyi Liu, Jian Ding Tan

entry.summary: VetoNet frames selective generative low-light enhancement as a decision problem: deciding when overriding a frozen restoration expert with a generative model is beneficial and refusing to switch when evidence is insufficient. It uses a certified, distribution-free veto on predicted regional override utility, yielding an auditable routing framework that balances hallucination risk against under-enhancement.

entry.title: Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: The paper proposes novelty patching for byte-level models like the Byte Latent Transformer: start a patch where upcoming bytes are unlikely to repeat recent context, using an LZ77-inspired two-byte lookup table fitted in seconds without labels or reference models. In BLT-style models trained from scratch on a math corpus at matched patch rates, this improves accuracy on computed results where entropy-based patching collapses.

entry.title: Jev-as-a-Judge for RAG Claim Verification: Confidence-Gated Cascading Between a Non-Generative Verifier and a Frontier LLM

author.name: Alden Do Rosario, Kirollos Atef

entry.summary: The paper compares a non-generative decision model that returns typed values with native probabilities against a frontier LLM configured for binary claim verification on 495 human-labelled LLM-AggreFact claims. The two are statistically indistinguishable on accuracy, motivating a confidence-gated cascade that avoids paying generation costs for one-bit verification decisions.

entry.title: No Single Tokenizer Feature Reliably Predicts Downstream Language Model Performance

author.name: Antonio Lopardo, Luis Frentzen Salim, Shikhar Srivastava, Kevin Jiang, Mridul Sharma, Catherine Arnett

entry.summary: Analyzing roughly 200 language models across nine languages, this study tests whether proposed intrinsic tokenizer metrics predict downstream performance without full training runs. The finding is a negative one: no tokenizer feature consistently predicts downstream performance across model families. This is a valuable caution for the tokenizer-design literature.

entry.title: Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes in Rett Syndrome with a Dual-LLM Consensus Pipeline

author.name: Daniel Palacios, Guantong Qi, Mikael Guzman Karlsson, Shawntel K. David, Mohammed Sameeruddin, Bernhard Suter, Zhandong Liu, Davut Pehlivan, Hu Chen

entry.summary: A dual-LLM consensus pipeline extracts 18 treatment-response phenotypes from 26,763 clinical notes of 108 Rett syndrome patients treated with trofinetide, enabling scalable real-world monitoring of the first approved Rett treatment. The architecture and prompts were selected on a development set then frozen. This demonstrates practical clinical NLP with consensus-based reliability controls.

entry.title: SpaceCache: Intermediate Feature Reuse for Efficient Semantic Segmentation on Point Cloud Streams

author.name: Dongheon Yang, Beomseok Kang, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: SpaceCache is a training-free caching scheme that reuses intermediate transformer features across overlapping frames in point-cloud streams, letting tokens for previously observed regions skip transformer blocks. It targets efficient semantic segmentation for autonomous driving and robotics with lightweight cache management to keep reused features reliable.

entry.title: DIAL: Dynamic and Informed Adjustment of the Native Stochastic Law for Reliable Weather Ensembles

author.name: Yucheng Wang, Haonan Guo, Tianhao Zhao, Di Wang, Yu Wu, Zengmao Wang, Bo Du

entry.summary: Introduces DIAL, which controls the frozen stochastic law of an ensemble weather forecasting model during inference to correct spread errors that vary across variables, scales, lead times, and weather states. It acts during forecasting on the ensemble as a whole, addressing limitations of pre-fixed training behavior and post-hoc output calibration.

entry.title: Edit4D: Editable 4D Scene Generation with Textual Control

author.name: Chanwoo Kim, Tackgeun You, Hwasup Lim

entry.summary: Presents a text-to-4D generation framework that decomposes scenes into separate background and dynamic character representations, enabling object-level editing and flexible camera control that holistic video generation does not allow. A stage-specific pipeline converts user instructions into prompts for each component while preserving geometry and temporal dynamics.

entry.title: FuseAdapt: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Semantic Segmentation with Missing Modalities

author.name: Xin Zhang, Robby T. Tan

entry.summary: Proposes FuseAdapt, which performs multimodal fusion inside the adaptation space of a frozen vision foundation model, giving each modality a lightweight adaptation branch rather than a standalone fusion network. This keeps segmentation robust when modalities are degraded or missing at test time while remaining parameter-efficient.

entry.title: Data-Efficient ConvNeXt Pretraining for High-Resolution Sentinel-1 GRD SAR Representation Learning

author.name: Yuki Natsume, Sang-Ho Yun, Chai Kiat Yeo

entry.summary: SparK-SAR is a sparse convolutional masked pretraining framework built on SparK and ConvNeXt for Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, targeting data- and compute-efficient self-supervised representation learning. Contributions include ConvNeXt-RS, a domain-adapted encoder with halved stem stride yielding four times more spatial tokens, plus additional efficiency techniques. It leverages convolutional inductive biases where ViT-based masked modeling has dominated but demands large resources.

entry.title: Pathology foundation models for training-free case retrieval in salivary gland tumors

author.name: Maximilian J. Roesel, Niklas Kiermeyer, Philipp Keyl, Frederick Klauschen

entry.summary: The authors explore whether pathology foundation models can support rare cancer diagnostics through training-free content-based retrieval, letting pathologists query a digitized tumor archive with a region of interest and retrieve morphologically similar cases with ICD-O codes. ROI selection can be manual or automated via gated attention. The study focuses on salivary gland tumors where rare subtypes strain pattern recognition.

entry.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection

author.name: Yaozhi Wen, Kun Zhao, Wei Wei, Haoyang Chen, Kangning Wang, Yi Sun, Shaowei Gu, Dingkun Liu, Shuang Qiu, Huiguang He

entry.summary: NeuroDETR applies structured discrete tokenization, including multiscale temporal codebooks and Spatial-Pyramid VQ over EEG channels, to asynchronous EEG event detection for brain-computer interfaces. These representations form a compact event memory used with a detection-transformer style head to jointly classify events and localize temporal boundaries in continuous recordings. It addresses practical BCI deployment where event boundaries are unknown at inference.

entry.title: Race to Recovery: Designing Advanced Safety Systems for Autonomous Driving via Learning Autonomous Racing

author.name: Teodor Ilie, Kleber Cabral, Sidney Givigi

entry.summary: This work trains an RL racing policy that learns drifting as a time-optimal maneuver, then adapts it into a vehicle recovery system for loss-of-control scenarios like icing or hydroplanning that fall outside production stability-control envelopes. It addresses gaps in prior recovery approaches by acting online with a principled definition of recovery.

entry.title: Manifold Generative Annealing for Contact Constraint-aware Impedance Control with Reinforcement Learning Prior

author.name: Zhilin He, Guoquan Qi, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: MGA is a joint model-free and model-based generative framework for motion-impedance optimization that organizes pretrained RL policies on a manifold and refines trajectories with receding-horizon optimization respecting constraint geometry and actual contact responses. This improves robustness when contact conditions differ from training.

entry.title: A 2D Image Feedback-Based Autonomous Endovascular Navigation Method: A Perception and Control Framework

author.name: Sheng Cao, Shuxiang Guo, Yonggan Yan, Jian Guo, Chunying Li, Bin Wang, Mingchao Ding, Yongxin Zhang, Yongwei Zhang, Pengfei Yang, Jianmin Liu

entry.summary: This paper formulates a perception-and-control pipeline for autonomous endovascular navigation that converts vessel masks from planar DSA/X-ray images into a labeled centerline graph and projects device-tip estimates onto a planned path to derive progress, deviation, and direction signals for a rule-based controller. It was validated on a physical dual-device robotic platform across 65 closed-loop runs with all runs reaching at least intermediate milestones.

entry.title: Illumination-Aware Active Perception for Spacecraft Inspection

author.name: Sagarika Rao Valluri, Benjamin Riviere

entry.summary: This work replaces geometric line-of-sight visibility metrics in spacecraft inspection planning with a learned information measure from a classifier VAE operating on captured images, accounting for eclipse, self-shadowing, and specular reflection. This prevents planners from declaring components inspected when images lack sufficient information.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Agent Pursuit with Preemptive Communication via Reachability-Based Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Madison Book, Justin Bradley

entry.summary: The paper unifies control and communication for multi-agent safety under intermittent communication: each agent computes reachable sets of neighbors from stale state information and uses control barrier functions to guarantee collision avoidance. The approach is demonstrated in pursuit-evasion scenarios with formal guarantees.

entry.title: Linkpost: Neural Networks Are Already Clean

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: A linkpost to Nick Cammarata's argument that mechanistic interpretability has quietly transformed: with modern agentic tooling, the vast majority of features and circuits in models up to trillions of parameters appear legible, and famous examples of tangled neurons were misunderstandings. He predicts ambitious interpretability will be solved by automated scientists, possibly soon.

entry.title: Confidence-Calibrated Inference Expansion for Evaluator-Guided Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Weida Liang, Kenji Kawaguchi

entry.summary: Formulates test-time reasoning as a compute-aware three-action control problem (accept, fall back, or expand) with explicitly priced compute cost, providing local action-gap analysis and expected regret bounds. It learns and calibrates action-specific confidence estimates with uncertainty penalties, improving performance on expansion and revision tasks.

entry.title: CodeHealth Predicts the Token Cost of Agentic Code Review: A Pre-Registered Study of 465 Agent-Authored Pull Requests

author.name: Lo Gullstrand Heander, Markus Borg, Emma S\"oderberg, Christofer Rydenf\"alt

entry.summary: A pre-registered observational study of 465 agent-authored pull requests showing that baseline CodeHealth predicts the token cost of multi-agent LLM code review beyond pull request footprint, across three LLMs in a frozen five-agent pipeline. It links low code quality directly to higher agent review costs, extending maintenance-cost arguments to agentic workflows.

entry.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Shadi Omari, Bashar Khoury, Assaf Schuster

entry.summary: Studies using predicted quantiles as distributional controls for pretrained diffusion forecasters, finding that residual control throughout the denoising network gives the most consistent improvements. Instantiates this as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen, improving CRPS across eight benchmarks with competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods. Bridges quantile forecasts and trajectory-based diffusion uncertainty.

entry.title: Ranked Right, Sized Wrong: Ensemble Spread Fails Silently at Streamflow Extremes

author.name: Justin Gallant, Tyler Wilson

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LSTM ensemble spread remains a reliable uncertainty signal for streamflow forecasting under extreme flows, finding error is about twice the corrected spread at ordinary flows and up to four times at the highest flows, with the discrepancy growing with flow magnitude. This means ensembles may rank errors correctly but systematically underestimate them precisely during climate-driven extremes. The finding is a warning for operational hydrologic AI deployed under out-of-distribution conditions.

entry.title: HyCo: Hybrid Drafting for Cost-Efficient Mobile-Cloud Speculative Decoding

author.name: Hanbin Bae, Heejin Choi, Joohyung Lee, Byoung Jin Choi, Sangjun Park, Hoon-Young Cho

entry.summary: HyCo improves device-cloud speculative decoding by executing the server model's native multi-token prediction head on the mobile NPU using returned hidden states and KV entries, with a single SLM pass handling alternative draft branches. Quantization, restricted vocabulary, and a relaxed sampling-preservation rule make it practical; it was demonstrated on a Galaxy S26 Ultra.

entry.title: From Observation to Intervention: Distilling Self-Generated In-Context Demonstrations via Executable Causal Intervention

author.name: Minming Ye, Min Liu, Haoang Chi, Ciheng Wu, Naiyang Guan

entry.summary: The paper identifies observational equivalence as a flaw in filtering self-generated in-context demonstrations, since spurious post-hoc rationales can look as good as faithful causal ones from outputs alone. Drawing on independent causal mechanisms, it proposes transfer invariance as a criterion and instantiates it as an executable causal intervention method for demonstration distillation.

entry.title: PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems

author.name: Shuo Lin, Jinzhe Li, Chenlu Guo, Yanhan Li, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: PremiseSQL is a benchmark of 1,800 flawed NL2SQL queries across four premise-failure categories plus their 1,800 originals, designed to test whether text-to-SQL systems can recognize unanswerable or flawed queries and abstain rather than emit misleading SQL. An evaluation framework measures premise-aware behavior across three prompting settings. It addresses a real safety gap in deployed NL2SQL systems.

entry.title: GeoPano: Towards Geometrically Accurate 3D Reconstruction from a Single Panorama

author.name: Jing OU, Zidong Cao, Liaoyuan Fan, Zhuoxiao Li, Shuai Zhang, Yinrui Ren, Dongli Wu, Haoang Li, Hui Xiong, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: GeoPano is a feed-forward framework for single-panorama 3D reconstruction that recovers geometrically accurate, cross-view-consistent point clouds despite spherical ERP distortions. Its key innovations address the cross-view inconsistencies that arise when panoramas are decomposed into independently processed perspective views, with applications in robotics and AR/VR.

entry.title: MedPAO-VL: Interpretable and Protocol-Compliant Agent for Structured Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Shrish Shrinath Vaidya, Gowthamaan Palani, Minmini Selvam, Gokulraja Srinivasaraja, Ganapathy Krishnamurthi

entry.summary: Presents a multimodal plan-act-observe agent that generates structured, protocol-compliant radiology reports from chest X-rays iteratively and explainably, rather than via monolithic black-box generation. The design targets hallucination reduction, grounded findings, and adherence to domain-specific structuring protocols.

entry.title: WaveLLM: Wavelet-Domain LLM Entropy Modeling for Lossless Image Compression

author.name: Yue Yu, Bowei Kang, Changsheng Gao, Dong Liu, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: WaveLLM proposes a wavelet-domain LLM-based entropy model for lossless image compression, arguing that predictability of the input representation matters as much as model capacity. By decomposing images into multi-level wavelet subbands, it separates heterogeneous signal patterns into homogeneous prediction streams rather than serializing raw pixels or residuals. This improves entropy modeling accuracy and compression performance.

entry.title: GRID-Planner: Graph-Structured Relational Reward Shaping for Diffusion Planning

author.name: Zhao Yang, Zezhong Qian, Yinan Shi, Longjun Liu, Yawei Jueluo

entry.summary: GRID-Planner integrates graph-aware importance weighting, a time-indexed relational reward surrogate, and an advantage-weighted diffusion objective into diffusion-based autonomous driving planning, so structured relational signals actively shape policy improvement rather than only informing representations. It targets safe, rule-compliant, comfortable trajectory selection in multi-agent planning-critical scenes.

entry.title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins

author.name: Zhou Daniel Hao, Umer Masood Chaudry, Robert Shaw, Andrew Cheney, Nick Ludford, Mark Sims, Hongbiao Dong

entry.summary: As part of the UK Space Agency-supported ISPARK project, this paper evaluates a digital-twin prototype for robotic welding in reduced-gravity, low-pressure environments, combining a finite-volume thermal weld-pool model with phase change and thermocapillary transport, Gaussian-process and neural surrogates, and a simulated six-axis manipulator. The work de-risks in-space manufacturing before costly flight-like testing.

entry.title: When Correctness Feedback Erases Evidence: Phase-Separated Completeness Auditing in Verus

author.name: Adarsh Agrawal (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: Shows that correctness feedback in formal verification pipelines suppresses the very evidence needed to audit specification completeness, demonstrating that independent no-feedback discovery more than doubles certified-witness yield over a corrective-feedback loop on Verus/Rust tasks. The result is consistent across four model families and holds under matched call budgets and format-matched controls.

entry.title: EvolvingBrain: An Adaptive Skill System for Multi-modal Agents Self-Evolution in Open Worlds

author.name: Runxuan Liu, Jingqi Shi, Baoxin Wang, Honghong Zhao, Haoyuan Xu, Yueqing Sun, Jiafeng Liang, Tao He, Dayong Wu, Qi Gu, Shijin Wang, Ming Liu, Bing Qin

entry.summary: Proposes EvolvingBrain, an adaptive skill system for multi-modal agent self-evolution that extracts procedural and problematic patterns from model-specific trajectories and distills them into an evolving stratified skill library. It aims to combine the imitation benefits of supervised fine-tuning with the exploration benefits of outcome-based RL while using intermediate trajectory information.

entry.title: ClaimScope: Label-Blind Witness Verification for Mathematical Claim Auditing

author.name: Mushir Akhtar

entry.summary: ClaimScope is a 72-task benchmark for auditing mathematical claims made by agents, requiring a verdict, scope analysis, counterexample, and repair across topics like optimizer-state transport and exact 2x2 linear algebra. A witness checker evaluates only the model's submitted state without reference labels, making evaluation label-blind while still conveying validity information. This offers a fresh take on evaluating mathematical reasoning beyond answer accuracy.

entry.title: CIM-Embed: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Multimodal Embeddings for Clustering

author.name: Yinghua Xu, Pengyang Xie, Yanxiang Zhou, Chuanzhi Tong, Xiao Xiao, Chaoqun Feng, Xiaoqing Wang

entry.summary: CIM-Embed learns multimodal embeddings conditioned on natural-language instructions so the same objects can be clustered differently under different criteria (e.g., grouping products by color vs. material). It uses supervised contrastive learning with heterogeneous structured batches, and at inference maps image, text, and instruction directly to an embedding for HDBSCAN clustering.

entry.title: GraphACM: Graph-based Action Consistency Measurement for Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents

author.name: Yaxin Ma, Wenbo Zhang, Satya Krishna Pothapragada, Alina Zare

entry.summary: GraphACM proposes fine-grained uncertainty quantification for LLM agents by merging equivalent states from multiple rollouts into a directed, action-labeled graph. It introduces node-level and global action-consistency measures that localize where behavioral differences occur, rather than collapsing consistency into a single task-level score.

entry.title: KULTURE Bench: A Benchmark for Assessing Language Model in Korean Cultural Context

author.name: Xiaonan Wang, Jinyoung Yeo, Joon-Ho Lim, Hansaem Kim

entry.summary: KULTURE Bench is a Korean-culture-specific evaluation framework built from cultural news, idioms, and poetry, designed to test comprehension and reasoning at word, sentence, and paragraph levels without relying on translated English benchmarks that import Western bias. The paper evaluates multiple models and finds cultural comprehension remains a challenge relative to general capability.

entry.title: Optimal Hydra: Model Heterogeneous Federated Learning for LLMs using Data-Informed Hydra-Nets

author.name: Gwen Legate, Rahaf Aljundi, Eugene Belilovsky

entry.summary: Optimal Hydra extends model-heterogeneous federated learning to LLM fine-tuning, adapting model size to heterogeneous client compute constraints using data-informed Hydra-Net sub-networks, where prior work was limited to pre-training and its sub-network selection conclusions do not transfer. This enables training on decentralized private data despite client resource limitations.

entry.title: TGrasp6D: Task-Informed Vision-Language Priors and Pose Refinement enable Zero-Shot Task-Oriented 6DoF Grasping

author.name: Manav Kulshrestha, Apoorva Vashisth, Damon Conover, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: TGrasp6D uses vision-language model priors to generate task-oriented 6DoF grasps zero-shot from a single RGB-D image, e.g., grasping a knife by the handle for slicing but leaving the handle clear for handoff. It avoids reliance on finite manually-annotated task-grasp datasets that cannot cover all task-object pairs. This advances practical robotic manipulation by leveraging language models for open-vocabulary task understanding.

entry.title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews

author.name: Dingjie Song, Zhiling Yan, Ziqian Zhang, Yuxuan Zhang, Lichao Sun

entry.summary: The paper introduces ReviewFact, a benchmark for factual errors in peer review comments across NLP, ML, and natural sciences, and PremiseCheck, an efficient framework where an LLM rewrites comments as explicit premises without reading the paper and a cheap decision model checks each premise against it. This hybrid achieves accuracy near frontier-LLM checking at lower cost and latency. It addresses growing concerns about review quality as both submissions and AI-assisted reviewing scale.

entry.title: FedSumUp: User-Auditable Privacy-Aware Representation Sharing for Resource-Constrained Federated Intelligence

author.name: Jingwei Zhao, Tiantong Sun, Yuanyuan Song, Jinhuan Guo, Wei Zishuo, Shengyu Huang, Ziyuan Ren, Wei Chen, Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FedSumUp, a federated data condensation method using a learnable lossy compressor on clients to produce compact, visually interpretable representations whose information capacity can be controlled to limit privacy leakage from reconstruction attacks. A dual-objective optimization preserves task-relevant semantics while suppressing reconstructable sensitive content, with low client-side compute for resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: Poison Valleys: Diagnosing Path-Dependent Failure in LLM Code Repair

author.name: Veljko Skarich

entry.summary: Poison Valleys is a diagnostic framework that traces code-repair agent failures back to the specific earlier commitment that caused them, tested across 1,844 model requests on two synthetic Python tasks. The authors inject plausible-but-incorrect software mechanisms into hypotheses or implementation plans and find that placing a misconception in the plan rather than the hypothesis increases failure by roughly 29-32 percent. It provides causal insight into how coding agents go wrong.

entry.title: Independent Data-Integrity Verification for LLM-Driven Functional Coverage Closure in Hardware Design

author.name: Venkata Krishna Kumar Vedantam

entry.summary: The paper describes an LLM agent that closes functional coverage in hardware verification by writing directed tests, with coverage read from simulator-exported reports and data integrity checked by independent scoreboards rather than the model's own claims. On three distinct RTL designs, the agent raised coverage from 67-92 percent to 100 percent within an 8-iteration budget. It demonstrates a trustworthy pattern for LLM agents in safety-critical verification workflows.

entry.title: Learning to Search for Executable Patternmaking from Certified Programs

author.name: Zhuotao Xu, Chi Zeng, Liying Yang, Xinxing Yu, Yanyan Liang

entry.summary: SemDraft is the first framework that learns to recover the editing steps between paired before-and-after sewing patterns, treating patternmaking as a search problem over executable editing programs rather than a one-shot generation task. By searching over editing actions and using a deterministic compiler to make recovered steps checkable, the system transforms unannotated pattern archives into verifiable program-level transformation data. This advances AI for design and fabrication by modeling the iterative edit process that real patternmakers use.

entry.title: Learning Rewards in Strategic Games

author.name: Antoine Bergerault, Cyrille Kone, Giorgia Ramponi

entry.summary: Studies reward inference in strategic multi-agent settings through the lens of strategic identifiability, showing that a reward explaining observed behavior may not induce optimal strategies when used for decision-making. The work extends inverse reinforcement learning theory to environments where agents adapt to one another, relevant to cybersecurity, driving, and markets.

entry.title: DemoStream: Batched Task-and-Motion-Plan Optimization for Automated Learning from Demonstration

author.name: Caelan Garrett, Neel Jawale, Fabio Ramos

entry.summary: Proposes DemoStream, a GPU-accelerated TAMP system that optimizes demonstration quality to enable automated learning from demonstration, addressing multi-modality in TAMP-generated solutions that makes them hard to learn from. It enables autonomous demonstration generation for general-purpose manipulation tasks without constant human involvement.

entry.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhixu Li, Keqian Tang, Litian Gong, Jingyu Yao, Wenqian Zhang, Tianze Xu, Zehao Wang, Yuping Wang, Junge Zhang, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a controlled benchmark separating task completion from preference satisfaction in personalized robotic manipulation. It probes five questions including zero-shot preference following, learning preferences from demonstrations, sample efficiency, generalization across layouts and tasks, and preference composition. Personalization is framed as essential for household robots.

entry.title: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention

author.name: Shiyu Ji, Peng Ling, Chen Lin, Shupeng Li, Yixuan Wang, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Introduces RoLaQ, an offline method for jointly calibrating rotation and quantization ranges for 2-bit KV cache compression in multi-head latent attention models. It refines a shared rotation within frozen key/value projection subspaces and jointly learns coupled quantization ranges, supervised by prediction matching and attention-output signals. This targets long-context inference memory costs for MLA-based architectures.

entry.title: Semantic Alignment of EEG and Text: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Decoding Imagined Speech

author.name: Shahryar G. Namdari, Francesco Iacomi, Riccardo Barbieri, Luca Mainardi

entry.summary: Adapts multimodal contrastive learning to imagined speech decoding from EEG, aligning EEG trial embeddings with those of a frozen pretrained text encoder using a composite objective with semantic reweighting and text-prototype discrimination. Evaluated on 39 intent categories, it moves beyond closed-set classification by exploiting relationships among linguistic intents, which matters for more flexible brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: INCONVENIENT: A Benchmark to Assess LLM Generalization Capabilities from Convenience Samples

author.name: Sara Rezaeimanesh, Chad Klochko, Kundan Thind, Mohammad Ghassemi

entry.summary: INCONVENIENT is a tabular benchmark designed to test model generalization under systematic sampling bias, where training data reflects convenience rather than population representativeness. Unlike existing OOD benchmarks that partition naturally occurring domains without controlling the induced distribution shift, this benchmark explicitly isolates and controls sampling-induced changes in feature-target relationships. This addresses a real and common gap between benchmark evaluation and real-world deployment.

entry.title: Predicting Live Birth After Fresh Embryo Transfer in IVF/ICSI: Differential ICM/Trophectoderm Morphology Encoding and a Hybrid Attention--Logistic Regression Ensemble

author.name: Abdul Raheem Shahzad, Jinxin Chen, Ming Zhang, Juan Deng

entry.summary: This paper builds a curated single-center dataset of 616 fresh embryo-transfer cycles and develops a hybrid attention network plus logistic regression ensemble to predict live birth before transfer. It introduces a novel differential weighting of inner cell mass and trophectoderm morphology and carefully addresses leakage-prone pathway-dependent variables in small clinical tabular data.

entry.title: Learning and Forecasting Multiscale Spatiotemporal Epidemic Dynamics with Lagrangian-Eulerian Graph Neural ODEs

author.name: Jinyi Duan, Qian Li, Biao Tang

entry.summary: The authors introduce LE-EpiGNODE, a graph neural ODE framework for medium- and long-range epidemic forecasting that replaces generic message passing with mechanism-guided neural operators: age-contact data drives Lagrangian infection generation while mobility data drives conservative Eulerian population transport within a structure-preserving universal differential equation. The model is evaluated on 14 controlled synthetic mechanisms plus real-world epidemic settings, aiming for more interpretable and physically grounded forecasting from partial observations.

entry.title: PocketTSLM: Deploying an On-Device Soft-Prompt Time-Series Language Model for Privacy-Preserving Smartphone Reasoning

author.name: Max Rosenblattl, Nikhil Krishnaswamy, Leon Nissen, Manuel Milling, Nicolas Zumarraga, Ning Wang, Thomas Kaar, Robert Jakob, Bj\"orn W. Schuller, Elgar Fleisch, Patrick Langer, Paul Schmiedmayer

entry.summary: PocketTSLM deploys a time-series language model on smartphones via soft prompts, enabling privacy-preserving reasoning over physiological sensor streams without sending raw data to the cloud. It avoids the temporal-structure loss of statistical aggregation or text serialization under on-device context and memory budgets.

entry.title: Sharp and Stable Label-Free Calibration Certificates from Logical Coherence

author.name: Takahiro Kato (NP-hard, Inc.)

entry.summary: This paper derives sharp, label-free lower bounds on calibration residuals for probabilistic predictors that answer logically related questions, using minimax theorems over bettor stake restrictions.
