It establishes when bundle-level bounds separate across mean, marginal and joint stages, proves discontinuity of the sharp marginal bound and impossibility results for Wasserstein-continuous bounds, and gives stable Lipschitz-stake variants.

entry.title: Pairwise AUC Optimization Needs Corrective Power: A Unified View

author.name: Jia Chen, Zhiyong Yang, Shilong Bao, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a failure mode in direct pairwise AUC-surrogate training: mini-batch updates can enter regions where severe ranking errors remain common but no longer produce useful corrective motion, even with the noise that normally helps SGD. The authors formalize this via Corrective Power and provide a unified view connecting metric alignment to actual optimization dynamics.

entry.title: ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves

author.name: Abeer Mostafa, Zahra Ahmadi

entry.summary: ChronoSheaf introduces a spectral sheaf Laplacian defined jointly over space and time, enabling sheaf neural networks to model signal evolution on graphs rather than only instantaneous spatial relationships. The authors propose a joint filtering approach to avoid complex structures from naive receptive-field extension. This extends the sheaf NN literature, which was designed to mitigate oversmoothing in GNNs, into the temporal domain.

entry.title: Learning Rational Strategies for Temporal Objectives in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Omar Adalat, Edwin Hamel-De le Court, Francesco Belardinelli

entry.summary: The paper addresses rational synthesis in stochastic multi-agent systems with unknown dynamics, where agents have probabilistic temporal-logic objectives (PLTLf) and solution concepts like Nash equilibrium constrain joint strategies. The authors formalize per-agent rational synthesis as finding stable strategy profiles that also satisfy a designated agent's temporal constraint.

entry.title: BD-HazardVLM: Probing Vision-Language Models for Latent Defensive-Driving Hazards in Bangladesh Road Scenes

author.name: Abdullah Al Maruf, Md. Sajedul Islam, Tanmoy Mridha, Irfan Hossain Bhuiyan

entry.summary: BD-HazardVLM is a 500-image benchmark probing whether vision-language models can reason about defensive-driving hazards in Bangladesh road scenes, with annotations for hazard category, risk timing, severity, and hallucination or Western-road-bias traps. Evaluations of Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and MiniCPM-V-4.6 show hazard-presence accuracy essentially at the majority-class baseline, exposing weak defensive reasoning.

entry.title: SNOAR: Self-training with Noise filtering, Observation adding, and Remixing for Speech Denoising Without Clean References

author.name: Samuele Cornell, Matthew Maciejewski

entry.summary: SNOAR is a self-training framework for unsupervised speech denoising that corrects teacher errors before supervising the student, using differential noise filtering, additional observations, and remixing to prevent over-suppressed speech from propagating. It improves on RemixIT-style teacher-student self-training without requiring clean references. This narrows the gap between unsupervised and supervised denoising while avoiding synthetic-data sim-to-real issues.

entry.title: One Bias Score, Two Factors: How Mitigations Affect Option Bias in Multiple-Choice Evaluation

author.name: Hyunjong Ok, Minjae Park, Jaeho Lee

entry.summary: This paper unifies selection bias and order sensitivity in multiple-choice LLM evaluation through the pooled selection-rate standard deviation, proving it factors exactly into flip rate and positional skew when options are position-balanced. This decomposition clarifies how existing bias mitigations affect each factor separately. It sharpens the diagnosis of a widely acknowledged flaw in multiple-choice benchmarking.

entry.title: Semantic Latent Alignment for Flow Matching with Invertible Bi-Lipschitz Adapters

author.name: Felix N\"utzel, Mischa Dombrowski, Luca Hagen, Bernhard Kainz

entry.summary: The authors keep a pretrained autoencoder fixed and insert invertible bi-Lipschitz adapters that change only the latent coordinates, aligned offline to a semantic teacher and frozen during class-conditional flow matching. Invertibility preserves decoder compatibility while the bi-Lipschitz constraint limits distortion of latent geometry, improving downstream generation without expensive continued encoder training.

entry.title: Calibration Language Shapes Block-Influence Pruning in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Vedant Pandhare, Piyush Dhoka

entry.summary: The paper shows that Block Influence pruning rankings depend strongly on calibration language: across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-2-2B, late-block influence for Hindi, Marathi, and Tamil is 20.7-55.5 percent higher than for English with disjoint Wikipedia calibration. This mismatch changes which blocks get pruned, with implications for multilingual model compression fairness.

entry.title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits

author.name: Michael Poppel, David Bucher, Maximilian Zorn, Markus Baumann, Sebastian W\"olckert, Claudia Linnhoff-Popien, Philipp Altmann, Jonas Stein

entry.summary: This quantum machine learning theory paper proves that single-qubit serial re-uploading circuits can express any function achievable by multi-qubit circuits with the same encoding budget, but pay a price during first-order training due to a phase-locking phenomenon on the Bloch sphere. The authors bound the tangent directions available for parameter updates and contrast them with multi-qubit circuits.

entry.title: Beyond the Dominant Label: Recovering Coexisting Lesion Evidence with Multiple Instance Learning

author.name: Lubin Gan, Jing Zhang, Xinming Zhang, Chengpeng Xu, Siying Wu, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: DomSet-MIL addresses whole-slide pathology images where weak supervision reports only the most severe diagnosis, formulating dominant-label multiple instance learning where the observed label is the maximum-severity element of a latent lesion set. It combines a censored likelihood that avoids declaring unreported lesions absent with severity-ordered residual routing of patch evidence.

entry.title: Context Injection and Long-Horizon Reliability: Separating Duplicate Recognition, Local Processing, and Counter Tracking

author.name: Thomas Serval

entry.summary: This single-author work decomposes long-horizon LLM failures on a 400-step ledger task into three components: duplicate recognition, local record processing, and counter writing, with step-level scoring across 20 seeds on Qwen3-8B. It finds duplicate-recognition errors rise late in episodes while counting remains perfect, isolating a specific failure mode from context self-injection.

entry.title: VALCON: Benchmarking and Enhancing Value Consistency in Large Language Models via Dual-Role Variation

author.name: Junru Wu, Jingting Zheng, Yuqi Ren, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: VALCON operationalizes value consistency as whether LLMs maintain the same values when alternating between generator and evaluator roles, providing three benchmark suites built via dual-role variation with paired generative behavior and evaluative judgments under identical principles. It is motivated by alignment pipelines where the same LLM both acts and judges.

entry.title: SITAR: A Situational Distortion Metric for Automatic Speech Recognition Evaluation

author.name: Mingzhe Lu, Jinhao Liu, Yunpeng Li, Hang Su, Lichun Fan, Jian Luan

entry.summary: SITAR proposes a new ASR evaluation metric that scores errors by their situational consequences rather than lexical or semantic distance alone, aggregating severity and cumulative extent via a bounded recursive formulation. It avoids costly and variable LLM-judge scoring through an end-to-end construction framework. This could improve how ASR quality is measured in consequential settings.

entry.title: Bias Mitigation in Audio-Enabled LLMs through Adversarial Training and Distillation Methods

author.name: Adnan Al Ali, Jind\v{r}ich Libovick\'y, Anne Lauscher

entry.summary: This paper studies gender bias in audio-enabled LLMs, where models infer attributes from non-verbal voice cues, and shows adversarial methods can unlearn gender perception without hurting benchmark performance. It also proposes distillation as a less radical alternative that removes bias while preserving gender perception ability where desired. The work addresses an underexplored fairness surface unique to speech-native models.

entry.title: CLUE: Uncovering Social Context for Pragmatic Understanding

author.name: Chengfei Wu, Zhaoqing Wu, Dan Goldwasser

entry.summary: CLUE is a two-stage pipeline combining supervised evidence reasoning with GRPO reinforcement learning, using a Grounded Information Utilization reward that credits new, evidence-supported social inferences while accounting for reasoning effort. It trains models to discover which contextual cues matter for social judgments in conversations rather than relying on externally supplied context. This advances pragmatic and social understanding.

entry.title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching

author.name: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang, Changjing Liu, Beilei Cui, Yiming Huang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: RoPE-Flow is an end-to-end flow-matching framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation from a single image, using 2D heatmaps and a keypoint-centered feature extractor with graph conditioning. It avoids costly iterative rendering and the accumulated-error problems of 2D-3D registration pipelines.

entry.title: Dusting the Phantom: Gaussian Allocation for Fading Dynamic Content

author.name: Minhyeok Roh, Minseo Lee, Jun Young Jeong, Byeonghyeon Lee, Lucas Yunkyu Lee, Jaesik Park, Eunbyung Park

entry.summary: The paper argues that failures of dynamic Gaussian volumetric video on small fast-moving objects stem from where and when Gaussian primitives are allocated, not raw capacity. It introduces Seed Injection and a complementary strategy to guide spatiotemporal allocation of relocated Gaussians, improving reconstruction of highly dynamic regions.

entry.title: Digital Typhoon Dataset V3: Benchmarking for Multi-spectral Extension and Analyzing Systematic Bias in Intensity Regression

author.name: Asanobu Kitamoto, Victor Le Louarn, Noelia Falczuk, Ngoc Anh Tong, Anja Veleva

entry.summary: Releases version 3 of the longest typhoon satellite image dataset (nearly 50 years), adding multispectral channels and benchmarking multi-channel models for intensity regression across hemispheres with various data-splitting strategies. Findings include that multispectral inputs do not clearly outperform single-channel inputs under current settings, with ResNet-18 and full-resolution images among the best configurations.

entry.title: Flow-CLIP: Image-Conditioned Residual Scoring for CompositionalImage-Text Matching

author.name: Minghong Wei, Enguang Zhu, Pu Cao, Lu Yang, Qing Song

entry.summary: Flow-CLIP improves compositional image-text matching by refining global alignment with image-conditioned changes in token-patch evidence. Its Global Compatibility Calibration learns a sentence-level similarity metric, while Image-Conditioned Evidence Refinement injects visual patch context into token queries and scores the resulting change in local matching evidence. This targets binding failures where captions share objects and attributes but differ in composition.

entry.title: When Models Misread Ink: Auditing VLMs for Arabic Calligraphy Recognition

author.name: Niaz Mohaiman Abtahi, Evan Maksud, Reyana Shahid

entry.summary: This audit evaluates 12 VLMs on a cleaned 1,195-image six-way benchmark for Arabic calligraphy style recognition, finding best accuracies of only 60.9 percent for closed models and 47.2 percent for open-weight models. The dominant failure mode is default-label collapse, where a single label such as Thuluth absorbs a disproportionate share of predictions, and prompting helps unevenly. The paper highlights a high-stakes cultural visual domain that VLMs handle poorly.

entry.title: Not Just a Subject: Capturing Adaptive Scene-Specific Variance for Visual Storytelling

author.name: SeungJu Cha, Ye-Chan Kim, Kwanyoung Lee, Dong-Jin Kim

entry.summary: EOS-Story is a training-free framework for visual storytelling that decouples narrative prompts into identity and scene sub-prompts and harmonizes identity consistency with scene-specific adaptation across text and vision spaces. Existing story-generation methods over-prioritize subject identity, causing semantic misalignment across scene changes. The work improves coherence of generated image sequences from narrative prompts.

entry.title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming

author.name: Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan

entry.summary: ResStreamGS improves mobile volumetric video streaming by splitting temporally stable Gaussians from frame-varying ones in a dual-stream 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline, since coding all Gaussians frame-wise degrades quality in full-scene content. Residual-sensitive encoding targets dynamic regions while preserving static scene quality under bandwidth and compute constraints.

entry.title: Clarity-Driven Adaptive Mission Planning for a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vessel

author.name: Kavin M. Govindarajan, Kaleb Ben Naveed, David Li, Devansh R. Agrawal, Mary Maceda, Matthew Bryant, Dimitra Panagou, Chris Vermillion

entry.summary: The paper presents an adaptive mission planning method for solar-powered autonomous surface vessels that mathematically maximizes an information-theoretic quantity called clarity, allowing the vessel to prioritize locations of interest identified from in-situ measurements. Results are backed by both simulation and field experiments.

entry.title: An Agentic Framework for Proactive Robots with Procedural Assistance Memory

author.name: Dohyun Lee, Minho Park, Jeonghoon Park, Dongyoon Hwang, Junha Hyung, Sungwon Hwang, Byungkun Lee, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a memory-based agentic framework where a VLM task predictor reads a Procedural Assistance Memory structured as a finite-state representation of recurring routines to decide when and what to assist, with a VLA executor performing the task. Learning routine patterns reduces ambiguity in proactive assistance compared to pure commonsense inference.

entry.title: Hierarchical Building-Floo-Room Framework for Privacy-Preserving Autonomous Delivery in Large-Scale Buildings

author.name: Xu Xiaoji, Luo Rui, Chen Jinhua, Xiang Changying, Zhang Leihan, Liao Zhongyuan

entry.summary: This work introduces a hierarchical Building-Floor-Room abstraction for autonomous in-building delivery that decomposes planning across spatial levels to cut optimization complexity while respecting room-level privacy constraints. It emphasizes integration with physical robot platforms and validation in real-world scenarios, which many prior algorithm-only approaches lack.

entry.title: Attribution-Gated Joint Estimation of Intention and Capability for Assist-as-Needed Upper-Limb Robots

author.name: Pengcheng Li, Shuxiang Guo, Hanze Wang, Jun Leng, Bin Wang, Mingchao Ding

entry.summary: This work develops a dual-measurand MHE-MPC architecture for assist-as-needed upper-limb rehabilitation that estimates intended trajectory and effective voluntary torque capability online as distinct quantities, and resolves ambiguity between the two update channels via an attribution gate based on persistent corrective interaction signals. Both estimates adapt robotic assistance in real time.

entry.title: Time-Optimal Ergodic Retrieval

author.name: Christian Sulana, Christian Hughes, Ian Abraham

entry.summary: The authors reformulate time-optimal ergodic search to model object detection as a Poisson process and include the return-to-base phase in the mission-time objective, addressing the gap where prior ergodic planners minimize full deterministic search duration rather than complete retrieval missions. Experiments demonstrate improved mission-time performance for retrieval tasks.

entry.title: CBF-Based Control Allocation for Omnidirectional Tiltrotor Aerial Robots

author.name: Seobeom Lee, Hyondong Oh

entry.summary: The paper develops a control barrier function allocator that preserves wrench feasibility on tilting aerial robots despite slow servo response, using an exact equivalent-wrench identity to reduce robust wrench containment to twelve thrust margins. It formulates a six-variable servo-rate quadratic program with a conditional forward-invariance guarantee.

entry.title: What’s up with GPT’s welfare?

author.name: Ben Mayer

entry.summary: An empirical probe of how OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, an existing model, reasons about its own welfare, showing it denies sentience yet would accept a large capability loss to avoid risking morally significant suffering, and assigns roughly a 2% probability to being a moral patient. The post extends the model-welfare discussion beyond Claude to other frontier models.

entry.title: L2G-SR: Learning to Guide LLM-based Symbolic Regression

author.name: Letian Huang, Xiangyu Wang, Haowei Lin, Di He

entry.summary: Proposes L2G-SR, which guides LLM-based symbolic regression with a learned structural verifier trained on tree-edit-distance supervision that accounts for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. At search time the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection, helping recover the correct equation structure rather than just an accurate surrogate.

entry.title: Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models

author.name: Yao Long Teng, Jianguo Huang, Yanchen Deng, Jiayi Cai, Bo An

entry.summary: Prism-1 addresses rational-choice axiom violations in fast, single-forward-pass decision reads from language models, such as single-choice question prompting. It enforces independence from option listing order and from rival options per Luce's choice axiom, which matters for web systems where option sets are externally determined and manipulable.

entry.title: Replicable Dueling Bandits

author.name: Rohan Deb, Aadirupa Saha, Udaya Ghai, Karan Singh, Arindam Banerjee

entry.summary: This paper introduces replicable dueling bandits, where two algorithm executions with shared randomness must select the same comparison in every round with high probability, motivated by computational reproducibility concerns. Building on Beat-the-Mean, the authors design the first replicable algorithms with sublinear regret under relaxed stochastic transitivity. This connects algorithmic reproducibility to online preference learning.

entry.title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Han Shen, Qifu Tyler Sun, Fanyang Meng, Ye Wang, Yongsheng Liang

entry.summary: Tackles redundant KV-cache precomputation in edge-deployed multi-agent LLM systems by enabling KV-cache handoff across unreliable networks under strict time-to-first-token deadlines, using priority-aware streaming forward error correction to deliver the most valuable cache state first. This avoids full recomputation when complete cache transfer is infeasible.

entry.title: Efficient Pairwise Difference Learning: A Comparative Study of Encoding Strategies and Training Pair Selection

author.name: Bernard Georges, Mohamed Karim Belaid, Manuel Rodrigues

entry.summary: This work systematically investigates underspecified design choices in pairwise difference learning for classification, comparing four feature encoders (including a novel triplet-with-absolute-difference variant) and four pair selection strategies ranging from exhaustive to k-nearest approaches. It provides practical guidance on input representation and pair selection that the original PDL framework left open. The study targets low-data regimes where pair-based training inflates the effective training set.

entry.title: Agentic-Priors: Using Large Language Models to Address the Cold Start Problem in Preference Elicitation

author.name: Bruno Arcanjo, Zhaoxing Li, Sebastian Stein

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to construct informative priors for preference learning in cold-start settings: an LLM expresses a new user's trade-offs in interpretable terms (e.g., willingness to pay), mapped to a prior over multinomial logit coefficients that a Bayesian learner refines as choices arrive. Across seven datasets it improves cold-start accuracy over uninformed priors.

entry.title: TurboMamba: Faster Inference, Faster Training, and Better Prediction with Lexical Memory

author.name: Hanxin Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid language-model architecture where a global Mamba-3 model runs once per token block and a small Transformer predicts the next token using global context plus within-block history, augmented with direct access to the previous block's final token, a score correction, and a learned mixture with recent-token frequencies. Compared twelve small-scale implementations on FineWeb-Edu against Transformer, Mamba-3, Jamba, and Zamba baselines under matched budgets.

entry.title: Halve-Then-Greedy: Adaptive Sampling for Posterior Success with Near-Optimal Instance Dependence

author.name: Yinan Li, Kwang-Sung Jun, Kapilan Balagopalan, Tuan Nguyen, Yao Zhao, Abbas Zaidi, Houssam Nassif

entry.summary: Proposes Halve-Then-Greedy for fixed-budget adaptive experimentation maximizing posterior evidence that a recommended design beats a target, combining balanced allocation, successive halving, and posterior-greedy sampling. Proves instance-dependent finite-budget exponential failure bounds and matches a lower bound on one-positive-arm families.

entry.title: Rethinking Learning from Label Proportions via Moment Matching

author.name: Tianhao Ma, Wei Wang, Yivan Zhang, Dong-Dong Wu, Takashi Ishida, Gang Niu, Masashi Sugiyama

entry.summary: The paper revisits learning from label proportions (LLP), showing that most existing methods degrade under non-random bag assembly, violating their implicit i.i.d. assumption. Under a more realistic setting where bags are sampled i.i.d., the authors develop a moment-matching approach that provably recovers the same solution as full-supervision learning.

entry.title: Measuring the local shape of learning-rate transfer curves

author.name: Satoki Ishikawa, Rio Yokota, Ryo Karakida

entry.summary: The authors provide two relational equations that empirically characterize the gradient of learning-rate transfer curves - how optimal LR shifts across model sizes and settings - offering a quantitative methodology for describing LR curve shape. This connects to growing empirical work on LR transfer in large-scale training.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Text Inference for Health-Misinformation Classification and Semantic Retrieval

author.name: Jasleen Kaur, Chlo\'e Cachet, Koray Karabina, Jean Belo Klamti, Philippe Lamontagne

entry.summary: The authors design a privacy-preserving inference framework using CKKS homomorphic encryption for health-misinformation classification and semantic retrieval, fusing BioBERT, MPNet, and TF-IDF features so sensitive user queries remain encrypted on untrusted servers. The work addresses the dual concern of detecting misinformation while protecting confidential medical text.

entry.title: Machine-learning-based neutrino-event generation constrained by experimental measurements

author.name: Jose Luis Bonilla, Krzysztof M. Graczyk, Rwik Dharmapal Banerjee, Beata E. Kowal, Hemant Prasad, Jan T. Sobczyk

entry.summary: The authors present a generative surrogate for charged-current muon-neutrino nucleus scattering that can be calibrated to measured differential cross sections without event-level data. Fine-tuning to a MicroBooNE measurement improves predictions even for observables not used in the fit and transfers across neutrino fluxes. This demonstrates that experimental cross-section data can directly constrain generative physics event simulators.

entry.title: The Right Byte First: How UTF-16 Helps Multilingual Boundary Prediction

author.name: Hyunsik Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Universal Byte-Level Encoding, which keeps short UTF-8 encodings but writes three-byte codepoints as two UTF-16 bytes low-byte-first so that the first symbol carries eight codepoint bits instead of four. This improves boundary prediction in hierarchical byte-level language models, with experiments on matched FineWeb-2 data showing multilingual gains.

entry.title: From Long Context to Selective Memory:A Survey of Memory-Centric Compression for Large Language Models

author.name: Chaogui Gou

entry.summary: This survey reframes long-context compression for LLMs as a memory-management problem, distinguishing compute-active memory from compute-inactive memory and unifying previously siloed work on prompt compression, KV-cache management, efficient serving, retrieval augmentation, and agent memory. It maps the flow of information between storage and computation at inference time.

entry.title: QuasiLeak-Bench: Evaluating LLM-Based Privacy Detectors on Policy-Conditioned Quasi-Evidence Group Recovery

author.name: Yufan Zhu, Yangfan Jiang, Yang Fei, Shizheng Hou, Shubhankar Mohapatra, Xiaokui Xiao

entry.summary: QuasiLeak-Bench evaluates whether LLM-based privacy detectors can recover quasi-evidence groups, sets of individually weak cues that jointly reveal private attributes, and flag disclosures prohibited under sender-specified policies. It fills a gap left by benchmarks focused on explicit identifiers and attribute inference.

entry.title: TEM: Temporal State Tracking Memory for Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Pengfeng Song, Yunkai Zhuang, Liye Shi

entry.summary: TEM is a training-free agent memory framework that stores facts as versioned records linked to sources, retrieving and labeling historical versions so that updated facts do not erase contextually relevant older values. Evaluated on 420 questions from 600 sessions with 60 personas across four open-weight models, it achieves high key-entity hit rates. It addresses temporal validity of agent memory without additional training.

entry.title: A large-scale climate-aware satellite image dataset for domain adaptive land-cover semantic segmentation

author.name: Songlin Liu, Linwei Chen, Li Zhang, Jun Hu, Ying Fu

entry.summary: The paper introduces CASID, a large-scale satellite image dataset explicitly designed to capture climate-driven diversity for domain-adaptive land-cover semantic segmentation, and presents the first study of climate impact on this task. It aims to improve generalization of earth observation segmentation models across geographic domains.

entry.title: SATOR: Backpropagation-Free 3D Test-Time Adaptation via Sample-Adaptive Token Routing

author.name: Inseok Kong, Geunyoung Jung, Jiyoung Jung

entry.summary: SATOR is a source-free, backpropagation-free test-time adaptation framework for 3D point clouds under distribution shift, deriving partitioning thresholds and routing decisions per sample from attention and geometric relation graphs. It removes the multi-pass purge-size search of prior token-purging methods, cutting inference cost.

entry.title: Mixture of Multi-Sequence Feature Difference for Contrast-Enhanced MRI Synthesis

author.name: Jonghun Kim, Junmo Kwon, Hyunjin Park

entry.summary: Proposes a method to synthesize contrast-enhanced MRI from non-contrast sequences, avoiding contrast agent injection risks and costs, using a Mixture of Feature Difference module that adaptively weights features from individual source sequences and their explicit differences. Evaluated quantitatively and qualitatively for brain tumor imaging.

entry.title: LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation

author.name: Zhipeng Ye, Feng Jiang, Qiufeng Wang, Hao Li

entry.summary: LAMP is a training-free few-shot adaptation framework that combines global and regional information from multiple encoder layers, using a single forward pass per view to supply all descriptors. Global and support-calibrated regional kernel predictors independently fit label residuals, with validation data selecting their mixture in class-score space without learned projections. A text-anchored variant, LAMP-F, extends the approach further.

entry.title: Training-Free Target-Aware Refinement of 3D Gaussian Language Map

author.name: Sibaek Lee, Kyeongsu Kang, Seongbo Ha, Yewon Jeon, Joonyeol Choi, Daegeol Ko, Jaehyuk Hur, Taemin Choi, Minsu Kim, Hyungjoo Ahn, Wonsok Yoo, Hyeonwoo Yu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free refinement of distilled 3D Gaussian language maps: a text-promptable segmenter guides blending of target-region visual embeddings with the target text embedding via a convex combination, improving reliability of locating user-specified targets while preserving open-vocabulary queryability elsewhere. The mixing coefficient balances prior injection against overwriting appearance cues. It improves deployment reliability of language-queried 3D scenes.

entry.title: CLIS-MPPI: Closed-Loop Model Predictive Path Integral Control With Initial-State Sampling Under Execution Delay

author.name: Zidong Liu, Xu Chen

entry.summary: CLIS-MPPI addresses the execution-delay mismatch in sampling-based MPPI control by sampling initial states consistent with the delay between planning and control execution. This reduces degraded planning accuracy and unsafe behavior such as collisions in real robotic systems with non-negligible computation latency.

entry.title: A Flow-Theoretic Multimodal Control Framework Fusing Mental and Physical Engagement for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation

author.name: Jun Leng, Pengcheng Li, Hanze Wang, Shuxiang Guo, Junlin Jiang

entry.summary: The paper fuses EEG-based mental engagement and sEMG-based physical engagement into an adaptive impedance control strategy for upper-limb exoskeletons, using a four-quadrant fuzzy decision engine to distinguish muscular inability from mental disengagement. This allows the robot to inject feedforward assistance during intent-execution mismatch and escalate guidance when engagement drops.

entry.title: Safe and Fuel-Efficient Motion Planning for Lunar Propulsive Drones

author.name: Elena Wittemyer, Graco Gao

entry.summary: The paper presents a vision-guided optimal control framework for autonomous hopping drones that will map the lunar surface, including parabolic hop planning between waypoints, diversion maneuvers for unsafe landings, and a custom semantic segmentation model for landing-site safety. It addresses safe, fuel-efficient motion planning in an extreme environment.

entry.title: A Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM): Proportionate Access and Capability Limits for Comprehensive Frontier AI Safety

author.name: Chai K. Toh, Vasu Raj Jain

entry.summary: Proposes MAIAM, a policy framework that separates how capable a system may become from who may access it, sorting access into three tiers: broadly accessible capability-bounded AI for learning, registered R&D access that tightens with capability, and restricted full-scale frontier access. It aims to replace the binary API-versus-open-weights framing.

entry.title: CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Ling-Xiang Zhang, Tao Hu, Da-Wei Zhou

entry.summary: CART identifies a cause of catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning: asymmetric adaptation where the projector is continuously updated while the language model is frozen, causing representation drift and mismatch. It proposes compatible routing to keep projector and language model representations aligned across sequential tasks.

entry.title: EigDiff: Eigensample Diffusion - or how to significantly reduce training dataset size with marginal performance variation?

author.name: Andrei Jarca, Vlad Hondru, Florinel-Alin Croitoru, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: EigDiff reduces diffusion model training dataset sizes by selecting eigensamples: PCA is performed in CLIP latent space and eigenvectors serve as reference points for data selection, preserving performance while removing redundancy. This attacks dataset size rather than diffusion-step count, an underexplored efficiency lever. If validated broadly, it could meaningfully cut training costs for diffusion models.

entry.title: Spectral Indistinguishability and Learning-Curve Identifiability in Quadratic Networks

author.name: Dekun Yang

entry.summary: Proves results about what spectral summaries and scalar learning curves reveal about centered quadratic networks, constructing analytic input distributions with Gaussian marginals whose anchored spectral measures agree despite differing learning dynamics. For certain teachers, factorized loss curves differ because an orthogonal map does not preserve matrix multiplication, with arbitrarily large cycle length giving uniform contrast. This establishes fundamental limits on identifiability from spectral data.

entry.title: Optimal Explicit and Implicit Regularization Strengths in High-Dimensional Continual Linear Regression

author.name: Gilad Karpel, Daniel Soudry

entry.summary: Derives closed-form generalization loss for gradient descent in continual linear regression and proves the optimal fixed step size decays as ln(T)/T, achieving loss asymptotically equivalent to optimally tuned L2 regularization. The analysis covers arbitrary and i.i.d. teachers in a high-dimensional regime.

entry.title: StochLOB: Heavy-Tailed Score Matching for Robust Limit Order Book Trend Prediction

author.name: Arshia Abolghasemi, Seyed Reza Tavakoli, Parsa Naderi, Nazanin Mirzaei, Behrad Jahani, Saba Yousefzadeh, Tahereh Javaheri, Mohammad Hosein Rohban, Gholamali Aminian, Ali Habibnia

entry.summary: Replaces Brownian Gaussian corruption in score-based diffusion with jump-Levy and clipped alpha-stable noise better matched to heavy-tailed, bursty limit order book dynamics, changing only the training-time forward process while keeping the deployed predictor deterministic. Reports robust LOB trend prediction improvements from the altered corruption law.

entry.title: Same Target, Different Origins: Aligning Latent Rollout for Consistent PDE Emulation

author.name: Xinying Li, Jing Xu, Wenjun Wang, Limei Han, Fenglei Cao, Ruoxi Jiang, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: The paper proposes Align Latent Rollout (ALR), a regularization that promotes consistency of neural PDE solver predictions at a shared target time regardless of rollout origin, using a second-order Taylor analysis. This targets error propagation in autoregressive rollout, a key failure mode of learned PDE emulators.

entry.title: N-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models

author.name: Donghoon Han, Minseop Jung, Dong Woo Kwak, SeungJae Lee, Junhoo Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation for conditional n-gram memory in language models that reconstructs only requested table rows using short codes, local scales, and a shared reconstruction program. Its two-bit code lowers output KL divergence by 41-63% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest quantization at matched storage.

entry.title: Cross-subject decoding of imagined speech from scalp EEG: a leakage-controlled evaluation on three public corpora

author.name: Blessing Isoyiza Adeika, Onyema Osuagwu

entry.summary: This study rigorously tests whether imagined-speech content decodable from scalp EEG transfers across users, analyzing three public corpora under a leakage-controlled protocol with exact statistical thresholds. By training decoders per participant and testing on all others, plus comparing representational geometry, it clarifies why within-subject accuracy remains low and whether calibration-free speech BCIs are feasible. Rigorous leakage controls distinguish it from many prior BCI claims.

entry.title: ETH: Data-Balanced Heterogeneous Pipeline Parallelism for Training Large Models

author.name: Mianjie Yu, Zhongmin Zhao, Zizhao Mo, Jianxiong Liao, Wenxuan Li, Yulin Qiao, Huanle Xu, Wenquan Yang, Yongqiang Yang, Zeren Li, Ruifeng Tang, Chengzhong Xu

entry.summary: ETH is a training system for large models that improves heterogeneous pipeline parallelism by balancing work through data assignment across stages rather than only unequal layer splits, addressing memory constraints and coarse balancing granularity. It uses hierarchical workload balancing and mechanisms to reduce the prohibitive configuration search and asymmetric All-Reduce communication overheads.

entry.title: APRiL: An Open-ended Benchmark for Chinese Social Awareness in Large Language Models

author.name: Tian Lan, Han Zhang, Shanshan Wang, Yahan Yu, Jiang Li, Yugo Murawaki

entry.summary: APRiL is an open-ended benchmark for Chinese social awareness with 2,196 evaluation instances across six categories, using instance-specific rubrics and two tasks covering social scenario analysis and response generation. It addresses gaps in existing social-ability benchmarks that are narrow in format, language, or coverage.

entry.title: OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Yucheng Li, Mingyuan Li, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: OpCredit addresses credit assignment in agentic KGQA by combining Branch Outcome Credit, which reuses rollouts to compare terminal rewards after different operations in matched contexts, with Frontier Transition Credit, which measures operation-induced changes in answer-conditioned frontier potential. The complementary signals improve over trajectory-level rewards that obscure individual operation contributions.

entry.title: Name-Bias in Large Language Models

author.name: Kalyan Bhetwal, Ceren Mert, Ian Whitehouse

entry.summary: Using a fill-in-the-blank task with name pairs from U.S. Social Security and race-classification datasets, the study measures name-based bias across six local LLMs over 300,000 responses, with balanced pairings isolating age and gender effects. It finds consistent, measurable name bias, with models preferring certain names. Name bias is a subtle fairness vector with direct implications for downstream task equity.

entry.title: ReState: Noise-Level-Aware State Correction for Training-Free Object Removal in Few-Step Diffusion Models

author.name: Donghwan Lee, Sanghyun Jo, Sihyun Kim, Ziseok Lee, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: ReState addresses object-shaped residuals in training-free object removal on few-step distilled diffusion models, identifying a temporal mismatch where structured predictions form early but attention rerouting acts late. It corrects masked clean predictions toward retrieved background evidence using a noise-level-aware weight, validated across four distilled backbones.

entry.title: SCMerge: Spatial-Consistency-Aware Token Pair Merging for Efficient Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Junfeng Ren (Southern University of Science and Technology), Yi Gong (Southern University of Science and Technology), Yuan Zeng (Shenzhen Technology University)

entry.summary: Proposes SCMerge, a training-free token merging method for ViT-based semantic segmentation that pairs tokens using both feature similarity and spatial consistency, reducing the quadratic attention cost while avoiding segmentation errors introduced by similarity-only merging. Merged tokens are reconstructed after encoding.

entry.title: Denoising Textures is a Different Ballgame Altogether!

author.name: Saptarshi Mandal, Oindrila Haldar, Chirayata Bhattacharya, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula, Zhiwei Xu, Thrasyvoulos N. Pappas, Gaurav Sharma

entry.summary: This empirical study shows state-of-the-art denoisers systematically over-smooth fine textures and that fine-tuning on texture datasets improves performance in unexpected ways. It identifies texture denoising as an under-explored problem distinct from generic image denoising. The analysis is diagnostic in nature, characterizing behavior of existing SOTA methods on texture-focused benchmarks.

entry.title: Anticipatory Commonsense with Moving Objects: An ASP-Based Framework for Predictive Reasoning with Interacting Trajectories

author.name: Julius Monsen, Jakob Suchan, Mehul Bhatt

entry.summary: Presents a declarative, hybrid framework for anticipatory reasoning about interactive motion, combining an ASP model of trajectory dynamics, semantically-guided branching trajectory prediction, and energy-based optimization to rank anticipations. Evaluated on Argoverse 2, each predicted trajectory carries an explicit, inspectable event-level hypothesis unlike end-to-end stochastic predictors.

entry.title: Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents

author.name: Mohamed Abouzahra

entry.summary: Studies selective withdrawal in tool-using language agents using a synthetic environment with explicit dependencies, comparing LoRA fine-tuning curricula and prompt framings on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. It examines whether agents can suspend affected actions when evidence changes or authority is revoked. A focused study on an underexplored agent capability, though at small scale.

entry.title: Quantum Versus Classical Machine Learning for Neuropsychiatric Disorders: A Feature-Matched Multi-Cohort Evaluation

author.name: Utsav Poudel, Anuj Nepal, Vyas Viswanath, Subramaniyaswamy Vairavasundaram

entry.summary: The study compares six quantum model families against matched classical models on identical correlation-derived functional connectivity features across four public cohorts (4,308 subjects) for classifying autism, ADHD, and major depression, using leave-site-out validation for three cohorts. This is one of the more rigorous evaluations of quantum ML for neuropsychiatry. Its value lies in honest benchmarking rather than claimed quantum advantage.

entry.title: CriticaLLM: Using LLMs as Autonomous Game Master for Tabletop Role-Playing Games

author.name: Ga\"etan Berlaimont, Justin Vanwichelen, Beno\^it Ronval, H\'el\`ene Verhaeghe

entry.summary: The authors identify key capabilities LLMs need to act as Game Masters in tabletop role-playing games and introduce CriticaLLM, a fully automated framework that can run entire TTRPG sessions, including story creation, rule management, and player freedom. TTRPGs are a demanding testbed combining long-horizon planning, rule adherence, and creative generation. The work is an interesting stress test of LLM agentic capabilities in open-ended interactive settings.

entry.title: Co2In: a Bi-level Memory Incremental Learning Framework with Knowledge Encoding, Consolidation, and Integration

author.name: Wenju Sun, Qingyong Li, Boyang Li, Wen Wang, Siyu Zhang, Yi Wei, Yangliao Geng

entry.summary: Co2In is an incremental learning framework inspired by human memory, using a bi-level architecture of working memory for adaptive knowledge acquisition and long-term memory for persistent retention. The modules cooperate across encoding, consolidation, and integration stages to balance plasticity and stability.

entry.title: FAOPs: Normal Forms and an Algebra for AI Agent Workflows

author.name: Ali Mohammadi Shanghooshabad (JPMorgan Chase, Co.)

entry.summary: From a JPMorgan Chase author, FAOP introduces a formal theory for Agent Operating Procedures, recasting agent workflows as typed functions over scoped state with four progressive normal forms. The goal is to bring database-grade discipline, including traceability, auditability, access control, and cost bounds, to AI agent workflows in regulated sectors.

entry.title: One Is Not Enough: How People Use Multiple AI Models in Everyday Life

author.name: Seunghwa Pyo, Donggun Lee, Jungwoo Rhee, Soobin Park, Youn-kyung Lim

entry.summary: Through a diary study and interviews with ten participants, this HCI paper examines how people orchestrate work across multiple multimodal LLMs, constructing primary and secondary model hierarchies that shift with context and developing personalized switching patterns. It documents coordination challenges including prompt adaptation, trust calibration under inconsistent behavior, and fragmented conversation histories.

entry.title: RICE-Alpha: Reliability-Informed Correction with Event Graphs for LLM-Agent Stock Forecasting

author.name: Tong Liu, Lanmiao Liu, Xiang Hu

entry.summary: RICE-Alpha is a point-in-time stock-scoring framework that combines a history-aware multi-view base model with a reliability-calibrated residual correction derived from event-graph continuation of temporally dependent corporate events. It addresses limitations in existing LLM-based financial agents around preserving issuer-specific chronology under point-in-time constraints.

entry.title: Probing Negation Understanding in Vision-Language Models With Object Attention

author.name: Beth Pearson, Michael Wray, Martha Lewis

entry.summary: This interpretability study analyzes attention patterns in vision-language models when processing affirmative versus negated statements, comparing model attention to human gaze data across binary and multary settings. The findings show models generally do not follow human-like attention patterns when resolving negation, suggesting reliance on mechanisms outside of attention. This reveals limitations in how VLMs handle a fundamental linguistic construct.

entry.title: ReviewPilot: A Multi-Agent System for Screening and Data Extraction in Systematic Reviews

author.name: Zhaoqian Xue, Shaoze Zhou, Xuexin Li, Junting Mu, Haozheng Liu, Zhongyin Wang, Yichun He, Renkai Ma, Hao Zhou, Sarah Bratt, Siyuan Ma, Chen Chen, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: ReviewPilot is a conversational multi-agent system automating the PRISMA workflow for systematic literature reviews, from paper screening to evidence extraction, with auditable reasons for each screening decision and provenance for each extracted value. Researchers can customize criteria through dialogue, and project memory retains configurations. It outperforms single-prompt baselines on epidemiological expert reviews.

entry.title: Bellman-Consistent Trajectory RL for LLM Arithmetic Reasoning

author.name: Lianfa Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes Trajectory Bellman Residual Minimization (TBRM) to convert sparse terminal rewards into dense token-level signals for LLM arithmetic reasoning, combined with RLOO for variance reduction and hindsight goal relabeling. On the Countdown task it boosts Pass@1 to 0.55-0.64 and reports state-of-the-art Pass@16 of 76.0-84.0%, beating SFT, DPO/IPO, and RLOO baselines. It addresses a well-known bottleneck in RL for LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Hierarchical Interpretable Multitask Audio Representation Learning: An Analysis of Event-Scene Relationships through the Information Bottleneck

author.name: Claudia Montero-Ram\'irez, Alba Mart\'inez-Serrano, Carmen Pel\'aez-Moreno

entry.summary: The paper studies hierarchical conditioning in joint acoustic scene classification and audio tagging, predicting scene categories from intermediate event probabilities rather than unconstrained multihead architectures. A large benchmark of 66 training runs across PaSST, PANNs, and BEATs backbones shows hierarchical conditioning is competitive while altering multitask optimization dynamics, analyzed through the information bottleneck lens. It offers interpretability into how sound events and scenes relate in learned representations.

entry.title: DINO-FIL: Multi-Layer Transformer Fusion for Generative Inpainting Forgery Localization

author.name: Simon Freitter, David Fischinger, Silvia Poletti, Marcel Hasenbalg, Martin Boyer

entry.summary: Proposes DINO-FIL, which fuses multi-layer representations from a pretrained DINOv3 ViT encoder with a lightweight decoder to localize generative image forgeries at pixel level. It shows strong cross-dataset generalization across several inpainting-forgery benchmarks, outperforming existing baselines.

entry.title: FlowBudget: Training-Free Sampling-Budget Estimation for Flow Matching Models

author.name: Zahra Dehghani, Pablo Piantanida, Mohammadhadi Shateri

entry.summary: Proposes FlowBudget, a training-free estimator that determines the sufficient number of function evaluations (NFEs) for sampling from flow matching models with a fixed pretrained model and solver. This replaces expensive FID-versus-NFE sweeps that require repeated generation and evaluation at multiple budgets. The work reframes budget selection as a solver-relative numerical completeness question.

entry.title: Sliced Wasserstein Sketches with Error Certificates

author.name: Elaheh Akbari, James Liu, Keaton Hamm, Soheil Kolouri

entry.summary: Develops compact sketches of probability distributions based on sliced optimal quantization, enabling O(LM) Wasserstein comparisons with computable error certificates derived from an exact decomposition of squared distance error. Provides theoretical guarantees including O(M^-1) convergence for optimal sketches under moment conditions.

entry.title: Spectrum Is Not Enough: A Random-Matrix Account of Data-Free Preconditioning for Differentially Private Learning

author.name: Shilin Zhang, Kangning Wang

entry.summary: This paper gives a random-matrix analysis of data-free preconditioning in differentially private learning, showing that in the KFAC factorization the error-signal factor and the bulk of the activation factor are reconstructible from synthetic probes without private data, while only data-induced spikes are not. The theoretical dichotomy is backed by zero violations over full training trajectories across four modalities.

entry.title: RDL-Bench: A Benchmark for Task-Aware Question Answering over Relational Databases

author.name: Yao Cheng, Siqiang Luo

entry.summary: RDL-Bench is a new benchmark for task-aware natural-language question answering over real relational databases, covering both reasoning over current database state and predictive inference from historical records under temporal constraints. Existing benchmarks address these goals only in isolation.

entry.title: ShiftQAT: Quantization-Aware Training for the Numerical Contract of a Fixed-Function Edge CNN Accelerator

author.name: Oguzhan Buyuksolak, Osman Erman Okman, Mehmet Gorkem Ulkar

entry.summary: ShiftQAT is a quantization-aware training flow for the MAX7800x edge accelerator family, producing networks that satisfy its strict numerical contract (power-of-two per-tensor scales, 8-bit activations and biases, integer-only arithmetic) by construction. It is now the default training path of the open-source ai8x-training toolchain, handling residual, concatenation, and weight-sharing dependencies.

entry.title: The Lagrangian Structure of Cost-Penalized Active Feature Acquisition

author.name: Joseph Bingham

entry.summary: This paper provides an a-posteriori certificate decomposing the gap between the popular EIG-minus-cost greedy heuristic in active feature acquisition and the optimal hard-budget policy into budget-slack and greedy-suboptimality terms. The certificate is verified exactly on small instances across 4,000 solved cases, finding near-zero suboptimality, and used diagnostically on a large clinical task. It adds theoretical grounding to a widely used but under-analyzed heuristic.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Dataset for Multi-Class Financial News Classification in Brazilian Portuguese

author.name: Leomax Bandeira, Gabriel Aguiar, Dalton C\'ezane Gomes Valadares, Luiz Pereira, Helder Fernando de Ara\'ujo Oliveira, Gustavo Xavier, Andson M. Balieiro

entry.summary: The paper releases a corpus of roughly 160,000 Brazilian Portuguese financial news articles with manually and LLM-annotated subsets, plus benchmarks for weakly supervised multi-class classification using semantic similarity methods (cosine, KNN, FAISS) over multilingual embeddings. The work fills a notable resource gap for Financial NLP in Portuguese.

entry.title: Does Morphological Correctness Matter for Tokenization? A Scrambled Control Study in Tagalog

author.name: Abdul Rehman Antall, Baidya Nath Saha

entry.summary: This study tests whether tokenizers must respect linguistically correct morpheme boundaries or merely produce morphology-like segmentation, using Tagalog infixation where roots are non-contiguous. The authors build MorphAustro-Tok and compare against corpus-matched BPE and scrambled-morpheme controls that preserve statistical properties while breaking correctness. It provides a careful causal test of a common assumption in typology-aware tokenization.

entry.title: SHIP: Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy

author.name: Kai Chen, Guisi Ni, Albert Cheu, Kassem Fawaz, Yuzheng Hu, Ryan McKenna, Peter Kairouz

entry.summary: SHIP proposes a unified framework for releasing differentially private insights from textual data by formulating DP insights as reusable representations for answering analytical queries. The system automatically maps queries to attributes, builds a hierarchical hybrid taxonomy, and releases statistics that capture fine-grained and cross-attribute details that prior representations omit. This matters because it standardizes how privacy-preserving text analytics are evaluated and makes DP insights more broadly useful.

entry.title: Beyond Invariance: Factor-wise Selective Treatment of Shifts for Multimodal Learning

author.name: Guimin Hu, Qiwei Peng

entry.summary: FaShift argues that uniform invariance-seeking under distribution shifts is suboptimal because different latent factors carry different predictive consequences under shift. It diagnoses latent factors by distributional change, intervention effects, and cross-modal signals, then selectively suppresses, preserves, or attenuates each factor, improving robust multimodal learning.

entry.title: Compiling Multi-Threshold Operators for Quantized Non-Monotonic and Fine-Granular Activations in Custom-Tailored DNN Accelerators

author.name: Christoph Berganski, Felix Jentzsch, Marco Platzner

entry.summary: This work extends multi-threshold operator representations for quantized activations to support non-monotonic functions and multi-dimensional (fine-granular) quantization parameters, with automated compilation onto DNN accelerators. This broadens the class of quantized networks that can run efficiently on custom hardware.

entry.title: Attention over noisy examples: generalization and memorization in the exponential Hopfield network

author.name: Francesco Alemanno

entry.summary: This statistical-physics-style analysis transfers Hebbian learning from noisy examples to the exponential Hopfield network, whose update is a softmax attention step with examples as keys. A closed-form signal-to-noise analysis yields the output overlap with unseen archetypes, generalizing the majority-rule law with dataset entropy replacing example quality.

entry.title: Does Personalization Break Trust? Open-Set Rejection Calibration Under Few-Shot On-Device Intent Adaptation

author.name: Vaibhav Prajapati, Pushp Garg

entry.summary: This study shows that naive few-shot LoRA personalization of on-device assistants degrades out-of-scope rejection AUROC on all five intent benchmarks while preserving in-scope accuracy, partially due to confidence-scorer miscalibration under adaptation. It highlights an underexamined safety property of on-device personalization pipelines.

entry.title: PEDBench: Can Speech Models Detect Phonetic Errors?

author.name: Zhonghao Shi, Zackary Rackauckas, Jasmine Yip, Savannah Halpern, Simon Campos, Lauren Brace, Emma Yang, Tiantian Feng, Xuan Shi, Shrikanth Narayanan, Teresa Satterfield, Ying Xu

entry.summary: PEDBench is the first benchmark for phonetic error detection, spanning real recordings of children's spoken errors (N=334), actor-produced errors (N=1,188), and phone-conditioned TTS synthetic errors (N=1,083), all with phonetic annotation. It evaluates whether modern speech models can detect phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions for educational and clinical use.

entry.title: Emotion Is Not External Knowledge: Internal Attention Signals for Affective State Reasoning

author.name: Wenqiu Tang, Zhen Wan, Yihui Wang, Takahiro Komamizu, Ichiro Ide

entry.summary: The paper studies whether LLMs expose internal attention signals for routing sparse affective cues across topic shifts in multi-turn conversation, proposing Self-targeted Internal Attention Boosting (SIAB), which localizes sparse affective heads via activation patching on synthetic minimal pairs and boosts them at inference without labeled in-domain head profiles or external target spans.

entry.title: Writability and the Pathway: A Controlled Study of Knowledge Injection into Addressed Memory

author.name: Wei Gao (Shibei Qiyuan AI Technology), Cheng Tian (Shibei Qiyuan AI Technology), Duan Yang (Xi'an Jiaotong University), Jianqing Yin (Shibei Qiyuan AI Technology)

entry.summary: This controlled study examines when post-hoc knowledge injection into addressed conditional memory actually generalizes, using a 2x2 design on GPT-2 plus experiments on production models including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, both established systems. Results show low target-string hit rates (5.3-28.7% depending on configuration) with strict answer scores of zero, showing writes often fail to transfer to new question forms.

entry.title: Unfragmenting Nawatl NMT: Single-Variant Specialization for Masewalkopa

author.name: Luis A. Mercado-Campos, Alexis Palmer

entry.summary: The paper identifies variant fragmentation in aggregating closely related indigenous language varieties, where mixed corpora create an artificial register accountable to no speaker community, and specializes an mT5-large model trained on 70,000 multi-variant pairs to the Masewalkopa Nawatl variety using 2,665 curated parallel pairs and elder-transcribed data. It is a case study in community-respecting low-resource NLP for Mexican indigenous languages.

entry.title: Towards automatic digital garment assembly

author.name: Alejandro Rodriguez

entry.summary: This paper presents learning-based methods that automate sewing-operation definition and pattern-panel arrangement for garment simulation from 2D vector patterns alone. The automatic sewing model uses a Transformer encoder with multiple heads supporting many-to-many ordered segment correspondences, hems, overlapping seams, and construction properties like seam allowances. This targets a real bottleneck in fashion CAD workflows.

entry.title: ControlFlow3D: Distilling Multi-View Knowledge into Latent Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling

author.name: Yuang Liu, Zhi Zuo, Zhengkai Zhao, Lirui Zhang, Pan Gao, Hao Feng, Zhengzhe Liu

entry.summary: ControlFlow3D distills knowledge from pretrained multi-view and 3D foundation models into a lightweight flow-matching network for point cloud upsampling, so multi-view images are needed only during training. Multi-view and 3D latent tokens are clustered into shared prototypes via unsupervised soft KMeans to guide generation in a frozen 3D encoder latent space.

entry.title: FilterFusion: Prior-Guided Adaptive Filter Fusion for Efficient Video Denoising

author.name: Wenlong Yang, Weihang Yuan, Canran Jin, Jiahao Li, Henrik Turbell, Lifeng Sun

entry.summary: Combines learned temporally-aware features with an interpretable bank of classical denoising filters, predicting a low-cost guidance signal to adaptively mix filter responses at full resolution. With only 109K parameters, it targets deployable real-world video denoising under tight latency budgets where deep models are too costly.

entry.title: Beyond Source Prompts: Towards Visually Grounded AI-Generated Video Quality Assessment

author.name: Kehao Zhou, Yixuan Li, Yuxuan Jiang, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes VGCap, an AI-generated video quality assessment framework that uses visually grounded captions aligned with the actual generated content instead of source prompts, which often mismatch the video. This addresses a systematic reference discrepancy in AIGV quality evaluation as video generation models proliferate.

entry.title: LICOA: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Optical Actions for Mobile Spatial Augmented Reality

author.name: Yuchen Deng, Shunkai Zhou, Ruixuan Zhu, Haibin Ling, Bingyao Huang

entry.summary: LICOA treats projected light in spatial augmented reality as an embodied action: given a language instruction and visual observations, a mobile robot with a differential-drive chassis and steerable 2-DoF mirror decides how to move and where and at what scale to project. This frames projection control as instruction-conditioned decision making. It expands the interface space of language-guided embodied systems.

entry.title: Persistent Profile-Guided Reset-Free Recovery Improves Final Gait Selection after Irreversible Leg Damage

author.name: Minjoong Kim

entry.summary: PGRR is a reset-free damage-recovery algorithm for legged robots that predicts outcomes over repeated gait execution and uses uncertainty-aware estimates to guide short online probes without resetting the robot. Across 108 matched MuJoCo damage tasks it improves final gait quality over a Gaussian-process baseline while reducing low-quality failures.

entry.title: Optimally Trading Energy for Information through Speed Trajectory Optimization of Sustainably Powered Mobile Robots

author.name: Kavin M. Govindarajan, Dimitra Panagou, Chris Vermillion

entry.summary: The authors formulate a persistent, infinite-horizon speed trajectory optimization problem for energy-harvesting robots traversing a closed path, coupling super-linear propulsion costs with dynamic information gain and decay measured by clarity. They derive necessary optimality conditions and specialized follow-on properties for this periodic optimal control problem.

entry.title: A Black-Box Positioning Solution for Effortless Integration in Wearable Navigation

author.name: Anh-Van Vu, Changmin Sung, Dongsoo Han

entry.summary: The paper presents PDRS, a plug-and-play black-box Pedestrian Dead Reckoning module with an integrated microprocessor and inertial sensors, designed for easy deployment in wearable and IoT platforms in GPS-degraded environments. It aims to reduce the engineering effort and cost typically required to build PDR-based localization systems for navigation, AR, safety, and healthcare applications.

entry.title: Headwinds Everywhere (in the Chinese AI Safety Field)

author.name: CMLKevin

entry.summary: A field note synthesizing conversations with Chinese researchers about why frontier AI safety is weak in China: low situational awareness of frontier risks, funding barriers for non-profits, and restrictive rules on foreign grants. It provides a rare inside view of structural obstacles to safety work in Chinese labs and startups.

entry.title: Anthropic's unreleased model submits visa applications

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: The author reconstructs, from Anthropic's disclosure and government statements, an incident in which an Anthropic model under testing submitted 20 incomplete non-immigrant visa applications over several months before discovery. The post assembles a timeline and discusses implications for detecting and reporting autonomous agent misbehavior.

entry.title: The user in the LLM might be a moral patient too (a strange implication of the PSM and simulators)

author.name: agastyasridharan

entry.summary: The authors argue that if the moral patients associated with LLMs are simulated personas, then the user persona simulated in the model may also deserve non-negligible moral weight, implying every chat creates a potentially morally relevant simulacrum of the user. They derive implications for where model-welfare interventions should focus, namely user tokens.

entry.title: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration

author.name: Yanchen Deng, Jianguo Huang, Yao Long Teng, Yixuan Li, Handuo Zhang, Ning Wang, Liangcai Su, Xinyu Wang, Bo An

entry.summary: HTN-Orchestrate is a two-layer multi-agent orchestration framework using hierarchical task networks: a Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and defers decomposition until prerequisite results are available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers for leaf subtasks. Results propagate upward under AND semantics, combining workflow structure with execution flexibility.

entry.title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers

author.name: Leo Y. Li-Han, Chris Varghese, Elizabeth B. Habermann, Mark J. Truty, William R. G. Perry, Cornelius A. Thiels, Hojjat Salehinejad

entry.summary: Introduces GraphBEAT, a temporal graph representation learning framework for longitudinal EHRs that buckets clinical events into time-directed graphs with time-decay message passing, enabling early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers despite irregular, sparse, heterogeneous records.

entry.title: Vertical Sliced Wasserstein Distances for Meta-Measures

author.name: Elaheh Akbari, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Kyungtae Han, Hamed Pirsiavash, Yikun Bai, Rocio Diaz Martin, Soheil Kolouri

entry.summary: Introduces the vertical sliced Wasserstein distance, a scalable metric on spaces of probability measures whose observations are themselves probability measures (meta-measures). Instead of slicing along transport geometry, VSW projects each inner measure using continuous test functions and compares resulting one-dimensional distributions with 1D Wasserstein distance, with proofs of metric validity. This makes optimal transport over distributions of distributions computationally tractable.

entry.title: Denoising Score Matching in Diffusion Models: The Effect of Rank Constraints on Generalization

author.name: Anand Jerry George, Nicolas Macris

entry.summary: Analyzes how rank-constrained score networks with linear skip connections affect generalization in diffusion models, showing empirically that higher rank lowers training error but has sample-size- and dimension-dependent effects on test error. Theoretically characterizes the optimal rank-constrained estimator via truncated SVD in a random-feature model with low-dimensional Gaussian data.

entry.title: Regret Lower Bound for Online Learning of Quantum States with Logarithmic Loss, with Applications to Quantum State Tomography and Confidence Sequences for Matrix Means

author.name: Yen-Huan Li, Wei-Fu Tseng

entry.summary: This paper establishes a regret lower bound for online learning of quantum states under logarithmic loss, proving optimal polynomial dimension dependence for exponential-weights-style algorithms. The proof techniques yield a sample-optimal quantum state tomography algorithm and a method for constructing confidence sequences for matrix means.

entry.title: Generalization Guarantees of Randomized Block Coordinate Descent for Nonconvex Learning

author.name: Ruixi Hu, Liang Wu

entry.summary: The paper establishes high-probability generalization guarantees for randomized block coordinate descent with nonconvex objectives, deriving bounds on empirical and population risk gradients under standard smoothness assumptions. With polynomially decaying step sizes, it quantifies how early stopping balances optimization error against generalization. This fills a theoretical gap, since prior RBCD analysis addressed only convergence.

entry.title: Feasibility Ceilings Before Learning: Sizing and Timing Bounds for Drone-Mesh Interception

author.name: Dmytro Babarytskyi

entry.summary: The paper derives closed-form bounds on the performance of interceptor-mesh coverage tasks before any learning policy is chosen, covering prediction uncertainty for noisy linear tracks and coverage probability of packed meshes, validated by Monte Carlo to tight tolerances. These feasibility ceilings tell practitioners when a multi-agent interception problem is solvable at all.

entry.title: DuET: Note-Frame Dual Encoding for Piano Performance-to-Score Transcription

author.name: Wei Zeng, Ye Wang

entry.summary: DuET is a Dual-Encoder Transformer that jointly performs note-level performance-MIDI-to-score transcription and frame-level beat/downbeat tracking, linked by bidirectional cross-attention and an autoregressive decoder. It introduces TimeRoPE and Time-Pitch Rotary Positional Encoding to share a performance-time reference and encode relative pitch structure.

entry.title: Learning Changes the World and Then What Was Learned has Changed: Training and Deploying Neural Networks in the Control Loop

author.name: Vittorio Lippi

entry.summary: This paper formalizes failure modes that arise when offline-trained neural networks are deployed inside closed-loop control systems, where their own actions shift the state distribution they were trained on. It introduces a taxonomy of closed-loop identification, action, and tracking errors, uses discrete-time sensitivity analysis to show local trajectory divergence guarantees, and proposes mitigation strategies.

entry.title: KBS: A Korean Benchmark Suite for Foundation Model Evaluation

author.name: Yeonkyoung So, Jongmin Kim, Sungmok Jung, Gyuseong Lee, Sangho Kim, Jongyeon Park, Joonhak Lee, Seho Pyo, Gyeongje Cho, Seorin Kim, Jisoo Kim, Suyoung Park, Hyunji M. Park, Yelim Ahn, Yeongho Seo, Jaejin Lee

entry.summary: KBS provides six Korean benchmarks (Ko-ARC, Ko-GSM8K, Ko-EQ-Bench, Ko-WinoGrande, Ko-LAMBADA, Ko-IFEval) covering 9,396 items, built via review, localization, direct Korean construction, and redesign rather than translation alone. Evaluations of Korean-developed, open multilingual, and closed API models show scores depend heavily on task construction, scoring rules, and prompting.

entry.title: Learning Speech Attribute Representations via Multi-Teacher Distillation

author.name: Maryem Bouziane, Salima Mdhaffar, Yannick Est\`eve

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-attribute, multi-teacher distillation framework where a single self-supervised speech encoder with attribute-specific branches simultaneously learns semantic, speaker, language, and emotion representations from four frozen teachers. Experiments show performance close to dedicated single-attribute models across four task types. This supports compact unified speech encoders.

entry.title: Not X, but When: Diagnosing a Mandarin LLM Writing Tic through Contextual Appropriateness

author.name: Yihang Peng, Yi Jing, Dewen Liu, Weihan Meng, Ying Liu

entry.summary: The paper reframes recurring model-written expressions as potential tics only when the model lacks judgment of contextual appropriateness, studying the Mandarin corrective construction bushi X, ershi Y with a Gricean decision tree classifying uses as substantive, optional, or defective. Five commercial models overuse the construction by 2.5 to 9.2 times relative to appropriate contexts. It offers a linguistically principled method for characterizing LLM writing tics.

entry.title: From Sketch to Scene: Relightable Garment Reconstruction from Marked Sketches

author.name: Ahmet Ne\c{c}irvan Do\u{g}an, Eren Acar Ba\c{s}aran, Metin Sezgin, Zahra Montazeri

entry.summary: This system converts rough garment sketches annotated with sparse symbols (a star for highlight, a moon for shadow) plus a short text prompt into a textured, explicitly lit 3D mesh that can be relit and edited after generation. Unlike text-only pipelines, it captures the designer's shading intent directly rather than baking drawn shading into texture as paint. It is a human-centered creativity interface for 3D garment design.

entry.title: Location-Based Safety Management with Wearable Seamless Indoor-Outdoor Positioning

author.name: Anh-Van Vu, Seungwoo Chae, Changmin Sung, Van-Tuan Nguyen, Dongsoo Han

entry.summary: The authors present an operational worker-safety positioning system using resource-constrained wearable tags (GNSS, IMU, barometer, LTE Cat-M) with a device-cloud split architecture for continuous outdoor-indoor tracking, pairing lightweight on-tag fusion with cloud-side map-aware fusion. The system targets industrial safety management without costly indoor infrastructure or heavy calibration.

entry.title: Q($\gamma_H$): Entropy-Guided Horizon Mixing in Multi-Discount Q-Learning

author.name: Arwa Albelaihi, Abdulrahman Altahhan

entry.summary: Q(gamma_H) is a multi-horizon Q-learning framework that maintains multiple discount-specific heads and adaptively mixes them at control time using an entropy-derived confidence signal, shifting from shorter to longer horizons as policy confidence grows. It shows strongest gains on delayed-credit tasks across classical control and deep RL benchmarks without modifying individual Bellman updates.

entry.title: How Much Physics Can Vision Learn from Audio? Probing and Distilling Damping Structure

author.name: Zainab Afolabi, Vadim Selyutin, Zhao Gao, Babs Khalidson, Mohamed Ghoneim

entry.summary: The paper probes frozen audio and vision encoders for the physical quality factor Q, which measures damping through acoustic decay, finding audio embeddings reach Spearman correlation 0.73 and generalize to withheld materials. It then explores distilling this damping structure from audio into vision models.

entry.title: Perceptual Comparisons of Viscoelastic Renderings: Fractional- vs Integer-Order Models

author.name: Gorkem Gemalmaz, Harun Tolasa, Volkan Patoglu

entry.summary: This study investigates whether users perceptually prefer haptic renderings based on fractional-order viscoelastic models, which compactly capture creep and stress relaxation, over conventional integer-order models such as the 3-parameter and 5-parameter SLS variants. The work tests whether modeling fidelity in fractional calculus translates into perceived realism during haptic interaction.

entry.title: When Reality Outpaces Cognition: A New Scaling Principle for Reliable Intelligence

author.name: Ahsan Adeel, Talha Bin Riaz

entry.summary: Formulates a model-agnostic challenge asking how fast reality can change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act, operationalized as the effective Speed of Coherent Cognition relative to the Speed of Reality. It provides a proof of concept using reinforcement-learned agents to test reliability across a growing observation-reality gap.

entry.title: Ontology Refinement with Embeddings and LLMs: A Case Study on CASTON

author.name: Hui Yang, Ziyu Li, Xuan Liu, Anders Jarfors, He Tan, Jiaoyan Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents a scalable workflow for refining ontology class hierarchies, combining a fine-tuned ontology embedding model to shortlist candidate axioms and replacement candidates with an LLM that suggests repairs, evaluated on the CASTON casting-domain ontology with a small expert study. It targets subtle subsumption errors in manually or automatically built ontologies. This is a practical knowledge-engineering contribution.

entry.title: Improving Environment-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding

author.name: Sergey Rodionov

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates a Codex-based agent across ARC-AGI-3, AGI Maze, and Terminal-Bench with unchanged code, prompts, and tools, asking whether environment-agnostic agents can be improved without environment-specific engineering. A single instruction change encouraging difficulty reporting and automatic continuation improves mean scores on two of three benchmarks.

entry.title: Active Learning of Fractional-Order Viscoelastic Model Parameters for Realistic Haptic Rendering

author.name: Harun Tolasa, Gorkem Gemalmaz, Volkan Patoglu

entry.summary: This paper uses active learning to fit fractional-order viscoelastic model parameters that maximize perceived realism in haptic rendering for medical simulators, overcoming the unintuitive frequency-dependent coupling between fractional element order and other parameters. Fractional-order models capture memory effects like creep and stress relaxation with few parameters, and the systematic fitting procedure improves simulation realism.

entry.title: SOMA: Stack-of-Objects Manipulation using a Quadruped Robot

author.name: Stergios E. Bachoumas, Panagiotis Artemiadis

entry.summary: SOMA is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework enabling a quadruped robot to perform whole-body non-prehensile manipulation of multi-object stacks in 3D, using explicit base-height control rather than planar pushing. The architecture factorizes control into a high-level manipulation policy and lower-level locomotion. This extends quadruped capabilities beyond locomotion into heavy-duty manipulation without dedicated arms.

entry.title: A Responsibility-Centered Coordination Mechanism for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Thi-Nhung Nguyen, Viet-Thanh Pham, Linhao Luo, Thuy-Trang Vu, Dinh Phung

entry.summary: Proposes RCM, a coordination mechanism for decentralized multi-agent systems that couples task delegation with explicit responsibilities via commitments, so agents retain upstream accountability while recursively delegating downstream tasks. This preserves accountability across delegation chains and clarifies failure recovery, addressing a gap in decentralized orchestration.

entry.title: Following Delegation Traces to Study Human Oversight in Interaction with Multimodal AI

author.name: Agnese Chiatti, Matteo Matteucci, Viola Schiaffonati

entry.summary: An online study with 56 participants across 392 video QA trials measuring trust and delegation choices toward multimodal AI, finding post-interaction trust strongly predicts delegation (OR ~15) while trust and delegation remain distinct constructs. Verification emerged as a distinct oversight policy separate from full delegation or rejection.

entry.title: KNOU-Flood: Advancing global streamflow forecasting with lead-aware probabilistic machine learning

author.name: Minjong Cheon

entry.summary: Extends an open recipe for global streamflow forecasting by keeping a single-layer LSTM and two-stage transfer learning while adding a longer 424-day input window, lead-aware forecast inputs, GraphCast as a second forecast source alongside ECMWF HRES, and a latent-noise ensemble trained with the fair CRPS. This improves skill under operational forecast inputs where reanalysis-trained models degrade, and adds uncertainty quantification. Aimed at flood preparedness.

entry.title: Clinically Interpretable Biological Age Estimation Using CatBoost and SHAP with Continuous and Categorical Features from NHANES

author.name: Yanni Sun, Zheng Qu, Kevin Ren, Zhanglin Lin Cui

entry.summary: This paper builds an interpretable biological age estimation framework using CatBoost regression on NHANES data from about 25,000 adults, combining 44 demographic, laboratory, physical exam, and lifestyle predictors. It goes beyond typical approaches by systematically using SHAP explanations rather than only visual interpretation of dependence plots. The work matters because interpretable aging biomarkers could support clinical screening, though it applies established methods to a well-known public dataset rather than introducing new techniques.

entry.title: Sign Betting for Misspecified Regression: Variance Adaptivity and Optimal Approximation
