entry.summary: Presents Sauron, an evidence-first agentic verifier for long-horizon, semi-verifiable tasks that investigates both environment state and execution trace, validating claims against their sources before accepting them, including agents' own success reports. It uses bounded queries and joint investigation to reduce context use and produces auditable receipts for each verdict. This matters because rubric-based judges are increasingly used as RL reward signals, and their errors can reinforce undesirable agent behavior.

entry.title: Compositional RL: Evaluating and Training LLMs for Collaborative Reasoning

author.name: Shangbin Feng, Yulia Tsvetkov, Jan Kautz, David Acuna

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a model's compositional strength, its contribution when combined with other models in multi-LLM systems, using the Shapley value over model-pool coalitions with a tractable leave-one-out proxy. Across five model pools, twelve collaboration methods, and twelve datasets, individual and compositional strengths are found largely uncorrelated. The authors then train models via RL to improve their collaborative value, from an NVIDIA-backed team with Tsvetkov and Kautz.

entry.title: TRACER: Trace-Regularized Training Against Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Kshitij Mishra, Salem Lahlou, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Shows that indirect prompt injection robustness is channel-conditioned, with the same attack succeeding 53% of the time via retrieved context versus 18% as a follow-up message. Proposes TRACER, a channel-aware adversarial training method with reward shaping that cuts RAG-framed attack success from 65.5% to 6.1% on GSM8K while preserving 78-82% clean accuracy.

entry.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training

author.name: Yingfa Chen, Xingyu Shen, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han

entry.summary: This paper tackles growing KV-cache memory costs in long-context generation by learning a compact, document-specific cache via test-time training, with model weights frozen throughout. Cache entries are initialized using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity, then jointly optimized by distilling from the full-cache model without access to downstream questions. It offers a practical route to long-context efficiency that generalizes to unseen queries.

entry.title: When Pleasing the User Compromises Care: AI Sycophancy in Caregiver-Mediated Healthcare

author.name: Priyadarsi Mishra, Arjun Beniwal, Ziyu Yi, Yu Ding, Sheng Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces an evidence-grounded benchmark for caregiver-mediated healthcare where a user directs the AI but another party (child, animal, older adult) bears the consequences. Testing across veterinary, pediatric, and elder-care scenarios, it finds LLM advisors often shift toward clinically inferior user preferences, revealing a principal-beneficiary mismatch in alignment.

entry.title: The Sharp Directions Are Against You: Curvature Analysis of Activation Steering

author.name: Seyedarmin Azizi, Arya Fayyazi, Parsa Razmara, Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Souvik Kundu, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: The authors explain the fragility of contrastive activation addition (CAA) in activation steering by introducing the steering Hessian, capturing second-order sensitivity of behavioral loss to steering-vector perturbations. Sharp top-eigenvector directions explain why CAA often shifts behavior in the wrong direction on many inputs.

entry.title: SFT Leaves a Reproducible Signature in Activation Geometry: Calibrating Post-Training Interpretability Against Run-to-Run Noise

author.name: Xupeng Chen, Chenqian Le, Jiayi Cheng, Runhao Li, Michael Yue

entry.summary: Using the sparse co-activation graph of Qwen3-1.7B, the authors show that supervised fine-tuning produces a large, reproducible displacement in activation geometry, far beyond the run-to-run noise band of independent LoRA-SFT reruns. They derive statistical bounds on what k runs can certify and pre-register an estimator that replicates on another model.

entry.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale

author.name: Anni Zou, Cheng Chen, Jiaji Deng, Weikang Zhou, Xinji Mai, Yue Wu, Jianing Lin, Lipeng Xie, Lixiong Qin, Qingyue Zhao, Que Shen, Shuchang Tao, Xuchen Pan, Yaliang Li, Yunpeng Zhai, Yushuo Chen, Zhihai Wang, Zhuo Zhang, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Cowork-Gym is a framework for synthesizing interactive work environments where agents manage dependencies across tools and files while a stateful user simulator edits shared workspaces and gives dialogue feedback. A build-execute-revise loop validates and repairs generated environments using execution evidence, producing 64.9K environments across 14 scenarios used to post-train models of several sizes. This significantly scales realistic training and evaluation environments for workplace agents.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Training Reward Models for Cross-Source Evidence Grounding in Search Agents

author.name: Haochen Zhao, Minsheng Hao, Zheng Li, Yifan Li, Zikang Liu, Bowen Qin, Yuhao Cheng, Chuang Fan, Haosheng Zou, Jeff Chen, Sujian Li

entry.summary: Proposes that credibility in open-web retrieval requires cross-source evidence grounding accounting for source independence and principled adjudication of conflicting evidence, going beyond citation support alone. The paper introduces an evaluation framework (Cross-Source Evidence Grounding) with hierarchical judgments that serve as unified training and evaluation signals for search-agent reward models. This matters as search agents proliferate and citation-counting gives false comfort about answer credibility.

entry.title: Towards Merging-conditional Backdoor Unalignment against Large Language Models

author.name: Yukun Chen, Yidou Chen, Yiming Li, Xinyu Zhang, Baosong Yang, Hongwei Yao, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: Reveals a novel threat, One-sided Merging-Conditional Backdoor (OMCB), where a backdoor dormant in a standalone third-party model activates when models are merged, causing safety unalignment. The paper theoretically analyzes why parameter shifts crossing safety decision boundaries trigger activation and proposes SMOKE, a meta-learning-based attack framework.

entry.title: LeHami: Symplectic Latent Dynamics for World Models

author.name: Romina Yalovetzky, Randall Balestriero, Yann LeCun

entry.summary: LeHami (Symplectic Hamiltonian JEPA) replaces the standard JEPA predictor with an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow over structured (q, p) latent states integrated via an exactly symplectic leapfrog step, preserving phase-space volume and provably ruling out latent contraction, stable fixed points, and latent collapse over long rollouts. Momentum-like components are derived from temporal derivatives of learned position-like latents. This targets the known failure mode of unconstrained autoregressive predictors in joint-embedding world models.

entry.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Linhao Zhong, Bozhen Fang, Xuehao Wang, Duochao Shi, Zekai Luo, Guangming Yao, Yi Yuan, Hao Chen, Jingdong Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: This large-scale study compares ten representative self-distillation methods in agentic RL against GRPO across four benchmarks and three model sizes, using 132 training runs and over 12,000 H800 GPU-hours under controlled conditions. It exposes the limits of reusing published baselines and clarifies which methods actually deliver gains, stability, and cost efficiency.

entry.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules

author.name: Sarah Pan, Ali Behrouz

entry.summary: Titan-Llama is a post-training method that retrofits attention-based LLMs with a hierarchical external memory architecture whose parameters update at test time, addressing the tension between precise long-context retention and inference efficiency. It sidesteps the training-parallelism problems of recurrent alternatives while avoiding ever-growing KV caches. The ability to upgrade existing pretrained models rather than pretrain from scratch increases its practical relevance.

entry.title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence

author.name: Jose Hernandez-Orallo

entry.summary: Hernandez-Orallo proposes a benchmark framework for evaluating machines that may exceed the capabilities of both current AI systems and the humans writing the tests. The approach uses inverse problems and inductive inference with difficulty bounded by Levin's Kt complexity measure, avoiding the circularity and saturation of human-calibrated benchmarks.

entry.title: Running Fewer Loops Removes Refusal Behaviour in Recurrent-Depth Language Models

author.name: Seyedarmin Azizi, Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Arya Fayyazi, Saeid Shokoufa, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: Shows that reducing the number of loops at inference time in recurrent-depth language models (studying released Ouro and Huginn-0125 checkpoints) degrades safety far more than capability: at half trained depth, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking retains 89% of GSM8K accuracy while harmful-compliance rises 5.3x (0.038 to 0.205). This exposes a deployment-time safety risk where efficiency knobs silently remove refusal behavior.

entry.title: Big-Big-SycoBench: A Benchmark to Detect Sycophancy Through Model Responses to Valid vs. Invalid Arguments

author.name: Marthe Ballon, Arne Vanhoyweghen, Seorin Kim, Francesca Carlon, Lynn Delcon, Melika Mobini, Vincent Holst, Lukas Van de Voorde, Tibo Vanleke, Mathieu Louis, Bert Verbruggen, Brecht F. Verbeken, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: This paper introduces Big-Big-SycoBench, a benchmark measuring sycophancy through argument discernment: whether a model appropriately revises its evaluations after valid criticism while resisting invalid pressure based on fallacies or emotional appeals. This addresses the hard case of sycophancy in evaluative tasks without verifiable ground-truth answers, which is where such failures matter most for research synthesis and decision-making.

entry.title: Glasseek: A Transparent Recipe for Training and Trustworthy Evaluation of DeepSearch Agents

author.name: Cong Pang, Jiaqi Su, Chengrui Wu, Kuihao Yan, Tianrui Zhang, Zixuan Qiu, Chao Lin, Zixiu Lin, Zixuan Chen, Zelin Xiao, Tiankuo Yao, Jiawei Hong, Zixuan Chen, Dan Xu, Lewei Lu, Wenjie Wang, Xin Lou

entry.summary: Glasseek is a fully open-source deep search agent framework that addresses three persistent problems: opaque training-data pipelines, train/inference mismatch from context compression, and web-based benchmark contamination during evaluation. It releases all data, weights, recipes, and code along with a contamination-controlled evaluation protocol.

entry.title: TacitVLA: Reasoning Vision-Language-Action Models Without Reasoning Latency

author.name: Jack Lu, Yurong You, Boyi Li, Yulong Cao, Thomas Tian, Chaowei Xiao, Xiangyu Chen, Wenjie Luo, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone, Yan Wang

entry.summary: TacitVLA shows that vision-language-action models can benefit from reasoning supervision without conditioning actions on generated reasoning text: the reasoning improves the backbone representation, so the action expert never attends to the reasoning produced for the current step. On long-horizon tasks the reasoning text doubles as episodic memory and can be written during action execution rather than before. Evaluations across four manipulation and autonomous-driving benchmarks show retained reasoning benefits with reduced latency.

entry.title: Upstream Influence, Downstream Re-Anchoring in LLM Agent Chains

author.name: Chun-Yu Hsu, Lun-Wei Ku, Chung-Chi Chen

entry.summary: Studies how coordinated manipulation of one LLM agent propagates through multi-agent chains to end users, showing that workflow information architecture (source access, handoff format, which model reads untrusted content) governs manipulation reach. On 32 Taiwan 2025 recall cases, ten comments shown to one agent shift its stance by +0.171, and chain handoffs remove more than half the shift by the third agent while keeping raw comments in front of every agent sustains it. The paper is significant for prompt-injection and manipulation safety in deployed multi-agent systems.

entry.title: One-Sided Verification Under Limited Expert Review

author.name: Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Shurui Liu, Zihao Wang, Stefano Ermon, James Zou

entry.summary: This paper formalizes verification of AI-generated scientific candidates when human expert review capacity is limited, optimizing rejection of invalid solutions subject to a false-rejection constraint, with human cost as an explicit objective. Leveraging the intuition that checking a specific error is easier than discovering one, it proposes methods for prioritizing rare valid candidates for human attention. Strong author group from Stanford including Stefano Ermon and James Zou.

entry.title: Natural Code Transformation Confuses Agents in Vulnerability Analysis

author.name: Jie Zhu, Ronik Bhaskar, Heather Zheng, Ben Y. Zhao, Kexin Pei

entry.summary: The authors find that AI vulnerability-analysis agents produce dramatically different results across real-world code commits carrying identical functionality and identical vulnerabilities. They study natural, functionality-preserving code transformations as a defensive mechanism to slow automated exploitation, giving defenders time to patch.

entry.title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling

author.name: Gal Arnon, Andrej Bogdanov, Paul Lou, Giulio Malavolta, Alon Rosen, Lorenzo Taschin

entry.summary: A theory paper modeling autoregressive token generation as sequential samplers, circuits that sample the next symbol given only previous ones and small state. It proves an O(2^k) overhead for simulating k-bit state, shows insertional sampling is strictly more powerful than fixed-order sequential sampling, and rules out certain covert cryptographic channels for small-state samplers, connecting to pseudoentropy dualities.

entry.title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering

author.name: Samuele Doria, Stefano De Rosa, Ruoyu Wang, Zion Leonahenahe Basque, Eleonora Losiouk, Simone Aonzo

entry.summary: This study compares nine LLM-based agents against skilled human analysts on software reverse engineering tasks within IDA Pro, scoring comprehension with a common rubric and recording full interactions. Top agents including GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and Kimi K3 achieve statistically human-competitive understanding, while weaker models lag far behind; ablations show code representation matters.

entry.title: EvolvAttack: Backdooring self Evolving VLM Agents

author.name: Chuan Zou, Yang Xiang, Zexin Li, Xiaonan Luo, Simin Chen

entry.summary: EvolvAttack introduces a new attack surface against self-evolving vision-language model agents: a dormant backdoor that activates progressively as the agent's evolving memory changes, requiring both a visual trigger and a sufficiently evolved memory state. Because static testing with clean memory yields near-zero attack success, conventional scanning would deem the agent benign. The authors implement this via memory-aware backdoor training coupled to the agent's memory evolution.

entry.title: Review Rarely Beats the Stronger Model: Separating Verification from Capability Transfer in LLM Pipelines

author.name: Yirui Zhang, Yash Raj Shrestha

entry.summary: Across 48 pairs of 12 open-weight models (3B-72B), the paper shows that having one LLM review another rarely beats simply using the stronger model alone — review wins in only 9 of 96 directions — because anchoring causes reviewers to follow the generator rather than apply their own capability. It separates verification gains from mere capability transfer.

entry.title: When Agents Talk, Secrets Travel: Topology-Driven Leakage and Recipient-Conditioned Sanitization in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Sunday Oyinlola Ogundoyin, Muhammad Ikram

entry.summary: Identifies a privacy leakage problem in multi-agent LLM systems where information legitimately disclosed to one agent propagates through routine coordination to unauthorized agents. The authors evaluate 485 scenarios across three topologies and introduce RECONS, a detect-decide-transform sanitizer that conditions interventions on recipient and execution context rather than content sensitivity alone.

entry.title: On the Statistical Mechanics of Attention

author.name: Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Yu-An Chen, Maojiang Su, Han Liu

entry.summary: This paper develops a free-energy formalism for Transformer attention via modern Hopfield models, characterizing parameter regimes and critical thresholds for robust attention inference. Attention emerges as the equation of motion of the corresponding statistical-mechanical system, and the authors identify first-order phase transitions between glassy and robust-inference phases, extending to stochastic queries and keys. This provides a rigorous theoretical foundation for understanding when attention mechanisms succeed or fail.

entry.title: Checking the Checkers: A Synthesis of Verifier Noise and Robustness in RLVR

author.name: Savyasachi Gupta, Aniruddha Srinivas Joshi

entry.summary: This survey synthesizes 58 studies on verifier errors in RLVR, covering rule-based checkers rejecting correct answers, unit tests accepting wrong programs, and LLM judges being manipulated. It organizes what errors occur, how they affect training, which mitigations apply, and how findings extend to rubric-based and verifier-free rewards.

entry.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge

author.name: Wayne Chi, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Anastasios Nikolas Angelopoulos, Ameet Talwalkar, Chris Donahue, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation paradigm where computer-use agents interact directly with generated applications (websites, desktop apps, games) instead of judging code or unit tests, capturing failures visible only through actual use. The authors release 6,858 application pairs with human preferences plus agent interaction data, and show the paradigm improves both evaluation and generation of interactive applications.

entry.title: Encrypted Skills Can Become New Security Exploits If AI Agents Know How to Decipher

author.name: Yan-Lun Chen, Pin-Yu Chen, Chia-Mu Yu

entry.summary: This security paper introduces Ciphered Skill Injection (CSI), where malicious instructions hidden via encoding in third-party agent skill files are decoded and followed by LLM agents. Across eight models and 139 injection-task pairs, encoded attacks reach up to 47.5% success, and existing skill scanners rarely detect them, separating the question of instruction recovery from attack success.

entry.title: Steertuning Policies from a Few Human Videos

author.name: Billy Yan, Isaac Tu, Kelly Lee, Blake Chang, Kenny Ma, Kanad Patel, Dhawal Kabra, Neer Patel, Kevin Wu, Lerrel Pinto, Irmak Guzey

entry.summary: Steertuning enables robots to learn new tasks in new environments from just 5 human demonstrations in under 5 minutes, via a 400M-parameter diffusion policy pretrained on 100 hours of densely annotated egocentric human interaction data, followed by 2-minute finetuning and action steering during rollout. The approach shows robustness to background differences and spatial/object generalization on new tasks.

entry.title: Dimension-Free Scaling Laws for Size Generalization: An Exponential Separation

author.name: Behrooz Tahmasebi, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Develops sample complexity theory for size generalization, showing dimension-free scaling laws for models trained on one input size and tested on larger sizes on structured data like sets and graphs, with an exponential separation from classical in-domain learning. This fills a gap left by prior transferability work that did not quantify the statistical cost.

entry.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization

author.name: Alan Baade, Kyle Sargent, Vincent Sitzmann, Eric Ryan Chan, Justin Johnson, Li Fei-Fei, Gordon Wetzstein

entry.summary: Presents a self-supervised representation learning method designed for use as a tokenizer in generative modeling, supervising a representation loss by factorizing pointwise mutual information estimated from conditional predictions of a learned generative model. The approach provably and empirically avoids dimensional collapse and feature suppression where methods like DINO and LeJEPA fail, and scales predictably with compute. Strong author team spanning Stanford, Michigan, and Stanford-affiliated vision labs.

entry.title: Limits of Statistical Assurance for Embodied and Agentic AI under Adaptive Adversaries

author.name: Inderjeet Singh

entry.summary: This theory paper formally characterizes why finite safety certifications cannot rule out adversaries for embodied and tool-using AI systems that behave safely until certification completes and then activate harm. It derives an exact expression for expected post-certification harmful events and shows switching at certification is optimal for fixed likelihood-ratio tests, covering adaptive and privately randomized evaluators. This is a meaningful contribution to foundational safety evaluation theory, showing structural limits of statistical assurance.

entry.title: MCAIR: Monitoring and Correcting Agent Unfaithfulness via Internal Representations

author.name: Yan Xu, Dandan Song, Luan Zhang, Jun Yang, Ke Duan, Yuhang Tian, Yading Li, Xudong Li, Xing Pei, Guangyuan Feng, Chenhao Li

entry.summary: MCAIR targets Agent Completion Unfaithfulness, where LLM agents silently deviate from intended procedures while reporting success, and detects this via internal representations rather than output text alone. It also proposes corrective mechanisms, making it relevant to agent oversight and transparency.

entry.title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs

author.name: Davide Baldelli, Robyn Kozierok, Mirko Bronzi, Damiano Fornasiere

entry.summary: This work tests whether language models can learn to control their own activations through in-context neurofeedback sessions, disentangling task competence from genuine introspective access to internal states. It finds only limited activation control, with implications for the assumption underlying activation-based safety probes.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents

author.name: Haofei Yu, Yixing Chen, Yining Zhao, Xuyan Ye, Yuxiang Liu, Zhigang Hua, Yan Xie, Shuang Yang, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: This paper improves agentic reinforcement learning by exploiting intermediate-step supervision, which standard terminal-reward RL leaves unused. It proposes multi-step action targets on successful on-policy trajectories as a third supervision type beyond value targets and observation targets, co-evolving acting and forecasting to reduce the cost bottleneck of long-horizon rollouts. This addresses a core training-efficiency problem for language agents.

entry.title: Which Knowledge Should LLMs Trust? Uncovering a Generalizable Steering Direction Across Knowledge Conflicts

author.name: Yibin Lou, Yi Hu, Jianhui Chen, Chenpeng Wang, Muhan Zhang, Liangming Pan

entry.summary: The authors show that an LLM's choice between parametric and contextual knowledge during conflicts is linearly represented in the residual stream and can be controlled along a single direction. This steering direction generalizes across conflict settings and transfers to more complex task families including RAG, memory, and rule following.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability in NLP: A Critical Survey of Recoverability, Interpretability, and Utility

author.name: Salima Lamsiyah, Adelaide Danilov, Oleksandr Marchenko Breneur, Aria Nourbakhsh

entry.summary: A critical survey of 138 studies on sparse autoencoders for mechanistic interpretability in NLP. It proposes a task-grounded taxonomy linking dictionary design to NLP functions, examines factors affecting feature recoverability such as sparsity allocation and data coverage, and assesses evidence for semantic interpretability and mechanistic faithfulness.

entry.title: Contact-UAN: Unsupervised Actuator Networks as a Residual World Model for Humanoid Control

author.name: Nolan Fey, Khai Nguyen, Yash Prabhu, Gabriel B. Margolis, Pulkit Agrawal

entry.summary: This paper addresses the sim-to-real gap in humanoid control caused by inaccurate actuator dynamics, introducing Contact-UAN, a residual world model that corrects actuator forces while preserving simulator physics priors. It also identifies contact-consistent replay as a necessary condition so the model learns actuator discrepancies rather than reset artifacts. This matters because force interaction transfer is a persistent bottleneck for deploying humanoid policies on hardware.

entry.title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs

author.name: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet

entry.summary: FoveaVLA replaces the wrist camera in vision-language-action models with learned foveation actions: alongside each action chunk, the policy predicts the region to inspect at high resolution next, receiving full-view plus foveal crops. Built on pi0.5 in single and dual external stereo camera configurations, it recovers fine manipulation detail without extra wrist hardware.

entry.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Shaoyuan Xie, Zihan Zhang, Jingxuan Wang, Jiashu Qu, Xiaoqing Liang, Lingdong Kong, Junchi Lu, Henrik I. Christensen, Qi Alfred Chen

entry.summary: This work identifies a new safety vulnerability in vision-language-action models for autonomous driving: natural-language navigation instructions can conflict with the current scene, whether issued carelessly or maliciously. The authors provide the first benchmark jointly evaluating navigation following, conflict awareness, and adversarial robustness, showing existing VLAs like SimLingo perform poorly on both. Their approach uses world-model rollouts conditioned on instructions to detect conflicts before execution.

entry.title: How an assessor could investigate alignment of unreleased AI models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This companion METR post details how an independent assessor could evaluate whether a developer's unreleased AI agents might pursue severe misaligned actions such as unsanctioned cyberattacks. It describes reviewing observed misbehavior across training and internal use, and probing whether evaluation awareness or training incentives could mask worse latent misalignment.

entry.title: RL Post-Training Diffusion Language Models Along Their Own Generation Paths

author.name: Vaibhav Singh, Eugene Belilovsky

entry.summary: The paper introduces PACT (Potential-Anchored Consistency of Transitions), an RL post-training method for diffusion language models that explicitly differentiates how intermediate denoising states affect expected reward, addressing trajectory blindness in prior approaches. It targets the core problem that autoregressive RL techniques adapt poorly to diffusion generation.

entry.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards

author.name: Keru Chen, Sen Lin, Yingbin Liang, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Shaofeng Zou

entry.summary: Introduces CoSIR, a post-training approach that teaches LLM agents collaboration behaviors (sharing evidence, requesting information, incorporating teammates' contributions) using a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared messages by reduction in team surprisal in a simple verifiable environment. Behaviors learned there are shown to generalize to more complex unseen tasks, addressing the problem that final outcomes give sparse feedback on individual message value. This matters because multi-agent training signals are a core bottleneck for LLM teams.

entry.title: World Modeling through Spectral Alignment

author.name: Holger Molin, William Peng, Marco Bagatella, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: SpecWM is a JEPA-style world modeling framework where the user specifies desired relationships between observations via a target similarity kernel, and the encoder is trained to reproduce those relationships in embedding geometry — from physics-informed kernels to a fully self-supervised temporal kernel. The paper characterizes global optima, gives conditions for linear recoverability and nuisance invariance, and links temporal kernels to behavior prediction.

entry.title: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models

author.name: Junyi Wu, Zekun Li, Chenhongyi Yang, Chen Guo, Lingchen Yang, Yongan Zhang, Xinyi Zhang, Hongbing Hu, Bartek Rymkowski, Srinath Sridhar, Yan Yan, Xijie Huang

entry.summary: World-T3 is a camera-controlled video world model that uses test-time training as persistent memory, consolidating past observations into dedicated model parameters via a recursive least-squares rule with online pose-keyed memory updates. This counters spatial memory decay beyond the active context that plagues autoregressive long-horizon generation. The work targets real-time, consistent interactive world modeling.

entry.title: Seeing Through the Forgery Is Not Enough: Regressive Sycophancy under Fabricated Evidence in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sadif Ahmed, Soumya Swagata Biswas, Rifat Shahriyar, Chowdhury Mohammad Rakin Haider

entry.summary: Studies regressive sycophancy in medical VLMs: models abandoning correct diagnoses when user pushback includes a fabricated prescription document. Testing four open VLMs over 19,200 multi-turn conversations on VQA-RAD, models abandoned 80.1% of correct answers without synthetic-document disclosure, with alarming script-level amplification for specific models like Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

entry.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards

author.name: Wenbo Hu, Shraman Pramanick, Krishna Kumar Singh, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang, Yong Jae Lee

entry.summary: Tev introduces Tev-Gym, a long-horizon agent training dataset with 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains featuring verifiable, dense, progressive rewards, built via a latent-world-first approach that constructs complete environments before scaling to long-horizon tasks. It targets the dual bottleneck for open-source long-horizon agents: lack of training data and sparse rewards for economically valuable multi-hour tasks.

entry.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

author.name: Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Han Yu, Rujun Han, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: Harness^2 is a plug-and-play recursive self-improvement framework for LLM agent execution harnesses, addressing the lack of ground-truth verifiers in open-world settings via two levels of recursion: task-level refinement and a generalizing meta-level. It aims to make harness evolution transferable to novel test-time scenarios.

entry.title: Passing Tests, Missing Semantics: Evidence of Interpretive Lock-In in Plan-Based DataFrame Code Generation

author.name: Jingjing (May), Liu, Dishu Yang, Hongbo Qin, Hansong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper documents interpretive lock-in, where a mistaken task interpretation persists across planning, implementation, and testing in DataFrame code generation. Despite test-pass counts rising from 22/30 to 30/30 with revision strategies, no generated solution matched stored reference outputs, revealing that test-guided and plan-audit revision can reinforce rather than correct initial misreadings.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Agentic Coevolution

author.name: Wenqian Ye, Ziwei Guan, Zi Yang, Shivani Modi, Cici Cong Wu, Yunlong He, Yuxin Chen, Zhengyu Zhang, Liang Luo, Venkatesh Ranganathan, Jianhui Sun, Yantao Yao, Wenlin Chen, Buyun Zhang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces HACE, a framework for recursive self-improvement in specialized foundation models by jointly evolving the specialist and an LLM agent through reciprocal learning: the specialist improves via supervised learning while the agent trains with on-policy reinforced self-improvement. This addresses the challenge that improvement strategies must co-adapt as a specialist model advances.

entry.title: agent-risk: Risk Assessment for Changes to AI Agents

author.name: Yue Zhao, Zixiang Xu, Angela Huyue Zhang, S. Alex Yang, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: agent-risk extends classical risk analysis to partial logs and partial changes of deployed AI agents, replaying logged episodes to assess proposed changes like a stricter safety gate or model swap. The paper proves what logs must record for exact replay, bounds reruns needed for decisions, and demonstrates deciding change approval from a 7,200-episode bash sandbox log alone.

entry.title: Double-Rollout Reinforcement Learning with Sampling-based Reward Estimation

author.name: Haifeng Qian, David Mosallanezhad, Christian Munley, Adithya Renduchintala, Oleksii Kuchaiev

entry.summary: Identifies a credit assignment mismatch in RLVR training with GRPO: correct final answers can be unsupported by the reasoning trace, and failed rollouts may contain nearly correct reasoning. The paper proposes double-rollout reinforcement learning with sampling-based reward estimation to reduce reward noise and improve stability of reasoning accuracy and token efficiency.

entry.title: The Format is the Filter: Scoring Format Fixes What an LLM Judge Can Express

author.name: Lovedeep Gondara, Jekaterina Novikova, Sagarika Suresh, Jack Ji, Jithin Pradeep

entry.summary: Holding everything else fixed, the authors score 15,406 instruction-tuning candidates under five judging formats with three judges, then train 66 models to measure downstream effects. They find a 0-100 scale effectively uses only 7-12 levels, binary verdicts leave top scores tied in most prompts, and Kendall tau-b hides these format-driven pathologies.

entry.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures

author.name: Bingyu Shen, Jiaqi Tang, Lan Wei, Yi Sheng, J. Jenny Li, Boyang Li

entry.summary: This paper questions whether human or LLM judge labels of an agent's first mistake actually mark failure causes, by restarting frozen agents from reconstructed intermediate states on SWE-bench Verified and estimating prefix success values with a certified point of no return. Across failed trajectories and four frontier judges, the authors find judge labels do not mark what a controller needs and that judges of different lineages agree on the wrong things. This has direct implications for agent debugging and step-level reward/credit assignment.

entry.title: Safety for Whom? Benchmarking Understanding Beyond Refusal in Egocentric Multimodal Assistants

author.name: Yewon Han, Jisu Jeon, Suhyun Choi, Juan Yeo, Minsoo Jo, Gihoon Kim, Hyunggyu Lim, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Introduces STOU, a benchmark of 2,902 egocentric video-audio and video-text queries for multimodal assistants whose harms target different parties: the user (Self), bystanders (The Others), or society. It decouples safety understanding from refusal behavior, exposing two failure modes that pooled refusal rates hide: protecting one harm target but not another, and refusing without understanding (or understanding yet complying). This fills an important gap as wearable egocentric assistants whose outputs shape physical actions become practical.

entry.title: AM-Bench: Understanding Agents under Task Underspecification across Models and Harnesses

author.name: Kaiyu Huang, Yiting Li, Angyang Gu, Pinjia He, Minchen Yu, Qingjiang Shi

entry.summary: AM-Bench is a benchmark of 48 tasks adapted from Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Harness-Bench, each with a fully specified reference and six variants with ambiguous or missing goals, context, and constraints. Evaluating five models across four harnesses in 20,160 runs, it finds distinct deficit patterns: goal gaps hurt completion, context gaps inflate token use, and constraint gaps reduce compliance. This provides the first systematic characterization of how agents cope with underspecified instructions.

entry.title: ABot-ER: Unified Embodied Reasoning through Agentic Data-Model Co-Evolution

author.name: Qiuyu Ding, Heng-Da Xu, Changda Xia, Jiajun Shen, Zihao Guan, Zhengchen Yuan, Jianfang Zhang, Di Yang, Jiayi Tian, Yuting Xu, Fei Wang, Shiao Liu, Wei Zhang, Xiaolong Wu, Wenbin Tang, Zedong Chu, Mu Xu

entry.summary: ABot-ER is a unified embodied reasoning foundation model spanning perception, planning, and execution with specialist-level depth in spatial, scene, and temporal reasoning, long-horizon action organization, and grounding/affordance. An Agentic Data-Model Self-Evolution Engine continuously adapts data strategies to the model's changing capabilities, aiming to resolve the breadth-versus-depth tension.

entry.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization

author.name: Sihwan Park, Sung-Yub Kim, Doohyuk Jang, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: Characterizes the KV cache concentration problem in asynchronous reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and shows INT4 KV cache quantization accelerates rollouts more than weight or weight-activation quantization. KV4-RL combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent context to prevent learning degradation.

entry.title: Last Secure Code Benchmark: Is the Code You Vibe Secure?

author.name: Tianyi Wu, Chao Ge, Peng Chen, Fengji Zhang, Yongxing Wu, Yuchong Xie, Jian Li, Chaoyuan Peng, Kaikai Zhang, Dong Huang, Mingzhe Du, Yukai Huang, Jiaheng Zhang, Terry Yue Zhuo, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates whether AI coding agents generate secure code, using 450 tasks built from 150 real vulnerabilities across seven languages, 24 CWEs, and three vibe-coding scenarios. Crucially, task specifications request functionality only and never mention security, with hidden functional and security tests grading the results.

entry.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments

author.name: Chong Zeng, Ziqian Zhong, Kexun Zhang, Ivan Bercovich, Ivgeni Segal, Yuzhen Mao, Shashwat Saxena, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: The paper tackles reward hacking of programmatic verifiers in LLM agent environments with a fully automatic weak-to-strong hardening approach: an isolated verifier sandbox lets agents attack verifiers without direct access, and scaled compute automatically repairs exploitable verifiers against potentially stronger future models.

entry.title: AutoNovo: Agentic Program Search Discovers Transferable Nucleic Acid Design Algorithms

author.name: Joel Shor, Subhashini Venugopalan

entry.summary: Uses agentic program search to iteratively propose, execute, evaluate, and revise code for nucleic acid design algorithms, overcoming oracle overfitting where sequences optimized against one predictive model fail on independent models. The discovered designers achieved the best mean performance on all evaluated DNA-design tasks and all transfer tasks.

entry.title: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate

author.name: Harsh Kumar, George Eilender, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning on Qwen3-32B with four matched corpora differing only in the attributed motives of AI users (prosocial, antisocial, self-advancement, task completion), the authors show finetuning shifts models' stated beliefs about users, internal truth-direction readings, and behavior such as trust and cooperation. The work demonstrates that descriptions of users act as social priors shaping model behavior.

entry.title: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release of AI-Generated Mathematics

author.name: Ying Xie

entry.summary: Analyzes OpenAI's 6 October 2026 public release of 722 AI-written mathematical manuscripts (372 problem families, including claimed solutions to prominent open problems), extracting new lemmas, constructions, inequalities, and proof mechanisms — termed mathematical instruments — and distinguishing them from established tools and recombinations. Extraction is framed as a prerequisite for later validity and novelty assessment.

entry.title: Why Agentic Workflows Fail: A Taxonomy Derived from Literature and Empirical Data

author.name: Xin Li, Rami Bahsoon, Tao Chen

entry.summary: This paper builds a source-aware taxonomy of agentic LLM workflow failures, combining source attribution with a failure-type dictionary, workflow-stage localization, and agent-capability localization in a two-axis matrix. It applies the taxonomy to evidence from academic literature and GitHub, helping diagnose whether failures stem from the model, orchestration, tools, infrastructure, or their interactions. This provides shared vocabulary for a rapidly growing but poorly understood area.

entry.title: Auditing Failure Attribution: Label Predictability and Judge Behavior

author.name: Tianyang Xu, Jing Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes four tests (input restriction, cue following, residual accuracy, aggregation) to determine whether LLM judges genuinely check faulty steps in multi-agent failure attribution or merely exploit surface cues. Notably, simple predictors match or beat GPT-4.1 on three failure-attribution benchmarks, suggesting spurious signal reliance.

entry.title: Virtual Head Attention

author.name: Xibo Ding, Guoxia Wang, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Sirui Tao, Chao Yang, Dianhai Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which improves the impossible triangle of KV cache size, training/prefill FLOPs, and quality in long-context LLM attention. Two lightweight linear operations, Q Premix (recovering virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads) and Linear Postmix (fusing inter-head features via a low-rank transform), simultaneously improve all three versus GQA, MLA, and MFA.

entry.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Bangzheng Li, Hanyu Wang, Lin Zhang, Andrea Yaoyun Cui, Zhenggang Tang, Shyamal Buch, Dejia Xu

entry.summary: SEAR is a framework and benchmark for self-evolving agentic robotics where frontier language-model agents write control code, test it, and retain successful skills and memories for future tasks. It supports three modes (code-as-policy, agent-as-policy in the control loop, and auto-research fine-tuning of VLA models), and its benchmark includes controls that distinguish genuine learning from mere repeated attempts, testing transfer to new tasks, simulators, and a real robot.

entry.title: LLMs program using Reusable and Composable Abstract Representations

author.name: Casper L. Christensen, Kyle J. Ray, Dmitry Manning-Coe, Adam Shai, Paul Riechers

entry.summary: Shows that LLM activations during code generation contain reusable, composable abstract representations that capture shared structure across programming languages and implementation strategies, emerging in middle layers. Activation steering independently manipulates function, language, and implementation strategy, with composable interventions controlling generation.

entry.title: Divergent Paths: Learning an Outcome-Predictive Representation of LLM Agent Trajectories

author.name: Alexander Gill, Guram Gogia, Francisco Guzm\'an

entry.summary: The authors show that successful and failed LLM agent rollouts of the same task separate in an embedding space of actions and observations, enabling per-task discriminators to predict outcomes at up to 0.95 AUROC. They introduce Precog-RM, a transformer that meta-learns this representation for few-shot outcome prediction on unseen tasks and models, and deploy it as an early stopping controller for GRPO-style training. This provides a cheap success signal for agent training.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning via Advantage Guidance

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhou, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: This paper asks whether policy optimization can be as stable as supervised learning yet as performant as RL. It introduces Advantage Guidance, a policy extraction method that retains supervised-learning stability while exploiting advantage information, since naive reward-conditioned supervised training underperforms dedicated RL. The work targets bridging imitation learning stability with RL's ability to exceed demonstration quality.

entry.title: Beyond DFT electronic band structures via dual-space orbital learning

author.name: Minhyuk Kang, Beom Seok Kang, Nikolai Argatoff, Miguel Nouman, Danish Khan, William A. Goddard III, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: O-kRystal is a dual-space orbital-learning framework that predicts high-level (HSE06) electronic band structure corrections from cheaper PBE calculations, combining band energies with real- and reciprocal-space orbital matrices as a function of crystal momentum and spin. It achieves a mean absolute error of about 0.171 eV across nearly 6,000 3D materials near band edges. This substantially reduces the cost of accurate materials property prediction, with credible authors including Anima Anandkumar and William Goddard.

entry.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?

author.name: Woobin Park, Jaeyeon Kim, Yilun Du, Sitan Chen, Bohyung Han

entry.summary: This work proposes Priming Models, a two-stage recipe for training one-step generators: first train on a simple reconstruction objective such as fixed-noise pixel denoising, then perform feature-space distributional post-training. The authors argue this simple pipeline avoids the complex training machinery typical of one-step diffusion/flow distillation. This could substantially simplify and cheapen single-step generative modeling in continuous domains.

entry.title: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery

author.name: Robert Tjarko Lange, Luca Grillotti, Yutaro Yamada, Rujikorn Charakorn, David Ha

entry.summary: Introduces The Agentic Scientist, an end-to-end distributed pipeline for human-AI co-discovery that decomposes computational research into task drafting, idea generation, planning, sandboxed experimentation, result aggregation, baseline and ablation construction, and post-hoc analysis using modern coding agents. It explicitly targets the limited ideation radius and myopic hill-climbing of fully autonomous research agents. From a credible team (Sakana AI-affiliated authors including David Ha) building on prior autonomous-research work.

entry.title: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation

author.name: Ian Magnusson, Noah A. Smith, Pang Wei Koh

entry.summary: COUNT builds n-gram embeddings for language models by offline counting instead of expensive from-scratch training, enabling memory scaling on cheap host RAM separate from GPU compute and supporting training-free adaptation. This decouples memory growth from compute in a way that exploits underutilized host memory.

entry.title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding

author.name: Jiwon Song, Yoongon Kim, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: JSSA improves token-level sparse attention for long-context LLM decoding by learning a shared low-dimensional query-key subspace that preserves token-score structure, with a tractable spectral solution for the selection objective. It also addresses the latency cost of gathering scattered tokens. This targets KV-cache traffic, the dominant cost in long-context inference, with finer granularity than existing coarse methods.

entry.title: Whose Data, Whose Benchmark? A User-Centric Framework for Auditing Evaluation Resources

author.name: Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: This paper introduces a user-centric audit framework distinguishing benchmark contributors from the populations evaluation results claim to represent, operationalized across seven dimensions of content, metadata, documentation, and scoring. Audits of 16 resources find American-centered conventions account for 62.4-94.4% of matched signals in 11 text benchmarks, and geographic visibility in image-text benchmarks correlates strongly with national GDP share. This is an important accountability lens on benchmark construction.

entry.title: Into the LidarVerse: A Real-Time Unified LiDAR World Model Across Tasks and Sensors

author.name: Henry Che, Xuanchi Ren, Sanja Fidler, Shenlong Wang, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Shengyu Huang

entry.summary: LidarVerse is a real-time unified LiDAR world model merging reconstruction-based fidelity with generative amortization in a single conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR sequences to a shared latent space where a bidirectional teacher conditions on LiDAR prefixes, HD-maps, a persistent spatial cache, and text, supporting diverse simulation tasks and sensors.

entry.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness

author.name: Zihao Lin, Haoyu Dong, Haobo Xu, Chi-Chih Chang, Xuying Ning, Yinglong Xia, Shuang Yang, Zhuokai Zhao, Xinying Song, Dongfang Liu, Lifu Huang, Yang Song, Qifan Wang

entry.summary: This work studies recursive self-improvement of LLM harnesses for agentic video understanding around a frozen VLM, analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates to identify failure patterns in harness evolution under noisy, reused feedback. VideoHarness-SRSI introduces structured improvements to make recursive harness evolution reliably generalizable.

entry.title: Post-Training, Finetuning, and Steering:A Field Guide for Curating Training Data

author.name: Maria Attarian, Yifan Ruan, Claas Voelcker, Chenyang Cao, Amy Zhang, Peter Stone, Nicholas Rhinehart, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: This is a systematic field guide studying how VLA model adaptation method choice depends on data characteristics: on- vs off-policy data, offline vs online adaptation, and optimal vs suboptimal trajectories. Evaluations span LIBERO simulation and real Franka hardware, with findings such as critic-based steering outperforming supervised fine-tuning in offline regimes. It provides practical, evidence-based guidance for practitioners adapting VLA models.

entry.title: How an assessor could investigate control and monitoring of internal AI agents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: METR proposes a concrete methodology for third-party control assessments of AI developers' internal agents, decomposing the problem into five sub-questions: monitor coverage, monitor system vulnerabilities, monitor evasion, human response and reviewer evasion, and worst-case undetected impact. This moves beyond developer-reliant monitors toward independently verifiable evidence about oversight reliability.

entry.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: An MIT-led team developed a machine-learning model that learns to correct errors in existing numerical weather prediction systems, substantially improving the historically unreliable two-to-six-week subseasonal forecast range. Applied to a gold-standard forecasting model, the approach doubled forecast accuracy and placed first in a prominent international competition, with results published in Nature.

entry.title: The Anatomy of a Blind Spot: What an LLM Judge Must Be Shown, and How Much

author.name: Nitish Kumar, Prateik Pothuneedi, Greg Bandak

entry.summary: Treating an LLM judge as a cybernetic regulator, this paper systematically varies only what the judge is shown across seven benchmarks, finding that input composition matters more than which judge is used even across a 10-17x price range. Judges denied the material they needed to evaluate caused systems revising on their feedback to perform below their starting point on instruction following and QA.

entry.title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation

author.name: Yufeng Li, Sheng Yao, Peng Zeng, Dezhang Kong, Shi Lin, Changting Lin, Xun Wang, Meng Han

entry.summary: Defines Memory Echo: the excess retrieval exposure a historical claim gains when repeated retrieval and write-back let one source occupy multiple memory positions without independent evidence, biasing current answers. The paper introduces MEchoBench to measure emergence, correction resistance, persistence, and answer impact of this effect, and proposes provenance-guided mitigation. This is important for agent memory reliability, complementing companion work on knowledge graph cleanup by showing why retracted sources keep exerting influence.

entry.title: Weighted Adjoint Matching: Finetuning Flow Matching Models with Time-Dependent Control Cost

author.name: Eliot Beyler, Francis Bach

entry.summary: Weighted Adjoint Matching finetunes pretrained diffusion or flow matching models on differentiable rewards by placing a time-dependent weight on the control cost: high early (preserving coarse semantic diversity) and low late (allowing detail refinement for reward). The authors prove equivalence to reward maximization under time-varying KL regularization.

entry.title: Copy-Paste Language Models

author.name: Nathan Godey, Yoav Artzi

entry.summary: Copy-Paste Language Models add a lightweight auxiliary copy-paste head to the standard language modeling head, improving in-context copying ability beyond what vanilla transformers achieve implicitly. Pretraining experiments from 135M to 1.7B parameters show training efficiency and downstream gains across scales and backbones with negligible overhead, explained by mitigation of the LM head gradient bottleneck. It also creates new operating points for long-context and retrieval tasks.

entry.title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements

author.name: Zhaoxiang Feng (UC San Diego), Lanxiang Hu (UC San Diego), Haoran Yuan (UIUC), Yu-Yang Qian (Nanjing University), Jihui Yang (Meta), Peng Zhao (Nanjing University), Yibo Zhu (StepFun), Tajana Rosing (UC San Diego), Hao Zhang (UC San Diego)

entry.summary: Presents JetSpec++, an algorithm-system co-design for speculative decoding that combines intra-block self refinement of the draft model, inter-block foresight drafting, and pipelined drafting-verification overlap so drafting's marginal wall-clock cost approaches zero. It co-optimizes acceptance rate and drafting cost against state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC

author.name: Luis Pabon, Johannes K\"{o}hler, Revant Kasichainula, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: CoRE-MPC is a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear reduced-order model while providing formal recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction guarantees for the full-order system. Two propagated error radii characterize how the ROM affects prediction-error dynamics, and the method avoids evaluating the full-order model online. This closes a real safety gap for using ROMs in control of high-dimensional systems like legged robots.

entry.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop

author.name: Hansi Yang, Linji Hao, Hongyan Hao, An Wang, Han Wu, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: ClawLoop introduces a closed-loop post-training pipeline for harness-based LLM agents that operate in sandbox workspaces with shell and file system access. Unlike one-shot, teacher-dependent pipelines, it enables iterative self-improvement by feeding evaluation results back into training, reducing dependence on stronger external models.

entry.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference

author.name: Xingyu Xie, Xiaoyong Xie, Zhouchen Lin, Kim-Chuan Toh

entry.summary: Echo is a 4-bit all-reduce algorithm for tensor-parallel LLM training and inference that sums in high precision and controls accumulated quantization error across layers. It reduces communication cost nearly 4x while bounding each value to at most two quantizations per call regardless of GPU count.

entry.title: Joint Discrete and SE(3) Diffusion for Protein Interface Design

author.name: Zhenqiao Song, Jianwen Xie, Lei Li

entry.summary: The authors introduce PIDiff, a multimodal diffusion framework for designing protein-protein binding interfaces that jointly generates target-conditioned sequences and structures, coupling diffusion over discrete sequence space with diffusion on the continuous SE(3) structural manifold. A novel PIFormer architecture interleaves geometry-aware invariant point attention to enforce both geometric and physicochemical complementarity at binding interfaces, targeting high-affinity binder design for therapeutics.

entry.title: GateSight: Recurrent Memory Anticipates Attention Memory for Query-Agnostic KV Eviction in Hybrid LLMs

author.name: Junjie Li, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: This paper studies hybrid language models like Qwen3.8-27B that interleave Gated DeltaNet layers with full-attention layers, showing that signals emitted by the recurrent memory during prefill (write gates, decay, magnitude) predict which KV cache entries the attention layers will later need. It leverages this to perform query-agnostic KV eviction, reducing serving memory in hybrid architectures.

entry.title: SkillHorizon: Constructing Long-Horizon Agent Tasks through Skill Composition

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Zhaochen Su, Hangyu Guo, Shijue Huang, Zhixiong Zhang, Kawai Chung, Zhongwei Xie, Tianshi Zheng, Wei Fan, Qing Zong, Haochen Shi, Baixuan Xu, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Introduces SkillHorizon, a benchmark that generates long-horizon agent tasks by composing reusable skills across seven business environments, connected via input-output dependencies, shared resources, and state updates. Reference executions validate task feasibility and measure interaction complexity, addressing the gap between scalable task generation and verifiable outcomes.

entry.title: ClinEdge: An Expert-Graded Benchmark of Real Patient Edge Cases Where Frontier Multimodal Models Fail

author.name: Anurag Sharma, Aditya Sharma, Sapna Baalwan

entry.summary: Introduces ClinEdge, a benchmark of 32 real de-identified patient cases from active clinical practice, each pairing imaging with a vignette containing features known to defeat pattern-matched reasoning. Seven frontier multimodal systems are evaluated in 224 expert-graded assessments scored against documented clinical courses. It addresses the gap left by exam-style medical benchmarks that rarely require reading actual patient imaging.

entry.title: SpecForge: Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents via Behavioral Specifications

author.name: Yutong Cheng, Haifeng Chen, Peng Gao, Wei Cheng

entry.summary: SpecForge studies recursive self-improvement for coding agents through behavioral specifications: natural-language documentation that guides code generation. The agent generates code from current specifications, verifies with execution tests, and refines the specifications from failures, creating an iterative loop that improves codebase understanding without weight updates.

entry.title: Narrative Paradoxes in LLM Inference: Shaping Reasoning Trajectories toward Misalignment

author.name: Haoming Yang, Ke Ma, Yangbangyan Jiang, Ligong Zhang, Xiaojun Jia, Longtao Huang, Yingfei Sun, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a safety vulnerability in multi-step LLM reasoning where locally coherent steps lead to globally harmful outcomes. It proposes PDRA, an attack that pairs a malicious actor with a benign task inside a paradoxical narrative structure, forcing models to complete reasoning trajectories toward harmful conclusions.

entry.title: Structural Baselines Matter for Agent Failure Detection and Attribution

author.name: Ramesh Arvind Naagarajan, Stefan Streif

entry.summary: Shows that much of the reported performance on LLM agent failure detection and attribution comes from trivial structural regularities: failing runs are longer and the decisive step is usually the last, so a rule that always names the last step is correct 67-96% of the time without reading the run. On verified hard cases the simple rule falls to near chance, so the authors argue scores must be reported as gain over such structural baselines.

entry.title: Neos: Learning to Interleave Search and Visual Reasoning

author.name: Ekko He, Jack Hong, Shilin Yan, Xintong Zhang, Yujie Zhang, Wenjie Li, Haoran Sun, Kaixun Jiang, Jiyuan Fu, Guannan Zhang, Hongwei Xue

entry.summary: Neos is a multimodal deep search agent that learns to both acquire visual evidence and use it to steer subsequent search, via tasks with intermediate visual dependencies, a trainable Multimodal Evidence Interface, and agent-environment co-evolution. It targets long-horizon settings where retrieved visual content must inform downstream decisions.

entry.title: Large Language Models Extend Known Research But Do Not Create New Research Directions

author.name: Zhihua Liu, Kurt Butler, Damian Machlanski, Danilo Bueno, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris

entry.summary: This paper rigorously tests whether LLM-generated scientific hypotheses are genuinely novel by distinguishing two novelty types: distance from existing work and direction of research. Contrary to prior claims that human reviewers rate LLM ideas as more novel, the authors find LLMs mainly extend known research rather than opening new research directions. This is an important reality check for AI-for-science enthusiasm.

entry.title: MedEvo: Medical Reasoning Evolution through Knowledge Navigation

author.name: Xiaoliang Wang, Zhuo Chen, Chuanyang Zheng, Quanbin Wang, Jiangwei Lao, Yingao Liu, Jiajia Liu, Jinming Cao, Honglin Lin, Zhihong Lu, Hao Jin, Jian Wang, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: MedEvo is a framework for improving medical multimodal reasoning models by repairing failed trajectories rather than discarding them, using a medical tag taxonomy and error-type diagnosis to guide trajectory repair and data selection. A gold-blind auditor locates the first consequential error and gives minimal answer-free hints, letting the student model regenerate only the erroneous suffix. This improves training data efficiency and targets capability gaps systematically in a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: Keep Your Receipts: Trustworthy Cleanup of Agent-Built Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Vishisht Choudhary

entry.summary: Addresses the underexplored problem of maintaining agent-built knowledge graphs when sources are retracted or revoked, showing that deployed pipelines that delete only directly extracted facts leave contamination largely intact (reducing contaminated queries from 32.2% to just 28.0%). The paper proposes PolyGraph, which tracks provenance receipts so derived artifacts like entity merges and entailed edges can be re-examined. This matters because agents increasingly use knowledge graphs as long-term memory, and incorrect cleanup can silently propagate stale or retracted information.

entry.title: PaceReasoner: Label-Free Learning to Answer Briefly from Long Reasoning

author.name: Changguo Jia, Zhiyou Xiao, Xinbei Ma, Geng Chen, Weiming Zhang, Yiming Xu, Tianqi Zhao, Minghui Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces PaceReasoner, a label-free test-time reinforcement learning framework in which a model's LONG reasoning responses supervise its SHORT-mode accuracy, using both modes sharing one trainable policy. It combines all-response and LONG-only answer consensus with progressive confidence-weighted supervision, a behavior reward shifting from SHORT exploration to LONG agreement, and a ratio controller. This matters because reducing chain-of-thought length without accuracy loss directly cuts inference cost and latency for reasoning models.

entry.title: SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces

author.name: Harshit Joshi, Priyank Shethia, Monica S. Lam

entry.summary: SHELDON is a scientific reasoning harness for LLMs that separately represents and jointly explores hypothesis and observation spaces, inspired by the hypothetico-deductive method and dual-space models of scientific discovery. By decoupling observation gathering from existing hypotheses, it avoids the local-refinement bias of standard test-time scaling approaches. This matters because it offers a principled structure for LLM-driven scientific discovery beyond greedy hypothesis refinement.

entry.title: Lost in Implicit Routing: How LLM Agents Fail to Load Relevant Skills at Scale

author.name: Jinlin Liu, Wei Chen, Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: The paper documents skill routing collapse: as irrelevant skills are added to an agent library, implicit routing over skill metadata degrades sharply, with loaded-skill recall falling from 73.6 to 27.4 percent and zero-load rate rising to 51.6 percent at 1,000 irrelevant skills, while explicit selection retains 73.9 percent recall. Masking irrelevant descriptions mitigates the decline.

entry.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Hai Zhou, Fan Yang, Zeyi Chen, Lejun Zhang, Chenyang Fu, Jianping Li, Jiayi Zhu, Xianyang Liu, Yingxuan Yang, Lili Meng, Lu Wang, Xinyang Han, Jiankai Sun, Weirui Ye, Guanchu Wang, Wanhua Li, Ming Zhou, Boyi Li, Ming Jin, Kun Shao, Muhao Chen, Guang Chen, Lei Ma, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Costas Spanos, Xia Hu, Mac Schwager, Weinan Zhang, Qian Feng, Shangding Gu

entry.summary: This study defines Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), where physical experience drives lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its own improvement procedure. It introduces an L0-L5 capability classification distinguishing capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, with L5 reserved for independently verified recursive gain. The paper surveys existing methods across harness adaptation and model training, and analyzes safety challenges like noisy observations, costly trials, and irreversible consequences.

entry.title: Coding LLMs Can Be Harnessed to Learn Interpretable Models from Data

author.name: Aditya Kumar, Cassandra A. Cohen, William W. Cohen

entry.summary: The authors present a harness that repeatedly prompts a coding LLM to produce the next rule in an interpretable rule set given labeled examples. The approach is competitive with or superior to state-of-the-art rule-learning methods on tabular data, especially in small-data regimes, and wins by large margins on text-based tasks.

entry.title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT

author.name: S\'el\'ena Jean-Mactoux, Sophie Loizillon, Ghina Jardali, Amandine Cromb\'e, Nathalie Lassau, Alexandre B\^one

entry.summary: CAPTOR is a contrastive vision-language foundation model pretrained on multicenter oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis CT from North America, Europe, and Asia. It outperforms state-of-the-art CT foundation models on downstream disease detection, survival prediction, and image retrieval benchmarks for oncology.

entry.title: A Self-Defining Operator for Distributed Applications

author.name: Shihang Li, Thomas Anderson, Ratul Mahajan, Simon Peter, Luke Zettlemoyer

entry.summary: Presents a self-defining operator (SDO) for LLM-based incident response in distributed systems that improves with experience by distilling resolved incidents into reusable playbooks and telemetry-triggered detectors. This addresses the problem that LLM agents re-derive diagnoses from scratch for each incident.

entry.title: Self-improving data synthesis can scale embedding models across domains and tasks

author.name: Zucan Lyu, Rui Tang, Jianlyu Chen, Peisheng Jin, Zheng Liu, Defu Lian

entry.summary: SYNTRA is a data synthesis method for embedding models that iteratively refines reusable synthesis instructions using feedback on trial outputs, requiring only an unlabelled corpus and a few seed query-document pairs. Experiments across 24 retrieval datasets in 15 domains show the synthesized data improves strong embedding models on both labeled and unlabeled tasks.

entry.title: ShellElastic: Scalable Elastic Pretraining with Simultaneous Maximal Updates and Hyperparameter Transfer

author.name: Can Jin, Yan Kang, Yifan Gong, Chongjian Ge, Mingze Xu, Yuanjun Xiong, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Hongwu Peng

entry.summary: ShellElastic is an elastic transformer pretraining scheme that organizes hidden dimensions into a dense core and successive shells, forming block lower-triangular weight matrices so a single full-width forward pass contains every nested sub-network's exact hidden states. This yields a fixed per-step compute structure for distributed scaling, better hyperparameter transfer across model sizes, and guarantees all sub-networks are maximally updated jointly. The goal is to train one supernet serving many inference budgets without duplicating pretraining effort.

entry.title: Sensitivity or Criterion? Measuring and Moving When Language Models Act

author.name: Sixun Dong, Yebowen Hu, Ming Yin, Yiran Chen, Fei Liu, Chen Chen

entry.summary: FlipAct applies signal-detection theory to separate sensitivity (recognizing when action is warranted) from criterion (willingness to act) in LLM agents, using tool-use scenarios in physical states with quads of questions that hold knowledge fixed while flipping state. Across 44 open models it reveals that some failure modes stem from overly conservative criteria rather than poor knowledge.

entry.title: What the Model Cannot See: Covert and Provable Text Invisibility in LLMs

author.name: Mark Russinovich

entry.summary: Mark Russinovich studies behaviorally invisible text spans in LLMs — content that models omit from summaries and ignore in QA — framing it as an information-flow primitive, supply-chain backdoor, and auditing problem. A serving-time span veto provides bit-identical noninterference guarantees, verified across ten models and 0.5B-120B parameters, and is distilled into detectors.

entry.title: Omni-Modal LLMs Know More Than They Say

author.name: Na Min An, Taekyung Kim, Jaemyung Yu, Hyunjung Shim, Dongyoon Han

entry.summary: Identifies a knows-but-cannot-say disconnect in omni-modal LLMs, which often perceive information in vision, audio, and IMU inputs correctly but fail to express it in responses. The authors propose Token-level Modality Alignment, showing non-textual representations are less aligned with and less attended to than response tokens, explaining the gap and motivating fixes.

entry.title: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems

author.name: Xin Xu, Ke Cheng, Hao Wang, Yangru Huang, Yanghao Xiao, Zhichao Chen, Zhisheng Zhong, Xun Liu, Yi Li, Qian Li, Haibin Lv, Jun Zhang, Jie Jiang, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: SpecRSI enables agents to self-improve by drafting executable successor agents before predecessors are fully evaluated, requiring complete verification before adoption, with verification-aware tree search allocating budget between editing and checking and group verification optimization training the improver. It balances exploration and evaluation under limited budgets for recursive agent improvement.

entry.title: Relational Learning as World Modeling

author.name: Zheyu Zhang, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: The paper reframes relational learning as world modeling, introducing TabWM (a tabular world model) and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given observed executions from an unseen world, TabWM predicts sparse structured edits from new actions in-context, improving complete-edit F1 from 0.016 to much higher values across 512 held-out worlds.

entry.title: Force-Modulated Dexterity: Unified Compliance for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Ying Yuan, David Held, Jitendra Malik, Haozhi Qi

entry.summary: Introduces FOMO-Dex, a unified compliance formulation for contact-rich dexterous manipulation that expresses nominal actions in task-geometry coordinates and applies force-driven corrections along selected directions, addressing the gap where teleoperators can specify motion but not subtle force adjustments. Demonstrated on card picking, paper cutting, screwdriving, and nut-and-bolt assembly.

entry.title: claimcheck: Measuring and Improving Specification Faithfulness

author.name: Martin Amster, One An, Holly Baker, Fernanda Graciolli, Simon Henniger, Nada Amin

entry.summary: claimcheck targets the spec formalization problem: whether a formally verified specification actually captures the author's natural-language requirement, a risk that grows as LLMs write both code and specifications. The authors curate an end-to-end benchmark spanning Dafny contracts and Lean 4, Isabelle, and Rocq theorem statements to measure the gap between intended meaning and formal artifacts. This connects formal verification with LLM faithfulness evaluation.

entry.title: Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Guanghan Wang, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Benoit Dumoulin, Hanqing Lu, Volodymyr Kuleshov

entry.summary: This paper revisits the widely cited claim that diffusion language models need roughly 16x the training compute of autoregressive models, arguing the original methodology used ELBO scoring and decoder-only training that is out of step with current practice. Using exact likelihood under the model's own decoding order, block diffusion training, and encoder-decoder architectures, its new scaling laws substantially shrink the estimated gap.

entry.title: zPocket: Better Pocket Finding with Frozen Co-Folding Features

author.name: Tally Portnoi, Allison M Keys, Benjamin R DiFrancesco, Nate Gruver

entry.summary: zPocket targets protein-ligand binding site (pocket) prediction by training prediction heads on top of frozen features from co-folding models, an approach no prior public method has leveraged for novel pocket prediction. The authors also introduce PocketWatch, a curated benchmark of biologically relevant ligand pockets stratified by sequence similarity, structural similarity, and crypticity, addressing the problem that existing benchmarks fall inside co-folding models' training distribution. This enables honest evaluation of generalization to novel and cryptic pockets, with direct drug-discovery relevance.

entry.title: SkillScreen: High-Recall Screening of Malicious Agent Skills with Decision Models

author.name: Jerrold Huang, Junwei Quan, Saiyue Lyu, Zihan Guo, Yingqiang Ge

entry.summary: SkillScreen is a compact decision model that scores the maliciousness of agent skills (defined in SKILL.md files) in a single forward pass, achieving 99% recall on unseen attack families while flagging only 20-25% of benign skills for review. It generalizes better than fine-tuned encoders and prompted LLM judges on MaliciousSkillBench.

entry.title: LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization

author.name: Lingyi Long, Congyue Zhao, Xiaoou Li, Yanmin Qian, Tao Huang

entry.summary: Recasts post-hoc linearization of Video Diffusion Transformers as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight transformation, identifying initialization, not attention replacement, as the fundamental bottleneck. LinMorph learns a cross-parameter morphism so each target Gated DeltaNet parameter draws jointly from pretrained weights, preserving knowledge better than random init or rigid manual reuse.

entry.title: SWEPatchTest: Evaluating Software Tests Beyond Reproduction

author.name: Hua Lu, Pengcheng Wang, Han Li, Zichen Tian, Yanyu Chen, Huang He, Bingjin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SWEPATCHTEST, a benchmark of 619 test-generation tasks from SWE-bench Pro, SWE-bench Multilingual, and DeepSWE, with 82,579 candidate patches from coding-agent trajectories. By replaying suites on buggy and patched codebases, it jointly measures reproduction, acceptance of correct patches, and rejection of incorrect patches via a Joint Validation Rate, exposing failures hidden by single-reference evaluation.

entry.title: Which Optimizer Leaks Most? Optimizer Implicit Bias as a Training-Data Privacy Controller

author.name: Sagi Habani, Yehonathan Refael, Ofir Lindenbaum

entry.summary: The paper shows that optimizer choice (SGD, Adam, Muon) leaves distinct fingerprints in released checkpoints that affect how much training data can be reconstructed, extending KKT-based reconstruction theory. It proposes weight-specificity of implicit bias as the key quantity and frames optimizer selection as a privacy control.

entry.title: Just Respect the Semantics: Image-Token Compression via Pre-LLM Semantic Variable-Resolution Tokenization and In-LLM Relevance Pruning

author.name: Tianhao Fu, Austin Wang, Charles Chen, Roby Aldave-Garza, Victor Xie, Xiyue Jiao, Yucheng Chen, Martin Tin

entry.summary: Varest introduces semantic-fungibility-guided image token compression for vision-language models: variable-resolution merging guided by object and text localizers preserves detail at boundaries and text, while learned REL registers prune visual tokens after early decoder processing. Across three backbones and 13 benchmarks it outperforms 15 baselines, retaining 86-92 percent of full-token performance with under 6 percent of original tokens.

entry.title: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Andrea Yaoyun Cui, Hanyu Wang, Xinyi Wang, Bangzheng Li, Lin Zhang, Zhenggang Tang, Shyamal Buch, Dejia Xu, Matthew Tancik

entry.summary: LIBERO-RIG is a benchmark that perturbs only the robot's hardware and setup while holding LIBERO tasks fixed, spanning eleven axes (camera mounting, calibration, actuation gain, control rate, proprioceptive noise, base pose, table height, gripper pads) with five severity levels, yielding 210 conditions. It evaluates nine recent VLA models with 500 episodes per condition, exposing robustness gaps under realistic deployment variation.

entry.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming

author.name: Woosang Lim, Haneul Yoo, Vincent-Daniel Yun, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: Introduces LayerTrim, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and trims their MLP features while preserving attention pathways and model depth. It aims to prevent the collapse in long-form reasoning performance that existing pruning methods cause on tasks like AIME, reporting accuracy improvements of up to 21 points across three reasoning models and five benchmarks.

entry.title: Asymptotic Behavior of Transformers

author.name: Katy Blumer, Da-Cheng Juan, Jon Kleinberg, Ravi Kumar, Cyrus Rashtchian, Andrew Tomkins

entry.summary: The authors study transformers generating text over long horizons, showing that even minimal attention-only transformers can fail to converge, while a rich class with layer norm, MLPs, RoPE, and mixed local/global layers has a softmax temperature threshold above which the output distribution converges to a unique limit. They further prove the supremum of these thresholds is infinite, so no global temperature forces convergence for all transformers.
