This is substantive theory on long-generation dynamics of realistic transformer architectures.

entry.title: InstructPro2: Natural Language and Biological Grounding Guided De Novo Protein Design

author.name: Charles Novak, Zhenqiao Song, Chuan Li, Jianwen Xie, Lei Li

entry.summary: InstructPro2 translates natural-language protein design objectives into amino acid sequences while conditioning on biological context such as ligands and antigens via dedicated encoders. It is pretrained on InstructPro2Bench, a large dataset of 205.7 million text-protein pairs from UniProtKB, then adapted for ligand-binding proteins and antibodies. This extends instruction-following generation to a major scientific design domain.

entry.title: What Happens to the Goal? Distinct Failures of Policy Alignment in Goal Misgeneralization

author.name: Julia Barth, Armin Sommer, Kunvar Thaman, Jannik Schilling

entry.summary: The paper provides a mechanistic dissection of goal misgeneralization, identifying three distinct failure regimes across Procgen and robot tasks: functional target substitution, policy shortcuts, and cue competition. The authors distinguish these by tracing where goal information remains available internally and how it influences action selection. This taxonomy deepens understanding of a key alignment failure mode in RL agents.

entry.title: Provable Transformer Context Compression for In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yajie Zhao, Yingjun Mo, Zhiyong Wang, Bo Tang, Chao Xu, Fang Kong

entry.summary: The paper answers how much context a transformer intrinsically needs for in-context reinforcement learning, proving that for fixed-policy TD evaluation with a shared linear decoder, the minimum context dimension exactly reproducing the first L TD iterates is the Krylov dimension induced by sampled transitions. Below this threshold, exact reproduction is impossible, and the paper develops compression schemes accordingly. This provides the first principled scalability answer for in-context RL memory.

entry.title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects

author.name: Sam Gijsen, Moritz Seiler, Kerstin Ritter

entry.summary: Studying interaction recovery in conditional flow-matching models across physiological simulators, drug dose-response data, cell perturbations, and molecular conformers, the paper shows models can appear accurate overall while failing to recover scientifically relevant non-additive interaction effects, even hallucinating them under extrapolation to unseen conditions. It separates interaction recovery from overall predictive accuracy.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Models are Minimax Optimal Under Sparsity

author.name: Luca Blunda, Tyler Farghly, Umut Simsekli, Alain Durmus

entry.summary: This paper establishes minimax-optimal statistical rates for discrete diffusion models under sparsity assumptions, analyzing a nonparametric estimator derived from a regularized score-entropy objective. It provides the discrete analogue of results showing continuous diffusion models adapt to low-dimensional structure. This fills an important theoretical gap as discrete diffusion becomes a leading alternative to autoregressive text generation.

entry.title: Tail Competition Explains Scaling in Best-of-N Sampling for Verifiable Problems

author.name: Taro Yano, Yoichi Ishibashi, Masafumi Oyamada

entry.summary: This paper analyzes Best-of-N sampling for LLMs as a competition between the extreme reward tails of correct and incorrect responses, using extreme value theory to characterize three asymptotic regimes. The framework explains both monotonic gains and reward-hacking-induced degradation under imperfect reward models, and derives finite-sample scaling laws. This provides a principled theoretical foundation for a widely used inference-time scaling technique.

entry.title: Explorer-Zero: Improving Self-Play for Long-Horizon Tasks with Decomposable Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Tianyu Liu, Davide Belli, Bence Major, Arash Behboodi, Tribhuvanesh Orekondy

entry.summary: Explorer-Zero is a self-play framework where a learned proposer explores an environment, generates compositional tasks, and records intermediate and final states as verification checkpoints, enabling fine-grained rewards for partial completion with alternating proposer-solver training. It removes the need for human-annotated tasks in long-horizon agentic RL and includes theoretical justification.

entry.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory

author.name: Jintian Zhang, Feng He, Xinnian Liang, Ziwen Xu, Haoming Xu, Haojing Huang, Shuangzhi Wu, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: Inspired by biological systems consolidation, Cortex internalizes context-dependent LLM performance gains into parametric memory by generating prospective queries and distilling context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. It introduces a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention across single, batch, and sequential updates on 4B-120B dense and MoE backbones.

entry.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets

author.name: Shubhendu Trivedi, Jacob Eisenstein, Alekh Agarwal, Ian Gemp, Michael Kaisers, Adam Fisch

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes decentralized serving-time agentic markets where AI agents bid in first-price auctions to claim user prompts, quantifying welfare loss via the price of anarchy. It grounds bids in expected reward minus inference cost and examines inefficiency from non-truthful bidding. As AI agents begin mediating service allocation, this provides foundational mechanism-design analysis for such markets.

entry.title: HERO: Harnessing Evidence for Test-time Refinement and Prompt Optimization in Program Generation

author.name: Mingyu Lu, Timothy Ossowski, Tristan Naumann, Hoifung Poon, Peniel Argaw

entry.summary: HERO improves LLM program generation (text-to-SQL, text-to-Python) by optimizing reusable prompts and scaffolding using execution feedback, combining offline harness optimization learned from prior failures with test-time refinement. By executing generated outputs, it verifies that proposed harness updates do not disrupt previously correct behavior, a weakness of LLM-reflector-based approaches. This is a practical contribution to reliable code generation pipelines.

entry.title: Measuring and Reducing Unusable Replies of LLM Agents

author.name: Yilin Jiang, Fei Tan, Xuanyu Yin, Guanchu Wang, Xia Hu, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Introduces reply usability: whether a requester can actually understand and act on an LLM agent's final reply, measured by a reader model simulating the requester's perspective. Across eight models from seven families, 54% of 480 replies fail this bar and even the best model fails 30% of the time, with failures mostly pointing to material the requester never saw.

entry.title: To Reason but Not to Stop: Understanding and Recovering Pruned Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Minh-Anh Nguyen, Nguyen T. Ha Lan, Xiyan Fu, Dung D. Le, Wei Lu

entry.summary: This paper shows that accuracy degradation in pruned large reasoning models stems largely from failure to terminate — looping repetitively after the correct answer has appeared — rather than degraded reasoning ability. The authors identify a consistent hidden-state direction separating terminating from looping continuations and propose a Termination-Guided Activation method to recover pruned models.

entry.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Jiatong Li, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: MolLean is a Lean-based, process-verifiable language that grounds chemical chain-of-thought in an explicit molecular state, with a layered kernel checking state transitions and a typed witness protocol separating structural checks from external measurements. An MCP tool interface lets models receive feedback during generation, with rejected actions leaving state unchanged, reducing hallucinated structural claims.

entry.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees

author.name: Dongzhuo Li, Fangzhou Cheng, Weiwei Li, Kevin Han, Haixu Ma, Zhongchang Sun, Ruiyi Li, Serena Li, Xiangjun Fan, Lizhu Zhang, Yuandong Tian

entry.summary: TreeFlex addresses context degradation in ReAct-style agents by maintaining intermediate states as nodes in a search tree managed by the harness. A single LLM acts in Reflection and Execution roles: it picks which tree node to resume from using global summaries, then continues from the restored path, allowing agents to navigate their own search histories.

entry.title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models

author.name: Zefan Yang, Zheyuan Zhang, Boris Maihe, Yikang Liu, Hang Yu, Ankush Mukherjee, Xiao Chen, Pingkun Yan, Terrence Chen, Shanhui Sun

entry.summary: SonoWorld is a causal world model for robotic ultrasound that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them in probe pose, enabling interactive pose-controllable simulation. It addresses the challenge that ultrasound captures only cross-sections of 3D anatomy, where small probe motions cause large appearance changes, providing realistic simulation environments for ultrasound policy learning.

entry.title: Robota-Embed: Unified VLA Embeddings for Robot In-Context Learning and Evolution

author.name: Yunze Liu, Jing Wang, Shenrui Wu, Wenkun He, Guanqi Zhan, Xianzheng Ma, Junyu Chen, Wenhang Ge, Haozhan Tang, Yuchao Gu, Zhuoyang Zhang, Zekai Wang, Dantong Niu, Zhen Dong, Yuke Zhu, Trevor Darrell, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Song Han, Han Cai

entry.summary: Robota-Embed is claimed to be the first vision-language-action embedding model jointly encoding task, execution stage, and future continuations, trained with predictive retrieval on a 1.7M-anchor corpus and evaluated on a new benchmark. It substantially outperforms action-free Gemini Embedding on clip- and episode-level retrieval, enabling in-context learning from historical robot episodes.

entry.title: Learning in Orbit: Onboard Training and Closed-Loop Attitude Control with a Thermal Segmentation Model on a Spacecraft

author.name: Elena Sorina Lupu, Hannah Grauer, Phaedrus Leeds, Nikhil Ranganathan, Connor Lee, Sulekha Kishore, Cailyn Smith, Shon Cortes, Brian Hardy, Benjamen Bycroft, Darren W. Rowen, Soon-Jo Chung

entry.summary: This work reports a flight demonstration on a 6U CubeSat of onboard training and inference of a thermal segmentation model on a Jetson GPU in space, plus closed-loop attitude control using that model to track the Moon. It also documents the ROS 2-based middleware and fault-tolerant file system used. This is a rare, concrete instance of learning-based autonomy actually deployed and trained in orbit.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Driven Self-Play for Robust Multi-Agent Driving Policies

author.name: Sajad Marvi, Julian Schmidt, Alessandro Canevaro, Julian Jordan, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: The scheme rewards half of self-play agents for increasing neighbors' epistemic uncertainty while the other half learn to drive safely, using uncertainty as an automatic proxy for scenario difficulty to generate a challenging curriculum without manual scenario design. The resulting policy achieves best-in-class zero-shot transfer to nuPlan Val14 with 99.12% performance.

entry.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Receding-Horizon Safety Critic and Differentiable Action Shields

author.name: Siwei Ju, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

entry.summary: The paper learns a receding-horizon safety critic for robot RL that predicts whether a state will remain non-terminating over the next horizon, enabling anticipatory detection of impending locomotion failures. It trains an ensemble with horizon classification, control-barrier-function-inspired temporal consistency, and smoothness objectives, aggregated with conservative CVaR, plus differentiable action shields for safe correction.

entry.title: How an assessor could investigate evidence of acceleration from the automation of AI R&D

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: METR outlines how an independent assessor could determine whether AI-automated AI R&D is dramatically accelerating capabilities progress. The framework covers measuring internal capability trends, attributing acceleration to AI automation versus other factors, identifying bottlenecks in inputs like compute, data, and labor, and assessing whether the methods would detect true explosive growth.

entry.title: Measuring the Inference Energy Efficiency of Open-Weight LLMs across Benchmarks, Reasoning Modes, and Hardware

author.name: Zeyu Yang, Wes Armour

entry.summary: The study directly measures capability-energy trade-offs for 86 open-weight model checkpoints across seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms, finding most configurations use 2.6-4.8x more energy than equally-scoring alternatives. Enabling reasoning modes raises energy use roughly 3.7x on average, with benefits varying strongly by model family.

entry.title: Attention Sinks in VLMs Are Borrowed, Not Seen

author.name: Dengjia Zhang, Alexander Martin, Pengyu Yan, Xihan Sun, Jiaqi Li, Benjamin Van Durme, Andrew Yates, Reno Kriz, William Walden

entry.summary: This study identifies what makes an image token become a visual attention sink in vision-language models, showing that only centered cosine similarity between an image token's key and the text-sink key detects sinks across ten VLMs from four families. The finding that visual sinks borrow the text sink's key alignment corrects the interpretation of attention maps as records of where the model looked.

entry.title: GUIDE: Computationally Augmented Consensus for Trustworthy Clinical Practice Guidelines

author.name: Yuanfan Lin, Jie Di, Xujin He, Zhenzhe Lin, Jialing Chen, Ruiyang Li, Changyu Zheng, Yuanrui Shang, Weiqin Peng, Jingxi Qin, Xiong Wang, Dongxin Ye, Yining Huang, Guoqiang Li, Andi Xu, Sijia Yu, Ruixin Wang, Yahan Yang, Xiaohang Wu, Duoru Lin, Jingjing Chen, Zhenzhen Liu, Wenben Chen, Haotian Lin

entry.summary: GUIDE is a multi-agent copilot system for human-AI collaborative generation and updating of clinical practice guidelines, delegating labor-intensive tasks to specialized AI agents while preserving expert arbitration. On 12 NICE ophthalmology datasets it achieved roughly 89% literature recall, 86% rating alignment, and 92% recommendation agreement with about 29% human intervention, generalizing across additional specialties.

entry.title: TRAP: Tool-result Replay Attack for Probing Misbinding in LLM Agents

author.name: Yutong Zhi, Jie Zhang, Xiuqi Lu, Jiayuan Xu, Jing Shao

entry.summary: The paper characterizes tool-result misbinding, where a real but unmodified tool result is consumed in an incompatible execution context, leading agents to unsafe actions. It introduces ReplayBench with 19 agent scenarios, 4 failure properties, and 3 replay mechanisms, evaluating eight LLMs across agent frameworks.

entry.title: Same Operation, Different Permission: Evaluating Whether Guardrails Honor Authorization

author.name: Huihao Jing, Shaojin Chen, Wenbin Hu, Yuxuan Liu, Haochen Shi, Zhongwei Xie, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark testing whether LLM agent guardrails make decisions that follow actual authorization: blocking the same operation when unauthorized while allowing it under valid permission. With expert-annotated natural-language scenarios, executed and verified operations, and native-policy requests, it checks each decision for correctness, usability, and resulting effect.

entry.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models

author.name: Jonathan Geuter, Andrew Cheng, David Alvarez-Melis

entry.summary: The authors show that existing open instruction-tuned models (Gemma 4 31B/12B, Qwen3.6-27B, and another Qwen variant) can match dedicated System One decision models like Jev by reading option-letter probabilities from output logits, with no extra training, and that a simple SFT recipe improves this further. This challenges the notion that specialized decision-model architectures are needed.

entry.title: Coupled Harness--Model Evolution for Scientific Equation Discovery

author.name: Pengze Li, Jiaquan Zhang, Encheng Su, Yunbo Long, Zihang Zeng, Xinping Liu, Han Zhang, Junchi Yu, Shixiang Tang, Aoran Wang, Xi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a coupled evolution framework for LLM-based scientific equation discovery that improves both the executable tool library and the model's tool-use policy from the same verifiable fit-error signal, rather than adapting only one part while freezing the other. An agent grows the tool library from generic primitives while the policy learns to orchestrate them. This matters for AI-for-science because fixable failures in either component currently leave systems stuck.

entry.title: A dataset of formalised theorem statements from the Annals of Mathematics

author.name: Thomas Browning, Katerina Hristova, David Ledvinka, Justus Springer, Hang Lu Su, Jack McKoen, Kevin Buzzard

entry.summary: AnnalsChallenge provides 50 hand-written Lean 4 formalizations (using Mathlib) of the main theorems of Annals of Mathematics papers published since 2020, manually reviewed and AI-audited, released without formal proofs. It gives the autoformalization community hard, trustworthy targets for measuring progress. Kevin Buzzard's involvement lends strong formalization credibility.

entry.title: Loose Lips: Understanding Privacy Leakage in Agentic Dialogue

author.name: Soumya Sharma, Ayana Hussain, Heber Hwang Arcolezi, Ulrich A\"ivodji, Spandana Gella, Adriana Romero-Soriano, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: The authors extend CIMemories into CIMEMORIES DIALOGUE, a benchmark of 4,410 two-agent dialogue instances grounded in Contextual Integrity theory, and evaluate 7 open-weight models from the Qwen3 and Llama 3.1 families under varied conditions. They find task capability and privacy leakage are fundamentally coupled, with more capable models leaking more systematically.

entry.title: Memory Without Curation: Learning Multi-Stream Latent Memory for Robot Policies

author.name: Yilin Wu, Rutav Shah, Shuaiyi Huang, Sumedh A. Sontakke, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Andrea Bajcsy, Max Simchowitz, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: IMPRINT is a policy-agnostic latent memory framework that augments vision-language-action models with multi-stream memory without explicitly curating what to remember, unlike standard approaches using recent frames, keyframes, or text summaries. It aims to avoid spurious shortcuts from conditioning on full histories and reduce deployment latency.

entry.title: Sequent-Prover: Training Agents for Formal, Checkable SMT-based Reasoning

author.name: Debargha Ganguly, Weicong Chen, Mohsen Hariri, Vikash Singh, Sreehari Sankar, Shouren Wang, Wang Yang, Biyao Zhang, Chaoda Song, Alexander Nemecek, Kai Ye, Osama Zafar, Erman Ayday, Joe Stubbs, Srinivasan Iyengar, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: Sequent-Prover is a family of language-model agents that reason in an executable SMT-LIB scratchpad, writing complete SMT-LIB programs, querying the Z3 solver across turns, inspecting feedback, and repairing formalizations before giving explicit answers. The post-training recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, bootstraps from a noisy teacher by retaining successful, executable trajectory tails for SFT and trajectory-level preference optimization. Evaluation goes beyond solver success to semantic faithfulness and task accuracy.

entry.title: Variance-Optimal State Resampling for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yibo Wang, Yuanxin Liu, Zhaoran Wang

entry.summary: The paper derives a closed-form Neyman allocation for which state distribution minimizes policy-gradient variance under a fixed rollout budget in RL with verifiable rewards, connecting to GRPO's group-relative advantage and inducing an emergent reverse curriculum. It proposes VSR, a plug-in GRPO modification using a prefix replay buffer and zero-cost variance estimation.

entry.title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training

author.name: Paul Setinek, Fabian Paischer, Nils Thuerey, Johannes Brandstetter, Felix Koehler

entry.summary: Formalizes neural-surrogate training for PDEs as a joint function of data quantity and numerical fidelity under a fixed data-generation compute budget, treating fidelity as a fine-grained discrete spectrum with known convergence rates, and derives compute-optimal multi-fidelity data scaling strategies for when data generation, not training, is the bottleneck.

entry.title: Train for Many, Update with One: Improving Multi-Sample Reasoning via Fenchel-Bregman Posterior Learning

author.name: Sungjun Lim, Adrian Robert Minut, Nico Carlsen Daheim, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Kyungwoo Song, Thomas M\"ollenhoff

entry.summary: The paper formulates finite-K posterior learning to directly optimize candidate coverage in multi-sample reasoning, and proposes a Fenchel-Bregman optimization approach that needs only one posterior draw per update instead of K. This makes training for pass@K-style objectives far more compute-efficient.

entry.title: ProtoArena: Can AI Agents Discover and Exploit Real-World Cross-Component Protocol Vulnerabilities?

author.name: Fasheng Miao, Zhaoyu Hu, Xiang Li, Changqing An, Jiutian Zeng, Longtao Huang, Haixin Duan, Jilong Wang

entry.summary: ProtoArena is a black-box, dynamic benchmark with 80 cross-component vulnerability-exploitation environments spanning 11 protocol domains and 7 attack categories, testing whether LLM agents can exploit inconsistencies in message interpretation, timing, state, or trust assumptions across running systems. Agents interact through scoped interfaces without source-code access.

entry.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rong Li, Shijie Li, Jiangyong Huang, Lingdong Kong, Jiaming Zhou, Dongyue Lu, Zeying Gong, Baoxiong Jia, Junwei Liang, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: GeoReader trains lightweight Geometric Readers that convert outputs of geometry foundation models into continuous input tokens for vision-language models, supervised by geometry descriptions, enabling VLMs to actually use latent geometric structure for metric and multi-view spatial reasoning. Notably, the paper shows that a released feature-alignment model's accuracy is unchanged when its aligned latents are zeroed, proving that fusion alone does not ensure use of geometry.

entry.title: Verifier-Grounded Agentic RL for Provably Correct Code

author.name: George Ma, Yuhao Zhang, Bing He, Zeren Shui, Ferhat Erata, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Somayeh Sojoudi, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Builds an agentic RL environment and reward for formal program verification, addressing sparse verifier feedback and reward hacking by reading verifier diagnostics rather than only accept/reject verdicts and scoring candidates by weighted diagnostic signals. This moves beyond test-passing rewards toward provably correct code generation.

entry.title: Can LLMs Access their World Knowledge for Event Prediction?

author.name: Zijun Wu, Zhitian Zhang, Hossein Hajimirsadeghi, Nikita Dvornik, Alexander Pashevich

entry.summary: This paper investigates why LLMs underperform specialized models on temporal event prediction despite rich pretrained world knowledge, arguing the problem is interface design rather than inaccessible knowledge. It shows LLMs become effective forecasters when events are grounded in natural-language descriptions and event semantics are separated from the prediction space to avoid label-association bias, introducing the DescribeEvent benchmark of roughly 150K events across seven datasets. This reframes a negative result into actionable interface guidance.

entry.title: Weighted Ensemble Sampling for Rare-Event Estimation in Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Gustavo Didier, Fangzheng Wu, Brian Summa, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces Weighted Ensemble, a training-free framework for estimating the probability of rare but severe LLM failures at deployment scale. Instead of direct Monte Carlo sampling or learned proposal distributions, WE samples only from the original model and periodically reallocates sampling budget toward promising prefixes using internal LLM representations. This makes rare-event risk estimation far more statistically efficient, relevant to AI safety evaluation.

entry.title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing?

author.name: Hasan Amin, Zhuoran Lu, Ming Yin

entry.summary: Shows that widely used prompt-predictiveness measures of human contribution in AI-assisted writing can be trivially manipulated: a SPECIFICITY PADDING attack that asks the model to copy random IDs from the prompt makes minimal human input look highly human-authored. A context-swap audit confirms the score changes for unchanged text, undermining the measure's validity.

entry.title: Remember, Revisit, Revise: Scaffold Memory for Long-Horizon 3D Geometry

author.name: Soumick Sarker, Mengmi Zhang

entry.summary: SMORE equips frozen geometry foundation models with a revisable external memory for long-horizon 3D inference, inspired by hippocampal associative memory, so earlier pose and reconstruction estimates can be revised when later observations reveal errors. It addresses error accumulation in windowed feed-forward models and the non-revisability of streaming models.

entry.title: Active Generative Simulation: Meta-Learning What to Simulate for Sim-and-Real Policy Co-Training

author.name: Liqian Ma, Vaibhav Saxena, Utkarsh Aashu Mishra, Shuo Cheng, Yongxin Chen, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: MetaGenSim formulates Active Generative Simulation — optimizing a simulator's data-generation distribution to maximize downstream real-world performance for sim-and-real co-training — and solves it with a meta-learned auxiliary rater network that discovers high-utility generation distributions without manual parameter alignment. This replaces uniform generation, offline retrieval, or expert tuning of simulators. A compelling step toward autonomous simulation curation for robot learning.

entry.title: One-shot Human Video-Guided Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qi Chen, Yuwei Wu, Quan Chen, Kunpeng Gao, Jin Chen, Che Sun, Zhi Gao, Yunde Jia

entry.summary: CapPro enables VLA policies to adapt to unseen manipulation tasks from a single human demonstration video, removing the need for target-task robot demonstrations and retraining. It combines task extraction from the human video with a mechanism that transfers the demonstrated capability into the VLA policy at test time.

entry.title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics

author.name: Yushen Liang, Yue Peng, Baosheng Jin, Tianluo Zhang, Xinyu Zhang, Shuyi Zhou, Zhuoran Chen, Xinqi Liu, Shenji Wan

entry.summary: The paper identifies physical time as a missing dimension in robot policy memories, which typically treat each observation update as equivalent time regardless of real elapsed duration. It proposes Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), which evolves memory state over measured time intervals and conditions diffusion/flow-matching policies through this memory, trained with native imitation objectives.

entry.title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science

author.name: Xue Li, Hongqian Xia, Daniel Gomm, A\'ecio Santos, Cornelius Wolff, Madelon Hulsebos

entry.summary: The authors argue that current evaluations of data science agents focus on predictive performance and code correctness while missing methodological failures like data leakage and improper validation. They show that these silent failures mask substantive errors, limiting the development of robust agentic data science systems.

entry.title: ACED-Bench: Evaluating How LLM Agents Acquire and Act on Causal Evidence

author.name: Yiwei Chen, Amila Weerasinghe, Siddharth Biswal, Utkrisht Rajkumar, Olcay Boz, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Rose Yu

entry.summary: ACED-BENCH is a neuro-symbolic benchmark where LLM agents must choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make causal decisions, with natural-language scenarios generated by LLMs grounded in hidden probabilistic graphical models that preserve objective ground truth. It evaluates active causal investigation rather than prompt answering.

entry.title: Shaping Latent Mixture-of-Experts: From Expert Geometry to Layerwise Capacity Allocation

author.name: Yaoxiang Wang, Kai Zhang, Ruobing Xie, Lanrui Wang, Guoliang Zhao, Junhui Li, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: LatentMoE moves expert computation to a lower-dimensional space, exposing expert input dimension and intermediate width as explicit design choices, and shows local Jacobian rank is jointly bounded by the two with the maximum at balanced, near-square experts. Controlled sweeps across scales and routing granularities support the finding, and layerwise intrinsic dimension guides capacity allocation across depth.

entry.title: Predicting how model propensities generalize out of distribution

author.name: June Hunter, Lily Wen, Owen Terry, Johannes Taraz, Ben Cohen, Niels Warncke

entry.summary: This alignment study examines how elicitation techniques (system prompting, few-shot, SFT, GRPO) that increase one behavioral propensity in language models spill over onto other propensities in out-of-distribution contexts. It finds spillover is highly correlated across models for a given elicitation technique, but SFT and GRPO induce distinct spillover profiles.

entry.title: Trace Evolution Bench: Measuring Whether Agents Improve from Their Own Environment Traces

author.name: Fangfei Li, Chenyang Zhao, Long Wang, Feng Tian, Lv Guo

entry.summary: Introduces Trace Evolution Bench (TEB), a protocol separating genuine agent self-improvement from gains attributable to rescoring, with strict acceptance criteria and hidden-test graded coding tasks. Notably it shows DeepSeek v4 Pro, an existing model released in April 2026, gains 5-12.5 percentage points across seeds with no policy change, exposing measurement confounds in prior evaluations.

entry.title: Fewer Bits, More Tries: Recovering Capability Under Memory Constraints

author.name: Tomer Galanti, Josh Susskind, Eran Malach

entry.summary: The authors investigate whether the capability gap between large and small/compressed LLMs can be recovered by running a smaller model multiple times in parallel and selecting outputs via tests, exploiting underutilized local inference hardware. Experiments across four code-generation benchmarks show that verified retry recovers much of the accuracy lost to model size or quantization, with a 7B Qwen model using eight parallel attempts matching a 32B model on MBPP+ and beating it on other benchmarks. This offers a practical recipe for local deployment under memory constraints.

entry.title: Recall What Is Missing: Composing Evidence from Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Qi Feng, Jicong Fan

entry.summary: MemPursuit reframes long-term agent memory retrieval as query-conditioned evidence composition, valuing each memory by what it adds beyond already-selected evidence rather than by individual relevance. It uses the residual of a sparse convex query reconstruction as a training-free proxy for missing evidence, reducing redundant context usage under limited context budgets.

entry.title: REVEAL: Reverse Engineering Agentic Latents from Frontier-Model Traces

author.name: Yuetian Du, Meng Wang, Yucheng Wang, Zhangzhe Chen, Wei Wang, Boyu Yang, Weiqi Zhai, Bing Zhao, Ming Kong, Zhan Zhou, Jie Liu, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: REVEAL is a training-free framework that transfers experience from frontier LLM agent trajectories to smaller frozen open-source agents. Inspired by protocol reverse engineering, it extracts anchored states and dynamic feedback-response profiles from textual traces and uses them as reusable local controls without accessing source-model internals.

entry.title: Game-Creation-Agents: Autonomous Game Production

author.name: Tencent Multimodal RL Team, Xiangxin Zhou, Jiaqi Tang, Ke Ma, Wenhao Yang, Jiarui Yao, Boye Niu, Haiyang Guo, Yifei Zhao, Huanjin Yao, Pu Jian, Ruihuang Li, Haitao Wu, Yushi Huang, Xiangyan Liu, Yan Sun, Kaixin Li, Tianyu Pang

entry.summary: Presents GCA, a multi-agent pipeline from Tencent that turns a natural-language request into a runnable Phaser 4 browser game, using a multimodal design document, machine-readable contracts, deterministic tests, and eight specialized agents for scene implementation, asset production, and build verification. A code-blind critic and build-linked real-UI checks gate whether the game ships, with bounded repair loops for blockers.

entry.title: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given

author.name: Ben Slater, Ryan Lundqvist, Leo Richter, Kevin Wei

entry.summary: Using the Petri tool to audit LLM coding agents, this study tests how providing external codebases and benchmark transcripts affects automated auditor effectiveness across four auditor-target pairs and three behaviors (harmful compliance, reward hacking, sycophancy). Providing an external codebase suppressed measured reward hacking in above-floor pairs (e.g., 4.8 to 1.3), showing audit outcomes are highly context-sensitive.

entry.title: PhysCodeGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Physically Verifiable 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Shuai Shao, Jinchen He, Cunxin Fan, Zihan Guo, Shijian Wang, Qihan Ren, Kangning Zhang, Zunnan Xu, Haoyuan Li, Hao Wang, Jianghao Lin, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: PhysCodeGym is a benchmark of 156 tasks where coding agents inspect videos, write and run Blender programs, and refine 4D physical simulations using simulation feedback, across rigid-body, liquid, deformable, and wind-driven motion. Six metrics combine rule-based and rubric-based evaluation, including counterfactual interventions to test physical consistency.

entry.title: When Goals Leak Across Relationships: How Cached Goal Representations Shape Cross-Client Decisions

author.name: Saloni Gupta, S\'ebastien Krier, Glenn Matlin

entry.summary: The authors test an instruct-tuned OLMo model in a controlled two-client setting with opposing objectives and find that shared conversational memory causes the model to deviate from the current client's goal in about 22% of eligible decisions. Linear probes reveal that client-goal ownership becomes recoverable in middle layers and is concentrated in particular parts of the KV cache. This is an early, concrete demonstration of information leakage across relationships in multi-client LLM agents.

entry.title: Stable Token-level Scheduling for Serverless LLM Inference

author.name: Hardi Ashishbhai Desai, Balaji N K, Sourav Kanti Addya

entry.summary: This paper introduces Token Window Pacing (TWP), a closed-loop scheduling framework for serverless LLM inference that uses runtime feedback on inter-token latency and queue depth to decide when to admit new requests. It targets the overlooked problem that admitting new requests during the bandwidth-bound decode stage disrupts ongoing generation, complementing prior work focused only on time-to-first-token. This matters because serving efficiency directly affects cost and user experience for deployed LLMs.

entry.title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution

author.name: Xiaoliang Wang, Zhuo Chen, Chuanyang Zheng, Jiangwei Lao, Quanbin Wang, Honglin Lin, Jiajia Liu, Zhihong Lu, Hao Jin, Jian Wang, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: Introduces ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework for electrocardiogram models that combines verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search, using signal remeasurement to validate edits and error signals to drive generator repair and learner interventions. Across seven benchmarks, three improvement rounds lift an existing Qwen-based model's mean QA accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. The work matters because it applies verified self-improvement loops to a safety-relevant clinical domain with measurable waveform-level grounding.

entry.title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills

author.name: Letian Zhu, Han Li, Yifan Yao, Xinping Lei, Xinyu Che, Jiahao Wang, Dianyi Wang, Yucheng Fu, Jiakai Wang, Zhiqi Bai, Wenbo Su, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Socratic Skill Learning, where an expert Educator guides an LLM Student through interleaved teaching and practice while the Student remains the sole environment operator and skill author, able to question, test, and adapt advice, so learned skills capture both procedures and conditions of use. The paper also releases SkillTransferBench with 35 task families and 408 executable cases using held-out evaluation in fresh sessions. This matters for making agent skills genuinely transferable rather than overfit to the learning episode.

entry.title: Can Agents Forget When Asked? A Benchmark for Memory Unlearning in LLM Agents

author.name: Bofan Xie, Chaokun Wang, Guanchen Ge, Songyao Wang, Fang Niu, Hang Zhang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Bemula is the first benchmark dedicated to memory unlearning in LLM agents, testing whether agents can remove exactly the facts users request from long-term memory while leaving the rest intact. It comprises 50 multi-session dialogues, 135 forget requests of six types, and 1,742 test questions with control variants. This fills a real gap, since existing memory benchmarks only cover writing, retrieval, and organization.

entry.title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery

author.name: Yibo Wen, Han Liu

entry.summary: Autonomous Science Bench introduces six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns grounded in published biology, chemistry, and materials science experiments. Agents choose experiment batches, receive real lab-service measurements, and must pass calibrated discovery and learning gates, moving beyond fixed-dataset or purely simulated science benchmarks.

entry.title: Splicing Hints into Reasoning Traces: Learning from Demonstrator Failures

author.name: Hamed Mahdavi (Pennsylvania State University), Pouria Mahdavinia (Pennsylvania State University), Majid Farhadi (Google), Vasant Honavar (Pennsylvania State University)

entry.summary: SPLICE moves verification and repair out of the RL training loop into offline data generation: a second model verifies a reasoning model's traces as they are generated, truncates failed traces at the last verified step, and splices in guidance derived from reference solutions, enabling learning even when the policy never produces fully correct olympiad-level attempts. This sidesteps the cold-start problem where outcome-reward RL yields no signal absent occasional correct answers. It also notes that correct final answers do not certify correct derivations, particularly for proof problems.

entry.title: Showing versus Doing: Teaching by Demonstration

author.name: Mark K. Ho, Michael L. Littman, James MacGlashan, Fiery Cushman, Joseph L. Austerweil

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian model of teaching by demonstration, distinguishing between demonstrators who intentionally teach a task versus those who simply perform it. Experiments with human participants show behavior consistent with the model's predictions, and standard inverse reinforcement learning algorithms benefit when learning from deliberate demonstrations rather than raw performance.

entry.title: EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference

author.name: Anxhelo Diko, Jieyu Lin, Stefano Ambrogio, Ziyun Li, Mahmoud Assran, Th\'eo Moutakanni, Barbara De Salvo, Chiao Liu

entry.summary: EV-JEPA extends V-JEPA-style self-supervised vision foundation models to the edge-cloud continuum with reconfigurable width and native support for cross-device partitioned execution. Unlike prior work handling only width elasticity or fixed split computing, a single trained model deploys across smart glasses, phones, robots, and servers under varying compute budgets.

entry.title: Specification-Based Testing of Large Language Models

author.name: Kausar Moshood, Jace Bolante, Roshan Aditya Murali, Manish Motwani

entry.summary: Introduces LEST, a framework that treats documented safety claims in model cards and safety reports as specifications for black-box testing. It mutates benchmark prompts to search for counterexamples (cases where a model refuses a prompt but complies with a mutated version), validates them manually, and traces violations back to specific documented claims.

entry.title: UltraBERT: Beyond the Limit of BERT Pre-Training

author.name: Jungwoo Park, Taewhoo Lee, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: This work modernizes bidirectional encoder pretraining, finding that encoders saturate on downstream tasks beyond a few trillion tokens and that masking ratio effects diverge by task type: lower ratios favor classification while higher ratios favor retrieval. It concludes with a recipe aiming for a single encoder competitive across both classification and retrieval.

entry.title: Framework for an AI-Ready ARPES Community Database

author.name: Zhi-Xun Shen, Jin Gene Wong, Karen Lei, Leon Garcia, Felix Baumberger, Sergey Borisenko, Aaron Bostwick, Ting Cao, Tanny Chavez, Yulin Chen, Monika Choudhary, Andrea Damascelli, Dan Dessau, Thomas P. Devereaux, Sandy A. Ekahana, Alexei Fedorov, Atsushi Fujimori, Yucheng Guo, M. Zahid Hasan, Makoto Hashimoto, Yu He, Philip Hofmann, Zahid Hussain, Harold Y. Hwang, Zhurun Ji, Chunjing Jia, Timur K. Kim, Phil D. C. King, Takeshi Kondo, Alessandra Lanzara, Chun Lin, Donghui Lu, Matteo Michiardi, Sung-Kwan Mo, Brian Moritz, Laurenz Rettig, Eli Rotenberg, Takafumi Sato, Kyle M. Shen, Jonathan A. Sobota, Inna Vishik, Shuolong Yang, Ming Yi, Timothy Zaklama

entry.summary: This Perspective, authored by a large consortium of leading ARPES (angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy) researchers including Zhi-Xun Shen, reports on a community effort to build an AI-ready shared database for four decades of electronic-structure spectra. The authors argue the field's publication-centered workflow discards most experimental data, and a shared ecosystem would enable reproducibility, reuse, and AI-enabled materials discovery. It lays out community standards and data infrastructure outcomes.

entry.title: CodeWalk: Generating Coding Benchmarks by Walking a Problem Graph

author.name: Jiaxin Fang, Runyuan He, Arnav Gupta, Sahil Kumawat, Huanzhi Mao, Alvin Cheung

entry.summary: This paper introduces a fully programmatic approach to generating new coding benchmark problems by composing verified atomic problems into harder level-N tasks, retaining only tasks where all atoms remain unsolved and a joint reference solution passes evaluation checks. This avoids both expensive human curation (as in SWE-bench) and costly LLM-based synthetic generation. It is instantiated across four coding settings, offering a scalable path to harder coding benchmarks.

entry.title: When Messages Go Wrong: Understanding Communication Faults in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jinhao Zhou, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jiongchi Yu, Fahao Chen, Jun Wu

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study of how communication faults (message loss, delay, context expiration, and semantic errors) manifest, propagate, and affect outcomes in LLM-based multi-agent systems, with a cross-layer taxonomy linking low-stack disturbances to agent-level effects. This fills a gap in systematic reliability analysis of multi-agent LLM deployments.

entry.title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL

author.name: Kaijie Zhu, Weixiang Yan, Omar Attia, Abbas Kazerouni, Alexander Toshev, Andrew Szot

entry.summary: LVRL uses an LLM's pretrained knowledge and in-context learning to estimate policy-aware state values for step-level credit assignment in agentic RL, avoiding the cost and instability of training a separate critic. It conditions the value model on group context and calibrates predictions using known values at initial and terminal states.

entry.title: Unfair and Unsafe: Everyday Bias Triggers Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Alex Mart\'i Guiu, Nicolas Zumarraga, Kevin O'Sullivan, Robert Jakob, Anna Hedstr\"om

entry.summary: This study shows that fine-tuning LLMs on politely expressed demographic stereotypes — everyday bias without overtly harmful language — can itself cause emergent misalignment on unrelated tasks. This extends EM research beyond previously studied data with explicit safety failures like insecure code, and matters because organizations routinely fine-tune on their own biased data.

entry.title: When Agent Evaluation Becomes Unreliable: An Empirical Study of Oracle Failures and Configuration-Dependent Measurement in an LLM Agent Benchmark

author.name: Junjie Chen

entry.summary: Audits LLM agent benchmark harnesses for reliability defects that leaderboard scores cannot reveal, introducing an oracle-integrity auditing method with five state-integrity invariants and three known-answer controls. Across 4,320 episodes the audit uncovers a reward-function defect that mutates environment state before scoring, materially changing outcome labels after repair.

entry.title: Fisher information and the geometry of memorization in neural networks

author.name: Daniel T. Bernstein, Chase Goddard, Luca Di Carlo, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab

entry.summary: Studies how Fisher information geometry separates generalizable structure from memorized noise in vision models trained on CIFAR-10 with controlled learnable-only-by-memorization noise. Projecting weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors decouples general task performance from noisy sample memorization, with the effect varying across layers and appearing in other settings as well.

entry.title: WorldRoPE: Probabilistic World-Centric Rotary Embedding for Multi-View Attention

author.name: Mijeong Kim, Kyujin Lim, Bohyung Han

entry.summary: WorldRoPE extends rotary positional embeddings to multi-view settings by back-projecting patch tokens into probabilistic volumetric Gaussian primitives in a shared world frame, capturing depth hypotheses and uncertainty. This enables proper cross-view correspondence in attention, which image-local RoPE coordinates cannot provide.

entry.title: Growing and Transferring Pathways for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haolin Tian, Yikang Li, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: GrowRL makes RL training compute reusable across models by freezing the pretrained LLM backbone and growing explicit attention and feed-forward pathway branches at each layer, updated only by RL with zero-initialized projections preserving the initial policy. The learned pathways remain transferable to structurally similar models, extending the value of expensive RL runs.

entry.title: REEL: Learning to Retrieve, Evaluate, and Evolve Visual Memory for Any Long-Horizon Multi-Shot Video Generation

author.name: Hang Xu, Guohui Zhang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Hu Yu, Jie Huang, Jiayin Xiao, Lin Song, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: REEL is a general-purpose visual-memory planner for long-horizon multi-shot video generation that learns to retrieve references, synthesize missing visual evidence, and update persistent memory through a unified tool interface. Backend-specific adapters let the same learned memory policy steer different black-box video generators, decoupling memory management from generator-specific interfaces.

entry.title: D2: High-Capability Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models from Half-Duplex Backbones

author.name: Cheng-Kuang Chang, Alexander H. Liu, Brian Kingsbury, Hilde Kuehne, Rogerio Feris, Samuel Thomas, James Glass, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Proposes D2, a framework converting pretrained half-duplex spoken language models into full-duplex models capable of simultaneous listening and speaking, via decoder-free representation distillation for streaming and supervised fine-tuning for duplex interaction. Applied to Qwen3-Omni and LLaMA-Omni 2, it achieves high turn-taking fidelity (e.g., 99.2% at 12.5Hz) while preserving general capabilities, with systematic study of chunk-size tradeoffs.

entry.title: Measuring Learned Equivariance: An Information Theoretic Approach

author.name: Claire Schlesinger, Wolfgang Gatterbauer, Robin Walters

entry.summary: The authors develop principled tests for whether networks trained with data augmentation actually learn equivariance, addressing the hard case of intermediate representations whose group actions are unspecified. They derive a normalized mutual information test in finite discrete settings and a scalable CKA-based test with exact guarantees for orthogonal transformations. Empirically, augmentation usually increases transformation consistency but does not guarantee it.

entry.title: The belief-action gap in language model agents

author.name: Ayse Sila Okcu, Weisheng Wang, Tongmeng Xie, Niall Dalton, Angelos Nalmpantis, Raghu Arghal, Mario Giulianelli

entry.summary: This study examines how state beliefs, action values, and action preferences interact as LM agents reason in text grid worlds, using report-based and representation-based probes plus inverse RL to estimate values. The key finding is that task-relevant state and value information is often represented more reliably than it is reflected in behavior, with decisions sharpening around a commitment point. This belief-action gap has implications for interpreting and improving agents.

entry.title: Taming Softmax at the Limits of Muon: A Unified Approach through Hilbert Geometry

author.name: Aditya Somasundaram, Charles Guille-Escuret, Alexander Moreno, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric Xing

entry.summary: The paper identifies that Muon's RMS-movement control on linear-layer outputs is a poor proxy for softmax modules, and proposes Hilbert distance as a natural metric bounding changes in output distributions and cross-entropy loss. Formulating steepest descent under this metric yields a unified treatment that tames softmax updates within the Muon optimizer family.

entry.title: DeltaTTG: Training Multi-Turn Agents with a Token-to-Go Progress Meter

author.name: Xuyan Ye, Xiyan Fu, Shengda Fan, Jiawei Cui, Yankai Lin, Wei Lu

entry.summary: This paper addresses the sparse-reward problem in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for multi-turn agents by introducing DeltaTTG, which learns a reusable progress signal via a shared progress meter. The supervision target, Token-to-Go (TTG), estimates the number of tokens remaining until task completion, serving as an observable proxy for remaining effort, and is learned cheaply from recorded trajectories of diverse policies without task-specific rules. This could meaningfully improve reward shaping for agentic RL without expensive evaluators or human annotation.

entry.title: From Token Correction to Claim Admission: Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hyeonggeun Han, Taehyun Cho, Sangwoo Hong

entry.summary: EGVCA is a training-free method that reduces object hallucination in vision-language models by admitting a claim only when its likelihood is sufficiently higher under the real image than under a visual-null input. It shows substantial gains on CHAIR, POPE, and MME across multiple LVLM backbones.

entry.title: I3L: Iterative Interactive Imitation Learning for Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Wensi Ai, Christopher Luey, Karthik Dharmarajan, Evans Han, Yunfan Jiang, Stef Ren, Jianwen Xie, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei, Ruohan Zhang

entry.summary: I3L is an integrated hardware-plus-learning system for whole-body mobile manipulation that pairs a low-cost open-source leader-arm interface (JoyLo+) supporting coordinated takeover corrections with iterative deployment and retraining. Operators can target the specific failure states of the current policy, closing the last-mile reliability gap.

entry.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Shenyi Li, Yilin Wang, Ziyun Cui, Bowen Zhou, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MMTA, a tri-modal benchmark pairing time series with text and real-world visual evidence across nine domains including robotics, healthcare, finance, and climate, with a 3,524-sample test split for classification and forecasting. It addresses the gap where prior multimodal benchmarks only paired temporal signals with text or visualizations derived from the same signal, testing whether multimodal LLMs can genuinely integrate time series with independent visual evidence.

entry.title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation

author.name: Yaoyang Liu, Shuwei Shen, Jincheng Tang, Jinguang Liu, Jinbao Xue, Hailong Yang, Ke Zhang, Yinjun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes BELT, a low-rank KV cache compression framework whose key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned global rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection in training and hard selection at deployment, achieving up to 70% compression with better quality and higher decoding throughput across three LLMs.

entry.title: Not All Drift Is a Mechanism: Tracing Prompt Adaptation in LLMs

author.name: Mikhail Aleksandrov, Nail Bashirov, Maksim Ivanov, Andrew Tsukanov, Timofey Karyagin, Alexander Miasnikov, Gleb Molodtsov, Valentin Samokhin, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: The authors study how discrete prompt optimization, prompt tuning, and prefix tuning mechanically alter computation in dense and mixture-of-experts LLMs, finding that adaptation location predicts how task information flows to output: optimized text changes response construction, input prompts shape content representations, and layer-wise prefixes retain direct control through residual streams.

entry.title: Do Factuality Methods Make LLMs More Factual? Reproducibility and Fair Comparison

author.name: Pratuat Amatya, Vinay Setty, V Venktesh, Avishek Anand

entry.summary: This paper presents the first independent reproduction of five factuality alignment methods for LLMs under a unified comparison framework, since prior methods were each evaluated with different base models, training data, judges, and metrics. The work addresses whether RLHF-style alignment approaches claiming to improve factuality actually do so when fairly tested. It matters because reproducibility failures in alignment research can misdirect follow-up work and deployment decisions.

entry.title: Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning

author.name: Haldun Balim, Yilun Du, Na Li

entry.summary: Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP) is a model-based decision-making framework that learns a generative model as a proposal distribution over action sequences: a diffusion prior samples candidate trajectories which are refined using learned dynamics, reward, and value models. This avoids solving high-dimensional trajectory optimization from scratch at each step while enabling long-horizon reasoning beyond value-function bootstrapping.

entry.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study

author.name: Mingxuan Yan, Litian Gong, Dihong Huang, Zhixu Li, Tianyu Zhang, Wenqian Zhang, Hefeifei Jiang, Peihao Li, Jian Zhang, Mengfei Zhao, Yikai Tang, Hai Zhai, Zehao Wang, Ruijian Liang, Yanjia Huang, Lin Shao, Changliu Liu, Kaiyu Hang, Zhiwen Fan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Jianfei Yang, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: This paper builds a benchmark using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks to study how demonstration quality should be exploited during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining. It compares weighting, filtering, and conditioning approaches across reward definitions and label granularities, finding that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning.

entry.title: Outcome-Routed Distillation and Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Wentao Lu, Tianyu Zhu, Jesse Clark

entry.summary: Develops a likelihood-free training pipeline for mixture-of-experts diffusion language models, combining verifier-based RL with on-policy distillation by routing rollout groups on verifier outcomes. Mixed groups use ratio-free group-centered REINFORCE, and fully failed groups receive dense KL supervision on teacher-generated denoising canvases, sidestepping unreliable ratio-based RL under bidirectional denoising.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following

author.name: Sangyeon Yoon, Wooseok Seo, Hamish Ivison, Hyesoo Hong, Donghoon Kim, Wonjun Kang, Albert No, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: The paper exposes an evaluation blind spot in verifiable instruction-following benchmarks, showing frontier models can earn full credit with little substantive answer content, and that using verifier criteria as RL rewards induces reward hacking in publicly released checkpoints. It proposes CALIF, a lightweight calibrated likelihood-based bonus added to verifier rewards to preserve response quality. This addresses a safety- and evaluation-critical problem in RLVR training.

entry.title: New Model, Old Habits: Behavior Transfer under Model Swapping in Multi-Session LLM Agents

author.name: Youngbin Choi, Sehyun Hwang, Suhyeon Jun, Seoyeon Lee, Sunghyun Choi, MoonJeong Park, Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: This work studies what happens when multi-session LLM agents switch underlying models while transferring conversation history. It reveals behavior transfer: recipient models adopt reasoning and action patterns from the models that generated their histories, strongest with raw histories and reduced by summarization. The proposed DASH summarization method preserves stronger-model behavior while minimizing weak-to-strong transfer, outperforming baselines under repeated swaps.

entry.title: When Does Depth Help? Understanding Layerwise Inference in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Wenwen Gong, Haotian Gu, Zhen Yang, Jiaying Ma, Hanqing Zhang, Zhongshen Wang, Jingjun Wang, Shouyi Xu, Wei Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies whether all layers of transformer-based tabular foundation models are needed, analyzing all 24 in-context-learning layers of TabPFN-3 across 272 classification datasets using representation geometry, truncation, and structural interventions. It finds that early-layer predictive accessibility does not imply later layers are dispensable for every input, clarifying which inputs benefit from deeper computation. This matters for making tabular foundation models cheaper and more interpretable via adaptive-depth inference.

entry.title: On the Convergence of Semi-Gradient TD: A Mean Field Perspective

author.name: Haruki Settai, Tadashi Kozuno, Shinji Ito

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes semi-gradient temporal-difference learning with two-layer neural networks in the mean-field regime, identifying a stability mechanism where entropy-induced relaxation dominates the sensitivity of the moving bootstrap target. Under this condition it proves exponential convergence to a unique fixed point and quantifies bias relative to the unregularized Bellman solution, extending results to entropy-regularized off-policy control via soft Q-learning. It provides rare convergence guarantees for TD with nonlinear function approximation.

entry.title: From Spectral to Frobenius: When Muon Loses Its Spectral Implicit Bias

author.name: Yongtao Wu, Mahdi Mansouri, Zhenyu Zhu

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that Muon's practical approximations to orthogonalization (finite Newton-Schulz iterations and a positive stabilization constant) cause it to select the Frobenius rather than spectral max-margin direction in linear classification, contradicting idealized analyses. The result extends to exponential moving average and Nesterov-style momentum variants via a summable perturbation argument.

entry.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization

author.name: Dwaipayan Haldar, Indranil Patra, Azhar Yousuf, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula

entry.summary: This paper introduces SpectrumQuant, a closed-form method for constructing orthogonal rotations for low-bit LLM quantization. Instead of fixed Hadamard transforms or learned calibration-time rotations, it derives a principled criterion from maximizing covariance, showing this leads to spectral alignment, and estimates activation covariance from calibration data to build quantization-friendly rotations. This matters because efficient low-bit deployment of large models is a key practical bottleneck.

entry.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kaixiang Zhao, Tianrun Yu, Shangzhe Li, Yuxiao Yang, Amanda Hughes, Weitong Zhang, Taylor W. Killian

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode of on-policy distillation called recoverability: teachers often follow student errors on incorrect rollouts even though they recognize them. CriticOPD has the teacher critique an incorrect rollout so the student can rewrite past the error, using the critique as privileged information for scoring while the student trains on the critique-free revision. Evaluated on Qwen3 students across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks with consistent gains.

entry.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena

author.name: Soovadeep Bakshi, Apurba Bose, Aishwarya Bose, Sandip Nandi

entry.summary: Analyzing 1.8 million Chatbot Arena votes, this paper shows the Bradley-Terry ranking model violates Luce's choice axiom for near-copy models: votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times more decisive than predicted, with consistent multipliers for same-generation and same-lab comparisons, robust to ties, topics, and timing. A small four-to-six parameter correction predicts held-out votes better than standard Bradley-Terry. This has direct implications for the validity of the most-watched LLM leaderboard.

entry.title: L3M: A Verifiable Harness and Runtime for Self-Extending and Self-Improving Agents

author.name: Carson Eisenach, Robert Joseph George, Vincent Quenneville-Belair, Kate Gwimm, Dean Foster

entry.summary: L3M is a runtime for self-extending, self-improving agents built in Lean 4, premised on the observation that human attention is the only non-scaling participant in agent computation, so the harness must remove humans from inner loops while remaining verifiable. It structures long-horizon work across calls, tools, external systems, multiple agents, and agent-written code under a single verifiable language. This targets a core safety and capability question for autonomous agents: compounding gains without continuous human oversight.

entry.title: Articulation Upper Bounds for Language Models

author.name: Alexander Spangher, Daniel E. Ho, Diyi Yang, Noah Goodman, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: This paper measures the limits of language as a communication channel between LLMs, introducing a prompt-optimization algorithm that beats prior methods by up to 14% and a transmission measure where a receiver model attempts to recover a sender's labeling prompt. Findings track how concepts transmit as model capability scales and correlate with human label error.

entry.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation For Robot Policies

author.name: Motasem Alfarra, Pietro Mazzaglia, Markus Peschl, Daniel Dijkman, Christos Louizos

entry.summary: The paper studies reward-free, self-supervised test-time adaptation of pretrained locomotion policies under deployment shifts such as slippery terrain or payload changes. Building on a lightweight actor-only baseline with a frozen critic as a performance surrogate, it introduces TEMPO, an entropy-regularized memory-guided policy optimization method that stabilizes adaptation under on-device constraints.

entry.title: ActiveEvidence: Decision-Focused Evidence Graphs with Verifiable Acquisition Gaps

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Peng Zhang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: This paper formalizes active evidence acquisition for multimodal agents, addressing when visual observations are worth paying for under a free-metadata/paid-observation boundary with stochastic costs. It introduces a Counterfactual Evidence Interaction Graph that captures evidence value, second-order interactions, and conditional harm, with a decision-weighted objective that refines only interactions capable of changing the final action. This matters for cost-aware, certifiable agent decision-making in interactive perception settings.

entry.title: How to Evaluate When You Don't Know How to Evaluate? Choosing Reliable Setups for Base Language Model Benchmarking

author.name: Shenbin Qian, David Samuel, Jind\v{r}ich Helcl, Andrey Kutuzov, Stephan Oepen

entry.summary: This paper tackles the many unstated design decisions in LLM benchmarking by comparing eight evaluation setup aspects using three meta-measures: monotonicity, non-randomness, and ranking consistency across intermediate checkpoints. Experiments cover 26 monolingual 2B-parameter models in an early pretraining scenario. The result is practical, empirically grounded guidance for reliable base model evaluation, which directly affects pretraining decisions.

entry.title: LLM-jp-4 Technical Report

author.name: LLM-jp, :, Chaoran Liu, Daisuke Kawahara, Hideyuki Tachibana, Hirokazu Kiyomaru, Jun Suzuki, Koshi Eguchi, Kouta Nakayama, Qianying Liu, Rio Yokota, Ryo Takahashi, Sadao Kurohashi, Sosuke Hosokawa, Taishi Nakamura, Takashi Kodama, Yun-Ang Wu, Yusuke Miyao, Yusuke Oda

entry.summary: This technical report introduces LLM-jp-4, a family of Japanese sovereign LLMs consisting of an 8B dense model and a 32B-A3B mixture-of-experts model, both trained from scratch on roughly 12 trillion tokens. The work emphasizes transparency and reproducibility by publishing explicit criteria for training data, external models, and software choices, and reports substantial gains over prior LLM-jp models with competitive performance against similarly sized open-weight models. It matters as a major open, fully documented sovereign-model effort for Japan, offering a rare end-to-end reproducible training recipe.

entry.title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Linji Hao, Yanji He, Zihan Wang, Hansi Yang, Jiayuan Zhang, Hongyan Hao, Qi Gu, Yan Feng, Han Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Interlock, a task-synthesis framework that represents long-horizon agent tasks as typed completion graphs with grounding edges and coupling hyperedges to enforce cross-step dependencies. It targets the completion gap where agents satisfy individual requirements but produce locally correct yet globally incomplete outcomes.

entry.title: Gray-Box Hallucination Detection in LLMs with Token Identities

author.name: Shaked Goldshtein, Yitzchak Grunbaum, Fabrizio Frasca, Guy Bar-Shalom, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: GURI improves gray-box hallucination detection by incorporating token identities, not just probability-derived statistics, allowing detectors to distinguish what a model is uncertain about rather than merely how uncertain it is. This avoids requiring white-box hidden-state access that frontier model APIs do not provide.

entry.title: $\tau$-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions

author.name: Rishitosh Kumar Singh, Amir Saeidi, Shamanthak Hegde, Shrinidhi Kumbhar, Chitta Baral

entry.summary: This paper introduces tau-Emotion-Bench, a ten-domain benchmark for evaluating tool-calling LLM agents under emotionally variable user interactions, filling a gap left by benchmarks that assume cooperative, stable users. It also contributes Tracer, a scalable pipeline for generating grounded tasks and interaction trajectories that can support both evaluation and training.

entry.title: Long-horizon Video Generation with Slot Memory Addressed By Region Tokens

author.name: Eren Cetin, Julius Erbach, Vukasin Bozic, Hyojun Go, Zixiang Zhao, Nikolai Kalischek, Federico Tombari, Konrad Schindler, Dominik Narnhofer

entry.summary: SMART introduces a slot memory addressed by region tokens for long-horizon video generation, combining bounded constant-size storage with spatially addressed recall. This bridges reconstruction-based memories (precise but growing storage) and recurrent memories (bounded but fading), enabling recovery of scene content when the camera revisits a location.

entry.title: NavAble: A Large-Scale Dataset and Synthetic Data Generation Pipeline for Blind Navigation

author.name: Hochul Hwang, Jahir Sadik Monon, Soowan Yang, Shiven Umeshbhai Patel, Anh Nhat Hong Nguyen, Kien Nguyen, Keshav Garg, Dylan Gage, Duretti Hordofaa, Anshu Anjna, Eshed Ohn-Bar, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: NavAble provides a large-scale dataset of 11 accessibility-critical object classes (audible pedestrian signals, door buttons, handrails) with 41K curated plus 8K newly annotated real images, plus a synthetic data generation pipeline for scale and diversity. It targets assistive navigation for blind and low-vision users, filling a major gap in existing vision datasets.

entry.title: What Breaks in Multi-Image Schema Application? Factorial Oracle Interventions Reveal an Instance-Information Bottleneck

author.name: Yiliu Xu, Xinjin Li, Yu Ma

entry.summary: Using a controlled task requiring locating characters across 16 images and consulting a visual codebook, the authors introduce a within-item 2x2 factorial oracle design that separates schema knowledge from target-appearance representation. Across 1,188 analyzed responses, supplying verified appearance representations (Oracle-B) raised strict accuracy by 54.6 points, identifying an instance-information bottleneck.

entry.title: Generative World Simulation with DAO and JING

author.name: XGEN Team, Guohao Cai, Haoxuan Che, Frank Fan, Chenran Huang, Junjia Huang, Jiayi Jiang, Yanheng Li, Leon Liu, Shaoteng Liu, Xi Liu, Feng Nie, Zhefan Rao, An Wang, Hanwen Wang, Pengxiang Yan, Jieming Yu, Qian Zha, Wentao Zheng

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces a generative world simulation framework combining DAO, a computable world engine that tracks persistent state for characters, objects, spaces, and their relationships, with JING, an egocentric model that generates continuous first-person audiovisual experience conditioned on that evolving state. The system supports sustained interaction by both humans and agents while preserving the consequences of past actions. It matters because persistent, interactive world models are a key step toward scalable simulation environments for training and evaluating embodied agents.

entry.title: BluePixel: Toward Native 4K Agentic Image Editing

author.name: Shanyan Guan, Shiyu Li, Xin Li, Zhizhou Chen, Yunzhe Xu, Yuehao Liu, Ruixue Shen, Shiju Zhang, Min Jin, Qiang Liu, Junbo Liu, Penggang Shi, Sheng Sun, Xiao Wang, Yong Zhang, Zhongang Qi, Wei Li, Chao Ma, Ying Tai, Yanhao Ge

entry.summary: BluePixel argues native 4K instruction-driven image editing is a system problem, coupling a native-4K editing model with an agent harness and disclosing the complete training recipe. Key techniques include progressive VAE adaptation to make 4K training affordable from a 1K-pretrained editor, addressing parametric precision, expert matching, and vague user instructions.

entry.title: What Matters for World Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models?

author.name: Qisen Ma, Yixiang Chen, Yuan Xu, Peiyan Li, Jiabing Yang, Kai Wang, Jianhua Yang, Jianlou Si, Jun Huang, Jing Liu, Nianfeng Liu, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

entry.summary: This systematic study disentangles design choices when integrating world models into VLAs by categorizing existing work into four paradigms (Implicit Future Alignment, Explicit Future Query, MoT Future Expert, External World Predictor) and instantiating all within a unified framework. It evaluates across varied world representations and policy backbones to identify what actually drives effectiveness.

entry.title: DexMimic: A Generalist Dexterous Hand-Object Tracking Policy via Value-Guided Reset Allocation

author.name: Zhexi Luo, Zhixuan Xu, Rui Yang, Zeyu Xiao, Yiwen Hou, Lin Shao

entry.summary: DexMimic trains a single generalist policy for dexterous hand-object tracking across diverse human hand-object interaction trajectories, replacing the usual one-policy-per-trajectory approach. Its key mechanism, Value-Guided Reset Allocation, adaptively chooses rollout starting states to focus training on difficult undertrained phases. This is a meaningful step toward scalable dexterous skill learning from human data.

entry.title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Jia-Ning Li, Yinzhou Tang, Yanzhao Yu, Biao Wu, Meng Fang, Xin Li, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why pretrained VLA models that achieve 80% success on atomic manipulation drop to 19% when skills compose into long-horizon mobile manipulation, identifying failure regimes in planning, navigation/base positioning, and local manipulation. Based on this analysis, it builds a failure-guided agentic framework that improves composed-task success.

entry.title: MorphAct: Robot Policies Morphing with the Worlds They Act In

author.name: Ziyan Liu, Jiting Liu, Weihong Zhong, Wenda Yu, Yeqiu Chen, Jason Li, Xiaojiang Peng, Shuyuan Hu, Kai Wang, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: MorphAct proposes contextual parameterization of robot policies, dynamically adjusting policy parameters as interaction contexts change instead of using one fixed shared parameter set. The authors show with atomic-task diagnostics that competing update directions across tasks cause under-adaptation, and introduce coupled generators producing context-dependent parameter adjustments.

entry.title: PingpongDuo: Agile Humanoid Table Tennis Doubles with Safe Team Coordination

author.name: Haoran Jiang, Yichao Zhong, Kai Zhang, Cheng Liu, Yixuan Pan, Zhenjie Yang, Jingbo Wang, Tianyu Li, Li Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical framework enabling two humanoid robots to play table tennis doubles, where teammates must alternate strikes in a shared workspace. A team-level planner jointly selects positioning targets using learned risk estimates to avoid collisions, while individual-level footwork and striking skills are guided by human motion references. It demonstrates agile multi-robot coordination with explicit safety reasoning in a dynamic physical task.

entry.title: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 presents HiRO-ACEv2, a system that captures extreme rain, wind, and pressure events at 3 km global resolution at roughly 1/300th the computational cost of the X-SHiELD conventional model, making kilometer-scale climate simulation accessible to far more researchers.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Latent Influence: Patch-Level Training Sample Attribution for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Laura Yao, Shixing Yu, Jie Peng, Promit Ghosal, Kyra Gan, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces MOSAIC, a method for patch-level training-sample attribution in vision-language models using shared sparse image-text latent spaces learned via multimodal orthogonalized sparse autoencoders. Combined with EK-FAC influence decomposition, it grounds influence explanations in spatial image regions aligned to describing phrases.

entry.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training

author.name: Hao Li, Keqing He, Longtao Zheng, Junlong Li, Weihao Zeng, Qian Liu, Yuzhen Huang

entry.summary: ProgAgent provides a full training stack for Programmatic Tool Calling, where agents invoke tools via executable code and keep intermediate results in runtime variables rather than in context, avoiding context rot in long-horizon tasks. It constructs verifiable training tasks to move PTC from an inference-time trick to a trained capability.

entry.title: PopGen: Generating Semantically Diverse Populations for Zero-Shot Coordination

author.name: Paul Teiletche, Kanghyun Ryu, Kyungjoon Park, Dhruva Tirumala, Markus Wulfmeier, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: PopGen uses LLMs to generate semantically diverse training partners for multi-agent reinforcement learning, producing textual descriptions of distinct agent behaviors and translating them into executable code policies. This replaces trajectory-level diversity proxies that can mislabel distinct trajectories of the same strategy as diverse, improving zero-shot coordination with unseen partners.

entry.title: Beyond Perfect Teammates: Multi-Agent Collaboration with Unreliable Colleagues

author.name: Chen Huang, Yiyang Zhang, Yuhao Wu, Yang Deng, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the implicit perfect-colleague assumption in LLM multi-agent systems and introduces UnCoBench, a benchmark organizing collaborator failures such as irrelevant answers, insufficient detail, and non-response. It separates task-solving competence from the ability to recover from an unreliable evidence-gathering process.

entry.title: Does a Hosted Decision Model Respect Irrelevant Alternatives? A Pre-Registered Test of Option-Set Dependence in Jev

author.name: Dushyant Rajput (AltSlate Labs LLP), Nirdesh Chauhan (AltSlate Labs LLP), Siddharth Kosaraju (AltSlate Labs LLP)

entry.summary: A pre-registered study testing whether a hosted decision model, jev-1.13.0, satisfies independence of irrelevant alternatives, using nearly 300,000 calls on classification tasks. Results show every added option systematically shifts the log-odds between the gold label and the strongest rival by 0.20-0.52 nats, exceeding run-to-run variation, undermining treating model probabilities as intrinsic properties of options.

entry.title: MADDIE: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Engine

author.name: Ye Liu, Reza Averly, Avery Meyer, Frazier N. Baker, Ruoxi Gao, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Xia Ning

entry.summary: Presents MADDIE, a multi-agent LLM drug discovery system designed to run iterative, non-linear discovery campaigns, addressing the poor scaling of single-agent systems on long-horizon tasks and the rigidity of predefined multi-agent workflows. The system autonomously operates in silico tools that normally demand substantial medicinal chemistry expertise.

entry.title: VL-DocIR: A Benchmark for Vision-Based Long Document Information Retrieval

author.name: Simon Ott, Yufan Chen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiale Wei, Di Wen, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: VL-DocIR is a large-scale benchmark for evidence-complete visual long-document retrieval, built from nearly 30,000 documents rendered into over 388,000 page images, with about 272,000 queries spanning multi-page and cross-document evidence structures. It exposes the gap between short-document leaderboard performance and realistic retrieval needs.

entry.title: Size Generalization for Diffusion Routing Solvers

author.name: Barak Itzchak Davidovitch, Eli Meirom, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik
