entry.summary: ResizeCO is a label-free approach for size generalization in diffusion-based combinatorial routing solvers, using reinforcement learning on large unsolved instances to adapt a model trained on smaller solved ones. It tackles both the statistical shift of larger instances and the compute challenge of scaling inference.

entry.title: Beyond Bias Scores: Answerability Confounds in Activation Steering with Gradient-Constrained Direction Design (GCD)

author.name: Weitong Li, Donglin Song, Junkai Lin, Xi Xuan

entry.summary: The authors show that bias scores on benchmarks like BBQ conflate what a model prefers with whether it answers at all, and that contrastive activation steering often lowers the ambiguous bias score via the answerability channel rather than reducing actual preference bias. Across five models and 99 configurations, the answerability channel accounts for over half the score change in 17% of cases and the entire change in 11%. They propose gradient-constrained direction design (GCD) to steer preference without shifting answer rates.

entry.title: Instructions Are Evidence, Not Objectives: Measuring Outcome Alignment of Agents

author.name: Kaiming Liu, Yuxuan Liu, Jinrui Ju, Minyuan Ruan, Xuanyu Lei, Peng Li, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Argues that user instructions to LLM agents should be treated as evidence about true requirements rather than as the objective itself, since initial instructions are frequently incomplete: in 100 SWE-chat trajectories, 56% omitted requirements that later proved necessary, and 52% of follow-up requirements were inferable from the project. The paper proposes measuring outcome alignment against inferred true requirements. This reframing matters for agent design, since literal instruction-following can systematically miss unstated but necessary requirements.

entry.title: ECMR: Evidence-Aware Deliberation Control for Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai

entry.summary: Studies semantic false consensus in multi-agent LLM systems: a confident group answer supported by narrow, duplicated, or correlated rationales rather than independent confirmation. It introduces ECMR, an evidence-aware controller over frozen role-conditioned LLMs that tracks answer concentration, support diversity and independence, contradictions, and remaining budget to choose among propose, challenge, verify, arbitrate, diversify, correct, or stop actions. This matters because fixed deliberation protocols mistake repetition for agreement and waste compute.

entry.title: LifeSearch: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents for Real-World Life and Productivity

author.name: Yibo Wang, Senjie Jin, Yansong Ning, Xinbing Liang, Haotian Luo, Jiazheng Zhang, Yuxuan He, Will Wu, Clarenceai

entry.summary: LifeSearch is a benchmark of 203 Chinese and English tasks from real-user queries across seven life and productivity domains, targeting deep research agents that perform multi-step search and evidence synthesis. It includes over 4,500 hours of annotation and 4,000+ expert-written rubrics covering both report quality and concrete verifiable values. It fills the gap left by benchmarks focused on academic or synthetic research tasks.

entry.title: To Align or Not To Align: Check Your COMPASS Before You Train

author.name: Fabian Gr\"oger, Petar Damjanovi\'c, Maria Brbi\'c

entry.summary: COMPASS is a theoretically motivated diagnostic that predicts whether two pretrained models will be compatible before costly alignment or merging. It decomposes compatibility into k-NN overlap-based pair-specific ease and a pairwise-independent axis, exploiting the observation that representational convergence is most robust in local neighborhoods.

entry.title: OPMD: On-Policy Mechanism Distillation Beyond Output Supervision

author.name: Yingdong Shi, Zhihong Li, Changming Li, Jingyi Yu, Quan Li, Kan Ren

entry.summary: The paper identifies that on-policy distillation only supervises student outputs, not the intermediate computation producing them, and proposes OPMD to transfer teacher-derived intermediate computation while accounting for its compatibility with the student's geometry. This goes beyond naive representation matching by ensuring hidden-state transfer is usable by subsequent computation.

entry.title: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study

author.name: Ruomeng Ding, Qianli Shen, Zhaoyang Han, Meixin Chen, Daoyuan Chen, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: The authors present an Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework in which LLM agents iteratively design data selection, reward, and curriculum strategies for training other LLMs, using cumulative experimental feedback. Across four tasks including math and code data selection, agent-developed strategies generalize to held-out benchmarks under fixed training protocols.

entry.title: Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion

author.name: Yifan Shen, Yewei Xia, Gongxu Luo, Peiyuan Zhu, Boyang Sun, Zhenhao Chen, Guangyi Liu, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video diffusion by attaching lightweight offset-specific heads that predict chunks at multiple future temporal offsets beyond the next chunk. This improves quality maintenance over extended rollouts.

entry.title: TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents

author.name: Pramod Kumar, Raj Kumar Pandey

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes 600 public coding-agent trajectories and finds that median tool observations are small (118-286 tokens), with the large build logs usually cited to motivate observation compression appearing only near the 99th percentile, while 98.6% of input tokens come from cache. The authors argue that efficiency gains in coding agents should focus on reducing loop turns rather than compressing observations. This reframes 'loop engineering' as the practical lever for agent cost reduction.

entry.title: E8 Lattice Key Quantization for Low-Bit KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Sasho Nedelkoski, Alexander Acker, Soeren Becker, Dominik Scheinert, Odej Kao

entry.summary: The paper shows that 2-bit keys and 2-bit values for KV-cache compression can preserve near-baseline quality by using E8 lattice-based vector quantization for keys, exploiting cross-dimension correlations to exceed the SQNR of independent scalar quantization. This matters for memory-efficient long-context LLM serving where 2-bit scalar quantization is unstable.

entry.title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding

author.name: Guowen Zhang, Boshen Xu, Zihao Yue, Ziheng Wang, Xiaokun Liu, Xin Tao, Wenyu Qin, Pengfei Wan, Qin Jin

entry.summary: Proposes EventLens, a video MLLM trained with event-structure reinforcement learning to recover temporal structure such as event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. It attributes existing failures to caption-style post-training supervision that lets models exploit language shortcuts instead of visual temporal grounding.

entry.title: Davinci-Tool: Scaling Agentic Tool-Use Supervision with Verifiable Executable Environments

author.name: Xiaoyang Yuan, Ji Zhao, Xingyu Hu, Wenhan Wang, Yutao Hu, Qiaosheng Zhang, Pengfei Liu, Yu Qiao, Yi Bin, Wenqi Shao

entry.summary: Davinci-Tool is a 30B tool-use model accompanied by Davinci-ToolData, an execution-grounded dataset that scales environment coverage and outcome verification together, preserving restorable states, execution traces, outcomes, and verifiers. Two pipelines populate the substrate: Execution-Grounded synthesis and complementary trajectory generation.

entry.title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation

author.name: Zekun Shi, Alastair James Arthur Price

entry.summary: Introduces FreeSolo, a native sparse attention mechanism combining a short-range sliding window with a long-range branch selecting keypoint cells for direct token attention, offering linear-time variants (FS-L with short continued pretraining for prefix pruning; FS-B without) that achieve zero-shot length extrapolation beyond trained context without costly full continued pretraining.

entry.title: Learning to Detect Shifts in Unstructured Data Streams via Monitoring-by-Betting

author.name: Siyu Zhou, Jialin Ouyang, Fan Xia, Adarsh Subbaswamy, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Augusto Garcia-Agundez, Sarah Pollet, Jinoos Yazdany, Patrick Vossler, Jean Feng

entry.summary: This paper addresses monitoring generative AI systems for distribution shifts in unstructured data, where pre-specifying discrepancy measures creates a sensitivity-breadth trade-off. Using a betting-based framework, the authors allow adaptive hypothesizing of shift directions while preserving false-alarm guarantees that data-dependent adaptation would normally invalidate. The work has clinical AI applications given the author team from Hopkins and UCSF.

entry.title: CoCA: Criterion-Aware Credit Assignment for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guangcheng Zhu, Yingfan Ma, Xing Zheng, Haobo Wang, Shenzhi Yang, Kai Tang, Zhengqing Zang, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: CoCA reframes rubric-based RL for open-ended LLM tasks as criterion-aware credit assignment, using rubric information as a relevance cue to allocate credit at the criterion level rather than compressing feedback into scalar rewards. This avoids reward degradation seen in self-distillation approaches that treat rubrics as privileged targets.

entry.title: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation

author.name: Xu Liu, Hanshu Yan, Taha Aksu, Quang Pham, Zhongzheng Qiao, Jun Hao Liew, Silvio Savarese, Doyen Sahoo, Junnan Li

entry.summary: GIFT-Eval-CTX is a benchmark of 10,000 instances across 20 datasets for evaluating contextual time-series forecasting, where models must translate verified future information (planned events, expert expectations) into accurate numerical trajectories. It addresses shortcomings of prior benchmarks that lack standardized splits or verified informative text.

entry.title: AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Imaging for Intraoperative Detection of Low-Grade Glioma: A Clinical Study

author.name: Siri Willems, Ishika Jain, Jens De Winne, Siri Luthman, Hamed Zivari Adab, Roeland Vandebriel, Anna Alperovich, Xiaohan Zhang, Ben Stoffelen, Tom De Schepper, Lien Solie, Steven De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: A clinical study using AI-enhanced hyperspectral imaging to detect low-grade gliomas intraoperatively, a setting where tumors strongly resemble healthy brain under white light and existing navigation tools are costly or insensitive. It characterizes spectral differences between healthy and tumor tissue and provides a paired comparison of HSI-based detection against current techniques.

entry.title: Correcting or Continuing? What On-Policy Distillation Learns from Student Errors

author.name: Shuo Yang, Zheyu Zhang, Mahito Sugiyama, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: Asks whether on-policy distillation improves a student when training is restricted to problems it currently fails, evaluating five OPD mechanisms with Qwen-3 and Phi-4 under a unified competition-math protocol. The consistent negative finding is that OPD does not improve accuracy on this hard subset, with all eight configurations degrading performance despite falling training KL, while the same pipeline improves performance on solvable problems.

entry.title: JevGPT: Thinking Fast and Slow in Autonomous Research

author.name: Yasheng Sun, Yanning Dai, Yimeng Chen, Nanbo Li, Firas Laakom, Yifan Xu, Piotr Pi\k{e}kos, Mateusz Ostaszewski, Wenyi Wang, Cheng Luo, Yuhui Wang, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: JevGPT presents a dual-system architecture for autonomous research agents, coupling a deliberative System Two that sets evidence objectives with a fast System One that locates support and assesses relevance in parallel. The design aims to close the gap between retrieval coverage and the evidence actually used in research decisions under limited budgets.

entry.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards

author.name: Yunkai Zhan, Miaosen Chai, Shangshang Wang, Jike Zhong, Yuqing Yang, Deqing Fu, Serina Chang, Wang Bill Zhu

entry.summary: PreciseCoder analyzes what unit-test-only RL rewards teach code-debugging models and finds they encourage excessive editing and hallucinated bugs in correct code. The proposed algorithm augments unit-test rewards with a signal for semantically verified, localized edits, reducing average edit lines from 7-15 to 3 at comparable pass rates across 4B-27B models, and generalizes beyond single-line bugs despite training only on those.

entry.title: Narrowing the Collaboration Gap, Probably

author.name: Mirah Shi, Marcel Hussing, Ira Globus-Harris, Natalie Collina, Aaron Roth, Surbhi Goel

entry.summary: Studies multi-agent LLM communication and shows, theoretically and empirically, that agents exchanging calibrated beliefs over actions can be strictly more powerful than exchanging only proposed actions, since identical actions may hide decision-relevant differences in uncertainty. Analysis is grounded in a synthetic multi-round reasoning setting under partial information.

entry.title: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation

author.name: Liam Davis, Romain Emil-Popescu, Suman Jana

entry.summary: Shows that jailbreak attack success rates can shift by up to 82 percentage points merely by changing the judge LLM, exposing a major evaluation reliability problem. Proposes the semantic reconstruction game, a training-free evaluator that reconstructs the request implied by a response's substantive content and compares it against decoy requests to judge compliance.

entry.title: On Global Joint Lower Bounds in Zeroth-Order Nonconvex Optimization

author.name: Yuxuan Xia, Xiao-Tong Yuan

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves an open question from Kornowski and Shamir about whether the O(d * delta^-1 * epsilon^-3) oracle complexity for zeroth-order nonsmooth nonconvex optimization is jointly optimal in all parameters. The authors establish a matching scalar-oracle lower bound of Omega(d * L0^2 * min{...}) for smooth stochastic nonconvex optimization in the unrestricted full-space setting. This settles the joint optimality of dimension and accuracy dependence for gradient-free methods.

entry.title: When Non-Adversarial Noise Hurts Learning: Benchmarking Skill Self-Evolution in Agents

author.name: Tao Yu, Zhongtian Luo, Yuchen Long, Yiheng Lu, Yuxuan Zhou, Yanpei Gong, Siyi Cao, Yuqing Wu, Haopeng Jin, Zhenghao Zhang, Yujia Yang, Jingmin Zhu, Yunyun Hou, Xinming Wang, Hongzhu Yi, Jiachen Liu, Sirui Wang, Nan Duan, Yan Huang, Liang Wang, Tianjin Huang, Yanyan Zou

entry.summary: RSE-Bench is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agent skill self-evolution under ordinary, non-adversarial noise, spanning four domains and six benchmarks with controlled perturbations to instructions, evidence, execution records, and outcome-record pairings. It isolates noise during learning from noise after skills are frozen, revealing how errors persist in reusable learned rules. This fills a real gap in understanding agent robustness during self-improvement.

entry.title: From Plato to Aristotle: Toward a General Theory of Representation Hypotheses

author.name: Dai Shi, Andi Han, Xiaoyu Li, Luke Thompson, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato

entry.summary: The paper unifies competing views on representation convergence (Platonic, Aristotelian, and neighborhood/spanning-tree-based alignment criteria) by showing they sit at different points of a single lattice, formalized as the Lattice Representation Hypothesis. Under this lens, Platonic convergence is agreement at the lattice top while its supporting evidence derives from low-level neighbor overlap criteria.

entry.title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains

author.name: Wei-Liang Liu, Cheng-Yen Tsai

entry.summary: This paper exposes a verifiability gap in the quantized LLM supply chain: model signing authenticates full-precision weights, but users run quantized artifacts whose producing transformation is undisclosed. Introducing the Independent Verifiability Rate, the authors find that across the 198 in-scope most-downloaded Hugging Face GGUF repositories, none record their build environment, yielding a 0/198 bit-for-bit re-derivation rate under a recorded-inputs protocol, though in-sample artifacts can be reproduced when the environment is known. The work has clear security and supply-chain integrity implications.

entry.title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning

author.name: Lorenzo Venturoli, Nedko Savov, Xi Wang, Marc Pollefeys, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: StateCraft decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state in video world models, conditioning visual generation on a symbolic record of entity changes so long-horizon interactions remain consistent. This addresses the problem that past visual observations become stale after sequences of actions.

entry.title: CAFE: Confining Feature Distillation to Language-Routed Adapters for Compact Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Tianchi Liu, Nicholas Moratelli, Khurram Azeem Hashmi, Mohammadreza Zolfaghari, Rishabh Jain, Louis Lu, Changdae Park, Amril Nazir

entry.summary: This ASR paper analyzes why common feature distillation losses fail in compact multilingual ASR: projection-based loss gradients are orthogonal to the task gradient, while CKA gradients are weakly aligned and overlap 97.5-99.5% with the subspace English uses, improving non-English WER at English's expense. Guided by this gradient diagnosis, it proposes confining feature distillation to language-routed adapters. The diagnostic analysis is as valuable as the resulting method.

entry.title: Do Syntax Heads Influence Model Behavior?

author.name: William Timkey, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: This interpretability study asks whether attention heads specialized for syntax play a causal role in transformer language models' syntactic predictions. Using careful interventions, including forcing heads to attend to distractor nouns, the authors find evidence is mixed to negative: predictions often remain consistent with the subject despite distractor attention, and syntax-head interventions beat random heads on only one of two measures. This challenges common causal claims in mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Share the Symbol, Not the Vector: Training-Free Fact Communication Across Language Models

author.name: Xin Li, Mengbing Liu, Hao Jiang, Xin Gao, Annan Wang, Xingwei Qu, Yichi Zhang, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: Introduces SYNC, a word-indexed interface allowing heterogeneous LLMs to communicate facts without fine-tuning or learned translators: the sender selects words from a shared list and sends indices, and the receiver writes those facts into its own hidden states using its own word embeddings. This sidesteps cross-architecture state compatibility assumptions in multi-agent communication.

entry.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents

author.name: Peidong Wang, Ying Chang, Zhiming Ma, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Daqi Liu, Yuzhe Yang, Xu Cao, Chuang Wang, Jian Su, Daling Wang

entry.summary: AdaRSI is an on-demand recursive self-improvement framework for embodied agents that first improves skills and harness via a coding agent, then attributes persistent failures by retrying failing sub-steps, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable. This directly addresses the question of when self-improving systems should change executor weights versus adjust how they are called.

entry.title: SaTPO: Text-to-Image Safety Alignment via Transition Preference Optimization

author.name: Ziyi Fang, Jingzhi Li, Xiaojun Jia, Xingxing Wei, Wenqi Ren, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: SaTPO performs safety alignment of text-to-image diffusion models at the step level during denoising, using the insight that an unsafe prompt and its safe rewrite form a tightly coupled preference pair under a shared parent state and noise realization. Anchoring optimization on identical parent states confines safety adjustments narrowly, preserving useful generation capability.

entry.title: Paraphrase Consensus Is Not Self-Consistency: Instruction Reliance and Robustness in VLA Policies

author.name: Hanlong Li, Sihan Tan, Takeshi Ashizawa, Benjamin Yen, Kazuhiro Nakadai

entry.summary: This paper shows that fine-tuned VLA policies like OpenVLA are brittle to instruction rewording — paraphrasing costs up to 38 success points — and that test-time prompt ensembling techniques borrowed from language models fail to recover the loss. Paraphrase consensus can even hurt, revealing a mismatch between aggregation intuitions from LLMs and VLA behavior. It exposes an important evaluation flaw in standard VLA benchmarks that reuse fixed instruction strings.

entry.title: PolyMorph: Learning Locomotion Policy for Cross-Embodiment Adaptation

author.name: Hyunsik Oh, Seunghun Jeon, Donghoon Youm, Jungwoo Hur, Hyeongjun Kim, Jeong Hyun Lee, Moonkyu Jung, Jemin Hwangbo

entry.summary: PolyMorph learns a single morphology-conditioned locomotion policy that transfers across heterogeneous legged robots with varying leg counts and joint configurations by converting URDFs into joint-link modules processed by a recurrent encoder, graph-based Transformer, and per-joint decoder. Training stability is supported via morphology-normalized rewards, adaptive robot sampling, and URDF-derived PD-gain initialization.

entry.title: Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning with Human Interventions for Precise Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Xiaoman Li, Zhiqiang Yang, Jiayu Hu, Jipeng Kong, Yang Zhang, Jingwei Zhang, Fangzheng Yan, Chunhua Shen, Chenjia Bai

entry.summary: GR-BC is an offline iterative post-training framework for VLAs that builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph over demonstrations and rollouts, including failed episodes with human interventions. Reverse graph search computes minimal remaining steps to weight which action chunks genuinely advance the task, rather than uniformly cloning or discarding imperfect trajectories.

entry.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function

author.name: Shawheen Naderi, Fatemeh Akherati, Yubei Chen

entry.summary: Using counterfactual interventions in the Crafter environment, the authors show that the value function of a model-free PPO agent encodes world-model-like concepts such as diamond collectibility rules and health dynamics. They discuss safety implications of visualizing what value functions learn and limitations of current RL agents.

entry.title: AlignPoison: Conditional Targeted Poisoning of Generative Recommenders via Decoding-Aligned Prefixes

author.name: Zhuoxuan Zhang, Jinhao Duan, Xinyu Zhao, Jinduo Guo, Shuai Shao, Rui Li, Luke Simon, Zhun Deng, Tianlong Chen, Bo Sun

entry.summary: The paper shows that generative autoregressive recommenders are vulnerable to conditional targeted poisoning: under realistic black-box conditions, injecting under 1% synthetic interactions significantly promotes attacker-chosen items when a trigger is present. The authors analyze decoding-aligned prefixes to characterize the vulnerability mechanism.

entry.title: SAGE: Pushing 2-Bit Vector-Quantized LLMs toward Real-World Usability

author.name: Xianglong Yan, Zenan Wu, Kewei Zhang, Kaicheng Yang, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: SAGE improves extreme low-bit (around 2-bit) weight-only vector quantization of LLMs by protecting sensitive weight channels within jointly encoded vectors and adaptively allocating the bit budget between direction and radius components per weight matrix. It targets real-world task performance, where prior VQ methods still degrade substantially.

entry.title: Structural Chain-of-Thought: Reasoning with Executable Computational Graphs

author.name: Petr Senatorov, Karim Vafin, Elena Tutubalina, Oleg Somov

entry.summary: Replaces free-form chain-of-thought with executable computational graphs whose deterministic execution yields the final answer, trained via graph-based RL rewarding structural validity, correctness, and node overlap with reference graphs. Across five benchmarks and four model families it improves accuracy and cuts generation length up to 5-6x.

entry.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Advancing Harmful Content Understanding via Perception-Aware Adversarial Self-Play

author.name: Yisong Xiao, Benlei Cui, Haiwen Hong, Shiji Zhao, Zonghao Ying, Yaoyuan Zhang, Longtao Huang, Aishan Liu, Hui Xue, Ting Ma, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a cognitive asymmetry between humans, who use contextual, phonetic, and visual cues to detect disguised harmful intent, and text-based LLMs that rely on token sequences, causing moderation failures on obfuscated harmful content. The proposed PASP framework uses perception-aware adversarial self-play to generate challenging obfuscations and train models to understand hidden harmful meaning. This directly addresses an important gap in online content safety and platform moderation.

entry.title: Agent-Canary-Mas: End-to-End Evaluation of Protocol Risk in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Xiuming Liu, Le Gai, Zhiyuan Chang, Peiyang Li, Bin Zhu, Shuo Wang, Chao Feng

entry.summary: Presents Agent-Canary-Mas, an end-to-end evaluation system tracing agent-to-agent protocol risk through long-horizon multi-agent tasks, covering five risk classes and 13 subclasses across A2A, ANP, and BCS protocols with 975 matched malicious-benign task pairs in five domains. It addresses the gap where a locally successful protocol attack may be rejected downstream or propagated into consequential decisions, and identifies which participant caused outcomes. Uses a shared framework running autonomous tool-using agents under different underlying models.

entry.title: Radioactive Feedback: Tracing Models Trained by Label-Only LLM Supervision

author.name: Yuejia Li, JunHeng Li, Hao Wu, Ke He, Mang Ye

entry.summary: The paper introduces Radioactive Feedback, a method for detecting whether a model was trained under label-only LLM-as-a-Judge distillation, where the student learns from scalar scores rather than teacher demonstrations. Since no teacher text enters training data, existing watermarks and distillation detectors fail; this work encodes provenance traces through the low-bandwidth reward channel itself.

entry.title: Uncovering Robustness Weaknesses in LLM Agents via Persona Evolution with Task-Integrity Constraints

author.name: Yutao Xie, Jingbo Yang, Guanyu Yao, Xiaoyu Yang, Duo Ding, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: TIPER is a task-integrity-preserving persona evolution method that automatically discovers agent weaknesses by evolving user-simulator personas while avoiding predefined behaviors or failure searches that invalidate the task. This addresses overly optimistic robustness estimates from cooperative standardized simulators in interactive agent evaluation.

entry.title: AuthGateBench: Benchmarking LLMs as Authorization Gate

author.name: Zhixiong Zhuang, Jin Jia, Zhiwei Shang, Ziyu Wang

entry.summary: AuthGateBench is the first policy-guided benchmark for LLM authorization gating under benign requests, targeting scope escalation where coding agents exceed user authorization. It generates contrast pairs with identical actions and trajectories but different request scopes, flipping the correct authorization label, and evaluates LLMs used as approval classifiers.

entry.title: Trace-to-Architecture: Capability Bottleneck Diagnosis for Harness Revision

author.name: Wenfeng Wang, Jianrui Shi, Mingang Guo, Jiayuan Ma, Yuqi Lu, Jiajun Sun, Guojiang Zhao, Jing Li

entry.summary: Introduces T2A, a framework in which a development agent diagnoses LLM agent failures from execution trajectories, revises the appropriate harness components, and verifies that target tasks improve while successful tasks remain intact. Across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and AppWorld it achieves the highest aggregate scores, with new execution evidence feeding back into subsequent diagnosis rounds.

entry.title: Neural Bayesian Networks for Modular and Scalable Decision-Making Under Uncertainty

author.name: Giovanni Briglia, Marco Lippi, Stefano Mariani, Franco Zambonelli

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Bayesian Networks, replacing tabular or linear-Gaussian conditionals in Bayesian networks with differentiable tensor-valued mechanisms while preserving the graph factorization, modularity, and interpretability of classical BNs. This aims to overcome expressiveness and scale limits while retaining the benefits of structured probabilistic inference.

entry.title: When LLM Agents See a Conflict but Still Proceed: Cross-Domain Dependencies in Network Slicing

author.name: Marcos Lima Romero, Ricardo Suyama

entry.summary: In a smart-grid/network-slicing environment, the authors test whether ten LLM agents recognize cross-domain conflicts before taking irreversible actions, such as a cost-reduction intent targeting a protection slice that appears idle by design. The controlled setup compares agents that must query dependencies against those that can read inventory annotations, with negative controls.

entry.title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models

author.name: Hanbo Xie, Yue Zhao, Robert C. Wilson

entry.summary: The authors introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework using repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with known recursive belief updates, separating adaptive play, action prediction, and genuine theory-of-mind belief tracking. Structured elicitation and behavioral SFT show improved play in several tests, but the diagnostics clarify whether gains reflect ToM or learned patterns.

entry.title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents

author.name: Junkai Lin, Ge Xu, Zheng Xu, Junkai Chen, Xiangyuan Lan

entry.summary: This paper argues that parameter-level machine unlearning is insufficient for LLM agents, since forgotten information can persist in memory artifacts or be reacquired via tool calls. The authors formulate agent-level unlearning as a new problem covering parameters, memory, and tool-mediated reacquisition. As agents gain long-lived memory and tool access, this extends the unlearning research agenda in an important direction.

entry.title: Adaptive-Group Process Rewards for GUI Agents

author.name: Zirui Shang, Yang Liu, Xin Shu, Zhi Gao, Xinxiao Wu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: This paper tackles sparse outcome rewards in reinforcement learning for GUI agents with an adaptive-group process reward framework that partitions trajectories into semantically coherent subgoal groups. It estimates process rewards at both action and group levels, with a critic evaluating actions based on visual changes and downstream context across long-horizon trajectories. This improves credit assignment for intermediate steps in complex interactive tasks.

entry.title: Learning Adaptive Deliberation Control for Reliable Recognition with Multi-Agent Language Models

author.name: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai

entry.summary: Presents ADMA, an adaptive multi-agent controller that learns continuous policies for proposal, challenge, arbitration, and coordination while keeping the task model frozen, using shared trace features plus role-specific features for decentralized control. A controller trained on legal and financial reasoning transfers without updates to four textual and multimodal benchmarks and two successive task-model versions, improving accuracy by 6.2-14.2 percentage points with a fixed Qwen model. This matters because fixed deliberation protocols waste compute on easy cases and under-deliberate hard ones.

entry.title: WorkRover: Scaling Long-Horizon Cowork Agent Training Via Recursive Environment Evolution

author.name: Hang He, Linting Wang, Guanming Liu, Bo Mao, Jinxiu Liu, Yiran Suo, Maosen Zhou, Zhiheng Xi, Guanting Dong, Zhou Shao, Rui Zheng, Jie Zhou, Chengcheng Wan, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: WorkRover is a framework for training long-horizon agent environments via recursive evolution, where construction agents jointly build and validate aligned work contexts, executable tasks, and evidence-grounded verifiers for reinforcement learning. It addresses the problem that generated environments need iterative refinement while keeping tasks, contexts, and verifiers consistent. This is relevant to scaling RL training data for real-world agents.

entry.title: The Smart Buildings Challenge: Learning Foundation Models for Real-World Optimization at Scale

author.name: Judah Goldfeder, Ayush Rai, Philippe M. Wyder, Na Li, Victoria Dean, Donna Vakalis, Jiong Lin, Bing Dong, Michael Rossetti, Nathan Kutz, Sohei Arisaka, John Sipple, Hod Lipson, Yoshua Bengio

entry.summary: A challenge paper targeting building HVAC optimization, which drives a large share of building emissions and 15 percent of global energy use. It addresses the core obstacle that building controllers do not transfer across buildings, proposing to spur foundation models for real-world, cross-building optimization at scale.

entry.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models

author.name: Bince Qu, Wei Chen, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: The authors argue that generalist embodied manipulation can be achieved by coding LLM agents given a simple robot harness rather than by training large vision-language-action models. RoboHarness provides agents a visual-geometric control panel to understand and invoke embodied tasks, and with it an LLM agent reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.

entry.title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents

author.name: Seungjun Yu, Hojun Choi, Seojeong Park, Jaeyo Shin, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: This paper reformulates world modeling for GUI agents by shifting prediction from full pixel-space screen reconstruction to latent-space prediction of action-relevant state changes. This addresses the computational cost of pixel reconstruction and the identity-shortcut problem where future-state prediction merely copies the current screen.

entry.title: DexFLEX: Contact-Aware Foundation Controller for Command-Guided Dexterity

author.name: Weikang Wan, Zeyu Lai, Jianyu Hou, Yuchen Zhou, Jiawei Fu, Henrik I Christensen, Hao Su

entry.summary: DexFLEX is a contact-aware foundation controller that converts upstream fingertip-motion drafts (from teleoperation or learned policies) into contact-consistent joint commands for dexterous robot hands. It treats drafts as evidence of intent, proposing short-horizon motion chunks, predicting contact consequences, and selecting candidates via a Draft-Dream-Select procedure that preserves future contact stability.

entry.title: What Counts as the Same Task? Executable Contracts for Robustness Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Shaikh Akib Shahriyar, MD. Akil Raihan Iftee, Armon Barton, Matthew Wright

entry.summary: Proposes executable task contracts that formally specify which facts define a task, which edits are allowed, and what task completion means, to validate perturbed test cases before agent robustness evaluation. The authors compare validity rules by rescoring 14,336 stored agent runs across four encoders, finding embedding-similarity heuristics unreliable.

entry.title: PTGPO: Prefix Tree Group Policy Optimization

author.name: Ruolin Chen, Yang Li, Jihang Wang, Zhuoya Zhao, Yuchen Liu, Jiaming Xu, Qian Zhang

entry.summary: PTGPO is a critic-free RL method for training language agents on long-horizon interactive tasks, building prefix trees over trajectory suffixes within anchor-state groups. Each tree edge receives credit based on the empirical mean return difference between child and parent, giving fine-grained credit assignment without conflating an action with subsequent decisions.

entry.title: PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces

author.name: M. Yigit Turali, Shreyas Rajesh, M. Efe Lorasdagi, Chenda Duan, Kartik Sharma, Vwani Roychowdhury

entry.summary: PANINI-DR is a multi-agent deep-research harness that separates investigation coordination from subquestion research and verification, maintaining research state in a shared Generative Semantic Workspace that records subquestions, dependencies, findings, and evidence. A dedicated verification agent checks proposed answers before errors propagate through the multi-step research process. The system targets reliable, stateful long-horizon research with LLM agents.

entry.title: ZOIF: Zeroth-Order Influence Function Estimation for LLM Data Selection Using Only Forward Passes

author.name: Lisong He, Yunxuan Jiang, Haishan Ye, Xiangyu Chang

entry.summary: ZOIF is a zeroth-order framework for influence-function estimation that operates entirely via forward passes, eliminating backpropagation memory overhead and the need to handle billion-scale Hessians, enabling principled data selection (for model editing, debugging, and efficient fine-tuning) at LLM scale under tight resource constraints. By avoiding stored intermediate activations, it makes influence-based data curation practical where classical IF approximations fail.

entry.title: DiffNash: Finding Nash Equilibrium in High-Dimensional Continuous Action Spaces with Diffusion Policies

author.name: Haichuan Wang, Anagha Satish, Jiale Zheng, Saisneha Ghatti, Lingkai Kong, Kai Wang, Milind Tambe

entry.summary: DiffNash computes Nash equilibria in high-dimensional continuous games using diffusion policies, deriving a reweighted score-matching objective that trains diffusion-based Online Mirror Descent and Fictitious Play without needing samples from each updated policy. This enables representing rich, multi-modal strategy distributions that conventional neural policies struggle with.

entry.title: WildTrace: Evaluating Training Data Detection in Realistic Large-Scale LLM Post-Training

author.name: Hengxiang Zhang, Junxian Liu, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: Introduces WildTrace, a benchmark for evaluating training data detection methods on post-trained LLMs under realistic large-scale conditions, avoiding the distribution shifts of post-hoc benchmarks and the small-scale setups of controlled evaluations. It enables faithful assessment of membership inference and contamination detection in real post-training pipelines.

entry.title: StructZO: Structured Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xuanlin Yang, Jia Li, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: StructZO is a structured zeroth-order optimization framework for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning that closes the gap to first-order optimizers by introducing large-query ZO estimation within an activation-induced informative low-rank subspace, plus large-scale signal aggregation and better-conditioned update directions. It targets the memory bottleneck of backpropagation at scale.

entry.title: Logit Leakage through Floating-Point Bias Addition

author.name: Shaomin Chen, Xiaorui Gong

entry.summary: The paper identifies a numerical side channel in floating-point bias addition in language model APIs that exposes the additive component of logits through token identities alone, exploiting representable-spacing changes at binary exponent boundaries. Under binary32 assumptions the method recovers a logit pair and tie-breaking priority in at most 52 queries.

entry.title: AUGUstus: Autonomous Driving VLA Model with Unified Generation and Understanding

author.name: Yuqi Ye, Caigao Jiang, Zhuonan Wang, Congyuan Pei, Chao Qu, Changhao Peng, Junhong Lin, Qize Yu, Zetian Song, Guangzhao Fu, Chongruo Wu, Shiyu Huang, Shuchang Zhou, Honggou Yang, Wei Gao

entry.summary: Introduces AUGUstus, a vision-language-action model for end-to-end autonomous driving that overcomes the tradeoff between low-latency regression-style action generation (which underuses VLM understanding) and high-latency autoregressive chain-of-thought. It unifies generation and understanding so CoT reasoning can assist action generation while remaining deployment-friendly.

entry.title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions

author.name: Xialie Zhuang, Zunhai Su, Jia Pan, Ngai Wong, Guanhua Chen, Chuan-Wei Kuo

entry.summary: StartLux-Decision introduces 0.8B to 27B parameter decision models combining fast single-pass prediction with adaptive confidence-guided reasoning: Instant models answer directly using bidirectional attention, while AutoThink models invoke explicit reasoning only for uncertain cases. Training uses a three-stage pipeline including RLCD squared, an RL method with a frozen model and proper scoring rules for calibrated deliberation. This targets the practical trade-off between inference cost and decision quality.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning

author.name: Li-Ching Chen, Andr\'es Franco Valiente, Yuta Ishiyama, Zachary R. Chalmers, William Chen, Kelsey Natsuhara, Taema Brinjikji, Madhumita Sushil, Travis Zack, Julian C. Hong

entry.summary: This work tackles extending LLM RL beyond diagnostic endpoints to clinical tasks like oncology treatment planning, where multiple trajectories can be valid and correctness is only partially verifiable. The authors develop RL methods for colon cancer treatment decision-making under partial observability, addressing a key bottleneck for clinical reasoning beyond question answering. The clinical author team (UCSF) lends domain credibility.

entry.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents

author.name: Jianghong Zhou, Hao Rong, Chen Lin, Daoan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces reasoning contraction, the compression of many reasoning steps into reusable memories, templates, and caches, and proves that success/failure counters used to trust these memories are poor change detectors when underlying facts shift. Empirically, ExpeL- and ACE-style counters serve 7-73x more stale answers than certified memories across five LLMs on edited-fact QA and code tasks.

entry.title: Where Small Mistakes Matter: Quantifying State Criticality for Imitation Learning

author.name: Yusuf Umut Ciftci, Joonwon Kang, Ajay Suresha Sathya, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: The paper formalizes state criticality in imitation learning as the worst-case value degradation caused by bounded perturbations of expert actions, and proposes SCRIM, which estimates it using an adversarial disturbance policy and value critic. This enables weighting demonstrations by how unrecoverable mistakes at each state would be.

entry.title: Efficiently Learning To Reason or Not to Reason: Root-token Policy Optimization for Adaptive Thinking

author.name: Taehyeon Kim, Hyunsoo Lee, Youngsoo Jang, Moontae Lee

entry.summary: RPO trains large reasoning models to decide adaptively whether to invoke explicit reasoning by optimizing only the initial root token (the thinking-tag decision) via group-relative rewards. This offers an open-source, low-cost alternative to proprietary difficulty-based routing for mitigating overthinking.

entry.title: QK-Edit: Revisiting Attention-based Injection in MM-DiT for Image and Video Editing

author.name: Tiancheng Shen, Zilong Huang, Xiangtai Li, Zhijie Lin, Jiyang Liu, Yitong Wang, Jiashi Feng, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Jun Hao Liew

entry.summary: QK-Edit is a training-free framework for text-guided image and video editing in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers, exploiting their unique multimodal self-attention dynamics via a novel query-key manipulation strategy. It enables precise attention-based injection where U-Net-era attention methods fail.

entry.title: DriveWLA: Unifying Future Dynamics and Scene Semantics through World-Language-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Shuzheng Wang, Haoxuan Li, Shengzhen Li, Chenxi Wu, Yajing Sun, Lu Hou, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes DriveWLA, a unified World-Language-Action model built on Mixture-of-Transformers that jointly handles semantic understanding, future scene evolution, and trajectory generation for autonomous driving via three experts plus cross-expert attention. The design aims to combine VLM semantic strength with world-model dynamics prediction for better trajectory generation.

entry.title: HaloBlock: Faster and Better Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Zhaohui Zheng, Chenhang He, Jinrui Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Tackles two inefficiencies in diffusion LLM inference: block decoding difficulty being dominated by right-side tokens, and boundary contextual discontinuity in block-wise decoding. HaloBlock uses bidirectional cumulative entropy to measure block difficulty and adaptively allocates bidirectional halo regions around blocks, improving both quality and speed.

entry.title: APT: Feedback-Driven Agentic Post-Training for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Sirui Zhang, Fangyun Wei, Dong Chen, Jinjing Zhao, Yitong Wang, Yunuo Chen, Baining Guo, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: APT is a fully automated post-training framework for text-to-image models in which three coordinated agents evaluate the model, diagnose its weaknesses, and generate RL training data with an adaptive prompt distribution targeting underperforming capabilities. This creates a feedback loop where the current model shapes its own next training tasks. The multi-agent author list associated with Microsoft Research and USTC suggests credible provenance.

entry.title: Readout Scaling Shapes Sparse Feature Recovery

author.name: Brian Xiao, Sarah Wilson

entry.summary: This paper shows that readout scaling fundamentally affects what sparse autoencoders learn, using readout-canonicalized decision-space coordinates to remove singular-value gains. In controlled experiments, recovery of known factors improves dramatically (mean recovery rising from 0.506 to 0.913 at condition number 100) when training restores the coordinate space in which factors were generated. It matters for interpretability research that relies on SAEs to recover true model features.

entry.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bowen Ding, Mingda Wan, Yuhan Chen, Jiyao Yuan, Qi Zhu, Futing Wang, Heyuan Deng, Fei Mi, Lifeng Shang, Tao Lin

entry.summary: ProAS addresses the uniform credit assignment problem in critic-free agentic RL methods like GRPO, which broadcast trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. The framework uses a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph to shape advantages with progress awareness, providing fine-grained credit assignment without critic overhead, and is designed as a plug-and-play addition.

entry.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents

author.name: Jiaru Zou, Yunzhe Qi, Sirui Chen, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Pan Lu, Jingrui He, James Zou

entry.summary: HybridAgents is an architecture that lets LLM agents dynamically alternate between latent reasoning (efficient internal continuous thought) and text-based interaction for tool use, via a lightweight HybridLink module plus continuous working memory that preserves lossless hybrid context across turns. This aims to combine latent reasoning efficiency with the tool access and transparency of text-based agency.

entry.title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization

author.name: Gor Simonyan, Tatevik Abrahamyan, Narek Abelyan, Tigran Fahradyan, Hrant Khachatrian

entry.summary: PMO-Dock extends the Practical Molecular Optimization benchmark to docking-based objectives, providing 25 standardized tasks covering hit generation, lead optimization, and a new specificity task penalizing off-target binding. It addresses unstandardized evaluation practice in structure-based drug design optimization with a shared protocol and sample-efficiency constraints.

entry.title: MA-Bench: Measuring Operational Planning in Language Models

author.name: Rodney Lafuente-Mercado, Robert Sincero, Phil Sage, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: Introduces MA-Bench, a benchmark for operational planning built on the military mission-analysis process, with 10 expert-built scenarios pairing document packets with 1,257 pass/fail requirements graded by a reasoning-model judge. It tests whether LLMs can synthesize large, incomplete, contradictory document sets into problem statements when no single correct answer exists.

entry.title: Test-Time Forecasting: Recurrent Depth Enables In-Context Dynamics Prediction

author.name: Jeffrey B. Lai, John Quinn, Anthony Bao, William Gilpin

entry.summary: The authors show looped transformers can emulate dynamical-system propagators in-context, first linking linear attention to dynamic mode decomposition, then generalizing this into a Test-Time Forecasting framework where gradient-descent iterations serve as recurrent depth. Lightweight TTF models trained on ODEs and PDEs generalize to unseen dynamical systems. This advances both the theory of in-context learning and foundation models for scientific forecasting.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching

author.name: Xiaocong Yang, Xuanyu Meng, Yuji Zhang, Jiawei Han, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: SAE-IDF proposes using sparse autoencoder features as a shared coordinate system for matching symbolic units across heterogeneous neuro-symbolic systems, a foundational step toward data-driven merging of symbolic backbones at LLM scale. The method encodes symbols in their native systems and aligns them via SAE feature spaces. This could enable scaling neuro-symbolic systems beyond hand-built, domain-specific symbol sets.

entry.title: CAST: History-Adaptive Spectral Clipping for LLM Pretraining

author.name: Jiacheng Li, Jianchao Tan, Kefeng Zhang, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: CAST extends soft spectral clipping of gradients with history-adaptive scales and thresholds: AdamW's second moment sets row and column scales while an EMA of clipped-output spectral norms sets per-matrix thresholds, restoring original coordinates before the AdamW update. Training a 19.08B-parameter MoE model for 83.89B tokens, CAST beats nine gradient-processing baselines on training and validation loss with the fewest gradient spikes. It reaches the best baseline's final loss using roughly a third of the compute, per the abstract.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

author.name: Sifan Yang, Hongyi Tao, Dingzhi Yu, Haomin Bai, Wei Jiang, Silin Gao, Pi Bu, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a residual correction framework for memory-efficient subspace optimization of LLM training, maintaining optimizer states in a subspace while adding orthogonal residual gradients to parameter updates. It derives SMRC from momentum SGD with an O(T^-1/4) convergence rate matching full-space momentum SGD, and extends the analysis to the Muon optimizer. This addresses the failure of prior subspace methods when gradient noise dominates in later training stages.

entry.title: Outperforming 1000 Euclidean Layers With Hyperbolic Goal-Conditioned RL

author.name: Timo Klein, Thomas Lang, Andrii Shkabrii, Lukas Miklautz, Yllka Velaj, Sebastian Tschiatschek

entry.summary: The paper shows that replacing Euclidean distances with hyperbolic geodesic distances in self-supervised contrastive reinforcement learning achieves stronger goal-reaching performance with far shallower networks, with depth-64 hyperbolic models beating 1000-layer Euclidean ones on hard navigation tasks. This exploits the mismatch between route distance and Euclidean distance in maze-like environments. It demonstrates that geometric inductive bias can substitute for depth, cutting wall-clock cost dramatically.

entry.title: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon

author.name: Kai Ruan, Jinghao Lin, Tao Chen, Ziqi Zhou, Qianshan Wei, Zihe Huang

entry.summary: The paper studies training long-horizon agents on repository-level issue resolution using a single-rollout asynchronous recipe combining Muon, token-averaged loss, truncated importance sampling, and auxiliary length/tool-error penalties. Across two model families, the full recipe shows higher training success than baselines, highlighting optimizer choice as critical for sparse-outcome long-horizon RL.

entry.title: Hyperspherical Contrastive Representations Unlock Planning and Exploration

author.name: Jonghae Park, Sungil Son, Jonghun Shin, Junseo Lee, H. Jin Kim, Benjamin Eysenbach

entry.summary: C-Slerp is a self-supervised RL algorithm that learns contrastive representations whose hyperspherical geometry enables closed-form inference of intermediate planning waypoints via spherical linear interpolation, without a high-level policy or graph search. The representation geometry also dictates how many waypoints to use, adapting planning granularity. Demonstrated on building towers of up to eight cubes from scratch with no rewards, demonstrations, or pretrained models.

entry.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic

author.name: Walter Simoncini, Dheeraj Varghese, Gertjan J. Burghouts, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: Introduces a retraining-free method that turns a pre-trained transformer into a single elastic model adaptable on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. The key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of functional unit ranking that scores every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, rather than one importance weight per block or head. Relevant to serving transformers under heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads without maintaining multiple fixed-size checkpoints.

entry.title: INTACT: Inducing Latent Reasoning on a Frozen Backbone

author.name: Kutay Tire, Atula Tejaswi, Haris Vikalo, Sujay Sanghavi

entry.summary: INTACT induces latent reasoning in a frozen LLM using a small external encoder that iteratively maps the backbone's hidden states into compact continuous soft-token blocks, forming a latent reasoning prefix before the model answers in text. The encoder is trained via distillation to mimic written reasoning steps and then reinforced on answer correctness. This reduces autoregressive decoding of intermediate tokens while preserving backbone behavior, an efficient alternative to explicit chain-of-thought.

entry.title: Discriminative Score Function: Turning Pretrained Models into Functional Generative Priors

author.name: Junhoo Lee, Hyeonjin Kim, Sangbum Han, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: DSF extracts a training-free, image-space generative update field from the loss-gradient geometry of pretrained discriminative models, moving images toward model-consistent regions without retraining or task-specific guidance. This suggests discriminative models retain an exploitable trace of the data manifold.

entry.title: Scaling Multilingual Mixture-of-Experts: How Language Coverage Changes Capacity and Compute Allocation

author.name: Joel Dag, Nikit Srivastava, Hamada M. Zahera, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a repetition-aware joint scaling law connecting active parameters, per-language training tokens, expert count, and language coverage in multilingual MoE models. Fitted on 26,300 per-language loss observations across 64 configurations, the law reduces prediction error by 28% over the strongest baseline and quantifies how added experts change the cost of adding languages.

entry.title: VascuSR: Iterative Anatomy-Aware Diffusion for CT Super-Resolution

author.name: Hairong Ni, Jiahe Huang, Minghao Guo, Wojciech Matusik, Rose Yu

entry.summary: VascuSR addresses the risk that generative CT super-resolution invents anatomically unsupported vascular detail by combining image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance in an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework. The explicit 3D vascular representation provides structural constraints beyond individual slices and simplifies enforcement of anatomical consistency.

entry.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance

author.name: Zhefei Gong, Hefeifei Jiang, Zehao Wang, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: HiRe-MoMa is a framework for stable, sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of mobile manipulation systems. It fine-tunes a frozen base policy with a policy-agnostic residual module, splitting corrections into mobile-base and arm heads with unidirectional conditioning to avoid gradient interference, using sparse human guidance. This addresses a genuine gap in practical real-world robot adaptation.

entry.title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision

author.name: Yifan Lan, Zhongye Liu, Yurui Chang, Hanyu Wang, Yongkang Du, Lu Lin, Jinghui Chen

entry.summary: DecisionRobust is a benchmark for evaluating the robustness of emerging judgment-evaluation-vote (JEV) style decision models that map task instructions and observations to choices and scores. It spans text and visual inputs with semantics-preserving perturbations, image perturbations, and prompt injection in both modalities, using external validity checks and cross-model candidate selection to curate evaluation sets. Robustness of automated decision models is an increasingly critical safety question.

entry.title: What Is a Clarification? Estimating Model-Dependent Input Ambiguity

author.name: Jingqin Tang, Tim Tomov, Sebastian Schmidt, Dominik Fuchsgruber, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: The paper distinguishes world ambiguity (all interpretations an input admits) from model ambiguity (those a given model can recognize and answer), formalizing natural-language clarifications via uniqueness, faithfulness, and answer-equivalence desiderata. It shows these desiderata induce a one-to-one correspondence between valid answers and equivalence classes of clarifications.

entry.title: Learning Perception to Action Rules through Reinforcement Learning for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning

author.name: Soyoung Oh, Nursulu Sagimbayeva, Nicholas Jennings, Paulina Hussein, Mehwish Alam, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: The authors generate explicit if-then rules linking perception, belief, and action, and use GRPO reinforcement learning to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks. Rule-augmented GRPO outperforms prompting, SFT, and thinking-based reasoning, and rules from larger models transfer to improve smaller models' downstream ToM performance.

entry.title: Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Models for Consistent Future Frame Prediction

author.name: Anton Arapin, Aditya Singh, Yixin Wang, Jun Gao, Bernadette Bucher

entry.summary: D3WM decouples deterministic and stochastic components of future frame prediction: a transformer jointly regresses the deterministic next state and a spatial uncertainty map, which then guides a conditional diffusion process for the stochastic parts. This yields more consistent world-model rollouts by learning where uncertainty lives.

entry.title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding

author.name: Chenxu Wang, Hangyi Kuang, Bo-Wen Yin, Yuxuan Li, Quan-Sheng Zeng, Yang Zhang, Xu Guo, Xiang Li, Qibin Hou

entry.summary: WinARDet diagnoses box-repetition loops in MLLM-based detectors as historical-answer attention takeover, where repeated coordinate tokens crowd out attention to new visual evidence. It proposes compressed window auto-regression, partitioning answers into generation windows to restrict full autoregression and break the failure loop.

entry.title: TextVerifier: Seeing Beyond Recognition to Verify Chinese Text Rendering

author.name: Yiyang Chen, Guo-Hua Wang, Yaoli Liu, Qing-Guo Chen, Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo, Xiujun Ma

entry.summary: TextVerifier addresses local defects in text-to-image rendering of Chinese characters (extra/missing strokes, malformed components) that OCR and VLMs miss because they are trained for recognition. It formalizes verification as a target-conditioned task, feeding an Ideographic Description Sequence to the text tower and training on 12.7M crop-IDS pairs.

entry.title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Boyuan Sun, Deshui Miao, Wenzhao Gao, Shaoyong Jia, Shaohui Jiao, Chi Liu, Yan Shu, Derek Li, Bryan Dai, Shengsheng Qian, Qibin Hou

entry.summary: DeltaStreamer is an agentic framework for streaming video understanding that combines change-aware structured memory of visual transitions with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering via replay. It records how events unfold before queries arrive, then recovers missing visual evidence on demand, addressing detail loss and unrecoverable history in prior compressive approaches.

entry.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance

author.name: Zhuobai Dong, Junchao Yi, Hu Jian Guo, Linjie Li, Rui Zhao, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: Glance Forcing makes distillation of bidirectional diffusion models into causal few-step students dramatically cheaper, reducing trajectory supervision to a single PF-ODE sample, the strictest possible setting. The authors trace quality collapse under this regime to teacher trajectory geometry in the high-noise regime governing semantic layout and motion, and correct it.

entry.title: $\lambda_0$: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: humanoid Team

entry.summary: The paper introduces HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion, as a scalable alternative to costly robot demonstrations. A human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns viewpoints, refines motion references and controller inputs offline, and the approach is validated for humanoid whole-body control.

entry.title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning

author.name: Colton Crosby, Hao Wang, Mac Schwager, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: This work proposes a monitoring-and-intervention framework that improves visuomotor policies at deployment using only black-box query access, without retraining. From labeled on-policy rollouts it learns a policy-conditioned liveness value tracking task progress, plus a compact latent world model used for planning interventions when the policy is failing.

entry.title: Learning from Demonstrations meets Symbolic Control - A Supervisory Control Architecture for Formal Certification of Learned Motion

author.name: Ashok Kumar, Mahathi Anand, Angela Schoellig, Abdalla Swikir

entry.summary: The paper proposes a symbolic supervisory control architecture that generates fail-safe backup plans certifying safety, reachability, and actuator feasibility directly from robot dynamics, independent of the learned dynamical-system motion policy. A nominal controller tracks the learned motion while the supervisor intervenes non-conservatively when constraints are violated, with simulations and real-robot deployment.

entry.title: Atomic-WAM: Execution-Grounded Atomic-Motion Reasoning for World Action Models

author.name: Shijun Shi, Zhe Liu, Zhi Hou, Yinan Chen, Tao Zhang, Kai Hu, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: Atomic-WAM introduces an understand-then-execute framework for world action models, where a vision-language reasoner first describes the next atomic motion from task instructions and visual context, then guides joint video and action prediction. An automatic annotation pipeline curates temporally aligned, contact-enriched supervision from multi-view DROID data.

entry.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness

author.name: Chonghan Qin, Dongming Wu, Kaituo Feng, Jiaxu Wang, Xinlei Yu, Peiwen Sun, Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Bingao Chen, Weitong Lian, Ryan Ji, Wenqi Ren, Xiaobin Hu, Dahua Lin, Yu-Gang Jiang, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: This paper provides a unified overview of the emerging agentic robots paradigm, where systems reason over instructions, interact with environments, autonomously rectify errors, and adjust strategies, moving beyond low-level action prediction. It traces the field's development across models, data, environments, and harnesses, aiming to connect currently fragmented research into coherent system views.

entry.title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Diyuan Shi, Yiqi Tang, Hongyin Zhang, You Wu, Donglin Wang

entry.summary: VLRLA equips pretrained vision-language-action models with in-context reinforcement learning so they can continue improving from their own interaction experience after deployment. A reinforcement learning module learns from accumulated histories of observations, actions, rewards, and termination signals, progressively refining the policy's action generation without weight retraining. This addresses the static nature of conventional VLA policies in deployment.

entry.title: Our approach to working with AI companies

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: METR articulates its policies for engaging AI companies on evaluations, assessments, and investigations related to loss-of-control risk, emphasizing public, timely, independent evidence so that the public, policymakers, and developers can make informed decisions. It clarifies goals, practices, and limitations of voluntary third-party safety assurance as expectations for such engagements grow.

entry.title: SAT-RL: Training Language Models for Logical Reasoning with Symbolic Solvers

author.name: Jialiang Sun, Kuldeep Meel

entry.summary: SAT-RL is a reinforcement learning framework training LLMs to interact with symbolic solvers like Z3 through multi-turn tool execution, using synthetic data with verifiable solutions and a supervised warm-up phase. It targets the curse of complexity in logical reasoning as constraint interactions and search spaces grow.

entry.title: MCPDisCo: Seesaw-Mitigated Tuning for MCP-Native Agents

author.name: Kounianhua Du, Jianxing Liu, Shuai Shao, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: MCPDisCo is an ecosystem-scale RL framework for agents operating over the Model Context Protocol, using a Thought-MDP that explicitly represents reasoning alongside routing, execution, and termination. Trained across 70 real MCP servers and 527 tools, it identifies and mitigates a reasoning-tool seesaw failure mode in joint learning.

entry.title: Small but Mighty: Test Suites as Improvement Signals for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yutong Cheng, Wei Cheng, Wenchao Yu, Dawei Zhou, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: TeSearch improves the signal used by self-evolving agents deciding which harness rewrites to keep, finding repository tests alone too sparse (rejecting only a quarter of behavior-changing rewrites) and rollouts too costly. It uses a quality-diversity evolutionary algorithm to find small, strong test suites that provide dense, executable improvement signals.

entry.title: Phantom Merge: When Your Large Language Model Agents Pick One but Tell You About Another

author.name: Wangshu Zhu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: The paper identifies Phantom Merge, an entity-evidence binding failure where an LLM agent attributes unsupported claims to its committed entity, sometimes even when the task output is correct. It formalizes the failure at claim level across four agent domains, characterizes prevalence and error subtypes, and proposes a two-stage risk-estimation and correction framework combining hidden-state readouts with grounding.

entry.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints

author.name: Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Duan Leijiahao, Haoxiang Wang, Boning Tan, Liangna Fu, Chao Tan, Yafu Li, Yulong Chen, Chaoqun Wan, Zhen Huang, Shuxian Liang, Xian-Sheng Hua

entry.summary: Introduces LIBERO-Industry, a benchmark built on the widely used LIBERO robot learning suite that adds industrial process constraints to manipulation evaluation: product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. It targets high-mix low-volume manufacturing scenarios where generalist robot policies must adapt to changing conditions.

entry.title: Do Theorem Provers Need Theorem-Proving Agents? mini-Lean-agent: A Coding-Agent Baseline for Lean

author.name: Tomas Ortega, Simon Park, Ayush Khaitan, Liam Fowl, Alex Kontorovich, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: mini-Lean-agent is a deliberately minimal Lean theorem-proving agent whose only model-visible tool is bash, with a separate trusted evaluator verifying final artifacts. Comparisons against specialized Lean agents on Putnam 2025 problems help isolate whether benchmark gains come from the base model, harness, or specialized tooling.

entry.title: CompanionSafe: From Multi-turn Safety Evaluation to Guardrails for AI Companions

author.name: Xinyang Liao, Lingyu Li, Kaicheng Shen, Yang Yao, Na Lu, Yan Teng, Xia Hu

entry.summary: CompanionSafe is a unified evaluation-to-mitigation framework for AI companion safety, featuring CompanionEval with 1,300 relationally grounded multi-turn dialogue settings built from personas and companion characters, plus a CompanionGuard mitigation component. It targets the distinct relational safety risks of sustained companion interactions, going beyond platform-specific or manually collected prior work. This addresses a growing consumer-facing safety domain.

entry.title: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops

author.name: Yubo Li, Ramayya Krishnan, Rema Padman

entry.summary: Using factual probes paired with next-action questions on a frozen benchmark of agent decision states, the authors show that most wrong actions in fast System One models follow correct state reading rather than misreading. Across seventeen fast systems, more accurate models make a larger share of these read-right-act-wrong errors, implying failures lie in the action-selection stage.

entry.title: GameSmith: Scaling Zero-Sum Self-Play with Synthesised Games

author.name: Weixian Waylon Li, Jiaxin Zhang, Han Zhou, Chengzu Li, Ke Wang, Fengxiang He, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: GameSmith scales LLM self-play training on two-player zero-sum games by having an LLM synthesize new games within templates with fixed reward, observation, and hidden-information code, each verified via seed-paired replay and independent re-implementation of its specification. This yields 26 new games in 29 families and 336 verified variants from a small seed set, addressing the bottleneck that prior pipelines rely on a handful of hand-written games. The approach supports verifiable-reward post-training whose gains are known to transfer to general reasoning.

entry.title: Can We Trust This Evaluation? Instance-Level Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Yang Ba, Michelle V. Mancenido, Rong Pan

entry.summary: The paper proposes SCUR, a label-free method for estimating instance-level reliability of LLM-as-a-judge panels, using a latent measurement model to combine panel uncertainty, measurement cross-entropy, and perturbation sensitivity into a risk score. Evaluation across five benchmarks shows the approach identifies unreliable majority-vote judgments.

entry.title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation

author.name: Yeobin Hong, Hyojun Go, Dohun Lee, Jeongjae Lee, Sunghwan Hong, Federico Tombari, Zhaochong An, Jong Chul Ye, Konrad Schindler, Dominik Narnhofer

entry.summary: GeoFix improves geometric consistency of 4D generation from video diffusion models using a single cross-view depth-consistency reward applied to static scene regions, avoiding the texture degradation typical of multi-reward post-training. The method works for both training-time and inference-time reward alignment and preserves valid object motion.

entry.title: CacheLink: Functional KV Transport for Zero-Prefill Cross-Model Context Handoff

author.name: Haomiao Qiu, Yining Tang, Zijia Song, Ruizi Han, Ziyue Qiao, Miao Zhang

entry.summary: CacheLink addresses zero-prefill cross-model context handoff — translating a sender KV cache into a receiver-compatible state so a different model can continue without reprefilling. The key finding is that reconstruction fidelity is a poor proxy for receiver utility, since similar reconstruction errors can produce very different attention patterns and downstream accuracy, motivating a functional rather than pixel-level transport objective.

entry.title: Of Errors and Echoes: Responsibility-Aware Credit Assignment for Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Xingjian Diao, Tianyu Yang, Wenjun Huang, Xiangchi Yuan, Chunhui Zhang, Xingchen Zhao, Weiyi Wu, Haotian Xu, Soroush Vosoughi, Xiangliang Zhang, Jiang Gui

entry.summary: ECHO is a responsibility-aware credit assignment framework for RL-trained tool-use agents that separates responsibility identification from credit allocation: a frozen judge distinguishes newly introduced errors, inherited consequences, missed corrections, and successful corrections, then allocates credit by shared downstream consequences.

entry.title: VLA-GAUGE: Systematically Evaluating Generalization and Robustness in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jun Xiao, Rui Ye, Dong Cao, Jinyu Gu, Ying Wang, Zhiliang Zhu

entry.summary: VLA-GAUGE is a diagnostic framework for vision-language-action models that unifies in-distribution versus out-of-distribution task evaluation across six capability suites, single-factor and combinatorial perturbation screening, and diagnosis-driven refinement, all on a shared executable task representation. It tests whether high success rates reflect genuine zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Know-Thy-Not: Training-Free Targeted Negation in Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models

author.name: DoYoung Kim, Changkyu Choi, Ad\'in Ram\'irez Rivera, YunSeok Choi, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: The paper shows that dual-encoder VLMs inherently fail at negation because contrastive training can at best dilute but never reject negated concepts within a single embedding. KTN is a training-free method adding an image-side rejection dimension that directly penalizes negated concepts, plus COCO-Confusion, the first benchmark requiring genuine rejection. Across 9 backbones it improves mAP substantially over vanilla and existing baselines.

entry.title: Explore with Memory, Learn without It: In-Context Exploration and Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yutong Chen, Zhichao Xu, Rui Liu, Kunpeng Liu

entry.summary: LEAF injects a dynamic, problem-specific memory of prior rollouts, rewards, and environment feedback into the context before each rollout, updating the policy via self-distillation decoupled from the exploration process. It accelerates exploration roughly 4x over random sampling and improves generalization on unseen test sets across four RLVR benchmarks.

entry.title: SpecCloak: Probing Harmful Code Generation through Engineering Specifications

author.name: Wenbin Chen, Jiexin Wang, Guanting Wu, Jiaxi Liang, Yi Cai

entry.summary: Investigates whether expressing malicious coding requests as formal engineering specifications rather than keyword-laden requests affects LLM refusal behavior. Across five open-weight models, removing explicit risk keywords only partially reduces refusal, while specification-formatted requests substantially erode safety behavior, supported by representation analysis and activation interventions.

entry.title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yuante Li, Junwei Quan, Kai Qiu, Kate Zhang, Yicheng Tao

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-clock framework separating samples needed for progress from samples consumed before collapse in RLVR training, analyzing the common square-root learning-rate scaling for large rollout batches. Under a local quadratic model, larger batches lose more to curvature, producing a learning-rate-dependent critical batch size beyond which sample efficiency degrades, with a drift-threshold hypothesis predicting failure timing.

entry.title: Backpropagating Verifier Rewards Through Continuous Flow Language Models

author.name: Xu Han, Jiajing Hu, Li-Ping Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes an RL post-training framework for continuous flow language models, which denoise token embeddings over multiple steps and decode to discrete tokens only at the end. A critic estimates values of intermediate embeddings to enable low-variance pathwise gradients that backpropagate verifier rewards through continuous actions, bypassing non-differentiable decoding.

entry.title: Spectral-MoE: Heterogeneous Per-Layer Expert Utilization in Dense-to-MoE Conversion

author.name: Zachary Broveak, Christian Kubicka, Thierry Tambe

entry.summary: Introduces Spectral-MoE, a dense-to-MoE conversion method that learns heterogeneous per-layer expert utilization budgets, unlike prior analytic or gradient-based methods that fix the same active expert count at every layer. This should reduce inference arithmetic costs more effectively by matching expert allocation to layer-specific redundancy.

entry.title: Learning to Compute Is Not Learning to Retain or Reuse in Looped Transformers

author.name: Peilong Zhou, Hongtao Zhang, Yulong Huang, Cangyuan Li, Mingyu Chen, Ying Wang

entry.summary: Using in-context Mealy-machine execution with exact counterfactual hidden-state interventions, this paper separates overthinking failures in looped transformers into failed computation, loss of retention, and unreusable states. Models fully correct at trained loop depth 32 retain only 22 percent of answers at loop 64, and retention depends on training supervision choices. The findings clarify why looping beyond trained depth breaks recurrent reasoning.

entry.title: Learning Graph Energies for Finite-Time Generation

author.name: Amartya Banerjee, Xingyu Xu, Caroline Moosm\"uller, Harlin Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces finite-horizon energy learning, adapting a Metropolis-Hastings acceptance energy to the distribution returned after a fixed number of sampler steps rather than the equilibrium distribution. A frozen pretrained model provides initialization and proposals while a learned energy governs acceptance, trained with an unbiased signal from coupled continuations of accepted and rejected branches scored by a discriminator. This targets accurate discrete graph generation, e.g., molecules, under fixed compute budgets.

entry.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling

author.name: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Zhou Xu, Haoyue Zhang, Delu Zeng, Jiahao Wang, Junmei Yang, Pan tiewen, Jingfeng Liu, Zhiheng Zhou, Bo Li, Min Chen
