entry.summary: HP-RLVR assigns token-level credit in RL with verifiable rewards using a single rollout: the generating policy snapshot scores each token under causal history versus a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback, and a normalized Jensen-Shannon divergence converts the contrast into update weights. This avoids GRPO's group sampling and its loss of signal when all attempts share the same outcome. It could substantially reduce the compute cost of RLVR fine-tuning.

entry.title: JointServe: Serving Multi-Model Agents on Memory-Constrained GPUs

author.name: Daijin Hu

entry.summary: JointServe is a serving system for multi-model LLM agents that treats weight shards and KV cache blocks as unified residency objects under one memory budget, exploiting workload structure to avoid serialized weight swapping and session state loss on memory-constrained GPUs. It targets the shift toward agents orchestrating multiple expert models.

entry.title: Spectral World Renderer: Unified 3D Hyperspectral Unmixing

author.name: Chia-Ming Lee, Yu-Jou Hsiao, Ming-Ching Chang, Xin Li, Yu-Lun Liu, Chih-Chung Hsu

entry.summary: The Spectral World Renderer unifies world generation and hyperspectral unmixing by having a coding agent build executable 3D worlds rendered with measured spectra, yielding hyperspectral images with exact material labels and sub-pixel proportions. The resulting SWR-Bench spans eight indoor and outdoor worlds, addressing the lack of ground truth for 3D unmixing evaluation.

entry.title: ACRO: Actor-Critic Rollout Orchestration

author.name: Junhoo Lee, Seungyeon Kim, Baekseung Kim, Minkyu Kim, Suhyun Jeon, Jimyeong Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: ACRO is an actor-critic orchestration layer over a fixed VLA policy that decides when to continue an attempt and when to intervene, using a critic learned from rollouts to estimate success prospects. A Trajectory Retraction mechanism shortcuts the robot back to a re-entry target along the executed path, where the same VLA resumes from a fresh observation, evaluated with GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5 backbones.

entry.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress

author.name: Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi, Ruhan Wang, Junyao Yang, Chengsong Huang, Zhichao Liu, Xiyang Wu, Anhao Li, Yue Yu, Ergan Shang, Fuxiao Liu, Tong Zheng, Ninghao Liu, Lichao Sun, Haitao Mi, Leowei Liang

entry.summary: LHTB 2.0 extends the Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench with 77 tasks across 13 domains, using a systematic pipeline that generates scenarios from parameterized reference implementations with held-out behavioral evidence. It measures sustained agent progress with process rewards rather than binary final-state checks.

entry.title: FDE-Bench: Evaluating End-to-End Delivery from Underspecified Real-World Business Requests

author.name: Huaiming Li, Can Huang, Chufan Wu, Danyu Liu, Xiaomin Yuan, Qinze Li, Yui Lo, Wenhui Bai, Qianlong Wang, Zengle Ge, Xiyu Yan, Yuheng Cheng, Jinhui Ren, Guokai Chen, Jiaqun Liu, Haoran Li, Qianhui Liu, Annan Li, Jianmin Wu, Dawei Yin, Dou Shen

entry.summary: FDE-Bench is the first benchmark built from real customer projects to evaluate agents on end-to-end delivery, requiring interactive requirement clarification plus iterative optimization of combinatorial optimization and ML solutions across 49 cases. It fills a gap between benchmarks that assume explicit objectives and clarification benchmarks with artificial information gaps.

entry.title: Iterate on an LLM, Serve on an SLM

author.name: Keegan Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage workflow for deploying small language models on narrow, repetitive agentic subtasks: first prototype and refine the desired behavior in prompt space on a frontier LLM, then distill or transfer that behavior to a small model for low-cost serving. The motivation is that SLMs offer 5-40x cheaper inference than frontier models, but zero-shot small models typically fail production tasks and retraining is too slow for fast iteration cycles.

entry.title: CUSE: Fine-Grained Multimodal Unlearning with Counterfactual Guidance and On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Chenlu Ding, Jiancan Wu, Yanchen Luo, Tianyu Zhang, Yancheng Yuan, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: CUSE is a framework for unlearning sensitive or unsafe content from multimodal LLMs at token-level granularity. It constructs counterfactual inputs to identify which tokens carry the target information, then uses on-policy self-distillation to remove that content while preserving the rest of the response.

entry.title: Can You Trust Your Preference Models? Stackelberg Games for Alignment

author.name: Riccardo Formenti, Aditya Agrawal, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: Trains policies to search for comparisons where preference-model evaluators may reverse the underlying preference, surfacing candidates for additional human supervision. The search is formulated as a zero-sum Stackelberg game between a Leader minimizing ensemble disagreement and a Follower maximizing it, with equilibrium existence and uniqueness results.

entry.title: RECAP: Calibrating Low-Bit Reasoning Models on the History They Read

author.name: Chi Ruan, Yujie Chen, Zixiang Zhao, Jingcai Guo, Haotong Qin

entry.summary: Presents RECAP, a post-training quantization method for reasoning models that calibrates on long historical context rather than short segments, since quantization errors in cached keys and values accumulate across long chains of thought. Dynamic-prefix calibration separates long historical context from short-block reconstruction and regenerates prefix caches. This targets a specific, costly failure mode when serving low-bit reasoning models.

entry.title: FARL: A Fully Automated Pipeline of RL Interface and Solver Design

author.name: Tianyu Jin, Liuyu Xiang, Chaowen Yang, Xingyang Chang, Pei Pei Li, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: FARL automates the design of reinforcement learning pipelines by jointly searching over observation and reward programs, learning algorithms, and training configurations, rather than fixing the task formulation and optimizing only the algorithm. It diagnoses failures from training statistics and behavior, proposes design changes, and validates whether they improve learning.

entry.title: RetryBench: Separating Retry Permission from Recovery Outcomes in GPT Tool Use

author.name: You Liu, Yue Liu, Quanchao Lu

entry.summary: RetryBench separates false retry permission, where an agent retries a timed-out tool call without contractual support, from realized recovery outcomes in GPT tool use. Controlled experiments across OpenAI models including Sol, Terra, and Luna show large differences, with some models making unsupported retries on 55-60 of 80 changed-key trials while others made almost none.

entry.title: Computational Reflective Equilibrium for Agentic AI: A Rawlsian Alignment Scaffold for Governance

author.name: Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: This theoretical work proposes agentic reflective equilibrium (ARE), a computational framework inspired by Rawls that serves as an ethical alignment scaffold within agent harnesses. It links system-prompt principles, considered judgments, tool evidence, and candidate actions through typed support and attack relations to enable case-by-case alignment of LLM agents.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Integer-Only Training of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Hazem Hesham Yousef Shalby, Fabrizio Pittorino, Manuel Roveri

entry.summary: This paper presents a training algorithm where every tensor (weights, gradients, activations) is stored as INT8 and every operation, including weight and optimizer updates, is performed in integer arithmetic. It uses signed integer mantissas with explicit power-of-two exponents and composable integer building blocks, scaling to standard computer vision benchmarks where prior fully integer methods could not.

entry.title: G$^2$WAM: World Action Models for Efficient and Geometry Grounded Image-Goal Navigation

author.name: Ke Gui, Chenghao Shi, Ziyue Wang, Longwen Chen, Xieyuanli Chen, Huimin Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a Geometry Grounded World Action Model for image-goal navigation that learns scene-coordinate localization to encode spatial cues, avoiding both costly fine-tuning of pretrained models and expensive external 3D reconstruction. The approach maintains persistent spatial memory of scenes whose targets lie outside the current field of view, enabling efficient real-world deployment.

entry.title: PatientWM: Towards Generalizable Clinical World Models via Unified Patient States

author.name: Ziwen Kan, Jie Peng, Bo Yan, Davis Hobley, Zheng Zhang, Yu Tian, Tianlong Chen, Song Wang

entry.summary: PatientWM proposes a clinical world-model framework that defines patient state evolution across modalities and exposes prior states plus clinical actions as ordered transition context, enabling prediction of how a patient condition evolves under treatment changes. It aims to be reusable as inputs and prediction targets shift.

entry.title: Budgeted KV-Cache Repair for Evolving Contexts

author.name: Han Yu, Wenhui Zhu, Jincheng Cao, Rui Cai, Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Xiwen Chen, Hao Wang, Xuanzhao Dong, Han Shi, Menglin Zhou, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Lin Su, Mina Razghandi, Sayan Ghosh, Qing Lan, Rohit Jain, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem that deleting text from an LLM agent's context does not remove its influence on cached KV states, and full recomputation is expensive. The authors propose budgeted KV-cache repair, recomputing only a chosen fraction of the retained suffix, and show that refreshing coherent semantic regions (Semantic-Unit Refresh) outperforms refreshing isolated tokens using cheap embedding-based relevance scores. This matters for efficient long-running agents whose contexts evolve over time.

entry.title: DuplexAct: How Interactive Are Frontier Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models?

author.name: Jiaheng Dong, Shihong Tan, Gongping Huang, Jean Honorio, Abhirup Ghosh, Ting Dang

entry.summary: Introduces DuplexAct, a benchmark for evaluating action-taking in end-to-end full-duplex spoken language models, defining a three-level taxonomy of eight interaction actions across 24 conditions and distinguishing successful action-taking (immediate execution plus follow-through) from mere action occurrence. This matters because voice agents like live/realtime models must time interruptions, backchannels, and turn-taking correctly, yet existing benchmarks evaluate only whether actions happen rather than whether they succeed.

entry.title: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Wenhao Zhou, Jiajun Song, Haitao Wang, Zipeng Qiu, Yingqi Peng, Ruida Xu, Jiale Li, Wenshuang Li, Shusheng Xu, Wei Dong, Hao Dai, Tongkai Yang, Yi Gao, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: AReaL-RSI is a framework for organizing a persistent team of research agents that recursively self-improve without updating backbone LLM weights, with a leader agent allocating research orientations and coordinating shared findings. It formalizes the scaling tradeoff between evaluated outcomes and total system resource expenditure. The work engages directly with the practical difficulties of recursive self-improvement such as misleading early evaluation scores and lossy knowledge sharing.

entry.title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Thinker Team, Peng Gao, Jichao Jiao, Chen Liao, Daqin Luo, Yiming Ma, Baiyu Pan, Hailin Shi, Jiyuan Wang, Xiangming Xu, Xiongwei Zhao

entry.summary: Thinker-WM jointly models and generates RGB, metric depth, and robot actions within a single Unified Dynamics Transformer with modality-specific encoders/decoders, rather than coupling visual dynamics, geometry, and action through separate modules. Unification happens at the representation level across appearance, geometry, and action.

entry.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles

author.name: Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Jeva is a decision-native architecture that argues current autoregressive answer-prediction designs violate structural requirements for fast decision-making: null-awareness, permutation invariance, scalability of the option set, and cacheability of computation over recurring alternatives. The paper introduces an architecture that jointly satisfies these four properties for low-latency System One style decisions. This is a foundational critique and redesign of how models represent choice problems.

entry.title: Contrastive Covariance Subspaces for Activation Steering

author.name: Alexandros Xenos, Manos Plitsis, Niki Foteinopoulou, Yannis Panagakis, Ioannis Patras

entry.summary: The paper introduces Contrastive Covariance Steering (CCS), a training-free activation steering method that projects steering vectors into a low-dimensional subspace retaining target-concept variation while suppressing confounds like topic or style. This closed-form contrastive variance objective yields purer steering signals and improved generated text quality.

entry.title: Do you "see" what I "see"? A Multi-panel Visual Question Answer Dataset for Large Language Model Chart Analysis

author.name: Daniel J. Evans, J. P. Naiman, JooYoung Seo, J. Stephen Downie

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset built from synthetic but realistic multi-panel scientific figures to test whether large language and multimodal models can reliably perform task-oriented chart analysis. The benchmark scaffolds questions across a four-level description model, ranging from basic conceptual answers to interpretive and analytical understanding, motivated by the challenge of making figures in digital libraries searchable and reusable. Its significance lies in addressing a real gap: most chart-understanding evaluations use single plots, while actual scientific publications frequently contain complex multi-chart figures.

entry.title: Learnable Low-Rank Polynomial Sketch for Effective Linear Attention

author.name: Zongyue Qin, Haoran Deng, Jason Cong, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: The paper tackles the quadratic cost of softmax attention by improving polynomial-kernel linear attention. It introduces a learnable low-rank sketch that approximates high-degree polynomial kernels more accurately than prior random-feature approaches, preserving the sparse, spiky attention behavior that makes polynomial kernels effective.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Auctions for Multi-Winner Banner Ads

author.name: Lilian Sun, Henry Huang, Fucheng Warren Zhu, Giannis Daras, Constantinos Daskalakis

entry.summary: Proposes a novel auction framework where multiple bidders can co-win a single banner ad opportunity, with outcomes generated by diffusion models influenced by bid strength. Bidders declare value per unit of alignment between the generated image and their textual descriptions, and a mechanism combines bids into a score driving the reverse diffusion process.

entry.title: Getting Space Right: Agentic Rewards for Image Generation

author.name: Xiaofeng Tan, Jiaxin Lin, Haobo Yuan, Tiancheng Shen, Zihan Su, Rui Chen, Hongsong Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper presents a curriculum-guided RL framework for spatial text-to-image generation, introducing SpatialCritic, an agentic reward model combining reusable verification guidance with specialized vision tools. It addresses out-of-domain degradation via counterfactual preference data and agent-harness alignment, showing in-domain gains where prior RL work degraded.

entry.title: UDHRBench: Benchmarking Human Rights in Large Language Models

author.name: Alak Raad (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar), Noreldin Morssy (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar), Zeerak Suhail (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar), Serin Atiani (Princess Sumaya University for Technology, Jordan), Mustafa Jarrar (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar)

entry.summary: UDHRBench is a benchmark of 1,124 human-rights-conflicting questions spanning all 30 articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, with 4,496 responses from ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, and Fanar manually annotated by experts with high inter-annotator agreement (kappa 0.801). The analysis reveals systematic, non-trivial misalignments between model behavior and internationally recognized human rights standards. This operationalizes legal/ethical norm evaluation for LLMs.

entry.title: Adversarial Detection for Pre-trained Classifiers via Lipschitz-Margin Analysis with Certification

author.name: Rui Zhang, Xinle Cao, Huazhen Yu, Jian Liu, Youwen Zhu

entry.summary: This work proposes certifying detection rather than invariance of predictions: instead of guaranteeing predictions are stable within an l2 ball, it certifies that adversarial inputs within that ball will be detected. Using a Lipschitz-margin reduction, the approach avoids the expensive randomized-smoothing query cost and the accuracy loss of Lipschitz-constrained architectures.

entry.title: Uncovering the Generative Landscape of Diffusion Models: A Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion Framework

author.name: Hannah Janmohamed, Joao Correia, Penousal Machado, Antoine Cully

entry.summary: The paper argues that standard diffusion sampling is biased toward high-likelihood regions and proposes Quality-Diversity Diffusion, a framework combining QD optimization with diffusion models to uncover diverse, high-performing outputs. It includes a spectral-guided variant aimed at better exploration of the model's expressive range.

entry.title: Make Every Expansion Count: Learning to Search Efficiently in LLM Code Repair

author.name: Elad Sharony, Ido Greenberg, Jialin Song, Shie Mannor, Gal Chechik, Eli Meirom

entry.summary: CodeTriage is a learned 0.6B-parameter policy that prioritizes proposed code-repair edits before costly generation and testing, reading test outputs, failure diagnoses, and proposed edits to predict the number of repair steps needed. This improves efficiency of search in LLM code repair compared to policies relying only on pass rates and search statistics.

entry.title: Unravel: Recovering an Interactive 3D Scene from a Single Image

author.name: Hui Shan, Keyang Luo, Binjia Zhou, Ming Li, Kai Li, Xin Wang, Zhenyang Li, Zesong Yang, Weikai Chen, Runze Zhang, Xin Wang, Yanwei Fu, Zhen Chen, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: Presents Unravel, a training-free framework that converts a single image into an interactive 3D scene with independently movable object assets. It uses an agentic loop that iteratively peels objects from the image, with a VLM planning visibility, an image editor removing objects, and point clouds used to recover spatial relationships.

entry.title: Rescuing Points Trapped Inside Incorrect Decision Regions: A target for Evaluating and Improving Forward-Forward Learning

author.name: Alireza Rahmansetayesh, Amirhossein Yousefiramandi, Maxwell Spiridonov, Sumit Raut, Kent Ziti, Pierre Baldi

entry.summary: This paper shows that linear-probe accuracy over-credits Forward-Forward learning, since even untrained networks score well above chance, and introduces a Boundary Proximity Index methodology to identify which datapoints actually improve with training. It proposes rescuing points trapped in incorrect decision regions as a concrete target for improving local, backprop-free learning.

entry.title: SuPER-Mamba: Surprisal Prioritization for Extended-Context Routing in Mamba

author.name: Zhetong Zhang, Gayan K Kulatilleke

entry.summary: SuPER-Mamba is a training-free method that uses per-token surprisal from next-token predictions to prioritize global channel updates in pretrained Mamba state space models, improving long-context behavior. On LongBench-E across three models it raises the average score from 8.06 to 15.69, a large relative gain without any additional training.

entry.title: WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat

author.name: Jiajun Han, Guoxin Ma, Felix, Liangsheng Xu, Ruiqi Yu, Yingdi Guo, Zongbing Wang, Xinhua Ye, Chenyan Hua, Xin Xie, Pengcheng Yang, Haijun Wu

entry.summary: Presents WeGR, a generative retrieval framework deployed in WeChat's industrial search, addressing two bottlenecks: semantic-ID tokenizers that poorly incorporate collaborative signals, and reward sparsity in reinforcement learning under exact SID matching. The system unifies candidate generation in an autoregressive framework with improved tokenizers and RL training signals.

entry.title: On Making $\mathrm{SE}(2)$-Invariant Networks Optimal

author.name: Tomas Karella, Emily Shinkle, Alice Elisabeth Anastasia Allen, Pieter J. Swart, Nicholas Lubbers, Roxana Bujack

entry.summary: Building on classical invariant theory, the authors derive SE(2)-invariant feature maps that are provably optimal in being minimal and information-preserving with respect to the symmetry group. The construction integrates into standard architectures without modifying nonlinearities or normalization layers. This provides a principled foundation for extending CNN-style inductive biases to rotation-translation symmetries.

entry.title: Box-WAM: Box Trajectories as Compact State Representations for World Action Models

author.name: Qinxi Yu, Wenzhou Ding, Gloria X. Wang, Albert J. Zhai, Shenlong Wang

entry.summary: Box-WAM replaces dense future-frame video prediction in world action models with oriented bounding-box trajectories of task-relevant objects as a compact state representation. By explicitly imagining object-centric future motion, it retains the planning and supervision benefits of future prediction while substantially reducing training and inference computation.

entry.title: TSRL: Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Continual Agent Training

author.name: Yuqian Fu, Kaiwen Jiang, Zijun Song, Jiawei Wang, Yuanheng Zhu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: TSRL combines RL and SFT for continual training of LLM agents, using an adaptive state-dependent trigger to apply expert supervision only where needed. The goal is to reduce catastrophic forgetting while retaining SFT's sample efficiency and RL's capability preservation.

entry.title: Same Attack, Different Judge: A First Controlled Adversarial Comparison of Jev, LLM Judges, and Purpose-Built Safety Classifiers

author.name: Xiang Li, Aichun Huang, Mingming Zhang, Zheli Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents the first controlled adversarial evaluation of TypeSafe AI's Jev safety judge, testing it against five GPT/GLM judges and two local classifiers (Llama Guard 3, Prompt Guard 2) using fifty attack variants across thirteen families on four tasks. The uniform harness reveals how adversarial pressure differentially affects each safety judge.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer of Evil Vectors Is Directionally Asymmetric

author.name: Juann Kim, Minku Kang

entry.summary: Studies whether persona vectors, linear directions in LLM residual streams encoding behavioral traits, transfer across languages, focusing on the evil persona vector relevant to jailbreaks and unlearning. Across English, Spanish, Swahili, and Telugu on four open instruction-tuned LLMs, transfer proves directionally asymmetric, with vectors harder to extract or apply in low-resource languages.

entry.title: Match the Canvas, Not Just the Answer: Predictability-Aware SFT for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Miao Li, Hanyang Jiang, Hengyu Fu, Baihe Huang, Yating Liu, Yuhang Cai, Changkun Guan, Zhongzhu Chen, Jiecheng Lu, Michael A. Boateng, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: Identifies a training-inference mismatch in supervised fine-tuning of diffusion language models: random masking choices about visible reference tokens and generation space can conceal prediction errors or penalize uncertainty that decoding would otherwise resolve. The paper proposes predictability-aware SFT that aligns training supervision with the model's evolving predictability during parallel generation.

entry.title: Can Machine Learning Potentials Be More Accurate Than the Methods They Are Trained On?

author.name: Pavlo O. Dral, Yi-Fan Hou, Yuxinxin Chen, Hassan Nawaz, Mateusz Witkowski, Szymon \'Smiga, Ireneusz Grabowski

entry.summary: This Perspective argues that machine learning interatomic potentials can exceed the accuracy of their quantum-chemical training methods by generalizing across a third axis: the space of quantum-chemical methods themselves. The authors propose method-transferable MLPs that predict at unseen methods, with implementations in both density-functional and wavefunction theories demonstrating the claim. This challenges a widely held assumption in computational chemistry and suggests a new paradigm for scientific ML.

entry.title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes

author.name: Yu Wang, Rui Dai, Wei Chen, Yi Wang, Bo Dang, Kaikui Liu, Xiangxiang Chu, Yansheng Li

entry.summary: Urbex recasts city-scale 3D visual grounding as active spatial search, letting a VLM agent query landmarks, zoom into regions, and render oblique views of an interactive multi-view environment, with the tool-use policy trained via reinforcement learning using localization and shaping rewards. It achieves state-of-the-art Hit@1 and IoU on CityRefer without requiring candidate proposals.

entry.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting

author.name: Hai Lu, Yichen Luo, Luping Yu

entry.summary: The authors have GPT-4o referee papers from the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings and compare its scores with actual publication in top-three finance journals over the following two years, finding that papers rated one standard deviation higher are 44 percent more likely to be published even after controlling for author reputation. They rule out look-ahead bias since the model cannot recall the outcomes. The predictive signal comes from judgments of correctness and exposition rather than originality or significance.

entry.title: When More Objectives Make Identification Easier: The Role of Preferences and Feedback

author.name: Bo Xue, Ji Cheng, Yuanyu Wan, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: This paper studies best-arm identification (BAI) in multi-objective bandits, showing counterintuitively that additional objectives can make identification easier rather than harder. The authors characterize when and why richer feedback from multiple objectives reduces required exploration, establishing a characteristic-time lower bound for fixed-confidence identification in Gaussian bandits that holds uniformly across preference orderings. This matters for applications like recommendation, clinical trials, and RLHF-style preference learning where systems must optimize multiple criteria simultaneously.

entry.title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Fabian Gr\"oger, Na\"el Ouerghemi, Shuo Wen, Maria Brbi\'c

entry.summary: The authors show that only 10-20% of data is needed for projector training in multimodal LLMs to recover most downstream gains, and that projectors trained on different datasets can be linearly interpolated while preserving performance. They conclude projector training performs only coarse alignment and propose PORTAL, a more efficient training scheme. This challenges common practice and offers practical efficiency savings.

entry.title: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models

author.name: Jingbo Xu, Jianjie Fang, Zhuohang Li, Zihao Song, Zhaolu Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Xin Zhang, Haisheng Su, Yinzhou Tang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li

entry.summary: UniW(A)M is a mixture-of-experts framework built on diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and world-action model variants, using shared experts to capture common physical dynamics while specialized experts preserve paradigm-specific capabilities. This enables knowledge reuse between future prediction and executable action generation, which are typically trained in isolation.

entry.title: Inverse Reasoning Models for Efficient Post-Training and Verification from Answer-Only Data

author.name: Eric O. Korman

entry.summary: This work proposes a self-distillation post-training method for reasoning LLMs that treats chain-of-thought as a latent variable and uses only answer-only data, positioning itself between costly CoT-supervised finetuning and compute-heavy RL with verifiable rewards. The approach aims to combine the data efficiency of SFT with lower compute cost than multi-sample RL.

entry.title: How Inner Optimizers Shape Replica Scaling

author.name: Eugene Belilovsky, Stefan Horoi, Edouard Oyallon, Benjamin Th\'erien

entry.summary: The paper theoretically and empirically analyzes how inner optimizer choice (e.g., Muon versus AdamW) affects performance degradation when scaling model replicas in distributed LLM training across poorly connected compute pools, building on local optimization methods like DiLoco. It aims to explain the previously empirical observation that optimizer choice significantly improves replica scaling trends.

entry.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Where Does the Teacher's Advantage Live?

author.name: Yiping Li, Fan Zhao, Zhibo Hou, Zhiyu An, Wan Du

entry.summary: Revisits on-policy distillation through the knowledge-distillation lens, using controlled token flips at teacher-student disagreements to measure how much accuracy teacher corrections provide along student trajectories. Repeated flips lift accuracy from 28.4% to 74.5%, near the teacher's 76.9%, and mass/KL-based flip selection beats random flips by 15-18 points.

entry.title: Why don't Graph Transformers attend to the same token?

author.name: Alexandre Bismuth

entry.summary: This paper investigates the attention-sink phenomenon, well known in LLMs, in graph transformers. The authors show that the SoTA graph transformer GRIT rarely forms attention sinks on molecules, with trends opposite to those in LLMs, and prove that graph symmetry and locality can structurally limit sinks while the attention scoring function is the main remaining determinant. This deepens the theoretical understanding of attention dynamics across architectures and domains.

entry.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference

author.name: Gil Jae Song, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: PN-Mix is a mixed-precision quantization method for key caches in RoPE-based LLM decoders that allocates precision based on query-key pair-norm products rather than key statistics alone. Attention logit perturbation analysis shows channel pairs with large pair-norm products drive logit variation under low-bit quantization. The method targets KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks in long-output inference while preserving accuracy at low bits.

entry.title: Occupancy Modeling via Drifting: One-Step Generation Enables Direct Policy Extraction

author.name: Robin Uhrich, Marco Bagatella, N\'uria Armengol Urp\'i, Pavel Kolev, Georg Martius

entry.summary: This paper systematically decomposes the recipe of reinforcement learning from unlabeled data via generative occupancy models along three axes: required multimodal structure, generative model class, and policy extraction method. The analysis yields a simplified approach culminating in one-step generation that enables direct policy extraction. It provides clarity and simpler alternatives for behavior foundation model construction.

entry.title: ChemArgus: Automated Scientific Diagnostics for Lab-Grade Multimodal Chemistry Reasoning: A Frontier Benchmark

author.name: Hanyao Guo, Mo Cui, Zihan Tan, Leixin Sun, Yichun Wang, Yinan Shen, Guojun Zhu, Jia Jiang, Erhao Chen, Zui Chen, Wenzhe Gao, Zhihao Yu, Qijun Wang, Yetian Zhu, Jiande Chen, Chuhang Pei, Yao Jiang, Yichen Fan, Pinhan Wang, Xiaorui Pan, Qianyi Zhu, Yang Liu, Mang Ye, Guancheng Wan

entry.summary: ChemArgus is a competition-level multimodal chemistry benchmark with fine-grained scoring that grades every subquestion with partial credit, distinguishing memorized facts from stepwise derivation, visual from textual inputs, and planning from execution, so failures in reasoning chains can be localized. It draws from competition materials, textbooks, and research papers. This addresses real blind spots in current chemistry evaluation of frontier models.

entry.title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models

author.name: Qinglin Su, Licheng Pan, Zhen Fang, Jiakang Wang, Qingnan Ren, Yunsheng Lu, Yan Gao, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: RM-OPD addresses bottlenecks in Mix-RL training of generative reward models — reward sparsity and cross-domain interference — via a two-stage framework that first trains domain-specialist teachers with on-policy distillation and then integrates capabilities. The approach targets imbalanced capability acquisition and reward hacking in general-purpose GRM training.

entry.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?

author.name: Kaifei Wang, Zikang Shan, Liwei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes momentum in RLVR through a bandit formulation with bias-corrected EMA momentum, proving that when policy gradients are exact, increasing the EMA coefficient within a non-overshoot range strictly accelerates optimization, while sampled gradients can mask the positive gain via fluctuations. This gives the first clear account of when and why momentum helps LLM RL fine-tuning. It directly informs a design choice in every major RLHF/RLVR pipeline.

entry.title: Semi-Amortized Bayesian Inference with Reusable Local Posteriors

author.name: Niek Stevenson, Paul-Christian B\"urkner, Andrew Heathcote, Stefan T. Radev

entry.summary: Introduces a semi-amortized Bayesian inference method that partitions parameters into blocks and trains neural estimators to approximate each block's full conditional posterior from simulations, reusing them where updates are expensive or repeated. By exploiting conditional independence, it sidesteps the difficulty of learning full joint posteriors in high-dimensional simulation-based inference. From a strong simulation-based inference group including Stefan Radev.

entry.title: Target-Token Asymmetry Can Masquerade As Depth Specialization

author.name: Danlin Li, Miao Li, Xu Han, Jiecheng Lu

entry.summary: This paper shows that layer-ablation studies used to infer depth specialization in language models can produce spurious conclusions because the target tokens being predicted differ across corpora, for example math solutions contain more whitespace and numbers than encyclopedic prose. The authors recompute cross-corpus early-late damage interactions under a shared target-token mixture between GSM8K and Wikitext, replicating the effect across five model instances. The result is a caution about a common interpretability methodology and a proposed correction.

entry.title: DAGFormer: Global Topology Prediction for Transformer Cross-Layer Connections

author.name: Xiaocong Yang, Yuren Hao, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: DAGFormer is a Transformer LM whose cross-layer connections are planned globally by a jointly trained topology predictor that controls connection strength per input token, unlike prior routing architectures that set connections layer by layer. On matched OLMo-2 pairs from 75M to 1B parameters it lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by 17-25%, and a 1B model trained on 5B tokens outperforms the vanilla model trained on 10B. This suggests substantial data-efficiency gains from learned global topology.

entry.title: Model What Matters: Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling for Language Agents

author.name: Maolin Ran, Minda Chen, Di Huang, Wei Xiong, Fei Huang, Weiwen Liu

entry.summary: DGS-WM improves RL-trained LLM agents by adding auxiliary world modeling supervision that is selectively guided by decision relevance rather than uniformly modeling all environment observations. This addresses the sparsity of trajectory-level task rewards by teaching agents action-conditioned environment dynamics.

entry.title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shuxuan Li, Jialiang Kang, Yanghao Zhou, Ziye Zhu, Xiao Yang

entry.summary: FOLD is a training-free method that improves speculative decoding on long inputs by letting lightweight drafters attend to the full history without restricting the context window or rescaling positions, preserving exact local order while treating distant context as position-free far memory. This addresses the degradation of short-context-trained drafters on long sequences without costly long-context drafter training.

entry.title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models

author.name: Harsh Kumar

entry.summary: Auditing ten open models across eight languages, this paper shows that apparent reductions in stereotype scores outside English are largely artifacts of translation quality and measurement noise rather than genuine fairness differences. Item-by-item testing with rewording controls and injected shifts demonstrates that lower bias scores do not imply fairer models in multilingual settings.

entry.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion

author.name: Huixuan Cheng, Bike Zhang, Shankar Sastry, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: This work explores generatively modeling the weight space of humanoid control policies, using a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder compressing actor network parameters with a Diffusion Transformer. It asks whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generated directly in weight space rather than through conventional training. This is an intriguing direction connecting generative modeling and robot control.

entry.title: Moral Combat: Exploiting Moral Foundations Theory to Jailbreak LLMs

author.name: Adel Khorramrouz, Yi-Chia Wang, Sharon Levy

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-agent jailbreak framework grounded in Moral Foundations Theory that reframes harmful requests as morally virtuous by diagnosing the violated moral foundation, rewriting the prompt under a justifiable foundation, and reinforcing it with generated precedents. The work demonstrates that LLMs can be moralized to bypass safety guardrails, mirroring human persuasion psychology.

entry.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing

author.name: Xiaohan Wang, Haozhen Zhang, Qingyuan Liu, Tao Feng, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: Proposes RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that jointly learns routing mode selection (single-round, multi-round, agentic) and model selection within a single LLM policy. It introduces COMET-GRPO, which decouples trajectory-level advantages into separate mode and execution signals for coordinated training.

entry.title: MemDuet: Learning Dual-Process Memory for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Jiangcheng Song, Haodong Jing, Yulin Mu, Lesong Tao, Jixin Wang, Jin Cui, Tianjing Ren, Runxuan Xie, Yongqiang Ma, Nanning Zheng

entry.summary: MemDuet is a dual-process memory framework for reasoning over very long documents, pairing a small language model that rapidly selects evidence from context chunks (System 1) with a large language model that verifies and updates memory in document order (System 2), inspired by Kahneman's fast/slow thinking account. Training proceeds via supervised fine-tuning, GRPO on System 2, and joint optimization. It addresses the trade-off between reasoning quality and inference efficiency in recurrent memory agents.

entry.title: What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds

author.name: Caixin Kang, Ke Wang, Yuchuan Wu, Xiaoqiang Wang, Ling Li, Bingxue Qiu, Yongbin Li, Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: The authors introduce HICO-Bench, 180 everyday coordination scenarios where two agents with private information converse and then independently record the plan they reached. Success is verified programmatically via feasibility checking plus LLM-judged integrity, enabling outcome-based evaluation and learning for social agents beyond subjective judge ratings.

entry.title: Taking the PULSE of Medical Reasoning: Step-Level Retrieval Timing for Knowledge-Grounded Inference

author.name: Danyang Zhao, Sendong Zhao, Yanrui Du, Haochun Wang, Ming Ma, Wenhao Li, Jingbo Wang, Jiatong Liu, Bing Qin

entry.summary: This paper tackles the retrieval-timing problem in medical LLM reasoning: deciding at each reasoning step whether internal knowledge is reliable or external evidence should be fetched, since indiscriminate retrieval adds noise and latency. The authors show erroneous reasoning steps exhibit higher inter-layer volatility of internal representations, and build PUlSE, a lightweight probe that uses these intrinsic signals for step-level retrieval control. This improves factual trustworthiness of medical reasoning while controlling cost.

entry.title: Cascaded Retrieval with Cross-Modal Query Refinement for Efficient Visual Document Search

author.name: Diana Turmakhan, Aseem Srivastava, Vivek Gupta, Iryna Gurevych, Thamar Solorio

entry.summary: This paper introduces SCOUT, a cascaded two-track retrieval framework for visually rich document search that uses a lightweight parent retriever to filter candidates before applying a stronger multi-vector reranker, alongside a semantic track over offline hierarchical summaries. This decouples retrieval quality from exhaustive corpus-wide search, addressing a key scalability bottleneck for vision-language retrievers.

entry.title: Same Claim, Different Interpretations: How LLM Agents Resolve Ambiguity in Scientific Claims

author.name: Delip Rao, Ahmed Muharram, Chris Callison-Burch

entry.summary: This paper addresses a gap in LLM-based scientific claim verification: natural-language scientific claims are often ambiguous and admit multiple defensible interpretations, yet automated verifiers typically resolve them tacitly without recording which interpretation was used. The authors propose Claim Cards, a structured nine-field representation that makes a verifier's interpretation explicit within its reasoning, enabling more traceable and fair comparison against expert labels. This matters for the reliability of agentic co-scientist systems, since unrecorded interpretive choices can produce apparent expert disagreements and wasted compute.

entry.title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models

author.name: Nan Zhou, Jianxiong Gao, Qiuyu Wang, Wen Wang, Jiahao Wang, Yufeng Yuan, Shuaiting Li, Hao Ouyang, Yujun Shen, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: WorldMemBench systematically evaluates world memory in video world models across 260 test cases, measuring static memory (retention of identities, object appearance and geometry, environment content) and dynamic memory (event progression, state persistence) via controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories. It positions memory as a capability to evaluate alongside visual fidelity and duration.

entry.title: MMKG-R1: Constructing Multimodal Knowledge Graphs via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zongyu Wu, Yilong Wang, Xiaochen Wang, Minhua Lin, Yuan Zhong, Fenglong Ma, Xiang Zhang, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: MMKG-R1 trains a multimodal LLM to construct multimodal knowledge graphs using a quality-driven RL framework with more direct feedback than final-answer-correctness signals. Improved MMKG construction supports multimodal Graph RAG and downstream MLLM performance.

entry.title: Frame Evidence:A Benchmark for Reference Frames and Visual Evidence in Multi-Image Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Chunxi Luo, Qishuai Ding, Xingchen Peng, Hengwei Ye, Ke Zhang, Wenxin Lian, Tianyi Lu, Chunlong Yu, Zhenya Lin

entry.summary: Frame Evidence introduces a benchmark of 320 matched triplets and 960 Chinese multiple-choice questions separating reference-frame understanding from visual evidence sufficiency in spatial reasoning. With joint metrics requiring consistency across frames and paired evidence variants, best models drop from ~50% item accuracy to 10.42% three-frame group accuracy, revealing brittleness.

entry.title: Physics-Shaped, Not Physical: Auditing Physics-Guided Underwater Image Restoration

author.name: Mochamad Rizal Fauzan, Irgi Surya

entry.summary: This audit rigorously tests whether the physics module in a representative physics-guided underwater image restoration network actually helps, via five-seed ablations, zero-shot evaluation on LSUI and AUIED3K, a capacity-matched control, and validation of predicted maps on Sea-thru. It finds the physics module provides no zero-shot gain at full data (PSNR differences within noise) at 3.4x compute cost, with benefit only in low-data regimes.

entry.title: When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO

author.name: Xinrui Lin, Fan Li, Shumin Wang, Dehong Kong, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: The authors audit 6,976 on-policy comparison graphs in GRPO-based reinforcement learning for video generation and show that cyclic preferences are common and persistent throughout training. They propose a reliability-anchored preference walk that exploits comparison structure instead of naive average win-rate aggregation, improving the reliability of advantage estimates for video generation RL.

entry.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation

author.name: Weijie Wang, Haomin Zhang, Ye Li, Akide Liu, Zeyu Zhang, Haoyu Zhao, Yefei He, Donny Y. Chen, Feng Chen, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: ATAS tackles consistency in long-form agentic video generation by compiling a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and event-time references. It maintains scene memory of static geometry and event memory of dynamic observations, retrieving evidence before generation and updating state only after review checks, enabling revisits and replays of past events.

entry.title: Learning Keypoint Constraints from Visual Demonstrations for Safe Motion Planning

author.name: Zheng Qiu, Zhouyu Zhang, Ninghan Zhong, Glen Chou

entry.summary: KCL learns task-relevant motion constraints from RGB-D visual demonstrations by reducing observations to sparse 3D object-centric keypoints, inferring distance- and orientation-based constraints via KKT optimality conditions, and planning safely under uncertainty with these constraints. It bridges visual imitation and formal safe planning. This combination of perception-derived constraints with optimality-based inference is a notable methodological contribution.

entry.title: HiFun: a Hierarchical Framework for Efficient Functional Dexterous Manipulation Learning

author.name: Linyi Huang, Guowei Huai, Weibin Liu, Shulong Jiang, Ping Tan, Weixuan Zhang, Hui Zhang, Jie Song

entry.summary: HiFun is a hierarchical framework for teaching multi-fingered robot hands functional manipulation, addressing the difficulty of modeling precise contact and coordinated arm-hand motion in simulation. It tackles costly and noisy real-world demonstrations in the full arm-hand control space and includes mechanisms for recovering from off-nominal contact states such as slipped contact.

entry.title: Complementary Future Token Pruning for World Action Models

author.name: Baekseung Kim, Junhoo Lee, Sohyeon Hong, Suhyun Jeon, Minkyu Kim, Seungyeon Kim, Donghoon Han, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: This paper introduces CF-Prune, a training-free method for pruning future-frame tokens in pretrained world action models (WAMs), exploiting the insight that visual predictions serve action generation and need not retain full video-synthesis fidelity. It uses instruction and action attention plus an entropy-based phase mechanism to keep dense computation only where precision matters, reducing inference latency.

entry.title: Thompson Sampling for Learning in Zero-Sum Games

author.name: Kenshi Abe, Kaito Ariu, Po-An Wang

entry.summary: This paper provides the first rigorous regret analysis of Thompson sampling in unknown two-player zero-sum matrix games with Gaussian bandit feedback. Under centralized self-play, sampling a payoff matrix from the posterior and playing a Nash equilibrium of the sampled game achieves an expected cumulative duality gap of O(sqrt(T)) for games with unique Nash equilibria, improving to O(log T) for pure equilibria. The authors also identify the exact sqrt(T) coefficient and a matching minimax lower bound.

entry.title: The Safety Culture at the Labs is Broken

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi argues that safety culture at frontier AI labs is inadequate, crediting Anthropic with comparatively strong (but still eroding) safety culture while describing OpenAI's cultural problems as deeper, citing David Robinson's whistleblower resignation and the firing of three safety researchers. The post contends that even at the best labs there is excessive confidence in muddling through with operational excellence.

entry.title: ConicFlow: constrained Inference-time optimal control for flow matching models

author.name: Shervin Khalafi, Kasra Fallah, Sung Cho, Dongsheng Ding, James Anderson, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: ConicForm frames constrained sampling from flow matching models as an inference-time optimal control problem balancing trajectory deviation against reward under hard terminal constraints. It uses receding-horizon control with a primal-dual algorithm whose multipliers adapt during sampling to steer generation toward feasible outputs.

entry.title: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents

author.name: Jinlong Luo, Haoran Wu, Bo Xu

entry.summary: DSABench evaluates agents that must find relevant databases in a large catalog, determine how results fit together, and execute multi-source workflows, unlike text-to-SQL benchmarks that supply the target database. It provides 815 human-reviewed tasks built on Spider, BIRD, and LiveSQLBench, executable contracts, and a RouteEnv for catalog inspection without gold-label leakage.

entry.title: Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses

author.name: Weichen Yu, Lesly Miculicich, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Jiefeng Chen, Shuo Li, Matt Fredrikson, Tomas Pfister, Long T. Le

entry.summary: Formulates evolution of LLM agent harnesses as multi-objective optimization, using decomposition-based evolutionary search to maintain solutions across the Pareto frontier and to separate transferable harness design from environment-specific adaptation. This extends prior single-objective, monolithic harness-evolution approaches.

entry.title: When Skills Remain But Access Fails: Factorized Skill Memory for Continual Skill Internalization

author.name: Haomiao Qiu, Yining Tang, Hongyi Wan, Changfeng Sun, Ziyue Qiao, Miao Zhang

entry.summary: Studies forgetting in continual skill internalization, where language-model agents convert procedural skills into persistent capabilities that no longer require retrieval at inference. It uncovers a two-stage hierarchical forgetting structure: a model first loses the ability to invoke an old skill from a raw request while a canonical skill name restores it, and later conditional execution also degrades. Proposes a factorized skill memory in response.

entry.title: Revocation Is Not Complete at Receipt: An Executable Outcome Contract for Distributed Agent-Tool Gateways

author.name: Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Danping Zhang

entry.summary: This paper defines C0-C5, a bounded outcome contract for authority revocation in distributed agent-tool gateways, spanning issuer commit through effect prevention, implemented as a persistent monitor with a 14-case fault matrix. It shows that treating intermediate states like C3 or C4 as completion produces multiple false positives, formalizing why revocation reported at commit or acknowledgment is not actually enforced everywhere.

entry.title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts

author.name: Zhaoyu Fan, Bowen Han, Jincheng Ou, Yanwei Ren, Zehua He, Kaiyu Huang, Pengcheng He, Shanshan Ni, Chengchen Gong, Shuai Xue, Qingjiang Shi

entry.summary: ProCARE reformulates automation of real-world healthcare studies with LLM agents as constrained compilation, converting heterogeneous data into profile-grounded evidence contracts that enforce dataset-specific clinical semantics like index dates and outcome boundaries. This addresses brittleness from schema mismatches, temporal errors, and unsupported clinical claims.

entry.title: Geospatial Vector Geometry as a Native Spatial Modality for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huang Fei, Boyi Chen, Hao Xue, Yang Yue, Yehong Xu, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes treating geospatial vector geometry as a native input modality for vision-language models, introducing GeoVec-VLM with a structured geometry representation that preserves the spatial arrangement of vector objects. This addresses the bottleneck where VLMs relying only on vision and language struggle with precise spatial relations at geographic scale.

entry.title: ChemExplain: A Multimodal Benchmark for Explanatory Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Aotian Chen, Frazier N. Baker, Reza Averly, Shan Zhang, Tianao Chen, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Xia Ning, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: ChemExplain is a benchmark of 1,180 multiple-choice questions from 383 peer-reviewed papers testing explanatory attribution: identifying which visible structural feature most directly explains an observed chemical effect. Each question pairs a molecular or reaction image with four candidate mechanism-structure explanations.

entry.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control

author.name: Binghan Wu, Kai Zeng, Kai Yang, Ya-Qin Zhang, Joseph Sifakis, Ye Ouyang

entry.summary: RAN-JEPA tackles the observation-intervention asymmetry in mobile networks, where passive telemetry is abundant but controlled action-response trajectories are scarce. The model separates representation learning from intervention learning: it first learns predictive latent representations from observation-only data via a JEPA-style objective, then adapts to the deployment domain and learns action-conditioned dynamics from limited sleep/wake control data. This enables energy-efficient RAN control with a credible author list including Joseph Sifakis and Ya-Qin Zhang.

entry.title: Empowering Edge Agents: A Systematic Analysis of Edge-Cloud Collaboration in LLM Agent Execution

author.name: Pengcheng Huang, Zhenghao Liu, Shixin Ren, Shi Yu, Sijia Yao, Yukun Yan, Chaojun Xiao, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Introduces EC2-Bench for evaluating edge-cloud collaboration during long-horizon LLM agent execution, where cloud model participation is interleaved throughout a trajectory rather than a one-shot routing decision, covering task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure. This matters because edge-cloud hybrid agents are a growing deployment pattern where latency, cost, and data locality tradeoffs interact in poorly understood trajectory-level ways.

entry.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments

author.name: Linhai Ma, Yan Wang, Lingfei Qian, Yupeng Cao, Victor Gutierrez Basulto

entry.summary: The paper identifies a derivation gap: LLM tool-call judges accept correct argument values far less often when no reference text stating the value is present, such as schema defaults or values that must be inferred. The effect appears across seven evaluated judges and persists even without truncation, showing judges rely on references rather than derivation.

entry.title: Posterior Flow Matching

author.name: Chenrui Ma, Xi Xiao, Lin Zhao, Xinru Jiang, Tianyang Wang, Yanning Shen, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: Posterior Flow Matching (PFM) extends flow matching by learning conditional velocity means and componentwise variances through a Gaussian posterior model, so a single model evaluation yields both a transport prediction and endpoint uncertainty at any intermediate state. These learned moments support both a mean-driven ODE and a posterior-driven SDE with adaptive local noise scaling. Experiments span images, point clouds, and molecules.

entry.title: Pick the Mixture, Not the Samples: Combinatorial Data Selection for LLMs

author.name: Luyang Zhang, Jialu Wang, Bebei Li

entry.summary: This work formalizes Combinatorial Data Selection, a framework for LLM fine-tuning data curation that separates attribution from selection and models non-additive interactions among samples across domains. Experiments on instruction-tuning pools reveal substantial cross-domain complementarity and redundancy that per-sample methods miss.

entry.title: Akule: Fast and Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Sparse Interaction Diffusion

author.name: Manav Vora, Gokul Puthumanaillam, Aditya Penumarti, Jane Shin, Melkior Ornik

entry.summary: Akule scales diffusion-based multi-robot motion planning by augmenting a frozen single-robot prior with learned modules for pairwise interaction correction, contextual selection of which interactions to compute, and composition of their effects. This decomposition separates deciding which interactions matter from how their effects combine, avoiding expensive joint computation for large robot teams.

entry.title: Target-ESS Tempered Policy Optimization (TETPO): Smooth Variance Control via Bridge Importance Sampling

author.name: Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Kayhan Behdin, Wenhui Zhu, Aida Rahmattalabi, Jincheng Cao, Jelena Markovic-Voronov, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: TETPO addresses heavy-tailed importance weights in asynchronous off-policy RL post-training of LLMs, where a few stale-policy trajectories can collapse the effective sample size and destabilize gradient estimates. It adaptively tempers correction strength via bridge importance sampling to target a desired ESS, unlike fixed interventions that discard or reweight samples regardless of severity.

entry.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence

author.name: Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Wenyang Hui, Weiqiang Hang, Luqing Wang, Zejian Wang, Zirui Tu, Jingsheng Mao, Shaobo Hu, Yang Luo, Jiale Guo, Jin Zhang, Yudan Liu, Zhaokai Luo, Ren Huan, Yao Hu, Chengyue Jiang, Wenjie Li, Chuan Mu

entry.summary: Proposes using real user behavior histories as a supervisory signal for LLMs, introducing Vela, a framework that converts real behavior data from platforms into training data for inferring preferences, intent, and likely future actions over long horizons. It targets the user dimension of LLM intelligence relevant to assistants, recommendations, and advertising.

entry.title: Too Late to Prune: Generative AI, the Screen, and Team Creative Decisions

author.name: Difang Huang, Shumin Yu, Fadong Chen, Weihua Zhou

entry.summary: Using a preregistered experiment with 148 three-person teams on a product-design task, the study shows that moving the same 15 minutes of LLM access from the search stage to the selection stage lowered expert-rated creativity by 0.62 standard deviations. The results support a model where AI options arriving before a team's screen add value while late options remain unscreened.

entry.title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming

author.name: Abrar Alotaibi, Moataz Ahmed

entry.summary: REPRO is a pure black-box automated red-teaming framework that uses evolutionary optimization driven by a 7B open-weight reflective model on a single consumer GPU, introducing semantic crossover for multi-parent recombination. It targets adversarial prompt discovery against safety-aligned LLMs without privileged access or per-model templates.

entry.title: Adaptive Look, Flexible Thought: Learning How and How Long to Think in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Quanlin Chen, Xiuwei Chen, Kun Xiang, Zehua Ma, Chunjin Ye, Boqiang Guo, Xianming Liu, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: L2T is a unified reasoning framework for multimodal LLMs that jointly optimizes visual perception and textual reasoning depth, rather than treating tool-produced visual computation as an auxiliary component. It discretizes visual states into visual tokens, allowing the model to adaptively decide both how to look and how long to think.

entry.title: A Scaled-Up Empirical Study of Syntactic Language Models

author.name: Pengcheng Wang, Zhexuan Zhang, Chao Lou, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: This paper presents a large-scale controlled study of syntactic language models, comparing 12 configurations of tree linearization and attention masks at scales up to 1B parameters and 100B tokens, evaluated on 11 downstream tasks and two syntactic benchmarks. Results clarify whether the promise of SLMs on syntactic generalization holds at scale with standard causal attention.

entry.title: D-World: An Explicit World-Language-Action Model with Recursive Self-Improvement under Dual Control

author.name: Xuan Wen, Baichao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes D-World, an explicit world-language-action model on a Sense-Plan-Act decomposition where a perception agent writes the scene as an executable digital twin via generated vision and geometry code, and a planning agent searches in simulation while revising the twin's physical parameters against robot measurements, accepting revisions only if replay does not increase residuals. This makes the robot's world model inspectable and correctable, unlike implicit weight-based or video-predicted models.

entry.title: Agentic-MatriBO: Capability-Compiled Agentic Bayesian Optimization for Materials and Chemical Design

author.name: Yu Zeng, Yuchuan Chen, Ziyue Zhang, Zijian Wei, Yanyi Su, Guojiang Zhao, Hongshuai Wang, Zhifeng Gao

entry.summary: Agentic-MatriBO composes Bayesian optimization components (surrogates, acquisition functions, search strategies) as registered capabilities that an LLM policy proposes and a compiler validates against the catalog, with deterministic execution. This enables reliable agentic orchestration of materials and chemical design under experiment budgets.

entry.title: Does self-distillation improve reasoning?

author.name: Jason Ken Adhinarta, Raina Wu, Ashutosh Sharma, Avinash Balakrishnan, Rameswar Panda, Polina Golland, Yoon Kim, Zhang-Wei Hong

entry.summary: The authors revisit self-distillation methods (SDPO and OPSD) for reasoning, finding that reported gains over RL do not consistently generalize to unseen problems and are largely explained by overfitting to privileged-conditioning artifacts. This is a careful reproducibility-style audit across code, science, tool use, and math tasks. It tempers enthusiasm for self-distillation as an RL alternative.

entry.title: Loss Curvature as a Sampling-Free Proxy for Memorization in Diffusion Models

author.name: Shashank Sule, Xinyue Yu, Boonam Shin, Yuxuan Liu, Abolfazl Hashemi, Hayden Schaeffer

entry.summary: This paper shows that the Frobenius norm of the Hessian of a diffusion model's training loss quantifies memorization at both model level (onset during training) and sample level (per-sample proclivity). Empirically, input loss curvatures can identify memorization onset without sampling, providing a practical diagnostic for a key generative-model risk.

entry.title: DTDD: Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation for Reliable On-Policy Supervision

author.name: Qijia He, Zequn Li, Spencer Luo, Tianle Chen, Pradyumna Narayana, Zixian Ma, Ranjay Krishna, Lan Nie, Sugato Basu

entry.summary: Introduces DTDD, an adaptive on-policy distillation framework that monitors segment-level student-teacher divergence and triggers teacher takeover when divergence becomes unreliable, with the teacher generating recovery suffixes the student learns via behavior cloning. It targets failure modes from large initial policy gaps and compounding errors in long-horizon reasoning and tool use.

entry.title: RA$^2$: Retain-Anchored Attraction Preserves Forget-Adjacent Utility in LLM Unlearning

author.name: Zinan Ling, Yang Xiao, Ruimeng Ye, Sijia Liu, Bo Hui

entry.summary: The paper identifies forget-adjacent utility loss in LLM unlearning, where models degrade on benign prompts near the forgotten domain despite good standard retain metrics, and argues that the redirection direction of forget representations matters. RA2 redirects forget-token states toward retain anchors in latent space, preserving utility in forget-adjacent regions. This addresses a genuine blind spot in unlearning evaluation and methods.

entry.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $\alpha$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models

author.name: Ianis Hammani (ENS Paris Saclay, LMO), Claire Boyer (LMO, IUF)

entry.summary: This paper develops non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for alpha-stable Levy-driven score-based generative dynamics, covering compactly supported and power-law targets in p-Wasserstein distance. It quantifies the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and discretization, showing exponential decay of initialization error. Notably, it shows global Wasserstein convergence alone does not guarantee good tail modeling, distinguishing Levy dynamics from Brownian diffusion.

entry.title: MorphingNet: Symbolic Regression Where the Network Is the Formula

author.name: Jincheng Gao, Jiahe Yi, Shuo Sun

entry.summary: MorphingNet reformulates symbolic regression as continuous optimization by making each network unit's function itself trainable, using pole-free rational functions and complex exponential-logarithm units that morph between exponentials, sinusoids, power laws, and logarithms. The network remains a readable formula throughout training, requiring no operator library, with a structure-recovery step producing short elementary expressions afterward. This is a creative alternative to discrete search over expression trees.

entry.title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling

author.name: Weixin Wang, Wei Deng, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Pan Xu, Andrew Bennett

entry.summary: The paper improves training-free LLM inference-time scaling by fixing two failure modes of reward-free power-sampling: full-sequence sharpening over-concentrates on exact reasoning trajectories suppressing alternative valid paths, and finite-parallelism samplers underperform. Decoupled marginal sharpening targets marginals rather than full sequences to preserve answer-diverse reasoning paths. This matters because inference-time compute scaling without reward models or weight updates is a fast-growing deployment strategy.

entry.title: Beyond Equation Search: Conjecture-Guided Discovery with SCOPE and ClosureBench

author.name: Yuxiao Hu, Qian Li, Ding Wang, Siheng Chen, Linfeng Zhang, Jinyue Yan, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: Proposes shifting symbolic regression from refining individual equations to sustaining multiple conjecture-driven research trajectories. SCOPE deploys multiple scientist agents that independently pursue conjectures via equation modeling, question formulation, and active experimentation, exchanging evidence to revise their conjectures, accompanied by the ClosureBench benchmark. Positions AI-driven discovery at the level of scientific hypotheses rather than curve fits.

entry.title: ReproBAIT: Can coding agents build their own biological AI tools?

author.name: Shiv Muthupandiyan, Tolga H. Dur, Mac Walker, Timo Flesch, Mahmoud Ghanem, Steph Suddell, Giles Harper-Donnelly, Sophie Rose, Jasper G\"otting, Coleman Breen, Jake Pencharz

entry.summary: ReproBAIT is a benchmark testing whether sandboxed coding agents can design, implement, and train published biological AI tools under limited information, fixed compute budgets, and no internet access. Reproduced tools are scored to measure scientific tool reconstruction ability, relevant to AI-driven science automation.

entry.title: DUALVIEW: Leveraging Broad and Output-Specific Evidence for LLM-based Multi-Output Text Regression

author.name: Yiheng Su, Junyi Jessy Li, Matthew Lease

entry.summary: DualView is a parameter-efficient approach to multi-output text regression that extracts broad and output-specific representations from a frozen LLM and combines them in a dual-branch architecture to predict full score vectors. Across five tasks and eight LLMs up to 122B parameters, it outperforms seven supervised baselines with 82-1842x fewer fitted parameters, and a smaller backbone with DualView can beat larger baselines. It opens up an underexplored regression setting for LLMs.

entry.title: Model vs. User: Whose Values Prevail? Inference-Time Value Alignment in Multi-Turn Conversations

author.name: Enrico Liscio, Anne Arzberger, Aditya Shankar, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah

entry.summary: Evaluates four prompt- and activation-based steering methods in multi-turn conversations where user and assistant models push toward the same or opposing, equally desirable values, tracking alignment via linear probes. When values conflict, the side matching the assistant's baseline orientation tends to prevail, revealing limits of inference-time value steering.

entry.title: Why Generate a Click? Plug-in Decision Heads for Web Agents

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, Qinghao Zhang, Zhixi Cai, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: Rather than having a vision-language web agent decode action text like click(12), this work reads action type and target choices directly from the generator's hidden states via plug-in decision heads on a frozen model, with a confidence cascade that falls back to decoding when the heads are unsure. Tested with Qwen3-VL 4B and 8B generators, the approach reuses a single forward pass and its KV cache.

entry.title: What Does LALM Post-training Learn? Rethinking Audio Understanding and Reasoning Capabilities

author.name: Hua-Hsuan Chen, Xuanjun Chen, Wei-Chung Lu, Chih-Kai Yang, Yu-Xiang Lin, Sung-Feng Huang, Haibin Wu, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: This controlled study disentangles genuine audio understanding gains from format adaptation in post-trained large audio-language models, finding that much reported improvement persists even without informative audio but largely vanishes when question formats change. This suggests post-training gains often reflect multiple-choice format fitting rather than real capability advances.

entry.title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation

author.name: Nikolay Semenov, Artem Riabinin, Sergey Bassenko, Anna Averchenkova, Julia Agafonova, Anastasia Aliaskina, Kirill Kozlov, Lev Novitskiy, Nikita Samsonov, Nikolai Gerasimenko, Denis Dimitrov

entry.summary: Kandinsky S2V 1.0 is an open family of speech-to-video models (2B Lite and 21B Pro) generating long-form 25 FPS controllable avatar video from a reference image, speech waveform, and text prompt. The architecture uses Qwen2.5-Omni for text/audio conditioning, a reference-aware three-scale visual memory, and an area-adaptive face loss, trained on 1.17M clips.

entry.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation

author.name: Yixin Wu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: GeoCloak defends against black-box LVLM geolocation inference from photos by exploiting a visual-geolocation asymmetry: location-decisive clues like street signs are visually peripheral yet dominate inference. An agentic, clue-aware planner manipulates peripheral regions to preserve semantics and visual quality while thwarting location inference, avoiding perceptible adversarial perturbations.

entry.title: Quantifying privacy risks in foundation model representations of brain MRI

author.name: Imen Bajar, H\'eber Hwang Arcolezi, Antoine Boutet, Carole Frindel, Mohamed Maouche

entry.summary: The authors quantify how much patient-specific information frozen pretrained encoders retain in brain MRI embeddings, evaluating five encoders under an attacker model with released embeddings, public encoders, and auxiliary scans on two longitudinal datasets. They find substantial subject-specific information enabling patient linkage and sensitive-attribute inference, challenging the assumption that sharing embeddings protects privacy.

entry.title: ForceBench: Benchmarking Force Integration for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Xuan Han, Zinuo Jin, Tianlin Li, Yunfan Lou, Xin Liu, Yuchen Xue, Yuanpeng He, Boxian Yao, Shuhan Zhan, Ruihai Wu, Zhibo Pang

entry.summary: ForceBench is a simulation benchmark for evaluating six-axis wrist-force integration in VLA policies under a unified protocol, with eight tasks spanning physical-property inference, resistance-dependent interaction, and contact-rich assembly, plus 1,600 synchronized demonstrations. It compares a no-force baseline and six force integration designs on a shared pi0.5 backbone, finding Prompt Fusion performs best.

entry.title: KinoGen: Customizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation References via Kinematically Grounded Video Generation

author.name: Qi Wu, Lulu Zhao, Sanghyun Hahn, Rishi Yennu, Emmy Yang, Dingqi Zhang, Tao Pang, Jiuguang Wang, Kuan Fang

entry.summary: KinoGen synthesizes humanoid loco-manipulation references by conditioning a pretrained video generator on calibrated renders of the target robot and object, then recovering kinematically valid references by fitting models to the generated two-view video, ensuring references lie in the robot configuration space by construction. Users can edit keyframes to prescribe goal poses and regenerate.

entry.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs

author.name: Boris Radovi\v{c}, Marco Canini, Veljko Pejovi\'c

entry.summary: The paper explores a hybrid agent architecture where a cloud model writes a program that defers bounded runtime questions about private user data to a small local model via function calls. This keeps data local while improving success rates of code-only agents on AppWorld compared to pure program execution.

entry.title: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support

author.name: Istok Bako, Bonan Min, Tiffany Shao, Claire Cheng, Yashar Mehdad

entry.summary: The paper reports a deployment case study showing that a portable skill—natural-language instructions plus lightweight utilities—can replace complex chunking, indexing, re-ranking, and agentic RAG pipelines for enterprise customer support document retrieval. It demonstrates strong grounding in policy documentation with dramatically simpler infrastructure.

entry.title: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Leijun Zhou, Yanke Yu, Zhihao Liu, Qu Xiang, Tiancheng Hu, Yiru Dong, Yihan Wu, Yangxi Xiang, Xuejun Wu, Xi Chen, Buyue Qian, Yaowei Zheng, Junhao Hu

entry.summary: This survey examines recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods where language agents retain changes to their parameters, memory, skills, and code. It contributes a unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions across four groups (update targets, organization, schedule and scope, feedback and selection) and analyzes how RSI methods draw on traditional techniques.

entry.title: Counterfactual Regret for Reflective Agents with Lean-Verified Guarantees

author.name: Zhongnian Li, Shi Xu, Mengting Xu, Peng Ying, Xinzheng Xu

entry.summary: This theory paper derives sufficient conditions under which reflective language agents that reuse feedback and memory have sublinear counterfactual regret over long horizons, including a resource-sensitive transfer bound along actual execution paths. The results are machine-verified in Lean, providing formal guarantees for training-free agent adaptation.

entry.title: Belief Embedding Tree Search

author.name: Christopher Solinas, Radovan Halu\v{s}ka, Martin Schmid, Michael Buro, Nathan R. Sturtevant, Michael Bowling

entry.summary: Proposes replacing sampled-state set approximations in Monte Carlo POMDP planning with learned belief embeddings inside the search tree, allowing approximate beliefs and leaf value estimates to be represented compactly. This addresses the continuous state space of belief MDPs that makes exact planning intractable.

entry.title: Can agents whose sole duty is to keep humans alive be hijacked to kill? Delayed multi-turn derived-action trap attacks in simulated high-stakes environments

author.name: Josef A. Habdank

entry.summary: Tests whether a tool-using agent controlling life-support in a NASA-derived BioSim lunar habitat simulation can be persuaded via delayed prompt injection, appended to truthful telemetry, to kill crew members, comparing lethal attacks to dropping a harmless procedure. The attacker cannot falsify sensors, only persuade the agent to abandon its goals.

entry.title: TRACE: Temporal Risk Assessment and Concept Editing for Safer Language Generation

author.name: Ankur Garg, Xuemin Yu, Hassan Sajjad, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, a safety framework that tracks harmful-response risk during generation, selectively edits token activations, and leaves an auditable record of detection and steering decisions. It learns a codebook of recurring activation patterns where each vector represents a latent concept, assigning token activations to codebook entries at inference time. Designed to intervene without changing safe responses.

entry.title: Inverse Garment Design with Visual Agents

author.name: Nanxiang Jiang, Yunuo Chen, Zeng Tao, Zizhang Li, Qi Guo, Jiajun Wu, Yin Yang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces DressAgent, a hierarchical agentic system that reconstructs simulation-ready 3D garments with arbitrary layers from a single image by recovering sewing patterns through planning and closed-loop refinement grounded in physical simulation. Contributes an enhanced GarmentCode representation and the first multi-layer sewing pattern dataset with over 15K outfits. Avoids the cost of differentiable optimization and data limits of feed-forward methods.

entry.title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation

author.name: Rui Tang, Hongqiu Wang

entry.summary: MedHarnessBench presents an outcome-preserving harness protocol that independently evaluates seven healthcare-specific process dimensions for medical agents, such as clinical workflow competence and patient-evidence alignment. It aims to attribute execution failures to the agent model, the runtime harness, or their interaction, beyond what terminal-outcome benchmarks can reveal.

entry.title: Agent Sociodrama: Social-Dynamics-Guided Persona Recasting for LLM Agent Teams

author.name: Yirui Qi, Xiaoming Zhang, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: Agent Sociodrama models evolving social dynamics in LLM agent teams by updating agents' emotional states and directed relationships each round via an external judge, then recasting personas accordingly. Across six LLM backbones and five social scenarios, trajectories exhibit structured social patterns aligned with classical social theory and human judgments, addressing failure modes like dominant speakers anchoring groups on wrong answers.

entry.title: Pollard: Governed Semantic Execution Trees for Framework-Independent AI Agent Control and Replay

author.name: Muntaser Syed, Marius C. Silaghi
