entry.summary: Pollard is a framework-independent agent runtime based on governed semantic execution trees that unify execution identity, governance, and replay, recording completions, refusals, resource settlements, and branch history. It supports strict verified replay without re-invoking operations and transactional coordination across concurrent workers, validated under deterministic freeze with invariant preservation.

entry.title: World Models Need a Physical Registry: Learning Internal Predictive States for Physically Plausible World Models

author.name: Shinseong Kim, Jaeseok Jeong, Jianlong Fu, Youngjung Uh

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Physical Registry: registry slots inside a video diffusion transformer that are initialized from observation-conditioned forecasts, co-evolve with video tokens, and receive future-representation supervision, making predictive dynamics an explicit readable state. This targets physically plausible generation rather than mere visual realism.

entry.title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation

author.name: Shu Gu, Matthew Youngman, Yuqin Zhao, Cristian Sestito, Ali Siddique, Ramesh Krishnamurthy, Danial Chitnis, Themis Prodromakis

entry.summary: Introduces a two-layer framework separating LLM orchestration from deterministic FPGA implementation and evaluation for post-route timing closure, comparing three agent control granularities across sixteen designs and seven LLMs. Results reveal a trade-off: expert-written recipes achieve 98.2% functional pass rates while direct EDA operations yield slightly larger Fmax gains but only 71.4% pass rates.

entry.title: Transparency as Answerability: Role-Dependent Information Flow Modeling

author.name: Mattias Br\"annstr\"om, Themis Dimitra Xanthopoulou, Lili Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes reconceiving AI transparency as a relation between a system and a stakeholder, formalized via information flow networks where transparency questions become network-structure queries and answerability is computed from that structure. This avoids failures of system-property views of transparency, such as assessments that do not transfer across organizational boundaries.

entry.title: EvoQuantLab: Training-Free Dual-Loop Evolution for Auditable Quantitative Research

author.name: Haolin Yang, Zhiqiang Qian, Chutian Chen, Jipeng Zhang, Zhenghao Zhu, Tangjia Deng, Jian Xie, Shuaishuai Gong, Yike Guo, Sirui Han

entry.summary: EvoQuantLab is a training-free framework for automated alpha factor discovery that combines an inner genetic-programming loop for token-efficient, structurally constrained factor evolution with an outer diagnosis loop that audits evidence across cycles. It explicitly targets backtest overfitting, a major failure mode of LLM-driven quant workflows.

entry.title: Generalizable field of view extension for diffusion MRI via conditional flow matching

author.name: Gaurav Rudravaram, Lianrui Zuo, Ema Topolnjak, Michael E. Kim, Adam M. Saunders, Elyssa M. McMaster, Paula Trujillo, Ely E. Wesley, Colin D. McKnight, Pratik P. Pandharipande, Mayur B. Patel, Cayce Strength, Brenda T. Pund, Amelia W Maiga, Robert S. Dittus, David A. Bennett, Julie A. Schneider, Konstantinos Arfanakis, The HABS-HD Study Team, Derek B. Archer, Timothy J. Hohman, Yelena Bodien, Daniel C. Moyer, Kurt G. Schilling, Bennett A. Landman

entry.summary: This paper proposes a conditional flow-matching generative model that extends the field of view of diffusion MRI by predicting apparent diffusion coefficients in six directions, enabling whole-brain tractography from incomplete acquisitions. By predicting ADC values rather than raw signal, the model generalizes across sites, b-values, and acquisition protocols without retraining. It is validated with a large multi-study author team spanning clinical and research datasets.

entry.title: REA: From Correct LLM Judgments to Safe Decision Delivery

author.name: Jingxiang Meng, Aofan Liu, Yaoshuai Ma, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: REA (Resolve-Express-Act) studies an overlooked failure mode in generative safety guards: a reasoning guard may classify a request correctly yet emit output that the application cannot parse, causing fallback behavior that either admits harmful requests or blocks safe ones. The framework traces judgments through parsing and fallback to application actions and shows that parsing the safety verdict preserves reasoning accuracy while stricter explanation requirements can reject correct predictions. It highlights the gap between model correctness and deployed-system safety.

entry.title: Seeing Depth but Choosing Cues in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhengtao Zou, Pekka Marttinen

entry.summary: Investigates whether vision-language models use depth information or image-plane cues (apparent size, vertical position) to judge object proximity, using controlled cue-conflict experiments, representation analysis, and interventions in rendered and real scenes. Across model families and scales, judgments shift toward misleading image-plane cues even though the correct depth order remains decodable from the objects' visual representations. This is an informative interpretability result about the gap between what VLMs represent and what they use.

entry.title: Monitoring latent reasoning in looped language models

author.name: Pawel Olszowiec, Paulina Tomaszewska, Maciej \.Zelaszczyk, Michal Byra, Neo Christopher Chung

entry.summary: This work builds a five-lens mechanistic interpretability inspection protocol and applies it to eight looped language models from four families, distinguishing carry loops (prompt held in looped state) from re-reading architectures (prompt re-supplied each iteration). It examines whether iterative layer reuse actually improves capabilities and whether models remain stable under prompt perturbation. As looped LMs gain popularity, this is foundational analysis of their internal dynamics.

entry.title: Order-Consistent Latent Geometry for Reliable Short-Horizon Planning in World Models

author.name: Junlin Wu, Wen Fan, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper shows that reliable ranking of candidate action sequences by terminal Euclidean distance in latent planners requires a pathwise no-reversal property, which the authors prove is exactly the classical self-approaching condition from geometry. They connect violations of this condition to exact finite-horizon order reversals and develop geometry fixes for discrete latent sequences in visual world models.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Voting: Fine-Grained Correction of LLM Reasoning through Graph Alignment across Sampled Traces

author.name: Haotian Liu, Yingjian Chen, Xiaohang Xu, Lang Huang, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Irene Li

entry.summary: DDRG improves on self-consistency by building claim-level reasoning graphs from a frozen bank of sampled traces and using graph alignment to expose localized disagreements. An answer-blind verifier adjudicates conflicts, enabling selective correction of intermediate reasoning steps rather than just voting over final answers.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness

author.name: Chuyang Wei, Haoxiang Guan, Minghang Zhu, Kexin Zhou, Jiyan He, Xiren Zhou, Huanhuan Chen, Yifei Shen

entry.summary: This paper formalizes harness self-evolution, in which an agent's scaffolding (prompts, memory, workflows, tools, and code) is revised across runs while model weights stay frozen. It frames the process as evolutionary optimization, provides continual PAC-learning style analysis including generalization and retention bounds, and separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It offers both a practical framework and theoretical grounding for self-improving agent systems.

entry.title: When Log Parsing Removes What Matters: Detecting Failures in Distributed GPU Workloads

author.name: Boyuan Cui, Yuyang Zeng, Yifang Tian, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: The paper introduces GF-Bench, a PyTorch-based framework and dataset with 220 labeled two-GPU executions covering normal runs, OOM failures, and straggler failures in distributed GPU workloads. Evaluations show that standard log-parsing-based anomaly detectors (DeepLog, LogAnomaly, LogBERT, LogPrompt) can miss critical failure signals removed by parsing.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Real-Robot Interaction without High-Quality State Estimates

author.name: Ryan Gao, Ashvin Anilkumar, Nicholas Corrado, William Cong, Josiah Hanna

entry.summary: This paper tackles robot RL where the true state must be estimated on-board, studying bipedal soccer goal scoring with an unscented Kalman filter and no external instrumentation. It addresses how UKF state-estimation errors corrupt policy inputs and rewards, enabling learning directly from physical experience in uninstrumented settings.

entry.title: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules

author.name: Samuele Giampieri

entry.summary: Cortex is a tool that treats coding-agent harness files (skills, rules, project instructions) as testable artifacts: it saves developer corrections as replayable tasks, writes candidate skills or rules, and retains them only when repeated runs show net gains without degrading any task. This brings empirical measurement to the practice of accumulating agent configuration text.

entry.title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos

author.name: Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li, Siyao Xiao, Runqing Cheng, Xiao Lin, Zhifang Liu, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: Presents DexCast, a framework learning dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D human videos via joint hand-object interaction reconstruction, removing the need for teleoperated demonstrations. It includes a DexHand Motion Perception Module to capture inter-joint dynamics and temporal context for action generation.

entry.title: Counterfactual Rollouts for Offline Contrastive Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tingrui Huang, Ai Bo, Junzhe Zhang

entry.summary: This work addresses confounding in offline contrastive RL when demonstrator information is hidden from the learner, formalizing the setting with confounded MDPs and introducing counterfactual transitions. The resulting CauCRL algorithm learns a pessimistic value that lower-bounds true occupancy, separating what the data identify from what they do not.

entry.title: To Defer or Not to Defer? Online Learning with LLMs and Congested Experts

author.name: Vasileios Saketos, William Reveillard, Alexandre Proutiere, Sebastian Dalleiger, Ming Xiao

entry.summary: This paper formulates online learning-to-defer with LLMs as a sequential decision problem where a system must decide whether to answer a query with the LLM or defer it to a capacity-constrained human expert queue. The LLM's confidence reliability is initially unknown and must be learned from selectively observed, delayed expert feedback, adding congestion-aware regret challenges. The work connects LLM deployment questions with online learning and queueing theory.

entry.title: In-Place Indic Tokenizer Expansion and Continual Pretraining of Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B

author.name: Avinash Benki, Prasanjith Pasunuti, Sutanshu Saksena Raj, Parijat Chatterjee, Nayanjit Sarkar, Daksh Maan

entry.summary: The authors adapt the existing Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B checkpoint for eight Indian languages via in-place vocabulary expansion with AdaptMix rebalancing, initializing new embedding rows from decompositions of existing rows before backbone updates. Continual pretraining over roughly 1.27 trillion tokens yields a 12.9-point gain on Indic MILU at a 3.4-point cost to English MMLU, and they transparently report negative results.

entry.title: Rethinking Human Intent-to-CAD: Parametric CAD Model Generation via Cooperative Multi-Task Alignment and Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingwang Zhang, Jiahao Li, Xiangdong Zhou

entry.summary: The paper proposes mapping multi-level human intent (hand-drawn sketches plus text) directly to executable parametric CAD code without assuming a prior target CAD model, supported by HiCAD, claimed to be the first large-scale dataset aligning sketches, text, and parametric CAD codes. A two-stage framework uses cooperative multi-task alignment and spatial-aware reinforcement learning.

entry.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution

author.name: Alan Wu, Wei Tao, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: This work introduces DeskIF-Bench, a benchmark of 255 artifact-verified desktop tasks across six applications, using software evolution as a natural source of interface variation to identify what makes desktop software easier or harder for LLM agents to use. By holding tasks and agents fixed while varying software releases, it isolates interface characteristics affecting agent usability.

entry.title: RINO: Renormalization Group Distillation with No Labels

author.name: Zichun Hao, Raghav Kansal, Abhijith Gandrakota, Chang Sun, Haoyang Li, Zihan Zhao, Ngadiuba Jennifer, Javier Duarte, Maria Spiropulu

entry.summary: RINO is a self-supervised pretraining method for high-energy physics that exploits the multi-scale renormalization group structure of particle jets, moving beyond image- and language-inspired inductive biases that transfer poorly. It addresses the bias from training on unfaithful labeled simulations by learning directly from real unlabeled collision data.

entry.title: Avoiding What Your Teacher Already Knows: Entity Familiarity for Deep-Search Distillation

author.name: Yifei Liu, Zhixiang Liang, Wentao Tan, Yicheng Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Nan Duan, Qiong Cao

entry.summary: Studies teacher-relative difficulty in distilling deep-search agents, showing that questions structurally hard can be easy for teachers familiar with their key entities, producing weak supervision. It proposes Evidence-Verified Entity Familiarity (EVF) as an early predictor of difficulty (AUC 0.60-0.70) and uses it to select harder, higher-value training examples across multiple teachers.

entry.title: BAT3R: Robust Online 3D Reconstruction with Bayesian Adaptive State Updates

author.name: Lijian Li, Yuanpeng He, Yudian Zheng, Chung-ju Huang, Linyu Li, Dongming Jin, Wenpin Jiao, Zhi Jin, Chi-Man Pun

entry.summary: BAT3R is a training-free Bayesian adaptation framework for streaming 3D reconstruction from long video, using state innovation gating and Bayesian-guided adaptive state updates to counteract the error accumulation typical of recurrent architectures. It addresses the impractical quadratic cost of feed-forward transformers on long sequences with constant memory.

entry.title: From Caricature to Collective Artifact: How Persona Construction Drives Polarization in Generative Social Simulations

author.name: Dimitris Michailidis, Petter T\"ornberg, Fernando P. Santos

entry.summary: Using a Twitter-like LLM-based generative social simulation with personas from the American National Elections Study, this work ablates layers of partisan identity to show that collective outcomes, including polarization dynamics, depend heavily on how survey responses are converted into personas. It demonstrates that persona construction choices propagate into emergent collective artifacts.

entry.title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization

author.name: Lihao Zheng, Zhenwei Shao, Zhou Yu, Yan Yang, Haoyi Sun, Qian Wang, Ning Mao, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: VAttnPO refines token-level credit assignment in multimodal RL with verifiable rewards by using answer-conditioned visual attention: a frozen old policy teacher-forces the correct answer to build a reference visual distribution, and Jensen-Shannon divergence in attention space modulates token advantages. This makes changes in visual-evidence use explicit beyond outcome-level rewards.

entry.title: Proactive Physical AI through Continuous Observation and Timely Intervention

author.name: Zhenhua Yang, Jiafeng Liang, Xingyu Zhou, Yi Jiang, Xiayu Cao, Zui Chen, Luqi Wang, Haiyang Sun, Yufei Xiang, Chang Li, Rongchuan Mu, Bowen Chi, Zihe Tong, Mingyu Li, Huijie Ma, Yiqiao Yang, Baoqi Ren, Zhiming Ma, Zhihao Zhu, Jiahao Ji, Zhuoyao Wang, Qianyu Wang, Xiangyu Liu, Wang Zixiang, Shunliang Zhang, Ming Liu, Xiaocheng Feng, Duyu Tang, Bing Qin

entry.summary: The paper defines Proactive Physical AI, where a system continuously observes the world, identifies situations warranting intervention, and acts at the right time without explicit task specification. The ProAgent system combines StreamingJev, a proactive timing model deciding whether and when to intervene, with a Response Model, forming an end-to-end pipeline from a large author team.

entry.title: ProbabilityBench: Model Evaluation and Calibration with Exact Ground-Truth Uncertainty

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Yuting Tang, Futoshi Futami, Takashi Ishida

entry.summary: Introduces ProbabilityBench, a benchmark with exactly computable instance-level class probabilities and Bayes error across three simulated text domains (peer review, covert information transfer, credit risk), enabled by fully specified data-generating processes and a proof that natural-language rendering preserves the generative probabilities. This permits direct measurement of calibration against exact ground-truth uncertainty.

entry.title: Phase-Conditioned Affordance Fields for SE(3)-Equivariant Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Xinzhe Chen, Liqi Huang, Sihua Ren, Haowen Sun, Mingyang Li, Zeyang Liu, Xingyu Chen, Xuguang Lan

entry.summary: This work identifies that SE(3)-equivariant visuomotor policies rely on a global rigid-transformation assumption that breaks down in multi-object real-world manipulation. It introduces phase-conditioned affordance fields, per-point scores over observed point clouds that provide learned anchors for canonicalization. The approach improves robotic manipulation robustness where task-relevant regions change across objects.

entry.title: Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing

author.name: Xiaolong Xu, Hao Jiang, Bo Jiang, Zhiwen Deng, Ningyuan Sun, Bingzhou Chen, Jin Chen, Chenxing Wei

entry.summary: Diff Diffusion is a diffusion-style LLM framework for code editing that predicts structured edit paths from an original snippet to its revised form instead of regenerating full code segments. This aligns dLLMs with IDE-style edit prediction, combining multi-token parallel updates with sparse edit representations.

entry.title: CineMem: Attention-Aligned Fine-grained Memory Retrieval for Multi-Shot Long Video Generation

author.name: Xiaoxue Wu, Xinyu Gao, Fang Yu, Yu Qiao, Xinyuan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces CineMem, a memory-retrieval framework for autoregressive multi-shot video generation that organizes memory online and retrieves query-adaptively at fine granularity instead of sharing frame-level context across all query tokens. This reduces redundant retrieval while maintaining semantic continuity across shot transitions with substantial visual changes.

entry.title: Holding Agents Accountable with Verifiable Agent Insurance

author.name: Cheng Hua, Taro Tsuchiya, Nicolas Christin, Giulia Fanti

entry.summary: The paper proposes verifiable agent insurance (VAI), a framework where agent providers financially commit, via smart contracts on an immutable ledger with monetary escrow, to programmatically-specified policies. Users who detect violations can trigger verifiers that review agent execution traces logged through the agent harness. This shifts the focus from preventing agent misbehavior to recovery and accountability after it occurs.

entry.title: PRISM: Calibrating Black-Box Judges with Counterfactual Probes

author.name: Kakei Yamamoto, So Kuroki

entry.summary: PRISM measures how an LLM judge's scores shift when evaluative attributes are emphasized or de-emphasized while content is held fixed, treats these counterfactual responses as a surrogate Jacobian, and learns a ridge-regression correction from human labels. The result is a rubric-free calibration protocol for black-box judges.

entry.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Chengtao Jian, Kai Yang

entry.summary: DPOison-VL is the first clean preference poisoning attack against vision-language DPO, manipulating alignment through imperceptible perturbations on a small fraction of training images while leaving prompts, responses, and preferences intact. It formulates poison construction as bilevel optimization with a gradient alignment surrogate. The work exposes a security gap in the preference-data supply chain for VLM alignment.

entry.title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation

author.name: Ziyang Song, Lia Shen, Yixuan Li, Qincheng Lu, Weihao Li, Haoran Xu, He Zhu, Xinyu Wang, Yue Li

entry.summary: SMI is a training-free framework that constructs ontology-grounded Semantic IDs for medical concepts by defining each concept as a coarse-to-fine path through an expert-defined medical ontology and aggregating frozen biomedical LM embeddings. It improves representation of rare, fine-grained clinical codes where hierarchy-agnostic LM embeddings degrade, particularly in long-tailed vocabularies.

entry.title: Fast Rates for Offline Q-Learning with KL Regularization

author.name: Yize Hao, Guangxin Jiang, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes KL-regularized Q-Learning (KLQ), a simple variant of classical Q-learning for finite-horizon MDPs, and proves it achieves near-optimal sample complexity without explicit pessimism by exploiting KL regularization. The authors then address the exponential dependence of the initial guarantee on the regularization parameter and horizon in an improved analysis.

entry.title: Data Density Scaling Laws for Image Self-Distillation

author.name: Alvard Barseghyan, Ani Vanyan, Hakob Tamazyan, Hrant Khachatrian

entry.summary: Through systematic experiments across seven diverse datasets including satellite, driving, ego-centric, and natural image corpora, this paper shows that sample repetition effects in image self-distillation are non-trivial and dataset-dependent. It identifies settings where repeated training on a smaller subset outperforms a larger unique sample set, and proposes a modified scaling formulation to account for this.

entry.title: Deep Generative Models for Phylogenetic Inference with Complex Evolutionary Processes

author.name: Ethan Baron, Alan N. Amin, Andrew Gordon Wilson

entry.summary: This work applies deep generative models (simulation-based inference) to phylogenetic tree posterior inference, where likelihood-based MCMC fails or is misspecified for realistic evolutionary processes. The approach, from a group including Andrew Gordon Wilson, targets pathogen tracking and evolutionary history reconstruction under complex models.

entry.title: PairIT: Autoregressive Transformers for Low-Data Molecule Optimization

author.name: Hannah Lawrence, Bodhi P. Vani, Ji Won Park, Natasa Tagasovska, Samuel Don Stanton, Andrew Martin Watkins, Michael Maser, Ewa M. Nowara

entry.summary: Presents PairIT, a training framework for autoregressive SMILES transformers that learns molecule optimization from structurally similar molecule pairs, enabling seeded, multi-property optimization in data-sparse regimes. Prompt tokens let users specify target properties and directions, making it practical for real drug-discovery workflows.

entry.title: Policy-Verified Self-Training: Learning Agent Compliance from Verifiable Policy Rewards

author.name: Min-Young Yu

entry.summary: PVST is a post-training paradigm where an LLM agent generates its own trajectories and an executable policy verifier, compiled from a written policy, judges action compliance; compliant trajectories are reinforced while violations become negatives for preference optimization. Beyond the policy gate and task-success signal, no stronger teacher or human preference data is needed. This repurposes runtime safety enforcement as a training signal, linking AI safety and self-training.

entry.title: TIMERSI: Towards Self-Improved Agentic Deployment for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Haoxin Liu, Deqing Fu, Lucheng Fu, Yiqiao Jin, Rushi Qiang, Harshavardhan Kamarthi, B. Aditya Prakash

entry.summary: TIMERSI wraps frozen time-series foundation models with a self-improving agentic system in which a coding agent translates task descriptions into executable pipeline changes, tests revisions against historical windows, and uses observed errors to guide further revisions. An adaptive selector then chooses among resulting pipelines at deployment. This reduces the human expertise needed to tailor forecasting models to specific domains.

entry.title: Asymptotically Exact Negative Guidance of Diffusion Models via Positive-Unlabeled Learning

author.name: Hirohane Takagi, Masashi Sugiyama

entry.summary: Existing negative guidance methods for diffusion models inject repulsive terms from local per-sample information and thus do not target an explicit density. This work proposes a negative-guidance sampler that targets an explicit density with a tunable avoidance strength, uniformly handling both reference-sample and score-based specifications, using positive-unlabeled learning to estimate the required quantity. The result has provably reducible bias as computation increases.

entry.title: Energy Consumption Analysis of Discrete Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Boris Ruf, Marcin Detyniecki

entry.summary: This benchmark compares inference energy of diffusion language models (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B) against autoregressive counterparts (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B), analyzing architecture, KV-cache optimization, and Joules-per-token efficiency. At longer sequences (200-600 tokens), diffusion models achieve roughly 2x better energy efficiency (2.5-2.7 J/token vs 5.3-5.7 J/token). The results inform architecture choices as inference energy becomes a first-order deployment concern.

entry.title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation

author.name: Zefeng He, Yunkai Chai, Xiaoyang Chen, Tong Zhu, Zongliang Wu, Yun Luo, Yafu Li, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: LatentLoop exploits an observed asymmetry in looped Mixture-of-Experts models: the first visit of a shared block contributes less than the second, so compressing the first visit's sequence while retaining full resolution in later visits preserves or improves performance. This asymmetric compute allocation improves efficiency of parameter-reuse architectures under matched budgets. It offers a practical lever for scaling recurrent-depth MoE designs.

entry.title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books

author.name: Fernando Acero

entry.summary: By training GPT-style autoregressive transformers on order flow from simulators with known latent parameters, the paper provides ground-truth references (Bayes-optimal predictor, generating state, exact entropy) for evaluating microstructure foundation models. It shows next-token pretraining on limit order books implements amortized Bayesian inference over market regimes, with the learned predictor approaching the exact Bayes optimum.

entry.title: Harness Policy Distillation: Aligning Agent Policies with Runtime Semantics

author.name: Junze Zhu, Weihao Chen, Zhiyang Zhou, Zhen Wu, Xinyu Dai

entry.summary: Harness Policy Distillation makes the runtime control semantics of an agent's execution harness (executable actions, state transitions, termination) an explicit training target alongside actions. It replays reference trajectories through the harness to recover implicit runtime semantics as control documents, providing privileged information for a teacher that supervises the agent policy.

entry.title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization

author.name: Renjie Xie, Juncheng Yang, Aoting Hu, Yan Liang, Mingxi Zhang, Zheheng Hong, Wei Xu, Yanzhi Chen

entry.summary: NatScale addresses mixed-precision quantization of mixture-of-experts LLMs by calibrating gradient-based expert importance weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings, jointly evaluating gate/up/down projections to estimate output error. This fills the gap between ranking experts and deciding how strongly to weight their quantization errors. It targets the significant memory footprint of MoE models where all experts are stored despite sparse activation.

entry.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness

author.name: Artin Tajdini, Manpreet Kaur, Peng Qi

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agents overfit to the interface they were trained on, with semantics-preserving perturbations such as action renaming degrading performance. The proposed Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR) replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each sample under two interfaces where equivalent actions are identifiable by construction, penalizing inconsistency. This self-supervised objective improves robustness to unseen interface perturbations without extra labels.

entry.title: From Copying to Composition: How Language Models Develop In-Context Learning

author.name: Minglai Yang, Xinyu Guo, Renxiong Wang, Sunjie Hou, Daniel Yue Zhang, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: Using a controlled diagnostic separating copying a nearby demonstration from integrating information across a prompt, this study finds across 17 models that roughly a third prefer copied answers while others prefer rule-consistent answers, the latter correlating with higher accuracy and control by the requested value. Checkpoint analyses show models prioritize task-relevant prompt tokens over conflicting examples well before surface ICL accuracy improves. It offers a developmental account of how in-context learning emerges beyond copying.

entry.title: Steering Vectors for Competing Ethical Frameworks Are Interchangeable: A Competing-Target Test for Activation Steering

author.name: Weilun Xu (EPFL), Zipeng Sun (McGill University, Mila)

entry.summary: The paper introduces a competing-target test for activation steering: instead of only comparing a steering vector against unsteered or random baselines, it compares vectors built for competing behaviours, with an equivalence test for when their difference falls below a meaningful margin. Applied to vectors for Kantian deontology versus act utilitarianism in open-weight models, the authors find the vectors are largely interchangeable, suggesting apparent behavioural gains may flow through shared components. This challenges the assumption that steering vector gains indicate direct control of the named behaviour.

entry.title: Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching

author.name: Zeyang Zhang, Linxiang Gao, Meiqi Gu, Xingyan Chen, Minrui Luo, Kaifeng Lyu, Tianxing He

entry.summary: From a circuit complexity perspective, the authors prove that vanilla flow-matching sampler trajectories can be simulated by a constant number of rounds of parallel model evaluations under mild regularity, so extra sampling steps cannot increase expressive power of a constant-depth backbone for visual reasoning. They then show a self-conditioning mechanism circumvents this barrier, enabling genuinely deep sequential reasoning in flow matching. This connects generative sampling theory with reasoning expressivity.

entry.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks on Flow-Based Intrusion Detection

author.name: Florian Spelter, Johannes F. Loevenich, Tobias H\"urten, Erik Adler, Maxime Schwarzer, Laurin Holz, Roberto Rigolin F. Lopes

entry.summary: The paper shows flow-based AI intrusion detection systems can be backdoored by poisoning as little as 0.001% of training data while maintaining clean performance, and proposes a diagnostic-first defense using constrained perturbation analysis and distilled-baseline drift detection. It highlights a critical operational security risk in deployed network defenses.

entry.title: SAM3RL: Memory Control via Reinforcement Learning for Visual Object Tracking

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} \v{C}\'i\v{z}ek, Matej Straka, Illia Volkov, Mat\v{e}j Kripner, Ervin Maci\'c, Jiri Matas, Klara Janouskova, Martin Schmid

entry.summary: SAM3RL extends the SAM 3 tracker by learning its memory-bank control policy with reinforcement learning instead of FIFO rules or hand-crafted update heuristics, framing memory management as sequential decision-making. Hand-crafted memory rules for SAM 2 transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone, motivating the data-driven approach.

entry.title: CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval

author.name: Xinyi Cheng, Tianfu Zhang, Jiwen Li, Xuesen Zhang, Shihao Yu, Pengfei Zhu, Renhuan, Heda Wang

entry.summary: CASI addresses credit assignment when LLM agents emit multiple retrieval actions that receive a single set-level reward, constructing counterfactual information via snapshot-grounded set interventions evaluated under common conditions. Shapley aggregation converts these marginals into within-set credit, used with bounded zero-sum advantage updates.

entry.title: Fantastic Metrics and How to Find Them: Meta-Evaluating Metrics for Multi-lingual Style-Personalized Generation

author.name: Anubhav Jangra, Adrian de Wynter

entry.summary: This paper proposes a regression-based meta-evaluation of text generation metrics and LLM judges that learns on calibrated metric outputs to predict human ratings, grounded against a constant-mean baseline and human agreement for comparability across settings. It is tested on a large-scale multilingual style-personalized generation benchmark. The work addresses the well-known instability of correlation-based metric meta-evaluation.

entry.title: Evolve Together, Fall into Place: How Social Scaffolding Shapes Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Seojin Hwang, Youngmin Choi, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: Introduces AGORA, a framework studying how team composition and interdependence structure (collaboration, conformity, competition) shape the evolution of self-evolving multi-agent LLM systems, drawing on scaffolding from developmental psychology. Across web search, codebase understanding, and document QA, evolution alone rarely helps and social structure plays a decisive role.

entry.title: A Strong Harness Narrows the Model Gap: A Comparative Evaluation for Legislative Document-to-XML Conversion

author.name: Palvika Bansal, Rittika Jindal, Ruichong Wang

entry.summary: An industrial pipeline converts U.S. state legislation into strict schema-constrained XML, and controlled ablations across three harnesses (zero-shot, single agent, multi-agent pipeline) and three Claude models on 153 gold bills show that harness engineering narrows the model gap. Notably, the weakest model in the full pipeline outperforms stronger models in weaker harnesses.

entry.title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingsong Xie, Jiahao Tian, Jiacheng Tang, Zhifeng Li, Madalina Ciobanu, Navan Preet Singh, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: The paper introduces ScreenRef, a 586K-screenshot GUI grounding dataset with over 633K referring expressions spanning desktop, web, and mobile domains, covering text recognition, visual matching, spatial understanding, and refusal cases. It pairs the dataset with a distillation-to-reinforcement learning pipeline for training robust GUI agents.

entry.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm

author.name: Qianru Meng, Xi Zhang, Konstantinos Papakostas, Congfeng Cao, Wenxiang Hu, Tianyi Lu, Xiao Zhang, Lun Zhou, Zaiqiao Meng, Zhaochun Ren, Xiaohui Yan, Yougang Lyu

entry.summary: SwarmRSI is a framework for recursive self-improvement in scientific agent swarms, introducing Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation to refine hypotheses and implementations using experimental feedback from other agents. It addresses ambiguity about whether to revise a hypothesis versus its implementation and prevents useful components from being hidden by aggregate scores.

entry.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence

author.name: Yuanyuan Gao, Zhirui Liu, Yuning Gong, Yifei Liu, Yifan Zhan, Kuixuan Jiao, Xiaolong Zhou, Yifan Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Dan Xu, Zhihang Zhong

entry.summary: Holi-Spatial 360 converts sparse panoramas from real-estate platforms into annotated multi-room 3D environments, using correspondence-guided geometric optimization to turn feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints. It addresses the gap between abundant but sparse panorama data and the photorealistic, semantically grounded 3D environments needed for spatial intelligence.

entry.title: No Way To Steal My Face: Proactive Defense Against Identity-Preserving Personalized Generation

author.name: Lizhi Xiong, Jun Li, Ziqiang Li, Weiwei Jiang, Zhangjie Fu

entry.summary: IDGuardian is a proactive privacy defense protecting facial images against identity-preserving personalized generation with diffusion models, covering both training-based and training-free personalization approaches. It claims to be the first generalizable, model-agnostic identity protection framework, abstracting the personalization process to defend across paradigms.

entry.title: Feasibility of a Patient-Specific Digital Twin for Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Trajectory Planning

author.name: Kritsanavis Chongsrid, Vich Yindeedej, Supaporn Konmun, Xulei Yang, Si Yong Yeo

entry.summary: This clinical study builds a patient-specific digital twin from preoperative CT that exhaustively searches entry points around Keen's point for the shunt trajectory maximizing intraventricular length under safety constraints, output as simple ruler measurements for freehand execution. In an 11-patient IDEAL Stage 2a trial it achieved Hayhurst Grade 1 placement in 10 of 11 versus 22 of 213 historically, with large statistical significance.

entry.title: OneLA: Learning Many Worlds from Latent Actions

author.name: Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun, Fan Jiang, Chiyu Wang, Junfeng Ni, Mu Xu

entry.summary: OneLA learns a unified latent action space across diverse domains from videos without explicit action supervision, using a shared orthogonal dictionary and a common predictive objective without task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses. This addresses the entanglement of domain-specific visual cues with transferable transition structure in world modeling.

entry.title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Huanyuan Zhou, Xin Hu, Sijia Chen, Zihan Guo, Kun Xiang, Yunshuang Nie, Tao Tang, Xinlong Zheng, Jia-Wang Bian, Xianming Liu, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: GeoThinker-F internalizes spatial perception in multimodal LLMs by transforming their own hidden states into predictive latent world representations, avoiding the latency and compute cost of external 3D encoders. The key insight is that intermediate semantics already contain enough information to predict useful geometry and future-semantic representations without exactly reproducing dedicated encoder features.

entry.title: E2DRL: End-to-End Differentiable Reinforcement Learning for 3D Obstacle Avoidance in Quadruped Robots

author.name: Cheng Fan, Bingyang Zhou, Gang Yang, Zixuan Zhuang, Aoqian Zhang, Pengzhi Yang, Xin Liu, Chunzheng Wang, Yan Rui Tan, Fan Shi

entry.summary: E2DRL extends differentiable reinforcement learning from blind or 2D tasks to end-to-end visual 3D obstacle avoidance in quadrupeds, using soft differentiable obstacle interactions with penetration penalties and velocity-conditioned stop-gradient shaping to preserve first-order training signals. A privileged teacher-student setup yields a deployable perception-control system.

entry.title: AutoRSR: Automated Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Generation for Scalable Robot Learning

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Chang Liu, Litao Deng, Tao Zhang, Qin Jin

entry.summary: AutoRSR automates the real-to-sim-to-real pipeline: from multi-view observations, robot states, and open-vocabulary queries, it reconstructs real workspaces, extracts object assets, calibrates coordinates, and generates manipulation data at scale. The aim is to remove the manual effort that makes simulation-based robot data generation expensive.

entry.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights

author.name: Sahil Garg, Ruhi Gottumukkala, Vishal Agarwal, Shubham Vishwakarma

entry.summary: The study evaluates 26 models, 19 open-weight and 7 closed, on CTI-REALM, a benchmark where agents convert threat intelligence reports into working detections. Its key finding is that open-weight models can match the strongest closed models at under a tenth of the cost when given enough interaction turns, and that the benchmark's message limit was a confound.

entry.title: CESNET-TimeSeries26: A Multi-Year Network Traffic Time Series Dataset for Annual Seasonality, Concept Drift, and Long-Term Anomaly Detection

author.name: Josef Koumar, Karel Hynek, Kamil Jerabek, Pavel Siska

entry.summary: CESNET-TimeSeries26 releases nearly three years of continuous traffic time series from the CESNET3 backbone plus a subnet covering about 4.5 years, spanning hundreds of institutions and hundreds of thousands of IP addresses. It enables long-horizon forecasting, annual seasonality modeling, concept drift analysis, and anomaly detection benchmarking that existing short datasets cannot support.

entry.title: FleetPilot: Fine-Grained Steering Empowers Real-World LLM Personalization

author.name: Kounianhua Du, Jianxing Liu, Kangning Zhang, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Jiarui Jin, Jianghao Lin, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FleetPilot, a personalization method for LLMs that infers query-dependent user preferences from sparse, heterogeneous interaction histories without the recurring costs of in-context management, parametric adaptation, or candidate scoring. It uses fine-grained steering to adapt model behavior at inference time.

entry.title: SkillFusion: Towards Reliable Multi-Skill Composition for LLM Agents

author.name: Enhao Huang, Xinye Zhao, Yiming Li, Bingrun Yang, Nanjun Zhou, Chunshu Xia, Hongwei Yao, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: Proposes SkillFusion, an offline compiler that reconciles independently authored agent skills which may impose incompatible requirements, competing preferences, and redundant instructions when jointly loaded. It makes composition decisions explicit via typed, scoped constraints linked to source directives, using a type-scope gate, interaction classifier, adversarial verifier, and resolver for hard and soft conflicts. Produces a reusable merged skill.

entry.title: Knowledge Interaction in Hypernetwork-based Continual Learning: Conflict and Composition

author.name: Jiaqi Zheng, Yi Hu, Yadong Mu, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: This work studies how knowledge from the base model, hypernetwork-generated parameter updates, and input context interact during continual learning of LLMs, focusing on conflict (whether new knowledge overrides outdated knowledge) and composition (multi-hop combination with existing knowledge). The analysis targets catastrophic forgetting in hypernetwork-based adaptation frameworks.

entry.title: Learning to GUIDE the Group: Self-Learning LLM Facilitation Across Multi-Party Tasks

author.name: Ziyi Liu, Tzu-Sheng Kuo, Jiale Liu, Deqing Fu, Nithum Thain, Crystal Qian

entry.summary: GUIDE is a framework for developing generalized LLM facilitators across multi-party contexts, evaluating facilitation on objective task outcomes plus subjective metrics like psychological safety and perceived friction. It addresses the gap left by facilitators fine-tuned for narrow task-specific objectives.

entry.title: PXRD-Bench: How Close Are We to Determining Crystal Structures from Powder Diffraction?

author.name: Dongyeop Woo, Nofit Segal, Nayoung Kim, Minkyu Kim, Rafael Gomez-Bombarelli, Sungsoo Ahn

entry.summary: PXRD-Bench is a unified benchmark for crystal structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction, extending evaluation to unknown per-element atom counts and two-phase mixtures, with about 4.1 million training structures and tests on experimental PXRD that exclude structurally matching database entries.

entry.title: When 1+1 Backfires: Rethinking Relevance-Diversity Balancing for Sample-Aware Visual Token Reduction

author.name: Yihang Huang, Peisong Wen, Chenhao Zhou, Difu Feng, Qianqian Xu

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption in visual token compression for vision-language models that a fixed relevance-diversity balance works universally, showing via systematic analysis that optimal weights vary substantially across benchmarks and even within a single benchmark. The authors propose a sample-aware token reduction approach based on these findings.

entry.title: Transparent Information Flow Modeling for Role-Aware AI Act Assessment

author.name: Mattias Br\"annstr\"om, Themis Dimitra Xanthopoulou, Lili Jiang

entry.summary: Applies the Information Flow Methodology to EU AI Act compliance assessment, representing decision systems as networks of information sites and transformation channels to analyze how information, decisions, and responsibilities flow across organizational boundaries. This addresses the limits of monolithic system views and disconnected checklists for high-risk AI governance.

entry.title: Learning Perceptual Geometry of Natural Odor Mixtures from LLM-Derived Descriptors

author.name: Farhad Pashakhanloo, Venkatesh N. Murthy

entry.summary: The authors use LLMs as scalable surrogates to derive mixture-level perceptual descriptions for over 1,200 food odor mixtures with more than 8,000 molecular components, then show language-derived representations predict held-out mixture similarities. This extends olfactory modeling from single molecules to natural multi-component mixtures.

entry.title: OpenDepth: Repurposing Image Editing Priors for Robust Open-World Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Mengke Zhang, Tianyi Yang, Xinzhuo Li, Anlong Ming

entry.summary: OpenDepth improves monocular depth estimation under open-world perturbations like illumination variation and adverse weather by repurposing image-editing priors instead of text-to-image priors, which are optimized for semantic synthesis rather than pixel-level structure. The core insight treats open-world depth as consistent geometric inference across modified views, reducing structural hallucinations. This targets a known fragility of generative-prior-based MDE methods.

entry.title: LLM Agents for Automated Post-Training via Structured Recipe Optimization

author.name: Ruohong Liu, Bohan Tang, Lekang Jiang, Jack Umenberger, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: The paper proposes optimizing a task-adapted recipe space for automated LLM post-training, where an agent constructs and optimizes coupled decisions over data sources, processing, composition, and training configuration under a limited budget. This bridges fixed predefined recipe search and open-ended agent exploration whose choices are hard to reuse.

entry.title: What Can Language Models Inherit from Solomonoff Induction? Limits, Attainable Properties, and What Served Conditionals Reveal

author.name: Luan Ozelim, Abicumaran Uthamacumaran, Hector Zenil

entry.summary: This theoretical paper applies algorithmic information theory and Bayesian consistency results to challenge the claim that scaling language models brings them closer to Solomonoff induction. The authors show no computable predictor family can uniformly approach Solomonoff induction, that each has environments it never learns, and that finite evaluation cannot certify agreement even pointwise.

entry.title: RUBATO: Decoupled Clocks Allow Full-Duplex Models to Think as Fast as They Can

author.name: Yi-Jen Shih, Puyuan Peng, Haohe Liu, David Harwath, Abdelrahman Mohamed

entry.summary: RUBATO argues that speech full-duplex models with internal thinking streams should not enforce a fixed decoding rate tied to a specific hardware latency profile. Instead, it decouples the clocks of conversational and thinking streams so each decodes at a hardware-adaptive rate, sustaining real-time conversation while letting thinking run as fast as the hardware allows.

entry.title: EarthAlign: Learning Language-Aligned Representations of Earth System Data

author.name: Fadillah Adamsyah Maani, Numan Saeed, Jiaqi Ma, Dat Tien Nguyen, Youssef Wehbe, Duncan Watson-Parris, Salman Khan

entry.summary: Introduces EarthAlign, a large-scale dataset spanning 2000-2024 that aligns Earth system data with language by combining 10 expert-curated natural event and disaster sources with climatology-derived normal-weather samples, each with temporal and geospatial context. It targets general-purpose language grounding of Earth system conditions beyond task-specific weather models.

entry.title: Training a Compact, Strong, and Realistic Text-to-Speech Model

author.name: Runyuan Cai, Yu Lin, Yiming Wang, Xiaodong Zeng

entry.summary: Audio8-TTS is a compact 0.6B-parameter zero-shot voice cloning model claiming state-of-the-art intelligibility and speaker similarity with strong perceptual naturalness. The key contribution is a training signal aligned with human perception rather than signal-level fidelity, targeting the realism gap in TTS.

entry.title: OceanFlow: Coherent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Ocean Modeling

author.name: Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Hao Wu, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: OceanFlow introduces a coherent flow matching framework for probabilistic global ocean modeling, ensuring ensemble members are jointly calibrated and physically consistent rather than producing ad-hoc perturbation spread. Probabilistic modeling supports risk-aware marine operations and climate analysis where the full conditional distribution matters.

entry.title: Embedding Information in Policy Randomness: Distribution-Preserving Implicit Communication in MDPs

author.name: Gongpu Chen, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: The paper shows that an agent executing a prescribed stochastic policy can embed covert information in its action randomizations without changing the policy's action distribution, casting this as a channel coding problem. It proposes PRAM, a posterior-matching randomness modulation scheme using common randomness, with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Reflected Proximal Dynamics for Accelerated High-Accuracy Log-Concave Sampling

author.name: Bo Yuan, Wei Guo, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces reflected proximal dynamics, a sampling method for strongly convex, smooth log-concave distributions that combines the exact target preservation of the proximal sampler with momentum-style directional persistence from underdamped Langevin dynamics, via exact reflection of an auxiliary variable. This aims at faster high-accuracy sampling with improved complexity in the condition number.

entry.title: CryptoFlowBench: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning on Blockchains for Cryptocurrency Fund Tracing

author.name: Runang He, Tongya Zheng, Jing Cao, Yucheng Ying, Shunyu Liu, Bingde Hu, Yang Gao, Zeyuan Hu, Jianrong Zhang, Mingli Song

entry.summary: CryptoFlowBench is a benchmark built from authoritative reports on illicit cryptocurrency incidents, with four tasks spanning local to multi-hop fund tracing that challenge both GNNs, whose static predictions do not generalize to multi-hop tracing, and heuristic-based tracing methods. It exposes substantial gaps in current adaptive reasoning over blockchain graphs.

entry.title: InfoVis: Unified Slide Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Xiyan Jiang, Chenyuan Wu, Haoqiang Zhang, Xin Luo, Yueze Wang, Defu Lian, Bo Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Zheng Liu

entry.summary: InfoVis unifies slide image generation and editing, requiring text rendering, instruction following, grounding, design, and precise editing on one canvas. The authors build a data engine with over 13M pretraining and 1.9M fine-tuning records plus VisSlideBench (1,527 manually screened instances), and train a model covering four slide-centric tasks.

entry.title: Bottlenecked semantic compression by representation reconstruction

author.name: Xiaoya Tang, Shilong Liu, Daniel Smolyak, Xiwen Li, Quynh Nguyen, Tolga Tasdizen

entry.summary: ReConV proposes reconstruction-guided visual token condensation for Vision Transformers: a compact Summary Bank summarizes the full token sequence, and tokens whose information is not captured (high reconstruction residuals from a lightweight position-conditioned decoder) are explicitly retained. This reduces computational cost on long token sequences while preserving poorly reconstructed details, with results on image classification and other tasks.

entry.title: LatentRiskBench: Measuring State-Dependent Risks in Enterprise Agents

author.name: Jingyue Cong, Estrid He, Zhuang Li, Nan Wu, Li Shen, Yameng Peng, Xinshu Li, Andy Song

entry.summary: LatentRiskBench evaluates state-dependent safety risks in enterprise agents, where the same action can be safe in one workflow state but violate policy in another. It pairs risky trajectories with benign counterparts sharing the same terminal action but differing in latent policy-relevant states, and introduces residual-risk metrics requiring context reconstruction rather than action-level cues.

entry.title: Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes

author.name: Yiqing Peng, Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Dongyi Zhang, Zhengjie Zhu, Yi Han, Yangyang Zheng, Hao Wang, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: The paper introduces DoF, a continuous configuration framework that interpolates between centralized and decentralized coordination in LLM-based multi-agent systems by controlling how much decision space is delegated to downstream agents. This enables systematic study of the trade-offs between coordination bottlenecks and local autonomy.

entry.title: TStruct: Learning Shared Temporal Structures for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yangze Li, Zhengyang Zhou, Qihe Huang, Pengkun Wang, Binwu Wang, Yang Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes temporal relationship matrices across standard time-series datasets and finds that samples from different temporal positions and variables share dominant, recurring temporal relationship structures. Building on this empirical finding, TStruct learns these shared structures to achieve stable long-term forecasting under temporal distribution shifts and noise.

entry.title: FedGraph: Defending Federated Large Language Model Fine-Tuning Against Backdoor Attacks via Graph-Based Aggregation

author.name: Xi Chen, Chunyi Zhou, Rui Zeng, Xiaogang Xu, Zhe Liu, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: FedGraph defends federated LLM fine-tuning against backdoor attacks by exploiting the observation that malicious clients produce unusually consistent model updates while benign clients produce diverse ones, modeling client relationships as graphs for aggregation rather than relying on high-dimensional anomaly detection. This addresses a key security weakness in privacy-preserving collaborative fine-tuning. It matters as federated LLM adoption grows and poisoning threats become more practical.

entry.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts

author.name: Giovanni Pio Delvecchio, Stefano Fantazzini, Giacomo Frisoni, Gianluca Moro, Lorenzo Bacchiani, Mario Bravetti, Thomas Troels Hildebrandt

entry.summary: SolBehave is a benchmark evaluating behavioral correctness of LLM-generated Solidity smart contracts beyond compilation checks, using 250 real reproducible Ethereum contracts and three tests: differential fuzzing, historical-transaction replay, and synthetic-transaction replay guided by Dynamic Condition Response graphs. This matters because deployed contracts are immutable, making latent faults permanent and exploitable.

entry.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Minghao Luo, Liang Chen

entry.summary: DoubtLess is a training-free decoding method for shortening reasoning chains: a smaller reasoning model reads the large model's chain of thought twice, once prompted to be brief and once verbose, and the scaled logit difference steers the large model toward brevity. This avoids per-model retraining, steering vectors, or brittle heuristics like early stopping or banning filler words that can hurt accuracy.

entry.title: Who Should We Listen to More? Welfare-Aware Preference Acquisition for Pluralistic Alignment

author.name: Ruomeng Ding, Tianwei Gao, Lianrui Geng, Mohit Bansal, Zhun Deng

entry.summary: The paper studies how to allocate limited human feedback across individuals for pluralistic alignment, defining a social welfare objective over supervision utilities that accounts for simulation accuracy variation across people. It frames each query's marginal welfare gain in terms of expected improvement, current utility, and application-designated weights.

entry.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization

author.name: Aryan Das, Arnab Bhattacharya, Vinay Kumar Verma

entry.summary: FSPO is a single-policy framework for RLVR that combines privileged adaptation with function-space temporal consolidation, storing sparse historical next-token distributions as fixed targets instead of maintaining a persistent self-teacher. This stabilizes the moving-target problem in self-distillation for token-level reasoning supervision. The approach densifies reward signal for reasoning RL while avoiding teacher-model overhead.

entry.title: MAPLE: A Multi-Axis Parametric Knowledge Extraction Lens for LLM Evaluation

author.name: Minsuh Joo, Youna Kim, Choonghyun Park, Soo Kyung Kim, Hyunsoo Cho

entry.summary: MAPLE is a unified diagnostic framework for evaluating Knowledge Extraction Enhancement (KEE) techniques such as activation steering, decoding adjustments, and prompting in LLMs. It disentangles effects that aggregate accuracy conflates, separating recovered failures from disrupted successes at surface, probability, and other levels. The work improves evaluation methodology for how well LLMs surface parametric knowledge in their outputs.

entry.title: Continuum Attention

author.name: Afshin Khadangi

entry.summary: Introduces Continuum Attention, a causal attention operator that replaces discrete key-value lookup with integration over a continuous piecewise-linear memory curve weighted by an exponential relevance density, yielding closed-form normalized attention via exponential moments. Gradients follow analytically from low-order moments, enabling parallel GPU implementation while retaining quadratic complexity and the standard decoder structure. Empirically reduces validation negative log likelihood versus softmax and focal attention on byte-level modeling.

entry.title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells

author.name: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou

entry.summary: V-PaSS is a physics-aware architecture for predicting perovskite solar cell performance on new materials, representing mixed-cation/mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX3 endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. This enables extrapolation to unrecorded alloys and unfamiliar cell architectures, unlike prior categorical-label or rigid-crystal-graph approaches. It matters for accelerating materials discovery for renewable energy.

entry.title: Embedding Geometry Shapes LLM Routing: Tracing Failure Modes and Improving Generalization

author.name: Leonardo Torti, Emanuele Rimoldi, Tomer Galanti, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: This paper studies LLM routing based on semantic prompt embeddings and traces a clear failure mode: features determining neighbors of unseen prompts are unreliable proxies for model selection, explaining poor out-of-distribution generalization. Replacing semantic embeddings with hidden states from a partial forward pass of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at a deep layer improves routing generalization. Practically relevant as multi-model routing becomes an operational necessity.

entry.title: Convergence Rates of Gaussian Process Thompson Sampling for Efficient Global Optimization

author.name: Haowei Wang, Yilin Zheng

entry.summary: The paper establishes worst-case expected simple-regret bounds of order N^(-nu/d) sqrt(log N) for Gaussian process Thompson sampling with Matern kernels under RKHS assumptions, covering both discrete and continuous settings via a nested-grid argument, with matching lower bounds. This gives the first rigorous convergence-rate theory for GP-TS in Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: Mixed Poisson diffusion models and application to posterior sampling

author.name: Thibaut Pellerin, Alain Durmus, Elinor Berger, Eric Barat

entry.summary: The authors develop Mixed Poisson Diffusion Models (MPDM), a diffusion framework whose noising dynamics are driven by multivariate counting processes rather than Gaussian noise, motivated by Poisson inverse problems such as photon-limited imaging. The framework enables principled posterior sampling where observations follow Poisson noise.

entry.title: GraphRAG-LTM: A Layered Threat Modeling Framework for Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yining Tang, Junyu Zhang, Haomiao Qiu, Yongchao Liu, Jiajun Zheng, Zhao Wang, Ziyue Qiao, Chao Wu

entry.summary: GraphRAG-LTM is a layered threat modeling framework for attacks on GraphRAG, testing three nested attacker-access levels: black-box query editing under semantic constraints using ranking feedback, white-box query crafting with retriever gradients, and graph-aware white-box attacks that delete bridge triplets to disrupt multi-hop reasoning. It highlights underexplored vulnerabilities in the seed-chunk-to-evidence-graph pipeline.

entry.title: Qwen-MT-Lumen at WMT2026: Instruction-Specialized Translation via Quality-Aware Training and On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Hao Wang, Yangyang Liu, Xiaohu Zhao, Heng Liu, Zifu Shang, Tianhao Li, Ruize Gao, Jialong Tang, Liangying Shao, Haoran Wei, Baosong Yang, Linlong Xu, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: Describes Lumen, a Qwen-based open-source submission to the WMT 2026 General MT shared task targeting instruction-specialized translation with fine-grained style, terminology, and format constraints. The four-stage pipeline combines continued pre-training, SFT, an online extension of M2PO preference optimization, and on-policy distillation.

entry.title: AFCS: Atomic-Fact-Conditioned Synthesis for Factual Knowledge Pretraining

author.name: Yunhao Wang, Feng Zhang, Tinghao Yu, Xing Wu, Jiang Zhou

entry.summary: AFCS is a synthetic-data pipeline for pretraining that first extracts source-supported atomic facts — including secondary entities, table entries, and temporal attributes — and then conditions generation on each retained fact, with structure-aware extraction and source-grounded verification. This goes beyond prior pipelines like WRAP and Nemotron-CC that rewrite passages without enforcing fine-grained fact coverage.

entry.title: Action Jets: Learning the Local Shape of the Action-conditioned Data Manifold

author.name: Anton Arapin, Chahyon Ku, Bernadette Bucher

entry.summary: Action Jets learns the local low-dimensional manifold of frames reachable by varying actions from a fixed state, via a network estimating per-region image motion per action axis. This avoids expensive high-dimensional world-model rollouts for short-horizon planners by supplying cheap local action-conditioned structure.

entry.title: PhyMetric: Diagnosing Physical Plausibility in Text-to-Video Generation via Scene-Level QA

author.name: Siwei Meng, Xuerou Cai, Rui Hu, Ping Liu

entry.summary: PhyMetric is a diagnostic benchmark recasting physical plausibility evaluation of text-to-video models as verifiable, scene-grounded question answering, with 1,115 scenes across 50 physical categories and six domains, plus 8,920 answer-balanced binary questions over 12 dimensions. Each scene pairs targeted yes/no questions with a structured physical property profile to identify which physical behavior fails and why.

entry.title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing

author.name: Zhuobai Dong, Xiaobing Tu, Xiantao Zhang, Jinkui Ren, Yinggui Wang, Yue Ma, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: StreamErase enables real-time video object removal with sub-second latency and up to 26 FPS streaming on a single GPU, versus minutes per video for prior methods. It transfers erasing capability from a strong bidirectional foundation model to an efficient unidirectional streaming eraser via mask-conditioned text-to-video generation.

entry.title: Coordi-pi: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yiming Meng, Yanming Shao, Weijie Shen, Kunyang Lin, Jiayu Sun, Ping Luo, Yao Mu

entry.summary: Coordi-pi introduces a structured action representation for bimanual dexterous manipulation, encoding right and left arm-hand actions as individual tokens in an interleaved sequence to make cross-hand interactions explicit, rather than concatenating both sides into one vector. Hand identity is explicitly encoded within the action sequence for VLA policies.

entry.title: Tactile-Guided Robot Learning: From Representation Learning to Foundation Models

author.name: Kiyanoush Nazari, Luchen Li, Haoshu Fang, Nima Fazeli, Zhibin Li, Fumiya Iida, Thomas George Thuruthel

entry.summary: This survey reviews tactile-guided skill learning from a learning-centric perspective, organized by the functional role of touch across the learning and control pipeline. It covers tactile representation and policy learning, tactile foundation models, and predictive/adaptive control, synthesizing the rapid shift from hardware-focused tactile sensing research toward learning-based manipulation.

entry.title: DiffGIPC: Differentiable Mixed-Coordinate Contact Dynamics on GPU

author.name: Kemeng Huang, Bowen Ren, Xinyu Lu, Minchen Li, Taku komura

entry.summary: DiffGIPC is a GPU-accelerated differentiable simulation framework based on Incremental Potential Contact for optimizing contact-rich deformable and rigid-deformable interactions. It preserves IPC's guaranteed non-penetration through geometric barriers and continuous collision detection while reducing the cost of repeated forward-backward passes in full-space FEM, notably by exploiting nearly rigid components. This enables efficient gradients for contact-rich inverse problems.

entry.title: I trained GPT-2 with full-batch gradient descent so you don't have to

author.name: shawnghu

entry.summary: The author trained GPT-2 with full-batch gradient descent on a fixed 800M-token dataset to empirically test whether gradient noise is essential for neural network training to generalize. The results show that optimization dynamics, not just data, measurably shape qualitative training outcomes, contradicting the naive view that data alone determines the solution. The released artifact offers a study object for compute-constrained learning-dynamics research.

entry.title: Which Metadata Matters for LLM Tool Selection in MCP? Evidence from Controlled Factor-Level Interventions

author.name: Xiaofan Li, Fengchun Qiao, Xing Gao

entry.summary: Analyzing metadata from over 367,000 MCP tools, the authors find large schema variation among functionally similar tools and use controlled single-factor interventions across five LLMs to isolate how names, descriptions, and parameter schemas affect tool selection. The study provides causal evidence on what metadata drives pre-call tool choice.

entry.title: Decoupling Knowledge Forgetting and Refusal Learning in MLLM Unlearning

author.name: Haodong Chen, Shengtao Wen, Dong Liang, Lingbing Guo, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies two hidden failure modes in multimodal LLM unlearning: suppression-induced confabulation and refusal-only training that erases behavior but not knowledge (models still answer multiple-choice probes correctly). It proposes Forget-Aware Self-Distillation (FASD) to achieve honest ignorance, where the model genuinely loses knowledge and acknowledges gaps.

entry.title: EvoCowork: A Benchmark for Real-World Office Tasks

author.name: Zhou Liu, Xingyan Chen, ZhaoYang Han, Zewei Pan, Zeli Su, Ningxin Pan, Xue Hu, Kaixiong Ting, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: EvoCowork is a 240-task benchmark for harness-level recursive self-improvement on office work across presentations, documents, spreadsheets, and cross-file workflows, with model weights held fixed. It scores artifacts for content, native structure, formulas, cross-file consistency, and visual quality, and tests whether improvements transfer as reusable procedures rather than task-specific fixes.

entry.title: SpecFit: Not All Draft Tokens Cost the Same in Offloaded MoE Inference

author.name: Hongliang Cao, Xiuyu Li, Siqi Wang, Ziming Wang, Jingmin Zhu, Hailong Yang

entry.summary: Observes that in MoE models with expert weights offloaded to host memory, speculative decoding can be slower than autoregressive decoding because larger draft trees transfer more experts over the host-to-device path. SpecFit selects the verified draft subtree to maximize predicted throughput rather than acceptance length, estimating expected committed tokens against transfer cost. Improves speculative decoding for memory-constrained MoE serving.

entry.title: Visible but Not Avoided: State-Dependent Re-Proposal of Rejected Candidates in Catalog-Based LLM Optimization Loops

author.name: Jianlin Chen, Wenhui Chen, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that LLM proposers in optimization loops frequently re-propose candidates they already rejected, with static base-state probes underpredicting re-proposal rates in the loops' own trajectories. Re-proposals consumed 28-63% of valid iterations across three open LLMs in a GUI-agent editing task, and probes and loops rejected systematically different edits.

entry.title: Correct Choices, Failed Sequences: Choice2Seq Benchmarks Correctness Retention Across Output Interfaces

author.name: Tianyou Lai, Wentao Yue, Zhiying Deng, Qilei Li

entry.summary: Choice2Seq is a diagnostic benchmark measuring whether models that correctly select an answer can also construct it through a sequence of local decisions, quantified by the Sequence Composition Rate. Findings show dramatic gaps, e.g., a model with 97-99% selection accuracy retains only 33% and 2% of correct choices under serial construction.

entry.title: Recursive Environment Scaling for General Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Lingxiao Jing, Zhengbo Jiao, Yichen Xiang, Bofan Zhu, Lingbei Meng, Yan Ni, Haorui Chen, Ran Ran, Zhirong Shen, Yuheng Yang, Chenhang Cui, Yaosong Du, Rui Huang

entry.summary: RES is a framework that transforms existing benchmark environments to increase difficulty while preserving task objectives: a proposer changes information access, resource relations, and dependencies, with execution-grounded validation and inheritance across rounds. Experiments across 294 tasks from three benchmarks show success drops of 57-77 percentage points for six evaluation models.

entry.title: Acceptable Misalignment

author.name: Maud van Lier, Ludovica Marinucci, Vieri Giuliano Santucci, Raja Chatila, St\'ephane Doncieux, \'Emiland Garrab\'e, Richard Duro

entry.summary: Argues that full value alignment of open-ended learning autonomous robots is theoretically and practically impossible given design-time unknowns about deployment, learning, and behavior, and proposes a framework of acceptable misalignment instead. The paper reframes how designers of open-ended learning systems should think about ethical development under irreducible uncertainty.

entry.title: Does a Governed Confidence Score Know When a Text-to-SQL Answer Is Right? An Exploratory Study on BIRD and a Pre-registered Confirmation on Spider

author.name: Raghu Venkat, Tricha Anjali

entry.summary: This audit of a production text-to-SQL confidence score, tested on BIRD dev with GPT-5.1 as the generating model, finds weak discrimination between right and wrong answers (AUROC 0.624) and that the score withholds 35.7 percent of correct answers. A pre-registered confirmation on Spider strengthens the exploratory findings.

entry.title: Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Yaolun Zhang, Yiran Wu, Joe Nguyen, Shengyu Dai, Saba Moeinizade, Zhenwen Shao, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: UCoE addresses a weakness of training-free self-improving agents: on open-ended tasks the model-based verifier can be wrong, corrupting both the current response and the accumulated harness state. The method co-evolves an executable verifier program together with the agent's harness state while keeping model parameters frozen, so the verifier stays calibrated as responses and task demands shift. This contributes to the growing area of memory- and harness-based agent self-improvement.

entry.title: Agentic4PDM: Host-Governed Evidence Admissibility for Industrial Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Nam V. Nguyen, Hoang Van Truong, Hieu D. D., Duy Khuong Nguyen, Quang Pham, Tung Kieu

entry.summary: Introduces Agentic4PDM, a framework for industrial fault diagnosis that separates adaptive LLM-agent investigation of sensor time series from host control over evidence admissibility, preventing unconstrained interpretation from overstating weak or conflicting signal evidence. It addresses scarce labels and changing operating conditions by leveraging reusable analytical tools rather than repeatedly retraining specialized classifiers. This matters for deploying LLM agents in high-stakes industrial settings where evidence discipline is required.

entry.title: Efficient Safety Guardrails through Latent Dual-Hypothesis Reasoning with On-Demand Trace Reconstruction

author.name: Md Asiful Islam, Fahmida Alam, Mihai Surdeanu

entry.summary: LR-Guard is an efficient guardrail that distills a frozen teacher's dual-hypothesis safety analysis (safe and unsafe prompt interpretations plus comparison) into compact latent representations, jointly trained for safety prediction and on-demand reconstruction of the teacher's explicit reasoning traces. This provides explainable safety decisions without paying the inference cost of explicit chain-of-thought for every input. It targets the overhead problem of reasoning-based guardrails.

entry.title: Configuring RAG Systems: What Breaks, Where Originates, and How to Fix

author.name: Liangyu Chen, Youpeng Ma, Yulong Ye, Zezhen Xiang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: The first large-scale empirical study of configuration-related failures in RAG systems, covering 654 real-world issues from 10 diverse systems. It provides a full categorization of symptoms, root causes, affected pipeline stages, and fix patterns, plus guidance on how to repair configuration problems.

entry.title: Knowing the User Is Not Knowing What We Established: Grounding Awareness in Personal Agents

author.name: Jiajun Chen, Xinyue Chen, Yicheng Jiang, Hua Shen

entry.summary: The paper introduces Grounding Awareness: a personal agent's ability to distinguish accepted, unacknowledged, revised, and scoped arrangements when choosing actions, rather than treating any remembered proposal as authorized. A controlled benchmark shows strong memory performance does not translate into correct grounding-aware behavior across agents and memory systems.

entry.title: VH-GPO: Verified Handoff for LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoze Li, Peng Zhou, Peiyuan Wu, Weijie Zhao, Yinan Xin

entry.summary: VH-GPO addresses the collapse of group-relative RL advantages when all rollouts in a group fail: a frozen teacher repairs the student from a failure state, but control returns to the student as soon as outcome verification confirms the student can succeed from the handed-back state, avoiding fully teacher-generated suffixes. This outcome-verified teacher-student handoff preserves a meaningful learning signal for the student. It extends GRPO-style methods for LLM agent training.

entry.title: CoEvoke: Evoking Multi-Agent Collaboration for Trajectory Collection

author.name: Lin Wu, Shu Yao, Yuheng Wang, Jingru Fan, Huatao Li, Yihan Li, Liu Yixuan, Cheng Liu, Jian Chang, Zeyu Zhao, Aohua Zhang, Huiying Zhao, Shuyuan Zhu, Chen Qian

entry.summary: CoEvoke is a framework that evokes checking, feedback, and repair interactions during multi-agent trajectory collection by injecting controlled perturbations and restricted reference-based guidance. It produces a dataset of 4,567 reconstructable trajectories over software-engineering and reasoning tasks, with experiments showing feedback gains of 47.72-100 percentage points across task pairs.

entry.title: One Model, Multiple Compute Budgets: Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE for Flexible Compute Across Turns

author.name: Yiyang Fu, Zihao Huang, Dongchen Han, Shukai Gong, Zhen Dong, Qiyang Min, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE enables a single shared model to support multiple token-to-concept compression ratios (2x, 4x, 8x) that can be flexibly assigned per turn in multi-turn interactions. Lightweight full-token modules and ratio-specific components avoid rebuilding history states when switching compute budgets.

entry.title: The RNN Homunculus: Learning to Gate Long-Term Memory

author.name: Zeyu Fan, Alexandru-Dragos Manolache, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: This analytical paper studies how gated RNNs (GRUs, LSTMs) learn their gate values, showing that the standard additive-copy-path explanation is incomplete: gated architectures still suffer vanishing gradients when all training samples require long-range memory. The authors show via controlled interventions that adding short-dependency samples enables gate learning, which then unlocks long-range memory.

entry.title: SceneForesee: Learning Scene Evolution for Spatiotemporal Reasoning

author.name: Chaoyue Li, Shoudong Han, Haoyang Wu, Boxue Yang, Sijia Chen, Yufan Chen, Ruping Zhang

entry.summary: The authors formulate Scene Evolution Understanding (SEU), a task requiring models to track entity continuity and predict future trajectories, events, and visual evidence from observed video. The SceneForesee benchmark contains roughly 145K temporal pairs and over 1M entity centroids with paired observed and future scenes sharing entity identities.

entry.title: Rethinking Activation Functions: Reducing Bias Can Improve Learning

author.name: Zirui Peng, Heyi Zheng, Ziming Liu

entry.summary: Studies activation bias, the nonzero post-activation mean produced by ReLU, GELU, Swish, and Sigmoid, showing it accelerates early loss reduction but causes overshooting and steeper loss landscapes. Reducing activation bias slows initial learning but yields lower final loss, demonstrated on vision and language models.

entry.title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
