author.name: Tejas Vaidhya, Gaurav Sahu, Irina Rish

entry.summary: Tab-Loop replaces the untied in-context learning blocks of a tabular foundation model with tied blocks applied k times, matching an untied baseline at matched pretraining and inference compute with 62% fewer parameters. The result suggests ICL depth, not per-layer parameters, drives adaptation in tabular foundation models.

entry.title: Accuracy and Uncertainty in Machine Deception Detection (Research White Paper)

author.name: Heng-Sheng Chang

entry.summary: This white paper proposes a Machine Deception Detector that reads every layer of a language model's internal activations to catch deceptive-looking-honest responses, learns which tokens carry deception evidence from response labels only, and calibrates thresholds to keep false-positive rates below prescribed levels. An ensemble of detectors quantifies uncertainty in alarms, addressing the brittleness of layer-dependent activation probes. The goal is deception monitoring whose alerts merit trust.

entry.title: SARATHI: Decoupled Data-Free Probing and Adaptive Reconstruction for Structured LLM Pruning

author.name: Sankar Behera, Dhruv Singh, Satyadev Ahlawat, Yamuna Prasad

entry.summary: SARATHI decouples neuron selection from weight reconstruction in structured LLM pruning: a data-free NMF Residual Subspace Probe scores neurons from intrinsic weight geometry with a formal connection to Robust PCA, and Adaptive OBS reconstructs weights with localized calibration at O(d^2) peak memory per layer. This avoids domain bias from shared calibration data and OOM failures at high sparsity.

entry.title: SurgiCLAW: An Interpretable Atomic-Skill Agent for Precision Robotic Micromanipulation

author.name: Angen Ye, junjie xie, Yujia Song, Junkai Huang, Dapeng Zhang

entry.summary: SurgiCLAW is a hierarchical framework for precision surgical robotics that restricts a multimodal LLM to visual understanding, structured explanation, and atomic skill selection, while delegating execution to verifiable deterministic control programs. It is evaluated on brain-machine-interface implantation as a representative high-precision task.

entry.title: SLDBench v2: Active Scaling Law Discovery

author.name: Lingbei Meng, Rui Huang, Zhirong Shen, Jinxin Liu, Lingxiao Jing, Haorui Chen, Yaosong Du, Haowei Lin

entry.summary: Extends SLDBench to test whether LLM agents can actively discover scaling laws by choosing which experiments to run under recorded compute costs, not just fit laws from given data. It expands to 127 scenarios (30 challenging ones spanning over 10^23 FLOPs of source training compute) and introduces active experiment-selection evaluation.

entry.title: LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers

author.name: Zhixiong Zhao, Zukang Xu, Xing Hu, Lifeng Liu, Guangyu Sun, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: LoopQuant introduces a loop-aware post-training quantization framework for Looped Language Models, addressing cross-loop activation dynamics, heterogeneous loop sensitivity, and recursive error propagation that break feed-forward PTQ methods at low precision. Its components include cross-loop distribution canonicalization for accurate low-bit deployment.

entry.title: Heuristics are Not Enough: Calibrated and Corrected Caching for Video Diffusion Acceleration

author.name: Jiyue Jiang, Zhiyu Huo, Yuhan Chen, Yanruisheng Shao, Gong Zhang, Lei Deng

entry.summary: AlignCache is a closed-loop feature-caching framework for accelerating video diffusion models, aligning caching decisions with true influence on final output via phase-adaptive budget routing, replacing heuristic difference measures and global thresholds while validating and correcting budget estimates against actual approximation error. This addresses systematic bias in existing training-free caching.

entry.title: StableJudge: A Lightweight Adversarial Defense Framework for LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Anning Hu, Yangyu Li, Yuqi Huang, Shengchao Hu, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: StableJudge defends LLM-as-a-Judge pipelines against score-hijacking prompt injection by externalizing mitigation as a reusable pre-scoring capability centered on a compact 0.1B model, rather than modifying the judge itself. This makes the defense independent of judge scale, training, or replacement.

entry.title: Event-Centric Earthquake Monitoring with a Multi-Station Transformer

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Weiqiang Zhu

entry.summary: EQNet2 is a geometry-aware multi-station Transformer that jointly predicts phase arrivals, first-motion polarities, source location and magnitude, and arrival-to-event association, rather than processing stations independently and fragmenting tasks. On Northern California, Ridgecrest, and Bay Area data it recovers more complete and reliable earthquake catalogs. This unifies previously separate seismic monitoring tasks in one model.

entry.title: Benchmarking Self-Supervised 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models and Transferability Estimation

author.name: Jiaqi Tang, Yu Wang, Yang Liu, Jing Tao, Fandong Zhang, Zhou Zhen, Xiahai Zhuang, Qingchao Chen, Yining Yang, Yizhou Yu

entry.summary: This study benchmarks 23 self-supervised 3D medical vision foundation models across 14 segmentation, classification, and regression tasks spanning multiple anatomies and modalities, addressing the incomparability of published evaluations. It also examines transferability estimation to predict which model suits a new task without costly fine-tuning; no candidate dominated all tasks.

entry.title: HelpMeOut: A Neuropsychology-Grounded Benchmark for Error-Aware Monitoring of Household Task Execution

author.name: Haoran Wang, Jingwei Huang, Anqing Duan, Ho Seok Ahn, Bruce Macdonald

entry.summary: HelpMeOut is an embodied AI benchmark for monitoring household task execution when humans make structured errors, motivated by cognitively impaired and older-adult populations. It operationalizes neuropsychological research on everyday action errors into 20,000 paired activity episodes across nine error categories, requiring agents to detect and diagnose execution errors as early as possible in streaming activity trajectories. This fills a real gap, as existing household benchmarks largely assume correct human task execution.

entry.title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience

author.name: Bo Ni

entry.summary: FracLearn is a framework where a language model iteratively proposes mechanical designs, observes simulated fracture responses, abstracts observations into conditional principles, and generalizes them to new designs. On a Tetris-inspired fracture game, the campaign shows progressive refinement and beats earlier design records.

entry.title: A Few More Tokens Ahead: Reinforcing Parallelism in Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Jiahao Kuang, Yangfan Gao, Tao Gui, Yuanbin Wu, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang, Tao Ji

entry.summary: The paper reveals that diffusion LLMs degrade severely under parallel generation, with all tested models scoring below 15% on math and code at 16 tokens per step under fixed-quota evaluation. It proposes RePara, which reinforces short consecutive token blocks via group-relative policy optimization, improving GSM8K and MATH-500 on LLaDA and SDAR with a 1.96x training speedup. This directly targets the parallelism advantage that motivates diffusion LLMs.

entry.title: Geometric Calibration of Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jianzhu Bao, Jia-Chen Gu, Qingyuan Liu, Haozhen Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows SFT induces dense updates that perturb the spectral geometry of pretrained weights along principal directions, potentially disrupting prior knowledge, and proposes SPACE, a lightweight post-hoc method that selectively reverts SFT update components in the principal subspace of pre-SFT weights. This connects fine-tuning pathology to weight spectral structure. It offers a cheap way to preserve model capabilities during SFT.

entry.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs

author.name: Divyanshu Bathla, Parag Singla, Jitin Singla

entry.summary: This paper argues that for low-resource machine translation with LLMs, the pre-LLM technique of back-translation outperforms continued pretraining when moderate monolingual data is available: the fine-tuned LLM translates monolingual sentences, and resulting pairs train the reverse direction with interleaved parallel-data updates. With only 1K parallel pairs on Odia and Swahili, back-translation beats continued pretraining.

entry.title: Token Utility for On-Policy Distillation via Local Trust-Region Optimization

author.name: Narayanan Sadagopan, Yilan Chen, Vijay Lingam

entry.summary: The paper derives token importance for on-policy distillation directly from the distillation objective, defining utility as the loss reduction achievable under an equal local KL budget, expressed via logit gradients and a categorical Fisher matrix. For reverse-KL this equals a student-weighted variance of log-probability ratios, and for forward-KL it equals Pearson chi-squared divergence.

entry.title: One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models

author.name: Joshua Cheung, Zhang He

entry.summary: The paper challenges the common practice of selecting JEPA world models by one-step prediction loss, introducing a frozen-decoder protocol that reports one-step error in physical units and decomposes it into encoder-inherent versus predictor-added error. Applying it to an end-to-end JEPA world model across continuous-control environments shows that prediction fidelity does not reliably predict goal-conditioned planning performance. This is a useful cautionary evaluation-methodology result for model-based learning.

entry.title: Enhancing Latent World Models with Associative Memory

author.name: Yuwei Sun, Siyu Zhu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a memory-enhanced latent world model that augments JEPA-style prediction with a content-addressable memory bank operating at multiple temporal scales in a shared latent space. Two complementary losses encourage slot diversity and balanced temporal utilization to prevent representational collapse. Experiments on PushT, Tworoom, Reacher, and OGBCube demonstrate improved long-horizon embodied planning.

entry.title: Universal Sample-Based Embeddings of Higher-Order Objects

author.name: Radovan Halu\v{s}ka, Christopher Solinas, Nathan R. Sturtevant, Martin Schmid, Michael Bowling

entry.summary: This work proposes a unified framework representing any higher-order object (distributions, functions, graphs) as a fixed-size embedding vector learned over a family of such objects, with an encoder operating on samples from the object. Unlike prior approaches tailored to specific object types, this works across types and generalizes to unseen members of the family. It enables neural networks to reason about relational, non-vector data compactly.

entry.title: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization

author.name: Yaroslav Gusev, Eugene Golikov, Dmitry Yarotsky

entry.summary: The authors identify and characterize the accuracy well phenomenon: under small initialization, accuracy rises early in training, then drops, and only much later recovers, observed across deep linear networks, MLPs on MNIST, CNNs on CIFAR-10, and synthetic tasks with multiple losses and optimizers. They give a three-stage explanation and rigorous theory for shallow and deep linear networks. This refines the standard picture of training dynamics and has implications for early stopping and initialization practice.

entry.title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning

author.name: Viet The Nguyen, Vijay Prakash Dwivedi, Gunther Gust

entry.summary: Reassesses how far simple propagation-based methods can go on relational deep learning benchmarks, where data is represented as temporal heterogeneous graphs over relational databases. The authors adapt fixed low-pass feature propagation to exploit target attributes, relational attributes, and historical labels, challenging the assumption that GNN and Transformer complexity is necessary. Helps calibrate how much architectural complexity current relational benchmarks actually require.

entry.title: Online Tokenization with Optimal Delay in Linear Time

author.name: Mina Dalirrooyfard, Christopher Ye

entry.summary: This paper presents online algorithms for full tokenization, including special-token segmentation, pretokenization, and byte-pair encoding, that stream input to output with optimal delay in linear time, improving on the sequential pipeline structure of prior work. Building on recent ICML, ASPLOS, and PLDI results, it completes the open problem of efficient online tokenization. This reduces latency and memory footprint for LLM inference and training pipelines.

entry.title: SNACK: A Sequential Notation Framework for Probabilistic Graph Generation

author.name: Hohyun Kim, Hyesung Kim, Min-hwan Oh, Seunggeun Lee

entry.summary: SNACK is a string linearization of graphs via lower-triangular adjacency entries that gives a bijection between valid sequences and ordered adjacency matrices, enabling invalid logit masking that guarantees 100% structurally valid outputs and principled GFlowNet training respecting node-order symmetries. It advances molecular and general graph generation with sequence models.

entry.title: ELARSpeech: A 30K-Hour Dataset Across 675 Underrepresented Languages for Long-Tail Multilingual Speech Technologies

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Yejin Jeon, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: ELARSpeech is a 30,202-hour multilingual speech corpus drawn from the Endangered Languages Archive, covering 675 underrepresented languages across diverse recording conditions and language families. The authors demonstrate its use for extending ASR and TTS to long-tail languages, with gains from pseudo-labeling unlabeled data, while acknowledging inherent limitations.

entry.title: Are We Really Measuring Forgetting? Pitfalls in Evaluating Machine Unlearning for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Oscar Chew, Po-Yi Lu, Yi-Jie Cheng, Kunal Jain, Hsuan-Tien Lin, Zhengzhong Tu, Kuan-Hao Huang

entry.summary: The paper identifies three pitfalls in evaluating machine unlearning for multimodal LLMs: missing heldout evaluation to distinguish concept-level forgetting from instance-level overfitting, reliance on synthetic fine-tuned knowledge rather than pre-training knowledge, and unfair comparisons from identical training settings across methods. It proposes remedies for more rigorous unlearning evaluation.

entry.title: Delta Tokenizer: Reference-Identical Tokenization of Session Deltas and Segment-Parallelism for Long Prompts on Multicore CPUs

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang, Zhichao Cao

entry.summary: Presents Delta Tokenizer, a CPU tokenization front end that tokenizes only the delta between consecutive requests in a session while remaining reference-identical to full tokenization, addressing the overlooked cost of re-tokenizing shared prefixes each turn. This reduces time-to-first-token and CPU consumption for long-prompt agentic workloads.

entry.title: Truthful and Expected-Payment-Optimal Model Routing in Graph-Based Agentic Workflows

author.name: Jiayuan Liu, Mingyu Guo, Jiarui Gan, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: The paper formulates LLM task routing in graph-based agentic workflows as a single-parameter procurement auction where providers may strategically misreport real-time unit costs, proposing STAR, a strategy-proof, topology-aware routing mechanism. Its allocation and payment rules minimize virtual-cost-weighted workloads while ensuring truthful reporting.

entry.title: The Gap Is in the Geometry: A Convergent Meta-Analysis of Multi-Facet Aerial and Remote Sensing Video Understanding

author.name: Georgios Angelidis, Aggelos Psiris, Maria Vakalopoulou, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos, Giorgos Sfikas, Iraklis Varlamis

entry.summary: This meta-analysis argues that evaluating aerial/remote-sensing video like web video with MLLM multiple-choice questions measures the wrong capability. Across four evidence tiers it finds parameter scale yields only +3.4 accuracy points per tenfold increase on aerial benchmarks versus a human gap of 19+ points, while acquisition conditions dominate perception in 315 of 318 within-paper contrasts.

entry.title: Why 3D Reconstruction Breaks Down on Under-Ice AUV Video, and How to Predict It

author.name: Ana-\c{S}tefania Kog\u{a}lniceanu, Kl\'ara Orb\'an, Ashwin Nedungadi, Stefan L\"udtke, Kuderna-Iulian Ben\c{t}a

entry.summary: This study tests four reconstruction approaches (classical SfM, differentiable splatting, volumetric depth fusion, and a pose-free feed-forward foundation model) on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video, finding all fail in distinct ways. The authors trace all failures to a shared capture-system deficiency and propose a way to predict when reconstruction will break down.

entry.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis

author.name: Yinzhen Huang, Jiahe Xie, Yitong Sun, Ruochen Zhang, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: The paper proposes backdoor detection for multimodal large language models based on analyzing dual-flow trajectories of model internals rather than static snapshots or attack-specific heuristics. This unified approach targets diverse threats including textual injections, sub-perceptual noises, and coordinated cross-modal triggers that evade static-cue defenses.

entry.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Qihang Cao, Haoyuan Li, Zihan Guo, Sensen Gao, Zihui Gao, Huixin Zhang, Fan He, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Xiaodan Liang, Jia-Wang Bian

entry.summary: The paper identifies a static-dynamic interference problem where 3D post-training degrades 4D dynamic understanding and vice versa, tracing sensitivity to late-layer MLP parameter groups. DynThinker proposes a unified framework using Decoupled Exponential Moving Average with configurable group-wise averaging to jointly strengthen static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning.

entry.title: PACER: Process-Aware VLA Policy Learning from Human Corrections for Robotic Disassembly

author.name: Chang Liu, Sibo Tian, Litian Gong, Zhiwen Fan, Jiachen Li, Xiao Liang, Minghui Zheng

entry.summary: PACER learns VLA policies for robotic disassembly of end-of-life products by exploiting both the policy's own rollouts and human corrections of its errors, using progress-aware evidence reweighting within SFT. This addresses data scarcity and distribution shift in contact-rich disassembly, where product variation and prerequisite sequencing matter. It turns otherwise wasted failure and correction data into policy improvement.

entry.title: Towards Certifiable State Estimation under Observability Degeneracy

author.name: Baoshan Song

entry.summary: This paper establishes a universal candidate-driven dual certification framework for non-convex state estimation under severe sensing degeneracy, where standard SDP relaxations fail due to rank expansion. It proves from an epigraph perspective that cost tightness and multiplier recovery survive degeneracy, enabling global optimality verification without direct semidefinite solving.

entry.title: ASIWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in a Persistent Survival Sandbox

author.name: Jianfeng Lin, Runze Wang, Haorong Hong, Yuxuan Xie, Zeno Zeng, Zhongyuan Liu

entry.summary: ASIWorld is a persistent survival-sandbox benchmark evaluating whether autonomous agents can sustain coherent goal pursuit over long interactions, with persistent world and character state, character-scoped observations, and a programmable asynchronous interface for agent-authored programs. Evaluation covers task success plus delayed-effect and adaptation behaviors.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Visual Agent via Margin Reward

author.name: Wenxi Yang, Yuzhong Zhao, Baochang Zhang, Yunfan Liu, Qixiang Ye

entry.summary: Proposes Marvo, a self-evolution approach where a challenger agent generates question-answer pairs from unlabeled images and a solver agent learns tool invocation via reinforcement learning. A margin reward encourages questions difficult enough to require tools yet still solvable, eliminating the need for curated QA data or expert demonstrations.

entry.title: State Representation Shapes Long-Horizon Agent Learning and Transfer: An Empirical Study

author.name: Dong Nie, Rui Lan, Yixin Nie, Lingzi Hong

entry.summary: An empirical study of how the state representation used during training affects agent learning and transfer in deterministic tool workflows, using 1.7B, 8B, and 27B Qwen models. It distinguishes failure to learn an action from failure to apply it as state changes, finding dramatic representation-dependence: compact-trained 1.7B adapters complete 50/50 held-out tasks in compact view but 0/50 in full view. Horizon-matched supervision yields high completion but poor transfer to longer workflows.

entry.title: Suggested Is Not Superseded: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of a System-One Model as a Memory-Retirement Gate

author.name: Xupeng Chen, Chenqian Le

entry.summary: This paper builds a task contract distinguishing SUPERSEDED, NEEDS-CONFIRMATION, and COMPATIBLE memory updates for assistant long-term memory, then labels 500 test pairs with LLM annotators and human adjudicators. It evaluates a typed System-One decision model called Jev under pre-registered hypotheses, showing that a large fraction of benchmark-labeled changed pairs do not meet the bar for established change.

entry.title: Imitation Holds a Key to Evolution: Localized Repair and Verified Skill Acquisition for Adaptive Agents

author.name: Kai Hu, Hua Huang

entry.summary: The paper formulates passive imitation as an architectural loop that localizes a violated contract, extracts a local goal, proposes an effect-matched skill, tests a small patch, and retains evidence after full-task verification. A deterministic symbolic instantiation solves all 600 cold held-out composition tasks across ten tool worlds within three trials versus 6.17% for a whole-trajectory control.

entry.title: EvoWeb: A Benchmark for Coding Agents on Evolving Web Applications

author.name: David Nukrai, Bar Alon, Nativ Levy, Ido Andrew Atad, Ido Cohen, Itamar Zimerman, Lior Wolf, Eli David, Ilan Naiman

entry.summary: EvoWeb evaluates coding agents on iterative web development through 320 cumulative requests over 32 applications with real product features and functional dependency graphs. A multimodal web agent tests each intermediate application in a live browser, assessing new functionality, cross-request integration, and regression on prior requests.

entry.title: Observe, Share, or Predict? Disentangling Partner Information in Embodied Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Adri\'an Szlatincs\'an, Filippo Ziliotto, Bruno Lepri, Luciano Serafini, Massimiliano Luca, Tommaso Campari

entry.summary: Studies whether LLM-controlled embodied agents can collaborate without sharing intentions, by disentangling three channels on the PARTNR benchmark: observing partner state, exchanging object knowledge, and predicting the partner next action. Using a decoupled partial observability regime with zero-shot decentralized ReAct planners, it measures how each channel affects coordination and whether agent roles are symmetric.

entry.title: Get In, Decide, Prove: A Merchant-Side Readiness Benchmark for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Adrian de Valois-Franklin, Alex Bogdan, Anas Ibrahim, Ibrahim Shaer, Tamaz Andguladze

entry.summary: Rather than benchmarking AI shopping agents, this paper benchmarks the merchant side: whether a website admits agents, publishes purchase-relevant terms precisely enough for decisions, and leaves auditable evidence of agreements. Its central metric, decision sufficiency, rates buyer-mandate criteria as determinate, indeterminate, or unknown based on merchant-published evidence. This fills a real gap as agentic commerce grows, since most work evaluates only the buyer agent.

entry.title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents

author.name: Taeyun Roh, Suhyeong Park, Gijin Kim, Wonjune Jang, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic study of memory representation in VLM-based GUI agents, finding that the preferred memory modality is strongly step-dependent rather than fixed, and introduces SwitchMem to adaptively select memory modality across interaction steps. This matters because memory-augmented GUI agents currently use static representation strategies, and choosing the wrong modality at a given step can discard useful experience.

entry.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch

author.name: Peng Jiang, Dongyang Li, Quanying Liu, Xiaoxuan Jia

entry.summary: ResearchFlow-Eval is a fine-grained evaluation framework for autoresearch systems that scores continuous scientific execution at both stage and claim levels, grounded in published anchor papers with stage-specific rubrics. It moves beyond isolated-task or final-artifact scoring to measure multi-stage workflows and iterative revision as evidence accumulates. This addresses a genuine evaluation gap as AI systems take on whole research projects.

entry.title: Input-Conditioned Search for Efficient Test-Time Scaling of Recursive Reasoners

author.name: Haochen Shi, Tianwen Fu, Qianggang Ding, Yinhan Lu, Yizhan Li, Huan Zhang, Yajie Zhao, Xingdi Yuan, Hengyang Lu, Bang Liu

entry.summary: For recursive reasoners that apply learned update rules to latent states, the authors propose scaling inference by applying different input-conditioned update maps to the same latent state, exploring diverse reasoning traces without extra training. This avoids convergence to incorrect attractors that plague depth and perturbation-based width scaling.

entry.title: PreSO: Privileged Representation Isolation for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yuhang Yang, Mingxuan Xia, Chao Ye, Shuai Zhu, Shouqing Yang, Haobo Wang, Shenzhi Yang, Zhengqing Zang, Chenglong Wang

entry.summary: PreSO studies on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), where a self-teacher conditioned on privileged information converts sparse RLVR outcomes into dense token-level supervision, and asks which privileged changes are worth distilling when the teacher's advantage relies on information unavailable at inference. Using cross-problem recurrence as a cue, the authors find compact hints produce more concentrated and directionally consistent representation shifts than full solutions, yielding more sustained downstream gains, and build PreSO around this insight. The work sharpens when privileged-information distillation is safe and beneficial.

entry.title: Rotate the Loop: Blockwise Conformality for Looped Transformers

author.name: Alexey Zemtsov, Albina Klepach, Vadim Lomshakov, Andrei Polubarov, Nikita Lyubaykin, Alexander Derevyagin, Vladislav Kurenkov, Alexander Nikulin

entry.summary: The paper analyzes looped transformers where one shared block recurs across steps, showing that state tracking depends geometrically on the residual map between recurrent steps. It proposes blockwise conformal injections that rotate residual groups with per-group timescales, improving performance on demanding state-tracking tasks.

entry.title: TraceSampler: Making Sampling Errors Predictable and Correctable for Accelerated Generative Sampling

author.name: George Matthew (University of Exeter, United Kingdom), Guoqiang Zhang (University of Exeter, United Kingdom), Kenta Niwa (NTT Communication Science Laboratories, Japan)

entry.summary: TraceSampler is a post-training method that corrects endpoint errors introduced by low-step sampling in continuous-time generative models without modifying the pretrained model. It treats error prediction as a sample-specific supervised problem using a higher-step reference integration as target, with a compact trace-based representation making high-dimensional errors predictable.

entry.title: Compositional Concepts Erasing: Disentangling Object-Style via Domain Manifold Unlearning

author.name: Yang Xiao, Kaiyuan Deng, Gen Li, Zinan Ling, Zhiwen Fan, Xiaolong Ma, Bo Hui

entry.summary: Proposes Domain Manifold Unlearning (DMU) for diffusion models, addressing object-style combination unlearning, which prior object-only or style-only methods miss. It uses an EMA-updated feature proxy from intermediate diffusion features and mitigates catastrophic forgetting across multiple unlearning requests.

entry.title: Across Viewpoints and Time: Trajectory-Generalizable Physical Attacks on World Models and Video Understanding Models

author.name: Song Xia, Meiwen Ding, Chenqi Kong, Wenhan Yang, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: This paper studies physical adversarial textures that remain effective as viewpoint and object-camera trajectories vary in the real world, targeting world models and video understanding models. The proposed TARA method uses trajectory-aware optimization and refinement to handle heterogeneous video semantics and poorly aligned gradients across uncontrolled trajectories. It exposes a robustness gap in models increasingly deployed in dynamic visual environments.

entry.title: Pessimistic Latent Task-aware Optimization for Robust Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chang-Hoon Jeong, Kisung Shin, Hanwool Sul, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: PLATO addresses the failure of context-based offline meta-RL on out-of-support tasks by exposing the policy to off-support latents during training, under a manifold assumption that out-of-support tasks lie near the boundary of the latent task manifold. This pessimism-oriented training improves robustness where task encoders extrapolate beyond training support.

entry.title: BridgeCodec: Mamba Enhanced Neural Audio Codec with Schr\"odinger Bridge at Low Bitrate

author.name: Zijian Lin, Jing Yang, Jinghao Luo, Zhuo Wang, Fan Fan, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces BridgeCodec, a framework that decouples the encoder-decoder pairs of neural audio codecs by translating latent representations between mismatched, frozen codecs, addressing the interoperability problem of closed codec ecosystems. It formulates the cross-codec translation as a Schoedinger Bridge optimal transport problem and uses a Mamba-enhanced U-Net to capture long-range temporal dependencies, validated by mapping an 8 kHz source encoder to a higher-resolution 48 kHz endpoint at low bitrate.

entry.title: TabMosaic: Unified In-Context Diffusion for Tabular Generative Tasks

author.name: Jayoung Kim, Sanghyun Hong, Noseong Park

entry.summary: TabMosaic unifies tabular generative tasks (synthesis, imputation, conditional generation) as joint conditional modeling of arbitrary target-cell sets given observed cells, using a diffusion objective defined jointly over all target cells for in-context operation on unseen tables. This avoids table-specific training and extends beyond single-cell in-context prediction.

entry.title: Personalized LLM Recommendation with Semantic IDs: Autoregressive Beam Search vs. Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Sejoon Oh, Fernando Amat Gil, Evan Smothers, Dan Iter, Mark Thornburg, Dawit Mureja Argaw, Sourabh Medapati, Thea Wang, Ria Verma, Qiuling Xu, Harshit Syal, Ehsan Gholami, Moumita Bhattacharya, Ashish Rastogi

entry.summary: Authored by a Google team, this paper compares how LLM-based recommenders should generate hierarchical Semantic IDs: constrained autoregressive beam search versus multi-token prediction with parallel heads. It analyzes the decoding trade-off between accuracy and inference latency in large-scale personalized recommendation.

entry.title: Dream2Discern: Learning from Hard Latent Variants for Runtime Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Boxuan Zhang, jianing Zhu, Xiaotian Han, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: Presents Dream2Discern, a runtime auditor for LLM multi-agent systems that predicts terminal outcomes from execution prefixes. It uses self-guided implicit augmentation, perturbing the auditor's representation operators to create hard latent variants of recorded prefixes, avoiding costly new trajectory execution and verification.

entry.title: SLEM: Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging

author.name: Dohyeon Kim, Bedionita Soro, Bruno Andreis, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: SLEM is an expert merging method for mixture-of-experts models that consolidates experts in a learned latent space rather than by direct parameter interpolation, aiming to avoid meaningless parameter-space averaging and reduce dependence on calibration data. It addresses the memory overhead of storing all MoE parameters.

entry.title: Growing to See: Efficient Pretraining of Self-Supervised Vision Transformers

author.name: Amir Mohammad Karimi Mamaghan, Ferdinand Kapl, Andrea Dittadi, Karl Henrik Johansson, Kaitlin Maile, Johannes von Oswald, Stefan Bauer

entry.summary: This work systematically studies progressive depth growth for pretraining self-supervised vision transformers in the MAE and DINOv3 families, examining effects on downstream performance, intermediate representations, and internal computations across global and dense tasks. Motivated by recent successes of progressive growth in language model training.

entry.title: MID: Mask-Image Distributional Divergence for Evaluating Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Vincenzo Marcian\`o, Xiaoming Zhang, Gianluca Guglielmo, Sebastien Ourselin, Michela Antonelli, Maria A. Zuluaga

entry.summary: MID is a distribution-level evaluation metric for medical image segmentation that assesses whether a collection of predictions matches the distributional structure of ground-truth masks, rather than relying solely on sample-wise Dice or Hausdorff comparisons. This enables evaluation on unlabeled data and captures population-level anatomical plausibility. The work addresses two concrete practical limitations of current segmentation evaluation protocols.

entry.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching

author.name: Ruchang Yao, Shi Guo, Junhao Zhuang, Mingde Yao, Xin Cai, Jiahao Zhan, Bin Fu, Xinyuan Chen, Yu Qiao, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: FlashVSR+ improves one-step diffusion-based video super-resolution with a hybrid attention architecture exploiting the strong locality of pretrained VSR models while retaining sparse global interaction, plus a Reward-Yield Distribution Matching training strategy for human-preference alignment. It achieves 2x DiT speedup and 45% lower peak memory, enabling untiled 4K VSR on a single RTX 4090.

entry.title: Posterior-Averaged Bellman Flow Matching for Distributional Critics

author.name: Zeqiao Li, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: The paper improves flow-based distributional critics in RL by observing that intermediate bridge states can be compatible with multiple Bellman endpoints, so their velocity should average over the posterior of possible endpoints. This replaces noisy single-endpoint supervision in distributional RL with flow matching.

entry.title: Evaluating the Causal Faithfulness of SHAP as a Candidate Attribution Method for SAE Features

author.name: Samuel Xie, Noura Al-Moubayed

entry.summary: Applies SHAP-based attribution to sparse autoencoder (SAE) latent features and evaluates it against direct causal interventions, using sentiment classification with GPT-2 Small and a 32,768-feature SAE as the testbed. It compares SHAP against Integrated Gradients, GradientxInput, and probe-weight baselines, scoring each against feature ablation and activation steering.

entry.title: From Policy Evaluation to Off-Policy Control: Provable Emergence of In-Context Q-Learning

author.name: Yingjun Mo, Yajie Zhao, Fang Kong

entry.summary: This paper proves that a two-layer attention-only Transformer can implement a finite-temperature form of Q-learning, with temperature controlling approximation to greedy action selection. Experiments on randomly generated MDPs show the theoretically predicted parameter structure, including internal greedy policies, emerges during training. This provides rigorous theory for how off-policy control emerges in-context within Transformers.

entry.title: AffectWorld: Benchmarking Emotion-Driven Future World Prediction

author.name: Changhao Song, Yacong Chen, Hui Gao, Yazhou Zhang, Peng Zhang

entry.summary: AffectWorld is a benchmark for evaluating whether world models capture the Emotion-Action-World State chain, with 1,498 annotated everyday videos, three consistency tasks, and a 233-sample counterfactual subset that changes an agent's emotion under fixed scenarios. It fills a gap since existing world-model benchmarks test only physical plausibility and perceptual quality.

entry.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models

author.name: Changyeon Kim, Kimin Lee, Yashraj Narang, Yijie Guo

entry.summary: ACCRUE is a continual off-policy RL framework for robot foundation models that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, reusing behavioral and value knowledge while adapting the critic only on current-task transitions. It addresses the gap between on-policy continual RL methods with limited forward transfer and off-policy methods that ignore cross-task persistence. This is directly relevant to deployable, continually improving robot policies.

entry.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Human and Agent Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Kaiyuan Chen, Shuangyu Xie, Uksang Yoo, Xinyue Zhu, Cael Magner, Alvin Zhu, Daehwa Kim, Eric Heiden, Erwin Coumans, Miles Macklin, Spencer Huang, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: RoboSimStudio is an interactive toolkit built on the open Newton physics simulator that makes solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, enabling both humans and coding agents to rapidly create and refine robot-manipulation simulations from observed behavior. It supports human-guided real2sim via visual evaluation and force feedback, plus agentic Real2Sim2Real workflows.

entry.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics

author.name: Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: ChunkAct brings action chunking to LLM-driven agentic robotics, where per-primitive LLM reasoning over full interaction history makes episodes expensive. By observing that primitives following a chosen sub-goal are largely redundant reasoning, the system launches a chunk of chained primitives with a single LLM call that then executes autonomously.

entry.title: Riding the Fixed-Point Curve: Image Classification in the Continuous Thought Machine

author.name: Thomas Hannagan

entry.summary: Analyzes how the Continuous Thought Machine (CTM) classifies images, showing each thinking step is an attracting but strongly non-normal map with balanced amplification, and that training promotes non-normality. Using Banach's theorem, the paper characterizes the thought trajectory as a curve traced by locally unique attracting fixed points that move each step.

entry.title: Dynamic Graph World Modelling: Learning Future Dynamics from Temporal Context

author.name: Bo Li, Yue Yang, Yujin Huang, Siao Liu, David Lemphers, Sara E Rodriguez Gomez, Luke Borgnolo, Can Wang, Xin Zheng

entry.summary: DyG-WM is presented as the first framework for dynamic graph world modelling, jointly predicting future node and relation representations from temporal context by addressing what has evolved, how, and what will evolve next. It tackles challenges including differing historical evidence for nodes and relations, path-dependent structural evolution, and sparse future targets. This extends world-modelling ideas to structured relational domains.

entry.title: VaryST: Generalizable Spatio-Temporal Forecasting Beyond the Closed-World Setting

author.name: Shengnan Guo, Jinjun Cheng, Xiaowei Mao, Jianhao Zhang, Haochen Lv, Yang Jiang, YiHeng Huang, Yan Lin, Youfang Lin, Huaiyu Wan

entry.summary: VaryST is a spatio-temporal forecasting model trained from scratch that generalizes beyond its training environment by dynamically constructing predictive context from available long-term observations, handling evolving temporal distributions, changing spatial domains, and shifting observation availability. This moves beyond node-specific representations and fixed spatial support that tie existing models to closed-world settings. It targets robust real-world deployment.

entry.title: On the Limits of Representation-Based Test-Time Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Pi\'orczy\'nski, Wojciech Masarczyk, Damian S\'ojka, Sebastian Cygert, Bart{\l}omiej Twardowski

entry.summary: The paper shows that representation-based test-time adaptation, which works well for CLIP-like contrastive models, largely fails to recover accuracy of generative multimodal LLMs under common corruptions, even when target data is used offline. The authors attribute the failure to the nature of corruption shifts in MLLMs lacking a shared domain-shift direction. This is an important negative result delimiting where TTA methods apply.

entry.title: In-Context Batch Black-box Optimization via Flow Matching

author.name: Quoc-Anh Hoang Nguyen, Xinyu Zhang, Daolang Huang, Julien Martinelli, Samuel Kaski

entry.summary: FMTR is an amortized in-context approach to batch black-box optimization that learns offline a history-conditioned continuous proposal distribution via conditional flow matching on refined Thompson-sampling argmaxes, from which variable-size batches can be sampled. This avoids increasingly complex batch-selection procedures of conventional Bayesian optimization in few-round, parallel-evaluation regimes.

entry.title: ReAl: Refine neural operators via aligning dynamical flow

author.name: Jing Xu, Zenglin Xu, Li Yi, Ruoxi Jiang, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: ReAl is a model-agnostic plug-in that refines pretrained neural PDE surrogates with a conditional flow-matching model trained on the residual distribution around the deterministic base prediction, recovering high-frequency fine-scale structure that MSE training loses. An alignment stage counters error accumulation in autoregressive rollouts. This combines the stability of deterministic surrogates with the detail-capture of generative models for physical simulation.

entry.title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?

author.name: Hengguang Zhou, Yuanhao Ban, Jiaqi Feng, Xiaohuan Pei, Justin Cui, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: This paper explores whether general-purpose coding agents can generate images by writing executable programs, introducing AgentDrawBench with 200 prompts for zero-shot drawing evaluation. Agents excel at structural precision and compositional constraints but fall short on photorealistic perceptual richness, revealing a complementary capability profile versus specialized generative models. It suggests program-based image construction as a viable alternative paradigm for constraint-heavy visual tasks.

entry.title: On the Optimisation Landscape of Overparameterised Weighted MMD

author.name: Tharrshann Jayan Logarajah, Jeremias Knoblauch, Louis Sharrock

entry.summary: The paper proves that for one-dimensional Gaussian-kernel maximum mean discrepancy over weighted atomic measures, sufficiently many particles make every local minimum approximately optimal, and spurious stationary points are unstable; for finitely supported targets there are provably no spurious local minima beyond an explicit threshold. This gives landscape guarantees relevant to particle-based distribution approximation.

entry.title: Posterior Frequencies and the Cost of Not Fitting: A Correction to a Memorization Lower Bound

author.name: Zhenisbek Assylbekov, Rustem Takhanov

entry.summary: The authors give an exact three-point counterexample to Feldman's memorization lower bound in its conditional and averaged forms, showing the ratio of proposed penalty to actual excess risk can grow exponentially so no constant-factor repair exists. They derive an exact replacement based on full-sample posterior probabilities, characterizing when it depends on multiplicity and the full frequency profile.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models Integrate Conflicting Evidence Like Biased Bayesian Observers

author.name: Josh Barua, Kyle Mahowald, William Rudman

entry.summary: This work models how vision-language models reconcile conflicting text and image evidence using a two-parameter Bayesian cue-combination framework with modality-specific biases. The model accurately predicts modality preferences under unseen combinations of input degradation and transfers to new unreliability types without refitting, separating evidence strength from integration bias.

entry.title: Rationale Distribution Distillation via Flow Matching for Distributional Continuous Latent Reasoning

author.name: Mingyeong Kim, Gyusang Cho, Juho Lee, Giung Nam

entry.summary: Proposes rationale distribution distillation (RDD), training a conditional flow over fixed-length latent sequences distilled from multiple textual chain-of-thought paths, with within-query mixup to expand distillation targets. This moves continuous latent reasoning from single point-valued rationales to distributions, improving answer coverage and exploration.

entry.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models

author.name: Bohan Sun, Zunhai Su, Xialie Zhuang, Jianjin Li, Ngai Wong, Chuan-Wei Kuo

entry.summary: ReaDy is the first speculative decoding method to exploit the recurrent states of hybrid linear attention models as position-specific context for drafting, using learned queries to retrieve supplementary context from the target's committed recurrent state. This improves draft alignment with target predictions in efficient HLA architectures.

entry.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation

author.name: Zhixin Cai, Ruoqi Yuan, Xinchen Yang, Zhuofan Chen, Jun Bai, Chuantao Yin, Wenge Rong

entry.summary: ARP-CD is a training-free contrastive decoding framework that reduces hallucination in video LLMs by constructing negatives directly in representation space, guided by attention mass on visual tokens at answer-prediction positions. This gives finer control over the model's visual reliance than prior predefined perturbation or masking approaches.

entry.title: LED-BENCH: A Benchmark for Large-format Engineering Drawing Understanding

author.name: Ke Li, Tianyi Wang, Enning You, Chaoqun Wan, Zhen Huang, Shuxian Liang, Xian-Sheng Hua

entry.summary: LED-BENCH is a multidisciplinary benchmark for evaluating fine-grained understanding and complex reasoning over large-format, information-dense engineering drawings, where practical questions require integrating evidence across regions and views. It fills a gap left by existing benchmarks that cover only constrained visual settings.

entry.title: A Diagnostic Study of World-Space Human Recovery Under High Camera Dynamics

author.name: Hao-Jen Chien, Wei-Lun Chao, Yu-Lun Liu

entry.summary: This diagnostic study introduces the K-Pop stress test of broadcast dance videos with fast camera motion and dense multi-person choreography, showing that leading world-space human recovery methods produce plausible per-frame meshes but drift badly in world coordinates. The authors systematically show the drift arises from combining camera and human estimates recovered at mismatched scales, not from either estimate failing alone.

entry.title: A Valid Watermark Is Not a Valid Identity: Spatial-Spectral Adversarial Face Evasion with Watermark Preservation

author.name: Jefferson David Rodriguez Chivata, Davide Ghiani, Simone Maurizio La Cava, Marco Micheletto, Giulia Orr\`u, Gian Luca Marcialis

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a watermark-preserving face evasion attack showing that facial watermarking for provenance does not guarantee reliable biometric identity. The black-box PGD-L2 attack uses spatial and spectral preservation terms to defeat face recognition while leaving hidden watermark cues intact, succeeding across two watermarking schemes, two recognition models, and two datasets.

entry.title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents

author.name: Yue Zhang, Han Lin, Zun Wang, Yidong Huang, Zaid Khan, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: WEDGE generates training environments for embodied agents guided by the specific failure modes of a pretrained policy, rather than generic realism or diversity objectives. An LLM proposes executable weakness features from contrasting successful and failed rollouts, validates them, and steers environment generation at each adaptation round.

entry.title: Collective Learning for Unified Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Dynamics Adaptation

author.name: Shaocheng Liu, Yuan Meng, Zhenshan Bing, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: The paper introduces PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that separates shared task-space intent from embodiment-dependent transition dynamics, enabling a single manipulation policy across different robot embodiments. Naive multi-robot data aggregation can average incompatible action modes, and PACE addresses this via a pretrained representation layer plus dynamics adaptation. This contributes to the growing cross-embodiment generalization agenda.

entry.title: GS-PRM: Gaussian Visual Roadmap for Image-Goal Navigation

author.name: Ashraf Siddique, Kyung Min Han, Young J. Kim

entry.summary: GS-PRM builds a navigation roadmap directly from 3D Gaussian Splatting renderings, defining render-based collision-free configurations and paths without needing occupancy grids or signed distance fields. Panoramic depth and edge-aligned orthographic rendering validate milestones and connect visually specified endpoints for image-goal navigation.

entry.title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Hanlin Liu, Zichen Zhou, Jiacheng Zhang, Liuyuan Na, Jin Jin, Guangyan Chen, Yufeng Yue, Gen Li, Fangqiang Ding

entry.summary: RAIN predicts the action errors of a lightweight manipulation policy at different refinement levels before performing any refinement, deciding whether and how much to refine each action proposal. An ensemble trained by comparing proposals with their refined versions enables adaptive allocation of expensive iterative refinement only where needed.

entry.title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC

author.name: Jelena Trisovic, Rahel Rickenbach, Marek Landert, Panagiotis Minos, Melanie N. Zeilinger

entry.summary: VIGOR-MPC is a modular student-teacher framework for navigation under vision-only perception: a privileged, field-of-view-aware long-horizon MPC teacher in simulation is distilled into a lightweight short-horizon MPC whose cost parameters are set online from vision. The design addresses noisy, occluded, variable-length perception and constrained onboard compute.

entry.title: Testing Conditional Distribution Equality Using Generative Models

author.name: Zekai Jin, Yi Zhang, Yun Yang, Xiaofeng Shao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a test for equality of conditional distributions that leverages generative models to compare distributions using both observed and synthetic samples, addressing power loss in high-dimensional conditioning. A sample-splitting and studentization scheme controls estimation error, yielding asymptotic normality under the null and local power guarantees. Notably, the theory requires only consistency of the learned conditional distribution, permitting a broad class of generative models, with applications to causal inference, model diagnostics, and transfer learning.

entry.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions

author.name: Sylvain Dehayem Kenfouo, Aaron Zweig, Mingxuan Zhang, Elham Azizi

entry.summary: The authors propose a training-free method for increasing diversity in conditional diffusion sampling by using local pullback geometry to find directions of maximal output sensitivity in conditioning-embedding space. Steering trajectories along these directions yields distinct generations while preserving prompt alignment and image quality.

entry.title: MontageFlow: Physically Valid High Fidelity EEG Generation

author.name: Sudarshan Regmi, Nabaraj Subedi, Arvind Pillai, Yu Yvonne Wu, Yuliang Chen, Michael V. Heinz, Lisa Marsch, Nicholas C. Jacobson, Andrew Campbell

entry.summary: MontageFlow is a flow-matching generative model for clinical EEG data that enforces the exact linear identities between electrode channels that real recordings satisfy. The paper shows that prior EEG generators silently violate these physical constraints even when fidelity metrics look good, and demonstrates that constraining outputs to be montage-valid improves both validity and downstream utility.

entry.title: LYNX: Analytical Program Synthesis via Grounding and Closed-Loop Refinement

author.name: Ruichen Xia, Xiao Han, Dingyu Yang, Luwei Yang, Sai Wu, Dongxiang Zhang, Binhui Yao, Gang Chen

entry.summary: LYNX is a multi-agent framework translating natural language instructions into executable analytical programs over real databases, treating the problem as schema- and knowledge-constrained synthesis. It runs a closed loop of planning, generation, verification, and refinement to improve execution reliability and semantic consistency.

entry.title: WeatherBridge: Forecast-Aware Multi-Source Input Adaptation for Pretrained Weather Forecasting Models

author.name: Mutian Xi, Xinyu Su, Xiaohui Zhong, Hao Li

entry.summary: WeatherBridge is a source-conditioned adapter that maps heterogeneous operational NWP initial states onto ERA5-like reference states so pretrained data-driven weather models can be deployed without retraining. It predicts structured residual corrections with a Swin-UNet and injects source embeddings at multiple spatial scales.

entry.title: Certify the Decision, Not Every Score: Exact Top-k Selection from Few Evaluations

author.name: Yuhe Sui, Yingzhi Tang

entry.summary: Introduces Certified Adaptive Selection (CAS), which returns the exact top-k set of candidate algorithms or schedules as soon as remaining uncertainty cannot change the result. It maintains guaranteed bounds on Expected Shortfall and proves that, for information-disjoint intervals, its one-cut stopping test is necessary and sufficient.

entry.title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Zhaoyuan Qiu, Sachith Seneviratne, Yu Xia, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: Proposes HarnessNet, a framework for hierarchical joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems built from Agentrons, each combining an evolvable forward harness, a frozen foundation model, and a local optimizer restricted to its own harness. The layered-graph architecture addresses scaling limits of a single global optimizer and access-restriction constraints.

entry.title: Scalable Robust MCTS with Anytime Deterministic Optimality Guarantees

author.name: Tomer Massas, Vadim Indelman

entry.summary: Presents the first deterministic anytime guarantees for robust online MDP planning with Monte Carlo Tree Search under model uncertainty. The method restricts computation to the sampled search tree while deterministically bounding contributions of unsampled trajectories, deriving lower and upper bounds for any fixed policy. This addresses the exponential tree growth and extra optimization cost of robust backups.

entry.title: Engram Injection: A Study of Temporal Validity in Parametric Language-Model Memory

author.name: Sam Siavoshian, Omar Ramadan, Amir K. Saeed, Benjamin A. Johnson, Benjamin M. Rodriguez

entry.summary: Engram Injection stores facts in LoRA adapters and supplies a clock via FiLM conditioning on a frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct model, testing whether models can learn temporal fact validity and answer correctly from only a question and current time. The paper includes a careful training audit ruling out test-age leakage and compares against prompting and retrieval baselines on before/after question pairs.

entry.title: Handoff Curves: Initial Selection, Later Handoff, and Supervision Targets in Multi-turn LLM Routing

author.name: Daniel Matos, Lu Liu, Yanfeng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces handoff curves to study how initial model selection, later handoff timing, and supervision targets affect success and cost in multi-turn LLM routing. Using 34,204 executions of Qwen models across BFCL, MultiWOZ, and tau-retail benchmarks, it finds that later handoff often fails to improve utility over initial selection and can increase cost.

entry.title: ScreenASR-Bench: A Tiered Benchmark for Speech Recognition with Visual Context

author.name: Mingwei Fu, Zheshu Song, Zhikai Zhou, Shen Huang, Shidong Shang, Mengxiao Zhu

entry.summary: ScreenASR-Bench is a tiered benchmark with three levels of progressively harder visual context for speech recognition: direct on-screen text, visible non-textual content, and implicit scene-level inference. Experiments across ASR models, large audio-language models, and omni models show visual context substantially helps with acoustically ambiguous words.

entry.title: HyWe: Unifying Search and Operation for Real-World Hybrid Web Tasks

author.name: Zijian Cai, Haowei Liu, Kailai Chen, Lin Peng, Cong Wan, Ziqi Zhang, Chunfeng Yuan, Bing Li, Weiming Hu, Haiyang Xu

entry.summary: HyWe unifies information search and page operation within a single web-agent model and trajectory, using dedicated prompts, tool sets, and explicit mode switching with shared history. The authors also build HyWeCollector, an automatic pipeline generating verified hybrid trajectories, and train a 35B model that unifies both capabilities.

entry.title: RAP-WAM: Learning World-Action Models through Predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations

author.name: Yuanpeng He, Ceyao Zhang, Fangjing Li, Kefei Zhu, Lijian Li, Yueheng Li, Tianjia He, Wenpin Jiao, Zhi Jin, Yaodong Yang, Yuanpei Chen

entry.summary: RAP-WAM adapts video generation priors for joint prediction of future observations and robot actions, using predictive rehearsal on model-generated inputs, action perturbations with measured video-response changes, and spatiotemporal credit assignment to allocate visual supervision for policy learning.

entry.title: Separating Prompt Harmfulness from Interaction Safety via Partial Generation

author.name: Ram Vikas Mishra, Shashank Aggarwal, Jahnavi Kumar, Amit Awekar

entry.summary: Argues that prompt-only safety guardrails over-reject because harm depends on what the model actually writes, and observes that interaction safety can often be inferred early from partial generations. The paper proposes judging safety from partial output rather than the full response, reducing both unnecessary refusals and the cost of full-generation evaluation.

entry.title: Understanding Personalization Gains in Whisper

author.name: Sergei Katkov, Antonio Liotta

entry.summary: This study analyzes when LoRA adaptation improves Whisper-style ASR models, comparing zero-shot, pooled, and group-specific adapters across Common Voice, LibriSpeech, and VoxPopuli. It finds adaptation gains are concentrated in hard, high-error groups, and that pooled LoRA often matches or beats group-specific LoRA.

entry.title: Learning to Play: Reinforcement Learning and Games

author.name: Aske Plaat

entry.summary: This is an arXiv abstract for a comprehensive work (likely a survey or textbook-style monograph) by Aske Plaat covering reinforcement learning applied to games. It traces landmark achievements from Backgammon, Checkers, Chess, Atari, Go, Poker, and StarCraft, spanning techniques from exact planning algorithms to adaptive sampling and deep function approximation, and discusses implications for progress toward general AI.

entry.title: SchemaWeaver: Accelerating On-Device Mobile Agentic AI via Schema-Guided Parallel LLM Decoding

author.name: Boyuan Yang, Wei Gao

entry.summary: SchemaWeaver speeds up LLM tool calling on mobile devices by exploiting output schemas to produce multiple tokens per decode pass, attacking the memory-bandwidth-bound decode phase that dominates latency on mobile processors. The technique is presented as generically applicable to schema-constrained tool calls. This supports the growing push toward on-device agentic AI without cloud round trips.

entry.title: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment

author.name: Qingchuan Ma, Yuexiao Ma, Xiang Meng, Yixuan Zou, Tianyu Xie, Wang Chen, Yuhui Zeng, Yuhang Wu, Xiawu Zheng, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: RoTA-Bench evaluates whether vision-language models can convert 2D observations into actionable 3D understanding via an interactive task: rotating a 3D object reconstructed from a 2D icon to match a target silhouette within an action budget. An automated pipeline yields 674 tasks with guaranteed solvability, and results show a persistent human-model gap across VLMs. It probes rotation reasoning and feedback-driven refinement, which underpin robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Understanding Gene Expression-to-Image Learning: Spatial Structure and Information Fidelity

author.name: Xiaoqing Lian, Pei Liu, Jiahui Tan, Quan Zou, Chen Lin, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: This work provides a controlled analysis of Gene Expression-to-Image (GE2I) learning, where single-cell RNA sequencing values are arranged on pixel grids for convolutional networks. The authors identify a fundamental trade-off between spatial smoothness and gene-level fidelity: structured mappings yield smooth low-frequency patterns that speed early optimization, while multi-gene pixel assignments obscure expression. It brings mechanistic clarity to a popular but poorly understood bioinformatics technique.

entry.title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms

author.name: Lachlan Tychsen-Smith, Mark Cox, Brett Wood, David Haddon, Kenrick Anderson, Benjamin Duck, Jim O'Malley, Noel W Duffy, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: Presents Tricorder, an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system for under-panel photovoltaic assets such as connectors, cabling, and fasteners that aerial surveys cannot see, combining LiDAR-inertial SLAM with geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal imagery and ML-based detection and segmentation. This matters because these defects are small, occluded, and hard to localize, and reliable inspection at scale affects renewable energy infrastructure economics and safety.

entry.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs

author.name: Yu Mi, Licheng Pan, Jiayi Zhu, Qirui Liu, Yitong Qiao, Changtong Xu, Tao Wei, Fei Sun, Zhixuan Chu, Kui Ren

entry.summary: The paper identifies modality misrouting as a failure pattern in omnimodal LLMs where joint audio-visual predictions are wrong even though the relevant unimodal branch could recover the correct answer. It proposes CaRe, a training-free inference-time method that uses a text-only modality probe to detect counterfactual modality-specific branches and correct misrouting. This offers a practical route to reducing cross-modal hallucinations without retraining.

entry.title: AssetForge: Asset-Augmented Task Synthesis for Business Automation Agents

author.name: Xiangrui Liu, Shuo Tang, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: AssetForge is a task-construction pipeline for training business automation agents that pairs a reusable library of construction assets (application interfaces, world-state components, policy evidence, native assertions) with task-specific rubrics. This decouples business logic from repeated infrastructure work when creating executable, verifiable training tasks.

entry.title: Compare to Correct: Pairwise-Guided Logit Adjustment for LLM Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Cong Hua, Qianqian Xu, Zitai Wang, Zhiyong Yang, Shilong Bao, Linchao Zhang, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Inspired by the Condorcet principle, the method computes pairwise confidence comparisons between reasoning paths supporting different answers and combines this comparative evidence with voting via a KL-regularized objective. The authors prove this comparative advantage is equivalent to adjusting traditional voting logits, yielding the Pairwise-Guided Logit Adjustment method.

entry.title: Unlocking Token Rewards via Training-Free Reward Attribution

author.name: Sitong Wu, Haoru Tan, Bin Xia, Xichen Zhang, Jingyao Li, Shaofeng Zhang, Xiaojuan Qi, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free method to extract token-level reward signals from an existing process reward model (PRM) by attributing the overall reward to individual tokens. It defines each token's influence as the reward change when the token is replaced with a semantically null token, and uses a first-order Taylor approximation to make this computation efficient instead of requiring N forward passes. This matters because dense token-level rewards are a key bottleneck for improving RL fine-tuning of LLMs.

entry.title: PLDiv: Measuring Dataset Diversity and Semantic Collapse via Persistence Landscapes

author.name: Yang Ba, Michelle V. Mancenido, Rong Pan

entry.summary: PLDiv is a dataset diversity metric derived from persistence landscapes that quantifies the structural organization of a dataset's distribution, capturing how neighborhoods evolve as samples connect. It targets the problem of semantic collapse as AI-generated data enters training pipelines, going beyond lexical or pairwise-similarity measures.

entry.title: Beyond Discrimination: Evaluating Probability Calibration in Radiomics-Image Fusion for Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Morgan May, Abraham Campbell, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Simon Caton, Pierpaolo Dondio

entry.summary: The authors evaluate whether fusing radiomics features with image models improves not just discrimination but probability calibration for renal cell carcinoma classification using 396 patients from KiTS23. Across 12 matched comparisons, fusion improved AUC and AP universally and improved Brier score, NLL, and calibration error in most cases.

entry.title: GG-Nav: Goal-oriented Grounding Chain-of-Thought Elicits Reasoning in Navigation Foundation Models

author.name: Shaohao Zhu, Wensi Huang, Siqi Zhang, Yuqiang Yang, Meng Wei, Chenyang Wan, Tianle Liu, Tai Wang, Jinming Xu

entry.summary: Identifies insufficient use of streaming observations and imprecise target localization as key failures of navigation foundation models, and proposes GG-Nav, which learns a structured two-stage chain-of-thought via supervised fine-tuning to localize goal-relevant instances and accumulate grounding evidence for navigation decisions.

entry.title: Prior-Fitted and Frozen Scorers for Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Tillmann Rheude, Roland Eils, Benjamin Wild

entry.summary: This work replaces handcrafted similarity scorers (e.g., cosine similarity) in multimodal contrastive learning with a Transformer, showing that even a randomly initialized, frozen Transformer scorer can beat strong handcrafted baselines. Jointly optimizing the scorer with encoders is found to be less effective, challenging assumptions about scorer design.

entry.title: Have You Been Convinced? A Neuro-symbolic Argumentation Reasoning Approach to Detecting Persuasiveness in ChangeMyView Discussions

author.name: Siddharth Bhargava, Sara Tonelli, Patricia Mart\'in-Rodilla

entry.summary: This paper introduces NARS, a neuro-symbolic system that detects persuasiveness in online discussions by combining retrieval-augmented iterative LLM reasoning to extract bipolar argument structures with gradual argumentation semantics to propagate influence. The authors also contribute CMV2BAS, a new dataset of long multi-threaded ChangeMyView discussions built from the Webis-CMV-20 corpus. The work demonstrates a principled way to bridge formal argumentation theory with LLM-based discourse analysis.

entry.title: A Sovereign, Indic-First, Reasoning Model

author.name: Sutanshu Saksena Raj, Prasanjith Pasunuti, Parijat Chatterjee, Daksh Maan, Purusharth Malik, Nayanjit Sarkar, Avinash Benki

entry.summary: Gnani-Evon-v3.3-30B-A3B is a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts reasoning model for English and eight Indian languages, built by adapting NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B (an existing open checkpoint released in late 2025) through in-place vocabulary expansion and continued pretraining. The vocabulary grows from 131K to 163K tokens, reducing Indian-language fertility by 38.6%, with direct 131K-token context training.

entry.title: What DNA Foundation Models Learn Beyond Sequence Composition

author.name: Vincenzo Yuto Civale, Andrew David Bagdanov, Alberto Magi

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether frozen representations from five genomic foundation models carry predictive information beyond simple k-mer sequence composition, across 57 genomic classification datasets and gene-expression regression tasks. Simple k-mer baselines remain competitive with most models, but NTv3 shows a consistent incremental advantage, improving 46 of 57 datasets under a matched Random Forest protocol.

entry.title: Query Your Way Out: Benchmarking Multi-Turn Knowledge Reasoning through Generalized Puzzle Solving

author.name: Xin Cheng, Junming Yang, Ning Xu

entry.summary: Introduces the Active Probing Benchmark (APB), which casts concept identification as an interactive multi-turn reasoning task combining active information gathering with specialized knowledge across roughly 960 target concepts. It moves beyond static puzzle benchmarks with rigid mechanics toward verifiable, partially observable interactive reasoning.

entry.title: Explicitly Aligned Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction from Variable-Length Screening Histories

author.name: Solveig Thrun, Zijun Sun, Suaiba A. Salahuddin, Kristoffer Wickstr{\o}m, Elisabeth Wetzer, Stine Hansen, Robert Jenssen, Michael Kampffmeyer

entry.summary: This paper improves mammography-based breast cancer risk prediction by explicitly aligning corresponding tissue regions across longitudinal screening exams while jointly exploiting both craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views, unlike prior methods that treat views independently. This could enable better risk stratification and personalized screening schedules in clinical practice.

entry.title: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents

author.name: Zian Yuan, Wei Li

entry.summary: PrivacyGuard addresses PII leakage from cloud GUI agents that send screenshots and instructions to remote planners, via source-linked sanitization that reconstructs fragmented evidence and a reference lifecycle that resolves entity mentions locally without exposing raw values. It reduces leakage while preserving entity continuity across multi-turn sessions.

entry.title: The Value of Being Wrong: Self-Mined Visual In-Context Learning from Errors

author.name: Shu Zhao, Tan Yu

entry.summary: Introduces SMILE, a method for visual in-context learning in vision-language models that builds demonstration pools from the model's own prediction errors rather than relying on multi-stage counterfactual pipelines. By treating failures as natural counterfactual demonstrations encoding failure modes, it simplifies example selection while retaining adaptivity at test time.

entry.title: Thinking Outside the Bots: Human Ideas in AI's Semantic Blind Spots Are Not Inferior

author.name: Kibum Moon, Dan R. Johnson, Kostadin Kushlev, Benjamin Lira, Indre Viskontas, James C. Kaufman, Roger E. Beaty, Angela L. Duckworth, Adam E. Green

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces EDGE (Expansion of Divergent Generative Expression), a method for mapping AI's semantic blind spots by comparing human-generated ideas against task-matched AI-generated idea sets across three open-ended tasks, including college admissions essays and alternative-uses exercises. The study addresses whether the human idea diversity that AI fails to represent reflects genuinely valuable thinking or merely lower-quality output, finding that human ideas falling outside AI's semantic coverage are not inferior to those AI captures.

entry.title: Mitigating Black-Box Score-Based Query Attacks via Gradient Confusion

author.name: Ali Javeri, Javad Hezareh, Radin Shahdaei, AmirMahdi Sadeghzadeh

entry.summary: The Gradient Confusion Defense is a retraining-free, deterministic test-time wrapper that shapes the probability vector returned to black-box score-based attackers by solving a constrained optimization problem grounded in the model's Jacobian, actively misleading gradient estimation. Unlike stochastic perturbation defenses, it does not rely on randomness that attackers can average out. This offers a new defense class against query-based adversarial attacks.

entry.title: VeriPIE: Checkable Query Plans and Evidence-Guided Selection for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Piyush Jha, Cruise Song, Zhengyu Li, Yatharth Sejpal

entry.summary: VeriPIE is a neurosymbolic text-to-SQL framework that combines language-model generation with symbolic verification, using QuerySketch structured plans checked by a Lean-implemented backend before SQL generation. Plan diagnostics guide repair, and execution agreement with bounded distinguishing searches helps select between candidate SQL queries. It is motivated by financial AI governance requirements for independent validation and effective challenge of AI computations.

entry.title: HiSTOR: Structured Treatment-outcome Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Longitudinal Data

author.name: Chuanqi Lao, Junzhou Huang, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: HiSTOR is an end-to-end framework for estimating potential outcomes under alternative treatment sequences, combining nonlinear dimensionality reduction with longitudinal counterfactual prediction. It learns structured low-dimensional representations of patient states and histories that account for shared and distinct relationships with treatments and outcomes.

entry.title: GLST: Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Memory Decomposition Framework for Online Chained-Goal Navigation

author.name: Yousef Liang, Ryan Ardalan, Yarden Goraly, Chenhao Zhu, Yue Yin, Jonas Frey, Claire Tomlin, Marco Pavone, Shankar Sastry

entry.summary: Studies online chained-goal navigation, where goals are redirected or newly emerge mid-episode without explicit transition signals, creating conflicting memory needs between continued exploration and strategic revisitation. GLST decomposes latent beliefs into global and local spatio-temporal components to handle these shifting requirements under partial observability.

entry.title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhiwei Chen, Zhongtao Rao, Waikit Xiu, Yuxiang Zhang, Shuting Cui, Jian Chen, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: This paper addresses performance degradation (up to 90%) when multi-agent LLM systems reuse non-prefix KV caches across agents with conflicting tasks. LatentRemedy introduces a few task-conditioned latent tokens that help a target agent correctly interpret reused context without recomputation. This improves inference efficiency for multi-agent deployments where context sharing would otherwise be unsafe.

entry.title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory

author.name: Qian Chen, Xianyin Zhang, Lifan Guo, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs document-level heading hierarchies across long documents, using a level-wise multimodal memory to maintain consistency despite page-by-page processing constraints. It addresses a practical gap between page-level OCR/parsing and the coherent structure needed for downstream RAG applications.

entry.title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing

author.name: Yuxuan Ren, Jiatong Li, Ziqiao Meng, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: STAMP introduces a molecular representation that explicitly encodes motif identity, attachment sites, and tree topology, enabling fragment-level learning and precise structural editing of molecules. Its representations improve activity-cliff prediction on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder and support scaffold-preserving subtree operations. This matters for drug discovery workflows that require chemically meaningful, editable molecular units.

entry.title: Aligning Faithfulness for Theory-Scale Autoformalization

author.name: Yuming Feng, Tadd Mao, Dhruva Arekar, Tianjun Zhong, Jiani Huang, Xujie Si, Ziyang Li

entry.summary: This paper reformulates autoformalization faithfulness evaluation as a context-aware align-then-label problem, identifying phrase-level correspondences between informal and formal mathematical statements rather than issuing whole-item verdicts. It addresses the theory-scale nature of mathematics, where statements derive meaning from surrounding conventions. This matters for building reliable automated verification of formalized mathematics.

entry.title: Falsification-proof non-market allocation mechanisms

author.name: Eduardo Perez-Richet, Vasiliki Skreta

entry.summary: This mechanism design paper characterizes optimal falsification-proof rules for non-market resource allocation, showing that naively optimal rules invite manipulation of reported characteristics, causing inefficiency and negative externalities. The authors derive optimal robust rules under a broad range of falsification technologies and provide an honesty condition under which these rules solve the unconstrained planner problem balancing allocative surplus and agent welfare. The work is relevant to allocation systems increasingly delegated to AI, such as matching, rationing, and resource-targeting settings.

entry.title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design

author.name: Johanna Magdalena Kuch, Maud van Lier, Daksitha Senel Withanage Don, Patrick Gebhard, Tanja Schneeberger, Elisabeth Andr\'e

entry.summary: This human-subjects study examines whether zero-shot voice cloning of a familiar voice transfers associated personality impressions to an embodied virtual character. Across two studies, the authors test whether cloned vocal identities could be exploited to make people perceive virtual characters as capable social actors, raising manipulation concerns relevant to AI safety and character design.

entry.title: Lotus: Learning to Understand Time-series by Learning to Forecast

author.name: Van Dai Do, Huu Hiep Nguyen, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Manh Nguyen, Hung Le

entry.summary: LOTUS introduces forecast grounding, a pretraining principle requiring language-aligned time-series representations to remain predictive of future signal evolution before downstream adaptation. It patches time-series channels into an LLM embedding space and predicts the next patch from hidden states, encouraging representations that preserve dynamics rather than just linguistic alignment.
