entry.title: Contextual Credit Policy Optimization

author.name: Huiwen Han, Ziyao Zeng, Zihao Zhu, Sisong Bei, Hao Wang, Hongyu Xu, Yan Han, Degui Zhi, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: CCPO improves group-based RL for LLM agents in long-horizon tasks by weighting observation-matched peer trajectories by contextual similarity computed from frozen LLM representations and trajectory statistics. This addresses the problem that identical observations arise in different contexts and that favorable terminal outcomes can mask redundant actions.

entry.title: Imagining Goals with Geometric Horizon Models for Policy Generalization

author.name: Daniel Lawson, Dhruv Sreenivas, Adriana Hugessen, Khimya Khetarpal, Glen Berseth

entry.summary: Proposes geometric horizon models for goal-conditioned RL that improve zero-shot compositional generalization by generating imagined goals and mitigating the difficulty of long-horizon world model rollouts. The method targets offline-trained policies that must handle unseen task combinations.

entry.title: FireGraphNet: Sub-daily wildfire spread prediction with directed graph neural networks

author.name: Aiyshwariya Paulvannan Kanmani, Miguel Esparza, Ali Mostafavi

entry.summary: Formulates 12-hour wildfire growth as node classification on directed H3 graphs with wind, terrain, fuel, and barrier features on edges, achieving average precision 1.7-1.9x the strongest baseline on California test fires and 1.62x out of state. Ablations show the skill comes from message passing and edge features rather than cell features alone.

entry.title: Where to Start, How to Move: Analyzing Curricula under GRPO for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Minchan Kim, Sungho Bae, Youngjin Kim, Hyunwoo Park

entry.summary: The paper studies Guide-Assisted GRPO for training long-horizon LLM agents, examining how starting positions, handoff units, and movement rules affect unassisted task completion when all-fail rollout groups provide no learning signal. Experiments across three model sizes on BFCL show that starting near completion with a turn-level threshold rule works best, and outcome-informed tool-call selection outperforms finer handoffs alone. This offers practical guidance for curriculum design in agentic RL.

entry.title: MIPS: Mitigating Mode Collapse in Reinforcement Learning for Large Outcome Spaces

author.name: Armaan Sandhu, Abhijeet Sinha, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: MIPS addresses mode collapse in group-based policy gradients like GRPO, where inverse probability scaling fails when outcome spaces are large and outcomes rarely repeat within sampled groups. The method performs marginal evaluation, combining signals across trajectories leading to the same outcome, to obtain usable probability estimates where direct computation is intractable. This improves diversity of high-quality solutions in RL for large outcome spaces.

entry.title: Beyond Static Positional Encoding: Bayesian Time-aware Attention for Non-Stationary Long-term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xinjie Lan, Yunbo Mei, Leheng Zhou, Hao Qi

entry.summary: The paper reinterprets self-attention in long-term time series forecasting as a Bayesian posterior, with a content-based prior from dot-product similarity and a temporal-evidence likelihood from positional encoding. From this view the authors derive a population-level ELBO and propose Bayesian time-aware attention for non-stationary dependencies. This gives a principled probabilistic account of how positional encoding shapes attention.

entry.title: ReGRA: Residual-Gradient Adaptation for Complementary Low-Rank Fine-Tuning

author.name: Fanyao Li, Yuxi Liu, Xiaohao Liu, He Chang, Zhaoxin Wang, Zhulin Tao

entry.summary: Motivated by the observation that higher-rank LoRA additions can degrade performance, ReGRA is a two-stage method that estimates task gradients on a calibration set, removes projections onto the subspace of the first-stage update, and aggregates residual gradients to form a complementary second-stage low-rank update. This makes better use of a fixed rank budget. It targets more effective parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: Efficient contextual partial monitoring with general function approximation

author.name: Kapilan Balagopalan, Hao Qin, Kwang-Sung Jun, Chicheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies contextual partial monitoring, a sequential learning setting with only partially informative feedback, and introduces E2D.PMSide built on the Estimation-to-Decisions meta-algorithm. It achieves computationally efficient algorithms with general function approximation via an online regression oracle for estimating outcome distributions. This extends modern efficient RL techniques to a broader class of feedback structures.

entry.title: MolHop: Scaffold-Hopping Molecular Design with Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanyi Su, Chenyan Wang, Yulei Gong, Yeyun Chen, Xiaohui Yang, Jun Cheng

entry.summary: MolHop is an agentic reinforcement learning framework for cross-scaffold molecular discovery, distinguishing scaffold hopping (finding structurally distinct molecules preserving function) from local molecular optimization that typical LLM-based design agents perform. It enables exploration of broader chemical space while retaining functional characteristics of reference molecules. This addresses a meaningful gap in AI-driven drug and material design.

entry.title: Trainable at Depth, Solvable at Small Size: What the Loss Surface of a Polynomial Activation Dictates for Designing, Initializing and Training Networks

author.name: Xiuyi Yang

entry.summary: The paper studies deep network trainability using a clamped, sphere-projected polynomial activation with an identity path, showing the construction trains 100-layer networks on MNIST without normalization. At small scale, the loss reduces to a polynomial system solvable exactly, and this small-scale analysis prescribes design, initialization, and training choices for the deep stack.

entry.title: TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design

author.name: Tianmeng Hu, Biao Luo, Ke Li

entry.summary: TANGO formulates RNA inverse design as a joint topology-and-geometry co-design problem, arguing that geometry-only objectives miss the secondary base-pairing topology that specifies functional RNA folds. It proposes a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with a staged curriculum that first learns topology-aware policies before refining to full 3D objectives.

entry.title: Non-asymptotic Convergence of Average-reward Q-learning with Options

author.name: Kintan Saha, Ahana Deb, Anders Jonsson, Debabrota Basu

entry.summary: The authors establish the first O(1/iterations) mean-square convergence guarantees for average-reward option Q-learning in both inter- and intra-option settings, proving multi-step span contractions for option Bellman operators under unichain assumptions. This connects hierarchical RL with the average-reward continual-learning formulation that discounted/episodic analyses miss. It provides a finite-sample theoretical foundation for options in continual tasks.

entry.title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers

author.name: Saatvik Kher, Hyungrok Do, Judy Zhong, Padhraic Smyth

entry.summary: Formulates online selection of agents or classifiers that jointly balance predictive accuracy and subgroup fairness as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit with Thompson Sampling, accommodating delayed ground-truth labels. This extends bandit-style model selection into the fairness-aware setting where labels arrive late. Empirical results on real-world datasets demonstrate the policy trade-offs.

entry.title: Discovering Undisclosed Concepts in LoRA Adapters for Diffusion-Based AIGC Models

author.name: Yupeng Qiu, Han Fang, Dhananjai Sharma, Ee-Chien Chang

entry.summary: This work develops a mechanism to discover the concept a LoRA adapter was trained to generate, supporting content moderation of shared diffusion-model personalizations where harmful content is not disclosed. It formulates concept discovery as searching for a conditioning input that maximizes output coherence, distinctiveness from the base model, and alignment with the learned LoRA subspace. This addresses a real moderation gap in the widely shared LoRA ecosystem.

entry.title: Learning in Strategic Queuing with Geometric Recharge: From Bandits to Systems

author.name: Cristian Palma Foster, Eva Tardos

entry.summary: This paper analyzes packet routing where queues are selfish agents running no-regret algorithms to select servers with unknown service rates, showing the single-queue buffered-server setting is equivalent to recharging bandits with geometric recharge. With Eva Tardos as co-author, it proves guarantees connecting bandit learning theory to systems settings and characterizes learning behavior with small data-center-like buffers. A nice bridge between online learning theory and networked systems.

entry.title: Generalizing Identifiability Results in Causal Discovery from Complete Data to Missing Data Settings

author.name: Matteo Ceriscioli, Shohei Shimizu, Mallika Gupta, Karthika Mohan

entry.summary: This paper establishes general sufficient conditions under which causal graphs remain uniquely identifiable when data contains missing values, including Missing Not At Random regimes. It provides a framework for extending correctness guarantees of existing complete-data causal discovery algorithms to missing-data settings, with conditions such as non-interacting missingness mechanisms and no self-caused missingness. This matters because missing values are ubiquitous in real-world observational data, and most causal discovery theory assumes complete data.

entry.title: Scaling LLM Inference via Parallelism: Throughput-Latency Trade-off

author.name: Javad Mirzaei, Jeebak Mitra

entry.summary: This work studies how tensor, pipeline, and hybrid parallelism configurations affect the prefill (time-to-first-token) and decode (inter-token latency) phases of LLM serving, and how optimal configurations depend on workload, latency requirements, and context length. It provides empirical characterization of a poorly understood but operationally critical design space. The findings inform cost-efficient distributed GPU inference deployment.

entry.title: On Inherent Privacy of Posterior Sampling: A Unified R\'enyi-Divergence Framework

author.name: Ruyu Zhou, Fang Liu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper develops a unified Renyi-divergence framework showing that Bayesian posterior sampling can provide differential privacy guarantees without added noise. The authors prove that privacy loss in One-Posterior-Sampling is governed by posterior exponential moments of the log-likelihood ratio, deriving explicit DP guarantees under bounded, sub-Gaussian, and sub-exponential tail conditions across representative Bayesian models.

entry.title: HACHIMI-II: From Role-Play to Learner Behavior Modeling for Faithful Student Simulation

author.name: Yilin Jiang, Fei Tan, Xuanyu Yin, Jing Leng, Aimin Zhou

entry.summary: This work recasts simulated students for tutoring research from LLM role-play to third-person behavioral prediction of a specific learner, building a student model from learner history to reproduce individual success and failure patterns. This yields simulations that actually err like real learners rather than at the LLM's own competence level.

entry.title: Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds

author.name: Vahe Karagulyan, Miko{\l}aj Kasprzak, Pierre Alquier

entry.summary: The paper extends minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of Markov chains from single trajectories to compact continuous state spaces, achieving minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors for chains with Lipschitz transition densities. Combined with concentration inequalities, this enables applications to confidence intervals, generalization bounds, and rested bandits with Markov rewards.

entry.title: Gap Detection: Mitigating Homogenization through Demand and Defensibility

author.name: Xucheng Yu, Haibo Jin, Xiaoqi Wang, Runze Kong, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Gap Detection, a framework for generating diverse alternatives to LLM answers by searching for unoccupied directions in a shared embedding space. Its GapScore objective combines query relevance (Demand) with dissimilarity to existing responses (Defensibility), then maps candidate directions to concepts for constrained prompting.

entry.title: Pre-Trained Language Models as Zero-Shot Tools for Social Science Research

author.name: Noah Dasanaike

entry.summary: This paper shows pre-trained LLMs can perform record linkage and demographic inference from names zero-shot, without task-specific training data. It introduces EnsembleLink, which combines pre-trained embeddings with string-based scorers for candidate retrieval and matching, matching or exceeding prior approaches while generalizing across scripts and formats. This has practical value for social science pipelines where labeled data is costly.

entry.title: Beyond Corrected Actions: Training LLM Agents on Textual Critiques

author.name: Thomas Zeng, Zelei Cheng, Mingyang Zhou, Sambit Sahu, William Campbell, Genta Indra Winata

entry.summary: This paper proposes Critique-Augmented Agentic Fine-Tuning (CAFT), which uses expert models to generate textual critiques explaining why student agent actions are wrong, providing richer supervision than behavior cloning or action correction alone. The study demonstrates that training on such critique feedback improves multi-turn LLM agents.

entry.title: Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop

author.name: Bin Zheng, Zheng Chen

entry.summary: Trains a shared candidate-answer reader on a frozen Qwen3.5-4B backbone to unify direct answering with on-demand, interruptible reasoning, using a benefit gate, a natural-state trigger, and an entropy-based stopping rule. On 768 questions across ProofWriter, LogiQA 2.0, and ARC-Challenge, accuracy rises from about 71% to 84% over direct reading while measuring the tradeoff between reasoning work and pipeline time.

entry.title: Beyond Benchmark Accuracy: A Diagnostic Test for LLM Chemical Prediction

author.name: Yanyi Su, Yu Zeng, Hongshuai Wang, Chenyan Wang, Zhifeng Gao, Xiaohui Yang

entry.summary: Introduces the Identity-Blinded Reasoning Diagnostic framework, which hides target entity identity in chemical prediction tasks and instead specifies targets via a known source entity plus an explicit structural edit operation. This distinguishes transferable structure-property reasoning from contextual leakage or memorization that inflates benchmark scores.

entry.title: TreeSpark: Learning to Draft the Trees You Verify for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jihao Zhao, Qianyu Jiang, Shuaishuai Zu, Pengfei Li, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Biao Qin, Zhibin Wang, Baochuan Yang

entry.summary: TreeSpark extends the DSpark semi-autoregressive speculative decoding architecture with a unified training and inference framework that builds parent-conditioned candidate draft trees. It introduces survival negative log-likelihood and a capped coverage hinge loss to supervise tree expansion and pruning, improving accepted draft length over prior parallel drafters.

entry.title: Repairing Speech Access After Text Updates with Frozen Affine Fields

author.name: Ming-Hao Hsu, Yuxiang Wang, Yingda Shen, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: This paper addresses the mismatch where knowledge added to a language model via text updates remains hard to access through spoken queries. The authors propose AFFIRM, a detachable operator that repairs speech-only access in a single pass while keeping the knowledge-bearing checkpoint frozen, using a frozen base correction plus zero-mean query-specific corrections of speech hidden states. This matters for maintaining multimodal speech-capable models without costly retraining of the full model.

entry.title: From Unreliable to Usable: Decomposing Failure Modes and Confidence Signals in LLM Entity Extraction - Evidence from Cyber Threat Intelligence

author.name: Jiahong Qian

entry.summary: A preregistered, frozen evaluation of entity extraction from cyber threat intelligence reports compares low-cost models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash) against the flagship GPT-6.1-Sol across 354 incident campaigns. Results show severe unreliability persists across model tiers, with very low precision and poor verbalized calibration, raising questions about whether confidence signals can make such output usable.

entry.title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory

author.name: Minghao Guo, Qingyue Jiao, Xiujin Liu, Jianhong Pang, Ruimeng Yang, Naihao Xu, Liwei Che, Haochen Xue, Ziqi Wang, Xinying Cai, Jiaxuan Luo, Jiaxin Deng, Xuesong Ye, Jintao Qu, Wenyao Gao, Jingwen Gu, Chenyang Zhao, Shichun Liu, Guibin Zhang, Zefang Liu, Siyin Wang, Wujiang Xu, Danrui Li, Zeru Shi, Woongyeong Yeo, Shuang Liu, Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Tianyu Yang, Kangsan Kim, Yebowen Hu, Bowen Wen, Bowen Jiang, Haohao Su, Ming Yin, Sheldon Yu, Mian Zhang, Yuyan Chen, Hanrong Zhang, Kai Mei, Zihao Zhang, Mingyu Jin, Xi Zhu, Hengyi Wang, Tianxin Wei, Linyong Nan, Zhenwen Liang, Zhendong Chu, Ziqi Huang, Yongye Su, Sixun Dong, Shujian Liu, Kaiqu Liang, Jiaojiao Han, Zhaoye Fei, Kun Wang, Shihan Dou, Zhichun Guo, Xingjian Diao, Zeqi Gu, Heng Wang, Tao Feng, Cheng Qian, Hamid Palangi, Silei Xu, Xi Yun, Yi Zhu, Shilong Liu, Qingsong Wen, Sung Ju Hwang, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Yiyu Shi, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Jiaxuan You, Julian McAuley, Mengdi Wang, Jiawei Han, Philip S. Yu, Ziyi Ye

entry.summary: This large-collaboration survey provides a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory, organized around how multimodal information is represented and maintained across sessions. It addresses the challenge of enabling long-horizon, lifelong multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information and refine memory-management policies.

entry.title: MultiPartyTurnBench: Benchmarking Floor Control in Multi-Party Spoken Dialogue

author.name: Puneet Mathur, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: MultiPartyTurnBench provides 240 synthetically generated, channel-separated conversations with two to five speakers and six interaction types to evaluate floor control in full-duplex speech systems. It defines two tasks: distinguishing genuine end-of-turn from holds, and distinguishing successful interruptions from failed floor takeovers.

entry.title: Data-free Multistep Diffusion Distillation

author.name: Ngoc Duy Tran, Kien Do, Duc Thanh Nguyen, Truyen Tran

entry.summary: PMDD proposes progressive multistep data-free distillation of diffusion models, assigning a dedicated adapted network per student distribution to avoid the biased distribution matching and instability caused by one network approximating multiple score functions simultaneously. This enables multistep distillation at high resolution without training data.

entry.title: DeBoneDiT: Depth-Driven Conditional Bridge Diffusion Transformers for Bone Suppression in Chest X-Ray Images

author.name: Yifei Sun, Fenglei Fan, Junhao Jia, Wenming Deng, Hongxia Xu, Changmiao Wang, Ruiquan Ge

entry.summary: DeBoneDiT uses a depth-driven conditional bridge diffusion transformer to suppress bony structures in chest X-rays, addressing limitations of diffusion approaches like reconstruction-biased latent compression, prior-induced domain gap, and scarce paired data. It aims to match dual-energy subtraction quality without specialized hardware or extra radiation.

entry.title: MagicGarment: Benchmarking Single-Image Standalone 3D Garment Reconstruction

author.name: Jia Chen, Ruyang Zhao, Jun Bai, Chao Huang, Saishang Zhong, Xinrong Hu

entry.summary: MagicGarment is a benchmark for single-image standalone 3D garment reconstruction with 1,518 professionally constructed assets across 17 composite garment types, aligned multimodal annotations, and a unified evaluation protocol. It also establishes a garment-aware baseline adapting a pretrained image-to-3D backbone with grounded semantic refinement and a flow-time-route LoRA.

entry.title: SPECTRA-VLA: Base-Fine Hyperspectral Token Transfer at Frozen Vision-Language-Action Interfaces

author.name: Chih-Chung Hsu

entry.summary: This paper introduces SPECTRA-VLA, a method for adding hyperspectral sensing capabilities to pretrained vision-language-action models without retraining their frozen encoders or action decoders. It uses a learned continuous residual, calibrated via normalized false-color references, projection, norm control, and validation-based injection, to enrich target tokens with spectral information. On 86 held-out acquisitions, category-balanced accuracy improves from 0.812 to 0.883, and own-token addition improves external probe reuse on frozen decoder logits (0.701 vs 0.590).

entry.title: SceneAE: Scene Generation and Reconstruction in Queryable 3D-Anchored Latent Space

author.name: Shuofeng Sun, Wenzhao Zheng, Yunpeng Zhang, Yi Wu, Linqing Zhao, Haibin Yan

entry.summary: SceneAE represents scenes as a sparse latent point cloud where each latent combines an explicit 3D position with an implicit content feature, enabling both scene reconstruction and generation in a queryable 3D-anchored space. It is motivated by 3D memory mechanisms used in video world models and offers an alternative to conventional video-VAE latents.

entry.title: PAWA: Panoramic Action-conditioned World Modeling for Multiple Agents

author.name: Siqi Yang, Yimu Wang, Ziqi Cai, Chengxuan Zhu, Shuchen Weng, Erwin Wu, Zhaofei Yu, Kaipeng Zhang, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: PAWA introduces a dataset and framework for multiplayer action-conditioned world modeling in Minecraft, pairing synchronized POV and panoramic videos with player actions so models can predict changes to a shared environment, including outside a player's field of view. No prior dataset provided this combination for multi-agent settings.

entry.title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents

author.name: Shuo Wang, Sifan Zhou, Xiaobo Wang, Tianyu Fu, Chenxu Zhao, Anyang Su, Hanning Wang, Ping Jiang, Minghui Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces STP-GUI, a query-guided token pruning framework for vision-language models powering Web-GUI agents that interact with interfaces via screenshots. Unlike existing pruning methods tuned for natural images that select tokens independently and can fragment small UI elements like buttons and icons, the approach preserves spatially local visual structures while reducing the token overhead caused by high-resolution screenshots and multi-turn histories. This matters because GUI agents are an increasingly practical application area and inference cost is a key deployment bottleneck.

entry.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation

author.name: Yubo Huang, Yuxuan Zhang, Jiaming Liu, Sirui Zhao, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: This paper addresses latency in interactive video generation, showing that larger bidirectional modeling windows improve video quality and GPU utilization versus small chunks. It proposes a speculative sampling strategy that pads with noise latents to expand the modeling window, caches predictions for reuse, and delivers them incrementally while keeping uncommitted future frames replaceable.

entry.title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Seungmi Choi, Ji-Hyoun Choi, Suhyun Jo, Tae-Gwon Park, Hui Yong Kim

entry.summary: This paper introduces MFGS, an end-to-end feed-forward framework for compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting scene representations from sparse multi-view images. It replaces the conventional generate-then-compress pipeline, which encodes geometry and appearance separately with non-differentiable steps, with a multi-view feature coding approach that can exploit cross-attribute redundancy for better rate-distortion performance. This matters because efficient 3D scene compression is a key enabler for streaming and storing neural 3D content.

entry.title: Tread: A Visuo-Inertial Framework for Terrain and Locomotion Context-Aware Gait-Phase and Speed Estimation in Wearable Robotics

author.name: Debadrata Sarkar, Akash Bachhar, Aman Arora

entry.summary: Tread is a causal visuo-inertial pipeline for wearable assistive robots that jointly estimates terrain type, locomotion mode, gait phase, and walking speed from a chest camera and lower-limb IMUs. It achieves strong terrain classification accuracy (96.3%) and anticipates terrain transitions over a second in advance. This unification of previously separate terrain-specific models under one protocol is valuable for practical assistive exoskeletons and prostheses.

entry.title: RoboSpan: Learning Modular Coordination Policies for High-DoF Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation with Teleoperation

author.name: Keqiang Ren, Xuecheng Ye, Hanyu Liu, Zhihua Wang, Tao Jian, Yunsheng Ma, Jiayi Wen, Xinran Li, Zhigong Song

entry.summary: RoboSpan provides a teleoperation platform for 29-DoF whole-body mobile manipulation with dexterous tactile sensing, paired with a Hierarchical Modular Framework that decouples the action space into hand, arm, and mobile-base branches. Its Coordinated Modular Embodied Transformer (COMET) learns coordination across these heterogeneous modules to counter error accumulation in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: MUCO: A Mani-Unit-Structured Manipulation Framework for Compositional Long-Horizon Robot Tasks

author.name: Xiangyi Wei, Hanzhe Yao, Jingwen Shang, Zhenhong Wu, Yang Li, Changbo Wang

entry.summary: MUCO introduces manipulation units (MUs) as reusable operations with local goals, initiation conditions, and success/failure criteria, learned and verified individually, then composed for long-horizon tasks. Given language and vision inputs, MUCO constructs MU sequences, matches them to policies in a frozen capability registry, and dispatches execution while managing coupling through shared environment dynamics.

entry.title: ObjDream: Guiding Vision-Language-Action Models with Object-Level Understanding and Future State Prediction

author.name: Huailiang Ma, Yuxuan Li, Ziyi Zhao, Xinkai Wang, Mingyu Li, Xinyu Guo, Lifeng Zhu, Aiguo Song, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun

entry.summary: ObjDream is an object-centric VLA framework that moves beyond image-level representations by using a spatio-temporal object encoder and predicting future object states, targeting robustness under out-of-distribution object layouts, clutter, and background variation. The goal is fine-grained object understanding for manipulation.

entry.title: All-St3R SLAM: Real-time RGB Dynamic SLAM with Pixel-wise Motion Masking

author.name: Yewon Kim, Paul Hongsuck Seo, Sang Chul Ahn

entry.summary: The paper proposes a real-time dynamic SLAM system that removes moving objects at the pixel level without predefined labels or segmentation models. It combines pixel motion predicted by ego-motion via DUSt3R with point tracking from All-Tracker, masking only pixels whose motion is inconsistent with camera movement. This addresses over-removal and computational cost issues in prior dynamic SLAM approaches.

entry.title: PEARL: Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Jie Yang, Mianqiu Huang, Yiwei Zhao, Bo Wang, Yang Liu, Yuxin Wang

entry.summary: PEARL improves credit assignment for multi-turn agents trained with terminal rewards, without adding a critic. Given two continuations from the same history with different outcomes, it locates the first divergence, builds feature representations of local decisions, and clusters them in success/failure memory to identify recurring patterns that guide updates.

entry.title: Pre-Registered Genesis Accounting for Recursive Self-Improvement: First Audited Operator-Genesis Events in a Physics-Discovery Runtime

author.name: Wenbin Mao, Pei Zou

entry.summary: The paper introduces a pre-registered two-tier accounting scheme distinguishing machine-generated content from machine-authored mechanisms, and reports the first audited events where a discovery runtime registered a new operator of its own. In the flagship case, compositional search over elementary operators, validated on real NIST hydrogen data, rediscovered the Rydberg-level inverse-square form.

entry.title: WorkBorne: Discovering Agentic Tasks from Real-World Artifact Transitions

author.name: Junyi Zhou, Yufei Wang, Qiyuan Zhang, Chuhan Wu, Zhengxi Li, Wentao Zhao, Jie Zhou, Le Tian, Xiao Zhou, Chen Ma

entry.summary: WorkBorne is a synthesis framework that generates agentic tasks by modeling real-world artifact transitions, who performs a task and how artifacts anchor initial and target states, coupling realistic instructions with interactive environments. It addresses the asymmetry where instruction-oriented synthesis yields fake environments and resource-oriented synthesis yields trivial tasks.

entry.title: GesBench: When and Where Do Multimodal Language Models Perceive Social Meaning?

author.name: Zonghuan Li, Hayley Hung, Chirag Raman

entry.summary: Introduces GesBench, a benchmark evaluating cue-level, incremental social perception in multimodal LLMs using cumulative sub-utterance clips grounded in interactional Gestalt principles. It measures when models form stable interpretations of speaker intent from facial, gestural, and prosodic cues rather than final-answer recognition over complete episodes.

entry.title: SuperAI: Merging Capabilities Across Heterogeneous Foundation Models

author.name: Jingtong Dou, Chuancheng Shi, Wenhua Wu, Wei Bao, Fei Shen, Zhiyong Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes a cross-architecture fusion framework that transfers complementary capabilities from multiple source models into a host model despite incompatible representations. It extracts task-relevant low-dimensional representations using shared anchor samples and aligns them orthogonally. Aims at compositional reuse of knowledge distributed across heterogeneous foundation models.

entry.title: From Stages to States: Unified Iterative Reasoning for MLLMs

author.name: Chuang Yu, Xuefei Ma, Yuanhao Feng, Wuxiong Zeng, Bo Wang, Minghong Cai, Dongming Wu, Fei Zhou, Chen Tang, Wenwen Tong, Lewei Lu, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Proposes ReState, a framework reformulating multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning for MLLMs from a stage-driven pipeline into a state-driven dynamic process. It combines Unified Reasoning State Modeling and Closed-Loop Reasoning to fix fragmented reasoning and the training-inference reasoning-state gap left by stage-centric optimization. Targets improved complex multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: ADAPT: Audio-Depth Action Planning with Transition-Aware Rewards for Lights-Out Industrial Navigation

author.name: Wenjun Huang, Shenghao Fu, Yian Jin, Yang Ni, Yifan Li, Lichi Li, Xingjian Diao, Pengfei Zhang, Yutong Song, Hanning Chen, Jiarui Cui, Tianyu Yang, Shilong Li, Yu Kong, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: ADAPT addresses navigation in unlit industrial environments using spatial audio for target localization and depth sensing for obstacle geometry, introducing DarkNav-Bench with 24 scenes and four acoustic conditions. Its reinforcement-learning contribution, transition-aware reward shaping (TARS), provides pose-aware shaping for closed-loop audio-depth navigation.

entry.title: Interactive 4D Volumetric Liquid Forecasting under Moving-Solid Interaction

author.name: Jongwon Ryu, Sunjae Yoon, Junyeong Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes a new task: forecasting the future dense 3D liquid velocity field conditioned on how a solid object moves through it, serving as an upstream primitive for robotic liquid manipulation, digital twins, and rigid-fluid video generation. Existing flow-prediction work covers static or prescribed geometries and does not handle interactive liquid dynamics.

entry.title: EPOCH: Coverage-Aware Evolution with Experiential Preference Optimization for LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design

author.name: Oguzhan Gungordu, Ayse Tursucular, Siheng Xiong, Faramarz Fekri

entry.summary: EPOCH improves LLM-based automated heuristic design for combinatorial optimization by making instance coverage the objective of the evolutionary search and fine-tuning the generator to internalize natural-language reflection rather than leaving it in the prompt. Parent selection, operator allocation, and stagnation recovery are all coverage-aware. This addresses a real weakness where scalar fitness signals hide which problem instances a heuristic actually solves.

entry.title: Back to the Future: Reverse-Consequence Modeling for Long-Horizon Particle Dynamics

author.name: Leyan Zhang, Nantian He, Jiajun Ma, Yanpeng Zhao, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: ReStep reverses conventional forward prediction for long-horizon physical dynamics: a stochastic model first predicts the final resting state (which is often more predictable in dissipative systems), then Anchored Diffusion generates goal-conditioned intermediate trajectories. This mitigates the cumulative error drift of autoregressive rollouts. It is relevant to mechanical understanding and robotic control.

entry.title: Delegating Earth science model calibration to knowledge-guided LLM agents

author.name: Zhanliang Zhu, Ziwei Li, Liujun Zhu, Yuchen Liu, Junliang Jin, Jianyun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors build a general calibration harness where knowledge-constrained LLM agents handle end-to-end calibration of process-based Earth science models: defining parameter domains, observation mappings, and generating model-specific code that is frozen and verified before numerical search. Workflows executed across six model families with reproducibility safeguards.

entry.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents

author.name: Ashutosh Hathidara

entry.summary: The paper calibrates agents' verbalized confidence against the eventual outcome of a multi-step episode rather than per-step correctness: under GRPO, rollout groups supply success labels and a proper scoring rule trains per-step confidence. Experiments use offline RL on recorded Qwen agent trajectories.

entry.title: The Future of AI-assisted Physics: Discovering, Verifying and Organizing Results via Formalization

author.name: Sven Krippendorf, Leopoldo Sarra, Joseph Tooby-Smith

entry.summary: This position paper argues that formalization is an essential layer for verifying and trusting AI-driven discoveries in physics, reviewing AI's role in computational and theoretical physics. The authors contend AI lowers the barrier to formalization though it remains weaker at choosing definitions and designing libraries than at writing proofs.

entry.title: Co-adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining for Structured Knowledge Retrieval

author.name: Zhisheng Qi, Haoyu Han, Jiaxi Li, Bing He, Huiyuan Chen, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi, Mahantesh M. Halappanavar, Jin Lu, Yu Zhang, Tianming Liu, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CoRE, a framework that jointly learns which reasoning rule to assign to each query and how to retrieve evidence under that rule from structured knowledge bases, eliminating the need for predefined query-rule supervision. A routing agent selects a rule and a corresponding retriever traverses and ranks rule-constrained evidence.

entry.title: Lingdan-V2: Large language models for clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine

author.name: Rui Hua, Yu Wei, Ziri Jin, Zhuo Sun, Kai Chang, Jianan Xia, Zixin Shu, Xiaodong Li, Dongmei Jia, Fei Dong, Runshun Zhang, Jian Yu, Hao Xu, Haibin Yu, Jiansheng Li, Baoyan Liu, Wenjia Wang, Xuezhong Zhou

entry.summary: Develops a family of TCM language models (4B, 8B, 14B parameters) using a staged clinical alignment framework: continued pretraining on TCM and clinical records, reasoning supervision, and prescription-centered reinforcement learning. Herbal prescription generation is formulated as a structured task integrating syndrome differentiation, treatment principles, and dosing.

entry.title: Fitting Every Hint Is Not Enough: Premature Floods in Recurrent Algorithmic Reasoners

author.name: Amin Najafgholizadeh, Mohsen Afsharchi

entry.summary: The paper identifies a premature flood failure mode in recurrent algorithmic reasoners trained with per-step hints: on BFS in SALSA-CLRS, models can reproduce every training hint yet fail on deep graphs by declaring nodes reached too early. The authors trace the failure to hidden-state dynamics and input distribution tails, finding none of the flooding models actually counts steps.

entry.title: North or South? Diagnosing LLMs' Understanding of North Korean Language, Society, and Knowledge

author.name: Kiwoong Park, Seyoung Song, Donghyun Woo, Alice Oh

entry.summary: The authors introduce LENS, a human-validated benchmark of 1,765 questions evaluating LLMs on North Korean language and society across linguistic robustness, sociocultural perspective alignment, and domain-specific knowledge. Evaluating recent LLMs, they find modest performance drops on North Korean language inputs but larger gaps in sociocultural alignment, showing models largely reflect South Korean norms and discourse. The study highlights blind spots in low-resource sociolinguistic contexts.

entry.title: ELECT: Settling Identity Before Rendering for Scalable Story Visualization

author.name: Mehrajul Abadin Miraj, Md. Mahmudul Hasan, Meherun Farzana, Aniket Joarder, Mahmudul Hasan, Abir Chakraborty Partha, Md. Ahasanul Alam, Redwan Ahmed Rizvee, Md. Fahim Arefin, Md Mahmudur Rahman, Md. Tanvir Alam, Md Mosaddek Khan

entry.summary: ELECT is a training-free method for story visualization that resolves cross-frame entity identity before final rendering via language-guided scene-entity mapping and stationary anchors elected from model drafts, making per-frame render cost independent of story length. It achieves 8.3 seconds per frame under 20 GB VRAM from 10 to 1000 scenes, versus over 96 GB for joint attention at 32 scenes.

entry.title: Gen Through the Lens: Camera-Controllable Video Generation via Cross-Coordinate Conditioning Fusion

author.name: Shuai Li, Jinxu Xiang, Xinyuan Li, Hanlei Guo, Xiyang Tan, Alan Zhao, Xiaotong Zhao, Ran Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents an image-to-video generation framework with precise camera control that decomposes conditioning across camera, world, and object coordinate spaces — intrinsic parameters, spatial geometry hints, and 3D bounding boxes — and fuses them via cross-coordinate conditioning. This enables realistic, physically consistent camera operations on a reference image.

entry.title: Look Back to Move Forward: Learning to Revisit for Agentic Compositional Image Generation

author.name: Zixu Wang, Xiaoran Zhao, Yahui Liu, Feng-ao Wang, Junhao Xiao, You Shu, Bing Liu, Yiting Liu, Songlei Jian, Zhiliang Tian, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: Introduces GenRevisit, an agentic framework for compositional text-to-image generation that learns to jointly select the continuation state and the next action, allowing the agent to revisit earlier images when iterative editing has degraded the current one. This extends prior agentic image generation pipelines that are anchored to the latest image.

entry.title: Answer It or Not? Towards Prompt-Adapted Adversarial Images on Vision Language Models

author.name: Shunyuan Bai, Yuchen Ren, Le Yang, Chenhao Lin, Chao Shen, Zhengyu Zhao

entry.summary: The paper identifies that existing adversarial-image privacy protections for VLMs are prompt-agnostic, indiscriminately rejecting all questions including legitimate ones, and proposes ProAda adversarial images optimized to reject harmful prompts while permitting correct responses to benign ones. This enables more nuanced visual privacy protection.

entry.title: Learning Incompressible 3D Flows from Sparse Samples: A Set Transformer Approach to Divergence-Free Kernel Fitting

author.name: Ramzi Idoughi, Radouan Boukharfane, Peter Wonka

entry.summary: DFK-Former is a set-to-field transformer that reconstructs divergence-free 3D velocity fields from sparse, noisy, irregularly sampled observations by predicting parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation. Incompressibility is satisfied exactly by construction rather than via soft penalties, and the model is invariant to sample count and ordering.

entry.title: From Suboptimal to Optimal: One-Step Latent Flow Policies for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shenghua Lu, Zixuan Yang, Rongxu Zhao, Bohao Qu, Jifeng Hu, Hechang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes MeanFlow2Better (MF2B), which reframes offline RL as generative optimization of decision chunks from current to better performance states in a latent space, avoiding the multi-step denoising cost of diffusion/flow policies that start from uninformative Gaussian noise. This enables one-step generation and better use of suboptimal trajectories.

entry.title: HASTE: Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Tripti Shukla, Shwetha Somasundaram, Akshat Gupta, Rohit Garg, Paul Duff, Ian Anderson

entry.summary: HASTE shows that adding hierarchical and attribute-level supervision to generative recommendation models that autoregressively generate semantic IDs improves training efficiency and long-tail recommendation performance. Standard causal cross-entropy ignores the hierarchical structure of semantic IDs, and tail items suffer from sparse supervision. The approach directly exploits semantic ID structure during training.

entry.title: PrT-Flow: Probability-Tractable Flow Matching for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Congzhong Sun, Ning Tan

entry.summary: PrT-Flow enables flow-matching policies to output exact action probabilities while retaining multimodal, multi-step generation, via a Jacobian-Tractable Transformer whose sampling steps are invertible with efficiently computable Jacobian determinants. Conditional Euler-step Training supervises per-step displacements, with a proof that it shares minimizers with fitting the Euler solution under stated assumptions.

entry.title: MERIT: Multimodal Evidence Reasoning over Image Tables

author.name: Haoyang Jiang, Zhuotong Fan, Mingyang Yi, Ju Fan, Lanqing Hu, Xiao Zan

entry.summary: Proposes MERIT, a three-stage framework for reasoning over table images rather than lossy serialized text, identifying visual evidence acquisition as the bottleneck and introducing table-specific components. Serialized tables can serve as optional auxiliary inputs when available.

entry.title: When Do Learned Blocks Preserve Causal Meaning? Block Identifiability and Constructive Causal Abstractions

author.name: Karim Zaghw, Wieland Brendel, Patrik Reizinger

entry.summary: This theory paper connects block-identifiability of learned representations to constructive causal abstraction, asking when multidimensional latent blocks retain causal meaning under the transformations identifiability leaves unresolved. It characterizes block-diagonal invertible transformations plus compatible permutations as the maximal class preserving all constructive causal abstractions. This has implications for interpretable representations and interventional reasoning.

entry.title: Let the Mind Conceive, Let the Hand Achieve: Following Multimodal Instructions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Youpeng Wen, Gang Wang, Tianyu Huang, Weiwei Zhang, Zhijian Huang, Wei Chen, Xieyuanli Chen, Yunhui Liu

entry.summary: Orchestra is an agent harness for long-horizon robotic manipulation that separates planning and execution management from action generation, decomposing multimodal instructions into ordered subtasks with tracked progress, spatial grounding, and a shared context consumed by an action policy and a progress evaluator.

entry.title: Tiny Recursive Message Passing

author.name: Tommaso Salvatori, Matteo Forasassi, Alexis Toumi, Giovanni de Felice

entry.summary: The paper applies recursive transformer training techniques (deep supervision, truncated recursions, discrete deduction lattices) to message passing neural networks, showing the ingredients are complementary and parameter-efficient. It achieves about 99% test accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme with a 16k-parameter model trained in roughly 10 minutes. Demonstrates tiny models can perform demanding algorithmic reasoning.

entry.title: RadarGSOcc: Doppler-Aware 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction Using 4D Radar Tensor with Geometric-Semantic Feature Extraction

author.name: Christofel Rio Goenawan, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: RadarGSOcc is an efficient framework for 3D semantic occupancy prediction that directly processes 4D radar tensors, separately extracting geometric and semantic features including Doppler information via a deformable attention-based refinement module. The work also introduces the K-Radar 3DSemOcc benchmark, the first large-scale benchmark for 4D-radar-based semantic occupancy prediction, targeting robustness in adverse weather where cameras and LiDAR degrade.

entry.title: How Many Ranks Does a Token Need? A Noise-Floor Squelch for Rank-One LoRA Experts

author.name: Mei Okonkwo, Owen Castellanos, Ingrid Solberg, Yusuf Demirel

entry.summary: SQUELCH is a router-free mixture of rank-one LoRA experts that soft-thresholds each token's responses against its own robust noise level, allowing the active rank to vary per token. The paper frames token-level expert count as a detection problem, showing trained LoRA responses sit on a Gaussian noise floor matching untrained adapters.

entry.title: Genesis Steering: Better Activation Steering Through Training Data

author.name: Tora Bodin, Eric Aubinais, Ilaria Torre, Chih-Hong Cheng

entry.summary: Genesis steering derives steering vectors from contrastive examples in a model's own fine-tuning data, with a membership-inference-based proxy when those data are unavailable, plus theoretical results on optimal displacement to the decision boundary and reduced proxy bias. It is evaluated on Tulu-3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with public safety training data.

entry.title: Exact Scaling Laws for a Random-Features Bigram Model

author.name: Julian Enoch, Elvis Dohmatob

entry.summary: Derives exact scaling laws for a capacity-limited bigram model with Zipf-distributed token statistics, using fixed random embeddings as an explicit representational bottleneck. The analysis isolates scaling due to representational constraints as a function of model width, vocabulary size, and Zipf exponent, complementing optimization-dynamics-based accounts.

entry.title: Train to Stitch: Topology-Preserving Regularization for Interoperable Representations

author.name: Akshay Malhotra, Nicolas Zilberstein, Shahab Hamidi-Rad

entry.summary: The authors introduce topological regularization that aligns the latent spaces of independently trained autoencoders, allowing encoders and decoders with different architectures to interoperate without coordination during training. With a conditional theoretical justification, this could fundamentally change how compressed-data models are built and updated independently. This addresses model interoperability, an increasingly important concern in a foundation-model ecosystem.

entry.title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Selective Margin Preservation for Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yuxuan Wang, Guangxiang Zhao, Xinyu Tan, Yahui Han, Xinxiang Yin, Zhonghai Wu, Xiangzheng Zhang, Lin Sun, Tong Yang

entry.summary: SRP-SFT introduces a soft margin-preserving auxiliary loss for supervised fine-tuning that applies a hinge to reference-scaled lower bounds on non-target token rank relations at teacher-forced prefixes, rather than matching the full reference distribution. The authors derive the KL cost of margin violations, characterize the feasible region, and give finite-step conditions. This offers a more surgical alternative to distribution-matching regularization in SFT.

entry.title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning

author.name: Mohamed Bouadi, Nassim Bouarour, Aditya Tanna, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: OrionMoE-Small is a compact tabular foundation model combining a dual-axis Transformer with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation, activating experts along the feature axis based on both feature representations and dataset context. This enables in-context learning on tabular data without task-specific parameter updates while allocating compute adaptively. It extends the tabular foundation model line (e.g., TabPFN) toward sparse architectures.

entry.title: Delay Complexity Dimension: Learning with Delayed and Censored Labels

author.name: Madhava Gaikwad

entry.summary: Studies PAC learning of binary classifiers when labels arrive after random delays and are censored beyond an observation window, proposing the Delay Complexity Dimension (DCD) — a distribution-dependent sample complexity measure combining VC dimension with the label-information rate of the observation channel. Proves an Omega(DCD/eps^2) lower bound matching an oracle pseudo-label ERM learner up to constants and logs on the bound's instance family. Connects learning theory with censored-data statistics.

entry.title: Smart Alone, Blind Together: Why Accuracy Fails to CertifyTheory of Mind in Multi-Agent Teams

author.name: Will Beaumaster, Paul Schrater

entry.summary: This paper argues that inference accuracy is the wrong certificate for multi-agent coordinators acting on beliefs about teammates, because the required accuracy depends on deployment costs and errors are positively or negatively correlated in ways that make a single threshold fail predictably. Experiments in task assignment, Level-Based Foraging, and Hanabi with injected errors support these predictions. It offers a useful conceptual corrective for evaluating multi-agent and theory-of-mind systems.

entry.title: Who's Behind the Text? Robust Model Authorship Attribution

author.name: Minseok Ko, Hyunseok Lee, Woomin Song, Beomjun Kim, Jinwoo Shin, Kunwoong Kim

entry.summary: This paper tackles Model Authorship Attribution, identifying which LLM generated a given text, with emphasis on robustness to unseen domains, writing settings, and future model versions unavailable at training time. Existing MAA methods degrade substantially under distribution shift, motivating the proposed approach. Reliable attribution supports detection of academic misconduct, unauthorized distillation, and misuse, contributing to AI safety.

entry.title: AtomSearch: Evidence-Grounded Tree Search for Agent Skill Optimization

author.name: Jia Tong, Senyou Deng, Min Peng, Jianfeng Pan

entry.summary: AtomSearch optimizes editable agent skills via atomic rule edits linked to successful and failed executions, using a Skill-State Tree Search that evaluates and retains edit compositions as revisitable states, plus outcome memory with repair and regression statistics. It makes skill revisions more inspectable than bulk edits while avoiding purely local myopic judgments.

entry.title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry

author.name: Ren Zhuang, Ben Wang, Shuifa Sun

entry.summary: LSPO defines a lifted state space where textual answers acquire learned continuous coordinates and an energy function orders them, treating cost-adjusted local transitions from flawed to better reasoning states as the primary learning unit. A shaped reward drives energy descent and an internalization loss distills low-energy answers into the generator, reaching 71.8% aggregate accuracy with Qwen3.5-27B, an existing open model, on math, science, code, and logic benchmarks.

entry.title: One Block Ahead: Promoting Sampler State in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yangyi Shen, Pin-Jui Ku, Nicolai Oswald, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Yonggan Fu, Stefano Ermon, Jure Leskovec, Boris Ginsburg, Ante Juki\'c

entry.summary: One Block Ahead (OBA) is a training-free decoding algorithm for block-diffusion language models that denoises the next block concurrently with the current one by promoting the next block's tokens together with the sampler state, including self-conditioning signals and denoising time. The paper derives conditions under which concurrent decoding is advantageous for uniform-state diffusion LMs.

entry.title: OpenTWBench (Open Taiwan Benchmark): Taiwan-Domain Knowledge Evaluation for Large Language Models, and How the Measurement Apparatus Shapes the Score

author.name: Liang-Hsun Huang, Min-Yi Chen, Chao-Chun Chuang, Yu-Wei Liu, Che-Yu Wu, Po-Feng Lee

entry.summary: Releases OpenTWBench, an evaluation suite for Taiwan-domain knowledge with tw-exam-bench (over 253,000 verified questions from fifteen years of national examinations across 148 subjects) and tw-formosa-bench (1,696 difficulty-curated questions on contemporary Taiwan), plus analysis of how measurement apparatus choices shape scores.

entry.title: SoK: Grading Open-Text Legal Answers, from Law School Exams to Trustworthy Rubric Judges

author.name: Sebastian Nagl

entry.summary: This systematization-of-knowledge paper derives eight desiderata for evaluating open-text legal answers from educational measurement and exam law, including validity, reliability, credit for defensible alternatives, and robustness to gaming. It then compares eight evaluation paradigms, from human grading to LLM judges with instance-specific rubrics, against these criteria.

entry.title: Scaling Multilingual Safety and Reasoning Evaluation through Reasoning-Guided Translation

author.name: Zahraa Al Sahili, Ioannis Patras, Matthew Purver

entry.summary: This work presents a reasoning-guided translation framework for scaling safety and reasoning benchmarks to many languages while preserving task-specific meaning, separating translation strategy selection from large-scale generation. It targets hard cases like harmful requests, math reasoning, and conversation where naive translation distorts intent.

entry.title: Manac\'a-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge

author.name: Bruno Leonardo Santos Menezes, Carlos Leonardo Souza Cardoso, Fabio Andr\'e Machado Porto

entry.summary: This paper describes the second-generation safety alignment of Manaca-1B, a 1.72B-parameter model trained from scratch for Brazilian Portuguese, documenting three failed DPO attempts (including reward margins that rose while behavior did not change) and a safety-SFT approach that succeeded. It also identifies a silent failure mode of LLM judges and validates findings with statistical rigor.

entry.title: LintEval: Benchmarking LLMs on Linter-Guided File Refactoring

author.name: Tongwei Deng, Jinyu Zhu, Yue Cao, Chenxu Wang, Yanzhen Zou, Bing Xie

entry.summary: LintEval is a multilingual benchmark (C++, Python, Java) with 13,061 functionally correct programs and over 171,000 lint alerts for evaluating linter-guided file refactoring. It jointly scores functionality preservation, alert reduction, new-alert avoidance, and edit minimality, a dimension absent from existing code benchmarks.

entry.title: RDCompGS: Rate-Distortion Optimization for Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting with Image Codecs

author.name: Huiping Ren, Shuai Wan, Luqian Bai, Zhang Chen, Fuzheng Yang

entry.summary: RDCompGS adds overall rate-distortion optimization to 3D Gaussian Splatting compression by mapping Gaussian attributes to 2D representations for image codecs, incorporating a differentiable estimate of coding rate into optimization. This accounts for coding cost during Gaussian optimization, which prior methods ignored.

entry.title: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching

author.name: Minghao Liu, Tutian Tang

entry.summary: OmniPoser recovers full-body SMPL human motion from flexible combinations of heterogeneous inputs such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, and head-mounted 6-DoF poses within a single model, using a cross-modal masking mechanism and Masked Conditioning Encoder. Built on flow matching rather than diffusion, it aims for real-time-capable inference under any sensor subset.

entry.title: Beyond Kinematic Tracking: Preserving Expressive Characteristics in Humanoid Whole-Body Control

author.name: Lingfan Bao, Hanshang Zhu, Yan Pan, Jincheng Wang, Jingyang Yu, Tianhu Peng, Yiyang Jia, Dimitrios Kanoulas, Chengxu Zhou

entry.summary: This work shows that minimizing positional tracking error in humanoid whole-body control does not preserve the expressive characteristics of motions such as dance, and proposes a residual learning framework with compensation objectives for amplitude, energy, body expansion, lean, and pelvis height. The result is humanoid motion that retains stylistic qualities, not just joint trajectories. It opens an interesting direction in expressive robot motion.

entry.title: Accelerating VLA Inference with Perturbation Informed Execution

author.name: Jehun Lee, Hajun Lee, Jimin Ryu, Youhan Lee, Beomseok Kang, Jonghyun Choi, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: PICES is a training-free method that jointly selects action chunk sizes and execution horizons for action-chunking VLA models, amortizing expensive policy inference over more actions while preserving opportunities for precise corrections. It uses perturbation-informed signals to adaptively decide how many predicted actions to execute before re-invoking the policy.

entry.title: DD-GBP: Anytime Multi-Arm Planning and Continuous Execution via Distributed Dynamic Gaussian Belief Propagation

author.name: Zhao Jin, Fengyi Dai, Yuetong Yin, Yunan Wang, Wenjie Chen, Chuxiong Hu

entry.summary: DD-GBP plans joint-space trajectories for multiple robot arms through parallel local inference using distributed dynamic Gaussian belief propagation. It unifies adaptive planning horizons, interpolation, and continuous execution via GP parameterization, with asynchronous message passing, event-triggered updates, and theoretical accuracy and stopping guarantees.

entry.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos

author.name: Wei Lin

entry.summary: Reels-RSI treats explainer videos as programs (script, storyboard, per-frame animation code) rendered deterministically rather than pixel outputs, enabling readable, diffable, auditable artifacts. It is an open-source reel director with program-level self-improvement: revisions are logged, retrospective lessons are compiled into enforceable static-check rules.

entry.title: PsyMemBehav: Psychology-Informed and Memory-Grounded Two-Level Identity-to-Action Reasoning for Social-Media Behavior Simulation

author.name: Wenji Zhang, Xilong Cheng, Yunxiao Qin, Mai Tu, Tongye Zhu, Yuhao Zhou, JingBo Ji, Yuting Tan, Duoyin Li, Hongjiang Xiao, Yuan Zhang

entry.summary: PsyMemBehav simulates real social-media users by mapping psychology-informed profiles and retrieved memories to platform behaviors via two-level identity-to-action reasoning. It contributes a large benchmark built from 5.57M observed behaviors of 5,862 real users across Reddit, Bluesky, and Twitter, modeling target selection plus comment/like/repost and response generation.

entry.title: MHWA: Multi-timescale Hierarchical World-Action Model

author.name: Pengcheng Pan, Guoqing Ma, Yuhan Zhang, Yang Chen, Yichen Liu, Ziheng Li, Shan Yu

entry.summary: MHWA is a hierarchical world model for sample-efficient decision making that uses a strided high-level context channel to reduce global context update frequency, curbing drift in autoregressive open-loop rollouts. The design aims to obtain the benefits of temporal abstraction without the structural complexity that has limited prior hierarchical world models.

entry.title: How Should a Camera-First AI Agent Work?

author.name: Xiaofan Wu, Xi Zeng, Miaoxia Chen, Peishan Chen, Shuyan Li, Chen Wang, Xiaohan Wang, Wanling Xu, Jiyun Yao, Hanyong Zhong, Jiahao Zhu

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that the key obstacle for camera-first AI agents is not recognition but timing, formalizing Ephemeral-Target Interaction and a Perceptual Deadline Contract that separates hard memory deadlines from soft reasoning deadlines. It proposes architectural principles for agents that must act on fleeting visual evidence before it disappears.

entry.title: Probable but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of Decision Models as Synthetic Survey Respondents

author.name: Mantas Lukauskas, Viktorija \v{S}arkauskait\.e

entry.summary: This audit tests whether decision models (LLMs returning rating-scale probabilities) and generative LLMs can stand in for human survey respondents, evaluating fourteen decision models and 47 generative LLMs against a real Lithuanian organisational-psychology survey. The best generative model, MiniMax M3, reaches a Psychometric Similarity Score of 0.813, on par with a Gaussian copula baseline fit only to other respondents.

entry.title: VC-OPD: Visual Counterfactual On-Policy Distillation for Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Jiahe Feng

entry.summary: VC-OPD improves on-policy distillation for vision-language reasoning by identifying tokens whose correctness depends on image-specific evidence via visual counterfactuals, prioritizing them for dense token-level supervision. After a teacher-supervised warm start, this grounding-aware weighting improves over standard OPD that treats all teacher-preferred tokens equally.

entry.title: Single-step Retrosynthesis via Reinforcement Learning from Forward Feedback

author.name: Zixun Lan, Zhenfu Liu, Yi Li, Xinheng Wang, Mingmin Chi, Qibiao Wang, Jie Zhu, Xiaohui Tian, Fei Ma

entry.summary: Proposes RetroRLFF, which optimizes single-step retrosynthesis with reinforcement learning using both reference agreement and forward consistency: a frozen forward reaction model verifies that generated reactant sets actually produce the target product. This addresses the one-to-many nature of retrosynthesis that exact-match training and evaluation penalize.

entry.title: Words to World: Benchmarking LLMs in Interactive Physical Environments

author.name: Xinnan Dai, Kaiqi Yang, Yaxin Li, Cheng Luo, Wanli Li, Mingqing Xiao, Xinyang Jiang, Daoan Zhang, Kaitao Song, Fengze Liu, Zefan Cai, Caihua Shan

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark evaluating LLMs in closed-loop physical interaction, where models control a harness connected to real robotic arms, cameras, and sensors, issuing instructions, interpreting physical feedback, and adapting subsequent actions. It addresses the gap between static-text or simulated evaluation and real-world action.

entry.title: OneShot: Label-Efficient Detector Weighting for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: ONESHOT uses a single operator-confirmed anomaly to weight a pool of time series anomaly detectors rather than selecting one or averaging blindly. Scoring detectors on the confirmed anomaly and forming a soft mixture nearly matches the best detector for the series, exploiting the reality that deployed monitors do receive some labels.

entry.title: ReTAC: Residual Test-Time Agentic Computation for Video Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Yike Wu, Keyan Chen, Qixiong Wang, Xi Xiang, Maofei Que, Xiaolong Jiang, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: ReTAC is a training-free multiagent framework for video spatial reasoning that allocates extra computation only to requirements the base model has not resolved, and after localized failure recomputes only affected states. It plans ordered steps to gather missing spatial evidence and combines observations with base-model predictions.

entry.title: Making Language the Low-Rate Code of Vision: Successive Refinement from Words to Pixels

author.name: Ruilin Gong, Hao Gong

entry.summary: The paper proves that under pixel-reconstruction objectives, captions can be independent of the first half of a rate-optimal visual code, so language is not inherently the low-rate code of an image. It constructs captioning and text-to-image generation as successive refinement with a distortion measure shifting from caption log-loss to pixel distortion.

entry.title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search

author.name: Yingtao Ren, Aolin Li, Cheng Cheng, Huiyun Hu, Huasheng Liang, Baoxing Xie, Jun Yuan, Haijun Wu, Chenxing Wang

entry.summary: Presents WeFair, a fidelity-aware alignment approach for compact query rewriters in short-video search that decides when personalization is warranted while preserving the user immediate information need. It leverages users actual reformulations and behavioral traces rather than synthetic reasoning, guarding against intent drift toward merely more engaging candidates.

entry.title: Reasoning for Propaganda Detection via Label-Guided CoT Optimisation

author.name: Zeba Afroz, Harsh Vardhan, Md. Shad Akhtar

entry.summary: ReCoT is a reasoning-conditioned framework for propaganda detection that captures definitional cues of persuasive techniques through population-level refinement and performance-guided resampling, without extra explanation annotations. It approaches the SFT upper bound on two datasets while remaining interpretable.

entry.title: What Makes a Latent Space Shared? Direct and Recoverable Compatibility in Motion VAEs

author.name: Iago Brito, Walcy Rios, Lucas Fernandes, Kaiki de Oliveira, Arlindo Galv\~ao Filho

entry.summary: This work disentangles what it means for latent spaces from different schemas to be shared, separating direct compatibility from recoverable correspondence and decoder reuse. Experiments on a controlled multi-schema motion VAE with HumanML3D show raw interchangeability is poor (about 6-18% Recall@1) even when correspondence is nearly perfectly recoverable after linear calibration, and that a small number of paired clips dramatically improves direct retrieval. The paper clarifies a commonly conflated assumption in representation learning.

entry.title: RadixFlow: Filling Execution Bubbles in Prefix-Cached Hybrid LLM Serving

author.name: Huihao Jing, Wenbin Hu, Shaojin Chen, Haochen Shi, Haoyu Huang, Sirui Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Zhongwei Xie, Haoran Li

entry.summary: RadixFlow is a serving-system scheduler improvement for prefix-cached hybrid (attention plus recurrence) LLMs, decoupling prefix matching from recurrent-state readiness so blocked consumers no longer cause head-of-line blocking and idle batch slots. Its state-ready traversal fills execution bubbles with independent work. This addresses a concrete throughput loss unique to hybrid architectures under prefix reuse.

entry.title: Rethinking Quality in Large Language Model Routing: Security-Conditioned Model-and-Budget Selection

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Zhenxiang Huang, Yuyang Zhang, Yuchen Yang

entry.summary: SCRouter is an LLM router that distinguishes ordinary queries, where utility matters, from security-sensitive queries, where refusal and resistance to malicious instructions matter, and allocates model and token budget accordingly. It estimates within-budget completion probability per model-budget pair and conditions quality prediction on detected security needs.

entry.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Xiaoguang Guo, Yaohao Long, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: BLADE is a training-free framework for failure attribution in LLM multi-agent systems that audits how information was used, not just where it flowed, distinguishing agents that misused correct information from those that propagated errors. It uses structured probabilistic judgments (via a tool called Jev) with dependency probabilities to localize the responsible agent and decisive error step. This addresses a growing operational need as multi-agent LLM deployments expand.

entry.title: Physics-Informed State Space Models for Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

author.name: Phil Aupke, Muhammad Hassan, Khalid Ali, Seema, Andreas Kassler, Andreas Theocharis

entry.summary: The authors propose a physics-informed state space framework combining a differentiable PV conversion model with a PowerMamba state space backbone for day-ahead solar power forecasting. A physics-residual decomposition uses a structured physics baseline (solar geometry, irradiance, inverter limits) while the SSM learns corrections from numerical weather prediction inputs.

entry.title: SAGE: Efficient Protected Vision-Language Inference on Smart Glasses

author.name: Zhimin Li, Pan Wang, Jingxian Chen, Yuantao Tang, Qian Lou, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: SAGE is a hardware-aware framework for efficient privacy-protecting vision-language inference on smart glasses, keeping raw images on-device, executing shape-specialized INT8 graphs, and compressing protected representations into compact 256-dimensional INT8 packets before transmission. It addresses the cost of on-device encoding and wide protected tokens in split inference.

entry.title: Deep learning from a control vantage point

author.name: \'Alvaro Rodr\'iguez Abella, Jo\~ao Pedro Silvestre, Bahman Gharesifard, Paulo Tabuada

entry.summary: This survey reviews deep learning developments through the lens of control theory, covering feedforward and residual networks, transformers, LLMs, and selective state space models. It explains how viewing residual networks as discretizations of continuous-time control systems enables control-theoretic analysis, illustrated with two technical results on approximation and representation properties.

entry.title: Scale, Drivers, and Limits of Representational Alignment Across Large Language Models

author.name: Jialin Wu, Meenakshi Khosla

entry.summary: Introduces Neighborhood-Weighted RSA (NW-RSA), a refinement of representational similarity analysis that weights stimulus pairs by proximity, resolving where across geometric scales different LLMs agree and which linguistic properties support that agreement.

entry.title: Exploring Jailbreak Vulnerability Across Depth-Based Dynamic Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Lass Najmuldeen, Seyedhamidreza Mousavi

entry.summary: This paper investigates how depth-based dynamic inference, which generates outputs from intermediate LLM layers for efficiency, affects robustness against jailbreak attacks. The authors provide a comprehensive study of the intersection of inference-efficiency techniques and safety alignment, an interaction that had not previously been explored. The work suggests efficiency modifications may carry hidden safety costs.

entry.title: HGA-Quant: Heterogeneity-Aware Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models

author.name: Xinmeng Liu, Xianglong Yan, Kaicheng Yang, Weisheng Dong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: HGA-Quant is a training-free post-training quantization framework for autoregressive visual generation models, combining Tail-Aware Bounded-init Grid Refinement for weight quantizers with Coarse-to-Fine Activation Precision Scheduling to reduce low-bit quality degradation. The goal is enabling deployment of computationally heavy image-generation models on edge devices. The method addresses the heterogeneity of weights and activations across ARVG generation steps.

entry.title: When Does Compensating Inherited Quantization Error Help? Mean-Square Guarantees for Layer-Wise Quantization and Their Limits

author.name: Tianhao Guo

entry.summary: The paper derives mean-square output-error guarantees for layer-wise post-training quantization with compensation of inherited error, showing for linear networks that under zero conditional-mean rounding (e.g., subtractive dither) and invertible calibration Gram matrices, compensation with strengths in [0,1] guarantees no-worse error — and characterizes when it does not help.

entry.title: Autoregressive Decoding as a Martingale: Characterizing the Stochastic Dynamics of LLM Generation

author.name: Xiahui Zhu, Zhenyi Qi, Wanwei Liu, Haoang Chi, Yang Tan, Xinyu Sun, Ji Wang

entry.summary: Provides a rigorous probabilistic characterization of LLM autoregressive decoding, proving that the cumulative per-step prediction error process is a martingale with respect to the decoding filtration, implying zero conditional first-order moment. This offers theoretical tools for analyzing generation dynamics.

entry.title: A Survey of Flow Matching in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nabuat Zaman Nahim, Fairoz Nower Khan, Peizhong Ju

entry.summary: Surveys the rapidly growing use of flow matching as a generative modeling framework in reinforcement learning, providing a taxonomy covering offline continuous control, online fine-tuning, and foundation model alignment. It highlights flow matching's advantages over diffusion policies, including ODE-based sampling with lower inference latency and easier RL objective integration.

entry.title: VisExMEM: Visual Evidence-Based Explainable Multimodal Evaluation Metric

author.name: Subhadeep Roy, Christoph Leiter, Steffen Eger

entry.summary: VisExMEM is a reference-free image-text evaluation metric that decomposes captions into atomic claims, localizes and verifies visual evidence for each claim, and aggregates claim-level support into a global score with explanations grounded in the same evidence. The authors train Qwen3.5-based 4B and 9B models and report top descriptive composite results among open-source evaluators across eight benchmarks.

entry.title: Before Attention Sinks Form: Hidden-State Geometry Reveals and Modulates Their Formation

author.name: Fan Yang, Yue Song

entry.summary: This interpretability study shows that measurable hidden-state geometric changes precede attention sink formation, detectable via spectral summaries a few layers before sinks appear in the same model and layer. The authors also modulate this geometry to influence subsequent sink formation.

entry.title: SPLICE: Sparse Physics Library Identification and Compositional Expansion

author.name: Lucas Thil, Jesse Read, Guillaume Doquet, Rim Kaddah

entry.summary: Introduces SPLICE, a framework for neural operator libraries that discovers individual physical-mechanism operators from unlabeled trajectories where multiple mechanisms act simultaneously, using convex optimization to attribute contributions and a calibrated test to assign mechanisms — removing the need to pre-specify and label the library, with detection of out-of-library failure cases.

entry.title: Towards Green AI: Evaluating Energy Efficiency for Quantized LLM Inference

author.name: Petar Basta

entry.summary: This work presents the first unified evaluation of weight-only quantization strategies for LLM inference in terms of energy usage and carbon intensity, across varying sequence lengths and GPUs. It benchmarks 10 post-training quantization methods on five open models across four datasets and four NVIDIA GPUs, identifying novel trends in the energy-accuracy-runtime tradeoff.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for AI System Optimization with Selectively Verified Feedback

author.name: Shuang Wu

entry.summary: The paper studies Gaussian process bandit optimization of AI systems (prompts, retrieval, agent workflows) when cheap model-based evaluations may disagree with trusted outcomes, developing selective verification with a fixed audit design under a hard audit budget. It establishes finite-time regret bounds accounting for audit costs and a safe adaptive variant.

entry.title: Cost-Efficient Privacy Enforcement for Email-Generating LLM Agents under Strategic Information Requests

author.name: Qikun Cai, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: Proposes local contract-conditioned rewriting as a cost-efficient privacy enforcement layer for LLM email agents, intercepting outgoing drafts locally instead of repeatedly invoking remote action and checker LLMs under checker-repair defenses. It targets strategic requests for exact values or raw records that induce leakage-heavy drafts.

entry.title: A CaLLM Judge is a Better Judge: Mitigating Bias in LLM-as-a-judge

author.name: Cesare Barbera, Luca Stradiotti, Lorenzo Cascioli, Lorenzo Perini, Niek Tax, Daniel Haimovich, Jesse Davis, Andrea Passerini, Andrea Pugnana

entry.summary: The paper tackles systematic biases (position, verbosity, family bias) in LLM-as-a-judge evaluation by framing each bias as miscalibration on an identifiable group and applying multicalibration. This provides a principled framework for making LLM judges more faithful proxies for human preference. The work is relevant to the widespread use of LLM judges in model evaluation.

entry.title: TextualRL: Textual Reinforcement Learning for Context Management

author.name: Tianyu Huai, Jie Zhou, Bo Mao, Qin Chen, Liang He, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: TextualRL is a gradient-free RL framework in which LLM agents adapt by revising the textual context guiding their behavior rather than changing parameters. Its Groupwise Policy Critique treats a group of rollouts per task as the unit of critique, contrasting successful and failed rollouts and drawing on cross-task evidence when outcomes are uniform. The author group includes Xipeng Qiu (Fudan), indicating credible provenance.

entry.title: Lightweight but Linguistically Fair? Quantisation Robustness across Bavarian, German, and English

author.name: Jophin John, Michael Hoffmann, Piroska Lendvai, Florent Dufour

entry.summary: This study evaluates how post-training quantization affects performance across Bavarian, Standard German, and English using an aligned three-language benchmark and 14 open-weight 7B-10B models. It finds 8-bit GPTQ stays close to BF16 while 4-bit methods (GPTQ and AWQ) degrade accuracy by about 1.4-1.5 points and destabilize regional-language behavior.

entry.title: MemoryVLN: From Ego-Aware Memory Representation to Cross-Context Memory Reuse in Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Xueyao Wei, Yifei Wang, Delun Li, Shaoan Wang, Junzhi Yu, Wenjie Song, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: MemoryVLN tackles long-horizon vision-language navigation by building a unified memory system: forgetting-curve-inspired temporal sampling compresses navigation histories while cross-context memory reuse lets agents reliably exploit past spatial experience. This addresses context-length limits and unstable spatial alignment that degrade LVLM-based navigation agents over long trajectories. It is relevant to embodied agents operating in extended real-world environments.

entry.title: The Geometry of Language Model Logits: Generic Structure and Learned Departures

author.name: Swathi Shree Narashiman, Aravind Ramana Venkatramanan, Nambi Seshadri

entry.summary: The paper empirically shows that vocabulary-ordered logits of autoregressive LMs follow a consistent log-linear relation (z(r) approximately mu - alpha log r) across architectures and scales, emerging during pretraining. It provides the first systematic analysis of this logit geometry and separates generic order-statistic structure from learned departures. This informs theoretical understanding of decoding and output distributions.

entry.title: Nudge the Judge: Uncovering Program Decision Hijacking in Real-World Jev Applications
