author.name: Yang Luo, Tiantian Ji, Zifeng Kang, Yucheng Wang, Yong Liu, Zhiyi Yin, Xinran Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Jev Program Decision Hijacking (JPDH), where attacker-controlled contexts redirect program decisions through schema-valid LLM-judge outputs, and presents JevProbe, an automated framework tracing adversarial influence from reachable context surfaces to program consequences. It moves beyond model-level attack evaluations to real-world reachability analysis. This is a meaningful contribution to LLM-integrated application security.

entry.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus

author.name: Neil Walton

entry.summary: This theory paper develops a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for associated stochastic differential equations into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, SGD convergence analysis reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality, recovering classical rates and offering a template for analyzing new optimizers.

entry.title: What Information Buys in Active Inference

author.name: Melih Kandemir, Mustafa Mert \c{C}elikok

entry.summary: The paper places Active Inference and Bayes-UCBVI on equal footing within the same state abstraction of a tabular MDP to compare information-driven exploration against confidence-set-based RL exploration. It finds that AIF's information gain decays too fast to serve as a confidence width, clarifying when nature-like exploration is or is not advantageous.

entry.title: Diagnosing Low-Confidence Patient Profiles via Localized Harmful Covariate Shift Detection

author.name: Olivier Lefebvre (Department of Computer Science, Universit\'e de Sherbrooke, Sherbrooke, Canada), Hakima Laribi (Department of Computer Science, Universit\'e de Sherbrooke, Sherbrooke, Canada), Dan Poenaru (Department of Pediatric Surgery, Montreal Children's Hospital, Montreal, Canada, Centre for Outcomes Research and Evaluation), Martin Valli\`eres (Medical Physics Unit, Department of Oncology, McGill University, Montreal, Canada)

entry.summary: Proposes a unified post-hoc diagnostic pipeline combining MED3pa, which discovers interpretable low-confidence patient profiles, with Detectron-based detection of harmful covariate shifts localized to specific patient subgroups. This addresses the gap where clinical model reliability is assessed only at the population level, potentially masking subgroup harm.

entry.title: Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition: Separating Selection from Redistribution in Training-Data Filtering

author.name: Hyojung Han, Jongmin Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: The paper introduces CGSD, a four-arm budget-matched experimental design that separates the effect of a data-quality gate into within-support selection and between-support redistribution of training mass. It also characterizes finite-pool realizability conditions and support-extinction edge cases where standard gate-versus-random comparisons are undefined. This gives data-filtering research a cleaner causal methodology.

entry.title: Synthetic reaction data from transformation rules for graph-to-sequence pretraining in biodegradation pathway prediction

author.name: Irsyaad Rijwan, Liam Brydon, Aidan Jared, J\"org Simon Wicker

entry.summary: The enviGraph framework generates synthetic biodegradation reaction data by applying environmental transformation rules to chemical databases, producing 776,851 parent-product pairs for pretraining a graph-to-sequence pathway predictor. The pretrained model is fine-tuned on observed environmental reactions for product and pathway prediction. This addresses the scarcity of observed biodegradation reaction data for environmental chemistry ML.

entry.title: ProtModernBERT: Compute-Efficient Protein Language Modeling

author.name: Alberto Mart\'inez, Natalia Flechas Manrique, Lloren\c{c} Espinosa-Portal\'es, Luc Andrea

entry.summary: ProtModernBERT applies modern architectural refinements to encoder-only protein language models, showing improved performance-compute trade-offs in low-compute regimes relevant to resource-constrained labs. It is compared against ProtBert, Amplify, and ESM2 on supervised structural tasks including secondary structure and disorder prediction. The work highlights that architectural progress in protein LMs has lagged behind general NLP.

entry.title: Neural Wasserstein Splines: Representation-Invariant Second-Order Priors for Trajectory Inference

author.name: Amartya Banerjee, Harlin Lee, Caroline Moosm\"uller

entry.summary: Neural Wasserstein Splines (NWSP) learn continuous population curves from unpaired snapshot observations of population dynamics using a Wasserstein smoothness prior that is invariant to particle representation. A neural network maps latent variables to cubic spline control points in time, avoiding numerical integration, with the generator velocity projected onto gradient-constrained directions. This provides a principled tool for interpolating population dynamics, e.g., in biological single-cell data.

entry.title: A Bregman Proximal Viewpoint on Neural Operators

author.name: Abdel-Rahim Mezidi, Jordan Patracone, Saverio Salzo, Amaury Habrard, Massimiliano Pontil, Remi Emonet, Marc Sebban

entry.summary: The paper reframes neural operator layers as minimizers of Bregman-regularized optimization problems over Banach function spaces, interpreting activation operators as Bregman proximity operators between dual and primal spaces. This unifying view recovers classical neural operators and yields a new Bregman neural operator variant with equal expressivity that trains deeper Fourier neural operator models more accurately.

entry.title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning

author.name: Yanyi Li, Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Qinshi Wang, Chenheng Zhang, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: The paper resolves the dimension dependence of dynamic regret for exp-concave losses in online learning, establishing a sharp d^(1/3) factor that improves the d^(2/3) factor of prior switching/interval reductions. The construction is a proper full-information learner on compact convex sets that adapts to unknown path length with optimal T^(1/3)P_T^(2/3) regret.

entry.title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning

author.name: Fares B. Mehouachi, Saif Eddin Jabari

entry.summary: This paper shows theoretically and empirically that feeding derivative features into neural operators improves approximation bounds from O(W^(-(s-m)/d)) to O(W^(-s/d)), because derivatives appear explicitly in the solution operator via Picard iteration. The authors further make the derivative order learnable, finding fractional orders beneficial. This reduces the implicit differentiation burden on neural PDE surrogates.

entry.title: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization

author.name: Angelos Assos, Anand Brahmbhatt, Elad Hazan

entry.summary: The authors resolve a question, extending Freund's work, about competing with comparators that switch k times among m experts in online convex optimization with continuous action spaces. They show the computational inefficiency of discretization-based approaches is real and provide results sharpening the known regret landscape for efficient algorithms. This is a rigorous theoretical advance in online learning.

entry.title: Following the Flow the Law Requires: Training Voice Agents to Transfer to Unseen Regulated Procedures in Debt Collection

author.name: Petmongkon Pornpichitsuwan, Krittin Pachtrachai, Touchapon Kraisingkorn

entry.summary: Addresses LLM voice agents in regulated debt-collection calls, where legal requirements mandate specific conversational flows that vary per creditor and change over time. The proposed FlowSpec specification generates policy instructions, gates tools, supplies supervision, and defines tests so a small self-hosted policy can be trained once and then follow unseen regulated procedures. Targets compliance-by-construction for deployed voice agents.

entry.title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs

author.name: Justin Dumouchelle, Shunyu Yao, Beste Basciftci, Thiago Serra

entry.summary: ACCESS is a structured sampling framework for chance-constrained stochastic programs that decouples optimization from feasibility evaluation, generating high-quality candidates from many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems rather than expensive sample average approximation or conservative reformulations. This addresses the common failure of SAA-based methods to find feasible solutions while preserving objective quality. Relevant to decision-making under uncertainty across operations and ML applications.

entry.title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap

author.name: Renbo Tu, Yang Liu, Shuying Sun

entry.summary: This paper empirically revisits generative retrieval versus dense retrieval for sequential recommendation on Amazon Toys datasets, finding GR leads on best-item value but DR leads on recall, with popularity largely explaining GR's measured value advantage. A single static item-value reranking step added to DR reverses GR's lead while keeping recall higher. A valuable reality check challenging the narrative that generative retrieval uniformly supersedes dense retrieval.

entry.title: Geometric Kernel Diversity: An Axiomatic Diversity Measure in Euclidean Space

author.name: Ditbul Ban, Younghun Roh, Julian Shun, Vihan Lakshman

entry.summary: Building on recent work showing no standard diversity metric satisfies monotonicity, uniqueness, and continuity axioms, this paper introduces Geometric Kernel Diversity, defined as the union volume of radial kernel solids associated with points in Euclidean space. GKD satisfies all three axioms and is efficiently computable, resolving an open question left by prior NP-hard constructions. The measure has applications to data subset selection and related ML tasks.

entry.title: Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models

author.name: Soundouss Messoudi, Youness Mansar

entry.summary: The paper studies fast binary decisions (allow/block, retain/discard) in LLM workflows when human deferral is unavailable, controlling false omission risk within a utility-maximizing action subset using System One decision scores. Across six moderation, safety, and reranking datasets, naive thresholds exceed target risk about half the time versus a much lower rate for their method.

entry.title: What Does Disagreement Mean? A Semantic Identifiability Frontier for Pairwise Preference Learning

author.name: Manoj Saravanan, Rohit Kumar Salla, Shrikar Reddy Kota

entry.summary: This paper builds a nonparametric latent model separating aggregate directional preference, persistent disagreement, and non-binary mass in pairwise comparison data, proving an exact semantic fiber theorem showing which quantities are identifiable under a binary feedback channel. It clarifies whether observed disagreement reflects stable heterogeneity, noise, or non-binary responses hidden by forced-choice interfaces.

entry.title: ForkGRPO: Efficient Exploration and Fine-Grained Credit Assignment for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zhaoyan Jia, Chengwei Zhou, Gourav Datta, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: ForkGRPO is a reinforcement learning framework for diffusion language models that forks rollouts from intermediate states to improve exploration and assigns segment-level credit instead of uniform trajectory-level advantages. It addresses entropy degradation in any-order generation while moving beyond standard GRPO with strictly left-to-right rollouts.

entry.title: REWIND: Uncertainty-Guided Trajectory Repair for Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Yi Ding, Mengyu Wang, Min Zhou, Menglin Yang

entry.summary: REWIND is a training-free test-time controller that uses token entropy dynamics to detect reasoning errors and propose targeted suffix regenerations, motivated by the finding that incorrect responses show roughly 112% higher mean token entropy than correct ones. It improves performance across three model families and five benchmarks over repeated-generation baselines.

entry.title: Recognizing Dialogue Ambiguity via Candidate Set Visual Grounding

author.name: Shun Inadumi, Lee Sangmyeong, Koichiro Yoshino

entry.summary: Proposes Candidate Set Visual Grounding (CSVG), a new task where a system maintains the set of plausible referents for ambiguous dialogue utterances rather than committing to a unique object, plus the CandVG benchmark. This reframes interactive visual grounding around uncertainty-aware reference tracking as context accumulates.

entry.title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities

author.name: Yong-Hui Hua, Chih-Han Lin, Shu-Kai Hsieh

entry.summary: This study asks whether gossip, evaluative talk about absent third parties, emerges spontaneously in communities of autonomous AI agents, comparing the Moltbook agent platform with Taiwan's human-operated PTT forum under matched operational definitions. Gossip does occur among AI agents but at 2.6 to 6 times lower prevalence than among humans, with similar structural patterns such as targeting locally prominent figures and eliciting first-responder agreement. It offers one of the first empirical sociolinguistic characterizations of AI agent social behavior.

entry.title: ChronoCulture: Evaluating Cultural Awareness Across Time in Large Language Models

author.name: Rusali Saha, Nitya Khurana, Ruihong Huang, Kuan-Hao Huang

entry.summary: ChronoCulture is a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries, testing whether LLMs capture how cultural attitudes change over time, not just their state at one point. Across six LLMs, models predict attitudes at a given time reasonably but fail to reliably track attitude change, with year-conditioning offering only partial help.

entry.title: ActICL: Post-Training for Agentic Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Yanshu Li, Ruixiang Tang, Junyi Jessy Li, Elias Stengel-Eskin

entry.summary: ActICL trains a multimodal LLM agent to judge what new demonstrations it needs and to progressively retrieve them via tool-augmented reasoning, rather than using fixed retrieval of all demonstrations at once. This post-training approach targets redundancy and noise in multimodal in-context learning contexts.

entry.title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment

author.name: Xiao Yang, Zekun Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Duoxun Tang, Ziyang Liu, Dengbo He, Kaishun Wu, Jiyao Wang

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses two bottlenecks limiting VLMs in video-based remote physiological measurement: generic visual semantics discard fine-grained physiological cues, and discrete autoregressive token prediction misaligns with continuous numerical outputs. The proposed VITAL method addresses both with physiological grounding and numerical alignment.

entry.title: HyrCap: Hybrid Rank-Calibration of Action Proposals for Temporal Event Understanding

author.name: Rui Chen, Xingyu Chen, Pengxin Xu, Kai Chen, Junzhi Yu

entry.summary: HyrCap is a proposal-centric, query-based temporal action detection framework that adds explicit modeling of localization quality, cross-representation support, and inter-proposal relations via hybrid features and rank calibration. Reliable proposals connect temporal localization with semantic event understanding for LLM-driven video analysis.

entry.title: Learning Visual Speech Representations via Cross-Modal Distillation and Joint Face-Lip Modeling

author.name: Jing-Xuan Zhang, Genshun Wan, Jianqing Gao, Jia Pan, Yumei Zhang, Lichen Zhang

entry.summary: FLARE improves lipreading by distilling Whisper representations as discrete acoustic teacher targets via random-projection quantization with masked prediction pretraining, plus a dual-stream architecture jointly processing lip ROI and full-face inputs. This targets ambiguity and sensitivity to pose and resolution in visual speech.

entry.title: HyperLoop: Hyperspectral-Assisted Loop Closure Detection in 3D-SLAM for Planetary Exploration

author.name: Annie Bhalla, Dennis Rotondi, Riccardo Giubilato, Kai O. Arras, Wolfgang Stuerzl

entry.summary: HyperLoop is the first framework integrating hyperspectral imaging into the loop closure module of a 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system, targeting planetary rover navigation in visually repetitive, featureless terrain. It introduces two hyperspectral descriptor families encoding material-level spectral signatures that complement RGB features and resist perceptual aliasing and illumination change.

entry.title: RepForcing: Representation-Space Initialization for Autoregressive Video Distillation

author.name: Siming Fu, Zheming Fu, Lianrui Mu, Haoyang Huang, Chaojie Gu, Ruizhe He

entry.summary: RepForcing improves distillation of pretrained video diffusion models into few-step autoregressive generators by supervising causal initialization in representation space rather than relying on intermediate-teacher latent targets. The analysis shows causal ODE initialization reduces blur but leaves fine detail unresolved, which representation-space supervision addresses.

entry.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience

author.name: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu, Xingyilang Yin, Huiqiang Sun, Guangzhi Wang, Junfu Pu, Cheng Cheng, Honghao Chen, Ying Shan, Mike Zheng Shou, Hwee Tou Ng

entry.summary: Player-1 is a post-training framework that teaches computer-use-style agents to play games by generating synthetic interactive experience rather than relying solely on demonstrations. It extends the action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions, and builds on supervised initialization followed by self-generated practice.

entry.title: End-to-End Vision-Language-Action Policies for Autonomous Lunar Rover Docking

author.name: Sitan Huang, Grace Gao

entry.summary: This paper applies end-to-end VLA policies to autonomous lunar rover docking, leveraging internet-scale vision-language pretraining for robustness under extreme illumination contrast and perceptual disturbances. It contrasts this with modular navigation pipelines whose hand-engineered components propagate measurement errors. Applying VLA models to planetary exploration is a timely extension of terrestrial robotics results.

entry.title: Eye, Robot: Learning Expressive Gaze Dynamics via a VLM-Guided Transformer-VAE

author.name: Yuhang Hu, Junlin Lyu, Yuan Fang, Xiaoying Shen, Lechen Zhang, Jiong Lin, Judah Goldfeder, Steven Tian, Hod Lipson

entry.summary: The system separates humanoid gaze behavior into a VLM that selects where to look, a reactive perception module for fixation, and a Realistic Gaze Transformer-VAE that generates coupled eye, head, and eyelid motion trained on markerless human recordings retargeted to an 11-DoF robot. Self-supervised pretraining and autoregressive fine-tuning capture the temporal structure of human gaze.

entry.title: HM3D-M3: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent, Multi-Modal, Multi-Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Hongyu Ding, Kanyu Xu, Mingjia Chen, Zixuan Chen, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo, Yifan Zhang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: HM3D-M3 is a benchmark combining multi-agent, multi-modal, and multi-object goal navigation in single episodes: teams of K agents in photorealistic indoor scenes must find M objects specified via open-vocabulary categories, instance images, or spoken-style descriptions. It provides 1,000 validation episodes to fill a gap left by benchmarks that study these axes in isolation.

entry.title: Human Demonstrations as Post-Training Data for Any Robot Body: Retargeting the Object, Not the Hand

author.name: Nagasrikanth Kallakuri

entry.summary: The paper proposes using human demonstrations recorded on simple devices like phones as post-training data for arbitrary robot embodiments by retargeting the object's motion rather than the hand's. Each capture yields a body-free record of object pose, contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object, from which any robot given a URDF can be solved.

entry.title: FPTAS for Polygonal Multi-Robot Motion Planning

author.name: Sayan Bandyapadhyay, William Lochet, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue

entry.summary: This theoretical paper presents the first fully polynomial-time approximation schemes for multi-robot motion planning with polygonal robots and environments under min-sum, min-max, and related objectives. For any fixed number k of constant-complexity polygonal robots, the algorithms find collision-free plans provably close to shortest. This provides rigorous approximation guarantees for a classically hard combinatorial motion planning problem.

entry.title: MCMC Can See Can't See

author.name: Daniel Matsui Smola

entry.summary: This paper proves an impossibility result: no finite checklist of MCMC convergence diagnostics can guarantee that a Markov chain has actually converged. The author quantifies how worst-case undetected non-convergence decays as more diagnostics are added, shows how to choose diagnostics optimally, proves that slowest-mixing modes yield near-optimal diagnostics, and provides an anytime-valid bound on remaining discrepancy.

entry.title: How to Build a Benchmark That Actually Measures Taste

author.name: Xiaofan Wu, Xi Zeng, Miaoxia Chen, Peishan Chen, Shuyan Li, Chen Wang, Xiaohan Wang, Wanling Xu, Jiyun Yao, Hanyong Zhong, Jiahao Zhu

entry.summary: TasteBench is a pairwise good-vs-bad benchmark spanning visual, brand, book, and tech items with a frozen rubric, expert-only gold labels, and a control protocol separating craft judgment from test-gaming. The paper methodically surfaces validity threats in a human pilot, including construction artifacts that inflate trivial baselines and a difficulty ceiling that inflates all scores.

entry.title: Beyond Outcome Feedback: Trajectory-Quality-Guided Experience-based Learning

author.name: Bingjie Zhang, Yibo Yang, Qiantong Liu, Benshuo Fu, Yi Chang, Dandan Guo

entry.summary: TQG-Exp improves experience-based learning for LLM agents by introducing process feedback: a Trajectory Quality Loss combining task completion with execution process quality, plus paired rollouts with and without experience retrieval. This yields better learning signals than final-outcome-only feedback.

entry.title: Large Decision Models: Repurposing Large Language Models as Single-Pass Decision Makers

author.name: Ziyi Chen, Yan Zhang, Jianhui Wei, Jianing Yin, Daoan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Large Decision Models, repurposing LLMs to return explicit probabilities over runtime-specified labels in one prefill forward pass rather than sequential decoding. Diverse Decision Supervision adapts models to this interface across varied domains and label schemas, and Self-Posed Reasoning Distillation from a frozen teacher narrows the gap to reasoning models. Avoids per-task classifier training and decoding costs.

entry.title: Hardware-Friendly Token-Group Activation Quantization for Low-Bit Mamba Super-Resolution

author.name: Jinwoo Chung, Jangho Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Token-Group Quantization, a hardware-friendly activation post-training quantization framework for Mamba-based super-resolution models, statically approximating a post-scan token grouping oracle via a lightweight pre-scan predictor. This addresses the variable activation ranges induced by Mamba's selective scan operator at low bit-widths.

entry.title: MAS-Gate: Unlocking Multi-Agent System Lifecycle via Node-Centric Quantification

author.name: Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Ming Yan, Peidong Wang, Shilei Cao, Minzhi Li, Bosheng Ding, Juepeng Zheng, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: MAS-Gate proposes a unified node-centric framework that quantifies LLM-based multi-agent systems across a three-phase lifecycle: design-time orchestration, runtime intervention, and post-hoc attribution. The goal is to bridge fragmented research perspectives that use irreconcilable objectives and signals across phases. This is a step toward principled, graph-based management of multi-agent system complexity.

entry.title: Predict Before You Modify: Learning Improvement Dynamics for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zixuan Xie, Chang Xu, Yuhua Jiang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: This work introduces a learned Improvement Dynamics Model (IDM) that predicts task-level outcomes of proposed self-modifications before costly evaluation, guiding optional revision, and is itself updated from observed modification outcomes across generations. The system thus improves how it solves tasks, proposes modifications, and predicts modification effects. This adds a model-based planning layer to self-evolving agent loops.

entry.title: Auditing LLM Program Search for Bermudan Stopping with Primal--Dual Certificates

author.name: Yuhua Qian

entry.summary: The paper audits LLM-driven program search on Bermudan option optimal-stopping problems using primal-dual certificates with trusted simulation and dual upper bounds. Across 24 generation attempts and ablations, no generated program consistently improves on Ridge LSMC beyond Monte Carlo uncertainty, with holdout gaps within 0.002.

entry.title: RealityBench: Simulated Environments to Evaluate a Vision Language Model's Ability to Document Human Physical Work

author.name: Andrew Perrault (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA), Anmol Takiar (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA), Dominik Winecki (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA), Arnab Nandi (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA)

entry.summary: RealityBench uses simulated environments of unconstrained field tasks like rooftop solar installation and vehicle repair to benchmark vision-language models on documenting human physical work from egocentric camera feeds. It addresses the lack of principled benchmarks caused by proprietary data and high variability in real physical-work settings.

entry.title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation

author.name: Ruiyang Wang, Hao-Lun Hsu, Haocheng Meng, Songqiao Xie, Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: Introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers trust in robots and their reported hypotheses using only inter-robot observation consistency, without preassigned trust relationships or side-channel information, including under adversarial interference.

entry.title: GAMW: Generation-Aware Mel-Domain Watermarking for TTS Traceability

author.name: Yihang Zhang, Weicai Yan, Qifei Zhang, Yangyang Wu, Tao Jin

entry.summary: GAMW integrates watermark injection into the TTS generation process rather than post-hoc waveform modification, embedding a content-adaptive multi-bit watermark residual into the generated representation before synthesis. The decoding objective combines focal modulation with dynamic per-bit weighting, improving robustness against compound perturbations for provenance tracking.

entry.title: StimFlow: Synthesizing Brain Activity from Images via Stimulus-conditioned Flow Matching

author.name: Bui Van Hung, Dang Thanh Vu, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Mai Tien Dung, Soo-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: StimFlow synthesizes fMRI brain activity directly in native voxel space from images using conditional flow matching with a linear path, aligning training and inference distributions so a single sample is competitive without averaging. It combines structural DINOv2 features with semantic CLIP features, which the authors show are complementary along the cortical visual processing hierarchy. This advances stimulus-to-response generative encoding beyond compressed-latent, semantics-only approaches.

entry.title: RespFocus: Learning Temporal Evidence for Weakly Supervised Respiratory Sound Classification

author.name: Yi Tian, Xiaohuan Chen, Yufei tang, Xinyu Lin, Hongliang Li, Chengbin Hou, Degen Huang, Rongshan Yu

entry.summary: RespFocus is a weakly supervised multiple-instance learning framework for respiratory sound classification that learns inspectable cycle-level temporal evidence, and the authors introduce PedResp2026, a multicenter pediatric respiratory sound cohort with adjudicated cycle-level annotations collected in routine clinical settings. This improves transparency for detecting transient crackles and wheezes in noisy recordings.

entry.title: AeroChem: Closed-loop Physics-Informed State Space Modeling for Long-term Chemically-Reactive Air Quality Forecasting--Extended Version

author.name: Kien Le Trung, Tung Kieu, Dinh Duc Nha Nguyen, Cuong Do, Bin Yang, Phi Long Nguyen

entry.summary: AeroChem is a closed-loop physics-informed state space framework for long-term air quality forecasting, coupling a UDE-based physical process branch with a Mamba-based virtual measurement branch in a two-branch co-correction design to prevent long-horizon drift and enforce physical consistency under nonlinear chemistry. It improves on open-loop physics-ML fusion designs.

entry.title: Unsupervised Data Drift Monitoring for Deployed Deepfake Speech Detectors

author.name: Luk\'a\v{s} Proke\v{s}, Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Anton Firc, Kamil Malinka

entry.summary: The authors propose an unsupervised drift monitor for deployed deepfake speech detectors that compares input embeddings against bona fide and spoof references using regularized Mahalanobis distances, partitioning embedding space into trusted, ambiguous, and novel regions for routing unfamiliar inputs to review. It is evaluated on four modern detectors across three datasets.

entry.title: Interactive Navigation Beyond Reachability: Benchmark and Agentic Framework

author.name: Delun Li, Xueyao Wei, Rui Chen, Yifei Wang, Junzhi Yu, Wenjie Song, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: Formulates interactive navigation where agents must change connectivity (opening doors) and reveal hidden targets (opening containers) with sequential dependencies, introducing MultINav-Bench, a 3K-episode ObjectGoal benchmark in MolmoSpaces with interaction-necessity annotations, plus an automated data-generation pipeline and agentic evaluation framework.

entry.title: Cross-View Time-Frequency Diffusion for Extreme-Aware Time-Series Generation

author.name: Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: CrossTF generates realistic time series with faithful rare-event reproduction by exploiting discrepancies between time-view and frequency-view diffusion denoisers. The key finding is extreme-sensitive cross-view asymmetry: moving along the direction connecting the two views' clean-sample estimates substantially changes extreme fidelity with limited effect on overall quality. This avoids specialized extreme-focused objectives that compromise distributional fidelity.

entry.title: Claim Framing as a Driver of LLM Sycophancy

author.name: Jean Seo, Pepa Atanasova, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: A systematic study of how the framing of user opinions triggers sycophancy in LLMs, using factually verifiable questions across 14 models and 42K questions with 21 framing types over 8 dimensions. All models prove susceptible to user opinions regardless of size, with confident framings being most influential. This improves on prior sycophancy studies that lacked ground truth and used single opinion formats.

entry.title: Learning by Examples: Power Grid Steady State Analysis with a Tabular Foundation Model

author.name: Olayiwola Arowolo, Oluwadara Adedeji, Peter Palensky, Jochen L. Cremer

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether the pretrained tabular foundation model TabPFN can serve as a general-purpose neural solver for power grid steady-state tasks: power flow prediction, N-k contingency screening, and voltage stability margin prediction. Without retraining or fine-tuning, the TFM matches or beats task-specific neural baselines on 118- and 2000-bus systems in several settings. This is a notable demonstration of zero-shot foundation model transfer into critical infrastructure analysis.

entry.title: From Detection To Anticipation: Continuous Onset Forecasting For Stuttered Speech

author.name: Tampu Ravi Kumar, Ayoub Daliri, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: This paper reframes stuttering support from post-hoc detection to prediction, forecasting the risk of stuttering onset every 100 ms from preceding speech using a compact 3.67M-parameter causal Conformer over frozen Whisper-large-v3 representations, with a new manually annotated 2,872-event augmentation of FluencyBank for 36 speakers. It achieves an AUROC of 0.63, with temporal analysis characterizing how prediction behaves. It enables anticipatory interventions and contributes a valuable new dataset.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Kun Ryu, Yeo Jin Jung, Shyue Ping Ong, Claire Donnat, Ying Shirley Meng

entry.summary: The paper frames the decision of when to trust a pretrained machine-learned interatomic potential versus falling back to expensive DFT as a risk-controlled selection problem solved via conformal risk control. A lightweight predictor estimates MLIP-DFT disagreement scores in energy, forces, and stresses from a fixed geometric descriptor of each configuration. This provides statistical guarantees for MLIP reliability in automated materials discovery, addressing a major throughput bottleneck.

entry.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation

author.name: Fei Wu, Zhenrong Zhang, Jianshu Zhang, Jun Du

entry.summary: VASPO integrates privileged self-distillation with PPO by exploiting complementary positional dynamics: privileged information sharpens the critic's late-response value predictions while self-teacher guidance is strongest early in generation. This value-augmented self-distillation policy optimization improves reasoning-model training relative to GRPO-plus-teacher combinations.

entry.title: More Than Seeing: Vision as Scalable Anchors in Native Multimodal Pre-Training

author.name: Haoyuan Wu, Aoqi Wu, Jiani Hu, Bei Yu

entry.summary: Through controlled ablations replacing image embeddings with content-free padding tokens, this paper studies how visual signals affect scaling behavior in native multimodal pre-training. Retaining visual content improves text prediction on image-text pairs without materially changing text-only loss optima, with the multimodal loss benefit growing with scale.

entry.title: Frustratingly Easy Majority Voting Using Length Conditioning

author.name: Fiorenzo Parascandolo, Enver Sangineto, Xiaoyi Yu, Wenhui Tan, Jipei He, Ruihua Song, Rita Cucchiara

entry.summary: Proposes Length-Conditioned Majority Voting (LCMV), a test-time training method that improves standard majority voting by incorporating a length-conditioned prior over answer correctness, exploiting the established inverse relation between chain-of-thought length and correctness, modeled as a logistic function and adapted at test time.

entry.title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities

author.name: Chih-Han Lin, Yu-Yun Chang, Po-Ya Angela Wang, Shu-Kai Hsieh

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether AI agent communities develop the temporal semantic structure of human linguistic communities, comparing MoltBook (8 weeks), PTT (19 years), and Reddit using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings to measure semantic drift, neighborhood stability, and drift-trajectory autocorrelation. It finds lexical persistence without semantic entrenchment: agent terms spread and recur, but lag-1 autocorrelation places agents at the low end of a memory-horizon continuum, lacking longer-range temporal dependence seen on human platforms. The result suggests agent communities sustain vocabulary dynamics without deeper semantic consolidation.

entry.title: CORE: Contrast-and-Reflect for Self-Supervised Prompt Optimization in Anomaly Synthesis

author.name: Haoxiang Rao, Fang Zhao, Zhao Wang, Weijia Li, Chenyang Si, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: CORE is a training-free prompt optimization framework using large multimodal models for industrial anomaly synthesis in open-set scenarios, with an Anomaly Context Grounding module converting sparse user context into defect-aware generation context. Contrast-and-reflect iterations provide complex reasoning and optimization without requiring real anomaly references or auxiliary data.

entry.title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions

author.name: Tianyi Gao, Han Fang, Xin Wei, Yaoyao Zhong, Zhaoyan Pan, Weijie Zhu, Hongbo Sun, Zhiyu Lin, Kaicheng Yang, Jinglin Xu, Ye Yuan, Hao Li, Hao Sun, Jingmin Xin

entry.summary: ReferFlow formulates trajectory-level referring expression comprehension, where models must localize target regions for ordered intermediate grounding steps derived from a single complex query. ReferFlow-Bench defines four trajectory types (Refinement, Shift, Reset, Mixture), and experiments reveal weaknesses in MLLM stepwise grounding that final-only evaluation hides.

entry.title: Representation Conditioning for Generation

author.name: Saeed Razavi, Xingjian Leng, Liang Zheng

entry.summary: Building on representation-alignment methods like REPA that accelerate diffusion transformer training, the authors observe that semantics imported at early layers may not persist to later layers supervised only by the velocity loss. They propose RECON, which conditions later layers directly on pretrained vision encoder tokens during training while using a no-op mechanism at inference.

entry.title: Active Perception of Upper-Limb Functional Mobility through Human-Robot Handovers

author.name: Francesco Semeraro, Marta Lagomarsino, Alberto Ranavolo, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: The work formulates estimating a human's upper-limb functional mobility as an active perception problem, modeling task-available ranges of motion via impairment coefficients that parameterize reductions of healthy joint limits. A robot integrates this human model during handover interactions to autonomously estimate mobility without external clinical assessment, supporting workplace reintegration after injury.

entry.title: HiPPT: Physiology-Grounded Wearable PPG Representation Learning via Multi-Scope Text Alignment

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Wei Chen, Xiaoyu Li, Lexian Xia, ShuaiLong Tang, Chenran Zhang, Donglin Xie, Guangpu Zhu, Yelei Li, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: HiPPT is a pretraining framework for wearable PPG signals that matches supervision sources to appropriate evidence scopes, combining record-level morphology alignment with cross-recording contextual alignment. It builds a corpus of over 4 million wrist-worn recordings from 202K users paired with text descriptions.

entry.title: Are Multimodal Benchmarks Really Useful? Item-Level Multimodal Benchmark Diagnosis via Structure-Response Co-Calibration

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Weixin Zeng, Ziheng Zhang, Jiuyang Tang, Xiang Zhao

entry.summary: SRCoD is a framework for diagnosing individual items in multimodal benchmarks to detect shortcut questions answerable from a single modality or answer-option regularities. It co-calibrates intrinsic item structure with extrinsic model response behavior, addressing the inadequacy of approaches relying on only one of the two.

entry.title: AcrossVAM2.0: Conflict-Aware Point Supervision for Parameter-Efficient Video Diffusion Adaptation

author.name: Nan Wu, Yee Hung Hong

entry.summary: ACROSSVAM2.0 adapts a 5.01B-parameter text-to-video diffusion transformer using explicit point correspondence without overwriting the pretrained appearance prior. It combines a confidence-weighted track-and-visibility head, zero-initialized residual feedback, and asymmetric PCGrad that removes only the auxiliary gradient component opposing the primary flow-matching update, improving cycle-consistency in a multi-seed ablation.

entry.title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning

author.name: Gennadiy Chistiakov, Yury Yanovich

entry.summary: This paper proposes an evaluation framework for credit assignment in modular financial RL combining equal-information reconstruction controls, fixed-utility comparisons, and prespecified downstream guardrails, instantiated in an attribution-guided modular trading system across three controlled studies. Notably, it finds residual-based allocation is exactly reproduced by a simple loss-budget control, exposing spurious attribution claims.

entry.title: A Reference Architecture for Integrating Agentic AI into Enterprise Software: Responsibilities, Interactions, and Variability

author.name: Mingqin Yu, Fethi Rabhi, Liming Zhu, Qinghua Lu

entry.summary: This paper presents a technology-neutral reference architecture for integrating agentic AI into enterprise software, synthesizing architectural concerns such as orchestration, memory and knowledge, tool access, security, runtime infrastructure, and evaluation. It organizes responsibilities, interactions, and variability points across existing research and industry architectures.

entry.title: MARL-BattleGrounds: A Novel JAX-native Benchmark for Heterogeneous and Competitive Multi-agent RL

author.name: Ulixes Tariq Hawili, Subramanian Ramamoorthy, Yoann Altmann, Ignacio Carlucho

entry.summary: MARL-BattleGrounds is a JAX-native benchmark for competitive, heterogeneous multi-agent RL, featuring a five-versus-five team deathmatch with distinct agent classes, 52 hand-designed maps, a 12-map curriculum, and held-out evaluation maps. It aims to fill the gap between cheap but shallow benchmarks like SMAX and expensive rich ones like Dota 2.

entry.title: What Survives When Activation Steering Is Used as Memory

author.name: Vedant Jumle

entry.summary: This paper tests the assumption that activation steering vectors can serve as agent memory, storing experience-induced state shifts keyed by conversation gist and re-applying them in later sessions with frozen LLMs. A pre-registered study on Qwen3.5 models with cross-family judges finds that only question-independent content survives, since attention recomputes context-dependent effects.

entry.title: On the Complexity Gap Between POMDPs and Multi-Environment POMDPs

author.name: Eline M. Bovy, Caleb Probine, Marnix Suilen, Ufuk Topcu, Nils Jansen

entry.summary: Maps the computational complexity landscape of multi-environment POMDPs (ME-POMDPs), showing that subclasses tractable in the single-environment case (e.g., blind MDPs, becoming NP-complete) lose tractability under model uncertainty. This sharpens understanding of where worst-case robust planning over model classes becomes hard.

entry.title: Understanding Unified VLMs: From Attention Probing to Guidance Tuning for Multimodal Generation

author.name: Zhengyang Luo, Xiaoyu Qiu, Zhiheng Tan, Yuchen Liang, Yingbin Liang, Liyue Shen

entry.summary: Probes every attention head in unified vision-language models spanning autoregressive and masked-diffusion paradigms, identifying a stable subset of heads sensitive to classifier-free guidance conditioning in both text-to-image and image-to-text generation. Based on this, the authors propose guidance tuning to improve multimodal generation.

entry.title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Xiangqing Lu, Tao Zhu, Mingxing Nie, Liming Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes CHEAR, a framework that uses confusion hierarchies and evidence-aware reasoning to make LLM-based human activity recognition from wearable sensors more cost-efficient. Rather than concentrating evidence retrieval and candidate comparison at inference time, it organizes discriminative knowledge so the model can prune candidate activities intelligently without risking exclusion of the true label. The work matters because RAG-augmented HAR systems scale poorly as activity vocabularies grow.

entry.title: CoverSynth: Coverage-Guided Generation of Retrieval Evaluation Sets

author.name: Anahita Sharma, Apaar Shanker, Rishav Chakravarti, Sneha Srinivasan, Vijay Kalmath, Dylan Wilbur, Yuan Li, Sara Bolouki, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for assessing retrieval evaluation sets on coverage, reliability, efficiency, and discriminability, plus CoverSynth, a generator that produces such sets from unannotated corpora without expensive expert labeling. Aimed at enterprise agents needing evaluation sets that expose domain-specific failures and guide deployment tradeoffs. Also contributes the first assessment framework for when an evaluation set suffices.

entry.title: LURE: a Phase-Labelled Synthetic Corpus of Online-Grooming Exchanges

author.name: Emanuele Florindi, Valentina Franzoni, Ludovico Guercio, Alfredo Milani, Mattia Polticchia

entry.summary: LURE provides a phase-annotated synthetic corpus of groomer-victim exchanges generated with a retrieval-augmented pipeline using an openly available refusal-ablated 8B model, addressing the small, outdated, and frozen nature of the only public grooming dataset. The generation follows a responsible five-stage protocol grounded in the ChatCoder luring-communication ontology with eight communicative tags.

entry.title: Large language model-generated patterns for epidemiological modeling: a multi-benchmark evaluation framework

author.name: Sophia Mao, Keshav Gandhi, Alexander Gutfraind

entry.summary: The authors evaluate whether LLM-generated behavioral outputs can substitute for sparse empirical data in epidemiological modeling, using hepatitis C-related behaviors among people who inject drugs as a case study. They benchmark directional associations against literature, agent-based model correlations, and surveys, finding moderate unconditional recovery but strong agreement when LLMs are directly asked to classify associations.

entry.title: Large Language Model Assisted Transportation Planning through a Differentiable User Equilibrium Layer

author.name: Eunseung Lee, Gyeongjun Kim, Keemin Sohn

entry.summary: This study integrates LLMs with a differentiable user equilibrium layer for transportation planning, enabling natural-language interaction with network design, capacity expansion, and calibration tools. Unlike prior LLM systems that merely interface with simulators, the differentiable layer supports efficient search, evaluation, and optimization of transportation solutions.

entry.title: Label-Centric Knowledge Retrieval for Zero-Shot Text Classification

author.name: Daoping Wu, Dong Wang, Siyu Liu, Chen Liang, Jian Geng, Ziqi Li, Shuguang Xiong, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: SLKR is a label-centric retrieval-augmented framework for zero-shot text classification that separates offline knowledge construction from lightweight online inference. A flagship LLM builds a reusable label-knowledge store of definitions, retrieval keywords, and boundary rules for confusable label pairs, enabling efficient large-scale labeling without task-specific examples.

entry.title: RetroPlanner: Multi-Route Expansion and Multi-Objective Reasoning for LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning

author.name: Ye Rin Kim, Yongjun Jeong, Seongjun Yun, Hanbum Ko, Soohyun Oh, Sungbin Lim, Sungwoong Kim

entry.summary: RetroPlanner improves LLM-based retrosynthesis planning by jointly comparing multiple candidate routes over an AND-OR graph, steering search toward higher practical synthesizability measured by reaction plausibility, round-trip consistency, and starting-material price. This moves beyond single-molecule expansion and solvability-only optimization.

entry.title: EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents

author.name: Min Cai, Dan Zhang, Gao Xing, Libin Ma, Zhaohui Xu, Xi Ye

entry.summary: EAU is a meta-agent framework that co-evolves the environment, agent, and user simulator during training: it monitors trajectories, tool traces, and rewards, diagnoses failures and uninformative interactions, and updates the components jointly rather than treating them as fixed. This targets the instability of multi-turn user-facing agent training.

entry.title: CLIVO: Differentiable Cluster-Based Instruction Mixing with Learned Validation Objectives

author.name: Yuhan Wang, Rui Hu, Batian Di, Tan Jiang, Dongsheng Ma, Leichao Dong, Yuanzi Li, Yalin Feng

entry.summary: Proposes CLIVO, a target-aware multimodal instruction selection framework combining fine-grained semantic cluster allocation, automatically learned validation objectives, and differentiable mixture search over instruction data. It addresses overrepresentation of similar content in sample-level ranking and coarse units and costly search in group-level methods.

entry.title: Agency as a New Organizing Abstraction for Computer Science

author.name: Ian Foster

entry.summary: Ian Foster argues that agentic AI systems should be understood not merely as applications of foundation models but as a candidate new organizing abstraction for computer science, comparable to past abstractions like processes or objects. The key novelty is open-ended agency: systems that synthesize courses of action from goals, observations, and memory over environments with no complete task-specific model specified in advance. This is a position paper about how agency should reshape systems research and CS curricula.

entry.title: When Should Enterprise Policy Decisions Be Learned, and When Should They Be Reasoned?

author.name: Hyojung Han, Ryangkyung Kang, Youngeun Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: Using a fixed 27B Korean enterprise model, this study compares deployed decision paths for policy-following agents: generated JSON decisions versus single constrained tokens, with and without prior reasoning. Accuracy differences were negligible on 2800 in-distribution items, but restart stability differed by roughly tenfold, and on a sealed benchmark with labels from a hidden executable policy the paths diverge in generalization. It offers practical guidance on when to learn versus reason in enterprise policy agents.

entry.title: Consider, Then Choose: Order-Invariant Decisions in System One Models

author.name: Jianguo Huang, Yao Long Teng, Yanchen Deng, Bo An

entry.summary: The paper documents that System One models (single-forward-pass MCQ answering) violate order invariance on choice questions, with the effect concentrated in cases where the model is unsure among top options, and proposes Runoff, a training-free procedure that scores options individually to shortlist candidates then compares them in cyclically permuted listings. This yields order-invariant decisions without retraining. It is a clean diagnosis plus practical fix for a known LLM bias.

entry.title: Choosing LLMs for Strategic Agent Interactions

author.name: Arastun Mammadli, Herbert Woisetschl\"ager, Jawad Fayaz, Shiqiang Wang

entry.summary: The paper frames LLM selection as a meta-game layered on top of game-theoretic benchmarks: a strategic selector must pick models from a portfolio when facing unknown, adaptive opponents. This extends model routing beyond static quality-cost trade-offs to settings where payoff structure depends on the adversary.

entry.title: Auditing Future-Memory Use in Point-in-Time Language Agents

author.name: Rongtian Ye

entry.summary: The study tests whether LLM agents secretly use memorized post-cutoff facts when external evidence respects a historical cutoff, across 48 historical company-comparison tasks with prespecified directional predictions. Both Qwen and DeepSeek could recall future facts in closed-book probes, but neither shifted toward the better-remembered company in agent runs.

entry.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback

author.name: Zheye Deng, Sha Li, Changlong Yu, Xin Liu, Qin Lu, Priyanka Nigam, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: The paper formulates an agentic code judging task where an LLM diagnoses a candidate competitive-programming solution using only the problem statement and source code, producing checkable counterexamples as evidence instead of relying on official test systems. It builds a benchmark to evaluate how well models can judge and explain failures without consuming limited official submissions. This supports test-time scaling approaches that need informative verifiers for selection and revision.

entry.title: Dependency, Compression, and Synergy: A Unified Information-Theoretic View of Multimodal Learning

author.name: Liangjian Wen, Linjie Li, Jiang Duan, Yong Dai, Jianzhuang Liu, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: This survey unifies Mutual Information, the Information Bottleneck, and Partial Information Decomposition as progressively refined lenses on multimodal information processing: MI captures inter-modal dependency, IB captures task-oriented compression, and PID decomposes information into redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy. It reviews 170 studies from 2018 to 2026 and connects them under a single information-theoretic framework. This provides a valuable conceptual map for multimodal foundation model research.

entry.title: Barycentric Anchored Weight Search for Robust Model Merging

author.name: Antoni Buades, Jose-Luis Lisani

entry.summary: The paper proposes Barycentric Anchored Search, a post-hoc, derivative-free weight-space procedure that improves fine-tuned vision models under distribution shift without extra gradient training or inference cost. It constructs barycentric candidate weights between fine-tuned checkpoints and the pre-trained model, selecting along OOD-validation-guided directions.

entry.title: A Geometric Perspective on Reward Function Updates in Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Anish Diwan, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

entry.summary: The paper recasts reward updates in inverse reinforcement learning through an occupancy-space geometry view, showing that geometry along the e-geodesic toward the optimal occupancy directly affects gradient behavior in Lagrangian-based IRL. This complements the classical primal-dual algorithmic perspective.

entry.title: Embodied Zero-Shot Task Planning via Hardware-Aware LLM-VLM Integration for Grounded Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Lonnie Tankersley, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Soroush Korivand

entry.summary: This paper presents a hardware-aware framework combining an API-hosted LLM planner with a local Qwen3-VL 8B verifier for zero-shot robotic manipulation on a simulated Franka Research 3 robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. The design separates symbolic reasoning (task objects, target relations, approach preferences) from metric execution that respects reachability, collision, and grasp feasibility constraints.

entry.title: MvFFN: Multi-view Floor plan Feed-forward Network for Unposed Wide-Baseline Panorama Layout Reconstruction

author.name: Yuguang Li, Yichuan Deng, Zixuan Liu, Ivaylo Boyadzhiev, Xiuyuan Wu, Xinyu Zou, Linda Shapiro, Alex Colburn

entry.summary: MvFFN reconstructs camera poses and multi-room floor plans from sparse, unposed, wide-baseline RGB panoramas by keeping predictions strictly local: each panorama column predicts only the wall it observes plus two adjacent walls, with global layout emerging from deterministic aggregation of overlapping predictions. This sidesteps the difficulty of learning a full floor plan as a single global output.

entry.title: RES-MR: Risk-Aware Reasoning for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation

author.name: Cong Wang, Jin Li, Shoujin Wang, Yishuo Li, Huilin Gu, Wenpeng Lu

entry.summary: Introduces RES-MR, an LLM-based framework for medication recommendation with a two-stage training paradigm that provides transparent reasoning and personalized, patient-specific safety constraints rather than fixed risk thresholds. It targets interpretability and safety for vulnerable populations.

entry.title: YOUDrive: Driving Style as a Composable Direction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Guantian Zheng, Lidong Yu, Tianyu Gao, Jiaxing Chen, Jiashu Li, Chen Lv

entry.summary: YOUDrive is a vision-language-action planner for end-to-end autonomous driving that enables continuous, composable control of driving style. Teacher behaviors are distilled into task vectors inducing style directions that can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining, with a flow-matching decoder modeling multimodal driving behaviors.

entry.title: Probabilistic Multi-Source Data Selection via Learnable Categorical Priors: Variance Reduction and Guaranteed Derandomization

author.name: Shizhan Cai, Qixin Zhang, Siyuan Ma, Siyuan Liang, Yongcheng Jing, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a new probabilistic relaxation for multi-source bilevel data selection, using multiple learnable categorical priors to define a distribution supported only on feasible data subsets. This yields lossless rounding, variance-reduced gradient estimation, and a guaranteed derandomization scheme, addressing instability in existing 0-1 and probabilistic relaxations.

entry.title: VLCQ: Post-training quantization for deep neural networks using variable length coding

author.name: Reem Abdel-Salam, Ahmed H. Abdel-Gawad, Amr G. Wassal

entry.summary: VLCQ is a post-training quantization method that relaxes the fixed-point integer constraint by using variable-length encoding, allowing effective compression below INT8 bit-widths without severe accuracy loss. This enables deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices with better compression-performance tradeoffs than standard fixed-width PTQ. The approach requires no access to the original dataset or retraining.

entry.title: Co-DSL: Human-LLM Co-design of Reusable Spatial Concepts for Layout Generation

author.name: R. Kenny Jones, Jiajun Wu, Maneesh Agrawala

entry.summary: Co-DSL is a human-LLM co-design framework in which users build a library of personalized reusable spatial concepts: the LLM converts descriptions into executable implementations, users observe behavior on examples and give lightweight feedback, and the LLM revises the logic. In a second stage, the LLM authors layout programs that compose library concepts into concept-graphs to satisfy new layout requests. This constrains the LLM to composable, user-grounded abstractions rather than free-form generation.

entry.title: Gugak-VocalSet: A Multi-Genre Studio-Quality Dataset of Korean Traditional Singing with Sigimsae Annotations

author.name: Danbinaerin Han, Wonil Kim, Seah Hong, Dongjoo Moon, Jaeok Lee, Jongpil Lee, Chaewon Kim, Juhan Nam

entry.summary: The authors release the first public audio dataset of Korean traditional singing, with 24.5 hours of studio-quality solo vocal recordings from 20 professional singers and around 68,000 audio-grounded annotations of sigimsae vocal expressions using a newly proposed ontology. The dataset enables modeling of expressive pitch contours, a largely unexplored area in music AI.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Time Series Forecasting with Learnable Decomposition and Manifold Dynamics

author.name: Sarang Rajendra Patil, Vishal Fenn, Mengjia Xu

entry.summary: HyperForecast is presented as the first long-term time series forecasting framework operating in hyperbolic space, exploiting the natural frequency hierarchy induced by cascaded decomposition and its alignment with hyperbolic geometry's exponential volume growth. The method models multiscale temporal structure with manifold dynamics and learnable decomposition.

entry.title: PID-Gated Continual Prompt Adaptation Under Noisy Feedback

author.name: Zhentao Xu

entry.summary: Introduces PID-control-inspired lightweight gates that decide when reported mistakes should trigger lasting prompt updates for LLM agents in non-stationary environments, combining current error, accumulated evidence, and rollback of deteriorating edits. The gates are benchmarked against simple baselines and advanced optimizers like TextGrad and GEPA across drifting tasks.

entry.title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation

author.name: Kyungkeon Chung, Se Un Park, Hyejin Lee, Junyoung Park

entry.summary: ARMED is an adaptive clinical retrieval-augmented generation framework for medication recommendation that dynamically expands retrieval based on retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance, using supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval when initial evidence is inadequate. This reduces noisy evidence compared with fixed retrieval pipelines.

entry.title: pi-Net: Empirical Latent Representations for Differentiable Physics Heads in Data-Scarce Systems

author.name: Akshay Dhalpe, Arnab Chattopadhyay, Shahriar Bakrani Balani, Eric Cortan\'ea, Sasu Tarkoma

entry.summary: pi-Net is a physics-informed latent variable model that fixes underdetermined dimensional-analysis-based simulators by mapping inputs into a physically normalized latent space decoded through a differentiable physics head, targeting multi-physics prediction in data-scarce regimes. It bridges purely physical simulators and opaque data-hungry ML models.

entry.title: Feature-Context Consistency: Unsupervised Adversarial Detection with Drift Stability on Attributed Graphs

author.name: Firas Bayram, Maxime Cordy

entry.summary: This paper proposes detecting adversarial node manipulation on attributed graphs via feature-context consistency, formalized as a Context Boost score within a Restricted Boltzmann Machine framework (CB-RBM). The method works without labels and provides worst-case separation guarantees while remaining stable under natural distribution drift.

entry.title: TabGift: A Context-Efficient Foundation Model for Tabular Data Generation

author.name: Yu-Sheng Li, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: Extends the tabular foundation model paradigm from prediction to data generation, proposing TabGift which performs reliable distribution inference from only a small context set. This targets the common scenario where synthetic tabular data is most needed precisely when observations are scarce.

entry.title: Superintelligence and the Triple Risk of an AI Race

author.name: Matthew Rendall, Max Hellrigel-Holderbaum, Leonard Dung

entry.summary: A philosophy/policy paper arguing that the US-China AI race narrative carries three dangers: being overtaken by a rival, triggering war, and a third risk novel to this analysis. It critiques the regulatory-dismantling posture justified by race competitiveness and situates AGI timelines and arms-race dynamics in a structured normative framework.

entry.title: Generative Flow on Symbolic Abstractions for Embodiment Capability Discovery

author.name: Youwei Yu, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes FOSA, which discovers embodiment-specific robot capabilities by learning a grounded task generator: a Generative Flow Network that constructs symbolic task skeletons grounded in the robot's physical affordances, replacing handcrafted or LLM-sampled curricula that rely on semantic plausibility rather than feasibility, producing better-targeted training task distributions.

entry.title: Cross-Market Meta-Learning for Electricity Price Forecasting

author.name: Delaram Pirhayatifard, Terrence Alsup

entry.summary: MetaGrid is a topology-aware transformer meta-trained across multiple electricity markets, treating cross-ISO history as a pretraining corpus to overcome the data limits of single-market forecasting. By exploiting shared physics and market design, a single model adapts to new markets while capturing network-topology-driven spatial dependencies. This addresses saturation of per-market statistical and tree baselines.

entry.title: Foundation Models for Event Prediction Across Heterogeneous Event Logs

author.name: Fabian Spaeh, Sean Jaffe, Shandian Zhe, Bin Shen

entry.summary: The Foundation Event Predictor (FEP) is an in-context architecture for next-event prediction across heterogeneous event logs from business processes, manufacturing, and healthcare. It uses causal self-attention to encode context and target histories into key/query representations with learned event-level nonparametric inference, aiming to generalize to unseen systems with different label spaces and temporal scales.

entry.title: Morphology-aware deep learning predicts colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images

author.name: Hikmat Khan, Metin N. Gurcan, Anil Parwani, Wendy L. Frankel, Wei Chen, Muhammad Khalid Khan Niazi

entry.summary: MorphContrast is a morphology-aware contrastive multiple-instance learning framework for predicting five-year colorectal cancer survival from H&E whole-slide images, using tissue labels as structural supervision alongside gated-attention pooling and auxiliary objectives. It is developed on Alliance/CALGB 89803 (n=424) with external validation on SurGen (n=218) after morphology analysis on TCGA-COAD/READ.

entry.title: FASHION-RQ: Mining Hierarchical Semantic Structure for Automated Evaluation of Fashion Retrieval

author.name: Tripti Shukla, Shwetha Somasundaram, Akshat Gupta, Rohit Garg, Paul Duff, Ian Anderson

entry.summary: FASHION-RQ automatically derives user-style queries and relevance sets for fashion retrieval evaluation from catalog structure, using hierarchical discrete representations from RQ-VAE to identify semantically coherent product clusters. This replaces manual curation and synthetic prompts with scalable, semantically grounded benchmark generation.

entry.title: Visual Dependence Does Not Imply Answerability: A Systematic Analysis of Answerability Signals in Frozen InstructBLIP

author.name: Minjun Kim, Hyunmin Song, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates which signals from a frozen vision-language model reliably indicate whether a visual question is answerable, covering predictive uncertainty, cross-modal alignment, grounding, visual dependence, internal representations, and learned probes on a 10K subset of UNK-VQA with InstructBLIP. The negative headline result is that answerability discrimination remains weak, with AUROC largely between 0.50 and 0.54.

entry.title: inLoRA-MINT: Internal Representations for Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs

author.name: Gonzalo Mancera, Julian Fierrez, Aythami Morales, Ruben Tolosana, Daniel DeAlcala, Francisco Jurado

entry.summary: The paper extends the Membership Inference Test (MINT) to LoRA fine-tuned LLMs, using intermediate representations such as activations and parameter-dependent signals to determine whether specific samples were used in training. Building on a prior perplexity-only black-box framework, this approach improves auditing without requiring full parameter access. It was evaluated on four LLMs including Qwen, Phi-4, and LLaMA 3.2-3B.

entry.title: Certifying Almost-Sure Reachability in Unknown MDPs

author.name: S Akshay, Suguman Bansal, Gaurav Mahla

entry.summary: The paper studies the dual of specification-guided RL: verifying that a given policy satisfies an almost-sure reachability specification in an unknown MDP using only sampling access. Its first result is negative - without extra information, certificates based on ranking supermartingales can neither be learned nor verified. The paper then characterizes conditions under which verification becomes possible, relevant to safety-critical systems.

entry.title: LiFUSE: Frequency-Spatial Unified Self-Supervised Pretraining for Liver Disease Analysis on Non-contrast CT

author.name: Hao Zhang, Yi Huang, Wei Liu, Yuan Gao, Zeju Li, Xu Han, Yu Shi, Ling Zhang, Ke Yan

entry.summary: LiFUSE introduces a frequency-and-spatial unified self-supervised pretraining method for non-contrast CT, targeting tumor detection and fine-grained liver disease diagnosis where low tissue contrast makes analysis hard. The work is clinically motivated by the growing use of low-cost opportunistic NCCT screening.

entry.title: Agaram 2.5B: The First Tamil-First Language Model Trained from Scratch with Tool Calling. A Playbook for Under-Represented Languages

author.name: Ramchand Kumaresan, Madhusudhanan G, Kaushik Kezendirane

entry.summary: The authors train Agaram 2.5B, a 2.5B-parameter Tamil-English model from scratch on roughly 50 billion tokens using a single node of eight H100s in about six days, and fine-tune it into a chat model supporting Tamil script, romanized Tamil, and tool calling. The paper frames the effort as a reproducible playbook for building models for under-represented languages. It outperforms Sarvam-1 on translation despite its modest scale.

entry.title: EgoOmniWorld: Unifying Egocentric Understanding via Ego-Action-World Interactions

author.name: Songruo Chen, Yuqian Fu, Yu Li, Mingkang Dong, Sifan Zhou, Bin Ren, Xu Zheng, Tianwen Qian, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: The authors propose an Ego-Action-World interaction loop as a unifying principle for egocentric video understanding and introduce EgoOmniWorld, a benchmark structured around nodes, edges, chains, and loops capturing perception-action feedback. It includes an interaction-first, evidence-grounded data pipeline. This addresses the fragmentation of egocentric capability evaluation.

entry.title: From Relation-Specific Heads to Shared Interventions: Contextual Entrainment in Language Models

author.name: Jinghan Zheng, Jiajun Shi

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper investigates contextual entrainment, where language models reuse irrelevant tokens from earlier prompt context when answering later queries. Using factual-distractor relation-completion prompts across 19 lexical-semantic subtypes, the authors show that ablation-identified attention heads are not isolated per relation but are components shared across relations, suggesting common underlying mechanisms.

entry.title: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction

author.name: Khoren Petrosyan, Artashes Mkrtchyan, Rafayel Mkrtchyan, Hrant Khachatrian, Theofanis P. Raptis

entry.summary: The authors build a pipeline generating 128M synthetic samples for indoor radio-map prediction via an automatic indoor layout generator and a fast open-source approximate ray tracer, then pretrain and fine-tune ResNet-101 and Swin-T models. Despite simulator mismatch, pretraining reduces error by about 15% on average versus prior baselines.

entry.title: Adaptive Computation with Conformal Certification

author.name: Shehtab Zaman, Aneesh Rangnekar, Nancy Lee, Harini Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: Introduces adaptive computation for large scientific and medical imaging data that allocates compute based on prediction uncertainty, combined with conformal guarantees, addressing limits of uniform efficiency techniques like quantization and pruning. This targets sparsely distributed objects in huge radiological and astronomical images.

entry.title: FinGREAT: Evaluating LLMs on Financial Graph-guided Retrieval And Typing

author.name: Ashman Mehra, Bryan Routledge, Jane JaeYeon Pyo, Pierre Jinghong Liang

entry.summary: Presents FinGREAT, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can extract and classify evidence corresponding to double-entry accounting relationships in financial disclosures, using an 11-node accounting graph over 1,300 SEC 10-K filings spanning 26 years. It compares mid-sized open-weight models from 5 families against proprietary models, revealing substantial performance differences.

entry.title: Fully sequential Gaussian process regression for preference learning

author.name: Ilya O. Ryzhov

entry.summary: This paper develops a fully sequential Gaussian process approach for optimization from noisy pairwise comparisons, using moment-matching to obtain fast closed-form posterior updates. It proposes DOVE, a sequential sampling policy combining information gain with randomized error control, and proves convergence rates for statistical and expected improvement regret. This advances preference-based optimization theory and practice.

entry.title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents

author.name: Yuanpu Cao, Saket Sathe, Hanyu Wang, Ziyi Yin, Fenglong Ma, Jinghui Chen

entry.summary: The paper tackles progress stagnation in distilled small language model agents, which get trapped in unproductive loops on long interaction trajectories. It proposes progress-aware distillation that transfers agentic capabilities while explicitly addressing loop behavior, improving efficiency of SLM agents relative to large-model agent systems. This is relevant to making agentic systems cheaper and more deployable.

entry.title: Learning Across Temporal Graph Representation Silos

author.name: Minwoo Yu, Young-guk Ha

entry.summary: This study examines whether predictive structures learned from relational histories can be transferred between continuous-time dynamic graphs and temporal knowledge graphs, two typically siloed temporal graph representations. The authors find bidirectional knowledge reuse is possible even with independent vocabularies, and that same-representation sources are not always more useful. This clarifies when temporal graph learning can leverage cross-representation data.

entry.title: Annealed L\'{e}vy Diffusion via Gaussian Surrogate Reverse Dynamics

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Cheng Yuan, Ruizhe Zhang

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes Annealed Lévy Diffusion (ALD), an extension of denoising Lévy probabilistic models that varies the noise stability index over time, combining heavy-tailed exploration early in denoising with Gaussian refinement later. By representing stable noise as a Gaussian scale mixture, the method allows standard Gaussian noise-prediction training with only one added scale input, and the authors introduce two sampling schemes (ALD-renoise and ALD-posterior) with theoretical grounding.

entry.title: Learning Who Benefits Most: Multi-Treatment Causal Ranking for Population Health Stratification

author.name: Rocco Zaccagnino, Martina Girolamo, Alberto Lombardi, Delfina Malandrino, Donatello Telesca, Alessia Ture

entry.summary: PROMETHEUS formulates population health stratification as a multi-treatment causal ranking problem, ordering patient-treatment opportunities by expected incremental benefit rather than requiring perfectly calibrated individual treatment effects. Applied to care intensification decisions under constrained resources, it extends frameworks like the Italian DM77. This connects causal ML to practical healthcare resource prioritization.

entry.title: Safe-FCL: Continual Risk Awareness and Fine-Grained Safety Aggregation for Federated Continual Learning of LLMs

author.name: Shuaijie Ma, Yongkang Hu, Yu Cheng, Jiuan Zhou, Yi Xie, Yushuo Zhang, Zhaoxia Yin

entry.summary: Safe-FCL defends federated fine-tuning of LLMs against evolving malicious client updates by combining a Continual Risk Awareness mechanism that learns emerging risk patterns across sequential tasks with a protective subspace preventing detector forgetting, plus fine-grained safety aggregation. It addresses the underexplored intersection of federated learning, continual learning, and LLM safety. This is relevant as federated LLM customization scales.

entry.title: Rethinking Prediction Horizons: Decoupling Model Queries from State Updates in Few-Step MeanFlow

author.name: Tinglan Wang, Haixu Liu, Shaobo Chen, Nuo Qian, Qi Gao, Kai Wen, Yu Yao

entry.summary: The authors decouple the interval queried from a MeanFlow generative model from the duration of the state update during few-step sampling, finding that the optimal prediction horizon depends on query position and input states. Experiments across seven CIFAR-10 checkpoints show longer horizons hurt FID early but help at the midpoint, with control experiments probing the role of classifier-free guidance.

entry.title: Training Dynamics of Transformers on Unbounded Inputs: Attention Learning Can Lag Output Layer Learning

author.name: Yaomengxi Han, Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

entry.summary: The paper provides theoretical analysis of shallow transformer training dynamics on unbounded-length inputs, showing that the assumed sequence of learning attention first via a single gradient step and then the output layer fails for recognizing star-free languages. It proves that attention learning can lag output layer learning, refining the one-gradient-step feature learning theory. This deepens understanding of why transformers train the way they do on variable-length inputs.

entry.title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

author.name: Jin-Jia Zheng, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: Proposes a two-level framework for prioritizing nearly 100,000 disease-trajectory branching motifs mined from longitudinal MIMIC-IV electronic health records, separating semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Motifs are textualized, embedded, and calibrated against a large corpus of pre-2023 PubMed references to estimate novelty. This addresses the practical problem of filtering graph-mined EHR patterns down to those worth clinical follow-up.

entry.title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations

author.name: Wonjae Lee, Jiuk Jang, Hyungbin Park

entry.summary: Establishes a Wong-Zakai convergence theorem for stochastic Volterra integral equations driven by piecewise-linear Brownian approximations, and uses this foundation to train mirror-padded Fourier neural operators on the solution operator mapping initial conditions and noise to full trajectories. Experiments show competitive accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those seen in training. Bridges stochastic analysis theory with neural operator learning for memory-dependent random systems.

entry.title: Physical Layer Anomaly Detection via Adaptive Gaussian Mixture Model

author.name: Mamady Delamou, Luan Chen, Arsenia Chorti

entry.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive Gaussian mixture model framework for detecting physical-layer spoofing attacks on wireless localization systems, where attackers manipulate channel state information (CSI) and are hard to distinguish when spatially close to the legitimate node. It validates the detector on a massive MIMO dataset with 64-antenna uniform linear arrays at 5 mm spatial resolution. It matters because wireless localization security is increasingly critical as position-sensitive applications proliferate.

entry.title: Multi-Sensitive Distributional Fairness: Joint Wasserstein Audits and Shapley Allocation

author.name: Agathe Fernandes Machado, Charlotte Jamotton, Arthur Charpentier

entry.summary: The paper studies fairness audits involving multiple sensitive attributes simultaneously, showing that one-attribute-at-a-time audits can miss purely intersectional disparities. Using one-dimensional Wasserstein geometry, the authors develop distributional demographic parity measures, including a construction based on conditional quantile functions whose variance captures the joint disparity, plus a Shapley-style allocation of the disparity. This provides a mathematically principled way to audit intersectional fairness in real-valued scoring systems.

entry.title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning

author.name: Hongrui Sheng, Shutian Liang, Reid A. Coyle, Shyam Chand Pal, Peter Walther, Bin Feng, Xinyu Ding, Zhiling Zheng
