entry.summary: ActMOF introduces an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing active-learning and Bayesian optimization strategies in aluminum-carboxylate metal-organic framework synthesis, emulated from measured microwave syntheses with crystallinity indices. It addresses the lack of benchmarks for comparing search strategies in materials synthesis. This enables principled selection of optimizers for chemistry experiment planning.

entry.title: A Graph-Based Analysis of Comparability, Scale, and Attribution in Private Transformer Inference

author.name: Souvik Das, Ariful Azad, Nitesh Saxena

entry.summary: The paper systematizes private Transformer inference (PTI) by constructing an empirical graph of 62 systems, mapping attributes to nodes and evaluation compatibility to edges, then analyzing attribution, comparability, and scale of reported gains. It finds cryptographic progress drives performance across systems but always co-occurs with confounds like model fidelity, hardware, and cost accounting. This brings much-needed evaluation rigor to a fast-moving subfield.

entry.title: Learning Individual Scientific Taste with Privileged Hindsight Distillation

author.name: Hanwei Fan, Yanqiao Wang, Yiqi Zhu, Xuanyu Lei, Peng Li, Yang Liu

entry.summary: The paper models individual researchers' scientific taste as a personalized mapping from evidence-grounded criterion assessments to preference rankings, using a population-level cold-start and a Privileged Hindsight Distillation method. This could support personalized research-direction recommendation for AI-assisted science.

entry.title: The minimal width of neural networks and immersions of real projective space

author.name: BaoZhi Chu, Ben Weinkove

entry.summary: This theory paper proves lower bounds on the minimal width of deep networks approximating continuous functions on compact sets, connecting the question to whether real projective space admits a smooth immersion into Euclidean space. It establishes that ReLU network minimal width is n+m for specific dimensions, extending prior results via differential topology.

entry.title: MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA

author.name: Junyi Zou, Avrova Donz

entry.summary: The paper presents MMLA-RSI, a recursive self-improvement scheme in a Memory-Mediated Learning Architecture where Reasoning-Time Training updates the policy and Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation updates memory, with each route also improving its own adaptation method. Successor updaters are admitted independently across generations within bounded executable rule languages.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Multilingual Abstractive Summarization: A Comprehensive Study of English and Bengali

author.name: Khan Mahi Al Atahar, Nazifa Tasneem, Ajwad Abrar

entry.summary: This benchmark study evaluates eight closed and open-weight LLMs zero-shot on size-matched English and Bengali XL-Sum test sets, combining lexical and semantic metrics with reference-free factuality checks and LLM-as-a-Judge assessment. Results show substantial cross-lingual variation: GPT-5.6 Luna, an existing OpenAI model, leads English lexical metrics but loses its advantage in Bengali. It highlights persistent low-resource language gaps in summarization quality and factual consistency.

entry.title: PersEvalBench: Can LLM Evaluators Judge Contextually Appropriate Use of Persona Information?

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Hooshang Nayyeri, Emine Yilmaz, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Charith Peris, Hari Thadakamalla

entry.summary: PersEvalBench tests whether LLM evaluators can reliably judge appropriate versus inappropriate use of user history in personalized assistants, using 403 multi-episode scenarios spanning under-personalization, over-personalization, and misapplied-state errors across nine error subtypes. Results across five evaluators show limited recognition of controllable personalization errors.

entry.title: PA1-OPD: One-Step Prefix-Augmented On-Policy Distillation for Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Zhenhe Wu, Jian Yang, Yaping Jin, Xinlai Kang, Jie Hu, Hanting Chen

entry.summary: PA1-OPD augments corpus-path knowledge distillation for pretraining with teacher feedback after one student-sampled transition per prefix, expanding supervised states while retaining next-token prediction and corpus-path KD. Using data-anchored roots for parallel sampling and differentiable tree attention, it improves held-out cross-entropy over KD across C4, PG-19, and Pile in continued-pretraining settings.

entry.title: Does the Linguistic Register of Thinking Matter? Wenyan as a Compact Reasoning Register for Chinese LLMs

author.name: Minghan Li, Guodong Zhou

entry.summary: Explores whether emitting chain-of-thought in Classical Chinese (wenyan) improves reasoning efficiency for Chinese LLMs, fine-tuning Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 on register-rewritten traces with a compact modern-Chinese control to isolate register shift from generic compression. Results are evaluated across budget-sensitive settings.

entry.title: EGCForest: Structured Agent Memory Organization for Enterprise Group Chats

author.name: Lingxi Cui, Jinhao Ruan, Wenqing Wei, Guo Yi, Li Rao, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: Presents EGCForest, a multi-view hierarchical memory framework for enterprise group chats that organizes an immutable message log into Channel, Actor, and Artifact forests to capture temporal workflows, speaker-conditioned context, and deliverable lifecycles. It addresses retrieval failures of chunk-based RAG and summary-based memory for distributed evidence.

entry.title: Anuvani-LID: Robust and Calibrated Spoken Language Identification for Indian Languages

author.name: Stephen Fernandes, Narayan Choudhary

entry.summary: This work examines whether modern speech models genuinely possess latent language identification capability across India's 22 scheduled languages spanning four language families under short, noisy, code-mixed conditions. The authors find major gaps, such as Whisper-family models having language tokens for only 15 of 23 tested languages and Gemini 3.5 Flash reaching only 0.52 macro-F1 on one-second inputs, and propose Anuvani-LID as a robust and calibrated LID solution. Reliable LID matters because errors propagate silently through downstream recognition, translation, and routing pipelines.

entry.title: DivAlgo: A systematic evaluation of algorithmic diversity for code generation models

author.name: Anubhav Jangra, Smaranda Muresan

entry.summary: DivAlgo is a benchmark of algorithmically diverse solutions to programming problems plus a lightweight similarity metric enabling large-scale evaluation of code diversity. Across 24 code generation models, uncontrolled generations capture only about 31% of human solution diversity, and the best steering strategies reach about 70%, revealing a substantial gap.

entry.title: SEA-HELM Audio: Evaluating Multilingual ASR-LLM Pipeline Performance Across SEA-HELM Subsets

author.name: Yixian Tan, Aulia Adila, Jonathan Heng, Kunat Pipatanakul, Donghang Wu, Anocha Sutaveephamochanon

entry.summary: SEA-HELM Audio extends the text-based SEA-HELM benchmark to measure degradation in cascaded ASR-LLM pipelines across five Southeast Asian languages, comparing speech-input and text-input accuracy on reasoning and instruction-following tasks. The study finds substantial speech gaps of 9 to 18.5 percentage points, quantifying a real weakness in deployed voice pipelines.

entry.title: Robust Real-Time Monocular Human Pose Estimation with Insole-Based Sensor Fusion

author.name: Liang Yu, Tao Zhu, Xiangqing Lu, Wenjian Luo, Liming Chen

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether unobtrusive smart-insole pressure and acceleration sensors can resolve monocular pose estimation failures during lower-body occlusion and out-of-frame intervals. It systematically studies sensor fusion to improve physically plausible lower-limb reconstruction and foot-ground contact estimation in real time.

entry.title: MicroSDF: Microfacet-Driven Hybrid Neural SDFs for Mixed-Reflectance Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Lejia Ye, Yuhua Xu, Yulan Guo, Lian Xu, Xiaohu Zhang

entry.summary: MicroSDF is a neural implicit framework for 3D reconstruction that jointly handles reflective and non-reflective surfaces using microfacet theory. It extracts multi-scale surface normals from a signed distance field and regularizes them with a new microfacet normal consistency loss for physically plausible geometry and reflectance.

entry.title: VisibilitySplat: Ray-Traced Occlusion for Relighting with 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Sven Kluge, Oliver Staadt

entry.summary: VisibilitySplat augments the standard rasterized 3DGS inverse-rendering pipeline with a sparse visibility oracle that estimates transmittance-weighted occlusion from sampled lighting directions, implemented with a BVH-accelerated point-based ray tracer. Shading uses a physically based microfacet BRDF formulation while retaining the 3DGS rasterization loop for training efficiency.

entry.title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing

author.name: Zhengjie Xu, Ruihao Gong, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: DreamHMR adapts video generation pretraining priors for human mesh recovery, including fine hand articulation under occlusion in real-world scenes. It uses a global-to-local strategy that first grounds video representations in human geometry, then refines body and hand details with reliable local evidence.

entry.title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation

author.name: Yuheng Chen, Yufan Chen, Zhuojun Cai, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiale Wei, Di Wen, Weijia Fan, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: The authors introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset and benchmark requiring models to produce a single page-level parse with bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized text, and alt-text descriptions of visual elements. This bridges fragmented document understanding evaluations and tests semantic accessibility of figures and captions, not just structure.

entry.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action

author.name: Ao Liang, Youquan Liu, Mingxiao Li, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Yue Liao, Dongyue Lu, Yu Yang, Wei Yin, Runnan Chen

entry.summary: VITAL derives driving action targets directly from visual motion within world-action models, coupling a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual tokenizer encoding the trajectory error the scaffold leaves. This makes visual motion the primary source of action supervision, improving precision over independently defined trajectory representations.

entry.title: A Mode-Unified, Continuous, and Biomimetic Control Strategy of a Robotic Lower Limb Prosthesis

author.name: Hanjun Kim, Sixu Zhou, John Shim, Xinyuan Guo, Kinsey R. Herrin, Aaron J. Young

entry.summary: The paper presents a prosthesis control framework representing knee and ankle biomechanics as continuous functions of terrain slope and gait phase, replacing the usual discrete per-locomotion-mode controllers. RBF interpolation unifies locally optimized models while preserving accuracy, and the resulting impedance parameters run within a single finite-state machine. This simplifies and improves biomimetic prosthetic control across walking, ramps, and stairs.

entry.title: FOMI: A Force-Feedback Manipulation Interface for Teaching Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Yishu Shen, Yiming Luo, Ruilin Wang, Bowen Yang, Shuai Yang, Fangyi Xu, Yujun Shen, Fu Zhang, Boyu Zhou, Yinghao Xu

entry.summary: FOMI is a handheld demonstration-collection interface with a scissor-shaped mechanism that transmits object interaction forces directly to the operator without force sensors, supporting intuitive real-time adjustment during robot-free collection of contact-rich demonstrations. It is embedded in a full demonstration-collection system including sensor calibration and data acquisition.

entry.title: Learning-Based Adaptive MPC for Magnetorquer-Only Satellite Attitude Control

author.name: Patrick Schwartz, Abhishek Cauligi

entry.summary: This paper presents a learning-based adaptive model predictive control algorithm for nanosatellite attitude control using only magnetorquers, accounting for their loss of control authority. A learned magnetic field model, trained in simulation with low-fidelity data, replaces the need for full planetary magnetic field knowledge in planning.

entry.title: CoWear: Towards Collaborative Wearable Inertial Localization with Multiple Smart Devices

author.name: Zhuoyuan She, Zhanpeng Zhang, Yapeng Chen, Jiale Wang, Xin Xie, Ming Xia

entry.summary: CoWear introduces a large-scale dataset and framework for collaborative inertial localization using a smartphone, smartwatch, and smart glasses worn simultaneously. It covers over 30 participants, 300 walking sessions, and 30+ hours of motion-capture-tracked trajectories, with role-specific estimators predicting displacement of a common reference device across heterogeneous body locations. It addresses a real gap in benchmarks lacking synchronized multi-device ground truth.

entry.title: The basic argument for making AI better at moral philosophy

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld crossposts

entry.summary: Caspar Oesterheld makes a structured case for investing in making AI systems better at moral philosophy, arguing it is near-competitive with the most important interventions for some scopes of work. The post defines what moral philosophy capability means, proposes concrete interventions, and addresses importance, tractability, and neglectedness, plus common objections. It serves as an archetype for a broader class of AI capability interventions.

entry.title: Agent memory the human can still audit: primary sources, epistemic status markers, and user sign-off

author.name: Florian_Dietz

entry.summary: Foresight Institute-funded work on agent memory systems designed for auditability, proposing immutable per-topic chronological LOG files as primary sources to prevent memory drift, plus epistemic status markers and user sign-off mechanisms. It contrasts these with existing tools like git history and Karpathy's log.md that are awkward for agents to use.

entry.title: AegisVox: Factorized Privacy and Clinical Preservation for Long-Form Speech

author.name: Praphul Singh, Akshat Agarwal, Ratul Ghosh, Aashna Kanuga, Devashish Khatwani, Anurag Dwarakanath, Sri Gadde, Krishnaram Kenthapadi

entry.summary: AegisVox is a factorized framework for de-identifying long-form clinical speech, assigning consistent surrogate voices and editing identifier-bearing turns with document-consistent replacements. Evaluated on 390 conversations (63.6 hours), it disentangles replacement realization from speaker linkage and clinical signal preservation, comparing TTS rendering against codec-based speech editing.

entry.title: Bridging Risk Approximation Gaps in Model Predictive Task Sampling via In-Context Modeling

author.name: Jiarong Wen, Qi Tao, Kaiyu Zhang, Yun Qu, Lizhou Cai, Heming Zou, Yuhang Jiang, Qi Wang

entry.summary: The paper improves model predictive task sampling for RL and LLM post-training by addressing two failure modes of risk predictive models: sparse optimization histories and estimation gaps. It uses in-context modeling to generalize risk estimates across the task space, improving sample efficiency in meta-RL, domain randomization, and LLM training settings.

entry.title: SkillForgeBench: Evaluating Agent Reliability Grounded in Agent Skill Specifications

author.name: Zhengxi Li, Junyi Zhou, Qiyuan Zhang, Chuhan Wu, Fuyuan Lyu, Le Tian, Xiao Zhou, Chen Ma, Yufei Wang

entry.summary: SkillForgeBench uses agent skill specifications as execution blueprints to build an evaluation benchmark balancing broad domain coverage with deep procedural complexity, via three co-designed stages covering resource preparation, task construction, and reliability scoring. It targets measuring whether agents can strictly satisfy procedurally complex requirements.

entry.title: Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking

author.name: Zhimeng Jiang, Yuening Li, Ruixiao Sun, Yuanzhen Lin, Kun Jin, Chuan He, Liang Liu

entry.summary: CDS introduces chain length as a new scaling dimension for recommendation rankers: a single feature-interaction block with shared parameters is applied repeatedly, adding no new parameters, with a residual connection for stability. It supports a compression regime (shallow blocks, long chains) and quality gains at fixed parameters, deployed in industrial short-video ranking.

entry.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yuchen Lu, Julian McAuley, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: CarryOn is an object-oriented context runtime that organizes long-horizon agent context around reusable task objects and continuation carriers rather than compressed interaction histories. It maintains a live tail of recent interactions alongside a structured view of durable task progress. This matters because context management is a central constraint for agents operating over long horizons.

entry.title: MRFlow: Mechanism-Structured Residual Flow Matching for Virtual Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Haojie Yang, Ran Su

entry.summary: MRFlow treats virtual-cell perturbation prediction as conditional transport between empirical single-cell distributions, using a variational latent state space and a mechanism-structured residual flow-matching vector field to move control cell populations toward perturbed ones. Unlike models that predict average expression shifts, it can represent rare states, resistant subpopulations, and context-dependent effect sizes. This aligns generative modeling more closely with perturbation biology.

entry.title: Is the Future Predictable? Modeling Future Predictability for Reliable Temporal Reasoning

author.name: Yongyi Huang, Huaping Zhang, Wenyao Cui, Qiuchi Li, Lei Li, Baohua Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces ChronoRegime, a temporal reasoning task requiring models to judge whether historical evidence justifies commitment to a future answer, plus Confidence-Aware Temporal Reasoning (CTR), which regulates answer commitment based on estimated future predictability. CTR commits only when reconstructed evidence supports the target future state.

entry.title: Beyond Gate Weights: Decision-Level Interpretation of Radiomics-Image Feature Fusion for RCC Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell

entry.summary: This work shows that gate coefficients in a fused radiomics-image classifier do not necessarily reflect branch contributions at the decision output. Exploiting a linear classification head on a 3D MedVAE-radiomics model for renal cell carcinoma, the authors exactly decompose the decision logit and define an effective radiomics dominance measure that can differ substantially from structural gate weighting.

entry.title: AlignAudio: A Unified Dual-Alignment Framework for Noise-Robust Speech-Conditioned Generation

author.name: Yixuan Li, Xuenan Xu, Zeyu Xie, Mengyue Wu

entry.summary: Proposes AlignAudio, a noise-robust speech-conditioned generation framework based on dual alignment: aligning representations of clean and noisy speech to preserve semantics, and enforcing generation-level consistency within a flow matching paradigm to improve conditioning fidelity under noisy inputs.

entry.title: Select or Rewrite: Oracle-Guided Fine-Tuning for Generative ASR Post-Editing from N-Best Hypotheses

author.name: Shiran Liu, Gaohui Xu, Sergio Burdisso, Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Petr Motlicek

entry.summary: The paper proposes oracle-guided fine-tuning for LLM-based ASR post-editing, constructing three supervision pools: corrections for selection, regularizers where top-1 is correct to discourage over-editing, and hard negatives where the reference is absent to suppress hallucination. This curated supervision outperforms random subset fine-tuning and fixes brittleness of prompt-only correction.

entry.title: Anchor-and-Harvest Curriculum: A Fully Unmasked Non-LLM Curriculum for Craftax

author.name: Jiayu Zhu, Luyuan Li, Yuyuan Shi, Hanyi Dong

entry.summary: AHC is a domain-informed, rule-based curriculum for the Craftax-Full RL benchmark that combines achievement-oriented tasks, harvested initial-state progress, difficulty adaptation, bounded task selection, and original-task practice, using no LLM inference and keeping all 43 actions available. Three primary runs achieve native-task return of 46.70 versus 41.91 for fresh PPO-GTrXL at 2 billion rollout transitions, evaluated on 1024 fixed worlds with ablations. It demonstrates curated curricula can beat LLM-generated task curricula in hard exploration.

entry.title: bharatSetu: a 1M x 22 bridge for indic translation

author.name: Haq Nawaz Malik, Nahfid Nissar, Faizan Iqbal

entry.summary: BharatSetu is a row-aligned resource of roughly 985K English sentences each machine-translated into all 22 Eighth Schedule Indian languages (~21.7M cells), enabling 506 directed translation pairs including low-resource pairs like Bodo, Dogri, Santali, and Kashmiri that lack direct bitext. A confidence layer lets users filter pivot-derived pairs.

entry.title: MixLID: Token-Level Language Identification in Mixed-Language Text

author.name: Seongtae Hong, Youngjoon Jang, Seungyoon Lee, Jungseob Lee, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: MixLID is a token-level language identification model covering 111 language-script combinations, trained in two stages: monolingual language discrimination followed by training on mixed-language data using code-switching corpora and loanword-based word-substitution augmentation. It outperforms baselines on monolingual identification and handles code-switched text.

entry.title: Audit Before You Distill: A Controlled Workflow for Reasoning Transfer into Compact Medical Language Models

author.name: Tiago Martinelli, Jo\~ao Paulo Papa, Adriano Jos\'e Pereira

entry.summary: The authors audit how teacher rationales affect a student model answering Brazilian Portuguese medical residency exam questions, finding correct rationales raise correct-answer probability by 21 percentage points while wrong ones lower it by 14. They use this audit to guide selective distillation into compact medical language models.

entry.title: MAGNET: Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network for Connectome Generation

author.name: Protyay Dey, Ayush Roy, Hyuna Cho, Won Hwa Kim, Vishnu Suresh Lokhande

entry.summary: Proposes MAGNET, a graph diffusion network that generates functional brain connectomes using a normalized-Cholesky representation of the correlation-matrix manifold to guarantee matrix validity, with relational denoising over brain regions and class-anchored techniques to recover class-conditional geometry beneath coarse labels.

entry.title: Dissociating Answerability from Extraction in LLM Question Answering over Radiology Reports

author.name: Priyanshu Sinha, Kelsey McDonald

entry.summary: The paper proposes an evaluation method for RadQA-style clinical QA that separates answerability decisions from span extraction, reporting false-answer and over-abstention rates alongside F1. Applying it to 13 LLMs shows that models with similar F1 differ more than twofold in false-answer rates, and that adding an unanswerable demonstration changes when models answer rather than how well they extract.

entry.title: Dynamic K-Head: Difficulty-Supervised Budget Selection for Continuous Latent Reasoning

author.name: Ying Li, Yuqi Chen, Sixuan Li, Yunfeng Cai

entry.summary: Dynamic K-Head introduces a question-conditioned, pre-rollout selector for the number of latent reasoning updates in continuous chain-of-thought, jointly trained with the reasoner using difficulty supervision from question-only scores. It also highlights that latent-update counts can misrepresent end-to-end cost when short latent rollouts shift computation into longer explicit continuations.

entry.title: LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers

author.name: Wei Fan, Qingyue Yang, Chao-Hong Tan, Qian Chen, Wen Wang, Xiangang Li, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: LoOPSD explores whether self-distillation guidance can come from changing how a model uses its own layers rather than from extra context: it searches over layer execution orders (repeating layers with weights frozen) to construct a stronger teacher, then distills its predictions on student-generated prefixes. Search and distillation alternate iteratively. This is a novel take on self-improvement exploiting looped/adaptive computation.

entry.title: Graph-free Retrieval with Graph-Modified Embeddings

author.name: Federica Santi (Cognee Inc), Vasilije Markovi\'{c} (Cognee Inc), Daniel Scott (Cognee Inc), Lazar Obradovi\'{c} (Cognee Inc)

entry.summary: This paper compares five offline graph-based embedding transformations that let dense retrieval recover evidence connected through intermediate entities without query-time graph access. A multi-stage strategy that uses graph-modified embeddings to guide search while retaining originals improves evidence recovery, notably on linked-fact and comparison questions.

entry.title: Knowledge Graphs as Files: An Agent Harness Where Tool Creation and Tool Use Co-Evolve

author.name: Yuyang Bai, Yu Wang, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: DKGI is an agent harness in which LLM agents write Python tools directly over complete knowledge-graph node and edge files, interleaving execution feedback with shell search and file inspection so tool creation and use co-evolve. This bypasses restrictive predefined graph interfaces and enables bulk processing of large node sets. It improves how agents access text-rich knowledge graphs.

entry.title: IR-PRM+ with Previous-Utility Prediction: Constant Regret and Best-Iterate Convergence

author.name: Michael Sullins, Ian A. Kash

entry.summary: This paper extends IREG-PRM+, a regret-matching variant with strong convergence guarantees, to optimistic and alternating update schemes via a new previous-utility prediction analysis. It provides constant regret and best-iterate convergence results for game-solving algorithms used in normal-form and extensive-form settings.

entry.title: TEX-MEX: Similarity-Guided Temporal Contrastive Learning for Time Series

author.name: Aditya Radhakrishnan, Maxwell A. Xu, Wanting Mao, Santosh Kumar, Harish Haresamudram, James M. Rehg

entry.summary: TEX-MEX unifies structural and temporal notions of similarity in time-series contrastive learning by using the encoder to identify structurally similar windows and pulling each window toward temporally shifted versions of structurally similar samples while pushing away dissimilar ones. This addresses the difficulty of designing meaningful augmentations for time series. It is demonstrated with credible authorship spanning mobile-health and HAR contexts.

entry.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM

author.name: Alessia Rossi, Felipe Campelo, Gabriel L. Oliveira

entry.summary: CAP-SAM replaces Sharpness-Aware Minimization's fixed perturbation radius with a curvature-aware adaptive scheme, reinterpreting the radius as perturbation signal intensity that should vary with local geometry. This avoids the failure modes of too-small perturbations failing to escape sharp basins and too-large perturbations hurting convergence. Improving SAM's efficiency and generalization has broad relevance across deep learning.

entry.title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes

author.name: Stavros Nousias, Akis Nousias, Konstantinos Gkrispanis

entry.summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts architecture for steady PDE surrogates in which a discrete Hodge Laplacian partitions the solution among transformer experts specializing in different spectral scales, with a mesh-conditioned gate recombining per-vertex outputs. Evaluated on a RANS airfoil benchmark (AirFRANS) on coarse unstructured meshes. Combines discrete differential geometry with MoE scaling for engineering surrogate modeling.

entry.title: Structure-aware Bayesian full waveform inversion via diffusion-regularized Stein variational gradient descent

author.name: Chao Li, Mrinal K. Sen, Sergey Fomel, Yangkang Chen

entry.summary: This work enhances annealed Stein variational gradient descent for Bayesian full waveform inversion by replacing handcrafted Gaussian/smoothing priors with diffusion-model priors that capture complex geological structures, approximating the posterior with an ensemble of velocity models for uncertainty quantification. This improves robustness to inaccurate initial models and noisy, incomplete seismic data. Relevant to geophysics and as a case study in learned priors for Bayesian inverse problems.

entry.title: Typed Decision Models on Tabular Data

author.name: Baowen Zhang, Hangting Ye, Hongyuan Zha

entry.summary: This paper studies typed decision models, language models that return probabilities over a fixed answer set instead of generating text, on tabular tasks including row classification, fact verification, and anomaly detection. Under 21 content-preserving rewrite types, decision models match LLM accuracy at lower cost and are substantially more robust to question reformulation, though no tested model is robust to table reorganization. The robustness findings are notable for anyone deploying models on tabular data.

entry.title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators

author.name: Meenakshi Krishnan, You Zhang, Ramani Duraiswami, C. Phillip Brown

entry.summary: SPARO formulates head-related transfer function upsampling as operator learning, mapping sparse spatial measurements to a continuous HRTF field queryable at arbitrary directions via learned spherical latent modes and Transformer processing. It achieves the best log-spectral distortion and interaural level difference error across sparsity levels on the SONICOM dataset.

entry.title: Evaluating Compressed Memory: Dependence, Utility, and Content Benefit

author.name: Minsu Oh, Seunghui Jwa, Chanjun Park, Yeo-Chan Yoon

entry.summary: The paper critiques standard evaluation of compressed-memory language models, showing that zeroing memory vectors can lower scores without proving the memory actually beats a memory-free alternative. Across nine systems, some memory-dependent models perform worse than models trained without memory, with evidence from story-state prediction and TriviaQA/xRAG experiments.

entry.title: Beyond Reachability: A Relation-Semantic Reasoning Framework for Biomedical Multi-hop QA

author.name: Ziyang Ling, Ziyi Chen, Ronald X. Xu, Mingzhai Sun

entry.summary: Identifies the reachable-but-invalid problem in biomedical knowledge-graph multi-hop QA, where retrieved answers lack evidentially valid relation paths. ReSemReason shares a question-induced distribution over typed relation schemas between candidate discovery and evidence selection, using schema compatibility to guide search and a ReSemAttn attention mechanism.

entry.title: Not All Criteria Matter: Importance-Aware Criteria Weighting for Rubric-Based LLM Evaluation

author.name: Haocheng Yang, Licheng Pan, Yiming Dong, Xiaoxi Li, Yuan Lu, Zhenhao Chen, Jiajun Fan, Shuai Shao, Chunyuan Zheng, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Importance-Aware Criteria Weighting (ICW), which derives criterion weights for rubric-based LLM evaluation from pairwise importance comparisons rather than uniform weighting or unreliable holistic LLM-assigned weights. This prevents minor overlapping criteria from masking essential ones in evaluation scores.

entry.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios

author.name: Ali Zamani, Soroush Esfahanian, Erfan Shahabi, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar, Azadeh Shakery, Yadollah Yaghoobzadeh

entry.summary: PerSo is a benchmark that jointly evaluates cognitive and behavioral social intelligence of LLMs on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline rather than synthetic scenarios. It moves beyond prior work that assessed mental-state inference and social action selection in isolation.

entry.title: Adaptive Observation Control for Active Visual Recognition

author.name: Dikai Li, Weijia Wang, Yuan-Gen Wang

entry.summary: The paper extends a fixed-step active recognition pipeline (AdaptiveNN-DeiT-S) with a controllable observation interface that adapts both field of view and number of fixations per input, using per-fixation scale prediction, scale-gated foveation, a residual detail-token branch, and a label-grounded stop head. This lets recognition models allocate spatial evidence and computation adaptively.

entry.title: LiFi: LiDAR Generation from Multi-View Images via Geometric and Semantic Collaborative Guidance

author.name: Sizhuo Zhou, Xiaosong Jia, Fanrui Zhang, Qifeng Li, Junjie Li, Zirui Wang, Yukang Feng, Yu Hong, Shaofeng Zhang, Wenlong Liao, Tao He, Juyong Zhang, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: LiFi is a dedicated latent diffusion framework for generating geometrically and semantically aligned LiDAR point clouds from multi-view camera images, guided by complementary geometry and semantics branches. It targets controllable data synthesis, cross-modal simulation, and perception applications where existing monocular or semantics-only methods fall short.

entry.title: Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Konstantinos Almpanakis, Anna Kreshuk

entry.summary: The authors propose out-of-batch regularization for joint-embedding self-supervised learning, maintaining a dataset-level regularization state in CPU memory and using globally constructed per-instance targets during minibatch training. On natural image and biomedical datasets, this approximates full-dataset regularization more faithfully than minibatch estimation at small batch sizes, with consistent gains for SimCLR and SIGReg-style methods.

entry.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views

author.name: Yongzhen Hu, Hao Yu, Jiawei Wang, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Xingliang Liu, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Sida Peng

entry.summary: InfiniSplat v2 improves feed-forward Gaussian splatting reconstruction under large viewpoint changes by decoupling geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligning predicted Gaussians with ground-truth poses during training, and using large-angle target view supervision. It achieves state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS across six datasets.

entry.title: $S^3$-Nav: Structured Spatial-Semantic Decision Making for Language-Guided Robot Navigation

author.name: Chaemin Lee, Hae Min Cho

entry.summary: S3-Nav constructs persistent spatial-semantic state incrementally under partial observability and exposes only a capacity-controlled, task-conditioned view to the high-level navigation policy. High-level decisions are provisional and validated against grounded semantic evidence, decoupling what the robot retains from what the policy inspects. This structured separation addresses reliability in language-guided navigation.

entry.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google describes Earth AI, geospatial agent systems applying AI to planetary-scale challenges such as climate and environmental monitoring. The supplied content is a stub, indicating an applied AI-for-impact program announcement.

entry.title: Relational Semantic Grounding for Test-Time Discovery

author.name: Tianle Liu, Gongbo Cheng, Chenggong Ni, Minming Gu, Tao Zhou, Fuyuan Hu, Fan Lyu

entry.summary: SEGA adds interpretability to test-time discovery by using LLMs to generate attribute-rich descriptions of known classes and building an attribute-anchored visual-semantic space during training. At test time, relational semantic grounding places unknown samples relative to similar and dissimilar known-class anchors, enabling interpretable labels rather than anonymous cluster IDs.

entry.title: AlphaRLM: Aligning Language Models for Literature-Grounded Symbolic Factor Discovery

author.name: Jie Huang, Yuecheng Hong, Yao Chen, Hao Zhong, Linfeng Xiao, Xudong Liu, Hao Xia, Jianxuan Xin

entry.summary: AlphaRLM trains LLMs with reinforcement learning to construct executable symbolic alpha factors for quantitative finance from financial literature, via Literature-Guided Operator Assembly and alignment of the generation policy with market feedback. It moves beyond prompting and seed-evolution approaches to direct policy learning for factor construction.

entry.title: MoMaTune: Model, Match, Then Tune Language Models for Numerical Records

author.name: Weimin Lyu, Jingfen Zhang, Lingdao Sha, Peng sun, Xiaowei Chen, Vincent Gao, Rui Song

entry.summary: Addresses decoder LLM failures on tabular numerical data by identifying two weakly supervised structures: within-value digit-position sensitivity and across-field statistical dependence. MoMaTune introduces a model-match-tune pipeline adding auxiliary losses over the serialized measurements and their dependencies beyond target-only tuning.

entry.title: CondMSP: Condition-Informed and Resource-Aware Inorganic Materials Synthesis Planning

author.name: Heewoong Noh, Gyoung S. Na, Elton Pan, Namkyeong Lee, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: Proposes CondMSP, extending materials synthesis planning from recipe prediction to execution-aware planning that jointly predicts temperature, time, and atmosphere as process context for constructing synthesis routes. It also addresses which candidate routes should be executed under limited experimental resources. Bridges AI-driven materials discovery and experimental realization.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Pathogen Forecasts: Predicting Shared Respiratory Hospital Burden from Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV

author.name: Gaurob Saha, MinJae Woo, Lior Rennert

entry.summary: This work builds a supervised 1-to-4-week-ahead forecasting framework for combined hospital admissions from influenza, COVID-19, and RSV, comparing summing pathogen-specific forecasts against directly forecasting the combined burden target. It frames respiratory forecasting as both a target-construction and modeling problem for hospital planning.

entry.title: Constructed regional photovoltaic generation fields improve ultra-short-term distributed solar forecasting

author.name: Dayin Chen, Xiaodan Shi, Xin Xu, Zhongyue Su, Shibo Zhu, Dongxiao Zhang, Yuntian Chen, Jinyue Yan

entry.summary: SatPV-Field reformulates fleet-level solar forecasting from discrete station time series to predicting spatially structured regional photovoltaic generation fields, transforming distributed PV measurements into image-like fields. This regional-to-local approach better captures rapid local variations than external meteorological or satellite products.

entry.title: Encounter-Driven City-Scale Human Mobility Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Chao Li, Renhe Jiang, Chuan Xiao, Jiawei Wang

entry.summary: EncounterMob extends LLM-based human mobility generation beyond individual trajectories to jointly preserve population-level encounter structure, via a coarse-to-fine Encounter Generator capturing city-level encounter rhythms and an iterative coupling framework. This matters for urban planning and epidemiological modeling where co-occurrence patterns, not just individual paths, are key. It addresses a real blind spot in prior resident-centric generation work.

entry.title: Output Discipline Sets the Floor: A Falsification-Guided, Model-Agnostic Agent Protocol for Auditable Hypothesis-Driven Decision Making

author.name: Jing Liu, Yongxing Qi, Ping Yao, Ting Wu

entry.summary: Using the TCMEval-SDT benchmark for Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome differentiation, the authors show that output discipline and reasoning structure — not model scale — bind performance on auditable decision tasks, since two years of model scaling moved scores negligibly while discipline failures persisted in frontier models. They propose a model-agnostic five-stage agent loop enforced by a candidate-by-evidence falsification protocol. The finding that protocol structure dominates capability is broadly instructive for agent design.

entry.title: SemTree: Judge-Aware Semantic Decision Trees for Inspectable and Repairable Rule Decisions

author.name: Jincheng Gao, Wei Ding, Shuo Sun

entry.summary: SemTree represents rule decisions (content moderation, compliance, eligibility) as semantic decision trees where each node is a natural-language question with explicit Yes/No/Unknown criteria answered by a pluggable semantic judge. The executed path constitutes the reasoning behind each decision, enabling local repair of single nodes, replay of the rule, and conversion of corrections into judge training labels. This makes LLM-based rule application auditable and correctable.

entry.title: LabInstruct: Benchmarking Situated Instructional Video Generation for Lab Procedures

author.name: Yuming Fu, Weijia Wu, Jing Chen, Jiahao Tang, Feifei Chen, Hongyu Zhu, Xin Jin, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: LabInstruct is a benchmark for evaluating AI-generated instructional videos that guide humans executing lab procedures, positioned as a human-facing interface for self-driving laboratories. It targets fine-grained, long-horizon, visually grounded laboratory tasks where reliable full robotic automation is not yet possible.

entry.title: Coarse-Graining Recursive Expert Computation: Continuation-Relative Interfaces and Failure Modes

author.name: Shihua Yu, Yanzhi Wang, Tianchi Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents a continuation-relative evaluation framework for computational coarse-graining, where a sequence of expensive updates is replaced by a cheaper module judged by downstream task quality and execution cost. It offers an exact loss decomposition separating replacement effects and explicitly catalogs failure modes of such substitutions.

entry.title: InCLAD: A Continual Learning Benchmark for Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection

author.name: {\L}ukasz Marcjan, Dorota Wilk-Ko{\l}odziejczyk, Roberto Corizzo

entry.summary: InCLAD frames continual industrial anomaly detection as a task-incremental, semi-supervised problem where each industrial component defines a task and models must preserve performance on prior components while learning new ones. The benchmark addresses a gap left by static anomaly detection datasets that assume full supervision or isolated settings.

entry.title: GeoBridge: Evolving Transferable Decoder Topologies for Geometric Vision

author.name: Rui Wang, Haoyu Zhang, Ran Cheng

entry.summary: GeoBridge is an evolutionary neural architecture search framework for decoder topologies in geometric vision, making stage-internal topology searchable via residual, sequential, and parallel composition of primitives within a shape-preserving multi-scale scaffold. A functional-tree representation enables a decoder optimized for depth estimation to be transferred and reused for Gaussian splatting reconstruction. The work targets shared multi-scale feature processing across related geometric tasks.

entry.title: Improving the Bounds on Approximating Weighted Maximin Share for Chores

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni, J\"{o}rg Rothe

entry.summary: This theory paper improves approximation guarantees for fair allocation of indivisible chores under arbitrary positive agent weights, proving every instance admits a 4.124234528-WMMS allocation and giving a polynomial-time algorithm achieving 4.12424-WMMS for rational inputs, alongside lower-bound constructions. It advances the fair division frontier for weighted chores.

entry.title: PatTransBench: an ipc-stratified, multi-dimensional benchmark for patent machine translation evaluation

author.name: Xiaowei Su, Xusen Cheng

entry.summary: PatTransBench is a 12,000-item Chinese-English/Japanese/Korean patent machine translation benchmark with IPC-stratified sampling, covering short and long text and a four-dimensional protocol spanning n-gram metrics, cross-lingual semantic similarity, 38-probe-language consistency, and serving performance under concurrency. A case study on PatMT2-7B quantization variants reveals direction-dependent effects.

entry.title: DTA-GT: Direction- and Topology-Aware Graph Transformer for Neural Network Representation Learning

author.name: Yuxiang Zeng, Kun Xie, Yang Wang, Jigang Wen, Xiaocan Li, Guangxing Zhang, Gaogang Xie, Jiannong Cao

entry.summary: DTA-GT is a graph transformer for neural architecture representation that preserves directed computational semantics across the encoder via direction- and topology-aware node initialization, Magnetic Laplacian spectral encoding, and direction-dual mechanisms. It targets architecture attribute predictors for neural architecture search on operation-labeled DAGs.

entry.title: SonicWorld: Source-Centric Latent Dynamics for Spatial Audio Reasoning

author.name: Chenlong Wei, Hanling Wang, Mingjin Lou, Yufan Shi, Yandong Sun, Sheldon Yu, Xiaohui Zhu, Xiaobo Jin, Yiwei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Sonic-Bench, a spatial audio reasoning benchmark with 2.8K first-order Ambisonics clips and 28.8K question-answer pairs across 480 simulated indoor scenes covering localization, distance estimation, and motion reasoning, plus SonicWorld, a model that maintains persistent source states from physical, learned acoustic, and semantic features and projects them into an Omni LLM for reasoning under overlapping speech and source motion.

entry.title: 4LC: 4D Latent Cache for Efficient Conditioning in Dynamic World Modeling

author.name: Jianhui Zhang, Zuyao Lin, Pengxin Xu, Jingdong Wang, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: 4LC is a 4D latent cache that reuses visual representations of static and dynamic content as conditioning for repeated video generation at different times and viewpoints, avoiding per-request RGB rendering and re-encoding. It binds representations from multiple encoders (VAE, DINO, V-JEPA, VGGT) to shared geometry and motion via a flexible spatiotemporal access interface.

entry.title: Saliency-Guided Replay for Continual Learning in Deep Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Francesco Panetta, Federico Di Valerio, Michela Proietti

entry.summary: Combines Experience Packing and Replay with Spike Activation Maps, forward-only explanations derived from spike activity, to select informative image patches for replay instead of storing full images in deep spiking neural networks. Tested on Split CIFAR10/100 with low-latency VGG9 SNNs, targeting memory-efficient continual learning for neuromorphic computing.

entry.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression

author.name: Or Ronai, Vladimir Kulikov, Tomer Michaeli

entry.summary: H-DDCM improves training-free diffusion-based compression by replacing dense Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries, exploiting the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform for efficiency. This overcomes memory and computation bottlenecks of prior codebook approaches like Turbo-DDCM at the large latent dimensions of modern image and video generators. It preserves strong perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates.

entry.title: Do Perturbation Predictors Learn Gene Interactions? Diagnosing Extrapolation in Agentic Screening

author.name: Ziyuan Gao

entry.summary: This paper introduces additive disagreement (AD), a diagnostic comparing model predictions for unseen gene combinations against a simple additive baseline of observed single-gene effects. Across eight prediction methods and three Perturb-seq datasets, it examines whether specialized neural models genuinely learn interaction effects beyond additive extrapolation in agentic screening.

entry.title: Lag: A Mean-Field Optimal Policy for Online Assignment with Reusable Resources

author.name: Keerthana Gurushankar

entry.summary: The paper models online task assignment with reusable resources as a contextual restless multi-armed bandit, deriving an occupancy-measure LP upper bound and from its dual a closed-form index policy called Lag. It introduces a mean-field scaling regime and presumably establishes near-optimality guarantees, with applications in reviewer assignment, call routing, and dispatch.

entry.title: FUSE: Fairness-aware Update Screening against Byzantine Exploitation in $q$-Fair Federated Learning

author.name: Tiantong Sun, Jinlin Liu, Xingru Wei, Zequan Fang, Wei Chen, Qiang Yang, Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: FUSE addresses a neglected security gap in q-fair federated learning, where fairness-driven amplification of high-loss clients can be indistinguishable from malicious update scaling by Byzantine clients. The paper formalizes Byzantine-robust q-FFL under an update-only interface and proposes fairness-aware update screening to separate legitimate from malicious amplification.

entry.title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort

author.name: Jon Sporring

entry.summary: This critical narrative review develops a common mathematical account of when human corrections become useful learning signal, unifying active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation. It uses exact Bayesian updates, excess-risk decomposition, and conditional information decompositions to compare methods at matched human effort. Such a unifying treatment is valuable for anyone designing human-in-the-loop systems.

entry.title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

author.name: Jin-Jia Zheng, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: The authors present a leakage-controlled, graph-enhanced framework on MIMIC-IV that discovers disease progression motifs from train-only consecutive-admission transitions and uses a time-aware Transformer with endpoint-specific cross-attention to forecast clinical endpoints and event times. The catalog of 99,527 branching motifs yielded small but consistent gains in micro-AUPRC and reduced event-time MAE across five seeds. It emphasizes inspectable trajectory evidence and censor-aware outcomes for clinical forecasting.

entry.title: Edgewise Envelopes Between Balanced Forman and Ollivier-Ricci Curvature

author.name: Giorgio Micaletto, Tebe Nigrelli

entry.summary: Derives explicit two-sided piecewise-affine bounds connecting Ollivier-Ricci curvature, which requires solving an optimal transport problem per edge, and the cheaper combinatorial Balanced Forman curvature. The deterministic bounds depend only on 2-hop local combinatorics, reducing per-edge computation from an LP to roughly O(max degree^2.5) time. Empirical benchmarks confirm scalability on large graphs, useful for curvature-based graph rewiring and analysis.

entry.title: Neural Supervised Clustering for Learning Individualized Treatment Rules with Many Treatments

author.name: Daixi Huang, Yixin Yuan, Yifan Dai, Yufeng Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes NSCF, a neural Q-learning framework for learning individualized treatment rules with many treatments, using shared nonlinear covariate representations, low-dimensional treatment embeddings, and supervised clustering to fuse treatments with similar learned contrasts. An alternating algorithm with validation-based partition selection yields an interpretable treatment partition and lowered regret versus baselines. Useful for precision medicine and other multi-action decision settings with limited per-arm data.

entry.title: High-Probability Regret Bounds for Feel-Good Thompson Sampling

author.name: Xuheng Li, Qingyue Zhao, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: The paper derives the first high-probability regret bounds for both cumulative and current-step Feel-Good Thompson Sampling in contextual bandits with general realizable function approximation, complementing prior expectation-only guarantees. Bounds depend on decoupling coefficients and prior mass near the true reward, with minimax-optimal rates in the linear setting. This strengthens the theoretical footing of a well-known exploration-augmented posterior sampling algorithm.

entry.title: FlowSep-RF: Rectified Flow Matching for Single-Channel Radio-Frequency Signal Separation

author.name: Mohamed Kamel, Tamer Nadeem

entry.summary: FlowSep-RF applies rectified flow matching to single-channel RF signal separation, learning a clean-endpoint transport from a received mixture to the signal of interest. Combining time-domain IQ samples with frequency-domain features, it recovers separated waveforms in a single velocity evaluation, avoiding the iterative sampling cost of diffusion-based alternatives.

entry.title: Retrieve What Helps, Only When It Helps: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Machine Translation

author.name: Shijun Li, Yang Liu, Najmeh Sadoughi, Dongmei Wang, Xinjie Li, Zhu Liu, Rohith Mysore Vijaya Kumar, Yuzong Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SRAT, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for selective retrieval-augmented translation that learns both when to retrieve and what evidence to acquire, based on the observation that parametric knowledge suffices for many inputs. This avoids uniformly applying predefined retrieval strategies across all inputs.

entry.title: PRISMATIC : Prescription Risk Inspection System for Multi-Agent Treatment Interaction in Clinical Decision-Making

author.name: Ziyang Ling, Shuyu Lu, Ziyi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces PRISMATIC, a blackboard-based multi-agent architecture where role-specialized agents collaboratively generate and refine drug regimens for multimorbid patients, governed by adaptive coordination mechanisms to catch prescription interaction risks stemming from fragmented specialist decision-making.

entry.title: MemeTrace: A Multimodal LLM-Based Agent for Safety-Aware Meme Provenance Analysis

author.name: Bo Shao, Yihan Ma, Yiting Qu, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: MemeTrace is a multimodal LLM-based agent that traces the provenance and potential societal risks of memes, going beyond per-image safe/unsafe classification to examine origin, spread, and cultural symbolism. It targets the moderation gap created by memes' rapid evolution and strong contextual dependence.

entry.title: CoDy: Codec Dynamics as Complementary Priors for Unsupervised Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Tianyu Yan, Qingyi Yang, Qin Yang, Xufei Guo, Yuan Tang, Rui Wang, Yixue Hao, Long Hu

entry.summary: CoDy exploits an overlooked property of video codecs for unsupervised temporal action localization: group-of-pictures quantization patterns preserve category-discriminative dynamics, while motion vectors and residuals respond strongly around action transitions. The framework uses these codec signals as complementary supervision alongside RGB and optical-flow representations.

entry.title: VisualWorldBench: A Fine-Grained Multi-Task Benchmark for Evaluating Visual World Knowledge in MLLMs

author.name: Chen Chen, Zheming Liang, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: VisualWorldBench is a fine-grained, multi-task benchmark evaluating visual world knowledge in multimodal LLMs, designed with broad open-ended category coverage and rigorous task construction that prevents models from succeeding via coarse cues, vague associations, or elimination strategies. It targets knowledge-intensive visual QA and fine-grained entity understanding.

entry.title: GLoD-LVSM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Continuous-LoD Scene Representations for Large View Synthesis Models

author.name: Weikai Lin, Nicholas Milef, Carl S Marshall, Grant Kaijuin Yang, Todd Keeler, Yuhao Zhu

entry.summary: GLoD-LVSM reduces token redundancy and rendering cost in large view synthesis models via a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation with continuous levels of detail. A learned field initializes a flexible number of anchors to match any budget, and a condenser with geometry-grounded attention compresses scene information while preserving rendering quality.

entry.title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration

author.name: Xu Zhang, Jun Wan, Lefei Zhang, Liangpei Zhang

entry.summary: PreActIR is an agentic image restoration framework in which a tool-conditioned world model forecasts each candidate tool's effect on degradation, quality, fidelity, risk, and uncertainty before execution. An independent verifier commits or rolls back outputs, and the framework audits whether performance is limited by the selector or the candidate tool space.

entry.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?

author.name: Jahyeok Koo, Hyeonseo Yu, Seungho Jang, Jaewoo Jung, Jiwon Kang, Seokju Cho, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Ask4NV investigates whether 3D language understanding can supervise novel-view generation, building on a unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that injects camera geometry into VAE and ViT representations. Understanding features participate in generation through joint self-attention, testing cross-capability transfer from spatial question answering to view synthesis.

entry.title: IMU-Bench: Benchmarking Wrist IMU Representations Across Kinematic, Semantic and Clinical Tasks

author.name: Yiquan Li, Aidan Bradshaw, Chenfeng Gao, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: IMU-Bench is a benchmark of ten wrist-IMU tasks across eight datasets studying multi-task performance and cross-task transfer, comparing six self-supervised pretraining methods on classification, pose and velocity estimation, and IMU-language retrieval. It reveals how supervision for one task affects transfer to others and whether shared representations help. A useful community resource for wearable sensing representation learning.

entry.title: Tiered-Resolution Volumetric Mapping for Real-Time Simultaneous Planning and Mapping on Natural Outdoor Environments

author.name: Afonso E. Carvalho, David Portugal, Paulo Peixoto, George Kantor

entry.summary: The paper introduces a tiered-resolution volumetric mapping mechanism that integrates LiDAR at two resolutions simultaneously: fine within a corridor around the robot's plan and coarse elsewhere, closing a feedback loop where planning informs mapping. Validated on real-world teleoperated data in natural outdoor environments.

entry.title: VETNET: Assembling Benchmark Datasets for AI-Driven Veterinary Innovation

author.name: Katherine J. Koebel, Renata Ivanek, Parminder Basran, Jennifer Sun, Casey Cazer, Gayatri Anil, Tommaso Banzato, Liz Barton, Dottie Cimino Brown, Leszek Bukowski, Marta Castelhano, Simon Coghlan, Christopher De Sa, Nikki Dutta, Hala Ghali, Julio Giordano, Joshua Glass, David C. Hogg, Nicholas Hollingshead, Adam Kiehl, Ziang Liu, Monica Meduri, Param Mohapatra, Kim Nayyer, Amelia Nelson, Peter-John Mantyla Noble, Christopher Pinard, Beryl Rabindran, Scott Ross, Ron Seccia, Moira Sheehan, Fei Wang, Tracy L. Webb, Kilian Q. Weinberger, Heather M. Whitney, Chen Xin

entry.summary: VETNET is an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks for AI in veterinary medicine and animal science, built through multi-institutional collaboration including Cornell-affiliated researchers. It aims to close the gap between fast-moving human medical AI and the fragmented veterinary AI field.

entry.title: Energy Ring: Stabilizing Feature Energy for Reliable Test-Time Discovery

author.name: Tianle Liu, Fan Lyu, Tingliang Feng, Chenggong Ni, Tianqi Wang, Zhang Zhang, Fuyuan Hu, Rui Yao, Tao Zhou

entry.summary: Energy Ring addresses test-time discovery, where a deployed model must separate known from novel classes on an unlabeled stream, by showing the natural energy gap between known and unknown classes is unstable. A lightweight adapter anchors the two class types on separate energy rings, enlarging a norm-based gap while preserving known-class directions, plus a perturbation consistency module.

entry.title: Think in Strategies, Act with Tools: Traceable Agentic Optimization for Combinatorial Problems

author.name: Zhongnian Li, Shi Xu, Peng Ying, Weikang Gong, Zhixiao Wang, Xinzheng Xu

entry.summary: TASA improves on Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO) by decomposing optimization into traceable strategy selections planned from the trajectory, plus LLM-constructed problem-specific tools with a strategy-guided adaptive selection mechanism. This addresses OPRO's difficulty in tracking and reusing information across iterations.

entry.title: PEAM: On-device Communication Agent for Personalized, Efficient and Autonomous Mobile Network Configuration

author.name: Haowen Wan, Shangzhuo Xie, Syue-Ju Syue, Xianyue Wu, Runhua Li, Qianqian Yang

entry.summary: PEAM is an on-device LLM agent that generates personalized mobile network-configuration rules executable within milliseconds, fine-tuned on annotated real-user data. It uses a two-phase design to satisfy strict latency constraints for decisions triggered by app switches or changing connectivity.

entry.title: Knowledge transfer between simple discrete worlds

author.name: Silv\`ere Gangloff, Jan Hula

entry.summary: Studies generalization in a depth-recurrent model trained on Sudoku-like puzzles built from combinations of rules, testing four levels of novelty from new puzzle instances to entirely unseen rule instances, with rules given symbolically or as solved examples. The setup probes which forms of novelty models can handle.

entry.title: SocraticRepair: Planning-Guided Socratic Tutoring for Program Debugging and Misconception Repair

author.name: Mykhailo Kopytskyi, Jianhua Yang, Mir Seyedebrahimi

entry.summary: Presents SocraticRepair, a planning-guided tutoring framework for program debugging that fine-tunes Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (an existing model released in 2024) on synthetic multi-turn Socratic dialogues, designed to avoid prematurely revealing solutions and to track the learner's debugging objective. Evaluated with independent metrics and benchmarks in the Python domain.

entry.title: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching

author.name: Bui Van Hung, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Dang Thanh Vu, Soo-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: Introduces MultiFlow, a generative framework for fMRI encoding that models neural responses as distributions rather than point estimates, using Conditional Flow Matching. Its Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching conditions the source distribution on the stimulus via a temporal convolution with an HRF-length receptive field, shortening the transport path. This better captures physiological and cognitive variability in brain responses.

entry.title: Cross-Protocol Personality Assessment with LLMs: Aligning Behavioral Evidence with Human Ratings

author.name: Wei Shan, Tianyi Zhang, Yuan Zong, Wenming Zheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes CEPA, a framework for personality assessment from asynchronous video interviews that aligns behavioral representations across different interview protocols with differing question sets and question-trait mappings. It projects source behavioral records into target-protocol representations so human-rated evidence can transfer across protocols.

entry.title: Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning via Confidence-Guided Adaptive Debate

author.name: Seungdong Yoa, Ye Seul Sim, Suhee Yoon, Sanghyu Yoon, Dongmin Kim, Soonyoung Lee, Bumsoo Kim, Junhyun Lee

entry.summary: LASE is a leader-centric multi-agent debate framework that engages interaction only in non-neutral regimes, motivated by theory that symmetric debate is neutral in expectation. It uses an asymmetric leader-supporter architecture with confidence-guided invocation to direct information flow and reduce wasted debate cost.

entry.title: XAI-Guided Fourier Domain Generalisation for Pure-Simulation Sim-to-Real Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wei Yao, Chuyao Wang, Ziwei Wang, Nabil Aouf

entry.summary: XFD uses explainability signals to guide Fourier-based domain generalization for sim-to-real transfer of vision-based driving policies, replacing unguided domain randomization with perturbations targeted at what the model actually relies on. It requires no target-domain data, operating purely from simulation.

entry.title: Queue-Aware Token Communications: Bridging AI Representation and Wireless Service

author.name: Yuquan Xiao, Qinghe Du, Chaoyang Zhang, Wenchi Cheng, Jingqing Wang, Tao Chen, Jiangzhou Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Queue-Aware Token Communications, extending the token communications paradigm for AI-native wireless networks by explicitly modeling queueing dynamics from the mismatch between token generation workloads and time-varying wireless service capacity. The paper presents an end-to-end architecture integrating AI service pipelines with queue-aware transmission.

entry.title: AutoMARS: Automatic and Scalable Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Supply Chain Risk Assessment

author.name: Yinzhu Quan, Zefang Liu, Frederick Benaben, Benoit Montreuil

entry.summary: AutoMARS is a multi-agent LLM framework for automated, scalable supply chain risk assessment that plans tasks, coordinates specialized agents, invokes external tools, and parallelizes comparisons across locations. It integrates heterogeneous risk factors spanning socioeconomic, disaster, environmental, and transportation domains.

entry.title: An FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Network for Spatiotemporal Pattern Learning and Classification

author.name: Jingang Jin, Yue Ma, Zhenhang Zhang, Qinru Qiu

entry.summary: The authors implement multilayer spiking neural networks on FPGA hardware with both inference and on-device training, using a temporal-forward-only training algorithm that avoids the memory and latency costs of backpropagation through time. A mixed-precision scheme and architectural optimizations balance stability with resource efficiency, and they identify and fix timing hazards during training. This targets energy-efficient edge deployment of SNNs.

entry.title: A Node Embedding Framework for Model-Centric Conformance Checking in Process Mining

author.name: Mostafa Abbasi, Homayoun Najjaran

entry.summary: The paper proposes PetriNetGraph, a model-centric evaluation framework for process mining that converts Petri net process models into graph representations and compares node embeddings of ground-truth and discovered models using Procrustes alignment. This offers a noise-robust alternative to traditional fitness and precision metrics, which are highly sensitive to event-log deviations. It gives a more consistent way to assess process discovery algorithms.

entry.title: Fresh at Decision, Stale at Action: Routing New Information to LLM Decisions Already Made

author.name: Ayoub Merimi, Souhail Bakkali, Abdeljalil Sakat

entry.summary: The paper introduces a timestamp theory of decision validity and a persistent decision ledger that routes newly published information to already-made LLM decisions before their revision deadlines, factoring accuracy into routing and temporal judgment capabilities. This addresses the underexplored gap between when an LLM makes a decision and when the resulting action executes in a changing world. It is a novel framing for temporal correctness of agentic decisions.

entry.title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration

author.name: Yevgeny Rakita, Paul Todd, James R. Neilson, Simon J. L. Billinge

entry.summary: This paper proposes Provenance Action Graphs for materials synthesis, representing reaction steps and their outputs as events so that learning algorithms can encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways, supporting both forward prediction and inverse design of kinetically stabilized materials. It comes from a credible Columbia materials science group (Simon Billinge) and demonstrates the framework's potential. The goal is to turn trial-and-error synthesis knowledge into learnable structure.

entry.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Zheng Gao, Chiwun Yang, Zhizhou Sha

entry.summary: This theoretical paper models recursive AI self-improvement as a stochastic multiplicative process where improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of current capability. It derives exact distributions for the explosion time (geometrically weighted sums of exponentials, Gamma distribution for Lomax-sized improvements) and studies detection limits.

entry.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization

author.name: Trieu Nguyen, Frazier N. Baker, Ruoxi Gao, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Xia Ning

entry.summary: MFG is a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules across multiple turns using computational or experimental feedback, targeting simultaneous improvement of multiple properties while preserving molecular structure. It addresses the gap that existing LLM-based molecular optimization methods are single-turn and not trained to exploit iterative feedback. This has direct relevance to drug discovery pipelines.

entry.title: SharedSAE: a unified sparse dictionary across u-net blocks and denoising time for diffusion models

author.name: Longhao Lei, Lan Yao

entry.summary: SharedSAE learns a single sparse autoencoder dictionary shared across four U-Net attention blocks and all 50 denoising steps of SDXL 1.0, using a block-specific low-rank input adapter and a temporal conditioning module to absorb non-stationarity. This provides one coherent feature space for concept localization and intervention across network depth and denoising time. It addresses a real limitation of per-block, per-timestep SAEs in diffusion interpretability.

entry.title: Bias Robustness of Genetic Multi-Criteria Sorting versus Learned Rankers under Proxy Skew and Label Contamination

author.name: Vladyslav Shevchuk, Carlos Uziel P\'erez Malla, Philipp Wissgott

entry.summary: This paper compares label-free genetic multi-criteria sorting against label-trained learning-to-rank models (LightGBM, XGBoost, RankSVM) under proxy-skew and label-contamination protocols across four ranking datasets. Genetic sorting shows much lower correlation with biased proxy signals, though learned rankers achieve higher clean nDCG, positioning the two on a bias-utility frontier.

entry.title: Two-Stage Multi-modal Learning for Dynamic Audio-Visual Navigation: From Physical Alignment to Scene Aggregation

author.name: Jia Li, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: The paper addresses dynamic audio-visual navigation where sound sources move, proposing a two-stage framework with an Intensity-Calibrated Geometry Encoder performing physics-informed alignment of auditory and visual cues before scene aggregation. This improves generalization to unheard sound categories and fine-grained spatial reasoning over semantic-feature approaches.

entry.title: AphaVoice: Text-to-Speech Model for Aphasia Patient Simulation

author.name: Al Varrel Putra Kusuma, Fernando Bello, Joshua Brown

entry.summary: Introduces AphaVoice, a TTS framework that synthesizes realistic aphasic speech for training medical professionals in language therapy simulations. It outperforms state-of-the-art TTS systems on temporal dysfluency metrics while preserving speaker identity, leveraging latent features.

entry.title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning

author.name: Julien Roger, Sam Bodmer, Jian Qian, Benjamin Riviere

entry.summary: The paper studies average-reward RL where a reward-agnostic m-step mixing policy is given, regularizing the learned policy toward it to control contraction and exploration. It provides finite-time analyses of Q-learning and Q-planning with multiple regularizer choices and identifies regularizer-dependent objects governing the guarantees.

entry.title: scHFBiMamba: a bidirectional Mamba autoencoder for cardiac disease-state classification from single-nucleus RNA-seq data

author.name: Ugo Lomoio, Pietro Hiram Guzzi, Pierangelo Veltri

entry.summary: scHFBiMamba is a bidirectional Mamba (state-space model) autoencoder that classifies species, cell type, and heart-failure disease state from single-nucleus RNA-seq profiles, using 13.2M parameters versus 192.9M for a comparable dense denoising autoencoder. It maps 16,545-gene profiles to compact 350-dimensional latent representations while providing interpretable gene attributions. Evaluation on 38,275 held-out cardiac nuclei uses rigorous statistical testing.

entry.title: Siam-ALS: An Explainable Siamese Deep Learning Framework for Early ALS Detection Using EEG and Eye-Tracking Signals

author.name: Abdur Rahman, A. A. M. Muzahid, Istiak Ahmed, Dipto Biswas, Hua Han, Yujin Zhang, Ferdous Sohel

entry.summary: Siam-ALS is an explainable Siamese deep learning framework for early detection of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that jointly models synchronized EEG and eye-tracking signals with modality-specific encoders. It aims to provide objective, data-driven diagnosis for a condition whose clinical assessment is slow and heterogeneous.

entry.title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Liang Yuan, Maryam Khanian Najafabadi, Mashud Rana, Varvara Vetrova

entry.summary: This systematic literature review consolidates findings on security risks of LLM-assisted coding, covering insecure code generation, vulnerability of models to attacks, benchmark contamination, and weak security metrics. It concludes human oversight remains essential and calls for security-aware architectures, better benchmarks, and human-AI collaboration frameworks.

entry.title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification

author.name: Alan Tang, Lifeng Wang, Gang Wu, Tao Zhang, Yantao Jia, Xiaofeng Zhu

entry.summary: SkillMarker introduces a watermarking method for reusable agent skill assets that must preserve factual and procedural accuracy. It combines quality-constrained rewriting with signal-oriented candidate search to embed KGW-style watermarks that enable ownership verification and leakage tracing without degrading skill functionality.

entry.title: AI Representations of Mental Health Stigma: Quantifying the Gap Between AI Estimations and Human Perceptions Across Gender Groups Using GPT-Based LLMs

author.name: Soojong Kim, Hye Min Kim, Kwanho Kim, Dongdong Zhu

entry.summary: Evaluates whether GPT-4 and GPT-5 represent mental health stigma perceptions consistently across gender groups, using established psychometric measures and comparing AI estimations against the Healthy Minds Study dataset of over 76,000 respondents. The work quantifies both bias and misalignment between model estimates and real human perceptions.

entry.title: Towards a Benchmark for Fire Safety Code Interpretation in the Hong Kong AEC Industry

author.name: Le Qiu, Zhuan Anne Zhang, Hok Ming Adeline Chan, Emmanuele Chersoni

entry.summary: Creates an expert-validated benchmark of multiple-choice and open-ended questions on Hong Kong fire safety codes and evaluates 12 proprietary and open-source LLMs. Proprietary models reach 80-90% on MCQs but only 50-70% on expert-assessed open-ended answers, revealing significant gaps in regulatory compliance reasoning.

entry.title: Estimating the Causal Impact of Social Navigation Signals in Corridor Scenarios

author.name: Francesco Baldo, Luca Castri, Gloria Beraldo, Nicola Bellotto

entry.summary: The paper applies causal inference to human-robot social navigation, building a causal model to estimate whether emitting a social signal in corridor scenarios causally improves robot transit success, correcting for confounders that bias observation-based inference. This offers a principled framework for deciding when social signals are worth emitting.

entry.title: PATMT2: Two-stage domain adaptation for multilingual patent translation

author.name: Xiaowei Su, Xusen Cheng

entry.summary: PatMT2 adapts the existing Tencent Hy-MT2-7B translation model via a two-stage LoRA pipeline for Chinese/English/Japanese/Korean patent translation, improving up to +8.8 BLEU over the base and exceeding Qwen3-32B on macro average, including under AWQ INT4 quantization. It also probes 38 held-out languages, documenting reproducible failure modes in four low-resource languages.

entry.title: Few-for-Many Best-Arm Identification in Multi-Objective Bandits

author.name: Bo Xue, Yilu Liu, Haodong Jing, Hongzong Li, Xi Lin, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper introduces few-for-many best-arm identification in multi-objective bandits: selecting a small arm set that minimizes worst weighted degradation from objective-wise optima, with algorithms GFM-Elim and AFM-Elim offering instance-dependent sample-complexity guarantees, including a matching lower bound for latent-group Gaussian settings.

entry.title: Governing Copyright Responsibly in the Era of Generative AI

author.name: D. Kochetkov

entry.summary: A policy analysis coding 40 legislative, judicial, and soft-law instruments from 2019-2026 (primarily EU and US, with UK, China, and international comparators) against a Responsible Research and Innovation framework to assess how copyright governance protects authors whose works were used in LLM training. It proposes what a more responsible governance alternative would require, including work-level transparency for authors.

entry.title: Calibrated Typed Decisions for Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction

author.name: Yang Wang, Hanlin Xiao, Yanan Ma, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: Introduces CalOn, a unified 0.6B-parameter encoder for entity, relation, and event extraction that jointly encodes text and type definitions and uses combined evidence across requested types before assigning types, providing a common probabilistic formulation for all three tasks with improved cross-domain and cross-schema transfer.

entry.title: ClearNav: Perception-Aligned Quadrotor Flight Using Differential-Physics

author.name: Aditya Azad, Arthur Huang, Guanrui Li

entry.summary: ClearNav attributes most sim-to-real quadrotor collisions in cluttered environments to motion in directions the onboard camera does not observe, such as misaligned heading and lateral excursion during avoidance. It trains a navigation policy with reward terms constraining motion to the observed direction, including a forward-looking heading target and lateral penalties. This is a simple, mechanism-targeted fix for perception-alignment in drone navigation.

entry.title: YUBI-Real2Sim: 3DGS Scene Verification for Reliable Policy Evaluation

author.name: Hiroki Nishizawa, Takehiko Ohkawa, Nicola Scianca, Tatsuya Matsushima, Shigeo Morishima, Kei Ota

entry.summary: YUBI-Real2Sim is a framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting based real-to-sim evaluation of vision-language-action robot policies, focusing on wrist-mounted fisheye camera views where reconstruction artifacts like holes and floaters degrade policy performance.
