The work quantifies the reconstruction quality needed for reliable policy evaluation and provides an integrated reconstruction-and-evaluation pipeline.

entry.title: RELAY: Selective Self-Distillation with Adaptive Hand-off for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kunwang Zheng, Xinyu Sun, Yu Cao, Shuocheng Li, Lei Cheng, Ying Liu, Qilong Zhang, Jinlong Chen, Hua Yang, Qianglong Chen

entry.summary: RELAY addresses limitations of rubric-based RL, where collapsing multiple criteria into one reward discards rubric detail and gives zero GRPO gradient for tied groups. It uses a frozen teacher reading the rubric as privileged context for token-level supervision, selectively distilling on chosen rollouts, with a plateau detector that retires the teacher so Stage 2 continues with GRPO alone.

entry.title: FETALFusion: Resolution-Aware State-Space Modeling for Multi-Domain Fetal Head Segmentation

author.name: Ammar Bhilwarawala, Mainak Bandyopadhyay

entry.summary: Presents FETALFusion, a dual-path CNN-Mamba encoder-decoder for fetal head segmentation across transabdominal and transperineal ultrasound, applying four-directional state-space scans at high-resolution stages and routing bottleneck features through domain-specific channel gates. Evaluated against ten methods on 471 held-out images at native resolution with surface-distance metrics.

entry.title: ChampionKV: Head-Wise Adaptive Budget Allocation for KV Cache Compression

author.name: Yuechuan Chen, Yanda Guo, Xiaoxi Liu, Weilin Ruan, Huanbo Xu, Ruyi Wang, Wei Zhu

entry.summary: ChampionKV improves long-context KV cache compression by allocating compression budgets per attention head based on an observation-window attention concentration proxy, rather than uniform budgets. It plugs into existing compressors like SnapKV and PyramidKV without altering their token selection, adding robustness mechanisms for weak-attention cases. This is a practical plug-in for cheaper long-context inference.

entry.title: When Missingness Follows the Graph: Beyond Feature Propagation for Missing Features

author.name: Enrico Chial\`a, Francesco Ferrini, Antonio Longa, Bruno Lepri, Filippo Maria Bianchi, Manfred Jaeger, Veronica Lachi

entry.summary: This paper identifies that GNN methods for missing node features have been evaluated only under unrealistic uniformly random missingness, and formalizes graph-structured mask dependence where missingness propagates among connected nodes, as in localized sensor failures. The work develops methods and evaluation for these realistic settings. This corrects an overly optimistic evaluation paradigm in the field.

entry.title: SimInter: Evidence-Grounded User Simulation with Interview-Based Profile Enrichment for Conversational Recommender Systems

author.name: Erfan Shahabi, Amirhossein Roshandel, Mohammad Sadegh Sadeghi, Azadeh Shakery

entry.summary: SimInter enriches LLM-based user simulators for conversational recommender systems by eliciting implicit attributes like decision-making style and aspect-level preferences via synthetic interviews between two LLM agents, grounded in statistical profiles and conversation history. An audit agent flags potential fabrication and stereotyping before enrichment.

entry.title: Learning Perturbation-Specific Representations through Conditional Energy Prior for Cellular Response Prediction

author.name: Yuchen Yan, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: PerturbEnergy introduces a conditional energy-based prior that biases latent representations toward regions compatible with a given genetic or chemical perturbation, improving cellular response prediction for drug discovery. The method integrates into autoencoder architectures via an evidence-lower-bound formulation. It addresses the common failure mode where perturbation effects are obscured by general cellular variation.

entry.title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time

author.name: Yifan He, Manon Reusens, Sofie Goethals, David Martens

entry.summary: This study measures how five LLMs assign compensation for a delayed appointment across 193 countries, comparing responses with GDP per capita, mean income, and patience indices. Results show LLMs value people's time differently by country with varying robustness under prompt perturbations. It offers a novel lens on cultural bias and fairness in deployed assistants.

entry.title: On Symmetry for Characterizing Agent Heterogeneity in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jianhong Wang, Jonathan Lawry

entry.summary: This theoretical work defines policy-evaluation symmetries in finite-horizon POSGs, forming a group whose orbits classify structural agent types independent of policy or initial state distribution. It proves every componentwise environment automorphism is such a symmetry but not conversely, and applies the framework to cooperative Dec-POMDPs. This gives a unified structural test for agent heterogeneity.

entry.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers

author.name: Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: LLM2R casts 3D part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only LLM, using Point-BERT encoders and a Q-Former to compress parts into geometric token blocks processed by a LoRA-adapted causal LLM. This avoids pairwise relations or iterative verify-and-refine schemes that scale poorly with part count. It demonstrates transfer of LLM reasoning to geometric reconstruction tasks.

entry.title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report

author.name: OneRec Team, Chenglong Chu, Guohong Mu, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Hui Wang, Jian Liang, Jiangxia Cao, Jiao Ou, Jiaxin Deng, Lu Ren, Muhao Wei, Ruiming Tang, Tianle Xu, Wenwu Ou, Xingmei Wang, Zhixin Ling, Zhiyuan Liang, Ziqi Wang, Chaoyi Ma, Haixiao Gao, Kuo Cai, Renpu Liu, Ruochen Yang, Wenlong Xu, Xinqi Jin, Yan Sun, Yifan Wang, Yingzhi He, Yiyu Wang, Yusen Huo, Zhaojie Liu, Zihan Zhou

entry.summary: This technical report from Kuaishou's OneRec team describes KSA-V2, addressing bottlenecks in hybrid summary-token/full-attention architectures such as fixed per-layer compression windows and wasted computation in full-attention layers. It proposes flexible per-layer KV cache compression for streaming recommendation-scale context. Relevant to efficient long-context serving at industrial scale.

entry.title: Where Do LLM Ensemble Gains Come From? Decomposing Candidate Value, Diversity, and Aggregation

author.name: Donghwan Kim

entry.summary: This paper decomposes LLM ensemble gains under four matched comparison conditions (Direct, Single-slot, Duplicate, Multi-candidate), splitting candidate value into additional-candidate and candidate-context contrasts. Experiments on MultiHopRAG show the measured gain depends heavily on the control baseline chosen, with a repetition gap of about 8 percentage points, cautioning against naive single-baseline ensemble evaluations.

entry.title: Do Vision CIL Methods Transfer to Protein? A Diagnostic Benchmark of Frozen Protein Encoders

author.name: Ziyuan Gao

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks nine class-incremental learning methods across five protein encoders and two enzyme datasets under frozen-encoder, controlled settings, asking whether vision-developed CIL methods transfer to protein function annotation. The key finding is that no method transfers reliably across encoders, with failures persisting under alternative settings.

entry.title: Towards Training and Inference of Graph Neural Networks in Graph Databases

author.name: Victor Pekkari, Harry Wik, Alfred Clemedtson, Borun Shi, Xuan-Son Vu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that graph databases can directly host GNN training and inference, executing sampling, feature retrieval, and even full forward passes via Cypher queries. Optimizations speed training by roughly 2.5x while maintaining accuracy, and fully in-database inference is shown to be feasible.

entry.title: Refined Topology-Pass Scheduling: Damped Trust-Region Compensation for Dynamic k-NN Graphs in SE(3)-Equivariant Structure Prediction

author.name: Jiankai Huang, Hanwen Shen

entry.summary: Proposes a two-pass scheduling design for equivariant structure prediction where a cheap pass records graph state and a second pass conservatively compensates for kNN graph topology changes, formulated as a damped fixed-point iteration whose fixed point matches full per-boundary graph rebuilding. The paper derives exact non-flip certificates bounding deviations from the expensive scheme.

entry.title: Robust Explanatory Analysis for Structured Optimization Networks (REASON) in Learning

author.name: Vahid Jebraeeli, Hamid Krim, Keisuke Fujii

entry.summary: REASON formulates a two-loop, System 1/System 2-inspired mechanism for hierarchical resolution of residual error under composite learning objectives: a fast loop resolves evidence-addressable residuals and a slower loop actively acquires additional evidence, measuring its informational value through residual reduction. The authors prove the medium-loop optimum is no worse than the fast-loop optimum over nested solution spaces and demonstrate robustness under distribution shift and perturbation.

entry.title: W-JEPA: Wavelet Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Wearable Activity Recognition

author.name: Yogesh Prabhu, Loki Natarajan, Jingjing Zou

entry.summary: W-JEPA is a self-supervised framework for wearable activity recognition that exploits the multiscale structure of inertial signals via wavelet-based joint-embedding predictive architecture, targeting cross-dataset and cross-participant generalization challenges. By preserving scale-specific activity-relevant variation, it addresses heterogeneity in sensor placement, channel counts, and sampling rates. This brings JEPA-style self-supervision to mobile-health sensing.

entry.title: CTIA-ODE: Continuous-Time Inter-Variable Attention for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Chengyi Pan, Huangqimei Zheng, Hao Xue

entry.summary: CTIA-ODE is a continuous-time forecasting framework that embeds inter-variable attention inside an ODE solver, letting an endogenous trajectory query static exogenous context along the integration path without rigid temporal alignment. This addresses a real limitation of discrete-time architectures when heterogeneous exogenous variables are involved. It is a useful architectural contribution for multivariate time series forecasting.

entry.title: CARD: Closing the Teacher-Student Loop for Adversarial Robustness Distillation

author.name: Zhi Li, Haowei Liu, Hongchen Yang, Xiaoxuan Wang, Song Gao, Zhenli He, Wei Zhou, Shaowen Yao

entry.summary: CARD introduces a closed-loop adversarial robustness distillation framework where the distilled student provides feedback to refine the robust teacher, with careful mechanisms to avoid propagating student errors during weak-to-strong transfer, then transfers teacher gains back to the student. This departs from the standard one-way fixed-teacher paradigm. It could improve robustness of compact deployed models.

entry.title: A Large-Dimensional Analysis of Least-Squares Federated Learning via Generalized Total Variation Minimization

author.name: Ekkehard Schnoor, Malik Tiomoko, Alexander Jung

entry.summary: Using random matrix theory, the paper analyzes Generalized Total Variation Minimization for least-squares federated learning on decentralized networks, quantifying the trade-off between noise suppression through collaboration and bias from node heterogeneity. It derives exact asymptotic performance expressions for i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. Gaussian mixture data that hold universally across network structures.

entry.title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Robust Planetary Landing

author.name: Miguel Leiva-V\'elez, Nicolas Gaston-Rozado, Andrea Scorsoglio, Hodei Urrutxua, V\'ictor Rodr\'iguez-Fern\'andez

entry.summary: The paper uses adversarial RL to train robust planetary landing controllers, with a secondary agent generating physically constrained, spatiotemporally correlated perturbations in an asymmetric sequential zero-sum game. A three-stage training pipeline (baseline learning, adversary training, robust fine-tuning) produces policies more robust than those trained with standard independent random disturbances.

entry.title: When Does Task-Aware Imputation Matter? An Analysis of Robustness Under Train-Test Mismatch

author.name: Maria V. Salvador, Ana F. Sequeira, Jaime S. Cardoso

entry.summary: This paper frames missing-data imputation as a task-conditioned optimization problem rather than a preprocessing step, instantiating it as an amortized approach for missingness at both train and test time and a latent optimization approach when only training data is incomplete. Evaluation spans 98 tabular datasets, characterizing when task-aware imputation improves robustness under train-test mismatch in missingness mechanisms. This matters for reliable deployment of ML on real-world messy data.

entry.title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory

author.name: Tongxi Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that for average-reward RL, learning from a single continuing trajectory does not necessarily require more samples than free-state-action sampling: the authors give an algorithm that learns where to collect information and prove matching upper and lower bounds on interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. This is a sharp sample-complexity characterization for single-trajectory learning in the average-reward setting.

entry.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation

author.name: Luka Todorovic, Kaushal Gianchandani, Sai Ravela

entry.summary: Introduces PolyNets, which couple continuous-time polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network so that, when governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training while preserving a prescribed numerical scheme. Compared against finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural emulators on the Korteweg-de Vries equation using analytical soliton references. Demonstrates that neural-network structure can encode known physics directly rather than learn it.

entry.title: Bayesian Causal Forests for Zero-Inflated Continuous Outcomes

author.name: Hugo Gobato Souto, Eric Wang, Igor Shuryak

entry.summary: Proposes ZIC-BCF-Smear, a two-part nonparametric estimator for heterogeneous treatment effects with semicontinuous outcomes combining a Probit Bayesian Causal Forest for participation and a Gaussian BCF for positive intensity with Duan's smearing. Existing methods either ignore the zero mass, impose fragile parametric assumptions, or suffer computational cost. Addresses a common real-world data type in causal inference.

entry.title: Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models

author.name: Allan Peter Engsig-Karup

entry.summary: This paper introduces physics-informed weak regression (PIWR) for estimating parameters in epidemic compartment models, integrating the model in time to avoid differentiating noisy data and estimating the initial state jointly with high-order accuracy. Both PIWR and physics-informed regression are wrapped in split conformal prediction using a physics-model-generated calibration population for distribution-free, simultaneous uncertainty intervals. It strengthens rigorous uncertainty quantification for epidemic modeling.

entry.title: TopicMerge: A Divide and Conquer Approach to Topic Modeling

author.name: Matthew Raffel, Lizhong Chen, Sai Munikoti, Sameera Horawalavithana

entry.summary: TopicMerge is a multi-stage pipeline that combines efficient embedding-based clustering with LLM-based labeling to get the best of both worlds in topic modeling. It first over-segments a corpus into fine-grained, semantically pure micro-clusters, then merges them into final topics, achieving strong clustering performance at much lower computational cost than pure LLM approaches. This is a practical efficiency contribution for large-scale document analysis.

entry.title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent

author.name: Zijun Chen, Zihan Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of random reshuffling SGD with constant component stepsize nearly 1/L, removing previous requirements that stepsizes scale inversely with the number of components. Since the final iterate, not the average, is what practitioners use, this closes an important gap between theory and practice for finite-sum optimization. The proof handles sampling bias at random comparison points.

entry.title: Evidence-Anchored Overdose Death Prediction from Death Investigation Reports

author.name: Raavi Gupta, Ziqing Yang, Karli R. Hochstatter, Talia Nadel, Nicole D'Anna, Jason K. Graham, Hannah Johnson, Kelsey Opozda, Nabila El-Bassel, Anubhav Jangra, Smaranda Muresan

entry.summary: The authors present an expert-guided NLP framework that classifies suspected overdose deaths from death investigation reports while producing explanations guided by expert knowledge, addressing delays in US overdose death confirmation. They compare explanation types for predictive performance and evaluate architecture choices for the task. This demonstrates AI with direct public-health impact on timely mortality surveillance.

entry.title: Few-Shot Adaptation for Anomalous Sound Detection at Low False-Positive Rate

author.name: Simone Lugani, Christof Pichler, Hannes Wegleiter, Christoph Feilmayr, Rodolfo Zunino, Edoardo Ragusa

entry.summary: A two-stage anomalous sound detection system for industrial machinery: an unsupervised model is deployed on normal audio, then a few-shot adaptation after the first fault exploits newly acquired anomalous samples to improve detection. The approach raises AUPR from 23.0 to 64.0, targeting industrial constraints on false positives.

entry.title: Contrastive uncertainty learning for robust multi-structure segmentation in lower-pelvic MR

author.name: Bilal Sidiqi, Yipei Wang, Wen Yan, Shaheer U. Saeed, Daniel C. Alexander, Yipeng Hu

entry.summary: This paper proposes Contrastive Uncertainty Learning (CUL), which uses Monte Carlo Dropout-derived voxel-wise uncertainty to directly guide representation learning during segmentation training rather than as a post-hoc quality filter. It structures embedding geometry so low-uncertainty voxels form stable clusters, improving boundary delineation in ambiguous prostate MRI regions.

entry.title: Hypothesis Selection via Weighted Medians

author.name: Liang-Yu Zou

entry.summary: This theory paper gives an algorithm for proper hypothesis selection that achieves the optimal 3-approximation factor and sample complexity using weighted medians, running in time whose failure-probability dependence improves from polynomial to logarithmic. The result tightens the computational guarantees for a classical learning-theoretic problem.

entry.title: NEPSEE: A Double-Annotated Benchmark for Nepali Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Gaurab Baral, Mimansak Nepal, Grishma Basnet

entry.summary: NEPSEE is a double-annotated Nepali sentiment benchmark: two annotators blindly labeled 5,614 tweets from Nepali public figures on a five-point scale, retaining 3,189 agreement-filtered sentences for a three-class benchmark plus an adjacent-label five-point task. NepBERTa and IndicBERTv2 achieve macro-F1 near 0.87, with commercial LLMs from 0.882-0.896 zero-shot, and on the five-point task Claude Opus 5.5, an existing Anthropic model, performs competitively. It raises the annotation-quality bar for low-resource sentiment datasets.

entry.title: The Sum of All Summaries: PROPALIGN for Graded Proposition Salience Evaluation

author.name: Lin Ai, Emma Thronson, Katherine Conhaim, Amir Zeldes

entry.summary: PROPALIGN estimates graded proposition salience by aligning propositions across multiple summaries, accompanied by PROPALIGNBANK, a dataset of 138K alignments over 35K propositions across spoken and written genres. The authors show that direct model judgments of salience are inconsistent while summary-based graded metrics are more stable.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Document-Level Data Augmentation via Discourse Parsing

author.name: Ruilin Shang, Shilong Hou, Zi Long, Xianghua Fu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a document-level data augmentation framework that combines LLMs with discourse structure parsing: it identifies rhetorical relations between sentence pairs and extracts key phrases, then performs replacements while preserving inter-sentential coherence and logical flow. This addresses a real gap, since common augmentation techniques like synonym replacement and back-translation operate at word or sentence level and often break discourse structure. The approach is relevant for low-resource NLP tasks that depend on document-level reasoning.

entry.title: J-tau: A Fully Localized Japanese Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction

author.name: Chihiro Yano, Jun Hirako, Hiroaki Yamagiwa, Ryota Hirobuchi

entry.summary: J-tau is the first public Japanese benchmark for tool-using LLM agents in interactive customer-support scenarios, created by localizing tau-bench with machine translation, entity adaptation, and human review to handle locale-specific entities. During localization the authors also discovered and fixed two flaws in the original tau-bench, including invalid tasks and a score aggregation error.

entry.title: BANGLAPLAN: A Benchmark for Constraint-Based Planning and Decision-Making in Bangla

author.name: Md Rayhanul Masud, S M Maksudul Alam, Mohammad Jaminur Islam

entry.summary: Presents BANGLAPLAN, a 1,000-problem benchmark spanning ten task families for constraint-based planning and decision-making in Bangla, including feasible and infeasible problems across four language registers grounded in everyday Bangladeshi contexts. It fills a gap for the world's seventh most spoken language in planning evaluation.

entry.title: Language Exposure Matters: Distribution and Order in Multilingual BabyLM Pre-training

author.name: JiWoo Hwang, Lukas Edman, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: The study investigates how the distribution and ordering of language exposure affect multilingual pre-training under limited-data BabyLM conditions across English, Dutch, and Chinese. It finds mixed multilingual training outperforms curriculum-style training (monolingual-dominant followed by balanced exposure), with performance varying with both amount and order of exposure.

entry.title: When Occupation-derived Skills Don't Help: On the Limits of Skill-Augmented Career Path Prediction

author.name: Ege S\"ualp, Elena Senger, Toine Bogers, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: This paper critically tests whether explicit skill representations improve career path prediction, evaluating fusion strategies and neural architectures with both predicted and ground-truth ESCO skills. Across two benchmarks, skill augmentation yields only marginal and inconsistent gains over strong text-only baselines, challenging a common assumption in the field.

entry.title: Anuvani-Diarization: Zero Shot Speaker Diarization and Annotation Conventions Across 22 Languages

author.name: Stephen Fernandes, Narayan Choudhary

entry.summary: This work presents a systematic zero-shot study of speaker diarization across all 22 scheduled Indian languages on a new benchmark, IndicDiarBench, covering conversational speech with mixing, overlap, telephone, meeting, and media conditions. It introduces Anuvani-Diarization, which adapts a self-supervised end-to-end segmentation model using uncertainty-aware silver supervision, along with annotation conventions for the task. Diarization underpins speaker-attributed transcription, voice agents, and contact-center analytics for over a billion speakers.

entry.title: From Triage to Impact: A Multi-Hop Reasoning Benchmark for Explainable Persian Hate Speech

author.name: Ghazal Kalhor, Sima Kamandloo, Mehrsa Shamsian, Behnam Bahrak

entry.summary: The authors present a fine-grained, multi-hop benchmark for explainable Persian hate speech analysis spanning triage, target identification, tactic and moral foundation analysis, evidence extraction, and severity assessment. Evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs shows performance degrades as tasks demand finer semantic and inferential reasoning.

entry.title: Plant Memory: Technical Language Processing and a Verified Maintenance Ontology for Agent-Accessible Failure Knowledge from SAP PM Work Orders

author.name: Akash Raj

entry.summary: Plant Memory is a system that applies technical language processing to SAP Plant Maintenance work order exports, building an ISO 14224-aligned ontology where every extracted statement is a reified fact with confidence scores and evidence. This makes tacit diagnostic knowledge from senior technicians machine-accessible for reliability engineering and agent workflows.

entry.title: Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering

author.name: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Tong Lei, Dahan Wang, Peter Bell

entry.summary: This work studies how the design of textual interfaces affects automatic prompt optimization for audio-visual question answering, comparing a single OmniLLM, a captioner-reasoner pipeline, and an agentic architecture with subagent OmniLLMs using Qwen3-Omni and Gemini. The findings inform how multimodal reasoning should be exposed to text-based optimizers.

entry.title: LAMP: 3D Source-Aware Lighting Estimation at Multiple Points

author.name: Yanqiao Wang, Jin Sun

entry.summary: LAMP leverages VLM scene understanding for point-conditioned, source-aware illumination estimation from a single RGB image, building a shared inventory of active light sources, ranking contributors per query point, and predicting 3D query-to-source directions. It uses procedurally controlled indoor scenes for supervision.

entry.title: Mapping Arctic Polynyas from Sea Ice Concentration Data Using Hierarchical Partitioning and Differentiated Region Growing: Sensitivity to Threshold and Product Choices

author.name: Tianyu Zhang, Haiyi Ren, Zhilun Zhang, Yang Hong, Chunlei Mi, Xiao Cheng, Fengming Hui

entry.summary: This paper presents a daily mapping framework for Arctic coastal polynyas using hierarchical partitioning, connected-component analysis, and differentiated region growing, achieving 96.74% accuracy and kappa 0.93 across ice seasons 2002/03 to 2024/25. Sensitivity experiments show absolute polynya extent is strongly threshold-dependent while major temporal features remain robust.

entry.title: Q-MAGIC: Quad-only Mesh Autoregressive Generation via Singularity-Aware Circular Relative Offset Tokenization

author.name: Yuming Zhao, Zezeng Li, Weimin Wang, Xiang Wu, Na Lei

entry.summary: Q-MAGIC is an autoregressive model for generating quad-only 3D meshes, addressing the stricter topological constraints quads impose versus triangles. It introduces a serialization scheme requiring at least two new vertices per next face plus singularity-aware circular relative offset tokenization to enable unambiguous deserialization of connectivity.

entry.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Jaeyeon Heo, Geuntaek Lim, Yukyung Choi

entry.summary: This paper identifies relational semantic inertia, a failure mode in video scene graph generation where models keep stale relationship predictions after the underlying relation changes. RTAformer is a one-stage transformer that separately models entity persistence and relation transitions, injecting calibrated inter-frame relation differences to detect changes.

entry.title: CommerceGen-Studio: An End-to-End Framework for Commercial-Grade Main-Image Generation

author.name: Xiaoli Xu, Zhengtao Wu, Zhengze Xu, Tao Liu, Yongchao Du, Zuan Gao, Xingjian Wang, Hao Yan, Mengting Chen, Wei Li, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: CommerceGen-Studio is an industry-oriented end-to-end system for generating commercial main images for e-commerce SKUs, combining a prompt-eval-refine loop agent (PERL-Agent), a layout optimization module (LTO), and a diffusion transformer (SKU-DiT) trained with a Reinforce-Distill-Reinforce strategy. The pipeline extracts selling points from heterogeneous product metadata and generates multi-condition product imagery. It demonstrates how LLM/VLM agents and generative models are being assembled into production-grade, domain-specific content creation systems.

entry.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition

author.name: Weichen Lyu, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong, Long Xu, Shengjun Zhang, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: PhySGA handles complex 3D object compositions such as hanging, gravity-driven settling, and hidden containment by grounding the construction process in physics space rather than static LLM coordinate prediction or diffusion-prior visual alignment. It uses interactive construction with global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation within an agentic framework.

entry.title: Receding-Horizon Next-Best-View Planning for Highly Occluded Target Perception

author.name: Ayse Gul Yildiz, Rekha Raja

entry.summary: The authors reformulate local next-best-view planning as a short-horizon sequential decision problem, proposing RH-NBV, which evaluates multi-step viewpoint sequences rather than greedily maximizing immediate information gain. This helps robots perceive heavily occluded targets where myopic viewpoint selection stalls. The receding-horizon formulation is a clean improvement to a classic active perception problem.

entry.title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Yushen Hu, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Apurv Kushwaha, Jonathan King, Zhu-Tian Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes representing digital twin physical properties (mass, friction, center of mass) as probability distributions rather than fixed values, simulating actions across these distributions to predict outcome ranges and likelihoods. These probabilistic predictions can guide both human and robot actions under physical uncertainty in shared workspaces. This reframing addresses a practical weakness of precision-dependent digital twins.

entry.title: Dungeon and Visibility World Generator

author.name: Edwin M\'eriaux, Antonio Lor\'ia, Gregory Dudek

entry.summary: An open-source framework for generating reproducible 2D and 3D environments with controllable geometry and line-of-sight evaluation, aimed at benchmarking robotic exploration, coverage, and multi-agent deployment algorithms. It supports multiple geometry types and six construction families with configurable parameters and probability distributions.

entry.title: Learning Navigation from Multimodal Demonstrations with Geometric Candidate Modes

author.name: Chengyang Peng, Zhihao Zhang, Upama Pant, Yiming Wang, Keith A. Redmill, Ayonga Hereid

entry.summary: The paper addresses multimodality in offline navigation demonstrations, where behavior cloning averages conflicting valid actions into unsafe routes. It proposes a hierarchical policy that computes candidate modes directly from local geometry, with a high-level policy selecting modes and a low-level policy executing them.

entry.title: Maximum likelihood, neural networks and posterior mean for inferring fractional Brownian motion parameters

author.name: Daniel S. Han, Vaishnavi Ananthanarayanan, Matthew J. Simpson

entry.summary: The paper studies joint estimation of the Hurst exponent and generalized diffusion coefficient of fractional Brownian motion from noisy density measurements and single-particle trajectories. The authors show a single density time point cannot identify both parameters, and demonstrate that a simple neural network trained with squared error approximates the exact posterior mean of H at negligible inference cost. Combined with a profile-likelihood estimate of the diffusion coefficient, this yields a practical pipeline for anomalous diffusion analysis.

entry.title: Some interesting internal documents from Anthropic litigation

author.name: loops

entry.summary: The post curates and quotes internal Anthropic documents released through the book copyright litigation, including a July 2021 concise research roadmap describing the goal of safe beneficial AGI and a general AI coding assistant as a proof of concept. The author contextualizes these as individual authors' views rather than corporate stances. It offers historical insight into early frontier-lab strategy and safety reasoning.

entry.title: The PPA: A New Approach to Anthropics

author.name: Onid

entry.summary: The opening piece of the PPA series proposes a new anthropic model that treats epistemic uncertainty SSA-style and aleatoric randomness SIA-style, claiming to dissolve major paradoxes including Doomsday, the Presumptuous Philosopher, and infinite-universe issues. It also introduces a single-universe Basic Model that exposes multiple anthropic paradoxes at once.

entry.title: Your prompt… plus everything you've ever (publicly) written

author.name: kromem

entry.summary: Argues that improving latent-space fidelity in frontier models means prompts increasingly implicitly retrieve everything a user has publicly written online, effectively personalizing outputs in ways users do not realize. The post suggests this is underappreciated and worth proactively addressing with model configuration.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A peer-reviewed article describing Seal, an AI system for spatiotemporal modeling of gene regulation and genetic variant effects in the developing human brain. No body text was available, so the assessment relies on the title, which suggests a machine-learning tool applied to developmental neurogenomics with potential to interpret disease-relevant variants.

entry.title: Actionable Meta-Requirements for AI Robustness Auditing

author.name: Joshua Owotogbe, Roya Nasiri, Indika Kumara, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel

entry.summary: Through design science research combining literature and domain experts, the paper consolidates meta-requirements specifying what AI robustness auditing frameworks should support. It addresses the unresolved question of foundational requirements for judging whether evidence suffices for a robustness conclusion under distribution shift and perturbations.

entry.title: Self-Representation Alignment in Diffusion Models for Video Background Music Generation

author.name: Jincheng Zhang, Gy\"orgy Fazekas, Charalampos Saitis

entry.summary: Proposes U-SRA, a diffusion U-Net architecture that aligns weaker earlier-layer representations (at higher noise) with better later-layer representations (at lower noise) during training via an alignment loss. Applied to video background music generation, it aims to overcome the finding that internal diffusion representations are insufficiently meaningful. Improves a challenging multimodal generative task.

entry.title: Overtaught, Underlearned: Learner-Centered Distillation from Multi-Agent Discussion

author.name: Mengtao Zhou, Jianxiao Wang, Xiupeng Chen, Cailiang Liu, Jie Song

entry.summary: The paper identifies over-teaching (multiple correct solutions collapsing to one lesson) and under-learning (missed training questions) in distilling multi-agent discussion to a single student. It introduces FAR (Fold-Attempt-Revisit), a distillation procedure that organizes supervision around the student's own learning state.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Sharing: TrueMAD for Targeted Peer Engagement in Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Dezheng Bao, Sihang Du, Renhong Huang, Zhizhang Yuan, Yifei Sun, Yang Yang

entry.summary: TrueMAD is a backbone-agnostic test-time plug-in for multi-agent debate that inserts one-to-one, free-form peer advice (support, rebuttal, refinement) between answer broadcasting and self-revision, addressing the problem that broadcast-style MAD lets reliable reasoning be drowned out by majority responses. The targeted engagement aims to preserve sound minority reasoning and give actionable feedback on errors. It improves multi-agent reasoning at inference time.

entry.title: UA-Bench: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models on Underwater Acoustic Recognition

author.name: Zhe Sun, Liang An, Jiayu Yao, Ronglai Qian, Jianing Cai, Ziwei Huang, Qing Fan, Zhiyuan Yang, Yujun Cai, Hongli Cao, Yiwei Wang, Xiaoyan Wang

entry.summary: UA-Bench is the first large-scale benchmark evaluating large audio-language models on underwater acoustic recognition, using a faithful synthetic data pipeline modeling pulses, communication waveforms, ship noise, sound-speed profiles, geometry, and multipath propagation. It tests whether general audio pretraining transfers to maritime and ocean-sensing domains.

entry.title: Chasing Label Shifters: A Change-Aware Framework for Dynamic Graph Node Classification

author.name: Junghoon Kim, Seungyoon Choi, Hyunsung Kim, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: This work identifies shifters, nodes whose class labels change between consecutive snapshots in dynamic graphs, as systematically underperforming in all major dynamic GNN architectures. It proposes a change-aware framework for node classification that improves shifter detection, which matters for timely intervention in high-stakes domains like finance and healthcare.

entry.title: Fan Out or Relay? Ownership-Aware Routing for LLM Agents Querying Siloed Tables

author.name: Zhexi Feng

entry.summary: This single-author paper studies how LLM agent coordinators should query data distributed across owners who never share their tables: fanning out to all owners versus relaying queries in sequence. Across thirteen settings on PeopleJoin and BIRD, fan-out is more accurate for single-owner questions but fails badly (1-4% accuracy) on multi-owner joins, with the outcome determined by data ownership rather than query shape. The paper proposes ownership-aware routing as the deciding principle.

entry.title: Lifting Finite-Sample Gaussian Approximation of Wide Neural Networks to Functional Convergence

author.name: Luis Wiederhold, Nil Ayday, Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

entry.summary: This theory paper lifts finite-sample bounds on the convergence of wide random neural networks to Gaussian processes into functional convergence guarantees in quadratic Wasserstein distance. It combines the explicit constants and m^{-1/2} rate of finite-sample bounds with the sample-refinement robustness of functional bounds, removing prior limitations like spherical inputs or weaker metrics. This strengthens the theoretical foundations of the neural tangent/kernel regime.

entry.title: Task-evoked eye movements as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults

author.name: Youxiang Sun, Yujie Nie, Zhuoru Wu, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Xiang Li, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan

entry.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 155 participants aged 14-20, the authors show that task-evoked eye-movement features, such as reduced gaze-allocation entropy, correlate with depression severity as measured by the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. The work positions interpretable eye-movement markers as candidate digital biomarkers to complement clinical symptom assessment. This could enable more objective and timely depression evaluation in young populations.

entry.title: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Svar Rajankumar Patel, Kshitij Jerath

entry.summary: ADiCo is a two-timescale framework for adaptively controlling behavioral diversity in cooperative multi-agent RL: a fast Diversity Control loop regulates system diversity toward a target, while a slower extremum-seeking control loop adapts that target online during training. This enables role specialization and richer joint behaviors without costly task-dependent manual tuning of diversity levels.

entry.title: Tracing Morphology, Semantics, and Divergence in Language Acquisition

author.name: Forough Shirin Abkenar, Haoshuo Fu, Liang Feng, Ning Yan, Masood S. Mortazavi

entry.summary: Using intermediate checkpoints from open-source models like Pythia and OLMo under teacher-forcing evaluation, this study tracks language acquisition dynamics across training steps and model scales. It examines morphological structure acquisition, embedding drift, repetition dominance, and co-occurrence effects, characterizing how statistical representations evolve into structured linguistic capability.

entry.title: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing

author.name: Jose Miguel Lara Rangel, Mixtli Vazquez Mendoza

entry.summary: Introduces BeTINN, a structured conditional architecture extending time-induced modulation with multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway, evaluated on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE. It improves joint accuracy including economically relevant first- and second-order sensitivities in physics-informed neural network solutions.

entry.title: CktHGVAE: A Symmetric Design/State Heterogeneous Graph Variational Autoencoder for Transistor-level Analog/Mixed-signal Circuit Design and Analysis

author.name: Shigeyasu Uno

entry.summary: CktHGVAE is a heterogeneous graph VAE for transistor-level analog/mixed-signal CMOS circuits that models both design and state variables, achieving median R2 above 0.9 against SPICE simulation for typical amplifiers with a single hyperparameter configuration. Latent-space optimization with Bayesian and evolutionary search is demonstrated for circuit design. This shows useful ML acceleration for analog circuit design workflows.

entry.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection

author.name: Yaozhi Wen, Kun Zhao, Wei Wei, Haoyang Chen, Kangning Wang, Yi Sun, Shaowei Gu, Dingkun Liu, Shuang Qiu, Huiguang He

entry.summary: NeuroDETR is a framework for detecting events and their temporal boundaries directly from continuous EEG recordings, combining multiscale temporal codebooks, Spatial-Pyramid VQ over channels, and an event-aware detection head. The compact event memory allows joint classification and boundary detection without predefined event boundaries at inference. This advances practical brain-computer interfaces that must operate on unsegmented neural streams.

entry.title: An Initial Study of Physiological Markers for Deepfake Speech Detection

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Michal Fri\v{c}, Kamil Malinka, Anton Firc

entry.summary: Tests whether deepfake speech can be detected through inconsistencies in human physiological speech markers — respiration, phonation, and temporal coordination — using 36 handcrafted features with logistic regression and SVM classifiers. The best in-domain system reaches a 21.40% equal error rate, and the approach aims to generalize better than artifact-based detectors under unseen attacks. An initial study for a security-relevant hypothesis.

entry.title: Noisy-Label Calibration with Multiple Unreliable Labels

author.name: Keisuke Hanada, Futoshi Futami

entry.summary: The paper proposes Noise Corrected ECE, a binned estimator of expected calibration error under class-conditional noise from multiple noisy annotators, with non-asymptotic bias bounds, plus practical algorithms for estimating unknown noise probabilities. This enables unbiased calibration evaluation and recalibration in medical annotation and crowdsourcing where ground truth is unavailable. It addresses a real gap in trustworthy model evaluation under label noise.

entry.title: Multimodal Medical Image Parsing with Task-Specific Low-Rank Adapters

author.name: Taha Sabir, Alberto Montero Molina, Thinh Quang Ly, Veronika Dmitrenko, Mohammad Yaqub, Tausifa Jan Saleem

entry.summary: The paper adapts a shared frozen 4-bit Qwen3.5-9B vision-language backbone to medical image parsing across six task families and seven modalities using input-selected LoRA adapters with tuned ranks, prompt customization, and class rebalancing for FLARE 2026 Task 3. It reports solid macro balanced accuracy, micro-F1, and counting error results.

entry.title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization

author.name: Arth Sojitra, Muhammad Abid, Omer San

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates extreme super-resolution of turbulent flows at x32 and x64 factors by training a WDSR network on overlapping patches from a single high-resolution realization of homogeneous isotropic turbulence. Unseen flow fields are reconstructed via patchwise prediction with Hann-window overlap-add assembly.

entry.title: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback

author.name: Li Wang, Chen Zhang, Yirong Yang, Xingyu Chen, Jinkun Zhao, Tianhao Peng, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: SkillGrain is a framework for learning reusable personalized skills from user feedback by decomposing it into atomic rules, predicting each rule's transferability, and retaining only those likely to generalize to future requests. It combines rubric-guided skill rewards with fine-grained credit assignment to avoid negative transfer from request-specific corrections.

entry.title: RCCM: Diagnosing Gains and Harms in Reasoning-Prompt Transfer

author.name: Yuqi Zhang, Di Zhang

entry.summary: Examines reasoning-control capability mismatch, where a reasoning prompt improves one LLM deployment but degrades another, by pairing answers with records of how generation ends. Across five open-weight deployments and nine strategies, aggregate accuracy hides substantial question-level gains and harms, with concise reasoning helping Phi but sharply hurting Qwen under a token cap.

entry.title: VLX-Go: Robust Embodied Tracking through Multi-Stage Learning and On-Policy Refinement

author.name: Kyusong Lee, Heting Ying, Tiancheng Zhao

entry.summary: VLX-Go is a vision-language waypoint policy for embodied visual tracking built on the hypothesis that visual and language representations should be aligned before learning tracking-specific motion, combining complementary representations with multi-stage learning and on-policy refinement. It targets the large performance drop from single-target to distractor tracking in person-following.

entry.title: Quantifying Annotation Agreement in Object Detection with Optimal Transport

author.name: Kirill Prokhorov, Alexandr A. Kalinin

entry.summary: This paper proposes an optimal transport-based metric for measuring agreement between object detection annotation sets, assigning graded costs to matched and unmatched boxes instead of binarizing overlap. The authors provide theoretical analysis and show the metric better captures the degree and structure of annotation disagreement than standard binarized metrics.

entry.title: F2A-ObjectNav: An Adaptive Agentic Architecture for Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Seyed Ali Mirghasemi, Alireza Taheri

entry.summary: The paper studies object-goal navigation through a two-stage process: first a fixed modular framework reveals trade-offs among exploration, detection, and target-validation methods, then motivates F2A-ObjectNav, an adaptive agentic architecture that adjusts its configuration to conditions rather than committing to one fixed setup.

entry.title: RASSG: Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating for Streaming Tool Execution

author.name: Daijin Hu, Xi Wang

entry.summary: RASSG addresses stale tool execution in streaming speech assistants, where premature launches become invalid after user self-corrections and irreversible effects persist. It launches tools after three consistent recognition results and combines calibrated argument-invalidation risk with execution costs to decide cancellation at the last feasible opportunity.

entry.title: Theoretical and Practical Advances in Hierarchical Bayesian Deep Learning Methodology

author.name: Neil K. Chada, Simon Cotter, Kody J. H. Law, Xinzhu Liang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MLPMMH, combining pseudo-marginal hyperparameter inference with coupled sequential Monte Carlo across network-width truncations for joint inference of neural network parameters and prior hyperparameters, using a trace-class neural network prior. This targets reliable uncertainty quantification where conventional MCMC struggles with strong dependencies.

entry.title: KoAGE: Do Large Language Models Know, Learn, and Coin Korean Neologisms?

author.name: SungHo Kim, Eojin Jeon, SangKeun Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces NeoTrace, an automated framework for collecting and dating Korean neologisms, and KoAGE, a cutoff-aware benchmark with acquisition and generation tasks across 4,271 entries. Evaluating 21 models reveals that lexical recall diverges from contextual inference: models define only 13-30% of cutoff-year words yet can often infer meaning from a single usage.

entry.title: CB-Agent: Concept-Based In-Context Learning for Sequential Action Selection

author.name: Qingyue Zhang, Huaze Tang, Minyu Zhang, Yuxiang Yan, Wenbo Ding, Shao-Lun Huang

entry.summary: CB-Agent extends concept-based in-context learning to sequential action selection for LLM agents, extracting environment-action decisions from expert trajectories into reusable concepts rather than feeding full demonstrations or vague natural-language summaries. This lets expert action choices directly supervise a reusable scoring rule while conserving prompt space.

entry.title: GREAT-ESDD: Graph Edge Attention Network for Effectively Steered Delivery Decisions

author.name: Attila Lischka (Jeff), Ze Zhou (Jeff), Xuegang (Jeff), Ban, Bal\'azs Kulcs\'ar

entry.summary: The paper develops a neural solver for the capacitated vehicle routing problem using a graph edge attention network, trained to handle varying instance sizes and re-optimize partially executed routes. It embeds this solver in a dynamic pricing-and-routing framework for same-day delivery with home and out-of-home options.

entry.title: Continuous Risk-Based Scheduling for Food Safety Inspection: Integrating Historical Decay with Event-Driven Consumer Review Signals

author.name: Akriti Bhat, Wayne Zhu, Ishan Gupta

entry.summary: Introduces the Continuous Inspection Risk (CIR) system, which dynamically re-ranks food-safety inspection queues using decay-weighted historical scores plus real-time consumer reviews triaged by an LLM classifier. A temporal partition rule excludes reviews predating the latest inspection to prevent data leakage, targeting facilities that deteriorate between clean inspections.

entry.title: OntoAR-HAR: Ontology-Guided Agentic RAG with Personalized Memory for Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Xiangqing Lu, Tao Zhu, Liang Yu, Shuangjian Li, Lulu Ban, Furong Duan, Mingxing Nie, Liming Chen, Yaping Wan

entry.summary: Proposes OntoAR-HAR, an ontology-guided agentic RAG framework for wearable-sensor human activity recognition that combines static population knowledge with personalized motion patterns. A tree-structured activity ontology decomposes the activity space to avoid comparing unrelated candidates using uniform population evidence. Enables training-free, target-user inference.

entry.title: Comparative Study of Canvas- and Coordinate-Based Geometry-Conditioned Neural Networks for Real-Time Prediction of Indoor Environments with Varying Room Dimensions

author.name: Shaofan Wang, Philipp Geyer

entry.summary: This paper compares canvas-based and coordinate-based geometry-conditioned neural network surrogates for rapid prediction of indoor airflow and temperature fields across varying room dimensions, as a fast alternative to computational fluid dynamics in iterative building design. The comparison targets real-time assessment of whether conditioned supply air effectively covers rooms of different sizes.

entry.title: When a Conceptor Complement Becomes Gain: Operator Geometry and Behavioral Attribution in Language Models

author.name: Shuhul Razdan, R Balamurugan

entry.summary: This work examines which component of a conceptor-based steering intervention causes behavioral change in language models, by removing its fitted covariance filter while preserving target-specific center and gain. Across three models and seven targets, the matrix correction contributes little additional target-specific effect, suggesting the gain, not the covariance map, drives most behavior.

entry.title: Does the Explanation Drift Before the Guarantee? Label-Free Early Warning on Evolving Graphs

author.name: Tomasz Szanda{\l}a, Damian Raczkowski

entry.summary: The paper studies whether attribution drift on graph streams can serve as a label-free early warning for the loss of conformal prediction coverage. It repairs two flaws in naive drift statistics, conditioning on edge presence and aggregating over structural roles to survive node relabeling, and tests six pre-registered regression configurations.

entry.title: PRAISE: A Reproducible Workflow for Non-Programmer Scientists to Implement Published AI Models

author.name: Max Achterweust, Stefan Groot Nibbelink, Vincent J. de Beer, Stefan Schipper, Zeynep Y\"uksektepe, Pedro Andrade da Silva, Aurelia Peppelaar, Martijn J. van der Willigen, Christophe B. Minkenberg, Robert F. van der Willigen

entry.summary: PRAISE is a hands-on, step-by-step workflow helping non-programmer scientists and students implement published AI models on their own data, anticipating common implementation failures and providing a fallback route for each. It bridges the gap between single-step guidelines and the full route from a published model to working predictions, demonstrated as a proof of principle.

entry.title: Reliable Text-to-SQL in Resource-Constrained Settings with Small LLMs via Iterative Retry Workflows

author.name: Bilel Abderrahmane Benziane, Xavier Schepler

entry.summary: The paper evaluates small and medium open-source LLMs (1B-8B) for text-to-SQL under controlled inference budgets on Spider, finding SQL-specialized models consistently more reliable than general-purpose ones and high prompt sensitivity. An iterative retry workflow reduces this variability without retraining.

entry.title: AgentStripes: An Evidence-Graded Maturity Model for AI Agents

author.name: Nutan Kumar Naik, Vijay Prasad Poudel, Aditya Kumar Saroj, Saurav Samantray, Abhishek Patel

entry.summary: AgentStripes proposes a maturity model for AI agents with levels 0-7, twelve process areas holding 40 capabilities, three gates (basic, safety, proof), and evidence grades E0-E5. Capabilities receive ratings and evidence levels combined into severity-weighted scores, providing a framework for assessing whether released agent versions have reliable, safe, and observable engineering controls.

entry.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards

author.name: Xin Gao, Yifan Yang, Xin Li, Pan Wang, Yan Li, Muzhao Tian, Mingxi Cheng, Bei Liu, Kai Qiu, Qi Dai, Dong Chen, Yue Dong, Leandros Tassiulas, Rex Ying, Ji Li, Chong Luo

entry.summary: AesCode generates visual artifacts such as slides, posters, and dashboards as code, using an image generated from the same prompt as aesthetic guidance while keeping content grounded in the prompt. It represents the target canvas as a design graph so that layout and color properties are individually attributable, enabling decoupled cross-modal rewards for training. This targets the gap where code models cannot see the visual result of their choices.

entry.title: Jevolution: A Framework for Studying Communication and Collective Dynamics in AI Agents

author.name: Xirui Huang, Nikhil Hooda, Utkarsh Gupta

entry.summary: Presents Jevolution, an instrumented spatial predator-prey simulation framework for studying communication and collective dynamics among AI agents. It separates the evolving world, asynchronous scheduling, controller adapters, and experiment records, documenting mechanisms via the ODD protocol and releasing synthetic data.

entry.title: Depth-progressive 3D seismic velocity model building via 2D generative diffusion models

author.name: Shijun Cheng, Randy Harsuko, Mohammad H. Taufik, Tariq Alkhalifah

entry.summary: This paper achieves 3D seismic velocity model building using 2D generative diffusion models by mapping the depth dimension of 3D velocity patches to the channel dimension of a 2D U-Net. The depth-progressive framework synthesizes patches from shallow to deep, conditioning deeper predictions on shallower ones and on geophysical constraints like well logs.

entry.title: Dynamic Conflict Clustering with Lightweight Learning and Strategic Repair for Distributed Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Raziyeh Moghaddas, Fabio Caraffini

entry.summary: DCC-Incomplete is a repair-based solver for distributed constraint satisfaction problems that combines conflict-centered decomposition, structured coordination, strategic repair, and lightweight learning for stagnation recovery. It reduces the broad repeated peer-to-peer communication that hampers existing reactive DCSP solvers on hard instances.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal Sensor Fusion with JEPA Representations for Breathing Activity and Pose Recognition

author.name: Yunxiang Luo, Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Xiaoting Wu, Nhi Nguyen, Le Nguyen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: This work transfers frozen V-JEPA2 features to heterogeneous sensors (RGB, depth, radar) for breathing activity and pose recognition, using a shared fusion model with modality queries and explicit sensor availability to handle all seven non-empty sensor subsets. It provides a controlled evaluation of subset supervision and pooling on 39 subjects.

entry.title: OT-FlowRec: Optimal Transport-Guided Multi-Bridge Flow for Multimodal Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Miao Sun

entry.summary: Proposes OT-FlowRec, an optimal transport-guided multi-bridge flow matching framework for multimodal sequential recommendation that models concurrent, multi-centric user interest distributions via parallel interest-specific transport flows instead of single-path generative models. It targets e-commerce settings where preferences evolve dynamically within sessions.

entry.title: KNN Implementation Details Can Dramatically Change Performance: An Example from Cover Trees

author.name: Amol Khanna, Edward Raff

entry.summary: The paper shows that seldom-reviewed implementation details materially change nearest neighbor search performance, using the Cover Tree as a case study and releasing RustKNN, a unified Rust implementation of three construction variants and three query modes. Findings include strategy-dependent performance across k values and datasets that alter comparative conclusions about algorithms.

entry.title: AIPOCH Open-Science: An Open-Source AI Research Workbench with Reproducible .science Packages

author.name: Wen Ouyang, Bocheng Huang, Qianyu Yao, Fei Sun, Minying Deng, Haoyue Cheng, Wenwen Zhou, Lei Mou, Yusi Wei, Jiang Li, Kun Zhu, Lei Wang, Yi Feng, Jiaheng Dai, Ke Qian, Dan Wang, Yahui Wang, Chenyi Wang, Mingsheng Lyu, Yaqiang Zhang, Ping Zheng, Chunhua Tang, Xinge Ma, Xu Zhang, Youjia Fan, Can Lu, Zhijun Dai, Man Hu, Qiqi Xie, Beinan Liu, Yuanning Guo, Yunze Liu, Jinhong Jiang, Xianjun Fu, Mingwei Zhang, Yuanji Xu, Shilin Xia, Bowen Yang, Mingjun Yu, Jingdun Xie, Xuwei Chen, Xia Zou, Yuzhou Xue, Jianguo Zhou, Chunhao Cao, Donghao Tian, Lei Huang, Jinxiao Li, Shengrong Long, Zefeng Song, Honglin Li, Jiang Luo, Wenying Jiang, Shanshan Li, Lei Dai, Ning Jiang, Ying Cai, Chaohui Li, Chunyan Peng, Hetong Zhao, Angqing Li, Chunyan Yang, Chongyang Sun, Yong Li, Xinyu Shi, Wei Dai, Ming Peng, Chen Sang, Yuanyuan Han, Desong Qiu, Haixin Miao, Jian Xu, Yi Chen, Xiaoliang Shi, Tian Shen, Teng Hu, Shuhao Wang, Yingyong Hou, Huimei Wang

entry.summary: Presents an open-source research workbench that records the relationships between instructions, computations, artifact revisions, and checks in AI-assisted research, packaged as portable .science session files with an exchange contract supporting attribution, workspace remapping, explicit omissions, and fork separation. A controlled session validated exports against source records across correction and revision scenarios.

entry.title: Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Han Bao, Shinsaku Sakaue, Kazuki Watanabe

entry.summary: This paper provides a unified convex-analytic framework for query selection in MDP safety verification, where queries bound weighted sums of failure probabilities against a convex safe region. Directions are scored by support-function gaps normalized by error units, and the maximal score equals the smallest safe-region enlargement achievable by a query.

entry.title: Uncertainty Evaluation: Bridging Machine Learning and Measurement Science

author.name: Dario Petri, Luca Mari

entry.summary: This paper draws conceptual analogies between uncertainty evaluation in machine learning and the metrology framework from the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (GUM). It critiques the conventional aleatoric/epistemic dichotomy by analogy to the outdated random/systematic error distinction, and distinguishes process-level from result-level quality. The goal is to ground ML trustworthiness, especially in safety-critical applications, in established measurement science.

entry.title: Looped Reasoning Finishes Earlier Than You Think

author.name: Sumin Park, T. Konstantin Rusch

entry.summary: The paper analyzes looped reasoning models with dynamic depth through the lens of learned dynamical systems, showing that slowly decaying oscillatory modes can bottleneck convergence of latent trajectories that oscillate or drift rather than settle. It proposes adding rotational degrees of freedom so symmetry-generated rotational motion separates from reasoning-relevant computation, enabling earlier, cleaner stopping. This connects recurrence dynamics to adaptive-compute efficiency.

entry.title: A Controlled Evaluation of Curvature Inspired Scalar Feature Scaling for Domain Generalization

author.name: Sunny Gupta, Amit Sethi

entry.summary: This paper audits HyperDG, a domain generalization method described as curvature-inspired, and finds that its actual implementation merely rescales Euclidean encoder features with learned positive scalars during training rather than using hyperbolic (Lorentz or Poincare) representations, geodesic prediction, or a SAM inner loop. The authors run a controlled evaluation of six conditions across PACS, VLCS, Office Home, and TerraIncognita with 384 total runs to isolate what the technique actually contributes. The work matters because it provides a reproducibility-style reality check on a fashionable geometric learning idea, clarifying whether gains come from curvature itself or from simple feature scaling.

entry.title: FALLNEST: Dual-Domain Dataset Condensation of Imbalanced IMU Data for Wearable Fall Detection

author.name: Rashi Niyas P, Ritika Jain, Hitika Tiwari

entry.summary: FALLNEST condenses large, imbalanced IMU datasets into tiny class-balanced synthetic training sets for wearable fall detection, using normalized-gradient and embedding-matched time-frequency condensation built on dual-domain time-series condensation. It aims to cut training data and compute while handling rare fall events.

entry.title: Bytes to Threats: Byte-Sequence Transformer For Malware Detection

author.name: Abdelrahman Yassin Eljamal, Abdeltawab Hendawi

entry.summary: MalwareFormer is a transformer-based, byte-level malware detection framework that operates directly on raw executable bytes, avoiding handcrafted static or dynamic analysis features, and captures long-range dependencies that CNN-based methods miss. This improves scalability and robustness against increasingly complex and diverse modern malware.

entry.title: Graph Coarsening Enables Escaping Local Optima in Compute-Constrained Nonconvex MAX-CUT

author.name: M. Harper Langston, Pierre-David Letourneau, Dalton Jones, Harris Teague, Peter Scott, Mingu Lee, Richard Lethin, Chris Lott, Roland Memisevic, Fatih Porikli

entry.summary: The paper warm-starts Particle Polynomial Relaxation with Combinatorial Multigrid spectral graph coarsening to escape local optima in MAX-CUT under compute constraints. The combined pipeline reaches 97.5% of optimum on a benchmark instance with known exact optimum and matches published optima across sixty Biq Mac instances with local-search refinement.

entry.title: Historical-Feature Residual Adaptation for Sequential Screening

author.name: Yixiang Hong, Yuchen Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes acquisition-time residual adaptation for sequential screening: a small ranking correction built from fixed historical features and anchored to base scores recorded before feedback is revealed, instantiated by augmenting AssayFormer representations with 64 historical directions. On 20 retrospective screens it raised the source-macro fraction of hits recovered from 22.58% to 28.61%, beating six prespecified comparisons.

entry.title: BFHD: Bidirectional Feature Harmonization Decomposition for Heterogeneous Clinical Assessments

author.name: Yuanhao Zhuo, Zixi Qin, Ling Qin, Wanqing Li

entry.summary: BFHD frames clinical assessment harmonization across heterogeneous measurement systems as a bidirectional recoverability problem, identifying which measurements can be reliably translated between systems within a tolerance. The framework enforces bidirectionally coupled translation with feature-wise output gating to separate non-translatable components. This improves measurement-level integration of clinical data across centers and time.

entry.title: SPARS: A Stability-Plasticity-Aware Region Selection Framework for Continual Learning

author.name: Teif Aldaajani, Huda Hakami, Maha A. Thafar

entry.summary: SPARS is a replay-free hybrid continual learning framework combining global, modular, and local approaches to balance stability and plasticity while avoiding the privacy, memory, and scalability issues of memory replay. It selects regions of the network for updating to prevent catastrophic forgetting without storing past samples. It offers a practical middle ground between parameter isolation and regularization methods.

entry.title: Seeing at the Edge: Energy Characterization of Vision-Language Model Inference on Edge Platforms

author.name: Junlin Liao, Harshit Kondle, Di Liu, Zonghua Gu

entry.summary: The paper measures system-level energy, latency, and thermal behavior of Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct on a Raspberry Pi 5 with an Hailo NPU and a Jetson Orin Nano, decomposing per-request fixed energy from output-length-dependent energy. Key findings include that NPU offloading substantially cuts energy per generated token on the Pi, while differing quantization and serving stacks complicate silicon-level comparisons.

entry.title: MAEM: Mitigating Recency Bias via a Replay-Free, Capacity-Controlled Dynamic Mixture of Experts for Class-Incremental Graph Learning

author.name: Junlin Chen, Wenhao Wang, Junchao Xu, Qingsong Yao, Fei Xue, Li Sun, Xiao Wang, Ruijie Wang

entry.summary: MAEM is a replay-free, capacity-controlled dynamic mixture-of-experts framework for class-incremental graph learning that combats recency bias without requiring task identities at test time. It addresses router drift by controlling continual router fine-tuning so routing does not collapse toward recently learned components.

entry.title: Distinguishing Process Change, Instrument Fault and Data-Path Corruption in Streaming Telemetry: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark

author.name: Oleksandr Klymenko

entry.summary: Formalizes the three-cause problem in streaming telemetry — process change, instrument failure, or data corruption — proving which pairs a single channel cannot separate. It combines a bank of online detectors (Kalman tracker with CUSUM/EWMA, Hampel with generalized-ESD, robust noise statistics with ADWIN) under a deterministic attribution rule, released as a public library. Provides a reference implementation and benchmark for an under-formalized monitoring problem.

entry.title: State-Matched Sequence Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ruihang Han, Li-Hsiang Lin

entry.summary: SMSCP improves sequential conformal prediction by building an explicit one-sided local-linear state from pre-target information and using state similarity to select a matched reference set of past calibration scores, rather than relying only on recency. This handles settings where comparable states recur at nonadjacent times with unknown recurrence patterns. It retains standard conformal order statistics for valid coverage.

entry.title: When Does the Dependency Graph Help Code-to-Architecture Mapping?

author.name: Rakhshanda Jabeen, Morgan Ericsson, Jonas Nordqvist, Anna Wingkvist

entry.summary: This study formulates code-to-architecture mapping as semi-supervised node classification over a typed dependency graph, comparing GCN, GAT, and graph-free MLP baselines with iterative self-training from a small labeled sample. It clarifies when graph structure actually helps recover intended modular decomposition to manage architectural technical debt.

entry.title: Continual pretraining Prostate MRI ViT Encoder for task alignment

author.name: Bilal A. Sidiqi, Yipei Wang, Shaheer U. Saeed, Shiqi Huang, Daniel C. Alexander, Yipeng Hu

entry.summary: This paper explores continual pretraining of a vision transformer encoder on prostate MRI using LoRA, arguing that task alignment between pretraining and downstream objectives has been underexamined in medical foundation models. It shows that domain-specific continual pretraining improves downstream task performance on prostate MRI analysis.

entry.title: Crossing the Gender Binary: Modelling Gendered Reference in Science Fiction and General Fiction

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Haim Dubossarsky, Ruth Ahnert

entry.summary: This computational humanities study masks gendered terms (man, woman, person) in science fiction and general fiction corpora and analyzes RoBERTa's predicted substitutes, testing whether science fiction linguistically unsettles gender more than general fiction. Both corpora cross the gender binary, but unequally, with masculine substitutions predicted about twice as often where woman is masked. It offers a careful, statistically grounded look at gendered language in genre fiction.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Efficiently Identify Appliance Faults? Insights From Diagnosing a Simulated Appliance

author.name: Lucas H. McCabe, Sarah Lukens, H. Howie Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces CoffeeBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on fault diagnostics for a simulated industrial appliance, targeting Industry 4.0 asset management beyond exam-style benchmarks. The authors find that most models struggle to identify faults from sensor data alone, though the best performers improve through iterative reasoning.

entry.title: How Do LLMs Understand Legal Philosophy? Diagnosing Legal-Philosophical Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Shuyuan Zheng, Yun-seo Lee, Xing Gao, Jialu Wu, Jiabao Hu, Katrina Qiyao Wang, Xinbo Lin, Qianying Liu, Chuan Xiao, Tao Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces LePhilBench, a benchmark assessing whether LLMs can apply legal-philosophical perspectives (judicial views on the nature and sources of law) in legal reasoning, with two tasks and a supporting dataset. This targets a previously overlooked dimension that explains why judges reach different conclusions from identical materials.

entry.title: MakSafe: A Spatiotemporal Semantic Framework for Formal Specification and Compliance Checking of Road Vehicle Safety Rules

author.name: Maksym Labzhaniia (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Julien Deantoni (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Marie-Agn{\`e}s Peraldi-Frati (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric Mallet (Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, I3S, KAIROS, UniCA)

entry.summary: Presents MakSafe, a formal spatiotemporal framework for specifying and checking road vehicle safety rules using semantic zones, action-based forecasting, and trace-tree reasoning without uniform time discretization. It includes executable rules such as front-vehicle identification and time-to-collision verification, with scalability benchmarks over traffic density and branching.

entry.title: CSWBench: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Code-Switching in Creative Writing

author.name: Zewen Jiang, Yahan Li, Chenlu Guo, Diana Inkpen, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: This paper introduces CSWBench, a benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can decide when, where, and why to switch languages contextually in creative writing, tested in Focused and Extended Narrative settings. It also proposes CSWEval, a theory-informed framework with event-level criteria (Licensing, Contextual Appropriateness, Functional Gain) and whole-text evaluation. The work fills a real gap, since multilingual proficiency does not imply pragmatically appropriate code-switching.

entry.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Mahdieh Mallahnezhad, Masoud Jafaripour, Mohamadali Tofigh, Sheila Schoepp, Osmar R. Zaiane

entry.summary: This survey organizes post-training approaches to improving spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs, from supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on datasets. It categorizes the literature into dataset design, dataset construction, and evaluation, providing a data-centric lens on a known MLLM weakness.

entry.title: MonoMIP: Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping for Monocular 3D Object Detection

author.name: Emir Ulurak, Furkan K{\i}ra\c{c}

entry.summary: MonoMIP adds Bird's-Eye View geometric reasoning to depth-guided monocular 3D detection by performing inverse perspective mapping across K elevation planes, producing height-conditioned metric BEV features that reduce above-ground misprojection. A BEV decoder with multi-scale deformable attention aggregates this multi-height evidence alongside perspective features.

entry.title: Reducing the Gap Between Spatial and Space-Filling Curve Neighbors in 3D Point Cloud Segmentation

author.name: Konan Sasaki, Junya Komori, Kazuhiro Hotta

entry.summary: The paper proposes a loss function that reduces the mismatch between proximity along space-filling curves and Euclidean proximity in 3D point clouds, by optimizing feature similarity for SFC-adjacent but spatially distant point pairs. Incorporated into an existing segmentation model, it improves results across three datasets.

entry.title: FPV-CRASH: A Dataset for Offline Crash Moment Localization in Drone First-Person-View Videos

author.name: Jifan Zhang, Tingyu Wang, Qian Liu, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: FPV-CRASH is a new dataset and evaluation protocol for localizing the major physical impact moment in drone first-person-view videos, containing 1,052 clips split evenly between crash and normal footage with standardized annotations. It fills a gap since existing crash-video datasets target surveillance or dashcam footage with incompatible task formulations.

entry.title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT

author.name: Bowen Xiang, Dingjie Su, Jon S. Heiselman, Michael I. Miga

entry.summary: The paper proposes a reusable, label-aware front end for cinematic CT Gaussian splatting that maps a patient's CT, anatomical labels, and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B Gaussian positions without per-patient optimization. A population-trained neural prior preserves vessels under real-time display budgets while other attributes remain per-patient.

entry.title: RingNav: Task-Shaped Circular Memory for Visual Heading

author.name: Naitri Rajyaguru, Aryan Tajne, Stephen Jardim, Cornelia Fermuller, Yiannis Aloimonos

entry.summary: RingNav is a tiny (10.6k-parameter) visual heading estimator whose memory state is constrained to the circular manifold, learning only the turn between consecutive images and composing heading directly on the circle. It reduces turn error by 27 percent and accumulated heading error by 15 percent on TartanAir versus a comparably sized learned-memory baseline.

entry.title: MIND: Instruction-Conditioned Incremental Grounding for Robots

author.name: Mohamed Abouagour, Junhyun Nam, Wonse Jo, Byung-Cheol Min

entry.summary: MIND maintains language-conditioned target-room decisions in changing environments without re-evaluating every room after each event, by compiling instructions into semantic dependencies and intersecting them with event footprints. It refreshes only affected judgments, preserving the results of full recomputation under deterministic conditions. This is an efficient approach to persistent instruction following under partial observability.

entry.title: Dual-arm Cooperation for Tabletop Wiping with Temporal Object Removal

author.name: Pengqi Zhang, Longchang Yu, Daohan Li, Liang Yan, Hangxin Liu

entry.summary: A dual-arm planning framework for wiping tabletops where one arm rearranges scattered objects while the other wipes, enabling coverage of previously obstructed regions. It uses action primitives combined with a geometry-aware MILP planner and Logic-Based Benders Decomposition to optimize action sequencing and timing.

entry.title: EarlyCommit: Calibrated Word-by-Word Commitment for Robots Acting Before You Finish Speaking

author.name: Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: EarlyCommit is an open-source tool letting a robot commit to the intended object while an instruction is still being spoken: after each recognized word, a fine-tuned text encoder scores objects, and the robot acts when calibrated probability exceeds a user-set risk threshold. It includes streaming speech input, scene/instruction generation with word-level ground truth, and scripts.

entry.title: Subdata Selection for Measurement-Constrained Linear Regression under Model Misspecification

author.name: Yundi Kong, Min Yang, Ping-Shou Zhong

entry.summary: This paper addresses settings where responses are expensive to measure, so only a small subset of units can be selected for outcome collection from a large pool with available covariates. The authors develop subdata selection methods for measurement-constrained linear regression that remain statistically efficient under model misspecification, unlike prior subsampling work that assumes correct specification and targets computational rather than measurement savings.

entry.title: PPA 9: Putting it All Together

author.name: Onid

entry.summary: The culminating installment of a nine-part LessWrong series on the Parametric Process Assumption (PPA), a proposed new framework for anthropic reasoning. It synthesizes earlier arguments, showing that SSA-style Doomsday bias weakens as the number of species in a reference class grows, and lays out a Basic Model decomposing anthropic effects into propensity for life, longevity, and diversity.

entry.title: MemeLogos: Knowledge-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection

author.name: Hexiang Gu, Saihui Hou, Changlan Liu, Min Ren, Huijia Wu, Hongxun Gu, Zhaofeng He
