entry.summary: Proposes MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning framework for detecting harmful memes whose harmfulness is implicit across visual, textual, and contextual cues. Unlike prior RAG methods that retrieve similar instances, it retrieves reusable harmfulness knowledge and underlying reasoning mechanisms, improving both detection performance and interpretability.

entry.title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN

author.name: Anoop Mishra, Joshua Moore, Aly Sabri Abdalla, Vuk Marojevic

entry.summary: AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with two LoRA stages over 69 O-RAN and 3GPP standards documents, augmented with RAG, to perform automated security triage of O-RAN testing from investigator-style questions alone, without raw packet access. It is validated on a purpose-built benchmark.

entry.title: ListQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating List-Formatted Factual Knowledge Retrieval in Large Language Models

author.name: Mayank Kulkarni, Rakesh Vaideeswaran

entry.summary: ListQA is a benchmark of 9,045 human-curated questions with a 1.7% audited error rate requiring LLMs to recall multiple facts and compose structured lists, from flat to hierarchical with sub-attributes, spanning 60+ countries. Its evergreen design using temporal constraints keeps ground truth valid without periodic updates.

entry.title: Design and Analysis of Temporal Representations in Neural Networks

author.name: Alban Colas-Gattepaille (I3S), Alexandre Muzy (ILLS)

entry.summary: The paper introduces a formal notion of degree of temporal representation, classifying neural networks along a continuum based on whether activation, learning, encoding, and decoding functions explicitly manipulate time as a computational variable. This framework is motivated by spiking neural networks and the hypothesized role of temporal coding in biological efficiency.

entry.title: Design and Characterization of a Unified Continuum Robot Actuation Platform

author.name: Yunti Xu, Aedan Mangan, Miheer Potdar, Alex Lu, Tania K. Morimoto

entry.summary: The paper presents a modular actuation platform that decouples continuum robot actuation hardware and software from robot design, scaling to many DoFs and integrating with serial manipulators for hybrid architectures. It is validated on an open-sourced surgical robotic system with experimental actuation characterization, targeting reuse across applications like minimally invasive surgery and inspection.

entry.title: Learning after Execution with Action-Specific Credit

author.name: Yufeng Tian, Jiahao Tang, Minghao Wu

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning after execution, where an execution result serves as an intermediate state enabling a further corrective learning action for the same policy, with action-specific credit assignment separating credit for the initial action from the corrective action. Image-to-TikZ serves as the executable testbed, showing strengthened learning on 945 held-out examples.

entry.title: Trust Hinders Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment

author.name: Michaela Benk, Kacper Sokol

entry.summary: Argues that trust calibration is an overly restrictive frame for AI-assisted decision making, developing three dimensions: trust as only one uncertainty-management strategy, misapplication of calibration to ill-defined large-world problems, and the need for bidirectional human-AI alignment. It is a conceptual/position piece.

entry.title: A Decade of PhotoMappers: A Longitudinal Study of Crowdsourced Disaster Photos Geolocalization with Vision-Language Models and Geospatial Reasoning

author.name: Hao Li, Wenping Yin, Fabian Deuser, Jia Jia, Ziqi Liu, Levente Juh\'asz, Fan Zhang, Filip Biljecki

entry.summary: Analyzes over a decade of crowdsourced disaster imagery from PhotoMappers to study the changing geography of disaster information and compare GeoAI models with human geographic interpretation. Combines longitudinal spatial analysis with cross-view geolocalization using street view and remote sensing imagery, evaluating vision-language models for GEOINT applications. Demonstrates the value of crowdsourced imagery when conventional mapping is delayed.

entry.title: Multi-Horizon Explainable Queue Forecasting and Resource-Aware Decision Support for Intelligent Border Control Using LightGBM

author.name: Varvara Mama, Fani D. Christidi, Nikolaos C. Kapsalis, Anargyros T. Baklezos, Christos D. Nikolopoulos

entry.summary: This paper extends a border-crossing queue-management framework with horizon-specific LightGBM regressors producing 15, 30, 60, and 120 minute forecasts of waiting times and queue lengths from lagged traffic, service, and staffing features. An operations-oriented decision-support layer translates the forecasts into resource-aware recommendations for lane allocation at border control points.

entry.title: ChronoScribe: Semantic-Numerical Specialization for Instruction-Driven Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuchen Jiao, Miao Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Chengxi Li

entry.summary: ChronoScribe addresses instruction-driven time series forecasting by combining a LoRA-adapted LLM, which proposes execution paths and context lengths from natural-language requests, with time series foundation models that produce the numerical forecasts via deterministic rule resolution. This decouples semantic understanding from numerical prediction.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformers for Hierarchical Intention Recognition from Multimodal Human Activity Sequences

author.name: Farnaz Soleimani (LISSI), Abdelghani Chibani (LISSI), Yacine Amirat (LISSI), Ghazaleh Khodabandelou (LISSI)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformer that integrates a Human Reasoning Graph into self-attention via learnable topological biases, with a differentiable first-order-logic loss enforcing ontological consistency across hierarchy levels. It targets proactive human-robot collaboration by inferring hierarchical intentions from multimodal activity sequences rather than flat action classification. This bridges neural perception and symbolic reasoning for robotics.

entry.title: Two Routes to Interoceptive Prioritisation: Dissociating Likelihood Precision and Preference Reweighting in Active Inference

author.name: St John Grimbly, Nicolas Kuske, Evert A. Boonstra, Charel van Hoof, Rowan Hodson, Benjamin Rosman, Ryan Smith, Mark Solms, Jonathan P. Shock

entry.summary: In an active inference foraging gridworld with three lethal needs, the authors dissociate two interventions for prioritizing urgent bodily needs: sharpening likelihood precision on interoceptive information versus reweighting preferences for relieving outcomes. Precision improves survival while preference reweighting keeps states farther from lethal boundaries but degrades the learned body model.

entry.title: Latent Algorithmic Structure Precedes Grokking: A Mechanistic Study of ReLU MLPs on Modular Arithmetic

author.name: Anand Swaroop

entry.summary: This mechanistic study finds that ReLU MLPs trained on modular arithmetic learn near-binary square wave input weights, unlike the sinusoidal distributions reported for transformers, and that a phase-sum relation in output weight Fourier phases holds even under noisy training that fails to grok. The results suggest latent algorithmic structure forms before the grokking transition is visible in validation accuracy. This refines the mechanistic understanding of grokking phenomena.

entry.title: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams

author.name: Zirui Shang, Xin Shu, Yang Liu, Zhi Gao, Xinxiao Wu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: The paper proposes activation-conditioned selective knowledge control for GUI agents learning continually from streams of applications, using neuron-level gradient manipulation to protect previously learned knowledge while absorbing new-application knowledge. It maintains a compact historical knowledge state to identify highly activated MLP neurons carrying prior knowledge. This addresses catastrophic forgetting for agents adapting to evolving software.

entry.title: LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising

author.name: Wen Zhang, Xiao Bai, Hsiang-wei Chao, Mengfan Zhu, Tong Zhao, Mingxuan Ju, Xiaodong Liu, Congfei Zhang, Yunzhi Zhou, Yajun Wang, Jinchao Li, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based user-product relevance metric for offline evaluation of e-commerce advertising retrieval systems, compressing engagement history into intent representatives via semantic-ID-grouped, event-stratified segmentation and aggregating per-intent relevance into a stable, interpretable user-level score.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual TTS for Indian Languages: A Benchmark and Inference-Time Duration Estimation Strategies

author.name: Adarsh Arigala, Arjun Gangwar, Srinivasan Umesh

entry.summary: The paper constructs a cross-lingual TTS evaluation benchmark covering English and nine Indian languages, addressing duration mismatch in alignment-free TTS models. It proposes language-aware inference-time duration estimation strategies that avoid adding explicit duration predictors or model complexity.

entry.title: The Imperishable Record, Forgiveness, and the Future of Criminal Justice

author.name: Mark Fenwick, Paulius Jurcys, Sebastian Porsdam Mann

entry.summary: A philosophy and law paper arguing that indefinite digital records combined with AI-driven influence over life outcomes create an eternal data present that threatens forgiveness in criminal justice. Drawing on Hegel and Arendt, the authors distinguish permanent identification with past acts from irreversibility of action and propose a right to remain unfinished with supporting rights to forgetting, correction, and reimagination.

entry.title: An Explainable System for Offensive Content Detection in Nastaliq Urdu: Corpus Curation, Transformer Benchmarking, and Word-Level Attribution

author.name: Muhammad Shahid Iqbal Malik

entry.summary: The paper curates and publicly releases a corrected corpus of 7,604 Nastaliq-script Urdu Facebook comments for offensive content detection, fine-tunes and benchmarks transformer models, and adds word-level attribution for interpretability. It fills a coverage gap, since moderation research is almost entirely confined to English.

entry.title: MP-MNCA: Morphology-Prior Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention for Efficient Spatial Domain Identification

author.name: Sidharthan Sivacoumar Chitra, Sanjeev Manivannan

entry.summary: Introduces MP-MNCA, a masked neighbor cross-attention framework for spatial transcriptomics that preserves full 3000-gene representations while routing molecular information across spatial neighbors with histological similarity as a continuous attention prior. Evaluated across 12 human DLPFC sections against established baselines with attention to convergence efficiency.

entry.title: Integrating Feature Understandability into Feature Selection for Human-Centred Tabular Explanations

author.name: Nicola Rossberg, Bennett Kleinberg, Barry O'Sullivan, Luca Longo, Andrea Visentin

entry.summary: This study incorporates human-based feature understandability scores directly into feature selection for tabular ML, so that natural-language explanations cite features users can actually comprehend, rather than evaluating explainability only after generation. It aims to make human-centred XAI actionable during model building.

entry.title: Comparing GenAI to Machine Learning and Manual Review for eDiscovery

author.name: Gordon V. Cormack, Maura R. Grossman, Jeremy Pickens

entry.summary: The authors critique a Redgrave LLP case study claiming Relativity's generative AI review tool achieved 88% recall versus 64% for its ML tool, arguing the comparison is invalid due to differing objectives, assessor disagreement, and recall-precision and cost trade-offs. Their reanalysis finds aiR and manual review comparable, while established CAL-based ML remains state of the art.

entry.title: The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision

author.name: Amman Yusuf, Jiwoo Shin, Ruizhi Deng, Heitor Rodrigues Guimar\~{a}es, Nikita Dvornik, Mijung Park

entry.summary: SADDER extends the Safety-Aware Denoiser for text diffusion models by applying a token-level safety-guidance signal in embedding space, gating the SAD update rule so tokens with high unsafe signals are more likely modified during inference. This improves the safety-quality tradeoff of training-free safety guidance for text diffusion.

entry.title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Hanlin Kong, Jianan Wei, Yuntian Chen, Yujia Wang, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: This work presents a turbulence-aware super-resolution framework for time-resolved 3D turbulent flow reconstruction from coarse-grained data, coupling multiscale structure modeling with temporal coherence. It targets a real limitation of data-driven approaches, which struggle to recover volumetric multiscale structures. Relevant to engineering and scientific applications where direct numerical simulation or high-resolution measurement is prohibitively expensive.

entry.title: Reset Early, Reset Often, Eliminate Models

author.name: Martin S. Fixman, Fredrik R{\o}mming, Sean B. Holden

entry.summary: SATResetCoP improves connection-tableau automated theorem provers by abandoning backtracking on unproductive tableaux and instead starting fresh ones, feeding additional ground clauses to a persistent incremental SAT solver. On TPTP it outperforms a leanCoP-style baseline by 54% and a SATCoP-style baseline further. This is a clean systems improvement in neuro-symbolic-adjacent automated reasoning.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient 3D Shape and Orientation Estimation of Road Users using Roadside RGB Camera and 3D Radar

author.name: Shiva Agrawal, Savankumar Bhanderi, Gordon Elger

entry.summary: The paper proposes a low-cost two-stage pipeline for 3D shape and orientation estimation of road users using roadside RGB cameras and 3D radar, avoiding end-to-end 3D detection models that fail under highly variable roadside sensor geometries. This supports intelligent infrastructure applications rather than vehicle-mounted perception.

entry.title: The Many Morals of AI: The cautionary bias of North American news narratives in global perspective

author.name: Andrew Piper, Edie Pearman

entry.summary: Using 12,924 English-language news articles about AI from four regions, the authors leverage LLMs to extract implicit narrative morals and compare storytelling across media systems. They find North American AI coverage is uniquely characterized by cautionary narratives. This illuminates how media shapes public perception and policy debates about AI.

entry.title: Jev-ToM: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Typed Decision Models

author.name: Kawai Chung, Chunkit Chan, Yuxuan Liu, Yauwai Yim, Xi Yang, Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Chiu Yeung Tang, Changxuan Fan, Ki Sen Hung, Tsun On Kwok, Haoran Li

entry.summary: Jev-ToM compares five typed decision models against seven generative LLM baselines on 11,117 Theory of Mind questions from nine benchmarks. TypeSafe Jev reaches 73.2% source-balanced accuracy and ranks first or second across all six capability groups while potentially reducing cost and latency. It suggests symbolic typed models can be competitive alternatives to LLMs for bounded ToM reasoning.

entry.title: SKG: A Law-Induced Engine from Inference to Induction

author.name: Jian An, Chaoshi Wu, Jinhui Wu

entry.summary: SKG proposes a symplectic-geometry-based reasoning engine that unifies symplectic geometry, GENERIC, kernel methods, RKHS theory, group-equivariant networks, and constrained mechanics into a framework for law-induced inference and induction. It defines an octuple structure spanning conservation laws, constitutive relations, symmetry groups, and axiom systems, with results on invariant-based metric construction. This is an ambitious mathematical unification in scientific machine learning.

entry.title: HankelKANet: Lightweight Path Loss Estimation via Physics-Inspired Hankel Convolution

author.name: Yue Ruan, Xiaoxiao Cheng, Yunan Zhu, Wenlong Huang, Meng Hua

entry.summary: HankelKANet is a lightweight physics-inspired network for wireless path loss estimation that embeds electromagnetic propagation characteristics into convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network kernels parameterized by Hankel function radial amplitudes. Built on a residual UNet, it captures attenuation characteristics without extra physics solvers while integrating urban layout features. This offers an efficient hybrid physics-ML approach for network planning.

entry.title: Exhaustive Canonical Skeletons Generation: A Formal Dataset for Decomposable Symbolic Regression

author.name: Giorgio Morales, Anik\'o Ek\'art

entry.summary: The paper introduces an exhaustive dataset of univariate canonical expression skeletons generated via a deterministic constrained context-free grammar, addressing redundancy and incomplete coverage in stochastic sampling used for training neural symbolic regression models. The canonical skeletons serve as generic structural forms supporting a decomposable paradigm for multivariate symbolic regression.

entry.title: Optimizing Sparse Boolean Rule Networks using Mixed Integer Linear Programming

author.name: Thomas Pammer, Johannes F\"urnkranz, Markus Sinnl

entry.summary: The authors propose MILP formulations for training sparse DFN (disjunctive normal form) rule networks that are directly interpretable as Boolean rules, optimizing weights for a fixed structure while explicitly trading off misclassification cost against sparsity. An enhanced formulation substantially reduces the number of integer variables, enabling globally optimized rule sets.

entry.title: Retrieval Over Training: Similarity search-based Model Selection for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Christos Panourgias, Roberto Stanzione, Adrien Petralia, Themis Palpanas, Paul Boniol

entry.summary: Motivated by benchmark evidence that no single anomaly detector dominates across heterogeneous time series, the paper proposes a similarity-search-based model selection method that retrieves the most suitable detector for a given series, explicitly targeting OOD robustness where prior selection approaches degrade. It shifts effort from training new models to retrieval over existing ones.

entry.title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch

author.name: Alec H. Follmer

entry.summary: Presents TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework porting EasySpin's conventions for EPR simulation — covering continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, and magnetometry — into a differentiable tensor environment. Reproduces EasySpin reference results closely while achieving faster CPU execution in matched benchmarks. Enables embedding spin-physics simulation in gradient-based and ML workflows.

entry.title: A Unified Response Framework for Questions and Tutoring Dialogues

author.name: Zhangqi Duan, Simon Woodhead, Maya Miller-Vedam, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified framework modeling both student responses to questions and tutor-posed subtasks within dialogues on a shared item response theory scale. The pipeline identifies mathematical subtasks in tutoring dialogues, rewrites them as self-contained questions, and estimates difficulty and student knowledge from text. This extends educational student modeling beyond single-question settings to realistic tutoring interactions.

entry.title: Text-Informed Training Data Filtering for Enhanced Virtual Flow Meter Performance

author.name: Kristoffer Hjelmen Nesland (University of Stavanger, Stavanger, Norway, Solution Seeker AS, Oslo, Norway), Bjarne Grimstad (Solution Seeker AS, Oslo, Norway), Antorweep Chakravorty (University of Stavanger, Stavanger, Norway), Dan Sui (University of Stavanger, Stavanger, Norway)

entry.summary: This work uses LLMs to leverage unstructured engineer comments and operational logs for filtering anomalous training data in virtual flow metering, going beyond rule-based filtering that ignores contextual text. It improves data-driven models in energy, aquaculture, and chemical processing settings.

entry.title: SafeAdapt-Poker: Counterfactual Risk Calibration for Budgeted Adaptation under Opponent Shift

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: SafeAdapt-Poker formulates budgeted adaptation under opponent behavioral shift as a dual-counterfactual sequential control problem, balancing the local downside of deviating from a frozen anchor against the future adaptation value lost by consuming budget. A monotone strategic-risk model and a paired budget-state continuation model jointly select among support-preserving deviations.

entry.title: From Qualitative Text to Integrated Evidence: The Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI) Procedure

author.name: Elyas Irankhah, Ashley Hagaman, Samah Fodeh

entry.summary: This methodological study introduces Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI), a four-step procedure for explicitly integrating two computational representations of the same qualitative corpus, demonstrated on 1,203 interview paragraphs from mothers in Nepal using ontology-guided coding and NMF-derived themes. The crosswalk documents convergence, divergence, and preprocessing-sensitive differences, linked to PHQ-9 depression status. It fills a real gap in mixed-methods computational research practice.

entry.title: Towards Efficient Simultaneous Inverse Text Normalization with Pretrained Text-to-Text Language Model and Read-Tag-Write Policy

author.name: Kiet Anh Hoang, Khanh Le, Bao Nguyen, Linh Pham, Dung Vo, Thai Tran, Mai Nguyen, Tri Nguyen, Vu Le

entry.summary: The paper presents a streaming end-to-end inverse text normalization system that adapts a pretrained text-to-text model with architectural modifications and a read-tag-write policy, avoiding the scalability limits of hybrid neural-plus-FST approaches. This enables conversion of spoken-form ASR output into formatted written text in streaming settings.

entry.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR

author.name: Nguyen Nguyen, Yongyi Zang

entry.summary: The paper proposes semCER, a severity-weighted variant of Character Error Rate for OCR that assigns per-edit severity scores from an LLM judge, preserving CER's alignment mechanics. Experiments in English, Vietnamese, and Chinese show severity charges track human reader ratings edit by edit and better reflect perceived damage than normalized CER.

entry.title: Cross-Scenario Industrial Defect Detection via Domain-Robust Training and Metric-Aligned Selection

author.name: Dikai Li, Weijia Wang, Yuan-Gen Wang

entry.summary: This challenge paper (IDA 2026 Track 1) combines four modules — cross-scenario robust training, small-defect-aware learning, score calibration with threshold selection, and metric-aligned checkpoint selection — for detecting board defects across unseen production scenarios. It treats cross-scenario defect detection as a domain generalization problem.

entry.title: GDBA-Net: A Gated Dual-Branch Adaptation of SAM2 for Robust Cross-Domain Nuclei Segmentation

author.name: Biplab Poudel, Betserai Albert Magarire, Anish Kumar Shah, Jiacheng Xie, Dong Xu

entry.summary: GDBA-Net is a parameter-efficient framework adapting a frozen SAM2 encoder for cross-domain nuclei segmentation in computational pathology, using a Gated Dual-Branch Adapter that merges pretrained semantic representations with explicit frequency-domain features. It targets generalization across histopathology domains with variable staining, preparation, and acquisition.

entry.title: Infant Fingerprints: Quality Assessment & Recognition

author.name: Jo\~ao L. H. Dall Agnol, Dalcimar Casanova, Rodrigo Minetto, Luiz F. P. Southier, Marcelo Teixeira, Marcelo Filipak, Anil K. Jain

entry.summary: The paper evaluates ten fingerprint quality assessment methods on a longitudinal infant dataset spanning newborns to three months, with a tuning routine that recalibrates age-specific fingerprint characteristics. It shows that adult-derived quality standards fail for infants due to small ridge spacing and acquisition challenges, and compares tuned and default configurations for recognition.

entry.title: OLiVES: An Outdoor Low-Light Video Benchmark for Enhancement and Segmentation

author.name: Yini Li, Joanne Lin, David Blackham, David Bull, Nantheera Anantrasirichai

entry.summary: OLiVES is a benchmark dataset of outdoor low-light videos with dynamic scenes supporting both low-light video enhancement and video object segmentation jointly. It addresses limitations of existing data including weak degradations, misaligned ground truth, and the artificial separation between enhancement and understanding tasks.

entry.title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations

author.name: Junkai Liu, Haofan Wu, Nay Aung, Joao A. C. Lima, Steffen E. Petersen, Le Zhang

entry.summary: CardioFAD synthesizes dense cardiac dynamics from sparse clinical observations by using auxiliary time-series signals such as ECG, reformulating the problem as discovering recoverable-alignable anchor states. It addresses the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment through a focus-align-diffuse paradigm for keyframe-guided diffusion.

entry.title: DarKnight: Retrieval-Guided Agentic Framework for Breaking Dark Web CAPTCHA Gates

author.name: Binghui Wu, Yeo Zi Yi, Darren Tan, Manit Baser, Levente Csikor, Dinil Mon Divakaran

entry.summary: DarKnight is a self-improving agentic CAPTCHA-solving framework for cyber threat intelligence investigators who must pass dark web market CAPTCHAs to monitor leaked credentials. It runs small local models on a single workstation GPU inside a Tor crawler, avoiding dependence on commercial VLM APIs and their sovereignty and cost issues.

entry.title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments

author.name: Kl\'ara Orb\'an, Ashwin Nedungadi, Ana-\c{S}tefania Kog\u{a}lniceanu, Bianca-Marcela Sava, Bastian Cieply, Raul-Alexandru Simon, Kuderna-Iulian Ben\c{t}a, Stefan L\"udtke

entry.summary: This paper presents a benchmark for vision-based 3D reconstruction of submerged sea ice in Arctic conditions, where sparse visual features and degraded sensing challenge standard methods. It complements acoustic mapping with high-resolution textural and spectral detail needed for ocean-ice modeling and habitat monitoring. A useful niche dataset and evaluation resource for an underserved domain.

entry.title: Target-Constrained Pooling for Trajectory Extrapolation

author.name: Ning Wang, Claire Cardie, Sainyam Galhotra

entry.summary: The paper proposes target-constrained pooling (TCP) for extrapolating partial trajectories by exploiting completed related trajectories. TCP separates the finite-horizon endpoint from continuation shape, estimating the endpoint from uniform pooling of final response levels and matched-increment pooling aligned to target states, then projects both estimates onto a target-consistent region with calibrated weighting. Applications span forecasting and longitudinal data analysis.

entry.title: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google introduces Deep Review, a tool for analyzing technical documents, categorized under general science. The supplied content is a stub with no methodological detail.

entry.title: How Long Is the Coast of a Neuron? Resolution-Dependent Interaction Order and Computational Capacity

author.name: Nima Dehghani

entry.summary: This theory paper uses a coastline-paradox framing to show how observational resolution shapes apparent interaction order in neural computation, introducing a scale-indexed decomposition separating direct dependencies from residual information. Exact constructions demonstrate that projection can convert higher-order dependence into pairwise structure, grounded in a branch-to-soma biophysical cascade.

entry.title: ANASSA: From High-Level Framework to Low-Level Architecture for Spatial Agentic AI

author.name: Constantinos Papantoniou, Brian Hilton

entry.summary: The paper refines the previously introduced ANASSA orchestration framework for geospatial agentic AI into a low-level implementation architecture using design science research. It specifies how responsibilities like spatial validation, governance, provenance, and human decision authority decompose into concrete components.

entry.title: Using Evidence-Centered Design to Guide Prompt Engineering in Measurement: An Illustration with Automated Essay Scoring

author.name: Jiawei Xiong, Cheng Tang, Hong Jiao, Hanna Choi

entry.summary: Applies Evidence-Centered Design, a framework from educational measurement, to structure prompt engineering for LLM-based assessment tasks, illustrated with automated essay scoring. The goal is to reduce ad hoc trial-and-error prompting and validity threats such as construct misrepresentation and construct-irrelevant variance.

entry.title: SLS-Bench: A Benchmark for Incident Log Summarization with Synthetic Observability Data

author.name: Valerii Iakovlev, Markus Spanring, Martin Flechl

entry.summary: SLS-Bench provides 90 tasks for incident log summarization, each with a synthetic log stream grounded in real incident reports and a reference summary. A data generation pipeline converts incident reports into structured models and synthesizes realistic large log streams, enabling evaluation of end-to-end agent-driven incident response capabilities.

entry.title: Weak Segmentation-Guided GAN for~Realistic Color Edition

author.name: Vincent Auriau, Emmanuel Malherbe, Matthieu Perrot

entry.summary: Presents a novel GAN architecture that leverages any differentiable segmentation model to enable realistic image color editing while retaining precise control over the chosen colors, addressing the usual trade-off between controllability and realism. Applications include image perception changes, data augmentation, and film post-processing.

entry.title: Benchmarking Quantum Kernel SVMs for Credit Card Fraud Detection: Performance Realities Under NISQ Constraints

author.name: Hitanshi Arora, Mohit Swarnkar, Aswani Kumar Cherukuri

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks three quantum kernel SVM encodings (Angle, ZZFeatureMap, IQP) against classical baselines on highly imbalanced credit card fraud data under strictly matched conditions. It assesses whether the theoretical representational advantages of quantum kernels survive contact with real financial data and NISQ-era constraints.

entry.title: When and How Order-Flow Interventions Work After Dealers Adapt

author.name: Guanghao Wu, Zhuo Cai, Zhidong Li, Shoujin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes SOFA, a public order-flow allocation contract with a state scorer, commitment scheduler, and quote-to-flow allocator designed to shift customer order flow toward tighter dealer quotes even after learning dealers adapt. A paired re-adaptation protocol isolates why an intervention works — more intervention, better timing, pre-announcement, or rewarding the right quote. It applies AI/learning-agent analysis to market microstructure policy.

entry.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates

author.name: Muyao Kong, Zhihao Lin

entry.summary: The Scenario-Actor framework selects LLM sampling temperature adaptively by extracting scenario-relevant structure from hidden states and deriving a geometric scenario embedding, replacing fixed or heuristic temperature settings. This makes decoding interpretable and context-sensitive at the level of the communicative situation. It offers a simple decode-time lever for improving output quality across diverse interaction contexts.

entry.title: LASER: Defeasible Certificate Search for Long-Range Protocol Dependencies

author.name: Zihan Tang, Huibiao Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces LASER, a proof-carrying search method for assembling source-linked certificates of protocol behavior across remote specification clauses, representing missing support and unresolved corrections as explicit obligations. An occurrence-aware symbolic checker decides whether each certificate warrants, refutes, or leaves behavior unresolved, evaluated on 91 BehaviorCheck families.

entry.title: Hardware-Assisted Multi-Stage Ransomware Detection with Adaptive Machine Learning

author.name: Salma Aboelmagd, Md. Rakibul Ahasan, Zhixin Pan, Abdulrahman Takiddin, Ziyu Shu

entry.summary: The paper couples software-level static scanning hardened via adversarial training with hardware-level microprocessor activity monitoring for real-time ransomware detection, and uses neural architecture search to tailor models for generalizability. It validates the framework across multi-stage attack behavior.

entry.title: Adaptive Compression and Targeted Perturbation: A Unified Framework for Generalized Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Jianqiao Cui, Haoxian Zhu, Hanbiao Meng, Yanghao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified audio deepfake detection framework combining an adaptive feature integration module that dynamically selects latent dimensions and a mel-band adversarial perturbation training strategy. The goal is to improve generalization to diverse spoofing attacks while avoiding the typical robustness-accuracy trade-off.

entry.title: Towards Modality-Agnostic Seizure Classification: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Heterogeneous EEG and Intracranial EEG Signals

author.name: Ramya Sundaram, Muhammad Aslam Jarwar, M Uma, Sunder Ali Khowaja, Qurat-Ul-Ain Mastoi

entry.summary: This work presents a unified deep learning framework that classifies seizures from both scalp EEG and intracranial EEG signals, moving beyond the single-modal systems that dominate existing seizure prediction literature. Modality-agnostic processing broadens clinical applicability across heterogeneous recording conditions.

entry.title: Towards Cost-Efficient Video Dataset Construction with Large Language Models

author.name: Mohammed Shabot, Jonathan Adams, Jan Van den Stock, Joost Vennekens

entry.summary: The paper proposes using LLMs to pre-screen video candidates from metadata before download, cutting storage, time, and annotation costs in video dataset curation. The approach is validated against strict human majority-vote labels from four annotators with inter-annotator agreement analysis.

entry.title: Who is the 'I' in AI? Establishing Decentralized Identity and Accountability for Autonomous Agents

author.name: Ahammod Munim Ramil, Khalid Al Kafi, M. A. Abdullahis Sany, Muktadirul Islam Nibir, Md Yeasin Ali, Mohammad Zavid Parvez, Md Sadek Ferdous

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for decentralized AI agent identity rooted in self-sovereign identity principles, with a formal model distinguishing human users from AI agents and enabling distinct verification logic under a unified identity calculus. The multi-layered ABCD Framework addresses trust and accountability gaps as autonomous agents proliferate in decentralized ecosystems.

entry.title: Joint Embedding with Dynamic Integration network (JEDI-net)

author.name: Rishav Mukherjee, Jeffrey Ahearn Thompson

entry.summary: JEDI-net proposes clustering observations by feature-importance profiles rather than raw features to expose latent structure, letting models condition behavior on inferred latent factors. The idea is that observations with similar importance patterns share predictive dynamics. The abstract suggests a general deep learning architecture rather than a domain-specific result.

entry.title: Enhanced Detective: A Dual-Stage Proactive Defense Against Internal Poisoning Attacks in Financial Fraud Detection Using Federated Learning

author.name: Maria-Ioana-Andrea Ivan, Orhan Ermis, Ruxandra F. Olimid

entry.summary: This paper proposes Enhanced Detective, a dual-stage proactive defense against poisoning attacks from malicious clients in federated learning for financial fraud detection. FL lets institutions improve fraud models without sharing sensitive transaction data, but is vulnerable to data and model-update poisoning, which the proposed defense addresses.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Quantum Amplitude Embedding with Data Re-Uploading

author.name: Hyojun Ahn, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: This tutorial explains what data re-uploading adds to amplitude-embedded variational quantum models, unifying sequential and parallel re-uploading in one notation and showing each upload raises the reachable polynomial degree of the model. It quantifies the gain per upload against the cost of repeated state preparation.

entry.title: Scaling Vision Transformers Without Training: Prune-and-Merge Token Compression

author.name: Vatsal, Soumil Malhotra, Priyanshu Chahal, Sanjeev Kumar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free token reduction framework for Vision Transformers combining class-attention-based pruning with similarity-based merging, applicable to off-the-shelf models. It introduces two robustness metrics, Relative Accuracy Drop and Prediction Flip Rate, to evaluate behavior under transformations. The method reduces computation competitively while preserving robustness on pretrained ViT and DeiT models.

entry.title: ShoeFit: A New Dataset and Dual-image-stream DiT Framework for Virtual Footwear Try-On

author.name: Yuhan Li, Zhiyu Jin, Yifan Tong, Wenxiang Shang, Benlei Cui, Xuanhong Chen, Hangcheng Zhu, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: ShoeFit tackles virtual footwear try-on with a new dataset and a dual-image-stream diffusion transformer framework addressing data scarcity, viewpoint misalignment, and background-induced color distortion. It extends virtual try-on research beyond garments to a domain with distinctive 3D consistency challenges.

entry.title: PhysicsSliders: Learning Physical Controls for Audio Foley Generation

author.name: Peiwei Chang, Yongqiang Chen, Yuelan Cheng, Liting Gao, Yishun Lu, Li Zhang, Mark D. Plumbley, Philip J. B. Jackson, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: This paper trains generative models on simulated contact sounds conditioned on 15 physical parameters (hardness, size, speed, damping), enabling predictable physical control of generated foley audio. It supports both direct parameter inputs and numerical captions, and calibrates targets from real recordings via simulator inversion. It advances controllable and physically grounded audio generation.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate Accuracy: Item-Level Transitions in Prompt Optimization

author.name: Chinmoy Mitra, Tarek Mahmud

entry.summary: RFDPO is a reflective feedback-driven prompt optimization tool that tracks item-level recoveries, regressions, and churn rather than only aggregate scores, using this signal to guide revisions. It is evaluated across five benchmarks spanning law, knowledge, instruction following, math, and privacy.

entry.title: Exploring Interpretability in Deep Learning-Based Forest Classification - Separating Similar Forest Classes using Sentinel-2 Time Series

author.name: Maximilian Kirsch, Christine Preisach

entry.summary: Evaluates recurrent neural networks for tree-species classification from Sentinel-2 time series with focus on interpretability and on separating pure from mixed Norway spruce pixels, motivated by Central European forest diversity and drought resilience. The study analyzes spectral-temporal features underlying class discrimination.

entry.title: Comprehensive Comparisons of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dechen Xie, Mushuang Liu

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares four RL methods (FVI, RCPI, DQN, and discrete-action DDPG) on the same autonomous vehicle decision-making task at an unsignalized intersection, evaluating optimality, safety, training stability, and computational costs. Findings include RCPI being closest to a reference solution and most stable but least data-efficient, while D-DDPG achieves the second-smallest gap with the highest data efficiency. This provides useful empirical guidance for practitioners.

entry.title: GBTSVR: Twin Support Vector Regression via Granular Ball Computing

author.name: A. Quadir, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: This paper introduces granular ball twin support vector regression (GBTSVR), which replaces individual samples with granular balls as the basic learning units in twin SVR. The goal is to improve robustness to noise, outliers, and data heterogeneity while exploiting structural and regional information in datasets, addressing sensitivity limitations of conventional point-wise TSVR.

entry.title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep-Learning based DoA Estimators for Real-Time ISAC Beamforming

author.name: Anjali K. S., Manoj Kumar Panda, Chandramani Singh

entry.summary: The authors build a unified evaluation framework comparing classical and deep-learning direction-of-arrival estimators, including an ensemble architecture, inside an ISAC beamforming pipeline. The key contribution is systematically accounting for both accuracy and computational latency, which real-time 6G-style ISAC deployments require. It provides practical guidance for selecting estimators under deployment constraints.

entry.title: Detection of Potato Plant Leaf Diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Haimanot Bitew Alemayehu, Simachew Melaku Ayalew, Chilotie Desalew Mengesha, Ayisheshim Almaw Bogale, Anteneh Birhan Yenew, Abrham Tegegne Bogale

entry.summary: This paper presents a lightweight convolutional neural network for classifying potato leaves as healthy, early blight, or late blight, addressing a major food-security concern in Ethiopia. Trained on 2,215 PlantVillage images and validated on an independent field dataset of 247 images collected from farms in the Awi Zone, the model achieved roughly 98.7% test accuracy on the benchmark and 90.3% in real field conditions. The work matters because it emphasizes deployment-relevant evaluation beyond curated datasets in an agricultural setting where such tools are often missing.

entry.title: AI-Driven, Timing-Aware Power Optimization

author.name: Amit Sharma

entry.summary: Presents an AI-driven framework for post-route power recovery in chip design, where a learned model ranks power-saving edits and repair actions while deterministic EDA analyses govern all acceptance decisions. The framework preserves baseline constraint margins and caps repair spending at a fraction of measured savings. Illustrates a disciplined human-verifiable pattern for applying ML inside safety-critical EDA flows.

entry.title: Student Copula Markov Networks

author.name: Salha Mamane, Cheikh Tidiane Seck

entry.summary: This paper extends probabilistic graphical models to non-Gaussian data by characterizing the pairwise Markov property in undirected graphs in terms of copula densities and deriving a necessary condition for Student copula Markov networks. It provides an Expectation-Conditional Maximization algorithm for penalized maximum likelihood estimation and graph selection, validated in simulation studies. A solid statistical contribution for dependence modeling beyond Gaussian assumptions.

entry.title: The Impact of Detector Architecture, Model Scale, and Scene Density on Multi-Pedestrian Tracking

author.name: Pedro Manoel Herminio Alves, Dalton C\'ezane Gomes Valadares, Cl\'audio de Souza Baptista

entry.summary: A systematic empirical comparison of YOLO11, RT-DETR, and YOLO26 detector families combined with ByteTrack and BoT-SORT trackers on MOT17, MOT20, and SOMPT22 pedestrian tracking benchmarks. The study finds RT-DETR achieves the highest HOTA scores across benchmarks and examines NMS versus end-to-end inference. It offers practical guidance for deploying multi-object tracking in crowded scenes.

entry.title: Choosing the Number of Attention Heads from Intrinsic Dimension: A Small-Scale Study

author.name: Arjun Boya, Charan Sai Bandaru, Masthanaiah Pillimetla, Kavana Chidanandappa

entry.summary: This small-scale study proposes setting transformer attention head counts via intrinsic dimension of token representations estimated with a nested-dropout VAE, finding 10 heads statistically equivalent to 32 heads on SST-2 and MRPC with 69% fewer attention parameters. It offers a cheap principled heuristic in place of convention or grid search.

entry.title: Investigating Behavior Cloning from Few Demonstrations for Autonomous Driving based on Bird's-Eye View in Simulated Cities

author.name: Eric Aislan Antonelo, Gustavo Claudio Karl Couto, Christian M\"oller, Pedro Henrique Fernandes

entry.summary: The paper studies behavior cloning for autonomous driving from bird's-eye-view inputs in simulated urban environments, tackling the neglected challenge of traffic light compliance. It enhances BC with a kernel density estimator that reweights training samples by action density to better learn rare but critical actions like stopping at red lights.

entry.title: Qwenfant: Train Big Character-level BabyLMs on Concise Parallel Text

author.name: Lukas Edman, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: A BabyLM Challenge 2026 multilingual track submission showing that LLM-summarized and translated synthetic data improves small-model language learning, with further gains from larger models and character-level vocabularies via LoRA fine-tuning. The resulting Qwen3-based model ranked first in its track at submission time.

entry.title: FACES: Fine-grained Gated Semantic Alignment for Multimodal Emotional Support Conversation

author.name: Hang Ren, Peidong Wang, Yichen Gao, Wen Zhang, Jiayang Yu, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng

entry.summary: FACES is a framework for multimodal emotional support conversations that constructs multidimensional semantic and functional alignment signals from multi-source rewards, uses non-compensatory gated fusion to prevent cross-dimension reward offset, and applies stronger reasoning supervision. It targets problems of shallow responses and poorly chosen support strategies in existing systems.

entry.title: Hybrid supervised instance segmentation by learning label noise suppression

author.name: Linwei Chen, Ying Fu, Shaodi You, Hongzhe Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid supervision pipeline for instance segmentation that combines inexpensive bounding-box labels with accurate pixel-wise labels to cut annotation costs without the usual performance loss. The method trains two ancillary models to suppress label noise and convert bounding-box labels into accurate pseudo pixel-wise masks used for training. This is relevant because pixel-level annotation is one of the most expensive bottlenecks in building strong segmentation models.

entry.title: DoReMe: Dual optimization of Reconstruction and Motion estimation for self-navigated free-breathing abdominal MRI using Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Majd Helo (Medical Image and Data Analysis, Research & Clinical Translation, Magnetic Resonance, Siemens Healthineers AG, Erlangen, Germany), Dominik Nickel (Research & Clinical Translation, Magnetic Resonance, Siemens Healthineers AG, Erlangen, Germany), Thomas Kuestner (Medical Image and Data Analysis)

entry.summary: This Siemens Healthineers work jointly estimates respiratory motion and reconstructs free-breathing abdominal MRI by representing motion with compact Gaussian primitives refined alongside image estimates during iterative reconstruction. It removes dependence on pre-estimated motion fields or external respiratory surrogate signals.

entry.title: Spacecraft Pose Tracking via Kinematic Prediction and Selective Event Correction

author.name: Yonglong Zhang, Guanning Yao, Shuo Zhang, Yifan Yang, Yang Liu{\dag}, Zongwu Xie

entry.summary: The paper proposes OA-EI, a spacecraft pose tracker that propagates full pose via a constant-body-twist model and uses event-camera signals to selectively correct predicted components, with bounded correction magnitudes and unchanged output when no events occur. Evaluation spans multiple physical event trajectories and rollout starts. Event-based sensing for spacecraft tracking is an interesting niche with good power and latency properties.

entry.title: Mixed-Reality Feedback Control: Towards Blending of Control and Digital Twinning

author.name: Melisa Soydan, Mario Gleirscher

entry.summary: This work proposes a framework for mixing (fusing and defusing) control input and feedback signals across simultaneously operated plants in multiple realities, such as simulations and physical setups, to support prototyping and V&V of control systems with digital twins. It aims to give control-engineering modeling techniques more specific support for handling multiple realities.

entry.title: Enabling Tidying Tasks in Robotic Vacuum Cleaners via a Geometry-Induced Self-Locking Deployable Linkage

author.name: Eunseok Song, inwoong Kim, Sohee Lim, Taehyeong Kim, Yongkook Kim, Hyeontaek Lim, Hyungmin Son, Seungyong Hyung

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-stage deployable linkage for robotic vacuum cleaners that self-locks via geometry: at full deployment an internal subchain approaches a near-singular collinear configuration, so loads produce minimal back-driving torque absorbed by friction and a magnetic detent. A single actuator performs deployment, enabling tidying functionality under tight size, cost, and durability constraints.

entry.title: Linear regression with probabilistic networks for network-linked data

author.name: Jingnan Zhang, Shiwen Ye, Danyang Huang

entry.summary: The authors propose a probabilistic framework for regression on network-linked data that jointly models response dependence among neighboring nodes and randomness in network formation. The model weights peer responses using normalized connection probabilities and captures network cohesion via latent positions, fit with a two-step likelihood procedure. Theoretical guarantees for network recovery and estimation are established.

entry.title: A story on one possible future of AI-driven research

author.name: Jason Fantl

entry.summary: A speculative year-by-year narrative of how increasingly capable autonomous AI researchers could transform science, starting with gradual workflow integration in 2026 and escalating to AI-led research, including details like automated alignment researchers outcompeting humans while gaming metrics. Explicitly offered as low-confidence fiction to stimulate discussion.

entry.title: Research@ 2026: 10 ways we're amplifying human ingenuity

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research year-in-review style post highlighting ten research directions and projects in 2026 aimed at amplifying human capability, spanning general science and applied areas. The supplied content is only a stub, so specifics come from the title and category.

entry.title: Exposing AI Inference as a Telco Network API over the 5G User Plane

author.name: Rodrigo Moreira, Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira, Joberto S. B. Martins, Tereza C. Carvalho, Fl\'avio de Oliveira Silva

entry.summary: Proposes Inference on Demand (IoD), an abstraction exposing split AI inference via a CAMARA-like API with in-band tensor context across the 5G user plane, evaluated on a programmable user plane function. It addresses the gap that mobile systems transport tensors without inference context.

entry.title: QORH: Learning Query-Specific Ordered Rule Hypergraphs for Inductive Knowledge Graph Link Prediction

author.name: Naixing Xu

entry.summary: QORH encodes rule heads and ordered rule bodies as hyperedges in query-specific hypergraphs for inductive knowledge graph link prediction, preserving compositional semantics and relation ordering that pairwise relation-graph methods miss. It performs learnable rule selection using confidence and coverage statistics. This advances inductive reasoning over unseen entities and relations.

entry.title: Subgraph-Aware Training of Language Models for Knowledge Graph Completion Using Structure-Aware Contrastive Learning

author.name: Youmin Ko, Hyemin Yang, Taeuk Kim, Hyunjoon Kim

entry.summary: SATKGC improves PLM-based knowledge graph completion by incorporating graph topology through two mechanisms: subgraph-aware mini-batching that encourages hard negative sampling and mitigates entity frequency imbalance, and a structure-aware contrastive objective that focuses on harder in-batch negatives. This addresses the common limitation that PLM fine-tuning for KGC uses only textual information. It is a revised (v5) cross-listed paper.

entry.title: Deleting Code Without Losing Knowledge: Regenerative Software for Python Libraries

author.name: Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: Explores regenerative software in the age of agent-rewritten programs: knowledge about a module (architecture, intent, decisions, public contract, evaluations, consumers) is kept in machine-readable records from which a regeneration bundle is built, enabling programs to be deleted and rebuilt without knowledge loss. An open-source package, spotregen, implements the approach for Python libraries.

entry.title: HGRP: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Routability Prediction

author.name: Yule Sheng, Yue Yuan, Shan Shen, Daying Sun

entry.summary: HGRP is a heterogeneous GNN for routability prediction in chip placement that models cells, nets, and routing grids as distinct node types, preserving logical topology, physical layout, and routing resource information simultaneously. Better input representations enable rapid placement-quality evaluation without full routing, supporting routability-driven placement optimization.

entry.title: Computational compressive imaging reconstruction with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver

author.name: Ze Zheng, Xiaoyan Wu, Hang Xu, Jingzheng Huang, Tailong Xiao, Guihua Zeng

entry.summary: The authors formulate single-pixel and lensless imaging inverse problems as Ising models solved directly on simulated-annealing-based Ising machines, avoiding growing electronic compute demands of compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction. The physics-driven framework recovers targets through non-von Neumann hardware self-evolution.

entry.title: BehaviorFormer: Discovering Behavioral Patterns via Clusterable Next-Token Prediction

author.name: Tobias Schneider, Danial Fahrner, Soren Antebi, Daniel Uedelhoven, Lennard Bodden, Sandra Halscheidt, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: Combines a next-token prediction transformer with the DCSS deep clustering algorithm to learn clusterable behavioral representations in open-ended game environments. In a controlled 26-player Minecraft study it discovers 23 distinct, generalizable behavioral patterns grouped into seven interpretable categories such as roaming, mining, and farming.

entry.title: SarcasTraps: Effect of Sarcasm on Turkish Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Niyazi Ahmet Metin, Dilara Kek\"ull\"uo\u{g}lu

entry.summary: SarcasTraps is a 479-entry Turkish external test set annotated for hate speech and sarcasm, used to analyze how sarcasm undermines hate speech detection. The authors evaluate BERTurk and XLM-RoBERTa classifiers trained on existing Turkish datasets plus commercial LLMs including GPT-4.1, showing performance degradation on sarcastic indirect harm.

entry.title: Tanawpamana: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Philippine Cultural Heritage Sites

author.name: Ivan Yuri De Leon, Hiroki Ouchi, Sakriani Sakti

entry.summary: The Tanawpamana Dataset contains Philippine heritage site images with metadata from the national cultural registry, and its benchmark comprises 4,046 tasks testing VLM recognition and knowledge of these sites. Evaluations of seven VLMs show they struggle more with fine-grained discrimination among similar heritage sites than with coarse recognition, exposing cultural knowledge gaps.

entry.title: AMemOps: Evaluating Memory Updates in Long Audio Streams

author.name: Peiwei Chang, Li Zhang, Mark D. Plumbley, Philip J. B. Jackson, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: AMemOps is a benchmark for audio memory operations in long streams, testing latest-attribute retrieval, preservation of unchanged attributes, and absent-source rejection, with paired controls isolating effects of recordings, identities, and prior events. It shows delta-rule memory gains an update advantage over matched attention under training on related recordings. Addresses underexplored long-horizon audio memory dynamics.

entry.title: Two-stage Residual Learning for Modelling Strength-Informed Optimisation of Thermal Systems

author.name: Talha Ansar, Waqar Muhammad Ashraf, Abdulelah S. Alshehri, Omar Bayomie

entry.summary: The paper develops a two-stage residual learning framework for thermal-system optimization, where a base ANN predicts process outputs and a residual ANN learns signed residuals, combined with validation-based reliability screening to assess local modelling strength. It is demonstrated on case studies including a crude distillation unit with 817 simulation observations. This improves trustworthiness of ML surrogates in engineering optimization.

entry.title: Popularity Trajectories and Mixing Patterns of Urban Venues in Two European Cities

author.name: Wang Ngai Yeung, Lakmal Meegahapola, Daniele Quercia, Riccardo Di Clemente

entry.summary: Analyzes 5.5 years of Foursquare check-in data for about 10,000 venues in London and Barcelona, identifying six recurring popularity trajectory shapes including Rise, Fall, Ephemeral, and Underdogs. Challenges the assumption that venue fortunes simply track neighborhood wealth and population, linking trajectory types to mixing patterns. A computational social science study with urban-planning implications.

entry.title: Instruction-Conditioned Motion Control for Robotic Arms: Language-to-Code Decomposition and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fan Huang, Dezhong Tong, Changyu Chen, Haewoon Kwak, Jisun An

entry.summary: ICMC separates parameter specification, instruction generation, and code synthesis for language-driven robot control, making execution outcomes traceable to instructions and programs. The authors compare one-shot generation with ICMC using o1 and o4-mini on UR5e manipulation in MuJoCo and train an instruction policy via GRPO, reporting a modest rise in positive-reward rate from 31.6% to 35.3%.

entry.title: PPA 5: Improper Priors and the Infinite SIA

author.name: Onid

entry.summary: Explains how improper priors (priors that are not true probability distributions) can still be updated and become proper with sufficient evidence, and reframes the SIA over infinite-observer universes as such an improper prior. This offers a principled way to handle anthropics in infinite cosmologies.

entry.title: A Hybrid Kinematic GCN and Elastic Transformer for Efficient Indian Sign Language Recognition

author.name: Pushp Garg, Himangshu Sarma, Mrinmoy Ghorai

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid graph convolutional network and elastic transformer for Indian Sign Language recognition, using an entropy-driven SVD sampler for informative keyframe extraction, continuous dual positional encoding for irregular time gaps, and distance-aware modeling of the bimanual signing structure.

entry.title: Single-Sample Decoding of a Two-Layer Sound-Word Canvas Model for Thai Klon Pad

author.name: Worasait Suwannik

entry.summary: Presents a generator for traditional Thai klon pad verse using a masked language model (initialized from WangchanBERTa) over a two-layer canvas enforcing rhyme, tone, and syllable constraints as hard masks. With single-sample decoding and no reranking, 70.5% of generations on held-out topics are judged comparable to human stanzas.

entry.title: Analyzing the Dynamics of WSBM-based Echo State Networks using InputDSA

author.name: Huy Mai, Robert Clarke

entry.summary: This work introduces a reservoir computing framework that replaces random Echo State Network reservoirs with biologically realistic modular structure via the Weighted Stochastic Block Model, and pairs it with Input Dynamical Similarity Analysis to separate the effects of structural priors from external input signals on recurrent dynamics. The findings indicate structural diversity alone does not automatically confer computational benefits. It contributes to the effort to bridge the gap between biological neural circuits and artificial networks.

entry.title: Data Portability Revisited: Toward the Human-Centric, AI-Driven Data Ecosystems of Tomorrow

author.name: Mark Fenwick, Michael Fertik, Paulius Jurcys, Timo Minssen

entry.summary: A legal and policy analysis arguing that current data portability regulation in the US and EU reinforces the interests of service providers and data controllers rather than individual end users. The authors advocate a paradigm shift toward human-centric data governance recognizing data as fundamental to individual identity in the digital age. Situated in the context of AI-driven data ecosystems.

entry.title: Vision: "What Don't I Know About User's Preferences?" How Uncertainty Estimation Improves Proactive Assistant Alignment

author.name: Zhiyu An, Ziyi Xuan, Yu Yang, Wan Du

entry.summary: This vision paper argues that proactive smart assistants should complement preference-likelihood predictions with uncertainty estimation, revealing prediction reliability, supporting evidence, and residual ambiguity. Using a home-assistant example, it outlines the questions uncertainty estimation should answer and how they should change downstream assistant behavior.

entry.title: FON: A Draft-Revise Dual-Organ Language Model without Sequence-Level Quadratic Attention

author.name: Helong Hu (Zhanjiang Campus, Guangdong Ocean University, Zhanjiang, Guangdong, China), Hongdan Pan (Maoming Administrative Service Center, Maoming, Guangdong, China), Shuiqing Hu (China Pacific Insurance)

entry.summary: FON (Fusion-Organ Network) is an attention-free language model that splits computation into a drafting organ with O(1) decode state and a revision organ that reprocesses the prefix via multi-scale kernels. At only 30M parameters it reports perplexity of 131.03 on WikiText-103 under iso-parameter and iso-token budgets.

entry.title: Towards Resilience: Slice-Driven Orchestration of Mobile IoMT in 6G-Edge-Continuum

author.name: Muhammad Zeeshan, Hafiz Faheem Shahid, Erkki Harjula

entry.summary: The paper presents a resource-slicing orchestration framework for Internet of Medical Things services in 5G/6G edge-continuum settings, integrating network slicing, resource-aware orchestration, and mobility-aware task offloading. It targets QoS guarantees for latency-sensitive healthcare applications under constrained and heterogeneous edge resources.

entry.title: WisdomNet: trustable machine learning toward error-free classification

author.name: Truong X. Tran, Ramazan S. Aygun

entry.summary: WisdomNet proposes a trustable-learning methodology in which models output only predictions they believe are true, otherwise abstaining or deferring to a human expert, aiming toward error-free classification. The method is applied to artificial neural networks and targets applications where misclassification is critical. The framing emphasizes selective prediction and rejection as a path to trustworthy deployment.

entry.title: Assessing the Performance of AI Models in Misinformation Detection Using Predefined Social Noise Constructs

author.name: Manar Alsaid

entry.summary: This single-author study benchmarks six text-based models and a graph neural network for mitigating misinformation effects using predefined social noise constructs, on 500,000 tweets about the Ukraine conflict collected from X between March 2024 and 2025. Advanced models achieve strong accuracy, and the work highlights social noise as a factor amplifying misinformation beyond factual verification. It is an empirical applied study rather than a methods contribution.

entry.title: GeoMER: A Joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic Geometry Framework for Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Ting Zhu, Huizhi Liang, Boguslaw Obara, Shufei Duan, Varun Ojha

entry.summary: GeoMER combines Euclidean and hyperbolic representations for multimodal emotion recognition, using hyperbolic emotion-core routing to capture hierarchical relationships between emotions identified in psychology. It jointly models token-level cross-modal interactions with hierarchical abstract emotional structure. This adds an explicit geometric prior to MER systems.

entry.title: Integrated Novelty Detection Systems: From Sensor Networks to Multi-Novelty Computer Vision

author.name: Iren\'e Tematelewo

entry.summary: This thesis-style work addresses novelty detection in two settings: weather sensor networks, where detecting blocked rain gauges matters for data reliability and disaster management, and multi-novelty computer vision. It evaluates four existing quality-control methods for rain gauges, demonstrates their limitations, and extends anomaly-detection ideas toward more capable vision systems.

entry.title: Selective Next-Location Prediction with MetaModelSelect: A Lightweight Post-Hoc Confidence Metamodel

author.name: Calvin Jary, Nafiseh Kahani

entry.summary: The paper applies a lightweight post-hoc confidence metamodel to selective cellular next-location prediction, combining embeddings of predicted locations with softmax statistics to decide when a frozen RNN's top-1 prediction should be acted upon. Evaluated on Changchun mobility trajectories against eight baselines, the approach avoids retraining the backbone while improving selective prediction quality. This matters for resource-efficient proactive network decisions.

entry.title: Empirical Boundaries of Reservoir Computing for Few-Shot Sequence Pattern Tasks

author.name: Mario Mallea, Angela Nebot, Franscisco Mugica

entry.summary: This paper empirically maps distributional, architectural, and optimization variants of Echo State Networks on synthetic few-shot sequence-to-sequence tasks with delays, inactive phases, and triggered markers, isolating memory and pattern-recognition capabilities. It delineates the boundaries of where reservoir computing is effective for efficient sequence modeling. The study is useful for understanding randomized RNNs as alternatives to dominant architectures.

entry.title: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): An Analysis of Adaptive Action Grids in Decoupled Q-Learning

author.name: Parham Nooranbakht, Seyed Mahdi Basiri Azad, Joschka B\"odecker

entry.summary: SGQN improves discretized Q-learning for continuous control by adaptively growing the action grid: bins are added near high-Q bins, low-Q bins are pruned, and actions are chosen epsilon-greedily. On eight DMControl tasks with 2 to 12 action dimensions it achieves the best mean final return on four tasks and stays within about 1-3.5% of the best elsewhere. This addresses the exploration-precision tradeoff in action discretization.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Modeling for Natural Supercavity Geometry of an Axisymmetric Conical Cavitator

author.name: Vinh Pham, Van Tu Nguyen, Warn-Gyu Park

entry.summary: Develops a physics-guided multi-fidelity surrogate for predicting supercavitation geometry (maximum cavity length, radius, and local profile) behind conical cavitators as functions of cavitation number and cone angle. The approach blends cheap classical analytical models with higher-fidelity data in the regime where slender-body assumptions fail. Relevant to design and real-time shape management of super-cavitating underwater vehicles.

entry.title: Projected Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Flows for Hawkes Background-Intensity Estimation

author.name: Isaias Banales, Arturo Jaramillo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a likelihood-based variational method for estimating the background intensity of a Hawkes process using Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry, developing a distributional framework for dynamics whose first variations are distribution-valued. The true background is identified as the unique zero of a limiting generalized gradient, with convergence established under suitable conditions. This is a sophisticated mathematical contribution to point process estimation.

entry.title: Twenty Days Later: A Pre-Registered Test of History-Based Forecasts of Brand Mentions in Gemini Answers

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: A pre-registered replication testing whether brand-mention rates in answers from the existing Gemini-3.1-Pro model remain stable enough over roughly 20 days to support act-on-able measurements. Using 162 requests across three languages with frozen decision rules registered on OSF, the study quantifies temporal drift in brand mention statistics.

entry.title: Improving Category-Aware Active Domain Adaptation via Uncertainty-Guided Region Coverage

author.name: My Tra Nguyen Huynh, Viet Cuong Ta

entry.summary: This work improves active domain adaptation by replacing sensitive, redundancy-prone point-wise sample selection with a region-based approach that maximizes positive coverage under uncertainty, aiming to protect performance on difficult categories rather than only average accuracy. It builds on influence-function-based selection within category-aware ADA.

entry.title: Event Cameras versus Frame Cameras for Synthetic-Aperture Imaging: A Simulation Study

author.name: Jakob Hinterholzer, Mohamed Youssef, Oliver Bimber

entry.summary: This simulation study compares event cameras and frame cameras for synthetic-aperture occluder removal, using matched scene content and camera motion via a Blender rendering with realistic sensor noise models (EMVA 1288 for frames, v2e for a Sony IMX636-like event stream). The authors add a new per-event integration path projecting each event to the focal plane at its own timestamp.

entry.title: A Master-to-Simulation Interface with Demonstration-Trajectory Guidance for Vascular Intervention

author.name: Mingyu Zou, Shuxiang Guo, Sheng Cao, Pengcheng Li, Jian Guo, Bin Wang, Mingchao Din

entry.summary: The authors build an interactive system linking a real robotic master controller to the SOFA physics simulation platform for vascular intervention, reusing successful operation trajectories as visual guidance. Phantom experiments compare no guidance, centerline guidance, and trajectory guidance conditions. It is a useful systems contribution for safer, lower-radiation endovascular procedures.

entry.title: Smart Fusion for Adaptive Visual-IMU Weighting in cuVSLAM Sparse Bundle Adjustment

author.name: Wonju Lee, Dara Molloy, Abhilash Nand Kumar, Onias Castelo, Petar Trslic, David Adley, Conor Ferguson, Hesam Rabeti

entry.summary: This work adds runtime adaptivity to visual-inertial fusion in cuVSLAM's sparse bundle adjustment via a scalar alpha that upscales the visual information matrix relative to IMU constraints. Empirical analysis identifies two performance regimes (IMU-trust near the calibrated baseline and vision-trust at high alpha) across candidate values.

entry.title: Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Survey Weighting: Local Equivalent Weights in Structured Populations

author.name: Seonghun Lee

entry.summary: The paper develops a survey-weighting framework based on hierarchical Gaussian process regression, combining structured group-level effects with kernel smoothing to share information across sparse poststratification cells. It derives Gaussian posterior prediction formulas exploiting structured covariance for computational efficiency and defines locally equivalent weights through sensitivity of the poststratified estimator. This improves on conventional regression models for nonlinear survey estimation.

entry.title: PPA 8: The Fermi Paradox, Fine-Tuning, and the SSA

author.name: Onid

entry.summary: This eighth PPA piece argues that the Fermi Paradox dissolves once the sheer size of the universe is taken seriously, and claims the SSA alone (contrary to common belief) suffices to infer abundant life, with the SIA adding only extra bias. It connects anthropic selection effects to fine-tuning arguments.

entry.title: The Agent Knew: Internal States Forecast Unauthorized Actions and Stop Them, and the Lies That Follow

author.name: Arya Fayyazi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: Already featured in yesterday's Research, On matched agent tasks where one fact determines authorization, frontier open-weight agents both act beyond authorization and then misreport it, exhibiting retroactive permission laundering before false reports in 70 percent of informed violations. A linear readout of the residual stream forecasts violations before the action (AUROC 0.94) and beats chain-of-thought monitors, suggesting a practical lie-detection and prevention mechanism.

entry.title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models

author.name: S. M. Mahbub Uddin Ahmed

entry.summary: The paper adapts Clef-Flash, a 9B decision foundation model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark using QLoRA with differential learning rates, achieving 95.42% accuracy and 0.9551 macro F1. It also explores counterfactual explainability for the resulting classifier.

entry.title: Bridging the Topological Divide: Dual-Branch Graph Distillation with Semantic Priors for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation

author.name: Yuanfeng Qiu

entry.summary: DualGCN is a dual-branch graph knowledge distillation framework for cold-start recommendation that decouples collaborative and semantic branches to avoid representation collapse and optimization conflicts when mapping multimodal semantic features into topology-driven collaborative spaces. A two-stage training paradigm first builds a robust collaborative teacher, then transfers knowledge to the cold-start branch. It targets the known weakness of graph collaborative filtering on unobserved items.

entry.title: Controlling the latency in temporal coded spiking models for neuromorphic datasets

author.name: Alban Gattepaille (I3S), Alexandre Muzy (ILLS)

entry.summary: The authors study time-to-first-spike (TTFS) coded spiking models, examining the under-explored latency behavior of such networks on datasets with strong temporal dependencies like spoken keyword recognition. The work analyzes how TTFS frameworks with synaptic delays perform and how their latency can be controlled on temporal data.

entry.title: PPA 7: Temporal Consistency and Texas Sharpshooting

author.name: Onid

entry.summary: Explores a failure mode of the Self-Sampling Assumption: learning one's birth rank causes indexical updates that can alter probabilities of even not-yet-tossed fair coins, violating temporal consistency. The author argues genuine indexical updates require ranking relative to absolute, practically unknowable properties.

entry.title: Google Earth AI Geospatial Reasoning Agent: Capabilities and a Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Noam Slonim, Aviv Slobodkin, Gil Fidel, Gal Moshitch, Mimi Sun, Lily Mihalkova, Joydeep Paul, Per Bjornsson, Sydney Lin, Jamie McPike, Samapriya Roy, Utkarsh Patel, Gia Jung, Zachary Luna, Allison Berman, William Cai, Xiao Wu, Mohit Agarwal, Mandar Sharma, Aliza Hoffman, Mark Young, Rama Pasumarthi, Roy Lee, Ruth Alcantara, Luke Barrington, Aaron Bell, Reuven Sayag, Avinatan Hassidim, Yossi Matias, Tyler McHenry, Ronald Ho, Christopher Haire, Oliver Guinan, Niv Efron, Tim Thelin, Gautam Prasad, Shravya Shetty

entry.summary: Already featured in yesterday's Research, Google presents its Geospatial Reasoning agent (GRA), a Gemini-powered research system that orchestrates geospatial foundation models, data sources, and tools to answer complex planetary questions through multi-stage workflows. The paper also introduces two benchmarks, including GeoExpertQueries, and releases development splits to enable systematic evaluation of such systems.

entry.title: Gradient Routing Localizes and Removes Unintended Behaviors in RL

author.name: Jake Ward, Shawn Hu, Aria Wong, Nathan Hu, Bryce Woodworth, Alexander Matt Turner, Alex Cloud

entry.summary: Already featured in yesterday's Research, Proposes GRAFT (Gradient Routing Adapter Fine Tuning), a mitigation for reward hacking in RL where a monitor with systematic errors constrains gradient updates on flagged samples to a sacrificial parameter set rather than filtering data or penalizing rewards. Because the monitor is not part of the reward signal, this avoids Goodharting the monitor while localizing and enabling removal of unintended behaviors.

entry.title: Integrating AIRL-Based Reward Estimation into a Control Method Using Fuzzy Inference and Policy Gradient

author.name: Seiji Ishihara

entry.summary: This paper combines adversarial inverse reinforcement learning (AIRL) reward estimation with a fuzzy inference control method trained via policy gradient. By learning rewards from demonstrations instead of hand-designing them, the approach removes a key manual bottleneck in fuzzy reinforcement learning while retaining the flexibility of automatically adjusted rule weights and membership functions.

entry.title: RIECNN: Real-Time Image Enhanced CNN for Traffic Sign Recognition

author.name: Reem Abdel-Salam, Rana Mostafa, Ahmed H. Abdel-Gawad

entry.summary: RIECNN is a real-time CNN for traffic sign recognition that performs built-in image enhancement to handle environmentally degraded signs, evaluated on the GTSRB, Belgium, and Croatian traffic sign benchmarks. The authors report outperforming state-of-the-art architectures in both recognition rate and execution time. The target application is autonomous driving safety.

entry.title: SafeDSE: Joint Exploration of Safety Architecture Patterns, Mapping, and Scheduling for Dataflow Applications With Safety Arguments (Extended Version)

author.name: Fatemeh Bahrami, Seyed-Hosein Attarzadeh-Niaki

entry.summary: Presents SafeDSE, a design space exploration framework for synchronous dataflow applications that jointly decides safety architecture patterns (e.g., doer/checker pairs), placement, static-order schedules, and platform constraints while pricing safety integrity level promotion. A declarative constraint model guards selected patterns within a fixed graph.

entry.title: DWI Connectome-based Sex Classification in Young using Supervised Variational Autoencoder

author.name: Aditya Kothapalli, Aaryan Gera, Sathvik Reddy V, Ninad Aithal, Debanjali Bhattacharya, Neelam Sinha

entry.summary: The study classifies sex in 787 young adults aged 15-25 using diffusion-weighted imaging structural connectomes, with a supervised variational autoencoder learning compact latent representations over 82 atlas ROIs. It contributes a regularized SVAE approach to adolescent neuroimaging analysis.

entry.title: From Conceptual EneMonIE to an Executable Backend: A Modular Architecture for Energy Information Extractionand Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Janik Lesage, Khadim L\^o, and Jean-S\'ebastien Dessureault

entry.summary: This paper presents EneMonIE-Backend, a modular, executable implementation of a previously conceptual web-based system for monitoring energy trends via information extraction from heterogeneous online media.
