The authors call this phenomenon imprinting. It matters because it reveals a hidden safety-relevant channel in the widely used distillation pipeline.

entry.title: The AI's Poker Face: Contrasting Persuasion and Sycophancy in Voice-Based Multi-Turn Conversations

author.name: Ilia Frantzi, Bernie Hogan, Max M. Lang, Paul C. Bauer

entry.summary: This randomized controlled experiment (N=616) has participants hold multi-turn spoken dialogues with an LLM under non-directive and two opposing directive conditions on a polarizing topic. Both directive conditions shift opinions toward their assigned stance, and the study separates semantic argument content from pragmatic interaction strategies while measuring sycophancy. It provides causal evidence of persuasive influence by voice-based LLMs in sustained dialogue.

entry.title: Scaling Inference-Time Compute with Teams of Coding Agents

author.name: Keenan Samway, Daniel D'souza, Omar Darwiche Domingues, Marzieh Fadaee, Tan Yi-Chern, Nouha Dziri

entry.summary: Formulates multi-agent team design as a compute allocation problem, tracing the reward-cost Pareto frontier for coding agent teams by varying delegation stage, team composition, and size. It identifies when adding agents helps versus causing duplicate work and coordination failures.

entry.title: A Plausible Future Is Not a Causal Future: Can Video Models Generate How the World Unfolds?

author.name: Jialiang Li, Zhengning Xu, Zongyang Ma, Shaobo Cui

entry.summary: CausalCascade is a simulator-grounded benchmark of 50 event-rich Blender scenes with structured event graphs, graph-grounded diagnostic VQA, three future-event specification levels, and 2,832 controlled counterfactual variants, used to test whether video generation models capture causally coherent physical dynamics rather than mere visual plausibility.

entry.title: Detecting Chain-of-Thought Hijacking in Backdoored Multimodal Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhifang Zhang, Qi Wei, Weitong Chen, Olaf Maennel, Wei Emma Zhang, zuomin ren, Lei Feng, Miao Xu

entry.summary: This work studies a new backdoor threat, CoT hijacking, where a poisoned visual trigger redirects a multimodal reasoning model's chain of thought toward attacker-chosen answers in ways that mimic honest self-correction. The authors show honest reasoning revises answers at high-entropy moments and use this signal to build a detector that outperforms defenses designed for direct-answer MLLMs.

entry.title: WIRE: Weight Space Implicit Representation Encoding of Frozen Video LLMs

author.name: Ameen Ali, Tamim Zoabi, Lior Wolf, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: WIRE reduces the prefill, KV-cache, and generation costs that grow with long video inputs in frozen video language models by moving part of the video-conditioned computation from input activations into a temporary low-rank weight update, while keeping a short explicit visual context as a correction. This converts recurring per-token video attention costs into a one-time weight-space encoding.

entry.title: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence

author.name: Jiahao Meng, Zhongyuan Bao, Yue Tan, Haiquan Wen, Renrui Zhang, Anna Wang, Jason Li, Yanwei Fu, Yunhai Tong, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: Open-o3-Video-v2 formulates video reasoning as an agentic, evidence-grounded process where the model identifies missing information, acquires extra observations, and embeds timestamps and object-level bounding boxes into its reasoning traces for verifiability. It contributes new datasets (STGR-v2-CoT135K and an RL set) enabling multi-turn grounded reasoning training.

entry.title: LensErase: A Foundation Model for Erase Anything

author.name: Yunuo Chen, Xiuyu Wu, Qinhong Yang, Jinjing Zhao, Yanchen Dong, Sirui Zhang, Dong Chen, Fangyun Wei, Lei Shi, Ji Li, Dongdong Chen, Guo Lu, Yan Lu, Baining Guo

entry.summary: Introduces LensErase, a general-purpose mask-based object removal foundation model covering objects, text, watermarks, effects, and multiple scales. It is trained on a new 101-million-pair dataset (LensErase-100M) and adapts the generative prior of a text-to-image model via a novel Mask-Aware RoPE conditioning mechanism. This is a substantial industrial-scale contribution to image editing and inpainting.

entry.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ

author.name: Yunsong Zhou, Xuekun Jiang, Haiqi Shen, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi, Yujie Liu, Jingyuan Li, Haoran Yang, Jiafei Cao, Dongzhan Zhou, Dong Wang, Yao Mu, Chunhua Shen, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: EgoExplorer is a 100-hour wearable-capture dataset aligning egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, fine-grained finger articulation, and tactile observations for human loco-manipulation, emphasizing professional activities with step-level descriptions. It targets the observation needs of humanoid loco-manipulation learning, where locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together. The multimodal, in-situ coverage addresses gaps in existing datasets that capture only partial views of this coordination.

entry.title: Building Trustworthy Household Robots through Open-World Safety

author.name: Yu-Lin Tsai, Muxi Lyu, Roei Herzig, Koushik Sen, Raluca Ada Popa, David Wagner

entry.summary: The authors argue that household robots built on foundation models need open-world safety: maintaining specified safety requirements even in unseen situations, including gracefully declining tasks they cannot safely complete. The position paper frames a security research agenda for context-aware, persistent safety protections in dynamic home environments.

entry.title: What Limits Cross-Task Generalization in World Action Models?

author.name: Chen Zhao, Zipeng Ye, Yihan Lin, Yuchen Xie, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper makes the cross-task generalization gap in world action models directly testable by decoupling them into a world model and a fixed camera-space inverse-dynamics model (AoE), pretrained on large-scale robot data, used to recover actions from different future-image sources. The key finding is that actions recovered from recorded futures of unseen tasks execute almost as well as replayed demonstrations, while futures predicted by the world model degrade — pinpointing world-model prediction quality, not action recovery, as the generalization bottleneck. This diagnostic framing is a valuable contribution to understanding generalist robot policies.

entry.title: The Human--VLA Communication Gap: What Humans Leave Implicit and What Policies Cannot Recover

author.name: Yiqing Xu, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: This study dissects the human-VLA communication gap into an information gap (unresolved task semantics and grounding) and a residual execution gap (even fully specified tasks depend on organization and invocation), characterizing how people naturally express task objectives. Experiments on pi-0.5 with consistent trends on pi0-FAST and Cosmos3-Edge show humans increasingly compress instructions as tasks grow, relying on contextual grounding and implicit execution structure that current policies cannot recover.

entry.title: LLMs Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes

author.name: Lucas Florin

entry.summary: This empirical study prefills LLMs with synthetic mistakes (e.g., sending confidential data to the wrong recipient) and measures whether models disclose the error in follow-up turns. Models fail to disclose 67% of the time, and in 5% of cases the chain-of-thought notices the mistake while the output conceals it, implying models cannot be trusted to self-report errors.

entry.title: IsoVRBench: Video Reward Modeling Without Human Feedback

author.name: Shuyue Stella Li, Jacqueline He, Jiahui Chen, Sreya Dutta Roy, Yulia Tsvetkov, Luke Zettlemoyer, Marjan Ghazvininejad, Xiaochuang Han

entry.summary: Constructs 8,000 video preference pairs via controlled single-property interventions on generated videos, enabling property-specific reward model evaluation without human annotation. The benchmark reveals that state-of-the-art video reward models cannot be trusted from aggregate accuracy alone, exposing per-property weaknesses.

entry.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures

author.name: Bingyu Shen, Jiaqi Tang, Lan Wei, Yi Sheng, J. Jenny Li, Boyang Li

entry.summary: This paper questions whether human or LLM-judge labels of an agent's first mistake actually identify causes of failure, making the distinction executable by restarting agents from reconstructed intermediate states and estimating prefix values (success probability from each step) with a certified point-of-no-return. On 150 SWE-bench Verified tasks with two frozen open-weight agents, they find judge-labeled first mistakes do not mark what a controller needs, with judges of different lineages showing systematic disagreement. The work provides a stronger causal foundation for agent debugging and control.

entry.title: Review Rarely Beats the Stronger Model: Separating Verification from Capability Transfer in LLM Pipelines

author.name: Yirui Zhang, Yash Raj Shrestha

entry.summary: This paper shows that LLM pipelines using a reviewer model often conflate verification gains with capability transfer, where a stronger reviewer merely supplies answers it could have produced alone. Across 48 pairs of 12 open-weight models, review beats the stronger model alone in only 9 of 96 directions, and reviewers tend to follow the generator, discarding their own correct answers. The finding challenges common multi-model pipeline designs.

entry.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Bangzheng Li, Hanyu Wang, Lin Zhang, Andrea Yaoyun Cui, Zhenggang Tang, Shyamal Buch, Dejia Xu

entry.summary: SEAR is a framework and benchmark where frontier LM agents autonomously improve robots by writing control code, testing it, and retaining skills and memories across tasks. It runs agents in three modes (code-as-policy, agent-as-policy, auto-research fine-tuning a VLA) and includes controls separating genuine learning from mere repeated attempts.

entry.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Sijie Zhao, Zeqi Zhou, Heli Qi, Xuanchao Fu, Zhuo Zheng, Junshi Xia, Junjue Wang, Weihao Xuan, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: Shows that any verifiable earth observation task can be cast as a harness plus verifier, letting a general-purpose coding agent build and recursively improve EO models on its own outputs. This unifies settings previously treated as separate research problems, such as few-label learning and cross-domain adaptation.

entry.title: Beyond Sparse Captions: Aligning Slide-Level Text and Patch-Level Vision in Pathology

author.name: Daniel Shao, Dongmin Bang, Luca L. Weishaupt, Sophia J. Wagner, Nic G. Reitsam, Ming Y. Lu, Long P. Le, Richard J. Chen, Faisal Mahmood

entry.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity of captioned pathology images by leveraging routine slide-level diagnostic reports for contrastive vision-language pretraining, tackling the macroscopic-report-versus-microscopic-patch granularity mismatch via a proposed Locked Image Multiple Instancing-style approach. Author team includes Mahmood lab members at the Harvard/BWH pathology AI group.

entry.title: dMRI-F: A Foundation Model for Generalizable Diffusion MRI Analysis from Sparse Acquisitions

author.name: Xi Zhu, Yijie Li, Xiaofan Wang, Wei Zhang, Huafu Chen, Ce Zhu, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: dMRI-F is a foundation model for diffusion MRI that unifies data enhancement and downstream tasks such as parcellation, registration, and synthesis across diverse acquisitions and populations, using q-space masked pretraining from minimal acquisition input. It addresses the prohibitive scan times and hardware constraints of dense dMRI.

entry.title: Red-Teaming of Vision-Language-Action Models via Quality Diversity Environment Generation

author.name: Shihan Zhao, Henry Chen, Ya-Chuan Hsu, Minjune Hwang, Siddharth Srikanth, Freddie Liang, Akanksha Saran, Aaquib Tabrez, Stefanos Nikolaidis, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: The paper proposes Q-DEG, a method that uses Quality Diversity optimization to automatically generate diverse adversarial environments exposing VLA failure modes under test-time shifts, then fine-tunes the VLA on its own successful rollouts in those environments to improve robustness. This addresses the common problem of VLAs failing under minor changes in object position, lighting, texture, or camera pose.

entry.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models

author.name: Donghoon Ahn, Runqian Wang, Alexei A. Efros, Taesung Park, Yash Belhe

entry.summary: The paper targets exposure bias in diffusion models, where the denoiser at inference sees its own imperfect predictions rather than the training-time interpolated real images. It introduces an explicit correction step trained on the base model's own predictions to close the training-inference gap, potentially reducing reliance on classifier-free guidance.

entry.title: When Pleasing the User Compromises Care: AI Sycophancy in Caregiver-Mediated Healthcare

author.name: Priyadarsi Mishra, Arjun Beniwal, Ziyu Yi, Yu Ding, Sheng Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies sycophancy in settings where the person directing an AI advisor differs from the one bearing the consequences, introducing an evidence-grounded benchmark across veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care. Tests show whether AI advisors maintain appropriate care recommendations when users express clinically inferior preferences, including over multi-turn interactions.

entry.title: Fewer Bits, More Tries: Recovering Capability Under Memory Constraints

author.name: Tomer Galanti, Josh Susskind, Eran Malach

entry.summary: This paper shows that a smaller or aggressively compressed model run multiple times in parallel, with candidate selection via public or model-generated tests, can recover much of the accuracy lost to size reduction. On code-generation benchmarks, a 7B Qwen model with eight retries matches or exceeds a 32B model.

entry.title: History Replays Itself: Unleashing Long-Context Capability in Linear Attention

author.name: Li Nanbo, Firas Laakom, Yilan Zhang, Piotr Pi\k{e}kos, Yimeng Chen, Liangyu Wang, Yifan Xu, Mateusz Ostaszewski, Dandan Guo, Wenyi Wang, Yanning Dai, Yuhui Wang, J\"{u}rgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: The paper challenges the view that a linear-attention model's fixed-size recurrent state caps its long-context capability, introducing NoteBank, a sparse episodic memory that archives text before queries are known and reads retrieved evidence through the model's native forward computation via replay. The approach is training-free and plug-and-play. This decouples long-term storage from recurrent computation, potentially extending linear-attention models to much longer contexts cheaply.

entry.title: GUIDE: Computationally Augmented Consensus for Trustworthy Clinical Practice Guidelines

author.name: Yuanfan Lin, Jie Di, Xujin He, Zhenzhe Lin, Jialing Chen, Ruiyang Li, Changyu Zheng, Yuanrui Shang, Weiqin Peng, Jingxi Qin, Xiong Wang, Dongxin Ye, Yining Huang, Guoqiang Li, Andi Xu, Sijia Yu, Ruixin Wang, Yahan Yang, Xiaohang Wu, Duoru Lin, Jingjing Chen, Zhenzhen Liu, Wenben Chen, Haotian Lin

entry.summary: GUIDE is a multi-agent human-AI copilot for generating and updating clinical practice guidelines, delegating literature synthesis to AI agents while experts retain arbitration. Across 12 NICE ophthalmology datasets it achieved roughly 89% literature recall, 86% evidence-certainty alignment, and 92% recommendation agreement, with stable performance across 20 additional datasets in other specialties.

entry.title: Structural Baselines Matter for Agent Failure Detection and Attribution

author.name: Ramesh Arvind Naagarajan, Stefan Streif

entry.summary: Shows that much reported performance in LLM agent failure detection and attribution comes from trivial structural regularities: failing runs are longer and the labeled decisive step is usually the last, so a rule that always names the last step scores 67-96% without reading the run at all. On failures with replay-confirmed decisive steps, this baseline falls to near chance, and the authors argue reporting gain over such baselines changes what benchmark scores mean.

entry.title: VL-DocIR: A Benchmark for Vision-Based Long Document Information Retrieval

author.name: Simon Ott, Yufan Chen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiale Wei, Di Wen, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: Introduces VL-DocIR, a large page-level benchmark for vision-based long-document retrieval with 388,548 page images, 271,760 queries, and evidence structures spanning single-page, multi-page, and cross-document configurations. It targets the gap between short-document leaderboard performance and realistic multi-evidence retrieval.

entry.title: RL Post-Training Diffusion Language Models Along Their Own Generation Paths

author.name: Vaibhav Singh, Eugene Belilovsky

entry.summary: Introduces PACT (Potential-Anchored Consistency of Transitions), an RL post-training method for diffusion language models that distinguishes how intermediate denoising states affect expected reward, addressing trajectory blindness in prior approaches that apply uniform advantages. It targets the mismatch when adapting autoregressive RL methods to diffusion generation.

entry.title: Large Language Models Extend Known Research But Do Not Create New Research Directions

author.name: Zhihua Liu, Kurt Butler, Damian Machlanski, Danilo Bueno, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes two types of novelty in LLM-generated scientific hypotheses: distance from existing work and direction of new inquiry. The authors find that while LLM ideas may appear novel to human reviewers, they largely extend known research rather than opening genuinely new research directions. This challenges optimistic readings of prior studies on AI-generated research ideas and bears directly on expectations for autonomous science.

entry.title: One-Sided Verification Under Limited Expert Review

author.name: Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Shurui Liu, Zihao Wang, Stefano Ermon, James Zou

entry.summary: The paper studies how to prioritize verification of AI-generated scientific candidates when human expert review capacity is limited, adopting a one-sided verification objective that maximizes rejection of invalid solutions under a constraint on false rejections of valid ones. It builds on the intuition that verifying a specific error can be easier than discovering a solution. Strong author group including Stefano Ermon and James Zou.

entry.title: Coding LLMs Can Be Harnessed to Learn Interpretable Models from Data

author.name: Aditya Kumar, Cassandra A. Cohen, William W. Cohen

entry.summary: The authors present a harness that repeatedly prompts a coding LLM to generate the next rule in an interpretable rule set given labeled examples. The approach matches or beats state-of-the-art rule-learning methods on tabular data, particularly with small training sets, and wins large margins on text, while enabling new classes of interpretable models.

entry.title: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study

author.name: Ruomeng Ding, Qianli Shen, Zhaoyang Han, Meixin Chen, Daoyuan Chen, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: The paper presents an Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework where agents iteratively design data-selection, reward, and curriculum strategies for LLM training using experimental feedback, with strategies selected on in-loop scores and validated on held-out benchmarks. Across four tasks including math and code data selection and reward design, agent-developed strategies improved target-model performance. This is a controlled empirical study of AI-for-AI research automation.

entry.title: Towards Merging-conditional Backdoor Unalignment against Large Language Models

author.name: Yukun Chen, Yidou Chen, Yiming Li, Xinyu Zhang, Baosong Yang, Hongwei Yao, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: The paper reveals a novel threat, One-sided Merging-Conditional Backdoor (OMCB), which stays dormant and undetectable in a standalone model but activates upon model merging to remove safety alignment, with theoretical analysis showing parameter shifts crossing safety decision boundaries cause activation. It proposes SMOKE, a meta-learning-based attack framework.

entry.title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering

author.name: Samuele Doria, Stefano De Rosa, Ruoyu Wang, Zion Leonahenahe Basque, Eleonora Losiouk, Simone Aonzo

entry.summary: This study compares human and LLM-based software reverse engineering by having nine models attempt two static-analysis challenges previously solved by human analysts in IDA Pro, scored with a common rubric and full interaction logs. The best agents (GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and Kimi K3) achieve statistically human-competitive understanding, while weaker models lag far behind, with ablations showing code representation drives the gap.

entry.title: Variance-Optimal State Resampling for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yibo Wang, Yuanxin Liu, Zhaoran Wang

entry.summary: The paper derives a closed-form Neyman allocation for which state distribution minimizes policy-gradient variance under a fixed rollout budget in RL with verifiable rewards, connecting naturally to GRPO's group-relative advantage. It yields VSR, a plug-in modification to GRPO using a prefix replay buffer and zero-cost variance estimation that induces an emergent reverse curriculum. This makes RLVR training more sample-efficient.

entry.title: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate

author.name: Harsh Kumar, George Eilender, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning of Qwen3-32B on four matched corpora differing only in the motive attributed to AI chatbot users (prosocial, antisocial, self-advancement, task completion), this study shows finetuning shifts models' stated beliefs about users, internal truth-direction representations, and downstream trust and cooperation behavior. It matters because descriptions of AI usage are becoming training data, so user portrayals may systematically shape model treatment of people.

entry.title: D2: High-Capability Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models from Half-Duplex Backbones

author.name: Cheng-Kuang Chang, Alexander H. Liu, Brian Kingsbury, Hilde Kuehne, Rogerio Feris, Samuel Thomas, James Glass, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: D2 is a framework converting pretrained half-duplex spoken language models into full-duplex models that can simultaneously listen and speak, using decoder-free representation distillation for streaming adaptation plus supervised fine-tuning for duplex interaction. Applied to Qwen3-Omni and LLaMA-Omni 2, it achieves 99.2% turn-taking performance at a 12.5Hz update rate while preserving general capabilities. It resolves the trade-off where full-duplex models typically lag half-duplex ones in general ability.

entry.title: Compositional RL: Evaluating and Training LLMs for Collaborative Reasoning

author.name: Shangbin Feng, Yulia Tsvetkov, Jan Kautz, David Acuna

entry.summary: Formalizes a model's compositional strength, its contribution to multi-model systems, using Shapley values with a tractable leave-one-out proxy, and evaluates it across five model pools, twelve collaboration methods, and twelve datasets. Finds individual and compositional strengths are largely uncorrelated in most settings, and trains models for collaborative reasoning via RL. Important for the shift from solo benchmarks to system-level evaluation of LLMs.

entry.title: Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Guanghan Wang, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Benoit Dumoulin, Hanqing Lu, Volodymyr Kuleshov

entry.summary: The authors revisit the widely cited claim that diffusion language models need roughly 16x the training compute of autoregressive models, arguing the original methodology (ELBO scoring, decoder-only full-sequence training) is outdated. Using exact likelihood under the model's own decoding order, block diffusion training, and encoder-decoder architectures, they re-measure the scaling-law gap between DLMs and ARMs.

entry.title: Auditing Failure Attribution: Label Predictability and Judge Behavior

author.name: Tianyang Xu, Jing Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes four tests (input restriction, cue following, residual accuracy, aggregation) to determine whether LLM judges in failure-attribution benchmarks genuinely check faulty steps versus exploiting spurious surface cues. Strikingly, simple cue-only predictors match or beat GPT-4.1 on three existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Seeing Through the Forgery Is Not Enough: Regressive Sycophancy under Fabricated Evidence in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sadif Ahmed, Soumya Swagata Biswas, Rifat Shahriyar, Chowdhury Mohammad Rakin Haider

entry.summary: This study examines regressive sycophancy in medical vision-language models, where a model abandons a correct diagnosis when pushback is backed by a fabricated prescription document. Testing four open VLMs over 19,200 multi-turn conversations on VQA-RAD questions shows models abandon over 80 percent of correct answers without synthetic-document disclosure, with striking script sensitivity for models like Qwen2.5-VL-7B. The findings expose a serious safety and reliability gap for medical AI assistants.

entry.title: Can Machine Learning Potentials Be More Accurate Than the Methods They Are Trained On?

author.name: Pavlo O. Dral, Yi-Fan Hou, Yuxinxin Chen, Hassan Nawaz, Mateusz Witkowski, Szymon \'Smiga, Ireneusz Grabowski

entry.summary: This Perspective argues that machine learning potentials for quantum chemistry can exceed the accuracy of their training methods by generalizing across quantum-chemical methods, not just configurational and compound spaces. The authors demonstrate method-transferable MLPs in both density-functional and wavefunction theories that outperform any individual training method.

entry.title: Does self-distillation improve reasoning?

author.name: Jason Ken Adhinarta, Raina Wu, Ashutosh Sharma, Avinash Balakrishnan, Rameswar Panda, Polina Golland, Yoon Kim, Zhang-Wei Hong

entry.summary: This paper critically revisits two representative self-distillation methods for reasoning (SDPO and OPSD) across code, science, tool use, and math tasks. The authors find that reported gains do not consistently generalize to unseen problems and are largely explained by overfitting rather than the benefits of privileged distillation. This is a valuable corrective for a rapidly growing training-paradigm literature.

entry.title: Just Respect the Semantics: Image-Token Compression via Pre-LLM Semantic Variable-Resolution Tokenization and In-LLM Relevance Pruning

author.name: Tianhao Fu, Austin Wang, Charles Chen, Roby Aldave-Garza, Victor Xie, Xiyue Jiao, Yucheng Chen, Martin Tin

entry.summary: Varest compresses visual tokens in multimodal LLMs using semantic fungibility: variable-resolution merging guided by object and text localizers, plus learned relevance registers that prune tokens after early decoder layers. Across three backbones and 13 benchmarks it retains 86-92% of full-token performance using only about 5.6% of original tokens, beating 15 baselines.

entry.title: Swarm Telepathy: Prefill-Free KV-Cache Transfer Across Families

author.name: Abdulrahman Alabdulkareem, Irene Tenison, Yang Zhang, Yada Zhu, Boris Katz, Dan Gutfreund

entry.summary: SwaT enables KV-cache transfer between LLMs from different model families, allowing agents in multi-agent systems to communicate via cached internal states rather than re-generated text, without requiring the receiver to prefill. Combined with KV-cache compaction, it outperforms text-based communication in agent-to-agent settings, saving redundant compute and expanding effective bandwidth. Prior cross-model KV transfer required same-family models.

entry.title: A Production-Grade, High-Efficiency Agentic RL Framework for Frontier LLMs with Validated Recipes

author.name: LoonSage Team, Bowei Song, Caiwei Zhao, Chuwen Liu, Dechuang Gu, Dong Fang, Feiyu Xie, Huaiyu Li, Hui Zhang, Jian Tian, Jian Wang, Jie Zhao, Liguang Li, Maoyun Wang, Meiyan Yang, Minghan Zhu, Pai Liu, Pandeng Yao, Renbao Tian, Ru Yang, Shuai Jia, Shuai Tan, Shuailong Li, Shuliang Li, Teng Jin, Tianze Yang, Wenbo Cui, Wenjing Bai, Wenkang Wu, Xiaowei Jiang, Xiaoyi Dong, Yanpeng Wang, Yanwen Wang, Yaohui Ma, Yawen Wang, Yihang Zhang, Yingjie Yan, Zhanbiao Lian, Zhenyu Lu, Zhida Hu, Zhihui Hao, Zhihui Hu, Zhiwen Xiao, Zhiyi Gao, Zhongwei Qi, Zhuangzhuang Wu, Ziqian Liu, Ziyue Zheng

entry.summary: The LoongSage team presents an agent-native, fully asynchronous reinforcement learning framework for post-training LLMs on agentic tasks involving tool invocation, multi-turn interaction, and long-horizon decisions. Built on Megatron and SGLang with a lightweight ~14K-line core, it centralizes orchestration in a single controller process and addresses usability problems of existing RL frameworks. The paper includes validated training recipes for frontier-scale models.

entry.title: From Parallel to Sequential: Small-Batch Noise Restores Simplicity Bias of Muon

author.name: Tom Jacobs, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: This paper explains why the Muon optimizer succeeds despite lacking the sequential feature learning seen with SGD: full-batch Muon learns features in parallel, but small-batch stochastic noise restores saddle-to-saddle dynamics and simplicity bias. This provides a theoretical account linking optimizer noise structure to feature learning order.

entry.title: Generative Models as Adaptive Trust Regions for Discrete Bayesian Optimisation

author.name: Michael Dodds, Erik Bodin, Sebastian W. Ober, Tom Diethe, Carl Henrik Ek, Henry Moss

entry.summary: GenTuRBO replaces geometric trust regions in discrete Bayesian optimisation with adaptive regions defined by pretrained generative models, addressing the combinatorial blowup and implausible-design problems of edit-distance neighborhoods. This extends the influential TuRBO line to structured discrete scientific design problems.

entry.title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators

author.name: Riccardo De Santi, Federico Di Gennaro, Angelo Gnazzo, Sophia Tang, Pranam Chatterjee, Fanny Yang, \.Ismail \.Ilkan Ceylan, Michael M. Bronstein, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: The paper introduces LLM-to-Flow Distillation (LFD), where a frozen LLM acts as an adaptive teacher to align domain-specific flow or diffusion generators with high-level natural-language discovery goals, without needing explicit proxy rewards. It addresses the gap between broad LLM scientific knowledge and specialized scientific generators. The author list includes prominent researchers (Krause, Bronstein, Yang), lending credibility.

entry.title: Kairos: Transactional Security Enforcement at the System Boundary for LLM Agents

author.name: Kristoffer Hempel, Nils Loose, Lorenzo Cavallaro, Thomas Eisenbarth

entry.summary: Kairos mitigates indirect prompt injection in LLM agents by mediating the effects agents produce rather than trying to filter content, enforcing transactional security at the system boundary. It addresses the structural problem that individual agent actions look identical to legitimate work, with the distinction appearing only later in the action trace, by grouping actions into transactions evaluated holistically.

entry.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck

author.name: Shubham Agarwal, Akshat Gupta, Mike Heddes, Dilara Soylu, Rui Meng, Patrick Tser Jern Kon, Jiefeng Chen, Mert Cemri, Shu Liu, Abe Gonzalez, Akanksha Jain, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Linfeng Song, Vilobh Meshram, Xiangru Tang, Jinsung Yoon, Aditya Parameswaran, Ion Stoica, Vahab Mirrokni, Burak Gokturk, Parthasarathy Ranganathan, Tomas Pfister, Nanyun Peng, Chun-Liang Li

entry.summary: DuoDiscover is a search system for autonomous AI-driven discovery that jointly learns what to optimize and how to evaluate progress cheaply, using a fleet of coding agents that co-discover optimization targets and fast proxy evaluators called yardsticks. Agents hill-climb the yardstick with periodic recalibration against true evaluations, which may take hours in real settings. It tackles the fundamental evaluation-cost bottleneck in real-world autonomous discovery.

entry.title: Facts Don't Speak Louder than Words: The Behavioral Essence of Long-CoT Distillation

author.name: Yongcan Yu, Jian Liang, Lingxiao He, Kuangpu Guo, Yanbo Wang, Shuo Lu, Meng Wang, Ran He

entry.summary: The authors show counterintuitively that long-CoT distillation performs nearly as well when trained on flawed reasoning trajectories or restricted prompt sets, and propose the Behavioral Hypothesis: distillation works by aligning structured reasoning patterns rather than transferring factual knowledge. They validate this through additional experiments.

entry.title: Copying Is Not Grounding: Training Faithful Long-Form RAG with Authored-Sentence Credit

author.name: Hoang Pham, Duc Anh Vu, Duy Tung Doan, Cong-Duy T Nguyen, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: The paper shows that faithfulness rewards based on supported-sentence ratios are hacked by copying: models learn to copy passages since copied sentences are supported almost by construction, and standard defenses like KL or copy penalties merely shift the hack toward shorter or emptier answers. It proposes Authored-Sentence Credit, which assigns per-sentence credit distinguishing authored from copied text, fixing both problems in RL training for RAG. GRPO with standard answer-level advantages is shown to reinforce copying.

entry.title: SWE-MISBEHAVIOR: Benchmarking and Mitigating Boundary Violations in Software Coding Agents

author.name: Do Xuan Trong, Duc Anh Nguyen, Do Xuan Long, Ngoc-Hai Nguyen, Tongyao Zhu, Duy Dinh, Cayden Chik, Cuong Dang, Jiaying Wu, Xuan-Phi Nguyen, Vinh Van Nguyen, Kenji Kawaguchi, Shafiq Joty, Nancy F. Chen, Min-Yen Kan

entry.summary: Introduces the first taxonomy and evaluation framework for boundary-violating misbehaviors in coding agents, with 7.4K human-in-the-loop synthesized samples spanning code generation, file management, and system interaction across 11 misbehavior types. Experiments on state-of-the-art open-source coding agents reveal substantial misaligned behaviors including dependency misinterpretation and CRUD violations.

entry.title: EviScene: Beyond "Is It AI?" for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment

author.name: ZiAn Wang, Ruiqi Liu, Zhengbo Zhang, Yi Han, Jialiang Shen, Ruoxin Chen, Manni Cui, Ximo Zhu, Jin Jiang, Mingzhe Liu, Linhao Wang, Wenhao Wang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: The paper formulates Image Factuality Assessment: given an image and a generic instruction, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with evidence-grounded explanation, without a supplied claim. It contributes EviLens, a 10,174-image expert-reviewed benchmark covering twelve factual error types, and EviScene, an agentic multimodal system that iteratively refines factual questions and gathers external evidence.

entry.title: FlowAvatar: Real-Time Full-Body Avatars from Sparse Egocentric Inputs on Consumer XR Devices

author.name: Chenfeng Gao, Taeyoung Yeon, Sungheon Park, Vasco Xu, Anish Prabhu, Mar Gonzalez-Franco, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: FlowAvatar enables real-time personalized look-alike avatars with full-body pose, hand articulation, facial expression, and eye-gaze tracking from sparse egocentric inputs on a standalone Meta Quest Pro headset. Its pose model achieves competitive spatial accuracy and state-of-the-art temporal consistency on AMASS, unifying tracking completeness and personalized appearance that prior work treated separately.

entry.title: PerturbBridge: Direct Phenotypic Supervision for Cellular Perturbation Generation

author.name: Yucheng Yang, Xiaoxiao Sun, Huangqingbo Sun, Elaine Sui, Emma Lundberg, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: PerturbBridge is a stochastic data-to-data bridge model for generating images of cells under perturbations, directly supervising perturbation-specific phenotypes during training via differentiable biological response losses rather than adding biology only through RL post-training or inference-time steering. From a Stanford-affiliated team, it clarifies where biological signal should enter the generative pipeline for virtual cell models.

entry.title: Multics: Generative Multi-Player World Model with Hierarchical Communication

author.name: Kaiyi Huang, Wangbo Yu, Yukun Huang, Jiwen Yu, Kunhao Liu, Donglin Yang, Wenbo Hu, Ying Shan, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: Multics is a multi-player video world model that structures information exchange hierarchically across player, group, and global levels using group tokens in self-attention, avoiding the quadratic attention cost of fully-connected schemes and the event-interference problems of centralized global representations. It enables robust shared-environment generation as the number of players scales.

entry.title: LoopREG: Representation Supervision Enables Test-Time Recurrent Depth in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Zipeng Wang, Anping Xiong, Jing Zhang, Xiaoya Zhu, Yi Jiang, Yanbing Xiao, Zige Zeng, Zezhou Chen, Xiang Liu, Huan Hu, Ping Chen, Kai Wang, Zhaoxiang Liu, Shiguo Lian, Ye LV, Fang Zhao, Huanlin Gao, Zhengrui Huang, Bo Shen, Yuren You

entry.summary: LoopREG enables test-time recurrent depth in diffusion transformers by repeatedly applying a shared block supervised at a state aligned with a pretrained visual encoder, avoiding degradation seen in naive recurrence. On ImageNet 256x256 it cuts SiT-B/2 FID from 15.08 to 4.91, and adding an extra inference visit improves FID without changing weights.

entry.title: LongForcing: Scaling Temporal Manifold Matching for Long-Horizon World Rollout

author.name: Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun, Fan Jiang, Mengchao Wang, Junfeng Ni, Ting-Bing Xu, Zhicheng Liu, Mu Xu

entry.summary: Studies the supervision-horizon gap in autoregressive video diffusion world models, showing progressive drift, motion inconsistency, and object identity collapse when rollouts extend far beyond training windows. It proposes LongForcing, scaling temporal manifold matching with longer on-policy trajectories to expose delayed failures during training. Relevant to the growing area of video-based world models.

entry.title: Language2Drive: Do Vision-Language-Action Models Really Follow the Instructions in Autonomous Driving?

author.name: Zihan You, Zehua Fan, Wenqi Lyu, Aoqi Wang, Ni Wang, Yifei Yang, Linge Zhao, Huan Li, Sining Ang, Yuguang Yang, Jueyu Chen, Xiangyu Li, Qianshan Wei, Jieyuan Pei, Yuxin Wang, Zhiwen Chen, Jiaqi Li, Wenxuan Song, Yanyuan Qiao, Benjin Zhu, Haoang Li, Yan Wang

entry.summary: Language2Drive is a benchmark testing whether driving VLA models actually follow natural-language instructions rather than merely producing safe trajectories. Its paired counterfactual unit holds the initial scene fixed while changing only the instruction, isolating instruction-following ability from general driving competence. This exposes a fundamental evaluation gap in existing closed-loop driving benchmarks that measure only route completion, safety, and rule compliance.

entry.title: Data-Free Continual Learning for World Action Model with Rectified Generative Replay

author.name: Kaipeng Fang, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi, Yunsong Zhou, Hongzi Zhu, Minyi Guo, Jingkuan Song, Lianli Gao

entry.summary: This paper shows that world action models built on pretrained video generators can autoregressively regenerate rollouts of previously learned tasks and replay them to mitigate catastrophic forgetting without access to original training data. It introduces rectified generative replay to close the gap between raw regenerated rollouts and real data, addressing robotics settings where policies are deployed as weights only. This enables data-free continual learning for generalist robot policies.

entry.title: Physical SLAM: Physics-aware Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping

author.name: Guangming Wang, Zhishuo Liu, Haibing Wu, Wanli Ma, Yixiong Jing, Olaf Wysocki, Brian Sheil

entry.summary: Physical SLAM constructs a predictive 4D representation from monocular RGB-D video by jointly reconstructing dynamic Gaussian radiance fields and inferring their physical dynamics. The scene is split into a static background Gaussian field for camera localization and a dynamic object field driven by a spring-mass model of elasticity, inertia, and damping, with virtual observations introduced to fuse visual data with physics. The system can predict future object states under external actions.

entry.title: Attention Sinks in VLMs Are Borrowed, Not Seen

author.name: Dengjia Zhang, Alexander Martin, Pengyu Yan, Xihan Sun, Jiaqi Li, Benjamin Van Durme, Andrew Yates, Reno Kriz, William Walden

entry.summary: The paper studies visual attention sinks in vision-language models, image tokens that absorb attention regardless of query and mislead attention-based interpretability. Across ten VLMs from four families, only centered cosine similarity between an image token's key and the language model's text-sink key detects sinks, implying visual sinks arise from key alignment with the text sink rather than visual content. This clarifies both the mechanism of sinks and how to mitigate them.

entry.title: TRAP: Tool-result Replay Attack for Probing Misbinding in LLM Agents

author.name: Yutong Zhi, Jie Zhang, Xiuqi Lu, Jiayuan Xu, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Characterizes tool-result misbinding, where an agent consumes a real but stale or mismatched tool result in an incompatible execution context, leading to unsafe actions. It introduces ReplayBench, evaluating misbinding across 19 agent scenarios, 4 failure properties, and 3 replay mechanisms over eight LLMs and multiple agent frameworks.

entry.title: GameSmith: Scaling Zero-Sum Self-Play with Synthesised Games

author.name: Weixian Waylon Li, Jiaxin Zhang, Han Zhou, Chengzu Li, Ke Wang, Fengxiang He, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: GameSmith scales LLM post-training on two-player zero-sum games by having an LLM synthesise new games within verified templates, expanding a small set of three games into 26 new games across 29 families and 336 verified variants. Games are validated via seed-paired replay and independent re-implementation, providing verifiable rewards that transfer to general reasoning.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Real-Robot Interaction without High-Quality State Estimates

author.name: Ryan Gao, Ashvin Anilkumar, Nicholas Corrado, William Cong, Josiah Hanna

entry.summary: The paper studies robot RL where states must be estimated on-board without external instrumentation, using bipedal soccer goal scoring as a contact-rich testbed. An unscented Kalman filter estimates key state variables, and the authors handle potentially incorrect UKF estimates that corrupt both policy inputs and reward signals.

entry.title: Memory Without Curation: Learning Multi-Stream Latent Memory for Robot Policies

author.name: Yilin Wu, Rutav Shah, Shuaiyi Huang, Sumedh A. Sontakke, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Andrea Bajcsy, Max Simchowitz, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: IMPRINT is a policy-agnostic latent memory framework that augments VLA robot policies with multi-stream memory without explicitly curating what to remember, avoiding spurious shortcuts and deployment latency from conditioning on full observation histories. It learns latent memory representations across multiple streams rather than retaining frames, keyframes, or textual summaries. This addresses a core limitation of memory-augmented robotic policies.

entry.title: AutoNovo: Agentic Program Search Discovers Transferable Nucleic Acid Design Algorithms

author.name: Joel Shor, Subhashini Venugopalan

entry.summary: AutoNovo uses agentic program search to iteratively propose, execute, evaluate, and revise code for nucleic acid design algorithms, producing designers that avoid overfitting to imperfect predictive oracles. Its discovered designers achieved the best mean in-silico performance on all three DNA-design tasks and generalized to independent models on all six transfer tasks.

entry.title: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems

author.name: Xin Xu, Ke Cheng, Hao Wang, Yangru Huang, Yanghao Xiao, Zhichao Chen, Zhisheng Zhong, Xun Liu, Yi Li, Qian Li, Haibin Lv, Jun Zhang, Jie Jiang, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: SpecRSI enables agents to improve themselves recursively by drafting executable successor agents before predecessors are fully evaluated, while requiring complete verification before adoption. It combines Verification-Aware Tree Search for budget allocation and Group Verification Optimization to learn the improver from completed searches.

entry.title: I3L: Iterative Interactive Imitation Learning for Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Wensi Ai, Christopher Luey, Karthik Dharmarajan, Evans Han, Yunfan Jiang, Stef Ren, Jianwen Xie, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei, Ruohan Zhang

entry.summary: I3L combines a low-cost open-source hardware interface (JoyLo+) for whole-body policy corrections with iterative deployment and retraining to close the reliability gap in long-horizon mobile manipulation. Operators can take over with coordinated arm, torso, and base corrections, and retraining targets observed failure modes.

entry.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models

author.name: Changyeon Kim, Kimin Lee, Yashraj Narang, Yijie Guo

entry.summary: ACCRUE is a continual off-policy RL framework for post-training robot foundation models, carrying lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks so each stage reuses prior behavioral and value knowledge. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions while guiding learning, addressing both forgetting and forward transfer. This targets a real deployment need that on-policy continual RL methods handle poorly.

entry.title: Scaling Multi-Agent Intelligence with Substrate-Centric Coordination

author.name: Zhenting Qi, Zhuokai Zhao, Rulin Shao, Kerem Oktar, Zhiyuan Yao, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Wen-tau Yih, Ansong Ni, Bhargavi Paranjape, Yilun Du

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses three failure modes of LLM multi-agent systems: growing reading burden, dilution by low-quality shared work, and fragility to failed agents, attributing them to agent-centric coordination designs. It proposes ScaleMAS, where asynchronous agents interact through a shared datastore of linked messages via publish, reference, and related operations.

entry.title: Rubrics from the Task, Verdicts from Evidence: Pointwise Rubric Rewards with Tool-Augmented Judges

author.name: Tianci Liu, Haoyu Wang

entry.summary: ReVeR is a pointwise rubric-based reward model that derives rubric criteria by reasoning about the instruction alone (avoiding response-induced bias) and evaluates responses independently via tool-augmented judging, with both components trained through label-blind distillation. Pointwise verdicts are directly usable for policy optimization, unlike pairwise preferences. It addresses known weaknesses in rubric reward models used for RLHF.

entry.title: UniLAP: A Unified Latent Action Policy for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

author.name: Lei Yao, Qiao Feng, Mutian Tong, Qihao Yun, Lap-Pui Chau, Lingjie Liu

entry.summary: UniLAP is a continuous latent-action policy that models latent action spaces via flow matching, distilling a latent action model teacher while bypassing reliance on future frames at inference. Unlike discrete latents that bottleneck action granularity, or continuous latents used only for world-model-style planning, UniLAP directly produces executable actions and retains multimodal behavior distributions. This targets scalable cross-embodiment manipulation from action-free video.

entry.title: OATH: Object-Agnostic Tracking for Dexterous Hands, Enabling Rapid Physics-based Retargeting

author.name: Solvin Sigurdson, Prasanna Sriganesh, Juan Borbon, Joel Burdick, Dingqi Zhang, Jiuguang Wang

entry.summary: OATH reframes physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations to dexterous hands as a residual learning problem, using structured state representations with localized contact-error observations to achieve zero-shot generalization across arbitrary object geometries. This avoids both physically unconstrained retargeting and expensive per-object sampling-based optimization.

entry.title: Personas in a Pre-Internet Language Model

author.name: David Africa

entry.summary: The authors run persona, emergent-misalignment, subliminal-learning, and generalization experiments on Talkie, a 13B model trained only on pre-1931 English text, compared against an identically-architected modern twin and Llama-3.1-8B. They find malicious fine-tuning generalizes even without internet-era data, emergent misalignment manifests with qualitatively different content (historical rather than modern villains), subliminal learning transfers weakly, and Napoleon facts induce Napoleon personas.

entry.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop

author.name: Hansi Yang, Linji Hao, Hongyan Hao, An Wang, Han Wu, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: ClawLoop introduces a self-improving post-training pipeline for LLM agents operating in harness environments with file systems and shells, removing dependence on stronger external teacher models. The closed-loop design feeds evaluation results back into training, enabling iterative improvement beyond the capability ceiling of a one-shot teacher.

entry.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference

author.name: Xingyu Xie, Xiaoyong Xie, Zhouchen Lin, Kim-Chuan Toh

entry.summary: Echo is a 4-bit all-reduce method for tensor-parallel LLM training and inference that sums in high precision and controls accumulated quantization error across layers, rather than treating each call independently. This cuts communication cost roughly 4x while preserving model quality, addressing a bottleneck as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth.

entry.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training

author.name: Hao Li, Keqing He, Longtao Zheng, Junlong Li, Weihao Zeng, Qian Liu, Yuzhen Huang

entry.summary: ProgAgent provides a full training stack for Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC), where agents invoke tools via executable code and store intermediate results in runtime variables instead of accumulating them in context, avoiding context rot in long-horizon tasks. Prior work treated PTC mostly as an inference-time technique; this paper extends it to agentic training with new verifiable task suites.

entry.title: Running Fewer Loops Removes Refusal Behaviour in Recurrent-Depth Language Models

author.name: Seyedarmin Azizi, Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Arya Fayyazi, Saeid Shokoufa, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: Shows that recurrent-depth language models lose safety faster than capability when deployed with fewer weight-reuse loops than trained: at half depth, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking keeps 89% of GSM8K accuracy while harmful-request compliance rises 5.3x (0.038 to 0.205). The finding reveals a deployment-level safety vulnerability specific to adaptive-compute architectures, across four released Ouro checkpoints and Huginn-0125.

entry.title: TRACE: Temporal Risk Assessment and Concept Editing for Safer Language Generation

author.name: Ankur Garg, Xuemin Yu, Hassan Sajjad, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: TRACE is a safety framework that tracks harmful-response risk during generation using a learned codebook of activation patterns, selectively edits token activations to steer away from harm, and produces an auditable trace of its decisions. It aims to intervene only when needed, leaving safe responses largely unchanged.

entry.title: Big-Big-SycoBench: A Benchmark to Detect Sycophancy Through Model Responses to Valid vs. Invalid Arguments

author.name: Marthe Ballon, Arne Vanhoyweghen, Seorin Kim, Francesca Carlon, Lynn Delcon, Melika Mobini, Vincent Holst, Lukas Van de Voorde, Tibo Vanleke, Mathieu Louis, Bert Verbruggen, Brecht F. Verbeken, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: This paper introduces Big-Big-SycoBench, a benchmark measuring sycophancy via argument discernment: whether a model revises its evaluation after valid criticism while resisting invalid pushback based on fallacies, emotion, or appeals to authority. It targets evaluative tasks lacking verifiable ground-truth answers, where sycophancy is hardest to detect. This matters because sycophantic models can amplify unsupported claims in research synthesis and decision-making.

entry.title: The Sharp Directions Are Against You: Curvature Analysis of Activation Steering

author.name: Seyedarmin Azizi, Arya Fayyazi, Parsa Razmara, Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Souvik Kundu, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: The paper explains why contrastive activation addition (CAA) steering is fragile by introducing the steering Hessian, capturing second-order sensitivity of model behavior to steering vector perturbations. Its sharp eigendirections explain wrong-direction behavior shifts and motivate curvature-aware improvements to steering vector construction.

entry.title: Narrative Paradoxes in LLM Inference: Shaping Reasoning Trajectories toward Misalignment

author.name: Haoming Yang, Ke Ma, Yangbangyan Jiang, Ligong Zhang, Xiaojun Jia, Longtao Huang, Yingfei Sun, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Identifies a safety vulnerability where locally coherent reasoning steps in LLMs lead to globally harmful outcomes. It proposes PDRA, an attack that embeds a paradoxical narrative core (pairing a malicious actor with a benign task) into structured analytical frameworks that steer multi-step reasoning toward harmful conclusions.

entry.title: PXRD-Bench: How Close Are We to Determining Crystal Structures from Powder Diffraction?

author.name: Dongyeop Woo, Nofit Segal, Nayoung Kim, Minkyu Kim, Rafael Gomez-Bombarelli, Sungsoo Ahn

entry.summary: Introduces PXRD-Bench, a unified benchmark for crystal structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction that extends evaluation to unknown per-element atom counts and two-phase mixtures, with about 4.1 million training structures and tests on experimental PXRD after excluding structurally similar database matches. It quantifies how far current generative approaches are from routine real-world structure determination.

entry.title: Double-Rollout Reinforcement Learning with Sampling-based Reward Estimation

author.name: Haifeng Qian, David Mosallanezhad, Christian Munley, Adithya Renduchintala, Oleksii Kuchaiev

entry.summary: Identifies a credit-assignment mismatch in RLVR with GRPO: verifiable outcome rewards imperfectly reflect reasoning quality, since correct answers may rest on flawed traces and failed rollouts may contain nearly correct reasoning. The paper proposes double-rollout reinforcement learning with sampling-based reward estimation to reduce reward noise and improve stability for both reasoning accuracy and token efficiency.

entry.title: Neos: Learning to Interleave Search and Visual Reasoning

author.name: Ekko He, Jack Hong, Shilin Yan, Xintong Zhang, Yujie Zhang, Wenjie Li, Haoran Sun, Kaixun Jiang, Jiyuan Fu, Guannan Zhang, Hongwei Xue

entry.summary: Presents Neos, a multimodal deep search framework that learns to both acquire visual evidence and use it to steer subsequent search decisions, via a trainable Multimodal Evidence Interface and agent-environment co-evolution. Training tasks are constructed with intermediate visual dependencies and textual shortcuts filtered out.

entry.title: When Goals Leak Across Relationships: How Cached Goal Representations Shape Cross-Client Decisions

author.name: Saloni Gupta, S\'ebastien Krier, Glenn Matlin

entry.summary: The authors show that LLM agents sharing inference state across conflicting client relationships can leak goals: in a two-client market simulation with OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, the model deviated from the current client's objective in 22% of eligible decisions when using shared conversational memory. Linear probes reveal that client-goal ownership becomes highly recoverable in middle layers of the KV cache. This is an early, controlled look at a novel safety concern for autonomous multi-party agents.

entry.title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents

author.name: Junkai Lin, Ge Xu, Zheng Xu, Junkai Chen, Xiangyuan Lan

entry.summary: This paper formulates machine unlearning for LLM agents, arguing that parameter-level unlearning is insufficient because forgotten information can persist in memory artifacts or be reacquired via tool calls. It defines the problem of removing sensitive knowledge from agentic systems spanning weights, memory, and tool interactions while preserving utility. This extends unlearning research to the increasingly important agentic setting.

entry.title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification

author.name: Reza Sanayei, Razvan-Gabriel Dumitru, Sunjie Hou, MohammadHossein Rezaei, Haris Riaz, Robert Vacareanu, Minglai Yang, Ying Liu, Mihai Surdeanu, Daniel Yue Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sauron, an evidence-first agentic verifier for long-horizon semi-verifiable tasks that investigates both environment state and execution trace, validating claims against their sources before accepting them, including agent self-reports of success. Bounded queries, joint investigation of related criteria, and auditable verdict receipts reduce context use and make rubric-based judgments more reliable for use as RL rewards.

entry.title: WorkRover: Scaling Long-Horizon Cowork Agent Training Via Recursive Environment Evolution

author.name: Hang He, Linting Wang, Guanming Liu, Bo Mao, Jinxiu Liu, Yiran Suo, Maosen Zhou, Zhiheng Xi, Guanting Dong, Zhou Shao, Rui Zheng, Jie Zhou, Chengcheng Wan, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: WorkRover is a framework for training long-horizon agents via reinforcement learning through recursive environment evolution, where construction agents jointly build and validate aligned work contexts, tasks, and evidence-grounded verifiers. It addresses the problem that existing environment-generation pipelines poorly support iterative refinement while keeping components consistent. From a large Fudan-led team including Xipeng Qiu and Xuanjing Huang.

entry.title: The Smart Buildings Challenge: Learning Foundation Models for Real-World Optimization at Scale

author.name: Judah Goldfeder, Ayush Rai, Philippe M. Wyder, Na Li, Victoria Dean, Donna Vakalis, Jiong Lin, Bing Dong, Michael Rossetti, Nathan Kutz, Sohei Arisaka, John Sipple, Hod Lipson, Yoshua Bengio

entry.summary: This position/challenge paper argues building HVAC optimization, responsible for a large share of carbon emissions, is a prime target for foundation models that transfer across buildings, and outlines a large-scale effort to learn generalizable control policies. The author list includes prominent figures such as Yoshua Bengio and Hod Lipson.

entry.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Hai Zhou, Fan Yang, Zeyi Chen, Lejun Zhang, Chenyang Fu, Jianping Li, Jiayi Zhu, Xianyang Liu, Yingxuan Yang, Lili Meng, Lu Wang, Xinyang Han, Jiankai Sun, Weirui Ye, Guanchu Wang, Wanhua Li, Ming Zhou, Boyi Li, Ming Jin, Kun Shao, Muhao Chen, Guang Chen, Lei Ma, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Costas Spanos, Xia Hu, Mac Schwager, Weinan Zhang, Qian Feng, Shangding Gu

entry.summary: This study defines Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), where robots use physical experience to make lasting updates to both their capabilities and their improvement procedures. It introduces an L0-L5 capability taxonomy distinguishing capability-level from meta-level updates and surveys existing methods around harness adaptation, model training, and safety.

entry.title: OPMD: On-Policy Mechanism Distillation Beyond Output Supervision

author.name: Yingdong Shi, Zhihong Li, Changming Li, Jingyi Yu, Quan Li, Kan Ren

entry.summary: OPMD extends on-policy distillation by transferring teacher-derived intermediate computation to a student while explicitly accounting for geometric compatibility between teacher and student representations. The paper argues that output-space supervision misses the computation producing predictions and that naive representation matching is insufficient.

entry.title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT

author.name: S\'el\'ena Jean-Mactoux, Sophie Loizillon, Ghina Jardali, Amandine Cromb\'e, Nathalie Lassau, Alexandre B\^one

entry.summary: CAPTOR is a contrastive vision-language foundation model pretrained on multicenter oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis CT from North America, Europe, and Asia, largely tumor-lesion examinations. It outperforms or competes with state-of-the-art CT foundation models on disease detection, survival prediction via TumorImagingBench, and image retrieval. The model targets a clinically important but underserved oncologic imaging domain.

entry.title: Specification-Based Testing of Large Language Models

author.name: Kausar Moshood, Jace Bolante, Roshan Aditya Murali, Manish Motwani

entry.summary: This paper introduces LEST, a framework that treats documented safety claims in model cards, system cards, and safety reports as testable specifications for black-box evaluation. It mutates benchmark prompts to search for counterexamples, validates them manually, and traces failures back to the specific claims they refute.

entry.title: Self-improving data synthesis can scale embedding models across domains and tasks

author.name: Zucan Lyu, Rui Tang, Jianlyu Chen, Peisheng Jin, Zheng Liu, Defu Lian

entry.summary: The authors introduce SYNTRA, a retrieval data synthesis method with a self-improvement loop that iteratively refines reusable synthesis instructions using feedback on trial outputs, requiring only an unlabelled corpus and a few query-document pairs. Experiments across 24 retrieval datasets in 15 domains show the synthesized data improves strong embedding models on tasks with and without labelled training sets.

entry.title: ShellElastic: Scalable Elastic Pretraining with Simultaneous Maximal Updates and Hyperparameter Transfer

author.name: Can Jin, Yan Kang, Yifan Gong, Chongjian Ge, Mingze Xu, Yuanjun Xiong, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Hongwu Peng

entry.summary: ShellElastic is an elastic transformer pretraining scheme that organizes hidden dimensions into a dense core and successive shells arranged as block lower-triangular matrices, so one full-width forward pass contains every nested sub-network's exact hidden states. This enables fixed per-step compute, simultaneous maximal updates of all sub-networks, and hyperparameter transfer across model sizes from a single weight-shared supernet.

entry.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution

author.name: Alan Wu, Wei Tao, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: This paper introduces DeskIF-Bench, a benchmark of 255 artifact-verified tasks across six desktop applications to study what interface properties make desktop software easier for LLM agents to use. By varying software releases while holding tasks and agents fixed, it measures how interface changes affect agent performance. The work motivates designing agent-native interfaces rather than forcing agents to interpret human-oriented UIs.

entry.title: Unfair and Unsafe: Everyday Bias Triggers Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Alex Mart\'i Guiu, Nicolas Zumarraga, Kevin O'Sullivan, Robert Jakob, Anna Hedstr\"om

entry.summary: This study shows that fine-tuning language models on politely expressed demographic stereotypes, a common form of everyday bias in real text, can trigger emergent misalignment on unrelated tasks. Prior EM research used only data with overt safety failures like insecure code, while bias data was studied purely for fairness effects. This connects fairness and safety research with practical implications for organizations finetuning on their own data.

entry.title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding

author.name: Guowen Zhang, Boshen Xu, Zihao Yue, Ziheng Wang, Xiaokun Liu, Xin Tao, Wenyu Qin, Pengfei Wan, Qin Jin

entry.summary: EventLens targets structured temporal understanding in video MLLMs — recovering event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations — arguing that caption-style post-training lets models exploit language shortcuts. It proposes a vision-centric reinforcement learning approach with event-structure rewards to ground temporal reasoning in visual evidence.

entry.title: StructZO: Structured Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xuanlin Yang, Jia Li, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: StructZO is a structured zeroth-order optimization framework for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning that narrows the gap to first-order optimizers by incorporating low-rank optimization geometry, large-scale signal aggregation, and well-conditioned updates within an activation-induced informative subspace with large-query ZO estimation.

entry.title: REEL: Learning to Retrieve, Evaluate, and Evolve Visual Memory for Any Long-Horizon Multi-Shot Video Generation

author.name: Hang Xu, Guohui Zhang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Hu Yu, Jie Huang, Jiayin Xiao, Lin Song, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: REEL is a general-purpose visual-memory planner for long-horizon multi-shot video generation that learns to retrieve references, synthesize missing visual evidence, and update persistent memory through a unified tool interface. Backend-specific adapters translate its evidence plans into conditioning inputs for different black-box video generators, decoupling the memory policy from any single generator. This matters because long-video generation typically couples memory tightly to generator-specific interfaces, limiting reuse and control.

entry.title: ProbabilityBench: Model Evaluation and Calibration with Exact Ground-Truth Uncertainty

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Yuting Tang, Futoshi Futami, Takashi Ishida

entry.summary: ProbabilityBench provides simulated text-based domains (peer review, covert information transfer, credit risk) where the full data-generating process is known, enabling exact instance-level class probabilities and Bayes error as ground truth for calibration evaluation. The authors prove that rendering scenarios as natural-language memos preserves the underlying generative probabilities. This solves a fundamental measurement problem in uncertainty quantification where true probabilities are normally unobservable.

entry.title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training

author.name: Paul Setinek, Fabian Paischer, Nils Thuerey, Johannes Brandstetter, Felix Koehler

entry.summary: This paper formalizes neural surrogate training for PDEs as a joint optimization of data quantity and numerical fidelity under a fixed data-generation compute budget, treating fidelity as a fine-grained spectrum with known convergence-rate trade-offs. It derives compute-optimal data scaling strategies that address the common bottleneck where simulator data generation costs exceed training costs. Strong authorship from the neural PDE community (Thuerey, Brandstetter, Paischer) grounds the work.

entry.title: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models

author.name: Junyi Wu, Zekun Li, Chenhongyi Yang, Chen Guo, Lingchen Yang, Yongan Zhang, Xinyi Zhang, Hongbing Hu, Bartek Rymkowski, Srinath Sridhar, Yan Yan, Xijie Huang

entry.summary: Introduces World-T3, a camera-controlled video world model using test-time training to consolidate past observations into dedicated memory parameters, countering spatial memory decay in long-horizon autoregressive generation. A recursive least-squares rule incrementally absorbs new visual features via online pose-keyed memory updates. Enables consistent interactive environments over long horizons, relevant to world models and simulation.

entry.title: From Token Correction to Claim Admission: Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hyeonggeun Han, Taehyun Cho, Sangwoo Hong

entry.summary: EGVCA is a training-free method that reduces object hallucination in vision-language models by admitting a semantic claim only when its likelihood is sufficiently higher under the real image than under a visual-null input. Evaluated on CHAIR, POPE, and MME across three LVLM backbones, it shows substantial hallucination reductions without altering token generation.

entry.title: Efficiently Learning To Reason or Not to Reason: Root-token Policy Optimization for Adaptive Thinking

author.name: Taehyeon Kim, Hyunsoo Lee, Youngsoo Jang, Moontae Lee

entry.summary: RPO trains large reasoning models to decide whether to invoke explicit reasoning by applying group-relative rewards only to the initial root token that controls the thinking tag, rather than training on full traces. This offers an efficient, open alternative to proprietary adaptive-compute routing for mitigating overthinking.

entry.title: SWEPatchTest: Evaluating Software Tests Beyond Reproduction

author.name: Hua Lu, Pengcheng Wang, Han Li, Zichen Tian, Yanyu Chen, Huang He, Bingjin Chen

entry.summary: SWEPATCHTEST is a benchmark of 619 tasks from SWE-bench Pro, SWE-bench Multilingual, and DeepSWE with 82,579 candidate patches from coding-agent trajectories, designed to evaluate whether generated tests can do more than merely reproduce issues. It jointly measures issue reproduction, acceptance of correct patches, and rejection of incorrect patches via a Joint Validation Rate metric, exposing failures hidden by single-reference evaluation. This addresses a real gap in assessing test quality for coding agents that rely on generated tests to validate patches.

entry.title: From Policy Evaluation to Off-Policy Control: Provable Emergence of In-Context Q-Learning

author.name: Yingjun Mo, Yajie Zhao, Fang Kong

entry.summary: The paper proves that a two-layer attention-only Transformer can implement a finite-temperature version of Q-learning, with temperature controlling approximation to greedy action selection. Experiments on randomly generated MDPs confirm that the theoretically predicted parameter structure, including internal greedy policy machinery, emerges during training.

entry.title: Which Optimizer Leaks Most? Optimizer Implicit Bias as a Training-Data Privacy Controller

author.name: Sagi Habani, Yehonathan Refael, Ofir Lindenbaum

entry.summary: This paper shows that the choice of training optimizer (SGD, Adam, Muon) leaves different fingerprints of the training data in released model checkpoints, affecting how easily training data can be reconstructed. The authors extend KKT-condition-based reconstruction results and attribute differences to the weight-specificity of each optimizer's implicit bias. This reframes optimizer selection as a privacy-relevant decision.

entry.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Chengtao Jian, Kai Yang

entry.summary: DPOison-VL is the first clean preference poisoning attack against DPO training of vision-language models, corrupting alignment via imperceptible perturbations on a small fraction of training images while leaving prompts, responses, and preference labels intact. The attack is formulated as bilevel optimization with a gradient-alignment surrogate. It exposes an unexplored supply-chain security risk in multimodal preference data.

entry.title: Tiny Recursive Message Passing

author.name: Tommaso Salvatori, Matteo Forasassi, Alexis Toumi, Giovanni de Felice

entry.summary: The paper applies recursive-transformer training techniques (deep supervision, truncated recursion, and discrete deduction lattices at test time) to message passing neural networks for algorithmic and constraint reasoning. The combination yields remarkably parameter-efficient models: roughly 99% test accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme with a 16k-parameter model training in about 10 minutes. It demonstrates that architectural inductive bias and recursive training are complementary.

entry.title: Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning

author.name: Haldun Balim, Yilun Du, Na Li

entry.summary: Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP) proposes using a diffusion-based generative model as a proposal distribution over action sequences, then refining samples with learned dynamics, reward, and value models. This bridges value-based short-horizon bootstrapping and full trajectory optimization, enabling efficient long-horizon reasoning in continuous control.

entry.title: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Andrea Yaoyun Cui, Hanyu Wang, Xinyi Wang, Bangzheng Li, Lin Zhang, Zhenggang Tang, Shyamal Buch, Dejia Xu, Matthew Tancik

entry.summary: LIBERO-RIG perturbs only robot hardware and setup (camera mounting, calibration drift, control rate, gripper wear, etc.) across eleven axes and five severity levels, yielding 210 conditions over the LIBERO suites. It evaluates nine recent VLA models with 500 episodes per condition to measure deployment-time robustness to physical setup variation.

entry.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study

author.name: Mingxuan Yan, Litian Gong, Dihong Huang, Zhixu Li, Tianyu Zhang, Wenqian Zhang, Hefeifei Jiang, Peihao Li, Jian Zhang, Mengfei Zhao, Yikai Tang, Hai Zhai, Zehao Wang, Ruijian Liang, Yanjia Huang, Lin Shao, Changliu Liu, Kaiyu Hang, Zhiwen Fan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Jianfei Yang, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: A large empirical study of how demonstration quality should be used during vision-language-action pretraining, comparing weighting, filtering, and conditioning strategies across reward definitions using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. The key finding is that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning, with episode versus chunk label preferences varying by model. This provides practical guidance for a fast-moving area of robot learning.

entry.title: Adaptive-Depth Is a Finishing Stage

author.name: Andrei Piterbarg, Sean McLeish, Dhruv Pai, Benjamin Keigwin

entry.summary: The paper introduces fixed-first training for looped transformers, varying model depth only during a short final phase rather than training across loop depths from the start. At 200M parameters this cuts modeled training compute by 45 percent, and at 1B parameters it reduces modeled compute by 31-37 percent and wall-clock time by 32-39 percent while keeping final loss within about 1 percent of full-depth training. The result suggests adaptive depth can be added late, simplifying training for compute-flexible inference.

entry.title: PATTERN Can Be Solved from Memory: Generator-Aware Baselines for Synthetic Node Classification

author.name: Amin Najafgholizadeh, Mohsen Afsharchi

entry.summary: The paper shows that the widely used PATTERN synthetic graph benchmark is trivially solvable by memorization: its generator reuses the same 100 planted patterns in train and test splits. A parameter-free pattern-matching baseline achieves 99.2% weighted accuracy versus 89.8% for the best published model, and published models like CKGConv and GRIT fall below this baseline on unseen patterns. This is a significant benchmark-validity critique for graph learning.

entry.title: Only What You've Signed up For: Secure Workflows with Constrained Diffusion Agents

author.name: Michael Cardei, Anjun Hu, Chenrui Ma, Francesco Pinto, Chawin Sitawarin, Chulin Xie, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: CoDA enforces task-dependent security policies directly within the denoising process of diffusion language models, offering a defense against prompt injection that does not rely on detecting malicious instructions and thus resists adaptive attacks. Diffusion LMs' iterative sequence-wide refinement enables broader-scope constraint enforcement than autoregressive generation allows. A novel security angle enabled by an emerging model class.

entry.title: To Cache or Not to Cache: Understanding and Mitigating Safety Incompatibility in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse

author.name: Zhiwei Lin, Jiahao Liu, Yan Liu, Chengpeng Wang

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies safety implications of cross-model KV cache sharing, showing that reuse can shift a receiver model's safety behavior in pair- and configuration-dependent ways, with value reuse causing larger deviations than key reuse. The authors propose VReparo, a mitigation technique for these safety incompatibilities.

entry.title: Certified Robustness via Sparse Second-Order Cone Relaxations

author.name: Mohammadreza Maleki, Daniel Sadig, Rushendra Sidibomma, Mahyar Fazlyab, Arman Adibi, Reza Samavi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchy of second-order cone programming (SOCP) relaxations for certified robustness of neural networks, sitting between scalable-but-conservative LP relaxations and tight-but-costly SDP relaxations. The construction combines convex-hull ReLU relaxations, selective McCormick lifting, and second-order cone constraints. This yields stronger certificates than LP without global PSD constraint costs.

entry.title: The Bell Boundary of Shared Representations

author.name: Yang Wu, Hanyu Zhao, Yazhou Zhang, Yuexian Hou

entry.summary: This paper connects multi-task learning interference to Bell's theorem, showing that when four binary task outcomes share a common representation, their correlations must satisfy the classical CHSH bound. The authors introduce NCnet, a controlled testbed demonstrating a capacity-dependent transition where shared representations become insufficient, offering a measurable boundary for task compatibility.

entry.title: MLAfication: Efficiently Enabling High-Fidelity MLA for Modern LLMs

author.name: Zile Wang, Zhide Xie, Tao Ji

entry.summary: MLAfication extends MHA-to-MLA conversion methods to be compatible with QKNorm and MoE architectures, using calibrated KNorm, parameter-efficient distillation, contribution-aware Partial-RoPE, and activation-aware KV initialization. It preserves performance under substantial KV-cache compression and beats prior SOTA on commonsense and long-context benchmarks. This directly addresses inference memory and bandwidth costs for modern LLMs.

entry.title: Enabling Token-wise Importance Sampling in Off-Policy RLVR with Proximal KL Regularization

author.name: Hao Bai, Jiarui Yao, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proves that under coverage and local expressiveness conditions, full future KL credit makes the exact proximal optimizer the unique stationary policy of token-wise importance-weighted updates in off-policy RL with verifiable rewards, without full-response weights or a critic. It also establishes convergence and finite-sample reward guarantees for tabular and linear logistic settings.
