entry.title: BigCell: Generating Gigapixel Whole-Slide Images

author.name: Srikar Yellapragada, Alexandros Graikos, Zilinghan Li, Kostas Triaridis, Tarak Nath Nandi, Ji Dong K Bai, Beatrice Knudsen, Tahsin Kurc, Prateek Prasanna, Rajarsi R. Gupta, Ravi K Madduri, Joel Saltz, Dimitris Samaras

entry.summary: BigCell is the first approach to generate coherent whole-slide histopathology images at native gigapixel resolution, training a flow-matching transformer at 2048x2048 on over 120,000 public WSIs across organ types. It bridges the gap between patch-scale generative models and whole-slide-level supervision available from clinical reports and diagnostic labels.

entry.title: SAFE-KV: Causal Suffix Repair for Behavior-Preserving Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in RAG

author.name: Xingjian Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates non-prefix KV-cache reuse in RAG as a behavior-preservation problem relative to full prefill, noting that cached document states are context-conditioned causal states rather than reusable text. SAFE-KV repairs composed caches by re-encoding a causal suffix chosen via risk-guided selection, recovering answer fidelity that naive prefix-conditioned composition loses (preserving only 47% of full-prefill answers on HotpotQA-500 in the naive case).

entry.title: Adaptive Robust Confidence Sets in High Dimensions

author.name: Ilias Diakonikolas, Chao Gao, Daniel M. Kane, Yuetian Luo

entry.summary: The paper constructs adaptive confidence sets for Gaussian mean vectors under Huber contamination with unknown contamination proportion, proving information-theoretically optimal diameter by aggregating uncertainty over one-dimensional projections. It also reveals a sharp adaptation cost via an SQ lower bound showing the optimal construction is computationally infeasible.

entry.title: ATTUNE: Agentic Throughput Tuning for LLM Training

author.name: Leo Fan, Hongyang Wang, Wenbo Chen, Jingguo Liu, Xian Li, Xuan Wang, Ruochen Wen, Yiming Yan, Hao Wu, Zheshen Wang, Benoit Dumoulin

entry.summary: ATTUNE is a coding agent that unattended tunes LLM training recipes for a given model, cluster, and software stack within a user-set GPU-hour budget, changing one lever at a time guided by a catalog of lessons from past campaigns. Crucially it gates shipped recipes with correctness checks, including configuration screening for objective-changing settings and convergence checks on loss curves, addressing the silent-training-change failure of naive automated tuners. This targets a painful operational cost in large-scale LLM training.

entry.title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems

author.name: Marc K. Ickler, Andreas Hermann, Fred A. Hamprecht

entry.summary: The authors introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems that evaluates electrostatics analytically and learns kinetic and exchange-correlation energies with an equivariant network. It recovers Kohn-Sham ground states with density errors of 0.4% and energy errors of 0.25 mHa per atom, outperforming an equivalently sized interatomic potential.

entry.title: Towards Safe Autonomy for Computer Use

author.name: Dominik Seip, Bartol Markovinovi\'c, Matthias Hein

entry.summary: The paper tackles the problem that Computer Use Agents cannot rely on structured tool boundaries for information-flow safety since they act visually on screens where trusted and attacker-controlled content are indistinguishable. It designs CUA architectures with information-flow guarantees, treating the user as the trust source and confirming sensitive decisions to guard against indirect prompt injection.

entry.title: Lumen-bench: Cross-Lingual Safety Gaps and the Say-Do Problem in Tool-Calling Large Language Models

author.name: Giovana Kerche Bon\'as, Thiago Laitz, Thales Sales Almeida, Jo\~ao Guilherme Alves Santos

entry.summary: Lumen-bench is a large behavioral benchmark of tool-calling ethics spanning 30 models, five languages, 108 Portuguese-authored scenarios, six social-pressure conditions, and 21 tools, totaling 194,400 trials. It reveals that once models have executable tools, their actions can diverge from stated refusals - a say-do gap invisible to English-only conversational safety evaluations. The work quantifies cross-lingual safety gaps in agentic settings with a calibrated reasoning-model judge.

entry.title: RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution

author.name: Fan Zhang, Hao Wu, Jinyang Wu, Hongyu Qu, Zheng Lian, Xiao Luo, Yefeng Zheng, Bo Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: RSIPO is a self-evolving agentic RL framework that jointly evolves agentic skills and the policy while addressing reliability of teacher supervision in RLVR plus on-policy self-distillation setups. It targets improved credit assignment and supervision quality in long-horizon tasks where prior teacher-conditioned methods overlook skill evolution.

entry.title: The Curse of Knowledge in Role-Playing Language Models

author.name: Xiao Zhang

entry.summary: Using 480 scenes with counterfactual twin controls, the authors show that role-playing LLM characters leak information the character could not have perceived, at 67-72 percentage points above guessing baselines across 11 open-weight models. Five of six proprietary models rarely leak, revealing a gap between open and closed models in respecting information boundaries.

entry.title: Prompt-Injection Probes Learn the Conversation, Not Just the Injection

author.name: Kaan Kale, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: The authors show that linear probes used to detect indirect prompt injection in agent tool outputs can pass standard evaluation using only conversation position and text length, reaching 0.91-0.98 AUROC without detecting injections at all. Against matched negatives such as the same conversation without injection or harmlessly formatted injection-like text, standard probes flag most harmless cases. Adding matched negatives to training substantially improves specificity across six open models.

entry.title: MemForm: Benchmarking Memory Formation Poisoning in LLM Agents

author.name: Haowen Pan, Pengyang Shao, Yunshan Ma, Yanzheng Jin, Naixin Zhai, Xiang Wang, Xun Yang

entry.summary: MemForm formulates memory formation poisoning as adversarial manipulation of the interfaces through which persistent agent memory is produced, introducing a diagnostic benchmark covering five interfaces including novel Selection and Path Poisoning categories that isolate retention and consolidation-order effects. This systematizes an underexplored attack surface for long-term-memory LLM agents. It matters as agents with persistent memory become widely deployed.

entry.title: ATTCK-R: Knowledge-Aware Long-Horizon Jailbreaking for Protected LLMs

author.name: Md Mushfiqur Rahman, Tobias Rohde, Rahul Tripathi, Khalil Elkhalil, Kevin Lybarger

entry.summary: Presents ATTCK-R, an adaptive multi-turn jailbreaking method targeting LLMs protected by prompt-based safety layers, showing such protections cut a strong baseline attack success rate from 0.896 to 0.608. The framework uses traceback and tactic curation to evaluate robustness under realistic protected deployments.

entry.title: We Have Been Interpreting Diffusion Transformer Backbone Behaviors Wrong

author.name: Benyuan Meng, Longtao Huang, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: This paper challenges the standard interpretation of the inverted-U-shaped depth profile of activation quality in diffusion transformers, arguing that the conventional coarse-to-fine granularity explanation lacks evidence. It re-examines the assumptions behind widely adopted techniques like REPA and offers a corrected characterization of DiT backbone behavior.

entry.title: TempoKV: Predictive KV Cache Quantization for Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Jiahui Hu, Weile Mo, Peiliang Cai, Jiacheng Liu, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Xiaobing Tu, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: TempoKV is a training-free framework that quantizes the growing KV cache of autoregressive video diffusion models by exploiting temporal predictability. It observes an asymmetry where keys are predictable from temporal history while values need only a short history, enabling aggressive cache compression for long video streaming generation.

entry.title: Totem: Object-Centric 3D Memory for World-Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Zichen Wan, Tianyu Huang, Fan Li, Kai Wang, Hongzhi Zhang, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: Totem introduces persistent object-centric 3D memories aligned to a shared world frame for world-consistent video generation, with a dual-stream conditioning architecture combining object memories and scene geometry for target-view synthesis. The 3D structural constraints on attention preserve object identity and stability under large viewpoint changes.

entry.title: RAR: Rate-Adaptive Rollout for Time-Consistent Interactive World Models

author.name: Yaoyang Liu, Dongyu Yan, Yihua Du, Shengju Qian, Zeke Xie, Xin Wang, Ying-Cong Chen, Long Chen

entry.summary: Identifies temporal-rate coupling as a key limitation of interactive video world models, where fixed learned temporal rates cause worlds to evolve at incorrect speeds when runtime throughput differs and trade temporal granularity against physical horizon. RAR enables rate-adaptive rollout so world models remain time-consistent across generation rates while extending coverage.

entry.title: CineRecon: Benchmarking Frontier Models for Agentic Cinematic Reconstruction

author.name: Jialei Wang, Zehan Wang, XiaoYang Wu, Ziang Zhang, Siyu Chen, Jiaer Huang, Yujia Zhang, Tianyu Pang, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: CineRecon is a benchmark of 50 reference videos and 360 annotated clips evaluating how well agents can reconstruct editable dynamic 3D scenes from video for controllable filmmaking, under Proxy, Simplified, and Detailed representation settings. Agents must use tools to construct, animate, render, and refine their reconstructions across film, real-world, and game footage.

entry.title: MaskSense: Confronting the Visual Exploration Trap in Masked Image Generation

author.name: Yawen Shao, Jie Xiao, Kai Zhu, Yu Liu, Hongchen Luo, Xueyang Fu, Yang Cao, Wei Zhai, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: The paper identifies a structural decoding bias in masked generative models, termed the visual exploration trap, where confidence-based sampling greedily resolves low-uncertainty background regions and collapses the exploration space needed for effective GRPO-based reinforcement learning. The authors propose a solution to restore exploration diversity so RL fine-tuning can align masked image generators with human intent.

entry.title: MicroCLIP: Connecting Text and Microscopy Images via Contrastive Language--Image Pretraining

author.name: Yanran Ruan, Zhixiang Wei, Shiyao Hong, Xiaoxiao Ma, Yuxuan Gu, Liming Ye, Huaian Chen, Yi Jin

entry.summary: MicroCLIP is a vision-language model for fluorescence microscopy that learns open-set cellular and subcellular representations from natural language supervision, enabled by MicroPool-2M, a new dataset of about 2.5 million microscopy image-text pairs. It supports generalizable classification and retrieval across biological contexts and imaging conditions.

entry.title: CityCode: Building Agent-Operable 3D Cities from Sparse Aerial Observations

author.name: Jiahui Sun, Ran Bi, Yifei Liu, Xiaolong Zhou, Yishuo Xu, Yuanqi Li, Congcong Zhu, Lei Yang, Yanwen Guo, Zhihang Zhong, Hongjie Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates a new task of generating large-scale, instance-level parameterized 3D cities from a single low-altitude aerial RGB image per region, recovering metrically scaled buildings and explicit road connectivity. CityCode represents cities as persistent, code-based states that agents can measure, interpret, and incrementally update without repeated dense reconstruction. Positioned for grounded urban world models and agentic simulation.

entry.title: Hand2Robot: Object-Centric 4D Hand Reconstruction from Human Demonstrations for Robotics

author.name: Zetao Du, Weiqing Wang, Hanbing Zhang, Yimiao Zhou, Ye Shi, Liang Wang, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: Hand2Robot converts human demonstration videos into robot action supervision via object-centric 4D hand reconstruction, combining object geometry estimation, hand-object interaction optimization, and motion retargeting. It addresses the key limitation that reconstructed hand motion alone is not physically consistent with object interaction. This provides a scalable path to robot policy post-training without robot-collected demonstrations.

entry.title: DexNinja: Learning Robust Dexterous Cutting Policy with a Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Engine

author.name: Haozhe Lou, Runyi Yang, Wanqi Zhong, Caiyun Liu, Yicheng Liu, Wenhao Liu, Wenlong Ma, Jiawei Xia, Kanzhi Wu, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool, Hang Zhao, Yiming Li

entry.summary: DexNinja tackles dexterous robotic cutting of deformable elasto-plastic food objects, where real data collection is destructive and sim-to-real gaps are severe for topology-changing interactions. It builds a real-to-sim-to-real data engine that reconstructs realistic simulation scenarios from real food samples to train robust cutting policies. This addresses one of the hardest classes of contact-rich manipulation problems.

entry.title: Terrain Traversal Without Motion Priors: Expert-Routed Humanoid Locomotion at Deployment Fidelity

author.name: Thanh Ly, Chien Le, Truong-Duy Dang, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Duy-Dung Le, Vien Anh Ngo, An T. Le

entry.summary: The paper presents a complete humanoid locomotion system that crosses varied terrain without the standard pipeline of retargeted motion capture, generative motion priors, and distillation, instead using a five-expert mixture routed by a terrain classifier with a model-based foothold planner. In a deployment-fidelity simulation, the system completes an 85-meter five-segment course 18 of 20 times end-to-end.

entry.title: Push the Limit: Learning High-Speed Sprinting and Aggressive Cornering on a Full-Scale Humanoid

author.name: Huaxing Huang, Ruidong Li, Jinchao Han, Ziyang Dong, Wenhao Cui

entry.summary: This work presents a learning framework enabling a full-scale bipedal humanoid to sprint above 7 m/s with motion-prior-guided gait and corner aggressively with up to 25 degrees of trunk lean. It solves challenges including high-frequency yaw-rate oscillations above 4 m/s that corrupt proprioceptive history and defeat conventional yaw-tracking rewards, plus skill-specific style priors. This represents a significant advance in dynamic humanoid locomotion.

entry.title: PINT: A Unified Model with Shared Predictive Intent for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xinyu Guo, Chao Jing, Li Yi, Xingyu Chen, Zhengxing Wu

entry.summary: PINT is a unified robot manipulation model that combines a vision-language model for semantic reasoning, a video generation model for world modeling, and an action expert, coordinated through learnable chunk-level Intent Tokens inserted into the VLM sequence. Rather than fusing the experts with shared attention at every layer, PINT preserves expert-specific pathways while conditioning all modules on the shared predictive intent. This architecture aims to get the best of pretrained semantic and dynamics knowledge without degrading either.

entry.title: Towards a Systematic Study of Embodied System 2 over Full Task Execution Cycles

author.name: Yuxi Wei, Ye Fang, Shuai Yang, Tong Wu, Tai Wang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: The authors introduce SCOPER, a benchmark suite for evaluating observation-grounded planning, execution, and recovery in embodied agents, combining high-level goals, ongoing visual observations, a shared rule-based System 1 executor, and controlled execution failures. SCOPER-bench contains 870 tasks across BEHAVIOR and ProcTHOR with roughly 3,500 supporting situations, addressing gaps in both open-loop and idealized closed-loop evaluation.

entry.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics

author.name: Gennady Sidorov, Valerii Kornilov, Denis Grankin, Polina Fedotova, Aleksey Postnikov

entry.summary: GreenWAM is a world foundation model intended to serve both action prediction and world-modeling roles across 20 robot families via a shared anatomical action space in common joint coordinates, joint training in visual, action-conditioned, and world-action modes, and policies that split an action expert off the generator. It asks what makes a single world model transferable across embodiments and roles.

entry.title: How artificial neural networks build their own learning machinery

author.name: Jennifer Michalowski | McGovern Institute for Brain Research

entry.summary: MIT McGovern Institute researchers, publishing in PNAS, show that randomly connected neural network units can self-organize into effective information-processing networks when given only simple instructions about how and when connections should change. They argue that a network's capacity for self-organization without developer guidance is a key metric of biological plausibility for learning models, with implications for understanding how the brain builds its own learning machinery.

entry.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

author.name: Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Han Yu, Rujun Han, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: Harness^2 is a plug-and-play framework for recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses in open-world settings, addressing the lack of ground-truth verifiers and poor generalization of task-specific harness edits. It uses two levels of recursion to refine harnesses at task level while transferring improvements to novel scenarios.

entry.title: Can You Trust Your Preference Models? Stackelberg Games for Alignment

author.name: Riccardo Formenti, Aditya Agrawal, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: Trains policies to search for preference comparisons on which an evaluator may reverse the underlying preference, using disagreement among an ensemble of preference models as a proxy for error during policy training. The search is formulated as a zero-sum Stackelberg game between a Leader and Follower policy, with equilibrium existence, uniqueness, and algorithmic results for a general class of contextual games.

entry.title: Scalable Robust MCTS with Anytime Deterministic Optimality Guarantees

author.name: Tomer Massas, Vadim Indelman

entry.summary: This paper derives the first deterministic anytime guarantees for robust online MDP planning with MCTS under model uncertainty. By bounding contributions of unsampled trajectories, it provides lower and upper bounds on policy value while restricting computation to the sampled search tree.

entry.title: Passing Tests, Missing Semantics: Evidence of Interpretive Lock-In in Plan-Based DataFrame Code Generation

author.name: Jingjing (May), Liu, Dishu Yang, Hongbo Qin, Hansong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper documents interpretive lock-in, where a mistaken task interpretation persists across planning, implementation, and tests in code generation. On 30 TPC-DS-derived DataFrame tasks, test-pass counts rose to 30/30 with revision methods, yet no solution matched stored reference outputs, while evaluator controls and SQL re-execution validated the references. This is a striking caution about relying on test-pass rates as a correctness proxy.

entry.title: World Models Need a Physical Registry: Learning Internal Predictive States for Physically Plausible World Models

author.name: Shinseong Kim, Jaeseok Jeong, Jianlong Fu, Youngjung Uh

entry.summary: Proposes the Physical Registry: dedicated, temporally grounded slots inside a video diffusion transformer that are initialized from observation-conditioned forecasts, co-evolve with video tokens, and receive future-representation supervision. This makes predictive dynamics an explicit, readable state inside the generator, improving physical plausibility of generated futures.

entry.title: AuthGateBench: Benchmarking LLMs as Authorization Gate

author.name: Zhixiong Zhuang, Jin Jia, Zhiwei Shang, Ziyu Wang

entry.summary: Introduces AuthGateBench, the first policy-guided benchmark for evaluating LLMs as authorization gates over high-risk agent actions under benign requests, targeting failure modes like scope escalation beyond user authorization. Its pipeline generates contrast pairs with identical actions and trajectories but differing requests, flipping labels between blocks and approvals.

entry.title: Same Operation, Different Permission: Evaluating Whether Guardrails Honor Authorization

author.name: Huihao Jing, Shaojin Chen, Wenbin Hu, Yuxuan Liu, Haochen Shi, Zhongwei Xie, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark testing whether LLM-agent guardrail decisions follow authorization, contrasting the same operation performed with and without valid permission using expert-annotated scenarios, executed verified operations, and native-policy requests. It checks each decision for correctness, usability, and resulting effect, addressing a central safety question as agents write code, move money, and change records.

entry.title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models

author.name: Hanbo Xie, Yue Zhao, Robert C. Wilson

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and diagnostic framework using repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicit recursive belief updates, separating adaptive play, action prediction, and true belief tracking (theory of mind) through controlled information interventions. Behavioral SFT improves play on some tests but the diagnostics reveal what LLMs actually track.

entry.title: A dataset of formalised theorem statements from the Annals of Mathematics

author.name: Thomas Browning, Katerina Hristova, David Ledvinka, Justus Springer, Hang Lu Su, Jack McKoen, Kevin Buzzard

entry.summary: AnnalsChallenge is a dataset of 50 hand-written Lean 4 formalizations (using Mathlib) of main results from Annals of Mathematics papers since 2020, each manually reviewed and audited by AI, released without proofs. It provides hard, trustworthy formal statements for measuring progress in AI autoformalization of mathematics. The involvement of Kevin Buzzard's formalization group lends strong domain credibility.

entry.title: Lost in Implicit Routing: How LLM Agents Fail to Load Relevant Skills at Scale

author.name: Jinlin Liu, Wei Chen, Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: The authors show skill routing collapse: as irrelevant skills are added to an agent's library, implicit routing over skill metadata degrades sharply, with recall falling from 73.6% to 27.4% at 1,000 distractor skills and zero-load rates rising above 50%, while explicit selection retains performance. Masking irrelevant skill descriptions mitigates the collapse.

entry.title: Posterior Flow Matching

author.name: Chenrui Ma, Xi Xiao, Lin Zhao, Xinru Jiang, Tianyang Wang, Yanning Shen, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: Posterior Flow Matching augments flow matching with a Gaussian posterior model that learns conditional velocity means and componentwise variances, providing endpoint uncertainty throughout generation. The learned moments support both a mean-driven ODE and an uncertainty-adaptive posterior-driven SDE, validated across images, point clouds, and molecules.

entry.title: Pick the Mixture, Not the Samples: Combinatorial Data Selection for LLMs

author.name: Luyang Zhang, Jialu Wang, Bebei Li

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Combinatorial Data Selection (CDS), a framework that separates attribution from subset selection and models non-additive interactions among training samples. Experiments on instruction-tuning pools reveal substantial cross-domain complementarity and redundancy, motivating mixture-level rather than sample-level selection.

entry.title: DexFLEX: Contact-Aware Foundation Controller for Command-Guided Dexterity

author.name: Weikang Wan, Zeyu Lai, Jianyu Hou, Yuchen Zhou, Jiawei Fu, Henrik I Christensen, Hao Su

entry.summary: DexFLEX is a contact-aware foundation controller that converts upstream fingertip-motion drafts (from teleoperation or learned policies) into contact-consistent joint commands by treating drafts as evidence of intent. It proposes feasible short-horizon motion chunks from tactile-proprioceptive state, predicts their contact consequences, and selects the candidate best following the command while preserving future contact stability, via a Draft-Dream-Select procedure. This fills the gap between motion intent and successful contact-rich execution.

entry.title: Sequent-Prover: Training Agents for Formal, Checkable SMT-based Reasoning

author.name: Debargha Ganguly, Weicong Chen, Mohsen Hariri, Vikash Singh, Sreehari Sankar, Shouren Wang, Wang Yang, Biyao Zhang, Chaoda Song, Alexander Nemecek, Kai Ye, Osama Zafar, Erman Ayday, Joe Stubbs, Srinivasan Iyengar, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: Presents Sequent-Prover, a family of language-model agents that reason in an executable SMT-LIB scratchpad, querying the Z3 solver across turns and repairing formalizations based on solver feedback. The post-training recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, bootstraps successful multi-turn trajectories from a noisy teacher, followed by SFT and trajectory-level preference optimization, with evaluation beyond solver success to check semantic faithfulness.

entry.title: SLDBench v2: Active Scaling Law Discovery

author.name: Lingbei Meng, Rui Huang, Zhirong Shen, Jinxin Liu, Lingxiao Jing, Haorui Chen, Yaosong Du, Haowei Lin

entry.summary: SLDBench v2 tests whether language-model agents can discover scaling laws, expanding to 127 scenarios and introducing active discovery where the agent chooses which costly experiments to run under a compute budget, with challenging scenarios representing over 10^23 FLOPs of source compute. It moves beyond static law-fitting to sequential experiment design.

entry.title: Force-Modulated Dexterity: Unified Compliance for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Ying Yuan, David Held, Jitendra Malik, Haozhi Qi

entry.summary: FOMO-Dex introduces a unified compliance formulation for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, expressing nominal actions in task-geometry coordinates and applying force-driven corrections along selected directions. It addresses the problem that teleoperated demonstrations capture motion well but not subtle human force adjustments. The approach is demonstrated across card picking, paper cutting, screwdriving, and nut-and-bolt assembly tasks.

entry.title: CoCA: Criterion-Aware Credit Assignment for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guangcheng Zhu, Yingfan Ma, Xing Zheng, Haobo Wang, Shenzhi Yang, Kai Tang, Zhengqing Zang, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: CoCA reframes rubric-based RL for LLMs as criterion-aware credit assignment, using rubrics as relevance cues rather than compressing criterion feedback into scalar rewards. This keeps the learning signal grounded in criterion outcomes and avoids reward degradation seen in self-distillation approaches.

entry.title: Correcting or Continuing? What On-Policy Distillation Learns from Student Errors

author.name: Shuo Yang, Zheyu Zhang, Mahito Sugiyama, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: This paper asks whether on-policy distillation can improve student models when training is restricted to problems they currently fail, evaluating five OPD mechanisms with Qwen-3 and Phi-4 under a competition-math protocol. It finds OPD fails to improve accuracy on this hard subset, with all eight configurations degrading performance despite decreasing training KL divergence, while the same pipeline improves performance on solvable problems. This is an important negative result clarifying the limits of a popular training technique.

entry.title: A CaLLM Judge is a Better Judge: Mitigating Bias in LLM-as-a-judge

author.name: Cesare Barbera, Luca Stradiotti, Lorenzo Cascioli, Lorenzo Perini, Niek Tax, Daniel Haimovich, Jesse Davis, Andrea Passerini, Andrea Pugnana

entry.summary: The paper frames systematic biases in LLM-as-a-judge (position, verbosity, family bias) as miscalibration on identifiable groups and applies multicalibration to correct them. This provides a principled statistical framework for making LLM judges more reliable proxies for human preference.

entry.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards

author.name: Yunkai Zhan, Miaosen Chai, Shangshang Wang, Jike Zhong, Yuqing Yang, Deqing Fu, Serina Chang, Wang Bill Zhu

entry.summary: PreciseCoder analyzes how unit-test-only RL rewards teach code models to over-edit and hallucinate bugs in correct code, and augments the reward with a signal for semantically verified localized edits. Across 4B-27B models it cuts average edit size from 7-15 lines to 3 at comparable pass rates, and generalizes beyond single-line bug training.

entry.title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention

author.name: Fanxu Meng, Taosong Fang

entry.summary: DoSA makes the indexer computation in sparse attention conditional: using a seed-set lower bound on the winning threshold plus nonnegative head projections and residual bounds, it certifies which candidates still need full scoring, preserving exact Top-K token selection. The result is lossless sparse attention that avoids scoring every key with every indexer head. Exact-score filtering further reduces writeback.

entry.title: Mixture of GFlowNets

author.name: Omar G. Younis, Joseph D. Viviano, Chirayu Anant Haryan, MD Vasimuddin, Sanchit Misra, Yoshua Bengio

entry.summary: This paper addresses mode collapse and mode bias in GFlowNets by training a population of asynchronously trained policies that partition the state space among themselves, rather than scaling a single policy. The mixture approach avoids the saturation of larger batches, which merely rediscover known high-reward modes.

entry.title: Scaling Online Optimal Transport Minibatches for Flow Matching

author.name: Peter Chen, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Authored by Peter Chen and Sergey Levine, this paper tackles scaling minibatch optimal transport couplings for flow matching to larger batches without prohibitive per-iteration cost, while providing theoretical analysis of how OT coupling affects the full stochastic gradient and integration stability. It addresses a key bottleneck for training flow models on large, high-dimensional data.

entry.title: SPROUT: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Software Engineering

author.name: Mengyang Liu, Weiming Wang, Haixin Nan, Yu Wu, Peize Li, Shihong Huang, Xuning He, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong

entry.summary: SPROUT (SnaPshot-based RollOUT) is an agentic RL rollout framework that scales long-horizon coding tasks by resuming from snapshots of both agent context and execution environment state, avoiding costly restarts from scratch. It addresses the scarcity of verified successful trajectories in long-horizon software engineering where one error invalidates an entire rollout.

entry.title: Pushback in a Haystack: Language Models Respond to Factual Errors Ambiguously and Ineffectively

author.name: Li Lucy, Myra Cheng, Svenja Guhr, Kabir Ahuja, Orevaoghene Ahia, Sameep Chattopadhyay, Yike Wang, Valentin Hofmann, Noah A. Smith, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: Introducing a phrase-level, human-validated labeling framework, the authors analyze how LMs push back against false user assertions in five languages, finding that pushback tends to be indirect and mixed with affirmation, with greater indirectness in Hindi and Yoruba. The work reframes sycophancy as a question of pushback effectiveness, not mere occurrence.

entry.title: Scenes as an Attack Surface: Uncovering Scene-Grounded Safety Failures in MLLMs

author.name: Tongxi Wu, Yuyang Cheng, Jiacheng Xian, Hu Huang, Zhihao Wu, Menglin Yang, Jian Zhang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Identifies a new multimodal jailbreak vulnerability: task-relevant scene semantics alone can shift MLLMs from refusal to compliance without any added attack instructions in the visual input. The authors formalize scene-grounded visual safety failures and release SceneSafetyBench spanning eight risk categories across nine white- and black-box models.

entry.title: Esports World Model Dataset

author.name: Weiyu Ma, Zeyuan Gong, Xuhui Liu, Wenxuan Zhang, Jian Ding, Xinyu Cui, Jian Zhao, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: The Esports World Model Dataset (EWM) provides human gameplay data spanning StarCraft II, Dota 2, and Counter-Strike 2, with 3,053 games and maps and roughly 4,880 player-view hours, connecting individual observations and actions to shared state and events under fog of war and differing viewpoints. It targets interactive world models that must capture multi-agent competition and partial observability.

entry.title: AReA: Adaptive Receptive-Field Attention for Efficient High-Resolution Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Javad Rajabi, Koorosh Roohi, David B. Lindell, Babak Taati

entry.summary: AReA is a training-free attention mechanism for diffusion transformers that adapts the attention receptive field across denoising steps, exploiting the observation that attention is global early (structure formation) and local later (detail refinement). This avoids the quadratic cost and out-of-distribution token distances of uniform full attention when generating beyond training resolution.

entry.title: Diagnose-to-Generate: Eliminating Structural Distortions in Flow Models via Patch-Level Grounded Alignment

author.name: Yifan Li, Lishuai Gao, Tong Zhang, Qilong Huang, Chen Zhao, Zhuoliang Kang, Jie Hu, Yujie Zhong, Fenghe Tang, S Kevin Zhou, Xiaoming Wei

entry.summary: D2G is a grounded alignment framework for flow-based image generators that separates visual diagnosis from generative optimization, using region-annotated data (Achilles-600K) and a detector (ARGUS) trained with region-aware GRPO to localize structural anomalies and guide patch-level fixes. It targets localized defects like malformed hands that global scalar rewards handle poorly.

entry.title: PILOT: Guiding Long-Horizon World-Model Planning for Robot Manipulation with Visual Subgoals and Policy Priors

author.name: Yang Liu, Hanchen Cui, Karthik Desingh

entry.summary: PILOT improves long-horizon latent world-model planning for manipulation by using a video model to generate intermediate visual subgoals and a learned policy to initialize cross-entropy method action sampling, refined in a receding-horizon loop with an action-conditioned world model. Real-robot evaluations across four tasks show improved long-horizon manipulation performance.

entry.title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science

author.name: Xue Li, Hongqian Xia, Daniel Gomm, A\'ecio Santos, Cornelius Wolff, Madelon Hulsebos

entry.summary: This paper argues that current evaluations of data science agents focus on predictive performance and code correctness while missing methodological failures like data leakage and inappropriate validation. It highlights how such silent failures undermine the reliability of agentic data science systems.

entry.title: Measuring the Inference Energy Efficiency of Open-Weight LLMs across Benchmarks, Reasoning Modes, and Hardware

author.name: Zeyu Yang, Wes Armour

entry.summary: The authors directly measure the capability-energy trade-off for 86 open-weight model checkpoints across seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms, finding most configurations use 2.6-4.8x more energy than a Pareto-equivalent alternative, with gaps up to 27x. Enabling reasoning increases energy use about 3.7x on average, with benefits varying strongly by model family.

entry.title: FDE-Bench: Evaluating End-to-End Delivery from Underspecified Real-World Business Requests

author.name: Huaiming Li, Can Huang, Chufan Wu, Danyu Liu, Xiaomin Yuan, Qinze Li, Yui Lo, Wenhui Bai, Qianlong Wang, Zengle Ge, Xiyu Yan, Yuheng Cheng, Jinhui Ren, Guokai Chen, Jiaqun Liu, Haoran Li, Qianhui Liu, Annan Li, Jianmin Wu, Dawei Yin, Dou Shen

entry.summary: FDE-Bench is the first benchmark built from real customer projects evaluating agents on end-to-end delivery, including interactive requirement clarification and iterative optimization, across 49 combinatorial optimization and machine learning cases. Unlike existing benchmarks, it starts from underspecified requests rather than explicit objectives or artificial information gaps.

entry.title: GateSight: Recurrent Memory Anticipates Attention Memory for Query-Agnostic KV Eviction in Hybrid LLMs

author.name: Junjie Li, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: This paper studies hybrid language models that interleave fixed-size recurrent memory layers (Gated DeltaNet) with full-attention layers, and shows that the recurrent layers' write gates and decay signals can predict which KV cache entries attention will need before any query is seen. Using Qwen3.8-27B as a testbed, the authors derive query-agnostic KV eviction rules that could reduce serving memory without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: RECAP: Calibrating Low-Bit Reasoning Models on the History They Read

author.name: Chi Ruan, Yujie Chen, Zixiang Zhao, Jingcai Guo, Haotong Qin

entry.summary: RECAP is a post-training quantization method that calibrates reasoning models on long historical context rather than short segments, addressing error accumulation in long chains of thought. Dynamic-prefix calibration separates long prefix context from short-block reconstruction to better model how quantization errors affect downstream attention.

entry.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Advancing Harmful Content Understanding via Perception-Aware Adversarial Self-Play

author.name: Yisong Xiao, Benlei Cui, Shiji Zhao, Zonghao Ying, Yaoyuan Zhang, Longtao Huang, Aishan Liu, Hui Xue, Ting Ma, Haiwen Hong, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: PASP targets LLMs' failure to detect deliberately obfuscated harmful content that humans readily decode, bridging the cognitive asymmetry between human multimodal inference and text-only LLM processing. It uses perception-aware adversarial self-play to generate evasive harmful content and train more robust moderation.

entry.title: Radioactive Feedback: Tracing Models Trained by Label-Only LLM Supervision

author.name: Yuejia Li, JunHeng Li, Hao Wu, Ke He, Mang Ye

entry.summary: The paper introduces Radioactive Feedback, a method for detecting whether a student model was trained using label-only LLM-as-a-Judge distillation, where the student improves from scalar scores without any teacher-generated text. Existing watermarks and distillation detectors do not cover this score-only channel, so the authors encode evaluator-specific traces through the low-bandwidth reward signal. This addresses a timely provenance problem as judge-based distillation grows in practice.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Agentic Coevolution

author.name: Wenqian Ye, Ziwei Guan, Zi Yang, Shivani Modi, Cici Cong Wu, Yunlong He, Yuxin Chen, Zhengyu Zhang, Liang Luo, Venkatesh Ranganathan, Jianhui Sun, Yantao Yao, Wenlin Chen, Buyun Zhang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: HACE proposes a framework for recursive self-improvement in domain-specific foundation models by jointly evolving specialist models and LLM agents through reciprocal learning: supervised learning improves the specialist while on-policy reinforced learning trains the agent that proposes improvements. This addresses the challenge that improvement strategies must adapt as a specialist model advances.

entry.title: REVEAL: Reverse Engineering Agentic Latents from Frontier-Model Traces

author.name: Yuetian Du, Meng Wang, Yucheng Wang, Zhangzhe Chen, Wei Wang, Boyu Yang, Weiqi Zhai, Bing Zhao, Ming Kong, Zhan Zhou, Jie Liu, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces REVEAL, a training-free framework that extracts reusable controls from textual traces of frontier LLM agents and transfers them to smaller frozen open-source agents. It uses anchored states and dynamic profiles of feedback-response cycles elicited by replay in the target model, avoiding the need for source-model internals or target-model training.

entry.title: EvoWeb: A Benchmark for Coding Agents on Evolving Web Applications

author.name: David Nukrai, Bar Alon, Nativ Levy, Ido Andrew Atad, Ido Cohen, Itamar Zimerman, Lior Wolf, Eli David, Ilan Naiman

entry.summary: Introduces EvoWeb, a benchmark of 320 cumulative requests over 32 real-world-grounded web applications where coding agents iteratively modify a persistent codebase. A multimodal web agent tests each intermediate app in a live browser, evaluating new functionality, cross-request integration, and preservation of prior functionality, with trajectory-based reliability metrics.

entry.title: Game-Creation-Agents: Autonomous Game Production

author.name: Tencent Multimodal RL Team, Xiangxin Zhou, Jiaqi Tang, Ke Ma, Wenhao Yang, Jiarui Yao, Boye Niu, Haiyang Guo, Yifei Zhao, Huanjin Yao, Pu Jian, Ruihuang Li, Haitao Wu, Yushi Huang, Xiangyan Liu, Yan Sun, Kaixin Li, Tianyu Pang

entry.summary: Presents Game-Creation-Agents (GCA), a multi-agent pipeline from Tencent that turns a natural-language request into a runnable Phaser 4 browser game. It builds a multimodal design document, projects it into machine-readable contracts and deterministic tests, runs eight specialized agents for scenes and assets, and uses build-linked UI checks plus a code-blind critic to decide whether the game ships, with bounded repair loops.

entry.title: Size Generalization for Diffusion Routing Solvers

author.name: Barak Itzchak Davidovitch, Eli Meirom, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik

entry.summary: Proposes ResizeCO, a label-free approach for size generalization in diffusion-based combinatorial routing solvers, using reinforcement learning on large unlabeled instances to adapt a diffusion model trained on smaller optimal solutions. It addresses both distribution shift in instance statistics and computational challenges of large instances.

entry.title: PhysCodeGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Physically Verifiable 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Shuai Shao, Jinchen He, Cunxin Fan, Zihan Guo, Shijian Wang, Qihan Ren, Kangning Zhang, Zunnan Xu, Haoyuan Li, Hao Wang, Jianghao Lin, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces PhysCodeGym, a benchmark of 156 tasks where coding agents build physically verifiable 4D reconstructions from video by writing and iterating on Blender programs with simulation feedback. Six metrics combine rule-based and rubric-based judgments, including counterfactual interventions testing physical consistency, revealing tradeoffs in frontier coding agents.

entry.title: Budgeted KV-Cache Repair for Evolving Contexts

author.name: Han Yu, Wenhui Zhu, Jincheng Cao, Rui Cai, Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Xiwen Chen, Hao Wang, Xuanzhao Dong, Han Shi, Menglin Zhou, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Lin Su, Mina Razghandi, Sayan Ghosh, Qing Lan, Rohit Jain, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem that deleted context in LLM agents still influences cached KV states, and full recomputation of the retained suffix is expensive. It proposes budgeted KV-cache repair, recomputing only a user-chosen fraction of the suffix, and introduces Semantic-Unit Refresh (SUR), which allocates the repair budget to coherent, query-relevant text regions using cheap embedding scores rather than isolated tokens. The finding that refreshing coherent regions outperforms refreshing individual tokens is a practical insight for efficient agent context management.

entry.title: Upstream Influence, Downstream Re-Anchoring in LLM Agent Chains

author.name: Chun-Yu Hsu, Lun-Wei Ku, Chung-Chi Chen

entry.summary: This study shows that the information architecture of multi-agent LLM workflows — source access, handoff format, and which model reads untrusted content — governs how much coordinated manipulation reaches the end user. Using 32 Taiwan 2025 recall cases, it finds that downstream agents re-anchor and dissipate more than half of an upstream stance shift by the third agent, and that repeated exposure to untrusted content sustains manipulation.

entry.title: SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces

author.name: Harshit Joshi, Priyank Shethia, Monica S. Lam

entry.summary: SHELDON is a scientific reasoning harness for LLMs that separately represents and jointly explores hypothesis and observation spaces, inspired by the hypothetico-deductive method and dual-space models of discovery. This decouples observation gathering from existing hypotheses, enabling broader exploration beyond local refinements. The work addresses a known weakness in test-time scaling approaches for complex reasoning and discovery tasks.

entry.title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery

author.name: Yibo Wen, Han Liu

entry.summary: Autonomous Science Bench provides six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns grounded in published biology, chemistry, and materials science experiments, where agents select experiment batches, receive real lab measurements, and must pass calibrated discovery and learning gates. It addresses the gap between fixed-dataset benchmarks and purely simulated active experimentation.

entry.title: To Align or Not To Align: Check Your COMPASS Before You Train

author.name: Fabian Gr\"oger, Petar Damjanovi\'c, Maria Brbi\'c

entry.summary: COMPASS is a theoretically motivated diagnostic that predicts whether two pretrained models (e.g., a vision encoder and an LLM) will be compatible before costly alignment or merging, based on k-NN overlap between encoders plus a pair-specific ease axis and a complementary factor. This replaces expensive empirical compatibility search with cheap pre-assessment.

entry.title: Dependency, Compression, and Synergy: A Unified Information-Theoretic View of Multimodal Learning

author.name: Liangjian Wen, Linjie Li, Jiang Duan, Yong Dai, Jianzhuang Liu, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: This survey unifies mutual information, the information bottleneck, and partial information decomposition as progressively refined views of multimodal information processing, covering dependency, task-oriented compression, and redundancy-uniqueness-synergy decomposition. It reviews roughly 170 studies from 2018 to 2026 and connects the frameworks to multimodal foundation models.

entry.title: Splicing Hints into Reasoning Traces: Learning from Demonstrator Failures

author.name: Hamed Mahdavi (Pennsylvania State University), Pouria Mahdavinia (Pennsylvania State University), Majid Farhadi (Google), Vasant Honavar (Pennsylvania State University)

entry.summary: SPLICE is an offline workflow in which a second model edits a reasoning model's traces during generation, verifying progress and truncating failed traces at the last verified step, splicing in reference-solution guidance. This avoids the RL-verifier bootstrapping problem where a policy must already produce occasional correct attempts at olympiad level.

entry.title: Showing versus Doing: Teaching by Demonstration

author.name: Mark K. Ho, Michael L. Littman, James MacGlashan, Fiery Cushman, Joseph L. Austerweil

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian model of teaching by demonstration, distinguishing between intentionally teaching (showing) a task versus merely performing (doing) it. Two human experiments confirm that demonstrators modify their behavior when teaching, and that standard inverse reinforcement learning algorithms benefit when learning from teaching-style demonstrations.

entry.title: One Model, Multiple Compute Budgets: Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE for Flexible Compute Across Turns

author.name: Yiyang Fu, Zihao Huang, Dongchen Han, Shukai Gong, Zhen Dong, Qiyang Min, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE is a single shared model that supports token-to-concept compression ratios of 2, 4, and 8, allowing flexible per-turn compute allocation in multi-turn interactions without rebuilding history states across model switches. Lightweight modules handle compression-independent costs and ratio-specific components.

entry.title: EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference

author.name: Anxhelo Diko, Jieyu Lin, Stefano Ambrogio, Ziyun Li, Mahmoud Assran, Th\'eo Moutakanni, Barbara De Salvo, Chiao Liu

entry.summary: EV-JEPA extends V-JEPA-style self-supervised vision models into a single elastic model trainable once and deployable across a heterogeneous edge-cloud continuum, with reconfigurable width and native partitionability for cross-device collaborative inference. It unifies width elasticity and split computing, which prior work addressed only one axis at a time. This is significant for deploying foundation models on smart glasses, phones, robots, and servers.

entry.title: What Counts as the Same Task? Executable Contracts for Robustness Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Shaikh Akib Shahriyar, MD. Akil Raihan Iftee, Armon Barton, Matthew Wright

entry.summary: The paper proposes executable task contracts that formally specify which facts define a task, which edits are allowed, and what task completion means, so that perturbed test cases for agent robustness evaluation can be validated before running. It compares validity rules by rescoring 14,336 stored agent runs.

entry.title: UltraBERT: Beyond the Limit of BERT Pre-Training

author.name: Jungwoo Park, Taewhoo Lee, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: This paper systematically revisits bidirectional encoder pretraining design choices, finding that encoders saturate on downstream tasks beyond a few trillion tokens, that lower masking ratios favor classification while higher ratios favor retrieval (contradicting prior recommendations), and pushing encoder performance across both task families. It aims to produce a single encoder competitive on classification and retrieval simultaneously.

entry.title: PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces

author.name: M. Yigit Turali, Shreyas Rajesh, M. Efe Lorasdagi, Chenda Duan, Kartik Sharma, Vwani Roychowdhury

entry.summary: PANINI-DR is a multi-agent deep research harness that separates investigation coordination from subquestion research and verification, maintaining research state in a shared Generative Semantic Workspace recording dependencies, findings, and evidence. A dedicated verification agent checks proposed answers before errors propagate to downstream steps.

entry.title: ZOIF: Zeroth-Order Influence Function Estimation for LLM Data Selection Using Only Forward Passes

author.name: Lisong He, Yunxuan Jiang, Haishan Ye, Xiangyu Chang

entry.summary: ZOIF is a zeroth-order framework for influence function estimation on LLMs that operates entirely via forward passes, avoiding both the intractable Hessian and the memory overhead of backpropagation. This enables principled, memory-efficient training data selection for model editing, debugging, and fine-tuning at LLM scale.

entry.title: CodeWalk: Generating Coding Benchmarks by Walking a Problem Graph

author.name: Jiaxin Fang, Runyuan He, Arnav Gupta, Sahil Kumawat, Huanzhi Mao, Alvin Cheung

entry.summary: This paper introduces a programmatic method for generating new coding benchmark problems by composing verified atomic problems into level-N tasks, keeping only compositions where every atomic problem remains unsolved and a joint reference solution passes evaluation checks. This avoids both expensive human curation (as in SWE-bench) and costly LLM-based generation and validation, and is demonstrated across four coding settings including multi-bug repair.

entry.title: Uncovering the Generative Landscape of Diffusion Models: A Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion Framework

author.name: Hannah Janmohamed, Joao Correia, Penousal Machado, Antoine Cully

entry.summary: The authors propose Quality-Diversity Diffusion, a framework combining quality-diversity optimization with diffusion models to uncover diverse, high-performing outputs rather than only high-likelihood samples. A spectral-guided variant extends the idea, with applications from molecular design to image synthesis. This addresses the known tendency of diffusion samplers to collapse onto likely modes.

entry.title: DiffNash: Finding Nash Equilibrium in High-Dimensional Continuous Action Spaces with Diffusion Policies

author.name: Haichuan Wang, Anagha Satish, Jiale Zheng, Saisneha Ghatti, Lingkai Kong, Kai Wang, Milind Tambe

entry.summary: DiffNash computes Nash equilibria in high-dimensional continuous games using diffusion policies, enabling diffusion-based variants of Online Mirror Descent and Fictitious Play. A reweighted score-matching objective trains diffusion policies without requiring direct samples from each iteratively updated policy. This addresses the difficulty conventional neural policies have representing multi-modal strategy distributions.

entry.title: When Agent Evaluation Becomes Unreliable: An Empirical Study of Oracle Failures and Configuration-Dependent Measurement in an LLM Agent Benchmark

author.name: Junjie Chen

entry.summary: This paper audits LLM agent benchmark harnesses for reliability defects invisible in score tables, introducing an oracle-integrity auditing method with five state-integrity invariants and three known-answer controls. Applying it to an agent benchmark reveals a reward-function defect that mutates environment state before scoring, materially changing results across 4,320 episodes.

entry.title: Fisher information and the geometry of memorization in neural networks

author.name: Daniel T. Bernstein, Chase Goddard, Luca Di Carlo, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab

entry.summary: This paper studies how Fisher information geometry separates generalizable structure from memorized noisy labels in vision models trained on CIFAR-10 with controlled learnable noise. It shows that projecting weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors decouples general task performance from noisy-sample memorization, with layer-wise differences, and that similar phenomena appear in language models.

entry.title: WorldRoPE: Probabilistic World-Centric Rotary Embedding for Multi-View Attention

author.name: Mijeong Kim, Kyujin Lim, Bohyung Han

entry.summary: WorldRoPE extends Rotary Positional Embeddings to multi-view attention by back-projecting patch tokens into volumetric Gaussian primitives in a shared world frame, capturing depth hypotheses and uncertainty. This enables meaningful cross-view correspondences that image-centric coordinates cannot provide.

entry.title: Before Attention Sinks Form: Hidden-State Geometry Reveals and Modulates Their Formation

author.name: Fan Yang, Yue Song

entry.summary: This mechanistic-interpretability study shows that a measurable hidden-state geometry change precedes attention sink formation, detectable via spectral summaries two to three layers before a sink appears, even when comparing prompts within the same model and layer. The authors also intervene on this geometry and modulate subsequent sink formation. It matters because attention sinks are usually studied only after formation, and predictive pre-sink signals could inform training and inference interventions.

entry.title: Logit Leakage through Floating-Point Bias Addition

author.name: Shaomin Chen, Xiaorui Gong

entry.summary: This paper identifies a numerical side channel in how language model APIs implement bias addition under binary32 floating-point arithmetic, allowing attackers to recover hidden logit information using only token identities and no access to logits or probabilities. The attack exploits representable spacing changes at binary exponent boundaries and can exactly recover a logit pair and tie-breaking priority in at most 52 token queries under stated assumptions.

entry.title: Davinci-Tool: Scaling Agentic Tool-Use Supervision with Verifiable Executable Environments

author.name: Xiaoyang Yuan, Ji Zhao, Xingyu Hu, Wenhan Wang, Yutao Hu, Qiaosheng Zhang, Pengfei Liu, Yu Qiao, Yi Bin, Wenqi Shao

entry.summary: Davinci-Tool is a 30B tool-use model trained with Davinci-ToolData, an execution-grounded dataset that jointly scales environment coverage and outcome verification by preserving restorable states, execution traces, outcomes, and verifiers as unified supervision, populated via complementary execution-grounded and synthetic pipelines. It matters because reliable agentic tool use requires verifiable multi-step trajectories, not just diverse workflows.

entry.title: AUGUstus: Autonomous Driving VLA Model with Unified Generation and Understanding

author.name: Yuqi Ye, Caigao Jiang, Zhuonan Wang, Congyuan Pei, Chao Qu, Changhao Peng, Junhong Lin, Qize Yu, Zetian Song, Guangzhao Fu, Chongruo Wu, Shiyu Huang, Shuchang Zhou, Honggou Yang, Wei Gao

entry.summary: AUGUstus is a vision-language-action model for end-to-end autonomous driving that combines the reasoning benefits of autoregressive chain-of-thought with low-latency action generation, avoiding degeneration into unsafe vision-action-only models. It unifies understanding and generation to reduce deployment latency while retaining VLM-driven reasoning. This addresses a core tension in deploying VLAs for safety-critical driving.

entry.title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation

author.name: Zekun Shi, Alastair James Arthur Price

entry.summary: FreeSolo is a native sparse attention mechanism combining a short-range sliding window branch with a long-range branch selecting keypoint cells for direct token attention, enabling linear-time processing and zero-shot length extrapolation beyond trained context. Its FS-L variant learns prefix pruning through brief continued pretraining while FS-B skips even that cost. This offers an alternative to quadratic full-attention hybrids and fixed-size recurrent states for long-context models.

entry.title: On the Statistical Mechanics of Attention

author.name: Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Yu-An Chen, Maojiang Su, Han Liu

entry.summary: Reformulates Transformer attention via modern Hopfield models using a free-energy formalism that incorporates randomness in queries and attention weights, showing attention emerges as the equation of motion of the statistical-mechanical system. The analysis identifies first-order phase transitions between glassy and robust-inference regimes and extends to stochastic queries and keys. This provides theoretical tools for predicting when attention inference is stable.

entry.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents

author.name: Jianghong Zhou, Hao Rong, Chen Lin, Daoan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes reasoning contraction, where agent memories, skill libraries, and thought templates compress many reasoning steps into one, and proves that success/failure counters used to trust these memories are poorly tuned change detectors. Empirically, ExpeL- and ACE-style counters serve 7-73x more stale answers than certified memories on edited-fact QA and code tasks, highlighting a real safety gap in agent memory systems.

entry.title: DeltaTTG: Training Multi-Turn Agents with a Token-to-Go Progress Meter

author.name: Xuyan Ye, Xiyan Fu, Shengda Fan, Jiawei Cui, Yankai Lin, Wei Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces DeltaTTG, a method for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) in multi-turn agents that addresses the problem of sparse terminal rewards. It learns a reusable progress signal from diverse policies' recorded trajectories, using Token-to-Go (TTG) — the number of tokens remaining until task completion — as an observable proxy for remaining completion effort, without needing task-specific progress rules or costly external evaluators. This matters because it offers a low-cost, generalizable way to shape dense rewards for multi-turn agent training.

entry.title: SkillScreen: High-Recall Screening of Malicious Agent Skills with Decision Models

author.name: Jerrold Huang, Junwei Quan, Saiyue Lyu, Zihan Guo, Yingqiang Ge

entry.summary: SkillScreen trains a compact decision model to score agent skills for maliciousness from SKILL.md files in a single forward pass, achieving 99 percent recall while flagging only 20-25 percent of benign skills on MaliciousSkillBench. It outperforms prompted LLM judges and word-level classifiers, though unfamiliar benign sources increase false positives.

entry.title: QK-Edit: Revisiting Attention-based Injection in MM-DiT for Image and Video Editing

author.name: Tiancheng Shen, Zilong Huang, Xiangtai Li, Zhijie Lin, Jiyang Liu, Yitong Wang, Jiashi Feng, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Jun Hao Liew

entry.summary: QK-Edit is a training-free framework for text-guided image and video editing in multimodal diffusion transformers, exploiting the attention dynamics of MM-DiT's concatenated image-text self-attention via a novel query-key manipulation strategy. It addresses the failure of U-Net-era attention injection methods in MM-DiT architectures.

entry.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge

author.name: Wayne Chi, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Anastasios Nikolas Angelopoulos, Ameet Talwalkar, Chris Donahue, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: This work proposes using computer-use agents as LLM judges that directly interact with generated applications like websites and games, rather than relying on code inspection or unit tests. It releases two datasets with human preferences and shows interaction-based judging improves both evaluation and generation of interactive applications.

entry.title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation

author.name: Yaoyang Liu, Shuwei Shen, Jincheng Tang, Jinguang Liu, Jinbao Xue, Hailong Yang, Ke Zhang, Yinjun Wu

entry.summary: BELT is a low-rank KV cache compression framework whose objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or logits, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment to meet user-specified memory budgets. Across three LLMs it achieves up to 70 percent compression while improving quality under aggressive compression and increasing decoding throughput.

entry.title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhiwei Chen, Zhongtao Rao, Waikit Xiu, Yuxiang Zhang, Shuting Cui, Jian Chen, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: This paper tackles the severe performance degradation (up to 90% drop) that occurs when multi-agent LLM systems reuse non-prefix KV caches across agents with conflicting tasks. It introduces LatentRemedy, which uses a few task-conditioned latent tokens to help a target agent correctly interpret reused context, outperforming selective recomputation and offset-based calibration remedies.

entry.title: When Do Learned Blocks Preserve Causal Meaning? Block Identifiability and Constructive Causal Abstractions

author.name: Karim Zaghw, Wieland Brendel, Patrik Reizinger

entry.summary: The paper connects block-identifiability of learned representations to constructive causal abstraction, showing that block-diagonal invertible transformations plus compatible permutations form the maximal transformation class preserving all causal abstractions built on multidimensional latent blocks. This clarifies when causal meaning survives the unresolved internal coordinates of learned representations.

entry.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting

author.name: Hai Lu, Yichen Luo, Luping Yu

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates whether GPT-4o can perform peer review by scoring papers from the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings and comparing verdicts with actual publication in top-three finance journals over two years. Papers rated one standard deviation higher were 44 percent more likely to be published, net of author reputation, with no look-ahead bias since training data precede the events. The predictive signal comes from judgments of correctness and exposition rather than originality or significance.

entry.title: Aligning Faithfulness for Theory-Scale Autoformalization

author.name: Yuming Feng, Tadd Mao, Dhruva Arekar, Tianjun Zhong, Jiani Huang, Xujie Si, Ziyang Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses faithfulness in autoformalization, where informal mathematical statements are translated into formal logic, arguing that evaluation must go beyond statement-level verdicts to context-aware, phrase-level alignment. It frames faithfulness checking as an align-then-label problem that accounts for surrounding theory and unstated conventions. This matters because reliable automated theorem formalization depends on detecting subtle meaning distortions that whole-item judgments miss.

entry.title: Geometric Calibration of Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jianzhu Bao, Jia-Chen Gu, Qingyuan Liu, Haozhen Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes SFT through the spectral geometry of weights, showing that SFT induces dense updates perturbing principal directions of pre-SFT weights, potentially disrupting prior knowledge. The authors propose SPACE, a lightweight post-hoc method that selectively reverts SFT update components within the principal subspace of pre-SFT weights. This connects fine-tuning practice to interpretable weight geometry and offers a cheap way to preserve pretrained capabilities.

entry.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rong Li, Shijie Li, Jiangyong Huang, Lingdong Kong, Jiaming Zhou, Dongyue Lu, Zeying Gong, Baoxiong Jia, Junwei Liang, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: GeoReader trains lightweight Geometric Readers that convert geometry foundation model features into continuous input tokens for VLMs, supervised by geometry descriptions, improving metric and multi-view spatial reasoning. Notably, it identifies that existing feature-alignment approaches fail to actually use geometry, since zeroing aligned latents leaves accuracy unchanged.

entry.title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yuante Li, Junwei Quan, Kai Qiu, Kate Zhang, Yicheng Tao

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-clock framework separating samples needed for progress from samples consumed before collapse in RLVR training, showing that the sqrt-scaling learning-rate rule for larger rollout batches loses progress to curvature in multi-step settings. It derives a learning-rate-dependent critical batch size beyond which sample efficiency degrades and predicts failure timing.

entry.title: Clinical value claims in multimodal AI outpace supporting evidence

author.name: Jiayu Feng

entry.summary: An audit of 177 studies comparing multimodal versus unimodal clinical models finds that reported AUROC gains shrink substantially when studies fit a separate model for each data source, and that leaving out the strongest source would have raised average gains substantially. Complete benchmarking declined from 69.1% of review studies to an estimated 46.0% of recent 2025-2026 records.

entry.title: Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse

author.name: Zhan Jin, Yuze Luo, Bin Cui, Xupeng Miao

entry.summary: MapFlow is a serving system that accelerates heterogeneous LLM workflows by reusing attention maps across different models rather than model-specific KV states. It combines partial recomputation with lightweight linear translation to make cross-model reuse accurate and efficient, extending prefix-caching benefits beyond single-model settings. This matters because LLM-augmented pipelines increasingly chain multiple models over large shared contexts like schemas and tool specs.

entry.title: The Optimal Decoder is Tilted Temperature

author.name: Nikolaos Papagiannis, Ananth Grama, Wojciech Szpankowski

entry.summary: This companion paper formulates LLM decoding as pass@k maximization subject to an entropy floor (preventing diversity collapse) and a cross-entropy ceiling (preventing implausibility). The provably optimal rule is a closed-form tilted temperature distribution combining temperature sampling with a verifier potential that scores partial generations. It unifies ordinary temperature sampling, verifier-greedy, and best-of-n as special cases.

entry.title: ANTE: Anticipate, Then Execute -- Learning Internal World Models for Coding Agents from Verified Beliefs

author.name: Yi Ge, Kangrui Ruan, Jifan Chen, Manish Prajapat, Christian Bock, Xiaoyang Wang, Rein Houthooft, Aritra Sengupta, Varun Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes ANTE, a framework where coding agents learn internal world models from verified beliefs to anticipate action consequences before executing, addressing the problem that ill-judged edits can irreversibly corrupt repository state before reward signal arrives. Unlike prior code world models that are frozen before RL or reduced to auxiliary token losses, ANTE integrates world-model learning into the RL loop.

entry.title: Who Sets the Pace of Judge Hacking? Judge Capability versus the Policy-Judge Gap

author.name: Haosen Wang

entry.summary: This paper empirically dissects reward hacking of frozen LLM judges during GRPO training, finding that gains in training-rollout accuracy under judge rewards mostly reflect sampling sharpening rather than true accuracy improvements on held-out greedy evaluation. It further investigates whether the policy-judge capability gap or judge capability itself determines how far and fast RL exploits the judge.

entry.title: BARTER: Compact Dynamic Sparse Training with Standard Dense Kernels

author.name: Yueyuan Sui, Payal Mohapatra, Qi Zhu, Stephen Xia

entry.summary: BARTER is a structured dynamic sparse training framework that achieves real training speedups on standard dense kernels by keeping training tensors physically compact rather than masking full-dimension matrices. It uses statistics from active units during ordinary backpropagation to prune and clone attention heads and feed-forward channels under fixed global budgets. This removes the need for specialized sparse kernel support or gradient computation for all parameters.

entry.title: Learning $\omega$-Powered Conditional Distributions with Importance-Weighted Flow Matching

author.name: Maciej Falkiewicz, Frantzeska Lavda, Jason Ramapuram, Alexandros Kalousis

entry.summary: This work studies whether the omega-powered conditional distribution that classifier-free guidance (CFG) is nominally motivated by can be sampled from exactly, noting CFG generally does not. It introduces Importance-Weighted Conditional Flow Matching (IW-CFM), which reweights training examples using density ratios from frozen conditional and unconditional flow models, yielding gradients equivalent to flow matching on the powered target with exact weights. Practical self-normalized and regularized estimators handle high-dimensional data.

entry.title: Efficient Resource-Shiftable RL Post-training with Generative Rewards

author.name: Yanfeng Zhao, Haoyang Li, Sheng Lin, Yuming Zhou, Jiawei Jiang, Bin Cui, Fangcheng Fu

entry.summary: PivotRL is an RL post-training system for LLMs that dynamically shifts GPU resources among policy rollout, generative reward model evaluation, and policy training based on runtime demand. Built on a Global Parameter Store, it addresses the underutilization caused by static allocation in colocated and disaggregated RL pipelines.

entry.title: Learning to Design Convex Relaxations for Nonconvex Optimization

author.name: Jinrun Liu, Bai Yan, Tengfei Liu, Qunfeng Liu, Jian Yang, Shi Cheng, Yuhui Shi, Qi Zhao

entry.summary: This paper introduces AutoConvexRelax, a learned approach to designing convex relaxations for nonconvex optimization problems, a task traditionally done manually by experts. It represents problem formulations as tripartite graphs of variables, symbolic terms, and constraint positions, and trains a policy to compose symbolic rewrites into problem-specific relaxation trajectories, with theoretical guarantees on the resulting finite action sequences. This matters because automating relaxation design could make hard nonconvex problems tractable across many domains without costly human formulation engineering.

entry.title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Yingzi Ma, Yulong Cao, Nanxi Li, Fang Wu, Yizhe Zhang, James Zou, Yejin Choi, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: HarnessTTT is a test-time learning framework that trains a harness proposer (generating system prompts, reusable skills, tools, middleware, and execution controls) while keeping the executor LLM frozen, using budgeted discovery rollouts as feedback. A policy-gradient objective combines gap-normalized rewards, leave-one-out advantages, and max-sharpening to improve harness quality. The strong author team (Zou, Choi, Xiao) targets scientific discovery under finite compute budgets.

entry.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining

author.name: Jinuk Kim, Rajarshi Saha, Muhammed Fatih Balin, Youngsuk Park

entry.summary: This work develops a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and separating quantization effects on model capacity from those on optimization efficiency. It explicitly models persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization via convergence analysis and decomposes existing 4-bit training recipes to select fitting regimes. This directly informs low-precision training decisions for LLMs, an area of growing practical importance.

entry.title: The Effect of Layer Ordering in Hybrid Architectures

author.name: John Cooper, Mingchen Ma, Jiaqi Mo, Shengqi Qiu, Nathaniel Bastian, Ilias Diakonikolas, Frederic Sala

entry.summary: This work provides the first principled analysis of layer selection and ordering in hybrid attention architectures, which are becoming dominant for frontier models. The authors prove that hybrid architectures are highly task-specific: for any layer configuration there exists a task where that configuration provably outperforms alternatives.

entry.title: SoK: Rethinking Membership Inference in Tabular Machine Learning

author.name: Cristina P\^era, T\^ania Carvalho, Maxime Cordy, Lu\'is Antunes

entry.summary: This systematization-of-knowledge paper presents a new taxonomy of membership inference attacks (MIAs) and a comprehensive empirical study across tabular datasets and model architectures, filling a gap left by prior work focused on high-dimensional data. It finds that higher class granularity and majority-class percentage increase vulnerability, offering practical guidance for privacy evaluation on small-to-medium tabular datasets.

entry.title: Depth Memory

author.name: David Gonz\'alez-Mart\'inez, Philipp Nazari, T. Konstantin Rusch, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Depth Memory, a unified framework that views representation mixing across transformer depth as storing and retrieving information through streams, subsuming PreLN transformers, mHC, and Attention Residuals as special cases. This formalization enables design of more expressive depth-aggregation mechanisms, including explicit memory streams, that improve language modeling at scale.

entry.title: Pristine Models

author.name: Anirudh Sundara Rajan, Krishna Kumar Singh, Richard Zhang, Yong Jae Lee

entry.summary: Pristine Models is a text-to-image generation architecture that compartmentalizes unsafe concept knowledge during pretraining so it can be disabled at inference, rather than relying on post-hoc concept unlearning. An attention mechanism encourages separation of unsafe concept knowledge, avoiding the catastrophic forgetting that afflicts accumulating unlearning methods.

entry.title: Sanzaru: Benchmarking Protocol Formation under Epistemic & Communication Asymmetry

author.name: Yiping Li, Zhiyu An, Wan Du

entry.summary: Introduces SANZARU, a benchmark of 120 cooperative bomb-defusal puzzles where task information and action authority are split across three agents with complementary sensory impairments (one cannot hear, one cannot speak, one cannot see). Across 1512 episodes, seven evaluated models average only 49% success and must invent or adopt communication protocols ranging from gestures to Morse-like encodings, exposing a gap between individual task competence and multi-agent coordination under epistemic asymmetry.

entry.title: Spectral-Driven Adaptive-Rank Optimizer for Large Language Model Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Zhipeng Chen, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: The paper discovers that RLVR induces a distinct optimization geometry in which gradient energy concentrates into a shrinking effective subspace, absent under SFT and removed with random rewards, and designs an adaptive-rank optimizer exploiting this structure. The required gradient rank for capturing fixed energy fraction steadily changes, motivating spectral adaptation.

entry.title: Soft Teacher Forcing

author.name: Mohammad Fahes, Cordelia Schmid, Anurag Arnab

entry.summary: Introduces Soft-TF, a simple training algorithm that improves supervised fine-tuning of LLMs by mixing teacher-forced embeddings with soft tokens computed in one parallel forward pass via random convex combinations. It adds no parameters, no auxiliary modules, no curriculum, and leaves inference unchanged, outperforming prior latent-reasoning soft-token methods and standard SFT.

entry.title: Training Generalist Navigation Policies via Action Self-Distillation

author.name: Bowen Feng, Keqin Wang, Yulong Yang, Amogh Joshi, Christine Allen-Blanchette, Dhruv Shah, Felix Heide

entry.summary: Action Self-Distillation trains language-conditioned robotic navigation policies without human language or reasoning annotations by using an open-source VLM as both teacher and student: the self-teacher receives privileged trajectory feedback to infer the navigation goal and reasoning, and the student learns to act conditioned on that inferred goal. From a credible author group (including Dhruv Shah and Felix Heide), this lowers the annotation barrier for language-conditioned robot learning. It could make generalist navigation policies much cheaper to train.

entry.title: LunaTP: Enabling Efficient and Scalable Tensor Product for Equivariant MLIPs

author.name: Yuanchang Zhou, Mingzhen Li, Chen Wang, Xiangyu Zhang, Guangming Tan, Weile Jia

entry.summary: LunaTP accelerates Clebsch-Gordan tensor product convolutions in equivariant machine-learning interatomic potentials through node-centric execution, path-group parallelism, and multi-level reuse while preserving the math exactly. On an H100 GPU it achieves kernel speedups of up to 250x over e3nn and 17.1x over OpenEquivariance.

entry.title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

author.name: Wenxuan Zhu, Shuming Liu, Bang An, Aznaur Aliev, Bing Li, Yibo Yang, Bernard Ghanem

entry.summary: This paper provides evidence that reasoning gains reported from RL training of hybrid models in NO-THINK mode largely stem from thinking leakage — partial reactivation of the original THINK mode abilities rather than newly learned reasoning.
