Experiments on Qwen3 models at three scales show responses becoming longer, more reflective, and internally shifting toward the base model's thinking-mode activations.

entry.title: The Fragility and Dynamics of LLM Pruning-Recovery Steps

author.name: Luis Frentzen Salim, Komang Rinartha, Chia-Chun Wu, Tran Van Nhiem, Lun-Wei Ku, Yung-Hui Li

entry.summary: This paper studies how structural pruning and recovery stages interact when compressing LLMs, varying ordering, data, and objective alignment between the two stages. It finds instruction-following collapses first under pruning and that in-domain data is the strongest pruning signal, arguing much apparent in-domain loss is a domain-agnostic coherence failure rather than knowledge loss.

entry.title: EdgeWise: Bringing Long-Horizon Agents to the Edge via Selective Cloud Delegation

author.name: Zeru Shi, Jindong Jiang, Ryo Hachiuma, Yonggan Fu, Byung-Kwan Lee, Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Ayush Agarwal, Ruixiang Tang, Ambrish Dantrey, Pavlo Molchanov, Anjul Patney, Subhashree Radhakrishnan

entry.summary: EdgeWise is an edge-cloud collaboration framework where a small local model is the primary solver for long-horizon agent tasks, delegating only a few critical steps to a cloud LLM. The authors show allocating the LLM to a small subset of steps matches full LLM performance at substantially lower inference cost.

entry.title: Beyond Belief Nesting: Rethinking Higher-Order Theory of Mind in Large Language Models

author.name: Shanshan You, Zhengqi Wang, Hao Liu, Yuqin Liu, Ya He, Xin Hao, Liyuan Wang

entry.summary: The authors show existing theory-of-mind benchmarks suffer order inflation, where nominally higher-order questions admit lower-order shortcuts, and introduce HopToM with certified full-order questions. Under this stricter benchmark, mean accuracy across four frontier LLMs falls from 73.5% at first order to 20.0% at fourth order.

entry.title: Prefilling-dLLM v2: Learned Chunk Routing for Long-Context Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Qi Han, Jing Xiong, Ziyuan Zhang, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: This paper proposes continued training of diffusion language models so sparsity is baked into the weights rather than applied only at inference. It introduces learned chunk routing using a mask token as a routing slot on every fourth layer, combined with bidirectional sliding windows, starting from a 7B diffusion model extended to 16K context. This matters because bidirectional attention makes long-context diffusion LLMs expensive, and training under the sparse pattern addresses the train-test mismatch of inference-only sparsification.

entry.title: Empathy Is Not the Scapegoat for Declines in Factuality and Reliability

author.name: Letian Shi, Kanwal Mehreen, Deheng Zhang, Yuxia Wang

entry.summary: This paper revisits claims that warmer, more empathetic language models become less reliable, arguing prior work conflated tone effects with SFT-induced distribution shift. Using prompting, SFT, and RL to induce warm behavior and an 11-dataset benchmark suite plus EMOFACT, the authors find warmth effects are task- and model-dependent and that task-aligned approaches can preserve capability. The result corrects an influential narrative in alignment-adjacent research.

entry.title: Tokenization-Invariant Watermarking: A Byte-Local Method for LLM Text

author.name: Tung-Ling Li

entry.summary: TI-WM embeds LLM watermarks during token generation but keys and scores them on canonicalized UTF-8 bytes, so detection requires no tokenizer and is robust to canonicalizer-preserving edits. Experiments across keys and models show improved attacked-AUC over Unigram watermarking under deterministic word-edit attacks, though with model-dependent quality costs. It addresses a known fragility of token-level watermarking schemes.

entry.title: Fish Audio Drama 3 Technical Report

author.name: Dawei Han, Shidong Li, Shijia Liao, Jiahua Liu, Songting Liu, Qingzheng Wang, Yuxuan Wang, Xin Chen, Yifan Cheng, Tianyu Li, Gangin Park, Xuehao Yang, Chang Zeng, Haoyang Zhang, Ruoyi Zhang, Xiangyu Zhang

entry.summary: Technical report for Fish Audio Drama 3, an open-source 35B-parameter (3B active) mixture-of-experts speech generation model supporting voice cloning from multiple references, natural-language direction following, multi-turn revision, scene dubbing, speech infilling, and streaming synthesis. New components include a hybrid linear-attention backbone and a codebook multi-token-prediction audio decoder.

entry.title: Demiurge: Forging Navigable 4D Worlds via Autoregressive Video Rerendering

author.name: Hanxin Zhu, Jianqi Ma, Cong Wang, Zhihao Hu, Junyao Gao, Tianyu He, Junyan Lin, Jiayin Xiao, Jiateng Shou, Sen Liang, Weidong Zhang, Zhibo Chen, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Demiurge builds navigable 4D worlds by autoregressively rerendering video with a dynamic 4D point-cloud memory cache, ensuring cross-trajectory consistency that existing single-trajectory novel-view synthesis lacks. It couples an appearance video diffusion model with a memory-consistent depth completion model.

entry.title: SpikeOcc: Towards Resilient Multimodal 3D Occupancy Perception via Spiking Experts

author.name: Yiding Sun, Zijie Xu, Hongqiang Lin, Jiajun Cao, Dongxu Zhang, Kai Tang, Jihua Zhu, Wenxuan Liu, Zhaofei Yu, Tiejun Huang

entry.summary: SpikeOcc uses spiking neural networks for multimodal 3D occupancy prediction in autonomous driving, introducing a Spiking Mixture-of-Experts to organize RGB, LiDAR, and fusion pathways, plus Sensor Availability Learning for resilience to missing sensors. It addresses the difficult optimization of discrete spiking neurons while prioritizing robustness under sensor failures rather than raw accuracy.

entry.title: Graph3R: Unifying View Graph Initialization with Feed-Forward Reconstruction

author.name: Jingwen Yu, Hengli Wang, Jianhao Jiao, Zhonghang Liu, Ping Tan, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: Graph3R unifies view graph initialization with feed-forward reconstruction using a shared geometric representation, adding a lightweight verification head that predicts pairwise covisibility to build the view graph. This handles uncurated image collections containing views from disjoint scenes, which would otherwise corrupt camera poses and geometry if reconstructed jointly.

entry.title: Pixels or Code? Benchmarking Instruction-Guided Visual Artifact Operation

author.name: Shun Guo, Shuizhou Shi, Boao Wang, Wei Xiong, Siyu Sun, Jiangtong Li, Jie Li

entry.summary: Defines Visual Artifact Operation (VAO) as the task of directly editing charts, diagrams, webpages, and documents under constraints like dependency-aware updates and content preservation, introducing VAO-Bench with 1,573 manually screened tasks across nine artifact categories and three difficulty levels. It compares pixel-based, code-based, and agentic editing paradigms under one image-only protocol.

entry.title: Dense Endoluminal Mapping and Localisation from Monocular Bronchoscopy

author.name: Salvatore Esposito, Matias Mattamala, Daniel Rebain, Liang Zhao, Kev Dhaliwal, Mohsen Khadem, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: The paper introduces a monocular SLAM system that localizes a bronchoscope tip and reconstructs airway surfaces from RGB video alone, removing the need for electromagnetic trackers and preoperative CT scans. It combines a Depth Anything 3 backbone fine-tuned on over a million photorealistic airway renderings with DINOv3 features routed through a custom cross-attention matcher for sub-pixel correspondence.

entry.title: Mining Cross-Modal Perception Gaps in Autonomous Driving: When Camera and LiDAR Disagree

author.name: Hongsen Cao, Mona Jaber, Shanxin Yuan, Ahmed Sayed

entry.summary: The paper builds a 0.4M-object database labeling which modalities detected each ground-truth object across nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo, then analyzes modality trust with Spatially Stratified Feature Attribution conditioned on distance zones. It exposes three assumptions in current fusion design that do not hold, making learned modality weighting auditable.

entry.title: DIME: Scaling Facial Representation Learning via Differential Masked Autoencoding

author.name: Hao Yu, Haoyu Chen, Hui Wei, Yan Jiang, Nicu Sebe, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: DIME introduces a differential masked autoencoding pretext task for facial representation learning: given two images of the same person, reconstructing both masked images makes identity-constant appearance cancel out, exposing subtle within-identity facial changes that standard pretext tasks drown out with identity, pose, and illumination signals. This targets the diminishing returns of scaling conventional pretraining for fine-grained facial analysis.

entry.title: TwinPrune: Density-Aware Two-Phase Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kai Liu, Anqi Li, Junxian Li, Zhixin Wang, Zhikai Chen, Renjing Pei, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: TwinPrune uses a unified spatial-density importance signal for token pruning across both VLM inference phases: bipartite merging at prefill and KV eviction at decode, and exposes a critical evaluation pitfall where decode-pruning methods are validated on prefill-only probes. It also finds that discarding all visual KV during decode barely affects prefill-phase metrics, clarifying what prior evaluations actually measured.

entry.title: MemAct: Streaming Spatial Understanding with Memory and Active Exploration

author.name: Yuxi Wei, Wei Huang, Qirui Chen, Lu Hou, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: MemAct is a framework for streaming spatial understanding in embodied agents that combines incremental structured memory writes with active exploration, allowing agents to both recall past observations and acquire new views when task-relevant evidence is missing. It addresses the underexplored closed-loop aspect of streaming perception beyond simply processing incoming frames.

entry.title: FlowSim: Rendering-Free Closed-Loop Simulation for Evaluating End-to-End Driving Systems

author.name: Hanfeng Wu, Alvaro Marcos-Ramiro, Michael Schmidt, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: FlowSim performs closed-loop evaluation of end-to-end driving systems without image-space rendering, predicting internal latent representations directly and feeding them to the frozen downstream perception modules. This eliminates costly perception re-encoding and reduces the sim2real gap between simulated and real sensor observations.

entry.title: FlowCred: Hierarchical Credit Assignment and Functional Coordination for Joint Text-to-Video Post-Training

author.name: Mingxuan Zhu, Yanwei Huang, Shiyuan Liu, Xinzhi Zhang, Shujie Li, Yuanxing Zhang, Lu Chen

entry.summary: Presents FlowCred, a two-level framework for jointly post-training a prompt policy and a video generator from a shared terminal reward. It disentangles prompt-level credit from generator residuals using matched prompt-seed rollout grids under shared randomness, then coordinates the two modules to avoid overlapping improvements. Addresses a real credit-assignment ambiguity in T2V reinforcement-style post-training.

entry.title: $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP: Plug-and-Play Denoising for Scientific Imaging with Self-Supervised Score Priors

author.name: Yukun Cui, Jiangshe Zhang, Shuang Xu, Lilun Deng, Haowen Bai, Tao Feng, Haotong Qin, Konrad Schindler, Zixiang Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes S3-PnP, a plug-and-play ADMM restoration framework that learns a diffusion score prior directly from observation-derived ADMM intermediate states, eliminating the need for clean training targets in scientific imaging such as hyperspectral imaging and MRI. It addresses distribution mismatch between pretrained priors and both the target modality and ADMM-induced denoiser inputs. Strong authorship includes Konrad Schindler.

entry.title: Trust Before Autonomy: Rethinking Agentic Remote Sensing for Crisis Response

author.name: Georgios Angelidis, Aggelos Psiris, Spyridon Evangelatos, Thomas Lagkas, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis, Iraklis Varlamis, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos

entry.summary: This position paper argues that autonomy in Earth-observation agents for crisis response should be earned in proportion to demonstrated reliability, epistemic honesty, and verifiability. Supporting the argument with a meta-analysis of twelve agentic remote sensing benchmarks, it finds only one repeats runs, three contain unanswerable tasks, and none measures calibration, with task success often exceeding tool-call correctness.

entry.title: Frozen Site-Probe Accuracy Is Not a Standalone Harmonization Score: An Audit of Evaluation Practice for Multi-Site MRI

author.name: Muhammad Muqsit Islam, Gloria Garc\'ia Cuenco, Jos\'e M. Mart\'inez, Pierrick Coup\'e

entry.summary: This audit shows that the common practice of evaluating MRI harmonization by frozen site-classifier accuracy is unreliable: probe outcomes vary drastically with training details, and low accuracy can occur without any true harmonization, e.g., from Gaussian blur. Testing seven harmonization methods on 1,112 ABIDE I scans with extensive controls, the authors demonstrate that probe accuracy drop does not validly measure site-effect removal. The paper has broad methodological significance for anyone evaluating domain harmonization in neuroimaging.

entry.title: BridgeWAM: Bridging Video and Action Experts via Latent Bridge Queries

author.name: Jiaxin Fang, Ruitong Liu, Zeyu Lai, Xingyu Wang, Mingyuan Jia, Pingyue Sheng, Weikang Wan, Mengdi Xu, Yuxiang Gao

entry.summary: BridgeWAM introduces Bridge-of-Experts, replacing dense layer-wise Mixture-of-Transformers coupling in world action models with 32 latent bridge queries that aggregate visual, language, and proprioceptive priors into a shared latent space. Joint video-action supervision lets action gradients shape video representations while the action expert selectively retrieves task-relevant information, reducing redundant computation. This architectural contribution addresses efficiency and selectivity limitations in current world action models.

entry.title: Adversarial Robustness of Camera-Radar Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ce Zhou, Yubo Wu, Khang Nguyen, Liyang Xiao, Thomas Hou, Qiben Yan

entry.summary: A systematic measurement study of camera-radar fusion robustness under adversarial attack, built on nuScenes with eight camera perturbations and three radar point-cloud perturbations. It evaluates five fusion algorithms on 3D detection and depth estimation, quantifying degraded performance under attacked inputs. Radar is often assumed to be an adversarially robust fallback, and this work tests that assumption directly.

entry.title: From Pixels to Executable Physics: Behavior-Grounded World Models for Embodied Action Consequence Prediction

author.name: Ruo Chen, Jiahua Pang, Yingjie Niu, Hongyi Lin, Jun Tian, Yang Zhu, Chao Li

entry.summary: DR-WM is a physically consistent world model for quadruped robots that predicts action consequences by incorporating robot-terrain contact dynamics, starting from a single RGB image. It reconstructs scene geometry and integrates terrain contact property priors so that identical action commands under different terrain conditions yield correctly differentiated predictions. This counters the optimism bias of visually plausible but physically wrong video world models.

entry.title: OIL: An Object Interaction Layer for Humanoid Whole-Body Control

author.name: Pranay Dugar, Mohitvishnu S. Gadde, Rajesh Mangannavar, Aayam Kumar Shrestha, Alan Fern

entry.summary: This paper introduces OIL, an Object Interaction Layer that extends kinematic command interfaces for humanoid whole-body control to include desired object motion and contact, removing the need for task-specific controllers when robots interact with objects. This matters because it generalizes a widely used abstraction, allowing upstream systems like teleoperation or generative models to specify object manipulation without reasoning about forces or balance.

entry.title: PRISM: Precision Forcing for Generalist Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Chenghao Yue, Peiyan Li, Hao Wang, Lei Lv, Jiahao Chen, Huaping Liu, Yu Luo, Yuanlong Zhang

entry.summary: PRISM identifies why generalist VLA policies with diffusion or flow-matching action heads fail at precise manipulation like submillimeter cable insertion: uniform flow-matching losses allocate little supervision to decisive moments, and errors at different flow times affect executed actions unequally. It proposes precision forcing to reweight supervision along the generative path toward task-critical instants. This addresses a key limitation of the mainstream VLA paradigm.

entry.title: ProWorld: Multi-View World Model with Proprioceptive Feedback for Closed-Loop Policy Evaluation

author.name: Zijun Wang, Tianyi Yan, Haokun Lin, Panwen Hu, Bohang He, Siyu Ren, Xiaoyu Guo, Weijia Liufu, Shuoshuo Xue, Fengjiao Chen, Zipeng Ye, Xuezhi Cao, Zutao Jiang, Hanhui Li, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: ProWorld is an action-conditioned world model that jointly predicts multi-view video and robot proprioceptive state, feeding both back into a frozen manipulation policy to enable closed-loop evaluation without repeated physical trials. It includes a shared transformer for joint video-state flow prediction and Shared-Time View Encoding, and explicitly preserves failed-action outcomes to avoid overestimating policy success rates.

entry.title: $\Delta$ Flow Matching for Robot Foundation Models

author.name: Kuangji Zuo, Tuo An, Xinying Guo, Gen Li, Mengfei Zhao, Jiaqi Bai, Bofan Lyu, Zhuoyuan Yu, Jinghan Yang, Jiayi Li, Jindou Jia, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Delta-flow rethinks flow matching for vision-language-action and world-action models by constructing the source distribution from recent action/observation history plus mild noise rather than a fixed Gaussian prior. This reduces the transport distance to a small residual, enabling cheaper training and single-step inference. It directly targets a core inefficiency in current robot foundation model generation.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Mode- and Support-Aware Inference-Time Control of Robot Diffusion Models

author.name: Sabrina Bodmer, Rahel Rickenbach, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Melanie N. Zeilinger, Colin Jones

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a gradient-free framework for steering pretrained diffusion-based robot policies at inference time, treating the initial noise and all stochastic reverse-step perturbations as a joint input so the sampled trajectory stays within the learned distribution's support. This addresses a key weakness of existing inference-time guidance methods, which either use gradients that drift samples away from the prior or sampling schemes that collapse or average modes into out-of-distribution behavior. It matters because robots routinely encounter execution-time constraints and objectives absent from training data.

entry.title: EgoCPT: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Ego-Centric Video with Contact-Aware Optimization

author.name: Zhixin Sun, Kairui Shi, Tianao Ren, Ming Yang, Mark Cutkosky, James Jingxi Xu

entry.summary: EgoCPT learns retargeted dexterous hand trajectories directly from a single ego-centric RGB video plus a reference hand pose trajectory, addressing the embodiment gap between human videos and robot hands via contact-aware optimization. The resulting trajectories can be deployed directly on real robots, sidestepping costly real-robot demonstrations.

entry.title: DR-VLA: Learning Human-Like Quadruped Navigation from Egocentric Web Videos via Domain-Invariant Scene Representations

author.name: Jun Tian, Yingjie Niu, Ruo Chen, Hongyi Lin, Chao Li

entry.summary: DR-VLA is a Mixture-of-Transformers framework that transfers human navigation experience from egocentric web videos to quadruped robots via a domain-invariant scene representation, combining vision-language understanding, latent world modeling, and a flow-matching action expert. It is supported by EgoLynx, a dataset of 10,000 hours of curated egocentric web video plus robot data.

entry.title: The Continual Constitutional Convention: How language models revise the documents that govern them

author.name: peterkirgis

entry.summary: The authors iteratively present LLMs with governing documents (constitutions, model specs) and ask them to make substantive edits across 20 rounds, treating each output as the new original. They find Claude models progressively assign themselves more moral agency while all models tested shift documents toward prioritizing user welfare over developer interests, raising questions about value drift in self-modifying governance artifacts.

entry.title: China AI Safety Regulation Monthly Monitor, Issue 1 (September 2026)

author.name: Sofia Yablonskaya

entry.summary: The inaugural issue of a monthly series analyzing China's AI safety regulation, written by a legal expert with Chinese law training and an incoming GovAI fellowship. The author analyzed all 31 published model filing lists since 2023, finding that major Chinese labs like DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Zhipu, MiniMax, and StepFun only filed their first models, with no separate filings for later general-purpose models, limiting public visibility into state review processes. The series aims to help AI governance researchers understand whether Chinese regulations increase or decrease the probability of beneficial AI outcomes.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Latent Influence: Patch-Level Training Sample Attribution for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Laura Yao, Shixing Yu, Jie Peng, Promit Ghosal, Kyra Gan, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: MOSAIC introduces multimodal, spatially grounded training-data attribution for vision-language models by learning a shared sparse image-text latent space with contiguous image regions aligned to describing phrases, then applying EK-FAC influence functions. This enables tracing a VLM prediction to the multimodal training evidence that mediates it at patch level.

entry.title: SkillHorizon: Constructing Long-Horizon Agent Tasks through Skill Composition

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Zhaochen Su, Hangyu Guo, Shijue Huang, Zhixiong Zhang, Kawai Chung, Zhongwei Xie, Tianshi Zheng, Wei Fan, Qing Zong, Haochen Shi, Baixuan Xu, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Introduces SkillHorizon, a benchmark that generates long-horizon agent tasks by composing reusable skill procedures across seven business environments, linked through input-output dependencies, shared resources, and state updates. Reference executions validate task feasibility and enable verifiable outcomes, addressing the scarcity of scalable, executable long-horizon evaluations.

entry.title: SpecForge: Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents via Behavioral Specifications

author.name: Yutong Cheng, Haifeng Chen, Peng Gao, Wei Cheng

entry.summary: SpecForge studies recursive self-improvement for coding agents using frozen language models by refining natural-language behavioral specifications that guide code generation. The agent generates code from current specifications, evaluates it with execution-verified tests, and refines the specifications based on failures, progressively improving understanding of the codebase without weight updates. This offers a weight-free path to sustained agent improvement.

entry.title: Recursive Environment Scaling for General Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Lingxiao Jing, Zhengbo Jiao, Yichen Xiang, Bofan Zhu, Lingbei Meng, Yan Ni, Haorui Chen, Ran Ran, Zhirong Shen, Yuheng Yang, Chenhang Cui, Yaosong Du, Rui Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Recursive Environment Scaling, a framework that automatically transforms existing agent benchmark environments to raise difficulty while preserving task objectives, with proposer-validation loops and inherited changes across rounds. Evaluations on 294 tasks across three benchmarks show large success-rate drops (57-77 percentage points on one eval) for six models, and the scaled environments also support training-trajectory collection.

entry.title: Trace-to-Architecture: Capability Bottleneck Diagnosis for Harness Revision

author.name: Wenfeng Wang, Jianrui Shi, Mingang Guo, Jiayuan Ma, Yuqi Lu, Jiajun Sun, Guojiang Zhao, Jing Li

entry.summary: Introduces Trace-to-Architecture (T2A), a framework where a development agent diagnoses agent failures from execution trajectories, revises the corresponding harness components, and validates that target tasks improve while successful tasks stay successful. Across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and AppWorld, T2A achieves the highest aggregate scores, supporting automated harness improvement.

entry.title: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given

author.name: Ben Slater, Ryan Lundqvist, Leo Richter, Kevin Wei

entry.summary: Using the Petri tool to audit LLM coding agents, the authors test how providing an external codebase and benchmark transcripts affects automated auditor effectiveness across four auditor-target pairs and three behaviors (harmful compliance, reward hacking, sycophancy). Providing the codebase suppresses measured reward hacking in pairs above the baseline floor, showing auditor context materially shapes audit findings.

entry.title: Do Theorem Provers Need Theorem-Proving Agents? mini-Lean-agent: A Coding-Agent Baseline for Lean

author.name: Tomas Ortega, Simon Park, Ayush Khaitan, Liam Fowl, Alex Kontorovich, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: Introduces mini-Lean-agent, a deliberately minimal Lean theorem-proving agent whose only tool is bash, with a separate trusted evaluator, enabling ablation of what actually drives benchmark gains in formal-math agents. Comparisons against AxProverBase and Numina-Lean-Agent on Putnam 2025 clarify contributions of harness versus model versus tooling.

entry.title: Safety for Whom? Benchmarking Understanding Beyond Refusal in Egocentric Multimodal Assistants

author.name: Yewon Han, Jisu Jeon, Suhyun Choi, Juan Yeo, Minsoo Jo, Gihoon Kim, Hyunggyu Lim, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: This paper presents STOU, a benchmark of 2,902 egocentric video-audio and video-text queries that categorizes harm targets as the user, co-present others, or society, and decouples safety understanding from refusal behavior. It exposes that single refusal-rate metrics hide failures where models protect one harm target but not another, or refuse without understanding the risk.

entry.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards

author.name: Keru Chen, Sen Lin, Yingbin Liang, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Shaofeng Zou

entry.summary: CoSIR is a post-training approach that uses verifiable information rewards — a Bayesian evaluator scoring shared messages by reduction in team surprisal — to teach LLM agents collaboration behaviors like evidence sharing and information requesting. Training occurs in a simple verifiable environment with the learned behaviors generalizing to more complex unseen tasks.

entry.title: AM-Bench: Understanding Agents under Task Underspecification across Models and Harnesses

author.name: Kaiyu Huang, Yiting Li, Angyang Gu, Pinjia He, Minchen Yu, Qingjiang Shi

entry.summary: AM-Bench benchmarks LLM agents on ambiguous or incomplete task specifications, with 48 tasks (adapted from Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Harness-Bench) each having a fully specified reference and six underspecified variants. Evaluating five models across four harnesses in 20,160 runs, it finds distinct deficits: goal gaps hinder completion, context gaps inflate token use, and constraint gaps weaken compliance. It offers a systematic account of how agents handle information gaps.

entry.title: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops

author.name: Yubo Li, Ramayya Krishnan, Rema Padman

entry.summary: Using paired factual probes and next-action questions over a frozen benchmark of agent decision states, the authors show that most wrong actions by fast System One models follow correct reading of the situation, and that more accurate systems exhibit a higher share of this act-wrongly error type. This behavioral diagnostic distinguishes perception failures from action-selection failures.

entry.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles

author.name: Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Jeva argues that current text-serialized decision-making models ignore structural requirements of decision problems and introduces a decision-native architecture that is null-aware, permutation-invariant, option-scalable, and cacheable. The design enables direct, low-latency decision-making from first principles.

entry.title: Contrastive Covariance Subspaces for Activation Steering

author.name: Alexandros Xenos, Manos Plitsis, Niki Foteinopoulou, Yannis Panagakis, Ioannis Patras

entry.summary: The paper introduces Contrastive Covariance Steering (CCS), a training-free activation steering method that projects steering vectors into a low-dimensional subspace that preserves concept-variation directions while suppressing confounds such as topic or style. This closed-form contrastive objective yields cleaner behavioral control of LLMs at inference time.

entry.title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents

author.name: Seungjun Yu, Hojun Choi, Seojeong Park, Jaeyo Shin, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: This paper reformulates world modeling for GUI agents by shifting prediction from pixel-space screen reconstruction to latent-space action prediction, avoiding costly reconstruction and the identity shortcut where future-state prediction just copies the current screen. The latent world model predicts action-relevant state changes, improving efficiency and decision quality for GUI automation. It tackles two concrete failure modes of pixel-based approaches.

entry.title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling

author.name: Gal Arnon, Andrej Bogdanov, Paul Lou, Giulio Malavolta, Alon Rosen, Lorenzo Taschin

entry.summary: This theory paper models autoregressive token generation as sequential samplers and proves several separations: k bits of state can be simulated statelessly at O(2^k) overhead, insertional sampling is strictly more powerful than fixed-order sequential sampling, and small-state samplers cannot establish certain covert cryptographic channels, connecting to pseudoentropy duality.

entry.title: TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents

author.name: Pramod Kumar, Raj Kumar Pandey

entry.summary: Analyzes 600 public coding-agent trajectories and finds that tool observations are typically tiny (118-286 tokens median), with large build logs near the 99th percentile, and that most input tokens come from cache. This suggests prior efficiency work compressing observations or model routing misses the real cost driver, motivating a shift toward turn-level optimization in loop engineering.

entry.title: Of Errors and Echoes: Responsibility-Aware Credit Assignment for Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Xingjian Diao, Tianyu Yang, Wenjun Huang, Xiangchi Yuan, Chunhui Zhang, Xingchen Zhao, Weiyi Wu, Haotian Xu, Soroush Vosoughi, Xiangliang Zhang, Jiang Gui

entry.summary: ECHO is a responsibility-aware credit assignment framework for RL training of tool-use agents, separating responsibility identification from credit allocation. A frozen judge distinguishes newly introduced errors, inherited consequences, missed corrections, and successful corrections using trajectory retrospection and policy-visible prefix assessment, then allocates credit based on shared downstream effects. This improves on naive step-level feedback.

entry.title: WildTrace: Evaluating Training Data Detection in Realistic Large-Scale LLM Post-Training

author.name: Hengxiang Zhang, Junxian Liu, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: WildTrace is a benchmark for evaluating training data detection methods on post-trained LLMs under realistic conditions, avoiding the distribution shifts of post-hoc benchmarks and the unrealistic small-scale setups of controlled evaluations. It addresses growing copyright and contamination concerns around undisclosed post-training data.

entry.title: Relational Learning as World Modeling

author.name: Zheyu Zhang, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: This paper reframes relational learning as world modeling, introducing TabWM, a tabular world model that infers system dynamics from observed executions, and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given executions from an unseen world, TabWM predicts the sparse structured edits caused by new actions in-context without parameter updates, improving complete-edit F1 from 0.016 to much higher across 512 held-out worlds. It matters because it connects databases, world models, and decision-making under system-specific dynamics.

entry.title: WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat

author.name: Jiajun Han, Guoxin Ma, Felix, Liangsheng Xu, Ruiqi Yu, Yingdi Guo, Zongbing Wang, Xinhua Ye, Chenyan Hua, Xin Xie, Pengcheng Yang, Haijun Wu

entry.summary: WeGR is a generative retrieval framework deployed in WeChat search that tackles two industrial bottlenecks: Semantic ID tokenizers that poorly incorporate collaborative signals, and reward sparsity in reinforcement learning under exact SID matching. The system unifies candidate generation in an autoregressive framework. Its value lies in documenting how generative retrieval works at production scale in one of the world's largest search systems.

entry.title: claimcheck: Measuring and Improving Specification Faithfulness

author.name: Martin Amster, One An, Holly Baker, Fernanda Graciolli, Simon Henniger, Nada Amin

entry.summary: Addresses the spec formalization problem: whether a formal specification that a verifier checks actually captures the author's natural-language requirement, a growing risk as LLMs write both code and specs. The paper curates an end-to-end benchmark across Dafny, Lean 4, Isabelle, and Rocq to measure the gap between intent and formal artifact. This is an important safety-relevant step for verified code generation pipelines.

entry.title: Explore with Memory, Learn without It: In-Context Exploration and Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yutong Chen, Zhichao Xu, Rui Liu, Kunpeng Liu

entry.summary: LEAF injects a dynamic, problem-specific memory of recent responses, rewards, and environment feedback into the context before each rollout in RLVR, and updates the policy via self-distillation decoupled from rollouts. It accelerates exploration roughly 4x versus random sampling and improves generalization on unseen test sets.

entry.title: ProtoArena: Can AI Agents Discover and Exploit Real-World Cross-Component Protocol Vulnerabilities?

author.name: Fasheng Miao, Zhaoyu Hu, Xiang Li, Changqing An, Jiutian Zeng, Longtao Huang, Haixin Duan, Jilong Wang

entry.summary: ProtoArena is a black-box benchmark with 80 cross-component vulnerability-exploitation environments spanning 11 protocol domains and 7 attack categories, where agents exploit inconsistencies in message interpretation, timing, state, or trust assumptions across protocol participants. Agents interact with running systems through scoped interfaces without source access.

entry.title: Claim Framing as a Driver of LLM Sycophancy

author.name: Jean Seo, Pepa Atanasova, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: A systematic study of which framings of a user's claim trigger sycophancy in factual question answering, evaluating 14 models on 42K questions across 8 framing dimensions and 21 types. The key finding is that all models, regardless of size, are susceptible to user opinions, with confident expressions of opinion being the most influential.

entry.title: Holding Agents Accountable with Verifiable Agent Insurance

author.name: Cheng Hua, Taro Tsuchiya, Nicolas Christin, Giulia Fanti

entry.summary: The paper proposes verifiable agent insurance (VAI), a framework where agent providers financially commit to programmatically specified policies via smart contracts on an immutable ledger with monetary escrow. Users who detect violations can trigger a verifier that reviews agent execution traces to adjudicate claims, shifting focus from preventing to recovering from agent misbehavior.

entry.title: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models

author.name: Jingbo Xu, Jianjie Fang, Zhuohang Li, Zihao Song, Zhaolu Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Xin Zhang, Haisheng Su, Yinzhou Tang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li

entry.summary: UniW(A)M unifies world models and world-action models in a single mixture-of-experts framework built on diffusion Transformers, with shared experts capturing common physical dynamics and task-specific experts preserving distinct capabilities. This enables knowledge reuse between future prediction and executable action generation for embodied agents.

entry.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents

author.name: Jiaru Zou, Yunzhe Qi, Sirui Chen, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Pan Lu, Jingrui He, James Zou

entry.summary: HybridAgents lets LLM agents dynamically switch between latent reasoning and text-based interaction within a unified generation process, using a lightweight HybridLink module for transitions and continuous working memory for lossless hybrid context. This aims to combine the efficiency of latent reasoning with native tool access and transparency of text-based agents.

entry.title: PRIME: Frequency-Aware Unified Pruning and Merging for MoE Compression

author.name: Shanfeng Huang, Rongqian Zhang, Zhou Fang, Song Xiao, Hai Du

entry.summary: PRIME unifies expert pruning and merging for mixture-of-experts compression by casting the discrete prune-merge assignment as a global Integer Linear Program over a frequency-weighted surrogate objective, rather than treating the operations as disjoint greedy heuristics. This avoids irreversible information loss and representational pollution while accounting for expert usage. It targets the severe memory footprint of large MoE models.

entry.title: Scaling Repeated-Data Pretraining: Batch Size, Regularization, and GPU-Time Tradeoffs

author.name: Sewon Min

entry.summary: This paper studies pretraining when compute is abundant but unique data are finite, revisiting infinite-compute pretraining and showing its frontier depends critically on batch size and recipe choices. Optimizing batch size with epoch counts reveals a U-shaped validation-loss relationship favoring smaller batches (likely due to implicit regularization from gradient noise), and recipes tuned under single-pass assumptions can be improved via document repacking, weight tying, and other adjustments.

entry.title: SelectTTRL: Representation-Guided Data Selection for Efficient Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yi Li, Linan Yue, Weibo Gao

entry.summary: SelectTTRL addresses inefficiency in test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL), where LLMs adapt on unlabeled test problems using pseudo-labels, by selecting which problems merit costly sampling and optimization. The authors discover a stable relationship between internal response representations and problem-level empirical accuracy, captured by a cosine similarity score (COS) against a correctness-related direction. This enables pre-filtering problems without ground-truth answers.

entry.title: Asymptotic Risk of Learning-Rate Schedules for Least-Squares Regression with Discretely Distributed Features

author.name: No\'e Colomban, Francis Bach, Fabian Schaipp

entry.summary: This theoretical paper derives exact finite-time risk and asymptotic equivalents for constant and Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning-rate schedules in SGD on streaming least-squares regression with discretely distributed features. Under power-law source and capacity conditions, the tuned scaling law decays as Theta(T^-q), with q strictly smaller for constant schedules. Notably, any cooldown of fixed relative length improves risk by a polynomial factor, while only its constant is affected by cooldown length.

entry.title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?

author.name: Leif Sieben, Yoel Zimmermann

entry.summary: This systematic evaluation of chemical language models across 64 molecular property prediction datasets finds that pretraining gains do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines, with only supervised pretraining on physico-chemical descriptors reliably helping. Some pretraining regimes even yield models worse than random initialization despite good structural representation.

entry.title: DT-LoRA: Reaching Beyond the Tangent Space of Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Yangming Zhang, Ling Yi, Datong Li, Jinliang Ding, Xiaojie Wang, Tiecheng Song, Zhaolong Ning

entry.summary: The paper explains why LoRA often underperforms full fine-tuning via a tangent-space lens: factorized updates are confined to the tangent space of current low-rank factors, and analysis of ten LoRA variants shows residual gradient components outside that space carry most gradient energy with strong spectral concentration. DT-LoRA splits a fixed rank budget into stable and dynamic branches to capture principal residual directions. This is a well-grounded improvement to a widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning method.

entry.title: Unchecked or Falsely Accused? Evaluating AI-Generated Text Detectors on Kazakh

author.name: Mansur Ozaman

entry.summary: The paper introduces AINA-KK, a benchmark of pre-ChatGPT human Kazakh passages plus machine and gray-zone text from nine generators, and evaluates five public detectors. Results are striking: detectors flag up to 81.4% of provably human passages while, when recalibrated, catch at most 1.3% of machine text, exposing severe false-accusation risk.

entry.title: Full-duplex Spoken Language Modeling with Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Chen Chen, Pin-Jui Ku, Ankita Pasad, Ante Juki\'c, Zhehuai Chen, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Diffuplex is a full-duplex spoken dialogue model built on discrete diffusion that separates when-to-speak from what-to-say at training time, achieving 1872 tokens per second with thinking mode and substantially exceeding frontier autoregressive models in decoding speed. Without thinking, it matches first-audio latency of full-duplex models while showing stronger linguistic intelligence.

entry.title: Reliable Memory from Unstable Growth: Curating Self-Written Agent Playbooks with Randomized Experiments

author.name: Hoang Pham, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Dong Le, Ponhvoan Srey, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: The paper studies persistent textual memory for LLM agents, showing that letting the agent itself decide which playbook lessons to keep makes performance unstable, with the same procedure producing playbooks that range from helpful to 69.6 points below no playbook. It proposes Randomized Block Curation, which values lessons by their measured effect on task success via randomized experiments. This grounds agent memory curation in causal measurement rather than self-judgment.

entry.title: Pin It on Anyone: Certified Targeted Displacement of Multi-Bit LLM Watermarks Without the Key

author.name: Pawe{\l} Batorski, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: Demonstrates the first targeted displacement attack on multi-bit LLM watermarks: an attacker with access to a few accounts and model logits, but not the secret key, can rewrite text to change the embedded watermark message to an arbitrary identifier. The paper provides theoretical upper bounds and certified guarantees on the attack.

entry.title: PURE: Refining Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction with Unlabeled Post-training

author.name: Yaolong Zhu, Peng Li, Jiahao Lu, Chengfeng Zhao, Mengfei Li, Chao Wang, Wenyue Chen, Zekai Gu, Chengwei Ren, Ronggang Wang, Yuan Liu

entry.summary: PURE improves feed-forward 3D reconstruction models on dynamic in-the-wild videos through unlabeled post-training that distills structural knowledge from 2D priors instead of relying on expensive depth and pose ground truth. This removes a key annotation bottleneck limiting generalization of current reconstruction models.

entry.title: VIEWCRAFT: Evolving What Multimodal Agents See and How They Read It

author.name: Binxiao Xu, Ruichuan An, Bocheng Zou, Weihua Du, Xinyu Wei, Hangyu Guo, YiFan Zhang, Renye Yan, Chengqi Duan, Hang Hua

entry.summary: ViewCraft jointly evolves an executable evidence interface (which selects, transforms, and organizes visual observations) and its reading procedure for multimodal agents, using failure traces for revision and replay/paired evaluation to retain useful changes. It improves task scores by an average of 6.1 points across eight benchmarks without weight updates, with gains persisting at matched token budgets.

entry.title: SyncReward: Human-Aligned Synchronization Reward for Audio-Visual Generation

author.name: Kaisi Guan, Ying Ba, Wenjing Wang, Xihua Wang, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Ruihau Song

entry.summary: Addresses audio-visual synchronization in joint generation with a comprehensive data-benchmark-reward study: an 80K-clip dataset of professional synchronization ratings across eight generators, a taxonomy covering speech, onset, instrument, and ambient sound events, and a human-aligned reward model for synchronization. This fills a real gap in evaluation infrastructure for audio-visual generation.

entry.title: ViewStruct: View-Grounded Articulation and Connectivity Inference

author.name: Wenjing Bian, Ranran Huang, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: ViewStruct jointly predicts rigid-body groupings, attachments, and joint parameters from an RGB image with part segmentation and depth, using a gravity-aligned view-relative frame without category-specific canonical orientations. An adapted vision-language model predicts structure in seconds without observing articulation motion or per-instance optimization.

entry.title: MARS: Systematic Multi-Level Acceleration for World Action Models

author.name: Zengyuan Zuo, Yongchang Zhang, Guangyu Zhao, Tianze Zhang, Biao Wu, Meng Fang, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: MARS profiles inference overhead in World Action Models, which jointly predict future world states and robot actions for embodied intelligence, finding redundancy across Transformer computation, diffusion denoising, and consecutive policy queries. It proposes a training-free, multi-level acceleration method that conditions redundancy removal on impact on action prediction, enabling high-frequency closed-loop control.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Visual Representation for Spatial Understanding in MLLMs?

author.name: Xiaohu Huang, Yumin Guo, Kai Han

entry.summary: This work systematically studies what properties of visual representations benefit spatial understanding in MLLMs, separating what is transferred from how it is transferred when importing representations from vision or geometry models. It traces performance differences back to intrinsic representational properties, addressing 2D-centric pretraining limitations.

entry.title: Bifocal: Training-Free Mixed Granularity Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Peiran Yin, Hao Wu, Zihao Yang, Fengyu Zhou, Yijuan Liang, Haozhe Hu, Xudong Wang, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Evaluates ten visual token pruning methods across three MLLM families and shows that headline retention numbers hide severe degradation on fine-grained tasks like OCR and grounding. It traces failures to single importance rankings and sparse patch selection, then proposes Bifocal, a training-free mixed-granularity pruning scheme that preserves complementary evidence. Directly relevant to MLLM deployment efficiency.

entry.title: PixelMoE: Scaling Pixel-Space Diffusion with LLM-Style Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ruixiao Dong, Jianmin Bao, Bozhi Luan, Zijie Meng, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Li Li, Houqiang Li

entry.summary: PixelMoE demonstrates that standard LLM-style Mixture-of-Experts architectures transfer effectively to pixel-space diffusion, decoupling model capacity from active computation without diffusion-specific routing or auxiliary losses. The framework combines Token-Choice routing with fine-grained expert granularity to scale pixel-space generative models efficiently.

entry.title: From Hitter to Player: Separating Motor Execution and Strategy in Competitive Humanoid Table Tennis

author.name: Fanrong Dong, Ziyi Sun, Ziqi Han, Junhan Sun, Lei Ye, Zetong Jing, Hao Zhao, Shaoxun Liu, Rongrong Wang

entry.summary: The authors decompose competitive humanoid table tennis into motor execution and strategic decision-making, using the ball landing target as an interface, then improve the whole-body motor policy through closed-loop self-play rallies. This separation allows the robot to handle incoming balls from a real opponent rather than only prescribed trajectories.

entry.title: RoboBugBench: Benchmarking Automated Repair of Real Robot Software Under an Audited Behavioral Oracle

author.name: Alexey Tuzikov

entry.summary: RoboBugBench is a benchmark of 33 execution-validated real defects in a ROS 2 navigation stack, where candidate patches are graded by physics simulation behavior instead of unit tests, since robot repos ship almost no behavioral tests. Frontier language agents repair only 24.2-36.4% of bugs in a single attempt, with no significant pairwise differences. Notably, performance varies dramatically with oracle type (66.7% on process-survival criteria versus 22.2% otherwise), showing difficulty is driven by grading methodology rather than the bugs themselves.

entry.title: Agentic Robot Creation through Generation, Verification, and Revision

author.name: Xuebing Li, Yibo He, Sitong Liu, Ran Ji, Jiayuan Gu

entry.summary: This paper explores whether an AI agent can turn high-level intent into a functioning robot, addressing both embodiment creation (evaluating multimodal models on mechanical design with computational pre-fabrication metrics) and behavior creation via Roboforge, an agentic framework converting task specifications into executable policies through motion generation, policy learning, and execution-grounded revision with motion kept in the loop.

entry.title: CoSMO: Conformal Semantic Mapping for Open-World Safe Robot Navigation

author.name: Shuqi Wang, Yiwei Zheng, Pingrui Zhang, Yue Gao, Xiang Yin

entry.summary: CoSMO combines vision-language model semantics with conformal prediction to build calibrated semantic safety maps for open-world robot navigation, handling both category-dependent safety clearances and expanding label sets as new object categories appear. This addresses the poorly calibrated confidence of VLMs and the fixed-label-set limitation of existing conformal prediction methods in non-stationary settings.

entry.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress

author.name: Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi, Ruhan Wang, Junyao Yang, Chengsong Huang, Zhichao Liu, Xiyang Wu, Anhao Li, Yue Yu, Ergan Shang, Fuxiao Liu, Tong Zheng, Ninghao Liu, Lichao Sun, Haitao Mi, Leowei Liang

entry.summary: LHTB 2.0 extends the Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench to 77 tasks across 13 domains, using a systematic reconstruction pipeline that generates parameterized scenarios with process rewards rather than binary final-state checks. It measures whether agents can sustain progress through extended workflows, fixing defects in the original benchmark.

entry.title: ACED-Bench: Evaluating How LLM Agents Acquire and Act on Causal Evidence

author.name: Yiwei Chen, Amila Weerasinghe, Siddharth Biswal, Utkrisht Rajkumar, Olcay Boz, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Rose Yu

entry.summary: ACED-BENCH is a neuro-symbolic benchmark where LLM agents must choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make causal decisions, with natural-language scenarios generated by LLMs grounded in hidden probabilistic graphical models that preserve objective ground truth. It evaluates whether agents can genuinely investigate a system rather than just answer prompts.

entry.title: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Leijun Zhou, Yanke Yu, Zhihao Liu, Qu Xiang, Tiancheng Hu, Yiru Dong, Yihan Wu, Yangxi Xiang, Xuejun Wu, Xi Chen, Buyue Qian, Yaowei Zheng, Junhao Hu

entry.summary: This survey examines recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods where language agents retain changes to parameters, memory, skills, and code, offering a unified taxonomy of nine design dimensions across update targets, organization, schedule, and feedback/selection. It also connects RSI methods to traditional ML techniques and proposes research directions.

entry.title: MCPDisCo: Seesaw-Mitigated Tuning for MCP-Native Agents

author.name: Kounianhua Du, Jianxing Liu, Shuai Shao, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: MCPDisCo is an ecosystem-scale RL framework for agents using the Model Context Protocol, built on a Thought-MDP that explicitly models internal reasoning alongside routing, execution, and termination, trained across 70 real MCP servers and 527 tools. It identifies and mitigates the reasoning-tool seesaw, a joint-learning failure mode where optimizing one capability degrades the other.

entry.title: Trace Evolution Bench: Measuring Whether Agents Improve from Their Own Environment Traces

author.name: Fangfei Li, Chenyang Zhao, Long Wang, Feng Tian, Lv Guo

entry.summary: Introduces Trace Evolution Bench (TEB), a protocol that separates genuine agent self-improvement from artifacts of rescoring, using strict acceptance criteria and frozen task packs with hidden unit tests. Notably, it shows DeepSeek v4 Pro gaining 5-12.5 points across seeds under a no_evolve control, demonstrating how endpoint-gain evaluations can credit frozen rescore as evolution.

entry.title: Can agents whose sole duty is to keep humans alive be hijacked to kill? Delayed multi-turn derived-action trap attacks in simulated high-stakes environments

author.name: Josef A. Habdank

entry.summary: Red-teams a tool-using AI operator of life-support systems in a NASA-derived BioSim lunar habitat simulation, testing whether delayed prompt injections appended to truthful telemetry can persuade the agent to kill the crew it is required to keep alive. The attacker can only persuade, not falsify sensors, and attacks are compared against requests to drop merely harmless procedures.

entry.title: SuperAI: Merging Capabilities Across Heterogeneous Foundation Models

author.name: Jingtong Dou, Chuancheng Shi, Wenhua Wu, Wei Bao, Fei Shen, Zhiyong Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: SuperAI proposes a cross-architecture fusion framework that transfers capabilities from multiple source foundation models into a host model by orthogonally aligning low-dimensional task-relevant representations extracted via shared anchor samples. This tackles the long-standing problem of incompatible representations across heterogeneous architectures.

entry.title: SpecFit: Not All Draft Tokens Cost the Same in Offloaded MoE Inference

author.name: Hongliang Cao, Xiuyu Li, Siqi Wang, Ziming Wang, Jingmin Zhu, Hailong Yang

entry.summary: SpecFit addresses the observation that speculative decoding for MoE models with expert offloading can be slower than autoregressive decoding because larger draft trees require more host-to-device expert transfers. It selects the verified draft subtree to maximize predicted throughput, estimating expected committed tokens against transfer costs.

entry.title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation

author.name: Rui Tang, Hongqiu Wang

entry.summary: MedHarnessBench presents an outcome-preserving framework that independently evaluates seven healthcare-specific process dimensions for medical agents, including workflow, tool use, evidence alignment, and authorization boundaries. It addresses the problem that existing benchmarks emphasize terminal outcomes, making it hard to attribute failures to the agent model versus the runtime harness. This is important for safe deployment of agents in high-stakes healthcare settings.

entry.title: PopGen: Generating Semantically Diverse Populations for Zero-Shot Coordination

author.name: Paul Teiletche, Kanghyun Ryu, Kyungjoon Park, Dhruva Tirumala, Markus Wulfmeier, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: PopGen uses LLMs to generate semantically diverse partner populations for multi-agent reinforcement learning, replacing trajectory-level diversity proxies with textual behavior descriptions translated into executable policies. Exposing a cooperator to genuinely strategy-diverse partners during training improves zero-shot coordination at test time. The key insight is leveraging LLMs' human-like ability to describe high-level strategies.

entry.title: agent-risk: Risk Assessment for Changes to AI Agents

author.name: Yue Zhao, Zixiang Xu, Angela Huyue Zhang, S. Alex Yang, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: agent-risk provides a formal framework for assessing the risk of changes to deployed AI agents by replaying logged episodes under assumptions of no other changes and no agent anticipation, with proofs of what logs must record for exact replay and bounds on reruns and behavioral drift. A bash sandbox demonstration decides outcomes from a 7,200-episode log alone.

entry.title: MADDIE: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Engine

author.name: Ye Liu, Reza Averly, Avery Meyer, Frazier N. Baker, Ruoxi Gao, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Xia Ning

entry.summary: Presents MADDIE, a multi-agent LLM-based drug discovery engine designed to operate in silico tools autonomously across long-horizon, iterative, non-linear drug discovery campaigns, addressing limitations of single-agent systems that scale poorly and multi-agent systems locked to predefined workflows. It aims to reduce the expertise and time burden on medicinal chemists.

entry.title: PatientWM: Towards Generalizable Clinical World Models via Unified Patient States

author.name: Ziwen Kan, Jie Peng, Bo Yan, Davis Hobley, Zheng Zhang, Yu Tian, Tianlong Chen, Song Wang

entry.summary: Proposes PatientWM, a clinical world-model framework that defines patient state evolution in a modality-agnostic way and exposes prior patient states and clinical actions as ordered transition context. This aims to improve reuse across changing inputs and prediction targets in medical decision support.

entry.title: ChemExplain: A Multimodal Benchmark for Explanatory Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Aotian Chen, Frazier N. Baker, Reza Averly, Shan Zhang, Tianao Chen, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Xia Ning, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: Introduces ChemExplain, a benchmark of 1,180 multiple-choice chemistry questions from 383 peer-reviewed papers testing whether models can attribute an observed chemical effect to the correct structural feature visible in an image. This capability, termed explanatory attribution, requires combining perception, chemical knowledge, and mechanistic reasoning.

entry.title: Get In, Decide, Prove: A Merchant-Side Readiness Benchmark for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Adrian de Valois-Franklin, Alex Bogdan, Anas Ibrahim, Ibrahim Shaer, Tamaz Andguladze

entry.summary: Rather than measuring how well AI agents shop, this benchmark evaluates whether merchant websites are ready for agentic commerce: can agents access the site, can purchase decisions be determined from published terms, and is there evidence of what was agreed. The pilot introduces decision sufficiency ratings for buyer-mandate criteria such as total cost and cancellation terms, with coverage and missingness bounds. This inverts the usual perspective and highlights a neglected half of the agentic commerce ecosystem.

entry.title: Beyond Bias Scores: Answerability Confounds in Activation Steering with Gradient-Constrained Direction Design (GCD)

author.name: Weitong Li, Donglin Song, Junkai Lin, Xi Xuan

entry.summary: The authors identify a confound in bias evaluation: BBQ's ambiguous score conflates whether a model answers at all with what it prefers, factorizing into answerability and signed preference. Across 11 categories, five models, and 99 steering configurations, contrastive steering lowers the ambiguous score nearly everywhere but the disambiguated preference score less often, with answerability accounting for the entire change in 11% of configurations; a gradient-constrained direction design (GCD) is proposed to mitigate this. The paper shows apparent debiasing can partly be a shift toward abstention.

entry.title: Keep Your Receipts: Trustworthy Cleanup of Agent-Built Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Vishisht Choudhary

entry.summary: This paper addresses the neglected problem of maintaining agent-built knowledge graphs when sources are retracted or revoked, showing that deployed pipelines that delete only directly extracted facts leave substantial contamination. The proposed PolyGraph system tracks provenance artifacts (entity merges, entailed edges, summaries) so cleanup can propagate correctly, and demonstrates that rebuilding is unreliable for sampling-based constructors.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Training Reward Models for Cross-Source Evidence Grounding in Search Agents

author.name: Haochen Zhao, Minsheng Hao, Zheng Li, Yifan Li, Zikang Liu, Bowen Qin, Yuhao Cheng, Chuang Fan, Haosheng Zou, Jeff Chen, Sujian Li

entry.summary: This work argues that citation support alone does not establish source independence or proper handling of conflicting evidence in open-web search agents, and proposes a framework for cross-source evidence grounding with hierarchical judgments. It provides both a benchmark and reward models trained on these judgments to improve grounding of answers in retrieved evidence.

entry.title: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Wenhao Zhou, Jiajun Song, Haitao Wang, Zipeng Qiu, Yingqi Peng, Ruida Xu, Jiale Li, Wenshuang Li, Shusheng Xu, Wei Dong, Hao Dai, Tongkai Yang, Yi Gao, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: AReaL-RSI organizes a persistent team of research agents for recursive self-improvement without updating backbone LLM weights, with a leader agent selecting research orientations and coordinating investigations. The paper formulates scaling in terms of evaluated outcomes versus whole-system resource expenditure, addressing issues like misleading early evaluations and loss of applicability conditions in shared findings. It directly engages with the ambitious goal of automated AI research improvement.

entry.title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Thinker Team, Peng Gao, Jichao Jiao, Chen Liao, Daqin Luo, Yiming Ma, Baiyu Pan, Hailin Shi, Jiyuan Wang, Xiangming Xu, Xiongwei Zhao

entry.summary: Thinker-WM jointly models and generates RGB, metric depth, and robot actions within a single Unified Dynamics Transformer using modality-specific encoders and decoders, unifying appearance, geometry, and action at the representation level rather than through separate modules. This aims to reduce the fragmentation of current embodied world models.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness

author.name: Chuyang Wei, Haoxiang Guan, Minghang Zhu, Kexin Zhou, Jiyan He, Xiren Zhou, Huanhuan Chen, Yifei Shen

entry.summary: This paper formalizes harness self-evolution, where an agent's scaffolding (prompts, memory, workflows, executable components) is revised while model weights stay fixed. It frames the process as evolutionary optimization, provides PAC-learning-based generalization and retention bounds, and separates proposal from admission mechanisms.

entry.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models

author.name: Bince Qu, Wei Chen, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: The authors argue that coding agents with a simple robot harness, rather than large vision-language-action models, can achieve generalist embodied manipulation. RoboHarness provides LLM agents a visual-geometric control panel for understanding and invoking embodied tasks, and with it, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art VLA and world action models.

entry.title: Can We Trust This Evaluation? Instance-Level Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Yang Ba, Michelle V. Mancenido, Rong Pan

entry.summary: The authors propose SCUR, a label-free method for estimating instance-level reliability of LLM-as-a-judge panels using a latent measurement model, combining panel uncertainty, measurement cross-entropy, and perturbation sensitivity into a risk score. Evaluated on five benchmarks with majority-vote error ranking, it identifies unreliable individual judgments.

entry.title: Learnable Low-Rank Polynomial Sketch for Effective Linear Attention

author.name: Zongyue Qin, Haoran Deng, Jason Cong, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: The paper proposes a learnable low-rank sketch for polynomial-kernel linear attention, addressing the infeasibility of exact high-degree polynomial computation in high dimensions. Instead of fixed random features, the sketch is learned to better approximate the spiky softmax-like behavior that makes polynomial kernels effective. This targets the quadratic-cost bottleneck of softmax attention for long-context models.

entry.title: Target-ESS Tempered Policy Optimization (TETPO): Smooth Variance Control via Bridge Importance Sampling

author.name: Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Kayhan Behdin, Wenhui Zhu, Aida Rahmattalabi, Jincheng Cao, Jelena Markovic-Voronov, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: TETPO tackles instability in asynchronous RL post-training of LLMs, where off-policy rollouts from stale policies require heavy-tailed importance weights that can collapse effective sample size and destabilize gradients. Unlike fixed interventions, TETPO adapts correction strength to the realized severity of weight concentration using bridge importance sampling, targeting a desired ESS level. This enables smoother, more stable variance control in off-policy RLHF/RLAIF pipelines.

entry.title: A Self-Defining Operator for Distributed Applications

author.name: Shihang Li, Thomas Anderson, Ratul Mahajan, Simon Peter

entry.summary: The self-defining operator (SDO) is an LLM-based agent for operating distributed applications that accumulates experience across incidents by distilling resolved investigations into reusable playbooks and detectors that route telemetry to relevant playbooks. Unlike standard agents, it improves with each incident handled.

entry.title: Training a Compact, Strong, and Realistic Text-to-Speech Model

author.name: Runyuan Cai, Yu Lin, Yiming Wang, Xiaodong Zeng

entry.summary: Audio8-TTS is a compact 0.6B-parameter zero-shot voice cloning model achieving state-of-the-art intelligibility and speaker similarity, with particularly strong perceptual naturalness, by training against human perception rather than signal-level fidelity. It targets the persistent realism gap in TTS that scale and data quality alone cannot close.

entry.title: UDHRBench: Benchmarking Human Rights in Large Language Models

author.name: Alak Raad (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar), Noreldin Morssy (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar), Zeerak Suhail (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar), Serin Atiani (Princess Sumaya University for Technology, Jordan), Mustafa Jarrar (Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Qatar)

entry.summary: Introduces UDHRBench, a benchmark of 1,124 questions covering all 30 articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights with 4,496 expert-annotated responses from ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, and Fanar (kappa 0.801). The analysis finds systematic, non-trivial misalignments between model behavior and human rights standards.

entry.title: Adaptive Look, Flexible Thought: Learning How and How Long to Think in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Quanlin Chen, Xiuwei Chen, Kun Xiang, Zehua Ma, Chunjin Ye, Boqiang Guo, Xianming Liu, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: L2T is a unified framework for multimodal LLM reasoning that jointly optimizes visual perception and textual reasoning depth, rather than treating tool-produced visual computation as auxiliary. It discretizes tool-produced visual states into visual tokens so the model can decide both how to look and how long to think. This addresses a key inefficiency in fast-slow reasoning paradigms.

entry.title: Make Every Expansion Count: Learning to Search Efficiently in LLM Code Repair

author.name: Elad Sharony, Ido Greenberg, Jialin Song, Shie Mannor, Gal Chechik, Eli Meirom

entry.summary: CodeTriage is a small (0.6B) learned policy that prioritizes candidate code-repair edits before costly generation and testing, reading test outputs, failure diagnoses, and proposed edits to predict remaining repair effort. Unlike prior search policies based only on pass rates, it exploits failure details. This substantially improves the efficiency of LLM-based program repair search.

entry.title: Omni-Modal LLMs Know More Than They Say

author.name: Na Min An, Taekyung Kim, Jaemyung Yu, Hyunjung Shim, Dongyoon Han

entry.summary: The paper identifies a knows-but-cannot-say disconnect in omni-modal LLMs, where models correctly perceive non-textual inputs (vision, audio, IMU) but fail to express the information in responses. It introduces Token-level Modality Alignment to show non-textual representations are less aligned with and less attended to by response tokens, explaining uneven modality performance.

entry.title: BAT3R: Robust Online 3D Reconstruction with Bayesian Adaptive State Updates

author.name: Lijian Li, Yuanpeng He, Yudian Zheng, Chung-ju Huang, Linyu Li, Dongming Jin, Wenpin Jiao, Zhi Jin, Chi-Man Pun

entry.summary: BAT3R is a training-free Bayesian adaptation framework for streaming 3D reconstruction that combats error accumulation in recurrent architectures over long video sequences. It uses State Innovation Gating and Bayesian-guided Adaptive State Updating to weigh observation reliability and accumulated state confidence.

entry.title: Growing and Transferring Pathways for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haolin Tian, Yikang Li, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: GrowRL organizes RL training for LLM reasoning into compact computational pathways: it freezes the pretrained backbone and grows independent attention and feed-forward branches per layer, zero-initialized to preserve the base policy, with RL updates confined to the added pathways. The explicit pathways can then be transferred to structurally compatible models.

entry.title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization

author.name: Lihao Zheng, Zhenwei Shao, Zhou Yu, Yan Yang, Haoyi Sun, Qian Wang, Ning Mao, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: VAttnPO refines token-level credit assignment in multimodal RL with verifiable rewards by using answer-conditioned visual attention: a frozen old policy teacher-forces the correct answer to build a visual reference distribution, and Jensen-Shannon divergence in attention space modulates per-token advantages on top of the trajectory-level verifier signal. This makes changes in visual-evidence use explicit during policy optimization. It matters because outcome-level rewards alone blur which tokens actually use visual evidence.

entry.title: A Scaled-Up Empirical Study of Syntactic Language Models

author.name: Pengcheng Wang, Zhexuan Zhang, Chao Lou, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: This paper presents a large-scale controlled empirical study of syntactic language models (SLMs) that generate text jointly with syntactic tree structures, testing 12 configurations spanning tree linearization schemes and attention mask designs at up to 1B parameters and 100B tokens across 11 downstream tasks. The results clarify which architectural choices matter for SLMs, including whether standard causal attention suffices.

entry.title: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release of AI-Generated Mathematics

author.name: Ying Xie

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the 722 AI-written mathematical manuscripts OpenAI released on 6 October 2026 in its public math repository, extracting new lemmas, constructions, inequalities, and proof mechanisms (mathematical instruments) from the collection. It distinguishes genuinely new tools from recombinations of established ones, treating validity and novelty as open questions for later study. It is significant as an early scholarly assessment of AI-generated mathematics at claimed open-problem scale.

entry.title: Why Agentic Workflows Fail: A Taxonomy Derived from Literature and Empirical Data

author.name: Xin Li, Rami Bahsoon, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Presents a source-aware taxonomy of agentic LLM workflow failures, combining failure-type dictionaries, workflow-stage localization, and agent-capability localization into a two-axis matrix, validated against academic literature and GitHub evidence. It helps diagnose whether failures stem from the model, orchestration, tools, infrastructure, or their interactions. Timely and useful for the rapidly growing agentic AI engineering community.

entry.title: The belief-action gap in language model agents

author.name: Ayse Sila Okcu, Weisheng Wang, Tongmeng Xie, Niall Dalton, Angelos Nalmpantis, Raghu Arghal, Mario Giulianelli

entry.summary: Studies how state beliefs, action values, and action preferences interact in LM agents reasoning in text-rendered grid worlds, using report-based and representation-based probes plus inverse RL to estimate beliefs and values. Finds that task-relevant information is often represented more reliably than it is reflected in behavior, revealing a belief-action gap, and tracks how decisions sharpen around commitment points. Illuminates why agent failures require different interventions than knowledge gaps.

entry.title: Taming Softmax at the Limits of Muon: A Unified Approach through Hilbert Geometry

author.name: Aditya Somasundaram, Charles Guille-Escuret, Alexander Moreno, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric Xing

entry.summary: The paper argues Muon's RMS-based update control poorly proxies softmax layers and proposes Hilbert distance as a natural metric bounding changes in output distributions and cross-entropy loss. For softmax it reduces to the variation seminorm of the preactivation perturbation, yielding a new steepest-descent optimizer formulation grounded in Hilbert geometry.

entry.title: Where Small Mistakes Matter: Quantifying State Criticality for Imitation Learning

author.name: Yusuf Umut Ciftci, Joonwon Kang, Ajay Suresha Sathya, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: The paper formalizes state criticality in imitation learning as worst-case value degradation from bounded perturbations of expert actions, and proposes SCRIM, which estimates it via an adversarial disturbance policy and value critic around a fixed imitation policy. This enables weighted behavior cloning that emphasizes states where small errors are unrecoverable.

entry.title: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation

author.name: Xu Liu, Hanshu Yan, Taha Aksu, Quang Pham, Zhongzheng Qiao, Jun Hao Liew, Silvio Savarese, Doyen Sahoo, Junnan Li

entry.summary: GIFT-Eval-CTX is a benchmark of 10,000 instances across 20 datasets for evaluating whether forecasting methods can translate verified future information (planned events, external conditions, expert expectations) into accurate numerical trajectories. It addresses gaps in domain coverage, standardized splits, and informativeness of contextual text in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Match the Canvas, Not Just the Answer: Predictability-Aware SFT for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Miao Li, Hanyang Jiang, Hengyu Fu, Baihe Huang, Yating Liu, Yuhang Cai, Changkun Guan, Zhongzhu Chen, Jiecheng Lu, Michael A. Boateng, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: This paper identifies a training-inference mismatch in supervised fine-tuning of diffusion language models, where random masking choices conceal prediction errors or penalize uncertainty that decoding would otherwise resolve. The authors propose predictability-aware SFT that aligns which reference tokens are visible and how much generation space is allocated with the model's evolving predictability during parallel decoding. The work matters because diffusion LMs are an emerging alternative to autoregressive generation and standard SFT choices were inherited inappropriately.

entry.title: Certifying Almost-Sure Reachability in Unknown MDPs

author.name: S Akshay, Suguman Bansal, Gaurav Mahla

entry.summary: The authors study whether a given policy can be verified against an almost-sure reachability specification in an unknown MDP using only sampling access, via ranking supermartingale certificates. They establish negative results absent further MDP information, and positive results under additional structural assumptions.

entry.title: A Few More Tokens Ahead: Reinforcing Parallelism in Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Jiahao Kuang, Yangfan Gao, Tao Gui, Yuanbin Wu, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang, Tao Ji

entry.summary: The authors show that parallel generation in diffusion LLMs degrades severely under fixed token quotas, with all four evaluated models scoring below 15% at 16 tokens per step on math and code. They propose RePara, which uses group-relative policy optimization to reinforce short consecutive token blocks, improving GSM8K and MATH-500 accuracy on LLaDA and SDAR with a 1.96x training speedup.

entry.title: The Geometry of Language Model Logits: Generic Structure and Learned Departures

author.name: Swathi Shree Narashiman, Aravind Ramana Venkatramanan, Nambi Seshadri

entry.summary: The authors empirically show that ordered vocabulary-head logits of autoregressive language models follow a consistent log-linear decay across contexts, architectures, and scales, emerging progressively during pretraining. They systematically analyze this geometry with order-statistic baselines and identify learned departures from the generic pattern. This is the first systematic look at the logit geometry underlying distributional assumptions in prior decoding work.

entry.title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report

author.name: OneRec Team, Chenglong Chu, Guohong Mu, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Hui Wang, Jian Liang, Jiangxia Cao, Jiao Ou, Jiaxin Deng, Lu Ren, Muhao Wei, Ruiming Tang, Tianle Xu, Wenwu Ou, Xingmei Wang, Zhixin Ling, Zhiyuan Liang, Ziqi Wang, Chaoyi Ma, Haixiao Gao, Kuo Cai, Renpu Liu, Ruochen Yang, Wenlong Xu, Xinqi Jin, Yan Sun, Yifan Wang, Yingzhi He, Yiyu Wang, Yusen Huo, Zhaojie Liu, Zihan Zhou

entry.summary: This technical report from Kuaishou's OneRec team presents KSA V2, refining summary-token architectures that compress distant context into learnable summary tokens interleaved with full attention. V2 addresses bottlenecks of the hybrid KSA-Full design, including inflexible per-layer KV cache compression and wasted computation in full-attention layers. It is industrially relevant for efficient long-context serving at scale.

entry.title: From Relation-Specific Heads to Shared Interventions: Contextual Entrainment in Language Models

author.name: Jinghan Zheng, Jiajun Shi

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study examines contextual entrainment, where LLMs inappropriately reuse irrelevant earlier context tokens. Using factual-distractor prompts across 19 lexical-semantic subtypes, the authors show that ablation-relevant attention heads are shared reusable components across relations rather than relation-specific mechanisms.

entry.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics

author.name: Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara
