entry.summary: ChunkAct addresses the efficiency cost of placing an LLM agent in the robot control loop, where every primitive requires a full round of LLM reasoning over the interaction history. Observing that primitives within a chosen sub-goal follow routines already stored in memory, it launches chunks of chained primitives with a single call that then execute autonomously. This transfers the action-chunking idea from learned policies to LLM-driven agentic robotics.

entry.title: Reward-Aligned Distillation

author.name: Yilan Chen, Zian Su, Manish Prajapat, Dingmin Wang, Rein Houthooft, Rui Song, Vijay Lingam

entry.summary: RAD is a bilevel framework for on-policy distillation that weights token-level teacher supervision by its predicted effect on the student's post-update reward, instead of distilling every token equally. It differentiates through a temporary optimization step, addressing a key sample-efficiency gap versus RL with verifiable rewards in LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Terrarium: Growing Personal Assistants via Scalable Synthesis of App Worlds

author.name: Mengzhou Wu, Yuzhe Guo, Jiawen Tao, Xiaokun Yuan, Yuan Cao, Gang Cao, Yuetang Deng, Zhi Gong, Dezhi Ran, Linyi Li, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: Terrarium is a framework that synthesizes executable simulated app worlds from real-world application information, generates training tasks with evaluator-side rubrics, and iteratively refines both through agent rollouts. This tackles a key bottleneck for training LLM-based personal assistants: real apps restrict access and are hard to reset. The approach enables scalable training and evaluation environments for assistant agents.

entry.title: Conformal Sequential Decision Making With Cost and Sublinear Policy Regret Guarantees

author.name: Jayadev Naram, Giuseppe Durisi, Matteo Zecchin, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The authors propose OCEA, an online conformal episodic agent for sequential decision problems with hard per-episode cost constraints (e.g., safety violations, energy) and arbitrary state sequences. The method provides both cost satisfaction and sublinear regret against a reference policy. This bridges conformal prediction and safe sequential control, relevant to AI agents operating robots or network devices.

entry.title: Generalizable Model Editing Could Be More Than Direct Generalization

author.name: Xiaotian Ye, Chunyao Yang, Xiaohan Wang, Junkai Chen, Yongqi Duan, Mengqi Zhang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: The paper challenges the prevailing direct-generalization paradigm in LLM model editing, showing that classical editing methods exhibit surprisingly fluent generalization in in-the-wild chatbot-user settings. The authors argue that direct generalization is fundamentally limited as a formalization and propose reframing how editing generalization is evaluated.

entry.title: Backward Conformal Prediction under Covariate Shift

author.name: Amin Meghrazi, Yuanyuan Li

entry.summary: This paper extends backward conformal prediction (BCP), which fixes prediction set size and estimates miscoverage, to covariate shift settings via importance weighting. The authors show BCP's miscoverage report depends only on relative weights of missed calibration examples, explaining counterintuitive cases where better domain classifiers yield worse estimates. They propose estimating density ratios on sorted score vectors rather than high-dimensional inputs, with asymptotic guarantees.

entry.title: From Simulated Fluids to Living Tissue: Zero-Shot Foundation Model Transfer to Perturbed Embryos

author.name: Louisa Cornelis, Haewon Jeong, Irina Espejo, Payel Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune Walrus, a continuum dynamics foundation model pretrained on simulated continuous systems, on tissue velocity fields from only 12 wild-type Drosophila blastoderm videos, testing transfer to perturbed embryo conditions. This exploits the fact that tissue-scale Drosophila dynamics can be described as continuum flow, enabling cross-domain physical priors. The work evaluates autoregressive prediction in-distribution and zero-shot under mutations and environmental perturbations.

entry.title: Learning Operators for Symmetry Discovery: From Lie Groups to Local Symmetry Geometry

author.name: Pavan Karjol, Scindhiya Laxmi, Prathosh AP

entry.summary: This work frames symmetry discovery as learning an inverse symmetry operator that maps functions to their continuous symmetry structure, analogously to inverse PDE problems. It provides a representation-theoretic population characterization for Lie-group symmetries and extends the framework to local symmetry geometry learned across families of functions.

entry.title: TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings

author.name: F\'elix Lefebvre, David Holzm\"uller, Gioia Blayer, Myung Jun Kim, Marine Le Morvan, Ga\"el Varoquaux

entry.summary: TILE introduces a table-interfaced way to extract LLM embeddings for heterogeneous tables containing both numeric and free-form string columns, showing that the LLM-table interface matters as much as the LLM itself: with the right interface, larger LLMs consistently help, unlike naive cell-wise encodings. It combines row selection and other ingredients to feed LLM representations into table foundation models.

entry.title: CodeLift: Your Test Suite Is Secretly a Dense SWE Curriculum

author.name: Junjielong Xu, Huachao Zhu, Alyssa Wu, Zhichao Hu, Pinjia He

entry.summary: CodeLift is an RL method for software engineering agents that dynamically calibrates pass-rate rewards, since raw test pass-rate is an unreliable proxy for patch quality. It groups tests that kill the same patches and patches that pass the same tests, weighting test groups adaptively to form a curriculum from the existing test suite. This attacks the sparse binary reward problem in SWE-agent training.

entry.title: Two For The Price Of One: Curvature-Aware Pruning Preserves Influence Functions Too

author.name: Mehdi Makni, Natalia Ponomareva, Rahul Mazumder

entry.summary: The paper introduces CACTUS, an ADMM-based pruning optimizer with a curvature-aware objective that preserves both layer activations and backpropagated gradients, connecting compression quality to influence-function fidelity. It shows that pruning can simultaneously preserve downstream performance and gradient-information retention, compared against methods like LLM-Surgeon.

entry.title: TartanMatch: Towards Universal Dense Correspondence Across Modalities

author.name: Hyeokjoon Kwon, Jiting Cai, Ruogu Li, Kritan Bhandari, Geethika Hemkumar, Parv Maheshwari, Yuheng Qiu, Yuchen Zhang, Sebastian Scherer, Wenshan Wang

entry.summary: TartanMatch is a single unified model for dense correspondence across all 25 ordered modality pairs among RGB, event cameras, thermal, depth, and projected LiDAR, adapting an RGB-pretrained correspondence network with lightweight modality adaptation. It reduces endpoint error on zero-shot real-world benchmarks versus strong baselines. This is significant for multi-sensor robotics where training per-pair models scales poorly.

entry.title: CoLA: Multi-VLA Coordination via Learned Adapters

author.name: Ahaskar Kashyap, Jiawen Zong, Boyu Ma, Chuhao Zhou, Jingliang Li, Stefano V. Albrecht, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Introduces CoLA, which keeps vision-language-action model backbones frozen and trains lightweight learned message channels plus per-arm diffusion action heads for decentralized multi-robot coordination. Across tasks varying in observability, explicit communication proves necessary only when information is private, such as an occluded tray handover where one agent alone sees a color marker.

entry.title: Inference on the Value of Policy Improvement in Adaptive Experiments

author.name: Justin Whitehouse, Emma Brunskill, Vasilis Syrgkanis

entry.summary: The authors develop an asymptotically normal estimator for the value of policy improvement (VPI) under adaptively collected data, handling correlated samples, decaying propensities, and non-regularity when the optimal policy is non-unique. This enables principled inference on whether deploying a personalized treatment policy is worthwhile.

entry.title: Gluing Local Contexts into Global Meaning: A Sheaf-Theoretic Decomposition of Transformer Representations

author.name: Bryce Grant, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Builds a cellular sheaf over a paraphrase graph of transformer activations whose Laplacian defines a content subspace without training; at 20 dimensions it outperforms the LEACE concept-eraser subspace on held-out CounterFact fact retrieval by +17.1 pp across eight architectures. The spectral complement also concentrates causal influence useful for locating model behavior.

entry.title: Monitoring for Shifts at Unknown Times: Parameter-Free Conditional Conformal Martingales

author.name: Tuo Liu, Drew Prinster, Francesco Orabona

entry.summary: This work improves conditional conformal test martingales for detecting distribution shifts at unknown times by reframing penalized betting as portfolio selection in a three-asset market with a restarting universal portfolio and heavy-tailed wealth allocation. The resulting method requires no hyperparameters and provably adapts quickly to shifts after long stationary periods, with anytime false-alarm control. It is a clean theoretical contribution to sequential change detection and conformal methods.

entry.title: Encoding Context into LLM Weights: What Makes It Context?

author.name: Yue Wang, Qizhou Wang, Feng Liu, Gang Niu, Masashi Sugiyama, Bo Han

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time updates that encode context into LLM weights as an alternative to long in-context prompts, noting that encoding into knowledge-bearing weights obscures the information's contextual role. The authors associate encoded context with an identifier so it can be invoked and recited at inference, and analyze what distinguishes genuine context from baked-in knowledge. This touches a fundamental question about the boundary between parametric knowledge and context in LLMs.

entry.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Ziyu Wan, Nanye Ma, Long Zhao, Dong Chen, Hongyu Liu, Qifeng Chen, Dongdong Chen

entry.summary: The authors show that simple on-policy velocity regression alone provides a strong basis for 4-NFE diffusion generation, and enhance it with Pivot, a training-only residual proxy capturing teacher velocity variation, plus a mechanism repelling students from weak teacher predictions. The resulting SMD framework is entirely regression-based, requiring no auxiliary score models or specialized architectures.

entry.title: TL;QR: Querying Temporal Discursive Patterns in Textual Corpora

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois Hublet, Vladimir Krsmanovic, Jesus Solano, Ahmed Bouhoula, Ana Oliveira da Costa

entry.summary: TL;QR is a declarative query language and open-source engine for finding temporal discursive patterns in large text corpora, combining LLM-judged natural-language predicates with regular expressions and temporal logic operators. A symbolic engine aggregates local LLM judgments over time while keeping every match auditable against underlying passages.

entry.title: More Reasoning Is Not Always Better: Executing Clinical Guidelines with LLMs and Rules

author.name: Xiaoqian Lu, Guangfu Guo, Long Cheng, Kunpeng Liu

entry.summary: MedDEx separates clinical record interpretation (handled by LLMs) from guideline execution (handled by a deterministic rule executor), arguing that heavy multi-step reasoning or multi-agent setups add overhead without reliably preventing errors. Experiments show the hybrid achieves better guideline-based treatment planning with less computation.

entry.title: Strong yet Controllable LLM Abstention without Learning to Abstain

author.name: Junwei Zhang, Yifei Wang, Wanli Yang, Hexiang Tan, Rui Tang, Xin Chen, Jingang Wang, Du Su, Fei Sun

entry.summary: The paper decomposes abstention risk into answering ability and distinguishing ability, showing that abstention training improves performance mainly by improving answering rather than abstention discrimination. This motivates selective answering with strong confidence estimators, which retains the flexible coverage control that fixed-coverage abstention training lacks.

entry.title: PIG: Parallel Inconsistency Guidance for Accelerating Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Quentin Fruytier, Anton Xue, Sanjay Shakkottai, Sujay Sanghavi

entry.summary: PIG uses an auxiliary trained model to estimate, in a single forward pass, the inconsistency between parallel and sequential decoding trajectories in diffusion language models, adding tokens to the parallel decode set until estimated inconsistency stays acceptable. This mitigates the accuracy degradation of parallel decoding while retaining its speed benefits.

entry.title: Attacking Only Half the Data: Two-Sided Evaluation of AI-Text Detector Robustness

author.name: Apu Chandraw Shill, Rabindra Nath Nandi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a two-sided attack protocol for evaluating AI-text detectors, applying perturbations to both machine and human text rather than only machine text. Across two corpora and nine detectors, reported AUROC gains vanish, with attacked human text misclassified at rates up to 100%, and word-level synonym substitution remains an irreversible, meaning-preserving attack. This substantially weakens confidence in current AI-text detection.

entry.title: Retrieval Disagreement as a Signal: Diagnosing and Steering Multilingual Dense Embedders

author.name: Faeze Ghorbanpour, Shaghayegh Kolli, Jana Diesner, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: The authors show that multilingual dense retrievers return substantially different documents for the same question in different languages, and trace this to shared-index interference rather than weak per-language understanding. They diagnose the mechanism in the shared embedding space and use retrieval disagreement as a signal for steering. This is a useful contribution to making multilingual retrieval more reliable.

entry.title: StateHarness: Maintaining Evolving Project State for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Chuan Zou, Yujun Zhou, Xiaonan Luo, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes StateHarness, a training-free runtime framework that helps coding agents maintain an evolving view of project state, including current problem, hypotheses, findings, repository relationships, and unresolved work. Runtime prompts record and retrieve state to keep long-horizon edits connected to their consequences.

entry.title: Learning Transferable World-Action Models from Task-Paired Human Videos

author.name: Jeongeun Park, Taekyung Kim, Dongyoon Han, Sangdoo Yun

entry.summary: Introduces WATCH, a cross-video pre-training approach where a world-action model conditioned on one human demonstration predicts another demonstration's actions and future frames, discouraging reliance on appearance shared within a single video. This encourages learning task-relevant interactions that transfer across scenes and embodiments.

entry.title: Adversarial Gradient Forcing for Robust Few-Step Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Chenxi Xia, Yixuan Xu, Shan Liu, Jiapeng Wang, Maohua Li, Hanlin Tang, Kan Liu, Tao Lan, Weiyi Lu, Xinggao Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a local history robustness gap in autoregressive video generation: models remain highly sensitive to small errors in their generated history, amplifying them over long horizons. Adversarial Gradient Forcing trains on perturbed rollouts to harden models against this error accumulation, extending Self Forcing-style training.

entry.title: VideoEvoHarness: Self Evolving Agent Harness from Unlabeled Videos for Video Understanding

author.name: Weixin Xu, Yifan Liu, Yi Wang, Mingfei Rong, Zhenyu Yang, Zhisheng Zhong, Shengsheng Qian, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: VideoEvoHarness jointly evolves a Questioner and Solver agent harness from unlabeled videos with frozen model parameters, requiring no annotated question-answer pairs. The Questioner derives questions and reference answers from video memory records, with quality assessments and execution trajectories guiding policy revision.

entry.title: PhySimCode: A Benchmark and Evaluation Method for Physics Video to Code Generation

author.name: Souraja Kundu, Aditya Gupta, Joel Julin, Yizhou Zhao, Liuyue Xie, Laszlo A. Jeni

entry.summary: PhySimCode benchmarks whether multimodal LLMs can recover physical laws underlying videos by translating visual dynamics into runnable simulation code, going beyond plausibility and future-prediction evaluations. It tests dynamics inference, quantitative parameter estimation, and scene regeneration from code.

entry.title: Data-Centric Recursive Self-Improvement for Navigation via Policy-Synchronized Language-Action Dual Bootstrapping

author.name: Songze Li, Haoming Gu, Ziyang Gong, Zhitong Wang, Gengze Zhou, Zun Wang, Yuhan Zhu, Tianxiang Jiang, Juanzi Li, Qi Wu, Weinan Zhang, Yu Qiao, Wenwei Zhang, Yi Wang

entry.summary: RSI-Nav is a recursive self-improvement framework for vision-language navigation that unifies policy and instruction generation, synchronizing supervision data with the evolving policy instead of annotating trajectories with a fixed model. This dual bootstrapping reduces supervision lag and the cost of human annotation for navigation agents.

entry.title: Geometric Parrots: Rule Absence vs. Rule Fragility in Spatial and Physical Reasoning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bilal Jawaid, Hamza Hanif, Muhammad Maaz Uddin, Anas Zafar, Inad Alqurashi, Aizan Zafar, Osama Farooqui, Sheheryar Khan, Ferhat Sadak, Shaina Raza, Rizwan Qureshi

entry.summary: The paper introduces GRIP, a controlled benchmark with 34 procedurally generated reasoning domains, 100,000 images, and 600,000 questions for geometric, spatial, visual, and physical reasoning, with exact ground truth derived from deterministic scene code. It probes whether VLMs capitulate to confident but incorrect user assertions, distinguishing fragile correctness from beneficial correction via multi-turn interaction.

entry.title: ClothAtlas: Joint Garment Identification and State Estimation under Self-Occlusion

author.name: Jens Lundell, Alberta Longhini, Lei Shu, Hemal Arora, Evan Robert, Carlota Par\'es-Morlans, Marcel B\"usching, M{\aa}rten Bj\"orkman, Jeannette Bohg

entry.summary: ClothAtlas jointly identifies garments and estimates their complete configurations from partial point clouds using a shared graph-conditioned flow-matching model that samples candidate configurations from a library of canonical meshes and ranks them by observation fit. The approach handles varying mesh shapes and topologies so new garments can be added without retraining.

entry.title: Teaching Vision-Language Models to Decline: Support Completion Against Mirage

author.name: Alfaj Uddin Ahmed, Md. Shaown Miah, Md Arid Hasan, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury

entry.summary: Formalizes the mirage failure where VLMs answer questions about images they were never shown, showing cross-entropy training rewards image-blind predictors by only the conditional mutual information between answer and image. The proposed TIDE scheme trains with blank, same-domain wrong, and out-of-domain images paired with decline targets, and proves every image-blind predictor is strictly suboptimal under it.

entry.title: Image Tokenizers Should Be Trained Between Images

author.name: Ole Bei{\ss}wenger, Jan-Niklas Dihlmann, Hendrik Lensch

entry.summary: InterpTok argues that latent diffusion decoders should be robust not to noise but to codes lying between training codes, since generators produce interpolated mixture-like codes. The paper proposes training tokenizers on codes sampled in the space between training samples, improving generated image quality over noise-augmentation approaches.

entry.title: UniMetric: Universal Metric Scale Recovery for Visual Geometry Foundation Models

author.name: Lei Yang, Yuner Zhang, Ziyang Liu, Ziying Song, Kai WU, Yiyang Gao, Jiangtao Su, Yiming Li

entry.summary: UniMetric is a training-free framework that recovers metric scale for visual geometry foundation models by jointly constraining a reconstruction's shared scale using uncertain size priors of familiar objects, without extra sensors or task-specific metric supervision. It supports reliable physical-scale annotation for embodied pretraining from internet videos, motivated by general-purpose embodied reasoning models such as GPT-6 Astra, which has been available since September 2026.

entry.title: EgoProbe: Benchmarking Long-Range and Exact Memory in Streaming Egocentric Videos

author.name: Haokai Pang, Yuqian Fu, Yifei Wang, Yujiao Shen, Tianwen Qian, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Hongbo Fu

entry.summary: EgoProbe is a new benchmark evaluating streaming egocentric video memory along two complementary dimensions: long-range retention (how far back models can recall) and event-specific exact recall (which detail belongs to which recurring object, action, or location). It targets the memory requirements of wearable AI assistants that must process observations online and answer queries about distant past experiences.

entry.title: PLEDGE: Progressive Lossy Error-Bounded Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Mingze Xia, Yuxiao Li, Baixi Sun, Wenbo Li, Pu Jiao, Sheng Di, Franck Cappello, Hanqi Guo, Xin Liang

entry.summary: PLEDGE is a training-free, progressive, error-bounded codec for 3D Gaussian Splatting that translates four user-declared tolerances into per-primitive quantization bounds valid across a camera domain including unseen viewpoints, organizing residuals into a progressive bitstream. This gives users explicit distortion control that existing 3DGS codecs lack.

entry.title: Web Scale on a Budget: Tail-Aware Retrieval Evaluation

author.name: Boaz Meivar, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: The paper shows that instance-retrieval evaluation obeys a scaling law, with the number of distractors outranking a positive being Binomial in gallery size, enabling a gallery-scale-agnostic per-query hardness measure. This avoids the expensive full indexing of web-scale distractor sets like ILIAS's 100M images, saving hundreds of GPU-hours per model.

entry.title: VARI: Robust Text-to-Video Generation via Group-Structured Intent Alignment

author.name: Mingxuan Zhu, Hohei Chan, Shiyuan Liu, Yuanxing Zhang, Lu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces VARI, a group-structured post-training framework that treats verified paraphrases of the same visual intent as a shared supervision unit for text-to-video models. By cross-scoring videos against all equivalent prompt forms and applying wording-independent intent alignment, it improves robustness to prompt rewording. Targets a real reliability weakness of current T2V systems.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Deepfake Detection via Distance-Speech Consistency

author.name: Kyeongrae Kim, Kim Sung-Bin, Oh Hyun-Bin, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-aware talking-head deepfake detector that exploits the acoustic constraint that speech energy varies predictably with speaker-to-camera distance in real recordings, a coupling that generative fakes typically break. Unlike lip-sync detectors, it remains robust in dynamic, in-the-wild videos where lip cues are degraded or missing. A novel physical signal for media forensics with safety relevance.

entry.title: Segment Where You Look: Attention as the Interface Between Language Models and Segmenters

author.name: Eslam Abdelrahman, Hamza Omar Alkaf, Yuheng Li, Siddharth Srinivasan Iyer, Nanxuan Zhao, Eli Shechtman, Krishna Kumar Singh, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: This paper shows that in segmentation-capable vision-language models, the attention map of the [SEG] token over image tokens carries a much better localization signal than the token's hidden state that dominates current architectures. Probing a frozen model, attention yields 18-22 more gIoU than the hidden state under the same probe, suggesting attention should be the interface between the VLM and pixel decoders.

entry.title: ClothCode: Generative Modeling for Garment State Estimation and Dynamics Prediction

author.name: Yingdong Ru, Lipeng Zhuang, Shiyu Fan, Zhuo He, Florent P. Audonnet, Gerardo Aragon Camarasa

entry.summary: ClothCode is a unified generative framework for garment state estimation and action-conditioned dynamics prediction using a material-aligned residual VQ tokenizer and masked generative transformers with confidence-guided parallel refinement. It cuts mean displacement error by 26.6-37% versus baselines and predicts dynamics in 16.7 ms versus 556 ms for diffusion, improving real-world robotic cloth folding. Deformable object manipulation is a notoriously hard robotics problem, making this a notable advance.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Cortical Surface Reconstruction and Spherical Registration for Heterogeneous Brain MRI

author.name: Jesper Duemose Nielsen, Karthik Gopinath, Andrew Hoopes, Adrian Dalca, Axel Thielscher, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Oula Puonti

entry.summary: The paper presents a neural network for cortical surface reconstruction and spherical registration trained exclusively on synthetic MRI with random contrast and resolution, enabling application to nearly any MRI protocol rather than only 1mm T1-weighted scans. The model outputs vertex-wise uncertainty estimates and registration to fsaverage space, performing on par with existing state-of-the-art methods. This broadens surface-based brain analysis to heterogeneous clinical and research data.

entry.title: Code2Worlds-2: Physically Plausible Agent Harness for Embodied World Simulation

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Siming Li, Zeyu Zhang, Yi Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua, Hao Tang

entry.summary: Code2Worlds-2 extends LLM-driven 4D world generation into executable embodied simulation by adding a SimReady Scene Compiler that produces physically loadable collision geometry, mass, friction, inertia, and joint structure, plus an agent harness. The result is a world that a physics engine can load and step rather than a merely visually plausible scripted artifact. This bridges the gap between generative world synthesis and usable simulation environments.

entry.title: DexStitch: Learning and Composing Dexterous Skills from Human Videos via Contact-Aware Robotic Inpainting

author.name: Byeonggyeol Choi, Seongmin Jung, Unghui Nam, Youngbo Song, Sunhong Min, MinHyung Lee, Byonghyo Shim, Yongseok Lee

entry.summary: DexStitch converts long-horizon human manipulation videos into robot-executable skill sequences by segmenting videos into skills and transitions, converting human demonstrations into aligned robot observation-action-skill data via contact-aware robotic inpainting, and stitching learned skills into requested sequences. It addresses the costly supervision needed for both primitive skills and the transitions connecting them. This advances using human video as scalable supervision for compositional robot manipulation.

entry.title: FidLIF: Parallel Training of High-Fidelity Spiking Neurons with Exact BPTT

author.name: Kaixiang He, Yujie Wu

entry.summary: FidLIF enables full-sequence parallel training of spiking neural networks with exact BPTT, reconciling the incremental-update and hard-reset behavior of standard LIF neurons with parallelism. Unlike prior approaches that approximate spiking dynamics or use memory-hungry iterative fixed-point solvers, it preserves faithful LIF dynamics while removing the sequential bottleneck. This advances energy-efficient neuromorphic training on long sequences.

entry.title: In View or Out of View? A Vision-Aware Filter that Infers and Reacts to the Human's Field of View

author.name: Mengxue Fu, Ya-Chuan Hsu, Yinlong Dai, Erdem B{\i}y{\i}k, Dylan P. Losey

entry.summary: This paper enables robots to infer what a human has and has not seen during interaction and apply this estimate as a vision-aware filter on robot actions, unlike prior planners that assume full observability or always keep the robot visible. By accounting for the human's field of view, robots can better manage human uncertainty about robot intent.

entry.title: StreamingWAM: Streaming World Action Modeling via Chunk-Wise Staircase Flow Matching

author.name: Shaojie Ren, Jingwen Sun, Zezhi Liu, Hongjin Chen, Xin Jin, Wei Zou, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: StreamingWAM is a streaming-diffusion framework for world action model-based robot control, combining a noise ladder for chunk-wise action prediction, a prefix rollout module for cross-chunk continuity, and dense video-history memory to jointly address inference efficiency and jerky, discontinuous execution. It targets real-time, temporally consistent control built on pretrained video-generation world models.

entry.title: P-BFM: Perceptive Behavioral Foundation Models for Humanoid Control via Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xue Wang, Yitang Li, Yiming Zhang, Siqin Wang, Junhan Sun, Zhihao Liu, Yaojie Shen, Jingbo Yuan, Hao Zhao, Qingdu Li

entry.summary: P-BFM factorizes humanoid control into terrain-invariant intent and terrain-conditioned realization, using a forward-backward representation to map motion references, target states, and rewards into a shared intent space without terrain information. A perceptive policy then realizes each intent under actual terrain constraints, avoiding combinatorial enumeration of behavior-terrain pairs. This is a substantial step toward reusable humanoid behavior repertoires.

entry.title: Declarative Reactive Robot Behaviors from Imperative Language Models

author.name: Vincent Berenz, Tasha Kim, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM-based coding agents can generate declarative, reactive robot behavior programs — open-ended sensory-motor patterns with no termination condition — despite LLMs being trained almost exclusively on imperative code. Using Playful, a reactive scripting language, the authors show an LLM agent can produce correct declarative/reactive programs, bridging a fundamental mismatch between LLM training distribution and behavior-oriented robot programming. This complements the dominant plan/task-centric uses of LLMs in robotics.

entry.title: Smoothness Ranks Skill, Not Success: An Audit of Published Trajectory-Smoothness Curation Metrics Under Episode-Length Controls

author.name: Jaiveer Bassi

entry.summary: This audit re-examines trajectory-smoothness metrics (Spectral Arc Length and Trajectory-Envelope Distance) recently proposed as training-free signals for curating imitation-learning demonstrations, testing them on real robomimic data with episode-length controls. The results show the metrics are confounded by episode duration: SAL's apparent discrimination (AUROC 0.952) is matched or beaten by raw episode length alone, and within duration-matched bands SAL drops to 0.628 while the baseline mean jerk it was argued against rises to 0.896; on fixed-length data SAL is at chance and TED is inverted. The paper's takeaway is that these smoothness metrics rank operator skill rather than task success.

entry.title: Acting Through Registers

author.name: Yiwei Zhang, Yantai Yang, Jin Gao, Jin Lou, Andong Chen, Yufei Liu, Boyang Xing, Yuchen Zhu, Weiming Hu, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies how World Action Models (WAMs) organize action-relevant information, identifying persistent high-norm spatial outliers in their representations whose action relevance survives normalization and K/V projection. RegisterWAM adds learnable non-spatial registers used directly for action conditioning, and shows that pairing registers with observation flow-matching loss suppresses spatial outliers while concentrating high-norm responses in registers.

entry.title: LynxScenes: A Large-Scale Real-World Benchmark for Outdoor Wheel-Legged Robot Perception, Navigation, Imagination and Reconstruction

author.name: Jun Tian, Hao Wu, Ruo Chen, Yili Liao, Hongyi Lin, Jincheng Yu, Chao Li, Yingjie Niu

entry.summary: LynxScenes is a large-scale real-world dataset and benchmark from a LYNX M20 wheel-legged robot, containing about 100K 30-second navigation clips spanning 833.6 hours and 3,294.7 km, with 3.0M annotated frames, four fisheye cameras, dual LiDARs, IMU, and robot states, plus 20.82M oriented 3D boxes across 27 categories. It uniquely supports perception, socially compliant navigation, future-scene reasoning, and reconstruction together on a real wheel-legged platform.

entry.title: Walk Like This: Stylized Locomotion for Physics-Based Characters through Example-Driven Diffusion

author.name: Joshua Aurand, Agon Serifi, Sammy Christen, Ruben Grandia, Espen Knoop, Marco Hutter, Moritz B\"acher

entry.summary: This work presents a real-time framework for legged locomotion with independent control of velocity and style, using a style encoder trained on unstructured motion data to condition an autoregressive diffusion model that generates kinematic references for an RL tracking controller. Users supply a style reference clip and joystick commands at inference, and the method generalizes to unseen styles without explicit style labels.

entry.title: EgoMatrix: Physically Faithful Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Egocentric Human Videos

author.name: Ziheng Wang, Yanming Shao, Ting Mao, Kaihan Chen, Yiqun Wang, Xuanye Wu, Yao Mu

entry.summary: EgoMatrix is an end-to-end data engine converting monocular egocentric human videos into bimanual dexterous robot trajectories paired with robot observation videos, directly replayable on real hardware. It reconstructs hand-object interaction emphasizing relative geometry and contact rather than exact metric scene recovery, then uses retargeting and RL to reproduce the demonstrated behavior.

entry.title: Detecting NSFW and Harmful Prompts Through Geometry: Learning What's Safe Instead of What's Harmful

author.name: Igor Maljkovic

entry.summary: The post presents HyPE, an ICLR 2026-accepted harmful-prompt detector that uses hyperbolic geometry and learns only a single parameter from benign prompts, inverting the usual approach of modeling harmful content. It also introduces HyPS, a prompt sanitizer that identifies and replaces harmful words while preserving meaning, with strong performance against paraphrase and adversarial attacks on vision-language models.

entry.title: SAT-RL: Training Language Models for Logical Reasoning with Symbolic Solvers

author.name: Jialiang Sun, Kuldeep Meel

entry.summary: SAT-RL is a reinforcement learning framework training LLMs to interact with symbolic satisfiability solvers through multi-turn tool execution, using synthetic data with verifiable solutions and supervised warm-up. It aims to overcome the curse of complexity in LLM logical reasoning by leveraging scalable, verifiable solver reasoning.

entry.title: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents

author.name: Jinlong Luo, Haoran Wu, Bo Xu

entry.summary: DSABench evaluates agents on the full multi-database problem: discovering needed databases from a catalog, coordinating cross-source results, and executing workflows, rather than assuming a given target database. It provides 815 human-reviewed tasks built on Spider, BIRD, and LiveSQLBench, with executable contracts and a RouteEnv for catalog inspection.

entry.title: Belief Embedding Tree Search

author.name: Christopher Solinas, Radovan Halu\v{s}ka, Martin Schmid, Michael Buro, Nathan R. Sturtevant, Michael Bowling

entry.summary: Proposes representing POMDP beliefs as learned embeddings rather than sampled state sets within Monte Carlo tree search, so that approximate beliefs and value estimates live in a continuous learned space. This reframes belief-state planning to leverage function approximation inside the search tree, addressing the intractability of exact planning over continuous belief MDPs.

entry.title: When Skills Remain But Access Fails: Factorized Skill Memory for Continual Skill Internalization

author.name: Haomiao Qiu, Yining Tang, Hongyi Wan, Changfeng Sun, Ziyue Qiao, Miao Zhang

entry.summary: This work studies forgetting in continual skill internalization for LLM agents, revealing a hierarchical failure structure: models first lose the ability to invoke an old skill from a raw request while a canonical name cue restores it, and only later lose the behavior itself. It proposes factorized skill memory to address these staged failures.

entry.title: Revocation Is Not Complete at Receipt: An Executable Outcome Contract for Distributed Agent-Tool Gateways

author.name: Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Danping Zhang

entry.summary: The paper defines C0-C5, a bounded outcome contract characterizing when credential revocation in distributed agent workflows is truly complete, spanning issuer commit through effect prevention across cached authorities at tool gateways. It implements a persistent monitor with a 14-case fault matrix and shows that naively treating intermediate states as completion yields several false positives. This formalizes a real safety gap as agents delegate authority across distributed tool infrastructure.

entry.title: Coupled Harness--Model Evolution for Scientific Equation Discovery

author.name: Pengze Li, Jiaquan Zhang, Encheng Su, Yunbo Long, Zihang Zeng, Xinping Liu, Han Zhang, Junchi Yu, Shixiang Tang, Aoran Wang, Xi Chen

entry.summary: This work proposes a coupled evolution framework for LLM-based scientific equation discovery that jointly improves both the executable tool library and the model tool-use policy from a single verifiable fit-error signal. An agent grows the toolset from generic primitives while the policy adapts in parallel, correcting failures that fixed-tool or fixed-model systems cannot address.

entry.title: LLM Agents for Automated Post-Training via Structured Recipe Optimization

author.name: Ruohong Liu, Bohan Tang, Lekang Jiang, Jack Umenberger, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: The paper introduces optimization over a task-adapted recipe space for automated LLM post-training, where agents construct and optimize coupled decisions over data sources, processing, composition, and training configuration within a limited experiment budget. It aims to combine the systematic reuse of predefined search spaces with the adaptivity of open-ended agents.

entry.title: A Geometric Perspective on Reward Function Updates in Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Anish Diwan, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

entry.summary: The paper reframes reward updates in inverse reinforcement learning from a Lagrangian, gradient-based view to an occupancy-space geometric view, showing that geometry along the e-geodesic toward optimal occupancy directly affects gradient quality. Credible authors from the RL community (Diwan, Peters, Arenz) connect this geometry to algorithm design.

entry.title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation

author.name: Yeobin Hong, Hyojun Go, Dohun Lee, Jeongjae Lee, Sunghwan Hong, Federico Tombari, Zhaochong An, Jong Chul Ye, Konrad Schindler, Dominik Narnhofer

entry.summary: GeoFix improves geometric consistency of video-diffusion-based 4D generation using a single cross-view depth-consistency reward applied to static scene regions, avoiding the appearance degradation typical of multi-reward post-training. The reward is applicable both during training and at inference-time reward alignment. It targets structural inconsistencies without constraining appearance or penalizing valid object motion.

entry.title: Too Late to Prune: Generative AI, the Screen, and Team Creative Decisions

author.name: Difang Huang, Shumin Yu, Fadong Chen, Weihua Zhou

entry.summary: Through a preregistered experiment with 148 three-person teams randomly assigned to five schedules of LLM access during a product-design task, the authors show that moving the same 15 minutes of model access from the search phase to the selection phase lowered expert-rated creativity by 0.62 standard deviations. The results support a model where AI's value depends on whether its options arrive before or after a team's screening competition.

entry.title: Accuracy and Uncertainty in Machine Deception Detection (Research White Paper)

author.name: Heng-Sheng Chang

entry.summary: A white paper proposing a Machine Deception Detector that reads all layers of a language model's internal activations to catch deceptive responses, learns which tokens carry deception evidence from response labels only, and calibrates alarm thresholds for prescribed false-positive rates. An ensemble of detectors quantifies the uncertainty of individual alarms.

entry.title: Personalized LLM Recommendation with Semantic IDs: Autoregressive Beam Search vs. Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Sejoon Oh, Fernando Amat Gil, Evan Smothers, Dan Iter, Mark Thornburg, Dawit Mureja Argaw, Sourabh Medapati, Thea Wang, Ria Verma, Qiuling Xu, Harshit Syal, Ehsan Gholami, Moumita Bhattacharya, Ashish Rastogi

entry.summary: This industry-authored paper compares decoding strategies for LLM-based recommenders that generate hierarchical Semantic IDs of items: autoregressive constrained beam search versus multi-token prediction with parallel heads. It studies the accuracy-latency tradeoff in large-scale personalization where a single model unifies retrieval and content understanding. The analysis informs how production recommenders should generate SIDs.

entry.title: InfoVis: Unified Slide Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Xiyan Jiang, Chenyuan Wu, Haoqiang Zhang, Xin Luo, Yueze Wang, Defu Lian, Bo Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Zheng Liu

entry.summary: InfoVis unifies slide image generation and editing by formulating four slide-centric tasks, building a large data engine with over 13M continual-pretraining and 1.9M supervised fine-tuning records, and training a model covering text rendering, instruction following, grounding, design, and precise editing. It also releases VisSlideBench, a 1,527-instance benchmark with multidimensional evaluation validated against human rankings. It matters because slide generation demands a rare combination of capabilities in one canvas.

entry.title: Proactive Physical AI through Continuous Observation and Timely Intervention

author.name: Zhenhua Yang, Jiafeng Liang, Xingyu Zhou, Yi Jiang, Xiayu Cao, Zui Chen, Luqi Wang, Haiyang Sun, Yufei Xiang, Chang Li, Rongchuan Mu, Bowen Chi, Zihe Tong, Mingyu Li, Huijie Ma, Yiqiao Yang, Baoqi Ren, Zhiming Ma, Zhihao Zhu, Jiahao Ji, Zhuoyao Wang, Qianyu Wang, Xiangyu Liu, Wang Zixiang, Shunliang Zhang, Ming Liu, Xiaocheng Feng, Duyu Tang, Bing Qin

entry.summary: This paper formulates Proactive Physical AI, where a system continuously observes the physical world, decides whether and when intervention is warranted, and acts without an explicit user-specified task, and builds ProAgent with a StreamingJev proactive timing model plus a response model for people-facing actions. It matters because most physical AI assumes explicitly given goals, while real-world tasks often emerge from changing world states before a human formulates them.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning

author.name: Li-Ching Chen, Andr\'es Franco Valiente, Yuta Ishiyama, Zachary R. Chalmers, William Chen, Kelsey Natsuhara, Taema Brinjikji, Madhumita Sushil, Travis Zack, Julian C. Hong

entry.summary: Tackles clinical reasoning beyond question answering by applying RL to oncology treatment planning, where environments are only partially verifiable and multiple decision trajectories can be appropriate. The work extends clinical RL, which has mostly focused on verifiable diagnostic endpoints, to the harder partially verifiable setting of colon cancer treatment with clinical collaborators. An important step toward RL-trained medical decision support.

entry.title: Train for Many, Update with One: Improving Multi-Sample Reasoning via Fenchel-Bregman Posterior Learning

author.name: Sungjun Lim, Adrian Robert Minut, Nico Carlsen Daheim, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Kyungwoo Song, Thomas M\"ollenhoff

entry.summary: The paper formulates finite-K posterior learning to directly optimize candidate coverage in multi-sample reasoning, and proposes a Fenchel-Bregman optimization approach requiring only one posterior draw per update instead of K. This makes training for pass-at-K style objectives substantially more efficient.

entry.title: Fan Out or Relay? Ownership-Aware Routing for LLM Agents Querying Siloed Tables

author.name: Zhexi Feng

entry.summary: This paper studies how LLM agent coordinators should route questions when data is owned by multiple parties: fanning out to all owners at once versus relaying queries sequentially. Across thirteen settings, fan-out wins on single-owner questions but fails on multi-owner joins, and the winning strategy flips with data ownership rather than query shape, motivating ownership-aware routing.

entry.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts

author.name: Giovanni Pio Delvecchio, Stefano Fantazzini, Giacomo Frisoni, Gianluca Moro, Lorenzo Bacchiani, Mario Bravetti, Thomas Troels Hildebrandt

entry.summary: SolBehave is a benchmark of 250 real Ethereum contracts evaluating behavioral correctness of LLM-generated smart contracts via differential fuzzing, historical-transaction replay, and a core synthetic-replay method guided by Dynamic Condition Response graphs. It moves beyond compile-check evaluations at a critical moment since deployed contracts cannot be patched.

entry.title: Beyond Policy Rollouts: Embedding-Space Directional Exploration with Anchored Noise for LLM RLVR

author.name: Daijiao Liu, Huiyi Wang, Lina Yao, Dong Gong

entry.summary: The paper proposes EDEN, a method for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) that improves exploration by injecting anchored perturbations in embedding space at the rollout input level. This addresses the problem that small rollout groups from the same policy produce highly similar trajectories, weakening group-relative advantage signals. EDEN broadens exploration without changing rollout budgets or policy update mechanics.

entry.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

author.name: Alexander Miasnikov, Ruslan Kabirov, Gleb Molodtsov, Dmitrii Vlashchuk, Vladimir Aletov, Nail Bashirov, Daniil Tikhonov, Maxim Krutikov, Aleksandr Shestakov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Monarch-Muon is a structured matrix-aware optimizer applying Muon-style orthogonalization to Monarch-factorized weights, reducing weights, gradients, and optimizer state while decomposing the dense polar update into small independent subproblems with a blockwise trust-region interpretation. It improves over Monarch-AdamW on dense 257M and 1B MoE models at fixed structure. It targets the wall-clock and memory constraints of LLM pretraining.

entry.title: On the Monitorability of Natural Language Autoencoders: Identification vs Discrimination

author.name: Kevin Yandoka Denamgana\"i

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Natural Language Autoencoders, proposed oversight tools where an Activation Verbaliser explains an activation vector and an Activation Reconstructor maps the explanation back, as emergent-communication referential games. It distinguishes generative training games from the discriminative, partially observable oversight game, analyzing when a human monitor can distinguish true from false activation accounts.

entry.title: Solvating machine-learning interatomic potentials for solution-phase chemistry

author.name: Anton Z. Ni, Joonho Lee

entry.summary: Introduces AnySolv, a transferable implicit solvation potential that adds solvent-dependent energy and force corrections to existing gas-phase ML interatomic potentials without retraining, trained on 1.4M DFT-SMD computations across 36 solvents. It generalizes to 179 solvents via continuous solvent descriptors and reproduces solvation energies to 2-4 meV MAE.

entry.title: AlignPred: Error-Controlled KV Cache Compression via Alignment and Predictive Coding

author.name: Xu Yang, Jiapeng Zhang, Zhiwei Zuo, Yuxin Chen, Feiqiang Sun, Chengguang Xu, Feng Jin, Zhuo Tang

entry.summary: AlignPred is a codec for compressing persistent KV caches in long-running agents, combining local orthogonal transforms that align related heads or layers with token-wise and cross-head/layer predictive coding, then error-bounded lattice quantization and entropy coding of residuals — all without learned predictors or heavy search. It provides a configurable reconstruction-error budget and beats evaluated baselines on storage across three attention mechanisms. KV cache compression is a key efficiency lever for long-context agent workloads.

entry.title: Binding Phoneme Identity to Position in Neural Models and the Human Brain

author.name: Nafiseh Momeni, Malo Renaudin, Itzhak Fried, Yair Lakretz

entry.summary: The paper tests the NLP-derived onion hypothesis about how neural networks bind phoneme identity (filler) to serial position (role), comparing model representations with human brain recordings including from epileptic patients. It addresses a simple, well-defined case of the role-filler binding problem shared by NLP and cognitive neuroscience.

entry.title: HumanPhys: A Human-Centric Physical-World Perception Benchmark for Real-World Visual Reasoning

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Enzhi Zhou, Junan Lin, Dulan Zhou, Weiqiang Wang, Yuge Huang, Jian Liu

entry.summary: HumanPhys is a benchmark probing human-centric physical perception in vision models, covering quantities like depth, interpersonal distance, gaze angle, velocity, and contact deformation, plus illumination inference and camera ego-motion. Labels are derived programmatically from sensor calibration or renderer state, avoiding annotator noise.

entry.title: 1Step-WAM: Your World Action Model but Faster using 1-Step Action Generation

author.name: Rundong Su, Pengtao Chen, Haohan Geng, Sha Zhang, Zhihang Yuan, Yicheng Rong, Chong Yu, Hao Huang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: 1Step-WAM shows that action-denoising trajectories in world action models are approximately straight, so the first-step velocity strongly estimates the final action, and converts multi-step denoising into a single forward pass using a lightweight calibrator and bandwidth-constrained decoding. This removes a key latency bottleneck for real-world robot deployment.

entry.title: A Concept-informed Interpretable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis

author.name: Shengzhou Zhong, Ziying Wang, Liang Li, Lihua Yan, Shuochun Chen, Yudie Zou, Jifan Zhang, Wenhao Li, Huiling Zhang, Jiayin Lu, Ziting Xu, Qianjin Feng, Zhenwei Shi, Yan Chen, Yingjia Li, Yu Zhang, Zhenyuan Ning

entry.summary: IBUS is a concept-informed interpretable framework for breast ultrasound diagnosis incorporating BI-RADS descriptors and radiologist workflow knowledge, validated on what the authors describe as the largest multicenter collection of breast ultrasound images with structured BI-RADS annotations (9,941 patients, 20 datasets). It shows consistent cross-center generalization across 14 testing datasets.

entry.title: Self-Verifier Capture in Unified Visual Generators: Diagnosing and Repairing Closed-Loop Self-Reward

author.name: Binyan Chen, Tong Pan

entry.summary: Identifies and diagnoses self-verifier capture in unified visual generators, where reusing the model's own understanding pathway as a decode-free reward causes self-reward to rise while independently measured quality falls, via on-manifold blind-spot exploitation and shared-weight judge rewriting. Experiments on Scale-RAE with matched shared/frozen semantic and denoising cells isolate these failure routes.

entry.title: Vision Models Capture Complementary Representations in Children That Converge in Adults

author.name: Domenic Bersch, Timothy Schauml\"offel, Michela Proietti, Antonia Franaszek-Traczewska, Hannah Elisabeth Zwad, Siying Xie, Marlena Baldauf, Teresa Sylvester, Christina Maria Sch\"atz, Bert Turtleton, Moritz K\"oster, Stefanie H\"ohl, Radoslaw Cichy, Gemma Roig

entry.summary: Using time-resolved representational similarity analysis on EEG from 8-year-olds, 12-year-olds, and adults, the study finds CLIP aligns with children's brain responses earlier than vision-only models, with complementary structure persisting from age 8. Semantic structure (category, animacy) strengthens toward adulthood while low-level alignment stays weak.

entry.title: Make {\pi}0.5 Learn to Call Astra for Reliable Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jianli Sun, Chengxiang Li, Yonglin Tian

entry.summary: The authors equip a frozen pi0.5 robot policy with a lightweight CALL head that predicts when to invoke the GPT-6 Astra model for embodied reasoning, activating the large model only for critical recovery events and returning control afterward. Across 40 LIBERO tasks the hybrid achieves 97.5% success versus 95.5% for pure pi0.5, while Astra executes only about 5.5% of environment steps.

entry.title: ForkCast: Predictive Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Policies via Counterfactual Futures

author.name: Chenru Wen, Huajian Zeng, Haokai Ding, Jian Kang, Anqing Duan, Dawei Zhou, Dezhen Song, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: ForkCast adds predictive recovery to frozen VLA policies by evaluating three counterfactual candidates at each decision point — committing to the nominal action chunk, reobserving from a new camera viewpoint, or replanning the arm trajectory — using a candidate-conditioned world model to forecast latent outcomes. It decides whether and how to intervene without scripted repairs or recovery data in policy training.

entry.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function

author.name: Shawheen Naderi, Fatemeh Akherati, Yubei Chen

entry.summary: Using counterfactual interventions in the Crafter environment, the authors show that the value function of a model-free PPO agent encodes structured environment knowledge, such as rules governing diamond collectibility and health dynamics. The work suggests model-free RL may implicitly learn world models, with discussed safety implications of visualizing what agents know.

entry.title: AlignPoison: Conditional Targeted Poisoning of Generative Recommenders via Decoding-Aligned Prefixes

author.name: Zhuoxuan Zhang, Jinhao Duan, Xinyu Zhao, Jinduo Guo, Shuai Shao, Rui Li, Luke Simon, Zhun Deng, Tianlong Chen, Bo Sun

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that generative autoregressive recommenders are vulnerable to conditional targeted poisoning: injecting fewer than 1% synthetic interactions significantly increases promotion of adversary-chosen items under a trigger, even with black-box API access. The authors characterize the underlying susceptibility mechanism and introduce the AlignPoison attack.

entry.title: MontageFlow: Physically Valid High Fidelity EEG Generation

author.name: Sudarshan Regmi, Nabaraj Subedi, Arvind Pillai, Yu Yvonne Wu, Yuliang Chen, Michael V. Heinz, Lisa Marsch, Nicholas C. Jacobson, Andrew Campbell

entry.summary: MontageFlow is a flow-matching generative model for clinical EEG that enforces the exact linear identities among channels that arise because each electrode records voltage differences between two scalp contacts. The authors show prior generative models violate these physical constraints despite high apparent fidelity, and enforcing validity improves the usefulness of generated data.

entry.title: CUSE: Fine-Grained Multimodal Unlearning with Counterfactual Guidance and On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Chenlu Ding, Jiancan Wu, Yanchen Luo, Tianyu Zhang, Yancheng Yuan, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: CUSE is a framework for removing sensitive, copyrighted, or unsafe information from multimodal LLMs at token-level granularity rather than across whole responses. It uses counterfactual inputs (with target evidence removed) to identify which tokens carry the target information, then applies on-policy self-distillation for precise, behavior-aligned forgetting.

entry.title: State Representation Shapes Long-Horizon Agent Learning and Transfer: An Empirical Study

author.name: Dong Nie, Rui Lan, Yixin Nie, Lingzi Hong

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that the state representation used during training versus evaluation critically affects long-horizon agent learning and transfer in deterministic tool workflows. Using Qwen models of 1.7B to 27B scale, it finds stark transfer asymmetries, e.g., compact-trained adapters completing all held-out tasks in compact view but none in full view.

entry.title: Inverse Garment Design with Visual Agents

author.name: Nanxiang Jiang, Yunuo Chen, Zeng Tao, Zizhang Li, Qi Guo, Jiajun Wu, Yin Yang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: DressAgent is a hierarchical agentic system that reconstructs simulation-ready multi-layer 3D garments and sewing patterns from a single image using planning and closed-loop refinement with physical simulation. It contributes a GarmentCode-based representation and the first multi-layer sewing pattern dataset with over 15K outfits.

entry.title: Recall What Is Missing: Composing Evidence from Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Qi Feng, Jicong Fan

entry.summary: The paper reframes long-term memory retrieval for agents as query-conditioned evidence composition, valuing each memory by what it adds beyond already-selected evidence rather than individual relevance. It proposes MemPursuit, a training-free mechanism using the residual of sparse convex query reconstruction as a proxy for missing evidence. This improves context efficiency by avoiding redundant memories and retrieving complementary ones.

entry.title: Beyond Perfect Teammates: Multi-Agent Collaboration with Unreliable Colleagues

author.name: Chen Huang, Yiyang Zhang, Yuhao Wu, Yang Deng, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper challenges the perfect-colleague assumption in LLM multi-agent systems, introducing UnCoBench, a benchmark that organizes realistic behavioral failures such as irrelevant answers, insufficient detail, and non-response. It separates task-solving competence from the ability to recover from unreliable evidence-gathering teammates.

entry.title: HyWe: Unifying Search and Operation for Real-World Hybrid Web Tasks

author.name: Zijian Cai, Haowei Liu, Kailai Chen, Lin Peng, Cong Wan, Ziqi Zhang, Chunfeng Yuan, Bing Li, Weiming Hu, Haiyang Xu

entry.summary: Introduces HyWe, a framework unifying information search and page interaction in a single model and trajectory for real-world hybrid web tasks, with explicit capability switching and shared history. It also provides HyWeCollector, an automatic pipeline for generating verified hybrid trajectories, and trains a 35B model on them.

entry.title: EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents

author.name: Min Cai, Dan Zhang, Gao Xing, Libin Ma, Zhaohui Xu, Xi Ye

entry.summary: Introduces EAU, a meta-agent framework in which the environment, agent, and user simulator co-evolve during training of multi-turn LLM agents. EAU monitors trajectories and training statistics, diagnoses failures and uninformative interactions, and repairs unreliable tools, incomplete state coverage, and inconsistent user simulators rather than treating them as fixed.

entry.title: G$^2$WAM: World Action Models for Efficient and Geometry Grounded Image-Goal Navigation

author.name: Ke Gui, Chenghao Shi, Ziyue Wang, Longwen Chen, Xieyuanli Chen, Huimin Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a Geometry Grounded World Action Model for image-goal navigation that encodes spatial cues via a learned scene-coordinate localization module, avoiding both task-specific fine-tuning that underuses spatial priors and costly external 3D reconstruction. The world model supports counterfactual reasoning and persistent spatial memory for planning toward targets outside the field of view.

entry.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models

author.name: Jonathan Geuter, Andrew Cheng, David Alvarez-Melis

entry.summary: Shows that existing open instruction-tuned models such as Gemma 4 and Qwen3.6 variants can match specialized decision-making (System One) models by reading option probabilities directly from letter logits at the last token position, and that simple supervised fine-tuning improves this further. No generative decoding is needed.

entry.title: Generalizable field of view extension for diffusion MRI via conditional flow matching

author.name: Gaurav Rudravaram, Lianrui Zuo, Ema Topolnjak, Michael E. Kim, Adam M. Saunders, Elyssa M. McMaster, Paula Trujillo, Ely E. Wesley, Colin D. McKnight, Pratik P. Pandharipande, Mayur B. Patel, Cayce Strength, Brenda T. Pund, Amelia W Maiga, Robert S. Dittus, David A. Bennett, Julie A. Schneider, Konstantinos Arfanakis, The HABS-HD Study Team, Derek B. Archer, Timothy J. Hohman, Yelena Bodien, Daniel C. Moyer, Kurt G. Schilling, Bennett A. Landman

entry.summary: The paper proposes a conditional flow-matching generative model that extends the field of view of diffusion MRI by predicting apparent diffusion coefficients in six directions, enabling whole-brain tractography from incomplete acquisitions. By predicting ADC maps instead of raw 4D dMRI signal, the approach is designed to generalize across scanners and acquisition protocols without retraining. Validation appears to draw on large multi-site clinical and research cohorts.

entry.title: SchemaWeaver: Accelerating On-Device Mobile Agentic AI via Schema-Guided Parallel LLM Decoding

author.name: Boyuan Yang, Wei Gao

entry.summary: SchemaWeaver speeds up on-device LLM tool calling by enforcing schema-guided parallel decoding in the decode phase, producing multiple tokens per decode pass on memory-bandwidth-limited mobile processors. The technique exploits known output schemas of tool calls and is claimed to be generically applicable across models and devices. It targets the key bottleneck for practical mobile agentic AI: decode latency.

entry.title: MedEvo: Medical Reasoning Evolution through Knowledge Navigation

author.name: Xiaoliang Wang, Zhuo Chen, Chuanyang Zheng, Quanbin Wang, Jiangwei Lao, Yingao Liu, Jiajia Liu, Jinming Cao, Honglin Lin, Zhihong Lu, Hao Jin, Jian Wang, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: MedEvo improves medical multimodal reasoning models by repairing failed reasoning trajectories rather than discarding them, using a medical tag taxonomy and error-type diagnosis. A gold-blind auditor locates the first consequential error and supplies answer-free hints so the student model regenerates only the erroneous suffix, with data selection driven by identified capability gaps.

entry.title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution

author.name: Xiaoliang Wang, Zhuo Chen, Chuanyang Zheng, Jiangwei Lao, Quanbin Wang, Honglin Lin, Jiajia Liu, Zhihong Lu, Hao Jin, Jian Wang, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework for electrocardiogram AI models that combines verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits, construction errors drive generator repair, and learner errors motivate interventions validated on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three improvement rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean QA accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03.

entry.title: CompanionSafe: From Multi-turn Safety Evaluation to Guardrails for AI Companions

author.name: Xinyang Liao, Lingyu Li, Kaicheng Shen, Yang Yao, Na Lu, Yan Teng, Xia Hu

entry.summary: CompanionSafe is a unified evaluation-to-mitigation framework for AI companion safety, featuring CompanionEval with 1,300 relationally grounded multi-turn dialogue settings across personas and scenarios, plus a mitigation component. It targets safety risks specific to sustained relational interactions rather than general harms. This moves beyond platform-specific or manually collected conversation datasets.

entry.title: ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents

author.name: Wei Xie, Kaituo Feng, Shiming Fu, Yong Liu, Xiangyu Yue, Shuangjia Zheng

entry.summary: ReTerm trains terminal coding agents to recover from their own failures, using a curated 10K-example dataset of recovery demonstrations for SFT cold start and an online RL algorithm (ReTerm-GRPO) that forks from the agent's failure states to generate multiple independent self-recovery attempts. The approach targets a concrete failure mode of long-running coding agents.

entry.title: Knowing the User Is Not Knowing What We Established: Grounding Awareness in Personal Agents

author.name: Jiajun Chen, Xinyue Chen, Yicheng Jiang, Hua Shen

entry.summary: The paper introduces Grounding Awareness: a personal agent's ability to distinguish accepted, unacknowledged, revised, and scoped arrangements with the user when acting, rather than treating any remembered proposal as an authorized instruction. A controlled benchmark shows strong memory performance does not translate into correct grounding-aware behavior across agents and memory systems.

entry.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback

author.name: Zheye Deng, Sha Li, Changlong Yu, Xin Liu, Qin Lu, Priyanka Nigam, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: The paper formulates an agentic code judging task where a model diagnoses a candidate competitive programming solution using only the problem statement and source code, producing counterexamples as checkable evidence of failure. This avoids consuming limited official submissions while providing informative feedback for test-time scaling.

entry.title: When Log Parsing Removes What Matters: Detecting Failures in Distributed GPU Workloads

author.name: Boyuan Cui, Yuyang Zeng, Yifang Tian, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: The paper introduces GF-Bench, a PyTorch-based framework and dataset for fault injection in distributed GPU workloads, providing 220 labeled two-GPU executions with normal, out-of-memory, and straggler failures. Using it, the authors show that established log-based failure detectors can miss failures that log parsing removes, revealing a gap in existing methods for AI infrastructure.

entry.title: The Future of AI-assisted Physics: Discovering, Verifying and Organizing Results via Formalization

author.name: Sven Krippendorf, Leopoldo Sarra, Joseph Tooby-Smith

entry.summary: This position paper argues that formalization is essential for verifying and organizing AI-driven discoveries in physics, surveys AI's role in formalization, and contends that AI lowers formalization barriers but remains weaker at choosing definitions and designing libraries than at writing proofs. It also examines how AI speed creates new verification challenges.

entry.title: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules

author.name: Samuele Giampieri

entry.summary: Cortex is a tool that treats coding-agent harness files (project files, skills, rules) as testable artifacts: it saves developer corrections as replayable tasks, writes candidate skills or rules, and keeps them only if repeated runs with and without the change show net gain with no task regressing. This brings measurement-gated evolution to agent configuration rather than trusting single-session fixes. It targets practical reliability of agentic coding systems like Claude Code.

entry.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization

author.name: Sihwan Park, Sung-Yub Kim, Doohyuk Jang, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: KV4-RL addresses KV cache concentration in asynchronous rollout for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, showing INT4 KV cache quantization accelerates generation but can degrade learning. The method combines calibration-free INT4 quantization with selective INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent context.

entry.title: PTGPO: Prefix Tree Group Policy Optimization

author.name: Ruolin Chen, Yang Li, Jihang Wang, Zhuoya Zhao, Yuchen Liu, Jiaming Xu, Qian Zhang

entry.summary: PTGPO is a critic-free RL method for training language agents on long-horizon interactive tasks, constructing prefix trees over trajectory suffixes within anchor-state groups and assigning edge credits from differences between child and parent empirical mean returns. This yields fine-grained credit assignment that avoids conflating an action with subsequent decisions, improving over trajectory-level or state-group step-level advantage estimates.

entry.title: Have You Been Convinced? A Neuro-symbolic Argumentation Reasoning Approach to Detecting Persuasiveness in ChangeMyView Discussions

author.name: Siddharth Bhargava, Sara Tonelli, Patricia Mart\'in-Rodilla

entry.summary: Proposes NARS, a neuro-symbolic system that combines retrieval-augmented iterative LLM reasoning to extract bipolar argument structures with gradual argumentation semantics to propagate influence across those structures. The authors also contribute CMV2BAS, a dataset of long multi-threaded ChangeMyView discussions for persuasiveness detection.

entry.title: Sensitivity or Criterion? Measuring and Moving When Language Models Act

author.name: Sixun Dong, Yebowen Hu, Ming Yin, Yiran Chen, Fei Liu, Chen Chen

entry.summary: FlipAct applies signal-detection theory to agent tool use, separating sensitivity (can the model recognize when action is warranted) from criterion (is the model reluctant or eager to act), using graded evidence scores and 2x2 question quads that hold knowledge fixed while flipping physical state. Across 44 open models, the framework disentangles two failure modes that a single accuracy number conflates, and explores how criteria can be shifted.

entry.title: What DNA Foundation Models Learn Beyond Sequence Composition

author.name: Vincenzo Yuto Civale, Andrew David Bagdanov, Alberto Magi

entry.summary: This study evaluates frozen representations from five DNA foundation models against simple k-mer frequency baselines across 57 genomic classification tasks and gene-expression regression. It finds most models barely beat k-mer features, though NTv3 shows a consistent incremental advantage, improving 46 of 57 datasets. The work provides a sobering audit of what genomic foundation models actually learn beyond sequence composition.

entry.title: A Survey of Flow Matching in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nabuat Zaman Nahim, Fairoz Nower Khan, Peizhong Ju

entry.summary: This survey organizes the rapidly growing but fragmented literature on flow matching in reinforcement learning, covering expressive multimodal policy parameterization via ODE-based transport as an alternative to diffusion policies. It provides a taxonomy spanning offline continuous control, online fine-tuning, and foundation model alignment.

entry.title: Explicitly Aligned Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction from Variable-Length Screening Histories

author.name: Solveig Thrun, Zijun Sun, Suaiba A. Salahuddin, Kristoffer Wickstr{\o}m, Elisabeth Wetzer, Stine Hansen, Robert Jenssen, Michael Kampffmeyer

entry.summary: This paper presents a breast cancer risk prediction model from screening mammography that explicitly aligns breast tissue regions across longitudinal exams and jointly exploits complementary craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views. Prior methods either used implicit alignment or treated views independently; explicit multi-view temporal alignment aims to improve risk stratification for personalized screening.

entry.title: SLEM: Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging

author.name: Dohyeon Kim, Bedionita Soro, Bruno Andreis, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: SLEM is a MoE compression method that merges experts in a spectrum-aware latent space rather than via direct parameter-space interpolation, avoiding calibration-data dependence when estimating merging coefficients. It reduces the memory overhead of storing all experts in Mixture-of-Experts models.

entry.title: SuPER-Mamba: Surprisal Prioritization for Extended-Context Routing in Mamba

author.name: Zhetong Zhang, Gayan K Kulatilleke

entry.summary: SuPER-Mamba is a training-free method that uses surprisal from next-token predictions as an intrinsic signal to route long-range state updates in pretrained Mamba state-space models, improving long-context performance without query-dependent scoring or retraining. On LongBench-E across three state-space models it raises the average score from 8.06 to 15.69, roughly a 94% relative gain. It matters because degradation at long context is a core weakness of linear-complexity SSMs.

entry.title: Measuring Learned Equivariance: An Information Theoretic Approach

author.name: Claire Schlesinger, Wolfgang Gatterbauer, Robin Walters

entry.summary: Introduces a principled test for whether networks trained with data augmentation actually learned equivariance, using normalized mutual information in discrete settings and centered kernel alignment for high-dimensional activations with exact guarantees for orthogonal transformations. The work addresses a gap where augmentation does not guarantee symmetry-respecting behavior, especially at intermediate representations. Findings across architectures show augmentation usually improves transformation consistency.

entry.title: Benchmarking Self-Supervised 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models and Transferability Estimation

author.name: Jiaqi Tang, Yu Wang, Yang Liu, Jing Tao, Fandong Zhang, Zhou Zhen, Xiahai Zhuang, Qingchao Chen, Yining Yang, Yizhou Yu

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates 23 self-supervised 3D medical vision foundation models on the same 14 segmentation, classification, and regression tasks spanning multiple anatomies and modalities, providing directly comparable evidence for model selection. It also studies transferability estimation to predict which model suits a new task without costly fine-tuning, finding no single candidate dominates.

entry.title: TSRL: Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Continual Agent Training

author.name: Yuqian Fu, Kaiwen Jiang, Zijun Song, Jiawei Wang, Yuanheng Zhu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: TSRL addresses catastrophic forgetting in continual training of LLM agents by combining RL as the backbone with SFT triggered selectively in states where expert supervision is most needed. The state-dependent supervision mechanism aims to gain SFT sample efficiency without sacrificing RL capability retention.

entry.title: Same Attack, Different Judge: A First Controlled Adversarial Comparison of Jev, LLM Judges, and Purpose-Built Safety Classifiers

author.name: Xiang Li, Aichun Huang, Mingming Zhang, Zheli Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents the first controlled adversarial evaluation of TypeSafe AI's Jev safety judge against five GPT and GLM judges and two local classifiers, using fifty attack variants across thirteen families on four tasks. Findings expose how adversarial input shifts Jev's predefined-answer probabilities and compare robustness across judge types.

entry.title: SpecCloak: Probing Harmful Code Generation through Engineering Specifications

author.name: Wenbin Chen, Jiexin Wang, Guanting Wu, Jiaxi Liang, Yi Cai

entry.summary: This safety study shows that the format in which coding requirements are presented affects LLM refusal behavior on malicious code requests. The authors introduce PseudoSpec, a template that frames functional requirements as engineering specifications, and show across five open-weight models that removing explicit risk keywords only partially reduces refusal while specification-style framing further suppresses safety behavior, validated through representation analysis and activation interventions. The work exposes a bypass pathway relevant to code-generation safety.

entry.title: inLoRA-MINT: Internal Representations for Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs

author.name: Gonzalo Mancera, Julian Fierrez, Aythami Morales, Ruben Tolosana, Daniel DeAlcala, Francisco Jurado

entry.summary: This work extends membership inference testing (MINT) to LoRA-fine-tuned LLMs, using intermediate representations such as activations and parameter-dependent signals to detect whether specific samples were in the training data. It evaluates the approach across four LLM families including Qwen, Phi-4, DeepSeek-V3, and LLaMA 3.2-3B under near black-box conditions.

entry.title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes

author.name: Yu Wang, Rui Dai, Wei Chen, Yi Wang, Bo Dang, Kaikui Liu, Xiangxiang Chu, Yansheng Li

entry.summary: Urbex recasts city-scale 3D visual grounding from candidate ranking into active spatial search, letting a VLM agent query landmarks, zoom into regions, and render oblique views of an interactive multi-view city scene. The tool-use policy is trained with reinforcement learning using smooth localization and shaping rewards on CityRefer. It achieves state-of-the-art Hit@1 and IoU and supports candidate-free grounding.

entry.title: Do Factuality Methods Make LLMs More Factual? Reproducibility and Fair Comparison

author.name: Pratuat Amatya, Vinay Setty, V Venktesh, Avishek Anand

entry.summary: This paper presents the first independent reproduction and fair comparison of five factuality alignment methods for LLMs, addressing the problem that standard RLHF does not optimize for factual accuracy. Because prior factuality methods each used different base models, training data, evaluation sets, judges, and metrics, they were previously incomparable; this work standardizes the setup to assess whether the claimed factuality gains actually hold. It matters because it introduces much-needed reproducibility rigor into a growing subfield of alignment research.

entry.title: EgoOmniWorld: Unifying Egocentric Understanding via Ego-Action-World Interactions

author.name: Songruo Chen, Yuqian Fu, Yu Li, Mingkang Dong, Sifan Zhou, Bin Ren, Xu Zheng, Tianwen Qian, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: The authors propose the Ego-Action-World interaction loop as a unifying principle for egocentric video understanding, where a wearer perceives, acts, and receives world feedback. They introduce EgoOmniWorld, a benchmark structured around node, edge, chain, and loop interaction patterns with an evidence-grounded data pipeline. It matters because egocentric capabilities are usually evaluated in isolation despite being tightly coupled in real interaction.

entry.title: Nudge the Judge: Uncovering Program Decision Hijacking in Real-World Jev Applications

author.name: Yang Luo, Tiantian Ji, Zifeng Kang, Yucheng Wang, Yong Liu, Zhiyi Yin, Xinran Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Jev Program Decision Hijacking (JPDH), a security risk where attacker-controlled contexts redirect program decisions through schema-valid structured judgments produced by System One models. JevProbe is presented as the first automated framework tracing adversarial influence from reachable context surfaces through program control flow in real applications. This shifts LLM security analysis from model-level attacks to downstream program consequences.

entry.title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation

author.name: Ziyang Song, Lia Shen, Yixuan Li, Qincheng Lu, Weihao Li, Haoran Xu, He Zhu, Xinyu Wang, Yue Li
