entry.summary: SMI is a training-free framework that represents medical concepts as coarse-to-fine paths through expert ontologies, aggregating frozen biomedical language model embeddings into hierarchy-aware representations. It targets long-tailed clinical codes where standard LM embeddings lose information, which matters for rare-diagnosis and clinical coding tasks.

entry.title: PotentialEP: Backprop-Free Training of CIFAR-Scale Generative Models via Equilibrium Propagation

author.name: Alex Gower

entry.summary: This work trains CIFAR-scale generative models without backpropagation by combining Energy Matching, whose sampling is a gradient-descent relaxation on a time-independent potential, with a predictive coding network that supplies the gradient locally. The motivation is neuromorphic/analog hardware, where one low-power relaxation could replace hundreds of diffusion integration steps.

entry.title: Characterizing the Separability Gap in Prior-Data Fitted Networks

author.name: Julius Kobialka, Manuel H\"ulskamp, Thomas Nagler, David R\"ugamer

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that common priors used in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) are non-separable, contradicting standard PFN theory assumptions that feature distributions and label mechanisms are independent. The authors characterize the gap between predictions based on the full task posterior versus context-only posterior, showing the gap vanishes under posterior concentration but can persist under misspecification. This sharpens the theoretical foundations of in-context learning via PFNs.

entry.title: Beyond Adjacent Layers: Graph-Guided Layer Fusion for Compressing Large Language Models

author.name: Muhammad Usama, Yeoreum Jung

entry.summary: The authors challenge the assumption that functional redundancy in LLMs is local by computing full pairwise CKA similarity matrices across thirteen LLMs from six families, finding non-adjacent layers have 3.6-15.9x more high-similarity pairs than adjacent ones. Their FCM method uses spectral community detection over the layer-similarity graph to select and merge functionally equivalent non-adjacent layers. This improves on depth-compression methods restricted to adjacent-layer merging.

entry.title: Drift, Then Spread: Learning One-Step Generative Policies for Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chunyu Luo, Hongyu Zhao, Guangyi Ni, Yue Song, Lingkai Kong

entry.summary: DriftSpread is a one-step generative policy for online maximum-entropy RL that avoids the costly iterative sampling of diffusion- and flow-based policies. Building on an energy-based view of Drifting, it derives critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread updates learned sequentially in a single actor without needing samples from the critic-defined Boltzmann target.

entry.title: Dissipative Lagrangian Neural Networks for the Interpretable Modelling of Passive Mechanical Systems

author.name: Rob Seabourne, Alice Cicirello

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Dissipative Lagrangian Neural Network (dLNN), a continuous-time system identification method that separately learns conservative and dissipative dynamics of mechanical systems from data. Its novel parametrization structurally enforces passivity while remaining expressive enough to capture state-dependent damping and friction. Validation includes trajectory prediction on a chaotic double pendulum and inverse dynamics on a six-degree-of-freedom system.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Hawkes-Structured Networks for Market Making

author.name: Fernando Acero, Philipp Plank, Yufei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a model-free RL framework for market making under non-Markovian Hawkes order-flow dynamics, establishing non-asymptotic bounds quantifying the loss from approximating the infinite-dimensional Hawkes state with finite exponentially weighted features. Guided by this theory, it introduces the Hawkes-Structured Network (HSN), which encodes historical order flow via a learnable mixture-of-exponentials filter trained end-to-end with RL.

entry.title: Optimal Transport PAC-Bayes Bounds

author.name: Armin Beck, Peter Ochs, Jalal Fadili

entry.summary: The authors derive new PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds that replace the standard KL divergence between prior and posterior with optimal transport distances, including total variation and Wasserstein-p distances. This removes absolute continuity requirements on the posterior and incorporates the geometry of the probability space.

entry.title: Radial Tail Repair: Post-Training Correction for Diffusion and Flow Models

author.name: Hamza Cherkaoui, H\'el\`ene Halconruy, Antonio Ocello

entry.summary: The authors propose a post-training method to fix the poor tail behavior of diffusion and flow-matching models on heavy-tailed data. Using a radial-angular decomposition, they preserve the pretrained model's directional structure while rescaling only the radial tail, avoiding costly retraining or modified generative dynamics.

entry.title: Constant-Depth Rational-Weight GNNs and their Connection to Schanuel's Conjecture

author.name: Daumantas Kojelis, Carsten Lutz

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves that constant-depth graph neural networks with only rational (even integer) weights can match the expressive power of the 1-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test, provided Schanuel's conjecture from transcendental number theory holds. It also establishes a partial converse connecting the impossibility direction to the same conjecture, using standard activation functions like logistic sigmoid and tanh. The result is notable for linking GNN expressivity theory to deep open problems in number theory.

entry.title: Online LLM Personalization from Pairwise Preferences Across Users

author.name: Romain Puech, Georgy Salakhutdinov, Dimitris Bertsimas

entry.summary: The paper formulates inference-time LLM personalization as a contextual dueling bandit variant: users arrive sequentially, receive two persona-style responses per question, and the system learns from a single pairwise choice with no initial preference data. The objective is cumulative strong regret accounting for both displayed responses. It bridges bandit theory and practical LLM deployment for hidden, heterogeneous user style preferences.

entry.title: Deep Mesoscopic Dynamics

author.name: Yue Zhao, Shiqi Wu, Yihang Ouyang, Sergey Grebenchuk, Magdalena Grzeszczyk, Xiaoxu Zhao, Kostya S. Novoselov, Maciej Koperski, Qianxiao Li

entry.summary: DeepMesoD uses neural networks to learn effective mesoscopic field equations from microscopic simulation trajectories at a prescribed coarse-graining scale, learning free-energy functionals, spatial interaction kernels, and state-dependent dissipation operators constrained by fluctuation-dissipation relations. This bridges the gap between small-domain microscopic simulations and spatially averaged bulk descriptions. Co-authors include Kostya Novoselov (Nobel laureate), indicating strong physics credibility.

entry.title: Graph Metanetworks for Transformer Based Language Models

author.name: Yonathan Wolanowsky, Guy Bar-Shalom, Fabrizio Frasca, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: This paper develops symmetry-aware graph metanetworks for processing Transformer weights as data, fully accounting for the richer weight-space symmetry group that includes continuous general-linear symmetries of attention matrices and head permutations beyond neuron permutations. This fills a gap where prior metanetwork work covered only MLPs or partial Transformer symmetries.

entry.title: MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization

author.name: Yangchengyu Zhou, Zhiping Wu, Runchang Jiang, Dongdong Ren, Youfang Han, Wei Zhao, Dongqi Cai, Wenbin Li

entry.summary: MultiAlloc is a profiling-guided framework that allocates limited quantization resources across heterogeneous precision-preservation strategies (layer-wise and token-level) for KV cache compression in LLM inference under a fixed memory budget. It targets long-context and reasoning-heavy inference where KV cache memory is the dominant cost.

entry.title: SlideDP: Scaling Host-Resident LLM Fine-Tuning Across Multiple GPUs

author.name: Ruijia Yang, Shiyuan Lin, Yulong Ao, Zhiyu Li, Yingli Zhao, Xianduo Li, Yonghua Lin, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: SlideDP is a synchronous data-parallel runtime that enables full-parameter LLM fine-tuning beyond GPU memory via host-resident layer streaming across multiple GPUs sharing host resources. It maintains a single authoritative host state, decouples communication from state layout, and pipelines parameter delivery and gradient aggregation, with an analytical model for bottleneck prediction.

entry.title: ByteMark: A Unified Byte-Level Watermark for Detection Across Language Models

author.name: Xiaopu Wang, Runze Li

entry.summary: ByteMark defines an LLM text watermark directly on UTF-8 bytes rather than tokenizer or embedding representations, so a single public detector can verify text from models with different tokenizers under one shared key. This addresses a real deployment problem where watermark detection is incompatible across providers. It matters for provenance and detection of AI-generated text in the wild.

entry.title: Physics Foundation Models for Efficient Control of Fluid Flows

author.name: Mahindra Rautela, Shaifalee Saxena, Alexander Scheinker

entry.summary: Shows that a physics foundation model pretrained for PDE forecasting can be repurposed for closed-loop fluid-flow control by attaching lightweight Gaussian actor and critic heads to frozen representations and training with PPO. On HydroGym Kolmogorov-flow environments at multiple resolutions and Reynolds numbers, the frozen-PFM controller outperforms an MLP baseline trained identically while being more sample-efficient.

entry.title: Poisoned into Action: Context Attacks on Typed Decision Workflows

author.name: Chenkai Wu, Xing Chang, Jun Yan

entry.summary: Introduces an execution-aware protocol for evaluating context poisoning attacks on typed decision interfaces, tracing poisoned evidence through retrieval, model choice, automated action, and persisted state. In 1,659 fresh calls against a target system across two synthetic workflows, a standalone payload reached all 60 natural-retrieval trials and produced five security-violating executions, showing that schema-valid actions can still cause policy violations.

entry.title: How the Classical Baseline Shapes Machine-Learning Speed Claims in Topology Optimization

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This critical study re-runs released code for eight ML topology optimization methods and shows that reported speedups are often inflated by slow classical baselines and weaker learned designs. Simply optimizing the baseline finite-element solver cuts speedups by up to 20-fold, and published timings implying large gains can reverse once the classical code is timed to matching design stiffness.

entry.title: Think Before You Speak: Enabling Training-Free Latent Communication Between Language Models

author.name: Rishi Khare

entry.summary: This work removes the need for trained fusion adapters in KV-cache-based latent communication between heterogeneous LLMs, enabling training-free latent collaboration in multi-agent systems. By bypassing text-based exchange, it reduces information bottlenecks and prefill latency for downstream agents.

entry.title: Prorsa: Unleashing the Potential of Prefill-Decode Disaggregation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chiheng Lou, Xiangwei Deng, Bangjun Xiao, Xiaodong Ji, Yikai Zhao, Xin Jin, Hailin Zhang

entry.summary: Prorsa applies prefill-decode disaggregation, a technique from online LLM serving, to agentic RL rollout where multi-turn interactions cause prefill and decode workloads to coexist. It improves rollout efficiency by reducing interference among data-parallel attention modules, enabling stage-specific parallelism, and cutting end-to-end trajectory completion time.

entry.title: MENTOR: Procedural Shielding of Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Ashwani Anand, Ivi Chatzi, Ritam Raha, Anne-Kathrin Schmuck

entry.summary: Proposes MENTOR, a method for ensuring LLM agents comply with natural-language procedural manuals by providing procedural shielding of tool calls, rather than merely blocking problematic calls locally with LLM judges or hand-written rules. The approach aims to give agents constructive guidance toward correct progress while avoiding overly conservative behavior.

entry.title: GPU Goldmines: Tunable WebGPU Kernels for Edge LLM Inference

author.name: Rithik Sharma, Reese Levine, Zheyuan Chen, Ananthajit Srikanth, Yanwen Xu, Tyler Sorensen

entry.summary: This paper presents GPU Goldmines, a framework for specifying, executing, and auto-tuning WebGPU compute kernels for key LLM building blocks such as matrix multiplication and flash attention. Because WebGPU is portable and browser-accessible but hard to optimize per-device, the authors characterize kernel performance across devices, shapes, and browsers to select the best implementation per context. It matters for making edge LLM inference practical without native code.

entry.title: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving

author.name: Yunfei Feng, Jingkai He, Shiqi Liu, Cheng Zhang, Dong Du, Erhu Feng

entry.summary: FastEEP enables fast intra-instance elastic scaling of expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, avoiding the costly destroy-and-reconstruct cycle of instance-level scaling when workloads fluctuate. The system resizes the expert-parallel group within a live instance, reducing scaling overhead for production MoE deployments.

entry.title: MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain, A Multi-Sensor, Multi-Temporal Pretraining Dataset for Earth Observation

author.name: Carmen Oliver Huidobro, Mikolaj Czerkawski, Kevin Monsalvez-Pozo, Cesar Aybar, Gustau Camps-Valls, Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero

entry.summary: This dataset release provides 279,166 ten-kilometer Earth observation tiles combining Sentinel-2, Landsat, Sentinel-1, DEM, land cover, weather, and map data on a common grid, organized into mono-temporal, monthly, and denser temporal regimes. It is designed to support pretraining of generalist Earth observation foundation models, with tiles selected via AlphaEarth embedding clustering.

entry.title: Uniform Information Density-Based Preference Optimization

author.name: Yongyuan Li, Yang Xu

entry.summary: The authors propose UIDPO, a preference optimization algorithm for LLM alignment grounded in the psycholinguistic theory of Uniform Information Density rather than ad-hoc assumptions about chosen versus rejected pairs. By incorporating a well-established linguistic principle into the optimization direction, the method aims to steer models toward more human-preferred language. This represents a theoretically motivated alternative to purely empirical preference-pair objectives.

entry.title: Rate-Resolved Text Evaluation with Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Kun Zhao, Chenghua Lin, Nafise Sadat Moosavi

entry.summary: This work proposes using the masking rate of masked diffusion language models as a diagnostic axis, turning a single diffusion evaluation score into a vector of band-conditioned scores reflecting reconstruction difficulty. On SummEval, preserving rate structure yields complementary signal that improves fusion with autoregressive likelihood and survives control checks.

entry.title: CivWorldBench: Evaluating Language World Models in Structured Multi-Agent Sandbox Worlds

author.name: Ang Li, Haofei Yu, Zhengwei Tao, Liang Chen, Kuan Li, Miaomiao Li, Chenran Cai, Bin Liang, Jiaxuan You, Kam-Fai Wong

entry.summary: CivWorldBench is a benchmark built on a multi-agent strategy game engine with recorded internal states, controlled observations, and paired intervention rollouts, providing 1,900 decision points from 475 worlds. It evaluates language world models at three levels: association forecasting, belief inference, and intervention prediction. It addresses a real gap because real-world forecasting benchmarks lack hidden-state ground truth and controlled experiments.

entry.title: Ontology-Based Post-Coordinated Expression Assembly: from Clinical Narrative to Queryable Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Johann Pignat, Christophe Gaudet-Blavignac, Julien Ehrsam, Jean-Philippe Goldman, Cyrille Duret, Phil Cheng, Mina Bjelogrlic, Michel Cuendet, Christian Lovis, Olivier Michielin

entry.summary: This paper presents a method for converting free-text clinical oncology narratives into queryable knowledge graphs that conform to the SNOMED CT Extended Grammar across multiple ontologies. The approach defines five relation classes, each with construction rules that assemble annotated entities and relations into post-coordinated expressions, enabling large-scale cohort identification beyond what diagnostic codes or manual review can achieve.

entry.title: Distilling Text LMs into Speech-to-Speech LMs by Matching Internal Text Predictions

author.name: Ju-Chieh Chou, Jiawei Zhou, Karen Livescu

entry.summary: The authors introduce a speech-to-speech pretraining method that distills knowledge from pretrained text LMs by creating an internal text interface while preserving speech-only input and output. This extends text-to-speech-model distillation, previously explored only for speech-input/text-output models, to full speech-to-speech settings.

entry.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively

author.name: Guanting Dong, Xinyu Yang, Jiajie Jin, Yuyang Hu, Xiaoshuai Song, Yifei Chen, Xiaoxi Li, Jiejun Tan, Yutao Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua, Ji-Rong Wen, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Agent-Reflex is a three-stage training framework that incentivizes proactive reflection in LLM agents when tool services return noisy feedback or users intervene. It includes environment reflection skill discovery that injects perturbations, mines success-failure pairs, and distills reusable reflection meta-skills. The work targets failure recovery and self-correction, a key gap for deployed agents.

entry.title: CREATE: Creativity Evaluation of VLMs using the Visual Remote Associates Test

author.name: Ziqing Yang, Anubhav Jangra, Smaranda Muresan

entry.summary: CREATE introduces a semi-automatically constructed benchmark of 155 visual Remote Associates Test problems requiring solvers to find connections among three dissimilar images, validated with a 25-participant human study. Evaluating 11 vision-language models shows most underperform humans, with associative ability dependent on provided cue concepts. It fills a gap in principled measurement of visual lateral reasoning.

entry.title: Legal-R1: Agentic Retrieval for Evidence-Based Legal Reasoning

author.name: Huaiwen Pang, Jiale Han, Junying Chen, Wenjun Xiao, Benyou Wang

entry.summary: Legal-R1 is an agentic retrieval framework that decomposes legal question answering into a multi-agent workflow, where a Lawyer agent learns when to retrieve, which legal sources to query, and when evidence is sufficient, supported by a Legal Assistant agent handling authority-aware retrieval from statutes and precedent. It addresses the limits of one-shot retrieval-augmented generation for legally citable evidence. This targets a concrete gap in grounded legal AI.

entry.title: Hashrope: A Persistent Data Structure for Mechanisms of LLM Context Management

author.name: Muntaser Syed (Florida Institute of Technology), Ameerah Alsulami (Florida Institute of Technology), Marius Silaghi (Florida Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Hashrope shows that four recurring LLM context-management mechanisms — incremental context edits, branching and snapshotting for tree search, reusable-prefix identification for KV-cache reuse, and repeated-segment encoding — all reduce to a single persistent weight-balanced rope with polynomial subtree hashes over a Mersenne prime, supporting logarithmic edits and verified content-identity queries. The claims are validated with pre-registered, replicated experiments against deployed specialist structures. It offers a unifying systems abstraction for LLM serving.

entry.title: RoboFake: Are Deepfake Detectors Ready for Humanoid Face Robots?

author.name: Hao Chen, Junnan Xu

entry.summary: Introduces RoboFake, a face forgery where a humanoid robot is given a real person's face and driven with generated speech, creating a forgery recorded live by the camera with no pixel editing. Testing six detectors trained on FaceForensics++ shows they largely fail on physical and synthesized robot face videos.

entry.title: FreeCHROMA: Generative Chroma Keying from Unaligned Background References

author.name: Jiayi Wu, Tianfu Wang, Rui Zhao, Florian Schiffers, Zhimin Chen, Cornelia Fermuller, Yezhou Yang, Christopher Metzler, Yiannis Aloimonos

entry.summary: FreeCHROMA adapts a pretrained video diffusion model with parameter-efficient tuning to composite a foreground performance into new environments using one to three unaligned background references. This removes the need for coordinated background plates and dedicated harmonization in film production workflows, enabling flexible background choice and camera motion.

entry.title: What Really Works for Universal Multimodal Embeddings? A Controlled Study of Contrastive Training Strategies

author.name: Duo Li, Haojun Pan, Zuhao Yang, Xintong Wang, Chengfu Huo, Shijian Lu, Liang Ding

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates representative contrastive training strategies for universal multimodal embeddings under a unified, reproducible benchmarking framework on MMEB. Surprisingly, direct evaluations reveal that sophisticated strategies around negative selection, batch construction, and gradient modulation do not consistently deliver meaningful downstream gains.

entry.title: Semantically Steerable Image Tokenization

author.name: Danilo de Goede, Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani, Yuki M. Asano, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: GIST is an adaptive image tokenizer whose token allocation can be steered toward requested semantic fidelity rather than pixel-wise reconstruction error, preventing abrupt discarding of semantically essential content under heavy compression. It integrates semantic guidance into complexity-matched tokenization for multimodal models.

entry.title: PIGEONS: Incremental Long-Video Captioning with Persistent Identity Gallery and Evolving Overarching Narrative Summary

author.name: Xinlong Chen, Weihong Lin, Yuanxing Zhang, Xinyu Liu, Yue Ding, Bozhou Li, Bohan Zeng, Yang Shi, Qiang Liu, Pengfei Wan, Liang Wang, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: PIGEONS is an incremental long-video captioning model that maintains a persistent identity gallery and an evolving overarching narrative summary to keep subject references consistent and preserve long-range coherence across limited context windows. It scans the video to build an identity gallery before caption generation, avoiding fragmented segment-wise concatenation.

entry.title: EgoWholeView: Camera-Only Head-Mounted Capture of Body and Bimanual Hand Motion for Embodied Demonstrations

author.name: Yaoqing Hu, Xuguo He, Daohan Cui, Yukun Shi, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Presents a wearable six-camera head-mounted rig with a role-specialized pipeline that localizes the rig in a world frame while independently predicting SMPL-X body and MANO hand parameters from downward-facing views, fusing them with self-measured reliability cues. This addresses egocentric capture challenges like limited field of view and hand-object occlusion, supporting self-avatars, teleoperation, and embodied demonstrations relevant to robot learning.

entry.title: PathPilot: An Adaptive Question-Conditioned Multi-Magnification Navigation Agent for Whole-Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Zhengyang Xu, Han Li, Jingsong Liu, Ayako Ura, Shihui Zu, Shaohua Kevin Zhou, Nassir Navab, Peter Sch\"uffler

entry.summary: PathPilot is a whole-slide imaging agent that mimics how pathologists navigate slides, adaptively selecting magnifications and integrating evidence across scales conditioned on the diagnostic question, rather than operating at fixed or predefined magnifications. It explicitly models cross-magnification interactions for more clinically consistent slide analysis.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Semantically Consistent Visual Features via a Simple 3D Prior

author.name: Sebastian Day, Oisin Mac Aodha

entry.summary: This paper proposes a self-supervised method for learning visual features that support accurate semantic correspondence, addressing known failure modes of features from models like DINOv2 such as confusing left/right on symmetric objects. Unlike prior work requiring supervised keypoint annotations, camera poses, or restrictive sphere-like topology assumptions, it uses a simple 3D prior to handle topologically complex object categories.

entry.title: Hallucination-aware Faithful Reasoning in Remote Sensing

author.name: Yi Liu, Jing Zhang, Xiang Feng, Xiaoyu Tian, Haonan Guo, Di Wang, Zengmao Wang, Bo Du

entry.summary: Presents FaithRS, a hallucination-aware self-reflection framework for multimodal LLM reasoning in remote sensing, built on SFHD-43K, a dataset of 43K fine-grained hallucination annotations with types, causes, and visual evidence. Unlike prior post-training that optimizes only final-answer correctness, it supervises detection and correction of mid-reasoning hallucinations. Connects the hallucination-mitigation agenda to geospatial applications.

entry.title: CoTL: Compact Token Learning for 3D Scene Representation

author.name: Han Liang, Sibo Wu, Anpei Chen, R\"udiger Westermann

entry.summary: Presents CoTL, which learns compact per-view token sets from unposed multi-view images that aggregate across views into a view-consistent scene representation, decoded by a query-based Gaussian decoder into explicit renderable 3D Gaussian primitives. Token count grows sub-linearly with views and independently of resolution, enabling scalable scene representation. A solid feedforward 3D reconstruction contribution.

entry.title: GAD: Geometry Attention Distillation for Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Junfeng Ni, Ziyu Zhu, Fan Jiang, Yu Liu, Chiyu Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Zhaoxu Sun, Mu Xu, Siyuan Huang, Yixin Chen

entry.summary: GAD addresses temporal inconsistency in video diffusion models by distilling reliable cross-frame correspondences from a frozen geometry model's attention into the video model's attention, after showing current video attention spreads responses across regions when matching structure. The distilled correspondences link the same static surfaces and moving objects across frames to stabilize generation.

entry.title: Plan-Bench: Can Existing VLMs Go Well Beyond Perception to Reason and Plan in Embodied Worlds?

author.name: Juntong Feng, Qingan Liu, Jingru Dong, Yue Zhu, Weiming Zheng, Yujie Cheng, Xinzhe Han, Shuai Hao, Yunzhi Zhuge, Haiwen Diao, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Plan-Bench, a benchmark with 699 curated instances across 16 subclasses designed to evaluate whether vision-language models can perform high-level reasoning and multi-step planning for embodied tasks, independent of low-level action execution. By isolating planning from execution, it probes spatial integration, temporal state reasoning, and constraint satisfaction, offering a clearer picture of where current VLMs fall short as embodied planners.

entry.title: RAIN: Robotic Task Generalization with Region-Aware Interaction Networks

author.name: Seunghun Lee, Kyuhwan Shim, Yeogyeong Song, Seung Hwan Kim, Sihaeng Lee, Byoung-Tak Zhang, Sunghoon Im, Gunhee Lee

entry.summary: RAIN reformulates robotic tasks as sequences of goal-conditioned subtasks defined by action types and target-region masks, enabling learned skills to be reused and composed across novel objects and layouts. It introduces a Target-adaptive Cross-View Encoder and a planning transformer to counter trajectory memorization in vision-language-action models. The work is significant because task generalization and compositional skill reuse are central open problems in robot learning.

entry.title: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon Robotic World Models

author.name: Hao Wu, Tianyu Shao, Shengju Qian, Yizhou Zhao, Fan Zhang, Penghao Zhao, Weiyan Wang, Yufei Huang, Fan Xu, Kun Wang, Xin Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: ReCAP is a training-free context-scheduling method for autoregressive robot video world models that identifies a memory-role conflict in full-context decoding, where persistent scene information, recent states, and stale history compete for attention. It preserves an initial scene anchor and a recent window of complete states while pruning stale generated history, keeping the pretrained model frozen. The work addresses a key reliability bottleneck for long-horizon world models used in robot planning.

entry.title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy

author.name: Guangrui Ding, Haonan Lin, Rong Tang, Bethany Weinberg, Jianpeng Ao, Qing Xia, Guorong Hu, Dingcheng Sun, Jiaze Yin, Lei Tian, Ji-Xin Cheng

entry.summary: B2B is a self-supervised background removal method for high-dimensional microscopy that exploits the fact that backgrounds are more spatially correlated than signals. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, turning signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-style removal. It achieves over 40-fold background suppression across fluorescence, stimulated Raman, and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, revealing otherwise hidden signatures.

entry.title: CoFlu-Brain: An fMRI Connectivity Foundation Model with Cofluctuation-Based Pretraining

author.name: Ziteng Sui, Junfeng Xia, Wenhao Ye, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: CoFlu-Brain is a foundation model for fMRI functional connectivity that pretrains on framewise cofluctuation observations organized into multiple retained and dropped views rather than a single Pearson-correlation matrix per scan. It learns connectivity structure reproducible across views and predicts representations of dropped views, exploiting frame-resolved dynamics that conventional FC approaches ignore. This offers a richer foundation representation for brain-organization analyses.

entry.title: Residual Compliant Policy: Learning Compliant Policies from Few Demonstrations

author.name: Chunyu Jiang, Yichen Cai, Shuai Li, Wenbin Sun, Jo\~ao Carvalho, Kostas Daniilidis, Oleg Arenz, Cristiana de Farias, Jan Peters

entry.summary: This work presents a framework for learning contact-rich manipulation policies that are precise in free space and compliant in contact, making compliance explicit through teleoperation with a digital twin that visualizes commanded-versus-achieved pose error. The approach learns residual compliant behavior from few demonstrations, addressing the fact that compliance is not directly observable in demonstration data.

entry.title: AnyRank: Reliable Anytime Policy Ranking via Sequential Testing

author.name: Apurva Badithela, David Snyder, Tenny Yin, Jade Sceats, George Pappas, Nikolai Matni, Masha Itkina, Haruki Nishimura, Anirudha Majumdar

entry.summary: AnyRank is a sequential-testing method for ranking multiple robot policies from limited hardware trials, adaptively allocating trials to policies that are hard to separate while guaranteeing bounded probability of incorrect rankings at any stopping time. It can also exploit prior information from expert intuition or simulation to prioritize hardware evaluations. This tackles a real statistical weakness in how robot policies are commonly compared.

entry.title: Barrier-Constrained Guidance For Real-time Asynchronous VLA Execution

author.name: Wenbo Yu, Jifan Li, Wenke Xia, Yuchen Li, Yizhuo Zhang, Pei Ren, Zhengping Che, Di hu

entry.summary: This paper introduces FreeBar, a training-free inference-time plugin that addresses boundary misalignment in asynchronous execution of vision-language-action (VLA) models by formulating chunk alignment as a barrier-guided constraint in action space using control barrier functions. It aims to enable robust real-time robot control without the retraining, architectural changes, or fixed-prefix inpainting costs of prior delay-aware approaches.

entry.title: Exploring the Limits of Combinatorial Generalization in Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Xupeng Zhang, Yantai Yang, Chang Guo, Zhaokai Yin, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: This controlled study shows that VLA models trained end-to-end on limited skill sequences memorize templates, achieving 40% success on seen combinations but only 7.7% on recombination, and proposes Hierarchical Subtask Execution (HSE) as a diagnostic framework with shared planner, trigger, and policy interfaces. The finding is significant because it quantifies a core generalization failure of current VLA models in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Learning Robot Policies for Whole-Body Mobility Assistance via Dynamic Human Motion Generation

author.name: Shikun Ban, Shohei Nagai, Qingyang Song, Hanxi Wan, Eric Zhao, Thomas Wang, Zackory Erickson

entry.summary: This paper presents a simulation-based framework for learning whole-body assistive robot policies for tasks like sit-to-stand and lift-and-transfer, centered on a human policy trained with adversarial motion priors that produces realistic, cooperative care-recipient behavior. This overcomes prior work treating humans as static, enabling safer and more realistic policy learning for physically demanding care tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Planning: Differentiable Control-in-the-loop End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhidong Wang, Zirui Li, Zitong Shan, Zhiqi Mao, Qihang Huang, Zhan Chen, Jingsong Liang, Han Yu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: DIVA embeds an identified, differentiable actuator-level vehicle dynamics model inside the training loop of an end-to-end driving network, allowing gradients from actual vehicle motion to flow back into the planner. This addresses the traditional gap where hand-tuned tracking controllers block gradient flow, plus issues of aliased supervision, rate mismatch, and vehicle model discrepancy.

entry.title: WAVE-0: Bridging VLA Policies and WAMs with Lightweight Latent Future Prediction

author.name: Haomin Wang, Anqiong Ji, Ke Wang, Zhongshan Liu, Ru Ying, Ran Zheng, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: WAVE-0 connects vision-language-action policies with world action models through a lightweight latent world model, letting anticipated action consequences directly guide action generation rather than using future prediction only as an auxiliary target. This avoids the costly video generation or large-scale video pretraining relied on by most prior WAM approaches.

entry.title: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Zijun Xu, Wendi Chen, Xinkai Wang, Jiachen Zou, Hongjin Chen, Hairuo Liu, Bokai Lin, Shihao Ma, Ke Ma, Zhiwei Zhang, Zhuohao Yan, Ke Wu, Haoming Song, Xueqi Li, Chuan Wen, Jieru Zhao, Wenchao Ding, Cewu Lu, Lixin Yang

entry.summary: ForceWAM is a force world action model that separates task-compatible interaction outcome prediction from knowledge of how local actions change contact forces. A world model trained on demonstrations jointly predicts future video and six-axis force/torque trajectories, while a separate inverse dynamics model learns from both demonstrations and task-agnostic play data. This decoupling aims to improve contact-rich robotic manipulation where force feedback information is scarce in demonstrations alone.

entry.title: Shaping Latent Mixture-of-Experts: From Expert Geometry to Layerwise Capacity Allocation

author.name: Yaoxiang Wang, Kai Zhang, Ruobing Xie, Lanrui Wang, Guoliang Zhao, Junhui Li, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: LatentMoE moves expert computation into a lower-dimensional space, making expert input dimension and intermediate width explicit design choices, and shows Jacobian rank is jointly bounded by these dimensions with near-square experts optimal at fixed parameters. It also uses layerwise intrinsic dimension to guide capacity allocation across depth.

entry.title: Probable but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of Decision Models as Synthetic Survey Respondents

author.name: Mantas Lukauskas, Viktorija \v{S}arkauskait\.e

entry.summary: This audit tests whether decision models (language models outputting rating-scale probabilities) and generative LLMs can substitute for human survey respondents, evaluating 14 decision models and 47 LLMs against a real Lithuanian organisational-psychology survey with 263 respondents. The best generative model, MiniMax M3, reaches a Psychometric Similarity Score of 0.813, only matching simple statistical baselines like a Gaussian copula fit.

entry.title: Structural Chain-of-Thought: Reasoning with Executable Computational Graphs

author.name: Petr Senatorov, Karim Vafin, Elena Tutubalina, Oleg Somov

entry.summary: Replaces free-form chain-of-thought with generation of executable computational graphs whose deterministic execution yields the final answer, improving verifiability and faithfulness. Trained with graph-based RL rewarding structural validity, correctness, and node overlap, it improves accuracy across five benchmarks and four model families while cutting generation length 5-6x.

entry.title: SkillFusion: Towards Reliable Multi-Skill Composition for LLM Agents

author.name: Enhao Huang, Xinye Zhao, Yiming Li, Bingrun Yang, Nanjun Zhou, Chunshu Xia, Hongwei Yao, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: SkillFusion is an offline compiler that merges independently authored agent skills into a single coherent skill, resolving incompatible requirements, conflicting preferences, and redundant instructions. It uses typed scoped constraints, a type-scope gate, an adversarial verifier, and explicit priority or routing mechanisms for hard conflicts.

entry.title: Small but Mighty: Test Suites as Improvement Signals for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yutong Cheng, Wei Cheng, Wenchao Yu, Dawei Zhou, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: This paper tackles the improvement-signal problem for self-evolving agents that rewrite their own harness: agent rollouts are costly and subjective while repository tests are too sparse. TeSearch uses a quality-diversity evolutionary algorithm to find small, dense test suites as executable improvement signals, treating suite size as a behavior descriptor. This is a practical mechanism for safer and cheaper self-improvement verification.

entry.title: RAP-WAM: Learning World-Action Models through Predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations

author.name: Yuanpeng He, Ceyao Zhang, Fangjing Li, Kefei Zhu, Lijian Li, Yueheng Li, Tianjia He, Wenpin Jiao, Zhi Jin, Yaodong Yang, Yuanpei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RAP-WAM, a world-action model that adapts video generation priors to robot control using predictive rehearsal on model-generated inputs with recorded targets, plus action perturbations to measure prediction sensitivity. Action-response credit assignment combines these responses, prediction error, and a rehearsal prior to allocate visual supervision for policy learning.

entry.title: Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Yaolun Zhang, Yiran Wu, Joe Nguyen, Shengyu Dai, Saba Moeinizade, Zhenwen Shao, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: UCoE is a training-free method that co-evolves an executable verifier program alongside the agent's harness state while keeping all model parameters frozen, addressing the problem that stale or wrong verifiers degrade self-improvement on open-ended tasks lacking reference answers or tests. The method synthesizes feedback signals to update both the verifier and the harness that shapes later task handling. This targets a key weakness of model-based-verifier self-improvement loops.

entry.title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation

author.name: Yufeng Li, Sheng Yao, Peng Zeng, Dezhang Kong, Shi Lin, Changting Lin, Xun Wang, Meng Han

entry.summary: This paper defines Memory Echo — excess retrieval exposure gained by historical information from a single source without independent evidence — and introduces MEchoBench to evaluate its emergence, correction resistance, persistence, and effect on agent answers. Drawing on memory psychology, it proposes provenance-guided mitigation for repeated retrieval and write-back amplification in long-term agent memory.

entry.title: Rethinking Quality in Large Language Model Routing: Security-Conditioned Model-and-Budget Selection

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Zhenxiang Huang, Yuyang Zhang, Yuchen Yang

entry.summary: SCRouter is an LLM router that distinguishes security-sensitive queries from ordinary ones, learning when to prioritize refusal and resistance to malicious instructions over utility, and jointly selecting model and token budget using completion-probability estimates. It addresses a real gap in routers that optimize a single quality metric.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Voting: Fine-Grained Correction of LLM Reasoning through Graph Alignment across Sampled Traces

author.name: Haotian Liu, Yingjian Chen, Xiaohang Xu, Lang Huang, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Irene Li

entry.summary: DDRG builds source-grounded claim graphs from a frozen bank of sampled reasoning traces and uses graph alignment to expose claim-level disagreements, routing localized conflicts to an answer-blind verifier for selective correction. This refines self-consistency beyond final-answer voting by resolving intermediate disagreements without additional sampling.

entry.title: VH-GPO: Verified Handoff for LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoze Li, Peng Zhou, Peiyuan Wu, Weijie Zhao, Yinan Xin

entry.summary: VH-GPO addresses reward collapse in group-relative RL (GRPO) when all rollouts in a group fail, by having a frozen teacher repair student failures only up to a state from which the student can succeed, then handing control back. This outcome-verified handoff preserves meaningful student learning signal while providing targeted support.

entry.title: Rotate the Loop: Blockwise Conformality for Looped Transformers

author.name: Alexey Zemtsov, Albina Klepach, Vadim Lomshakov, Andrei Polubarov, Nikita Lyubaykin, Alexander Derevyagin, Vladislav Kurenkov, Alexander Nikulin

entry.summary: This paper analyzes looped transformers, where one shared block recurs, showing that state tracking depends on the geometric form of the residual map between recurrent steps. It proposes blockwise conformal injections that rotate residual groups with per-group timescales, improving performance on hard state-tracking tasks.

entry.title: Akule: Fast and Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Sparse Interaction Diffusion

author.name: Manav Vora, Gokul Puthumanaillam, Aditya Penumarti, Jane Shin, Melkior Ornik

entry.summary: Akule scales diffusion-based multi-robot motion planning by augmenting a frozen single-robot prior with learned modules: a pairwise correction model, a contextual selector deciding which corrections to compute, and a composer combining corrections with context-dependent signed weights. This decomposition separates interaction selection from effect combination, avoiding expensive joint computation for large robot teams. It enables coordinated denoising with sparse interaction computation.

entry.title: Co-DSL: Human-LLM Co-design of Reusable Spatial Concepts for Layout Generation

author.name: R. Kenny Jones, Jiajun Wu, Maneesh Agrawala

entry.summary: Co-DSL is a framework where users and LLMs collaboratively build a library of reusable spatial concepts: the LLM converts natural-language descriptions into executable concept implementations, and users give lightweight feedback on example executions to refine them. In a second stage, the LLM authors layout programs composed from the personalized concept library to satisfy new requests.

entry.title: When Messages Go Wrong: Understanding Communication Faults in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jinhao Zhou, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jiongchi Yu, Fahao Chen, Jun Wu

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study examines how communication faults, such as message loss, delay, and context expiration, manifest and propagate in LLM-based multi-agent systems, where semantic errors can silently alter task-relevant information in natural-language messages. The authors construct a cross-layer taxonomy linking lower-stack disturbances to task outcomes, filling a gap in systematic fault analysis for multi-agent LLM deployments.

entry.title: Unravel: Recovering an Interactive 3D Scene from a Single Image

author.name: Hui Shan, Keyang Luo, Binjia Zhou, Ming Li, Kai Li, Xin Wang, Zhenyang Li, Zesong Yang, Weikai Chen, Runze Zhang, Xin Wang, Yanwei Fu, Zhen Chen, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: Unravel is a training-free framework that converts a single image into an interactive 3D scene where each object is an independent movable asset. It uses an agentic harness that iteratively peels objects from the image layer by layer with a VLM planner and image editor, then reconstructs spatial relationships using point clouds.

entry.title: VLA-GAUGE: Systematically Evaluating Generalization and Robustness in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jun Xiao, Rui Ye, Dong Cao, Jinyu Gu, Ying Wang, Zhiliang Zhu

entry.summary: VLA-GAUGE is a diagnostic framework for vision-language-action models that unifies in-distribution versus out-of-distribution generalization testing with perturbation robustness analysis under a shared executable task representation. It includes six capability suites, combinatorial perturbation screening, and diagnosis-driven refinement loops.

entry.title: StableJudge: A Lightweight Adversarial Defense Framework for LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Anning Hu, Yangyu Li, Yuqi Huang, Shengchao Hu, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: StableJudge defends LLM-as-a-Judge pipelines against score-hijacking prompt injection by externalizing mitigation as a reusable pre-scoring capability built around a compact 0.1B-parameter sanitizer, rather than modifying the judge model itself. This keeps robustness independent of judge scale or training and survives judge swaps. It matters because scalar judge scores drive high-stakes downstream decisions like review and ranking.

entry.title: D-World: An Explicit World-Language-Action Model with Recursive Self-Improvement under Dual Control

author.name: Xuan Wen, Baichao Wang

entry.summary: D-World builds an explicit world model for robotics as an inspectable executable digital twin written by a perception agent, with a planning agent searching for actions in simulation and revising the twin's physical parameters after each executed action chunk. Parameter revisions are accepted only if replaying the latest chunk does not increase measured residuals, enabling recursive self-improvement under dual control. This addresses the opacity of implicit world models in robot policies.

entry.title: Learning to Detect Shifts in Unstructured Data Streams via Monitoring-by-Betting

author.name: Siyu Zhou, Jialin Ouyang, Fan Xia, Adarsh Subbaswamy, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Augusto Garcia-Agundez, Sarah Pollet, Jinoos Yazdany, Patrick Vossler, Jean Feng

entry.summary: Reframes distribution-shift detection for generative AI systems using a betting-based monitoring approach that allows adaptive hypothesis of shift direction while preserving false-alarm guarantees, overcoming the sensitivity-breadth tradeoff of pre-specified discrepancy measures. Applied to monitoring unstructured data streams, with clinical collaborators suggesting healthcare deployment contexts. Important for safely monitoring deployed generative systems.

entry.title: LatentRiskBench: Measuring State-Dependent Risks in Enterprise Agents

author.name: Jingyue Cong, Estrid He, Zhuang Li, Nan Wu, Li Shen, Yameng Peng, Xinshu Li, Andy Song

entry.summary: LatentRiskBench evaluates state-dependent safety risks in enterprise agents, where the same action may be safe in one workflow context but violate policy in another. It pairs risky trajectories with benign counterparts sharing the same terminal action but differing in latent policy-relevant states, and introduces metrics including residual risk measures.

entry.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression

author.name: Or Ronai, Vladimir Kulikov, Tomer Michaeli

entry.summary: H-DDCM replaces dense Gaussian codebooks in training-free diffusion-based compression with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries, exploiting the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform for efficiency. This makes generative compression at ultra-low bitrates scalable to the large latent dimensions of modern image and video generators.

entry.title: TextualRL: Textual Reinforcement Learning for Context Management

author.name: Tianyu Huai, Jie Zhou, Bo Mao, Qin Chen, Liang He, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: TextualRL is a gradient-free RL framework in which LLM agents adapt by revising textual context rather than model parameters, using groupwise policy critique that contrasts successful and failed rollouts within a task. It addresses overgeneralization of task-specific fixes in shared contexts by drawing on cross-task evidence when within-task outcomes are uniform.

entry.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Minghao Luo, Liang Chen

entry.summary: DoubtLess is a training-free decoding method where a small reasoning model reads the large model's chain of thought twice, once prompted to be brief and once verbose, and uses the contrastive logit difference to steer the large model toward concise reasoning. It avoids per-model training, steering vectors, or brittle early-stopping heuristics that hurt accuracy.

entry.title: MDN-VJEPA: Multimodal Probabilistic Joint-Embedding World Models

author.name: Yongchao Huang

entry.summary: MDN-VJEPA extends variational joint-embedding predictive architectures by instantiating the latent predictor as a mixture density network, representing multimodal futures with a Gaussian mixture encoding alternative futures, their probabilities, and within-mode uncertainty. The paper addresses temporal coherence of multimodal predictions across trajectories and belief consistency over time. This is relevant to world modeling for planning and control.

entry.title: On the Theoretical Limits of Learning Unconstrained Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Prajwal Ananth, Shuwen Yue

entry.summary: The paper proves that for unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials, the relationship between prediction error and sampling accuracy is exponentially ill-conditioned in dimension: exponentially small energy/force errors can coexist with near-maximal total variation distance between learned and target molecular distributions. The authors identify two failure modes, challenging the claim that energy-and-force matching alone suffices when physical inductive biases are relaxed.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Structured Pruning Under Resource Constraints for Hardware-Efficient Large Language Models

author.name: Cameron Barker, Andreas Paraskeva, Jan N. van Rijn, Elliot J. Crowley, Henry Gouk

entry.summary: The authors propose Heterogeneous Structured Pruning (HSP), a training-free, hardware-aware pruning framework that searches over a heterogeneous space of dense, unstructured, 2:4, block-sparse, and head/channel pruning options per sublayer. Unlike uniform-sparsity methods, HSP optimizes how each structure trades pruning error against latency and memory on target hardware.

entry.title: Sampling from Neural Operator Priors to Solve Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Andrew Millard, Joshua Murphy, Zheng Zhao

entry.summary: The paper pairs neural operator priors with pseudo-bootstrap sequential Monte Carlo (pBS SMC) for solving PDEs in function space from sparse observations and PDE residuals. It introduces a new proposal by adapting the DPM++ algorithm to the guidance setting, achieving the best error-time trade-off across five benchmark PDE systems. Wrapping the proposal in pBS gives the lowest error on most inverse problems, especially at few sampling steps.

entry.title: Intrinsic Geometry Matching: learning observation-equivariant process geometry

author.name: Manuel Lecha, Michael Bronstein, Iolo Jones

entry.summary: Intrinsic Geometry Matching learns the intrinsic geometry of an underlying data-generating process from indirect observations by learning the carre du champ operator, recovering diffusion geometry that is equivariant to the observation process. The method exploits natural perturbations such as time-series steps instead of relying on ambient-space geometry.

entry.title: Robustly Reliable Learning for Regression

author.name: Avrim Blum, Anh Tuan Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper introduces robustly reliable learning for regression under adversarial corruption: given a test point, dataset, corruption budget, and L-Lipschitz hypothesis class, output the optimal prediction range that any consistent predictor must fall within. The authors instantiate the analysis for L-Lipschitz classes under two corruption scenarios. It extends reliable learning theory from classification to the regression setting with concrete algorithms.

entry.title: Learning Source Structure: Bayesian Prediction with Transformers

author.name: Meir Feder, Ruediger Urbanke

entry.summary: The authors construct Markov sources with cross-context information sharing where observations in one context inform predictions in another, using an informed-Bayes reference predictor to quantitatively test what transformers learn. The main result shows transformers trained on such sources learn the shared source structure in ways earlier independent-context analyses did not capture.

entry.title: Screening Collapse under Recursive Synthetic Data

author.name: Jia Zhang, Xin Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes how recursive synthetic-data training degrades the variable-screening stage preceding model fitting: as each generation labels data for the next, target drift can erode or reverse active-inactive score margins, causing screeners to discard variables that clean-label screening would retain, a phenomenon termed screening collapse. The paper provides finite-sample bounds, a late-generation information-loss limit, and a minimax impossibility result in a Gaussian linear setting.

entry.title: Efficient Fr\'echet Distributional Decoder Alignment for Latent Generative Models

author.name: Xianghong Fang, Jiajun Zhu, Esma Aimeur, Dehan Kong, Tim G. J. Rudner

entry.summary: This paper identifies a decoder train-generation mismatch in latent generative models: decoders are trained on reconstruction latents but deployed on generator latents whose distributions differ. It introduces Fréchet Distributional Decoder Alignment (FDDA), an efficient post-training method that freezes the latent generator and fine-tunes the decoder with a distribution-level FD objective. This should improve output fidelity for latent diffusion and similar models with minimal cost.

entry.title: Self-Distillation with Verbal Regularization

author.name: Jiazheng Li, Yawei Li, Junru Lu, Zhenyi Shen, Di Yin, Lin Gui, Xing Sun, David R\"ugamer, Xinpeng Wang, Yulan He

entry.summary: VRSD addresses a bias in on-policy self-distillation where privileged information makes teacher supervision favor shortcut reasoning and sharply reduces output entropy. It uses system prompts as verbal regularization on the teacher, encouraging rethinking and exploration to counteract the entropy collapse.

entry.title: TETRIS-4DGS: Efficient Post-Training Compression of 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Chengzhen Wu, Kelei Liu, Sicheng Li, Lu Yu, Yiyi Liao

entry.summary: TETRIS-4DGS provides a generalized post-training compression framework for 4D Gaussian Splatting that applies importance-based adaptive quantization compatible with existing image and video codecs. This avoids per-scene optimization, enabling low-latency compression and better generalization for dynamic scene representation.

entry.title: Visually Legible but Adversarial: Watermark-Constrained Attacks on End-to-End VLMs for Document Understanding

author.name: Qingzhe Han, Fan Dang, Shengqi Chen, Xinyi Sun, Haoyu Xiong, Lingkun Li, Di Zhang

entry.summary: AR-AWM is a white-box adversarial attack that optimizes a small, spatially distributed watermark region to disrupt end-to-end VLM document understanding without using questions, prompts, or language-model gradients. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, watermarks covering under 8 percent of pixels sharply reduce DocVQA accuracy while remaining visually legible.

entry.title: VGGA: Geometry-Grounded Autoencoder for Video Generation

author.name: Chaofan Gan, Yian Zhao, Shijie Li, Tieyuan Chen, Zicheng Zhao, Mehrtash Harandi, Weiyao Lin

entry.summary: VGGA is a geometry-aware video autoencoder that treats video as 2D projections of dynamic 3D worlds, incorporating explicit geometric constraints into latent space learning rather than optimizing purely for pixel reconstruction. This yields more structured latents for downstream latent video generative models.

entry.title: Auditing Observation-Quality Shortcuts in the Evaluation of Person-Centered Motion for Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Chaehyun Kim, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: Introduces an observation-quality-aware evaluation framework for human-centered video anomaly detection combining quality diagnostics, quality balancing, motion orthogonalization, and robustness analyses. On UCF-Crime human-centered categories, quality-only features match or exceed the discrimination of multi-cue motion features, revealing that reported motion-based performance partly reflects detection and tracking quality shortcuts rather than task-relevant motion.

entry.title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models

author.name: Zihan Meng, Weidong Chen, Dexiang Hong, Xinyan Liu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: FoveaTree is a training-free, two-stage visual token pruning framework for video LLMs that uses merge-gain density estimation over a quadtree to decide token dropping, merging, and retention, plus a second stage addressing attention drift. It targets the high cost of encoding hundreds of visual tokens per frame while avoiding discarding critical evidence.

entry.title: Physical-Field-Bridged Material Parameter Inference from Multi-View Deformation Videos

author.name: Linrui Shou, Jie Li, Yu Liu, Tao Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a single-pass framework that infers simulation-ready material parameters from multi-view RGB deformation videos by first predicting dense physical response fields (force/contact masks, motion-flow, stress-response maps) and then conditioning constitutive classification and parameter regression on them, avoiding per-scene reconstruction or simulation-in-the-loop optimization. This matters for deformable-object manipulation in robotics.

entry.title: Multimodal Fusion of RGB and Complementary Modalities for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Hu Cao, Yifeng Cheng, Mu He, Mengyu Li, Yinlong Liu, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: The paper proposes a bidirectional polarity-aware cross-modality fusion (BPCF) module for RGB-X semantic segmentation, evaluated across six modality pairings including thermal, LiDAR, depth, event, polarization, and light field. It reports state-of-the-art results on eight public datasets such as MFNet and KITTI-360.

entry.title: Efficient Scene-Text Refinement via Pixel-Space Grouped Image Generation

author.name: Yaoli Liu, Guo-Hua Wang, Yiyang Chen, Qing-Guo Chen, Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo, Yao-Xiang Ding

entry.summary: Introduces PixText, a model that formulates local scene-text refinement as grouped pixel-space image generation, regenerating only target regions while preserving the rest of the image and using MeanFlow for efficient four-step sampling. It also releases Text Refinement Bench for evaluating text correction in generated images. Addresses the persistent weakness of generative models at rendering small, legible text.

entry.title: Refine Where It Matters: Contact-Adaptive Meshing for Deformable Object Manipulation

author.name: Gabriel Johnson, Tom Olesch, Fei Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a contact-adaptive mesh refinement framework for deformable object simulation that adds spatial resolution only where contact demands it, scoring candidate edges with geometric, elastic, and contact quantities from the solver. A fully GPU-parallel procedure selects a conflict-free refinement subset while updating mesh topology and physical state.

entry.title: FoundationVIO: Enforcing Metric Scale in Feed-forward Visual-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Jin Rhee, Yuhao Zhang, Frank Dellaert, Maurice Fallon

entry.summary: FoundationVIO addresses the ambiguous geometric scale of feed-forward geometric foundation models in emerging visual SLAM systems by integrating inertial measurements, drawing on classical visual-inertial odometry principles. GFM predictions are locally consistent up-to-scale but unanchored to physical measurement, which propagates into trajectories and reconstructions. The method enforces metric scale in GFM-enabled odometry pipelines.

entry.title: MIRROR: Reflecting Hidden Symmetries from Offline Robot Interaction Data

author.name: Shiqi Liu, Yihang Yao, Peide Huang, Mengdi Xu, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: MIRROR learns how a known symmetry group operates jointly on observations and actions in POMDPs directly from offline interaction data, using adversarial tuple matching over one-step transitions plus explicit group-consistency constraints. This removes the need for hand-specified, viewpoint-dependent pixel transformations that prior symmetry-aware policy learning requires. The learned coupled transformations can then be used for symmetry-aware policy learning and data augmentation.

entry.title: TRACE: Efficient Transfer Learning for Neural Whole-Body Control Across Humanoid Embodiments

author.name: Qingyu Lan, Zhihao Tian, Zifan Wang, Junwei Liang

entry.summary: TRACE enables efficient cross-embodiment adaptation of pretrained humanoid behavior foundation models by injecting kinematic priors into input/output projections, aligning nominal joint dynamics, and combining encoder distillation with low-rank RL fine-tuning on a quality-screened motion set using a two-phase curriculum. It preserves pretrained motion representations while specializing feedback control to the target robot.

entry.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights

author.name: Sahil Garg, Ruhi Gottumukkala, Vishal Agarwal, Shubham Vishwakarma

entry.summary: The authors evaluate 26 models (19 open-weight, 7 closed) on CTI-REALM, a benchmark where agents convert threat-intelligence reports into working detections against live telemetry. Their key finding is that open-weight models can match top closed models at under a tenth of the cost when given enough interaction turns, and that the original benchmark's message limit was a confound.

entry.title: ConicFlow: constrained Inference-time optimal control for flow matching models

author.name: Shervin Khalafi, Kasra Fallah, Sung Cho, Dongsheng Ding, James Anderson, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: ConicFormes constrained sampling from flow matching models as an inference-time optimal control problem balancing trajectory deviation against reward under hard terminal constraints. A receding-horizon primal-dual algorithm with adaptive dual multipliers steers generation toward feasible samples, with a terminal-estimate variant improving stability.

entry.title: Decoupling Knowledge Forgetting and Refusal Learning in MLLM Unlearning

author.name: Haodong Chen, Shengtao Wen, Dong Liang, Lingbing Guo, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows multimodal unlearning evaluations conflate two failure modes: knowledge suppression causing confabulation, and refusal training that alters behavior without erasing knowledge detectable via multiple-choice probing. It proposes Forget-Aware Self-Distillation to achieve honest ignorance, where the model genuinely loses target knowledge and acknowledges this.

entry.title: EvoCowork: A Benchmark for Real-World Office Tasks

author.name: Zhou Liu, Xingyan Chen, ZhaoYang Han, Zewei Pan, Zeli Su, Ningxin Pan, Xue Hu, Kaixiong Ting, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: EvoCowork is a 240-task benchmark for evaluating harness-level recursive self-improvement on office work spanning presentations, documents, spreadsheets, and cross-file workflows, with model weights held fixed. It scores artifacts for content correctness, native structure, formulas, cross-file consistency, and visual quality, and its protocol tests whether agents learn reusable procedures rather than task-specific fixes.

entry.title: Certify the Decision, Not Every Score: Exact Top-k Selection from Few Evaluations

author.name: Yuhe Sui, Yingzhi Tang

entry.summary: Introduces Certified Adaptive Selection (CAS), which returns the exact top-k candidate set as soon as remaining uncertainty cannot change the decision, using guaranteed lower and upper bounds on Expected Shortfall. A one-cut stopping test is proven necessary and sufficient for information-disjoint Cartesian intervals, with prediction used to guide evaluation rather than to certify.

entry.title: Words to World: Benchmarking LLMs in Interactive Physical Environments

author.name: Xinnan Dai, Kaiqi Yang, Yaxin Li, Cheng Luo, Wanli Li, Mingqing Xiao, Xinyang Jiang, Daoan Zhang, Kaitao Song, Fengze Liu, Zefan Cai, Caihua Shan

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark evaluating LLMs in closed-loop physical interaction, where models control a harness connected to real robotic arms, cameras, and sensors, issuing instructions, interpreting physical feedback, and adapting actions. This moves beyond static text, offline tool calls, and simulation-only evaluations toward real-world embodied competence.

entry.title: Large Decision Models: Repurposing Large Language Models as Single-Pass Decision Makers

author.name: Ziyi Chen, Yan Zhang, Jianhui Wei, Jianing Yin, Daoan Zhang

entry.summary: Large Decision Models repurpose LLMs to output explicit probabilities over run-time-specified labels in a single prefill pass, avoiding sequential decoding costs. Diverse Decision Supervision adapts models to this interface and Self-Posed Reasoning Distillation narrows the gap to reasoning models via teacher-generated tasks.

entry.title: From Stages to States: Unified Iterative Reasoning for MLLMs

author.name: Chuang Yu, Xuefei Ma, Yuanhao Feng, Wuxiong Zeng, Bo Wang, Minghong Cai, Dongming Wu, Fei Zhou, Chen Tang, Wenwen Tong, Lewei Lu, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: ReState reformulates multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning in MLLMs from a stage-centric pipeline into a state-driven dynamic process, via Unified Reasoning State Modeling and Closed-Loop Reasoning State Updating. This addresses fragmented reasoning and the training-inference reasoning-state gap.

entry.title: Knowledge Interaction in Hypernetwork-based Continual Learning: Conflict and Composition

author.name: Jiaqi Zheng, Yi Hu, Yadong Mu, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: This work studies how knowledge from a base model, hypernetwork-generated parameter updates, and input context interact during continual learning of LLMs. It analyzes conflicts that determine whether new knowledge overrides outdated knowledge, and multi-hop composition that tests whether new knowledge combines with existing knowledge for generalization. The findings inform methods for adapting models without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Uncovering Robustness Weaknesses in LLM Agents via Persona Evolution with Task-Integrity Constraints

author.name: Yutao Xie, Jingbo Yang, Guanyu Yao, Xiaoyu Yang, Duo Ding, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: TIPER automatically evolves user simulator personas to discover agent-specific weaknesses while preserving task integrity, avoiding the overly cooperative simulator bias that inflates robustness estimates. It improves on predefined user behaviors and failure-oriented search by exposing genuine robustness failures without invalidating the underlying task.

entry.title: RetroPlanner: Multi-Route Expansion and Multi-Objective Reasoning for LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning

author.name: Ye Rin Kim, Yongjun Jeong, Seongjun Yun, Hanbum Ko, Soohyun Oh, Sungbin Lim, Sungwoong Kim

entry.summary: Introduces RetroPlanner, an LLM-based retrosynthesis planner that expands and compares multiple candidate routes per step rather than a single molecule, optimizing across synthesizability objectives including reaction plausibility, round-trip consistency, and starting-material price. This steers search toward practically viable chemistry routes rather than merely solvable ones.

entry.title: When 1+1 Backfires: Rethinking Relevance-Diversity Balancing for Sample-Aware Visual Token Reduction

author.name: Yihang Huang, Peisong Wen, Chenhao Zhou, Difu Feng, Qianqian Xu

entry.summary: Systematically challenges the assumption of a universal relevance-diversity balance in visual token compression for vision-language models, showing via dataset-level grid search and per-sample oracle-weight recovery that optimal weights vary across benchmarks and even within a single benchmark. The work motivates sample-aware token reduction strategies rather than fixed relevance-plus-diversity combinations.

entry.title: Neural Bayesian Networks for Modular and Scalable Decision-Making Under Uncertainty

author.name: Giovanni Briglia, Marco Lippi, Stefano Mariani, Franco Zambonelli

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Bayesian Networks, where each conditional in a Bayesian network factorization is replaced by a differentiable tensor-valued mechanism while preserving the graph structure. NBNs retain the modularity and interpretability of classical BNs while addressing their expressiveness and scale limits of tabular or linear-Gaussian conditionals.

entry.title: When LLM Agents See a Conflict but Still Proceed: Cross-Domain Dependencies in Network Slicing

author.name: Marcos Lima Romero, Ricardo Suyama

entry.summary: Evaluates ten LLM models in a smart-grid network-slicing scenario where an agent must detect a cross-domain dependency before an irreversible action, such as decommissioning an intentionally idle protection slice. The study measures whether agents query or read dependency information before acting, with a negative control.

entry.title: REA: From Correct LLM Judgments to Safe Decision Delivery

author.name: Jingxiang Meng, Aofan Liu, Yaoshuai Ma, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: REA (Resolve-Express-Act) is a framework that traces safety-guard judgments through output parsing and fallback handling to the final application action, showing that correct classifications can be lost through formatting and parsing failures. Experiments show parsing the safety verdict preserves reasoning guards' accuracy advantages, while stricter explanation requirements can reject additional correct predictions. The work highlights an overlooked gap between a guard being correct and its decision being safely delivered.

entry.title: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment

author.name: Qingchuan Ma, Yuexiao Ma, Xiang Meng, Yixuan Zou, Tianyu Xie, Wang Chen, Yuhui Zeng, Yuhang Wu, Xiawu Zheng, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: RoTA-Bench evaluates whether vision-language models can turn 2D observations into actionable 3D understanding via interactive 3D-to-2D projection alignment: given a target silhouette, the model chooses successive rotations of an object to recover the projection within an action budget. An automated pipeline builds silhouette-preserving 3D objects from 2D icons with reversible initialization to guarantee solvability, yielding 674 tasks and a stratified 100-task test set. A substantial human-model gap persists, exposing weaknesses in embodied spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Adaptive-Group Process Rewards for GUI Agents

author.name: Zirui Shang, Yang Liu, Xin Shu, Zhi Gao, Xinxiao Wu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: This paper tackles sparse outcome rewards in RL training of GUI agents by proposing an adaptive-group process reward framework that dynamically segments trajectories into semantically coherent subgoal groups. It estimates process rewards at both action and group levels, with a critic evaluating actions based on visual changes and downstream evidence across long-horizon trajectories.

entry.title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills

author.name: Letian Zhu, Han Li, Yifan Yao, Xinping Lei, Xinyu Che, Jiahao Wang, Dianyi Wang, Yucheng Fu, Jiakai Wang, Zhiqi Bai, Wenbo Su, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: Socratic Skill Learning (SSL) interleaves expert teaching with student practice, where the student agent remains the sole environment operator and skill author, able to question, test, and adapt advice to learn transferable skills. The authors also introduce SkillTransferBench with 35 task families and 408 executable cases pairing public variation specifications with held-out evaluation in fresh sessions.

entry.title: LifeSearch: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents for Real-World Life and Productivity

author.name: Yibo Wang, Senjie Jin, Yansong Ning, Xinbing Liang, Haotian Luo, Jiazheng Zhang, Yuxuan He, Will Wu, Clarenceai

entry.summary: LifeSearch is a benchmark of 203 Chinese and English deep-research tasks derived from real user queries across seven life and productivity domains, with over 4,000 expert-written rubrics built from more than 4,500 hours of annotation. It evaluates whether deep research agents can handle practical, everyday information needs beyond academic-style tasks. Both report-quality and concrete value criteria are covered.

entry.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments

author.name: Linhai Ma, Yan Wang, Lingfei Qian, Yupeng Cao, Victor Gutierrez Basulto

entry.summary: The paper identifies a derivation gap in LLM tool-call judges: they accept correct argument values far less often when no reference text in their input states what the value should be, such as unmentioned schema defaults or values requiring inference. Controlled experiments across seven judges show this reflects reliance on references, not merely truncation artifacts.

entry.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents

author.name: Ashutosh Hathidara

entry.summary: The paper proposes calibrating an agent's verbalized per-step confidence against the eventual outcome of a multi-step episode rather than current-step correctness, using GRPO group rollouts to supply success labels and proper scoring rules under offline RL on recorded trajectories. This yields a signal for deciding whether to trust, abstain, or hand off to a human.

entry.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yuchen Lu, Julian McAuley, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: CarryOn is an object-oriented context runtime that organizes long-horizon agent context around reusable task objects rather than raw interaction histories. It builds a context view from continuation carriers, execution context, and a live tail of recent interactions, addressing how to keep the reusable basis valid as the environment changes.

entry.title: MRFlow: Mechanism-Structured Residual Flow Matching for Virtual Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Haojie Yang, Ran Su

entry.summary: MRFlow treats virtual cell perturbation prediction as conditional transport between empirical single-cell populations using flow matching in a variational latent space, preserving rare states and subpopulations rather than average expression shifts. The vector field decomposes into mechanism-structured components with greedy low-cost supervision.

entry.title: PreSO: Privileged Representation Isolation for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yuhang Yang, Mingxuan Xia, Chao Ye, Shuai Zhu, Shouqing Yang, Haobo Wang, Shenzhi Yang, Zhengqing Zang, Chenglong Wang

entry.summary: PreSO studies on-policy self-distillation where a self-teacher conditioned on privileged information converts sparse RLVR signals into dense token-level supervision, asking which privileged changes are worth distilling. It finds that compact hints produce more concentrated, directionally consistent representation shifts with more sustained downstream gains than full solutions, and isolates them accordingly.

entry.title: CoEvoke: Evoking Multi-Agent Collaboration for Trajectory Collection

author.name: Lin Wu, Shu Yao, Yuheng Wang, Jingru Fan, Huatao Li, Yihan Li, Liu Yixuan, Cheng Liu, Jian Chang, Zeyu Zhao, Aohua Zhang, Huiying Zhao, Shuyuan Zhu, Chen Qian

entry.summary: CoEvoke is a cross-domain framework that deliberately induces checking, feedback, and repair interactions during multi-agent trajectory collection by injecting recoverable perturbations and reference-based guidance. It yields 4,567 reconstructable trajectories over software-engineering and reasoning tasks, with feedback-driven gains of 47.72-100 percentage points in controlled pair experiments.

entry.title: Is the Future Predictable? Modeling Future Predictability for Reliable Temporal Reasoning

author.name: Yongyi Huang, Huaping Zhang, Wenyao Cui, Qiuchi Li, Lei Li, Baohua Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces ChronoRegime, a temporal reasoning task requiring models to judge whether historical evidence justifies committing to a future answer, and Confidence-Aware Temporal Reasoning (CTR), which regulates commitment based on estimated future predictability. This addresses LLM overconfidence on inherently volatile future facts.

entry.title: Beyond Discrimination: Evaluating Probability Calibration in Radiomics-Image Fusion for Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Morgan May, Abraham Campbell, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Simon Caton, Pierpaolo Dondio

entry.summary: Using 396 KiTS23 patients, this study evaluates whether fusing radiomics features with image models improves not only discrimination but also probability calibration for renal cell carcinoma classification. Across 12 matched comparisons, fusion improved AUC and average precision in all cases and improved Brier score and NLL in 11 of 12, with near-universal calibration gains. The work argues calibration and proper scoring rules should be standard in clinical model evaluation.

entry.title: RUBATO: Decoupled Clocks Allow Full-Duplex Models to Think as Fast as They Can

author.name: Yi-Jen Shih, Puyuan Peng, Haohe Liu, David Harwath, Abdelrahman Mohamed

entry.summary: RUBATO addresses full-duplex speech models with internal thinking streams by replacing fixed decoding rates with decoupled, hardware-adaptive clocks so each stream decodes as fast as hardware allows while maintaining real-time conversation. This removes the assumption of a specific latency hardware profile and better matches the intrinsically asynchronous nature of internal reasoning. The result is more accurate responses without breaking conversational flow.

entry.title: Rethinking Activation Functions: Reducing Bias Can Improve Learning
