author.name: Zirui Peng, Heyi Zheng, Ziming Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies activation bias, the nonzero mean of common activation functions like ReLU, GELU, Swish, and Sigmoid, showing it accelerates early loss reduction but causes overshooting and a steeper loss landscape. Reducing activation bias slows initial learning but yields lower final loss, validated on vision and language models.

entry.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence

author.name: Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Wenyang Hui, Weiqiang Hang, Luqing Wang, Zejian Wang, Zirui Tu, Jingsheng Mao, Shaobo Hu, Yang Luo, Jiale Guo, Jin Zhang, Yudan Liu, Zhaokai Luo, Ren Huan, Yao Hu, Chengyue Jiang, Wenjie Li, Chuan Mu

entry.summary: Vela proposes using real user behavior histories from platforms as a supervisory signal for LLMs, converting behavior data into training data that teaches models to infer preferences, intent, and likely future actions over long time horizons. It targets applications from personal assistants to recommendation and advertising.

entry.title: Getting Space Right: Agentic Rewards for Image Generation

author.name: Xiaofeng Tan, Jiaxin Lin, Haobo Yuan, Tiancheng Shen, Zihan Su, Rui Chen, Hongsong Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: This work identifies failure modes in RL for spatial text-to-image generation, namely unreliable spatial rewards in open-world settings and rollouts lacking a basic-to-complex progression. The authors propose a curriculum-guided RL framework featuring SpatialCritic, an agentic reward model combining reusable verification guidance with specialized vision tools, plus counterfactual-perturbation preference datasets and agent-harness alignment.

entry.title: To Defer or Not to Defer? Online Learning with LLMs and Congested Experts

author.name: Vasileios Saketos, William Reveillard, Alexandre Proutiere, Sebastian Dalleiger, Ming Xiao

entry.summary: Formulates LLM-to-human deferral as an online sequential decision problem where expert capacity is constrained, requiring the system to balance LLM confidence reliability (which must be learned from selectively observed, delayed expert feedback) against queue congestion. The framework captures realistic constraints of hybrid AI-human support systems.

entry.title: Across Viewpoints and Time: Trajectory-Generalizable Physical Attacks on World Models and Video Understanding Models

author.name: Song Xia, Meiwen Ding, Chenqi Kong, Wenhan Yang, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: Studies whether a single printed physical adversarial texture can fool world models and video understanding models across varying real-world camera-object trajectories, proposing TARA, a trajectory-aware optimization method that aligns adversarial gradients over evolving geometric viewpoints. The work exposes an underexplored physical robustness threat for models deployed in dynamic visual environments.

entry.title: E8 Lattice Key Quantization for Low-Bit KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Sasho Nedelkoski, Alexander Acker, Soeren Becker, Dominik Scheinert, Odej Kao

entry.summary: The paper shows that 2-bit keys and 2-bit values (k2v2) can preserve near-baseline LLM quality when keys are compressed with E8-lattice vector quantization, which exploits correlations across adjacent dimensions to exceed the signal-to-noise ratios of independent scalar quantization. This targets memory-constrained serving of long-context models, where KV-cache size is a primary bottleneck.

entry.title: SurgiCLAW: An Interpretable Atomic-Skill Agent for Precision Robotic Micromanipulation

author.name: Angen Ye, junjie xie, Yujia Song, Junkai Huang, Dapeng Zhang

entry.summary: SurgiCLAW is a hierarchical framework for precision surgical robotics that confines an MLLM to visual understanding, structured explanation, and atomic skill selection, while deterministic control programs handle physical execution. It is demonstrated on brain-machine-interface implantation, a high-precision task. The design prioritizes safety, interpretability, and verifiable low-level control.

entry.title: Autoregressive Decoding as a Martingale: Characterizing the Stochastic Dynamics of LLM Generation

author.name: Xiahui Zhu, Zhenyi Qi, Wanwei Liu, Haoang Chi, Yang Tan, Xinyu Sun, Ji Wang

entry.summary: This theoretical work proves that the cumulative per-step prediction error of autoregressive LLM decoding forms a martingale with respect to the decoding filtration, meaning its conditional first moment is zero. This provides a rigorous probabilistic foundation for analyzing sampling dynamics in language generation.

entry.title: LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers

author.name: Zhixiong Zhao, Zukang Xu, Xing Hu, Lifeng Liu, Guangyu Sun, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: LoopQuant is a loop-aware post-training quantization framework for Looped Language Models, addressing cross-loop activation dynamics, heterogeneous loop sensitivity, and recursive error propagation that break feed-forward-oriented PTQ methods. Its three components enable accurate low-bit deployment of parameter-efficient recursive architectures.

entry.title: From Caricature to Collective Artifact: How Persona Construction Drives Polarization in Generative Social Simulations

author.name: Dimitris Michailidis, Petter T\"ornberg, Fernando P. Santos

entry.summary: Using a Twitter-like generative social simulation with personas derived from ANES survey data, this study ablates three layers of partisan identity (affective polarization markers, party identification, vote choice) to see how persona construction choices shape emergent polarization. It finds collective outcomes depend heavily on how survey responses are encoded into personas.

entry.title: Audit Before You Distill: A Controlled Workflow for Reasoning Transfer into Compact Medical Language Models

author.name: Tiago Martinelli, Jo\~ao Paulo Papa, Adriano Jos\'e Pereira

entry.summary: This paper audits teacher rationales before using them for knowledge distillation into compact medical LLMs, using Brazilian Portuguese residency exam questions. It finds correct rationales raise the student's probability of a correct answer by 21 percentage points while wrong rationales lower it by 14 points, and uses this audit signal to filter training data. It matters because it demonstrates a concrete safeguard against propagating teacher errors during distillation in a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: SPLICE: Sparse Physics Library Identification and Compositional Expansion

author.name: Lucas Thil, Jesse Read, Guillaume Doquet, Rim Kaddah

entry.summary: SPLICE enables neural operator libraries for zero-shot physics simulation to be adapted and grown from unlabeled trajectory mixtures where multiple physical mechanisms act simultaneously, without predefined mechanism labels. Candidate operators are identified via convex optimization over trajectory contributions, with a calibrated test assigning discovered operators to mechanisms and detecting library failure cases. This advances compositional scientific machine learning by removing costly labeling requirements.

entry.title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions

author.name: Xialie Zhuang, Zunhai Su, Jia Pan, Ngai Wong, Guanhua Chen, Chuan-Wei Kuo

entry.summary: Introduces a family of decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters combining single-pass prediction with confidence-guided adaptive reasoning: Instant models use bidirectional attention for single-pass accuracy, while AutoThink models invoke explicit reasoning only for uncertain cases. A three-stage pipeline with a new RL method (RLCD squared) using frozen models and proper scoring rules trains calibrated deliberative decisions. This targets efficient, well-calibrated decision-making rather than generic chat.

entry.title: Know-Thy-Not: Training-Free Targeted Negation in Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models

author.name: DoYoung Kim, Changkyu Choi, Ad\'in Ram\'irez Rivera, YunSeok Choi, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: Shows that dual-encoder vision-language models fail at negation because single-embedding contrastive training can at best ignore negated concepts, never penalize their presence. Proposes Know-Thy-Not (KTN), a training-free image-side rejection dimension that directly penalizes negated concepts, plus the COCO-Confusion benchmark requiring genuine rejection. Achieves large gains (+25.6 mAP over vanilla VLMs) across nine backbones.

entry.title: Box-WAM: Box Trajectories as Compact State Representations for World Action Models

author.name: Qinxi Yu, Wenzhou Ding, Gloria X. Wang, Albert J. Zhai, Shenlong Wang

entry.summary: Box-WAM replaces dense future video prediction in world action models with oriented bounding-box trajectories of task-relevant objects, providing a lightweight state representation that preserves planning and supervision benefits. This reduces the computational cost of predicting full-frame futures during training and inference for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes

author.name: Yiqing Peng, Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Dongyi Zhang, Zhengjie Zhu, Yi Han, Yangyang Zheng, Hao Wang, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: The paper introduces DoF, a continuous framework quantifying how much decision space is delegated to downstream agents in LLM-based multi-agent systems, with endpoints recovering centralized and decentralized regimes. This enables systematic study of coordination trade-offs between control bottlenecks and local autonomy.

entry.title: Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing

author.name: Xiaolong Xu, Hao Jiang, Bo Jiang, Zhiwen Deng, Ningyuan Sun, Bingzhou Chen, Jin Chen, Chenxing Wei

entry.summary: Diff Diffusion adapts diffusion LLMs to code editing by predicting structured edit paths from an original snippet to its revised form, rather than regenerating full code segments. Denoising is reformulated as edit operations combined with multi-token prediction, matching the sparse, local nature of real IDE edits.

entry.title: LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization

author.name: Lingyi Long, Congyue Zhao, Xiaoou Li, Yanmin Qian, Tao Huang

entry.summary: LinMorph accelerates pretrained Video Diffusion Transformers by recasting post-hoc linearization (replacing attention with linear operators) as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight morphism. Rather than random initialization or rigid manual weight copying, it learns cross-parameter correspondences so each target Gated DeltaNet parameter draws from pretrained knowledge, addressing the initialization bottleneck the authors identify. This targets efficiency for compute-heavy video generation models.

entry.title: When Missingness Follows the Graph: Beyond Feature Propagation for Missing Features

author.name: Enrico Chial\`a, Francesco Ferrini, Antonio Longa, Bruno Lepri, Filippo Maria Bianchi, Manfred Jaeger, Veronica Lachi

entry.summary: This paper formalizes graph-structured mask dependence, where missingness itself propagates among connected nodes (e.g., localized sensor failures), contrasting with the uniform independent missingness assumed in prior GNN missing-feature work. It shows existing feature-propagation methods fail under this realistic setting and proposes approaches that account for structured missingness.

entry.title: LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers

author.name: Wei Fan, Qingyue Yang, Chao-Hong Tan, Qian Chen, Wen Wang, Xiangang Li, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: LoOPSD constructs a stronger self-distillation teacher by searching over the model's layer execution order (repeating layers) while keeping weights fixed, then distills the looped teacher's advantage into the standard student on student-generated prefixes. It alternates between teacher search and distillation for iterative self-improvement.

entry.title: JevGPT: Thinking Fast and Slow in Autonomous Research

author.name: Yasheng Sun, Yanning Dai, Yimeng Chen, Nanbo Li, Firas Laakom, Yifan Xu, Piotr Pi\k{e}kos, Mateusz Ostaszewski, Wenyi Wang, Cheng Luo, Yuhui Wang, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: JevGPT is a dual-system architecture for autonomous research agents that separates fast evidence processing (System One: locating and assessing source relevance in parallel) from deliberative research planning (System Two: setting evidence objectives and integrating findings). The design aims to close the gap between retrieval coverage and evidence actually used in research decisions. It includes Schmidhuber among the authors, indicating a strong research lineage.

entry.title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing

author.name: Yuxuan Ren, Jiatong Li, Ziqiao Meng, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: STAMP is a topology-aware molecular representation that explicitly encodes motif identity, attachment sites, and tree topology, enabling fragment-level learning and precise structural editing. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, improving activity-cliff prediction on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations also support scaffold-preserving molecular editing for drug discovery.

entry.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers

author.name: Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: LLM2R casts 3D part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only LLM: a Point-BERT encoder and Q-Former compress each part into geometric token blocks, which a LoRA-adapted causal LLM processes to predict SE(3) transforms. This avoids the poor scaling of pairwise-relation and iterative generate-and-verify methods on many-part objects. It demonstrates efficient reuse of LLM backbones for structured 3D reasoning.

entry.title: RadarGSOcc: Doppler-Aware 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction Using 4D Radar Tensor with Geometric-Semantic Feature Extraction

author.name: Christofel Rio Goenawan, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: RadarGSOcc is an efficient framework for 3D semantic occupancy prediction using 4D radar tensors, robust to low light and adverse weather where cameras and LiDAR fail. It separately extracts geometric and semantic features including Doppler information and introduces the first large-scale benchmark (K-Radar 3DSemOcc) for radar-based occupancy prediction.

entry.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs

author.name: Divyanshu Bathla, Parag Singla, Jitin Singla

entry.summary: This paper argues that for low-resource machine translation, pre-LLM-era back-translation of monolingual data outperforms continued pretraining with LLMs. With only 1K parallel pairs for Odia and Swahili, interleaved back-translation and parallel fine-tuning beats continued pretraining by wide margins.

entry.title: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Show Whether Two Codebooks on a VAE's Latent Space Agree

author.name: Yusuke Hayashi

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that standard VAE training reports cannot reveal whether the discrete codes written to and read from a VAE latent space agree, constructing two VAEs that reconstruct perfectly and match on all per-example ELBO terms and code histograms while codebook agreement is one in one model and zero in the other. It also derives ELBO-based bounds on how far measured agreement can shift. The result highlights an unenforced consistency assumption underlying systems that read VAE latents as discrete codes.

entry.title: Beyond a Better Score: Long-Horizon Agentic ML Development and Evaluation Protocol for Physics Time Series

author.name: Yue Ma, Lucas Venetoulias, Akbota Assan, Aobo Li

entry.summary: SIDERIUS is an LLM agent system for long-horizon ML development on physics time-series problems (dark matter, neutrinos, gravitational waves) that moves beyond score-chasing, which can produce shortcut-exploiting or scientifically invalid models. It combines contract-defined composable capabilities with an evaluation protocol designed to detect reward gaming and mode collapse. The work connects agentic automation of research with scientific validity safeguards.

entry.title: Decentralized Bandit Learning of Markov Perfect Equilibria

author.name: Felix H\"ofer, H. Mete Soner

entry.summary: The paper proves that in discounted infinite-horizon general-sum Markov games with continuous actions, fully decentralized bandit learning using simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation converges almost surely to the unique stationary Markov perfect equilibrium under strong monotonicity and small step sizes. It establishes an O(n^{-1/2}) convergence rate and extends to episodic finite-horizon settings. A rigorous multi-agent learning theory result.

entry.title: The Sample Complexity of Multicalibration with an ERM Oracle

author.name: Princewill Okoroafor

entry.summary: This work studies how many samples suffice to learn multicalibrated predictors when the auditor class is accessible only through an ERM oracle, rather than by enumeration as in prior epsilon^-3 algorithms for finite classes. It provides an algorithm with nearly matching sample bounds via oracle access.

entry.title: Sparsity Saves Compute, Not Samples: Oracle Inequalities for Dense and Sparse Mixture of Experts

author.name: Sagar Ghosh, Huy Nguyen, Alessandro Rinaldo

entry.summary: This theory paper derives oracle inequalities for least-squares estimation in dense and sparse mixture-of-experts models under Lipschitz experts and gating. Using a Gated Hilbert Space representation that separates routing and expert contributions, the authors obtain fast rates of order (K*d_pr,e + d_pr,g)/n for dense MoEs. The headline message is that sparsity reduces compute but not statistical sample requirements.

entry.title: Imperfect Verifiers, Exact Targets: Inference-Time Scaling for Continuous Generation

author.name: Kijung Jeon, Molei Tao

entry.summary: Presents CS-VGB, an inference-time scaling method for continuous generative models that samples from reward-tilted distributions via repeated denoising and renoising with verifier guidance. The key theoretical guarantee is that with correctly paired transitions, the stationary distribution matches the exact reward-tilted target even when intermediate verifiers are imperfect.

entry.title: Instance-Adaptive Online Multiclass Multicalibration

author.name: Zhiming Huang, Jamie Morgenstern, Aaron Roth, Claire Jie Zhang

entry.summary: The authors give an online multiclass multicalibration algorithm with beyond-worst-case guarantees: when adversarially selected outcome means lie in a low-dimensional affine subspace, error improves from the untenable worst-case rate to a dimension-adaptive rate, without knowing the subspace. The rate is minimax optimal up to constants, with implications for fair and reliable prediction.

entry.title: Memorization in image classification: test set behavior and scaling laws

author.name: Jeevesh Attri, Florentin Guth

entry.summary: This study investigates how neural networks trained to memorize randomized labels or pixels differ from generalizing networks in behavior and training dynamics, using CNNs on image classification. It finds that independently initialized memorizing networks learn different predictive functions on unseen images, indicating memorizers are not simple lookup tables. The work also examines scaling laws for memorization behavior.

entry.title: Mean Accuracy Is the Wrong Estimand for a Release Decision

author.name: Jaewon Choi, Jihye Kang, Namhyuk Ahn

entry.summary: Auditing 2,124 fine-tuned models across eleven language models, the authors show that release decisions based on mean benchmark accuracy violate a 10% deployment failure budget nearly half the time, because fine-tuning induces bimodal mode collapse that standard central-tendency reporting conceals. They argue release decisions should target catastrophic tail risk instead of mean accuracy.

entry.title: Towards Universal Calibration for In-Context Classification

author.name: Awik Dhar, Sunita Sarawagi, Arpit Agarwal

entry.summary: CALIBFORMER is a transformer-based universal calibrator for in-context classification that generalizes to new models and tasks without task-specific fine-tuning, addressing calibration degradation caused by biased in-context example selection. This preserves the core no-fine-tuning convenience of ICL while improving reliability.

entry.title: COMPASS: Membership Inference Attack Against Vision Large Language Models via Adaptive Noise Calibration

author.name: Damien Lo, Hong Kyu Lee, Ruixuan Liu, Li Xiong

entry.summary: COMPASS is a membership inference attack against vision-language models that systematically characterizes membership behavior under controlled Gaussian perturbations at fine noise resolution. The authors find that optimal perturbation magnitude and membership-signal direction vary across model-dataset pairs, and they adaptively calibrate noise accordingly. The work exposes privacy risks of VLLMs deployed in privacy-sensitive domains.

entry.title: Structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics for partial differential equations

author.name: Kyriakos Flouris

entry.summary: The paper observes that ML surrogates for PDEs trained on numerical solver data learn the modified equation rather than the true physics, and that test loss cannot distinguish the two. It proposes a suite of structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics — scores measuring whether a learned model respects conserved quantities, symmetries, or Hamiltonian structure — without access to training data or governing equations. This addresses a real evaluation blind spot in neural PDE surrogates.

entry.title: Follow the Perturbed Leader for Linear Bandits: $\sqrt{T}$ Regret over General Convex Sets

author.name: Chen-Yu Wei

entry.summary: This paper gives the first FTPL-based adversarial linear bandit algorithm achieving sqrt(T) regret over general convex action sets, attaining Otilde(d^{5/4} sqrt(T)) regret using only linear optimization oracles and near-optimal Otilde(d sqrt(T)) regret when an optimal-design exploration distribution is available. This improves the T^{2/3} regret of prior FTPL algorithms and generalizes recent results over special action sets. It is a clean theoretical advance in oracle-efficient bandit optimization.

entry.title: Causal Discovery Under Hard Selection Bias: A New Robust Score-Matching Approach

author.name: Yiwen Qiu, Francesco Montagna, Shimeng Huang, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work provides a general method for causal discovery from truncated (hard-selected) observational data using Additive Noise Models, showing score-based methods are well-suited because deterministic truncation preserves key score function properties. This fills a gap where prior selection-bias results were limited to local or interventional settings.

entry.title: How Vision Transformers Represent Position: A Mechanistic Comparison of Absolute and Rotary Positional Encodings

author.name: Mahmoud Mannes, Nikhil Maturi, Parva Mehta, Jiwon Jeong, Aravind Singaram Kannappan

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study shows that absolute positional embeddings (APE) and rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) encode spatial position through fundamentally different internal mechanisms in Vision Transformers. Using sparse autoencoders and interventions, they find APE stores position in explicit row/column features while RoPE builds position inside attention and can rebuild it when withheld.

entry.title: KedgeFlow: A Programmable Control Plane for Enterprise AI Agents

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: KedgeFlow proposes language-independent contracts separating trusted controllers that authorize state-changing operations from privileged gateways that enforce authority independently of agent reasoning, addressing failures like altered actions, permission reuse, and lost-response retries in enterprise AI agents. Inspired by OpenFlow, it ties evidence-backed policy checks, signed exact-action permissions, single-use allowances, and outcome records. Conditional correctness properties are proven under trusted issuance.

entry.title: From Acoustic Sensing to Physical Actions: A Comprehensive Survey of Security Risks in Edge-Deployed Audio LLM-Based Agents

author.name: Binhong Wang, Haidong Kang, Yanfeng Zhang, Hong-Ning Dai, Guo Yu, Shangce Gao

entry.summary: A survey introducing an Acoustic Sensing-to-Action (S2A) system model that traces security risks in deployed audio-LLM agents from acoustic input through model behavior to persistent state and physical execution across smart homes, vehicles, wearables, and embodied systems. It unifies previously siloed literatures on acoustic security, LLM agents, and edge deployment.

entry.title: Latent Taxonomies: How Property Induction Develops in Language Model Pre-training

author.name: Jan Sobotka, Ekaterina Goliakova, Marcin Detyniecki, Antoine Bosselut, Xavier Renard

entry.summary: Using synthetic taxonomies injected into continued pre-training of Pythia and OLMo 2 models from 70M to 7B parameters, the authors track how category-based property induction develops from next-token prediction alone. They find taxonomically aligned induction emerges, with properties learned for one entity transferring more to taxonomically close entities.

entry.title: CloneOT: predicting clone-specific perturbation responses with lineage-supervised neural inverse optimal transport

author.name: Yanshuo Chen, Wei Chen, Heng Huang

entry.summary: CloneOT is a neural inverse optimal transport method for predicting single-cell perturbation responses that learns the transport cost itself using lineage-tracing barcodes, rather than assuming a fixed squared Euclidean cost as in prior work like CellOT. Lineage links between pre- and post-perturbation cells of the same clone provide supervision for learning both the map and the cost.

entry.title: SSM-Attack: Learning Where to Perturb for Black-Box Face Privacy

author.name: Tunahan Parlay{\i}c{\i}, Erchan Aptoula, Y\"ucel Sayg{\i}n

entry.summary: SSM-Attack is a black-box face-privacy framework that uses a selective state-space model to predict, in one linear-time pass, which facial regions carry identity evidence, then refines perturbation values within a per-pixel budget. It achieves the highest reported average black-box attack success rates on three benchmarks while avoiding heavy generators and visible semantic edits. It is notable both as an application of SSMs and for privacy-protection tooling against ubiquitous face recognition.

entry.title: Learning Distributions from Samples and Qualities

author.name: Marc Jourdan, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: The authors study parameter estimation when each sample from a parametric distribution comes with a binary quality label governed by the same unknown parameter, showing that hard feasibility constraints on deterministic labels can accelerate estimation from the classical n^{-1/2} rate to n^{-1}. They establish this for identifiable and finitely ambiguous quality classifiers, and construct threshold-free pairwise preferences that retain the accelerated rate when the quality model is known only up to an additive constant. This is a strong statistical learning theory result.

entry.title: LADDER: A Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Benchmark

author.name: Petko Petkov, Giuliano Albanese, Nikolay Nikolov, Luc Van Gool, Jonathan Tremblay, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: LADDER is a benchmark for long-horizon robot manipulation that scales tasks from 1 to 10 subgoals within fixed environments across three simulation suites, 145 tasks, and 2,024 episodes per system, explicitly isolating horizon length from scene variation. It evaluates orchestration paradigms combining learned low-level policies and tool-selection agents, revealing degradation on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories

author.name: Dennis Grinwald, Ankur Singha, Khaled Kahouli, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: The authors show that diffusion models for sampling lattice field theory configurations can be trained without target samples by exploiting the target score identity with the unnormalized density, using importance-weighted or self-consistent fixed-point variants. This removes the circular dependency that normally reintroduces the sampling bottleneck.

entry.title: FidelityQ: Preserving Predictive Fidelity in Ultra-Low-Bit Language Model Quantization

author.name: Yujie Chen, Weiyan Zheng, Yiwu Yao, Tianchi Hu, Bo Wang, Jiyu Guo, Wenzhan Li, Jingcai Guo, Michele Magno, Haotong Qin

entry.summary: FidelityQ is a scalar quantization framework that preserves LLM predictive behavior at precisions down to 2 bits using Information-Aligned Analytic Coding, which shapes weight rows via randomized Hadamard mixing and fits a mirrored four-level minimum-distortion quantizer. The method focuses on translating accurate weight representation into consistent predictions from small calibration sets. It addresses the practical deployment challenge of extreme compression with regular arithmetic structure.

entry.title: Do LLM Tutors Actually Teach? A Process-Centered Synthesis of the Tutoring Loop

author.name: Sayantan Adak, Rima Hazra, Koyel Mukherjee, Digbalay Bose, Somnath Banerjee

entry.summary: A structured synthesis of LLM tutoring research organized around the tutoring loop from learner-state inference to pedagogical action, training, evaluation, and student simulation. The audit finds strong evidence for pedagogical evaluation but thin evidence for learner-conditioned intervention, human learning gains, and especially transfer or delayed retention.

entry.title: PAIR: Memory-Efficient and Fast Inference with Reading--Reasoning Fusion

author.name: Sejun Park, Haocheng Xia, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: PAIR is a multi-model inference scheme for context-based QA that pairs a smaller Reader retaining full context with a larger Reasoner seeing only the question, fusing their per-token logits so the combination behaves like a single large model. This reduces memory and computation compared to running one large model over the context.

entry.title: SpecGuardBench: Can Coding Agents Construct Reliable Validation Harnesses from Natural Language Specifications?

author.name: Zhiqing Zhong, Mingyu Chen, Aoyang Fang, Yuzhong Zhang, Haoye Tian, Lionel Briand, Boxi Yu, Pinjia He

entry.summary: SpecGuardBench tests whether coding agents can construct reliable validation harnesses that faithfully capture natural language specifications, using 291 tasks from 13 real-world repositories covering eight types of verification logic such as functional postconditions and interaction protocols. It goes beyond whether agent code passes available tests to whether agents can generate their own trustworthy evidence. This targets a key trust question for autonomous coding.

entry.title: Machine--human agreement in marking undergraduate assignments is specific to model, prompt and institution

author.name: Giulio Corsi, Maryam Abo-Tabik, Yael Benn, Georgiana Thorpe Apreutesei, Roni Tibon, Alexandru Marcoci, Deborah Talmi

entry.summary: Using 761 undergraduate psychology assignments from three UK universities, the authors evaluate three frontier LLMs as automated graders against human marks. Agreement varies widely with no universally optimal model or prompt, and all models compress marks toward the center, overvaluing weak work and undervaluing strong work; ensemble errors are correlated rather than independent. This is an important caution for deploying LLM grading in higher education.

entry.title: Estimating Surprisal from the Speech Signal

author.name: Zachary Hopton, Samuel Kiegeland, Francesco Ignazio Re, Patrick Haller, Matthew B. Winn, Ryan Cotterell, Eleanor Chodroff

entry.summary: This paper removes the text bottleneck in surprisal-theory testing by estimating surprisal directly from raw speech using a speech language model rather than from transcriptions with text-trained models. It addresses the unit-of-definition problem introduced by acoustic variability through a marginalization approach over realizations. This enables empirical tests of surprisal theory in the spoken modality, where language predominantly lives.

entry.title: Re-executing Coding-Agent Evaluations: Unchanged Decisions and Unresolved Policy Risk

author.name: Tianyu Ding, Yaocheng Tong, Muzhi Yang, Fei Jiang, Lei Yang, Boya Yu

entry.summary: Two preregistered re-execution studies of coding-agent leaderboard grading returned negative results: SWE-bench Pro v1's offline option rejected none of 59 accepted Go patches whose grading configuration changed, leaving a residual exposure risk unresolved, while a reconstructed module cache rejected accepted alternatives from four models. Re-executing selected patches shows evaluation decisions can be sensitive to dependency provenance. The paper highlights unresolved integrity risks in executable LLM benchmarks used for rewards and self-improvement.

entry.title: Thinking with Images without Coordinates

author.name: Meng Cao, Haoze Zhao, Yi Wang, Ian Reid, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: Identifies semantic and resolution gaps in coordinate-based visual grounding for thinking-with-images MLLMs, and proposes TiCO, which reformulates visual reasoning as semantic evidence discovery in latent space, injecting evidence as token-level regions without pixel coordinates.

entry.title: TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision

author.name: Hao Zhu, Heyu Sun, Shuo Jin, Jiayu Xiao, Feng Dai

entry.summary: The paper empirically identifies concept recognition, not mask quality, as the main bottleneck when SAM3 is applied to downstream segmentation, then proposes TAG, a text anchor re-grounding framework that corrects SAM3 concept recognition on target domains without dense supervision. SAM3 is an existing foundation model, and this work adapts rather than releases it.

entry.title: SPARE: Shared Perception and Adaptive Retrieval of Evidence for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Senbin Xu, Zijun Zhang, Xinhua Wu, Li He, Jubo Feng, Li Qiao, Zhen Gao, Yan Zhang, Jixiang Luo, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: SPARE handles streaming video question answering with a lightweight gate that decides whether recent frames suffice to answer, retrieving relevant historical clips via a multimodal embedding model only when needed. It also shares visual encoder computation to reduce cost, balancing recency against historical evidence.

entry.title: MORE: Learning Motion-Oriented Registers for Driving World Models and Planning

author.name: Yingdong Gu, Haoyu Wang, Shaocheng Yan, Zhenjun Zhao, Hao Han, Pengcheng Shi, Xianfei Li, Qinghua Tan, Wenlong Liao, Tao He, Jiayuan Li, Pai Peng

entry.summary: MORE argues that video pretraining for driving world models should directly learn motion-oriented state representations rather than inheriting dense visual features from pretrained encoders. It proposes compact motion-oriented registers that reduce computational cost of future prediction at higher resolutions and better serve end-to-end planning.

entry.title: Semantic Saliency from Multi-Modal Large Language Model Scene Understanding Maps

author.name: Ziqi Wen, Shravan Murlidaran, Jonathan Skaza, William Wang, Miguel P. Eckstein

entry.summary: AUTO-SUM computes semantic saliency fully automatically by removing individual objects, prompting MLLMs to describe original and modified scenes, and measuring description similarity via text embeddings, without fitting any parameters to human data. It predicts which objects draw human attention beyond what low-level saliency models capture.

entry.title: SlotAVS: Object-Centric Audio-Visual Segmentation via Bi-Modal Slot Attention

author.name: Arnav Sharma, Anand Mishra, Renu Rameshan

entry.summary: SlotAVS tackles audio-visual segmentation of multiple sounding objects using competitive bi-modal slot attention, shifting from global cross-modal fusion to explicit competitive binding of sound sources to object slots. Slots are initialized from temporal audio sequences and compete over spatial locations, reducing merged masks and unstable specialization in multi-source scenes.

entry.title: Not All Challenges Are Equal: Evaluating Interactive Liveness Detection Against Real-Time Face Swaps

author.name: Anton Firc, David Drtil, Martin Pere\v{s}\'ini, Milan \v{S}alko, Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Kamil Malinka

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates randomized interactive gesture challenges against live real-time face-swap attacks injected through virtual cameras, across 108 live sessions with six subjects, 24 impersonated identities, and two face-swap tools. Active-gesture windows reach a mean session-level AUC of 0.988 versus 0.878 for static calibration, with pose and combined gestures proving most informative.

entry.title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents

author.name: Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Zhaolong Shen, Xiaopeng Lin, Yao Zhang, Haishan Liu, Haotian Li, Yuliang Wei, Kai Hu, Yichao Du, Zhirui Zhang, Bailing Wang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: EvoSpatial is an experience-driven framework for tool-augmented vision-language agents that evolves a library of linked skills and tools for spatial reasoning, retrieving skills, reusing tools, and synthesizing helper functions during reasoning. It uses supervised outcome feedback from both successful and failed trajectories to improve when and how computations are trusted.

entry.title: X-Ragent: Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Evidence-Grounded Chest X-Ray Reasoning

author.name: Yi Wang, Zhenlong Yuan, Yuchan Guo, Maolei Huang, Zijian Song, Dapeng Zhang, Rongbin Tan, Jiyuan Wang, Zhiyuan Wang, Fangfang Lin, Shuhan Song, Huawei Cao

entry.summary: X-Ragent is a post-training framework combining tool-augmented reinforcement learning with validity-gated acquisition of quantitative measurements for chest X-ray reasoning, learning when auxiliary evidence is needed and preventing invalid evidence from entering diagnosis. It introduces Rad-CoT, a 7.7K-sample corpus of causally ordered tool-augmented reasoning chains.

entry.title: When Left Is Right? Camera-Motion Understanding beyond Screen

author.name: Chong Cheng, Ran Zhang, Xinyuan Li, Alan Zhao, Hao Wang, Xi Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that modern VLMs perform near chance on questions about camera motion direction (e.g., did the camera move left or right), and argues that solving this requires jointly coupling off-screen camera motion with on-screen flow dynamics and interpreting that representation through language rather than training a standalone pose estimator. CameraVLM pairs a motion-state representation with state-language alignment to close this gap.

entry.title: SWORD: Scene-Grounded Wasserstein Object-Relation Distance for 3D Scene Graph Prediction

author.name: U-Chae Jun, Jaeeun Ko, Yoonhyuk Choi, Jiwoo Kang

entry.summary: SWORD introduces a Wasserstein-based graph distance loss for 3D scene graph prediction that optimizes semantic proximity to the ground-truth graph instead of exact label recovery. By exploiting fixed node indices and supervised edge slots in prior protocols, it converts scene graph comparison into an aligned graph matching problem.

entry.title: COMPASS: Contextual Moment Prior Alignment for Generalizable AIGI Detection

author.name: Zhan Yang, Tiancheng Shen, Weijie Lyu, Shuo Chen, Bernard Ghanem, Yibo Yang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: COMPASS is a data-aware subspace adaptation framework for generalizable AI-generated image and deepfake detection that uses a small unlabeled semantic proxy set to estimate target activation statistics, addressing semantic misalignment in magnitude-based subspace methods applied to vision foundation models.

entry.title: Closing the Estimation Gap: Training-Free Transductive Inference for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Action Recognition

author.name: Changyi Li, Zeyu Yang, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: Performs an oracle analysis for cross-domain few-shot action recognition showing that prototypes from scarce support sets leave 7-20 percentage points of accuracy unrealized even with frozen representations. It then proposes a training-free transductive inference method that exploits unlabeled query data to close much of this estimation gap. A clean, well-motivated contribution to few-shot adaptation.

entry.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction

author.name: Yuhan Zhu, Xiangyu Zeng, Qingyi Si, Chenxu Yang, Yifei Li, Luozheng Qin, Junhao Zhou, Dingyu Yao, Jun Zhang, Chuanyu Qin, Zhiqiu Zhang, Yuandong Yang, Yuqi Xu, Tianyu Zhang, Hongcheng Guo, Jiaqi Wang, Nan Duan, Limin Wang

entry.summary: VideoJev is a family of models that adapts pretrained multimodal LLMs for video understanding and interaction by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared scoring head over temporal intervals and textual options. This unifies temporal grounding and multiple-choice video QA into structured decision outputs suited for visual agents that must act in real time.

entry.title: RootSLAM: Square Root Bundle Adjustment for Visual-Inertial SLAM

author.name: Tom\'as Santucci, Mateo de Mayo, Daniel Cremers, Taih\'u Pire

entry.summary: RootSLAM is a fully-featured multi-camera visual-inertial SLAM system built on Basalt that achieves accuracy competitive with learning-based state of the art while running up to 20 times faster. It demonstrates that classical geometry-based methods retain a decisive efficiency advantage for low-power devices in robotics, mixed reality, and drones. The strong efficiency-accuracy trade-off makes it practically important for real-world deployment.

entry.title: Do My Samples Help? Compute Budget Allocation for Real-World Sampling-Based MPC in Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Magnus Dierking, Jo\~ao Carvalho, Vince Kurtz, Jan Peters, Nils Dengler, Georgia Chalvatzaki

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how to allocate a finite computation budget in GPU-based sampling-based model predictive control for contact-rich manipulation, comparing trade-offs among exploration density, uncertainty representation, replanning frequency, and simulation-to-reality alignment. The controlled comparisons provide practical guidance for real-world sim-to-real control.

entry.title: Safety-Critical Quadrotor Navigation Using Fourth-Order Control Barrier Functions with Full Nonlinear Quadrotor Dynamics

author.name: Yanze Liu, Ya\c{s}ar \.Idikut, Dhruv Madhusudan Agrawal, Wei Xiao, Guanrui Li

entry.summary: This work develops a safety controller for quadrotors based on fourth-order control barrier functions that explicitly incorporates full nonlinear dynamics including attitude and torque-level actuation, resolving mixed-relative-degree issues via integral high-order CBFs. The formulation eliminates the mismatch between translational safety objectives and attitude evolution found in hierarchical architectures.

entry.title: Verify, Act, Distill: Turning Test-Time Compute into Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Kaneyoshi Hiratsuka, Satoshi Yamamori, Jun Morimoto

entry.summary: This framework consolidates test-time compute gains into VLA models themselves: a fixed verifier scores candidate actions from a flow-matching VLA, the weighted aggregate is executed, and observations plus aggregated chunks from successful episodes are distilled into LoRA parameters using the standard flow-matching loss. Unlike frozen-policy test-time methods, gains need not be recomputed at every execution and no extra reinforcement learning is required. It converts inference-time search into lasting adaptation.

entry.title: PointWalker: Mapless Quadruped Locomotion Directly From Raw LiDAR Point Clouds

author.name: Sicen Li, Zhen Chu, Chao Li, Jun Zheng, Qiuguo Zhu, Jun Wu

entry.summary: PointWalker is a mapless framework where a single RL policy directly consumes raw point clouds from four LiDAR sensors, encoding voxelized points with linear self-attention fused with proprioception, avoiding the cost and failure modes of terrain maps and depth cameras. This addresses robust locomotion over sparse, see-through terrain such as gratings and balance beams.

entry.title: ReTrace: Cross-Stage Failure Attribution for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yue Yu, Bin Zhu, Junhui Li, Jiayu Wang, Shijie Zhou, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: ReTrace is a self-improvement framework where multimodal foundation-model-controlled robots learn from failures via retrospective reasoning, tracing downstream failures back to earlier decisions without demonstrations or parameter updates. It targets cross-stage dependencies where locally successful actions cause later-stage failures. This addresses a key bottleneck for autonomous skill improvement.

entry.title: Task-Space Motion-Force Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Precise and Compliant Control under Uncertainties

author.name: Quang-Nam Nguyen, Ludovic Righetti

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified NMPC framework that plans and controls robot joints subject to task-space motion and force requirements, designed to generalize across platforms and tasks without platform-specific OCP redesign. It explicitly models task-space impedance rather than treating interactions as rigid contacts, improving robustness to modeling errors in dynamics and environment. The authors are from Lightracket/NYU-affiliated Righetti group, known for whole-body MPC.

entry.title: OccWAM: Occupancy World-Action Models with Joint Scene-to-Ego Flow Matching

author.name: Qihang Huang, Wenhui Huang, Collister Chua, Shiyu Fang, Zhan Chen, Songyan Zhang, Zhidong Wang, Daiying Tian, Chen Lv

entry.summary: OccWAM proposes a world-action model for end-to-end autonomous driving that jointly couples occupancy prediction and action generation via a joint scene-to-ego flow matching objective, avoiding the explicit generation order or role asymmetry of hierarchical and parallel multi-task designs. This enables reciprocal interaction between world prediction and planning in a metric occupancy representation.

entry.title: ReEnvision: Future-Guided Selective Action Repair for Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Xiyin Zeng, Xuewei Huang, Yi Lu, Weihao Yuan, Hao Wang

entry.summary: ReEnvision is a future-guided selective action repair framework for long-horizon manipulation that updates a joint future-action belief from execution feedback, then repairs only the affected actions rather than replanning whole chunks or correcting step-by-step. This avoids both the errors of regenerating valid actions from unfamiliar states and the late reactions of purely reactive correction.

entry.title: I2O2I-Nav: A Benchmark with a Modular Agent for Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor-to-Indoor Navigation

author.name: Zhengjie Shu, Wanyu Li, Di Xiao, Lingxin Jiang, Lai Jiang, Kaidi Hu, Xincheng Tang, Wenkang Hu, Haoran Wang, Jinchuan Zhang, Chang Chen, Wei Li, Jia Pan, Ruigang Yang

entry.summary: I2O2I-Nav is a physics-enabled benchmark with 20 composite real-world scenes spanning over 115,000 square meters, aligned 3DGS rendering and collision geometry, and a three-level evaluation that progresses from navigation primitives to full four-stage indoor-outdoor-indoor missions. Stages start from the actual endpoint of the predecessor, testing how heterogeneous navigation capabilities compose under continuous execution.

entry.title: Contact Trajectory Prompting: In-Context Transfer of Contact-Rich Behaviors from a Single Demonstration

author.name: Xian Nie, Yujie Zang, Yuhang Zheng, Yupeng Zheng, Songen Gu, Wendi Chen, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu, Wenchao Ding, Junchi Yan, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: CTP enables one-shot in-context transfer of contact-rich manipulation by encoding motion and contact information from a single demonstration into an ordered contact trajectory prompt capturing temporal evolution of the physical interaction. During execution the policy uses online sensory feedback to retrieve interaction-relevant information from the prompt, distinguishing behaviors with similar motions but different contact intensities.

entry.title: Interaction Latents as Actions for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Yuhang Zheng, Yujie Zang, Yuchen Liu, Yupeng Zheng, Zhennan Jiang, Zebin Xing, Shuai Tian, Songen Gu, Jingxiang Guo, Chen Gao, Zhongpu Xia, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: ILA proposes representing policy actions as decodable interaction latents that jointly encode motion, contact, and force evolution, rather than pure motion trajectories. These latents are learned via visually conditioned joint action-tactile reconstruction and provide a shared representation usable for action generation, evaluation, and offline improvement. This reframes how tactile information enters the action space of manipulation policies.

entry.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs

author.name: Boris Radovi\v{c}, Marco Canini, Veljko Pejovi\'c

entry.summary: The paper explores a hybrid privacy-preserving agent architecture where a cloud model writes a program that defers bounded questions over local user data to a small on-device model via function calls. On AppWorld this improves success rates of code-only agents while keeping user data local.

entry.title: Joint Discrete and SE(3) Diffusion for Protein Interface Design

author.name: Zhenqiao Song, Jianwen Xie, Lei Li

entry.summary: PIDiff is a multimodal diffusion framework that jointly designs target-conditioned protein sequences and structures for protein-protein complex design, coupling discrete sequence diffusion with continuous SE(3) structural diffusion. Its PIFormer architecture interleaves geometry-aware invariant point attention to achieve geometric and physicochemical interface complementarity.

entry.title: ASIWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in a Persistent Survival Sandbox

author.name: Jianfeng Lin, Runze Wang, Haorong Hong, Yuxuan Xie, Zeno Zeng, Zhongyuan Liu

entry.summary: ASIWorld is a persistent survival-sandbox benchmark for autonomous agents that combines persistent world and character state, character-scoped partial observability, and a programmable asynchronous interface where agent-authored programs keep running between model calls. It evaluates sustained goal execution, including interdependent production and exploration tasks where earlier decisions shape later opportunities.

entry.title: Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses

author.name: Weichen Yu, Lesly Miculicich, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Jiefeng Chen, Shuo Li, Matt Fredrikson, Tomas Pfister, Long T. Le

entry.summary: Introduces Harmony Harness, a framework for multi-objective, compositional evolution of LLM agent harnesses, using decomposition-based evolutionary search to maintain solutions across the Pareto frontier instead of optimizing a single monolithic objective. This separates transferable design from environment-specific adaptation and handles competing goals.

entry.title: RetryBench: Separating Retry Permission from Recovery Outcomes in GPT Tool Use

author.name: You Liu, Yue Liu, Quanchao Lu

entry.summary: RetryBench measures false retry permission (FRP) in GPT-model agents: retrying a timed-out tool call without support from the visible contract, separated from realized recovery outcomes. Controls across 720 and 240 responses show large differences among models (Sol, Terra, Luna differ dramatically in unsupported retries), and accepting a displayed bad key does not explain all errors. This gives a precise lens on agent reliability in tool use under failure.

entry.title: Phantom Merge: When Your Large Language Model Agents Pick One but Tell You About Another

author.name: Wangshu Zhu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: The paper identifies and formalizes Phantom Merge, an entity-evidence binding failure where LLM agents attribute unsupported claims to their committed entity, characterizing its prevalence across four agent domains and four backbone families. It proposes a two-stage framework combining hidden-state risk readout with correction to mitigate these binding errors.

entry.title: ReTAC: Residual Test-Time Agentic Computation for Video Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Yike Wu, Keyan Chen, Qixiong Wang, Xi Xiang, Maofei Que, Xiaolong Jiang, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: Argues that test-time agentic computation for multimodal models should be residual: only allocate extra planning, tool use, and reflection for requirements unresolved by the base model, and recompute only affected states after localized failures. ReTAC instantiates this as a training-free multi-agent framework for video spatial reasoning.

entry.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints

author.name: Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Duan Leijiahao, Haoxiang Wang, Boning Tan, Liangna Fu, Chao Tan, Yafu Li, Yulong Chen, Chaoqun Wan, Zhen Huang, Shuxian Liang, Xian-Sheng Hua

entry.summary: Introduces LIBERO-Industry, a benchmark built on the widely used LIBERO robot learning suite that adds industrial process constraints such as product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. It translates high-mix low-volume manufacturing conditions into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria for evaluating generalist robot policies.

entry.title: EPOCH: Coverage-Aware Evolution with Experiential Preference Optimization for LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design

author.name: Oguzhan Gungordu, Ayse Tursucular, Siheng Xiong, Faramarz Fekri

entry.summary: EPOCH improves LLM-based automated heuristic design by making instance coverage the objective of the evolutionary search and fine-tuning the generator LLM to internalize reflection signals that previously stayed in the prompt. Parent selection, operator allocation, and stagnation recovery all optimize joint coverage of training instances for combinatorial optimization problems. The approach bridges evolutionary search and learned generators in a structured way.

entry.title: Agency as a New Organizing Abstraction for Computer Science

author.name: Ian Foster

entry.summary: Ian Foster argues that agentic AI, general-purpose open-ended systems that synthesize courses of action from goals, observations, and memory, should be treated as a new systems-level organizing abstraction for computer science rather than merely an application of foundation models. The position paper articulates what is genuinely new about this form of agency and its implications for how the field structures systems and abstractions.

entry.title: OpenDepth: Repurposing Image Editing Priors for Robust Open-World Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Mengke Zhang, Tianyi Yang, Xinzhuo Li, Anlong Ming

entry.summary: OpenDepth argues that text-to-image priors, while data-efficient for monocular depth estimation, degrade under open-world perturbations like weather and illumination because they optimize semantics over pixel-level structure. The method instead repurposes image-editing priors, modeling open-world depth estimation as consistent geometric inference across appearance changes to avoid structural hallucinations. The approach aims for robust state-of-the-art depth estimation in adverse conditions.

entry.title: Instructions Are Evidence, Not Objectives: Measuring Outcome Alignment of Agents

author.name: Kaiming Liu, Yuxuan Liu, Jinrui Ju, Minyuan Ruan, Xuanyu Lei, Peng Li, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Analyzing 100 user-agent trajectories, the authors find that 56% of initial instructions omit requirements that later prove necessary, and argue agents should treat stated instructions as evidence for inferring true task requirements rather than as the objective itself. The paper proposes measuring outcome alignment against inferred true requirements instead of literal instruction-following.

entry.title: PaceReasoner: Label-Free Learning to Answer Briefly from Long Reasoning

author.name: Changguo Jia, Zhiyou Xiao, Xinbei Ma, Geng Chen, Weiming Zhang, Yiming Xu, Tianqi Zhao, Minghui Zhou

entry.summary: PaceReasoner is a label-free test-time reinforcement learning framework that uses a model's own long chain-of-thought responses to improve its short-mode answer accuracy, via both modes sharing a trainable policy. It combines all-response and LONG-only answer consensus with confidence-weighted supervision, a shifting behavior reward, and a ratio controller balancing accuracy against brevity.

entry.title: Can Agents Forget When Asked? A Benchmark for Memory Unlearning in LLM Agents

author.name: Bofan Xie, Chaokun Wang, Guanchen Ge, Songyao Wang, Fang Niu, Hang Zhang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Bemula, the first benchmark for memory unlearning in LLM agents, evaluating whether agents can delete exactly the requested facts while preserving the rest of memory. It contains 50 multi-session dialogues, 135 forget requests across six types, and 1,742 test questions with control variants. This fills a gap since existing memory benchmarks only cover writing, retrieval, and organization.

entry.title: Delegating Earth science model calibration to knowledge-guided LLM agents

author.name: Zhanliang Zhu, Ziwei Li, Liujun Zhu, Yuchen Liu, Junliang Jin, Jianyun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors build a general calibration harness where knowledge-constrained LLM agents define parameter domains, observation mappings, and objectives for process-based Earth science models, then generate model-specific code that is verified and frozen before numerical search. Agent-authored workflows were validated across six model families.

entry.title: Compare to Correct: Pairwise-Guided Logit Adjustment for LLM Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Cong Hua, Qianqian Xu, Zitai Wang, Zhiyong Yang, Shilong Bao, Linchao Zhang, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Inspired by the Condorcet principle, the paper introduces pairwise confidence comparisons between reasoning paths supporting different answers, combined with voting support via a KL-regularized objective; theoretically this comparative advantage equals an adjustment to traditional voting logits. The resulting pairwise-guided logit adjustment improves sampling-based test-time scaling.

entry.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Xiaoguang Guo, Yaohao Long, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: BLADE is a training-free framework for failure attribution in LLM multi-agent systems that audits how information was used rather than just tracing where it came from. It uses structured probabilistic judgments over dependencies to identify the responsible agent and the decisive error step.

entry.title: What Can Language Models Inherit from Solomonoff Induction? Limits, Attainable Properties, and What Served Conditionals Reveal

author.name: Luan Ozelim, Abicumaran Uthamacumaran, Hector Zenil

entry.summary: This theoretical paper applies algorithmic information theory and Bayesian consistency results to challenge the claim that scaling language models brings them closer to Solomonoff induction. It shows no computable predictor can uniformly approximate Solomonoff induction, and that finite evaluation cannot certify agreement, so any notion of closeness holds only pointwise per environment.

entry.title: SceneForesee: Learning Scene Evolution for Spatiotemporal Reasoning

author.name: Chaoyue Li, Shoudong Han, Haoyang Wu, Boxue Yang, Sijia Chen, Yufan Chen, Ruping Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates Scene Evolution Understanding (SEU), a task requiring models to estimate entity histories from video and predict scene continuations with future trajectories, events, visual evidence, and descriptions. SceneForesee is a large benchmark with 144.57K temporal pairs and 1.05M entity annotations featuring paired observed/future scenes with shared entity identities, evaluating entity continuity and change reasoning in large multimodal models. It probes a capability current LMMs likely lack.

entry.title: Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion

author.name: Yifan Shen, Yewei Xia, Gongxu Luo, Peiyuan Zhu, Boyang Sun, Zhenhao Chen, Guangyi Liu, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Prospective Forcing injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video diffusion by attaching lightweight offset-specific prediction heads to a rolling-window generator, extending supervision beyond the next chunk to stabilize quality over long rollouts. The heads share conditioning and predict chunks at multiple future offsets.

entry.title: Counterfactual Rollouts for Offline Contrastive Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tingrui Huang, Ai Bo, Junzhe Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes offline contrastive RL under confounded Markov decision processes, where a demonstrator's hidden information creates spurious action-outcome associations, and introduces counterfactual transitions separating identified from unidentified dynamics with worst-case occupancy lower bounds. The resulting method, CauCRL, learns pessimistic goal-conditioned values robust to confounding in offline demonstrations.

entry.title: Exploring Jailbreak Vulnerability Across Depth-Based Dynamic Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Lass Najmuldeen, Seyedhamidreza Mousavi

entry.summary: Investigates how depth-based dynamic inference, which generates outputs from intermediate layers for efficiency, affects LLM robustness to jailbreak attacks. The paper fills an unexplored intersection between efficiency techniques and safety alignment, examining whether early-exit flexibility weakens safety guarantees.

entry.title: World Modeling through Spectral Alignment

author.name: Holger Molin, William Peng, Marco Bagatella, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: SpecWM is a JEPA-style world-modeling framework in which desired relationships between observations are specified via a target similarity kernel, and the encoder is trained to reproduce those relationships in its embedding geometry, ranging from physically informed kernels to a purely self-supervised temporal kernel. The paper characterizes global optima of the objective, conditions for linear recoverability and nuisance invariance, and connects temporal kernels to behavior.

entry.title: RINO: Renormalization Group Distillation with No Labels

author.name: Zichun Hao, Raghav Kansal, Abhijith Gandrakota, Chang Sun, Haoyang Li, Zihan Zhao, Ngadiuba Jennifer, Javier Duarte, Maria Spiropulu

entry.summary: RINO is a self-supervised pretraining method for high-energy physics that exploits the multi-scale renormalization group structure of particle-jet formations, avoiding biases from labeled simulations. It distills representations across scales using real unlabeled collider data instead of physics-domain-agnostic inductive biases. This addresses a known fidelity gap between simulated training data and real detector data in HEP.

entry.title: Dream2Discern: Learning from Hard Latent Variants for Runtime Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Boxuan Zhang, jianing Zhu, Xiaotian Han, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: Dream2Discern is a runtime auditor for multi-agent LLM systems that predicts terminal outcomes from execution prefixes, trained by perturbing the auditor's own representation operators to create hard latent variants where prediction loss is high. This implicit augmentation expands effective training coverage without costly additional trajectory execution and verification.

entry.title: Heuristics are Not Enough: Calibrated and Corrected Caching for Video Diffusion Acceleration

author.name: Jiyue Jiang, Zhiyu Huo, Yuhan Chen, Yanruisheng Shao, Gong Zhang, Lei Deng

entry.summary: AlignCache is a closed-loop feature-caching framework for accelerating video diffusion models, replacing heuristic difference measures and global thresholds with phase-adaptive budget routing and calibration of scheduling decisions against their true influence on final generation quality. This corrects systematic bias that propagates uncorrected in prior caching methods.

entry.title: Unsupervised Data Drift Monitoring for Deployed Deepfake Speech Detectors

author.name: Luk\'a\v{s} Proke\v{s}, Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Anton Firc, Kamil Malinka

entry.summary: This paper proposes an unsupervised drift monitor for deployed deepfake speech detectors that compares each input's embedding against bona fide and spoof references via regularized Mahalanobis distances, defining trusted, ambiguous, and novel regions to route unfamiliar inputs for review. It is evaluated on four modern detectors across three datasets under evolving attacks and recording conditions. It matters because deployed detectors face shifting threats without labels, and knowing when to trust them is an open operational problem.

entry.title: From Suboptimal to Optimal: One-Step Latent Flow Policies for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shenghua Lu, Zixuan Yang, Rongxu Zhao, Bohao Qu, Jifeng Hu, Hechang Chen

entry.summary: MeanFlow2Better (MF2B) reformulates offline RL as generative optimization of decision chunks in a latent space, mapping trajectory chunks from current to better performance states to enable one-step flow-based action generation. This avoids the multi-step iterative generation and uninformative Gaussian noise starting points of diffusion/flow policy methods. The approach also better exploits suboptimal trajectories in offline datasets.

entry.title: On Making $\mathrm{SE}(2)$-Invariant Networks Optimal

author.name: Tomas Karella, Emily Shinkle, Alice Elisabeth Anastasia Allen, Pieter J. Swart, Nicholas Lubbers, Roxana Bujack

entry.summary: Uses classical invariant theory to derive provably optimal SE(2)-invariant feature maps that are minimal and information-preserving, and shows they integrate into standard architectures without modifying nonlinearities or normalization. This grounds symmetry-based inductive bias design in theory rather than ad hoc pooling choices. Includes a concrete implementation demonstrating the construction.

entry.title: HelpMeOut: A Neuropsychology-Grounded Benchmark for Error-Aware Monitoring of Household Task Execution

author.name: Haoran Wang, Jingwei Huang, Anqing Duan, Ho Seok Ahn, Bruce Macdonald

entry.summary: HelpMeOut is an embodied AI benchmark for monitoring household task execution by humans, built on neuropsychology research into everyday action errors. It contains 20,000 paired activity episodes across nine error categories, where agents must watch streaming human activity trajectories and detect and diagnose structured execution errors as early as possible — a setting relevant to assistive robotics for older adults and cognitively impaired people. It fills a real gap, since existing household benchmarks assume error-free human execution.

entry.title: Agentic-MatriBO: Capability-Compiled Agentic Bayesian Optimization for Materials and Chemical Design

author.name: Yu Zeng, Yuchuan Chen, Ziyue Zhang, Zijian Wei, Yanyi Su, Guojiang Zhao, Hongshuai Wang, Zhifeng Gao

entry.summary: Agentic-MatriBO combines LLM agents with Bayesian optimization for materials and chemical design, representing BO components as composable capabilities that a language policy proposes and a compiler validates against a catalog. A deterministic execution layer ensures proposed recipes and candidate plans are compatible and executable under budget constraints.

entry.title: ChampionKV: Head-Wise Adaptive Budget Allocation for KV Cache Compression

author.name: Yuechuan Chen, Yanda Guo, Xiaoxi Liu, Weilin Ruan, Huanbo Xu, Ruyi Wang, Wei Zhu

entry.summary: ChampionKV is an input-adaptive, head-wise budget allocator for long-context KV cache compression that assigns larger budgets to attention heads with dispersed attention and smaller budgets to concentrated heads. It plugs into existing compressors like SnapKV and PyramidKV without altering their token selection, using observation-window attention scores as a lightweight proxy.

entry.title: Not All Drift Is a Mechanism: Tracing Prompt Adaptation in LLMs

author.name: Mikhail Aleksandrov, Nail Bashirov, Maksim Ivanov, Andrew Tsukanov, Timofey Karyagin, Alexander Miasnikov, Gleb Molodtsov, Valentin Samokhin, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: This mechanistic study examines how discrete prompt optimization, prompt tuning, and prefix tuning alter internal computation in dense and mixture-of-experts language models. It finds that adaptation location predicts how task information flows: optimized text changes response construction, input-level prompts write into content representations, and layer-wise prefixes maintain direct control through the depth. Similar downstream outputs thus arise from different internal mechanisms.

entry.title: On Symmetry for Characterizing Agent Heterogeneity in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jianhong Wang, Jonathan Lawry

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies finite-horizon POSGs and defines policy-evaluation symmetries: transformations commuting with complete policy evaluation for all decentralized policies. These symmetries form a group whose orbits define structural agent types independent of the chosen policy, generalizing environment automorphisms. Applied to cooperative Dec-POMDPs, the framework provides a unified structural test for agent heterogeneity.

entry.title: Knowledge Graphs as Files: An Agent Harness Where Tool Creation and Tool Use Co-Evolve

author.name: Yuyang Bai, Yu Wang, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes direct knowledge graph interaction (DKGI), an agent harness where LLM agents write Python tools directly over complete node and edge files rather than using predefined graph interfaces. Agents interleave code execution with shell search, and execution feedback guides co-evolving tool creation and revision. This enables bulk processing of large node sets while returning selected evidence for model assessment.

entry.title: Fast Rates for Offline Q-Learning with KL Regularization

author.name: Yize Hao, Guangxin Jiang, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes KL-regularized Q-Learning (KLQ) and proves it achieves a fast O(1/epsilon) sample complexity in offline finite-horizon MDPs without explicit pessimism. The authors also address an exponential dependence on the KL parameter and horizon with an improved variant and analysis.

entry.title: Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE): Fine-grained Hallucination Detection for LLMs from Embeddings

author.name: Dilrangi Sankalpana, Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan, Uthayasanker Thayasivam, Kamal Premaratne

entry.summary: EGKE is a variant of Kernel Language Entropy for hallucination detection that replaces the NLI-derived semantic graph with an RBF kernel over dense sentence embeddings, removing the need to load a separate NLI classifier. This reduces computational overhead while retaining fine-grained hallucination detection based on semantic disagreement across sampled responses. It targets reliable LLM deployment.

entry.title: Random Fourier Features in Near-Linear Time

author.name: Sepideh Mahabadi, Sandeep Silwal, Tal Wagner

entry.summary: The authors construct a random feature map for shift-invariant kernels (e.g., the Gaussian kernel) computable in near-linear O((d+m) log d) time while retaining near-subgaussian concentration, closing a gap between fast structured features and strong statistical guarantees. The result comes from a tighter analysis of the Fastfood transform. This makes kernel approximations both fast to generate and statistically reliable.

entry.title: TLA-Verus: Generating and Solving Temporal Proof Obligations with LLM Agents

author.name: Kseniia Strelbytska, Bal\'azs Szil\'agyi, Anna M\'esz\'aros, Ferenc Husz\'ar

entry.summary: The paper addresses two limitations of TLA+ verification—no drift detection between implementation and specification, and weak tooling for temporal logic proofs—by translating TLA+ specifications into Verus, an auto-active Rust verifier, via both a deterministic transpiler and an agentic LLM translator. The LLM-based pipeline generates and discharges temporal proof obligations. This bridges industrial formal specification tooling with modern proof automation.

entry.title: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spiking Language Models

author.name: Dan Saunders, Benjamin Ren, Catherine He

entry.summary: The authors run the first Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP scaling study for spiking language models, sweeping SpikeGPT-family (RWKV backbone) models across compute budgets up to 1e19 FLOPs on FineWeb-EDU. They find the compute-optimal parameter scaling exponent (0.56) is close to dense transformers (0.50), and compare quality against non-spiking RWKV and transformer baselines. This characterizes the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking LMs at scale for the first time.

entry.title: GA-SVD: Generation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for LLM Compression

author.name: Shengkun Tang, Cong Zeng, Zongfang Liu, Dan Alistarh, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: Proposes GA-SVD, a generation-aware low-rank compression framework for LLMs, noting that existing SVD methods optimize multiple-choice benchmarks while degrading open-ended generation. It introduces Generation-Aware Weight Whitening using gradient/statistics information to improve rank allocation for generative performance.

entry.title: Mesh-Free Convolution: Learned Spectral Attenuation and Transport

author.name: Niloufar Zakariaei, Manav Manav, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: This paper proposes Mesh-Free Convolutions, filters defined in continuous space and discretized only at evaluation, enabling the same learned filters to generalize across grid resolutions for neural PDE solvers. This addresses instability and drift that arise when small spatial errors propagate autoregressively in learned time-dependent operators.

entry.title: Fast Quantized Johnson$-$Lindenstrauss Transforms

author.name: Angelos Korakitis, Vasileios Nakos

entry.summary: The authors introduce two constructions based on compositions of randomized Hadamard transforms with Gaussian rather than dense Gaussian projections, improving quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss (QJL) transforms used for 1-bit KV cache compression in LLM inference. The constructions retain the same embedding dimension while replacing dense Gaussian projections with structured embeddings. This yields faster transforms while approximately preserving attention inner products.

entry.title: OctMole: Multiscale 3D Molecular Generation with Hierarchical Spatial Flows

author.name: Yu-Tong Jin, Yi-Yang Tian, Qiwei Ye, Peng-Shuai Wang

entry.summary: OctMole is a multiscale octree flow framework for 3D molecular generation that separates a hierarchical occupancy flow, which resolves the sparse molecular support from coarse to fine, from a joint atom flow that assigns atom types and in-cell offsets. This combines efficient global structure modeling with subcell geometric precision, addressing limitations of single-scale atom-based diffusion and flow models.

entry.title: Can R\'enyi Accountants Beat Lossless Accountants for DP-SGD?

author.name: Jinho Bok

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that lossless privacy frameworks (privacy loss distributions, f-DP) always yield tighter DP guarantees than Renyi DP for DP-SGD. For fixed-size batches under replace adjacency, Renyi accounting can use a different dominating pair of worst-case distributions, and the author characterizes when Renyi-based analysis wins.

entry.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention

author.name: Guoxia Wang, Qianyue He, Siming Wu, Haoyang Xie, Qiwen Bao, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Tian Wu, Dianhai Yu

entry.summary: FlashMask-3 extends FlashMask's column-wise sparse mask compression for structured attention patterns to Hopper GPUs via FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA warp-specialized pipeline and multi-node context parallelism, achieving provably zero-communication mask localization per rank. This targets the growing bottleneck of combining structured masks (document, prefix-LM, sliding-window, block-sparse) with long-context distributed training of LLMs and multimodal models. From a Baidu-affiliated team, it is a systems contribution to efficient large-model training infrastructure.

entry.title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection

author.name: Wenlin Zhong, Hao Wang, Kun Yuan, Fan Yang, Jinluan Yang, Dian Jin, Xu Tan, Yiquan Wu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: SkillScaffold improves agentic RL for LLMs by adaptively assigning credit to textual skills distilled from prior interactions and selectively injecting only beneficial skills, avoiding the cost and instability of rollout-based utility estimation. Pilot studies show skill benefits vary across candidates and depend on the current policy's competence per query.

entry.title: CFG-Policy: Unified Diffusion Policy Learning Framework via Classifier-free Guidance

author.name: Shutong Ding, Zhaoyang Liu, Yimiao Zhou, Jingya Wang, Jiayuan Gu, Ye Shi

entry.summary: CFG-Policy applies classifier-free guidance to diffusion policies in reinforcement learning, using guidance to shape behavioral diversity for exploration during online and offline-to-online fine-tuning. The framework aims to improve task performance with RL post-training while preserving the pretrained diffusion policy's multimodal action distribution and acquired capabilities. It targets robotic control, VLA models, and world-model-based agents.

entry.title: Vision-Predictor-Action: Towards Efficient Embodied AI via Neuro-Symbolic JEPA Predictors

author.name: Yeonseok Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Goal-Conditioned Vision-Predictor-Action (VPA), which replaces autoregressive token-by-token action decoding in VLA models with a latent control loop combining a shared vision encoder, a neuro-symbolic discrete skill selector, a JEPA next-state predictor, and a flow-matching solver that emits whole action chunks in few steps. This removes per-token inference latency, enabling higher closed-loop control frequencies.

entry.title: FORGE: Procedural Weight Generation for Sparse MoE Inference

author.name: Chanyoung Moon, Travis Pence, Daisuke Yamada, Jiaqi Mo, Yanxin Zhang, Vikas Singh, Karthikeyan Sankaralingam

entry.summary: FORGE replaces stored sparse MoE expert weights with an on-chip accelerator that regenerates them on the fly from O(log^2 d) rotor parameters, approximating gigabytes of expert weights per layer with under a megabyte of seeds. This attacks the dual HBM-bandwidth and expert-parallelism memory bottlenecks of autoregressive MoE decode.

entry.title: Tight End-to-End Accounting for Differentially Private Synthetic Data

author.name: Georgi Ganev, Vadym Doroshenko, Arun Ganesh, Juan Felipe Gomez, Ryan McKenna, Bogdan Kulynych
