entry.summary: Develops tools for tight end-to-end differential privacy accounting of pipelines that compose heterogeneous mechanisms using different privacy notions (bounded range, zCDP, ADP), via privacy loss distributions, f-DP, and Gaussian DP. Includes new PLD and GDP analyses of bounded-range mechanisms like the Exponential mechanism, aimed at DP synthetic data pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond the End-Effector: Learning Whole-Arm Contact Manipulation from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Bo-Ruei Huang, Daniel Seita, Erdem B{\i}y{\i}k

entry.summary: The paper introduces WACL, a hierarchical framework for whole-arm contact manipulation that describes tasks with three robot-agnostic representations and hands them to a quasi-static surface-contact optimizer, letting robots exploit non-prehensile arm contacts as humans do. This goes beyond end-effector-centric manipulation, addressing contact selection, end-effector pose constraints, and safety. Whole-arm manipulation could improve robot efficiency and robustness in cluttered, human-like settings.

entry.title: Towards Robust Calibration Dataset for Domain-General Mixture of Experts Pruning

author.name: Luis Frentzen Salim, Chia-Chun Wu, Tran Van Nhiem, Lun-Wei Ku, Yung-Hui Li

entry.summary: An empirical study of how calibration set size, language, and distribution affect expert pruning in MoE models, using gpt-oss-20b as a testbed. Findings show pruning quality plateaus at small calibration sizes and that English-only calibration transfers well cross-lingually.

entry.title: ANCHOR: Assessing Naturalistic Constraint Hierarchies and Ordering in Repository-Grounded Agentic Coding

author.name: Wenqiang Zhu, Xinping Lei, Zhiyi Lai, Zhengshuo Gong, Tianzhuang He, Songwei Yu, Weihao Li, Jingxuan Xu, Zihang Xu, Gang Wu, Zhongqiu Wang, Yuhui Bai, Jie Li, Zhao Liu, Junhao Fan, Yan Wu, Yanan Wu, Jiaheng Liu, Ariel Deng

entry.summary: ANCHOR is a benchmark for engineering constraint following by repository-grounded coding agents, evaluating not just functional correctness but adherence to constraints on modification scope, workflow order, validation, tool use, and reporting. It provides a hierarchical taxonomy of 10 categories and 78 leaf types distilled from real developer interactions, with an automated task instantiation pipeline across eight language groups. It makes an under-measured capability visible to evaluation.

entry.title: Decouple to Forget: Semantic Mediation for Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

author.name: Jingyue Cong, Andy Song, Yang Yu, Tabinda Sarwar, Xinshu Li, Ziqi Xu, Xun Yi, Ke Wang, Bo Han, Estrid He

entry.summary: D2F is a targeted unlearning method that extracts a fact-level mediator representation from answers to be forgotten, removing only sensitive factual content while preserving non-sensitive meaning and surface expression. This avoids the utility loss of existing methods that treat whole responses as the unit of forgetting.

entry.title: Narrative Lookahead in LLMs: Event-Level Decodability, Predictive Advantage, and Steering

author.name: Donghoon Jung, Min Kim, Seojin Choi, Songeun Chae, Seohyon Jung

entry.summary: This interpretability study asks whether LLMs represent narrative events before writing them, extracting 23,355 events from 2,000 stories generated by four open-weight models and labeling them across three dimensions of change. Probing hidden states at event boundaries against matched text-only prefixes reveals decodable event information ahead of generation. The work extends mechanistic analysis from tokens to event-level semantics and explores steering.

entry.title: How Reliable Are System-One Decisions in Medicine? A Comparative Study of Jev, Jev-like Models, and LLMs

author.name: Yanrui Du, Danyang Zhao, Sendong Zhao, Wenhao Li, Yibo Gao, Haochun Wang, Zhuoer Xu, Shiwen Cui, Bing Qin

entry.summary: This comparative study evaluates fast, system-one decision models including Jev across 15 medical datasets and 8,742 instances, assessing accuracy, decision stability, and reliability awareness under a unified protocol. Results show Jev rivals leading models on text-driven tasks but struggles on numerically driven tasks, while exhibiting the lowest decision reversal rate under question-format variation. The work provides a useful capability boundary map for lightweight medical decision models.

entry.title: Looking Complete Is Not Being Grounded: Evaluating LLM Sitreps Against Human-Authored Situation Reports

author.name: Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: This study derives a 15-slot information schema from professional humanitarian situation reports and evaluates 121 human versus 261 LLM-generated crisis reports across five disasters. The best machine arm appears nominally above the human ceiling on one setting but the difference is statistically indistinguishable, and the ordering fails to replicate under a different judge model. It cautions that LLM reports can look complete without being grounded, and highlights evaluator dependence in such comparisons.

entry.title: TGuide: Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Historical Trajectory Guidance

author.name: Zhuo Chen, Bin Zou, Fanyue Wei, Lixin Duan, Angela Yao, Wen Li

entry.summary: TGuide accelerates autoregressive video diffusion to as few as four denoising steps using an Anchor-Transport-Correct predictor guided by historically correlated features across video chunks. This complements feature caching approaches that fail when inter-step feature changes are too large.

entry.title: LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders

author.name: Shiqiao Gu, Yang Yong, Fengjun Zhong, Ruihao Gong, Chengtao Lv, Xiangyu Fan, Lei Yang, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: LightVAE compresses video VAEs by exactly reparameterizing causal Conv3D layers into aggregate spatial responses plus difference-driven temporal corrections, then applying temporal low-rank compression guided by distinct sensitivity profiles. This reduces the substantial compute cost of encoding and decoding in latent video diffusion.

entry.title: Drive3R: Block-wise Streaming Geometric Foundation Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tianyi Yang, Haojun Yang, Jipeng Xiao, Xuesong Chen, Shaoshuai Shi, Li Jiang, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Drive3R adapts feed-forward geometric foundation models to long-horizon driving sequences via block-wise streaming with causal attention, avoiding the intractable quadratic cost of global attention. The design specifically counters compounding drift in causal streaming and trajectory fragmentation in chunk-then-align strategies for dense multi-view 3D reconstruction in closed-loop simulation.

entry.title: Genesis: Visual Augmentation Primitives for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Fan Yang, Lifeng Chen, Yipu Wang, Han Wang, Feilong Chen, Yidong Ma, Zhiyang Chen, Chaoyang Zhao, Lingxiang Wu, Hanqi Jiang, Yibo Chen, Xu Tang, Yao Hu, Ming Tang, Xiaojie Jin, Xiaolong Zheng, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: Genesis introduces Visual Augmentation Primitives, a data augmentation pipeline that uses state-of-the-art generative vision models to synthesize photorealistic samples with paired reasoning text, grounding each chain-of-thought step in visual evidence. It targets the degradation of MLLM reasoning in complex real-world scenes caused by purely linguistic CoT training data.

entry.title: VideoSlate: Stateful Commit Control for Temporally Grounded Agentic Video Reasoning

author.name: Shuo Zheng, Yuanjie Dang, Peng Chen, Jianjun Xiang, Ronghua Liang, Mohammed Bennamoun, Qiuhong Ke

entry.summary: VideoSlate introduces a stateful commit-control framework for agentic video reasoning, using a typed evidence blackboard that links candidate spans with provenance so accumulated information informs revision assessment and explicit adoption decisions govern downstream evidence. This prevents revisions from discarding useful evidence while correcting localization errors.

entry.title: ConDenseDrive: Knowledge-Dense, Token-Sparse Visual Encoder for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Shengzhen Li, Yongkang Li, Hao Gao, Chenxi Wu, Yajing Sun, Lu Hou, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: ConDenseDrive is a three-stage visual encoder for end-to-end driving that distills visual, semantic, and geometric knowledge from three vision foundation models, then adapts to multi-frame driving while pruning to a token-sparse representation for latency-constrained inference. It jointly improves representation quality and inference efficiency over generic image-pretrained encoders.

entry.title: DVTR-KD: Distilling Vision-Language Models via Intermediate Visual Token Reconstruction

author.name: Haolan Wei, Jiahui Wang, Junli Zha, Xinkai Lu, Yunxiao Zou, Chao Zhou, Xiang Song

entry.summary: DVTR-KD is a knowledge distillation framework for MLLMs that reconstructs the teacher's dense visual tokens from the student's compressed tokens, resolving token-count mismatches that complicate distillation. It targets efficient deployment of VLMs on edge devices under constrained compute budgets.

entry.title: ReDiS: Reasoning-Diagnosis Self-Evolution for Multimodal Reasoning in Remote Sensing

author.name: Yi Liu, Wentao Jiang, Shuo Ni, Zhiming Luo, Di Wang, Zengmao Wang, Jing Zhang, Bo Du

entry.summary: Introduces ReDiS, a framework that splits multimodal reasoning into two evolving role-specific experts from a shared backbone: a Reasoner that explores diverse reasoning paths and a Diagnoser that evaluates candidates, avoiding unreliable self-consistency supervision and costly pre-built trajectories. Targets reliable multi-step inference with fine-grained grounding in remote sensing. Notably shares an author group with FaithRS.

entry.title: Disentangling Task-Relevant Latent Dynamics for Reward Modeling

author.name: Dayou Li, Jionghao Wang, Peihao Wang, Jiuzhou Lei, Hao Wang, Jichen Chai, Hezhen Hu, Minghui Zheng, Zhangyang Wang, Xin Li, Wenping Wang, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: DiTaR learns rewards for robotic manipulation from videos by disentangling task-relevant latent state changes from extraneous visual variation, preventing learned rewards from responding to distractors. This offers a scalable alternative to handcrafted dense reward engineering in reinforcement learning. The approach addresses a core bottleneck for applying RL to real-world manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Beyond User-Side Defenses: Image Protection in Open-Weight Diffusion Models

author.name: Jihye Kang, Jiwon Park, Namhyuk Ahn

entry.summary: This paper proposes moving image protection from user-side adversarial perturbations into the weights of open diffusion models, defining four requirements: protection effectiveness, clean fidelity, compatibility, and tamper resistance. It uses long-horizon attack simulations to evaluate resistance to protection removal, showing improved resistance to re-alignment at some cost to clean fidelity with a single protection tool. It reframes prompt/image protection as a model-provider responsibility in open-weight deployments.

entry.title: Before We Act: Learning Action-Conditioned Team-Response Beliefs for Decentralized Multi-Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zihao Li, Yanan Zhou, Ranpeng Qiu, Guoqiang Ren, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: The authors present a framework for learning team-response beliefs in decentralized multi-robot manipulation, predicting how teammates will respond to candidate actions and separating each candidate's direct advantage from utility contributed by teammate adaptation. Calibrated selection then chooses between the nominal action and alternatives, with analysis of when response prediction changes the preferred action.

entry.title: From Video to Vision: Learning Generalizable Humanoid Carrying from Human Motion

author.name: Ziluo Ding

entry.summary: The paper presents MOVER, a multi-stage Teacher-Assistant-Student reinforcement learning framework for humanoid object carrying that removes the need for real-time reference trajectory modules and motion-capture-studio evaluation. It retargets ordinary video data using GENMO and GMR combined with augmentation to train policies that generalize spatially. This matters because it lowers the data-collection barrier for humanoid manipulation skills and improves real-world deployability.

entry.title: DEFT-VLA: Stage-Localized Force Specialization for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zan Huang, Yibo Qiu, Kan Ding, Xuanping Zhang, Ao Tian, Ronald X Xu, Mingzhai Sun

entry.summary: DEFT-VLA handles the stage-dependent sensory conflict in contact-rich manipulation by retaining a vision-dominant base expert for non-contact phases and adding a force-aware contact expert for post-contact stages, localizing force conditioning where it helps. A contact-localized force-attending curriculum prevents force signals from distracting during approach and visual shortcuts during contact. It improves VLA policies on force-critical tasks.

entry.title: RM-WAM: Reliable Memory-Augmented World Action Models for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Cui Miao, Junhao Yu, Ping Liu, Ning Yang, Xuhua Chen, He Zheng, Xiaodong Wang, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: RM-WAM augments World Action Models with a memory mechanism that treats history as a context-dependent predictive resource rather than universally useful context, filtering stale, stage-mismatched, or error-contaminated observations. This improves reliability of long-horizon manipulation where visually similar states can correspond to different task stages and interaction histories.

entry.title: Evaluating Long-Horizon Robot Planning under Uncertainty

author.name: Harsh Muriki, Gayathri Aravindan, Yuchen Zheng, Sonia Chernova

entry.summary: The authors introduce a benchmark of seven long-horizon household tasks in Habitat that vary initial robot memory and environment configurations, evaluating ReAct, VLM-TAMP, and Tru-POMDP adaptations within one shared execution framework across 1,350 episodes. ReAct achieves the highest overall task success (45.3%) and completion (71.7%), and accurate initial memory does not consistently help every planner. The benchmark measures success, partial completion, action efficiency, and rule-based trace analysis.

entry.title: Contractor Filters

author.name: Simon Rohou (ENSTA, Lab-STICC\_ROBEX)

entry.summary: Contractor Filters introduce a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers, representing feasible states symbolically as compositions of contractors rather than re-materializing geometric enclosures. The framework provides exact nominal recursion, guaranteed robust enclosures with validated flow inclusions, and optional sub-paving compression within a single algebra.

entry.title: RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories

author.name: Yunfu Deng, Sangwoo Shin, Brahma S. Pavse, Josiah P. Hanna

entry.summary: RoboFQE performs off-policy evaluation of visual robot policies directly from offline trajectories without new rollouts, combining fitted Q-evaluation with a pretrained vision foundation model and a learned terminal success predictor, avoiding behavior-policy density estimation. This sidesteps the infrastructure costs of rollout-based evaluation and compounding prediction errors of simulator or world-model evaluators.

entry.title: Which Metadata Matters for LLM Tool Selection in MCP? Evidence from Controlled Factor-Level Interventions

author.name: Xiaofan Li, Fengchun Qiao, Xing Gao

entry.summary: Analyzing metadata for over 367,000 MCP tools, the authors find large schema variation among functionally similar tools and run controlled one-factor interventions across five LLMs to determine which metadata elements affect tool selection. The study isolates the causal impact of server names, tool names, descriptions, and parameter schemas before any call is made.

entry.title: PEARL: Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Jie Yang, Mianqiu Huang, Yiwei Zhao, Bo Wang, Yang Liu, Yuxin Wang

entry.summary: PEARL improves credit assignment for multi-turn agents trained with terminal rewards by locating the first divergence between success and failure continuations from the same history, clustering local decision features in memory, and using recurring patterns to guide training. It requires no additional critic.

entry.title: WeatherBridge: Forecast-Aware Multi-Source Input Adaptation for Pretrained Weather Forecasting Models

author.name: Mutian Xi, Xinyu Su, Xiaohui Zhong, Hao Li

entry.summary: WeatherBridge is a source-conditioned adapter, implemented as a Swin-UNet predicting structured residual corrections, that maps heterogeneous operational NWP initial states to the ERA5-style inputs expected by pretrained data-driven weather models without retraining them. This addresses the distribution mismatch that degrades autoregressive forecasts when deploying research models operationally.

entry.title: FleetPilot: Fine-Grained Steering Empowers Real-World LLM Personalization

author.name: Kounianhua Du, Jianxing Liu, Kangning Zhang, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Jiarui Jin, Jianghao Lin, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FleetPilot, a personalization method that steers LLM behavior from sparse, heterogeneous, evolving user interaction histories without the recurring costs of in-context management, parametric adaptation, or personalized reward modeling. It targets query-dependent preference inference for realistic personalization settings.

entry.title: CondMSP: Condition-Informed and Resource-Aware Inorganic Materials Synthesis Planning

author.name: Heewoong Noh, Gyoung S. Na, Elton Pan, Namkyeong Lee, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: CondMSP extends materials synthesis planning from recipe prediction to execution-aware planning by jointly predicting temperature, time, and atmosphere as process context for route construction. It also addresses which candidate routes should be prioritized under limited experimental resources.

entry.title: Agent Sociodrama: Social-Dynamics-Guided Persona Recasting for LLM Agent Teams

author.name: Yirui Qi, Xiaoming Zhang, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: Agent Sociodrama models and validates evolving social dynamics in LLM agent teams, updating agents' emotional states and asymmetric directed relationships each round via an external judge LLM. Across six backbones and five scenarios, trajectories show structured social patterns like dominant-speaker anchoring and information-holder silence, validated against social theory and human judgments. Persona recasting guided by these dynamics improves team performance.

entry.title: Correct Choices, Failed Sequences: Choice2Seq Benchmarks Correctness Retention Across Output Interfaces

author.name: Tianyou Lai, Wentao Yue, Zhiying Deng, Qilei Li

entry.summary: Choice2Seq is a diagnostic benchmark measuring whether models that correctly select answers can also construct them through sequential local decisions, using the Sequence Composition Rate metric. The findings are striking: a model with 97-99% selection accuracy retains only 33% and 2% of correct choices under serial construction, with similar gaps for other models including character-level generation.

entry.title: Making Language the Low-Rate Code of Vision: Successive Refinement from Words to Pixels

author.name: Ruilin Gong, Hao Gong

entry.summary: Provides a rate-distortion analysis showing that captions are not the low-rate code of their images under pixel-optimal codes, and proves a caption can be independent of the first half of a rate-optimal pixel code. It then constructs codes via successive refinement with a distortion measure transitioning from caption log-loss to pixel distortion, so that each code length is compared at matched budgets.

entry.title: Observe, Share, or Predict? Disentangling Partner Information in Embodied Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Adri\'an Szlatincs\'an, Filippo Ziliotto, Bruno Lepri, Luciano Serafini, Massimiliano Luca, Tommaso Campari

entry.summary: Uses the Habitat-based PARTNR benchmark with a Decoupled Partial Observability regime to study which partner information helps LLM-controlled embodied agents collaborate without sharing intentions or plans. It augments decentralized zero-shot ReAct planners with partner-state observation, object knowledge exchange, and next-action prediction to disentangle their effects on coordination and task outcomes.

entry.title: EvoQuantLab: Training-Free Dual-Loop Evolution for Auditable Quantitative Research

author.name: Haolin Yang, Zhiqiang Qian, Chutian Chen, Jipeng Zhang, Tangjia Deng, Jian Xie, Shuaishuai Gong, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Proposes EvoQuantLab, a training-free dual-loop framework for LLM-driven alpha factor discovery that combines an inner genetic-programming loop for token-efficient factor evolution with an outer diagnosis loop that audits evidence across cycles. The design explicitly targets backtest overfitting in agent-based quant workflows.

entry.title: MAS-Gate: Unlocking Multi-Agent System Lifecycle via Node-Centric Quantification

author.name: Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Ming Yan, Peidong Wang, Shilei Cao, Minzhi Li, Bosheng Ding, Juepeng Zheng, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: MAS-Gate conceptualizes LLM-based multi-agent system development and operation as a three-phase lifecycle: design-time orchestration, runtime intervention, and post-hoc attribution, unified under a node-centric quantification framework. This bridges fragmented perspectives in MAS research whose objectives and signals are hard to reconcile. The unified formulation enables consistent measurement and intervention across the full system lifecycle.

entry.title: Learning Adaptive Deliberation Control for Reliable Recognition with Multi-Agent Language Models

author.name: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai

entry.summary: The paper presents ADMA, an adaptive multi-agent controller that learns continuous policies for proposal, challenge, arbitration, and coordination over a frozen task model, using shared trace features for quality, agreement, and progress. A controller trained on legal and financial reasoning transfers without policy updates to four textual and multimodal benchmarks and successive task-model versions, improving accuracy by 6.2-14.2 percentage points with Qwen3.5 held fixed.

entry.title: ECMR: Evidence-Aware Deliberation Control for Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai

entry.summary: ECMR is an evidence-aware controller over frozen role-conditioned LLMs that combats semantic false consensus — confident group answers supported by narrow, duplicated, or correlated rationales. At each step it summarizes answer concentration, support diversity, contradictions, and budget, then selects actions such as propose, challenge, verify, arbitrate, diversify, or stop.

entry.title: RadixFlow: Filling Execution Bubbles in Prefix-Cached Hybrid LLM Serving

author.name: Huihao Jing, Wenbin Hu, Shaojin Chen, Haochen Shi, Haoyu Huang, Sirui Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Zhongwei Xie, Haoran Li

entry.summary: RadixFlow addresses head-of-line blocking in prefix-cached serving of hybrid attention-recurrent LLMs, where a consumer branch may wait on recurrent state a producer branch is still computing, creating idle batch slots. It decouples prefix matching from state readiness via a state-ready traversal that converts a global scan barrier into per-branch scheduling. This targets inference throughput for increasingly popular hybrid architectures.

entry.title: Input-Conditioned Search for Efficient Test-Time Scaling of Recursive Reasoners

author.name: Haochen Shi, Tianwen Fu, Qianggang Ding, Yinhan Lu, Yizhan Li, Huan Zhang, Yajie Zhao, Xingdi Yuan, Hengyang Lu, Bang Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes input-conditioned search for recursive reasoners that explores diverse reasoning traces by applying different update maps to the same latent state, escaping incorrect attractors that depth or perturbation-based width scaling converge to, without additional training. This extends test-time scaling beyond depth/width to a third axis.

entry.title: Predict Before You Modify: Learning Improvement Dynamics for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zixuan Xie, Chang Xu, Yuhua Jiang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces an editable Improvement Dynamics Model (IDM) that predicts task-level outcomes of proposed agent modifications before costly evaluation, guiding optional revision and accumulating predictive knowledge across generations. This shifts self-evolving agents from reactive feedback to predictive self-evolution.

entry.title: PLDiv: Measuring Dataset Diversity and Semantic Collapse via Persistence Landscapes

author.name: Yang Ba, Michelle V. Mancenido, Rong Pan

entry.summary: PLDiv is a dataset diversity metric based on persistence landscapes from topological data analysis, capturing the structural organization of a data distribution beyond lexical or pairwise-similarity summaries. It detects semantic collapse as AI-generated data increasingly mixes with human data in training pipelines.

entry.title: Deep learning from a control vantage point

author.name: \'Alvaro Rodr\'iguez Abella, Jo\~ao Pedro Silvestre, Bahman Gharesifard, Paulo Tabuada

entry.summary: This survey reviews recent deep learning developments through the lens of control theory, covering feedforward and residual networks, transformers, LLMs, and selective state space models. It explains how residual networks can be interpreted as discretizations of continuous-time control systems, enabling control-theoretic analysis, and presents two technical results including approximation and robustness properties. It serves as a bridge between the control and deep learning communities.

entry.title: EarthAlign: Learning Language-Aligned Representations of Earth System Data

author.name: Fadillah Adamsyah Maani, Numan Saeed, Jiaqi Ma, Dat Tien Nguyen, Youssef Wehbe, Duncan Watson-Parris, Salman Khan

entry.summary: EarthAlign is a large-scale dataset spanning 2000-2024 combining ten expert-curated natural event and disaster sources with climatology-derived normal-weather samples to align Earth system data with language. It fills a gap in general-purpose language alignment for weather and climate beyond task-specific prediction.

entry.title: North or South? Diagnosing LLMs' Understanding of North Korean Language, Society, and Knowledge

author.name: Kiwoong Park, Seyoung Song, Donghyun Woo, Alice Oh

entry.summary: Introduces LENS, a human-validated benchmark of 1,765 questions evaluating LLMs on North Korean language, sociocultural perspectives, and domain knowledge, exploiting the Korea division as a natural testbed for low-resource sociolinguistic understanding. Findings show a modest linguistic drop but a larger gap in sociocultural perspective alignment for recent LLMs.

entry.title: Avoiding What Your Teacher Already Knows: Entity Familiarity for Deep-Search Distillation

author.name: Yifei Liu, Zhixiang Liang, Wentao Tan, Yicheng Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Nan Duan, Qiong Cao

entry.summary: The paper identifies teacher-relative difficulty in deep-search distillation: structurally complex questions can be easy for teachers familiar with key entities, yielding weak supervision. It introduces Evidence-Verified Entity Familiarity (EVF) to predict this difficulty, with AUCs of 0.60-0.70, and uses it to select training data that improves distillation of search agents.

entry.title: CryptoFlowBench: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning on Blockchains for Cryptocurrency Fund Tracing

author.name: Runang He, Tongya Zheng, Jing Cao, Yucheng Ying, Shunyu Liu, Bingde Hu, Yang Gao, Zeyuan Hu, Jianrong Zhang, Mingli Song

entry.summary: CryptoFlowBench is a benchmark for multi-hop cryptocurrency fund tracing built from authoritative reports on illicit incidents, with four tasks spanning local to multi-hop tracing. It exposes that static GNN fraud detection and heuristic tracing methods struggle with adaptive multi-hop reasoning over pseudonymous blockchain flows.

entry.title: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents

author.name: Zian Yuan, Wei Li

entry.summary: PrivacyGuard addresses PII leakage from cloud GUI agents that send screenshots and instructions to remote planners. It reconstructs fragmented or overlapping PII evidence for complete source sanitization and maintains a structured reference lifecycle that resolves entity mentions locally without returning raw values to the upload path. It matters as GUI agents proliferate, exposing personal data across turns and sessions.

entry.title: Growing to See: Efficient Pretraining of Self-Supervised Vision Transformers

author.name: Amir Mohammad Karimi Mamaghan, Ferdinand Kapl, Andrea Dittadi, Karl Henrik Johansson, Kaitlin Maile, Johannes von Oswald, Stefan Bauer

entry.summary: The authors systematically study progressive depth growth as an efficient pretraining strategy for self-supervised vision transformers, evaluating masked autoencoders (MAE) and DINOv3. They analyze how layer insertion during training affects downstream performance on global and dense tasks, intermediate representation quality, and internal computational patterns.

entry.title: Event-Centric Earthquake Monitoring with a Multi-Station Transformer

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Weiqiang Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces EQNet2, a geometry-aware multi-station Transformer that jointly predicts phase arrivals, first-motion polarities, source location and magnitude, and arrival-to-event association, replacing fragmented single-station, single-task pipelines. Demonstrated on Northern California data and continuous Ridgecrest and Bay Area waveforms, it recovers more complete and reliable earthquake catalogs. Advances ML-based seismology with a joint event-centric formulation.

entry.title: Towards Green AI: Evaluating Energy Efficiency for Quantized LLM Inference

author.name: Petar Basta

entry.summary: This work presents a unified evaluation of weight-only post-training quantization strategies for LLM inference, measuring energy usage and carbon intensity alongside accuracy and runtime across multiple models, tasks, and GPUs (H100, A6000, A100, L4). The authors identify a novel trend in how quantization affects energy efficiency that is not captured by memory or runtime alone.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for AI System Optimization with Selectively Verified Feedback

author.name: Shuang Wu

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies Gaussian process bandits for optimizing prompts, retrieval systems, and agent workflows when cheap model-based evaluations may disagree with trusted task outcomes. It establishes finite-time regret bounds under an audit budget and provides a safe adaptation mechanism for selectively verified feedback.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer of Evil Vectors Is Directionally Asymmetric

author.name: Juann Kim, Minku Kang

entry.summary: The authors test whether the evil persona vector from activation steering transfers across English, Spanish, Swahili, and Telugu in four open-source LLMs. They find transfer is directionally asymmetric: vectors are harder to extract from low-resource language activations yet still steer behavior in those languages.

entry.title: AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Imaging for Intraoperative Detection of Low-Grade Glioma: A Clinical Study

author.name: Siri Willems, Ishika Jain, Jens De Winne, Siri Luthman, Hamed Zivari Adab, Roeland Vandebriel, Anna Alperovich, Xiaohan Zhang, Ben Stoffelen, Tom De Schepper, Lien Solie, Steven De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: This clinical study applies AI-enhanced hyperspectral imaging to detect low-grade gliomas during surgery, a case where tumors strongly resemble healthy brain tissue under white light. It characterizes spectral differences between healthy and tumor tissue and provides a paired comparison of HSI-based methods against standard intraoperative tools like iMRI and ultrasound. Real clinical data with a focus on an underserved tumor grade makes this a notable applied AI-health result.

entry.title: Lifting Finite-Sample Gaussian Approximation of Wide Neural Networks to Functional Convergence

author.name: Luis Wiederhold, Nil Ayday, Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

entry.summary: This theory paper lifts finite-sample Wasserstein-2 bounds on the Gaussian process approximation of wide random neural networks to functional convergence, removing dependence on the number of sample points. This bridges the gap between finite-sample bounds with good rates and functional bounds that avoid uninformative constants.

entry.title: Agaram 2.5B: The First Tamil-First Language Model Trained from Scratch with Tool Calling. A Playbook for Under-Represented Languages

author.name: Ramchand Kumaresan, Madhusudhanan G, Kaushik Kezendirane

entry.summary: Agaram 2.5B is a 2.5-billion-parameter Tamil-English model trained from scratch on about 50 billion tokens using one node of eight H100 GPUs in roughly six days, then fine-tuned into a chat model with tool calling that responds in Tamil script, romanized Tamil, and English. It reports better translation than Sarvam-1 and strong tool-selection results. The paper doubles as a reproducible playbook for building models for under-represented languages on modest budgets.

entry.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus

author.name: Neil Walton

entry.summary: This theory paper develops a rate-transfer method converting finite-time Lyapunov estimates for associated stochastic differential equations into convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under moment and smoothness conditions, SGD convergence analysis reduces to a calculus argument on an SDE generator inequality, recovering classical rates and enabling analysis of new algorithms.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Foundations of Online Temperature Sampling

author.name: Jin Sima, Nikolaos Papagiannis, Ananth Grama, Wojciech Szpankowski

entry.summary: The authors ground LLM decoding heuristics in information theory, showing via Kac's lemma and the AEP that maximizing sampling entropy under a cross-entropy plausibility budget yields temperature sampling offline. Their main contribution is the online variant, where conditionals arrive one at a time and the sampling distribution must be chosen causally under a coupled budget. This provides a principled foundation for adaptive temperature decoding aimed at reducing degenerate repetition.

entry.title: WUSPruner: Second-Moment-Optimal Transforms for Structured Pruning

author.name: Shengkun Tang, Dan Alistarh, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces WUSPruner, a transform-based framework for structured pruning of LLMs that formulates basis selection as a local linear reconstruction problem minimizing pruning-induced loss. Building on a second-moment transformation, it constructs a WUS transform from joint activation and weight statistics, showing pruning outcomes depend critically on the basis in which coordinate deletion occurs.

entry.title: DRanker: A Transformer-Based Multi-Task Ranking Model for the Disney+ Homepage

author.name: Priya Nirmal Singh Khokher, Daniel Nemirovsky, Benjamin P. Whitesell, Ethan Sukrae Lee, Eric Wulf, Tom Chee-Duffy, Nicholas Flores

entry.summary: This industry paper describes DRanker, a transformer-based multitask ranking model deployed globally on the Disney+ homepage, including its encoder-only architecture, causal debiasing mechanism, and large-scale inference stack. It reports over 1% lift in key engagement and 0.5% lift in daily active users, and shares practical lessons showing simpler designs outperformed more complex alternatives.

entry.title: Resample the Answer: Where to Spend Test-Time Compute in Recursive Reasoning

author.name: Maxime Illouz

entry.summary: Using the Tiny Recursive Model (TRM), this paper studies which latent state to perturb or resample when recursive reasoning fails, finding that failed trajectories carry their failure in the answer state y rather than the reasoning state z. At equal compute in depth and width, resampling y recovers more failures than any perturbation of z tested. The results clarify how to allocate test-time compute in recursive reasoning architectures.

entry.title: Guidance Without Labels: Flow Matching from Coupled Gaussian Mixtures

author.name: Stanislas Ducotterd, Bassam El Rawas, Michael Unser

entry.summary: The authors replace the Gaussian source in flow matching with a fitted Gaussian mixture, coupling each data point to a mixture component via entropic optimal transport; the resulting transport reduces to the standard problem plus a guidance-like correction. This correction is closed-form plus a small learned network term, enabling reuse of pretrained velocity fields and improving FID at every step count on CIFAR-10 and CelebA-HQ.

entry.title: Learning to Design SR Solvers: Harness Optimization for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Qian Li, Yuxiao Hu, Qihao Duan, Jinyue Yan, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: HarnessSR argues that the harness around LLM-based symbolic regression agents, prompts and workflows, should itself be optimized rather than hand-designed. The framework jointly optimizes prompts and workflows to build reusable SR agents that can wrap either PySR or LLM-based equation generators through tool-specific interfaces.

entry.title: Measure Neural Mappings

author.name: Ricardo Baptista, Edoardo Calvello, Bohan Chen, Andrew Stuart, Urbain Vaes

entry.summary: The paper defines measure neural mappings (MNMs), combining measure-dependent neural transport with ensemble consistency to learn operators on probability measures, with quantitative continuum limits for attention on noncompact laws. It bounds expected Wasserstein error for fixed self-attention transformers in terms of empirical input Wasserstein error. The framework targets scientific machine learning settings like Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification with unbounded state spaces.

entry.title: Position: Beyond Training Time, Test-Time Coordination is Essential for Cooperative MARL

author.name: Dongsu Lee, Sooraj Sathish, Joonkyung Kim, Woojun Kim, Amy Zhang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that cooperative MARL should treat test-time coordination as part of the problem definition, since CTDE provides no coordination channel at execution and fails for strongly coupled, non-stationary systems like warehouse robotics and cloud scheduling. The authors advocate exploiting global telemetry already available at deployment. It challenges the dominant paradigm's framing rather than proposing a single algorithm.

entry.title: Searching for What Matters: Open-Ended Discovery of Multiple Hypotheses with Agentic Data Exploration

author.name: Sanchit Kabra, Nurendra Choudhary, Jiangshu Du, Eddie Huang, Danai Koutra, Chandan K Reddy

entry.summary: This paper introduces the problem of open-ended multiple hypothesis discovery, where an agentic system receives only a large tabular dataset and an outcome and must discover multiple data-supported hypotheses without knowing relevant variables, forms, conditions, or mechanism count in advance. The authors build a benchmark from structural causal models grounded in real-world schemas with 351 planned hypotheses. This is relevant to AI-for-science and agentic data exploration capabilities.

entry.title: Same Function, Different Trajectory: No Standard Optimizer Is Equivariant to Transformer Reparameterization

author.name: Bum Jun Kim

entry.summary: The paper proves that functionally equivalent Transformer reparameterizations (e.g., scaling query and key matrices inversely) yield different training trajectories under standard optimizers like AdamW, since moment estimates fail to track parameter scale changes. It proposes balancing matrix pairs and jointly transforming moment estimates so runs restarted from equivalent checkpoints follow identical trajectories.

entry.title: Euclidean Distance-Based Flow Matching

author.name: Paul-Henrik Heilmann, Peter Ochs

entry.summary: This work replaces the squared Euclidean loss in flow matching with a plain Euclidean distance, reframing the regression target as a conditional geometric median and thereby importing robustness from robust statistics. The authors provide probabilistic interpretation and analyze distributional robustness of the resulting generative model.

entry.title: Statistical Vignettes on the Grokking Phenomenon

author.name: Baye Malick Gning, Elvis Dohmatob

entry.summary: This work studies grokking in an analytically tractable setting, disentangling effects of initialization, signal strength, weight decay, sample size, and input dimension, and distinguishing early nuisance-feature fitting, core feature learning, and delayed generalization. It gives sharp provable conditions for grokking and analytic expressions for generalization plateau lengths.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems for Knowledge-Grounded Material Substitution

author.name: Tarjei Paule Hage, Subhadeep Pal, Wei Lu, Yu-Chuan Hsu, Gayla Lyon, Jiezhu Jin, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: MARS is a hierarchical multi-agent reasoning system for knowledge-grounded material substitution, applied to replacing PFAS under scientific and manufacturing constraints. It decomposes substitution into closed-loop workflows of requirement analysis, grounded candidate generation, and manufacturability assessment with process design.

entry.title: SEEK: Agentic Knowledge Graph Retrieval for Secure Code Generation

author.name: Varun Gadey, Markus Tohn, Lichao Wu, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi, Alexandra Dmitrienko

entry.summary: SEEK is an agentic Graph RAG framework for secure code generation that builds a security knowledge graph structured on the CWE taxonomy and populated with curated real-world vulnerability data. Unlike flat similarity-based retrieval, the graph structure lets the system infer the relevant vulnerability space and retrieve targeted knowledge when no direct match exists. It aims to reduce exploitable weaknesses in LLM-generated code.

entry.title: Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Shuo Gao, Chenhao Zheng, Zhongzheng Ren

entry.summary: FramePack-U is a training-free frame packing framework that compresses arbitrarily long videos into a fixed-size visual representation with constant memory cost, avoiding the linear token-sequence growth that breaks vision-language models on hour-long videos. It requires no fine-tuning or architectural modification, unlike token reduction and keyframe selection methods that leave O(n) scaling intact.

entry.title: Trust-Calibrated VLA Policy Post-Training with Evolving Imagination

author.name: Wenzhan Li, Yiran Qin, Heng Zhou, Huirui Wang, Yulan Guo, Ruimao Zhang

entry.summary: MERL is a trust-calibrated RL post-training framework for vision-language-action models that couples policy optimization with an online-updated simulator consisting of a world model and reward proxy head. Simulator reliability adaptively controls the imagined-data ratio and rollout horizon, resolving the reliability-efficiency tension between model-free and model-based refinement.

entry.title: SCOPE Before You Sample: Conformal Scores Guide Posterior Exploration for Fast and Calibrated Bayesian Predictive Inference

author.name: Zahra Moslemi, Ziyi Liang, Babak Shahbaba

entry.summary: SCOPE uses conformal nonconformity scores to guide posterior computation toward the few parameter directions that determine the prediction region boundary, achieving MCMC-quality, calibrated predictive coverage at a fraction of the cost. This addresses miscalibration under model misspecification that plagues variational approximations.

entry.title: textGrain watermarking is harder to detect: can sum-tests still do it optimally?

author.name: Swapnaneel Bhattacharyya, Soham Bonnerjee

entry.summary: The authors analyze the textGrain LLM watermarking scheme, which calibrates its signal against sampling entropy via an entropy budget, modeling human edits as a sparse mixture where a fraction of positions retain the watermark and token uncertainty decays. They show entropy calibration carries a cost in the minimax detection bound under edits and study whether the proposed sum-based detector is optimal. This provides rigorous theory on the edit-robustness of a recent watermarking approach.

entry.title: Beyond the greenwash: do LLMs' ecologically sound decisions hold up under pressure?

author.name: Trent R. Northen, Mingxun Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces bioalignment, a measure of LLM biases toward biosystems and their robustness under pressure, using a known-dose calibration ladder of continued-pretraining arms to validate that behavioral scores track disposition depth rather than surface compliance. It targets hidden biases in closed-weight models that surface under stress.

entry.title: Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Guoming Ling, Yupei Lin, Zhongzhan Huang, Junxin Li, Junjie Liu, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: This is the first survey of benchmark compression, reviewing 119 papers on estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from partial evaluations. It develops a taxonomy covering compression within benchmarks, across suites, and during adaptive evaluation, plus work on redundancy and reliability verification. As evaluation costs grow with frontier models, this area is becoming practically important.

entry.title: TrajCFG: Token-Wise Classifier-Free Guidance via Denoising Trajectory Feedback

author.name: Jingyu Liu, Hao Jiang, Yikang Ding, Huafeng Shi, Xu Yang, Xiaoqiang Liu, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Proposes TrajCFG, a training-free method for flow-matching models that adapts classifier-free guidance per latent token based on historical changes in guided velocity direction, assigning stronger guidance where directions change more. It reuses standard CFG predictions with no extra model evaluations.

entry.title: FrameFold: Response-Guided KV Cache Consolidation for Autoregressive Long Video Generation

author.name: Muyu Liu, Mingming Liu, Hong Gu, Yuyao Zhang, Qin Lu

entry.summary: FrameFold is a training-free method for consolidating KV caches in autoregressive long video generation, showing that spatial queries depend on different historical content and that higher attention coverage does not guarantee better quality. It compares response-guided signals to decide what history to retain under a fixed cache budget.

entry.title: Align-VAE: Aligning Attention and Geometry in VecSet VAEs for 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Huaizhi Qu, Mingxin Yang, Xintong Han, Fangneng Zhan, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Align-VAE analyzes latent-to-geometry alignment in set-based VecSet VAEs for 3D shapes, identifying issues such as attention-sink-like tokens, periodic decoder attention artifacts, and mismatched normal supervision. It introduces four corresponding modifications including a shared learnable decoder token bank.

entry.title: Sharper Frames, Worse Rooms: Viewpoint Coverage Dominates Image Quality in Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Alibek Dadajonov, Hikmatillo Umarhojiyev

entry.summary: This paper shows that in feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction under a fixed view budget, selecting the sharpest frames is actively harmful: sharp frames concentrate during slow motion and yield narrow angular coverage, producing 48% room dimension error versus 3% for uniform temporal sampling across nine room scans. Viewpoint coverage, not image quality, dominates reconstruction accuracy.

entry.title: Tikhonov-Stabilized Bezier Representation Forecasting for Training-free Diffusion Acceleration

author.name: Lei Zhu, Mujie Lin, Ruochong Zheng, Guangyi Wang, Hao Li, Peng Jin, Chang Liu, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Proposes BeziCast, a training-free diffusion acceleration framework that forecasts output-proximal denoising representations using Tikhonov-stabilized Bezier extrapolation, avoiding the instability of Taylor-style finite-difference caching over long intervals and reducing error accumulation across denoiser blocks. It targets Diffusion Transformer inference cost without retraining or sampler modification.

entry.title: TableVision: Recovering Verified Structure from Historical Tables

author.name: Todd Y. Zhou, James M. Snyder Jr

entry.summary: TableVision treats structure recovery, not digit reading, as the core problem in historical table transcription, showing that strong open-source readers reproduce 99% of digits but misfile many into wrong cells on election-return panels, while TableVision correctly files 99.2% on degraded 1880s pages versus 1 of 1494 for Amazon Textract. It uses a dynamic program for volume-level block processing and exact-total consistency checks to verify released columns.

entry.title: When, Where, and Why: Hierarchical Causal Explainability for Video Face Understanding with MLLMs

author.name: Anubhav Kataria, Shreya Ghosh, Jingwen Ye, Abhinav Dhall

entry.summary: VideoFace-X-LLM targets explainable facial behaviour understanding in video by answering when an expression occurs, where the model attends, and why the evidence is necessary. It includes ExplainFace, a weakly supervised video-text corpus built from CelebV-HQ and validated through human evaluation, aiming to make MLLM explanations for subtle facial dynamics more faithful.

entry.title: Surface Reconstruction from Range Scans Under Visibility Constraints

author.name: Gabriel Lenain, Edmond Boyer, Jean Ponce

entry.summary: The paper formulates range-scan surface reconstruction as robust regression of predicted first-surface intersections along acquisition rays against measured depth, penalizing intersections between sensor and observed point. It represents the surface as the zero set of a 1-Lipschitz MLP, enabling linearly convergent optimization while using sensor visibility information most neural methods discard.

entry.title: Omni-RS: Unifying Multi-Task Understanding and Generation in Remote Sensing

author.name: Pan Yin. Shuai Yang, Yuanhao Liu, Datao Tang, Jialin Li, Hao Wang, Pei Liu, Kaiyu Li, Cong Zhao, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: Proposes Omni-RS, a unified remote sensing framework supporting four understanding tasks and five generation tasks, going beyond prior unified models limited to text-to-image. It uses a scene-guided two-stage training strategy in which a multimodal LLM adapted to remote sensing guides a diffusion transformer for generation. Bridges the understanding-generation divide for geospatial data.

entry.title: Orientation Estimation of Cryo-EM Images for Molecules with Arbitrary Symmetry by Semidefinite Programming

author.name: Yunpeng Shi, Amit Singer, Jinxin Wang, Ruiyi Yang

entry.summary: The paper extends the non-unique games framework to symmetric structures, formulating orientation estimation for cryo-EM images of molecules with point group symmetry as an optimization over rotation groups with a semidefinite programming relaxation. This provides a principled mathematical treatment for a previously ill-posed symmetric variant of the problem.

entry.title: From LLM Plans to Authorized Motion: Execution-Bound Authorization for Excavators

author.name: Mehdi Heydari Shahna, Seihun Kim, Soyi Jung, Soohyun Park, Jouni Mattila, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: This work proposes execution-bound authorization for LLM-directed excavators, binding a one-use lease to the generated action, motion, mission contract, and admission tolerance, with atomic dispatch rechecks and periodic supervision that can trigger safe stops if authority is revoked. The framework connects exact motion identity to dispatch integrity and is evaluated on a 672-case interface suite plus loaded digging scenarios.

entry.title: Imitation Learning via Discrete and Rhythmic Primitive Composition

author.name: Rafid Saif, Auke Ijspeert, Hsiu-Chin Lin

entry.summary: The authors propose Neural Dynamic Composition (NDC), a supervised framework that composes Dynamic Movement Primitives from raw trajectories given only one example per primitive, using parallel DMP combinations as a differentiable relaxation of categorical primitive selection. It handles both discrete and rhythmic movements without requiring MP labels, addressing sample-inefficiency of RL-based composition.

entry.title: Listen Before Act: Audio-Conditioned Robot Manipulation with ListenVLA

author.name: Jiaqi Fan, Rui Xu, Jiakun Xia, Xuyu Fan, Shuailei Ma, Yuefeng Wang, Qing Wang, Jiarui Zhang, Yili Fu, Xu Li

entry.summary: ListenVLA is an audio-conditioned VLA policy built on GR00T N1.7 that combines semantic audio embeddings with waveform-derived acoustic cues over causal audio history to guide manipulation tasks where auditory cues matter. It introduces an audio-action binding objective using context-matched demonstrations. This extends VLA modality coverage beyond vision and language to sound.

entry.title: Belief Space Planning for Risk Signal Temporal Logic via Mixed-Integer Convex Programming

author.name: Shaohang Han, Joris Verhagen, Kaier Liang, Jana Tumova

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that Risk Signal Temporal Logic (RiSTL) planning in Gaussian belief space can be formulated as a mixed-integer convex program by using an information-form parameterization of the belief and a convex relaxation of the belief dynamics. This addresses the general non-convexity that makes gradient-based belief-space planners incomplete and suboptimal. The result gives formal guarantees (completeness/optimality within the relaxation) for task-and-risk-aware planning under state uncertainty with active information gathering.

entry.title: WoVR+: World Model as Reliable Simulator for Versatile VLA Policy Optimization with RL

author.name: Shangqing Zhou, Zhennan Jiang, Ning Ma, Xin Fu, Yupeng Zheng, Shuai Tian, Huangrui Li, Jiahao Liu, Chao Yu, Zhongpu Xia, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: WoVR+ extends a hallucination-aware world-model-RL framework for VLA training, redesigning the learned environment and imagined interaction protocol with a VLA-interface-aligned world model providing multi-view prediction and proprioceptive updates while mitigating hallucinations. Chunk-wise noise preserves flow-based policy exploration while limiting compounding rollout errors, reducing reliance on costly real-robot interaction.

entry.title: OneDemo: Unified Policy Learning and Data Generation from a Single Demonstration

author.name: Ying Qian, Jianshu Hu, Han Fang, Shuguang Li, Yutong Ban

entry.summary: OneDemo formulates demonstration editing as a structured reinforcement learning problem in which an editor learns, from sparse task-success rewards, when to transition between object states to turn one successful demonstration into diverse successful trajectories for new task configurations. This removes the manual transformation rules and task-specific engineering required by prior augmentation methods.

entry.title: Persistent LLM Orchestration of Heterogeneous Robot Teams via Partial Delegation to Multi-Agent Protocols

author.name: Maria G. Mendoza, Victoria M. Tuck, Zachary Ravichandran, Shankar Sastry, George J. Pappas

entry.summary: This work tackles LLM orchestration of robot teams in non-terminating, continuously changing environments such as disaster response, where existing LLM-planning approaches fail due to unbounded prompt growth, degraded reasoning as agents accumulate, and passive monitoring after initial coverage. The authors propose partial delegation of responsibilities to multi-agent protocols to keep the LLM orchestrator effective over long-running missions. It identifies concrete failure modes of LLM orchestration under mission persistence.

entry.title: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support

author.name: Istok Bako, Bonan Min, Tiffany Shao, Claire Cheng, Yashar Mehdad

entry.summary: This deployment case study shows that a portable skill consisting of a natural-language instruction and lightweight components can match complex agentic RAG pipelines for retrieving accurate resolution steps from enterprise policy documents in customer support. It challenges the assumed need for elaborate chunking, indexing, re-ranking, and bespoke retrieval infrastructure.

entry.title: SAGE: Pushing 2-Bit Vector-Quantized LLMs toward Real-World Usability

author.name: Xianglong Yan, Zenan Wu, Kewei Zhang, Kaicheng Yang, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: SAGE improves extreme low-bit weight-only vector quantization of LLMs by protecting sensitive weight channels within jointly encoded vectors and adaptively allocating a fixed bit budget between direction and radius components per weight matrix. It targets making 2-bit quantized models usable on real-world tasks.

entry.title: CESNET-TimeSeries26: A Multi-Year Network Traffic Time Series Dataset for Annual Seasonality, Concept Drift, and Long-Term Anomaly Detection

author.name: Josef Koumar, Karel Hynek, Kamil Jerabek, Pavel Siska

entry.summary: This dataset paper releases CESNET-TimeSeries26, containing 995 days of continuous traffic time series from the CESNET3 network plus a single subnet spanning about 4.5 years, covering 278,466 IP addresses and 285 institutions. It enables long-horizon forecasting, annual seasonality modeling, concept drift analysis, and anomaly detection evaluation that short-lived public datasets cannot support.

entry.title: Understanding Unified VLMs: From Attention Probing to Guidance Tuning for Multimodal Generation

author.name: Zhengyang Luo, Xiaoyu Qiu, Zhiheng Tan, Yuchen Liang, Yingbin Liang, Liyue Shen

entry.summary: Probes every attention head in unified vision-language models to identify heads sensitive to conditional guidance differences between the two classifier-free-guidance branches, finding a characteristic pattern stable across autoregressive and masked-diffusion paradigms and both T2I and I2T generation. The analysis is extended toward guidance tuning for improved multimodal generation.

entry.title: CoverSynth: Coverage-Guided Generation of Retrieval Evaluation Sets

author.name: Anahita Sharma, Apaar Shanker, Rishav Chakravarti, Sneha Srinivasan, Vijay Kalmath, Dylan Wilbur, Yuan Li, Sara Bolouki, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: CoverSynth is a generator that produces retrieval evaluation sets from unannotated corpora, designed for coverage, reliability, efficiency, and discriminability in enterprise agent settings. It also introduces an assessment framework for determining when an evaluation set meets these criteria.

entry.title: FARL: A Fully Automated Pipeline of RL Interface and Solver Design

author.name: Tianyu Jin, Liuyu Xiang, Chaowen Yang, Xingyang Chang, Pei Pei Li, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: FARL automates reinforcement learning pipeline design by jointly searching observation and reward programs, learning algorithms, and training settings, rather than fixing the task formulation by hand. It uses training statistics and observed behavior to diagnose failures, propose changes, and validate improvements. This reduces the human expertise currently required to apply RL to new tasks.

entry.title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts

author.name: Zhaoyu Fan, Bowen Han, Jincheng Ou, Yanwei Ren, Zehua He, Kaiyu Huang, Pengcheng He, Shanshan Ni, Chengchen Gong, Shuai Xue, Qingjiang Shi

entry.summary: ProCARE automates real-world healthcare studies using LLM agents by reformulating the task as constrained compilation, converting implicit clinical semantics like index dates and follow-up windows into profile-grounded evidence contracts. This addresses brittle schema mismatches, temporal errors, and unsupported clinical claims in EHR and claims analyses.

entry.title: Overtaught, Underlearned: Learner-Centered Distillation from Multi-Agent Discussion

author.name: Mengtao Zhou, Jianxiao Wang, Xiupeng Chen, Cailiang Liu, Jie Song

entry.summary: Identifies over-teaching and under-learning mismatches in full-graph distillation from multi-agent discussion graphs, where multiple correct solutions collapse to the same lesson for the student while some questions remain unlearned. It introduces FAR (Fold-Attempt-Revisit), a distillation procedure that organizes supervision around the student's own representations rather than treating each solution as a separate target.

entry.title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation

author.name: Shu Gu, Matthew Youngman, Yuqin Zhao, Cristian Sestito, Ali Siddique, Ramesh Krishnamurthy, Danial Chitnis, Themis Prodromakis

entry.summary: Introduces LATCH, a two-layer framework separating LLM orchestration from deterministic FPGA implementation and evaluation for post-route timing closure. Across sixteen designs and seven LLMs, it compares three agent control granularities, finding a stark reliability trade-off: expert recipes achieve 98.2% functional pass rates versus 17.9% for LLM-constructed procedures, while direct EDA operations yield slightly larger timing gains when they pass.

entry.title: Does a Governed Confidence Score Know When a Text-to-SQL Answer Is Right? An Exploratory Study on BIRD and a Pre-registered Confirmation on Spider

author.name: Raghu Venkat, Tricha Anjali

entry.summary: Audits a production text-to-SQL confidence score on BIRD using GPT-5.1, finding weak discrimination between correct and incorrect answers (AUROC 0.624) and that 35.7% of correct answers are withheld. A pre-registered confirmation on Spider strengthens the methodology.

entry.title: DuplexAct: How Interactive Are Frontier Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models?

author.name: Jiaheng Dong, Shihong Tan, Gongping Huang, Jean Honorio, Abhirup Ghosh, Ting Dang

entry.summary: DuplexAct is a benchmark for evaluating interaction action-taking in end-to-end full-duplex spoken language models, defining a three-level taxonomy of eight interaction actions and 24 conditions. It characterizes successful action-taking through immediate execution and follow-through, with action-specific evaluation, addressing gaps in prior benchmarks that measure action occurrence rather than success.

entry.title: Seeing Depth but Choosing Cues in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhengtao Zou, Pekka Marttinen

entry.summary: Through controlled depth-cue conflicts, representation analysis, and interventions, this paper investigates whether vision-language models use true depth information or image-plane cues like apparent size and vertical position for relative depth judgment. Across model families and scales, judgments shift toward misleading cues, yet correct depth order remains decodable from internal representations even when the model answers incorrectly.

entry.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch

author.name: Peng Jiang (Tsinghua University), Dongyang Li (Tsinghua University), Quanying Liu (Southern University of Science, Technology), Xiaoxuan Jia (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: ResearchFlow-Eval is a fine-grained evaluation framework for autoresearch systems that scores continuous scientific execution at both stage and claim levels, grounded in published anchor papers with stage-specific rubrics. It targets process-level capabilities like multi-stage workflows and experiment revision that existing end-artifact evaluations miss. This helps measure the gap between research plans and actual execution.

entry.title: Configuring RAG Systems: What Breaks, Where Originates, and How to Fix

author.name: Liangyu Chen, Youpeng Ma, Yulong Ye, Zezhen Xiang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study of 654 real-world configuration issues across 10 RAG systems, providing a categorization of symptoms, root causes, affected pipeline stages, and fix patterns. It is the first systematic treatment of configuration-related failures in RAG deployments.

entry.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization

author.name: Trieu Nguyen, Frazier N. Baker, Ruoxi Gao, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Xia Ning

entry.summary: MFG is a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules across multiple rounds using computational or experimental feedback, addressing the gap in single-turn-only prior methods. The task targets multi-objective molecular optimization while preserving structural similarity, a core drug discovery problem.

entry.title: SAGE: Efficient Protected Vision-Language Inference on Smart Glasses

author.name: Zhimin Li, Pan Wang, Jingxian Chen, Yuantao Tang, Qian Lou, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: SAGE is a hardware-aware framework for efficient privacy-preserving vision-language inference on smart glasses, keeping raw images on-device, using shape-specialized INT8 graphs, and compressing protected representations into compact 256-dimensional INT8 packets before transmission. It co-optimizes protection and hardware constraints rather than nominal model size alone.

entry.title: The RNN Homunculus: Learning to Gate Long-Term Memory

author.name: Zeyu Fan, Alexandru-Dragos Manolache, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the gate-learning problem in gated RNNs, showing that GRUs and LSTMs still suffer vanishing gradients when all training samples require long-range memory, since gate values themselves must be learned recurrently. Controlled experiments show that adding short-dependency samples lets gates be learned, after which long-range capability emerges. It refines the standard additive-copy-path explanation of gated recurrence.

entry.title: Compositional Concepts Erasing: Disentangling Object-Style via Domain Manifold Unlearning

author.name: Yang Xiao, Kaiyuan Deng, Gen Li, Zinan Ling, Zhiwen Fan, Xiaolong Ma, Bo Hui

entry.summary: Domain Manifold Unlearning (DMU) addresses object-style combination unlearning in diffusion models, using an EMA-updated feature proxy from intermediate diffusion features to erase compositional concepts without catastrophic forgetting across multiple unlearning requests. It targets illicit content and copyright risks.

entry.title: Prior-Fitted and Frozen Scorers for Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Tillmann Rheude, Roland Eils, Benjamin Wild

entry.summary: The paper replaces handcrafted similarity scorers in multimodal contrastive learning with a Transformer, showing that even a randomly initialized frozen Transformer can outperform strong handcrafted baselines, while jointly optimizing the scorer with encoders is less effective. This challenges assumptions about what scoring functions are needed for contrastive learning beyond two modalities.

entry.title: Framework for an AI-Ready ARPES Community Database

author.name: Zhi-Xun Shen, Jin Gene Wong, Karen Lei, Leon Garcia, Felix Baumberger, Sergey Borisenko, Aaron Bostwick, Ting Cao, Tanny Chavez, Yulin Chen, Monika Choudhary, Andrea Damascelli, Dan Dessau, Thomas P. Devereaux, Sandy A. Ekahana, Alexei Fedorov, Atsushi Fujimori, Yucheng Guo, M. Zahid Hasan, Makoto Hashimoto, Yu He, Philip Hofmann, Zahid Hussain, Harold Y. Hwang, Zhurun Ji, Chunjing Jia, Timur K. Kim, Phil D. C. King, Takeshi Kondo, Alessandra Lanzara, Chun Lin, Donghui Lu, Matteo Michiardi, Sung-Kwan Mo, Brian Moritz, Laurenz Rettig, Eli Rotenberg, Takafumi Sato, Kyle M. Shen, Jonathan A. Sobota, Inna Vishik, Shuolong Yang, Ming Yi, Timothy Zaklama

entry.summary: A perspective from a large collaboration of leading ARPES researchers proposing a community data ecosystem to preserve and organize four decades of Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy measurements into an AI-ready shared database. The authors argue fragmented, publication-centered workflows impede AI-enabled discovery in condensed matter physics.

entry.title: A Sovereign, Indic-First, Reasoning Model

author.name: Sutanshu Saksena Raj, Prasanjith Pasunuti, Parijat Chatterjee, Daksh Maan, Purusharth Malik, Nayanjit Sarkar, Avinash Benki

entry.summary: Gnani-Evon-v3.3-30B-A3B is a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts reasoning model for English and eight Indian languages, built from the Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B checkpoint via in-place vocabulary expansion and continual pretraining at 131K sequence length. The work demonstrates sovereign regional LLM development with substantial improvements in Indian-language fertility and reasoning, instruction following, and tool use.

entry.title: Gen Through the Lens: Camera-Controllable Video Generation via Cross-Coordinate Conditioning Fusion

author.name: Shuai Li, Jinxu Xiang, Xinyuan Li, Hanlei Guo, Xiyang Tan, Alan Zhao, Xiaotong Zhao, Ran Zhang

entry.summary: This work presents a camera-controllable image-to-video generation framework that decomposes control signals across camera, world, and object coordinate spaces, fusing intrinsics, spatial geometry hints, and 3D bounding boxes. The cross-coordinate conditioning enables realistic, physically consistent camera operations guided by a reference image. It improves precision of camera motion control over prior abstract-conditioning approaches.

entry.title: Query Your Way Out: Benchmarking Multi-Turn Knowledge Reasoning through Generalized Puzzle Solving

author.name: Xin Cheng, Junming Yang, Ning Xu

entry.summary: The Active Probing Benchmark (APB) generalizes puzzle-based LLM evaluation by casting concept identification as interactive multi-turn reasoning that combines specialized knowledge with active information-seeking, spanning 960 target concepts across eight domains. It tests whether models can strategically query under partial information rather than solve static puzzles.

entry.title: VisExMEM: Visual Evidence-Based Explainable Multimodal Evaluation Metric

author.name: Subhadeep Roy, Christoph Leiter, Steffen Eger

entry.summary: VisExMEM is a reference-free image-text evaluation metric that decomposes captions into atomic claims, localizes visual evidence, and verifies each claim, averaging claim-level support into a global score. The authors train Qwen3.5-based 4B and 9B models with multi-task SFT and evidence-aware GDPO, achieving top descriptive composite among open-source evaluators across eight benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Incompressible 3D Flows from Sparse Samples: A Set Transformer Approach to Divergence-Free Kernel Fitting

author.name: Ramzi Idoughi, Radouan Boukharfane, Peter Wonka

entry.summary: DFK-Former is a set-to-field transformer that reconstructs divergence-free 3D velocity fields from sparse, noisy, irregularly sampled observations by predicting parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation, guaranteeing incompressibility by construction. Unlike prior kernel methods that fix kernel bases, it learns the kernel itself. This bridges scientific computing and deep learning for fluid reconstruction from limited sensors.

entry.title: Interactive Navigation Beyond Reachability: Benchmark and Agentic Framework

author.name: Delun Li, Xueyao Wei, Rui Chen, Yifei Wang, Junzhi Yu, Wenjie Song, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: The paper formulates interactive navigation where reaching a goal requires environment manipulation (opening doors, revealing hidden objects in containers), unifying connectivity changes and visibility changes with sequential dependencies. It introduces MultINav-Bench, a 3K-episode ObjectGoal benchmark in MolmoSpaces with interaction-necessity annotations, plus an automated task-construction pipeline and agentic evaluation framework. This exposes limitations of current navigation systems that assume static traversability.

entry.title: Thinking Outside the Bots: Human Ideas in AI's Semantic Blind Spots Are Not Inferior

author.name: Kibum Moon, Dan R. Johnson, Kostadin Kushlev, Benjamin Lira, Indre Viskontas, James C. Kaufman, Roger E. Beaty, Angela L. Duckworth, Adam E. Green

entry.summary: Develops EDGE, a method to map AI semantic blind spots by measuring how strongly individual human ideas are represented in a task-matched AI comparison set, across essays, alternative-uses tasks, and interventions. The study finds that human ideas falling outside AI's semantic coverage are not lower quality, countering the concern that human heterogeneity merely reflects noise. This has implications for creativity research and human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching

author.name: Ruchang Yao, Shi Guo, Junhao Zhuang, Mingde Yao, Xin Cai, Jiahao Zhan, Bin Fu, Xinyuan Chen, Yu Qiao, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: FlashVSR+ improves diffusion-distilled video super-resolution with a hybrid attention architecture exploiting locality in pretrained VSR models plus a reward-yield distribution matching training strategy. It achieves up to 2x DiT speedup and 45% lower peak memory, enabling untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090 while better aligning with human preferences.

entry.title: HaloBlock: Faster and Better Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Zhaohui Zheng, Chenhang He, Jinrui Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: HaloBlock improves inference for diffusion language models by addressing two issues: decoding difficulty concentrating on right-side block tokens and boundary contextual discontinuity in block-wise decoding. It uses bidirectional cumulative entropy to measure block difficulty and adaptively allocates halo regions around each block. As dLLMs gain traction as an alternative to autoregressive LLMs, inference improvements here are timely and broadly applicable.

entry.title: Looped Reasoning Finishes Earlier Than You Think

author.name: Sumin Park, T. Konstantin Rusch

entry.summary: The paper analyzes looped reasoning models through the lens of dynamical systems, showing that slowly decaying oscillatory latent modes can bottleneck convergence without clean fixed points. It proposes adding rotational degrees of freedom that separate symmetry-generated rotational motion from reasoning-relevant dynamics, enabling earlier stopping.

entry.title: PRISM: Calibrating Black-Box Judges with Counterfactual Probes

author.name: Kakei Yamamoto, So Kuroki

entry.summary: PRISM calibrates LLM judges by measuring how their scores shift when evaluative attributes are emphasized or de-emphasized while holding content fixed, treating these counterfactual probe responses as a surrogate Jacobian. Ridge regression on human labels then learns a correction to the baseline score, yielding a rubric-free calibration protocol. This addresses systematic disagreement between LLM judges and human judgments.

entry.title: Falsification-proof non-market allocation mechanisms

author.name: Eduardo Perez-Richet, Vasiliki Skreta

entry.summary: This economics-theory paper characterizes optimal falsification-proof allocation rules when resource targeting relies on manipulable agent characteristics, covering broad falsification technologies. The authors show naive optimal rules induce costly falsification and negative externalities, and provide an honesty condition under which their rules solve the planner's unconstrained problem balancing allocative surplus and agent welfare. It is relevant to mechanism design for AI-era allocation systems.

entry.title: SIRNET: Causal Adaptation of Pretrained Embeddings for Semiparametric Treatment-Effect Estimation Under Surrogacy

author.name: Lei Shi, Qiuran Lyu

entry.summary: SIRNET adapts pretrained encoder embeddings of rich post-treatment objects (text, images, video) for causal treatment-effect estimation when outcomes are delayed or partially observed, learning a shared adapter jointly for outcome prediction and the estimation task. The framework addresses the mismatch between generic pretrained representations and the information a causal estimator actually needs. It bridges representation learning and semiparametric causal inference.

entry.title: When Dynamic Scaling Fails: A Scale-State Feedback Governs Recurrent-State Quantization in Linear-Attention and SSM LLMs

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes INT4 quantization of the recurrent state in linear-attention and state-space LLMs, showing that quantizer scale derived from the evolving state creates a feedback loop whose compounding errors destroy long-context recall over thousands of decode steps. Detaching the scale to a full-precision reference eliminates norm explosion but recovers only part of the degradation, revealing separable numerical-instability and resolution-loss failure modes. Practical guidance for long-context deployment of efficient architectures.

entry.title: The Gradient That Top-k Distillation Never Computes

author.name: Rasul Khanbayov, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Proves that top-k truncated distillation with renormalization makes the training objective depend only on log-odds among retained tokens, so the gradient in directions controlling tail mass is exactly zero. It derives the full-vocabulary gradient as truncated gradient plus a tail-mass-weighted residual, exposing a systematic flaw in widely deployed distillation pipelines.

entry.title: Sample-Optimal Multi-Group Learning with an ERM Oracle

author.name: Princewill Okoroafor

entry.summary: The paper resolves whether the optimal sample complexity for multi-group learning can be achieved using only an empirical risk minimization oracle, giving an algorithm with near-optimal sample complexity using polynomially many calls to a weighted ERM oracle. This avoids the infeasible requirement of tracking every group-hypothesis pair in large hypothesis classes.

entry.title: XForecast: The KDD 2026 Finance Day Challenge on News-Grounded Financial Forecasting

author.name: Jaehoon Lee, Jun Seo, Seunghan Lee, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Minjae Kim, Sungdong Yoo, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Soonyoung Lee, Yongjae Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: XForecast introduces a benchmark and competition for news-grounded financial forecasting, requiring prediction of four-week stock price movements using historical prices paired with curated news text. It covers 100 large-cap stocks from 2019-2023 and uses a weighted hit rate metric emphasizing news-relevant instances. The dataset is generated via FinTexTS, a multimodal text-generation method.

entry.title: ECHO: Correcting Time Series Foundation Model Forecasts with Historical Analogues and Errors

author.name: Boya Zhang, Xilin Dai, Yilin Wang, Qiang Xu, Luyao Dong, Xing He, Wen Wu

entry.summary: ECHO is a black-box correction framework for time series foundation model (TSFM) forecasts that combines two complementary signals: historical analogues showing how similar contexts evolved, and past forecast errors revealing a model's characteristic domain-specific deviations. Using only black-box access, ECHO learns from both sources via retrieved analogues assessed against the current context. This enables lightweight domain adaptation without retraining the TSFM.

entry.title: IND-Eval: Aligning Evaluation and Simulation for Industrial Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Vebj{\o}rn Haugland (Cognite), Pavel Gulin (Cognite), David Foss (Cognite), Peet Cremer (Cognite), Erlend Aune (Cognite), Simone Casolo (Cognite), Andreas Solbr{\aa} (Cognite), Milad Mobarhan (Cognite)
