entry.summary: IND-Eval is a public benchmark organizing industrial time series into source-specific forecasting tasks with finer sampling resolutions and more multivariate forecasting than benchmarks like GIFT-Eval. Evaluating Chronos-2, TiRex-2, and TimesFM-3, the authors find TimesFM-3 achieves the best source-balanced aggregate scores and leads in seven of nine sources, motivating domain alignment improvements during pretraining.

entry.title: Sequence Composition in EHR Foundation Model Pretraining

author.name: Joshua Placidi, Inigo Stibbe, Alfred J. Balston, Marek Rei, A. Aldo Faisal

entry.summary: The authors examine how pretraining sequence construction affects autoregressive EHR foundation models, arguing that the common global-stream approach misaligns with downstream clinical tasks by exposing long-sequence patients more and allowing attention across patient boundaries. They propose alternative composition strategies and evaluate their effect on clinical prediction.

entry.title: Which Geometry on Which Layer? Measured Sign-Spectral Assignment in Mixed-Optimizer Training

author.name: Hiroki Naganuma, Laura Gomezjurado, Mahdi Ghaznavi, Ganesh Talluri, Atsushi Nitanda, Seng Pei Liew, Ryuichiro Hataya, Ioannis Mitliagkas

entry.summary: The paper turns the heuristic choice between AdamW/sign-based updates and spectral updates per layer into a measurable layerwise decision problem, deriving finite-batch descent-lemma ratio bounds that separate signal efficiency from geometry-dependent curvature. It provides two-sided bounds determining which update gives the larger expected loss decrease. This gives principled grounding to mixed-optimizer recipes now common in LLM pretraining.

entry.title: JustOPD: On-Policy Distillation from Autoregressive to Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zikun Zhang, Jiayuan Sheng, David D. Yao, Wenpin Tang

entry.summary: JustOPD addresses on-policy distillation from autoregressive teacher models into diffusion language model students, resolving the mismatch between left-to-right AR decoding and the flexible decoding order of DLMs. Existing work mostly covered DLM-to-DLM distillation, and the lack of strong teacher DLMs complicates matters. This is a step toward making diffusion LLMs benefit from AR model quality.

entry.title: DisaggKD: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Teacher-Student Disaggregation and a Fused Loss

author.name: Ruixuan Tu, Yuyang Dong

entry.summary: DisaggKD decouples knowledge distillation across nodes, streaming teacher hidden states to the student with a fused loss that equals the full-vocabulary KD loss exactly without materializing full-vocabulary logits, plus a prefetch ring to pace producer and trainer. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B distillation pair, the disaggregated layout matches colocated LM loss while being faster, and the fused loss enables colocated runs on fewer nodes. This addresses a real memory bottleneck in distilling large LLMs.

entry.title: Recalibrating Many Questions with Few Labels: Minimax Rates and Identification Limits

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Chiwun Yang

entry.summary: The authors derive minimax rates for recalibrating probabilistic predictors across many related yes/no questions when only few labels exist per question, with identification limits over a nondecreasing shape class. The theory is motivated by decision models that output probabilities for arbitrary developer-written questions, making it relevant to modern calibration of LLM-style probability outputs.

entry.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuqi Huang, Xingyao Li, Yunlong Hou, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiachun Pan, Vincent Y. F. Tan

entry.summary: SP2ec is a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation for self-speculative decoding in vision-language models, exploiting a single-peak throughput pattern shared by methods like SWIFT, KnapSpec, and SpecVLM. It addresses the difficulty small trained drafters have with multimodal inputs by reusing parts of the target model.

entry.title: Disease-level drug approval forecasting from trial-agnostic public data

author.name: Samir Townsley, Pagkratios Tagkopoulos, Ilias Tagkopoulos

entry.summary: The authors build a model forecasting FDA approval for drug-disease pairs using only pre-clinical, trial-agnostic public data, with a cohort of 14,134 drug-disease pairs reconstructed from public sources. The work aims to reduce drug development time and cost by prioritizing which diseases to target for a given drug.

entry.title: What a Data Release Must Preserve for Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Kyungbok Lee, Yating Zou, Michael R. Kosorok

entry.summary: Characterizes exactly which distinctions a coarsened data release must preserve for off-policy evaluation to remain identifiable: identification holds if and only if action-specific evaluation weights are constant within each released record. The paper further derives the sharp bound on evaluation uncertainty induced by a release and frames release coarsening as a design optimization problem.

entry.title: AlphaPilot: Multi-Turn Tool-Using LLM Agents for Adaptive Alpha Mining with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Peiqi Jiang, Fan Zhang, Xin Xu, Tianhao Chen, Can Yang

entry.summary: Introduces AlphaPilot, a reinforcement learning framework training multi-turn tool-using LLM agents for formulaic alpha mining in quantitative finance: the agent reads market descriptions, proposes factor expressions, queries real-data evaluator feedback, and maintains a factor pool across turns. This jointly exploits market text, LLM financial knowledge, and empirical evaluation.

entry.title: Frequency-Step Cache: Separating Synchronization and Repair for Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion

author.name: Kerry Xu, Param Misra, Zachary Stenglein, Athri Karunamurthy, Fanjiang Ye, Yuke Wang

entry.summary: Frequency-Step Cache (FSC) is a training-free caching method for autoregressive video diffusion that decouples when to exactly synchronize the cache from how much computation to repair between anchors, using a frequency-resolved latent drift risk to choose whole-step replay, selective token recomputation, or full repair. Experiments on SkyReels-V2 show substantial compute savings from whole-step reuse.

entry.title: Small area learning

author.name: Katarzyna Reluga, Nicola Salvati, Setareh Ranjbar, Nikos Tzavidis, Mark van der Laan

entry.summary: The paper introduces small area learning (SAL), a learner-agnostic framework casting small area estimation as multi-target semi-supervised learning where outcome prediction is a nuisance task, allowing unrestricted covariate shift and structured conditional shift across areas. The authors establish consistency and asymptotic normality with variance estimators and confidence intervals for area means.

entry.title: Learning, Compression, and Meta-Complexity

author.name: Halley Goldberg, Mikito Nanashima, Igor C. Oliveira

entry.summary: This survey makes precise the long-standing intuition that learning is tied to compression, reviewing formal connections among learning algorithms, data compression, and computational complexity theory with emphasis on meta-complexity. It covers how complexity techniques guide algorithm design and how learning algorithms yield new complexity results.

entry.title: In-context classification: Calibration and noise in linear attention with softmax readout

author.name: Arman Rysmakhanov, Mary Letey, Yue M. Lu, Jacob Zavatone-Veth, Cengiz Pehlevan

entry.summary: Derives asymptotic predictions for in-context binary classification in a linear attention model with softmax readout trained on logistic loss, in a high-dimensional regime. The formula cleanly separates calibration, context noise, and parameter-estimation noise, and identifies the ridgeless separability regime.

entry.title: Risk-Averse Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment with Finite-Sample Guarantees

author.name: Yuchen Liang, Xian Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a risk-averse framework for inference-time alignment of diffusion models that balances expected cost and Conditional Value-at-Risk under trajectory-level KL regularization, characterizing the optimal path distribution as a function of the CVaR threshold. The alignment problem reduces to a one-dimensional (generally nonconvex) optimization, for which the authors establish sufficient conditions and finite-sample guarantees. This brings explicit tail-risk control to diffusion alignment without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Distance Prediction for Quantum Codes

author.name: Nadav Schneider, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: This paper addresses the computationally hard problem of estimating the distance of quantum low-density parity-check codes, focusing on Bivariate Bicycle codes relevant to fault-tolerant quantum computing. The authors build a dataset of distance upper bounds and train BB-Net, an attention-based network that predicts distances where exact solvers and search heuristics bottleneck.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs as Agentic Workflow Executors in Real-World Customer Support Skills

author.name: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Gundeep Singh, Xue-Yong Fu, Karol Chang, Kevin Sanders, Shi Zong, Tania Habib, Julien Bouvier Tremblay, Shayna Gardiner, Harsh Saini, Matthias Lee, Elena Khasanova, Quinten McNamara, Shashi Bhushan TN

entry.summary: The authors present a benchmark construction pipeline that mines real customer-support transcripts into structured skill workflows with MCP-compatible mocked environments and multi-turn tool-using dialogues, then evaluates 17 closed and open LLMs zero-shot as bounded skill executors. The work grounds agentic evaluation in genuine enterprise workflows.

entry.title: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xinhao Wang, Junbo Cui, Zhenghao Liu, Yuan Yao, Xiaohua Li, Yu Gu, Ge Yu

entry.summary: This work identifies a new vision-language model failure mode called Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination, where a model anchored to visually confusable evidence accepts a false textual premise and then describes a visually plausible but absent object. The authors build PVFH-Bench, inspired by cognitive science on perceptual bias, to systematically measure this phenomenon. It extends the object hallucination literature by connecting textual premise acceptance with visual anchoring errors.

entry.title: Feedback as an Interface: Controlling Form and Detail in LLM Translation Refinement

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Flavjo Tomori, Nafise Sadat Moosavi, Steffen Eger, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a controlled machine translation protocol that fixes evaluator content while varying the form and detail of feedback given to LLMs during translation refinement. Across seven models and six language directions, low-load feedback consistently outperforms high-load feedback under xCOMET evaluation.

entry.title: Evaluating Temporal Reasoning in Large Language Models: Event Temporal Relation Extraction with Allen's Interval Algebra, Logical Consistency, and Relative Time in Narratives

author.name: Adib Sakhawat, Fardeen Sadab, Tamjid Hasan Fahim, Multazam Mahmud, Tahsan Ferdous Lihan, Md Isfak Iqbal Chowdhury, Nafis Ahnaf Jamil, Md. Atik Shahriar, Sieam Shahriare, Wasi Omar Syed, M Safwan Hasan Khan, Tabib Hassan

entry.summary: Five LLMs are asked to reconstruct full networks of Allen's 13 interval relations over 360 narratives, evaluated with a pre-registered protocol for agreement, converse consistency, and logical satisfiability. No model beats the trivial always-answer-before baseline under the strict parser, exposing that headline accuracy is inflated by label skew.

entry.title: Batch-Paced: Fixed-Budget Batch Decoding in Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Shuai Zhang, Zhanchao Zhou, Huachuan Qiu, Anqi Li, Zhenzhong Lan

entry.summary: Batch-Paced formulates fixed-budget batch decoding for discrete diffusion language models and introduces a training-free method that reallocates decoding compute across requests to maximize overall batch quality. Experiments across two dLLM backbones and five benchmarks show consistent gains under matched budgets, with benefits growing with batch size. This addresses a real serving-level gap, since prior dLLM decoding work optimized single sequences.

entry.title: From Hindsight to Foresight: Dissecting Clinical Evidence Acquisition in Large Language Models

author.name: Ziyang Ling

entry.summary: This work dissects why LLMs that diagnose static clinical cases well fail at dynamic diagnosis requiring evidence acquisition over time. It introduces a hindsight-style analysis tracing failures through evidence identification, utilization, and diagnostic updating, using metrics beyond accuracy such as evidence coverage, trajectory dynamics, and information entropy. The framework aims to explain breakdowns rather than just measure them.

entry.title: Jev-Guard: Fast Routing and Auditing Agent Actions over Editable Policy Trees

author.name: Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Haochen Shi, Yuxuan Liu, Changxuan Fan, Sirui Zhang, Kawai Chung, Hanyu Yang, Zhenhuan Wang, Ziyi Chen, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Presents Jev-Guard, a unified model for low-latency safety classification and policy routing of agent actions, using an editable policy tree spanning content moderation, cybersecurity, privacy, and legal compliance. It navigates the tree to select the applicable audit policy and then classifies conditioned on that policy.

entry.title: Attribute-Centric Vision-Language Alignment for Fine-Grained Gait Understanding

author.name: Saihui Hou, Chenye Wang, Wenpeng Lang, Qiannan Guo, Zhengxiang Lan, Chao Fan, Shiqi Yu, Yongzhen Huang

entry.summary: The authors release RA-GAR, a large multimodal benchmark for gait attribute recognition with 1,001 subjects, 242,729 walking sequences, and annotations for 15 static and motion attributes. They also propose vision-language alignment that matches visual evidence directly to textual class representations instead of classifier output weights.

entry.title: CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection

author.name: Pratham Gupta, Haotian Qi, Tushar Sandhan, Gabriel Skantze

entry.summary: CAST-ASD is a causal joint model for active speaker detection that combines scene-level attention across faces in the current frame with causal temporal attention over each face history, achieving joint reasoning with zero lookahead. Its parameter count does not grow with the number of faces and it performs strongly on MSDWild.

entry.title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling

author.name: Xinge Peng, Zhen Fang, Ruibing Wang, Yongxuan Lv, Haodong Li, Guohui Zhang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Yiting Lu, Lin Chen, Zehui Che, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: ExeWorldBench benchmarks executable world modeling, evaluating whether coding agents can both understand the structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world and realize them in code whose behavior emerges from physical interaction. It fills a gap left by fragmented benchmarks focused only on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness.

entry.title: Structured Stateful Relational Scripts with a High-Quality Dataset for Multi-Shot Audio-Visual Video Generation

author.name: Chen Zhao, Lehan Shen, Qilong Huang, Hongyu Li, Zhuoliang Kang, Xiaoming Wei, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: SSRS is a structured textual supervision representation for multi-shot audio-visual video generation that separates persistent entity and voice identities from shot-specific states, encodes sound-source bindings and temporal relations, and links local actions via a global audio-visual event sequence. The paper also contributes a high-quality dataset.

entry.title: When Trackers Fail: VLM-Guided Verification and Recovery for Robust Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Valay Bundele, Susmit Agrawal, Mehran Hosseinzadeh, The Nam Nguyen, Hendrik P. A. Lensch

entry.summary: Dual-Agent is a failure-aware video object segmentation framework that adds explicit verification and recovery on top of SAM-based trackers, using a VLM to detect when propagated masks have drifted due to occlusion, reappearance, or distractors. This addresses the core weakness that incorrect predictions entering the memory loop propagate indefinitely.

entry.title: Learning Temporal Evidence Selection for Video Anomaly Understanding

author.name: Hangil Park, Seungheon Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: Reframes temporal sampling in video anomaly understanding as a downstream-aligned evidence selection problem, introducing a semantic-conditioned Temporal Sampling Q-Former that selects visual evidence supporting language-level explanations. This overcomes anomaly-centric or predefined sampling strategies that miss contextual cues and temporally distributed evidence.

entry.title: GHOST: Geometry-Constrained Hybrid Diffusion for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Changqun Feng, Wangxiandi Yin, Xin Hu, Ruiting Dai, Feiyang Yang, Jielei Wang, Tao He

entry.summary: GHOST jointly models continuous node geometry and discrete edge predicates in 3D scene graph generation via a hybrid diffusion process that denoises geometry to constraints to predicates, ensuring geometrically consistent open-vocabulary relation prediction. Language-grounded constraint induction maps predicate embeddings to differentiable geometric constraints guiding layout refinement.

entry.title: MHVF: Training-Free GUI Grounding via Verification-Guided Multi-Hypothesis Search

author.name: Minghua Chen, Xingming Liao, Weiqiang Zhong, Zhuowei Wang

entry.summary: MHVF is a training-free GUI grounding method that generates multiple spatial hypotheses from full-screen predictions and resolves ambiguity via zoomed local verification with a single pretrained vision-language model. It targets failure cases where dense, visually similar interface elements mislead single-prediction approaches.

entry.title: Flow-Support-Weighted Proposals for Test-Time Verified VLA Policies

author.name: Chen Zhao, Zipeng Ye, Haitao Shen, Guanlin Li, Yuchen Xie, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper identifies proposal contraction in flow-matching VLA decoders: fine-tuning concentrates sampled actions around one dominant mode, making test-time scaling ineffective since candidates become near-duplicates. The proposed Action Dynamic Sampling injects additional action candidates during training to maintain proposal diversity for verifier-based selection. The diagnosis of this test-time scaling bottleneck is a valuable conceptual contribution for VLA inference.

entry.title: Observation-Referenced Tissue Deformation Forecasting with Tool-Driven and Residual Dynamics

author.name: Tom Olesch, Nan Xiao, Xiongye Xiao, Jonathan C. DeLong, Fei Liu

entry.summary: The authors study forecasting tissue deformation from future surgical instrument motion using a scene-specific differentiable surface model, anchoring predictions to the last valid observation plus only the deformation induced by the planned tool trajectory. This observation-referenced formulation reduces sensitivity to reconstruction and initialization errors, supporting predictive planning for increasingly autonomous surgery.

entry.title: Test-Time Compute for Humanoid Behavior Foundation Models

author.name: Weiji Xie, Junsong Wu, Zibo Zhou, Yueru Chen, Xingyi Wang, Zhenhua Xiong, Weinan Zhang, Chenjia Bai

entry.summary: The paper shows that test-time compute can close the systematic command-execution gap in Humanoid Behavior Foundation Models without retraining. Test-Time Command Optimization adapts input commands via sampling-based optimization through closed-loop simulation of the BFM and robot dynamics, reducing mean global body-position error across three BFMs on AMASS. This improves whole-body accuracy needed for downstream loco-manipulation.

entry.title: Phase-Gated Constrained Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Capture and Detumbling of Non-Cooperative Targets

author.name: \'Alvaro Belmonte-Baeza, Celia Redondo-Verd\'u, Jos\'e L. Ram\'on, Miguel Cazorla, Leonard Felicetti, Jorge Pomares

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate that a single constrained RL policy can perform an entire active debris removal mission — free-space closing, fixture-free friction capture, and detumbling of an object with unknown inertia under noisy state estimates — replacing fragile phase-specific controller pipelines. A smooth phase-gating mechanism handles the contact-rich seam that conventional hand-designed switches handle poorly.

entry.title: FlowVLA: Enabling World Dynamics Understanding through Pluggable 3D Flow Learning

author.name: Junhyeong Go, Mingyu Jung, Woobin Im, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: FlowVLA is a reconstruction-guided, pluggable 3D flow learning framework that gives VLA models an understanding of action-relevant 3D dynamics without requiring 3D sensor inputs or inference-time architectural changes. It leverages temporally consistent 3D motion extraction from RGB to move beyond static 2D image-text priors that limit manipulation robustness. The pluggable design makes it applicable to existing VLA models.

entry.title: SHOES: Sim-to-real Hardware-adaptation via On-policy Expansion of Skills for Legged Robots

author.name: Kota Tsuruhara, Tsung-Yuan Chen, Kento Kawaharazuka

entry.summary: SHOES adapts quadruped/legged locomotion policies to footwear-induced morphology changes (altered foot geometry, mass, friction) by freezing a simulation-trained nominal policy and fine-tuning only lightweight identity-initialized modulation modules directly on the hardware. Inspired by how humans use shoes to change their ground-contact interface, the approach preserves the original gait while enabling sample-efficient on-robot adaptation. A supporting dataset/environment suite appears to be introduced alongside the method.

entry.title: Mobility-Budget-Constrained Submodular Maximization for Distributed Semantic Multi-Robot Exploration

author.name: Changxuan Yao, Sandilya Sai Garimella, Lu Gan, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: This work presents a distributed multi-robot semantic exploration framework combining Dirichlet mapping, budget-constrained trajectory selection, and resource-aware greedy coordination, where each robot selects paths by marginal information gain measured as expected Dirichlet entropy reduction. The framework offers a theoretical guarantee that joint per-round information gain is at least half the centralized optimum, degrading gracefully under limited communication.

entry.title: ForeTac: Predictive Contact Guidance for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Zhiyuan Chen, Shuai Chen, Haoran Zhou, Yizhe Zhao, Kaiyuan Yang, Zhixiang Duan, Shaoqing Xu, Ran Cao, Diyun Xiang, Yangwei You

entry.summary: ForeTac is a predictive contact-guidance framework for contact-rich manipulation organized as a represent-predict-evaluate-guide loop: it encodes tactile state, predicts tactile consequences of candidate action sequences, evaluates them with a contact-quality objective learned from successful and failed physical interactions, and guides generative policies via gradient propagation before execution.

entry.title: Benchmarking Interaction-Oriented Aerial Mobility across Heterogeneous Environments

author.name: Zhibo Duan, Hanlin Kong, Tianran Ma, Yuze Wu, Yuxuan Xu, Kenghou Hoi, Changheng Xie, Xin Zhou, Jianzhe Gao, Fei Gao, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: This work introduces CrossFly, a benchmark for long-horizon interaction-oriented aerial mobility containing 15K trajectories across more than 20 reconstructed scenes. It uniquely evaluates continuous indoor-outdoor transitions and the handoff from navigation to physical interaction, where prior aerial benchmarks initialized agents near targets and tested isolated stages.

entry.title: EqC: Equilibrium Energy Control for Introspective Lifelong Robot Learning

author.name: Haodong Yang, Runhan Huang, Bowen Zhang, Iofai Lei, Zunzhe Zhang, Xiangcheng Zhang, Shaoting Zhu, Linzhan Mou, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: EqC casts generative action refinement as equilibrium-seeking optimization on an explicit conditional energy landscape, where the geometry of refinement reveals whether generated behavior remains consistent with what the policy has learned. This competence signal enables Energy-Gated DAgger, in which persistent energy-consistency violations trigger expert takeover and recovery trajectories are aggregated for policy updates.

entry.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-improving Coding Agents for Physical Intelligence

author.name: Wenyi Li, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Chunyu Liu, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Zheng Jiang, Deyao Hong, Calvin Xiao, Kaisen Yang, Qinhuai Na

entry.summary: EmbodiedEvo extends the SWE-agent style self-improvement loop from digital environments to physical robot tasks, using code as both policy representation and the workspace where the agent inspects state, revises and executes code, and learns from feedback. The paper argues code is a more explicit and reusable control representation than direct VLA mappings. It addresses recurring failure patterns in physical execution that limit naive porting of agentic coding loops.

entry.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions

author.name: Sylvain Dehayem Kenfouo, Aaron Zweig, Mingxuan Zhang, Elham Azizi

entry.summary: The authors propose a training-free method for increasing diversity in conditional diffusion sampling by exploiting local pullback geometry to find directions of maximal output sensitivity in the conditioning-embedding space. Steering trajectories along these directions yields distinct generations without degrading prompt alignment or image quality.

entry.title: Counterfactual Regret for Reflective Agents with Lean-Verified Guarantees

author.name: Zhongnian Li, Shi Xu, Mengting Xu, Peng Ying, Xinzheng Xu

entry.summary: This theory paper derives sufficient conditions under which reflective language agents that reuse feedback and memory without weight updates achieve sublinear counterfactual regret over long horizons under resource constraints. The formal results are machine-checked with Lean, providing verified guarantees that local reflection yields long-term performance bounds.

entry.title: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching

author.name: Bui Van Hung, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Dang Thanh Vu, Soo-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: MultiFlow reframes fMRI encoding as generative distribution prediction using Conditional Flow Matching, with a stimulus-informed source distribution that shortens the expected transport path. It uses a Diffusion Transformer backbone and captures response variability that deterministic regression cannot.

entry.title: ADAPT: Audio-Depth Action Planning with Transition-Aware Rewards for Lights-Out Industrial Navigation

author.name: Wenjun Huang, Shenghao Fu, Yian Jin, Yang Ni, Yifan Li, Lichi Li, Xingjian Diao, Pengfei Zhang, Yutong Song, Hanning Chen, Jiarui Cui, Tianyu Yang, Shilong Li, Yu Kong, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: ADAPT addresses navigation in lights-out industrial environments without visible illumination, using spatial audio for target localization and depth for obstacle-aware geometry, evaluated on a new benchmark (DarkNav-Bench) with 24 scenes and four acoustic conditions. Its RL contribution, transition-aware reward shaping (TARS), provides pose-aware shaping for closed-loop navigation. This expands embodied navigation beyond RGB assumptions into a realistic industrial setting.

entry.title: Handoff Curves: Initial Selection, Later Handoff, and Supervision Targets in Multi-turn LLM Routing

author.name: Daniel Matos, Lu Liu, Yanfeng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies multi-turn LLM routing, comparing initial model selection against later handoff between models using handoff curves that trace success and cost as the handoff step varies. Using 34,204 executions of Qwen models on BFCL, MultiWOZ, and tau-retail, the authors find that later handoff often fails to beat well-chosen initial selection and can increase cost, while supervision targets matter for router training.

entry.title: Learning to GUIDE the Group: Self-Learning LLM Facilitation Across Multi-Party Tasks

author.name: Ziyi Liu, Tzu-Sheng Kuo, Jiale Liu, Deqing Fu, Nithum Thain, Crystal Qian

entry.summary: GUIDE is a framework for generalized LLM-based group facilitation that adapts to different multi-party tasks and group dynamics, evaluating interventions on both objective task outcomes and subjective measures like psychological safety and perceived friction. It moves beyond task-specific fine-tuning toward self-learning facilitators.

entry.title: Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning via Confidence-Guided Adaptive Debate

author.name: Seungdong Yoa, Ye Seul Sim, Suhee Yoon, Sanghyu Yoon, Dongmin Kim, Soonyoung Lee, Bumsoo Kim, Junhyun Lee

entry.summary: Proposes LASE, a leader-centric multi-agent debate framework that engages interaction only in non-neutral regimes, guided by confidence and reconciling theory suggesting debate is regime-dependent with practice. It uses an asymmetric leader-supporter architecture enabling directed information flow to improve efficiency over symmetric debate.

entry.title: Does a Hosted Decision Model Respect Irrelevant Alternatives? A Pre-Registered Test of Option-Set Dependence in Jev

author.name: Dushyant Rajput (AltSlate Labs LLP), Nirdesh Chauhan (AltSlate Labs LLP), Siddharth Kosaraju (AltSlate Labs LLP)

entry.summary: This pre-registered study tests whether a hosted decision model, jev-1.13.0, satisfies independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA), a rationality axiom required if option probabilities are treated as stable properties of the options. Across roughly 300,000 API calls on intent and topic classification benchmarks, the authors find every added distractor option systematically shifts the log-odds between the correct label and its strongest rival by 0.20-0.52 nats, exceeding run-to-run variation by 1.2-3x. The result matters because it empirically undermines a common practice in which decision-API probabilities are interpreted as intrinsic, option-set-independent measures.

entry.title: Acceptable Misalignment

author.name: Maud van Lier, Ludovica Marinucci, Vieri Giuliano Santucci, Raja Chatila, St\'ephane Doncieux, \'Emiland Garrab\'e, Richard Duro

entry.summary: Argues that full value alignment of open-ended learning autonomous robots is both theoretically and practically impossible given design-time unknowns about deployment, learning, and behavior. The paper proposes the notion of acceptable misalignment, reframing how designers of ethically sound open-ended learning systems should reason about residual divergence from human values.

entry.title: Understanding Personalization Gains in Whisper

author.name: Sergei Katkov, Antonio Liotta

entry.summary: Studies when LoRA-based adaptation improves Whisper-style speech recognition, comparing pooled versus group-specific adapters on Common Voice, LibriSpeech, and VoxPopuli. Findings show adaptation gains are condition-dependent and that pooled LoRA often matches or beats group-specific adapters.

entry.title: An FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Network for Spatiotemporal Pattern Learning and Classification

author.name: Jingang Jin, Yue Ma, Zhenhang Zhang, Qinru Qiu

entry.summary: The authors implement multilayer spiking neural networks on FPGA hardware where both inference and on-device training run on the same chip, targeting energy-efficient edge applications. The design uses a temporal-forward-only training algorithm that avoids the memory and latency costs of backpropagation through time, combined with mixed precision and hardware-level hazard resolution. This is relevant work for neuromorphic-style edge AI where cloud connectivity and power budgets are constrained.

entry.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control

author.name: Binghan Wu, Kai Zeng, Kai Yang, Ya-Qin Zhang, Joseph Sifakis, Ye Ouyang

entry.summary: RAN-JEPA is an action-conditioned world model for radio access network control that separates representation learning from intervention learning: it first learns predictive latents from abundant observation-only telemetry, adapts them to the deployment domain, then learns action-conditioned dynamics from scarce controlled sleep/wake trajectories. The design directly targets the observation-intervention asymmetry that plagues practical world models for network control, with an energy-efficiency application.

entry.title: Stable Token-level Scheduling for Serverless LLM Inference

author.name: Hardi Ashishbhai Desai, Balaji N K, Sourav Kanti Addya

entry.summary: This paper proposes Token Window Pacing (TWP), a closed-loop scheduling framework for serverless LLM inference that uses runtime feedback on inter-token latency (ITL) and queue depth to control when new requests are admitted. Unlike prior work focused on time to first token, TWP protects ongoing decode stages from disruption by computation-intensive prefill work, improving user-perceived latency.

entry.title: Monitoring latent reasoning in looped language models

author.name: Pawel Olszowiec, Paulina Tomaszewska, Maciej \.Zelaszczyk, Michal Byra, Neo Christopher Chung

entry.summary: The paper presents a mechanistic interpretability inspection protocol with five lenses applied to eight looped language models from four families, distinguishing carry loops from re-reading architectures. It examines whether iterative layer reuse actually improves capabilities and whether models remain stable under prompt perturbation. Looped LMs promise extra latent computation without additional storage, but analysis of their internals has been limited.

entry.title: Efficient Safety Guardrails through Latent Dual-Hypothesis Reasoning with On-Demand Trace Reconstruction

author.name: Md Asiful Islam, Fahmida Alam, Mihai Surdeanu

entry.summary: LR-Guard is an efficient, explainable safety guardrail that distills a frozen teacher's analysis of safe and unsafe prompt interpretations into compact latent representations, jointly optimized for safety prediction and on-demand reconstruction of explicit reasoning traces. It avoids the inference overhead of reasoning-based guardrails while retaining human-readable explanations. This tackles the latency-cost tradeoff in LLM safety filtering.

entry.title: Choosing LLMs for Strategic Agent Interactions

author.name: Arastun Mammadli, Herbert Woisetschl\"ager, Jawad Fayaz, Shiqiang Wang

entry.summary: This paper defines strategic model selection as a meta-game layered on top of base game-theoretic interactions, where a selector fields an LLM from a portfolio against an unknown, potentially adaptive opponent. It bridges game-theoretic LLM benchmarks and quality-cost LLM routing, arguing routers currently ignore strategic structure.

entry.title: Unlocking Token Rewards via Training-Free Reward Attribution

author.name: Sitong Wu, Haoru Tan, Bin Xia, Xichen Zhang, Jingyao Li, Shaofeng Zhang, Xiaojuan Qi, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free method to extract token-level reward signals from an existing process reward model by attributing the overall reward to individual tokens. It uses a first-order Taylor approximation to make the influence estimation computationally efficient, avoiding N forward passes for an N-token sequence.

entry.title: Barycentric Anchored Weight Search for Robust Model Merging

author.name: Antoni Buades, Jose-Luis Lisani

entry.summary: The paper proposes Barycentric Anchored Search, a derivative-free post-hoc weight-space procedure that searches along barycentric candidate directions connecting fine-tuned checkpoints to a pre-trained model to improve OOD robustness without gradient training or extra inference cost. Selected models show improved robustness-accuracy trade-offs on OOD benchmarks while retaining ImageNet accuracy.

entry.title: Embodied Zero-Shot Task Planning via Hardware-Aware LLM-VLM Integration for Grounded Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Lonnie Tankersley, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Soroush Korivand

entry.summary: This paper presents a hardware-aware LLM-VLM framework for zero-shot robotic manipulation on a simulated Franka Research 3 robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. It separates symbolic planning (API-hosted LLM) from metric execution, using a local Qwen3-VL 8B verifier to ground plans in workspace geometry, reachability, and grasp feasibility. The work addresses the gap between plausible language-generated plans and physically executable robot actions.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Auctions for Multi-Winner Banner Ads

author.name: Lilian Sun, Henry Huang, Fucheng Warren Zhu, Giannis Daras, Constantinos Daskalakis

entry.summary: This paper proposes a new auction mechanism where multiple bidders can co-influence a single banner ad image generated by a diffusion model, with bids tied to alignment between the generated image and each bidder's textual description. The mechanism drives the reverse diffusion process with a score combining bids and descriptions.

entry.title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos

author.name: Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li, Siyao Xiao, Runqing Cheng, Xiao Lin, Zhifang Liu, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: DexCast learns dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D human videos using joint hand-object interaction reconstruction, eliminating the need for teleoperated demonstrations. A DexHand Motion Perception Module captures inter-joint dynamics and temporal context for future action generation.

entry.title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Tejas Vaidhya, Gaurav Sahu, Irina Rish

entry.summary: Tab-Loop replaces the 12 untied in-context learning blocks of TabICLv2 with 4 tied blocks applied k times, keeping everything else identical, and matches the untied baseline at matched pretraining and inference compute with 62 percent fewer parameters (10.4M vs 27.6M). The result suggests the ICL stage of tabular foundation models needs depth rather than independently parameterized layers.

entry.title: VLCQ: Post-training quantization for deep neural networks using variable length coding

author.name: Reem Abdel-Salam, Ahmed H. Abdel-Gawad, Amr G. Wassal

entry.summary: VLCQ is a post-training quantization method that relaxes the fixed-point encoding constraint by using variable-length encoding, enabling compression below INT8 without the usual severe performance degradation. It targets efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices without requiring retraining or original data access.

entry.title: BridgeCodec: Mamba Enhanced Neural Audio Codec with Schr\"odinger Bridge at Low Bitrate

author.name: Zijian Lin, Jing Yang, Jinghao Luo, Zhuo Wang, Fan Fan, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces BridgeCodec, a framework that decouples the rigidly co-trained encoder-decoder pairs of neural audio codecs by translating latent representations between mismatched, frozen endpoints. It frames this cross-codec translation as a Schrödinger Bridge optimal transport problem and uses a Mamba-enhanced U-Net to capture long-range temporal dependencies in speech. The approach is validated on an extreme scenario mapping a lightweight 8 kHz source encoder to a 48 kHz target, addressing interoperability across codec ecosystems.

entry.title: CacheLink: Functional KV Transport for Zero-Prefill Cross-Model Context Handoff

author.name: Haomiao Qiu, Yining Tang, Zijia Song, Ruizi Han, Ziyue Qiao, Miao Zhang

entry.summary: CacheLink tackles zero-prefill cross-model context handoff: translating a sender model's KV cache into a receiver-compatible state so the receiver continues without re-prefilling. Key insight is that reconstruction fidelity is a poor proxy for downstream utility, since similar KV reconstruction errors can produce very different attention patterns and accuracy, motivating a functional (utility-oriented) transport objective.

entry.title: Towards a Benchmark for Fire Safety Code Interpretation in the Hong Kong AEC Industry

author.name: Le Qiu, Zhuan Anne Zhang, Hok Ming Adeline Chan, Emmanuele Chersoni

entry.summary: This work builds an expert-curated benchmark of multiple-choice and open-ended questions on Hong Kong fire safety codes and evaluates 12 proprietary and open-source LLMs. Top proprietary models score 80-90% on MCQs but only 50-70% on expert-assessed open-ended answers, showing limited reliability for regulatory compliance in architecture, engineering, and construction.

entry.title: Rescuing Points Trapped Inside Incorrect Decision Regions: A target for Evaluating and Improving Forward-Forward Learning

author.name: Alireza Rahmansetayesh, Amirhossein Yousefiramandi, Maxwell Spiridonov, Sumit Raut, Kent Ziti, Pierre Baldi

entry.summary: This work critiques Forward-Forward learning evaluation, showing that linear-probe accuracy can over-credit training since untrained networks already achieve above-chance probe accuracy. It introduces the Boundary Proximity Index methodology to identify which datapoints learning actually rescues from incorrect decision regions.

entry.title: Few-for-Many Best-Arm Identification in Multi-Objective Bandits

author.name: Bo Xue, Yilu Liu, Haodong Jing, Hongzong Li, Xi Lin, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: This theory paper introduces few-for-many best-arm identification in multi-objective bandits: selecting a small arm set minimizing worst weighted degradation from objective-wise optima, under both known and latent objective groups. It proposes GFM-Elim and AFM-Elim with instance-dependent sample-complexity guarantees and proves an asymptotically attainable lower bound for the latent-group Gaussian case. It matters for deployment settings where systems serve many objectives but can only release a few options.

entry.title: The Value of Being Wrong: Self-Mined Visual In-Context Learning from Errors

author.name: Shu Zhao, Tan Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces SMILE, a method for visual in-context learning in vision-language models that builds demonstration pools from the model's own prediction errors, treating failures as natural counterfactual examples encoding failure modes. This simplifies prior multi-stage counterfactual selection pipelines requiring attribute extraction and caption engineering. It matters because it offers a cheaper, model-specific route to better test-time adaptation for VLMs.

entry.title: Phase-Conditioned Affordance Fields for SE(3)-Equivariant Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Xinzhe Chen, Liqi Huang, Sihua Ren, Haowen Sun, Mingyang Li, Zeyang Liu, Xingyu Chen, Xuguang Lan

entry.summary: Proposes phase-conditioned affordance fields (PAF) over point clouds to fix a weakness of SE(3)-equivariant visuomotor policies: their global rigid-transformation assumption breaks down in real manipulation where the task-relevant region varies across objects. The per-point affordance score provides a learned canonicalization anchor and guidance for the equivariant policy. This improves real-world robotic manipulation robustness.

entry.title: VeriPIE: Checkable Query Plans and Evidence-Guided Selection for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Piyush Jha, Cruise Song, Zhengyu Li, Yatharth Sejpal

entry.summary: VeriPIE is a neurosymbolic text-to-SQL framework that ensembles direct LLM SQL generation with a structured plan language (QuerySketch) verified by a Lean-implemented backend, using plan diagnostics to repair failures before SQL generation. It targets financial AI governance requirements like independent validation and effective challenge of AI-generated computations, where queries that agree on one database may still express different computations.

entry.title: HiSTOR: Structured Treatment-outcome Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Longitudinal Data

author.name: Chuanqi Lao, Junzhou Huang, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: HiSTOR is an end-to-end framework for estimating potential outcomes under alternative treatment sequences, combining nonlinear dimension reduction with longitudinal counterfactual prediction. It learns structured low-dimensional representations of patient states and histories to jointly handle high-dimensional covariates and time-varying confounding.

entry.title: Posterior-Averaged Bellman Flow Matching for Distributional Critics

author.name: Zeqiao Li, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a method for training flow-based distributional critics in reinforcement learning, where the full return distribution is modeled for exploration and risk-sensitive control. The key contribution is a posterior-averaged Bellman flow matching objective that handles the ambiguity of intermediate bridge states, which may be compatible with multiple Bellman endpoints, rather than relying on noisy single-endpoint supervision. This addresses a core training instability in recursively generated flow critics.

entry.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Shenyi Li, Yilin Wang, Ziyun Cui, Bowen Zhou, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: MMTA is a tri-modal benchmark pairing time series with text and real-world visual evidence across nine domains including robotics, healthcare, and finance. It provides a 3,524-sample test set for classification and forecasting tasks, addressing the gap where prior benchmarks only paired signals with text or derived visualizations.

entry.title: Evaluating the Causal Faithfulness of SHAP as a Candidate Attribution Method for SAE Features

author.name: Samuel Xie, Noura Al-Moubayed

entry.summary: This paper tests whether SHAP-based attribution faithfully estimates the causal influence of sparse autoencoder (SAE) features in language models, comparing it against Integrated Gradients, Gradient-times-Input, and probe-weight baselines. Using GPT-2 Small on sentiment classification with a 32,768-feature SAE, the authors score each method against direct causal interventions such as feature ablation and activation steering. The work addresses a real gap, since SAE feature interpretation is still mostly correlational despite widespread interest in mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: FETALFusion: Resolution-Aware State-Space Modeling for Multi-Domain Fetal Head Segmentation

author.name: Ammar Bhilwarawala, Mainak Bandyopadhyay

entry.summary: This paper introduces FETALFusion, a dual-path CNN-Mamba encoder-decoder for fetal head segmentation across transabdominal and transperineal ultrasound domains, applying state-space scans only at high-resolution stages plus domain-specific channel gating and a weak landmark shape prior. The method is evaluated against ten baselines on a held-out test set of 471 images using surface distances at native resolution. It matters because reliable automated fetal head circumference measurement is a routine clinical need and domain-general segmentation remains difficult.

entry.title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Hanlin Kong, Jianan Wei, Yuntian Chen, Yujia Wang, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a turbulence-aware framework for time-resolved 3D turbulent flow super-resolution from coarse-grained data, coupling multiscale modeling with the dynamics of turbulence. This aims to overcome limitations of prior data-driven methods in recovering volumetric multiscale structures and their temporal evolution.

entry.title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory

author.name: Qian Chen, Xianyin Zhang, Lifan Guo, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a vision-language model framework that incrementally reconstructs document-level heading hierarchies for long documents, where page-by-page VLM parsing typically produces inconsistent heading levels. A level-wise multimodal memory allows the system to maintain global structural coherence without processing all page images jointly. This matters for downstream applications like retrieval-augmented generation that need coherent document structure.

entry.title: FedGraph: Defending Federated Large Language Model Fine-Tuning Against Backdoor Attacks via Graph-Based Aggregation

author.name: Xi Chen, Chunyi Zhou, Rui Zeng, Xiaogang Xu, Zhe Liu, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: FedGraph defends federated LLM fine-tuning against backdoor attacks by exploiting the observation that malicious clients produce strongly consistent updates while benign clients produce diverse ones. It represents client relationships as a graph and uses graph-based aggregation rather than high-dimensional anomaly detection on parameters directly. This addresses a key vulnerability in privacy-preserving collaborative fine-tuning.

entry.title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time

author.name: Yifan He, Sofie Goethals, Manon Reusens, David Martens

entry.summary: This study probes how LLMs price human time across countries by varying only the user's nationality and measuring compensation deemed appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay, across 193 countries and 5 models. LLM responses are compared against GDP per capita, mean income, and patience indices. The work reveals noticeably different and sometimes brittle country-conditioned time valuations, relevant to fairness in globally deployed assistants.

entry.title: When More Objectives Make Identification Easier: The Role of Preferences and Feedback

author.name: Bo Xue, Ji Cheng, Yuanyu Wan, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: This paper studies best-arm identification in multi-objective bandits, showing counterintuitively that extra objectives can make identification easier because richer feedback reduces exploration needs. For Gaussian bandits, the authors establish a characteristic-time lower bound for fixed-confidence identification uniform across preference orders, plus matching algorithmic results. The work clarifies when and why multi-objective feedback helps.

entry.title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design

author.name: Johanna Magdalena Kuch, Maud van Lier, Daksitha Senel Withanage Don, Patrick Gebhard, Tanja Schneeberger, Elisabeth Andr\'e

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests whether cloning a familiar person's voice onto a virtual character transfers associated personality impressions to that character. Across two studies, the authors probe whether zero-shot voice cloning could be used to manipulate users into treating virtual characters as capable social actors, a relevant AI safety and human-AI interaction concern.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Cloth Dynamics with Physics-Informed Neural ODEs

author.name: Yingdong Ru, Lipeng Zhuang, Zhuo He, Gerardo Aragon Camarasa

entry.summary: ContinuousCloth embeds a spring-mass ODE inside a neural trajectory model for cloth simulation, allowing queries at arbitrary timestamps and derivatives via automatic differentiation. It matches high-precision solvers on six boundary-condition scenarios while running up to 17.4x faster, and fuses with sparse noisy observations using the physics prior.

entry.title: VitaBench: Memory Lifecycles Beyond Retrieval

author.name: Muquan Yu, Dihan Hu

entry.summary: VitaBench is a benchmark that evaluates memory lifecycle decisions in language agents, namely whether memories should be kept exact, compressed, consolidated, or deleted, rather than only measuring retrieval. It formalizes lifecycle evaluation with repeated memory reviews and full-horizon counterfactual scoring across a diagnostic tier and more realistic settings. This fills a real gap, as existing long-term-memory benchmarks stop at retrieval quality.

entry.title: CrossMean: Model Merging by Pairing Merged and Expert Activations

author.name: Moshe Eliasof

entry.summary: This paper reformulates closed-form model merging methods as a linear system and identifies that existing approaches reuse the same activation-statistics matrix on both sides. It introduces CrossMean, which pairs merged-model and expert activations via a bilinear statistic, and derives a label-free criterion for assessing merge quality. This addresses a real gap: merged layers receive inputs from previously merged layers, not individual experts.

entry.title: Anchors Enhance Controllability and Reasoning of Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Feiyu Qu, Zheng Huang, Andrea Zanette

entry.summary: AnchorDLM improves controllable generation in diffusion language models by having an anchor generator produce a short output fragment and its position, placed as control tokens to guide a frozen DLM's denoising. Exploiting bidirectional attention, anchors steer generation from arbitrary positions while preserving the model's original capabilities. The work targets the underexplored controllability dimension of diffusion LMs.

entry.title: FragFlex: Fragment-Based Flexible Molecular Generation for Exploring Vast Chemical Space

author.name: Sihyun Park, David Ryan Koes

entry.summary: Introduces FragFlex, a flexible-length discrete diffusion model for molecular graph generation that performs node insertion and deletion at the fragment level, jointly learning fragment identities, graph size, and connectivity during denoising. A neural attachment-site predictor and valence-aware assembler ensure chemical validity, aiming to improve drug-discovery exploration of chemical space.

entry.title: MERIT: Scaling KG Foundation Models with Relation Transformers

author.name: Cosimo Gregucci, Daniel Hernandez, Antonio Vergari, Steffen Staab

entry.summary: Introduces MERIT, the first knowledge graph foundation model using a transformer over relations instead of message-passing or random-walk ensembles over large relation graphs, aiming to reverse the rising training and inference costs of recent KGFMs like ULTRA, MOTIF, TRIX, and FLOCK. The design targets efficiency while supporting complex reasoning tasks such as complex query answering.

entry.title: Context-Aware Precision Scheduling for Small Language Models

author.name: Mukund Athmaram, Manoj Rao, Liang Ma

entry.summary: This paper addresses the accuracy-latency tradeoff for on-device small language models by dynamically selecting mixed-precision configurations that depend on context length. The authors calibrate a timing model from real measurements rather than assuming fewer bits always means faster execution, and combine it with tensor sensitivity analysis to pick configurations under latency or accuracy budgets.

entry.title: Preserving Updates in Low-Bit Recurrent State Quantization

author.name: Haotian Li, Liran Dong, Kaicheng Xiao, Guoliang Xing

entry.summary: This paper addresses quantization of recurrent states in linear attention and recurrent models, where states are requantized at every step and errors accumulate over time. The authors identify that quantization errors are highly coherent across steps, driven mainly by small updates lost during rounding, and propose a Low-Rank Bypass (LRB) mechanism that accumulates small updates before rounding. This matters because low-bit state quantization could significantly reduce memory and bandwidth costs for efficient sequence models at large batch sizes.

entry.title: Representational Difference Distillation

author.name: Abdulkarim Mugisha, Divin Irakiza

entry.summary: The authors propose Representational Difference Distillation (RDD), which improves knowledge distillation by locating where teacher and student representations structurally disagree and concentrating gradient signal there. Two asymmetric affinity matrices capture distinct misalignment directions: spurious student similarities and unlearned teacher relationships. This targets distillation effort more efficiently than uniform relational methods.

entry.title: Learning Graded Sparse Mechanisms: A Representation Theorem and Certified Generalization

author.name: Mark Kozdoba, Shie Mannor

entry.summary: This paper formally studies graded sparse mechanisms, functions where each element's update depends strongly on a few other elements and weakly on many, with the sparsity grading provided by the environment as weights. The authors define the class axiomatically, prove a representation theorem, and derive certified generalization guarantees. This is relevant to modeling flocks, particle simulators, and graph network neighborhood aggregation.

entry.title: Learn from Move: the Next Step for GUI Agents

author.name: Jiahao Lu, Yize Shen, Chuanyuan Tan, Mianqiu Huang, Shicheng Fang, Xinchi Chen, Yining Zheng, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: The paper introduces LatentGUIWorld, a benchmark of six tasks in matched pairs organized by the evidence needed for control, showing that frontier models struggle especially on tasks requiring learning action-response dynamics. It also proposes MOVE, which separates movement from button events and exposes intermediate visual feedback, together with demonstrations to improve GUI agent exploration in unfamiliar environments.

entry.title: OpenDGO: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Organizations Across Diverse Application Domains

author.name: Xunkai Li, Miao Zhang, Zekai Chen, Xuaner Chen, Yu liu, Rui Qian, Xun Wu, Hongchao Qin, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: OpenDGO is a controlled benchmark and analysis framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems that evaluates how agent organization structures (such as Star, Chain, Tree, or learned communication graphs) transfer across six real-world application domains and three collaboration settings. The paper addresses a real gap: prior work evaluates fixed organizational topologies on narrow task suites, leaving cross-domain generalization of agent organizations poorly understood. It matters because organization design is a key lever for multi-agent system performance and cost.

entry.title: CartoVec: General-Purpose Location Embeddings from Open Map Data

author.name: Furkan Gursoy

entry.summary: CartoVec is a coordinate encoder trained on open map data (Overture-derived land cover, land use, transportation, places, connectivity) at multiple spatial scales to produce location embeddings without imagery or downstream labels. Frozen embeddings are evaluated on Census outcomes, Airbnb prices, and crime prediction using spatial block cross-validation. It offers a practical alternative to image-based geolocation encoders for applied geospatial ML.

entry.title: MIRRA: Fast, High-Fidelity Molecular Generation with Chemistry-Informed Discrete Flow Matching

author.name: Ge Sun, Juan J. de Pablo

entry.summary: This paper introduces MIRRA, a discrete flow-matching generative model for molecular generation that uses chemical building blocks while handling the huge identity space (tens of thousands of candidate blocks per node). It employs chemistry-informed feature sharing, learned identity corrections, and a sampling strategy that decides which positions to refresh before computing probabilities, reducing wasted computation while keeping the full vocabulary accessible. This matters for accelerating drug and materials discovery with generative AI.

entry.title: A Sense of Proprioception in Language Models

author.name: Jonas Geiping

entry.summary: This position-style paper by Jonas Geiping argues that language models lack access to their own internal states during training, analogous to lacking proprioception, and that building a digital proprioceptive sense would give models access to verifiable self-state signals such as which MoE experts activated. The author argues this is a distinct, constructible sense with dedicated receptors and verifiable outcomes. It is conceptually relevant to interpretability and self-monitoring capabilities of models.

entry.title: Counterfactual Certification for Sequential Unlearning with Long-Run Performance Guarantees

author.name: Hanna Benarroch (DI-ENS), Jamal Atif (CMAP), Olivier Capp\'e (DI-ENS)

entry.summary: This paper extends certified machine unlearning to sequential, group-based deletion requests by certifying each model release against a counterfactual unlearning trajectory where the deleted group never participated. The authors prove that with a fixed fine-tuning budget per deletion, performance guarantees hold long-run for smooth strongly convex objectives, addressing the performance degradation or computation blowup of naive sequential unlearning.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped SGD with Linear Decay

author.name: Wei Jiang, Haomin Bai, Zechao Li

entry.summary: The paper proves high-probability last-iterate convergence rates for clipped SGD with linearly decaying learning rates under heavy-tailed noise with bounded central p-th moment (1 < p <= 2), extending to nonsmooth composite objectives, proximal updates, and adversarially corrupted gradients with matching lower bounds. This closes gaps in the theory of robust optimization under non-sub-Gaussian noise.

entry.title: BridgeTwist: Twisting Schr\"odinger Bridges for Training-Free Conditional Sampling

author.name: Mengyu Li, Qianqian Qu, Jun S. Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces BridgeTwist, the first training-free conditional sampling method for pretrained Schrödinger bridge generative models, implemented as a tempered twisted sequential Monte Carlo scheme with a closed-form plug-in twist surrogate. It fills a methodological gap, since training-free posterior sampling has been well developed for diffusion and flow models but not for Schrödinger bridges, which are increasingly popular as flexible stochastic transport models between arbitrary source and target distributions.

entry.title: Quasi-Binarized Autoencoders: An Architecture-Independent Information Bottleneck for Medical Image Anomaly Detection

author.name: Shouhei Hanaoka, Takahiro Nakao, Atsushi Takamatsu, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe

entry.summary: The paper introduces a quasi-binarizing (QB) layer that squashes latent elements into [0,1] with Laplace noise, creating an architecture-independent, quantifiable information bottleneck for reconstruction-based anomaly detection in medical imaging. This prevents autoencoders from learning identity mappings that would reconstruct anomalies.

entry.title: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization

author.name: Weixi Song, Donglin Wang, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: This RL paper proposes using a chunk world model as a differentiable training-time evaluator to optimize a chunk actor, avoiding recurrent rollouts and the compounding errors, latency, and BPTT instability of prior model-based RL. Collaborative chunk-wise prediction of the world model and policy enables gradient-based policy improvement without recurrent model invocation. It targets the core inefficiencies of latent-dynamics model-based RL.

entry.title: What Drives AI Citations? Content, Retrieval and Model Knowledge in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)

author.name: Mahe Chen, Nick Koudas

entry.summary: This large-scale study analyzes two 90-day collections totaling 158,099 generative-engine answers and 468,037 citations to determine what drives citation in systems like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. It finds that within a website, title and paragraph question-match matters while FAQ blocks and structured data only help across sites, and that page properties explain little within-site variation. The analysis separates content factors from retrieval dynamics and model knowledge.

entry.title: LiveAnon: Improving Privacy and Utility in Streaming Speaker Anonymization with Codec Language Models

author.name: Yejin Kim, Kyungsu Kim, Seungu Han, Kyogu Lee

entry.summary: Presents LiveAnon, a streaming speaker anonymization system that conditions an autoregressive codec language model on hidden features from a pretrained streaming ASR encoder, preserving emotion without emotion-specific supervision. Capped RVQ decoding predicts coarse codebooks sequentially and remaining codebooks in parallel, cutting latency, with improved intelligibility and emotion preservation on VPC24.

entry.title: Mobility Helps Learning: Unsupervised Model Adaptation for Object Recognition via Movement

author.name: Yanan Ma, Yihang Tao, Zhengru Fang, Senkang Hu, Xianhao Chen, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: The paper proposes MoCaFe, a model-agnostic, hyperparameter-insensitive test-time adaptation paradigm for movable agents that exploits prediction variance induced by observing the same object from different distances and viewpoints. Mobility-derived signals serve as free supervision for unsupervised adaptation in robotics and autonomous driving settings.

entry.title: Deep Speech Representations Track Word Timing along a Low-Dimensional Circular Trajectory

author.name: Burin Naowarat, Hao Tang, Sharon Goldwater

entry.summary: The authors show that circular trajectories in a two-dimensional temporal subspace, previously observed in HuBERT features, encode word timing as a general property of deep speech representations, emerging across nine additional models. This representational-geometry finding illuminates how speech models internally track word onsets and offsets.

entry.title: From a Large-Scale Teacher to Efficient Multimodal Students for Search Relevance Prediction

author.name: Tomasz Gniazdowski, Mohammadreza Momenifar, Nadia Vase, Shahram Khadivi, Wiktor Walentynowicz, Nicola Ueffing, Jan Pawlowski, Piotr Szymanski, Abraham Bagherjeiran

entry.summary: This paper distills an LLM-based relevance judgment system used in e-commerce search into small, efficient multimodal student models for predicting query-item relevance. It addresses the practical trade-off between expensive, high-quality LLM annotation and the low-latency throughput requirements of production search systems.

entry.title: JtT: Rethinking Point Trajectory Diffusion for Diverse and Rigid Motion from an Image

author.name: Gabrijel Boduljak, Yushi Lan, Christian Rupprecht, Andrea Vedaldi

entry.summary: JtT is a diffusion transformer that forecasts diverse, physically plausible rigid-body motion trajectories from a single image, operating directly in coordinate space without trajectory VAEs, depth inputs, or fixed grids. The authors show prior trajectory generators fail even on synthetic Kubric scenes and attribute success to architecture and parameterization choices validated through a systematic design-space study.

entry.title: On the Calibration of Crowdsourcing Aggregators

author.name: Gabriel Singer, Reda Arab, Ma\"issa Frikha, Samuel Gruffaz, Olivier Vo Van, Nicolas Vayatis, Argyris Kalogeratos

entry.summary: This appears to be the first theoretical and empirical study of calibration for crowdsourcing label aggregation, finding that common aggregators are severely miscalibrated in opposite directions: Majority Vote is underconfident while model-based aggregators are overconfident. The authors prove the Bayesian aggregator is perfectly calibrated under its data-generating model and show exact calibration of weighted majority votes requires restrictive conditions.

entry.title: ML Engineering Agents - A Data Management Perspective

author.name: Arnab Phani, Elias Strauss, Tim Schuster, Sebastian Schelter

entry.summary: A tutorial paper introducing ML engineering (MLE) agents, which use LLMs to iteratively synthesize, execute, and refine end-to-end ML pipeline code. It critiques current benchmarks for abstracting away data management challenges and outlines open research problems for the database community, including efficient pipeline execution and data discovery.

entry.title: Accounting for model error in ensemble variational data assimilation through learned generative dynamics

author.name: Marc Bocquet, Tobias S. Finn, Sibo Cheng

entry.summary: The authors combine sequential data assimilation with a generative forecasting model that stochastically approximates the conditional distribution of the successor state, replacing prescribed additive Gaussian model error in a weak-constraint 4D-Var formulation. They derive an ensemble variational algorithm, the generative iterative ensemble scheme, to make forecasts with geophysical models more robust to model error. This advances the growing intersection of machine learning and weather/geoscience data assimilation.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving GNN Inference on Financial Transaction Graphs via Homomorphic Encryption

author.name: H. \c{C}a\u{g}r{\i} Bilgi, Kemal Mutluergil, Ceren Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m, Kubilay Atasu, Erkay Savas

entry.summary: The paper proposes a privacy-preserving GNN inference framework for multi-bank anti-money-laundering, where a central server holds graph structure and model weights while banks keep transaction features encrypted under CKKS homomorphic encryption. An edge-centric GNN design makes encrypted inference practical without exposing plaintext features or predictions.

entry.title: Linear Last-Iterate Convergence Rates for Optimistic Learning in Harmonic Games

author.name: John Lazarsfeld, Anas Barakat, Jacob Abernethy, Vidya Muthukumar, Georgios Piliouras, Andre Wibisono, Juba Ziani

entry.summary: The authors prove that Optimistic Follow-The-Regularized-Leader achieves linear last-iterate convergence to Nash equilibrium in multiplayer harmonic games, for a broad family of regularizers. The analysis uses a dual energy-dissipation argument and extends to Extragradient FTRL.

entry.title: LongHisDoc: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chinese Long Historical Document Understanding

author.name: Zeyu Shan, Yongxin Shi, Shihang Wu, Peirong Zhang, Yuanyuan Fang, Zhaopeng Wang, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: This paper introduces LongHisDoc, the first benchmark for understanding long Chinese historical documents, with 1,012 expert-annotated QA pairs drawn from 101 full-book PDFs averaging 85 pages each. It tests large vision-language models on single-page, cross-page, multi-hop, and unanswerable questions across 10 document categories. The benchmark exposes how poorly current models handle full-book historical material, an important gap for digital humanities and cultural preservation.

entry.title: From Candidate Tokens to Final Outcomes: Decoding Relative Long-Horizon Candidate Value from Reasoning Model Representations

author.name: Yixin Yang, Yue Wang, Fandong Meng, Zhifang Sui

entry.summary: The authors define relative long-horizon candidate value to quantify how plausible next-token choices at a reasoning prefix differ in their eventual probability of leading to correct answers, and construct the RCTV dataset pairing math reasoning prefixes with candidates and empirical outcome values. Using sparse probing over hidden states, MLP outputs, and attention outputs, they examine whether reasoning model representations encode these long-horizon differences. The work connects token-level representation analysis with outcome-level reasoning quality.

entry.title: RIVO: Lightweight Adaptive Rerouting for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Mingchen Li, Jiatan Huang, Hong Yu

entry.summary: RIVO formulates adaptive rerouting in long-horizon Deep Research agents as state-conditioned trajectory correction, deciding when agents should stop, continue, or redirect unproductive searches. It avoids costly retraining and dense turn-level supervision while being optimized for downstream research utility.

entry.title: PersonaFactor: Preference Factors with Dynamic Selection for LLM Personalization

author.name: Hang Su, Zequn Liu, Jianghan Chao, Qiuyu Tian, Xuesong Lu, Yingce Xia

entry.summary: This paper introduces PersonaFactors, a framework that distills reusable and interpretable personalization factors from heterogeneous user interactions, building a library of thirteen evidence-grounded factors by clustering recurring behavioral patterns across tasks. A dynamic factor-guided generation mechanism selects the relevant factors for each user history and request. It matters because it moves LLM personalization beyond surface-level interaction logs toward shared underlying preference mechanisms.

entry.title: Nufo: A Benchmark for Ewe Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Christ Kekeli Keli, Steve Sanogo, Patrice Sebastiano, Hamad Aldenawi, Ryan Whetten

entry.summary: The authors consolidate existing Ewe speech data into a standardized 174-hour ASR benchmark, the largest for the language to date, and fine-tune Whisper and AfriHuBERT to establish baselines (WERs around 38-40%). This addresses the acute shortage of transcribed-speech resources for low-resource African languages.

entry.title: Cheap, Consistent, Calibrated, but Biased? Typed Decision Models as Judges

author.name: Fabian Lukassen, Christoph Weisser, Alexander Silbersdorff

entry.summary: Typed decision models, which return answer probabilities rather than generating text, are evaluated as cheap alternatives to LLM judges using the CALM benchmark's bias tests across eight TDMs and seven LLM judges. Every TDM shows biases in three to eight of twelve tests, with emotional tone swinging a typical TDM's accuracy from 99% to 42%, and all TDMs exhibit position-swap sensitivity that 2026 LLM judges largely avoid. The paper demonstrates TDMs are more biased than modern LLM judges.

entry.title: The Last Mile of Coding Agents for Long-Document Tasks: An Empirical Study on Clinical Trial Protocol Digitization

author.name: Jiacheng Lin, Geoffrey Low, Nishit Agarwal, Rahul Jain, Afrah Shafquat, Mandis Beigi, Jimeng Sun

entry.summary: The authors introduce TrialPD-Bench, an expert-annotated benchmark of 150 clinical trial protocol PDFs across four task categories, to study how reliably coding agents digitize complete long documents into structured outputs. Beyond final-answer accuracy, the evaluation examines process-level behaviors of agents on these long-document workflows. The study probes the gap between coding-agent competence on code tasks and reliable document-to-structure transformation in a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: Decomposing and Predicting Annotation Disagreement in Harmful Content Across Languages

author.name: Irem Ecem Yelkanat, Faeze Ghorbanpour, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: The authors propose predicting annotator disagreement in harmful-content labeling from interpretable semantic properties, using an LLM to answer binary questions about harm characteristics, borderline cues, and language-sensitive cues, then training a classifier on those answers. Experiments span four datasets in English, German, and Turkish. This treats disagreement as signal for routing difficult cases rather than noise to discard.

entry.title: RelLedger: Relational Information Governance for LLM Agent Organizations

author.name: Junxi Huang, Wenshuo Chen, Nuoxuan Li, Kailong Wang, Meitong Shen, Yuehan Kou, Leihao Zhao, Yutao Yue, Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces RelLedger, a framework for auditing how shared interaction histories in LLM agent organizations influence reporting decisions. By holding events, evidence, risk, and messages fixed while varying sender histories and event targets, it isolates which relational cues drive record creation and whether those records matter downstream.

entry.title: Image Diffusion Models Are Good 3D Human Motion Generators

author.name: Siyuan Yang, Chong Wang, Hao Cheng, Jun Liu, Bihan Wen, Alex Kot, Hedvig Kjellstrom

entry.summary: Shows image diffusion architectures can generate 3D human motion by organizing joint trajectories into topology-informed joint-time images plus a latent stream for root dynamics, using a text-conditioned Scalable Interpolant Transformer. This common representation accommodates heterogeneous skeletal layouts across motion benchmarks.

entry.title: InfraWorld: Motion-Aware World Modeling for Roadside 4D Occupancy Forecasting

author.name: Songkai Wang, Xiaokai Bai, Lei Yang, Hui-liang Shen

entry.summary: InfraWorld formulates roadside 4D occupancy forecasting as selective state evolution, combining a dense BEV scene state with persistent motion queries for moving regions. Components like Dynamic Query Initiation let it capture both global scene context and sparse local dynamics from infrastructure sensors.

entry.title: CAST: Real-Time Motion Capture for Any Skeleton Topology

author.name: Pu Pang, Zhongfei Qing, Ling-Hao Chen, Songnan Li, Hua Huang, Bo Hu

entry.summary: CAST addresses monocular motion capture when the target skeleton differs from the observed subject, combining learned local rotations with geometric correction guided by predicted global bone directions. The method includes an observability analysis of which rotational components bone directions can constrain, plus a reliability-gated alignment module to limit error propagation along the kinematic hierarchy.

entry.title: UniForge3D: Joint 3D Reconstruction and Generation in a Shared Anchor-Guided Space

author.name: Wenjue Chen, Wenyue Chen, Heliang Zheng, Rongfei Jia, Yuan Liu, Meng Li

entry.summary: UniForge3D jointly performs 3D reconstruction and generation from sparse unposed images in a shared anchor-guided space, resolving the coordinate mismatch between camera-relative reconstruction and canonical-space generation. It conditions each 3D location on relevant views to preserve observed geometry while completing unseen regions.

entry.title: Frozen History: When Temporal Losses Stop Accumulation in Learned Real-Time Supersampling

author.name: Hao Yu, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: This paper shows that temporal consistency losses in learned real-time supersampling can paradoxically suppress sample accumulation: with accurate registration the network copies its warped history instead of accumulating jittered samples. The authors identify four registration error types that hide this effect and build a model-free oracle and controlled training setup demonstrating correct registration makes freezing orders of magnitude cheaper on static pixels.

entry.title: Meaningful Moments: A Corpus of VLM-Derived Temporal Importance Labels for Video Action Recognition

author.name: Cameron Keith, SouYoung Jin

entry.summary: This paper introduces Meaningful Moments, a large-scale corpus of roughly 4.58 million per-segment importance scores generated by vision-language models for about 500,000 videos across Something-Something v2, Kinetics-400, and Diving-48, covering 622 action classes. The goal is to identify which short video segments carry decisive evidence for recognizing an action and to test whether these labels improve video action recognition. It matters because most video datasets lack action-conditioned temporal importance labels, and VLMs could make such labeling scalable.

entry.title: EgoAlign: Situated 3D Understanding without Situation Descriptions

author.name: Yiyang Li, Tianyi Ma, Zehong Wang, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: EgoAlign addresses situated 3D question answering by representing scenes in an agent-centric coordinate frame rather than relying on natural-language situation descriptions, and reveals that existing methods barely depend functionally on numerical pose (random shuffling causes little degradation). It adds an egocentric alignment stage with four complementary tasks including object recognition and direction prediction.

entry.title: Anomaly-Guided Observation and Two-Level Semantic Feedback for Training-Free Video Anomaly Analysis
