author.name: Hangil Park, Seungheon Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free semantic feedback framework where anomaly-score-guided active observation drives reasoning-based iterative frame selection, and anomaly-focused descriptions generated by VLMs and LLMs are fed back to refine temporal detection. This closes the loop between anomaly understanding and localization without any task-specific training.

entry.title: MiMaAlign: Hierarchical Micro-Macro Alignment for Physically Plausible Video Generation

author.name: Yansong Liu, Litong Gong, Weijie Li, Tiezheng Ge, Ming Zeng

entry.summary: MiMaAlign transfers complementary dynamics-oriented and event-oriented knowledge into different abstraction depths of a pretrained text-to-video diffusion model, aligning micro-level continuous dynamics and macro-level event interactions separately to improve physical plausibility. This treats plausibility as a hierarchical representation problem rather than a single-level one.

entry.title: NoduleFlow: Automatic 3D Lung Nodule Detection and Segmentation

author.name: Giulia Romoli, Filippo Ruffini, Francesco Di Feola, Valerio Guarrasi, Matteo Tortora, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: NoduleFlow addresses automatic 3D detection and segmentation of lung nodules in low-dose CT screening, aiming to go beyond coarse region-of-interest localization and reduce dependence on prior lesion annotations. It treats detection and segmentation jointly to improve accuracy and efficiency in follow-up monitoring of subtle temporal changes.

entry.title: Brain2Face: A Study on the Relation of EEG Signals and Spatio-temporal Head Avatars

author.name: Camilo Andr\'es Mart\'inez Mart\'inez, Olaf D\"unkel, Kartik Teotia, Maurice Rekrut, Christian Theobalt, Marc Habermann

entry.summary: This exploratory study asks whether head avatar geometry and appearance can be driven purely from EEG signals, contributing a new dataset pairing 64-channel EEG with per-frame expression latents of a personalized Gaussian head avatar, plus a baseline method. The task is largely unexplored and previously lacked public high-quality benchmarks.

entry.title: Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Scene Reconstruction: Methods, Systems, and Trade-offs

author.name: Ashim Dahal, Rabab Abdelfattah, Nick Rahimi

entry.summary: This survey synthesizes the 3D Gaussian Splatting literature since 2023, organizing scene-reconstruction work into five overlapping families spanning sparse-view generation, dynamic reconstruction, efficiency and compression, streaming, and SLAM, and connecting approaches into an end-to-end pipeline. It emphasizes the distinction between rendering an existing representation and constructing, updating, or maintaining scenes.

entry.title: ScenePercept: Scenario-Conditioned Perceptual Assessment of Real-World User-Generated Content Images

author.name: Shuhan Xia, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Peipie Li, Zekun Li

entry.summary: ScenePercept-Bench is a new benchmark of 23,100 real-world user-generated content images spanning 21 categories and 105 fine-grained scenes, designed to evaluate perceptual quality and aesthetics under scenario-conditioned criteria rather than uniform standards. It addresses distribution mismatch between existing task-oriented benchmarks and real UGC imagery.

entry.title: PUGS: Physics-Guided Uncertainty Modeling for Underwater Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Tingjun Li, Yuxi Wang, Guoqiang Zhong, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: PUGS models physics-induced uncertainty from underwater image formation (scattering, refraction, marine snow) within dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting, parameterizing each Gaussian's motion probabilistically rather than as a deterministic deformation. Uncertainty serves as a physical signal for reconstructing dynamic underwater scenes.

entry.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Zero-Shot Human-Object Interaction

author.name: Oriol Rabasseda, Zenjie Li, Kamal Nasrollahi, Sergio Escalera

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic benchmark of multimodal LLMs for zero-shot human-object interaction recognition and detection, combining an external detector with zero-shot multimodal reasoning. It introduces a unified taxonomy for zero-shot HOI evaluation. Useful for understanding where MLLMs fall short on structured visual relational reasoning.

entry.title: Recasting DiT for Extreme Image Compression with Hierarchical Visual Priors

author.name: Yunuo Chen, Jingnan Gao, Bing He, Jinjing Zhao, Chuqin Zhou, Xiaoyue Ling, Li Song, Guo Lu, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: PrismCodec adapts a pretrained Diffusion Transformer into a bitstream-grounded one-step generative decoder for extreme image compression, using the decoded latent both as a starting state and as hierarchical visual priors for guidance. A progressive adaptation strategy bridges the gap between stochastic iterative generation and deterministic one-step decoding.

entry.title: Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model for Vessel Extraction Using Physics-informed Synthetic Data

author.name: Jinkui Hao, Donald R. Cantrell, Ramez Abdalla, Sameer A. Ansari, Bo Zhou

entry.summary: The authors propose a Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model that formulates coronary artery extraction from X-ray angiography as image translation, trained entirely on physics-informed synthetic data without manual vessel annotations. A physics-based synthesis engine generates perfectly aligned contrast-enhanced and contrast-free image pairs, and the model preserves intra-arterial contrast information rather than producing binary masks. This matters clinically for coronary artery disease diagnosis and avoids costly annotation.

entry.title: Federated Coreset Subsampling for Distributed Memory Banks

author.name: Jason Witzemann, Daniel Pr\"oll, Sebastian Hegenbart

entry.summary: This work adapts the PatchCore memory-bank anomaly detection algorithm to federated settings spanning multiple factories with non-identical data distributions. It proposes two approaches, Double Subsampling for combining existing coresets and Federated Subsampling for creating new ones, improving cold-start performance and robustness to domain shift and unreliable participant availability. It is relevant to practical industrial deployment of anomaly detection across sites.

entry.title: Composable Dynamics for Cooperative Humanoids: A RoboCompiler Extension

author.name: Mehdi Heydari Shahna, Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: This paper extends the RoboCompiler framework to handle the dynamics of physically connected humanoid robots, including internal actuator loops, inter-robot forces, and changing ground supports. It introduces member-wise dynamics assembly, analytic constraint curvature for Coriolis factorization satisfying the power identity, and a two-level reduction that reuses individual robot models while composing their physical connections. This matters for building principled, efficient control software for cooperative humanoid teams rather than ad-hoc per-robot solutions.

entry.title: Successful but Unsafe: An Analytical Benchmark for Revealing Collisions in Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Hieu D. Pham, Quoc-An Luong, Dung D. Le

entry.summary: VLN-Safe is a benchmark revealing that vision-and-language navigation agents collide frequently even when standard success metrics look good, evaluating under both sliding regimes (which mask collisions) and blocking regimes that expose their consequences. Across six published agents on R2R-CE, a substantial fraction of apparently successful episodes involve collisions. This highlights a safety blind spot in prevailing VLN evaluation.

entry.title: Training-Free Multi-Agent Cooperative Embodied Search from Uncertain Vision-Language Priors

author.name: Fan Pu, Keshu Wu, Jiwan Jiang, Shiyu Shen, Zhiwen Fan, Zhengzhong Tu, Jiachen Li, Yang Zhou

entry.summary: This work presents a lightweight, training-free framework for cooperative multi-agent, multi-target search in mapless environments, where multimodal LLMs act only as hypothesis generators producing uncertain semantic cues. A graph-optimization backbone separates high-level semantic reasoning from low-level execution and explicitly handles uncertainty from partial observability.

entry.title: nanoflann: A Header-Only KD-Tree Library for Exact Nearest-Neighbor Search on Compile-Time Product Manifolds

author.name: Jos\'e Luis Blanco-Claraco

entry.summary: This paper introduces a header-only, dependency-free C++ library for exact nearest-neighbor search on non-Euclidean manifolds such as SO(2), SO(3), SE(2), and SE(3), which are common in robotics but handled incorrectly by standard Euclidean KD-trees. Users compose state spaces from base manifolds via a compile-time type alias, and the library synthesizes provably admissible, wrap-aware and double-cover-aware metrics for correct pruning, with experiments confirming exact recall.

entry.title: Have You Seen It Clearly? Uncertainty-Guided Belief Refinement for Zero-Shot Object Navigation

author.name: Jingzhi Huang, Junkai Huang, Yuhang Peng, Keyu Mu, Jiaru Zhong, Yi Wang, Lujia Wang, Lap-Pui Chau, Siyang Gao

entry.summary: This paper introduces RefBeliefMap, an uncertainty-guided mapping framework for zero-shot object navigation that explicitly separates target-location belief from spatial and semantic evidence uncertainty, modeling both intra-observation and inter-observation disagreement. The work matters because it addresses a persistent gap in LLM/VLM-based navigation systems: whether accumulated evidence actually justifies a navigation decision.

entry.title: Embodied Skill Bench: Benchmarking How Well Agents with Embodied Skills Perform on Physical Tasks

author.name: Zhi Han, Zihan Guo, Chenxi Zeng, Zicai Cui, Yue Xin, Ming Zhou, Dongzhan Zhou, Weinan Zhang, Yang Li

entry.summary: This paper packages robot modules (VLA policies, perception models, procedural knowledge) as embodied skills with explicit embodiment assumptions and conditions of use, building 250 skills from 1,052 resources. EmbodiedSkillBench evaluates LLM agents in closed observation-action loops across native control, skill-only, and a proposed Agent-Directed Reuse mode, recording success, tokens, and wall-clock time. It is the first systematic benchmark for reusable embodied skills.

entry.title: Imitation Learning of Avoidance Modes for Efficient Multimodal Model Predictive Control

author.name: Changyu Lee, Byung-Kwan Lee, Kanghoon Yoon

entry.summary: This paper proposes SideNet-MPC, which uses a graph neural network trained to imitate multimodal model predictive control (MM-MPC) and predict which side to avoid each obstacle, replacing the exponential enumeration of avoidance-side combinations. Edge features encode predicted obstacle-pair gaps at the moment of arrival, allowing a blocking neighbor to reverse the chosen side. The result is a substantial reduction in computational cost for motion planning among moving obstacles.

entry.title: Act4R: Action-conditioned 4D reconstruction for kinematics-free control

author.name: Zhaoliang Zhang, Chenhao Yu, Zhimin Shao, Xijun Liu, Cheng Peng

entry.summary: Act4R builds on 3D foundation models to predict action-conditioned 3D scene flow for robots, using a Spatial-Action Encoder that converts 2D observations and action signals into embeddings of future robot state in 3D, then fusing current and future spatial embeddings. The goal is to enable precise control across different robotic embodiments without dedicated kinematic models, sensors, or manual labeling, leveraging 4D representation learning lifted from plain 2D observations. If effective, this significantly lowers the engineering cost of deploying control across diverse robot hardware.

entry.title: Which Trajectory Is Safer? Combining Rule and Learning for Safety Evaluation

author.name: Xuewen Luo, Linlian Jiang, Bo Yu, Fan Ding, Xinxin Zuo, Yang Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces FutureRisk, a continuous metric for latent future risk of driving trajectories, quantified by how closely and persistently realized interactions approach unsafe states, addressing the coarseness of binary collision-rate evaluation. Its Context-Adaptive Risk Model blends a context-dependent safety-time distribution with an independently supervised critical-event-time distribution under a bounded safety criterion.

entry.title: SkipWorld: Latent Skip Planning with Distilled World Models for Efficient Visual Navigation

author.name: Yifei Yang, Zehua Fan, Zike Yan, Zhongyu Li, Yan Wang

entry.summary: SkipWorld addresses the training/deployment mismatch in world-model-based visual navigation by training models to recursively roll out future states in latent space (Latent AutoRoll), then distilling this into a skip world model that predicts long-horizon outcomes directly. This avoids expensive step-by-step candidate rollouts during planning, enabling efficient visual navigation.

entry.title: AutoAgent0: An Agentic Runtime for Safe Closed-Loop Driving

author.name: Jiageng Liu, Seth Z. Zhao, Zewei Zhou, Alejandro Huerta, Aidan Bayer-Calvert, Yuxin Bao, Haotian Lin, Robert Spataru, Zijun Cui, Yining Hong, Bolei Zhou, Jiaqi Ma

entry.summary: AutoAgent0 treats closed-loop driving safety as a test-time execution problem, wrapping existing end-to-end driving experts with an agentic runtime that adds independent scene detection, rule-based action verification, and feedback-driven recovery. The goal is to counteract accumulated closed-loop errors, especially in unseen scenarios, where a policy cannot recover from states it has drifted into. The work frames safety as an orchestration harness around driving models rather than a better planner.

entry.title: Designing for Prediction: Planning Formulas for Expected Out-of-Sample $R^2$ and $r$

author.name: Elizabeth Tipton

entry.summary: This statistics paper derives closed-form expressions for expected out-of-sample R-squared and observed-predicted correlations for OLS and ridge regression under leave-one-out cross-validation. The formulas relate these quantities to sample size, predictor count, assumed population R-squared, and a design efficiency factor, enabling researchers to run power-like design calculations before collecting data for prediction studies.

entry.title: HiPPT: Physiology-Grounded Wearable PPG Representation Learning via Multi-Scope Text Alignment

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Wei Chen, Xiaoyu Li, Lexian Xia, ShuaiLong Tang, Chenran Zhang, Donglin Xie, Guangpu Zhu, Yelei Li, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: HiPPT is a physiology-grounded pretraining framework for wrist-worn PPG signals that matches each supervision source to its appropriate evidence scope, combining record-level morphology alignment with cross-recording context alignment. It uses a corpus of over 4 million recordings from 202K users paired with text descriptions.

entry.title: Iterate on an LLM, Serve on an SLM

author.name: Keegan Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a develop-then-deploy workflow where desired narrow agent behavior is first iterated in prompt space on a frontier model, then transferred to a small language model for 5-40x cheaper inference on repetitive subtasks. It addresses the gap that zero-shot small models fail production tasks yet retraining is too slow for iteration.

entry.title: VC-OPD: Visual Counterfactual On-Policy Distillation for Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Jiahe Feng

entry.summary: VC-OPD improves on-policy distillation for vision-language reasoning by prioritizing tokens whose correctness depends on image-specific evidence, identified through visual counterfactuals, after a teacher-supervised warm start. This addresses the coarse credit assignment of sequence-level GRPO rewards and the noise of distilling template or visually irrelevant tokens.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Visual Agent via Margin Reward

author.name: Wenxi Yang, Yuzhong Zhao, Baochang Zhang, Yunfan Liu, Qixiang Ye

entry.summary: Proposes Marvo, a self-evolution approach for visual agents that learns tool invocation from unlabeled images using two agents: a challenger generating question-answer pairs and a solver learning tool use via reinforcement learning. A margin reward encourages training questions that are hard enough to warrant tool use yet still solvable.

entry.title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Zhaoyuan Qiu, Sachith Seneviratne, Yu Xia, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: Proposes HarnessNet, a framework for joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems built from Agentrons - units of evolvable forward harness, frozen foundation model, and a local optimizer with restricted visibility - arranged in a layered graph. This addresses scaling limits of a single global optimizer and constraints on sharing agent internals.

entry.title: Visible but Not Avoided: State-Dependent Re-Proposal of Rejected Candidates in Catalog-Based LLM Optimization Loops

author.name: Jianlin Chen, Wenhui Chen, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: This paper shows that LLM proposers in catalog-based optimization loops frequently re-propose candidates they have already seen and rejected, with static probe measurements underpredicting re-proposal rates in the proposers' own trajectories. Re-proposals of already-evaluated edits consumed 28-63% of valid iterations across three open LLMs improving a GUI agent. The findings expose a state-dependent failure mode that matters for LLM-driven optimization loops.

entry.title: Imitation Holds a Key to Evolution: Localized Repair and Verified Skill Acquisition for Adaptive Agents

author.name: Kai Hu, Hua Huang

entry.summary: The paper formulates passive imitation as an architectural loop that localizes violated contracts, extracts local goals, proposes effect-matched skills, tests small patches, and retains evidence after full-task verification. A symbolic controller instantiation solves all 600 cold held-out composition tasks across ten simulated tool worlds within three trials, versus 6.17% for a whole-trajectory control.

entry.title: XAI-Guided Fourier Domain Generalisation for Pure-Simulation Sim-to-Real Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wei Yao, Chuyao Wang, Ziwei Wang, Nabil Aouf

entry.summary: Proposes XFD, an explainable-AI-guided Fourier domain generalization method for sim-to-real transfer in vision-based autonomous driving RL, which targets perturbations at features the policy actually relies on rather than applying unguided domain randomization. It requires no target-domain data, unlike image-transfer domain adaptation.

entry.title: Geospatial Vector Geometry as a Native Spatial Modality for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huang Fei, Boyi Chen, Hao Xue, Yang Yue, Yehong Xu, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes treating geospatial vector geometry as a native spatial modality within vision-language models, introducing GeoVec-VLM with a structured geometry representation that preserves spatial arrangement of vector objects. The approach targets the bottleneck where visual observations alone cannot establish accurate spatial references at large geographic scales.

entry.title: Reasoning for Propaganda Detection via Label-Guided CoT Optimisation

author.name: Zeba Afroz, Harsh Vardhan, Md. Shad Akhtar

entry.summary: Proposes ReCoT, a reasoning-conditioned framework for propaganda detection that derives definitional cues of persuasive techniques through population-level refinement and performance-guided resampling without extra explanation annotations. It approaches SFT upper bounds on INDI-PROPspan and PTC while remaining interpretable.

entry.title: Empowering Edge Agents: A Systematic Analysis of Edge-Cloud Collaboration in LLM Agent Execution

author.name: Pengcheng Huang, Zhenghao Liu, Shixin Ren, Shi Yu, Sijia Yao, Yukun Yan, Chaojun Xiao, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: The paper introduces EC2-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating edge-cloud collaboration during long-horizon LLM agent execution, with executable digital-workspace tasks and metrics covering task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure. It studies trajectory-level effects of interleaved cloud participation rather than per-query routing decisions.

entry.title: Back to the Future: Reverse-Consequence Modeling for Long-Horizon Particle Dynamics

author.name: Leyan Zhang, Nantian He, Jiajun Ma, Yanpeng Zhao, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: ReStep reverses the conventional forward-prediction paradigm for physical dynamics: a stochastic model first predicts the final state (often more predictable for dissipative systems), then Anchored Diffusion generates goal-conditioned intermediate trajectories. This reduces the cumulative-error drift that plagues autoregressive long-horizon rollouts. Relevant to mechanical understanding and robotic control.

entry.title: Auditing Future-Memory Use in Point-in-Time Language Agents

author.name: Rongtian Ye

entry.summary: The paper audits whether point-in-time agents covertly use memorized post-cutoff facts, using prespecified directional predictions from closed-book probes across 48 historical company-comparison tasks with paired real versus anonymized identity runs. Neither Qwen nor DeepSeek showed the predicted shift toward better-remembered companies, suggesting no detectable leakage advantage in this setting.

entry.title: Auditing LLM Program Search for Bermudan Stopping with Primal--Dual Certificates

author.name: Yuhua Qian

entry.summary: The paper audits LLM-driven program search over Python exercise policies for Bermudan options using primal-dual bounds with Monte Carlo error accounting. Across 24 generation attempts and ablations, no generated program reliably improves on Ridge LSMC beyond sampling uncertainty, with holdout gaps within 0.002.

entry.title: TraceSampler: Making Sampling Errors Predictable and Correctable for Accelerated Generative Sampling

author.name: George Matthew (University of Exeter, United Kingdom), Guoqiang Zhang (University of Exeter, United Kingdom), Kenta Niwa (NTT Communication Science Laboratories, Japan)

entry.summary: TraceSampler is a post-training method that corrects endpoint errors from low-step sampling in continuous-time generative models without modifying the pretrained model. It models endpoint error as a sample-specific prediction problem, supervised by higher-step reference integration over the same interval, using a compact representation combining shared residual structure, trace-derived directions, and low-rank factors. This makes accelerated sampling errors predictable and correctable.

entry.title: Probabilistic Multi-Source Data Selection via Learnable Categorical Priors: Variance Reduction and Guaranteed Derandomization

author.name: Shizhan Cai, Qixin Zhang, Siyuan Ma, Siyuan Liang, Yongcheng Jing, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a new probabilistic relaxation for multi-source bilevel data selection that uses learnable categorical priors to parameterize distributions supported only on feasible data subsets, yielding lossless rounding. This addresses unstable gradient estimation and infeasible rounding in existing relaxations, with variance reduction and derandomization guarantees.

entry.title: StimFlow: Synthesizing Brain Activity from Images via Stimulus-conditioned Flow Matching

author.name: Bui Van Hung, Dang Thanh Vu, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Mai Tien Dung, Soo-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: StimFlow synthesizes fMRI brain activity directly in native voxel space from images using stimulus-conditioned flow matching with a linear path, combining structural DINOv2 and semantic CLIP features to match the cortical visual hierarchy. This generative view aligns training and inference distributions, achieving competitive performance with single samples and less reliance on trial averaging.

entry.title: ELECT: Settling Identity Before Rendering for Scalable Story Visualization

author.name: Mehrajul Abadin Miraj, Md. Mahmudul Hasan, Meherun Farzana, Aniket Joarder, Mahmudul Hasan, Abir Chakraborty Partha, Md. Ahasanul Alam, Redwan Ahmed Rizvee, Md. Fahim Arefin, Md Mahmudur Rahman, Md. Tanvir Alam, Md Mosaddek Khan

entry.summary: ELECT is a training-free story visualization method that resolves cross-frame entity identity before final rendering via language-guided scene-entity mapping and stationary anchors elected from the model's own drafts, making per-frame rendering cost independent of story length. It achieves 8.3 seconds per frame under 20 GB VRAM from 10 to 1000 scenes where joint attention exceeds 96 GB at 32 scenes, with strong results on a new Story50 long-story benchmark.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Time Series Forecasting with Learnable Decomposition and Manifold Dynamics

author.name: Sarang Rajendra Patil, Vishal Fenn, Mengjia Xu

entry.summary: HyperForecast is the first long-term time series forecasting framework operating in hyperbolic space, exploiting the observation that cascaded decomposition induces a frequency hierarchy aligned with hyperbolic geometry. It models multiscale structure with learnable decomposition and manifold dynamics. The approach offers a theoretically motivated alternative to Euclidean forecasters.

entry.title: PID-Gated Continual Prompt Adaptation Under Noisy Feedback

author.name: Zhentao Xu

entry.summary: The paper introduces lightweight PID-control-inspired gates that decide when noisy user feedback should trigger a lasting prompt update for deployed LLM agents in non-stationary environments, tracking current error, accumulating evidence, and rolling back harmful edits. The gates are benchmarked against baselines and advanced optimizers like TextGrad and GEPA across drifting tasks.

entry.title: PATMT2: Two-stage domain adaptation for multilingual patent translation

author.name: Xiaowei Su, Xusen Cheng

entry.summary: PatMT2 adapts the Tencent Hy-MT2-7B translation model (released August 2026) via a two-stage LoRA pipeline for Chinese/English/Japanese/Korean patent translation, reaching 43.39-43.57 macro-average BLEU, up to +8.8 over the base and beating Qwen3-32B on that average. The paper also probes cross-lingual retention across 38 languages, finding four low-resource languages collapse into reproducible failure modes.

entry.title: DTA-GT: Direction- and Topology-Aware Graph Transformer for Neural Network Representation Learning

author.name: Yuxiang Zeng, Kun Xie, Yang Wang, Jigang Wen, Xiaocan Li, Guangxing Zhang, Gaogang Xie, Jiannong Cao

entry.summary: DTA-GT is a graph transformer for neural architecture representation that preserves directed computational semantics encoder-wide, using direction- and topology-aware node initialization, Magnetic Laplacian spectral encoding, and direction-dual attention. It targets architecture attribute predictors that estimate accuracy or latency to cheapen neural architecture search. It matters because treating edge direction as a local cue loses the global computational flow that defines DAG-structured architectures.

entry.title: Generative Flow on Symbolic Abstractions for Embodiment Capability Discovery

author.name: Youwei Yu, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: FOSA discovers robot embodiment-specific capabilities by learning a grounded task generator that constructs symbolic task skeletons via a Generative Flow Network, avoiding LLM-sampled curricula based on semantic plausibility rather than physical feasibility. Skeletons are composed of verified skills grounded in the robot's affordances, producing curricula that surface non-obvious but learnable behaviors. This improves long-horizon skill training over handcrafted task distributions.

entry.title: Bottlenecked semantic compression by representation reconstruction

author.name: Xiaoya Tang, Shilong Liu, Daniel Smolyak, Xiwen Li, Quynh Nguyen, Tolga Tasdizen

entry.summary: Proposes ReConV, a reconstruction-guided token condensation method for Vision Transformers that summarizes the full visual sequence into a compact Summary Bank and retains only tokens whose information is poorly captured, as indicated by reconstruction residuals. A lightweight position-conditioned decoder identifies shared versus poorly reconstructed information at each compression layer. Improves efficiency on classification and dense prediction tasks.

entry.title: zPocket: Better Pocket Finding with Frozen Co-Folding Features

author.name: Tally Portnoi, Allison M Keys, Benjamin R DiFrancesco, Nate Gruver

entry.summary: The paper introduces PocketWatch, a curated benchmark of biologically relevant ligand pockets stratified by sequence and structural similarity and crypticity, addressing the problem that existing benchmarks fall within co-folding model training distributions. It then develops zPocket, which trains pocket-prediction heads on frozen features from co-folding models for improved binding-site prediction.

entry.title: AffectWorld: Benchmarking Emotion-Driven Future World Prediction

author.name: Changhao Song, Yacong Chen, Hui Gao, Yazhou Zhang, Peng Zhang

entry.summary: AffectWorld is a benchmark for evaluating whether world models can predict emotion-driven world evolution, testing the Emotion-Action-World State chain through three consistency tasks. It contains 1,498 annotated everyday videos plus a 233-sample counterfactual subset that varies an agent's emotion under fixed scenarios. Existing world model benchmarks mostly test physical plausibility, leaving social-affective reasoning untested.

entry.title: Readout Scaling Shapes Sparse Feature Recovery

author.name: Brain Xiao, Sarah Wilson

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how readout scaling affects what sparse autoencoders learn, using readout-canonicalized decision-space coordinates to remove singular-value gains while preserving decision information. In controlled experiments, training in the coordinate space where factors were generated restores sparse-factor recovery, raising mean recovery from 0.506 to 0.913 at condition number 100. The work provides concrete guidance for SAE training design in interpretability research.

entry.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Kaiyuan Chen, Shuangyu Xie, Uksang Yoo, Xinyue Zhu, Cael Magner, Alvin Zhu, Daehwa Kim, Eric Heiden, Erwin Coumans, Miles Macklin, Spencer Huang, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: RoboSimStudio is an interactive toolkit for real-to-sim calibration of robot manipulation, making solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable for both humans and coding agents. Built on the open Newton simulator, it supports visual evaluation, force-feedback, and agentic Real2Sim2Real workflows.

entry.title: Learning Non-Gaussian SEMs with Conditional Risk, and Why the Direction of Recursion Matters

author.name: Ujas Shah, Panagiota Birmpa, Rebecca Morrison

entry.summary: The paper shows that replacing conditional variance with conditional risk in recursive structure identification extends variance-based SEM discovery from Gaussian to non-Gaussian noise, with existing methods recovered as the least-squares special case. Exploiting the noise distribution improves structure recovery, and the authors analyze why top-down versus bottom-up recursion directions matter. A theory contribution to causal discovery.

entry.title: Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning of LLMs in Learnable Low-Rank Subspaces

author.name: Chuang Tong, Ling Chen

entry.summary: AdaSub-ZO is a forward-only fine-tuning framework for LLMs that iteratively learns layer-wise low-rank projection matrices from finite-difference feedback, replacing fixed random subspaces that often misalign with task descent directions. A subspace momentum mechanism smooths noisy zeroth-order gradient estimates. This targets memory-efficient fine-tuning where backpropagation is infeasible (e.g., black-box or privacy-constrained settings).

entry.title: Approximation in Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Yuanfan Li, Zihan Zhang, Yiming Ying, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: Provides approximation theory for contrastive representation learning, showing that the population target (pointwise mutual information) is approximated by inner-product models via a link to compact operators. D-dimensional inner-product models perform rank-D spectral approximation with error controlled by spectral decay, explaining why standard contrastive objectives work.

entry.title: When Participant Disjoint Validation Is Not Enough to Establish Generalization in Parkinson's Gait Classification

author.name: Md. Sifat, Sania Akter, Akif Islam, Md. Ekramul Hamid

entry.summary: This paper shows that participant-disjoint cross-validation can still yield optimistic generalization estimates when acquisition site and diagnosis are structurally dependent, using Parkinson's disease classification from pressure-walkway features across 133 WearGait-PD participants. Site alone achieved AUC 0.955, exceeding the gait-feature model at 0.882, revealing confounding by acquisition site. The work is a cautionary methodological analysis for clinical ML validation.

entry.title: FunDM: Cheap & Label-Free Decision Models from Frozen Language Models

author.name: Ujjawal K. Panchal

entry.summary: FunDM trains a small label-free decision head that distills a frozen language model's answer probabilities via KL divergence, recovering about 99% of the full model's multiple-choice accuracy while using two-thirds of its layers. Applied to Qwen3-8B, an existing open model, a 24-layer variant reaches 75.0% mean accuracy versus 75.7% for the full model with roughly 1.56x throughput gains.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Regret Bounds for Monotone Stochastic Optimization under Semi-Bandit Feedback

author.name: Tao Hu, Rohan Ghuge

entry.summary: The paper gives a general online-to-offline reduction for strongly monotone stochastic optimization under semi-bandit feedback achieving the improved Otilde(sqrt(nT)) regret rate, matching problem-specific results for optimal stopping and Pandora's box. Prior general reductions only achieved Otilde(n sqrt(T)). This answers an open question about whether general reductions can reach the better rate.

entry.title: On Sleep-Wake Disorder Identification from Polysomnographic Representations

author.name: Alvise Dei Rossi, Luigi Fiorillo, Giuliana Monachino, Alessia Calzoni, Julia van der Meer, Markus H. Schmidt, Claudio L. A. Bassetti, Silvia Santini, Francesca Faraci

entry.summary: The study compares frozen representations from large-scale self-supervised polysomnography foundation models versus sleep-staging supervised encoders for identifying six sleep-wake and circadian disorder groups in 7,906 held-out PSGs under a common downstream framework. Although PSG foundation models beat small supervised baselines, the ordering reversed when supervised pretraining reached comparable scale and modality coverage. This is an informative evaluation result for medical foundation model claims.

entry.title: ProTok: Unified Protein Tokenization via Modular Multi-Codebook Quantization

author.name: Romain Hardy, Xiaoman Zhang, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: ProTok is a unified protein tokenizer mapping sequence, structure, and functional annotations into a modular discrete vocabulary via product quantization with per-modality codebook groups and modality dropout, supporting inference from any modality subset without retraining. It ranks first among structure-only tokenizers on most StructTokenBench splits.

entry.title: Deterministic Prediction as Global Velocity: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecast

author.name: Jiajing Hu, Xu Han, Li-Ping Liu

entry.summary: DV-Flow is a unified flow-matching formulation for probabilistic time-series forecasting that embeds a deterministic predictor as a parallel velocity component rather than as the transport path endpoint, stabilizing joint training. This avoids the deep computational graphs and disrupted transport paths that plague existing hybrid approaches.

entry.title: Diagnosing Generalization Boundaries in AI-Based Vulnerability Detection via Calibrated Embedding Distances

author.name: Konstantin Ievtushenko, Ralf L\"ammel, Jan J\"urjens

entry.summary: The paper shows that calibrated embedding geometry with whitened nearest-neighbor scoring exposes hidden generalization boundaries in learning-based vulnerability detection, using CodeBERT and Qwen2.5-Coder on strictly paired vulnerable/patched code under pattern, project, and temporal shifts. Accuracy drops by over 35 percentage points under shift, with distance scores providing OOD detection (mean AUROC 0.739).

entry.title: JSIR: An Audio-Aligned, Multi-Task Dataset of Jazz Standard Recordings

author.name: Sihun Lee, Dasaem Jeong

entry.summary: Releases JSIR, a dataset of 267 recordings of 44 jazz standards (25.6 hours) with beat, downbeat, chord, and section annotations by a jazz musician across multiple revision passes, roughly 3.7 times the audio of the closest existing resource. Models trained with JSIR improve jazz performance on other jazz benchmarks, raising a state-of-the-art beat tracker's downbeat F-measure.

entry.title: When do explicit penalties improve flow matching?

author.name: Lea Kunkel, Alberto Gonz\'alez-Sanz, Sophie Langer

entry.summary: Analyzes when constraint penalties in flow matching actually improve generative accuracy, comparing penalized and unpenalized models through expected squared 2-Wasserstein error for both vector-valued and functional (Hilbert-space) data. The paper derives geometric criteria for constraint violations and solves the statistical comparison explicitly for specific settings, motivated by physics-informed flow matching.

entry.title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One

author.name: Alexander E. Black, Christoph Hertrich, Stefan Kober, Georg Loho

entry.summary: The paper resolves the core open problem on virtual extension complexity of polytopes, showing it can be exponentially smaller than standard extension complexity, and proves matroid base polytopes can have exponential virtual extension complexity. These results are motivated by the complexity of neural networks and relate to compositions of linear programs.

entry.title: When Repeated Measurements Hurt Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Yixiang Liu, Ruizhe Deng, Bibhas Chakraborty, Qiong Zhang, Yan Shuo Tan

entry.summary: Across six tabular foundation models, the authors show that repeated measurements at the same inputs can improve predictions at those inputs while degrading predictions elsewhere, an effect most frequent at low noise and amplified by irrelevant features. They trace the failure to a protocol mismatch: PFN-style IID pretraining treats repeated inputs as fresh evidence about the input distribution rather than about the response function.

entry.title: Calibrating LLM Explanations to Human Decisions with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dong Shu, Ziyang Guo, Negar Kamali, Matthew Groh, Jessica Hullman

entry.summary: Introduces HD-RL, an RL framework that optimizes LLM explanations for human decision quality rather than task performance or human preference, using a human decision simulator calibrated on observed decisions as a proxy reward. Applied to AI-generated text detection, with an initial human data collection phase.

entry.title: Where Did We Go Wrong? Localizing Errors to Repair Multi-Turn Conversations

author.name: Alessandro Morosini, Wei Sun, Georgia Perakis

entry.summary: The authors introduce Loci, a framework for localizing corrupted inferences in multi-turn LLM conversations, where a single misinterpretation can poison the assistant's working state and derail the dialogue. Instead of discarding the conversation, Loci locates and revises the specific erroneous turn while preserving valid information. This addresses a practical failure recovery problem for conversational assistants with gradually revealed user intent.

entry.title: A Step in the Right Place: Understanding and Optimizing Timestep Placement in Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Shutian Zheng, Zhihong Yu, Linye Wei, Zeyang Zhang, Meng Li

entry.summary: The authors show that in continuous diffusion language models, the placement of a fixed number of denoising steps along the trajectory substantially changes final latent representations and decoded token distributions. They introduce StepTune, an algorithm that searches for timestep placements that preserve quality with few denoising steps. This is a practical efficiency lever for an emerging parallel text-generation paradigm.

entry.title: Rule vs.Consequence: Dissociable Internal Representations of Moral Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Eugenie Shi

entry.summary: The paper probes whether LLMs internally distinguish rule-framed from consequence-framed moral questions, using a 2x2 factorial dataset crossing reasoning style with judgment polarity plus a cleanroom conflict-pair test set. Linear probing shows distinct internal representations rather than mere lexical sensitivity, relevant to deployment in morally sensitive contexts.

entry.title: BRIDGE: Selective Boundary Repair with Dependency Graph Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Encheng Su, Pengze Li, Ziheng Hua, Qiucheng Yu, Jianyu Wu, Chen Tang, Yizhou Wang, Lintao Wang, Junjia Xiang, Xinzhu Ma, Xi Chen, Shixiang Tang, Houqiang Li, Xi Chen, Aoran Wang

entry.summary: BRIDGE is a verifiable runtime control framework treating broken inter-agent handoffs as selective interventions over explicit dependency graphs, supported by a fault-attribution and calibration pipeline. It targets the pervasive failure mode where task context is omitted, misrouted, or ignored at collaboration interfaces despite locally plausible agent responses.

entry.title: Revisiting the Estimation of Unigram Surprisal in Computational Psycholinguistics

author.name: Zachary Hopton, Francesco Ignazio Re, Samuel Kiegeland, Andreas Opedal, Eleanor Chodroff, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: The paper argues that estimating contextual surprisal from neural language models while estimating unigram surprisal from independent corpus counts breaks their probabilistic link and introduces mismatch error. It proposes three principles for unigram surprisal estimation, including deriving both quantities from the same language model, and operationalizes this with a Monte Carlo estimator. This has direct implications for reading-time studies using surprisal theory.

entry.title: Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Tiantian Liu, Meng Wan, Zhiqiang Liang, Jue Wang, Ningming Nie, Yangang Wang

entry.summary: EG-Sparse is a training-free sparse attention framework for video diffusion transformers that adapts the competition domain per attention head: low-entropy heads use a grouped cross-head pool while high-entropy heads retain per-row local selection. A controlled diagnostic isolates the effect of the competition rule on token selection.

entry.title: Channel Match: Calibrating Shape Latents for Few-Step 3D Generation

author.name: Di Yang, Zhihao Li, Yanhai Xiong, Yufei Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a few-step distillation framework for native 3D flow-based generators using continuous self-consistency training, a custom JVP FlashAttention kernel, and analytic velocity regression for sparse structured 3D latents. It also identifies and addresses a previously overlooked failure mode of sampling-induced channel distribution shift in few-step native 3D generation.

entry.title: SurgCast: Action-Conditioned Future Skeletons for Controllable Surgical World Models

author.name: Wanhao Liu, Rulin Zhou, Liangjing Shao, Zhaocheng Lin, Dongyue Li, Jinsong Lin, Guoheng Ma, Hangheng Yang, Zhiqing Tang, Jing Chen, Panshuo Li, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: SurgCast predicts future instrument skeletons from current structure, robot state, and planned actions, then uses the forecast to control surgical video generation via dual-path injection of skeleton geometry and motion descriptors. Teacher and four-step causal student models improve quality and instrument-consistency metrics on SutureBot and porcine cholecystectomy data.

entry.title: MFlowHOI: Whole-Body Human-Object Interaction Generation via Part-Aware MeanFlow

author.name: Qiang He, Yonghao Zhang, Yinda Zhang, Chenyu Meng, Liufei Ouyang, Haoxiang Hu, Cangjun Gao, Xiaoming Deng, Cuixia Ma, Hongan Wang

entry.summary: MFlowHOI generates whole-body human-object interactions in a single step using a Contact-Aware Multipart RVQVAE that organizes body, hand, object, and contact signals into a structured latent space, with an ST-DiT modeling temporal dynamics via MeanFlow. It avoids the high inference cost of iterative diffusion or test-time optimization while coordinating heterogeneous HOI components.

entry.title: Not Every Cue Is Evidence: Cue Supportability for Forensic Distillation in Face Forgery Detection

author.name: Binjia Zhou, Dawei Luo, Shuai Chen, Feng Xu, Haoyuan Li, Jia wen Seow, Jiachi Wang, Jie Lei, Zunlei Feng, Yijun Bei

entry.summary: Identifies the correct-answer-wrong-evidence (CAWE) failure in explainable face forgery detection, where students distilled with privileged pipeline-derived cues articulate evidence they cannot perceive in low-quality inputs. A dual supportability audit filters privileged cues before distillation so explanations are grounded in actually observable image features.

entry.title: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception

author.name: Mengtan Zhang, Yu Ma, Shiqi Jiang, Yi Feng, Wei Ye, Xieyuanli Chen, Hanli Wang, Qijun Chen, Rui Fan

entry.summary: The paper addresses recovering accurate metric depth from generalizable monocular relative depth foundation models, proposing an interpretable metricization that handles spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships without relying solely on global affine transforms or fragile completion networks. It extends the authors' previous work to improve generalizable depth perception.

entry.title: HierarchiRetina: A Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Grading Cascade with Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Md Asif Uddin, Niloy Farhan, Rafeed Rahman, Md. Golam Rabiul Alam

entry.summary: HierarchiRetina is a screening-segmentation-grading cascade for diabetic retinopathy featuring HSMoE-AUNet, a U-Net with sparse heterogeneous mixture-of-experts blocks, plus explicit handling of ungradable images and end-to-end error propagation measurement. It provides inspectable intermediate outputs for clinical trustworthiness.

entry.title: WorldRecon: Generative Multi-View Mesh Reconstruction for Large-Scale 3D World

author.name: Mengchen Zhang, Yang Li, Chunshi Wang, Tong Wu, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: WorldRecon recovers complete, large-scale 3D scene meshes from unposed RGB images by using a coarse global point cloud and estimated poses as a scaffold, partitioning scenes into overlapping blocks for a 3D generative model. It augments TRELLIS.2 with reconstruction-based conditioning to leverage imperfect geometric priors while plausibly completing unobserved surfaces.

entry.title: Axiom-0: Hierarchical Self-Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Renbin Shu, Jing Yang, Xiangyuan You, Guolin Qiu, Yufei Xia, Yiming Zhu, Nanjun Dai, Fei Zhang, Feng Wu, Keke Tang

entry.summary: Axiom-0 is a vision-language-action policy that improves generalization to unfamiliar task compositions through hierarchical self-refinement: intra-VLM representation refinement strengthens intermediate features via consistency supervision, while VLM-action interface refinement recursively updates conditioning before action generation. The joint optimization targets both representation quality and its use for control. It contributes to the active effort to make VLA policies reliable across tasks and layouts.

entry.title: Hybrid Context Forests and Bilateral Viterbi Matching for 3D Rib Centerline Tracing in CT

author.name: Quan Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces ribline, an open-source three-stage framework for automatic extraction and anatomical numbering of all 24 rib centerlines in thoracic CT, combining an anatomy-anchored coordinate frame, a hybrid Semantic Context Forest plus 3D U-Net detector, and global bilateral Viterbi matching. It targets clinically important applications such as fracture detection, unfolded rib visualization, and surgical navigation. The method addresses hard cases like bone confluence, cartilage bridges, and kyphotic poses.

entry.title: From Field to Planning: Learning Temporal Polar Gradient Fields for Vision-based AAV Trajectory Planning in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Haowen Gao, Zhan Chen, Yinuo Xu, Yifeng Niu, Mengyun Wang, Chao Yan

entry.summary: The paper proposes F2P, a two-stage learning framework providing accurate and efficient safety gradients for aerial vehicle trajectory planning in dynamic environments, using an ego-centric polar occupancy representation matched to onboard camera geometry. This avoids the heavy computational burden and conservatism of static-map and obstacle-tracking approaches.

entry.title: Look Before You Move: Agent-Interface-Aligned Supervision for Open-World Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Ronghe Qiu, Teli Ma, Jiaming Zhou, Zeying Gong, Yiting He, Qiang Huang, Junwei Liang

entry.summary: The paper introduces AIDA, a data collection pipeline where a teacher directly selects and executes actions through the deployed agent's skill interface rather than converting planned trajectories into high-level labels, with teachers that maintain target visibility and recover lost targets for mobile manipulation. This addresses the key problem that shortest-path progress supervision gives little signal about where an agent should look.

entry.title: Same Goal, Different Words: Spatial Instruction Sensitivity in World-Action Models

author.name: Ali-Adeeb Abbas, Esmaeil Seraj, Behrad Toghi, Taskin Padir

entry.summary: This study evaluates instruction-sensitivity of world-action models across 864 rollouts from three models in four scenes, finding that describing spatial relations via the reference object rather than the target object reduces stable placement rates by 12.2 percentage points on average. It identifies relation reversals in language understanding and shows images can disrupt otherwise correct text-only interpretations. The work exposes brittleness of robot policies to instruction paraphrasing.

entry.title: Locomotion with Online Awareness of Dynamics for Precision Footholds

author.name: Kunzhao Ren, Zhishuo Zhu, Xiaobin Xiong

entry.summary: LOAD is a perceptive locomotion framework for narrow-beam traversal under unknown payloads, combining explicit inertial estimates with implicit dynamics features from separate recurrent modules on proprioception, with a height-map teacher distilled into a depth-based student. Experiments in simulation and on hardware show implicit features speed training, explicit inertial estimation boosts traversal success, and their combination approaches teacher-level performance.

entry.title: Collaborative Planning for UAV-UGV Teams under Operational Constraints via Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion

author.name: Zihao Deng, Qianhuang Li, Maggie Wigness, John Rogers, Donghyun Kim, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a masked error-bounded neuro-symbolic diffusion method for collaborative UAV-UGV planning under operational constraints, addressing two limitations of masked diffusion models: entropy-guided scheduling's distributional alignment assumption and the reliance on differentiable constraints for diffusion-time optimization. The setting pairs energy-limited aerial coverage with road-constrained UGV mobile recharging stations.

entry.title: Linear Regression Beyond Covariance: Latent Slope Spectra from Higher-Order Cumulants

author.name: Anirban Nath, Ming Yuan

entry.summary: The authors formalize the latent slope spectrum, showing ordinary least squares is a variance-weighted barycenter of distinct linear effects carried by latent components mixed within an observed regressor. Higher-order mixed cumulants can separate these components when the spectrum is sufficiently parsimonious, e.g., fourth-order cumulants identify the slope pair in a scalar one-confounder model via a small linear system. This extends linear regression theory beyond second-order covariance information.

entry.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos

author.name: Wei Lin

entry.summary: Reels-RSI treats explainer videos as programs (script, storyboard, per-frame animation code) rendered deterministically, enabling audit and diff-based revision, and implements program-level recursive self-improvement where check findings are compiled into enforceable rules. It is an open-source reel director applicable to any agent harness, improving at the program level rather than in weights.

entry.title: Are Multimodal Benchmarks Really Useful? Item-Level Multimodal Benchmark Diagnosis via Structure-Response Co-Calibration

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Weixin Zeng, Ziheng Zhang, Jiuyang Tang, Xiang Zhao

entry.summary: SRCoD is a diagnosis framework that identifies shortcut items in multimodal benchmarks, where questions can be answered from a single modality or answer-option regularities alone. It combines intrinsic item structure with extrinsic model response behavior for item-level assessment of modality dependence.

entry.title: LYNX: Analytical Program Synthesis via Grounding and Closed-Loop Refinement

author.name: Ruichen Xia, Xiao Han, Dingyu Yang, Luwei Yang, Sai Wu, Dongxiang Zhang, Binhui Yao, Gang Chen

entry.summary: LYNX is a multi-agent framework that translates natural language into executable analytical programs over real databases by treating the task as schema- and knowledge-constrained synthesis with closed-loop planning, generation, verification, and refinement. It aims to fix brittle execution and semantic inconsistency in LLM-powered data analytics on complex real-world schemas.

entry.title: What Survives When Activation Steering Is Used as Memory

author.name: Vedant Jumle

entry.summary: This paper tests whether activation steering vectors can serve as long-term agent memory by storing experience-induced shifts in late-layer states of frozen models, filed under whitened gist keys and reapplied in later sessions. Using pre-registered experiments on Qwen3.5-2B and 9B with cross-family judges, it argues such shifts can only preserve question-independent content since attention recomputes question-dependent effects in context.

entry.title: GesBench: When and Where Do Multimodal Language Models Perceive Social Meaning?

author.name: Zonghuan Li, Hayley Hung, Chirag Raman

entry.summary: Introduces GesBench, a benchmark evaluating cue-level, incremental social perception in multimodal LLMs using cumulative sub-utterance clips grounded in Gestalt principles of multimodal communication. It measures when models form stable interpretations of speaker intent, contrasting with existing benchmarks that only assess final answers over complete episodes.

entry.title: A Decade of PhotoMappers: A Longitudinal Study of Crowdsourced Disaster Photos Geolocalization with Vision-Language Models and Geospatial Reasoning

author.name: Hao Li, Wenping Yin, Fabian Deuser, Jia Jia, Ziqi Liu, Levente Juh\'asz, Fan Zhang, Filip Biljecki

entry.summary: Using over a decade of crowdsourced disaster imagery from PhotoMappers, this study analyzes the changing geography of disaster information and benchmarks vision-language models on cross-view geolocalization against human geographic interpretation. It combines longitudinal spatial analysis with street view and remote sensing imagery for actionable geospatial intelligence.

entry.title: Self-Representation Alignment in Diffusion Models for Video Background Music Generation

author.name: Jincheng Zhang, Gy\"orgy Fazekas, Charalampos Saitis

entry.summary: U-SRA enhances a diffusion U-Net by aligning weaker early-layer representations (high noise) with better later-layer representations (low noise) during training via an alignment loss. The method is applied to video background music generation, addressing the finding that internal diffusion representations are insufficiently meaningful.

entry.title: Engram Injection: A Study of Temporal Validity in Parametric Language-Model Memory

author.name: Sam Siavoshian, Omar Ramadan, Amir K. Saeed, Benjamin A. Johnson, Benjamin M. Rodriguez

entry.summary: Engram Injection stores facts in LoRA adapters and supplies the current time via FiLM conditioning on a frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct model, testing whether a model can learn fact-validity changes in its parameters and answer from a question plus the clock. The study includes careful audits for training/test leakage across 127,760 inputs and compares against prompting and retrieval baselines. It addresses temporal knowledge editing, an important limitation of parametric memory.

entry.title: Computational Reflective Equilibrium for Agentic AI: A Rawlsian Alignment Scaffold for Governance

author.name: Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: This work proposes agentic reflective equilibrium (ARE), a computational framework inspired by Rawlsian philosophy that scaffolds ethical alignment inside agent harnesses, linking system prompt principles, considered judgments, tool evidence, and candidate actions through typed support and attack relations. It aims to make case-by-case alignment of tool-using agents more structured and auditable.

entry.title: Pollard: Governed Semantic Execution Trees for Framework-Independent AI Agent Control and Replay

author.name: Muntaser Syed, Marius C. Silaghi

entry.summary: Pollard is a framework-independent agent runtime based on governed semantic execution trees that unify execution, governance, and replay identities, supporting verified replay without re-invoking operations and transactional coordination across concurrent workers. The authors provide formal guarantees about what logs must record and demonstrate invariant-preserving execution across replicas.

entry.title: Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking

author.name: Zhimeng Jiang, Yuening Li, Ruixiao Sun, Yuanzhen Lin, Kun Jin, Chuan He, Liang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Chain Dimension Scaling, a third scaling axis for recommendation rankers that repeatedly applies one parameter-shared feature-interaction block, adding no parameters as chain length grows. CDS supports both a compression regime (shallow blocks, longer chains matching deeper baselines) and scalable growth, reducing parameter, communication, and training costs for industrial ranking models.

entry.title: Learning Perceptual Geometry of Natural Odor Mixtures from LLM-Derived Descriptors

author.name: Farhad Pashakhanloo, Venkatesh N. Murthy

entry.summary: Uses LLMs as scalable surrogates to derive perceptual descriptions for over 1,200 food odor mixtures with more than 8,000 molecular components, then shows language-derived representations can predict held-out mixture similarity. The work extends odor perception modeling from single molecules to complex natural mixtures.

entry.title: What Makes a Latent Space Shared? Direct and Recoverable Compatibility in Motion VAEs

author.name: Iago Brito, Walcy Rios, Lucas Fernandes, Kaiki de Oliveira, Arlindo Galv\~ao Filho

entry.summary: This work disentangles what it means for a latent space to be shared, separating recoverable correspondence, direct compatibility, and decoder reuse in motion VAEs. Experiments on HumanML3D show that even identically parameterized schemas produce low raw cross-space retrieval and cosine agreement while remaining almost perfectly recoverable after linear calibration, and that only a few paired clips suffice to fix direct compatibility. The paper clarifies a common conceptual conflation in multi-schema representation learning.

entry.title: When Should Enterprise Policy Decisions Be Learned, and When Should They Be Reasoned?

author.name: Hyojung Han, Ryangkyung Kang, Youngeun Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: Using a fixed 27B Korean enterprise model, this study compares decision mechanisms for policy-answering agents: a generated JSON object versus a single constrained token, with and without prior reasoning. On 2800 in-distribution items accuracy is similar, but restart stability differs by roughly tenfold (3.00% versus 0.29% of actions flip), and on a sealed 300-item benchmark with hidden executable policy labels, reasoning shows benefits. The work offers practical guidance on structuring enterprise agent decision layers.

entry.title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents

author.name: Taeyun Roh, Suhyeong Park, Gijin Kim, Wonjune Jang, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies memory modality in VLM-based GUI agents, finding that the preferred memory representation is strongly step-dependent rather than fixed. Motivated by this, it introduces SwitchMem, which adaptively selects memory modality across interaction steps for better reuse of past experience.

entry.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs

author.name: Yu Mi, Licheng Pan, Jiayi Zhu, Qirui Liu, Yitong Qiao, Changtong Xu, Tao Wei, Fei Sun, Zhixuan Chu, Kui Ren

entry.summary: The paper identifies modality misrouting as a recoverable failure pattern in omnimodal LLMs under audio-visual interference, where the relevant unimodal branch can still produce the correct answer even when the joint prediction is wrong. It proposes CaRe, a training-free inference-time method that uses a text-only modality probe to identify and correct misrouted evidence. This offers a lightweight route to reducing cross-modal hallucinations.

entry.title: Order-Consistent Latent Geometry for Reliable Short-Horizon Planning in World Models

author.name: Junlin Wu, Wen Fan, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper connects reliable latent planning in world models to the classical self-approaching condition, showing that terminal Euclidean distance scoring is compatible with true transition progress exactly when latent distance never reverses transition-shortest rollouts. It links violations of this condition to concrete candidate-order reversals in finite-horizon planning.

entry.title: Latent Algorithmic Structure Precedes Grokking: A Mechanistic Study of ReLU MLPs on Modular Arithmetic

author.name: Anand Swaroop

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study finds that ReLU MLPs trained on modular arithmetic learn near-binary square wave input weights rather than the sinusoidal distributions previously reported, with output Fourier phases satisfying a phase-sum relation that persists even when training fails to grok. The results suggest latent algorithmic structure precedes the grokking transition.

entry.title: Physics-Informed State Space Models for Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

author.name: Phil Aupke, Muhammad Hassan, Khalid Ali, Seema, Andreas Kassler, Andreas Theocharis

entry.summary: The paper proposes combining a differentiable photovoltaic conversion model with the PowerMamba selective state space backbone, using physics-residual decomposition so the physics module provides a structured baseline and the SSM learns corrections from weather forecasts. This yields physically plausible, accurate day-ahead PV power forecasts.

entry.title: MvFFN: Multi-view Floor plan Feed-forward Network for Unposed Wide-Baseline Panorama Layout Reconstruction

author.name: Yuguang Li, Yichuan Deng, Zixuan Liu, Ivaylo Boyadzhiev, Xiuyuan Wu, Xinyu Zou, Linda Shapiro, Alex Colburn

entry.summary: MvFFN reconstructs camera poses and multi-room floor-plan layouts from sparse, unposed, wide-baseline RGB panoramas via a strictly local prediction design: each panorama column predicts only the observed wall plus two adjacent walls, with global layout emerging from deterministic aggregation of overlapping local predictions. This decouples pose, geometry, semantics, and layout that are otherwise tightly coupled. It targets a genuinely difficult open reconstruction setting.

entry.title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation

author.name: Ruiyang Wang, Hao-Lun Hsu, Haocheng Meng, Songqiao Xie, Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: NeST-Bayes is a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers trust in robots and their reported hypotheses in multi-robot systems using only inter-robot observation consistency, without preassigned trust relationships. It targets settings with partial observability and adversarial interference.

entry.title: Lingdan-V2: Large language models for clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine

author.name: Rui Hua, Yu Wei, Ziri Jin, Zhuo Sun, Kai Chang, Jianan Xia, Zixin Shu, Xiaodong Li, Dongmei Jia, Fei Dong, Runshun Zhang, Jian Yu, Hao Xu, Haibin Yu, Jiansheng Li, Baoyan Liu, Wenjia Wang, Xuezhong Zhou

entry.summary: Lingdan-V2 is a family of TCM language models (4B, 8B, 14B parameters) trained with staged clinical alignment: continued pretraining on TCM and clinical records, complementary reasoning supervision, and prescription-centered reinforcement learning. It formulates herbal prescription generation as structured reasoning integrating syndrome differentiation and dosage determination.

entry.title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning

author.name: Julien Roger, Sam Bodmer, Jian Qian, Benjamin Riviere

entry.summary: The paper studies average-reward RL where the Bellman operator contracts only under chain mixing, replacing mixing assumptions with a given reward-agnostic m-step mixing policy toward which the learned policy is regularized. It provides finite-time analyses of Q-learning and Q-planning with multiple regularization choices, exposing novel regularizer-dependent objects controlling contraction and exploration.

entry.title: scHFBiMamba: a bidirectional Mamba autoencoder for cardiac disease-state classification from single-nucleus RNA-seq data

author.name: Ugo Lomoio, Pietro Hiram Guzzi, Pierangelo Veltri

entry.summary: Applies a bidirectional Mamba autoencoder to single-nucleus RNA-seq profiles for joint classification of species, cell type, and disease state in heart failure. The 13.2M-parameter model achieves a 14.6x parameter reduction versus a dense denoising autoencoder baseline while producing interpretable gene attributions, evaluated on 38,275 held-out nuclei with proper statistical correction.

entry.title: Adversarial Detection for Pre-trained Classifiers via Lipschitz-Margin Analysis with Certification

author.name: Rui Zhang, Xinle Cao, Huazhen Yu, Jian Liu, Youwen Zhu

entry.summary: This paper proposes certifying that adversarial inputs within an l2 ball are detected, rather than certifying prediction invariance, providing a guarantee better matched to security-critical deployments where missed attacks are costlier than false alarms. Building on a Lipschitz-margin reduction, the approach avoids the query cost of randomized smoothing and the accuracy sacrifices of Lipschitz-constrained networks while working with pre-trained classifiers.

entry.title: SARATHI: Decoupled Data-Free Probing and Adaptive Reconstruction for Structured LLM Pruning

author.name: Sankar Behera, Dhruv Singh, Satyadev Ahlawat, Yamuna Prasad

entry.summary: SARATHI decouples neuron selection from weight reconstruction in structured LLM pruning: a data-free NMF Residual Subspace Probe scores neurons from intrinsic weight geometry (with a formal connection to Robust PCA), and Adaptive OBS reconstructs pruned weights with localized calibration in O(d^2) peak memory per layer. This avoids the domain bias and out-of-memory failures of coupled, calibration-dependent pruning methods.

entry.title: Embedding Information in Policy Randomness: Distribution-Preserving Implicit Communication in MDPs

author.name: Gongpu Chen, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: This paper shows that an agent's stochastic policy can serve as a covert communication channel: by modulating random action realizations, information can be embedded in behavior without changing the prescribed action distribution. It casts this as channel coding and proposes posterior-matching randomness modulation (PRAM) using common randomness. The result has implications for steganography and covert channels in learned agents.

entry.title: AI Representations of Mental Health Stigma: Quantifying the Gap Between AI Estimations and Human Perceptions Across Gender Groups Using GPT-Based LLMs

author.name: Soojong Kim, Hye Min Kim, Kwanho Kim, Dongdong Zhu

entry.summary: This study examines whether GPT-4 and GPT-5 (both established models) represent gendered perceptions of mental health stigma, using standard social-science measures and comparing AI estimates against the Healthy Minds Study with over 76,000 human respondents. It finds both disparities and misalignment between AI estimations and human perceptions.

entry.title: Look Back to Move Forward: Learning to Revisit for Agentic Compositional Image Generation

author.name: Zixu Wang, Xiaoran Zhao, Yahui Liu, Feng-ao Wang, Junhao Xiao, You Shu, Bing Liu, Yiting Liu, Songlei Jian, Zhiliang Tian, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: GenRevisit extends agentic text-to-image frameworks by letting the agent jointly select both the next action and the continuation state, allowing it to return to earlier images when the latest iteration has degraded, since iterative editing is not monotonic. The framework learns when to revisit prior states from interaction history to improve complex compositional generation.

entry.title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation

author.name: Kyungkeon Chung, Se Un Park, Hyejin Lee, Junyoung Park

entry.summary: ARMED is an adaptive retrieval-augmented generation framework for medication recommendation that dynamically expands retrieval based on retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance, using supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval. This avoids the noise and inflexibility of fixed retrieval pipelines in clinical recommendation.

entry.title: Answer It or Not? Towards Prompt-Adapted Adversarial Images on Vision Language Models

author.name: Shunyuan Bai, Yuchen Ren, Le Yang, Chenhao Lin, Chao Shen, Zhengyu Zhao

entry.summary: The paper identifies that existing adversarial-image privacy protections for VLMs are prompt-agnostic, indiscriminately rejecting all questions including legitimate uses. It proposes ProAda adversarial images optimized to balance rejecting harmful prompts while allowing correct responses to benign queries about the image.

entry.title: Feature-Context Consistency: Unsupervised Adversarial Detection with Drift Stability on Attributed Graphs

author.name: Firas Bayram, Maxime Cordy

entry.summary: This work proposes Context Boost (CB-RBM), an unsupervised adversarial-attack detector for attributed graphs based on the consistency between a node's attributes and its aggregated neighborhood attributes. It provides worst-case guarantees separating adversarial from benign expected scores and is designed to remain stable under natural distribution drift without labels. It matters because label scarcity and drift undermine most existing graph detectors.

entry.title: UA-Bench: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models on Underwater Acoustic Recognition

author.name: Zhe Sun, Liang An, Jiayu Yao, Ronglai Qian, Jianing Cai, Ziwei Huang, Qing Fan, Zhiyuan Yang, Yujun Cai, Hongli Cao, Yiwei Wang, Xiaoyan Wang

entry.summary: UA-Bench is presented as the first large-scale benchmark evaluating large audio-language models on underwater acoustic recognition, using carefully constructed synthetic data that models detection pulses, communication waveforms, ship-radiated noise, and propagation effects. It probes how far LALM pretraining transfers to this specialized maritime domain relevant to vessel monitoring and ocean sensing. It matters because specialized-domain transfer of general audio models is largely untested.

entry.title: TabGift: A Context-Efficient Foundation Model for Tabular Data Generation

author.name: Yu-Sheng Li, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: TabGift extends the tabular foundation model paradigm from prediction to data generation, tackling the core challenge of inferring reliable distributions from very limited context sets. It is designed for the low-data regime where generation is most needed but context is scarce. This fills a gap since tabular foundation models typically require large in-context sets for their predictive strength.

entry.title: MID: Mask-Image Distributional Divergence for Evaluating Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Vincenzo Marcian\`o, Xiaoming Zhang, Gianluca Guglielmo, Sebastien Ourselin, Michela Antonelli, Maria A. Zuluaga

entry.summary: Introduces MID, a distribution-level metric for medical image segmentation that evaluates whether a collection of predictions matches the joint image-mask distribution, unlike sample-wise metrics such as Dice or Hausdorff that require ground-truth masks per case. This enables evaluation on unlabeled data and captures population-level distributional structure. Addresses a real gap in medical segmentation evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Morphology-aware deep learning predicts colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images

author.name: Hikmat Khan, Metin N. Gurcan, Anil Parwani, Wendy L. Frankel, Wei Chen, Muhammad Khalid Khan Niazi

entry.summary: The paper presents MorphContrast, a morphology-aware contrastive multiple-instance learning framework using tissue labels as structural supervision for five-year colorectal cancer survival prediction from H&E whole-slide images. It uses TCGA-COAD/READ for morphology analysis, Alliance/CALGB 89803 (n=424) for development, and SurGen (n=218) for external validation.

entry.title: PrT-Flow: Probability-Tractable Flow Matching for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Congzhong Sun, Ning Tan

entry.summary: PrT-Flow makes flow matching probability-tractable for RL by introducing a Jacobian-Tractable Transformer with invertible sampling steps and Conditional Euler-step Training that supervises one-step displacements. It retains multimodal, multi-step action generation while enabling efficient density computation, with a proof that CET shares minimizers with the Euler-solvable objective under stated assumptions.

entry.title: DriveWLA: Unifying Future Dynamics and Scene Semantics through World-Language-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Shuzheng Wang, Haoxuan Li, Shengzhen Li, Chenxi Wu, Yajing Sun, Lu Hou, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: DriveWLA is a unified World-Language-Action model for autonomous driving built on a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture, with dedicated experts for future scene prediction, semantic understanding, and trajectory generation, connected via Cross-Expert Attention. By jointly modeling world dynamics, language semantics, and planning actions, it aims to improve end-to-end trajectory generation over pipelines that treat these capabilities separately. This reflects the growing trend of applying general multimodal foundation-model architectures to driving.

entry.title: Let the Mind Conceive, Let the Hand Achieve: Following Multimodal Instructions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Youpeng Wen, Gang Wang, Tianyu Huang, Weiwei Zhang, Zhijian Huang, Wei Chen, Xieyuanli Chen, Yunhui Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Orchestra, an agent harness for long-horizon robotic manipulation that separates task planning and execution management from action generation. It decomposes multimodal instructions into ordered subtasks, tracks progress, maintains a shared spatial context, and uses a separately trained progress evaluator to decide when to advance. This addresses acting on the right objects in the right order amid scene changes.

entry.title: The Many Morals of AI: The cautionary bias of North American news narratives in global perspective

author.name: Andrew Piper, Edie Pearman

entry.summary: Using 12,924 English-language news articles about AI from four regions since 2022, the authors use LLMs to extract implicit narrative lessons, or story morals, beyond sentiment or topic. They find North American AI coverage is uniquely characterized by cautionary framing relative to Chinese, Indian, and Middle Eastern media. The findings illuminate how media systems shape public and policy expectations of AI.

entry.title: Where Do LLM Ensemble Gains Come From? Decomposing Candidate Value, Diversity, and Aggregation

author.name: Donghwan Kim

entry.summary: This paper decomposes LLM ensemble gains under four matched comparison conditions (direct, single-slot, duplicate, multi-candidate), splitting candidate value into additional-candidate and candidate-context contrasts. It shows reported ensemble gains depend on the chosen baseline control, with a measured -8.33 pp repetition gap on MultiHop-RAG.

entry.title: ULPack: Reference-Conditioned Lossless Compression of Checkpoint Trajectories

author.name: Aniket Srinivasan Ashok (University of Waterloo)

entry.summary: ULPack is a lossless codec for model training checkpoint trajectories that conditions entropy models of ordered-integer residuals on the reference weight's exponent, which predicts displacement bit length without side information. It reduces storage by up to 27 percent versus ZipNN, 21 percent versus zstd-19, and 11.5 percent versus FM-Delta across bfloat16, float16, and float32 trajectories. This enables higher temporal resolution when studying training dynamics.

entry.title: Learning to Extrapolate in Depth with Looped Transformers

author.name: Huitao Yang, Jianhao Huang, Zixuan Wang, Baharan Mirzasoleiman

entry.summary: The authors analyze when a looped transformer block trained at depth K can be safely reused at greater depths, using all-pairs graph connectivity as a testbed. They prove that under exchangeability and symmetric positive initialization, training converges to a single-effective-parameter update rule with a finite extrapolation window whose endpoints they derive explicitly.

entry.title: Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents

author.name: Peize Li, Yingming Pu, Xingguo Xu, Yiming Cui, Yuansheng Gao, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Triage-PiEvo reformulates revision in LLM-based principle-evolving scientific agents as evidence admission: anomalies steer search immediately but only independently verified evidence can rewrite persistent principles, with retraction of contradicted ones. A staged verification gate across four scientific tasks and three backbones reduces bias from invalid revisions driven by evaluation artifacts.

entry.title: World2TS: Real-World Event Context for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Zhiding Liu, Jiqian Yang, Mingyue Cheng, Zhi Li, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: World2TS is a scalable construction pipeline for large-scale datasets aligning real-world events, interventions, and disruptions with the individual time series they affect, addressing the lack of context-aware forecasting benchmarks.
