This enables study of forecasting models that condition on event context rather than numerical history alone. It targets a well-recognized data gap in the field.

entry.title: Representation Drift in Continual Learning: LoRA versus N-gram Memory

author.name: Hao Wu

entry.summary: This empirical study measures internal representation drift in a 48-layer mixture-of-experts LLM under three continual-update mechanisms with identical data and budgets: updating only a pretrained N-gram memory, continual LoRA training, and per-task LoRA merging. It finds updating only the N-gram memory shifts base-model representations of math and code by 26%/15%, quantifying erosion of base capabilities. The work informs which components of LLMs should absorb online updates.

entry.title: DeltaNet-PC: Test-Time Memory Without Backpropagation Through Time

author.name: Todd Morrill, Richard Zemel

entry.summary: DeltaNet-PC enables test-time memorization of sequential information in predictive-coding networks without backpropagation through time, by treating the per-step memory update as a latent variable and optimizing a prediction-error energy function with local updates. This addresses BPTT's enormous memory requirements while adding sequential memory, which prior predictive-coding methods lacked. Relevant to alternative, biologically plausible training of sequence models.

entry.title: GuidanceNFT: NFT-Based Reward Fine-Tuning of Guided Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiayin Liu, Zeyu Michael Li, Bingshuo Qian, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: GuidanceNFT extends DiffusionNFT reward fine-tuning to classifier-free guided diffusion models, diagnosing that directly applying NFT to guided samples fails due to a mismatch between the reference velocity in the NFT loss and the guided distribution's score. The method optimizes rewards over the guided output distribution while retaining prompt alignment.

entry.title: Error Correction in Trained TTT Layers

author.name: Yuhe Hu, Wen Jia Hu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how test-time-training (TTT) layers revise stored associations via gradient-based fast-weight updates. It characterizes the absence of a prediction-error residual in dot-product objectives, proves equivalence conditions between inner-loop ascent and descent after reparameterization, and derives the inner gradient for the LayerNorm-based objective in TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP, identifying a prediction-derived component that cancels at the released initialization. Empirical measurements then assess functional error-correction behavior.

entry.title: Characterizing and Mitigating Distributional Bias in Physics-Informed Generative Models

author.name: Tanja Bien, Samir Darouich, Llu\'is Pastor-P\'erez, Vinh Tong, Loay Mualem, Mathias Niepert

entry.summary: The paper identifies a conflict in residual-regularized diffusion models with physics constraints: constraint satisfaction can degrade data fidelity through two failure modes, avoidance of states with high residual sensitivity and leakage to feasible states outside the data support. The authors propose a data-anchored penalty that weights prediction errors by residual sensitivity to mitigate this bias.

entry.title: DR-APO: Decoupled-Representation Advantage-Guided Policy Optimization from Continuous Control to Embodied Navigation

author.name: Runhua Zhang, Yingjie Niu, Chao Li

entry.summary: DR-APO proposes a representation-agnostic policy optimization interface for generative RL policies (diffusion, flow-matching), decoupling the optimization from the policy's internal generation process to avoid weak update signals from accumulated likelihood ratios. The method aims to unify continuous control and embodied navigation training across policy classes.

entry.title: One-Layer Transformers Provably Learn In-Context K-Nearest Neighbor Prediction with Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Lyumin Wu, Yuan Cao

entry.summary: The paper proves that a one-layer transformer trained with chain-of-thought can learn in-context K-nearest-neighbor prediction, extending prior work showing one-layer transformers learn 1-NN without CoT. This provides a fully analyzable theoretical setting for understanding how CoT enables capabilities that attention alone cannot express.

entry.title: Masked Attention Pooling Is Invariant to Padding and Permutation: A Formal Proof in Lean

author.name: Yusuf Khaled Sadek, Enes Yilmaz

entry.summary: The paper formally proves in the Lean proof assistant that masked attention pooling is invariant to padding and permutation, provided padded rows are excluded from both numerator and softmax normalizer. It catalogues how common masking idioms (zeroing, -infinity masking, large-negative constants) fail or hold only under side conditions, and defines a guarded-normalizer formulation.

entry.title: Density-Matrix Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chiuman Ho

entry.summary: The author proposes storing RL policies as density matrices on classical hardware, with diagonal entries as standard action probabilities and off-diagonal coherences capturing pairwise action relationships. The paper gives exact answers for when this missing relational structure matters. It imports a quantum-information data structure into classical RL, expanding the expressivity of policy representations.

entry.title: Variable Input Masked Autoencoders for Wrist-Worn Accelerometry

author.name: Harish Haresamudram, Wanting Mao, Aditya Radhakrishnan, Maxwell A. Xu, James M. Rehg

entry.summary: VarMAE is a variable-input masked autoencoder that learns a single wearable-sensor representation across heterogeneous sampling rates and temporal contexts, using long/high-frequency and short/low-frequency views with masked reconstruction including a cross-resolution variant. This addresses the fixed-duration, fixed-rate assumptions of existing human-activity foundation models. It improves flexibility for deployment-constrained wearable applications.

entry.title: Neural Dimensional Analysis: Foundations of Dimensionless and Scale-Consistent Computation

author.name: Bum Jun Kim, Makoto Kawano, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Neural Dimensional Analysis (NDA) introduces a unified framework based on dimensional consistency to explain how Transformers maintain scale control, defining neural units that specify how tensors rescale and which quantities can be added, analogous to physical units. It yields diagnostic Unit Violation Indices for detecting scale mismatches, unit-consistent mechanisms, and principled conversions between gradient and parameter units. This offers a unifying theoretical lens on normalization, attention temperatures, loss weighting, and adaptive updates.

entry.title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Xiyang Wu, Zhichao Liu, Shengxin zhang, Zongxia Li, Ming Li, Tianyi Zhou, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: BELIEFWEAVER is a framework helping long-horizon agents recover from distant failures by maintaining a relational belief state over attempts, frontiers, and checkpoints, plus an implicit world model that evaluates repair hypotheses. The recurring reasoning components are distilled into a 9B student model via supervised training.

entry.title: Multi-Stream Residual Computation in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Ekaterina Alimaskina, Suren Kazarian, Gleb Molodtsov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: The paper equips masked diffusion language models with multiple persistent residual streams and adaptive routing, finding that visible and masked positions learn distinct routing patterns without predefined roles. Two streams reduce reconstruction perplexity by about 5.7% on validation and 5.1% across external corpora versus standard residual connections.

entry.title: Unbalanced W-Flow: Unbalanced Wasserstein Drifting under Finite-Batch Marginal Fluctuations

author.name: Jongwook Jeon, Mingue Park, Jiwon Choi, Jaihoon Kim, Yunhong Min, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: UW-Flow improves teacher-free one-step generative W-Flow models by replacing balanced Sinkhorn divergence with a debiased unbalanced variant, addressing artifacts caused by finite minibatch fluctuations. The method retains the original cross-minus-self velocity structure, recovers the balanced limit, and preserves target identifiability under stated assumptions.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating Training Instability in Large-Scale Recommender Systems: A Cascade Perspective

author.name: Yuening Li, Zeyu Wang, Zhen Zhang, Jiayi Liu, Zhimeng Jiang, Yuji Roh, Weikai Xu, Mingyan Gao, Onkar Dalal, Chuan He, Liang Liu

entry.summary: This industrial paper analyzes the gradient-weight-loss (G-W-L) divergence cascade in billion-scale short-form-video recommender training, where distribution shifts trigger gradient explosion propagating to weight and loss explosion. It proposes a structured mitigation framework mapping interventions to specific cascade stages.

entry.title: Dissecting the Carbon-SLO Tension in Geo-Distributed LLM Serving

author.name: Burak Topcu, Musa Cim, Zuhal Ozturk, Mahmut Taylan Kandemir

entry.summary: This systems paper builds a latency-centric simulator of geo-distributed LLM inference, calibrated with hardware-measured latency and power data, to study the tension between carbon-aware scheduling and latency SLOs. Unlike prior work, it models queueing and continuous batching dynamics of modern inference engines. It quantifies how much carbon can actually be saved under realistic latency constraints.

entry.title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Has Many Edges of Stability

author.name: Peter Zaika, Zakhar Shumaylov

entry.summary: Analyzes stability of non-Euclidean gradient descent for quadratic objectives, showing that unlike the sharp single threshold of standard GD, the intermediate regime between generalized-sharpness and curvature bounds admits many edges of stability. This refines the edge-of-stability theory that has animated recent deep learning optimization research.

entry.title: Minimax Rates and Improved Spectral Convergence for Multi-Manifold Clustering

author.name: Haoyu Chen, Chenghui Li

entry.summary: The authors establish minimax rates n^{-s/(d+2s)} for eigenpair estimation of the tensorized density-weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator from data on intersecting multi-manifold mixtures, and show a KDE plug-in estimator attains this rate. They further prove eigenpair convergence for a manifold-agnostic graph Laplacian estimator, connecting to spectral clustering guarantees.

entry.title: Harmonic Representations in Symbolic Music Transformers are Localized and Controllable

author.name: Adi Silberschein, Megan Wei, Tamar Rott Shaham

entry.summary: Through activation patching and linear probes on Aria, a LLaMA-based symbolic music transformer, the authors show harmonic decisions in Bach chorales are causally localized from middle layers onward and become progressively decodable. This mechanistic understanding enables steering of music generation via internal harmonic representations.

entry.title: RIFT: Token Influence Follows the Path of Least Resistance

author.name: Tingan Jin, Shuhang Dong, Haosong Li

entry.summary: RIFT models transformer layers as a resistive causal network where attention weights act as conductances, scoring a token's influence on the answer by the series resistance of its least-resistance path, computed exactly via shortest-path dynamic programming. It validates the method against interventions on synthetic retrieval and extractive QA tasks, addressing faithfulness gaps in attention rollout and flow.

entry.title: Differential Privacy Protected Preference Alignment on Survey Derived Data

author.name: Xiuyuan Qi, Yi Wang, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies privacy-preserving preference alignment of language models on questionnaire-derived data from the World Values Survey, where supervision takes the form of ordinal labels rather than pairwise rankings. It demonstrates model vulnerability, formulates alignment as rating prediction, and introduces label differential privacy tailored to survey data.

entry.title: Predicting Mental Health Help-Seeking Behaviour on Reddit: A Survival Analysis of Linguistic and Behavioural Signals

author.name: Nisar Ahmed, Ammara Kazmi, Irtaza Bashir Raja, Didier Devaurs

entry.summary: Reframes mental health help-seeking prediction as a time-to-event (survival) problem rather than post-hoc classification, using a two-arm Reddit cohort with genuine right-censoring to predict who will seek support and how soon. Features are restricted to pre-clinical activity with user-grouped cross-validation and a multi-year external check.

entry.title: Selective Inference for Clustering Under Unknown Covariance

author.name: Yiqun T. Chen, Lucy L. Gao

entry.summary: The authors propose a selective test for differences in cluster means that controls Type I error when the same data are used for clustering and testing, extending prior selective inference results beyond known or isotropic covariance to arbitrary unknown covariance matrices. Notably, the test statistic does not require estimating the covariance. This is a solid statistical contribution for validating unsupervised discoveries.

entry.title: From Orbit Matching to Docking: A Hierarchical Reinforcement-Learning Approach to Multiphase Rendezvous Trajectory Design

author.name: Mariko Storey-Matsutani, Anatoly Zlotnik, Lee Holguin, Zigfried Hampel-Arias, Richard Linares

entry.summary: The study presents a hierarchical reinforcement-learning framework for autonomous spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations covering the full trajectory from orbit matching through far-range approach to terminal docking, with five specialized lower-level controllers coordinated by a higher-level policy. This avoids the manual switching conditions typical of prior RL approaches to RPO. It demonstrates a credible path toward autonomous multiphase spacecraft guidance.

entry.title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration

author.name: Neel Dey, Adrian V. Dalca

entry.summary: The authors propose using per-voxel semantic representations from a 3D foundation model (anatomix) instead of raw intensities or coarse segmentation labels for whole-body PET/CT registration. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art utility in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge.

entry.title: TeachGrade: Training-Free Short Answer Scoring with Teacher Evidence

author.name: Jinhao Yan, Zhihong Shen, Shengjie Wang, Yiting Ren, Wentao Zhang, Yilei Wang, Peichao Lai

entry.summary: TeachGrade is a training-free framework for multi-subject, multi-step short answer grading that builds frozen memories from teacher-graded examples - a Skill memory capturing contextual teacher preferences and a CaseBank of local evidence - then performs retrieval-cued two-stage judging. On 3,829 SAS-Bench answers it lifts macro collaborative consistency from 67.99 to 81.32 and achieves QWK of 84.71, beating Native, OpenJudge, ProofGrader, and Trojsten. The result matters for scalable, consistent educational assessment.

entry.title: Mixed Feelings, Single Polarity

author.name: Emily \"Ohman, Saif Mohammad

entry.summary: The paper tests where mapping emotion categories onto single positive/negative valence works and fails, using SemEval-2018, GoEmotions, EmoBank, and a controlled annotation study across languages. Mixed-valence texts are only 9.0% of polar SemEval tweets yet cause 54.8% of learned-projection polarity errors and resist rescue by stronger models.

entry.title: The Multilingual Artificial Hivemind: Do All LLMs Think Alike in Every Language?

author.name: Xaver Raphael Davey, Shubhra Mishra, Anton Adel\"ow, Siyao Liu

entry.summary: This study investigates whether the previously reported homogenization of LLM-generated English text extends to other languages, comparing diversity across 23 open-weight models and 13 languages. It examines whether artificial hivemind effects match patterns observed in human text. The findings have implications for long-term homogenization of both model and human thought.

entry.title: Everyone Was Right: Lexical Representations in Language Models Are Both Abstract and Holistic

author.name: Zachary Nicholas Houghton, Yu Zhou, Dan Pluth, Vijay K. Gurbani, Vsevolod Kapatsinski

entry.summary: Decomposing contextual word representations into item, class, and word-class interaction components across six transformers, the authors find the interaction term is consistently present, grows across layers, and encodes information beyond shared class effects. The interaction even emerges in artificial-language learners trained on purely additive structure.

entry.title: Many Right Answers, One Training Example: Removing Responder Noise from GRPO for LLM Recommenders

author.name: Xin Li, Hao Jiang, Jinghao Guo, Weisi Lin, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: The authors identify that Rank-GRPO for LLM recommenders derives most advantage variance from which reply is sampled rather than list quality, and propose ReMaRk, which scores each list once against the union of all replies and samples requests equally. On seven backbones and three datasets, ReMaRk reaches prior validation recall in 25-53% of the RL steps.

entry.title: From Agents to Edges: Paired Optimization for Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Feng Lin, Xiaotian Yu, Yifan Yang, Aijun Li

entry.summary: PACO treats the communication edge between agents as the unit of optimization, jointly refining the instructions at both endpoints and their shared convention while keeping weights, roles, and topology fixed. A state-aware discounted bandit selects edges for refinement guided by end-to-end execution feedback. The approach targets the insight that strong individual agents do not guarantee effective multi-agent collaboration.

entry.title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models

author.name: Jie Chi, Zakaria Aldeneh, Masha Fedzechkina, Maureen de Seyssel, Natalie Schluter

entry.summary: The authors propose a lightweight method for detecting code-switching directly from speech, identifying language-selective hidden-state dimensions in pretrained speech encoders using monolingual probes, without needing accurate multilingual transcriptions. This enables finding code-switched utterances in large speech collections to expand underrepresented training data. It is a practical data-discovery tool for multilingual speech processing.

entry.title: A Persian Vision-Language-Action Dataset and Benchmark for Ambiguity- and Infeasibility-Aware Instruction-to-Plan Grounding

author.name: Abdollah Pourasghari, Saeedeh Sadat Sadidpour, Mohammad Roustaei

entry.summary: The authors introduce the first Persian vision-language-action dataset for instruction-to-plan grounding, with 258 instances over 230 real household and office photographs annotated with reference plans, deliberate ambiguity and infeasibility labels, disambiguating question-answer pairs, and chain-of-thought rationales. They ablate retrieval augmentation, chain-of-thought prompting, and an agentic disambiguation step. This extends VLA research to a low-resource language and to realistic ambiguous instructions.

entry.title: Local Citation Recommendation Without Graph Signals

author.name: Benjamin Basseri, Pavlos Protopapas, Kemeng Zhang, Alberto Accomazzi, Stephanie Jarmak, Anna Kelbert

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Local Citation Recommendation Corpus, 14,735 scientific statements from astrophysics review papers with accessible full-text citation targets, enabling citation recommendation research without relying on citation-graph signals that bias toward popular or recent works. Using this dataset the authors systematically compare retrieval methods and develop a recommendation system. It removes a key data bottleneck for full-text-based citation recommendation.

entry.title: OmniCompass: A Holistic Benchmark for Omni-Modal Video Grounding and Understanding

author.name: Xuyang Liu, Shihao Wang, Xinyu Wei, Minghan Li, Zeqing Wang, Zuhao Yang, Zichen Wen, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces OmniCompass, a holistic benchmark for omni-modal video understanding with two tracks: vision-language and audio-visual, each covering temporal grounding, spatial grounding, and question answering. It enables systematic diagnosis of video understanding capabilities beyond partial-dimension existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Can Synthetic UAV Benchmarks Be Trusted? Real-Synthetic Validation for UAV Model Selection

author.name: Yuyi Zhi, Min Du, Bill Shi, Guodong Yuan, Junheng Liang, Peifan Liao, Xin Guan

entry.summary: The authors study when synthetic UAV imagery preserves model-selection conclusions drawn from real data, using bootstrap analysis and matched resampling across two cases. They find ordering and top-model decisions can be preserved in one benchmark but reversed in a stress test, showing visual plausibility alone does not validate synthetic evaluation.

entry.title: PixARG: Pixel-Asynchronous Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion for Fast and Realistic Image Generation

author.name: Zewei Xin, Qinya Li, Chaoyue Niu, Fan Wu

entry.summary: PixARG integrates dynamic real-image retrieval into the diffusion pipeline, constructing pixel-level affinity maps between text prompts and retrieved images to shape heterogeneous noise initialization. This simultaneously improves generation speed and realism while supporting dynamic or private data adaptation.

entry.title: EmoTrace-Bench: Diagnosing Emotional Expression in Text-to-Video Generation through Controlled Cues and Intensity

author.name: Yeheng Wang, Liudan Shi, Yi Zheng, Jingke Li, Shiyuan Liu, Xin Tao, Yuanxing Zhang, Guoyu Sun

entry.summary: EmoTrace-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark with 448 controlled prompts covering eight emotions, two intensity levels, and varied affective cue conditions, used to generate and evaluate 5,376 videos from 12 text-to-video models. It decomposes failures into target-emotion expression, intensity control, and specific audiovisual cues.

entry.title: ScenePlacer: Reformulating Scene-Level Object Pose Estimation as Visibility Field Learning

author.name: Ken Deng, Jiarui Liu, Guibiao Liao, Kunming Luo, Mochu Xiang, Hongyu Yan, Yebin Liu, Shenghua Gao, Yizhou Yu, Ping Tan

entry.summary: ScenePlacer decouples object generation from pose estimation when placing generated 3D objects into scenes, reformulating alignment as conditional visibility-field learning from partial geometric observations. This avoids the poorly conditioned problem of regressing pose from complete generated shapes and preserves generative priors.

entry.title: All-St3R SLAM: Real-time RGB Dynamic SLAM with Pixel-wise Motion Masking

author.name: Yewon Kim, Paul Hongsuck Seo, Sang Chul Ahn

entry.summary: All-St3R SLAM is a real-time dynamic SLAM system that removes moving objects at the pixel level by combining ego-motion predictions from DUSt3R with point tracking from All-Tracker, masking only actually moving pixels without predefined labels or segmentation models. This addresses over-removal and computational costs of prior dynamic SLAM approaches.

entry.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Fine-grained Urban Scene Reconstruction via Semantic-guided Density Control and Loss Design

author.name: Yueling Liao, San Jiang, Xing Zhang, Zhongwen Hu

entry.summary: SG-GS integrates SAM-derived semantic segmentation into 3D Gaussian Splatting density control and loss design to better reconstruct fine-grained structures in complex urban scenes. A semantic-constrained adaptive density control mechanism dynamically allocates Gaussian capacity toward structurally important regions.

entry.title: EviStress: Evidence Stress Learning for Generalizable Face Forgery Detection with Textual Explanations

author.name: Jiuyao Jing, Xuanyu Yi, Yu Zheng, Chunlei Peng

entry.summary: EviStress improves generalizable face forgery detection by addressing uneven patch-level decision dependence in LoRA-adapted CLIP detectors, using a two-stage framework that stresses highly dependent evidence to improve robustness to unseen manipulations while providing textual explanations. It targets authenticity assessment under evolving generation pipelines and web dissemination distortions.

entry.title: HairFlow: Modeling 3D Hair Strands with Multi-Modal Conditioned Diffusion

author.name: Yating Wang, Kui Wu, Ran Yi, Zixuan Lu, Tongtong Wang, Zhongtian Zheng, Lizhuang Ma, Yuefan Shen

entry.summary: HairFlow is a multimodal-conditioned diffusion framework for strand-based 3D hair modeling, conditioning generation on a coarse mesh for global shape and 2D orientation cues, avoiding the costly per-instance optimization of prior approaches that fit foundation-model priors to strand representations. It targets efficiency, controllability, and generalization given scarce high-quality hair data.

entry.title: SchemaPose: RGB-Based Category-Level Pose Estimation with Parametric Category Schema

author.name: Shuang Wu, Jiude Wei, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun

entry.summary: Proposes SchemaPose for RGB-only category-level 9D pose estimation (3D translation, rotation, and size), learning a parametric category schema that disentangles category-level commonality from instance-specific variation. Tackles the entanglement of pose cues and appearance in the monocular RGB setting. A targeted contribution to 3D object perception.

entry.title: The Federated Tumor Segmentation and Classification (FeTS++) Challenge

author.name: Wenyi Tang, Carla Pitarch-Abaigar, Siddhesh Thakur, Verena Chung, Konstantinos Koukoutegos, Alexandros Karargyris, Holger R. Roth, Spyridon Bakas

entry.summary: This paper describes the FeTS++ challenge, the continuation of the first dedicated federated learning challenge in medical imaging, returning with a substantially larger and more diverse cohort and adding an official classification task alongside tumor segmentation. It aims to push real-world validation of FL methods in multi-institutional brain tumor analysis.

entry.title: Game2Real-Bench: Do Toy Games Reveal and Transfer to Real-World Visual Reasoning?

author.name: Qingan Liu, Juntong Feng, Yue Zhu, Yujie Cheng, Xinzhe Han, Shuai Hao, Yunzhi Zhuge, Haiwen Diao, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: Game2Real-Bench studies whether visual reasoning abilities measured in toy games transfer to real-world visual reasoning, covering fine-grained perception, spatial reasoning, constraint reasoning, and sequential planning with over 1,000 curated real examples. It addresses an unresolved validity question about procedurally generated evaluation tasks for VLMs.

entry.title: SenseWeather: Multimodal Sensing for Robust Robotic Perception under Extreme Conditions

author.name: Fucai Ke, Sukai Huang, Junyi Hao, Kal Backman, Naim Rastgoo, Gholamreza Haffari, Hamid Rezatofighi

entry.summary: SenseWeather introduces a controlled multimodal benchmark with registered RGB, depth, and infrared data for robotic perception under severe rain, snow, dust, fog, and darkness. It explores using complementary sensors upstream to restore task-compatible RGB observations without retraining downstream models. The benchmark addresses a genuine robustness gap since most perception stacks remain RGB-centric despite robots carrying multiple sensors.

entry.title: CIPHEUR: LLM-Guided Structural Search Control for Conflict-Graph Optimization

author.name: Yuqing Cheng, Yan Jia, Yanjie Song, Xiaolu Liu, Lining Xing, Feng Yao

entry.summary: CIPHEUR uses large language models to guide conflict-graph search by connecting conflict evidence to coordinated intervention and recovery through Structured Intervention Units, with both offline synthesized policies and online contextual decisions. Asynchronous online control sustains native search during inference while preserving the original objective and feasibility constraints. Evaluation spans eight satellite-ground scheduling conflict views with repeated runs and long search budgets.

entry.title: When pose graphs are not enough: a failure analysis of pose-graph-based camera estimation for Gaussian splatting

author.name: Senthil Palanisamy, Azwad Sabik, Alan Dolhasz, Mira Slavcheva

entry.summary: The paper analyzes when dense pose-graph optimization fails as a cheaper alternative to bundle adjustment for camera pose estimation in exterior Gaussian-splatting capture, using a fixed drone-capture recipe for real-estate twins. By characterizing failure regimes, it clarifies the boundary conditions for using PGO instead of joint pose-and-point optimization.

entry.title: Global Optimality of Pose Graph Optimization

author.name: Shuan Ding, Ruishuang Chen, Mengfan Cao, Zaiyue Yang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper establishes a sufficient condition for global optimality in pose graph optimization, showing the nonconvex landscape is benign and attractive near the global minimizer when noise is below an explicit a priori bound. The authors identify a basin of attraction containing the global minimizer with three main technical results. PGO underpins localization, mapping, and navigation, so such guarantees matter for SLAM reliability.

entry.title: Funnel planning and control for manipulators using neural Signed Configuration Distance Functions

author.name: Bernhard Wullt, Christos K. Verginis, Per Mattsson, Mikael Norrl\"of, Thomas B. Sch\"on

entry.summary: This work improves Kinodynamic Motion Planning via Funnel Control by using a neural Signed Configuration Distance Function to compute funnels, replacing computationally demanding prior approaches. Funnel control guarantees closed-loop evolution inside a collision-free region around a nominal trajectory, providing robustness guarantees for manipulator motion under disturbances. The neural distance function increases expressiveness and performance.

entry.title: Analytic Robot Self-Model: Learning Screw-Axis Kinematics for Rendering and Model-Based Control

author.name: Chen Xu, Ning Tan

entry.summary: This work presents an explicit analytic robot self-model learned from multi-view images and joint readings, requiring neither deformation networks nor URDF/CAD templates; Gaussian appearance plus sparse end-effector poses yield closed-form forward kinematics and analytic Jacobians via identified screw axes. Unlike implicit visual self-models, the result exposes metric joint parameters usable for model-based control and extrapolation beyond the fitting range.

entry.title: REFLEX: A Learned On-Board Reflex for Robust Autonomous Collision Recovery of Soft Quadrotors

author.name: Jakob Hermeler, Luca Girardi, Gabriel Maquignaz, Stefan Leutenegger, Stefano Mintchev

entry.summary: REFLEX is a learned collision-recovery flight mode running entirely on a quadrotor flight controller, using a proprioceptive recurrent policy that stabilizes the vehicle without position, velocity, heading, or altitude estimates after impacts. It reinitializes the translational estimate and uses a trust gate before handing control back to the stock autopilot. No contact sensors or companion computer are needed.

entry.title: ReAP: From Visual Failure Recognition to Action-Conditioned Risk Prediction for Runtime Failure Monitoring

author.name: Jingyuan Liu, Yunpeng Qing, Changxu Wei, Zhi Hou

entry.summary: ReAP is a runtime monitoring framework combining visual failure recognition with action-conditioned failure prediction, forecasting the consequences of proposed actions before execution rather than only estimating risk from current observations. A visual detector trained on successful and failed rollouts learns a failure-relevant representation, and an action-conditioned predictor anticipates risk. This enables timely warnings for brittle generalist policies.

entry.title: Beyond Safe Execution: Safe Online Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving with Value Calibration and Adaptive Guidance

author.name: Zeqiao Li, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: SOAR-Flow is a framework for safe, stable online fine-tuning of offline-initialized flow-based driving policies, combining a CBF-MPC safety filter with Gaussian-return-aware value calibration based on calibrated Q-learning and adaptive guidance. The goal extends beyond merely avoiding unsafe actions to ensuring stable policy improvement and reduced dependence on corrections.

entry.title: Intent-guided Adaptive Stiffening for Visuomotor Policies under Unknown Resistance

author.name: Francesco Cufino, Carmela Mariniello, Mario Selvaggio, Andreas Sochopoulos, Fabio Ruggiero

entry.summary: The paper proposes a residual stiffening layer placed underneath an unmodified generative visuomotor policy, enabling robots to impose force along high-friction directions (e.g., unscrewing, sliding) whose required authority is unobservable from vision alone. The layer adaptively increases impedance when resistance exceeds what a compliant controller can exert under bounded tracking error.

entry.title: Filtering for Liveness: Recurrence via Backup Reachability Control Barrier Functions

author.name: David E. J. van Wijk, Pio Ong, Aaron D. Ames, Joel W. Burdick

entry.summary: The authors extend the control barrier function safety-filter paradigm from set invariance to recurrence, guaranteeing that a closed-loop trajectory regularly revisits a prescribed set within bounded time even if it must leave the set. The framework combines backup reachability analysis with a filter that adjusts a nominal controller only when necessary. This addresses liveness objectives that conventional CBFs cannot express.

entry.title: WorkBorne: Discovering Agentic Tasks from Real-World Artifact Transitions

author.name: Junyi Zhou, Yufei Wang, Qiyuan Zhang, Chuhan Wu, Zhengxi Li, Wentao Zhao, Jie Zhou, Le Tian, Xiao Zhou, Chen Ma

entry.summary: WorkBorne is a synthesis framework that generates terminal-based agentic tasks from real-world artifact transitions, treating the transition (who performs it, which artifacts anchor initial and goal states) as the central primitive for full task life-cycle modeling. This addresses the asymmetry where instruction-oriented synthesis produces fake environments and resource-oriented synthesis yields trivial tasks.

entry.title: OneShot: Label-Efficient Detector Weighting for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: OneShot exploits the fact that deployed anomaly monitors receive operator-confirmed alarms, using a single confirmed anomaly to score and softly weight an entire detector pool rather than selecting one detector. The paper shows one confirmed anomaly suffices to approach the performance of the best detector for a series.

entry.title: SemTree: Judge-Aware Semantic Decision Trees for Inspectable and Repairable Rule Decisions

author.name: Jincheng Gao, Wei Ding, Shuo Sun

entry.summary: SemTree represents rule decisions (content moderation, compliance, eligibility) as semantic decision trees with natural-language yes/no/unknown questions answered by a pluggable judge, so the executed path explains every decision. Errors can be repaired at a single node and replayed, with corrected nodes serving as judge training labels.

entry.title: Rethinking Human Intent-to-CAD: Parametric CAD Model Generation via Cooperative Multi-Task Alignment and Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingwang Zhang, Jiahao Li, Xiangdong Zhou

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified pipeline mapping incomplete human intents, such as hand-drawn sketches and text, directly to executable parametric CAD code without assuming a target CAD model exists, supported by HiCAD, the first large-scale dataset aligning sketches, text, and parametric CAD code. A two-stage framework uses cooperative multi-task alignment followed by spatial-aware reinforcement learning to improve generation quality.

entry.title: AeroChem: Closed-loop Physics-Informed State Space Modeling for Long-term Chemically-Reactive Air Quality Forecasting--Extended Version

author.name: Kien Le Trung, Tung Kieu, Dinh Duc Nha Nguyen, Cuong Do, Bin Yang, Phi Long Nguyen

entry.summary: AeroChem is a closed-loop physics-informed state space framework for chemically reactive air quality forecasting, using a two-branch co-correction design: a UDE-based process branch provides a structured physical prior while a Mamba-based virtual measurement branch captures long-range temporal dependencies. It targets long-horizon drift and physical consistency issues of purely data-driven models.

entry.title: Calibrated Typed Decisions for Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction

author.name: Yang Wang, Hanlin Xiao, Yanan Ma, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: CalOn is a unified 0.6B-parameter encoder for entity, relation, and event extraction that jointly encodes text and type definitions, giving all three tasks a common probabilistic formulation with calibrated decisions. It supports cross-domain and cross-schema transfer where user-specified types alone are insufficient, considering combined evidence across requested types before assignment. This targets the persistent generalization gap in information extraction models.

entry.title: Cross-Market Meta-Learning for Electricity Price Forecasting

author.name: Delaram Pirhayatifard, Terrence Alsup

entry.summary: Presents MetaGrid, a topology-aware transformer meta-trained across multiple electricity markets, treating cross-market history as a pretraining corpus to overcome the data limits of single-market day-ahead price forecasting. By exploiting shared physics and market design across ISOs, a single model captures spatial dependencies from network topology and congestion. Targets improved forecasting where per-market baselines saturate.

entry.title: 4LC: 4D Latent Cache for Efficient Conditioning in Dynamic World Modeling

author.name: Jianhui Zhang, Zuyao Lin, Pengxin Xu, Jingdong Wang, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: 4LC introduces a 4D latent cache that reuses composite visual representations from multiple encoders (VAE, DINO, V-JEPA, VGGT) bound to shared geometry and motion, providing conditioning for video generation in dynamic world modeling without per-request RGB rendering and re-encoding. It includes a flexible spatiotemporal access interface for generation at different times and viewpoints.

entry.title: MemoryVLN: From Ego-Aware Memory Representation to Cross-Context Memory Reuse in Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Xueyao Wei, Yifei Wang, Delun Li, Shaoan Wang, Junzhi Yu, Wenjie Song, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: MemoryVLN is a memory-driven vision-language navigation system addressing long-horizon degradation in LVLM-based agents through memory construction and management. Long Sequence Compression uses forgetting-curve-inspired temporal sampling to keep dense recent evidence and sparse representative distant observations, while a cross-context reuse mechanism transfers past spatial experience. This tackles context-length limits and unstable spatial alignment across time.

entry.title: Riemannian Graph Tokenizer for Structural Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Qimin Zhou, Haibo Liu, Yujie Wang, Li Sun, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a Riemannian Graph Tokenizer (RGT) that converts non-Euclidean graph structure into quantized discrete representations to enable cross-domain structural knowledge transfer for graph foundation models. It uses Riemannian geometry to bridge structural semantics and tokenized representations, addressing an early-stage area analogous to text tokenizers for LLMs.

entry.title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Wildfire Size Using Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Isaac Lee, Bryan Shaddy, Assad Oberai

entry.summary: The authors present a probabilistic model forecasting wildfire size time series via conditional flow matching, predicting 3-hour changes in fire area from current and past size estimates plus spatially averaged weather, terrain, and fuel features. Trained on 140 coupled atmosphere-wildfire simulations, the approach reduces computational cost versus spatially resolved fire progression models, enabling integration with early warning and risk systems.

entry.title: Probabilistic Simulation of Gas-Liquid Interfaces with Coupled Flow Matching on Spherical Harmonics

author.name: Kiet Bennema ten Brinke, Rachna Ramesh, Douwe Orij, Ivo Roghair, Vlado Menkovski

entry.summary: This paper proposes a neural surrogate for bubbly flows that jointly predicts bubble trajectories and interface deformation in a shared representation, treating forecasting as conditional generative modeling rather than deterministic regression. Trained and evaluated on BubbleSH, a front-tracking dataset of rising deformable bubble swarms, it replaces costly mesh-resolved simulation with fast generative inference. Evaluation uses trajectory, shape, and distributional metrics.

entry.title: Bayesian Test-Time Inference of Task-Aligned Similarity from Weak Interactive Feedback

author.name: Weida Liang, Kenji Kawaguchi

entry.summary: BASIS is a training-free Bayesian method that uses weak test-time feedback (scalar scores, preferences, verifier outputs) to infer which similarity criterion from a task-specific library should govern retrieval, ranking, or response-revision decisions. It maintains a joint posterior over targets and criteria and selects probes by expected information gain.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate Drift: Optimal Client-Specific Windows in Federated Learning

author.name: Yuriy Dorn, Dmitrii Vishovan, Kirill Novoselov, Ilya Kuruzov, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: Studies federated learning under per-client distribution drift, showing that a single shared memory window forces fast-changing clients to carry the noise of slow stationary ones. The paper gives each client its own window sized to its noise, arrival rate, and drift, refreshed by restarted accelerated methods, with tracking-error analysis supporting client-specific optimality.

entry.title: Colored Graph Signal Diffusion Models

author.name: Yi\u{g}it Berkay Uslu, Samar Hadou, Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: Exposes the coarse-to-fine generation hierarchy of standard diffusions as spectrally non-neutral and makes it a tunable axis via a family of colored score-based diffusions on graphs, building both drift and denoiser from graph filters of the graph shift operator. A spectral rate parameter couples drift and diffusion to control the generation hierarchy.

entry.title: RegExtract: A Benchmark for PFAS Regulatory Information Extraction with LLMs

author.name: Defne Circi, Krystelle Lionti, Sarathkrishna Swaminathan, Daniel P. Sanders, L. Catherine Brinson, Bhuwan Dhingra, Basel Shbita, Mohab Elkaref, Sara Capponi, Tim Erdmann, Brandi Ransom

entry.summary: RegExtract is a benchmark for structured information extraction from PFAS regulatory documents, with 488 human-annotated field instances across 20 US state documents and 46 regulations, including value provenance for verification. It targets the growing, legally dense body of chemical regulation where scattered facts must be traced to sources. The benchmark tests LLMs on a high-stakes, traceability-critical extraction task relevant to manufacturers and policymakers.

entry.title: Perturbation, Not Provenance: Why Activation Steering Does Not Make a Robust Text Watermark

author.name: Sergey Pletenev

entry.summary: The authors test whether steering LLM generation along a semantic linear direction can serve as a robust watermark recoverable by probing activations of re-encoded text, varying steering strength, four directions, two model families, and two paraphrase attacks. Activation-steering watermarks are outperformed by a standard watermark under paraphrasing, showing steering is a perturbation rather than a provenance signal.

entry.title: TRACESTEER: Trace Driven Activation Steering for Hallucination Mitigation in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xin Zhang, Yili Wang, Yue Tan, Xin He, Rui Miao, Yixin Liu, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: TRACESTEER adapts activation steering to diffusion language models by using preceding denoising predictions as feedback to jointly adjust steering direction and strength, via step-specific steering components. It addresses the dynamic denoising states and time-varying hallucination risk that break static steering vectors. The work extends hallucination mitigation to the emerging dLLM paradigm.

entry.title: TGSR: Text-Grounded Diffusion for Faithful Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Zhiming Hu, Ran Zhang, Angela Ye, Raghav Goyal, Faraz Ali, Tristan Ty Aumentado-Armstrong, Samrudhdhi B. Rangrej, Konstantinos G. Derpanis, Iqbal Mohomed, Alex Levinshtein

entry.summary: Reformulates text super-resolution as selective generation, resolving text only when reliable generation is expected while fully super-resolving other content, to combat text hallucinations in diffusion SR. TGSR provides text-grounded control over when generative priors are applied to textual content.

entry.title: ASM-6D: Fast Certified Pose-Shape Inference with Complete Correspondence Flow Maps

author.name: Ho Jin Choi, Minku Kim, Nadia Figueroa

entry.summary: ASM-6D couples generative complete-geometry prediction with explicit category-level pose-shape inference through shared correspondences, fitting rotation, translation, metric scale, and instance shape directly from RGB-D input without a separate correspondence-assignment stage. Analytic elimination of translation and shape coefficients reduces fitting to a nine-variable problem, with certification of the inference.

entry.title: Stereo-Planner: Learning Stereo-to-Trajectory Planning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Quadrotor Navigation

author.name: Hongming Shen, Junjie Lu, Xun Chen, Wei Wang, Xinhang Xu, Bailing Tian, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: Stereo-Planner is an end-to-end vision-to-trajectory framework that generates quadrotor trajectories directly from stereo RGB, formulating planning as state- and scale-conditioned querying of latent stereo geometry, with a pretrained vision grounding foundation model providing domain-invariant geometric cues. It achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer without dedicated depth sensors.

entry.title: Constraint-Decomposed Impedance Control from Generative Policy for Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Kyungseo Park, Byeongdo Lim, Jungbin Lim, Minseok Choi, Frank C. Park

entry.summary: This paper proposes constraint-decomposed impedance control for articulated object manipulation (doors, drawers, bolts), using the sampling diversity of a generative policy to estimate feasible motion directions and set task-appropriate impedance gains. It bridges learning-based policies and classical impedance control without rigid force-position separation. The approach addresses a practical gap in selecting impedance parameters.

entry.title: Improving Policy Learning from Delayed Interventions

author.name: Xiru Zhu, David Meger, Gregory Dudek

entry.summary: This paper studies imitation learning under delayed expert interventions in human-supervised robot systems, challenging the assumption that interventions immediately follow expert errors. It finds that learning from delayed interventions is overall less effective than non-delayed ones at demonstrating error avoidance, contrary to the view that delay acts as beneficial noise. The proposed Learning from Delayed Intervention (LDI) method mitigates these effects.

entry.title: Breaking the Average: Overcoming Convergent Defaults in Robotic Manipulation via Diagnostic Chain-of-Thought and Structured Guidance

author.name: Mohammed Daba (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu, China), Waleed Abdulrahman Saleh AlAkwa (University of Sana'a, Sana'a, Yemen)

entry.summary: This paper identifies distributional convergence in VLA models like pi-0.5, where policies regress to safe but suboptimal mean behaviors (convergent defaults) due to mode averaging in training data. The authors propose a training-free three-stage methodology — probing for defaults, diagnostic chain-of-thought root cause analysis, and structured guidance — to identify and correct these behaviors without parameter updates.

entry.title: PACT: Posture-Aligned Co-Design Technique for Hand Configuration and Retargeting in Multi-Finger Imitation Learning

author.name: Koyo Sasazaki, Satoshi Funabashi, Pranav Ponnivalavan, Alexander Schmitz, Tetsuya Ogata, Shigeki Sugano

entry.summary: PACT jointly optimizes the mechanical parameters of a 17-servo robot hand (link lengths, joint offsets, mounting angles, base placements) and its nonlinear posture retargeter based on human grasping postures, enforcing full-finger joint correspondence. This co-design improves the fidelity of teleoperated demonstrations used for imitation learning, where hand hardware and retargeting are usually chosen independently.

entry.title: VETNET: Assembling Benchmark Datasets for AI-Driven Veterinary Innovation

author.name: Katherine J. Koebel, Renata Ivanek, Parminder Basran, Jennifer Sun, Casey Cazer, Gayatri Anil, Tommaso Banzato, Liz Barton, Dottie Cimino Brown, Leszek Bukowski, Marta Castelhano, Simon Coghlan, Christopher De Sa, Nikki Dutta, Hala Ghali, Julio Giordano, Joshua Glass, David C. Hogg, Nicholas Hollingshead, Adam Kiehl, Ziang Liu, Monica Meduri, Param Mohapatra, Kim Nayyer, Amelia Nelson, Peter-John Mantyla Noble, Christopher Pinard, Beryl Rabindran, Scott Ross, Ron Seccia, Moira Sheehan, Fei Wang, Tracy L. Webb, Kilian Q. Weinberger, Heather M. Whitney, Chen Xin

entry.summary: VETNET is an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks for AI in veterinary medicine and animal science, built through multi-institutional collaboration. It aims to close the gap between rapid AI progress in human medicine and the fragmented state of veterinary AI.

entry.title: PsyMemBehav: Psychology-Informed and Memory-Grounded Two-Level Identity-to-Action Reasoning for Social-Media Behavior Simulation

author.name: Wenji Zhang, Xilong Cheng, Yunxiao Qin, Mai Tu, Tongye Zhu, Yuhao Zhou, JingBo Ji, Yuting Tan, Duoyin Li, Hongjiang Xiao, Yuan Zhang

entry.summary: PsyMemBehav simulates real social-media users by mapping psychology-informed profiles and retrieved memories to platform behaviors via two-level identity-to-action reasoning. It contributes a large benchmark of 5.57 million observed behaviors from 5,862 real users across Reddit, Bluesky, and Twitter, modeling target selection and engagement actions.

entry.title: AegisVox: Factorized Privacy and Clinical Preservation for Long-Form Speech

author.name: Praphul Singh, Akshat Agarwal, Ratul Ghosh, Aashna Kanuga, Devashish Khatwani, Anurag Dwarakanath, Sri Gadde, Krishnaram Kenthapadi

entry.summary: AegisVox anonymizes clinical speech by assigning consistent surrogate voices and editing identifier-bearing turns with document-consistent replacements, while preserving clinically useful delivery cues. Across 63.6 hours of non-patient conversations, it compares TTS rendering versus codec-based editing for replacement realization and clinical preservation.

entry.title: MHWA: Multi-timescale Hierarchical World-Action Model

author.name: Pengcheng Pan, Guoqing Ma, Yuhan Zhang, Yang Chen, Yichen Liu, Ziheng Li, Shan Yu

entry.summary: MHWA is a hierarchical world-action model that curbs rollout drift in autoregressive world models by reducing global context update frequency via a strided high-level channel, mitigating error accumulation without the structural complexity of prior hierarchical designs.

entry.title: Pre-Registered Genesis Accounting for Recursive Self-Improvement: First Audited Operator-Genesis Events in a Physics-Discovery Runtime

author.name: Wenbin Mao, Pei Zou

entry.summary: The paper introduces a pre-registered two-tier accounting scheme distinguishing machine-generated content from genuinely machine-authored mechanism types, and reports the first audited example of the latter: a compositional search over elementary operators rediscovered the Rydberg-level form for hydrogen spectral lines from real NIST Balmer measurements. This provides a falsifiable framework for claims of recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Beyond Outcome Feedback: Trajectory-Quality-Guided Experience-based Learning

author.name: Bingjie Zhang, Yibo Yang, Qiantong Liu, Benshuo Fu, Yi Chang, Dandan Guo

entry.summary: TQG-Exp is an experience-based learning framework for LLM agents that uses process-level trajectory quality feedback rather than only final task outcomes. It introduces a Trajectory Quality Loss combining task completion and process quality, and uses paired rollouts with and without retrieved experience to build better learning signals for reusing past executions.

entry.title: Trust Hinders Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment

author.name: Michaela Benk, Kacper Sokol

entry.summary: Argues that trust calibration is an overly narrow framing for AI-assisted decision making, developing three dimensions: trust as only one uncertainty-management strategy, misapplication of calibration to ill-defined large-world problems, and the neglect of bidirectional alignment between human and AI. It reframes what appropriate reliance should mean.

entry.title: OntoAR-HAR: Ontology-Guided Agentic RAG with Personalized Memory for Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Xiangqing Lu, Tao Zhu, Liang Yu, Shuangjian Li, Lulu Ban, Furong Duan, Mingxing Nie, Liming Chen, Yaping Wan

entry.summary: OntoAR-HAR combines ontology-guided retrieval with personalized memory for LLM-based human activity recognition from wearable sensors. A tree-structured activity ontology decomposes the search space and combines static population knowledge with user-specific motion patterns for training-free target-user inference.

entry.title: MemeLogos: Knowledge-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection

author.name: Hexiang Gu, Saihui Hou, Changlan Liu, Min Ren, Huijia Wu, Hongxun Gu, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: MemeLogos is a retrieval-augmented reasoning framework for harmful meme detection that retrieves reusable harmfulness knowledge and reasoning mechanisms rather than merely similar instances. This improves both detection performance and interpretability for implicitly harmful multimodal content.

entry.title: Suggested Is Not Superseded: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of a System-One Model as a Memory-Retirement Gate

author.name: Xupeng Chen, Chenqian Le

entry.summary: This paper designs a task contract distinguishing established change from a hint of change for assistant memory retirement gates, labeling 500 test pairs with multiple LLM annotators and human adjudication. It evaluates a typed System-One decision model, Jev, under pre-registered hypotheses, showing many benchmark-marked change pairs do not meet the bar for established change. The pre-registered, provenance-reported methodology is a strength.

entry.title: LURE: a Phase-Labelled Synthetic Corpus of Online-Grooming Exchanges

author.name: Emanuele Florindi, Valentina Franzoni, Ludovico Guercio, Alfredo Milani, Mattia Polticchia

entry.summary: This paper introduces LURE, a synthetic, phase-annotated dataset of groomer-victim conversations intended to support research on detecting online grooming of minors. The authors address the scarcity and stagnation of existing labeled data (the Perverted-Justice archive) by using a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline with an 8-billion-parameter refusal-ablated language model, following a responsible-generation protocol grounded in the ChatCoder luring-communication ontology.

entry.title: Large language model-generated patterns for epidemiological modeling: a multi-benchmark evaluation framework

author.name: Sophia Mao, Keshav Gandhi, Alexander Gutfraind

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLM-generated behavioral outputs can fill gaps in epidemiological models when empirical behavior data are sparse, using hepatitis C behaviors among people who inject drugs as a case study. Against literature, agent-based model, and survey benchmarks, unconditional LLM recovery of association directions is modest (46-68%) but improves substantially when LLMs classify associations directly.

entry.title: Interactive 4D Volumetric Liquid Forecasting under Moving-Solid Interaction

author.name: Jongwon Ryu, Sunjae Yoon, Junyeong Kim

entry.summary: The paper introduces the task of predicting future dense 3D liquid velocity fields conditioned on how a solid moves through them, providing a physical forecasting primitive for robotic liquid manipulation, digital twins, and video generation. It addresses the gap left by methods limited to static or prescribed solid geometries.

entry.title: Hardware-Friendly Token-Group Activation Quantization for Low-Bit Mamba Super-Resolution

author.name: Jinwoo Chung, Jangho Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Token-Group Quantization, a hardware-friendly post-training quantization framework for Mamba-based super-resolution models that statically approximates post-scan token grouping, using a lightweight predictor to infer clipping-range groups from pre-scan features. This addresses the variable activation ranges induced by Mamba's selective scan operator.

entry.title: When a Conceptor Complement Becomes Gain: Operator Geometry and Behavioral Attribution in Language Models

author.name: Shuhul Razdan, R Balamurugan

entry.summary: Investigates which component of a conceptor-based steering intervention deserves behavioral credit by removing the fitted covariance filter while preserving target-specific center and gain. Across three models and seven targets, the matrix correction contributes little beyond the gain term, suggesting much of the steering effect comes from simple scaling rather than the learned filter.

entry.title: SLS-Bench: A Benchmark for Incident Log Summarization with Synthetic Observability Data

author.name: Valerii Iakovlev, Markus Spanring, Martin Flechl

entry.summary: Presents SLS-Bench, a benchmark for incident log summarization with 90 tasks grounded in real-world incident reports, each pairing a synthetic log stream with a reference summary. A data-generation pipeline converts incident reports into structured incident models to enable synthetic large-scale log generation.

entry.title: Separating Prompt Harmfulness from Interaction Safety via Partial Generation

author.name: Ram Vikas Mishra, Shashank Aggarwal, Jahnavi Kumar, Amit Awekar

entry.summary: Argues that prompt-only safety guardrails over-reject, since harm depends on what the model actually writes, while output guards judge only completed responses. The paper proposes inferring interaction safety early from partial generation, separating prompt harmfulness from interaction safety to reduce unnecessary refusals in conversational information systems.

entry.title: Transparent Information Flow Modeling for Role-Aware AI Act Assessment

author.name: Mattias Br\"annstr\"om, Themis Dimitra Xanthopoulou, Lili Jiang

entry.summary: Explores the Information Flow Methodology for assessing EU AI Act compliance, modeling decision systems as networks of information sites and transformation channels to analyze how information, decisions, and responsibilities flow across organizational boundaries. The approach aims to capture socio-technical complexity better than monolithic system views or disconnected checklists.

entry.title: Encounter-Driven City-Scale Human Mobility Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Chao Li, Renhe Jiang, Chuan Xiao, Jiawei Wang

entry.summary: EncounterMob is an LLM framework for encounter-aware human mobility generation that jointly preserves individual trajectories and population-level interaction structure, addressing the limitation that resident-centric generation fails to recover encounters when people co-occur in place and time. It combines a coarse-to-fine Encounter Generator capturing city-level encounter rhythms with an Iterative Coupling Framework. The work has applications in urban planning, epidemiology, and simulation.

entry.title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms

author.name: Lachlan Tychsen-Smith, Mark Cox, Brett Wood, David Haddon, Kenrick Anderson, Benjamin Duck, Jim O'Malley, Noel W Duffy, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: The paper presents Tricorder, an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system for under-panel photovoltaic assets, combining LiDAR-inertial SLAM with geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal imagery plus ML-based detection and segmentation. It addresses defects that aerial surveys miss, such as small, occluded connector and cabling faults under solar arrays.

entry.title: Consider, Then Choose: Order-Invariant Decisions in System One Models

author.name: Jianguo Huang, Yao Long Teng, Yanchen Deng, Bo An

entry.summary: The paper shows that single-forward-pass models violate order invariance on multiple-choice questions, especially when unsure among top options even while looking listwise-confident. It proposes Runoff, a training-free method that scores options individually to shortlist candidates, then compares them in listings where each candidate occupies every position. This reduces order sensitivity without training.

entry.title: AssetForge: Asset-Augmented Task Synthesis for Business Automation Agents

author.name: Xiangrui Liu, Shuo Tang, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: AssetForge is a pipeline for constructing executable training and evaluation tasks for business automation agents, pairing a reusable library of construction assets (interfaces, world-state components, policy evidence, assertions) with task-specific rubrics. This decouples business logic from repetitive infrastructure setup, making it cheaper to generate verifiable agent tasks.

entry.title: AgentStripes: An Evidence-Graded Maturity Model for AI Agents

author.name: Nutan Kumar Naik, Vijay Prasad Poudel, Aditya Kumar Saroj, Saurav Samantray, Abhishek Patel

entry.summary: AgentStripes proposes an evidence-graded maturity framework for AI agents: levels 0-7 across 12 process areas and 40 capabilities, gated by basic, safety, and proof gates, with capability ratings combined with evidence grades E0-E5 into severity-weighted scores. It complements benchmarks by assessing whether a released agent version has engineering controls for reliability, safety, and observability.

entry.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards

author.name: Xin Gao, Yifan Yang, Xin Li, Pan Wang, Yan Li, Muzhao Tian, Mingxi Cheng, Bei Liu, Kai Qiu, Qi Dai, Dong Chen, Yue Dong, Leandros Tassiulas, Rex Ying, Ji Li, Chong Luo

entry.summary: AesCode generates code for visual artifacts like slides and dashboards by using an image generated from the same prompt as aesthetic guidance, since code models cannot see how layout and color render. It represents targets as design graphs with attributable properties and applies RL with decoupled content and aesthetic rewards.

entry.title: SharedSAE: a unified sparse dictionary across u-net blocks and denoising time for diffusion models

author.name: Longhao Lei, Lan Yao

entry.summary: SharedSAE learns a single sparse feature dictionary shared across four U-Net attention blocks and all 50 denoising steps of SDXL, using block-specific low-rank adapters and temporal conditioning to handle distributional drift. This enables consistent concept localization and intervention across the diffusion network.

entry.title: LabInstruct: Benchmarking Situated Instructional Video Generation for Lab Procedures

author.name: Yuming Fu, Weijia Wu, Jing Chen, Jiahao Tang, Feifei Chen, Hongyu Zhu, Xin Jin, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: LabInstruct is a benchmark for evaluating AI-generated instructional videos that guide humans executing lab procedures in self-driving laboratories. It targets the human-in-the-loop gap where AI plans still require human execution, assessing whether video generation can produce clear, spatially grounded experimental guidance.

entry.title: Beyond Gate Weights: Decision-Level Interpretation of Radiomics-Image Feature Fusion for RCC Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell

entry.summary: This paper shows that gate coefficients in a fusion layer do not reflect actual branch contributions at classifier output, and exactly decomposes the decision logit of a linear-headed 3D MedVAE-radiomics model for renal cell carcinoma classification. It defines effective radiomics dominance as the radiomics term's share of output-level contributions and contrasts it with structural gate weighting. The finding has implications for how multimodal fusion interpretability is measured.

entry.title: Co-adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining for Structured Knowledge Retrieval

author.name: Zhisheng Qi, Haoyu Han, Jiaxi Li, Bing He, Huiyuan Chen, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi, Mahantesh M. Halappanavar, Jin Lu, Yu Zhang, Tianming Liu, Yu Wang

entry.summary: CoRE jointly learns which reasoning rule to route each query to and how to retrieve evidence under that rule over structured knowledge bases, eliminating the need for predefined query-rule supervision. A routing agent selects a rule and a corresponding retriever traverses and ranks rule-constrained evidence.

entry.title: GG-Nav: Goal-oriented Grounding Chain-of-Thought Elicits Reasoning in Navigation Foundation Models

author.name: Shaohao Zhu, Wensi Huang, Siqi Zhang, Yuqiang Yang, Meng Wei, Chenyang Wan, Tianle Liu, Tai Wang, Jinming Xu

entry.summary: GG-Nav improves goal-oriented navigation in navigation foundation models by learning a structured two-stage chain-of-thought via supervised fine-tuning that localizes goal-relevant instances and accumulates grounding evidence from streaming observations. A motivating study attributes failures to underused observations and imprecise target localization.

entry.title: YOUDrive: Driving Style as a Composable Direction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Guantian Zheng, Lidong Yu, Tianyu Gao, Jiaxing Chen, Jiashu Li, Chen Lv

entry.summary: YOUDrive is a vision-language-action planner for end-to-end autonomous driving that enables continuous, composable driving-style control by distilling each teacher behavior into a task vector inducing a style direction in the planner's representation. These directions can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining, with a flow-matching decoder modeling multimodal outputs.

entry.title: GAMW: Generation-Aware Mel-Domain Watermarking for TTS Traceability

author.name: Yihang Zhang, Weicai Yan, Qifei Zhang, Yangyang Wu, Tao Jin

entry.summary: GAMW integrates watermark injection into the TTS generation process itself, embedding a content-adaptive multi-bit watermark residual into generated representations before waveform synthesis, with a decoding objective combining focal modulation and dynamic per-bit weighting. This makes provenance watermarking more robust than post-hoc waveform modification, which is vulnerable to compound perturbations.

entry.title: HGA-Quant: Heterogeneity-Aware Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models

author.name: Xinmeng Liu, Xianglong Yan, Kaicheng Yang, Weisheng Dong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free post-training quantization framework for autoregressive visual generation models, combining tail-aware bounded-init grid refinement for weight quantizers with coarse-to-fine activation precision scheduling. The goal is to reduce low-bit image-quality degradation for edge deployment of ARVG models.

entry.title: In-Place Indic Tokenizer Expansion and Continual Pretraining of Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B

author.name: Avinash Benki, Prasanjith Pasunuti, Sutanshu Saksena Raj, Parijat Chatterjee, Nayanjit Sarkar, Daksh Maan

entry.summary: This companion paper details the tokenizer expansion technique: growing the vocabulary in place from 131,072 to 163,072 entries using continued byte-pair encoding and careful initialization of new embedding rows from decompositions of their constituent rows, followed by roughly 1.27 trillion tokens of continual pretraining. It reports honest negative results alongside a 12.9-point gain on Indic MILU with a 3.4-point loss on English MMLU.

entry.title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming

author.name: Abrar Alotaibi, Moataz Ahmed

entry.summary: REPRO is a pure black-box red-teaming framework that discovers adversarial prompts via evolutionary optimization driven by a compressed open-weight 7B reflective model on a single consumer GPU. It introduces semantic crossover, an LLM-guided multi-parent recombination operator, isolated in ablations, to improve population-level attack diversity without privileged access or per-model templates.

entry.title: TabMosaic: Unified In-Context Diffusion for Tabular Generative Tasks

author.name: Jayoung Kim, Sanghyun Hong, Noseong Park

entry.summary: TabMosaic unifies tabular generative tasks, including synthesis, imputation, and conditional generation, as modeling the joint conditional distribution of arbitrary target cells given observed cells of an unseen table, using a diffusion objective defined jointly over all target cells. This enables in-context learning across multiple tabular tasks without table-specific training, going beyond prior single-cell in-context approaches.

entry.title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification

author.name: Alan Tang, Lifeng Wang, Gang Wu, Tao Zhang, Yantao Jia, Xiaofeng Zhu

entry.summary: SkillMarker is a watermarking method for LLM agent skills that embeds ownership signals into reusable skill instructions while preserving factual and procedural accuracy. It unifies quality-constrained rewriting with signal-oriented candidate search to balance functionality and watermark strength. This addresses an emerging gap in IP protection for agent knowledge assets.

entry.title: OT-FlowRec: Optimal Transport-Guided Multi-Bridge Flow for Multimodal Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Miao Sun

entry.summary: This paper proposes OT-FlowRec, a recommendation framework that uses optimal transport to guide a mixture of parallel, interest-specific flow-matching paths, explicitly modeling concurrent multi-interest user intent in e-commerce sessions. It addresses a limitation of global-attention methods that compress history into a single representation.

entry.title: Reflected Proximal Dynamics for Accelerated High-Accuracy Log-Concave Sampling

author.name: Bo Yuan, Wei Guo, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces reflected proximal dynamics, a sampling algorithm for strongly convex and smooth log-concave distributions that combines the exact target preservation of the proximal sampler with the directional persistence of underdamped Langevin dynamics via reflection of the auxiliary variable. This aims to improve acceleration and high-accuracy sampling guarantees.

entry.title: MixLID: Token-Level Language Identification in Mixed-Language Text

author.name: Seongtae Hong, Youngjoon Jang, Seungyoon Lee, Jungseob Lee, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: MixLID is a token-level language identification model covering 111 language-script combinations, trained in two stages: monolingual language discrimination followed by mixed-language training using code-switching data and loanword-based substitution augmentation. It outperforms all baselines on monolingual identification and handles token-level mixed text.

entry.title: Comparing GenAI to Machine Learning and Manual Review for eDiscovery

author.name: Gordon V. Cormack, Maura R. Grossman, Jeremy Pickens

entry.summary: This analysis critiques a Redgrave LLP case study claiming Relativity's generative AI review tool achieved 88% recall versus 64% for its ML tool, arguing the comparison conflates different objectives, ignores inter-assessor disagreement, and mixes recall-precision and cost-benefit trade-offs. Reanalyzing the data, the authors find generative AI and manual review comparable, while continuous active learning remains state of the art. It matters for how AI tool claims in legal technology are evaluated.

entry.title: MAGNET: Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network for Connectome Generation

author.name: Protyay Dey, Ayush Roy, Hyuna Cho, Won Hwa Kim, Vishnu Suresh Lokhande

entry.summary: MAGNET generates functional brain connectomes using a graph diffusion network operating on a normalized-Cholesky representation of the correlation matrix manifold, guaranteeing valid correlation matrices. It lifts noisy latents into region tokens with relational inductive bias over brain atlas regions and employs class-anchored mechanisms to recover class-conditional geometry beyond coarse labels. This enables valid and geometrically informative synthetic neuroimaging data.

entry.title: Mitigating Black-Box Score-Based Query Attacks via Gradient Confusion

author.name: Ali Javeri, Javad Hezareh, Radin Shahdaei, AmirMahdi Sadeghzadeh

entry.summary: Proposes the Gradient Confusion Defense (GCD), a retraining-free deterministic test-time wrapper that actively shapes the probability vector exposed to score-based black-box attackers by solving a constrained optimization based on the model Jacobian. Unlike stochastic perturbation defenses, it aims to prevent attackers from recovering stable gradient estimates even with larger query budgets. Addresses adversarial robustness of deployed ML systems.

entry.title: Cross-View Time-Frequency Diffusion for Extreme-Aware Time-Series Generation

author.name: Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: Presents CrossTF, a diffusion framework for generating realistic time series that preserves rare but high-impact extreme events by exploiting discrepancies between time-view and frequency-view denoisers. The key finding of extreme-sensitive cross-view asymmetry allows targeted control of extreme fidelity without harming overall distribution quality. Relevant to simulation and stress-testing applications where extremes matter.

entry.title: Foundation Models for Event Prediction Across Heterogeneous Event Logs

author.name: Fabian Spaeh, Sean Jaffe, Shandian Zhe, Bin Shen

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Foundation Event Predictor (FEP), an in-context architecture for next-event prediction over heterogeneous event logs from business processes, manufacturing, and healthcare. It uses causal self-attention with learned event-level nonparametric inference to generalize to previously unseen systems with different event semantics and temporal scales.

entry.title: RELAY: Selective Self-Distillation with Adaptive Hand-off for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kunwang Zheng, Xinyu Sun, Yu Cao, Shuocheng Li, Lei Cheng, Ying Liu, Qilong Zhang, Jinlong Chen, Hua Yang, Qianglong Chen

entry.summary: RELAY addresses the reward collapse problem in rubric-based RL by distilling token-level supervision from a frozen teacher that reads the rubric as privileged context, selectively targeting positive-advantage and zero-advantage rollouts. A plateau detector retires the teacher and continues with GRPO alone, with one model-domain calibration transferring to others.

entry.title: TStruct: Learning Shared Temporal Structures for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yangze Li, Zhengyang Zhou, Qihe Huang, Pengkun Wang, Binwu Wang, Yang Wang

entry.summary: This paper empirically shows that temporal relationship matrices across different positions and variables share dominant recurring structures in real-world time series. TStruct exploits this to learn shared temporal structure representations that improve long-term forecasting robustness under distribution shift.

entry.title: CineMem: Attention-Aligned Fine-grained Memory Retrieval for Multi-Shot Long Video Generation

author.name: Xiaoxue Wu, Xinyu Gao, Fang Yu, Yu Qiao, Xinyuan Chen

entry.summary: CineMem introduces an attention-aligned, fine-grained memory retrieval framework for autoregressive multi-shot video generation, moving beyond shared frame-level retrieval toward query-adaptive access to organized online memory. This lets the model balance visual change across shot transitions with semantic continuity across a long video. The approach targets redundancy and inefficiency in existing long-video generation memory systems.

entry.title: Cost-Efficient Privacy Enforcement for Email-Generating LLM Agents under Strategic Information Requests

author.name: Qikun Cai, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: The paper proposes local contract-conditioned rewriting as a cost-efficient privacy enforcement layer for LLM agents that draft emails on a user's behalf, replacing expensive repeated remote checker-repair loops. It specifically targets strategic requesters who solicit exact values, raw records, or source evidence to induce leakage-heavy drafts. The work is relevant as delegated agent communication grows and privacy enforcement needs to scale economically.

entry.title: Scaling Vision Transformers Without Training: Prune-and-Merge Token Compression

author.name: Vatsal, Soumil Malhotra, Priyanshu Chahal, Sanjeev Kumar

entry.summary: Prune-and-Merge ViT is a training-free token compression framework for pretrained ViTs and DeiTs that combines class-attention-based pruning with similarity-based merging. The paper also introduces two robustness metrics, Relative Accuracy Drop and Prediction Flip Rate, to evaluate consistency under transformations.

entry.title: Reset Early, Reset Often, Eliminate Models

author.name: Martin S. Fixman, Fredrik R{\o}mming, Sean B. Holden

entry.summary: SATResetCoP improves connection-tableau automated theorem provers by abandoning unproductive tableaux without backtracking, instead starting fresh tableaux that feed additional ground clauses into a persistent incremental SAT solver. On TPTP it outperforms a leanCoP-style baseline by 54% and a SATCoP-style baseline.

entry.title: A Controlled Evaluation of Curvature Inspired Scalar Feature Scaling for Domain Generalization

author.name: Sunny Gupta, Amit Sethi

entry.summary: This paper critically audits a domain generalization method called HyperDG, which despite curvature-inspired framing reduces to rescaling Euclidean encoder features with learned positive scalars at training time, using a plain linear classifier on unscaled features at inference. The authors run a controlled evaluation of six conditions across PACS, VLCS, Office Home, and TerraIncognita benchmarks (384 total runs) to isolate what actually drives performance. The work matters because it clarifies that claims of hyperbolic/Lorentz or geodesic representations are not backed by the executed objective, an example of careful scientific scrutiny in a crowded subfield.

entry.title: LiFUSE: Frequency-Spatial Unified Self-Supervised Pretraining for Liver Disease Analysis on Non-contrast CT

author.name: Hao Zhang, Yi Huang, Wei Liu, Yuan Gao, Zeju Li, Xu Han, Yu Shi, Ling Zhang, Ke Yan

entry.summary: LiFUSE is a self-supervised pretraining method for liver disease analysis on non-contrast CT, combining frequency and spatial domains to overcome NCCT's low tissue contrast. It targets tumor detection and fine-grained diagnosis where subtle lesions are hard to identify. This has clinical relevance given growing use of opportunistic NCCT screening.
