entry.title: Learning Perturbation-Specific Representations through Conditional Energy Prior for Cellular Response Prediction

author.name: Yuchen Yan, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: PerturbEnergy introduces a conditional energy-based prior over perturbation representations for predicting cellular responses, assigning lower energy to representations compatible with a given perturbation to tilt the latent space toward perturbation-preferred regions. It can be integrated into autoencoder architectures with a modified ELBO. The goal is to accelerate drug discovery by better isolating perturbation effects from cellular complexity.

entry.title: PhysicsSliders: Learning Physical Controls for Audio Foley Generation

author.name: Peiwei Chang, Yongqiang Chen, Yuelan Cheng, Liting Gao, Yishun Lu, Li Zhang, Mark D. Plumbley, Philip J. B. Jackson, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: PhysicsSliders is a generative audio model trained on simulated contact sounds with 15 material, geometry, and contact parameters, enabling predictable control of hardness, size, speed, and damping for foley generation. Two variants accept direct parameters or numerical captions, and real recordings define effective-damping targets verified via simulator inversion. It matters for controllable, physically grounded audio synthesis.

entry.title: Jev-ToM: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Typed Decision Models

author.name: Kawai Chung, Chunkit Chan, Yuxuan Liu, Yauwai Yim, Xi Yang, Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Chiu Yeung Tang, Changxuan Fan, Ki Sen Hung, Tsun On Kwok, Haoran Li

entry.summary: Jev-ToM compares five typed decision models against seven generative baselines on 11,117 questions from nine Theory of Mind benchmarks. TypeSafe Jev reaches 73.2% source-balanced accuracy and ranks first or second across all six capability groups, leading on beliefs, goals, and emotions, with suggested cost and latency advantages. The work positions structured decision models as an alternative to generative LLMs for bounded ToM reasoning.

entry.title: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Svar Rajankumar Patel, Kshitij Jerath

entry.summary: ADiCo is a two-timescale framework that adapts behavioral diversity online during cooperative MARL training: a fast Diversity Control loop regulates diversity toward a target while a slower extremum-seeking controller tunes that target automatically. This removes costly, task-dependent manual tuning of diversity levels that enable role specialization.

entry.title: On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness

author.name: Maximilian Wong, Chenyu Xu, Jiajin Li, Yiping Lu

entry.summary: This paper builds a theory of hyperparameter transfer across model depth by characterizing how Lipschitz and L-smoothness constants of the loss scale with depth K, moving beyond architecture-specific toy-block analyses. It aims to let practitioners find optimal training configurations on cheap proxy models before large-scale training.

entry.title: Query-Adaptive Neuron Steering for LLMs

author.name: Yanxi Pan, Jingwen Wu, Yan Ma, Xiang Chen, Xinyi Zeng, Xuetong Wang, Yunyan Zhang, Yue Zhang, Yu Tian, Jianfeng Pan, Hongyi Zhou

entry.summary: This work investigates whether internal steering of LLMs can be made query-adaptive, using query-induced activations to guide which neurons are amplified at inference time. Pilot studies reveal subject- and layer-dependent neuron activation patterns, and the method adapts interventions to each query rather than applying fixed steering.

entry.title: Understanding Hidden Spatial Preferences in Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Maria B{\aa}nkestad, Jens Sj\"olund

entry.summary: This paper shows that GP posterior variance in Bayesian optimization is systematically larger near domain boundaries, giving variance-based acquisition functions an unintended boundary bias. The authors decouple model uncertainty from exploration preference using spatial weight fields amortized with neural surrogates. This clarifies a previously implicit source of exploration behavior in a widely used method.

entry.title: Formalizing Forgetting: Theory of Forgetting for Online Continual Learning

author.name: Renjie Cao, Yifei Cheng, Li Shen

entry.summary: The authors derive explicit upper bounds on expected final forgetting for single-pass Shuffle SGD in online continual learning under strongly convex and general convex objectives. The bounds clarify how per-task data amount, task similarity, and other factors govern catastrophic forgetting. This fills a theory gap, since prior analyses were limited to linear or NTK regimes.

entry.title: Contrastive Linearized Laplace: Loss Geometry, Valid Repairs, and Reliable Cores

author.name: Francisco J. S\'aez-Maldonado, Luis A. Ortega, Andr\'es R. Masegosa, Thomas D. Nielsen

entry.summary: This paper shows that applying linearized Laplace approximation directly to contrastive embeddings does not yield reliable pointwise uncertainty for downstream tasks like retrieval or clustering, since embedding variance alone does not reflect decision stability. It develops a post-hoc framework that propagates encoder uncertainty through the downstream task and characterizes when repairs are valid. This connects loss geometry to trustworthy uncertainty quantification for self-supervised encoders.

entry.title: Compositional Average Velocity Modeling for Efficient Diffusion Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Thanh Nguyen, Abu Hanif Muhammad Syarubany, Hwanhee Kim, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: InsQL is a single-step generative policy learning framework for offline RL that keeps the expressivity of diffusion policies while eliminating iterative denoising sampling and backpropagation through time. It builds on flow matching, replacing marginal velocity parameterization with average-velocity modeling plus a compositional mechanism with theoretical grounding. This targets the scalability limits of diffusion-based offline RL.

entry.title: HiPAD: A Unified Gait, Audio-Visual, and Personality Fusion Network for Depression Detection, with a Hierarchical Personality Ablation and the Calibration Limits of Domain-Adapted LLMs

author.name: Karol Chlasta, Piotr Struzik

entry.summary: The authors present HiPAD, a single multimodal fusion network for depression detection entered in all six sub-tracks of the MPDD-AVG 2026 challenge, combining gait, audio, and video signals with personality descriptions. A shared BiLSTM with cross-modal attention encodes available modalities, while personality is fused by concatenation and dominates the results. Because the architecture is identical across sub-tracks, performance differences reveal properties of the data itself.

entry.title: LexiCan: Lexicographic Canonicalization of Point Clouds for Machine Learning Applications

author.name: Daniel Sanchez, Djordje Mihajlovic, Federica Valeau, Luka Beni\'c, Raghuwansh Raj, Soutrik Sarangi, Snir Hordan

entry.summary: LexiCan is a canonicalization method for 3D point clouds that resolves rotational and permutation ambiguity by selecting a unique orbit representative, enabling standard architectures like transformers to process point clouds. It is provably invariant under O(3) or SO(3), achieves empirical rotational invariance to roughly 1e-6 angstroms on QM9 and QM-sym, and mitigates the discontinuity jumps of existing canonicalizations. Useful for molecular ML applications.

entry.title: Correlation-Aware Reconstruction for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Md. Johir Raihan, Zahra Zamanzadeh Darban, Yueyang Liu, Flora D. Salim, Levin Kuhlmann, Mahsa Salehi

entry.summary: Proposes CARMA, a reconstruction-based anomaly detector for multivariate time series that explicitly separates inter-channel dependency anomalies from normal temporal patterns. This targets cross-channel anomalies where individual sensors look normal but joint behavior deviates, a known weakness of entangled reconstruction representations.

entry.title: Truncation Samplers Are Nested: Comparing Decoding Rules Is a Measurement Problem

author.name: Rasul Khanbayov, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Observes that nearly all deployed truncation sampling rules keep prefixes of the probability-sorted vocabulary, making any two such rules nested at every decoding step. This yields a closed-form per-step distance, a coupling under which samplers emit identical text until first disagreement, and a separation certificate computable from existing logs, reframing decoding-rule comparison as a measurement problem.

entry.title: A Dependency-Aware Multi-GPU Training Framework for Temporal Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Yang Zhao, Yue Dai, Liang Qiao, Buxin Tu, Bo Liu, Sen Zhang, Yi Zhang, Xiaoyu Hao, Jun Shi, Junshi Chen, Hong An

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-GPU training framework for temporal graph neural networks that relaxes strict event-dependency preservation in memory updates, which limits parallelism and causes costly cross-GPU synchronization. The authors show many dependencies can be handled flexibly without harming training quality, enabling better scalability.

entry.title: Error-Based Bidirectional Predictive Coding Enables Deep, 4-Bit Predictive Coding Networks

author.name: Garrett Kinman, Zeljko Zilic

entry.summary: The paper shows that combining bidirectional predictive coding with a recent method enables the full predictive-coding property set (local learning, joint discrimination/generation, energy-based inference) in deep networks with 4-bit precision, where canonical state-based PC fails due to exponential signal decay with depth. This makes PC networks viable targets for efficient hardware acceleration.

entry.title: Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment

author.name: Xizhe Zhang, Jingfeng Zhang, Meng-Fen Chiang

entry.summary: This paper identifies two coupled failure modes in multimodal entity alignment (MMEA): Detail Missing-induced overvaluation, where absent local modalities cause overreliance on blurred representations, and Context Imbalance-induced suppression. It argues prior work wrongly treats feature missingness and structural asymmetry as isolated preprocessing problems rather than coupled fusion failures. The authors systematically formulate and evaluate these modes.

entry.title: DEFlow: Deep Equilibrium Flow Maximum-Entropy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ruslan Ageev, Huaze Tang, Runqing Miao, Jiarong Li, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: DEFlow introduces a deep equilibrium flow policy for maximum-entropy RL that replaces explicit Euler sampling with implicit Euler integration, solving intermediate actions jointly as an equilibrium system. Implicit differentiation with a discrete change-of-variables formula enables off-policy soft actor-critic training without backpropagating through solver iterations, yielding roughly 10% relative improvement in successful coverage on multi-goal docking tasks.

entry.title: TPPO: Tracking-Value PPO For Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Futing Wang, Chenxi Li, Jianhao Yan, Yun Luo, Zhi Wang, Yizhuo Li, Runzhe Zhan, Yu Cheng, Tao Lin

entry.summary: TPPO improves PPO for RL with verifiable rewards in language-model reasoning by modeling value evolution along trajectories via a Bayesian decomposition with additive log-odds updates, and constructing a cumulative value parameterization that sums position-wise scalar outputs into value logits. Learned through terminal-outcome supervision on reconstructed values, it improves credit assignment under sparse rewards.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking

author.name: Yitian Lu, Weinan Wang

entry.summary: The paper presents an AI-assisted workflow combining symbolic regression, admissibility checks, coefficient refitting, and LLM ranking to infer tumor-growth laws from sparse noisy data. Notably, it finds that PINN-based refitting often increases growth-law error while classical nonlinear least squares usually reduces it, offering a sobering empirical comparison.

entry.title: Protocol Choices Matter More Than the Aggregation Algorithm: Federated Learning for In-Hospital Mortality Prediction in Care-Unit and Multi-Hospital Federations

author.name: Rodrigo Tertulino, Ricardo Almeida, La\'ercio Alencar

entry.summary: This study rigorously compares seven federated learning aggregation strategies (FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedAdagrad, FedAdam, FedYogi, FedCluster) for in-hospital mortality prediction across two federations built from MIMIC-IV care units and 49 eICU-CRD hospitals, with uniform tuning, 10 seeds, and statistical testing. SCAFFOLD ranked first nearly everywhere, but its margin over the runner-up was tiny (never exceeding 0.008 AUC-ROC), suggesting evaluation protocol choices matter more than the aggregation algorithm itself. This is a valuable methodological caution for the federated healthcare learning literature.

entry.title: When Sparsity Breaks Connectivity: Functional Reachability and Guided Topology Dynamics in Extreme Sparse Training

author.name: Mohammad Pasande, Mateusz Jaworski, Jeroen Rook, Elena Mocanu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes forward, backward, and functional reachability on layered sparse graphs and shows that at extreme sparsity (99%+) dynamic sparse training destroys input-output pathways, matching closed-form expectations. Guided by reachability analysis, the proposed Reachability-driven method biases pruning toward non-functional edges and regrowth toward functional candidates. This gives theory-backed pruning guidance for extreme sparsity.

entry.title: MissPath-FM: Flow Matching with Structured Priors for Partially Observed Time Series

author.name: Genpei Zhang

entry.summary: MissPath-FM redesigns the source prior and probability path of conditional flow matching for partially observed time series, using structured priors such as interpolation and Gaussian process posteriors so the flow starts close to observed signal rather than pure noise. A missingness-aware smooth path allocates transport capacity only where data is unknown, avoiding wasted model capacity on already-observed entries. This addresses a fundamental misalignment between standard flow matching and incomplete data.

entry.title: Improving Neural Symbolic Regression with a Diverse Prior and Post-training Alignment

author.name: David Otte, J\"org K. H. Franke, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: The authors present RASR, a neural symbolic regression method arguing that prior underperformance on noisy real data stems from training recipe rather than the paradigm. They improve the synthetic prior using a tabular foundation model and add post-training alignment, closing the gap with genetic programming baselines.

entry.title: Teach Me After You Learn It: Lookahead Self-Distillation for RLVR

author.name: Zepeng Zhai, Meilin Chen

entry.summary: LEAD extends on-policy self-distillation for LLMs with inter-instance supervision: virtual RL updates on disjoint rollout subsets create lookahead teachers that then provide cross-group token-level supervision to the student. This moves beyond same-instance privileged information used in prior OPSD methods.

entry.title: Approximating Optimal Policies in Heterogeneous Asynchronous Multi-player Bandits

author.name: Sacha Arroues-Paykin, Etienne Boursier, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: This paper addresses heterogeneous asynchronous multi-player multi-armed bandits, where players have different activation probabilities, a setting relevant to decentralized cognitive radio networks. It tackles the previously open problem of efficiently computing optimal resource allocations when the homogeneous-player simplification no longer applies.

entry.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs

author.name: Mattie Ji, Indradyumna Roy, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: The paper initiates the problem of generating graphs whose persistence diagrams match a target topological descriptor exactly, rather than approximately via soft regularization as in existing topology-aware generators. It proposes two approaches with guarantees, proving that a local degree-based iterative method always realizes the target PD and reaches every degree-based PD-equivalent graph.

entry.title: PsyBer-Agent: A Psychology-Driven User Agent for Recommender Systems

author.name: Chong Zhang, Qijie Shen, Haichao Zhang, Can Wang, Xiaobo Jin, Jia Wang

entry.summary: PsyBer-Agent is a psychology-inspired LLM user simulator for evaluating recommender systems that models long-term dynamics like fatigue, affect, and shifting preferences via three evolving latent states in a Psy-Engine. It calibrates simulated behavior against real logs using Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport alignment.

entry.title: A Stochastic Analysis Perspective on Diffusion Models

author.name: Stanislas Strasman (SU, LPSM)

entry.summary: A theoretical survey/perspective connecting score-based generative models to classical stochastic analysis, linking Langevin sampling, score matching, Gaussian smoothing, and diffusion time reversal. It emphasizes the distinction between dynamics preserving a fixed distribution and dynamics transporting prescribed marginals, motivating a path-space treatment.

entry.title: Learn the Dynamics, Enforce the Physics: Generative Latent Operators for High-Dimensional Beam Evolution

author.name: Haohan Zou, Alexander Scheinker, Yuanyuan Shi

entry.summary: GLOBE is a physics-constrained generative latent operator that models 3D beam-field dynamics in particle accelerators, compressing states covering 10 million spatial cells into a latent space split between a control-conditioned neural operator and a generative residual model. It enables fast surrogate modeling for accelerator configuration exploration, virtual diagnostics, and controller design that would otherwise be limited by particle-in-cell simulation cost.

entry.title: Minimum Volume Optimal Transport for Multivariate Conformal Prediction

author.name: Chuchen Zhang, Haojie Ren, Zhaojun Wang, Yajie Bao, Changliang Zou

entry.summary: The paper proposes Minimum-Volume OTCP, which learns a Mahalanobis ground cost within optimal transport-based multivariate conformal prediction to directly minimize prediction-region volume while retaining distribution-free finite-sample coverage. Using a metric Brenier representation, it derives a volume-based objective optimized jointly with the transport map. This yields sharper multivariate prediction sets than fixed Euclidean-cost OT methods.

entry.title: MoSAIC: Learning DAG Scheduling Heuristics from Optimal Schedules through Motif-Aware Recovery and LLM-Guided Reasoning

author.name: Shiva Ahir, Hashmath Shaik, Alex Doboli, Nadeem Yaseen, Simona Doboli

entry.summary: Presents MoSAIC, a framework that uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to generate optimal DAG schedules and then distills compact priority-based scheduling heuristics via Bayesian optimization, with LLM reasoning used to relate DAG structural motifs to scheduling functions. The goal is to bridge exact but slow optimal solvers and fast but suboptimal heuristics for heterogeneous computing systems.

entry.title: Latent-Space Importance Weighting under Covariate Shift

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Yang Xiang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Fusheng Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a covariate-shift transfer learning algorithm that performs importance weighting in a learned lower-dimensional latent space rather than the ambient space, estimating density ratios of latent features for weighted prediction. The paper establishes explicit excess-risk rates, dimension comparisons under smoothness conditions, and variance comparisons between true and fixed predictive weights.

entry.title: ProtoPur: Prototype-Purity Pseudo-Labeling for Weakly Supervised Instance Learning in Pathology

author.name: Chen Shu, Chengyang Zhang, Boyu Fu, Ting Yin, Wenchuan Zhang, Jie Chen, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu

entry.summary: Proposes ProtoPur, which estimates class-balanced local purity over prototype regions built from frozen foundation-model features to assign pseudo-labels to high-purity regions in weakly supervised whole-slide pathology images. The approach improves instance-level supervision beyond attention scores, negative bags, or spatial refinement heuristics.

entry.title: Grounding Deep Learning Framework Testing in Data Flow

author.name: Jiatao Ge, Yanzhou Mu, Yinglong Zou, Yibo Hu, Zhenyu Chen, Chunrong Fang

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Tensor Flow Graph (TFG), a representation capturing runtime tensor states, properties, and operator input requirements, enabling deep learning framework testing that goes beyond operator topology. Built on TFG, the proposed approach detects data-flow-related bugs that topology-only methods miss.

entry.title: Using Line Segment Tracking to enable ML-based Track Reconstruction in CMS

author.name: Aashay Arora on behalf of the CMS Collaboration

entry.summary: The work presents the first ML-based charged-particle track reconstruction algorithm deployed in the CMS experiment, using physics-driven Line Segment Tracking triplets as inputs to a Transformer encoder with geometrically masked sparse self-attention. This hybrid approach tackles HL-LHC high-pileup conditions where combinatorial tracking becomes intractable.

entry.title: A Nonlinear Time-Series Theory for Constant-step SGD with Momentum

author.name: Younghun Lee, Jake Zummo, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: The paper treats constant-step SGD with momentum as a nonlinear time series, proving geometric forgetting of initialization, a unique stationary causal solution, and an invariance principle with quenched Gaussian limits for averaged iterates. A small-learning-rate analysis yields Gaussian limits for the last iterate and regime results in a stochastic-curvature quadratic model.

entry.title: Equilibrium Learning in Unbounded Stochastic Games with Gaussian Transitions

author.name: Jonathan Anthony Mavroforas, Fred Roosta

entry.summary: The authors study learning Nash equilibria in discounted general-sum stochastic games with unbounded states and Gaussian transition noise, using Gaussian-process models of the drift fit from a single trajectory. They prove that equilibrium selection stability plus uniform KL accuracy of the transition models yields regional uniform convergence of values and approximate Nash behavior.

entry.title: Explaining Heterogeneous Treatment Effects with Causal Forests and the Hoeffding Functional Decomposition

author.name: Ga\"etan Patinier, Cl\'ement B\'enard, Margaux T\"ornqvist

entry.summary: CausalTreeHFD extends causal forests with an interpretable decomposition based on the Hoeffding functional decomposition adapted to tree ensembles, breaking CATE predictions into covariate and pairwise interaction contributions. This directly addresses the black-box nature of state-of-the-art heterogeneous treatment effect estimators.

entry.title: Code-Interactive Visual Reasoning for Financial Candlestick Understanding

author.name: Chenxi Zhang, Youwei Pang, Xiaoqi Zhao, Ziliang Gan, Rongjunchen Zhang, Shanshan Feng, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Fin-Thinker, built on the existing Qwen3.5-9B model (released in March 2026), generates and executes code to gather evidence and perform numerical reasoning on financial candlestick charts, using tool feedback to guide further reasoning. The authors also release FinKLine-32K, a dataset of 32,184 replay-verified code-observation trajectories built via teacher-guided student exploration.

entry.title: Carve VFM: Carving Specialists out of Generalists, Automatic Task-Specific Compression of Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Lotfi Abdelkrim Mecharbat, Abdelrahman Elsayed, Ibrahim Almakky, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: Carve VFM performs automatic task-specific structured pruning of vision foundation models, jointly handling subnetwork selection and recovery rather than treating them separately, with layer-wise capacity allocated by task sensitivity. The goal is compact specialists that retain generalist representations at a fraction of the inference cost, avoiding expensive distillation training.

entry.title: Minimax Optimality of Shampoo for Nonstationary Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Abir Sarkar, Nirmalya Mandal, Martin T. Wells

entry.summary: Provides finite-horizon high-probability tracking-error bounds for Matrix Shampoo in nonstationary stochastic optimization, disentangling initialization, drift, momentum, noise, and preconditioning effects. The analysis yields explicit guidance on how momentum parameters should be tuned depending on noise- versus drift-dominated regimes.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells

author.name: Ning Zhang, Arto Nurmikko

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end spiking neural network that reconstructs dynamic visual scenes entirely within the spike domain from recordings of up to 1836 retinal ganglion cells in mouse retina, rather than reconstructing single frames with dense-valued ANNs. The work informs both understanding of the retinal code and visual prosthesis design.

entry.title: Value-Preserving Action Quantization

author.name: Max Muchen Sun, Jueun Kwon, Benjamin Riviere, Todd Murphey

entry.summary: Shows that for search-based policy learning like MCTS over continuous action spaces, action quantization should preserve effects on future states and values rather than minimize reconstruction error, proving that value-function error is tightly bounded by a value-relevance criterion. This yields a principled quantization scheme for robot learning with search.

entry.title: Formal-Verification-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Non-Intrusive Last-Mile Coverage Closure

author.name: Chengjia Liu, Priyadarsi Mishra, David Kebo Houngninou, Michael Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, Jiang Hu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a non-intrusive workflow for closing residual functional coverage bins in chip verification: AST parsing and cone-of-influence tracing map remaining coverage targets to existing testbench controls, then Bayesian optimization is compared against constrained-random verification under a matched simulation budget, with formal reachability analysis providing additional guidance. This addresses a costly, real bottleneck in hardware verification pipelines.

entry.title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Christian Sanchez-Leon, Dongming Chen, Dongqi Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents STRATA-S12, an open co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus built via Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition, which treats dataset construction as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a hemisphere-corrected class-season-region stratification with strict temporal pairing, quality gates, and human-in-the-loop deficit repair. This addresses geographic and seasonal dropout endemic to opportunistically collected Earth-observation datasets. Better-stratified multimodal corpora should improve self-supervised learning for remote sensing.

entry.title: SPARCL: Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning in Chest X-ray Analysis

author.name: Juho Jung, Seongjae Kang, Mijoo Kim, Sungduk Cho, Yunkyoung Jun, Sunghoon Joo, Yoona Hwang

entry.summary: SPARCL is an active learning method for chest X-ray lesion segmentation that balances predictive uncertainty with cumulative spatial coverage using a concave coverage function imposing diminishing returns on previously annotated regions, plus an entropy gate to revert to standard uncertainty sampling. This corrects a bias in existing AL strategies that perform inconsistently across focal versus diffuse pathologies. Better annotation efficiency matters for costly medical pixel-level labeling.

entry.title: Rarity Determines Minimax Rates of Semantic Entropy From Weak Pairwise Judgments With a Known Channel

author.name: Xiaoli Yu, Jiamiao Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical minimax rate analysis for estimating the semantic entropy of language model outputs when meanings are unobserved and must be inferred from noisy pairwise equivalence judgments. It shows the statistical difficulty of the problem is governed by how many meanings can be rare, refining prior worst-case vertex-dominated bounds.

entry.title: Robust Logical Anomaly Detection under Capture Shifts via Synthetic Anomalies

author.name: Ufuk Efe, Alptekin Temizel

entry.summary: The paper shows that state-of-the-art logical anomaly detectors like CSAD and SALAD, despite near-perfect AUROC on MVTec LOCO, lose 10 to 34 AUROC points under capture-condition shifts such as brightness reduction or zoom-out. The authors propose a framework using synthetic anomalies to train a classifier that restores robustness to such distribution shift.

entry.title: Minimax rates for pointwise CATE estimation: the role of design smoothness

author.name: Yuxuan Hou, Zhenghan Li

entry.summary: The paper derives minimax upper and lower bounds for pointwise conditional average treatment effect estimation, showing how covariate design smoothness affects achievable rates. Under rough designs, rates can be slower than under uniform design even with identical smoothness of the treatment effect and nuisances.

entry.title: Multimodal Co-Generation With Continuous Bitstream Diffusion

author.name: Georgios Batzolis, Georgios Kontos, Bruno Trentini, Pranam Chatterjee, Micha Livne, Mark Girolami, Luca Ambrogioni

entry.summary: This paper shows that continuous bitstream diffusion, originally for language, provides a unified joint and conditional multimodal generation framework across image-text, speech-text, and protein sequence-structure settings using a shared architecture and binary score-matching objective. Single checkpoints support joint and conditional generation by masking different parts of the bitstream.

entry.title: The Constitution Speaks Nheengatu: An Open MT System and Reproducible Corpus Pipeline for the Amazonian L\'ingua Geral

author.name: Fabr\'icio Carraro, Rodolfo Joel Zevallos, Rodrigo Gon\c{c}alves de Souza, Caio Henrique Faustino da Silva, John E. Ortega

entry.summary: This paper introduces the largest parallel corpus for Nheengatu, an endangered Amazonian language with 6-10 thousand speakers, comprising 14.5k Portuguese-Nheengatu pairs anchored by the 2023 official translation of the Brazilian Federal Constitution. The authors also release the first MT evaluation set built from transcribed spontaneous speech and the first open-weight bidirectional Portuguese-Nheengatu translation models. Notably, they find that translation quality plateaus on held-out constitutional articles regardless of training duration, highlighting the limits of small-data MT for morphologically rich low-resource languages.

entry.title: Who Receives Respect? A Counterfactual Benchmark for Honorific Allocation Bias in Bengali

author.name: Ajwad Abrar, Md Kamrul Hasan, Hasan Mahmud

entry.summary: This paper exploits a unique property of Bengali - obligatory honorific register for every third-person reference with no English equivalent - to measure how LLMs allocate social respect in translation. Using 2,016 counterfactual sentences across 72 occupations with gender-swapped pairs, it reports a single Honorific Bias Score per model. The design provides a clever, language-specific probe of gender and occupation bias that English-centric benchmarks cannot capture.

entry.title: Do Personalized LLMs Need the Whole Conversation? Matching the Full History with Only 5% of Its Text via Relevance-Filtered Context

author.name: Erika Hayashi, Andrew Shin

entry.summary: This paper shows that sentence-level relevance retrieval over conversation history matches full-history personalization accuracy on PersonaMem-v2 using only 5% of the text, cutting judge model input roughly 20-fold. An LLM summary of the same length performs comparably but requires reading the entire history, whereas retrieval needs only a small embedding model. The result offers a simple, cheap efficiency win for personalized assistants.

entry.title: Towards Autopilot Labeling for Short Video Content Governance

author.name: Junwen Chen, Hongwei Wang, Zixuan Wang, Jingbing Wang, Gorden Liu, Sheng Siong Ong, Xiaojiao Zang, JuChin Chao, Ze Jin, Kaiwen Men, Yin Li, Jeremy Li, Zhuolin Hao, Hongyu Xiong, Yang Song

entry.summary: A multi-stage framework that progressively automates short-video content labeling, moving from human expert labeling to a fine-tuned discriminative MLLM labeler and then to a domain-adaptive MLLM doing zero-shot labeling. The staged autopilot design reduces cost and iteration time for content moderation at scale.

entry.title: L\"ushi-1840: Building and Probing a Knowledge Cutoff for a Classical Chinese Language Model

author.name: Alex Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents Lushi-1840, a 983M-parameter model trained from scratch on 12,262 pre-1840 Chinese books, including a careful re-dating and cleaning pipeline after discovering twentieth-century contamination in a prior corpus. It probes the knowledge cutoff by measuring surprisal on annals compiled after 1840, a tool for studying historical hindsight.

entry.title: ToolHACE: A Dataset for Detecting Hallucinations in Tool-Based LLM Responses

author.name: Nikolay Ivanov, Sergey Pletenev, Elisei Rykov, Anatolii Frolov, Bogdan Monogov, Alexander Potekhin, Maria Marina, Daniil Moskovskiy, Viktor Moskvoretskii, Alexander Panchenko, Ilseyar Alimova

entry.summary: ToolHACE is a span-level benchmark for detecting hallucinations in tool-augmented LLM responses, covering five fine-grained categories, targeting errors that occur after correct tool calls, a stage existing benchmarks overlook. It addresses cases where models contradict accurate tool outputs, omit critical details, or generate unsupported claims. This refines where tool-use reliability actually breaks down.

entry.title: UMCR: Universal Medical Concept Recognition through Guideline Integration and Agentic Linking

author.name: Fabrice Lamarche, Amal Zouaq

entry.summary: UMCR is a pipeline for medical concept recognition that extracts and links spans to any target ontology without ontology-specific retraining, using direct guideline integration and an agentic linking module. It targets the generalization shortcomings of LLM-based predecessors like REAL and AutoPCR.

entry.title: The Image Still Has a Say: Final-Answer Repair for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Yulan Pan, Xiaoyu Xu, Zhihong Shen

entry.summary: Instead of improving multimodal reasoning traces, this work repairs the final answer at readout time using the still-available image while keeping the reasoning trace fixed, based on the observation that reasoning drifts away from visual evidence. This avoids costly retraining, resampling, or decoding-time grounding.

entry.title: SparPR: Runtime KV-Cache Recovery for Resource-Constrained LLM Inference on Consumer Hardware

author.name: Jieyun Deng, Keming Hu, Yanghe Liu, Li Feng

entry.summary: SparPR is a training-free runtime mechanism for KV-cache management on consumer GPUs, coupling query-aware key-block selection, dynamic budget control with cost estimation, and on-demand local recomputation with cost-aware fallback. It addresses the memory and bandwidth bottleneck of KV-cache growth without modifying weights. The work targets practical LLM deployment on single consumer GPUs.

entry.title: Receiver Decides Agent-to-Agent Negotiations

author.name: Fardeen Sadab, Alif Hasnain, Afsana Shehrin, Md. Azam Hossain, Abu Raihan Mostofa Kamal

entry.summary: The paper runs a round-robin tournament of 1,049 negotiations among fifteen LLM agents, where a requester attempts to obtain money from a holder instructed to keep a $100 endowment. Which agent holds the money explains 47% of variance in transferred amounts versus 2% for the requester, and the best-holding agents tend to refuse opening requests. The findings suggest receiver-side identity and behavior dominate economic outcomes in LLM agent negotiations.

entry.title: The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval

author.name: Jianbo Chen

entry.summary: This audit tests request independence in seven open Jev-style checkpoints using constructed three-passage states, with paired interventions on requested questions, displayed evidence, and candidate eligibility. Request expansion induces strict binary flips in a notable fraction of judgments and changes selection-or-abstention actions, with field masking tracing flips to schema fields. It documents context-contamination behavior in compact retrieval models evaluated independently per question.

entry.title: VoTSpeech: Decoupling Voice Design from Speech Generation in Instruction-Following TTS

author.name: Wenbing Yang, Qihang Lu, Zihan Sun, Peilei Jia, Yingming Gao, Ya Li, Jun Gao

entry.summary: VoTSpeech decouples voice design from speech generation in instruction-following TTS via an explicit intermediate voice latent predicted from text instructions by a flow-based module, which then conditions both a language model and an acoustic diffusion transformer before a VAE decoder produces waveforms. This separates what the voice should sound like from how speech is generated, enabling text-driven voice control. It is a clean architectural contribution to controllable TTS.

entry.title: More Reader Data or a Better Teacher? Updating a Model of Crowd Highlights in Late 2026

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki, Keisuke Watanabe

entry.summary: Empirically compares three strategies for a sentence-highlighting model on reader behavior data: using stronger modern LLMs directly, using them as teachers, or collecting more reader data, with a pre-registered evaluation design. Seven LLMs released by October 2026 rank sentences zero-shot worse than a 3B model trained on reader highlights alone, and teacher distillation results inform which upgrade path wins.

entry.title: Video-Arena: A Scalable Agentic Video Benchmark for Spatiotemporal Capability

author.name: Kuan Zhang, Yukun Chen, Zhihao Yang, Yue Su, Xiangnan Wu, Zirong Chen, Run Luo, Tao Tan, Yinhe Zheng, Yiming Li

entry.summary: Introduces Video-Arena, a benchmark using competitive games as scalable, verifiable tests of how well video models understand evolving world states, covering perceiving critical events, integrating events, and tracking. It sidesteps the annotation difficulty of real-world videos with partially observable state.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Recognition of Abdominal Wall Layers During Optical Trocar Entry

author.name: Shreeram Athreya, Andrew Melehy, Carter Prentice, Michael Robinson, Corey Arnold, James Wu, William Speier

entry.summary: The authors build a pipeline combining a gradient-boosted emission classifier, learned temporal smoothing, spatial regularization, and an anatomically ordered hidden Markov model to recognize abdominal wall tissue layers during optical trocar entry in surgery. Evaluated on 71 recordings with clinician-annotated sectors, it targets safer surgical navigation.

entry.title: Automatic assembly modeling through attention-based assembly feature mate prediction and assembly feature pattern recognition

author.name: Ziheng Dai, Wanbin Pan, Zhihong Tang, Shuming Gao

entry.summary: This CAD paper proposes a data-driven framework that performs automatic assembly modeling from unassembled B-Rep parts via attention-based assembly feature mate prediction, reducing the constraint candidate space without predefined assembly faces. It can output editable B-Rep assembly constraints rather than just poses.

entry.title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Thermal Human Perception from Dataset to Deployment

author.name: Kailai Sun, Yue Cui, Xinwei Wang, Zijie Gao, Baoshen Guo, Zhiqing Hong, Irfan Qaisar, Xu Yang, Yueting Li, Dian Fan, Qianchuan Zhao

entry.summary: The authors introduce Indoor RGB-T, a large-scale paired RGB-thermal dataset covering 20 indoor rooms with over 90,000 thermal frames and 115,000 annotated bounding boxes, aimed at privacy-preserving indoor perception. They establish benchmarks for occupant-state detection and occupancy estimation in unseen rooms and demonstrate real-world deployment.

entry.title: Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation via Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations

author.name: Jie Gui, Hang Tu, Yunfeng Dou, Wen Sha, Xiuquan Du, Shuo Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces RADAR, a parameter-efficient framework for text-guided medical image segmentation that combines BiomedCLIP for medical semantic understanding with MedSAM2 for mask decoding, adapted via LoRA. The approach targets hard cases like low-contrast lesions and ambiguous boundaries, where translating natural-language instructions into accurate pixel-level prompts remains difficult. It matters because flexible language-driven segmentation could reduce the manual effort clinicians spend specifying regions of interest.

entry.title: TIDE: Trajectory-Informed Skill Distillation for Efficient Text-to-Video Prompt Optimization

author.name: Chengxing Zhou, Yuliang Huang, Jingwei Song

entry.summary: TIDE distills expensive inference-time prompt optimization search into a reusable, interpretable prompt-rewriting Skill composed of source-conditioned rule modules per semantic dimension. Once trained on only 100 prompts, the frozen Skill generates positive and negative prompts in a single LLM call followed by one T2V generation, eliminating test-time visual search and backbone fine-tuning.

entry.title: BaT-SAM: Introducing Inductive Bias into SAM via a Mixture of Convolutional Experts for Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Sumiaya Jannat, Md Mahedi Hasan, Md Shamimul Islam, Md Nur Hossain

entry.summary: BaT-SAM adapts the frozen SAM ViT encoder for fully automatic brain tumor MRI segmentation using Conv-LoRA, a sparsely gated mixture of multi-scale convolutional experts that injects translation-equivariant inductive bias. It removes the need for user prompts at inference with parameter-efficient tuning.

entry.title: RSAJEV: Training-Free Abstaining Prototype Memory for Eliminating Silent Hallucination in JEV-Based Remote Sensing Classification

author.name: Man Chen, Antai Chen, Shuai Xu, Chengjie Gu, Huaping Zhou, Kelei Sun, Tao Wu, Yongjie Huang

entry.summary: RSAJEV analyzes joint embedding vision-language classification for remote sensing and shows letter-binding prompts behave erratically out of vocabulary, even assigning higher confidence to unseen classes than seen ones. It proposes a training-free abstaining prototype memory that detects and abstains on silent hallucinations in open-set settings.

entry.title: Removing the Compute Bottleneck for Event-based Visual Place Recognition with Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Somayeh Hussaini, Tobias Fischer, Michael Milford

entry.summary: The paper trains a two-layer spiking network with additive STDP for event-based visual place recognition, producing a strongly bimodal weight matrix amenable to aggressive pruning so that inference reads only weights for active query spikes. This resolves event-based VPR queries in tens of microseconds on a commodity CPU, avoiding dense frame-like computation.

entry.title: DIGS: Distribution-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation

author.name: Zhifan Zeng, Wenbo Xiao, Arcot Sowmya, Changming Sun

entry.summary: DIGS is a training-free framework for open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian segmentation that maintains an explicit top-M label distribution per Gaussian, updated by a tempered Dirichlet rule, avoiding the hard commitment of per-primitive single features that degrades boundaries. It decouples class-agnostic instance discovery from linguistic naming in two stages.

entry.title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization

author.name: Jaehyun Kim, Wonseok Kang, Tae-Wan Kim

entry.summary: Proposes History-Guided Pose Reselection, which uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to disambiguate candidates when repetitive structures give incorrect poses more inlier support. HPR requires no odometry, uses prediction only for selection rather than refinement, and improves recall within 5 meters and 10 degrees across all 12 main HLoc and MASt3R configurations with a single threshold.

entry.title: 3D-VITAL: Visibility-aware Identity Training from Artificial Liftings of 3D Reconstruction model for Cross-View Object Re-Identification

author.name: William Grolleau, Astrid Sabourin, Guillaume Lapouge, Catherine Achard

entry.summary: The paper tackles single-view aerial-ground re-identification by lifting source images into textured 3D meshes via large-scale single-view reconstruction and rendering new viewpoints for training. It explicitly handles two failure modes of this pipeline: geometrically incorrect reconstructions and visibility-related unreliability, using visibility-aware identity training.

entry.title: A unified three-branch deep learning framework for automated detection and counting of wildlife in aerial imagery

author.name: Zeyu Xu, Tiejun Wang, Andrew Skidmore, Megan Claase, Harry Wells, Isla Duporge, Ramiro D. Crego, Richard Lamprey

entry.summary: This work presents an end-to-end pipeline for automated aerial wildlife surveys combining three components: WildSeg for delineating counting strips from aircraft markers, WildMatch for teacher-student correspondence learning to detect image overlap without geolocation metadata, and WildDet for dual-scale animal detection with density supervision. It addresses a real ecological monitoring workflow including double-counting correction.

entry.title: CrossPortrait: Cross-Species Portrait Animation via Adversarial Motion Alignment

author.name: Gezhong Pan, Zhe Li, Yunfan Tao, Yongheng Zhao, Shiqi Zhou, Juyong Zhang, Xiaosong Jia, Yanyong Zhang, Shuquan Ye, Shaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: CrossPortrait enables animating a source portrait of one species using a driving video of another (human-to-animal, animal-to-human, cat-to-dog), decomposing motion into rigid head pose and expression keypoints with adversarial motion alignment to avoid driving-species leakage that plagues fine-tuned human animation models. It handles substantial anatomical facial differences across species.

entry.title: Hierarchical Curriculum Learning for Surgical Video Generation: Focusing on Bilateral Axillo-Breast Approach Robotic Thyroidectomy Datasets

author.name: Youngbin Kong, Seungho Lee, Jae Kyung Shin, Jong-hyuk Ahn, Hyoun-Joong Kong, Kyu Eun Lee

entry.summary: The paper adapts text-to-video diffusion models to surgical video generation for robotic thyroidectomy using hierarchical phase-task-action annotation and curriculum transfer learning. High-fidelity surgical video synthesis could benefit education, simulation, and downstream AI training where real data is scarce.

entry.title: Frequency Routing and Identity Conditioning for Thermal-to-Visible Face Translation

author.name: Haojie Li, Xinlong Sun, Xiaohaoyang Lei, Kai Cheng, Yiguo Qiao, Xu Yang, Cunjian Chen

entry.summary: FreqID-Control is a parameter-efficient framework for thermal-to-visible face translation that routes thermal guidance by spectral reliability and semantic role, separating local structure from global identity while preserving a pretrained generative prior. Applications include nighttime biometric recognition and low-light surveillance.

entry.title: Human-Inspired Asymmetric Collaboration for Dual-Student Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Huiyi Ren, Ziming Fang, Jiaming Cai, Rui Xu, Haojie Li

entry.summary: Proposes HAC, a dual-student semi-supervised framework for medical image segmentation that adaptively calibrates augmentation difficulty using reinforcement-guided signals, mimicking human feedback-regulated instruction. It addresses the tradeoff between student homogenization and augmentation-induced anatomical corruption. A solid methodological contribution for label-scarce medical imaging.

entry.title: Dual-Domain Sparse-View 4D CBCT Reconstruction with Spatial-Temporal Consistency Learning

author.name: Qi Lai, YuTong He

entry.summary: Proposes STCNet, a sparse-view 4D cone-beam CT reconstruction framework combining physics-driven positional encoding for projection-domain geometric consistency and temporal latent encoding for respiratory motion, reconstructing from only 16 projections per phase. Reducing projections directly cuts radiation dose and scan time in image-guided radiotherapy. A competent clinical-imaging contribution from a two-author team.

entry.title: PlanPath: Exploration-Guided Orchestration for Patient-Level Pathology Reasoning

author.name: Jiusong Ge, Mingzhao He, Qidong Liu, Chunbao Wang, Chunze Yang, Di Zhang, Jiashuai Liu, Mireia Crispin-Ortuzar, Huazhu Fu, Chen Li, Zeyu Gao

entry.summary: PlanPath is an agentic framework for patient-level pathology visual question answering that converts a question into an exploration plan, routes to relevant slides across a patient's specimens, and integrates site-specific evidence while measuring morphology quantitatively. It addresses the gap left by slide-by-slide agents that describe rather than quantify findings.

entry.title: Concealed Handgun Detection using WiFi Signals

author.name: Erik Persson, David Gustafsson, Tomas Wilkinson

entry.summary: This paper proposes using WiFi Channel State Information to detect concealed handguns as a complement to cameras and metal detectors, avoiding occlusion limits and congestion from narrow screening points. The authors collect a new dataset to train and evaluate detection models on this sensing modality.

entry.title: PLAYGROUND: Progressive Layout Generation with Render-Grounded Planning

author.name: Jaeho Lee, Junhwan Heo, Junghyun Park, WonJun Moon, Eunju Yang, Seungho Jang, Seongchan Kim, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: This paper introduces PlayGround, a progressive framework for generating editable graphic design layouts that adapts dynamically to the rendered canvas rather than following a predetermined plan. It combines a Progressive Planner, Layout Generator, Visual Verifier, and Structure-Aware Retriever in an iterative design loop, mirroring real-world design workflows. It matters because it improves adaptability and editability in ML-driven graphic design tools.

entry.title: C$^2$LUE: Clinically Aligned Patient-Level Ultrasound Diagnosis via Evidence-Aware Multi-Instance Learning

author.name: Qin-Yi Zhang, Linying Cao, De-Xing Huang, Haichuan Lin, Yi Yang, Manzhi Wang, Xiao-Hu Zhou, Chen Chen, Shuangyi Wang, Zeng-Guang Hou

entry.summary: C2LUE is a multi-instance learning framework for patient-level ultrasound diagnosis that couples evidence-aware aggregation with risk-aligned regularization to handle asymmetric diagnostic risks and heterogeneous cues across views. It uses multi-query cross-attention on a LoRA-adapted DINOv3 backbone to prevent attention collapse and preserve evidence diversity. The work matters because clinical deployment requires calibrated sensitivity-specificity trade-offs, not just accuracy.

entry.title: Perception Beyond the Visible: Incompleteness-Aware Scene Understanding for Robot Autonomy

author.name: Rohit Mohan

entry.summary: This is a research-vision paper organizing robot scene understanding around three challenges: incomplete evidence, incomplete knowledge, and incomplete sensor reliability. The author surveys contributions across amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world scene understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty handling. It provides a unifying framing for building perception systems that reason about what is not observed.

entry.title: Assessing the Marginal Utility of Exocentric Head Views in UMI-Style Large-FoV Wrist-Camera Manipulation

author.name: Yuhui Duan, Shi Jin, Yuntian Wang, Jin Wang, Siao Liu, Wenchang Gao, Zhaxizhuoma, Yan Ding

entry.summary: This controlled-variable study revisits the assumption that more cameras improve robot manipulation, comparing bimanual tabletop policies with two large-FoV wrist cameras against those with an added head view on a real platform. Across three tasks, adding a head view does not consistently improve performance when wrist cameras already cover objects, grippers, and goal regions.

entry.title: CoPlanVLM: Coordinated Path Planning for a Robot Team using Vision Language Models

author.name: David R. Martin, Jared Paquet, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque, Pramod Khargonekar, Kyle Volle, J. Humberto Ramos, Scott Nivison

entry.summary: CoPlanVLM uses a vision-language model to convert a single natural-language instruction plus an image into coordinated collision-free paths for a two-robot team. It tackles the known weakness of VLMs in spatial reasoning via image overlays marking free space and obstacles, task classification to select planners and prompts, and task-specific chain-of-thought for role allocation and route verification. This demonstrates a practical pattern for wrapping general-purpose VLMs into reliable multi-robot planning pipelines.

entry.title: PC7 Model: Dynamics of Expanding and Contracting Soft Robots using Piece-wise Constant 7D Deformation Based on Similarity Transformation Group

author.name: Yamato Kudo, Taiki Ishigaki, Ko Ayusawa, Ko Yamamoto

entry.summary: This paper introduces the PC7 model, a soft robot deformation model that extends the piece-wise constant strain (PCS) framework from SE(3) to SIM(3), adding a seventh scaling dimension to capture expansion and contraction of actuators like artificial muscles. The shared mathematical structure between the two Lie groups allows direct extension of existing kinematic and dynamic tools. This is a principled geometric contribution relevant to soft robot simulation and control.

entry.title: CAG-WAM: Causal Action-Gain World Action Models for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Peizheng Guo, Cheng Zhang, Xingyu Zhang, Changwen Zheng, Wenwen Qiang

entry.summary: This work formulates a structural causal model for evaluating candidate actions in World Action Models, separating action-induced changes from environment-driven changes in predicted futures. The insight is that directly scoring a predicted future can misjudge an action when environmental trends dominate, and the proposed causal action-gain formulation corrects this. It improves action evaluation for model-based robot manipulation.

entry.title: Embodiment-Aware Inference-Time Search for Human Reaction Selection in Humanoid Retargeting

author.name: Yongpeng Cao, Masahiro Hirano, Yuji Yamakawa

entry.summary: This work proposes an inference-time reaction selection method for human-to-humanoid motion retargeting, allowing human-human reaction datasets to serve as a shared motion representation across different humanoid embodiments. Because a reaction preferred in human motion space may not suit a specific robot morphology, the method searches for embodiment-appropriate reactions at inference rather than training a specialized model per robot.

entry.title: LERR-Nav: Learning to Coordinate Exploration, Recovery, and Reminiscing for Object Navigation

author.name: Jingzhi Huang, Junkai Huang, Yuhang Peng, Keyu Mu, Hailong Huang, Haoyang Yang, Renbo Luo, Lujia Wang, Yi Wang

entry.summary: LERR-Nav tackles object navigation in unseen environments by combining LLM/VLM-enhanced semantic mapping and waypoint selection with a high-level policy that coordinates specialized strategies for exploration, recovery from stalled progress, and revisiting overlooked target cues. The approach is motivated by an analysis of failed navigation episodes, aiming to make embodied agents more robust to unproductive behaviors.

entry.title: Learning Safety-Constrained Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation for Lunar Surface Operations

author.name: Alvaro Belmonte-Baeza, Miguel Cazorla, Gabriel J. Garc\'ia, Carlos J. P\'erez-Del-Pulgar, Jorge Pomares

entry.summary: This paper presents a constrained RL framework for quadrupedal mobile manipulators targeting lunar operations, learning a single whole-body policy for 6D end-effector pose tracking with operational limits enforced during training. Notably, the locomotion-manipulation transition emerges from reward geometry rather than explicit gating, with a stability term derived from a Gravito-Inertial Inclination Margin.

entry.title: Model-Based Trailer-Sway Suppression for Autonomous Passenger Vehicles

author.name: Alec McFadyen, Pablo Covarrubias De La Torre, Connor McGovern

entry.summary: This work addresses trailer sway, a significant cause of towing crashes, which current autonomous vehicle stacks do not handle. It analyzes how improper cargo placement reduces or inverts tongue load, degrading yaw stability, and proposes model-based suppression to prevent divergent oscillation and jackknifing. It fills a genuine safety gap as automation extends to towing scenarios.

entry.title: Constrained Differentiable Policy Learning for Safe Quadrotor Navigation

author.name: Yan Rui Tan, Praveen Krishnapur, Zeyu Feng, Han Bao, Yew-Soon Ong, Fan Shi

entry.summary: This work formulates obstacle avoidance as an explicit constraint rather than a weighted penalty in differentiable-simulation-based policy training, using primal-dual gradient descent-ascent for quadrotor navigation. Two technical contributions enable stable training: a bounded clearance-based constraint function and log-mean-exp aggregation of constraints. This removes manual safety-performance trade-off tuning.

entry.title: DeTac: Dual-branch Decoupling of Texture and Force Signals in Vision-Based Tactile Sensors

author.name: Zhirui Zhang, Yunkai Tang, Jiahang Li, Fan Fei, Jinnuo Zhang, Kairan Ding, Jieji Ren, Yandong Guo, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: DeTac is a dual-branch generative framework that separates clean shading and marker images from a single mixed observation of a vision-based tactile sensor, decoupling surface texture from contact force signals. It avoids the mask-sizing pitfalls of prior serial inpainting approaches through full-image synthesis and cross-branch synergistic optimization. This enables finer-grained perception for dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: LiDAR-based Humanoid Navigation in Dynamic, Non-Convex Environments via Spatio-Temporal Safe Corridors

author.name: Shubham S. Kumbhar, Panagiotis Artemiadis

entry.summary: This paper presents a real-time humanoid navigation pipeline that builds spatio-temporal safe corridors directly from LiDAR-based particle representations, avoiding the convex-obstacle simplifications of prior work, and couples them with LIP-based footstep planning and whole-body control. The system navigates around and within moving non-convex structures, demonstrated in simulation on the Digit humanoid with a 96% success rate. It integrates onboard perception, dynamic occupancy prediction, and dynamic locomotion control.

entry.title: ATOM: Abstract Transition and Option Modeling - Experience-Informed Hierarchical Navigation

author.name: Changxuan Yao, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: ATOM is a hierarchical navigation framework combining high-level graph planning over 3D scene graphs with reusable low-level option policies, storing a policy and cost-to-go per abstract transition for efficient repeated navigation in large 3D environments. Across repeated tasks it maintains a smoothed empirical distribution over option initiation states to improve decision-making.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Object-Centric SE(3) Forecasting for Real-Time Proactive Dynamic Grasping

author.name: Yirui Zhou, Hongli Xu, Ying Zheng, Yi Wang, Lap-Pui Chau

entry.summary: This work argues that contact-relevant rigid-body state in SE(3) is a compact, task-sufficient abstraction for proactive dynamic grasping, leading to a lightweight forecast-then-select framework that predicts future object trajectories from short pose histories and picks feasible interception states under kinematic and timing constraints via a reachability-aware selector. It runs in real time without needing visually complete future scenes.

entry.title: RESTA: Time-Scaling Augmentation for Data-Efficient Robot Imitation Learning

author.name: Yunpeng Jiang, Jianshu Hu, Han Fang, Zhiyuan Guan, Paul Weng, Yutong Ban

entry.summary: RESTA improves data efficiency in imitation learning by exploiting time-scaling augmentations: trajectory reversal with relabeling between paired tasks with opposite objectives, and temporal-stride resampling of demonstrations. The authors treat reversal as an approximate paired-task prior rather than a strict physical symmetry, which is a realistic framing for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems

author.name: Tianyi Xia, Ryan K. Cosner

entry.summary: The paper introduces reach-avoid contact certificates for stochastic hybrid systems where continuous flow follows an SDE and guard-triggered resets follow a controlled stochastic kernel. Unlike prior certificates requiring spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times or finite horizons, these certificates guarantee, over an infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with a prescribed probability. Conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, easing computation.

entry.title: Prior-Informed Generalizable Low-Rank Representation Learning via Regularized Adversarial Reweighting

author.name: Keyao Zhan, Junwei Lu, Tianxi Cai

entry.summary: PILLAR extends group distributionally robust optimization to low-rank matrix estimation across heterogeneous sources by regularizing adversarial source weights toward a user-specified reference distribution, smoothing a challenging nonconvex-concave objective. The prior-informed reweighting improves generalization under distribution shift. The method targets problems where high-dimensional parameters admit low-rank structure.

entry.title: When are safe Pareto improvements individually rational?

author.name: Anthony DiGiovanni

entry.summary: This post develops the game-theoretic conditions under which AI systems or their principals would rationally opt into safe Pareto improvements (SPIs), using renegotiation SPIs as a running example. It catalogs mechanisms that could make opting out seem individually rational, including settings with non-simultaneous commitments, extending the CLR SPI research agenda.

entry.title: How to Build a Benchmark That Actually Measures Taste

author.name: Xiaofan Wu, Xi Zeng, Miaoxia Chen, Peishan Chen, Shuyan Li, Chen Wang, Jiyun Yao, Hanyong Zhong, Jiahao Zhu

entry.summary: TasteBench is a pairwise good-vs-bad benchmark of expert craft judgment across visual, brand, book, and tech items under a frozen rubric with expert-only gold labels. Its control protocol separates craft judgment from test-gaming and surfaces validity threats including positional artifacts and a difficulty ceiling that inflate scores.

entry.title: MARL-BattleGrounds: A Novel JAX-native Benchmark for Heterogeneous and Competitive Multi-agent RL

author.name: Ulixes Tariq Hawili, Subramanian Ramamoorthy, Yoann Altmann, Ignacio Carlucho

entry.summary: MARL-BattleGrounds is a JAX-native benchmark for heterogeneous competitive multi-agent RL, positioned between simple-but-shallow environments like SMAX and rich-but-costly ones like Dota 2. Its Team Deathmatch mode features five distinct agent classes with synergistic and counter abilities, 52 hand-designed maps including a 12-map curriculum and held-out evaluation maps.

entry.title: AlphaRLM: Aligning Language Models for Literature-Grounded Symbolic Factor Discovery

author.name: Jie Huang, Yuecheng Hong, Yao Chen, Hao Zhong, Linfeng Xiao, Xudong Liu, Hao Xia, Jianxuan Xin

entry.summary: AlphaRLM is an RL framework that trains LLMs to construct executable symbolic alpha factors from financial literature without seed expressions, using Literature-Guided Operator Assembly for semantic priors and policy alignment with market feedback. It moves beyond prompting and evolutionary search toward direct policy learning for formulaic alpha mining.

entry.title: Single-step Retrosynthesis via Reinforcement Learning from Forward Feedback

author.name: Zixun Lan, Zhenfu Liu, Yi Li, Xinheng Wang, Mingmin Chi, Qibiao Wang, Jie Zhu, Xiaohui Tian, Fei Ma

entry.summary: Proposes RetroRLFF, which optimizes single-step retrosynthesis with reinforcement learning using both reference agreement and forward consistency: a frozen forward reaction model predicts products from generated reactant sets, providing reward beyond exact-match supervision. This addresses the one-to-many nature of retrosynthesis that reference-based training and evaluation ignore.

entry.title: ScreenASR-Bench: A Tiered Benchmark for Speech Recognition with Visual Context

author.name: Mingwei Fu, Zheshu Song, Zhikai Zhou, Shen Huang, Shidong Shang, Mengxiao Zhu

entry.summary: ScreenASR-Bench is a tiered benchmark for visually contextualized speech recognition with three levels of visual evidence: explicit on-screen text, visible non-text content, and implicit scene-level inference. Experiments across ASR models, large audio-language models, and omni models show visual context substantially aids recognition of acoustically ambiguous words.

entry.title: ChronoScribe: Semantic-Numerical Specialization for Instruction-Driven Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuchen Jiao, Miao Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Chengxi Li

entry.summary: Presents ChronoScribe, which divides instruction-driven time series forecasting between a LoRA-adapted LLM that proposes execution paths and context lengths, and deterministic rules plus time series foundation models that handle the numerical prediction. This specialization avoids forcing a single system to be both instruction-following and numerically precise.

entry.title: Output Discipline Sets the Floor: A Falsification-Guided, Model-Agnostic Agent Protocol for Auditable Hypothesis-Driven Decision Making

author.name: Jing Liu, Yongxing Qi, Ping Yao, Ting Wu

entry.summary: On the TCMEval-SDT benchmark for Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome differentiation, the authors find that output discipline and reasoning structure, not raw model capability, are the binding constraints: two years of model scaling moved zero-shot scores marginally while format and termination failures persist in frontier models. They propose a model-agnostic five-stage agent protocol with a candidate-by-evidence falsification matrix enforcing auditable decisions. The finding challenges assumptions about scaling alone improving structured decision tasks.

entry.title: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams

author.name: Zirui Shang, Xin Shu, Yang Liu, Zhi Gao, Xinxiao Wu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: The paper proposes activation-conditioned selective knowledge control, a lightweight continual learning method for GUI agents that uses neuron-level gradient manipulation to protect highly activated MLP neurons preserving historical knowledge while adapting to new applications. It balances shared versus app-specific knowledge across application streams.

entry.title: RealityBench: Simulated Environments to Evaluate a Vision Language Model's Ability to Document Human Physical Work

author.name: Andrew Perrault (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA), Anmol Takiar (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA), Dominik Wienecki (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA), Arnab Nandi (Relantic, Inc., Columbus, OH, USA)

entry.summary: RealityBench is a benchmark of simulated unconstrained field environments (e.g., rooftop solar installation, vehicle repair) for evaluating whether VLMs can document human physical work from first-person camera views. It addresses the lack of benchmarkable physical-work data, which is proprietary and high-variance compared to structured settings like kitchens and warehouses. It measures documentation and task-understanding capabilities of current models.

entry.title: Scale, Drivers, and Limits of Representational Alignment Across Large Language Models

author.name: Jialin Wu, Meenakshi Khosla

entry.summary: The paper introduces Neighborhood-Weighted RSA (NW-RSA), which weights stimulus pairs by representational proximity to resolve how representational alignment between LLMs varies from local neighborhoods to global geometry. It analyzes scale, drivers, and limits of alignment across models.

entry.title: Fitting Every Hint Is Not Enough: Premature Floods in Recurrent Algorithmic Reasoners

author.name: Amin Najafgholizadeh, Mohsen Afsharchi

entry.summary: On breadth-first search in SALSA-CLRS, the authors find recurrent algorithmic reasoners can reproduce every training hint yet fail on deep graphs by prematurely declaring nodes reached, a failure they call a premature flood. They trace two mechanisms for the failure, including hidden-state propagation triggered by out-of-distribution degree inputs and a sum-versus-average neighbor aggregation issue, showing none of the flooding models counts steps.

entry.title: When Does Compensating Inherited Quantization Error Help? Mean-Square Guarantees for Layer-Wise Quantization and Their Limits

author.name: Tianhao Guo

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical conditions under which layer-wise post-training quantization error compensation guarantees lower network output error than no compensation. For linear networks, with invertible calibration Gram matrices and zero-conditional-mean rounding errors (e.g., subtractive dither), fixed-strength compensation yields mean-square error no larger than the uncompensated scheme. It precisely characterizes when the technique helps and its limits.

entry.title: pi-Net: Empirical Latent Representations for Differentiable Physics Heads in Data-Scarce Systems

author.name: Akshay Dhalpe, Arnab Chattopadhyay, Shahriar Bakrani Balani, Eric Cortan\'ea, Sasu Tarkoma

entry.summary: pi-Net is a physics-informed latent variable model that fixes underdetermined dimensional-analysis-based imperfect simulators, using an encoder that maps inputs into a physically normalized latent space decoded by a differentiable physics head. It targets multi-physics prediction where full simulators are expensive and pure ML is data-hungry and opaque.

entry.title: SarcasTraps: Effect of Sarcasm on Turkish Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Niyazi Ahmet Metin, Dilara Kek\"ull\"uo\u{g}lu

entry.summary: SarcasTraps is a 479-entry Turkish external test set annotated for hate speech and sarcasm, used to show that sarcasm — harmful intent conveyed through mock praise or apparent politeness — degrades hate speech detection by fine-tuned BERTurk and XLM-RoBERTa classifiers and by large models including GPT-4.1. It matters because indirect harm evades detectors trained on explicitly hateful wording, and non-English languages are under-tested.

entry.title: SonicWorld: Source-Centric Latent Dynamics for Spatial Audio Reasoning

author.name: Chenlong Wei, Hanling Wang, Mingjin Lou, Yufan Shi, Yandong Sun, Sheldon Yu, Xiaohui Zhu, Xiaobo Jin, Yiwei Wang

entry.summary: SonicWorld tackles dynamic spatial audio reasoning, associating changing acoustic observations with sources to recover spatial states under overlapping speech and source motion. The paper introduces Sonic-Bench, with 2.8K first-order Ambisonics clips and 28.8K question-answer pairs across 480 simulated indoor scenes covering localization, distance estimation, and motion reasoning. The model fuses physical, acoustic, and semantic features into persistent source states projected into an Omni LLM.

entry.title: HASTE: Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Tripti Shukla, Shwetha Somasundaram, Akshat Gupta, Rohit Garg, Paul Duff, Ian Anderson

entry.summary: Proposes adding explicit hierarchical and attribute-level supervision to generative recommendation models that autoregressively generate semantic IDs for items. The approach improves training efficiency and long-tail recommendation performance compared to standard causal cross-entropy objectives that ignore the hierarchical structure of semantic IDs. Authored by an industry team, it targets practical recommendation quality for sparse tail items.

entry.title: Dissociating Answerability from Extraction in LLM Question Answering over Radiology Reports

author.name: Priyanshu Sinha, Kelsey McDonald

entry.summary: The paper proposes an evaluation method for RadQA-style radiology report QA that separates false-answer rates from over-abstention rates, splitting F1 changes into answerability and extraction components. Evaluating 13 LLMs reveals that models with similar F1 differ more than twofold in false-answer rates, and that adding an unanswerable demonstration changes when models answer rather than how well they extract.

entry.title: Dynamic K-Head: Difficulty-Supervised Budget Selection for Continuous Latent Reasoning

author.name: Ying Li, Yuqi Chen, Sixuan Li, Yunfeng Cai

entry.summary: Dynamic K-Head introduces a question-conditioned selector that chooses the number of latent recurrent updates before rollout, jointly trained with the reasoner using difficulty supervision derived from the question alone. It also shows latent-update counts can misrepresent true cost because short latent rollouts can shift computation into longer explicit continuations.

entry.title: FASHION-RQ: Mining Hierarchical Semantic Structure for Automated Evaluation of Fashion Retrieval

author.name: Tripti Shukla, Shwetha Somasundaram, Akshat Gupta, Rohit Garg, Paul Duff, Ian Anderson

entry.summary: FASHION-RQ is an automated framework that generates user-type queries and relevance sets for evaluating fashion retrieval directly from catalog structure, using hierarchical discrete representations from RQ-VAE that organize products into semantically coherent clusters. This avoids manual curation and synthetic-prompt limitations of prior benchmarks.

entry.title: GLST: Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Memory Decomposition Framework for Online Chained-Goal Navigation

author.name: Yousef Liang, Ryan Ardalan, Yarden Goraly, Chenhao Zhu, Yue Yin, Jonas Frey, Claire Tomlin, Marco Pavone, Shankar Sastry

entry.summary: GLST tackles online chained-goal navigation, where goals change mid-episode without explicit transition signals, creating conflicting memory requirements between continued exploration and strategic revisitation. The framework decomposes latent beliefs into global and local spatio-temporal components to handle both needs under partial observability. The author list includes well-known robotics researchers (Tomlin, Pavone, Sastry), lending credibility.

entry.title: Lightweight but Linguistically Fair? Quantisation Robustness across Bavarian, German, and English

author.name: Jophin John, Michael Hoffmann, Piroska Lendvai, Florent Dufour

entry.summary: This study examines whether post-training quantization degrades performance unevenly across a regional language variety, comparing Bavarian, Standard German, and English on a newly introduced aligned multiple-choice benchmark. Across 14 open-weight 7B-10B models, 8-bit GPTQ stays close to BF16 while 4-bit methods (GPTQ and AWQ) are much less stable and reduce accuracy by about 1.4-1.5 points. The fairness question of whether compression disproportionately harms low-resource varieties is directly addressed.

entry.title: Task-evoked eye movements as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults

author.name: Youxiang Sun, Yujie Nie, Zhuoru Wu, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Xiang Li, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan

entry.summary: This clinical study of 155 participants aged 14-20 investigates whether task-evoked eye movements during emotional-spatial free-viewing and memory-guided recall tasks serve as digital biomarkers of depression severity. Greater severity was associated with lower gaze-allocation entropy among 19 prespecified eye-movement features analyzed with covariate-adjusted models. Interpretable objective measures could complement symptom-based depression assessment in youth.

entry.title: Variance Fingerprints: Component-Wise Identification of Content Factors by Augmentation Design

author.name: D. Hudson Smith

entry.summary: The paper asks whether augmentation design in self-supervised learning can make individual content factors identifiable, assigning each instance a fixed recorded set of augmentation strengths so that differing factor responses yield distinguishing variation patterns. Under decoder and support assumptions, the authors prove factor identifiability in a conditional Gaussian setting. It advances theory on when SSL recovers disentangled factors rather than an entangled content subspace.

entry.title: DEFT: Disentanglement-Enhanced Fine-Tuning for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Yuqiu Deng, Muyun Jiang, Zongpeng Zhang, Mingqing Xiao, Yansen Wang, Peiliang Gong, Xinliang Zhou, Yi Ding, Ziyu Jia, Cuntai Guan, Chenyu Liu

entry.summary: DEFT is a plug-and-play adapter for EEG foundation models that disentangles pretrained tokens into task-oriented content and subject-consistent style branches, then predicts from the content branch alone. Using recursive Gaussian refinement and temporal-variance reweighting, it reduces the subject-variation burden on downstream classifiers, especially in cross-subject settings.

entry.title: Prediction with Expert Advice under Heavy-Tailed Losses

author.name: Yuki Shibukawa, Shinji Ito

entry.summary: The paper characterizes the minimax pseudo-regret rate for prediction with expert advice under heavy-tailed losses where only a fractional (1+epsilon)-moment is bounded, showing existing epsilon=1 methods are suboptimal when epsilon<1. It proposes Adaptive Heavy-Tailed FTRL using robust scale adaptation and truncation to achieve the minimax rate without knowing epsilon or theta in advance. Gap-dependent lower bounds are also established.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning based Topology-Agnostic Defense for Virtual Power Plants

author.name: Pooja Algikar, Stefano Fenu, Kumarsinh Jhala, Siby Plathottam

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid cyber-physical defense for virtual power plant aggregated distributed energy resources, combining game-theoretic perturbation planning with model-free RL under Bayesian belief updates. Key novelty is topology agnosticism: the defense assumes no access to grid network models or operating conditions, matching third-party aggregator constraints. It targets coordinated cyberattacks that could disrupt distribution, bulk, and market operations.

entry.title: DC-Flow: Target-Conditioned Cyclic Peptide Design via Delayed-Coupling Flow Matching

author.name: Yitian Wang, Minjie Cheng, Yaning Cui, Maohua Yang, Dongdong Wang, Hongteng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes DC-Flow, a staged generative framework for target-conditioned cyclic peptide design built on Delayed-Coupling Flow Matching, which postpones sequence and side-chain activation until a target-conditioned backbone forms. This avoids local traps of predictor-assisted workflows and structural ambiguity of end-to-end generators, coordinating side chains with macrocyclic closure.

entry.title: ML-CLAPPS: A Probabilistic Framework for Imbalanced Multilabel Learning under Class Prioritization
