author.name: Priel Hazan, Nir Almog, Noam Keidar, Yael Yaniv, Assaf Schuster

entry.summary: ML-CLAPPS is a learnable sampling framework for imbalanced multilabel learning that optimizes a distribution over training instances to control model exposure to different classes, jointly handling label co-occurrence and the need to prioritize high-risk conditions. It is motivated by clinical ECG classification where false negatives for rare high-risk conditions are very costly.

entry.title: Spectral Considerations on Unsupervised Time-domain EEG Representation Learning with Deep Networks

author.name: David Aquilu\'e-Llorens, Abel Puigseslloses, Angel Blanco, Claire Braboszcz, Aureli Soria-Frisch

entry.summary: This study systematically examines how unsupervised time-domain deep learning architectures under-represent high-frequency EEG information, a concern amplified by EEG's 1/f power decay that can mask disease-relevant signatures. It compares three autoencoder architectures (LSTMVAE, VAEEG, Transformer) and a state-of-the-art EEG foundation model through a spectral lens. The findings inform design choices for biomarker extraction from raw neural signals.

entry.title: Learning Deployable Causal Action Geometry under Temporal Non-Stationarity

author.name: Changjian Liu, Tianyu Wang, Yuwei Xu, Xiaoxuan Deng, Zhilin Zhang, Yong Gao, Chuan Yu, Jian Xu, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: The paper addresses learning continuous decision response laws from non-stationary observational time series, where naive pooling conflates action effects with shifting baselines. The authors define deployable causal action geometry, the action-response shape that remains stable after anchoring away action-independent level shifts, and propose an estimation approach for it.

entry.title: Masked Diffusion for Travel Diaries Synthesis

author.name: Pascal Jutras-Dub\'e, Raziq Zaman, Fabian Bastin, Cinzia Cirillo, Ruqi Zhang

entry.summary: DiaryBridge is a masked diffusion model that synthesizes complete household travel diaries as single token sequences, using count tokens and special symbols to keep variable-length household structure whole instead of splitting or cropping. The representation-preserving design maintains cross-segment dependencies that prior pipelines destroy.

entry.title: GeoNIRS: Geometry-Aware Pretraining for Heterogeneous fNIRS Representation Learning

author.name: Zongsheng Li, Shengyuan Zhu, Zimo Zhang, Hanyao Li, Shengming Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: GeoNIRS is a geometry-aware pretraining framework for functional near-infrared spectroscopy that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts, compressing variable channel sets into fixed-size latents with bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction and temporal masking. Base and large models are pretrained on eight and 22 heterogeneous datasets respectively without downstream labels or data. This enables transferable foundation-model-style representations for a portable neuroimaging modality.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimization of CVaR with Unknown Hyperparameters

author.name: Valentin Margraf, Jonas Hanselle, Viktor Bengs, Serafima Lebedeva, Eyke H\"ullermeier, Marcel Wever

entry.summary: The paper proposes HE-CV-UCB, the first no-regret algorithm for Bayesian optimization of Conditional Value-at-Risk when GP kernel hyperparameters are unknown and must be estimated from limited data. It adaptively eliminates inconsistent surrogate models from a finite candidate set, addressing the tail-risk distortion that misspecification causes.

entry.title: A Refresh Interval Does Not Fully Specify a Refresh Schedule: Learning-Rate-Dependent Placement in Kronecker-Preconditioned Language Model Training

author.name: Xinyu Wang (McGill University), Zhiwei Zhai (The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Yu Gu (McGill University), Zijun Yu (McGill University), Sicheng Lyu (McGill University), Jingrui Tian (McGill University), Lei Ding (University of Manitoba), Ziyang Song (Ohio University), Xiao-Wen Chang (McGill University)

entry.summary: This paper shows that for Kronecker-preconditioned optimizers like Mousse, the placement of periodic curvature eigendecomposition refreshes matters: at a fixed refresh count, moving middle refreshes changes held-out loss at equal compute, and the best placement reverses as learning rate changes. The finding means single-learning-rate comparisons can rank schedules inconsistently.

entry.title: Metric-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Object Hallucination Reduction in LVLM-Based Image Captioning

author.name: Thanh Nguyen, Hee Suk Yoon, Tung Minh Luu, Eunseop Yoon, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: This paper proposes an RL framework to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language model image captioning, using NLP metrics as reward signals to avoid costly human feedback. It explicitly analyzes and mitigates pitfalls of metric-only rewards such as reward hacking and spurious shortcuts. This offers a scalable alternative to RLHF for hallucination reduction.

entry.title: Harnessing SPAD Noise: Test-Time Gated Attention for Indoor Depth Estimation

author.name: Yiquan Gao

entry.summary: Proposes treating native single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) noise as an informative prior encoding environmental characteristics rather than an artifact to denoise, introducing a test-time gated attention method for indoor depth estimation that fuses monocular and SPAD modalities. This reframing addresses scale ambiguity, edge bleeding, and zero-shot generalization issues in metric depth prediction.

entry.title: NetRL: Powering Network Decisions via NetGRPO-Driven Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lingfeng Peng, Xiaohui Xie, Yang Bao, Yong Cui

entry.summary: NetRL is a two-stage framework applying LLM-based reinforcement learning to network decision-making tasks like adaptive bitrate streaming, load balancing, and congestion control. It combines supervised fine-tuning on demonstration trajectories with online policy optimization via a NetGRPO-style objective, using a mixed textual-numeric interface to generalize across heterogeneous network tasks.

entry.title: Online Individualized Treatment Selection under Partial Feedback: False Discovery Control and Minimax Optimality

author.name: Runzhe Gu, Zinan Zhao, Wenguang Sun, Xintao Xia

entry.summary: PAITS addresses online individualized treatment selection with partial feedback, combining sequential estimation of local null risks, randomized exploration, and feedback-driven threshold updates to preferentially treat individuals benefiting from treatment. It establishes asymptotic false discovery rate control and sublinear gap-weighted assignment regret relative to a population oracle.

entry.title: LLM-HB: Language-Aware LLM-Guided Hotword Biasing for Code-Switching ASR

author.name: Yuxuan He, Genshun Wan, Pengcheng Li, Gongping Huang, Jianqing Gao, Yanmin Qian

entry.summary: LLM-HB improves automatic speech recognition on code-switching speech by combining a mixture-of-experts adaptor and language prediction head with LLM-prompted hotword biasing. It reports a 20.30% relative reduction in mixed error rate on the ASRU2019 code-switching challenge test set.

entry.title: A Generalized McDiarmid Inequality: Sample Reuse and Non-Uniform Unbounded Differences

author.name: Jeremiah Birrell

entry.summary: Develops a generalization of McDiarmid's concentration inequality supporting unbounded, non-uniform difference functions and quantifying benefits of training sample reuse alongside auxiliary random variables. It is applied to derive concentration bounds for score-based generative modeling.

entry.title: A Differentiable 3D Scene Graph Metric via Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry

author.name: U-Chae Jun, Yoonhyuk Choi, Jiwoo Kang

entry.summary: The authors propose Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry, a graph-level differentiable supervision objective for 3D scene graph prediction that measures semantic and structural discrepancy between predicted and ground-truth scene graphs, reinterpreting classifier outputs as an aligned probabilistic scene graph. This addresses the limitation of slot-wise losses that treat mild label errors and structurally disruptive relational errors the same. It could improve scene understanding for robotics and 3D perception.

entry.title: Hierarchical Time Series Forecasting with Operator-Valued Kernels

author.name: Junjie Yang (LPSM), Adeline Fermanian (LMO, IUF), Claire Boyer (LMO, IUF), G\'erard Biau (LPSM)

entry.summary: The authors formulate hierarchical time series forecasting as multivariate regression in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space, using structured operator-valued kernels so that hierarchical coherence holds by construction rather than via post-hoc reconciliation. They derive excess risk bounds and propose tailored kernel constructions for hierarchical data.

entry.title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models

author.name: Michalis Pistos, Bart{\l}omiej W. Papie\.z

entry.summary: This work investigates SAM2 object pointers, compact object-level representations produced during segmentation, as transferable features beyond standard encoder embeddings. Experiments on two PET/CT tumour prediction tasks show that pointers learned with segmentation supervision alone encode tumour-discriminative information useful for downstream medical prediction.

entry.title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks

author.name: J. Arturo Esquivel, Jorge A. Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo, Sergio Pablo-Garc\'ia, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik, Vianey Leos-Barajas

entry.summary: This paper introduces a neural simulation-based inference pipeline using shared 1D-CNNs and permutation-invariant set attention to learn summary statistics from multi-experiment time series, jointly performing model selection and posterior estimation for chemical reaction networks. It outperforms classical SMC-ABC approaches that rely on handcrafted summaries.

entry.title: SciCurateBench: Curating Experimental Data from Heterogeneous Scientific Literature with Verbal-Action Agents

author.name: Minuk Ma, Kaiyun Guo, Jiarui Ding

entry.summary: SciCurateBench is a benchmark of 200 expert-annotated life-science papers requiring systems to verify conjunctive experimental criteria from raw, unprocessed literature. The authors show that plain LLMs and popular reasoning, tool-using, and feedback-based agents all struggle with the task.

entry.title: Social Bias in Chinese Large Language Models under Social Media Expressions

author.name: Mo Zhou

entry.summary: This study builds 73 paired probes spanning gender, region, and occupation to test how Chinese LLMs express social bias under realistic social-media-style expressions, including internet slang, emoji, and sarcasm, which prior template-based benchmarks miss. It reframes the task from plausibility judgment to social consensus estimation and distinguishes stylistic from sarcastic packaging that preserves or reverses polarity. Six Chinese models are evaluated, revealing how safety alignment compresses conventional bias ratings.

entry.title: Learning Proposition-Level Links from Sentence-Level Supervision for Neuro-Symbolic NLI

author.name: Xuyao Feng, Antonis Bikakis

entry.summary: This paper improves neuro-symbolic natural language inference by introducing a trainable atom linker that jointly predicts link existence, source selection, and relation type between propositional units of independently translated premise and hypothesis representations. Without atom-pair annotations, the method treats cross-formula links as latent variables and trains from sentence-level NLI labels alone. This improves on prior AMR-plus-SAT systems that relied on fixed, untrained linking components.

entry.title: SIREN: Situation-aware Index for Response and Emergency ActioNability in Crisis Translation

author.name: Maria Carmen Staiano, Lifeng Han, Johanna Monti, Francesca Chiusaroli

entry.summary: SIREN is a human evaluation framework assessing whether machine translation choices in multilingual crisis communication preserve protective action, directive force, and urgency. Applied to HOPE-annotated Italian-English translations from ChatGPT-4o and Google Translate, roughly 32-49 percent of errors compromise actionability, mostly affecting protective actions. It highlights that standard MT quality metrics miss safety-critical failures in emergency contexts.

entry.title: Worth Their Weights? Evaluating Generative Models for Discourse Parsing

author.name: Luke Gessler, Amir Zeldes

entry.summary: The authors compare generative and discriminative approaches to RST discourse parsing at matched parameter counts, finding discriminative parsers much stronger, though large generative models sometimes win, with generative models especially good at EDU segmentation. They report new state-of-the-art results on the RST-DT benchmark.

entry.title: Where Words Begin and End

author.name: Husein Zolkepli

entry.summary: Comparing nine forced-aligner configurations against human word boundaries on read, conversational, and telephone English, the authors find MFA most precise while CTC aligners start words late due to blank-token dominance. They then fine-tune Whisper with LoRA on 47 hours of human-placed boundaries across 87 languages to predict timestamp tokens, outperforming MFA in precision.

entry.title: PAINT: A Framework for Multilingual Pain Representation from Medical Licensing Exams to Real-World Clinical Texts

author.name: Boya Zhang, Yuanchao Ma, Jiageng Wu, Krittaphas Chaisutyakorn, Rodrigo Gameiro, Ahram Han, Chien-Yu Huang, Nikhil Jaiswal, Marianna Leite, Miriam Mora-Mau, Jaime Pineda-Moreno, Siena Placino, Ryohei Yamamoto, Yugang Jia, Jie Yang, Leo Anthony Celi, Douglas Teodoro

entry.summary: PAINT is a multilingual framework for studying pain representation in medical text, with nine dataset partitions spanning English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, covering both licensing exam questions and real-world clinical notes with clinician involvement. Pain expression varies by language, documentation type, and demographics, and prior work is largely monolingual. The resource supports clinically meaningful NLP for a symptom central to care.

entry.title: Word-Aligned Prosody Reflects Speaker Differences More Than Depression or PTSD Severity

author.name: Hsiang-Chen Yeh, Aurosweta Mahapatra, Shreeram Suresh Chandra, Ryan L. Boyd, Berrak Sisman

entry.summary: This measurement-focused study examines the stability of word-aligned prosody used for depression and PTSD detection across four corpora of acted, spontaneous, and clinical speech. Word-specific deviations show little cross-context recurrence while speaker-level summaries are far more stable, and these representations reflect speaker differences more than symptom severity. The findings question the clinical validity of a common prosodic measurement practice.

entry.title: SliderEdit++: Improved Slider Trajectories in Instruction-Based Image Editing

author.name: Arman Zarei, Sayan Nag, Bryan Wang, Franck Dernoncourt, Varun Manjunatha, Nedim Lipka, Soheil Feizi, Samyadeep Basu

entry.summary: Studies continuous slider-based control of edit intensity in instruction-based image editing, introducing SlideBench with metrics for monotonic progression, perceptual continuity, and slider disentanglement. SliderEdit++ regularizes slider trajectories to fix abrupt jumps, non-monotonic changes, and interference between jointly controlled sliders.

entry.title: UMAS3D: Unified Mask-Free 3D Editing with Region-Adaptive Source Preservation

author.name: Xianlin Zeng, Xiaolong Shen, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: UMAS3D is a training-free, inversion-free 3D editing framework that needs no external masks, converting text, bounding box, and reference-image conditions into common target-view guidance. Addition, deletion, modification, appearance, and pose editing share one downstream generation process with online edit-region estimation for source preservation.

entry.title: Seg2Click: Learning Pixel-Level Action Masks for GUI Visual Grounding

author.name: Jingchao Wang, Dingjiang Huang

entry.summary: Seg2Click reformulates GUI visual grounding as executable-region prediction, using bounding-box supervision to predict pixel-level masks of where a click can validly execute an instruction, rather than single-point coordinates or patch scoring tied to visual-token footprints. This reduces spatial ambiguity in crowded screenshots for GUI agents.

entry.title: Towards Complementary Keypoint Detection via Mixture of Detectors

author.name: Xiaoyong Lu, Guobao Xiao, Dong Liang, Songlin Du

entry.summary: MoD distills heterogeneous keypoint detectors into a unified model that predicts diverse detection maps in a single forward pass, then formulates detector selection as a patch-wise, budget-conditioned decision process. This adaptively composes complementary detector strengths for dense matching pipelines.

entry.title: PolUR: Polarization Aware Multimodal Degradation Perception for Underwater Image Restoration

author.name: Wenshuo Zhang, Xiangyue Zhang, Junlin Li, Wenjie Tian, Yubo Zheng, Hongli Xu, Jingyu Ru, Xinde Li

entry.summary: PolUR jointly uses polarization and RGB information in a language-driven framework to identify underwater degradation types and severity via structured semantic instructions, then performs joint restoration. It extends polarization cues beyond clear-water conditions to mixed degradations including color casts, haze, and low light.

entry.title: Noise2Match: Self-Supervised Low-Dose CT Denoising via Adaptive Inter-Slice Matching

author.name: Langrui Zhou, Guang Li, Xinyu Huang, Ziteng Zhou, Zuyang Huang, Hongming Shan, Shouhua Luo, Ning Gu

entry.summary: Proposes Noise2Match, a self-supervised low-dose CT denoising method that uses adjacent slices as training signal while adaptively handling the non-rigid anatomical misalignment between slices that breaks naive inter-slice approaches. This avoids the need for paired noisy-clean data that is impractical to collect. A competent domain-specific methodological advance.

entry.title: DuplexBridge: Coordinating Understanding and Generation for Unified Image Editing

author.name: Yidi Liu, Jie Xiao, Chaojie Mao, Jingfeng Zhang, Xueyang Fu

entry.summary: DuplexBridge coordinates the understanding and generation capabilities within a unified model for image editing, using the model's own understanding to enhance prompts for its generation without external modules. It introduces source-grounded bridges, independent supervision per role, and reciprocal trust checks, plus the CE-Bench benchmark, to attribute edit failures correctly.

entry.title: Scalable Multi-Human Cooperative Manipulation via Commander-Executor Coordination

author.name: Buzhen Huang, Xingchen Wu, Yuanwang Yang, Chenyi Xie, Kun Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical commander-executor framework for multi-human cooperative object manipulation, where a commander performs semantic and geometric planning, decomposes tasks into role-specific subtasks, and generates shared object-centric coordination plans with timing and action specifications. It extends humanoid collaboration beyond simple carrying to role-dependent, long-horizon sequential tasks. Multi-agent humanoid cooperation is an underexplored and challenging control problem.

entry.title: VbotNav-0: Asynchronous Cloud-Edge Dual-Policy Navigation across Indoor and Outdoor Environments

author.name: Shiqi Tan, Yujun Zhang, Keyu Li, Shuaixi Pan, Siyu Zhou, Hailong Qin, Yinan Yu

entry.summary: VbotNav-0 is a cloud-edge dual-policy navigation system where a cloud policy generates subgoal guidance from visual history and instructions while an edge policy produces local trajectories from RGB and LiDAR, connected via asynchronous policy-to-policy conditioning. A shared route representation spans indoor paths and outdoor map routes, and training combines demonstrations, corrective data, and grounding supervision. It targets continuous indoor-outdoor navigation with a responsive local loop.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Visual History: Learning Motion-Adaptive Temporal Receptive Fields for Complex-Terrain Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Hao Zhang, Yuping Yan, Yitian Hong, Luying Feng, Tianhong Wang, Fengqi Dai, Wei Chen, Yaochu Jin

entry.summary: TempoLoco is a body-aware visual perception framework for quadruped locomotion that organizes depth history according to the robot's current speed, posture, and gait phase, learning multiple complementary temporal views from a long depth buffer. This fixes the mismatch where fixed temporal receptive fields are insufficient in some motion states and misaligned in others. It improves perceptive locomotion over complex terrain.

entry.title: Anticipatory Textile MMG-Strain Sensing for Confirm-Then-Assist Soft Knee Exosuits

author.name: Zheng Ma, Xiao Jin, Zhenhua Yu

entry.summary: This letter introduces a knitted textile interface co-sampling a three-channel mechanomyography array and a strain sensor on a single 500 Hz clock, showing MMG activation precedes knee motion by roughly 320-344 ms during sit-to-stand, with strain slope resolving movement direction on 649 of 650 transitions without per-participant training. This enables a confirm-then-assist control paradigm for soft exosuits that anticipates movement onset more robustly than sEMG.

entry.title: Directional Pullback Regularization for Long-Horizon Rollout of Latent World Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Shatadal Mishra, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Nejib Ammar

entry.summary: The paper introduces Directional Pullback Regularization, which defines a kinematics-aware anisotropic Riemannian metric in decoded state space respecting nonholonomic vehicle constraints and pulls it back through the decoder Jacobian to shape latent transitions. This improves long-horizon rollout quality of driving world models without changing the predictor architecture. It is a geometrically principled alternative to architecture redesign.

entry.title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation

author.name: Silvia Terrile, Kaichen Shi, Taejun Kwon, Jiseok Lee, Nathan Lepora, Yeejin Lee, Saekwang Nam, Efi Psomopoulou

entry.summary: This work combines limited real-world validation data (82 camera-tracked contacts), high-fidelity ANSYS FEM simulation, and graph neural networks to predict 2D tactile deformation in soft sensors in real time. The key idea is decoupling validation from training: the small real dataset only tunes and validates the FEM model, which then generates 768 synthetic configurations for GNN training. This sidesteps both FEM's computational cost and the impracticality of large physical datasets for fragile sensors.

entry.title: LAG-IO: Multi-IMU State Estimation for Legged Robots Using Factor Graphs

author.name: Yicheng Zhou, Longwen Chen, Qinghua Yu, Junhao Xiao, Huimin Lu, Xieyuanli Chen

entry.summary: LAG-IO is a factor-graph-based multi-IMU state estimation framework for legged robots that tightly couples a main body IMU, multiple leg-mounted IMUs, and joint encoders in sliding-window optimization, with handling for non-stationary foot-ground interactions. It targets robust proprioceptive odometry where EKF approaches drift during slippage or dynamic locomotion.

entry.title: Cross-Embodiment Affordance Transfer for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Sawera Yaseen, Serge Thill, Rekha Raja

entry.summary: This paper addresses the mismatch between human-annotated affordances and what a specific robot can physically execute, proposing a framework that translates human affordance labels into robot-executable affordance predictions conditioned on the robot's physical properties and a 3D point cloud of the object. The network predicts which surface regions are geometrically and mechanically feasible for the robot to act on.

entry.title: Quickest Change-point Detection in Generalized Linear Models with Variational Estimation

author.name: Jonghyeok Lee, Yao Xie

entry.summary: The authors propose a window-limited CUSUM procedure for quickest change-point detection in generalized linear models with unknown post-change parameters, estimating the parameter via a variational-inequality formulation. This matters in settings like monitoring whether a learned representation's relationship with a response drifts over time, where only limited post-change observations are available. VI estimation offers favorable finite-sample accuracy for noncanonical links compared to maximum-likelihood alternatives.

entry.title: AcrossVAM2.0: Conflict-Aware Point Supervision for Parameter-Efficient Video Diffusion Adaptation

author.name: Nan Wu, Yee Hung Hong

entry.summary: ACROSSVAM2.0 adapts a 5.01B-parameter text-to-video diffusion transformer using explicit point correspondence supervision without overwriting the pretrained appearance prior. It combines confidence-weighted track-and-visibility heads, zero-initialized residual feedback, and asymmetric PCGrad on shared LoRA parameters, with a four-way multi-seed ablation.

entry.title: Relational Semantic Grounding for Test-Time Discovery

author.name: Tianle Liu, Gongbo Cheng, Chenggong Ni, Minming Gu, Tao Zhou, Fuyuan Hu, Fan Lyu

entry.summary: SEGA improves test-time discovery by using LLM-generated attribute descriptions of known classes to build an attribute-anchored visual-semantic space, then grounding unknown samples against similar and dissimilar anchors at test time. This makes discovered novel classes interpretable rather than anonymous clusters.

entry.title: Bridging Risk Approximation Gaps in Model Predictive Task Sampling via In-Context Modeling

author.name: Jiarong Wen, Qi Tao, Kaiyu Zhang, Yun Qu, Lizhou Cai, Heming Zou, Yuhang Jiang, Qi Wang

entry.summary: The paper improves model predictive task sampling (MPTS) for RL by replacing risk predictive models trained on sparse optimization histories with in-context modeling that generalizes across the task space. This targets sample efficiency in meta-RL, domain randomization, and LLM post-training where agent-environment interaction cost is the bottleneck.

entry.title: SkillForgeBench: Evaluating Agent Reliability Grounded in Agent Skill Specifications

author.name: Zhengxi Li, Junyi Zhou, Qiyuan Zhang, Chuhan Wu, Fuyuan Lyu, Le Tian, Xiao Zhou, Chen Ma, Yufei Wang

entry.summary: SkillForgeBench is a benchmark that uses agent skill specifications as execution blueprints across three co-designed stages to evaluate whether agents strictly satisfy diverse, procedurally complex requirements. It aims to combine the domain breadth of crowdsourced benchmarks with the procedural depth of expert-curated ones.

entry.title: On the Complexity Gap Between POMDPs and Multi-Environment POMDPs

author.name: Eline M. Bovy, Caleb Probine, Marnix Suilen, Ufuk Topcu, Nils Jansen

entry.summary: Maps the computational complexity landscape of multi-environment POMDPs (ME-POMDPs), showing that subclasses tractable in the single-environment case (such as blind MDPs, proven NP-complete) can become intractable under model uncertainty. This sharpens the known PSPACE-completeness boundary for robust finite-horizon reward maximization.

entry.title: Knowledge transfer between simple discrete worlds

author.name: Silv\`ere Gangloff, Jan Hula

entry.summary: Studies rule-based generalization in small discrete worlds using Sudoku-like puzzles with composable rules, training a single depth-recurrent model and testing at four novelty levels from new puzzles to entirely unseen rule instances. The model receives rules either symbolically or as solved examples, enabling analysis of what knowledge transfers across worlds.

entry.title: Does the Explanation Drift Before the Guarantee? Label-Free Early Warning on Evolving Graphs

author.name: Tomasz Szanda{\l}a, Damian Raczkowski

entry.summary: Studies whether attribution drift on evolving graph streams can serve as a label-free early warning of impending conformal-coverage failure. The paper repairs naive drift statistics twice, conditioning on edge presence and aggregating over structural roles to survive edge relabeling, then tests six pre-registered regimes for predicting coverage loss.

entry.title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search

author.name: Yingtao Ren, Aolin Li, Cheng Cheng, Huiyun Hu, Huasheng Liang, Baoxing Xie, Jun Yuan, Haijun Wu, Chenxing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes WeFair, a fidelity-aware alignment approach for compact personalized query rewriters in short-video search, leveraging users' actual reformulations and behavioral traces to avoid intent drift from engagement-optimized but unfaithful rewrites. The system targets strict latency constraints while deciding when personalization is warranted and preserving the user's immediate information need.

entry.title: Agentic4PDM: Host-Governed Evidence Admissibility for Industrial Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Nam V. Nguyen, Hoang Van Truong, Hieu D. D., Duy Khuong Nguyen, Quang Pham, Tung Kieu

entry.summary: Agentic4PDM is a framework for industrial fault diagnosis that separates adaptive LLM-agent investigation of sensor time series from host-side control over which evidence is admissible. Reusable analytical tools exploit periodicity, trends, and transients, while governance prevents the agent from overstating weak or conflicting signal evidence, reducing reliance on repeatedly retrained specialized classifiers.

entry.title: Two-Stage Multi-modal Learning for Dynamic Audio-Visual Navigation: From Physical Alignment to Scene Aggregation

author.name: Jia Li, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: The paper tackles dynamic audio-visual navigation with moving sound targets, proposing a two-stage framework where an Intensity-Calibrated Geometry Encoder performs physics-informed spatial reasoning before scene aggregation. This moves beyond semantic auditory features to improve generalization to unheard sound categories.

entry.title: Select or Rewrite: Oracle-Guided Fine-Tuning for Generative ASR Post-Editing from N-Best Hypotheses

author.name: Shiran Liu, Gaohui Xu, Sergio Burdisso, Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Petr Motlicek

entry.summary: The paper proposes oracle-guided fine-tuning for LLM-based ASR post-editing, constructing supervision from three curated pools: corrections to teach selection, regularizers with correct top-1 to discourage over-editing, and hard negatives with absent references to suppress hallucination. This yields more effective supervision than random subset fine-tuning and addresses the brittleness of prompt-only correction.

entry.title: Anchor-and-Harvest Curriculum: A Fully Unmasked Non-LLM Curriculum for Craftax

author.name: Jiayu Zhu, Luyuan Li, Yuyuan Shi, Hanyi Dong

entry.summary: Introduces AHC, a rule-based curriculum learning system for the Craftax-Full RL benchmark that combines achievement-oriented tasks, harvested initial-state progress, difficulty adaptation, and original-task practice without any LLM inference, keeping all 43 actions available. Across three runs it improves native-task return to 46.70 versus 41.91 for fresh PPO-GTrXL, evaluated on 1,024 fixed worlds.

entry.title: OceanFlow: Coherent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Ocean Modeling

author.name: Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Hao Wu, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: OceanFlow applies coherent flow matching to probabilistic global ocean modeling, explicitly optimizing the joint distribution of ensemble members rather than generating perturbation-driven spread, improving calibration and physical consistency. Probabilistic ocean states matter for risk-aware marine operations, climate analysis, and scientific decision-making where deterministic trajectories are insufficient.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal Sensor Fusion with JEPA Representations for Breathing Activity and Pose Recognition

author.name: Yunxiang Luo, Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Xiaoting Wu, Nhi Nguyen, Le Nguyen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: The authors transfer frozen V-JEPA2 features to a heterogeneous sensor suite (RGB video, depth video, radar) for breathing activity and pose recognition, using a shared fusion model with modality queries and explicit availability flags. It handles all seven non-empty sensor subsets, including missing sensors, on 39 subjects with controlled evaluation of subset supervision and pooling capacity. The model reaches about 75 macro-F1 for activity recognition.

entry.title: MP-MNCA: Morphology-Prior Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention for Efficient Spatial Domain Identification

author.name: Sidharthan Sivacoumar Chitra, Sanjeev Manivannan

entry.summary: MP-MNCA is a spatial transcriptomics framework that preserves full 3,000-gene representations while routing molecular information across spatial neighbors, using histological similarity as a continuous attention prior under a self-supervised masked contrastive objective. It is evaluated on 12 human DLPFC sections against established baselines with attention to convergence efficiency.

entry.title: KNN Implementation Details Can Dramatically Change Performance: An Example from Cover Trees

author.name: Amol Khanna, Edward Raff

entry.summary: This paper shows that rarely-reviewed implementation details materially change nearest-neighbor search performance, using the Cover Tree as a case study via RustKNN, a unified Rust implementation of three construction variants and three query modes. It finds optimal query strategy depends on k and dataset, so implementation choices can flip conclusions about algorithm superiority. It matters as a reproducibility caution for the widely used KNN literature.

entry.title: Graph-free Retrieval with Graph-Modified Embeddings

author.name: Federica Santi (Cognee Inc), Vasilije Markovi\'{c} (Cognee Inc), Daniel Scott (Cognee Inc), Lazar Obradovi\'{c} (Cognee Inc)

entry.summary: This industry paper from Cognee compares five offline graph-based embedding transformations that let dense retrieval recover evidence connected through intermediate entities without query-time graph access. Direct replacement of original embeddings hurts evidence recovery, but multi-stage strategies that use graph-modified embeddings to guide search while retaining originals improve it. The strongest configuration notably improves questions requiring linked facts or comparisons.

entry.title: Layer-wise Input Recoverability in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Maxwell Spiridonov, Alireza Rahmansetayesh, Pierre Baldi

entry.summary: The authors study how much of a convolutional layer's own input is recoverable from its output using a patch-level reconstruction probe, complementing information-bottleneck analyses that measure mutual information with the original image and labels. Probe size depends on channels and kernel size rather than feature-map size, making the analysis tractable for CNNs. This contributes to understanding information transformation across network depth.

entry.title: Learning to See through Action: Predictive Curiosity for Robots

author.name: Stelios Zarifis, Panagiotis Filntisis, George Retsinas, Petros Maragos

entry.summary: DySCOVER is a self-supervised framework for active robot visual learning in which a robot trains a visual autoencoder and a recurrent world model, with a policy driven purely by intrinsic rewards combining reconstruction error (novelty) and world-model error. Inspired by developmental learning through action, it studies whether curiosity-driven interaction improves visual representations. A robotics and intrinsic-motivation contribution.

entry.title: PGSB: Pretrained-Guided Shared Basis for LoRA Model Merging

author.name: Muqing Liu, Chongjie Si, Zhuoya Liu, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: PGSB improves LoRA model merging by learning a shared basis guided by the pretrained weights, asking which update directions provide reliable cross-task support rather than merging task updates directly in their original low-rank spaces. This yields a unified multi-task model without storing separate adapters per task.

entry.title: TagBO: LLM-Driven Task-Aware Graph Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Xinzhe Yuan, Zimu Zeng, Zhuo Chen, Jianshu Zhang, Jinzong Dong, Jingyi Chen, Nanyang Ye, Huan Xiong, Qinying Gu

entry.summary: TagBO integrates LLM-derived relational priors with descriptor-based structural information in graph Bayesian optimization for mixed-variable scientific optimization, relaxing the assumption that structural similarity implies performance similarity. It targets sample-efficient optimization over large combinatorial spaces under costly evaluations.

entry.title: Blending experimental electron density information to protein-ligand interaction

author.name: Seonghyun Park, Shuan Chen, Jun Jin Choong, Noboru Kuno, Gyubok Lee, Kaushalya Madhawa, Keisuke Ozawa, Hikaru Shindo, Sungsoo Ahn

entry.summary: CoDE is a coordinate-and-density encoder pre-trained on roughly 100K curated protein-ligand complexes, representing binding sites on a voxel grid combining atomic occupancy, experimental electron density, and gradient magnitude. This moves beyond single fitted structures to capture conformational heterogeneity and positional uncertainty at binding interfaces. It has potential relevance to structure-based drug discovery.

entry.title: RELAGRAM: Recursive Latent Graph Model for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem

author.name: Vladimir Kirill Bickov, Neil Yorke-Smith

entry.summary: RELAGRAM applies latent recursion to neural combinatorial optimization, encoding capacitated vehicle routing instances as edge tokens that a compact transformer recurrently refines, then decoding a feasible solution from an edge heatmap. It tests whether latent recursion, shown effective on structured puzzles, transfers to routing problems. Results on CVRP-100 are reported but truncated in the abstract.

entry.title: Sensitivity Fidelity Reveals Physical Dependencies Beyond Forecast Accuracy in Deep-Learning Earth-System Models

author.name: Qi Chen, Peng Zhan, Hongxing Cui, Wenqing Cui, Ibrahim Hoteit

entry.summary: Introduces sensitivity fidelity as a criterion for earth-system surrogate models: alongside forecast error, model responses to input perturbations should match a trusted reference. In a Rayleigh-Benard convection benchmark, four architectures with low forecast error encoded markedly different sensitivities, showing predictive skill and physical consistency can decouple.

entry.title: The Price of Precision: A Calibrated Cost Model for Mixed-Precision LLM Serving

author.name: Mukund Athmaram, Manoj Rao, Liang Ma

entry.summary: Builds a calibrated cost model for mixed-precision LLM serving that identifies the binding resource (compute, weight loading, or KV cache access) given phase, batch size, and context length, showing that fewer bits do not always mean faster serving. The model is used both to predict serving latency and to guide precision-configuration allocation.

entry.title: Attention-Graph Curvature for the Verification of Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Kanghyeon Kim, Johannes F. Lutzeyer, Yanzhu Guo

entry.summary: The authors investigate whether directed Forman curvature of a language model's attention graph, computed locally from attention weights, carries information about the correctness of individual reasoning steps in mathematical solutions. This offers a lightweight internal-signal approach to early error detection in natural-language proofs that cannot yet be verified by proof assistants.

entry.title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration

author.name: Wenpu Du, Peng Zhou, Yunlong Xia, Sinuo Xin, Congcong Zhang, Boyang Zhang, Yi Zhang, Wenzheng Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes PC-GNO, a physics-coupled graph neural operator that predicts the spatiotemporal six-component stress tensor field in concrete penetration, trained on mesoscale finite-element simulations and conditioned only on design-level inputs like strength grade, geometry, and projectile parameters. It links mesoscale heterogeneity to field-level predictions for engineering design.

entry.title: Random Probing for Structural Self-Interactions in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Saku Peltonen, H. \c{C}a\u{g}r{\i} Bilgi, Kubilay Atasu

entry.summary: DIAL is a message-passing layer that gives GNN nodes access to structural self-interaction features via diagonals of graph-derived operators using randomized probing with permutation equivariance. The authors prove expressiveness for cycle counts, subgraph centrality, and heat kernel signatures while avoiding expensive higher-order architectures.

entry.title: Teacher-Guided Tool Learning for Small Language Models via Bidirectional KL Constraints

author.name: Haoxuan Gao, Qin-Wen Luo, Xiang Chen, Yu Tian, Zequn Sun, Xiaofeng Cao, Jiangchao Yao, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: SeTPO trains small language models to use external tools by combining student RL exploration with selective reverse-KL teacher feedback on low-reward trajectories and persistent demonstration supervision, mitigating teacher-student distribution mismatch. This enables tool-use capabilities in resource-constrained deployment settings.

entry.title: Simple Linear Corrections for Compression in Late Interaction

author.name: Mihir Agarwal, Sabyasachi Basu, Viraj Agrawal

entry.summary: The paper investigates learning a global linear correction to the scoring function of late-interaction (multi-vector) retrieval models to recover quality lost to document-vector compression. Distilling the uncompressed model's score distributions per encoder-compressor-budget combination lets the encoder and compressor remain unchanged while restoring retrieval quality.

entry.title: DiffGA: Steering Frozen Diffusion Models for Materials Design via Evolutionary Search

author.name: Shivang Agarwal, Rodrigo Wang, Kevin Ryczko, Aayush R. Singh

entry.summary: DiffGA is a retraining-free framework for inverse materials design that injects evolutionary search into the sampling trajectory of a frozen diffusion model, evolving partially denoised states under arbitrary black-box oracles. This sidesteps per-objective retraining and brittle differentiable guidance for non-differentiable or changing objectives. It enables steering candidate generation toward simulation- or experiment-derived properties.

entry.title: Joint Contrastive-Adversarial Representation Learning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Zhou Yu, Fusheng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces JCAR, a two-stage unsupervised domain adaptation framework that learns a common representation from unlabeled source and target data via combined contrastive learning and adversarial alignment, then freezes it to fit a source-supervised predictor. The paper provides non-asymptotic excess-risk bounds coupling representation and discriminator estimation with explicit neural approximation errors.

entry.title: Robust Detection of Directional Adversarial Attacks in Deep Neural Networks for Radiological Imaging

author.name: Tristan Malaty\'nski, Joanna Jaworek-Korjakowska

entry.summary: Proposes a detection framework for adversarial attacks on radiological deep learning systems that uses subsequent attacks with random noise and analysis of response variations to identify perturbations and their directionality. Motivated by reported attack success rates above 90% on medical scans and growing hospital AI adoption, the work targets credibility of clinical imaging models.

entry.title: Lightweight Scheduling Policies for Continuously Batched LLLM Serving Across GPU Architectures

author.name: Ashman Mehra, Akshan Agarwal, Aryeh Carmi

entry.summary: This systems study evaluates eight lightweight continuous-batching scheduling policies for LLM serving across 1,152 runs using six Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral models on L40S, A100, and H100 GPUs with ShareGPT-derived traffic. It shows scheduler choice materially affects throughput, time-to-first-token, and latency without requiring learned schedulers or architecture changes.

entry.title: Exploration strategies for Gaussian process bandit optimization with inference regret guarantees

author.name: Hwanwoo Kim, Jungwoo Hong, Kyungjae Lee

entry.summary: The paper addresses the gap between cumulative regret bounds in Bayesian optimization and the quality of the final single recommendation under noise. It proposes swapping acquisition queries with exploration queries in any BO procedure, and derives inference regret bounds via the fill distance using Gaussian process posterior standard deviation.

entry.title: Variational Filtering for Bayesian Last Layers with an Independent Binary Probit Surrogate

author.name: Dimitrije Markovic, Conor Heins, Alexander Tschantz, Christopher L. Buckley

entry.summary: The authors treat the last layer of a deep classifier as the latent state of a linear-Gaussian state-space model and update it online with closed-form variational filtering steps, using an independent binary probit surrogate to restore conjugacy. This improves calibration and single-pass learning over temperature scaling, which only corrects calibration post hoc.

entry.title: Measuring Variable Importance Using Proportional Inclusive Marginal Effects

author.name: Youngseo Cho, V. Roshan Joseph

entry.summary: Proposes PRIME, a variable importance measure that fixes a flaw of Shapley-based measures, where inactive variables correlated with active ones receive positive importance. PRIME builds on proportional marginal effects by first using a model-free variable selection step and only including active variables, reducing computational cost and working for stochastic models.

entry.title: Deeply unrolled alternating projections for phase retrieval

author.name: Jiayi Yao, Vasileios Charisopoulos, Rebecca Willett

entry.summary: Proposes a deep unrolling framework for phase retrieval that augments alternating projections with a learned denoising step, arguing that measurement-geometry mismatch between training and deployment is not inherent to unrolling and can be mitigated by the choice of underlying iterative algorithm. It achieves high-quality reconstructions with improved robustness to geometry changes.

entry.title: CALM-5G: Event-Level Conformal Risk Control for Predictive Service-Assurance Alarms

author.name: \"{O}mer Faruk \.{I}\c{s}canl{\i}, Ya\u{g}mur Sabucu Sandal

entry.summary: CALM-5G is an assurance layer atop any forecasting backbone that issues telecom service-assurance alarms with distribution-free, finite-sample guarantees, calibrating on service-level violation events and reporting alarm duty cycle alongside certified miss rates. It is evaluated on four corpora including a production cellular network, commercial 5G traces, and open RAN testbeds. This shows conformal risk control delivering deployable statistical guarantees in an industrial setting.

entry.title: How Low Can You Go: Fine-Tuning LLMs with Bayesian Optimization (LlMBO)

author.name: Aditya Kulkarni, Davide Sartor, Carlos Soto, Nathan Wycoff

entry.summary: Building on TinyLoRA's finding that LLM fine-tuning can work with fewer than 10 parameters, the authors observe that such low-dimensional settings make global Bayesian optimization tractable. LlMBO is a gradient-free, sample-efficient, memory-light fine-tuning method that parallelizes across devices without synchronization.

entry.title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks implicitly generated by gauge-equivariant GNN message passing, showing a separation between rapid growth of contour length and slow spatial expansion with depth. The authors connect this hierarchy to loop expansions of fermionic observables in physics.

entry.title: Training-Free BioNEL-RAG: Advancing Biomedical Entity Linking through Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Large Language Model

author.name: Ziyi Chen, Hui Liu, Ziyang Ling, Ronald X. Xu, Mingzhai Sun

entry.summary: BioNEL-RAG is a training-free framework for biomedical named entity linking that combines a retrieval module for candidate entity generation with an LLM that selects the best candidate for normalization. By avoiding domain-specific training, the method improves cross-domain adaptability where prior supervised systems struggle. The approach demonstrates how RAG plus LLM reasoning can replace task-specific fine-tuning in specialized domains.

entry.title: Estimating Uncertainty of Omnimodal Large Language Models via External Omnimodal Embeddings

author.name: Iacopo Ghinassi, Hy Nguyen Gia La, Luke Ong

entry.summary: This paper proposes a model-agnostic uncertainty quantification framework for omnimodal LLMs that scores chain-of-thought responses entirely through external omni-modal embeddings, measuring grounding of reasoning in multimodal inputs and internal coherence. Unlike prior methods, it avoids requiring model internals or re-invocation of the model. It offers a practical family of signals with empirical characterization.

entry.title: When Does an ASR Error Matter? Task-Role Diagnostics for Tool-Using Voice Agents

author.name: Xiaolong Wang, Shijie Su, Naqi Xiong

entry.summary: SpeechEvalX is a paired diagnostic protocol measuring how task roles affected by ASR errors influence structured tool calls in cascaded voice agents, where word error rate fails to capture downstream consequence. Across 594 utterances, joint call accuracy drops from 82.3% with reference transcripts to 71.9-74.9% with ASR front ends.

entry.title: PACT: A Pragmatic Prompting Framework for Expressive and Voice-Preserving Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Yuchen Song, Satoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: PACT is a target-space prompting framework for expressive, voice-preserving speech-to-speech translation that extracts source pragmatic cues, projects them into the target language expression space, calibrates them to a realizable subspace, and converts them into continuous prompts for a frozen speech generator. It achieves the best overall performance on bidirectional Spanish-English expressive S2ST evaluation. The work addresses the gap between content-preserving and pragmatically faithful translation.

entry.title: Sparse All-Layer Connector for Domain Generalised Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Ruoyu Guo, Xin Kun Lin, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song

entry.summary: This paper challenges the default of depth-aligned cross-model fusion in foundation-model-based domain generalized segmentation, observing that different foundation models develop distinct representation hierarchies and depth-wise domain sensitivity. It proposes a sparse all-layer connector that fuses information across non-aligned layers for better generalization.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Semantic Reconstruction for 3D Instance Segmentation

author.name: Yuanhao Su, Shaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates 2D-to-3D semantic transfer for 3D instance segmentation as a masked semantic reconstruction task, training a 3D encoder to recover masked lifted 2D priors for explicit semantic distillation. A geometry-modulated scheme ensures transferred semantics align with underlying 3D structure rather than being naively concatenated.

entry.title: Adaptive Interaction Network for Human Motion Prediction During Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Mengyuan Liu, Yangting Lin, Qiongjie Cui

entry.summary: The paper formulates robot-aware human motion prediction, explicitly modeling how robots influence human motion in shared workspaces, and proposes AINet with a primary prediction branch and an auxiliary robot-trajectory branch coupled via a local-global mechanism. This supports safer and more efficient human-robot collaboration.

entry.title: Dynamic Interpolation for Training-Time Prediction Reshaping in Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Peirui Zhu, Shijie Hao, Jingxi Liao, Richang Hong, Meng Wang

entry.summary: The paper re-examines supervised low-light image enhancement through a training-dynamics lens, observing that brightness errors converge early while noise and structural artifacts lag. It proposes dynamic interpolation to reshape predictions during training, avoiding added architectural complexity or hand-tuned losses.

entry.title: GNFormer: Gaussian Neural Field Transformer for Efficient Camera-based Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Guangcheng Chen, Li He, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: GNFormer proposes a Gaussian neural field representation for camera-based 3D occupancy prediction, improving primitive utilization and shape expressiveness compared to existing Gaussian-based methods that waste capacity on empty space. This improves efficiency and scene understanding for autonomous vehicle and UAV perception. Occupancy prediction is a core perception task, and Gaussian-based representations are an active research direction.

entry.title: Load-Aware Quadruped Navigation with Online Contact-based Geometry Estimation

author.name: Qi Yin, XiaoLi Zhang, Yangming Shi

entry.summary: The authors propose a two-phase framework for quadruped robots navigating cluttered spaces while carrying objects, combining a load-aware RL navigation policy (LOADNav) with an online geometry predictor (CoGE) trained via imitation. Unlike prior systems that use fixed footprint inflation, the robot adapts clearance behavior to the carried object's geometry. This addresses a practical gap between load-aware locomotion and autonomous navigation.

entry.title: Learning Dynamic Grasping

author.name: Nga Kiu Kelly Ho, Yilin Liu, Hao Xu, Niloy J. Mitra

entry.summary: The authors tackle generating complete 4D hand-object grasping sequences from a single initial hand-object state, decoupling hand-motion generation from object-motion recovery. Conditional flow matching predicts the hand trajectory given an object point cloud and initial hand configuration, without requiring language, target grasps, or object trajectories as extra conditions. Applications include character animation, XR, and embodied agents.

entry.title: Predict in Chunks, Revise in Spans: History-conditioned Action Regeneration for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Yuntian Wang, Jiaying Tang, Chunzheng Li, Yang Liu, Siao Liu

entry.summary: CMAP is a visuomotor policy that refines action chunks via history-conditioned local regeneration: an action tape combines executed commands with masked future positions to produce coarse predictions and per-step uncertainty scores, then an uncertainty-guided mechanism reconstructs only the high-uncertainty span. This avoids regenerating entire chunks when errors are localized. It improves temporal coherence and efficiency in imitation-learned manipulation.

entry.title: Efficient Hybrid Hard--Soft Signal Temporal Logic MPC for Driving under Multimodal Uncertainty

author.name: Kumar Manas, Adrian Paschke

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid hard-soft Signal Temporal Logic MPC framework for automated driving under multimodal behavior uncertainty, imposing minimum-distance and speed predicates as hard constraints while using soft STL robustness terms for clearance, comfort, and interaction quality. This preserves feasibility while preventing safety-critical trade-offs against progress. It optimizes a single ego trajectory against all retained behavior hypotheses.

entry.title: PACE: Temporal-Role Tactile Conditioning for Chunk-Based Insertion Policies

author.name: Zhiyuan Chen, Shixiong Xu, Shuai Chen, Yangwei You

entry.summary: PACE organizes a shared tactile stream into three temporal roles for chunk-based insertion policies: persistent contact states condition chunk generation, abrupt contact events correct generated chunks, and contact-consequence predictions shape training representations. This addresses the limitation of single-pathway tactile fusion in visuotactile policies. It targets contact-rich assembly tasks.

entry.title: Human-Like Redundancy Resolution for Real-Time Bimanual Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Chao Tan, Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Shuxian Liang, Chaoqun Wan, Zhen Huang, Xian-Sheng Hua

entry.summary: The paper proposes a redundancy-resolution framework for teleoperating bimanual humanoids that combines adaptive elbow guidance with singularity-robust wrist tracking, solving the problem that wrist-only tracking of 7-DoF arms causes elbow drift or abrupt configuration changes. Shoulder-wrist geometric retargeting generates robot-scale targets, and an adaptive elbow-offset criterion scales its guidance near singularities where fixed anthropomorphic constraints would block necessary redundancy adjustments. The system targets real-time operation.

entry.title: ReForesight: Occlusion-Robust Re-Identification and Future Occupancy Forecasting for Dynamic Semantic Mapping

author.name: Didar Seyidov, Faith Ogunwoye, Hajira Amjad, Danil Tolkachev, Yuri Sarkisov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: ReForesight is an open-source ROS 2 toolkit adding instance-level future occupancy forecasting (up to 3 seconds ahead via a 36.6k-parameter MLP with Kalman fallback) and re-identification after occlusion to a particle-based semantic mapping pipeline. Forecasted objects are represented as ghost point clouds in the map frame without an occupancy decoder. Evaluated on held-out CODa sequences, the lightweight MLP improves prediction metrics, and the toolkit integrates cleanly with existing ROS stacks.

entry.title: Actionable Meta-Requirements for AI Robustness Auditing

author.name: Joshua Owotogbe, Roya Nasiri, Indika Kumara, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel

entry.summary: This design-science paper consolidates literature and expert input into meta-requirements specifying what AI robustness auditing frameworks should support, addressing the unresolved question of requirements for dependable AI systems under distribution shift and perturbations.

entry.title: Energy Ring: Stabilizing Feature Energy for Reliable Test-Time Discovery

author.name: Tianle Liu, Fan Lyu, Tingliang Feng, Chenggong Ni, Tianqi Wang, Zhang Zhang, Fuyuan Hu, Rui Yao, Tao Zhou

entry.summary: Energy Ring addresses test-time discovery, where a deployed model must both recognize known classes and detect novel ones from an unlabeled stream. It stabilizes the unstable energy gap between known and unknown classes using a lightweight adapter and a perturbation consistency module, improving separation of features.

entry.title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning

author.name: Gennadiy Chistiakov, Yury Yanovich

entry.summary: This paper proposes an evaluation framework for credit assignment in modular financial RL combining equal-information reconstruction controls, fixed-utility comparisons, and downstream guardrails. Its controlled studies show some attribution methods add no decision-relevant information, e.g., residual-based allocation is exactly reproduced by an ordinary loss-budget control.

entry.title: How Should a Camera-First AI Agent Work?

author.name: Xiaofan Wu, Xi Zeng, Miaoxia Chen, Peishan Chen, Shuyan Li, Chen Wang, Jiyun Yao, Hanyong Zhong, Jiahao Zhu

entry.summary: This position-style paper formalizes the challenge of camera-first AI agents acting on ephemeral visual targets through the Ephemeral-Target Interaction (ETI) framework and a Perceptual Deadline Contract that separates hard memory deadlines from soft reasoning deadlines. The authors argue the core bottleneck is timing rather than recognition ability, advocating decoupled memory and reasoning pipelines.

entry.title: PEAM: On-device Communication Agent for Personalized, Efficient and Autonomous Mobile Network Configuration

author.name: Haowen Wan, Shangzhuo Xie, Syue-Ju Syue, Xianyue Wu, Runhua Li, Qianqian Yang

entry.summary: PEAM is an on-device LLM-based agent that autonomously generates personalized mobile network-configuration rules executable within milliseconds, fine-tuned on manually annotated real-user data. It operates in phases separating rule generation from millisecond-level execution, targeting latency-sensitive decisions as users switch apps or connectivity changes.

entry.title: MoMaTune: Model, Match, Then Tune Language Models for Numerical Records

author.name: Weimin Lyu, Jingfen Zhang, Lingdao Sha, Peng sun, Xiaowei Chen, Vincent Gao, Rui Song

entry.summary: Identifies why decoder LLMs handle serialized tabular-numerical data poorly - digit-position sensitivity and across-field statistical dependence are weakly supervised under target-only tuning - and introduces MoMaTune, a model-match-tune recipe that adds supervision for within-value and across-field structure.

entry.title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Xiangqing Lu, Tao Zhu, Mingxing Nie, Liming Chen

entry.summary: CHEAR improves cost-efficiency of LLM/RAG-based activity recognition by exploiting confusion hierarchies to organize which activity candidates to compare and when to invoke discriminative knowledge. This shifts evidence-organization decisions out of inference time, avoiding repeated processing of growing candidate sets.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Pathogen Forecasts: Predicting Shared Respiratory Hospital Burden from Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV

author.name: Gaurob Saha, MinJae Woo, Lior Rennert

entry.summary: The paper develops a 1-4 week-ahead forecasting framework for combined respiratory hospital admissions from influenza, COVID-19, and RSV, comparing summing pathogen-specific forecasts versus directly forecasting the total burden target. It frames hospital planning as a target-construction problem and evaluates with retrospective held-out testing.

entry.title: Large Language Model Assisted Transportation Planning through a Differentiable User Equilibrium Layer

author.name: Eunseung Lee, Gyeongjun Kim, Keemin Sohn

entry.summary: This work integrates LLMs with a differentiable user equilibrium layer so that transportation planning tasks like network design and capacity expansion can be optimized through natural-language interaction rather than serving merely as simulation interfaces. It aims to make strategic transport analysis accessible to non-expert decision makers.

entry.title: FON: A Draft-Revise Dual-Organ Language Model without Sequence-Level Quadratic Attention

author.name: Helong Hu (Zhanjiang Campus, Guangdong Ocean University, Zhanjiang, Guangdong, China), Hongdan Pan (Maoming Administrative Service Center, Maoming, Guangdong, China), Shuiqing Hu (China Pacific Insurance)

entry.summary: Proposes FON, an attention-free language model that splits a single weight stack into a drafting organ (causal, linear training cost, constant decode state) and a revision organ that re-processes the written prefix via multi-scale ripple kernels. At only 30M parameters it reports perplexity around 131 on WikiText-103 under matched parameter and token budgets.

entry.title: CLIVO: Differentiable Cluster-Based Instruction Mixing with Learned Validation Objectives

author.name: Yuhan Wang, Rui Hu, Batian Di, Tan Jiang, Dongsheng Ma, Leichao Dong, Yuanzi Li, Yalin Feng

entry.summary: Proposes CLIVO, a target-aware multimodal instruction selection framework combining fine-grained semantic cluster allocation, automatically learned validation objectives, and differentiable mixture search. It identifies target-relevant validation examples via correlations between merged-proxy losses and real probe performance, addressing overrepresentation of similar content in sample-level ranking methods.

entry.title: Transparency as Answerability: Role-Dependent Information Flow Modeling

author.name: Mattias Br\"annstr\"om, Themis Dimitra Xanthopoulou, Lili Jiang

entry.summary: This conceptual paper reframes AI transparency as a relation between a system and a stakeholder rather than an intrinsic property, defining transparency as the degree to which a stakeholder's legitimate questions can be answered from the system's structure. The authors formalize this using information flow networks, where transparency questions are expressed in terms of network structure and answerability becomes a computable or assessable property. This addresses known failures of component-based transparency approaches, such as findings that do not transfer across organizational boundaries or illuminate system-level behavior.

entry.title: AutoMARS: Automatic and Scalable Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Supply Chain Risk Assessment

author.name: Yinzhu Quan, Zefang Liu, Frederick Benaben, Benoit Montreuil

entry.summary: Presents AutoMARS, a multi-agent LLM framework for scalable comparative risk assessment across supply chain networks, integrating socioeconomic, disaster, environmental, and transportation risk factors via automatic task planning, agent coordination, and tool invocation with parallelized execution.

entry.title: Learning to Play: Reinforcement Learning and Games

author.name: Aske Plaat

entry.summary: This appears to be a comprehensive survey or textbook-style work by Aske Plaat covering reinforcement learning applied to games, tracing breakthroughs from Backgammon, Checkers, Chess, Atari, Go, Poker, and StarCraft up to discussions of general AI. It synthesizes the diverse techniques underlying these successes, from exact planning algorithms to adaptive sampling and deep function approximation. Its value lies in consolidating a now-mainstream research area rather than presenting new experimental results.

entry.title: Fresh at Decision, Stale at Action: Routing New Information to LLM Decisions Already Made

author.name: Ayoub Merimi, Souhail Bakkali, Abdeljalil Sakat

entry.summary: The paper introduces a timestamp theory of decision validity and a persistent decision ledger for LLM decisions, recognizing that actions committed at decision time may be affected by information published later. Accuracy factorizes into routing (delivering new information to affected decisions before revision deadlines) and temporal judgment (interpreting it for action time). This formalizes a neglected temporal aspect of LLM decision-making.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Sharing: TrueMAD for Targeted Peer Engagement in Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Dezheng Bao, Sihang Du, Renhong Huang, Zhizhang Yuan, Yifei Sun, Yang Yang

entry.summary: TrueMAD is a backbone-agnostic test-time plug-in for multi-agent debate that inserts one-to-one, free-form peer advice (support, rebuttal, refinement) between answer broadcasting and self-revision. It addresses the problem that broadcast-style debate lets reliable reasoning be drowned out by majorities and lets errors persist without actionable feedback. This improves the quality of multi-agent reasoning interactions.

entry.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Zheng Gao, Chiwun Yang, Zhizhou Sha

entry.summary: This theoretical work models recursive AI self-improvement as a stochastic multiplicative process, showing randomness leaves the explosion threshold unchanged but turns the blow-up date into an explicit distribution with derivable moments, tails, and asymptotics, plus results on detectability. For Lomax-distributed improvement sizes the explosion time is exactly Gamma distributed.

entry.title: Two Routes to Interoceptive Prioritisation: Dissociating Likelihood Precision and Preference Reweighting in Active Inference

author.name: St John Grimbly, Nicolas Kuske, Evert A. Boonstra, Charel van Hoof, Rowan Hodson, Benjamin Rosman, Ryan Smith, Mark Solms, Jonathan P. Shock

entry.summary: In a foraging gridworld with three lethal needs, the authors dissociate two active-inference mechanisms for prioritizing bodily needs: sharpening interoceptive precision versus reweighting preferences for need-relieving outcomes. Precision improves survival cleanly, while preference reweighting alters which states the agent learns from, narrowing the coverage of its learned body model.

entry.title: Bias Robustness of Genetic Multi-Criteria Sorting versus Learned Rankers under Proxy Skew and Label Contamination

author.name: Vladyslav Shevchuk, Carlos Uziel P\'erez Malla, Philipp Wissgott

entry.summary: This study compares label-free genetic multi-criteria sorting against learned learning-to-rank models under proxy skew and label contamination on several ranking benchmarks. Genetic sorting shows much lower correlation with leaked proxy signals than LTR peers, while both are evaluated on a bias-utility frontier with clean nDCG@10.

entry.title: Do you "see" what I "see"? A Multi-panel Visual Question Answer Dataset for Large Language Model Chart Analysis

author.name: Daniel J. Evans, J. P. Naiman, JooYoung Seo, J. Stephen Downie

entry.summary: This work introduces a multi-panel VQA dataset for evaluating whether LLMs and multimodal models can reliably extract trends and data from realistic synthetic scientific figures containing multiple charts. Tasks are scaffolded along a four-level description model from basic conceptual answers to interpretive and analytical understanding, motivated by digital library figure accessibility. It probes limits of current models on task-oriented visual data analysis.

entry.title: Coarse-Graining Recursive Expert Computation: Continuation-Relative Interfaces and Failure Modes

author.name: Shihua Yu, Yanzhi Wang, Tianchi Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents a continuation-relative framework for evaluating computational coarse-graining, where a sequence of updates (e.g., recursive expert computation) is replaced by a cheaper module, judged by downstream task quality and total execution cost jointly. It formally separates boundary representations, executed operations, and downstream loss, with an exact loss decomposition isolating replacement effects at fixed downstream actions and accounting for selection overhead. It also catalogs failure modes of such replacements.

entry.title: RES-MR: Risk-Aware Reasoning for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation

author.name: Cong Wang, Jin Li, Shoujin Wang, Yishuo Li, Huilin Gu, Wenpeng Lu

entry.summary: RES-MR is an LLM-based framework for medication recommendation featuring a two-stage training paradigm that adds explainable reasoning and personalized, patient-specific safety constraints rather than fixed risk thresholds. It aims to improve clinician trust and protect vulnerable populations.

entry.title: InCLAD: A Continual Learning Benchmark for Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection

author.name: {\L}ukasz Marcjan, Dorota Wilk-Ko{\l}odziejczyk, Roberto Corizzo

entry.summary: InCLAD frames continual industrial anomaly detection as a task-incremental, semi-supervised problem in which each industrial component defines a task and models must preserve performance on prior components while learning new ones. The benchmark addresses the gap left by static industrial anomaly benchmarks that assume full supervision or isolated datasets.

entry.title: GeoBridge: Evolving Transferable Decoder Topologies for Geometric Vision

author.name: Rui Wang, Haoyu Zhang, Ran Cheng

entry.summary: GeoBridge is an evolutionary neural architecture search framework for decoder topologies shared between depth estimation and Gaussian reconstruction, making stage-internal topology searchable via residual, sequential, and parallel compositions on a fixed multi-scale scaffold. A functional-tree mechanism enables transfer of the learned decoder organization across geometric vision systems.

entry.title: Pessimistic Latent Task-aware Optimization for Robust Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chang-Hoon Jeong, Kisung Shin, Hanwool Sul, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: PLATO addresses a failure mode in context-based offline meta-RL: on out-of-support tasks the task encoder produces latents outside the training support, where the policy has never been trained. By assuming task latents lie on a low-dimensional manifold and exposing the policy to off-support latents during training via pessimistic optimization, PLATO improves robustness on parameter-extrapolation tasks.

entry.title: bharatSetu: a 1M x 22 bridge for indic translation

author.name: Haq Nawaz Malik, Nahfid Nissar, Faizan Iqbal

entry.summary: BharatSetu 22-Indic 1M is a row-aligned resource of 984,764 English sentences each machine-translated into all 22 scheduled Indian languages, so any two columns form a translation pair, yielding 462 directed Indic-to-Indic pairs (506 including English) without direct bitext. The authors introduce the notion of pivot-derived pairs with a confidence layer for quality filtering, covering low-resource languages such as Bodo, Dogri, Santali, and Kashmiri.

entry.title: Adaptive Compression and Targeted Perturbation: A Unified Framework for Generalized Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Jianqiao Cui, Haoxian Zhu, Hanbiao Meng, Yanghao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified audio deepfake detection framework combining an adaptive module that dynamically selects latent feature dimensions from a compression pool and a mel-band adversarial perturbation strategy for augmentation. It targets the common generalization failure of fixed-bottleneck detectors across diverse spoofing attacks.

entry.title: Estimating the Causal Impact of Social Navigation Signals in Corridor Scenarios

author.name: Francesco Baldo, Luca Castri, Gloria Beraldo, Nicola Bellotto

entry.summary: This paper applies causal inference to human-robot social navigation, using a causal model to estimate whether emitting a social navigation signal causally improves transit success in corridor scenarios, accounting for confounding factors that bias observation-based inference. This supports principled decisions about when robots should emit social signals.

entry.title: PatTransBench: an ipc-stratified, multi-dimensional benchmark for patent machine translation evaluation

author.name: Xiaowei Su, Xusen Cheng

entry.summary: PatTransBench is a 12,000-item Chinese-English/Japanese/Korean patent translation benchmark with four-dimensional evaluation: literal n-gram metrics, cross-lingual semantic similarity, 38-language consistency probing, and serving performance under concurrency. A case study on PatMT2-7B and its quantized variants reveals direction-dependent behavior.

entry.title: Towards Cost-Efficient Video Dataset Construction with Large Language Models

author.name: Mohammed Shabot, Jonathan Adams, Jan Van den Stock, Joost Vennekens

entry.summary: This paper uses LLMs to pre-screen video candidates from metadata before download, avoiding storage, time, and annotation costs of judging relevance only after retrieval. The approach is validated against strict human majority vote from four annotators with inter-annotator agreement analysis. It matters because dataset curation cost is a growing bottleneck for video classification research.

entry.title: AIPOCH Open-Science: An Open-Source AI Research Workbench with Reproducible .science Packages

author.name: Wen Ouyang, Bocheng Huang, Qianyu Yao, Fei Sun, Minying Deng, Haoyue Cheng, Wenwen Zhou, Lei Mou, Yusi Wei, Jiang Li, Kun Zhu, Lei Wang, Yi Feng, Jiaheng Dai, Ke Qian, Dan Wang, Yahui Wang, Chenyi Wang, Mingsheng Lyu, Yaqiang Zhang, Ping Zheng, Chunhua Tang, Xinge Ma, Xu Zhang, Youjia Fan, Can Lu, Zhijun Dai, Man Hu, Qiqi Xie, Beinan Liu, Yuanning Guo, Yunze Liu, Jinhong Jiang, Xianjun Fu, Mingwei Zhang, Yuanji Xu, Shilin Xia, Bowen Yang, Mingjun Yu, Jingdun Xie, Xuwei Chen, Xia Zou, Yuzhou Xue, Jianguo Zhou, Chunhao Cao, Donghao Tian, Lei Huang, Jinxiao Li, Shengrong Long, Zefeng Song, Honglin Li, Jiang Luo, Wenying Jiang, Shanshan Li, Lei Dai, Ning Jiang, Ying Cai, Chaohui Li, Chunyan Peng, Hetong Zhao, Angqing Li, Chunyan Yang, Chongyang Sun, Yong Li, Xinyu Shi, Wei Dai, Ming Peng, Chen Sang, Yuanyuan Han, Desong Qiu, Haixin Miao, Jian Xu, Yi Chen, Xiaoliang Shi, Tian Shen, Teng Hu, Shuhao Wang, Yingyong Hou, Huimei Wang

entry.summary: AIPOCH Open-Science is an open-source research workbench for AI-assisted research that packages sessions into portable .science files capturing relationships among instructions, computations, artifact revisions, and checks. The system supports attributable version targets, explicit omission of eligible content, and separation of imported history from writable forks, validated with controlled sessions testing corrections and unexecuted steps. It targets reproducibility of AI-mediated scientific workflows.

entry.title: YUBI-Real2Sim: 3DGS Scene Verification for Reliable Policy Evaluation

author.name: Hiroki Nishizawa, Takehiko Ohkawa, Nicola Scianca, Tatsuya Matsushima, Shigeo Morishima, Kei Ota

entry.summary: YUBI-Real2Sim is a framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting-based real-to-sim policy evaluation under dual fisheye wrist-mounted cameras, such as those on YUBI handheld gripper data. It quantifies how reconstruction artifacts like holes and floaters in wide-angle views degrade policy evaluation and builds an integrated pipeline for reliable simulated assessment of VLA policies.

entry.title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience

author.name: Bo Ni

entry.summary: FracLearn is a framework that lets language models improve physical designs through iterative experience in a simulated fracture game, where the model proposes architectures, observes fracture outcomes, and abstracts observations into conditional engineering principles. A generalization phase then requires the model to combine learned principles into new designs that beat the previous record, demonstrating progressive refinement and hypothesis revision. It matters as a study of grounded, experience-based learning for LLMs in scientific and engineering design domains.

entry.title: Visual Dependence Does Not Imply Answerability: A Systematic Analysis of Answerability Signals in Frozen InstructBLIP

author.name: Minjun Kim, Hyunmin Song, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: The authors systematically evaluate which internal signals from a frozen InstructBLIP model can indicate whether a visual question is answerable, covering uncertainty, cross-modal alignment, grounding, visual dependence, and learned probes on a 10K subset of UNK-VQA. They find answerability discrimination is weak, with test AUROC largely between 0.50 and 0.54, suggesting current vision-language models lack reliable internal signals for abstention. This is a negative-result style study with implications for hallucination and abstention research in multimodal models.

entry.title: Saliency-Guided Replay for Continual Learning in Deep Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Francesco Panetta, Federico Di Valerio, Michela Proietti

entry.summary: The paper proposes a memory-efficient continual learning strategy for deep spiking neural networks that combines Experience Packing and Replay with Spike Activation Maps, forward-only explanations derived from spike activity. These saliency maps select the most informative image patches for replay rather than storing full images, tested on Split CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 with a BN-TT stabilized VGG9 SNN.
