It addresses catastrophic forgetting in energy-efficient neuromorphic computing under low-latency constraints.

entry.title: Uncertainty Evaluation: Bridging Machine Learning and Measurement Science

author.name: Dario Petri, Luca Mari

entry.summary: This conceptual paper draws analogies between uncertainty evaluation in machine learning and the metrology framework codified in the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement. It critiques the aleatoric/epistemic dichotomy, arguing it has limitations akin to the superseded random/systematic error distinction in measurement science.

entry.title: FALLNEST: Dual-Domain Dataset Condensation of Imbalanced IMU Data for Wearable Fall Detection

author.name: Rashi Niyas P, Ritika Jain, Hitika Tiwari

entry.summary: FALLNEST condenses large, imbalanced IMU datasets into tiny, class-balanced synthetic training sets for wearable fall detection, using normalized-gradient and embedding-matched time-frequency condensation. This reduces data and compute demands while handling rare fall events. It bridges hand-crafted feature approaches and full deep learning on raw signals.

entry.title: APTree: Extended Behavior Trees for Adaptive and Scalable Automated Robotic Task Planning in Construction

author.name: Shermin Sherkat, Thomas Wortmann, Andreas Wortmann

entry.summary: APTree is a model-driven framework combining automated task planning with modular execution via behavior trees for off-site construction prefabrication. It coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners at runtime and includes a domain-specific language for plan specification and validation. The work targets a domain where task planning is still largely manual, reducing a key barrier to robotic adoption in construction.

entry.title: GeoMER: A Joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic Geometry Framework for Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Ting Zhu, Huizhi Liang, Boguslaw Obara, Shufei Duan, Varun Ojha

entry.summary: GeoMER jointly models Euclidean token-level interactions and hyperbolic emotion-core routing to exploit the latent hierarchical structure of emotions in multimodal emotion recognition from speech and text. The hyperbolic component provides an explicit geometric prior for organizing abstract emotional representations. This addresses a gap where most MER methods rely solely on Euclidean embeddings.

entry.title: AMemOps: Evaluating Memory Updates in Long Audio Streams

author.name: Peiwei Chang, Li Zhang, Mark D. Plumbley, Philip J. B. Jackson, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: AMemOps is a benchmark for evaluating memory operations in long audio streams: latest-attribute retrieval, preservation of unchanged attributes, and absent-source rejection, with paired controls isolating recording, identity, and event-history effects. Experiments show training on other recordings of test instruments increases a delta-rule memory's update advantage over matched attention by 13.4 percentage points. It decomposes audio memory accuracy into interacting demands that aggregate metrics obscure.

entry.title: Bytes to Threats: Byte-Sequence Transformer For Malware Detection

author.name: Abdelrahman Yassin Eljamal, Abdeltawab Hendawi

entry.summary: MalwareFormer is a transformer-based framework detecting malware directly from raw executable bytes, avoiding handcrafted features and capturing long-range dependencies that CNN-based methods miss. It reduces reliance on specialized domain expertise and time-consuming static/dynamic analysis pipelines.

entry.title: LACRM: LLM-Guided Mining of Directed Advertiser Competition Relationships in E-Commerce Advertising

author.name: Xiang Shi, Yitian Kou, Bing Li, Shengsheng Niu, Chun Gan, Linghui Meng, Jie He, Zhangang Lin, Ching Law

entry.summary: LACRM uses LLMs to construct directed competition graphs among e-commerce advertisers, capturing rivalry externalities that existing interaction graphs, taxonomy rules, and single-embedding models miss. The mined competition relationships are intended as a reusable signal for ad platform optimization. It is an applied industrial ML paper likely from an e-commerce platform.

entry.title: Refined Grid Sampling for Efficient Implicit Neural Representations of Large-Scale Scientific Data

author.name: Guang Zhao, Xihaier Luo, Sean McCue, Luke P. Van Roekel, Seungjun Lee, Yihui Ren, Shinjae Yoo, Wei Xu

entry.summary: Refined Grid Sampling improves INR training on high-dimensional physical fields by combining stratified grid sampling, error-based refinement, and dynamic resolution adjustment, avoiding the overhead of full-grid error evaluation in coordinate pruning. On high-resolution Navier-Stokes fields it achieves higher reconstruction accuracy within fixed wall-clock budgets. Relevant to large-scale scientific simulation workloads.

entry.title: ConformalGuard: False-Positive-Controlled Action Gating for LM Classifiers

author.name: Bishnu Bista, Dhanraj Haibatrao Jadhav, Vibha Choudhary, Gaurav Saxena, Arun Pandiyan Perumal, Arjun Subedi, Jignesh Ammineni

entry.summary: ConformalGuard is a model-agnostic calibration layer that wraps fixed LM classifier scores to provide finite-sample control of false positives in high-stakes gating tasks like phishing screening and fraud triage. Notably, it finds zero-shot LM API scores can be so coarse (10-11 unique values) that temperature scaling and isotonic regression behave like raw thresholding.

entry.title: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration

author.name: Hang Liu, Zhengfei Chen, Zhengrui Chen, Hao Geng, Yu Li, Qi Sun

entry.summary: The paper integrates an LLM with Bayesian optimization for 2.5D/3D CPU-GPU heterogeneous chiplet design, extending an open-source chiplet simulator to graph-topology 3D designs and using an LLM to generate candidate points adaptively. The goal is to overcome scarcity of early-stage evaluation platforms and complex design-metric relationships.

entry.title: More Domains, No Gains? FLO: Fast-Slow Reciprocal Learning for Multi-Domain Graph Pre-training

author.name: Yupeng Tong, Lianze Shan, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Dongxiao He

entry.summary: The paper observes empirically and theoretically that existing graph foundation model pre-training methods fail to benefit from increasing domain diversity during pre-training. It proposes FLO, a fast-slow reciprocal learning framework for multi-domain graph pre-training that addresses this limitation. This challenges the intuitive assumption that more pre-training domains necessarily yield more generalizable graph representations.

entry.title: Groups Don't Move as One: A Bregman Clustering View of Linearized Group Influence

author.name: Hyunho Choi, Jaeseung Heo, Youngbin Choi, MoonJeong Park, Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: This work shows that first-order group influence function estimates can conceal opposing member effects that cancel, and frames group influence via a Bregman centroid formulation. It uses Bregman information to quantify hidden variation and proposes a clustered estimator with jointly optimized weights whose contributions recover the original aggregate. This improves attribution for group-level data removal decisions.

entry.title: Sequence-Structured Decision Learning for Branch-and-Bound in Mixed-Integer Linear Programming

author.name: Tengfei Liu, Jinrun Liu, Bai Yan, Yuhui Shi, Qi Zhao

entry.summary: Seq-BnB learns both branching and node selection in branch-and-bound from a shared global representation of the evolving search tree, serializing node creations, updates, and decisions into typed tokens processed by a self-attention encoder. This contrasts with prior learning approaches that optimize each decision in isolation from local views. The unified sequence framing better captures the coupled dynamics of the search.

entry.title: BSIPipe: Bidirectional Sequence-Level Interleaved Pipeline Parallelism for Long-Sequence Large Language Model Training

author.name: Yuzhou Ni, Ling Chen

entry.summary: BSIPipe co-schedules two opposing V-shaped interleaved pipelines at the subsequence level to improve throughput of long-sequence LLM training beyond unidirectional sequence-level scheduling. It bounds activation memory via a basic-unit concatenation mechanism and avoids bidirectional communication deadlock through topology-aware device mapping and communication-computation strategies. This is a systems contribution for large-scale training efficiency.

entry.title: Cross-Material Magnetic Core Loss Prediction via Operating-Condition Matching and Partial Optimal Transport

author.name: Cong Yao, Yu Zheng, Zehao Hou, Rui Xu

entry.summary: T-PCOT is a Transformer transfer-learning method for predicting magnetic core loss in new materials from limited measurements. It builds a sparse graph of comparable operating conditions (frequency, flux, temperature, waveform) and uses capacity-constrained partial optimal transport to distribute alignment across source measurements. This addresses a real weakness of global feature alignment in physics-adjacent transfer tasks.

entry.title: Toward a Multimodal Foundation Model for Plasma State Reconstruction

author.name: Bin Xia, Chuanfei Dong, Boting Li, Yilan Qin, Zikang Xie, Sung Hyun Son, Adam J. Stanier, Jongsoo Yoo, Hantao Ji, Ahmed Diallo, Han Ding, John Wise

entry.summary: A proof-of-concept multimodal foundation model for reconstructing plasma states during magnetic reconnection, motivated by the FLARE experimental facility. Using 250 synthetic VPIC simulations, the authors train a 5.5M-parameter residual 3D U-Net with spatiotemporal self-attention to reconstruct magnetic-field components and electron density from sparse, incomplete diagnostics. It is scoped explicitly as an early step rather than a mature foundation model.

entry.title: Harnessing VLM in Embodied RL: From Reward Regressor to Success Detector via Exploration-Augmented Key-Observation Gating

author.name: Xin Liu, Yutong Jiang, Jian Su, Ziheng Wang, Chuang Wang, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: Argues that VLMs are better used as binary success detectors than precise reward regressors in embodied RL, since detection aligns with their VQA strengths and avoids heavy annotation. Proposes VLMeg, using exploration-augmented key-observation gating to apply VLM success rewards, targeting the harder from-scratch RL setting.

entry.title: Testing Central Structure for Complex Networks

author.name: Qilong Wu, Yuxiao Li, Simeng Zhang, Xinying Liu, Yan Liu, Zengyou He

entry.summary: The authors propose a statistical hypothesis-testing framework to determine whether a network contains an identifiable central structure at all, before applying centrality measures. They use the adjacency spectral radius as a test statistic with empirical p-values from randomized networks under specified null models, evaluated on simulated benchmarks and 55 real networks.

entry.title: Fast and Accurate: Improving Personalized LLM Performance by Semantic Concentration Inspired Workload Split between RAG and Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xingke Yang, Sicong Li, Lingfeng Yao, Rui Chen, Changqing Luo, Xin Fu, Miao Pan

entry.summary: The authors propose PEFT Union RAG (PUR), which splits personalized LLM workloads between parameter-efficient fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation based on the semantic concentration of a user's historical data. The approach aims to jointly improve personalization accuracy and inference latency compared to PEFT-only, RAG-only, or combined baselines.

entry.title: Softmax-Free Attention in Spiking Transformers as the Zero-Temperature Limit of Two-Level Systems

author.name: Roberto C. Sotero, Pouya Taghipour, Jose M. Sanchez-Bornot

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that softmax-free, thresholded binary attention in spiking transformers corresponds exactly to the zero-temperature limit of a product of independent two-level statistical mechanics systems. This restores a thermodynamic framework for analyzing spiking attention, placing it in the frozen ordered phase and replacing the usual entropic cost with a Landauer-type physical floor tied to action-potential generation. The result provides a principled energy-efficiency analysis for spiking transformer architectures.

entry.title: Counting with Attention and LayerNorm: Norm Scaling and Representation Geometry

author.name: Ayyub Shaffy, Manoj Dhakal, Safal Shrestha, Keith W. Ross

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the cost of counting in a single attention layer, showing that unnormalized linear attention can count exactly with parameter norms independent of sequence length, while softmax attention requires parameter norms to grow with sequence length and cannot count exactly with finite parameters. The analysis characterizes how softmax attention and layer normalization shape the representation geometry from which counts are recovered.

entry.title: GpFlash: Maximizing Speed and Minimizing Memory for Gaussian Process Training and Prediction

author.name: Andre Marchildon

entry.summary: GpFlash is a Gaussian process library focused on fast training, low memory use, and high-dimensional scalability. Benchmarks against scikit-learn, GPy, GPflow, GPyTorch, and SMT show order-of-magnitude speedups and memory reductions, for example 9.6-35x less memory and 2.6-54x faster likelihood evaluations at 10k training points.

entry.title: ModRes: A modification of the ResPlan dataset ready for floor plan analysis and graph machine learning

author.name: Emma Shelley, Wassim Jabi, Thomas Woolley, Katerina Kaouri

entry.summary: The authors present ModRes, a cleaned and enriched version of the ResPlan dataset with 8,431 valid and unique residential floor plans, removing invalid and duplicate entries via a dedicated cleaning workflow. Each plan ships with 2D geometry, images, 3D representations, and three complementary dual graphs in CSV/JSON with graph-, node-, and edge-level features. It matters because it lowers the preprocessing barrier for spatial-connectivity and graph machine learning research on building layouts.

entry.title: Confine to the Task, Anchor the Rest: Concept-Guided Retention Regularizer for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ibna Kowsar, Ivan Medri, Fanyu Meng, Xin Liu

entry.summary: CGR is a plug-and-play regularizer for parameter-efficient fine-tuning that reduces catastrophic forgetting of pretrained knowledge by constraining both the weight and activation channels, using a frozen sparse autoencoder to softly confine updates to a task-concept subspace while anchoring general-purpose concepts to the frozen model. This concept-level approach goes beyond prior work that only constrains where weight updates lie. It is applicable on top of any PEFT base method.

entry.title: FRACTION: Fraud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context Navigation

author.name: Cecelia Soh, Jun Hu, Yuan Li, Cheng Chen, Hui Liu, Yanjia Zhu, Hao He, Bryan Hooi, Bingsheng He

entry.summary: FRACTION addresses graph fraud explanation generation by using an agentic framework that navigates graph context to produce human-readable explanations for risk labels. It identifies gaps in existing graph-enhanced LLM approaches, including lack of explanation-quality evaluation protocols and granularity mismatches.

entry.title: SYNPRED: A Synergistic Approach to Multimodal Learning for Clinical Prediction

author.name: Ivana Jan\'i\v{c}kov\'a, Yen Y. Tan, Thomas H. Helbich, Philipp Seeb\"ock, Julieta Di Marco, Zsuzsanna Bago-Horvath, Ulrike Heber, Thomas Spiegel, Georg Langs

entry.summary: SYNPRED is a synergistic multimodal VAE framework for clinical prediction that separates task-relevant unimodal and multimodal information from task-irrelevant variation, enabling use of complementary modality-specific signals that contrastive learning misses. The method retains benefits even with missing modalities at test time and is evaluated on medical imaging data.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding with Shared Spatial Fields

author.name: Jean Seong Bjorn Choe

entry.summary: The paper proposes an RL navigation policy for lifelong multi-agent path finding that computes a shared spatial field once per timestep with a convolutional network and derives per-agent movement preferences from a compact goal-conditioned operator. Trained with average-reward RL using throughput as reward, the policy generalizes to larger unseen maps and agent populations without retraining.

entry.title: Over-parameterization Is Neither Robust nor Fragile in Matrix Sensing: A Geometric Theory of Solution Robustness

author.name: Runze Shi, Ziye Ma

entry.summary: The authors develop a rank-aware robustness theory for Burer-Monteiro factorization in matrix sensing when search rank exceeds target rank, showing robustness depends jointly on over-parameterization degree and local geometry of second-order stationary points. Increasing search rank generally worsens sensitivity, but stationary points at the same rank can differ substantially.

entry.title: Fairness under Prediction Error in Predict-then-Optimize Pipelines

author.name: Hilda Adwubi Osei

entry.summary: This single-author study examines whether demographic parity enforced on predicted outcomes carries over to true outcomes in predict-then-optimize pipelines, showing empirically that the true-outcome fairness gap grows with prediction error and saturates per a fitted exponential form. It derives a theoretical bound connecting prediction error to realized fairness violation.

entry.title: Mira-Embeddings-V1: Domain-Adapted Semantic Reranking for Recruitment via LLM-Synthesized Data

author.name: Zhaohua Liang, Zhilin Wang, Renjie Cao, Yining Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces mira-embeddings-v1, a semantic reranking system for recruitment candidate sourcing that reshapes the embedding space using LLM-synthesized positive and hard-negative training data plus a lightweight reranking head. It frames candidate sourcing as a two-stage retrieval-reranking pipeline optimizing recall under a limited recruiter review budget.

entry.title: Learning to Sync at the Edge: Client-Side Adaptive Synchronization for Federated Learning

author.name: Ebasa Temesgen, Ammar Ahmed, Nathan Lechamo, Ali Anwar, Maria Gini

entry.summary: The paper proposes a client-side reinforcement learning synchronization framework for edge federated learning, where each client decides during training whether to upload, download, sync bidirectionally, or defer communication. A lightweight scheduler alongside the local model exploits client-observed progress, resource state, and communication conditions that server-side fixed schedules ignore.

entry.title: Identication and Estimation of Nonsymmetric Determinantal Point Processes

author.name: Christian Gouri\'eroux, Yang Lu

entry.summary: This statistics paper develops identification and estimation theory for nonsymmetric determinantal point processes, which unlike symmetric-kernel DPPs can model positive pairwise dependence. It establishes validity conditions, develops cardinality-truncated maximum likelihood and stochastic gradient estimators, and proves consistency and asymptotic normality. DPPs are widely used in ML for diverse subset selection, so enabling positive dependence broadens their applicability.

entry.title: Data-Topology Compatibility Enables Personalization in Decentralized Learning

author.name: Veronica Xu, Lingfei Wang, Chenlei Leng, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: This paper identifies a data-topology compatibility condition under which decentralized learning supports groups of coherent personalized models: when local objectives and the communication topology have approximately compatible automorphisms, agents within an orbit converge to shared limiting distributions while different orbits stay distinct. This reveals a new regime between global consensus and fully independent local learning, with orbit-wise decomposition of the stochastic dynamics. It offers a structural theory of personalization without explicit personalization mechanisms.

entry.title: Explicit Bounds on Hoffman Constants for Sparse Polyhedral Regularizers

author.name: Faris Chaudhry, Anthea Monod, Keisuke Yano

entry.summary: Derives explicit bounds on Hoffman constants for polyhedral systems arising in sparse regularization, decomposing the constants into spectral, geometric, and interaction components that determine scaling behavior. Hoffman constants govern error bounds, conditioning, and first-order convergence rates, but explicit values are rarely computable.

entry.title: Personalized Physiological-Model-Based Neural Network for Glucose Forecasting in Type 1 Diabetes

author.name: Yaowen Zhang, Shuhao Que, Ying Wang

entry.summary: Applies a physiological-model-based neural network to glucose forecasting, constraining a temporal convolutional network with a personalized four-parameter physiological model trained on CGM, pump, and meal data from 25 participants with type 1 diabetes. The combined forecast and neural-physiological agreement losses aim for accurate yet physiologically consistent multi-horizon predictions.

entry.title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning

author.name: Gunes Akbas, Naci Saldi, Berkay Anahtarci, Can Deha Kariksiz

entry.summary: The paper analyzes stationary discrete-time entropy-regularized mean-field games with average reward, proving span-seminorm contraction of the soft Q-operator and establishing existence, uniqueness, and geometric convergence of equilibria under explicit conditions. It also derives a model-free learning algorithm for the equilibrium from a simulator.

entry.title: Limit Theory for Online Expectile Estimation under Short and Long Range Dependence

author.name: Younghun Lee, Jake Zummo, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: The authors develop limit theory for one-pass constant-step stochastic gradient estimation of expectiles from stationary causal processes, proving a unique stationary solution, geometric forgetting, and asymptotic normality at sqrt(gamma) scale under short-range dependence. For long-memory processes, they identify a different scaling regime, with applications to financial risk measurement.

entry.title: Distributional Regression for Arbitrary Response Variables Using ReLU Neural Networks

author.name: Junpeng Ren, Carlos Misael Madrid Padilla, Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified framework for distributional regression over arbitrary response spaces by modeling conditional event probabilities indexed by measurable sets rather than scalar thresholds. It introduces two estimators, one based on separate regression of event indicators and one enforcing inclusion consistency via a directed acyclic graph, with general error bounds proved for both.

entry.title: Taming Nonconvexity with Epigraph Lifting

author.name: Clara Lage, Hok Shing Wong, Matthias Ehrhardt

entry.summary: The paper introduces a penalized epigraph lifting of neural networks with convex activations and unconstrained weights, showing the lifted problem admits a difference-of-convex decomposition with a finite exactness guarantee at an explicitly computable penalty threshold. It proposes H-DC, a homotopic DC scheme that avoids poor local minima in inverse problems regularized by trained networks.

entry.title: Scalable Identification of Physics-Based and Neural Dynamics from Partial Measurements

author.name: Yibo Zhou, Johannes K\"ohler

entry.summary: The paper presents a scalable system-identification method coupling the Prediction Error Method with Moving Horizon Estimation for nonlinear dynamics from partial measurements, supporting physics-based, neural, and gray-box models. A reformulation avoiding parameter-wide sensitivity matrices yields up to 215x speedup in hypergradient evaluation, demonstrated on racing-vehicle simulations.

entry.title: $\texttt{NFDiag}$: High-dimensional MCMC Convergence Diagnosis with Normalizing Flows

author.name: Kutay Nazl{\i}, Elena Sellentin

entry.summary: NFDiag uses a normalizing flow to assess MCMC convergence by examining the full multivariate joint posterior, including conditional structure that marginal-based diagnostics ignore in high dimensions. This matters because standard convergence statistics become unreliable beyond a few dozen parameters.

entry.title: RFWeave: Learning Wireless Propagation Across Scenes and Transceiver Configurations

author.name: Shurui Xu, Xiao Ye, Yijie Bian, Junjie Ai, Yuxuan Chen, Weicong Chen, Wankai Tang, Shi Jin

entry.summary: RFWeave is a learned wireless propagation model that generalizes across scenes, transceiver locations, and — unlike prior work — transceiver configurations such as array size, orientation, and transmit beam, using variable-length tokens for antenna elements. This enables flexible ray-level propagation prediction for communication system design without retraining per configuration.

entry.title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model

author.name: Mohamad H. Danesh, Raina Hu, Mengxue Xu, Hsiu-Chin Lin

entry.summary: CopyQuad transfers locomotion skills from a single side-view video to a quadruped robot without monocular depth estimation or per-clip 3D reconstruction, pinning the unobserved axis to the robot's stance width. A frozen 2D keypoint detector plus analytic retargeting yields reachable foot targets and a phase-indexed reward with only three tunable scalars per behavior.

entry.title: Sample-Size Extrapolation in Simulation-Based Inference via Statistical Scaling

author.name: Shiyi Sun, Lei Fang, Geoff K Nicholls

entry.summary: CE-NPE enables neural posterior estimators trained on a bounded range of sample sizes to extrapolate to larger datasets by combining a statistical center (closed-form statistic or simulator-based moment match) with an explicit contraction rate and learning residual densities in posterior-scale coordinates. The analysis decomposes how contraction amplifies center error into shape and location components.

entry.title: DiTSG: Context-Aware Air Traffic Scene Generation with Multi-Agent Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Seokbin Yoon, Kyungmin Kim, Taejung Kwon, Keumjin Lee, Peng Wei

entry.summary: Introduces DiTSG, a diffusion transformer with stacked multi-agent inverted Transformer layers that generates realistic air traffic scenes from recorded multi-aircraft trajectories, capturing controller interventions like speed advisories and radar vectoring. It addresses limitations of existing air traffic simulators.

entry.title: LocalTrain: Integer-Only Local Learning for Energy-Efficient CNN Training on Edge FPGAs

author.name: Shiqi Ding, Xuanyu Liang, Xinyang Liu, Boyang Li, Zhiqiang Que, Guosheng Hu, Jiayang Li

entry.summary: Presents an FPGA accelerator for fully integer-only on-device CNN training using local learning with regional auxiliary classifiers, achieving 76.57% on CIFAR-10 and 91.85% on SVHN at ~4.2 W. Compared to Jetson Orin Nano it cuts training energy by roughly 40% with ~1.8x throughput gains.

entry.title: A Method for Exact Enforcement of Boundary Conditions on General Curved Triangular Domains: Algorithm and Application to Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Suchuan Dong, Yuchuan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a method for exactly enforcing Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin boundary conditions on general curved triangular domains, combining exact domain mappings, theory-of-functional-connections constrained expressions, and Barnhill transfinite interpolation to build closed-form trial solutions. This complements prior work on quadrilateral domains and directly benefits physics-informed neural network training for PDEs. It matters for scientific ML where boundary-condition violations degrade solution accuracy.

entry.title: Geometric Structure Predicts Per-Example Neighborhood Loss Under PCA Truncation

author.name: Sriram Loganathan, Gokul Anand, Ragavan Arivazhagan

entry.summary: The study examines per-example neighborhood stability of text embeddings under PCA truncation, showing that degradation is highly uneven across examples and predictable from geometric properties such as the fraction of centered-vector energy retained by the truncated subspace. Different predictors dominate for different embedding families (CBOW, SkipGram, modern Matryoshka-style encoders). This offers guidance for compressing embeddings without silently harming specific items.

entry.title: Weighting-Based Strategies for Classification: Analysis and Local Peak Dynamics with CART Trees

author.name: Abdoulaye Sakho (LPSM), Emmanuel Malherbe (LPSM), Erwan Scornet (LPSM)

entry.summary: This work theoretically compares class-weighting rebalancing strategies against unweighted learning for imbalanced tabular data, proving that asymptotically they yield identical predictive performance up to a threshold shift. It further analyzes weighted versus unweighted CART trees and characterizes the PR-space geometry of both strategies.

entry.title: Lifting: Quantum State Discrimination Framework for Mid-Circuit Measurements

author.name: Chi Zhang, Neel Vora, Yilun Xu, Gang Huang, Fan Chen, Lei Jiang

entry.summary: Lifting is a framework for neural-network-based quantum state discrimination in mid-circuit measurements that improves on the Bayes risk floor imposed by available readout distributions and adapts to state deterioration as circuits execute. It addresses both accuracy and workload drift on noisy superconducting hardware.

entry.title: Autonomous Cyber Operations Gym for Training and Evaluating AI Models for Defence

author.name: Tobias H\"urten, Johannes F. Loevenich, Florian Spelter, Erik Adler, Laurin Holz, Maxime Schwarzer, Thies Moehlenhof, Roberto Rigolin F. Lopes

entry.summary: This work introduces a unified gym environment for autonomous cyber defense, combining high-fidelity network emulation, realistic benign and adversarial user behavior, and scenario generation toolkits. It supports training DNN-based intrusion detection systems and evaluating modular autonomous defense agents, with in-domain classifiers showing near-perfect recall.

entry.title: ASSET: Adaptive Speech Segmentation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Cihan Xiao, Yuan Tseng, Matthew Wiesner, Desh Raj, Leibny Paola Garcia Perera, Sanjeev Khudanpur, David Harwath

entry.summary: ASSET uses GRPO-based reinforcement learning to train a segmenter that adaptively partitions speech encoder outputs into variable-duration segments pooled into continuous audio tokens, balancing task performance against token rate. It targets the sequence-length bottleneck of speech LLMs built from acoustic encoders and LLM decoders.

entry.title: Do correct answers have stable latent knowledge support?

author.name: Chuancheng Shi, Shangze Li, Wenhua Wu, Kun Hu, Fei Shen, Zhiyong Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This paper proposes latent state stability and knowledge topology stability metrics to test whether LLM answers that are correct are backed by stable internal knowledge representations. By averaging internal representations of the same knowledge across elicitation conditions and removing shared shifts, the authors measure the stability of individual knowledge states and their relational structure. The work addresses whether output correctness genuinely reflects robust internal knowledge versus lucky sampling.

entry.title: NepPlural: A Human-Anchored Benchmark for Persona Annotation in Nepali Migration Discourse

author.name: Jinu Nyachhyon, Anish Khatiwada, Bimal Timilsina

entry.summary: NepPlural is a benchmark of 2,148 code-mixed Nepali YouTube comments on migration, annotated along a four-axis persona taxonomy with a 300-comment gold set labeled independently by three native speakers. It addresses Western skew in pluralistic-alignment datasets by grounding competing socio-cultural values in Nepali public discourse.

entry.title: Intent-Triggered Anchoring for Multi-Token Format Units in Parallel Decoding of Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Junhyeok Lee, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: The paper identifies a practical failure of parallel decoding in diffusion language models: co-committed tokens cannot see each other, breaking multi-token format units needed by parsers, causing 32.7-36.7 percent of chest X-ray reports to lack parseable headings. It proposes intent-triggered anchoring, a training-free decoding rule that completes a format unit once its first token is committed. It raises readable rates from about 63-67 percent to 100 percent with no latency regressions.

entry.title: From Sampled Evidence to Radiology Reports: Objectives, Constraints, and Realization

author.name: Kun Zhao, Haoteng Tang, Chenghua Lin, Liang Zhan

entry.summary: This work studies how sampled evidence should be converted into final decisions and text in radiology report generation, decoupling the decision signal, scoring objective, and feasible decision set. Controlled experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray across 13 generator configurations show objective and constraint choices materially change predictions and metric trade-offs.

entry.title: GENDIS: Gender-Related Discourse and Stance in Multilingual YouTube Comments from India, Kenya, and Nigeria

author.name: Luise Koch, Manuel Tonneau, Niyati Malhotra, Sunny Rai, Ana Maria Munoz Boudet, Victor Orozco-Olvera, Samuel P. Fraiberger, Sharath Chandra Guntuku

entry.summary: GENDIS is a dataset of 9,600 human-annotated multilingual YouTube comments from India, Kenya, and Nigeria, annotated with a two-level framework separating gender mentions from negative, positive, or neutral evaluative stances. This decoupling enables prevalence estimation of gender-related discourse independent of harm-focused framing.

entry.title: Swiss4Arg: A Parallel Dataset for Multilingual Argument Mining across Swiss National Languages

author.name: Sophia Conrad, Fatma-Zohra Rezkellah, Christina Niklaus, Reto Gubelmann

entry.summary: Swiss4Arg is a parallel multilingual argument mining dataset built from Swiss federal voting brochures in German, French, Italian, and Romansh. It covers 53 voting issues from 2019-2025 with annotations for argument components and relations by three native speakers per language. It is valuable for low-resource languages like Romansh and for cross-lingually aligned argument understanding.

entry.title: Breakdown of Conversational Involvement: A Joint Multi-Modal Analysis of Conversation Floors and F-formation Detection with Multiple Features

author.name: Zonghuan Li, Chirag Raman, Hayley Hung

entry.summary: The paper studies conversational involvement in free-standing conversations, arguing that the assumption that F-formations capture single conversations is insufficient. It uses speaking status to estimate conversation floors within F-formations and analyzes spatial characteristics across implementations. This refines the computational modeling of who can influence whom in multiparty interaction.

entry.title: Description Complexity Bounds for Analytic Approximations of Lipschitz Functions

author.name: Artem Vozmishchev

entry.summary: This theory paper proves upper and matching lower bounds on the number of bits needed to write an elementary analytic expression approximating any Lipschitz function on [0,1], using smoothed linear splines in a description language with a repetition construct. The bounds hold uniformly over accuracy and Lipschitz constants, with the lower bound valid for every description language. It contributes to the theoretical characterization of compact function descriptions relevant to expressivity questions.

entry.title: VisualCoding: Learning Executable Skills for Reliable Visual Reasoning

author.name: Liu Jiaqi, Jin Ruinan, Li Xiaoxiao

entry.summary: Proposes VisualCoding, which acquires reusable visual programs via execution-guided composition and revision of primitives into family-level solvers, then directly adopts validated answers on in-scope inputs at inference time. This reduces errors and hallucinations in the final implementation and answering steps of visual reasoning agents.

entry.title: Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers for Multimodal Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yuxin Jiang, Yunkang Cao, Weiming Shen

entry.summary: BAT addresses cross-modal interference in RGB plus point cloud anomaly detection by replacing static fusion of frozen encoder features with bidirectional adaptive transformers that establish latent semantic correspondence. This yields more complementary multimodal representations for industrial inspection.

entry.title: Engram Neuron Inspired Adaptive Memorization for Lifelong Learning

author.name: Suiyang Jiang, Bomin Wang, Hangqi Zhou, Jianfeng Feng, Xiahai Zhuang

entry.summary: This work integrates the full memory life cycle of engram neurons into artificial learners, constructing structured memory from gradient representations that regulates parameter updates and memory management. Evaluations across four benchmarks show promising lifelong learning capability with adaptive memory updating beyond just mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: TRIG: Toward Measuring Texture Realism in Image Generation

author.name: Zhiwei Xu, Jiali Cui, Zhiqiang Lao, Heather Yu, Liang Peng

entry.summary: TRIG is an evaluation metric targeting texture realism in generated images, motivated by the observation that backbones trained for classification or image-text alignment encode invariant features that miss low-level texture discrepancies. The paper analyzes metric backbones and proposes features that explicitly capture texture-specific differences in generative outputs.

entry.title: OmniRSI: Taming Latent Diffusion for Unified Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Generation

author.name: Hebaixu Wang, Jing Zhang, Haonan Guo, Di Wang, Jiayi Ma, Bo Du

entry.summary: OmniRSI is a unified multimodal remote sensing image generation model built on latent diffusion, using a remote sensing-specific VAE that captures multimodal priors and promotes locally smooth latents. It replaces sensor-specific fine-tuning of natural image generators with shared representations and robust conditioning.

entry.title: ProMoDD: Dataset Distillation for 3D Human Motion via Prototype-Conditioned Diffusion Models

author.name: Yijin Wei, Yawen Zou, Wenqi Cai, Guang Li, Hangli Ge, Katsuya Hotta, Chunzhi Gu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: ProMoDD performs dataset distillation for skeleton-based action recognition by conditioning a motion diffusion model on class-wise prototypes of temporally resolved recognition features, with diffusion training tailored to preserve skeletal configurations and temporal continuity. This avoids constraints violated by direct joint-coordinate optimization.

entry.title: DepthTile: Depth-Guided Existing-Image Self-Tiling with Input-Side Tileability Assessment

author.name: Rui Wang, Xi Chen, Hui Dai, Piaopiao Yu, Yixue Hao, Long Hu, Min Chen

entry.summary: DepthTile converts monocular depth into a spatial preservation prior integrated into the masking mechanism of Tiled Diffusion, enabling seamless self-tiling of an input image while retaining semantics without retraining the diffusion backbone. It also introduces an input-side tileability assessment to judge when an image can be made repeatable.

entry.title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression

author.name: Nikolaos Kegkeroglou, Bilal Sabillah, Myrto Inglezou, Vincent Placet, C\'endric Clevy, Antonios Porichis

entry.summary: This paper replaces slow finite element simulations for characterizing the transverse mechanical behavior of plant fibers with a deep learning pipeline using two coupled recursive U-Nets to predict deformation and stress fields, plus a regression CNN for downstream property estimation. It enables high-throughput mechanical characterization across realistic fiber populations for sustainable composite design.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM-Guided Visual Question Answering: Does Deeper Knowledge Integration Really Help?

author.name: Aneerban Saha, Vijay Kumar, Sameer Madhav D., Priyam Srivastava, Dhruv Bansal

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares two strategies for integrating LLM-generated reasoning guidance into a frozen ViT + FLAN-T5 framework for knowledge-based VQA on OK-VQA: decision-level late fusion versus attention-matrix injection, using Llama 3.3 70B to generate structured guidance. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, it finds that deeper architectural integration of LLM knowledge does not necessarily help.

entry.title: AttenIR: Aligning Dense Visual Attention with Mesh Warping for Unsupervised Image Retargeting

author.name: Yun Zhang, Zhiruo Zhang, Lifei Zhu, Zhe Zhu, Tong Li, Fang-Lue Zhang, Shengjuan Liu, Xinyuan Zheng

entry.summary: AttenIR is an unsupervised image retargeting framework that couples dense visual attention with content-aware mesh warping, formulating mesh deformation as saliency-guided vertex displacement regression. It aims to preserve global structure and content fidelity while avoiding manual labels and traditional optimization.

entry.title: EmoGenie: Benchmarking and Evaluating Expressed and Evoked Emotion in T2I Generation with MLLMs

author.name: Zixuan Xing, Lancheng Gao, Shengyan Li, Huiyu Duan, Zhaolin Cai, Guangtao Zhai, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: Introduces EmoGenie, a benchmark for evaluating emotions expressed and evoked by text-to-image generated images, extending beyond prior portrait-focused affective benchmarks of natural images. It studies whether MLLMs can reliably interpret emotion in AI-generated visual content. Addresses the underexplored affective dimension of generated imagery.

entry.title: MFVSR: A Multi-Style and Fine-Grained Benchmark for Video Subtitle Removal

author.name: Xiyan Huang, Qingdong He, Peng Tang, Bo Yin, Chaoyi Wang, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: Introduces MFVSR, a large-scale benchmark of 3,000 paired videos (plus 953 in-the-wild videos) for video subtitle removal with fine-grained, reliability-aware metrics capturing localized restoration errors, unintended edits, temporal instability, and incomplete outputs. Previous evaluation relied on low-resolution data and generic inpainting protocols. A resource contribution for a specific video restoration task.

entry.title: RSIgen: Reciprocal Self-Improvement for Agentic Visual Generation

author.name: Yidi Liu, Haozhe Wang, Jie Xiao, Kai Zhu, Xueyang Fu, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: RSIgen is a task-centric framework in which the agent and generator roles of a unified multimodal backbone improve each other, using Dynamic Responsibility Routing to decide which role should learn from experience and to construct compatible training targets. It also refreshes stale action supervision after generator updates and builds a recursive curriculum.

entry.title: MIST: Multi-Scale Spatial Context for Gene Expression Prediction from Histology

author.name: Koushik Howlader, Tirtho Roy, Md Tauhidul Islam, Wei Le

entry.summary: MIST is a multi-context spatial Transformer for predicting spatial gene expression from H&E histology images, augmenting self-attention with a coordinate-invariant local k-nearest-neighbor pathway and a whole-slide summary pathway in every layer. It predicts all spots in a single forward pass, extending molecular analysis to tissues lacking spatial transcriptomics measurements.

entry.title: RepProbe: Can Video Language Models Count Repeated Actions? A Diagnostic Benchmark

author.name: Mahsa Khoshnoodi, Sarah Adel Bargal

entry.summary: RepProbe is a 42K-clip diagnostic benchmark with real and synthetic videos containing exactly k (1-20) action repetitions, with controls for clip position, temporal coverage, and duration. It shows that repetition counting collapses at high counts across video language models, and controlled experiments indicate the failure is not explained by frame sampling alone, enabling localization of the failure within models.

entry.title: ArborSplat: Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Orchards

author.name: Alessandro Masini, Matteo Frosi, Mirko Usuelli, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: ArborSplat is an online semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system for orchard robots that couples LiDAR odometry with semantics optimized directly on the Gaussian map. It uses class-specific height-band constraints and multi-view label fusion to reliably capture thin structures like trunks and trellises that appearance-driven methods miss. This matters for agricultural robotics where semantic maps of small structures are critical for navigation and manipulation.

entry.title: RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction

author.name: Mengrui Yin, Tianxingjian Ding, Wufan Zhao, Ziyang Yan, Yu Tian

entry.summary: RePrior tackles sparse-view cone-beam CT reconstruction by reconciling learned anatomical priors with observed X-ray measurements during patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction. It addresses the non-uniform spatial discrepancy between prior and reconstruction and the projection-domain conflicts that arise when spatial corrections affect overlapping rays. This matters for reducing radiation dose in medical imaging while preserving reconstruction fidelity.

entry.title: Integrating 3D Posture Neutralization with Statistical Shape Modeling for Head-Neck-Shoulder Ergonomic Design

author.name: Jinbo Luo, Hang Ren, Yadie Yang, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: The paper builds a statistical shape model of the head-neck-shoulder region from 3D scans of 200 Chinese adults, fitting a parametric head-neck model to separate cervical pose from anatomy and neutralizing posture before modeling. The result supports ergonomic design of head-worn and neck-worn products such as helmets and cervical orthoses. It contributes both a dataset-derived population model and a posture-neutralization methodology.

entry.title: Collective Benefits and Efficiency in Coupled Echo State Networks

author.name: Polyphony Bruna, Rick Dale, Michael J. Spivey, Christopher T. Kello

entry.summary: This reservoir computing study uses coupled echo state networks trained to identify Japanese speakers from vowel recordings to examine whether interacting groups outperform independent ones. Model pairs with coupled feedback reproduce dyadic coordination advantages in accuracy and can be more efficient than independent aggregation, refining the wisdom-of-crowds picture. The work connects collective behavior research with computational modeling.

entry.title: Mapping Tire-Road Friction Coefficients Along Driven Trajectories

author.name: Risto Ojala

entry.summary: This paper presents FrictionMap, an offline post-processing method for mapping tire-road friction coefficients along driven trajectories using standard on-board vehicle sensors. Mapped friction data could be shared across connected vehicles to enable proactive safety measures in low-friction areas, filling a gap since prior work focused only on online estimation.

entry.title: StateSkill-Agent: An Effective and Efficient Embodied Agent via State-conditioned Skill

author.name: Changxu Wei, Jingyi Zhang, Zhiyu Zheng, Tianyi Lin, Yixian Zhang, Yunpeng Qing, Jingyuan Liu, Zhi Hou, Jiaxing Huang

entry.summary: StateSkill-Agent models embodied interaction as a finite-state machine, organizing skills around task-progress states, transitions, and state-conditioned guidance so a multimodal LLM agent can reuse and adapt skills as tasks unfold. The representation keeps skill contexts compact while remaining generalizable. This targets efficiency and transfer in embodied MLLM agents.

entry.title: Scaling Latent Motor Adaptation to Coordinated Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Seung-Bin Joo, Alessandro Albini, Luca Wiehe, Perla Maiolino, Daniel Olmeda Reino, Jo\~ao F. Henriques

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA), an embedding-based approach for conditioning actions on latent environment dynamics, scales from single-arm to coordinated bimanual manipulation with higher-dimensional control, coupled contacts, and shared object forces. Experiments on three contact-rich ManiSkill tasks with randomized YCB object properties probe the paradigm's limits. The findings inform whether latent adaptation generalizes to richer contact settings.

entry.title: LETS: Low-Overhead External-Torque Sensing for Force-Feedback Bilateral Teleoperation

author.name: Zonghao Guo, Dongchen Guan, Yubo Wang, Peng Yang

entry.summary: LETS is a physics-guided learning method for external-torque estimation that assigns rigid-body dynamics to recursive Newton-Euler inverse dynamics and learns only the robot-specific residual, using just the URDF model and joint feedback while excluding control commands. It trains on 12 minutes of free-motion data and avoids costly end-effector force/torque sensors. This enables accurate force-feedback bilateral teleoperation on standard commercial arms.

entry.title: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Safety-Aware Haptic Shared Control in Surgical Robotics

author.name: Zihao Zhang, Karl Handwerker, Balint Varga

entry.summary: The authors model surgeon-robot haptic shared control as a two-agent cooperative Markov game with centralized training and decentralized execution, comparing MADDPG, rMAPPO, and an epigraph-constrained approach against fixed-impedance baselines. This provides a principled MARL framework for surgical robotics where force coordination and safety geometry are jointly learned rather than hand-engineered.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Predictive Control for Walk-to-Run Bipedal Obstacle Crossing

author.name: Aashish Sahu, R. Prasanth Kumar

entry.summary: This paper presents a geometry-aware predictive control framework for bipedal robots crossing obstacles in both walking and running regimes. It uses a five-phase trajectory structure with obstacle-height and depth-adaptive swing-foot, stance, and pelvis adjustments tracked by constrained MPC. The interpretable phase decomposition across gait regimes is a useful contribution for legged locomotion.

entry.title: PathLift: Depth-Conditioned Metric Lifting for Visual-Navigation Priors

author.name: Gwanjun Shin, Hyeongseok Suh, Hongmo Jung, Jongwoo Lim

entry.summary: PathLift is a per-waypoint depth-conditioned adapter that converts unitless trajectories from pre-trained visual-navigation policies into metric paths by consuming explicit sensor-grade depth (RGB-D, stereo, projected LiDAR) and fitting per-waypoint magnitude and lateral residuals. It avoids both uniform scalar scaling errors and in-policy monocular depth error propagation near obstacles. This addresses a real deployment gap for generalist navigation policies.

entry.title: LABIT: Long-Horizon Robotic Assembly Benchmark for Industrial Tasks

author.name: Constantin Schempp, Christian Friedrich, Luca Kofler, Laura Suhm

entry.summary: LABIT is a benchmark for long-horizon industrial robotic assembly that covers multi-step assembly and subassembly sequences rather than isolated grasping or insertion tasks. It is motivated by the observation that single-task benchmarks cannot capture the interconnected nature of modern manufacturing processes. The benchmark targets compliant control and whole-assembly construction.

entry.title: Joint-Feasibility Margin Feedback for Bounded-Input Second-Order Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Siyuan Yang, Shaoming He

entry.summary: The paper addresses the problem of multiple second-order control barrier function (HOCBF) constraints exhausting shared control authority under bounded acceleration. It defines a signed local joint-feasibility margin whose sign exactly identifies whether the barrier half-spaces intersect the admissible input set, with a support-function dual revealing weighted constraint conflicts. A one-step-ahead prediction over task-directed candidates selects which QP to solve, aiming to preserve safety under input bounds.

entry.title: TacSpin: Tactile Tracking of In-Gripper Object Rotation on SO(3) via Axis-Magnitude Estimation

author.name: Yuhao Wu, Linhao Song, Huan Yin

entry.summary: TacSpin tracks in-gripper object rotation on SO(3) using only two vision-based tactile sensors, estimating rotation axis and magnitude separately rather than least-squares rigid-body fitting, with contact-boundary refinement and agreement-based fusion between fingers. It achieves lower mean checkpoint errors on standard objects and transfers calibration to real-world objects.

entry.title: RTISSLAM: In-air Imaging Sonar SLAM using a Robust Pose Graph and Occupancy Grid Mapping

author.name: Jan Steckel

entry.summary: RTISSLAM is a sonar-only SLAM system for embedded 3D imaging sonar that works where cameras and lidar fail — darkness, smoke, dust, and glass — combining a robust pose graph back-end with occupancy grid mapping. It uses energy-scapes from delay-multiply-and-sum beamforming with range-wise CFAR as place descriptors for sequence-verified loop closures, plus acoustic odometry to calibrate wheel odometry.

entry.title: De-biased Distribution Estimation for Locally Differential Private Survival Data

author.name: Yi Xiong, Li-Pang Chen, Liyue Fan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a nonparametric deconvolution-kernel estimator for the true survivor function from locally differentially private, right-censored survival data, correcting the distortion introduced by local perturbation. It provides valid statistical inference for time-to-event data shared under strong per-record privacy protection. The work addresses a real tension between clinical data privacy and analytic utility.

entry.title: Below the Frontier: The Battle for Good-Enough AI

author.name: ykevinzhang

entry.summary: An economic analysis arguing that the consequential AI competition is shifting below the frontier, where good-enough models can serve enterprise knowledge work, given limited consumer AI revenue relative to capex. It discusses recent agentic launches such as Meta's Muse and startup valuations, and predicts revenue concentration in coding will not generalize across enterprise knowledge work.

entry.title: RASSG: Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating for Streaming Tool Execution

author.name: Daijin Hu, Xi Wang

entry.summary: RASSG addresses stale tool execution in streaming speech assistants, where user self-corrections after a tool launches can invalidate arguments and cause irreversible side effects. It launches tools after three identical ASR results and uses calibrated invalidity risk with execution costs to decide cancellation at the last feasible point.

entry.title: Label-Centric Knowledge Retrieval for Zero-Shot Text Classification

author.name: Daoping Wu, Dong Wang, Siyu Liu, Chen Liang, Jian Geng, Ziqi Li, Shuguang Xiong, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: SLKR is a label-centric retrieval-augmented framework for zero-shot text classification that separates offline knowledge construction by a flagship LLM (label definitions, keywords, boundary rules for confusable pairs) from lightweight online inference. The reusable label-knowledge store reduces inference cost and latency for large-scale labeling.

entry.title: AlignAudio: A Unified Dual-Alignment Framework for Noise-Robust Speech-Conditioned Generation

author.name: Yixuan Li, Xuenan Xu, Zeyu Xie, Mengyue Wu

entry.summary: AlignAudio improves noise robustness of speech-conditioned audio generation through dual alignment: matching clean and noisy speech representations to preserve semantic cues, and enforcing generation-level consistency within a flow matching paradigm. It addresses the degradation of end-to-end models under environmental noise.

entry.title: BehaviorFormer: Discovering Behavioral Patterns via Clusterable Next-Token Prediction

author.name: Tobias Schneider, Danial Fahrner, Soren Antebi, Daniel Uedelhoven, Lennard Bodden, Sandra Halscheidt, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: The paper combines a next-token prediction Transformer with the DCSS deep clustering algorithm to learn representations with well-separated clusters, applied to open-ended player behavior in Minecraft. With 26 players it discovers 23 distinct, interpretable behavioral patterns grouped into seven categories, refining self-supervised representations into clusterable structure.

entry.title: Chasing Label Shifters: A Change-Aware Framework for Dynamic Graph Node Classification

author.name: Junghoon Kim, Seungyoon Choi, Hyunsung Kim, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: The paper identifies a systematic failure across major dynamic graph neural network architectures: nodes whose class labels change between snapshots (shifters) are consistently classified worse than stable nodes, even though detecting such transitions matters most for intervention. It proposes a change-aware framework to improve shifter classification on dynamic graphs.

entry.title: MERIT: Multimodal Evidence Reasoning over Image Tables

author.name: Haoyang Jiang, Zhuotong Fan, Mingyang Yi, Ju Fan, Lanqing Hu, Xiao Zan

entry.summary: MERIT is a three-stage framework for reasoning over table images rather than serialized text, arguing that serialization corrupts cell contents, structure, and visual cues. The work identifies visual evidence acquisition as the key bottleneck and introduces table-specific mechanisms, with serialized tables as optional auxiliary inputs. This contributes to the growing area of document and table understanding with multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: SimInter: Evidence-Grounded User Simulation with Interview-Based Profile Enrichment for Conversational Recommender Systems

author.name: Erfan Shahabi, Amirhossein Roshandel, Mohammad Sadegh Sadeghi, Azadeh Shakery

entry.summary: SimInter enriches LLM-based user simulators for conversational recommender systems by eliciting implicit attributes such as decision-making style and domain expertise through synthetic interviews between two LLM agents, grounded in user history. An audit agent flags potential fabrication and stereotyping before profile enrichment. This improves evaluation fidelity for CRSs at lower cost than human testing.

entry.title: Historical Anchors for Scientific Forecasting on Human-Aware Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Siu Tin Wu, Ryan C. Barron, Phoebe Upton Sanderbeck, Kim {\O}. Rasmussen, George Tompkins, Maksim E. Eren

entry.summary: This paper improves hypergraph-based embedding methods for forecasting future scientific connections by using historical anchors to set path-sampling budgets, addressing the problem that prediction quality depends non-monotonically on the number of sampled paths. The work targets predicting material properties and other scientific links on knowledge graphs that include researchers and concepts. It comes from a team with national-lab affiliations.

entry.title: Design Choices for Multimodal Transformer Learning with Missing and Longitudinal Healthcare Data

author.name: Rita Cordeiro Mendes, Maria Manuel Pereira, Carlos Santiago, Catarina Barata

entry.summary: The paper studies architectural design choices for Transformer-based multimodal fusion when healthcare data have missing modalities, intra-modal missingness, and longitudinal structure, focusing on tokenization granularity and use of temporal sequence structure. It provides guidance for building multimodal models on incomplete clinical datasets.

entry.title: One-Way Coupling via Patchwise Adaptive Normalization in Transformer Surrogates

author.name: Emmanuel Gottlob, Hugo Thimonier, Ludovico Buizza, August Martens, Alexandre Gavaudan, Thiago Guzella

entry.summary: PAdaNorm partitions exogenous fields (medium density, obstacle geometry) into patches aligned with state tokenization to explicitly represent one-way coupling in transformer PDE surrogates. Evaluated on three PDE families with a Walrus-inspired transformer, it matches or beats parameter-matched baselines by up to 16% in long-horizon variance-scaled error.

entry.title: Exact Phase-Type Point Processes for Certified Measurement and Prediction of Event Streams

author.name: Sayak Dutta

entry.summary: The paper shows that a single phase-type (Erlang-chain) state space supports both measurement and prediction of event streams with exact likelihoods. It builds a multiscale phase-type Hawkes process with linear-in-parameters, concave log-likelihood, a global optimum with a Fenchel duality-gap certificate, and closed-form shock responses with a spectral stability condition. This provides certified, tractable tools for temporal point process modeling.

entry.title: Making LoRA Identifiable: Orthogonal Alignment for Continual Learning

author.name: Pratik Rakesh Singh, Mohammadi Zaki, Akash Saha, Aneesh Mukkamala, Pankaj Wasnik

entry.summary: The paper proposes training a single identifiable LoRA module for continual learning via orthogonal alignment, avoiding the linear memory growth of per-task LoRA branches and gating mechanisms used in prior PEFT continual learning approaches. The approach aims to mitigate catastrophic forgetting while scaling across many tasks.

entry.title: Nearest Neighbor Functional Curve Completion for Intraday Probabilistic Revisions of Renewable Generation Forecasts

author.name: Guillermo Terr\'en-Serrano, Michael Ludkovski

entry.summary: The paper proposes a nonparametric functional curve completion method that fuses day-ahead renewable generation forecasts with partial intraday realizations to produce probabilistic nowcasts for the rest of the day. It builds weighted neighborhoods using similarity over the observed partial curve, the forecast, and calendar features across a large asset database.

entry.title: Stable-Plastic Subspace Construction for Differentially Private Continual LoRA

author.name: Jin Liu, Ning Xi, Yinbin Miao, Junkang Liu, Ke Cheng, Jianfeng Ma

entry.summary: This paper studies continual LoRA adaptation under differential privacy, observing that private training increases forgetting primarily during subsequent adaptation, that jointly perturbing both LoRA factors introduces bilinear noise interactions, and that DP aggravates the stability-plasticity dilemma. It constructs stable-plastic subspaces to balance retention and adaptation under record-level privacy constraints. This addresses the underexplored intersection of privacy and continual learning.

entry.title: Revisiting Error Feedback for Model Quantization

author.name: Wai-Yiu Keung, Chi Cui, Wing-Kin Ma, Jes\'us Cid-Sueiro, Hei Victor Cheng

entry.summary: The paper treats causal error-feedback coefficients in quantization as explicit design variables, formulating a metric-dependent trace optimization resembling GPTQ/LDLQ with Jacobian-aware designs. The authors prove the joint rotation-feedback trace minimum is n det(H)^(1/n) and show empirical benefits for language model quantization from downstream-sensitive feedback.

entry.title: Beyond Task Success: A Theory of Representation Reuse

author.name: Zibo Meng, Andrew C. M. Austin, Alin Achim

entry.summary: This theory paper formalizes when learned representations can be reused by future tasks, defining task-relevant state as the coarsest deterministic state sufficient for a family of tasks. It shows larger task families can require finer states, that losing a needed distinction makes future tasks unrecoverable, and separates information content from its presentation to downstream rules.

entry.title: BandPC: Learning Residual-Band Preconditioner Combinations for Flexible Conjugate Gradient Solvers

author.name: D. M. Li, Shang-Tian Yang, Xin Qiu

entry.summary: BandPC is a data-driven framework using graph neural networks to predict multi-stage preconditioning strategies for flexible conjugate gradient solvers, partitioning the iteration into residual-norm bands. It improves CG convergence on sparse SPD systems with diverse, irregular sparsity patterns where hand-designed preconditioners struggle to generalize.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Strategy, Not Just Data: A Statistically Rigorous Audit of Gender and Stereotypical Bias in Embedding Models for HR Recommendation Systems

author.name: Ekta Yadav

entry.summary: This paper audits six multilingual sentence-embedding models used in job-candidate matching for gender and stereotype bias using Bias-in-Bios and StereoSet, with careful statistical methodology. Notably, it identifies a non-independence error in naive significance testing that inflated a trivial 0.0046 mean difference to near-zero p-values. It shows that fine-tuning strategy, not just training data, shapes bias outcomes in HR retrieval.

entry.title: A temporal graph dissimilarity measure capturing epidemic spreading behavior

author.name: Salvatore Freni, Lorenzo Dall'Amico, Francesca Pistilli, Alain Barrat, Tatiana Tommasi, Ciro Cattuto

entry.summary: The authors introduce Time-Shift DTW for comparing epidemic curves and build EATGD, a temporal graph dissimilarity measure that compares networks by how spreading processes unfold on them rather than by structural features alone. This captures functional similarity between structurally different networks.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Deferred-Decision Trajectory Optimization with Anytime-Valid Target Retention for Moving Candidates

author.name: Farbod Siahkali, Mengxue Hou, Vijay Gupta

entry.summary: Develops a receding-horizon deferred-decision trajectory optimization controller for multi-agent interception of an unknown moving target among candidates, combining conformal prediction, sequential candidate rejection, and capacity-constrained assignment. It establishes fixed-time coverage and anytime-valid target retention guarantees.

entry.title: On the Optimality of Random Features under General Conditions: Misspecified Cases and Robust Learning

author.name: Caixing Wang

entry.summary: The paper provides an improved analysis of kernel ridge regression with random features under general conditions, including misspecified models and heavy-tailed noise, improving worst-case uniform bounds on the feature map. It establishes minimax optimal learning rates in the light-tailed setting and robust rates under heavy-tailed noise.

entry.title: Texture Interpolation as Texton Matching

author.name: Ido Madar, Gal Oren, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: This work reframes texture interpolation by replacing positional blending of pixels or features with appearance-aware matching of local textons, holding encoder and decoder fixed to isolate the effect of correspondence. The study shows that the hidden pairing choice is a major determinant of interpolation quality between unrelated textures.

entry.title: Active Learning for Finding a Needle in a Haystack

author.name: Emily Silcock, Simon L\"owe

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates whether active learning can correct the initial-selection bias that arises when rare-class examples (at roughly 1% prevalence) must be seeded via keyword search rather than random sampling. On AG News and Measuring Hate Speech, the authors compare random sampling with eight active learning strategies. The work provides practical guidance for the common real-world scenario of rare-class document classification like targeted hate speech detection.

entry.title: Label Collapse in Diffusion Language Model In-Context Learning

author.name: Ziye Guo, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: The paper defines label collapse, a failure mode where models generate query-independent labels in in-context learning, and shows it is architecturally universal at the tested 8-9B scale across five autoregressive and discrete diffusion models including Llama-3, Qwen3.5, and LLaDA variants. Collapse persists even under class-balanced alternating label arrangements. This systematically characterizes a bias affecting both standard and diffusion LMs.

entry.title: LegalRewardBench: Benchmarking Reward Models for Legal Preference Evaluation

author.name: Hui Huang, Jie Zhou, Hongli Zhou, Qundong Shi, Shuyuan Zheng, Yini Su, Shaochun Wang, Biyuan Lin, Muyun Yang, Tiejun Zhao

entry.summary: LegalRewardBench is the first human-verified benchmark for evaluating reward models on legal preference tasks, organized into five capability levels from knowledge to writing, with rubric-guided automatic judging plus human verification. The authors evaluate judge families spanning general and fine-tuned, generative and discriminative models. It targets the gap where reward model benchmarks focus on general-domain preferences.

entry.title: DuSRFlow: Dual-Lens Super-Resolution via Parallax-Aware Flow Estimation and Complementary Reference Warping

author.name: Fangpu Zhang, Huanjing Yue, Zifan Cui, Shaoxiong Tu, Qirui Yang, Jingyu Yang

entry.summary: DuSRFlow improves dual-lens super-resolution by learning parallax-aware correspondence and better reference aggregation, addressing failures of off-the-shelf optical flow under large parallax, occlusion, and cross-camera discrepancies. It enhances a wide-angle low-resolution image using a telephoto reference.

entry.title: CatPortrait: Taming Video Generative Models for Portrait Animation via In-context Conditioning

author.name: Ziqi Ni, Zhou Fang, Shijian Wang, Rui Li, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: CatPortrait enables controllable portrait animation by injecting 3D facial guidance as in-context conditioning through spatial concatenation, preserving the pretrained video generation backbone without architectural changes or extra conditioning modules. This maintains compatibility with pretrained image-to-video models while adding control.

entry.title: FireNav: Decision-Oriented Reconstruction Evidence Routing for Vision-Language Navigation in Indoor Fire Environments

author.name: Hongbo Ding, Xiang Chen, Jiangxin Dong, Jinshan Pan

entry.summary: FireNav aligns image restoration with navigation utility for vision-language navigation in smoke-degraded indoor fire environments, routing reconstruction evidence based on decision relevance rather than fidelity. It contributes FireVLN-Bench, a paired benchmark with clean references for this safety-critical setting.

entry.title: Visual Tokens on Demand: Visual Budgeting for Scalable and Efficient Multi-Image Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Aimon Rahman, Joymallya Chakraborty, Vidit Bansal, Abhishek Dan

entry.summary: This paper proposes visual budgeting for multi-image reasoning in multimodal LLMs, allocating visual tokens on demand across images rather than compressing each image independently. It addresses cross-image redundancy and distributed task-relevant evidence that single-image pruning, merging, and compression techniques do not handle.

entry.title: Exploring the Latent Structure of AMD Severity Using Retinal Foundation Models

author.name: Niccol\`o Fineschi, Jovana Panic, Atsushi Watanabe, Hideaki Hayashi, Kazuya Nishimura, Yuki Maeno, Samanta Rosati, Gabriella Balestra, Kohji Nishida, Hajime Nagahara

entry.summary: This study investigates how age-related macular degeneration severity is encoded in the embedding space of RET-CLIP, a retinal vision-language foundation model, using bilateral fundus images from the AREDS dataset. It characterizes the distribution of disease severity in representation space and evaluates how this structure affects downstream classification. The work provides interpretability insight into medical foundation models, informing their reliable clinical use.

entry.title: BGC-Nav: Cross-Altitude Multi-UAV Collaborative Navigation via Belief-Guided Coupling

author.name: Jiuwu Hao, Yueyang Wu, Liguo Sun, Haolin Song, Zao Zhang, Pin Lv

entry.summary: BGC-Nav is a training-free framework where a high-altitude UAV maintains a Global Belief Memory of task-conditioned priors to guide low-altitude UAVs in search-and-rescue navigation, replacing rigid goal-dispatching with belief-guided coupling. This handles observation uncertainty while preserving low-altitude exploration autonomy. It targets robust multi-UAV aerial VLN under partial observability.

entry.title: EnactOpt: Diagnosis-Guided Harness Evolution for Embodied Agents

author.name: ZhiYuan Feng, Zhuoshi Pan, Zhaolu Kang, Zhongxia Chen, Shuo Yang, Sen Ye, Heng Wang, Han Li

entry.summary: EnactOpt adapts the execution harness around foundation-model embodied agents without updating model parameters, evolving how observations are organized, actions guided, and feedback incorporated. It uses diagnosis to distinguish failures caused by missing evidence from those caused by poor use of available evidence, which task-level outcomes alone cannot reveal, while handling the coupling between the two. This improves agent performance at lower cost than retraining.

entry.title: When Sample-Splitting Choices Matter in TMLE and AIPW: Cross-Fitting, Targeting, and Repetition

author.name: M. Ehsan Karim, Rainie Fu

entry.summary: This simulation study systematically compares eight TMLE and AIPW estimator variants differing in cross-fitting, bias-targeting, and split repetition, under a shared nuisance library and controlled settings. Results show that with simple libraries and good overlap all main variants cover equivalently, but in-sample propensity fitting causes severe undercoverage. The paper gives practical guidance on when sample-splitting choices matter for doubly robust causal inference.

entry.title: Think in Strategies, Act with Tools: Traceable Agentic Optimization for Combinatorial Problems

author.name: Zhongnian Li, Shi Xu, Peng Ying, Weikang Gong, Zhixiao Wang, Xinzheng Xu

entry.summary: TASA improves on Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO) by planning strategy per step over an optimization trajectory, decomposing the process into traceable strategy selections, and having the LLM construct problem-specific tools with a strategy-guided adaptation mechanism. This improves solution quality and makes the optimization process trackable.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient 3D Shape and Orientation Estimation of Road Users using Roadside RGB Camera and 3D Radar

author.name: Shiva Agrawal, Savankumar Bhanderi, Gordon Elger

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage, low-cost pipeline for 3D shape and orientation estimation of road users using roadside RGB cameras and 3D radar, motivated by the failure of end-to-end models under drastically varying roadside sensor installations. Rather than direct 3D bounding box estimation, the two-stage design improves robustness across heterogeneous mounting heights, tilts, and fields of view. This supports infrastructure-based intelligent transportation systems without location-specific datasets.

entry.title: Stein Variational Distributional Reinforcement Learning: Score-Guided Particles for Multivariate Return Distributions

author.name: Manuel Hau{\ss}mann, Melih Kandemir

entry.summary: SVDRL addresses multivariate distributional RL, where categorical critics scale exponentially in reward dimension and particle-based critics cannot resolve events rarer than 1/M, by having the critic output Stein particles transported along a learned score field of the distributional Bellman target. The score field is learned via bootstrapped denoising score matching. This enables richer joint return-distribution modeling for multi-objective decision making.

entry.title: Optimal Online Regret for Context-Lumpable Bandits

author.name: Chenyu Lu, Zihan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper designs an algorithm for stochastic contextual bandits with unknown context-lumpable structure achieving expected regret matching the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors, improving prior upper bounds by a factor of r. The approach uses dyadic accuracy levels, baseline policies, and cross-context elimination.

entry.title: STREGO: A Scalable Implementation of a Trust-Region Framework for Noisy Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Youssef Diouane, Issmail El Hallaoui, Meisseme Kadri, Amina Lamghari

entry.summary: STREGO extends the TREGO trust-region Bayesian optimization framework to noisy function evaluations with convergence guarantees, and provides a scalable implementation using bi-objective batch selection over posterior mean and uncertainty. It addresses the deterioration of trust-region BO in high dimensions.

entry.title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting: Continual Learning for Radar Waveform Classification

author.name: Mohamed Rabie, Chinthana J. Panagamuwa, Konstantinos G. Kyriakopoulos

entry.summary: This work presents the first large-scale continual learning benchmark for radar waveform recognition, evaluating 18 CL methods on a sequential ten-task problem spanning four public datasets and 54 waveforms. It provides practitioners with evidence on which continual learning methods and mechanisms work in this RF domain.

entry.title: Concept Representations in Vector Space: Quantifying Sharedness and Idiosyncrasy of Meaning

author.name: Simon Josef Durstewitz, Denis Buehler

entry.summary: This study develops a pre-registered measurement framework for interindividual variation in concept representations using sentence embeddings, encoding short personal definitions from 125 participants and analyzing them with crossed random effects models. It yields concept-level quantities capturing how much meaning is shared versus idiosyncratic across people. The work bridges psycholinguistics and representation learning with questions about whether people mean the same thing by a concept.

entry.title: Lexical Redefinition Reveals Context-Sensitive Instruction Following

author.name: Roksana Goworek, Haim Dubossarsky

entry.summary: Using lexical redefinition tasks across 870 word pairs, the study shows that explicit instructions specifying how a word should be interpreted are not applied as fixed rules: subsequent contextual evidence can preserve, weaken, or fully reverse the instruction. This reveals context-sensitive instruction following with implications for how models reconcile conflicting prompt evidence. It offers a clean diagnostic probe for instruction robustness.

entry.title: AD-GS: Anatomical Density-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Dental CBCT Reconstruction

author.name: Zonglin Li, Kexian Xie, Feiran Li, Chu Zhou, Yixing Huang, Ruiyang Chen, Zhanyu Ma, Heng Guo

entry.summary: AD-GS reformulates Gaussian densification in 3DGS-based CBCT reconstruction as an attenuation-aware MCMC sampling process, concentrating capacity in high-attenuation anatomical regions. This addresses instability and over-smoothing of gradient-driven densification under sparse-view acquisition, which matters for reducing radiation dose in dental imaging.

entry.title: DDVR-Net: Degradation-Aware Decoupling and Visibility-Guided Restoration for Historical Document Recognition

author.name: Jiu Sha, Yu Weng, Mengxiao Zhu

entry.summary: DDVR-Net decouples intrinsic glyph structures from physical corruption at the feature level and predicts local visibility to estimate character reliability for historical document recognition, gating a contextual language model so it does not over-correct visually clear characters. It targets ink erosion and structural damage in cultural heritage digitization.

entry.title: ANASSA: From High-Level Framework to Low-Level Architecture for Spatial Agentic AI

author.name: Constantinos Papantoniou, Brian Hilton

entry.summary: This paper refines the previously introduced ANASSA orchestration framework for governed spatial agentic AI into an implementation-facing low-level architecture using Design Science Research.
