It addresses orchestration, spatial validation, governance, provenance, and human decision authority for agents operating over geospatial data.

entry.title: Learning after Execution with Action-Specific Credit

author.name: Yufeng Tian, Jiahao Tang, Minghao Wu

entry.summary: This paper proposes using execution results as intermediate states that support an additional learning interaction rather than as terminal feedback only, introducing an action-specific credit scheme separating initial and corrective action credit. It validates the approach on image-to-TikZ over 945 held-out examples, showing strengthened learning.

entry.title: A Reference Architecture for Integrating Agentic AI into Enterprise Software: Responsibilities, Interactions, and Variability

author.name: Mingqin Yu, Fethi Rabhi, Liming Zhu, Qinghua Lu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a technology-neutral reference architecture for integrating agentic AI into enterprise software, synthesizing architectural capabilities from research and industry systems. It organizes concerns across orchestration, knowledge and memory, model access, tools, security, runtime infrastructure, and evaluation, describing responsibilities, interactions, and variability points.

entry.title: SocraticRepair: Planning-Guided Socratic Tutoring for Program Debugging and Misconception Repair

author.name: Mykhailo Kopytskyi, Jianhua Yang, Mir Seyedebrahimi

entry.summary: Introduces SocraticRepair, a planning-guided tutoring framework for program debugging that prevents premature solution reveals and keeps focus on the learner's current objective, instantiated by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on synthetic multi-turn dialogues. Evaluation uses independent metrics across curated programming datasets.

entry.title: Analyzing the Dynamics of WSBM-based Echo State Networks using InputDSA

author.name: Huy Mai, Robert Clarke

entry.summary: The paper introduces a reservoir computing framework replacing random Echo State Network topologies with biologically inspired modular structure via the Weighted Stochastic Block Model. Input Dynamical Similarity Analysis is used to disentangle how structural priors shape intrinsic recurrent dynamics versus responses to external inputs.

entry.title: Cross-Protocol Personality Assessment with LLMs: Aligning Behavioral Evidence with Human Ratings

author.name: Wei Shan, Tianyi Zhang, Yuan Zong, Wenming Zheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces CEPA, a framework for personality assessment from asynchronous video interviews that aligns behavioral representations across interview protocols with different question sets and question-trait mappings. This enables human-rated evidence from one protocol to inform assessment under another, addressing protocol heterogeneity in automated recruitment evaluation.

entry.title: Queue-Aware Token Communications: Bridging AI Representation and Wireless Service

author.name: Yuquan Xiao, Qinghe Du, Chaoyang Zhang, Wenchi Cheng, Jingqing Wang, Tao Chen, Jiangzhou Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Queue-Aware TokenCom, extending token communications for AI-native wireless networks by explicitly modeling token queueing dynamics arising from mismatch between token generation workload and time-varying wireless capacity. The paper presents an end-to-end architecture integrating AI representation transmission with queue-aware service management.

entry.title: Understanding Gene Expression-to-Image Learning: Spatial Structure and Information Fidelity

author.name: Xiaoqing Lian, Pei Liu, Jiahui Tan, Quan Zou, Chen Lin, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: This work analyzes Gene Expression-to-Image (GE2I) methods that arrange single-cell RNA sequencing values on pixel grids for CNN processing, holding networks and training fixed to isolate the mechanism. The authors identify a trade-off between spatial smoothness and gene-level fidelity: structured mappings produce smooth low-frequency patterns that aid early optimization, while multi-gene pixel assignment obscures expression variation.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformers for Hierarchical Intention Recognition from Multimodal Human Activity Sequences

author.name: Farnaz Soleimani (LISSI), Abdelghani Chibani (LISSI), Yacine Amirat (LISSI), Ghazaleh Khodabandelou (LISSI)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformer that integrates a Human Reasoning Graph into self-attention via learnable topological biases, plus a differentiable first-order-logic loss enforcing ontological consistency across hierarchy levels. It targets inferring hierarchical human intentions for proactive human-robot collaboration rather than flat action classification. The approach bridges multimodal perception and symbolic reasoning.

entry.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates

author.name: Muyao Kong, Zhihao Lin

entry.summary: Scenario-Actor is an interpretable decoding framework that selects sampling temperature from a structured geometric embedding of the communicative scenario, extracted from transformer hidden states. It replaces fixed or token-level heuristic temperature calibration with context-adaptive decoding.

entry.title: AphaVoice: Text-to-Speech Model for Aphasia Patient Simulation

author.name: Al Varrel Putra Kusuma, Fernando Bello, Joshua Brown

entry.summary: AphaVoice is a TTS framework that synthesizes realistic aphasic speech, including the clinical feature of dysfluency, for training simulations of medical professionals treating post-stroke aphasia. It outperforms state-of-the-art TTS systems on temporal metrics while preserving speaker identity.

entry.title: Integrating AIRL-Based Reward Estimation into a Control Method Using Fuzzy Inference and Policy Gradient

author.name: Seiji Ishihara

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fuzzy control method that combines policy gradient learning with reward estimation based on adversarial inverse reinforcement learning (AIRL). By learning rewards from data rather than requiring a hand-designed reward function, it addresses a key limitation of prior fuzzy inference-plus-RL control methods while retaining flexible rule configuration and automatic tuning of weights and membership functions.

entry.title: Siam-ALS: An Explainable Siamese Deep Learning Framework for Early ALS Detection Using EEG and Eye-Tracking Signals

author.name: Abdur Rahman, A. A. M. Muzahid, Istiak Ahmed, Dipto Biswas, Hua Han, Yujin Zhang, Ferdous Sohel

entry.summary: Siam-ALS is an explainable Siamese deep learning framework that fuses synchronized EEG and eye-tracking signals for early detection of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, using a convolutional EEG encoder and an MLP eye-tracking encoder to learn complementary neural and oculomotor patterns. The work addresses the heterogeneity and subjectivity of current clinical ALS diagnosis with objective, patient-generated physiological signals.

entry.title: An Explainable System for Offensive Content Detection in Nastaliq Urdu: Corpus Curation, Transformer Benchmarking, and Word-Level Attribution

author.name: Muhammad Shahid Iqbal Malik

entry.summary: This work releases a cleaned corpus of 7,604 Nastaliq-script Urdu Facebook comments for offensive content detection, benchmarks fine-tuned transformers on it, and adds word-level attribution for explainability. It addresses the near-total absence of moderation resources for Urdu beyond short Twitter text. The released dataset and interpretability analysis fill a real resource gap.

entry.title: SafeDSE: Joint Exploration of Safety Architecture Patterns, Mapping, and Scheduling for Dataflow Applications With Safety Arguments (Extended Version)

author.name: Fatemeh Bahrami, Seyed-Hosein Attarzadeh-Niaki

entry.summary: SafeDSE is a design space exploration framework for synchronous dataflow applications on embedded platforms that jointly decides safety architecture patterns (such as doer/checker pairs), placement under a fault model, static schedules, and platform configuration while pricing safety integrity level promotion. A declarative constraint model and guarded pattern activation support formal safety arguments.

entry.title: Integrating Feature Understandability into Feature Selection for Human-Centred Tabular Explanations

author.name: Nicola Rossberg, Bennett Kleinberg, Barry O'Sullivan, Luca Longo, Andrea Visentin

entry.summary: This study incorporates human-based feature understandability scores directly into feature selection for tabular models, so that natural language explanations cite features users can actually comprehend, rather than evaluating explainability only after generation. It builds on the prior Feature Understandability Scale.

entry.title: Governing Copyright Responsibly in the Era of Generative AI

author.name: D. Kochetkov

entry.summary: This study analyzes 40 legislative, judicial, and soft-law instruments from 2019-2026 governing how LLM training data relates to authors' rights, coding them against a Responsible Research and Innovation framework. It focuses on the EU and US with UK, China, and international bodies as comparators, examining how copyright governance protects authors who lack work-level transparency about training use. It matters because it offers a structured normative assessment of a live policy debate.

entry.title: ClearNav: Perception-Aligned Quadrotor Flight Using Differential-Physics

author.name: Aditya Azad, Arthur Huang, Guanrui Li

entry.summary: Identifies a single mechanism behind many sim-to-real quadrotor collisions: motion in directions the onboard camera does not observe, caused by misaligned heading and lateral excursion during avoidance. ClearNav adds reward terms constraining motion to the observed forward direction, improving collision avoidance in cluttered environments on hardware. A focused, interpretable fix for perception-aligned drone navigation.

entry.title: Enhanced Detective: A Dual-Stage Proactive Defense Against Internal Poisoning Attacks in Financial Fraud Detection Using Federated Learning

author.name: Maria-Ioana-Andrea Ivan, Orhan Ermis, Ruxandra F. Olimid

entry.summary: The paper proposes Enhanced Detective, a dual-stage proactive defense against poisoning attacks by malicious clients in federated learning for financial fraud detection. It aims to let institutions collaboratively improve fraud models while keeping transaction data local and mitigating degraded global models from poisoned updates.

entry.title: The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision

author.name: Amman Yusuf, Jiwoo Shin, Ruizhi Deng, Heitor Rodrigues Guimar\~{a}es, Nikita Dvornik, Mijung Park

entry.summary: SADDER improves the Safety-Aware Denoiser for text diffusion models by applying the SAD update rule gated by a per-token safety-guidance signal in embedding space, so tokens with high unsafe signals are preferentially revised. This improves safety and quality trade-offs during inference for text diffusion models without training.

entry.title: ShoeFit: A New Dataset and Dual-image-stream DiT Framework for Virtual Footwear Try-On

author.name: Yuhan Li, Zhiyu Jin, Yifan Tong, Wenxiang Shang, Benlei Cui, Xuanhong Chen, Hangcheng Zhu, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: ShoeFit addresses virtual footwear try-on with a new dataset and a dual-image-stream diffusion transformer framework that handles viewpoint misalignment, data scarcity, and background-induced color distortion. Unlike garment-focused virtual try-on, footwear requires 3D consistency and texture authenticity under diverse lighting. The work fills an underexplored niche in generative try-on.

entry.title: Sparse-TD-JEPA: Improving Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning With Sparse Latent Task Representations

author.name: Duaa Nakshbandi, Zhiyu An, Wan Du

entry.summary: The authors identify that dense task representations in successor-feature-based zero-shot RL diffuse the inferred reward signal across the state space, weakening policy learning. They add an l1 sparsity penalty to concentrate reward-predictive structure into a smaller latent subspace, improving zero-shot policy recovery.

entry.title: DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion

author.name: Peiyuan Li, Yongqi Huang, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Dongxiao He

entry.summary: DeKoR is a framework for fusing LLM knowledge with graph neural networks on text-attributed graphs, targeting the knowledge-space mismatch between the two paradigms. It decomposes and routes knowledge to reduce the substantial computation that existing GNN-LLM fusion methods incur for limited gains. The work aims to make graph foundation-model-style learning more efficient.

entry.title: Disentangling Marginal Capacity from Geometry in Optimal-Transport Label Transfer

author.name: Ali Khodabandeh Yalabadi, Azim Dehghani Amirabad, Artem Moskalev, Yun-Ching Chen, Mehdi Pirooznia, Scott Oloff, Rui Liao

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in optimal-transport label transfer where, under uniform source weighting, rare classes have insufficient transport capacity and displaced mass is absorbed by high-capacity rather than geometrically similar classes, producing confident but wrong predictions. It proposes disentangling marginal capacity constraints from embedding geometry to fix this. This is a useful diagnosis of a systematic bias in OT-based label transfer.

entry.title: HodgePhaseNet: Discrete Hodge Decomposition of Semantic Flows in Transformer Attention

author.name: Kiyotaka Kasubuchi, Kazuo Fukiya

entry.summary: HodgePhaseNet represents semantic transitions in transformer attention as an antisymmetric 1-cochain on a simplicial complex, enabling discrete Hodge decomposition of pairwise relations into globally consistent direction, local circulation, and persistent circulation components. It extends a line of phase-based transformer modifications (WavePhaseNet, QuantumPhaseNet, ModularPhaseNet). The work brings discrete differential geometry tools into transformer interpretability/architecture.

entry.title: Sensor-Aware Joint Data Fusion and State Estimation under Sparse Multi-rate Distribution Grid Sensing

author.name: Pooja Algikar, Stefano Fenu, Kumarsinh Jhala, Siby Plathottam

entry.summary: The paper proposes a heterogeneous latent graph ODE that jointly learns sensor data fusion and distribution-grid state estimation, replacing the standard two-stage pipeline of fusing pseudo-measurements then estimating. This handles sparse, multi-rate, non-synchronized heterogeneous sensors typical of modern grids with local storage and generation. A domain-specific applied ML contribution to power systems.

entry.title: Split Conformal Interval Length under Huber Contamination

author.name: Xiao Zhang, Bowen Zhang, Lie He

entry.summary: Derives finite-sample upper bounds on split conformal prediction interval length under Huber contamination at training and calibration stages, uniformly over contaminating distributions, plus a matching minimax lower bound. It also gives an exact worst-case characterization for calibration contamination.

entry.title: Interpretable Graph Partitioning for Spatial Prediction

author.name: Yuta Shikuri

entry.summary: The author formulates spatial prediction interpretability as a graph partitioning problem that builds a global surrogate approximating black-box predictions with simpler per-cluster representations. Connected subgraphs are selected to minimize within-cluster residuals on vertex-level predictions, extending spatial regionalization to model-based point-level predictions. The method targets settings where interpretability is essential alongside predictive flexibility.

entry.title: HyBRA-EEG: Hyperbolic Global-Local Brain-Region Aggregation for Self-Supervised EEG Representation Learning

author.name: Xin Liu, Feng Lu, Wei Li

entry.summary: HyBRA is a self-supervised EEG pretraining framework that maps heterogeneous electrode channels into a fixed brain-region token space using electrode coordinates, region priors, and hyperbolic distances, improving transferability across montages and datasets. A channel-evidence injection branch incorporates noisy channel information.

entry.title: Efficient Preconditioned Optimization Methods with Frequent Directions

author.name: Sifan Yang, Yuanyu Wan, Yibo Wang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors accelerate preconditioned adaptive optimization by integrating frequent directions matrix sketching into adaptive subgradient methods under a primal-dual framework, adding back discarded cumulative information to obtain tighter regret bounds than prior state of the art. A doubling trick further reduces computational time while maintaining guarantees.

entry.title: Making Tensor Decoupling More Robust and Less Parametric

author.name: Maxime Rochkoulets, Joppe De Jonghe, Mariya Ishteva

entry.summary: The authors identify two weaknesses in tensor decoupling methods, sensitivity to mismatched output or gradient magnitudes and manual tuning of spline internals, and propose lightweight fixes. These include a Jacobian-rescaling preprocessing step and replacing B-splines with penalized splines selected via generalized cross-validation.

entry.title: Merit: Making every modality earn its contribution in multimodal attention decoding

author.name: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson

entry.summary: Merit is a multimodal auditory attention decoding framework that combines brain signals with behavioral cues from smart glasses and earbuds while preventing behavioral modalities from dominating when they are unreliable, such as when a listener cannot move their head. This targets hearing aid applications for the over 1.5 billion people with hearing loss, amplifying only the attended talker in multi-speaker environments. The contribution is a principled way to make each modality earn its contribution to decoding.

entry.title: Persistence Positional Encoding: A Minimal Transformer Recipe for Persistence Diagrams

author.name: Eunwoo Heo, Ganghyun Kim, Jaejun Yoo

entry.summary: This paper proposes Persistence Positional Encoding, a minimal recipe for using persistence diagrams (topological descriptors) with Transformers by confining design changes to point representation via fixed random Fourier features, leaving the Transformer backbone unchanged. The authors note prior topology-Transformer methods are hard to compare due to inconsistent inputs, splits, and model selection, and provide a standardized approach. This simplifies and standardizes topological deep learning with attention models.

entry.title: From Spectral Saliency to Finite Deletion: Evaluating Selective Language Model Edits

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Joyanta Jyoti Mondal

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why first-order spectral saliency fails to predict outcomes of selective component deletion in language models, since deletion is a finite rather than infinitesimal intervention. It decomposes prediction error into derivative transfer and nonlinear response terms and establishes conditions under which interval screening retains all feasible candidates.

entry.title: AERR-Nav: Adaptive Exploration-Recovery-Reminiscing Strategy for Zero-Shot Object Navigation

author.name: Jingzhi Huang, Junkai Huang, Haoyang Yang, Haoang Li, Yi Wang

entry.summary: AERR-Nav is a zero-shot object navigation framework for multi-floor environments that dynamically adjusts between exploration, recovery, and reminiscing states, addressing failure modes like getting stuck at intersections or failing to locate stair entrances. It builds on MLLM-based decision-making and spatial memory improvements from recent ZSON methods.

entry.title: Deterministic denoising of long-duration gravitational-wave signal candidates with $\alpha$-(de)blending

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Figura, Micha{\l} Bejger

entry.summary: The authors apply a deterministic diffusion-style generative model implemented as a U-Net to denoise candidate signals from continuous gravitational-wave searches for rotating neutron stars. They post-process F-statistic search outputs with iterative alpha-(de)blending and validate against simulated injected signals using structural similarity metrics.

entry.title: Strong Gaussian Approximation of Constant-Learning-Rate SGD: Bias and Trajectory Inference

author.name: Joseph Keslin, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: The paper derives strong Gaussian (KMT-type) approximations for constant-learning-rate SGD under heavy-tailed noise, enabling whole-trajectory-level, finite-sample simultaneous inference rather than inference on individual iterates. These quenched approximations imply functional central limit theorems and allow inference on SGD bias and trajectories. This provides sharper statistical tools for understanding optimization dynamics of ML training.

entry.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses

author.name: Xuexing Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces DisCo algebra, a compositional mathematical framework for joint probability distributions built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) over probability measures on [0,1]^n. It uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic one-dimensional summaries, showing that combination-then-disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, while disintegration-then-combination is lossy, formally characterizing the asymmetry between the two operations. This provides theoretical foundations relevant to how generative and inference processes compose, with potential implications for probabilistic modeling and causal reasoning.

entry.title: Deep Neural Mixed Models for Nonlinear Longitudinal Prediction with Subject-Specific Heterogeneity

author.name: Mahmud Hasan, Niloofar Ramezani, Hrishikesh Chakraborty

entry.summary: Proposes DGNMM, a deep generalization of generalized linear mixed models that learns nonlinear population-level effects with a neural network while training regularized subject-specific random effects for individual heterogeneity. Applied to longitudinal health data, it enables studying when added nonlinear representational capacity improves prediction.

entry.title: CLNO: Conservative Local Neural Operator for Compressible Flow Prediction

author.name: Buxuan Wang, Rongzu Li, Qingsong Zou

entry.summary: CLNO is a neural operator for autoregressive compressible flow prediction that encodes flows into subdomain-integrated conservative states and predicts interface fluxes for finite-volume updates enforcing discrete conservation, with a convolutional reconstruction network recovering fine-scale structure. The design exploits locality and translation invariance of local neural operators.

entry.title: Learning Reachability-Based Safety Representations for Real-Time Robot Navigation in Unknown and Dynamic Environments

author.name: Bojan Deraji\'c

entry.summary: This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on Hamilton-Jacobi reachability solutions to provide optimization-based robot controllers with real-time safety information in unknown, dynamic environments. The learned value function captures when collision avoidance is feasible given speed and obstacle motion, beyond geometric collision checking.

entry.title: Spectral Costs of Multinomial and Residual Resampling in High-Dimensional Particle Ensembles: A Free-Probability Analysis

author.name: Deming Song, Chi Kin Lam

entry.summary: Using free-probability tools in the regime d/N to a constant, the authors analyze how a single resampling step changes the spectrum of the particle second-moment matrix in particle filters, proving convex-order dominance and characterizing limiting count laws for multinomial and residual resampling. This gives theoretical insight into when resampling helps or distorts ensemble diversity.

entry.title: Amortised adaptive importance sampling

author.name: Arran Carter, V\'ictor Elvira, Esmeralda S. Whitammer

entry.summary: The authors build an amortized sampler on top of adaptive importance sampling, training learnable proposal components within the hierarchical importance sampling framework so that, once trained, high-quality samples can be drawn with much less computation at test time. This targets the high cost of training-free Monte Carlo methods.

entry.title: Time Window Optimization for Motor Imagery Classification via Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Huan Luo, Na Lu, Xiaopeng Wang, Ziyang Shang

entry.summary: Proposes TSE-RL, a constrained Markov decision process framework that embeds prior knowledge of motor imagery event structure (onset, sustain, offset) to adaptively optimize EEG decoding windows for brain-computer interfaces. It addresses fragmentation and physiological implausibility in prior window-selection methods.

entry.title: Representation Geometry and Inductive Biases in Quantum Classifiers across Classical Visual Benchmarks

author.name: Yu Yamaoka, Weng Ian Chan, Kosuke Mitarai

entry.summary: The paper empirically studies whether theoretical quantum advantages matter for realistic classical data by analyzing representation geometry and inductive biases of quantum classifiers on standard image benchmarks, examining how unitary and entanglement structure shapes learning behavior. This is a careful probe of the gap between QML theory and real-world performance. Its findings help calibrate expectations for quantum machine learning on natural data.

entry.title: Reliable Scale-Free Bandits via Empirical Likelihood

author.name: Pratham Gupta, Alhad Sethi, Shubhada Agrawal

entry.summary: The authors introduce EL-F, an anytime empirical-likelihood extension of the g-Forcing bandit policy that handles rewards without known scale or tail parameters. They characterize performance at three levels, preserving g-Forcing asymptotics for pseudo-regret while adding stronger finite-time guarantees.

entry.title: Probing the Geometry of Color Representations in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Pablo Loyola, Edison Marrese-Taylor, Andr\'es Hoyos-Idrobo

entry.summary: This interpretability study decomposes color representations in multilingual language models into perceptual alignment (to CIE-LAB) and cross-lingual symmetry axes, finding perceptual grounding peaks in intermediate layers then collapses toward outputs while language-specific structure grows with depth. Geometric properties predict task performance, with peak perceptual alignment coinciding with 96.7% color-classification accuracy.

entry.title: Understanding Circulant Permutation to Extend the CMinHash Estimator

author.name: Keegan Kang, Avery Hood, Benedict H. W. Wong

entry.summary: This paper develops a new analytical approach for circulant-permutation MinHash schemes, deriving explicit approximate variance expressions that can be extended beyond the original CMinHash estimator. The authors apply it to the Minner estimator and validate the theory against empirical MSE.

entry.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion

author.name: Chih-Hai Su, Tsung-Wei Ke, Yu-Lun Liu

entry.summary: Cepheid addresses the failure of learned residual priors for sparse-to-dense mesh motion completion when applied across geometry families, by learning a dimensionless prior and estimating physical amplitude from observables. The unified model beats harmonic extension baselines across all evaluated families.

entry.title: Agent-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction

author.name: Zhuangzhuang Pan, Yan Xia, Chee Seng Chan

entry.summary: The authors study an agent framework for emotion-cause pair extraction where a student agent selectively queries expert judgments for borderline predictions near its validation-selected F1 decision boundary, revising only queried outputs. At a nominal 10% query rate, selective fusion improves prediction quality, and the paper analyzes how delegation granularity, query selection, and response integration matter. It frames ECPE as an active information-acquisition problem.

entry.title: What Is the "Self" of a Large Language Model?

author.name: Yuchen Li, Zongqi Fan, Xintong Li, Ken-tye Yong, Nguyen H. Tran

entry.summary: This paper proposes a relational account of a functional self in LLMs: an actor-centered organization of information that distinguishes the model's recorded actions from externally supplied material, represented by a family of layer-specific source-binding components rather than a single static vector. Preliminary experiments on a 27B model show that assistant-versus-external displacement transfers strongly across message bodies. It contributes an interpretability framing relevant to self/other discrimination in models.

entry.title: Prompt or Policy? Optimizing Physician Slate Presentations with LLM User Simulators

author.name: Andrei Niculae, Adrian Cosma, Emilian Radoi

entry.summary: The paper formulates slate presentation optimization for physician recommendation: generating short case-specific summaries of ranked doctors to help patients compare, grounded in profile data. It uses persona-conditioned LLM simulators of patient choices in an offline framework and compares prompt-based versus policy-based optimization. This connects recommender systems with LLM simulation to avoid costly online experimentation.

entry.title: KhyontekAI at CheckThat! 2026: Multilingual Dense Retrieval and Cross-Encoder Reranking for Scientific Web Claims

author.name: Bhargab Jyoti Bhuyan, Pritam Deka

entry.summary: This system paper describes a two-stage multilingual retrieval framework combining fine-tuned dense retrievers with cross-encoder reranking for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Task 1 on retrieving scientific sources for social-media claims. It evaluates multiple transformer-based dense retrieval architectures. It is a competent shared-task entry applying established techniques to a socially relevant retrieval problem.

entry.title: DSR-Net: Learning Dynamic Skeletal Relations for 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Fan Li, Jian Xiang, LinLin Xue, Yuwei Gao

entry.summary: DSR-Net introduces a dynamic skeletal relation module that learns adaptive inter-joint dependencies beyond fixed GCN topologies, plus a hierarchical relation-aware fusion strategy for 3D human pose estimation. This improves adaptability to diverse motion patterns compared with predefined skeletal graphs or purely attention-based methods.

entry.title: [Re] Boosting the Visual Interpretability of CLIP via Adversarial Fine-Tuning

author.name: Anton Nuzhdin, Andrei Gruzitski, Bal\'azs Egyed, Aleksandr Raudvee

entry.summary: A reproducibility study of an ICLR 2025 paper on unsupervised adversarial fine-tuning for improving CLIP visual interpretability, testing claims about saliency quality, concept alignment, and zero-shot trade-offs. The authors also propose a saliency-guided regularization extension using an Energy Pointing Game loss to directly supervise spatial alignment of saliency maps.

entry.title: Region Aware Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks for Image Segmentation

author.name: Jack Roberts, Praneeth Tummala, Kavi Sarna, Jeova Farias Sales Rocha Neto

entry.summary: The paper generalizes Squeeze-and-Excitation modules for segmentation by replacing global average pooling with spatially guided pooling, proposing four variants: tiled regions, SLIC superpixels, semantic-map regions from a frozen network, and end-to-end learned soft region assignments. This enables region-aware channel recalibration that preserves spatial structure for dense prediction.

entry.title: Lesion-Aware Attention for Mammography Segmentation with Heterogeneous Supervision

author.name: Di Dai, Bo Liu, Liwei Wang

entry.summary: This work studies open-vocabulary mammographic lesion segmentation under mixed supervision, where pixel masks exist for base lesion types and only image-level labels for a broader set. It introduces lesion-aware attention to generalize to rare or weakly annotated categories despite costly dense annotations.

entry.title: Reference-Efficient Multimodal Bitstream-Corrupted Video Recovery via Depth-Conditioned Adaptation

author.name: Tianyi Liu, Jiaojiao Wang, Ye Lu, Kejun Wu, Chengtao Cai, Zhengguo Li, Chia-Wen Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for recovering visually faithful video from corrupted bitstreams using RGB and pre-transmitted depth information, selecting a single non-local RGB reference per recovery window to limit receiver computation and memory. Depth-conditioned adaptation provides geometric guidance when appearance data is unreliable after decoding.

entry.title: Building age estimation based on widely available multi-source1 geospatial data

author.name: Jialu Sui, Hongsheng Zhang, Rui Liu, Jing Ling, Ruisheng Wang, Hao Wu, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes the first deep-learning framework for building age estimation using widely available geospatial inputs like satellite imagery and digital surface models rather than harder-to-obtain street-view or material data. It also models the inherent temporal ordering among age categories, which prior local-texture-based approaches ignored.

entry.title: From Volpiano to Pixels: 30,000 Lines of OMR Ground Truth for Medieval Chant

author.name: Robert Klugseder

entry.summary: This resource paper creates 30,567 image-target pairs (nearly 2 million tokens) for optical music recognition of medieval chant by leveraging existing Volpiano transcriptions from the Cantus Database, with pipelines for staff location, clef inference, and six detector families for varied layouts. It addresses the lack of training data across notational families, though error definitions in sampling reviews are inconsistent.

entry.title: FrameLite: Decision-Oriented Aesthetic Cropping with a Compact Vision-Language Model

author.name: Jianze Li, Kai Liu, Ziqing Zhang, Weihang Zhang, Yong Guo, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: FrameLite builds a compact aesthetic image-cropping model on Qwen3.5-0.8B, using three-stage training (spatial/composition training, Quality-Guided Online Supervision over self-generated candidates, and Greedy-Referenced Optimization) based on the observation that a small model produces better crops than its first greedy answer suggests. It aims to bring VLM semantic knowledge to lightweight photography assistance.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Semi-Supervised Framework with Supervised Contrastive Learning for Sugarcane Leaf Disease Detection

author.name: Shalini Dangi, Divya Teja, Omkar Kabde, Shahid Shafi Dar, Nagendra Kumar

entry.summary: U-SSDNet is an uncertainty-aware Mean-Teacher semi-supervised network with supervised contrastive learning for sugarcane leaf disease detection, addressing intra-class variation, inter-class similarity, and label noise under scarce annotations. It targets practical agricultural deployment where labeled data is expensive.

entry.title: Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1)

author.name: Thierry Bouwmans, Anastasia Zakharova, Belmar Garcia, Marwa Chendeb El Rai, Meghna Kapoor, Badri Narayan Subudhi

entry.summary: Part 1 of a comprehensive two-part survey of infrared small target detection, covering model-based low-rank and sparse decomposition methods alongside the historical development of the field for civilian and military surveillance. It categorizes traditional unsupervised approaches that prior surveys treated in fragments. A reference resource rather than original research.

entry.title: Unsupervised and Supervised Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 2)

author.name: Thierry Bouwmans, Anastasia Zakharova, Belmar Garcia, Marwa Chendeb El Rai, Meghna Kapoor, Badri Narayan Subudhi

entry.summary: Part 2 of the infrared small target detection survey, covering deep learning approaches including CNNs, GANs, Transformers, mixture-of-experts, and graph/hypergraph networks. It complements Part 1 by documenting how supervised models overtook traditional unsupervised and low-rank decomposition methods. Completes a full-field reference.

entry.title: CryoTracer: A Synthetic-to-Real System for Filament Instance Tracing in Cryo-EM

author.name: Rados{\l}aw Kuczba\'nski, Wojciech Koz{\l}owski, Mateusz Grzesiuk, Konrad Karanowski, Lukas Frey, Andrzej Rzepiela, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba

entry.summary: CryoTracer reformulates cryo-EM particle picking for filamentous specimens as direct filament instance tracing rather than bounding-box detection with post-hoc linking, using a synthetic-to-real training pipeline. Preserving filament identity across gaps and crossings is particularly valuable for polymorphic specimens where instance-level association matters.

entry.title: Dog-Breed Text-to-image Flow Matching from Pretraining to Fine-Tuning on 4 Consumer GPUs

author.name: Reyhaneh Esmailizadeh, Xingjian Leng, Zhanhao Liang, Liang Zheng

entry.summary: The authors present MiniDog, a framework showing that small text-to-image flow-matching diffusion transformers can be pretrained in about an hour and fine-tuned in 15 minutes on four consumer GPUs. Using curated small datasets, feature caching, and a compact 22M-parameter architecture, the work democratizes hands-on training of generative image models. Its significance lies in lowering the barrier to entry for generative modeling research and education.

entry.title: Multi-modal Representation Fusion for Long-term Microsurgical Anastomosis Trajectory Anticipation

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Yating Luo, Yunfei Luan, Xinyao Zhou, Yuyang Zhuge, Yao Guo, Guang-Zhong Yang

entry.summary: This work proposes a cross-modal feature fusion framework for anticipating long-horizon instrument trajectories in microsurgical anastomosis, incorporating semantic and motion information beyond video frames and historical trajectories. Accurate anticipation supports surgical scene understanding, intraoperative planning, and robotic assistance in an extremely delicate procedure. It advances surgical robotics perception where existing methods underuse multimodal cues.

entry.title: Shared-Control Teleoperation of Omnidirectional Aerial Robots for Continuous Valve Rotation

author.name: Jinjie Li, Yicheng Chen, Haokun Liu, Moju Zhao

entry.summary: This paper extends an aerial teleoperation system for omnidirectional robots to enable continuous valve rotation despite the limited range of human forearm motion, initiating continuous rotation when the forearm angle exceeds a threshold. This addresses an industrial limitation of a previously proposed human-in-the-loop 6-DoF aerial manipulation system.

entry.title: B-Human '26 - Scalable Team Play up to 11 vs. 11

author.name: Arne Hasselbring, Tim Laue, Thomas R\"ofer, Philip Reichenberg

entry.summary: Team B-Human describes the system that won multiple competitions in the 2026 Middle Division of the new Humanoid Soccer League, including demo matches with eleven humanoid robots per side. The paper covers the transition from Standard Platform League robots, the behavior architecture enabling scalable team play, and lessons drawn from 11-player RoboCup leagues. It documents state-of-the-art multi-robot team coordination on humanoid hardware.

entry.title: SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X

author.name: Zide Fan, Jiahui Yuan, Kaixin Zhang, Junhao Fan, Xiaohe Li, Yiru Wang

entry.summary: SIGN-MAPPO tackles cooperative driving at mixed-traffic unsignalized intersections under imperfect V2X communication, having each CAV reconstruct a receiver-specific traffic graph from ego and peer state records and feeding a shared graph-attention policy that generates Stop/Go intentions. It addresses incompatibility of independently generated crossing decisions and uncommunicated human-driver intentions.

entry.title: Jacobian State Augmented Viable Kinematic Safety Filter

author.name: Siddharth Singh, Joshua Vaughan

entry.summary: The authors introduce a Jacobian-based kinematic safety filter that augments the state with task-space velocity and filters task-space acceleration to preserve feasibility of low-level filters. It aims to combine predictive safety filter benefits with viability guarantees at lower computational cost than viability kernel approximation. This contributes to certifiably safe robot control.

entry.title: Design and Analysis of a Nonlinear Parallel Mechanism Coupling for Dynamic Humanoid Legs

author.name: Rohit Kumar, Heiner Peters, Felix Wiebe, Franek Stark, Janne Janzen, Dennis Mronga, Shubham Vyas, Frank Kirchner

entry.summary: This hardware paper presents a series-parallel humanoid leg design with knee and ankle parallel mechanisms coupled nonlinearly, with all actuators placed near the hip to reduce distal inertia. As the knee flexes, the passive coupling assists ankle dorsiflexion for foot clearance and assists plantarflexion for push-off on extension, redistributing ankle loads through the knee transmission. The authors derive the coupling's nonlinear kinematics and analyze its force transmission properties.

entry.title: CALM: Decentralized Control of Cooperative Aerial Manipulation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiaxi Huo, Petre Ricioppo, Fausto Francesco Lizzio

entry.summary: CALM is a decentralized controller for UAV teams cooperatively carrying a basket payload while tracking a moving ground robot, combining a parameter-shared MAPPO policy with extended state observers, basket-mass estimation, goal estimation, and anticipatory formation-yaw feedforward. The system handles wind, payload motion, and noisy goal broadcasts in coupled aerial manipulation.

entry.title: Aerodynamic Promptness of Tilting-Propeller Multirotors

author.name: Antonio Franchi

entry.summary: This paper develops a geometric control theory for multirotors with tilting propellers, defining aerodynamic promptness via a Riemannian metric on the actuator manifold that compares propeller accelerations and tilt-mechanism rates. The actuator map covers fixed and mechanically coupled tilting propellers, capturing signed-quadratic thrust laws and configuration-dependent thrust directions. The theory connects actuator dynamics to musical-instrument-like responsiveness notions for aerial vehicles.

entry.title: CLASSO: a practical primal path-following algorithm for the constrained LASSO

author.name: Michael Hobson, Luke Butcher, Lindley Lentati

entry.summary: CLASSO is a path-following algorithm for the LASSO under general linear equality and inequality constraints, computing local solution-path derivatives via a quadratic program on an augmented active set. The authors prove the primal path is piecewise affine with finitely many kinks and that the construction recovers the classical LASSO-modified LARS direction when constraints vanish. This provides the first practical complete path algorithm for the constrained LASSO.

entry.title: How Molmo 2’s open release helped an MIT researcher rethink fish tracking

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Ai2 blog post describes how the open availability of the Molmo 2 model enabled MIT researcher Kai Van Brunt to build Molmo2Fish, an experimental system that tracks salmon in sonar footage and corrects tracking errors through natural-language instructions. It illustrates how openly released multimodal models can be adapted for scientific and ecological monitoring tasks.

entry.title: A Gated Catchment Hydrology Model (GCHM) for Physically-Interpretable Rainfall-Evapotranspiration-Runoff Simulation Across Diverse Hydroclimatic Regimes

author.name: M Jawad, HV Gupta, MA Farmani, A Behrangi, GY Niu

entry.summary: GCHM is a mass-conserving gated architecture built on the Mass-Conserving Perceptron, with five storage states and constrained gates governing precipitation partitioning through baseflow. It is evaluated across 50 CAMELS catchments spanning snowmelt-dominated to arid regimes, aiming for ML-level accuracy with physical interpretability.

entry.title: Exact power indices for plurality-voting ensembles

author.name: Ilie Sarpe, Theofanis Georgakopoulos, Aristides Gionis

entry.summary: This paper addresses attribution of each base classifier's impact in plurality-voting ensembles using cooperative game theory, deriving exact Banzhaf and Shapley power indices for games modeling plurality voting with random tie-breaking in binary and multiclass settings. Because a single classifier's impact depends on interactions with all other votes, exact indices require novel game formulations and computation methods. This provides principled explainability for ensemble predictions.

entry.title: Barycentric Guidance: Turning Foundation Image Editors into Continuous Affective Controllers

author.name: Harvey Mannering, Zhiwu Huang, Adam Pr\"ugel-Bennett

entry.summary: Barycentric Guidance is a training-free framework that converts pretrained foundation image editors into continuous controllers over the valence-arousal emotion space, addressing the poor calibration of prompt interpolation due to nonlinear emotion representations in text encoders. This extends affective editing beyond training-restricted VA regions and across datasets and domains.

entry.title: CB-Agent: Concept-Based In-Context Learning for Sequential Action Selection

author.name: Qingyue Zhang, Huaze Tang, Minyu Zhang, Yuxiang Yan, Wenbo Ding, Shao-Lun Huang

entry.summary: CB-Agent extends concept-based in-context learning to sequential action selection for interactive agents, extracting environment-action decisions from expert trajectories to directly supervise a reusable scoring rule. This avoids the prompt-space costs of full trajectories and the translation burden of natural-language summaries.

entry.title: GREAT-ESDD: Graph Edge Attention Network for Effectively Steered Delivery Decisions

author.name: Attila Lischka (Jeff), Ze Zhou (Jeff), Xuegang (Jeff), Ban, Bal\'azs Kulcs\'ar

entry.summary: The paper presents a dynamic pricing-and-routing framework for same-day delivery with home and out-of-home options, built around a neural solver for the capacitated vehicle routing problem using a Graph Edge Attention Network. The solver handles varying instance sizes and reoptimization of partially executed routes, combining competitive solution quality with fast inference.

entry.title: Data Portability Revisited: Toward the Human-Centric, AI-Driven Data Ecosystems of Tomorrow

author.name: Mark Fenwick, Michael Fertik, Paulius Jurcys, Timo Minssen

entry.summary: A legal and policy analysis arguing that current US and EU conceptions of data portability serve data controllers and service providers more than individuals. The authors advocate a human-centric paradigm in which data is treated as fundamental to personal identity in AI-driven data ecosystems.

entry.title: Constructed regional photovoltaic generation fields improve ultra-short-term distributed solar forecasting

author.name: Dayin Chen, Xiaodan Shi, Xin Xu, Zhongyue Su, Shibo Zhu, Dongxiao Zhang, Yuntian Chen, Jinyue Yan

entry.summary: SatPV-Field reformulates fleet-level solar forecasting from discrete station time series to predicting spatially structured regional photovoltaic generation fields, treating distributed measurements as image-like data. This regional-to-local approach improves ultra-short-term forecasting of dense distributed PV systems compared with station-wise modeling.

entry.title: Reliable Text-to-SQL in Resource-Constrained Settings with Small LLMs via Iterative Retry Workflows

author.name: Bilel Abderrahmane Benziane, Xavier Schepler

entry.summary: Evaluates 1B-8B parameter open-source LLMs on Spider under controlled inference budgets, finding SQL-specialized models consistently more reliable than general-purpose ones and that iterative retry workflows reduce performance variability across prompt formulations.

entry.title: QORH: Learning Query-Specific Ordered Rule Hypergraphs for Inductive Knowledge Graph Link Prediction

author.name: Naixing Xu

entry.summary: QORH encodes rule heads and ordered rule bodies as hyperedges in query-specific hypergraphs for inductive knowledge graph link prediction, jointly modeling dependencies among multiple relations. It uses statistical evidence like rule confidence and coverage for learnable rule selection and enhances relation representations. This addresses limits of pairwise relation-graph methods in preserving compositional and ordering semantics of path rules.

entry.title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration

author.name: Yevgeny Rakita, Paul Todd, James R. Neilson, Simon J. L. Billinge

entry.summary: The paper explores reaction graphs for materials synthesis, where events comprise reaction steps and outputs, aiming to let learning algorithms encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways including unpublished failures. It targets kinetically stabilized, technologically useful materials whose synthesis currently depends on trial and error. The work discusses potential and structure with a demonstration rather than a full system.

entry.title: Subgraph-Aware Training of Language Models for Knowledge Graph Completion Using Structure-Aware Contrastive Learning

author.name: Youmin Ko, Hyemin Yang, Taeuk Kim, Hyunjoon Kim

entry.summary: SATKGC improves PLM-based knowledge graph completion by incorporating graph topology through subgraph-aware mini-batching for hard negative sampling and a contrastive learning objective emphasizing harder in-batch negatives. This addresses the common neglect of long-tailed entity distributions and topological structure in text-only KGC methods.

entry.title: LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising

author.name: Wen Zhang, Xiao Bai, Hsiang-wei Chao, Mengfan Zhu, Tong Zhao, Mingxuan Ju, Xiaodong Liu, Congfei Zhang, Yunzhi Zhou, Yajun Wang, Jinchao Li, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: This industry paper proposes an offline user-product relevance metric for evaluating dynamic product advertising retrieval systems, compressing engagement history into semantic-ID-grouped intent representatives and aggregating per-intent LLM relevance judgments into a user-level score. It aims to replace sparse engagement metrics and costly online tests.

entry.title: Depth-progressive 3D seismic velocity model building via 2D generative diffusion models

author.name: Shijun Cheng, Randy Harsuko, Mohammad H. Taufik, Tariq Alkhalifah

entry.summary: This paper introduces a depth-progressive framework for 3D seismic velocity model building using 2D generative diffusion models, mapping the depth dimension to channels of a 2D U-Net and synthesizing overlapping depth patches sequentially from shallow to deep, conditioned on shallower predictions and geophysical constraints. This sidesteps the prohibitive memory and training costs of full 3D formulations.

entry.title: WisdomNet: trustable machine learning toward error-free classification

author.name: Truong X. Tran, Ramazan S. Aygun

entry.summary: Proposes trustable learning, where classifiers either output a confident true prediction or explicitly reject/defer to a human expert when misclassification risk is high, aiming toward error-free classification. The methodology is developed for artificial neural networks and applied to practical classification settings.

entry.title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Liang Yuan, Maryam Khanian Najafabadi, Mashud Rana, Varvara Vetrova

entry.summary: This systematic literature review consolidates findings on security risks in LLM-assisted coding, concluding that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training-data bias, that models themselves are attackable, and that current evaluation suffers from contamination and weak security metrics. It argues human oversight remains essential and calls for security-aware architectures, stronger benchmarks, and better human-AI collaboration frameworks.

entry.title: RespFocus: Learning Temporal Evidence for Weakly Supervised Respiratory Sound Classification

author.name: Yi Tian, Xiaohuan Chen, Yufei tang, Xinyu Lin, Hongliang Li, Chengbin Hou, Degen Huang, Rongshan Yu

entry.summary: RespFocus is a weakly supervised multiple-instance-learning framework that learns inspectable temporal evidence from cycle-level labels for respiratory sound classification, improving interpretability of crackle and wheeze detection in noisy clinical recordings. The authors also release PedResp2026, a multicenter pediatric respiratory sound cohort with adjudicated cycle-level annotations collected in routine clinical environments.

entry.title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN

author.name: Anoop Mishra, Joshua Moore, Aly Sabri Abdalla, Vuk Marojevic

entry.summary: AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with two LoRA stages over a curated corpus of 69 O-RAN and 3GPP standards documents, selectively augmented with RAG, for automated security triage of Open RAN testing. The model operates from investigator-style questions and scenario metadata without raw packet evidence. It is validated on a purpose-built benchmark simulating an automated analyst.

entry.title: Deleting Code Without Losing Knowledge: Regenerative Software for Python Libraries

author.name: Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that in the era of agent-rewritten software, code should not be the sole source of truth; instead, machine-readable records capture a module's architecture, intent, decisions, contract, evaluations, and consumers in regeneration bundles from which programs can be deleted and rebuilt. The open-source spotregen package implements this for Python libraries, building on Fowler's seven primitives for regenerative software. It reframes software maintenance practices for the AI-agent era.

entry.title: Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Han Bao, Shinsaku Sakaue, Kazuki Watanabe

entry.summary: The paper generalizes query selection in MDP safety verification with a unified convex-analytic framework that scores violation directions via support-function gaps normalized by an error unit. It shows the maximal score equals the smallest safe-region enlargement needed, providing a principled family of query selection rules extending prior Euclidean-violation approaches.

entry.title: Tanawpamana: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Philippine Cultural Heritage Sites

author.name: Ivan Yuri De Leon, Hiroki Ouchi, Sakriani Sakti

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Tanawpamana dataset and benchmark of 4,046 tasks evaluating vision-language models on recognition and knowledge of Philippine heritage sites, built from the national cultural registry. Evaluating seven VLMs shows they struggle more with fine-grained discrimination among similar sites than coarse recognition, highlighting gaps in culturally specific knowledge.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Quantum Amplitude Embedding with Data Re-Uploading

author.name: Hyojun Ahn, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: This tutorial explains what data re-uploading adds to variational quantum models using amplitude embedding, showing in a unified notation for sequential and parallel re-uploading that each upload raises the reachable polynomial degree of the model output. It quantifies the gain per costly state-preparation upload.

entry.title: How Reliable Are Large Language Models for Soil Organic Carbon Assessment? An Australian Benchmark

author.name: Yingxuan Cheng, Tong Li, Yayong Li, Yuchuan Fan, You-Gan Wang, Jinran Wu, Scott Chapman, Geoffrey J. McLachlan

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks seven general-purpose LLM configurations on three soil organic carbon tasks against measured Australian records, assessing validity, dispersion across repeated calls, and API cost. Additional measured soil attributes reduce concentration error by 13-62%, providing a grounded picture of where LLMs do and do not help in this agricultural domain.

entry.title: ST-GRU PredRNN-V2: A GRU-Based Reformulation of PredRNN-V2 for Video Prediction

author.name: Augusta van Haren, Hanna Hoogen, Luca Pattavina, Quincy Rommen

entry.summary: This work develops a spatiotemporal GRU (ST-GRU) unit as a simpler alternative to the ST-LSTM in PredRNN-V2, replacing three gates per memory state with two GRU-style gates and merging temporal memory states. The goal is to test whether simpler gating suffices for video prediction's spatiotemporal dependencies. It is a focused architectural simplification study in recurrent video prediction.

entry.title: Class-Conditional Conformal Prediction for Signal Temporal Logic Inference with Many Classes

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Danyang Li, Matthew Cleaveland, Roberto Tron, Mingyu Cai

entry.summary: The authors introduce a two-stage conformal prediction procedure for Signal Temporal Logic inference in multiclass time-series classification, quantifying formula satisfaction and codeword consistency with new metrics. A margin-based objective learns discriminative formulas, then thresholds are refined toward small positive robustness targets.

entry.title: From Transfer Probes to Expert Grouping: Evidence from LoRA Post-Training

author.name: Xueyang Wu

entry.summary: A single-author study asking whether transfer probes (train on one source, measure paired changes on all others) can discover which business lines should share LoRA experts when no taxonomy exists. Using seven public sources with a known label tree as a reference, it compares probe-derived groupings against alternatives under fixed per-source and per-expert budgets.

entry.title: From Rainfall to Road-Network Functionality: Transferable Graph Forecasting for Flood-Disrupted Transportation Networks

author.name: Junyan Wang, Naiyu Wang

entry.summary: G-R2R reframes rainfall-induced road-network disruption as a region-conditioned, topology-flexible graph forecasting problem, combining ego-centered subgraph sampling, terrain-conditioned representations, and dual-level static encoding. It aims to transfer flood-impact prediction to unseen transportation networks without local calibration or retraining.

entry.title: Ascent Conditions for Length-Normalized Single-Rollout Policy Updates

author.name: Levin David Schwab

entry.summary: This theory paper derives exact ascent thresholds for length-normalized single-rollout policy gradient updates in a finite trajectory model, showing a binary-reward example where the expected update direction actually decreases task success. It also gives an unbiased third-order U-statistic estimator of first-order return change and characterizes when natural-gradient ascent holds or fails.

entry.title: Linear-Time Non-Local Codec Placement for Machine Learning Model Compression

author.name: Matteo Spallanzani

entry.summary: The paper presents a linear-time graph algorithm for placing codec (encode/decode) operators in a computational graph so compressed operand representations remain compatible with target hardware. It introduces an absolute dominator notion via graph coloring to find natural observation points for traffic. This addresses the practical problem that naive codec placement can erase the traffic savings compression is meant to provide.

entry.title: How Shared Representations Become Specialized: Formation, Maintenance, and Latent Susceptibility

author.name: Toru Takahashi

entry.summary: Using minimal artificial learners, this study examines how shared internal representations become specialized across prediction targets, how such biases form, persist, and can be redirected. It shows matched learners with identical reconstruction measurements can respond differently to identical interventions, revealing latent differences not captured by surface metrics.

entry.title: DeepFlow: Two Convergent Differentiable Approaches for Pairwise Conditional Random Fields

author.name: John S. H. Baxter

entry.summary: The paper proposes two algorithms for integrating pairwise conditional random fields as structured output layers of neural networks, with provable convergence and well-defined derivatives. This enables spatial regularization in network outputs through a probabilistic graphical model lens without requiring substantially more data.

entry.title: ACED: Reference-Anchored Aggregation of Natural-Language and Executable Evidence for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Yiyi Lu, Jiaxiang Geng, Bing Luo

entry.summary: ACED treats natural-language self-consistency as a reference answer and executable program outputs as supporting evidence rather than interchangeable votes, combining them via a weighted logarithmic pool with a calibrated relative-evidence margin for overriding. Across five math word-problem benchmarks it matches or outperforms corresponding baselines in accuracy and cost.

entry.title: NBCLT: Parameter-Agnostic Norm-Ball Clipped Local Training

author.name: Linxuan Pan, Shucheng Yang, Junchi Yang

entry.summary: NBCLT is a unified local-training framework for federated and decentralized learning that combines a predict-and-correct local update rule with Euclidean projections onto flexible norm balls, inspired by Muon-type optimizers that constrain updates geometrically. This controls client drift from multiple local steps while encoding geometric priors and reducing hyperparameter sensitivity under heterogeneous data. It works parameter-agnostically across optimization geometries.

entry.title: Learning a Group Element from Its Action: Galois Correspondences, Optimal ERM, and an Abel-Ruffini Threshold for the Natarajan Dimension

author.name: Xiaoyu Li

entry.summary: This theory paper studies learning an unknown group element from action examples, connecting consistent hypothesis classes to cosets of pointwise stabilizers via Galois correspondence. It maps multiclass learning dimensions (DS, graph, Littlestone, teaching) to group invariants and proves ERM optimality among deterministic learners, with an Abel-Ruffini-type threshold.

entry.title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting

author.name: Jelena Simeunovi\'c, Baptiste Schubnel, Pierre-Jean Alet, Pascal Frossard, Rafael E. Carrillo

entry.summary: PING is a physics-informed graph neural network that models advection-diffusion processes as signals on graphs, targeting cloud motion forecasting from irregular weather-station networks to improve solar power predictions. It addresses the gap between classical numerical models and deep learning on irregular sensor layouts.

entry.title: Learning When to Transfer: Reinforcement Learning for Carbon-Footprint Modeling in New Manufacturing Domains

author.name: Muhammad Umar Farooq, Daniel R. Cooper

entry.summary: The paper proposes an RL-based method for selective knowledge transfer in manufacturing sustainability modeling, where a reward scores each transfer opportunity against supervised alternatives to avoid negative transfer when characterizing new materials or processes. This enables reliable carbon-footprint prediction before sufficient target-domain data exist.

entry.title: Human Pose Estimation by Probabilistic Mixtures of Gaussian and Uniform Distributions

author.name: Santiago Reina Alguacil, Ezequiel L\'opez Rubio

entry.summary: The paper proposes a post-hoc probabilistic framework for human pose estimation that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model plus spatially agnostic uniform distribution to raw heatmaps, requiring no retraining or architectural change. This continuous representation improves robustness to dense occlusions and out-of-distribution ambiguity compared to deterministic coordinate extraction.

entry.title: Decomposing A Neural Learner

author.name: Zelong Bi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a probabilistic decomposition of neural learners that separates a predictable component from an input-dependent reliability score, accounting for heterogeneous predictability across feature space. It develops an EM plus SGD training procedure and proves the decomposed learner recovers the response distribution within the predictable component.

entry.title: Rethinking Opinion Measurement Interfaces for Human-in-the-Loop Optimization

author.name: Changkun Ou, Sven Mayer, Daniel Buschek, Andreas Butz

entry.summary: This HCI study (N=360) evaluates six opinion measurement interfaces for human-in-the-loop optimization across text summarization and image color enhancement tasks, examining calibration, consistency, and completeness of sequential human feedback. It revisits the design space of rating and preference-elicitation interfaces that underpin RLHF-style optimization loops. Findings inform how human preference data quality depends on interface design.

entry.title: Energy-Guided Learning for Heat Equation with Noisy Source: Optimal Estimation and Generalization Bounds

author.name: Zixiang Zhou, Xiaohui Chen, Shanghua Teng

entry.summary: The paper characterizes statistical estimation and generalization for learning heat equation solutions from finite noisy data, deriving a novel variational formulation as energy-regularized, ellipticity-debiased Sobolev regression. It provides optimal estimation results and generalization bounds under physically meaningful norms for integrating data with PDE constraints. This gives a principled statistical foundation for physics-informed learning of dynamical systems.

entry.title: RF Fingerprinting of DSP Implementations using Machine Learning: An Over-the-Air Case Study

author.name: Stefan Scholl

entry.summary: Investigates whether differences between software DSP implementations of a transmitter, rather than hardware imperfections, can be identified from radiated signals, using five implementations of a 2-FSK RTTY waveform and CNN classifiers trained on augmented software-generated IQ, power-spectrum, and instantaneous-frequency representations. An over-the-air monitoring receiver successfully distinguishes the implementations.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Router Learning for Multi-Domain Medical Image Generation with Diffusion Experts

author.name: Yaoshuai Ma, Wei Yao, Yongxiang Liu, Feifan Wang, Da Chang, Pengxiang Xu, Shixun Zhang, Yonghong Tian

entry.summary: The paper studies router-learning strategies for combining domain-specialized diffusion experts in multi-domain medical image generation, comparing server-only supervised routing with an Anchor-Delta strategy that distills evidence from denoising losses of frozen experts. A proxy gate controls a subsequent refinement step, addressing limited and unrepresentative server data.

entry.title: MSC: Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control Framework with Uncertainty-Aware NMPC and RL-based Execution Layer

author.name: Jinho Park, Jeongtae Lee, Jeonghyeok Lim, Keun Ha Choi, Kyung-Soo Kim

entry.summary: MSC is a hierarchical planning-execution framework for autonomous mobile robots with freely swiveling casters, combining an uncertainty-aware nonlinear MPC with an RL-based execution layer. It targets the planning-execution gap caused by caster misalignment in low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers and improves robustness under state-estimation uncertainty.

entry.title: QBFF: Deep Quantum Bottleneck for Automatic Speaker Verification Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Anton Firc, Nouhaila Innan, Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Kamil Malinka, Martin Pere\v{s}ini, Zbyn\v{e}k Li\v{c}ka, Walid El Maouaki, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QBFF routes compressed speech representations through a small 8-qubit variational quantum circuit used as a drop-in bottleneck for deepfake speech detection, with a matched classical bottleneck as control. The quantum circuit yields better-calibrated confidence scores in most matched comparisons while remaining executable on real hardware.

entry.title: Amortized Variational Inference of Latent Intensities from Replicated Point Patterns

author.name: Wenqing Liu, Xenia Miscouridou, D\'eborah Sulem

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neural amortized variational framework that maps a variable number of replicated point patterns to a posterior over their shared latent point-process intensity, trained without ground-truth intensity supervision. At test time inference reduces to a single forward pass, and additional realizations yield narrower credible intervals with roughly stable coverage.

entry.title: Honeycomb Crystal in a Mass-Asymmetric Electron-Hole Bilayer

author.name: Shengdu Chai, Wangqian Miao, Yuqiang Li, Lei Wang, Xi Dai, X. C. Xie

entry.summary: A condensed matter physics paper using neural-network variational Monte Carlo to predict a density-driven transition from triangular to honeycomb electron-hole crystals in a mass-asymmetric bilayer, where heavy holes form a nonuniform stabilizing background. The honeycomb phase is stabilized at densities far above those of homogeneous electron gases.

entry.title: When Does Opponent Modeling Pay Off? Spatial Inference Stabilises Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability

author.name: Marcel Petran, Stefan Edelkamp

entry.summary: This work studies a transformer-based spatial opponent model trained with hindsight-relabelled goals, producing subgoal heatmaps fused into a dueling double DQN for partially observable competitive foraging games. The opponent model prevents training collapse seen in plain DQN, recovers most of the game value, and transfers zero-shot to unseen opponents.

entry.title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface

author.name: Emory Salaun, Syed Ayon, Kaleel Mahmood, Shaun Wallace

entry.summary: AIRRI presents a framework for rendering educational materials resistant to image-to-text extraction and LLM-based solving while remaining readable by humans, using spacing, opacity, and overlay transformations. It includes a dataset of higher-education assignments and an initial human readability evaluation.

entry.title: Modeling the Arrival Time of Information-Bearing Events in Natural Language

author.name: Leyi Lao, Yulin Ou, Yang Xu, Hao An

entry.summary: The paper applies neural temporal point processes to model when information-bearing events (new words, high-surprisal tokens) arrive in text, conditioning on event interval histories and LLM-derived semantic representations. It shifts from post-hoc information-theoretic analysis toward modeling the generation process of information timing.

entry.title: Evaluating Bias in Chinese Large Language Models across Tasks and Registers: Task Operationalization Effects and Irony Classification Risks

author.name: Mo Zhou

entry.summary: This preregistered audit of Chinese LLMs shows classification error rates rising sharply (from 10.9% to 23.5%) when toxic-content classifiers face ironic yinyang-register text, alongside effects of task operationalization on bias measurement. The authors carefully note label uncertainty as a partial confound.

entry.title: PAT: A Personality-Driven Augmentation and Transfer Learning Framework for Depression Detection on Social Media

author.name: Shengwu Zheng, Yuzhe Ding, Xiaohui Liang, Fei Li, Chong Teng, Donghong Ji

entry.summary: PAT addresses two limitations in social-media depression detection - noise in post screening from superficial lexical patterns and weak post-level encoder optimization - using a personality-driven augmentation and transfer learning framework. It first optimizes a post-level encoder before applying user-level supervision. The work targets earlier detection of depression, where automated screening can support timely intervention.

entry.title: An Interpretable Linguistically-Grounded Analysis of Scene Saliency in Movie Screenplays

author.name: Uday Bindal, Ishaan Karan, Manan Garg, Ekansh Goyal, Rahul Mishra, Rajakrishnan Rajkumar

entry.summary: This corpus study on the MENSA screenplay corpus asks whether Uniform Information Density predicts scene salience and what linguistic properties distinguish salient scenes from background, using a dual-stream classifier fusing a frozen BERT encoder with explicit linguistic features. Findings are nuanced: per-scene UID summaries carry no independent signal once length is controlled, but token-level UID distinguishes salient material in specific portions. The work offers an interpretable analysis of long-form narrative discourse.

entry.title: Lost in Contrast: Instruction-Preserving Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering

author.name: Haonan Zhang, Ting Jin, Wenzhong Tang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that visual contrastive decoding can destroy supported abstentions in VQA, both by filtering out the abstention token before comparison and by subtracting the reference branch's response to abstention instructions. It proposes instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the abstention instruction's effect intact while allowing contrast strength to be freely adjusted. This improves reliability of abstention behavior, an important calibration property.

entry.title: AD4EDU: Benchmarking University Lecture Audio Description across Accessibility Standards, Metrics, and Learner Preferences

author.name: Psychias Stylianos, Gao Yingqiang

entry.summary: AD4Edu provides a benchmark (AD4Edu-Bench) and a rule-diagnosable metric (AD4Edu-Eval) for generating and evaluating audio descriptions of slide-based university lectures for blind and low-vision learners. Existing guidelines and metrics target entertainment content and do not transfer to lectures, where descriptions must complement speech, resolve deictic references, and fit narrow pauses. The work consolidates accessibility standards and learner preferences into an evaluation framework.

entry.title: Text-Only vs. Image-Aware VLM Judges for Manga Translation Evaluation

author.name: Subaru Kimura, Jun Suzuki

entry.summary: The paper compares text-only and image-aware VLM judges for evaluating manga translation, using the same vision-language model in both roles on a page- and speech-bubble-aligned Japanese-English dataset. It examines how visual context such as speaker identity and scene tone changes evaluation outcomes. The findings inform how multimodal evaluation should be conducted for visually grounded translation tasks.

entry.title: DSM-Free UAV Visual Localization via Latent-Depth Variable Projection and Structure-Adaptive Coupling

author.name: Yibin Ye, Xichao Teng, Shuo Chen, Xiaokai Song, Yuli Sun, Qifeng Yu, Zhang Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes LDVP, a method for UAV visual localization against orthographic maps that eliminates the need for Digital Surface Models by treating unknown scales along perspective viewing rays as latent depths. It estimates pose directly via variable projection, avoiding indirect intermediate matrix estimation and decomposition used by prior orthographic-perspective geometry methods.

entry.title: Retraining-Free Depth Pruning of Vision Transformers: A Cross Domain Study of Layer Redundancy

author.name: Alessandro Viespoli, Loris Nanni

entry.summary: The authors extend similarity-based redundancy analysis from LLMs to vision transformers, measuring cosine similarity between layer inputs and outputs to identify low-impact transformations suitable for retraining-free depth pruning. The cross-architecture, cross-domain study systematically characterizes redundancy patterns in vision models.

entry.title: Rethinking Supervision in Document Unwarping: A Self-consistent Flow-free Approach

author.name: Shaokai Liu, Hao Feng, Wengang Zhou

entry.summary: DRNet is a deep network for document image rectification that exploits intrinsic geometric consistency instead of dense flow-based supervision, using a coarse-to-fine architecture built on representations of the distorted image. It targets smartphone-captured documents with warp distortions that hurt digitization.

entry.title: From Sound to Sense: An Anatomy of Semantic Supervision for Speech-Driven Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Zhongyu Pang

entry.summary: Analyzes what direct-audio speech-driven visual grounding models actually learn about language, grafting a frozen Whisper pathway onto a VLTVG grounding host in SemEcho so speech and text share one decoder, with synthesized text serving as a training-time teacher and same-host upper bound. The work measures semantic supervision quality for hands-free target acquisition in remote sensing.

entry.title: Revisiting Natural Language Prompts from Large Language Models for Open-Vocabulary Video Recognition

author.name: Haichen He, Weibin Liu, Weiwei Xing

entry.summary: P2CLIP investigates how LLM-generated prompts affect open-vocabulary video recognition with CLIP-style models, exploring how to generate higher-quality prompts for unseen categories and how to improve vision-text alignment using them. It aims to reduce overfitting from direct fine-tuning on limited video text information.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation With Stage-Wise Shared Adapters

author.name: Milad Rostamian, Mohammadreza Mohammadi, Ender Konukoglu, Mohsen Soryani

entry.summary: The paper introduces Block-Wise Shared Adapter (BWSA), a parameter-efficient mechanism for exchanging features across per-modality MRI encoders at multiple stages, with a trainable-gated variant (TG-BWSA) that learns per-stage blending weights. Evaluated on BraTS 2020, it targets reducing model complexity in multimodal brain tumor segmentation while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection

author.name: Arunachalam Venkatachalam, Mhafuzul Islam, Marwan Yusuf, David Van Hamme, Ben Stoffelen, James Foresi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a context-aware multimodal late-fusion approach for detecting pedestrians and road users under adverse conditions, integrating a lightweight gating network within a probabilistic calibration framework to adapt sensor fusion per operating context without retraining. This aims to maintain reliability across weather and lighting shifts that degrade pre-trained detectors.

entry.title: ToF-Wheel Odometry: Navigating Degeneration of Localization With Limited Sensing Capabilities

author.name: Xu Yang, Wenhao Li, Zhengyu Wei, Zening Li, Longxiang Huang, Bo Wang

entry.summary: ToF-Wheel Odometry tightly couples wheel kinematics with geometric constraints from Time-of-Flight cameras in a filtering framework for low-cost ground robots. Its main contribution is a degeneracy-aware, directional covariance-shaping strategy that infers process noise from geometry rather than heuristic online tuning, preventing divergence in featureless corridors or during wheel slip. This matters for reliable localization on sensing-limited robots.

entry.title: Automated carotid artery atherosclerotic inflammation segmentation in PET using MSR-Net

author.name: Ran Li, Abhinav K. Jha, Jie Zheng, Richard Laforest, Yongjian Liu, Mohamed Zayed, Tyler J. Fraum, Barry A. Siegel, Malak Itani, Joyce C. Mhlanga, Pamela K. Woodard

entry.summary: This work develops a two-stage multiscale residual network that segments carotid atherosclerotic inflammation on 64Cu-CANF-comb PET and quantifies uptake while accounting for partial-volume and tissue-fraction effects. It uses synthetic PET images with known fractional-volume ground truth generated via MR-derived activity maps and GATE Monte Carlo simulation.
