Reliable automated quantification supports carotid inflammation research and clinical workflows.

entry.title: Visual Sevoing from Lines

author.name: Nicolas Andreff, Bernard Espiau, Radu Horaud

entry.summary: This paper presents a line-based visual servoing approach built on a new binormalized Pluecker coordinate representation of lines, enabling a proper image-line alignment concept. The derived control law offers partial rotation-translation decoupling, analytical inversion of motion equations, and global asymptotic stability conditions, validated in simulation and experiment on an orthogonal trihedron. Despite appearing as a fresh arXiv cross-post, this is classic work from the visual servoing literature by well-known researchers.

entry.title: C2Flight: A Closed-Loop Co-Simulation Framework for Early-Stage Evaluation of Heterogeneous UAV Computing Systems

author.name: Xizhu Chen, Shuyuan Zhang, Yixuan Li, Huazhong Yang, Yu Wang, Jincheng Yu, Hongyang Jia

entry.summary: C2Flight is a closed-loop co-simulation framework representing UAV computing systems as parameterized dataflow graphs, integrating models of hardware under design with real physical hardware through a unified node interface for early-stage design evaluation. It captures how algorithm, hardware, communication, and topology choices interact through the robotic feedback loop. This fills a gap left by component-isolated benchmarks.

entry.title: Edge-Native Temporal--Graph Dual-Expert Inference for Dexterous Grasp Classification

author.name: Jiajian Zheng, Bin Zhang, Wen Fan, Yanan Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents an edge-native pipeline that recognizes grasped objects and predicts per-finger Stop events using only built-in joint-angle and actuator-load feedback, avoiding dense tactile arrays. A dual-expert architecture pairs a Temporal Convolutional Network for short-term contact dynamics with a Finger Graph Filter Network over finger relations, processing a compact 4-by-20 contact-evolution window. It prevents overloading early-contact fingers during multi-finger grasps without extra hardware.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Heterogeneous Task Allocation Under Spatio-Temporal Environmental Uncertainty for Multi-Robot Teams

author.name: Xi Lin, Yaxuan Li, Paul Szenher, Brendan Englot

entry.summary: The authors formulate a decentralized multi-robot task allocation problem for heterogeneous autonomous surface vehicles performing maritime tasks of varying types and appearance times under stochastic spatio-temporal disturbances. A reinforcement learning policy network is trained to be robust to uncertainty-induced observation deviations and to make effective individual decisions.

entry.title: Multimodal Sensor-Gated Mid-Air Launch and Vision-Based Recovery of a Child UAV on a Hovering Mothership Drone

author.name: Aashish Sahu, R. Prasanth Kumar

entry.summary: The authors build a mothership-child quadrotor system where mid-air launch and recovery transitions are gated by nonvisual sensing, using an upward-facing single-beam LiDAR occupancy detector with hysteresis plus RTK positioning. This addresses the failure mode where fiducial-based vision loses tracking near touchdown. It is a pragmatic systems contribution for heterogeneous drone teams.

entry.title: Behavioural self-monitoring for autonomous earth observation agents: The attribute reliability monitor (ARM)

author.name: Alejandro D. Mousist

entry.summary: ARM is a framework that accumulates evidence of suspicion over time to assess the reliability of individual semantic attributes output by language and vision-language models in autonomous systems, using a black-box approach with only observable responses. It was evaluated on a specialized VLM for satellite thermal infrared imagery, without access to internal states, confidence scores, or reference answers.

entry.title: Assessing the Quality of Concrete Scenarios Generated from Scenario Classes for Automated Driving

author.name: Lina Putze, Thies de Graaff, Jan Steffen Becker, Christian Neurohr

entry.summary: The paper proposes quality functions that aggregate scenario distance measures to quantify the diversity of concrete scenario collections generated from scenario classes for automated driving safety validation. High diversity among generated scenarios is essential for hazard analysis and verification coverage of the operational design domain. The work formalizes how to assess whether generated scenario sets are adequate for these tasks.

entry.title: Locally adaptive step sizes for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods

author.name: Jimmy Huy Tran, Tore Selland Kleppe, Nawaf Bou-Rabee

entry.summary: The paper explains and generalizes the locally adaptive step-size procedure recently introduced for No-U-Turn HMC, introducing alternative error measures that reduce reversibility-failure rejections. It extends locally adaptive step sizes to standard HMC and Metropolis-corrected kinetic Langevin/generalized HMC samplers. A numerical study compares the proposed variants across challenging target distributions.

entry.title: Arguments About AI Consciousness Remain Highly Motivated and At Best Overconfident

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's annual assessment of the AI consciousness debate, arguing little philosophical progress has occurred in the past year despite rapid AI capability gains. The post covers Anthropic's terms-of-service change on abusive treatment of Claude, recent consciousness arguments, and Anthropic's meetings with religious leaders, maintaining that most arguments are motivated and overconfident in both directions.

entry.title: Continuous Risk-Based Scheduling for Food Safety Inspection: Integrating Historical Decay with Event-Driven Consumer Review Signals

author.name: Akriti Bhat, Wayne Zhu, Ishan Gupta

entry.summary: Presents CIR, an event-driven pipeline that dynamically re-ranks food safety inspection queues using a decay-weighted historical score combined with consumer reviews triaged by an LLM classifier. A temporal partition rule excluding reviews predating the latest inspection prevents confounding, addressing facilities that develop severe violations after clean inspections.

entry.title: Neither True nor False: Do LLMs Represent Truth-Value Gaps in Plural Predication?

author.name: Duaa Nakshbandi, Zhiyu An, Yiping Li, Sachin Giri, Wan Du

entry.summary: The paper introduces HomogeneityNLI, a 1,000-item diagnostic dataset probing whether LLMs grasp truth-value gaps in plural definite descriptions, and finds a pervasive Bivalence Bias across seven open-weight models. Models incorrectly force plural sentences into true-or-false judgments that formal semantics treats as neither.

entry.title: LayerCanvas: Infographic Generation in AI Learning Assistants via Hybrid Layer-Set Diffusion

author.name: Keshav Gupta, Jeremy Owen, Christopher Lloyd, Shaunak Mishra, Manav Sharma

entry.summary: LayerCanvas generates infographics for AI learning assistants by conditioning a diffusion model on a hybrid layer-set representation that combines the editability and typography of SVG with the aesthetic richness of raster diffusion. This targets automated production of visually rich yet precisely laid out and editable educational graphics.

entry.title: Comparative Study of Canvas- and Coordinate-Based Geometry-Conditioned Neural Networks for Real-Time Prediction of Indoor Environments with Varying Room Dimensions

author.name: Shaofan Wang, Philipp Geyer

entry.summary: This study compares canvas-based and coordinate-based geometry-conditioned neural network surrogates for fast prediction of indoor airflow and temperature fields across varying room dimensions, as an alternative to expensive CFD. The canvas approach encodes room size by preserving occupied regions in a fixed canvas, while the coordinate approach parameterizes dimensions differently. It targets real-time HVAC assessment during architectural design.

entry.title: Weak Segmentation-Guided GAN for~Realistic Color Edition

author.name: Vincent Auriau, Emmanuel Malherbe, Matthieu Perrot

entry.summary: Presents a GAN architecture for realistic image color editing that leverages any differentiable segmentation model, aiming to jointly achieve controllability of target colors and artifact-free realism. The approach is positioned between histogram-matching methods, which are controllable but less realistic, and GANs, which are realistic but hard to control.

entry.title: Benchmarking Quantum Kernel SVMs for Credit Card Fraud Detection: Performance Realities Under NISQ Constraints

author.name: Hitanshi Arora, Mohit Swarnkar, Aswani Kumar Cherukuri

entry.summary: Evaluates quantum kernel SVMs with three encoding schemes against classical baselines on highly imbalanced credit card fraud data under strictly matched conditions. The work tests whether theoretical QML advantages survive on realistic financial data under NISQ-era constraints.

entry.title: Reference Wording Shapes Retrieval of Robot Task Instructions

author.name: Jahnavi Yelamanchi

entry.summary: This single-author study examines how the wording of reference descriptions affects retrieval of robot task instructions in RLBench, comparing five training-free lexical rankers over 80 random gallery choices of one description per task. Character n-gram TF-IDF achieves 61.3% mean top-1 accuracy versus 55.6% for BM25, with substantial variance across gallery choices. The paper demonstrates that instruction-retrieval performance for robot tasks is fragile and wording-dependent.

entry.title: When and How Order-Flow Interventions Work After Dealers Adapt

author.name: Guanghao Wu, Zhuo Cai, Zhidong Li, Shoujin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes SOFA, a public order-flow allocation contract combining a state scorer, a pre-announced commitment scheduler, and a quote-to-flow allocator, aimed at narrowing dealer quotes in markets where learning dealer agents settle on wide spreads. A paired re-adaptation protocol disentangles why an intervention works after dealers adapt. It sits at the intersection of multi-agent learning and market microstructure.

entry.title: LASER: Defeasible Certificate Search for Long-Range Protocol Dependencies

author.name: Zihan Tang, Huibiao Zhu

entry.summary: LASER is a proof-carrying search method that assembles source-linked certificates for protocol behaviors whose justification is spread across remote clauses and later corrections, representing missing support as explicit obligations. An occurrence-aware symbolic checker decides whether each certificate warrants, refutes, or leaves behavior unresolved, evaluated on 91 BehaviorCheck families.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual TTS for Indian Languages: A Benchmark and Inference-Time Duration Estimation Strategies

author.name: Adarsh Arigala, Arjun Gangwar, Srinivasan Umesh

entry.summary: The paper constructs a cross-lingual TTS evaluation benchmark covering English and nine Indian languages and proposes language-aware inference-time duration estimation strategies to fix duration mismatch in alignment-free TTS models without adding explicit duration predictors. It fills an evaluation gap for a set of languages that remain underexplored in cross-lingual speech synthesis.

entry.title: Gugak-VocalSet: A Multi-Genre Studio-Quality Dataset of Korean Traditional Singing with Sigimsae Annotations

author.name: Danbinaerin Han, Wonil Kim, Seah Hong, Dongjoo Moon, Jaeok Lee, Jongpil Lee, Chaewon Kim, Juhan Nam

entry.summary: The authors release the first public dataset of Korean traditional singing: 24.5 hours of studio-quality unaccompanied solo vocal recordings by 20 professional singers, with a unified ontology and roughly 68,000 audio-grounded annotations of sigimsae, a structured system of vocal pitch-contour expressions. The resource enables music information retrieval and expressive singing modeling for a culturally significant, previously unserved domain.

entry.title: Hardware-Assisted Multi-Stage Ransomware Detection with Adaptive Machine Learning

author.name: Salma Aboelmagd, Md. Rakibul Ahasan, Zhixin Pan, Abdulrahman Takiddin, Ziyu Shu

entry.summary: This framework couples software-level scanning hardened by adversarial training with hardware-level microprocessor activity monitoring for real-time ransomware detection and mitigation. It also uses neural architecture search to tailor detection models for better generalization. Validation covers multi-stage ransomware behaviors against obfuscated attacks.

entry.title: Towards Modality-Agnostic Seizure Classification: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Heterogeneous EEG and Intracranial EEG Signals

author.name: Ramya Sundaram, Muhammad Aslam Jarwar, M Uma, Sunder Ali Khowaja, Qurat-Ul-Ain Mastoi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified deep learning framework for seizure detection that handles both scalp EEG and intracranial EEG signals in a single modality-agnostic system, addressing the limitation that most existing seizure prediction systems are single-modal. The goal is broader applicability across heterogeneous clinical monitoring conditions.

entry.title: Superintelligence and the Triple Risk of an AI Race

author.name: Matthew Rendall, Max Hellrigel-Holderbaum, Leonard Dung

entry.summary: This philosophy/policy paper argues that a US-China race toward AGI presents three dangers: being overtaken by a rival, triggering armed conflict, and a third novel risk articulated in the paper. It engages with the current political narrative of deregulation to win the AI race and applies arms-race theory to frontier AI development. The paper contributes structured normative analysis to AI strategy debates.

entry.title: DTScribe: Generating Models for Digital Twin Reporting using Local Large Language Models

author.name: K\'erian Fiter, Angelica Portocarrero, Bentley Oakes

entry.summary: DTScribe automates digital twin reporting by ingesting digital twin documents and producing conceptual architecture visualizations and reporting pages using local LLMs. The tool addresses the tedious, time-consuming manual modeling previously needed for stakeholder consensus-building. It is an applied software-engineering contribution for the digital twin development workflow.

entry.title: DShuttleNet: A Badminton Doubles Dataset for Evaluating Team Coordination

author.name: Guan-Yi Jhang, Chiencheng Chiang, Wei-Kai Chen, Hui-Ching Yu, Hsu-Chao Lai, Hwai-Jung Hsu, Wang Chih-Chuan, Jhy-Cheng Huang, Jiun-Long Huang

entry.summary: DShuttleNet is a dataset for badminton doubles from elite BWF World Tour tournaments, designed to model team coordination rather than individual or ball-centric actions. It uniquely includes expert-labeled loss reasons for diagnostic causal tactical evaluation and defines geometry-driven representations (Teammate-Relative Angle, Vertical Shot Angle). It serves as a benchmark for multi-agent coordination in sports analytics.

entry.title: Do Artificial Neural Networks Need Dendritic Nanotubes? Two Reasons for Shrinking Importance Estimates in Continual Learning

author.name: Saurav K. Aryal

entry.summary: Motivated by dendritic nanotubes, the paper studies transient lateral links that diffuse importance tags between hidden units in regularization-based continual learning, finding random links with limited lifetimes improve Permuted MNIST accuracy. The analysis shows this random diffusion implements linear shrinkage of importance estimates toward the layer mean, giving a statistical explanation of the biologically inspired mechanism. Four studies connect the biological motif to shrinkage estimation.

entry.title: DPAL: A Test-Time Adaptation Loss for Financial Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Wuzhou Lian, Haochun Wang, Yuefan Deng

entry.summary: DPAL is a direction- and price-aware adaptation loss for test-time adaptation of financial forecasters, combining pointwise return fitting with directional and price-calibration terms. It plugs into existing TSF-TTA frameworks without modifying the source model or adapter architecture.

entry.title: Multi-Token Random-Walk Learning via Meeting-Triggered Information Exchange

author.name: Taichun Yeh, Xingran Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes decentralized learning with multiple random-walk tokens that exchange information when they meet, under Average-Gradient and Average-Model policies. The authors establish iteration complexity lower bounds for non-convex, convex, and strongly convex objectives, clarifying the fundamental benefit of meeting-triggered interactions. This formalizes the advantages of parallel multi-token exploration in communication-constrained learning.

entry.title: Pro-t-VAE: Closed-Form Student's t Mixtures for Robust Prototype Discovery

author.name: Zhikang Xu, Jiarui Xing, Jian Wang

entry.summary: Pro-t-VAE builds a deep generative framework for unsupervised image prototype discovery using a heavy-tailed Student's t mixture prior, constructed via a Bayesian scale-mixture formulation to yield a fully closed-form augmented ELBO. This combines statistical robustness with analytic tractability, avoiding noise-prone Gaussian priors and expensive diffusion sampling. It offers both explicit latent structure and scalable optimization.

entry.title: Algorithmic Fairness Over Time: Advances & Prospects

author.name: Miriam Rateike

entry.summary: This short position-style paper presents a taxonomy of static versus temporal fairness notions in algorithmic decision-making, motivated by feedback loops that can introduce selection bias and distribution shift over deployment time. It identifies implicit temporal assumptions in prior work and outlines open questions for measuring and ensuring fairness over time. It is a research-agenda contribution rather than a new method.

entry.title: FENAS: A Few-Shot Meta-Ensembling Framework for Efficient Neural Architecture Search with Synergized Zero-Cost Proxies

author.name: Yifeng Mao, Yuze Feng, Yutong Shen, Liyang Gao, Zhixiang He

entry.summary: Proposes FENAS, a topology-agnostic few-shot framework for NAS performance prediction that ensembles complementary zero-cost proxies instead of costly GNN-based predictors. Its CAST feature pipeline converts initialization priors into robust ranking signals to improve estimation accuracy under tight evaluation budgets.

entry.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Anomaly Detection in Real-World Cloud Telemetry

author.name: Sumit Dhyani, Sougata Mukherjea

entry.summary: This empirical benchmark evaluates GRU, Transformer, TimesNet, and Autoformer architectures for anomaly detection on real IBM Cloud Console telemetry using the timing-aware Numenta Anomaly Benchmark metric. TimesNet achieves the best scores due to early-detection sensitivity, while Transformers detect early but with higher false-positive rates.

entry.title: Compression Through Time: An Interplay of Separability, Stationarity and Capacity

author.name: Nikolaus Kopp, Franz Pernkopf, Bernhard Geiger

entry.summary: Using discretized LSTMs with finite embedding spaces, the authors study the temporal dynamics of information compression in recurrent networks, observing compression concentrated at final timesteps. They explain this through three competing mechanisms: class separability, shared recurrent dynamics propagating pressure across timesteps depending on stationarity, and limited representational capacity opposing prolonged compression.

entry.title: FedLoRD: Personalized Federated Learning based on Low-Rank Structures of Model Parameter Differences

author.name: Tsutahiro Fukuhara, Junya Hara, Hiroshi Higashi, Yuichi Tanaka

entry.summary: FedLoRD is a personalized federated learning method that exploits the low-rank structure of differences between global and personalized model parameters, replacing the empirical l1/l2 regularization choices of prior work with a data-driven prior. Clients regularize toward the global model using this learned low-rank structure during local training. This improves personalization under biased local data distributions.

entry.title: Operator Surrogates

author.name: Christoph Schwab, Josephine Westermann, Jakob Zech

entry.summary: This is a mathematical survey chapter on operator surrogates: finite-parametric maps approximating nonlinear operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces via the encoder-approximator-decoder paradigm. It covers representation systems (Banach frames, PCA, active subspaces, autoencoders) and surveys key surrogate methods.

entry.title: Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages

author.name: Romi Fadli, Rusdah, Wahyu Ramadani Putri Utami, Zulfa Malika Amana

entry.summary: A pre-registered evaluation of calibrated typed-decision models (Jev and Laya-multilingual) on Indonesian regional languages using NusaX and NusaTranslation sentiment benchmarks. The study finds accuracy correlates with lexical closeness to Indonesian and that presenting human translations raises accuracy by up to 37.2 points, with calibration error analysis included.

entry.title: Moment-Based Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Mixed Data

author.name: Davide Ferrari, Andrea Nicolodi

entry.summary: The paper proposes an anomaly detection method for high-dimensional mixed-type data using standardized moment-based transformations to produce interpretable feature-level scores, aggregated in a dependence-aware way into a Mixed-data Influence score. Using higher-order moments lets it detect changes in variability and skewness, not just location shifts.

entry.title: KARAMEL: Knowledge-Aware Ranking for Multimodal Entity Linking in the Arts via Heterogeneous Graphs

author.name: Raffaele Scaringi, Alejandro Sierra-M\'unera, Gennaro Vessio, Giovanna Castellano, Ralf Krestel

entry.summary: KARAMEL performs multimodal entity linking in the cultural heritage domain by fusing a vision-language encoder with a heterogeneous graph neural network that injects sociohistorical and contextual knowledge. This supports relational reasoning beyond surface-level multimodal alignment.

entry.title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score

author.name: Yuan Xinjie, Dier Tang, Shaolun-Huang

entry.summary: For distributed estimation where a center node has auxiliary side information, the paper orthogonally decomposes the joint function space to derive locally extractable features that are task-independent and non-redundant with the side information. It introduces a distributed nested H-score objective and proves mean-squared-error optimality under a limited feature budget in weak-dependence regimes.

entry.title: Statistical Downscaling of Daily Precipitation from ERA5 Atmospheric Fields to IMERG over West Africa

author.name: David Sagna, Redouane Lguensat, Samo Diatta

entry.summary: The authors use U-Net and GAN-based architectures to downscale coarse ERA5 reanalysis fields to high-resolution IMERG satellite precipitation over West Africa for 2000-2024 monsoon seasons, finding deterministic networks are systematically too dry and lose sub-synoptic variance. This motivates a stochastic GAN alternative for the challenging convective regime.

entry.title: Link Both Views: Cross-Image Routing Attention for Dual-Endpoint V2I Beam-Pair Power Prediction

author.name: Shiliang Lu, Lu Bai, Ziwei Huang, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes CIRA, a cross-image routing attention mechanism that fuses propagation-relevant features from dual-endpoint RGB images for sensing-aided vehicle-to-infrastructure communication. The resulting CiFormer predicts mmWave beam-pair power matrices and improves top-1 beam selection accuracy by 3.15 points over the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Convergence-Rate-Guided Algorithm Design of Expected Improvement for Continuous Simulation Optimization

author.name: Songhao Wang, Jianglin Xia, Haowei Wang, Szu Hui Ng

entry.summary: The paper derives a high-probability upper bound on simple regret for expected improvement with stochastic kriging under unknown heteroscedastic noise, and uses convergence-rate analysis to systematically choose the incumbent definition, replication level, and terminal recommendation. This replaces ad hoc heuristics with principled, bound-guided design choices.

entry.title: On Collusion-Free Teaching in Planar Graphs

author.name: Khazaliya Liana, Kuske Clemens

entry.summary: The authors prove a tight upper bound of two on the non-clashing teaching dimension for closed-neighborhood concept classes in planar graphs, establishing the conjectured NCTD versus VC dimension inequality for this family. They also analyze the positive-only variant NCTD+ for the same classes.

entry.title: Do LLMs differentiate linguistic traits internally?: A layer-wise analysis

author.name: Samhita Bollepally, Takashi Yamauchi, Manju Muralee, Motunrayo Adebimpe

entry.summary: The authors conduct layer-wise probing with geometric distance measures on two equal-size pretrained models, Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma-3-1B-PT, to determine whether and where these models internally differentiate linguistic traits such as conventional versus idiomatic meaning. Results show that even with equal capacity, the models organize linguistic information in fundamentally different ways. The study contributes to interpretability by mapping representational geometry across layers.

entry.title: HexaBee-4B: Six-Language Translation with Multilingual Answering and Bidirectional Supervision

author.name: Iman Barati, Mohammadmostafa Rostamkhani, Mohammad Badzohreh

entry.summary: HexaBee-4B is a translator adapted from Gemma 3 4B IT through three stages: Wikipedia continued pretraining, joint multilingual answering and answer translation using 19.46 million records, and bidirectional translation specialization. It targets meaning-preserving six-language translation with multilingual question answering.

entry.title: The interpreter as developer: An autoethnographic design study of building a computer-assisted interpreting tool through human-LLM co-creation

author.name: Zeming Zhao (College of Foreign Languages, Capital Normal University, Beijing, China)

entry.summary: An autoethnographic study in which a professional interpreter with no programming background built a local-first computer-assisted interpreting tool through vibe coding with an LLM architect and a coding agent. The analysis externalizes tacit professional knowledge into design and documents in-booth appropriation mechanisms during a public scientific event. It is notable as a case study of domain experts building software via LLMs.

entry.title: TDR: Tagalog Diacritic Restoration Dataset

author.name: Ivan Yuri De Leon, Lanz Railey Fermin, Zachary Aldridge Africa, Richell Isaiah Flores

entry.summary: The paper introduces TDR, an annotated corpus covering 40 frequent Tagalog homographs from news text, plus a collocation-driven retrieval method to expand the dataset and counter class imbalance. Diacritic restoration supports downstream tasks like prosody selection in text-to-speech.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Bangla Task-Oriented Dialogue Understanding

author.name: Afrina Alam Lamia, Sumiaya Sharif, Prottoy Modak, Ohiduzzaman Rayhan, Nafis Sadeq

entry.summary: BanglaTOD is a tri-lingual parallel benchmark for task-oriented dialogue understanding in Bangla, English, and romanized Banglish, with 209 multi-turn dialogues across nine Bangladesh-specific domains and 4,689 annotated turn records. The authors provide baselines with mBERT, BERT, and BanglaBERT for joint intent classification and slot filling. It fills a genuine resource gap for Bangla NLP.

entry.title: RALI@iKAT 2026: Retrieval-aware User Profile Denoising via Personalized Conversational Dense Retrieval

author.name: Yuchen Hui, Fengran Mo, Jia Ao Sun, Yuxing Tian, Wenhao Xu, Jian-Yun Nie

entry.summary: A system paper for the iKAT 2026 challenge that denoises accumulated user profiles by integrating personalization directly into conversational dense retrieval rather than separate rewrite-then-retrieve pipelines. It improves relevance modeling while handling noisy personalization signals.

entry.title: ScalLoc: Continuous Oblique Thermal UAV Geo-Localization with a 2D Satellite Map

author.name: Xiaoran Zhang, Yu Liu, Jinyu Liang, Huaxin Xiao

entry.summary: ScalLoc is a scale-aligned local-to-map framework for UAV geo-localization using oblique thermal imagery and only geo-referenced 2D satellite maps, targeting GNSS-denied environments. It follows a reconstruction-refinement-anchoring-propagation design that reconstructs local geometry from thermal sequences and refines camera pose against the map.

entry.title: ChangeT$^3$: Evaluating Vision Test-Time Training for Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Sharukshan Niranjan, Oshadha Samarakoon, Nichula Wasalathilaka, Roshan Godaliyadda, Parakrama Ekanayake, Vijitha Herath

entry.summary: ChangeT3 applies visual test-time training to bitemporal remote sensing change detection by combining a hierarchical ViT3-Tiny encoder with a ChangeFormer decoder in a Siamese configuration, adapting a compact inner model to each image instead of using explicit token-to-token attention. It evaluates whether TTT preserves spatial detail while capturing contextual change information.

entry.title: From Failure Prediction to Component Selection in Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Minhui Kang, Yiyao Zhang, Peizhe Long, Jiafeng Qi, Hongyu Jin, Jiayun Zheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a decision-centered evaluation framework for component-level failure prediction in semantic segmentation, connecting what a score predicts, what can be learned from its fields, and what its ranking actually delivers in downstream selection decisions. Experiments across three segmentation systems on Cityscapes and ACDC at 90% retention show that an adapted MetaSeg reduces retained failures relative to forecast entropy in all twelve architecture-population comparisons, but does not outperform simple direct probability ranking. The work highlights the gap between predictive performance metrics and practical decision value.

entry.title: Throwing4: Phase-Aware Pose Modeling for Throw-Distance Prediction in Elite Athletics

author.name: Bikash Kumar Badatya, Kartike Tiwari, Jyotirmoy Amin, Ravi Hegde

entry.summary: Curates Throwing4, a dataset of 500 elite throwing clips across javelin, discus, hammer, and shot put with 2D pose sequences, frame-level phase annotations, and official distances, and studies whether explicit phase alignment of pose dynamics improves throw-distance prediction from broadcast footage. Full-sequence and phase-aware models are compared under realistic conditions.

entry.title: Contrastive learning for video reuse detection

author.name: Tristan J. B. Cann, Arjun Biswas

entry.summary: The authors build a Siamese network fine-tuned with contrastive learning to identify potential source videos for key frames, targeting copyright and content-reuse detection in large video collections. The framework reduces complex video datasets to a compact set of key visuals (under 10% of the original size) while enabling source identification.

entry.title: Detecting Unreliable Classifications from Quantized Models

author.name: Ananya Kotla, Jorge T. Gomez

entry.summary: This work proposes a label-free method for detecting unreliable predictions from INT8 quantized models by computing cosine similarity between the FP32 and INT8 models' output probability vectors in a single forward pass. The output-agreement signal separates lower-accuracy predictions across four architectures, outperforming confidence-only baselines.

entry.title: An Open MuJoCo Simulation Framework for a Quadrotor Carrying a Tendon-Driven Soft Continuum Arm

author.name: Haitham El-Hussieny

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-source MuJoCo-based simulator for a quadrotor carrying a tendon-driven soft continuum arm, modeling the arm as a pseudo-rigid-body chain of twelve compliant hinge segments actuated by three tendons. An SE(3) geometric tracking controller flies the vehicle, enabling study of the coupled dynamics of free-flying bases and deformable underactuated manipulators.

entry.title: Kinematic Reward, Measured Effort: Hardware-Validated RL Morphology Optimization of a Planar 2R Manipulator

author.name: Gunesh Gupta (Independent Researcher, Haridwar, India), Arvind Kumar Mishra (Department of Electrical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee, Roorkee, India), Sohom Chakrabarty (Department of Electrical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee, Roorkee, India)

entry.summary: The paper uses reinforcement learning with RSL-RL PPO to optimize the link morphology of a 2R SCARA-type manipulator using Yoshikawa's manipulability index as reward, validated against analytical optima for circular tasks and transferred to real hardware. It bridges a common gap where kinematic morphology optimization is only studied in simulation. The hardware validation loop is the main value.

entry.title: Extending Wire-Driven Parallel Robots to Multi-Floating-Link Systems with an Inter-Body Wire

author.name: Shintaro Inoue, Kento Kawaharazuka, Temma Suzuki, Sota Yuzaki, Keita Yoneda, Kei Okada

entry.summary: This paper extends wire-driven parallel robots, traditionally limited to a single end effector, to systems with multiple floating links using an inter-body wire arrangement. This enables powerful actuation over large workspaces for multiple coordinated links despite wire-link interference issues. It expands the design space for large-scale cable-driven robotics.

entry.title: Sim4RAD: A MATLAB Toolkit for Design-Phase Sizing, Actuator Selection and URDF-Model Verification of Serial Robotic Arms

author.name: Jingchen Li

entry.summary: Sim4RAD is a MATLAB toolkit supporting the early design phase of serial robotic arms, covering actuator sizing, selection, and verification of URDF models before CAD exists. It provides static, dynamic, and stochastic analyses plus torque-speed envelope checks so specifications rest on a broad class of motions rather than a single trajectory.

entry.title: MARTS: A Modular Agricultural Robot for Targeted Spraying of Diseased Tomato Plants in Greenhouses

author.name: Rajmeet Singh, Manveen Kaur, Yusuf Adamu, Lochan Kshetrimayum, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: This paper presents MARTS, a low-cost greenhouse robot combining a Clearpath Husky mobile base, a UR5 arm, a novel modular spraying end-effector, and an RGB-D camera to detect tomato leaf disease and deliver spray only to affected tissue. It closes the loop from plant-level disease detection to leaf-localized spraying, reducing pesticide use and worker exposure compared to broadcast spraying.

entry.title: Copula Active Subspaces II: Error Decomposition, A Posteriori Estimation, and Sharpness of the Bounds

author.name: Joshua Chen, Peter Jan van Leeuwen

entry.summary: This follow-up to the Copula Active Subspaces method provides an exact decomposition of the KL divergence between the true and estimated observation-noise density into marginal, projection, and reduced-density terms, with a priori and a posteriori bounds. The authors use weighted nearest-neighbour entropy estimation and subsample-based score fitting to make the error assessment practical. The bounds are shown to be sharp.

entry.title: UNISON: A Unified Framework for Learning from Scored Bags

author.name: Ofek Kirshenboim, Or Shkuri, Shani Finkelshtein, Yoram Louzoun

entry.summary: Presents UNISON, a framework unifying multiple instance learning and recommendation systems as learning from scored bags of (item, score) pairs, decomposed into universal item representations, lightweight personalized preference parameters, and bag-level inference. A first-order analysis justifies the linear bag-specific scoring choice.

entry.title: Is the Platform Part of the Measurement? A Protocol and Simulation Study for Cross-Platform Equivalence of Machine-Labelled Policy Sentiment

author.name: Asad Ikram, Ella Haig

entry.summary: The paper adapts psychometric equivalence tools, including generalizability theory, measurement invariance, differential item functioning, and score linking, to machine-labelled policy sentiment across social media platforms, treating the platform as a survey mode. It specifies a six-step protocol with anchored events to test whether classifier scores are comparable across platforms.

entry.title: Calibrated Disambiguation for Partial Multi-label Learning

author.name: Zhuoming Li, Yuheng Jia, Mi Yu, Zicong Miao

entry.summary: This paper proposes PML-CD, a calibrated disambiguation model for partial multi-label learning where instances are annotated with both relevant and irrelevant labels, common in crowdsourced data. Unlike prior curriculum-learning approaches with non-adaptive weighting, the authors derive an optimal weighting function for curriculum-based disambiguation, equivalent to a calibration procedure. This provides theoretical grounding for label disambiguation in noisy supervision settings.

entry.title: Improving the Evaluation of Biomedical Question Answering with Few Human Preference Signals

author.name: Shakila Mahjabin Tonni, Xiang Dai, Sarvnaz Karimi, Xiaomei Li, Samuel C. Andrew, Stephen Wan

entry.summary: The paper addresses misalignment between automatic metrics and human judgments in evaluating RAG-based biomedical QA, showing that a small amount of human preference signal can calibrate direct-assessment metrics. Calibrated metrics consistently outperform baselines that average all metrics or pick a single best one.

entry.title: Neural Network Preconditioning: A Case Study for the Solution of the Parametric Helmholtz Equation

author.name: Luc Giraud (Inria, Concace joint team between Airbus CR&T, Cerfacs and Inria, Cerfacs, Concace joint team between Airbus CR&T, Cerfacs and Inria), Carola Kruse (Cerfacs, Concace joint team between Airbus CR&T, Cerfacs and Inria), Paul Mycek (Cerfacs, Concace joint team between Airbus CR&T, Cerfacs and Inria), Maksym Shpakovych (Inria, Concace joint team between Airbus CR&T, Cerfacs and Inria, Current affiliation: Opticalp), Yanfei Xiang (Inria, Concace joint team between Airbus CR&T, Cerfacs and Inria, Current affiliation: IRMA, Universit\'e de Strasbourg, MACARON, Inria)

entry.summary: The authors train a self-supervised U-Net to approximate the inverse of the discretized 2D parametric Helmholtz operator via a residual-norm loss, then use it as a nonlinear preconditioner inside flexible GMRES. The network alone is insufficient as a solver but substantially improves FGMRES convergence.

entry.title: Appearance Compensation in Volume Rendering

author.name: Jianghong Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies an identifiability question in emission-absorption volume rendering: whether a volume that reproduces all external RGB views can nonetheless have incorrect density. The author characterizes how a shared spatial appearance field can compensate density changes by replacing removed radiance along rays, deriving an optimal density-only gain under spherical-harmonic source refitting and conditions for positive gain. The results are relevant to the theoretical foundations underlying neural volume rendering methods.

entry.title: Exposing AI Inference as a Telco Network API over the 5G User Plane

author.name: Rodrigo Moreira, Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira, Joberto S. B. Martins, Tereza C. Carvalho, Fl\'avio de Oliveira Silva

entry.summary: Proposes Inference on Demand (IoD), an abstraction that exposes split edge-AI inference through a CAMARA-like API and carries split-aware tensor context in-band across the 5G user plane, evaluated on a programmable UPF. This addresses the gap that mobile networks can transport tensors but not their inference context.

entry.title: Using Evidence-Centered Design to Guide Prompt Engineering in Measurement: An Illustration with Automated Essay Scoring

author.name: Jiawei Xiong, Cheng Tang, Hong Jiao, Hanna Choi

entry.summary: Applies Evidence-Centered Design, a principled framework from educational measurement, to structure LLM prompt engineering for automated essay scoring, countering ad hoc trial-and-error practices that introduce validity threats like construct misrepresentation and construct-irrelevant variance.

entry.title: Who is the 'I' in AI? Establishing Decentralized Identity and Accountability for Autonomous Agents

author.name: Ahammod Munim Ramil, Khalid Al Kafi, M. A. Abdullahis Sany, Muktadirul Islam Nibir, Md Yeasin Ali, Mohammad Zavid Parvez, Md Sadek Ferdous

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for decentralized AI agent identity rooted in self-sovereign identity principles, with a formal model distinguishing human users from AI agents and distinct verification logic per class within a unified identity calculus. Its ABCD Framework provides a multi-layered approach to agent identity aimed at trust and accountability in decentralized ecosystems. It addresses a growing need as autonomous agents proliferate.

entry.title: Assessing the Performance of AI Models in Misinformation Detection Using Predefined Social Noise Constructs

author.name: Manar Alsaid

entry.summary: Evaluates six text-based models and a graph neural network for misinformation detection that accounts for social noise, using 500,000 tweets about Ukraine from the Russia-Ukraine conflict (March 2024 to March 2025). Models achieve strong accuracy, highlighting the role of social noise constructs alongside factual verification. Contributes to content moderation research on a high-stakes real-world dataset.

entry.title: Full Waveform Inversion with a Learned Preconditioner

author.name: Jeongjin Park

entry.summary: Investigates using a neural operator trained on reverse-time-migration images as a learned preconditioner for full-waveform inversion in geophysics. Comparing FNO and Jacobian-informed FNO variants applied to the true Devito FWI gradient, the JI-FNO preconditioner achieves the lowest model error, improving convergence of this ill-conditioned problem.

entry.title: NFMap: Topographic 2D Manifold Learning with Invertible Normalizing Flows

author.name: H\'el\'ena Alexandra Gaspar

entry.summary: NFMap extends Generative Topographic Mapping by replacing the RBF latent-to-data map with a fully invertible normalizing flow, retaining parametric embedding, explicit likelihood, and out-of-sample projection, plus a Student-t mixture option against map crowding. The likelihood serves as an effective out-of-distribution signal on chemical datasets.

entry.title: C{\AE}NL: Collapse-Based Active Neural Learning with Objective-Aligned Representation Control

author.name: Saad Alqithami

entry.summary: CAENL studies how active learning interacts with the representations used to acquire subsequent labels, introducing Dynamic Collapse Regularization that penalizes within-class to between-class scatter residuals above a frozen reference. The paper provides theoretical analysis of scatter invariances, descent guarantees, and coefficient bounds, complemented by a large 104-run empirical study. It shows that clean representation geometry alone cannot guarantee input robustness.

entry.title: Reliable Risk Estimation with Kernel Mean Matching under Dependent Sampling

author.name: Alexey Zaytsev, Diana Koldasbayeva, Egor Serov

entry.summary: This paper extends finite-sample guarantees for Kernel Mean Matching under covariate shift to dependent (temporal, spatial, clustered) samples by substituting effective sample sizes via Bernstein inequalities for strongly mixing processes. The resulting bounds explicitly separate overlap, dependence, and smoothness effects.

entry.title: Token-Budgeted Candidate Retrieval for 3D Scene-Grounded VLMs: Category Names vs. Pairwise Geometry

author.name: Micha{\l} Zakrzewski, Mariia Shpir, Taras Rumezhak

entry.summary: This empirical study compares strategies for selecting which 3D scene objects and relations to pass to a scene-grounded VLM under a fixed token budget, on ScanNet referring benchmarks. It finds that matching queries to object category names outperforms pairwise geometry scoring at every reported K, with the largest gaps at high recall.

entry.title: Calibrated $\alpha$-Barycenters for Multiobjective $f$-Divergence Optimization

author.name: Dier Tang, Peijie Li, Xiaoyuan Zhang

entry.summary: CAL-alpha-MODM constructs a calibrated barycentric surrogate for matching one distribution to many targets under f-divergence objectives, establishing exact-oracle stationarity and local convergence guarantees including cubic convergence under common matching geometry. Sensitivity-based initialization further accelerates the method, supported by high-precision experiments.

entry.title: Feature Normalization under Finite Training Budgets

author.name: Johan Larsson

entry.summary: This theoretical work characterizes when standardizing a rare feature helps SGD learn its effect within a finite observation budget, deriving optimized rare-subgroup risks for standardized versus unscaled training with constant learning rates and deterministic stopping. For two binary features it shows the preferred scaling changes exactly once as signal moves toward the rare feature.

entry.title: Comprehensive Workflow for Uncertainty-Aware Ionic Liquid Solvent Discovery

author.name: Alexander Lobo, Urvi Awasthi, Leonid Zhukov

entry.summary: Presents an uncertainty-aware machine learning workflow for ionic liquid solvent discovery, addressing brittle out-of-distribution screening in sparse, noisy, and unevenly sampled chemical spaces. The workflow emphasizes comparing candidates consistently despite limited thermodynamic coverage.

entry.title: Steering the Fidelity in State Preparation on Noisy Bosonic Systems with Risk-Seeking Optimization

author.name: Riccardo Piantoni, Riccardo Pellini, Maurizio Ferrari Dacrema, Paolo Cremonesi

entry.summary: The paper proposes risk-seeking optimization for variational quantum state preparation on bosonic systems, targeting the fidelity distribution across photon-loss event sequences rather than only average fidelity. This shifts optimization toward the higher-fidelity tail of prepared mixed states, improving worst-case preparation quality.

entry.title: Grid or Nodes? Probing Object Memory in World Models Under Partial Observability

author.name: Justin McMillen, Yasin Yilmaz

entry.summary: The paper compares spatial-grid world model memory (FloWM) against a numeric node-based memory (an oracle-fed Kalman tracker) on out-of-view object memory tasks in a block world. Results show grid representations probe better in-view while the node tracker matches out-of-view performance with dramatically less memory.

entry.title: Information-based Unified Design Framework for NMR Magnetic Tracking System

author.name: Se\c{c}kin Eren Yetim, Mehmet Efe Tiryaki

entry.summary: The authors present an information-based framework using local covariance analysis to design NMR magnetic tracking configurations for medical robotic guidance, evaluating receiver geometry, marker separation, and source configuration in on/off-board settings. Numerical evaluation shows planar-array precision depends jointly on receiver count and geometry, with triangular lattice arrays performing best for 9-20 receivers.

entry.title: Structured SDEs for Realized GARCH: Continuous-Time Volatility Modelling and Component-Level Analysis

author.name: Hongyu Yao, Zhengyang Chi, Junbin Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a continuous-time stochastic volatility model for one-day-ahead integrated-variance forecasting that lets a realized-measure state feed directly into latent variance dynamics with correlated Brownian innovations. Across 17 equity indices, the model outperforms GARCH, GARCH-Ito, Realized GARCH, HAR, and HEAVY benchmarks under QLIKE, MSE, and MAE. Ablations attribute the gains to realized-measure feedback within the framework.

entry.title: Vision: "What Don't I Know About User's Preferences?" How Uncertainty Estimation Improves Proactive Assistant Alignment

author.name: Zhiyu An, Ziyi Xuan, Yu Yang, Wan Du

entry.summary: This vision paper argues that proactive smart assistants should pair preference predictions with uncertainty estimation to know when predictions are reliable, which evidence supports them, and why ambiguity remains. Using home-assistant examples, it outlines questions uncertainty estimation should answer and how it should change downstream behavior such as asking versus acting. It is a research agenda rather than an empirical contribution.

entry.title: Boosting the Learning for Ranking Patterns

author.name: Nassim Belmecheri, Noureddine Aribi, Nadjib Lazaar, Yahia Lebbah, Samir Loudni

entry.summary: Formulates learning user-specific pattern-ranking functions in pattern mining as a multicriteria decision problem, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process to elicit weights over interestingness measures from user preferences. It adds an active learning mode with sensitivity-based handling to reduce required training samples and time.

entry.title: PRAISE: A Reproducible Workflow for Non-Programmer Scientists to Implement Published AI Models

author.name: Max Achterweust, Stefan Groot Nibbelink, Vincent J. de Beer, Stefan Schipper, Zeynep Y\"uksektepe, Pedro Andrade da Silva, Aurelia Peppelaar, Martijn J. van der Willigen, Christophe B. Minkenberg, Robert F. van der Willigen

entry.summary: Presents PRAISE, a hands-on workflow guiding non-programmers through implementing published AI models on their own data, covering the full route from paper to working predictions and anticipating common failures with fallback routes for each step. A proof-of-principle demonstration targets science and education use cases.

entry.title: A Node Embedding Framework for Model-Centric Conformance Checking in Process Mining

author.name: Mostafa Abbasi, Homayoun Najjaran

entry.summary: The paper introduces a model-centric evaluation framework for process mining that combines node embeddings with Procrustes alignment for cross-graph comparability, using a PetriNetGraph transformation to make Petri net models embedding-compatible. Comparing embeddings of discovered models against ground truth offers a more noise-robust alternative to traditional fitness and precision conformance metrics.

entry.title: Jevolution: A Framework for Studying Communication and Collective Dynamics in AI Agents

author.name: Xirui Huang, Nikhil Hooda, Utkarsh Gupta

entry.summary: Jevolution is an instrumented spatial predator-prey simulation framework for studying communication and collective dynamics in AI agents, separating the evolving world, asynchronous scheduling, controller adapters, and experiment records. It documents mechanisms via the ODD protocol and provides free synthetic data.

entry.title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models

author.name: S. M. Mahbub Uddin Ahmed

entry.summary: The paper adapts Clef-Flash, a 9-billion-parameter decision model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark using QLoRA with differential learning rates, achieving 95.42 percent accuracy and 0.9551 macro F1. It frames decision foundation models as a faster alternative to autoregressive LLMs for clinical classification and adds counterfactual explainability.

entry.title: RIECNN: Real-Time Image Enhanced CNN for Traffic Sign Recognition

author.name: Reem Abdel-Salam, Rana Mostafa, Ahmed H. Abdel-Gawad

entry.summary: Introduces a real-time CNN that integrates image enhancement for traffic sign recognition, evaluated on the German, Belgium, and Croatian traffic sign benchmarks. The approach reports improved recognition rate and execution time over state-of-the-art architectures, targeting environmental degradation in autonomous driving.

entry.title: Improving the Bounds on Approximating Weighted Maximin Share for Chores

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni, J\"{o}rg Rothe

entry.summary: This theory paper improves approximation guarantees for fairly allocating indivisible chores among agents with arbitrary positive weights: it establishes that every instance admits a 4.124234528-weighted-maximin-share allocation and gives a polynomial-time algorithm computing a 4.12424-WMMS allocation for rational inputs, complemented by lower-bound constructions with strictly positive gaps.

entry.title: DWI Connectome-based Sex Classification in Young using Supervised Variational Autoencoder

author.name: Aditya Kothapalli, Aaryan Gera, Sathvik Reddy V, Ninad Aithal, Debanjali Bhattacharya, Neelam Sinha

entry.summary: The study classifies sex in 787 young adults (15-25) using diffusion-weighted structural connectomes and a supervised variational autoencoder to extract compact latent features from 82 brain ROIs. The work explores adolescent brain development differences tied to hormonal changes.

entry.title: Joint Embedding with Dynamic Integration network (JEDI-net)

author.name: Rishav Mukherjee, Jeffrey Ahearn Thompson

entry.summary: Proposes clustering observations by feature-importance profiles rather than raw features to expose latent structure, integrating that latent-factor information into a joint embedding network to improve predictive performance. The idea targets erratic deep learning behavior caused by unobserved latent factors. The abstract suggests a general-purpose architectural contribution without specifying benchmarks.

entry.title: Better Capturing Interactions Between Products in~Retail: Revisited Negative Sampling for~Basket Choice Modeling

author.name: Jules D\'esir, Vincent Auriau, Martin Mo\v{z}ina, Emmanuel Malherbe

entry.summary: This work revisits negative sampling for basket choice modeling, aiming to better capture product interactions for retail tasks like assortment optimization and promotion planning. Improved modeling of substitutes and complements helps retailers minimize cannibalization and keep complementary products jointly available. It is an applied ML contribution to choice modeling rather than a core AI architecture paper.

entry.title: Generalized PINN-Based Inverse Estimation of Spatially Varying Heat Transfer Coefficients with Transfer Learning

author.name: Pradipan Maitra, Jariful Hassan, Arijit Hazra

entry.summary: This paper estimates spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients in jet impingement cooling using physics-informed neural networks with piecewise-linear and neural-network boundary estimators, validated against CFD references at several Reynolds numbers. It explores transfer learning across noise levels and source configurations, with an independent adjoint-FEM inverse-method comparison. A domain-specific scientific ML contribution.

entry.title: Agreement versus Softmax under Spatial Disambiguation

author.name: Micha{\l} Zakrzewski, Mariia Shpir, Taras Rumezhak, Volodymyr Karpiv

entry.summary: This paper analyzes calibration of cross-epoch agreement as a substitute for unlogged per-query logits in referring expression grounding on ScanRefer, finding softmax similarly miscalibrated on Unique and Multiple scenes while fixed-final and modal-vote agreement show large calibration gaps. Error analysis shows most Multiple-scene errors are same-class wrong-instance selections. A focused empirical calibration study.

entry.title: When More Memory Fails: Hidden Feasibility Holes in Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization

author.name: Mahesh Reddy Pagadala

entry.summary: This paper shows that Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization (DTR) exhibits non-monotone feasibility: certain memory budgets fail even though both smaller and larger budgets complete training, termed feasibility holes. Using the simrd simulator on public DTR traces, the author documents the phenomenon and reports no holes under a written sweep protocol on six confirmatory traces, with unresolved timeouts limiting certainty.

entry.title: Random Feature Pruning for Multi-Class Classification

author.name: Mohammad Amin Omidi, Babak Seyfe, Shahrokh Valaee

entry.summary: The paper addresses redundancy in random kitchen sink feature extraction for multi-class classification, formulating feature selection as sequentially nested model selection. The proposed SEED-MAX algorithm recursively computes empirical risks to find a parsimonious informative feature subset, with an analytical lower bound on the probability of correct selection. A classical kernel-methods contribution rather than deep learning work.

entry.title: Guarded Block Transfers for Polytope Distance: Linear Convergence with Explicit Constants and Gap-Certified Screening for SVM Training

author.name: Mayank Gupta

entry.summary: The paper introduces guarded block transfers for the Triangle Algorithm solution to hard-margin SVM training, aggregating multiple MDM transfers into one exact line search guarded by comparison with the best single transfer. On the Minkowski-difference polytope, the authors prove global linear convergence with explicit constants, avoiding combinatorial swap-step bounds.

entry.title: A 4-Qubit Variational Quantum Classifier for Sequence-Specific Classification of DNMT3A and DNMT3B Flanking Methylation Preferences

author.name: Murat Isik, Yusuf Moinuddin, Humaira Gowher, Sabre Kais

entry.summary: This work applies a four-qubit variational quantum classifier to distinguish flanking sequence preferences of DNA methyltransferases DNMT3A and DNMT3B using 4,096 experimentally derived NNNCGNNN motifs. It demonstrates quantum machine learning on a real epigenetics classification task via an exact statevector simulator. The work bridges quantum computing and computational biology in a niche but concrete application.

entry.title: The Language of Looking: Motion Tokens Reveal Domain-Dependent Local Structure in Gaze Sequences

author.name: Virmarie Maquiling, Enkelejda Kasneci

entry.summary: Using motion tokenization across four gaze datasets, the authors show that human gaze sequences share a reusable motion-token vocabulary but organize tokens into different local transition patterns depending on dataset and task context. The findings highlight limits of naive data pooling for gaze modeling and offer a diagnostic framework for behavioral sequences.

entry.title: DASS: A Solver-Adaptable Dynamic Auxiliary Search Strategy for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Yuxiao Hu, Qian Li, Ding Wang, Yekun Zheng, Jinyue Yan, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: DASS is a dynamic auxiliary search strategy for symbolic regression that constructs and refines a high-potential auxiliary search subspace, usable across different SR solvers to improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in a combinatorially explosive search space. It aims to provide shareable search guidance rather than solver-specific strategies.

entry.title: Effect of Spherical Parameter Space on Number of Non-Forgetting Tasks and Capacity of Continual Learning

author.name: Nazanin Mirhosseini

entry.summary: The author proposes a theoretical continual learning formulation with T non-forgetting tasks on a high-dimensional spherical parameter space, modeling each task's acceptable loss region as a geodesic ball and task dependencies via a Neyman-Scott clustered point process. The asymptotic analysis characterizes how many tasks can be retained without forgetting. It is a stylized theoretical model of continual learning capacity.

entry.title: A Time-Synchronous Prequential Evaluation Framework for Next-Week Student Disengagement Prediction from Moodle LMS Logs

author.name: David Otoo-Arthur, Terence L. van Zyl

entry.summary: This paper proposes a time-synchronous prequential evaluation framework for predicting next-week student disengagement from Moodle learning management system logs, ensuring model development, calibration, and evaluation are chronologically separated as they would be in real deployment. It compares online models including SGD logistic regression, OS-ELM, and echo state networks under different thresholding policies. The work matters because retrospective evaluation of early-warning models can overstate real-world performance in educational settings.

entry.title: Early Detection of Pension-Sponsor Distress from Public Filings: A Sponsor Vulnerability Index, Stress-Augmented VaR, and Dynamic Self-Investment Caps

author.name: Ravil Akhtyamov

entry.summary: This single-author paper builds a transparent early-warning pipeline for pension-sponsor distress using public SEC EDGAR data, combining a gradient-boosted Sponsor Vulnerability Index with stress-augmented Monte Carlo VaR and dynamic self-investment caps. It achieves 0.887 AUC-ROC on 36 U.S. sponsors with leave-one-firm-out cross-validation.

entry.title: Physics-informed random neural architectures on compact boundaryless multiply connected manifolds for random-operator models in machine learning and uncertainty quantification

author.name: Christian Soize

entry.summary: This paper introduces stochastic physics-informed neural networks for stochastic boundary-value problems with random operators, where a shared Gaussian stochastic germ couples the random PDE operator and a manifold-based, intrinsically random non-feedforward network. Random neuron placement and sparse geodesic connectivity are generated via a latent Gaussian field and an inhomogeneous Poisson process on a compact boundaryless manifold. The method targets uncertainty quantification for random-operator models.

entry.title: Dependency Reasoning for Aspect Sentiment Quadruple Prediction

author.name: Shima Esfandyar, Seywan Soleymanbaigi, Fardin Akhlaghian Tab, Fatemeh Daneshfar, Mourad Oussalah

entry.summary: DRIFT improves aspect sentiment quadruple prediction by linearizing dependency parse trees and injecting them directly into LLM prompts as explicit relational context, enabling single-pass reasoning over aspect-opinion dependencies. It combines this with retrieval-augmented in-context learning. The work treats ASQP as a relational reasoning problem rather than pure sequence generation.

entry.title: A Bethe-Ansatz Source of Early Token Correlations: A marginal-preserving construction for parallel proposals

author.name: Abraham Chachamovits

entry.summary: This theoretical paper constructs joint token-distribution laws from the periodic XXZ chain via coordinate Bethe ansatz, comparing them to maximum-entropy pairwise projections at matched moments, and shows where a controllable correlation gap vanishes exactly at a specific anisotropy. A nonlinear readout transfers the gap into early token positions of parallel decoding proposals while preserving marginals.

entry.title: Better together? A performance theory of human-machine skill policies under generalization difficulty

author.name: Riccardo Zanardelli

entry.summary: The paper develops a formal theory of human-machine teaming policies under the squared rule, decomposing achievable gains from pairing skills into a systematic part secured by commitment and a residual representing the value of knowing which skill each instance favors. It characterizes how routing and other workflows determine realized performance given instance-level generalization difficulty.

entry.title: Implicit and explicit reparameterizations of the Folded Normal and Rice distributions

author.name: Luis Aldama, Kevin Dalton, Minhuan Li, Doeke Hekstra

entry.summary: Derives implicit and explicit reparameterized pathwise gradient estimators for folded Normal and Rice distributions in PyTorch, comparing their variances analytically and empirically in the context of variational inference for crystallography. Implicit estimators achieve lower variance for location derivatives, particularly at small location-to-scale ratios.

entry.title: Beyond RMSE and Granger Gain: Multi-Horizon Forecast-Error Entropy for Nonlinear Predictive Coupling

author.name: Andrei Velichko

entry.summary: The author introduces FEDE, a predictive-causality framework that quantifies how the full signed forecast-error distribution changes across horizons when adding an auxiliary series to a target-only forecasting model. Using LightGBM-based matched forecasts, the method recovers hidden nonlinear source-target dependencies that RMSE and Granger gain miss.

entry.title: Evaluating Semantic Relation Knowledge through Bidirectional Relation Prediction from Gloss Pairs

author.name: Zhihan Cao, Adam Nohejl, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: The authors propose a task where LLMs predict semantic relations between sense glosses presented in both orders, checking consistency with relation symmetry or asymmetry, across monolingual and cross-lingual settings. The dataset covers 3,069 sense pairs verbalized in multiple languages.

entry.title: CultureBot: A Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Exploration of Cultural Heritage Data

author.name: Vasileios Karampinis, Angelos Vlachos, Giorgos Filandrianos, Maria Lymperaiou, Paraskevi Tzouveli, Chrysoula Zerva, Giorgos Stamou

entry.summary: CultureBot is an interactive framework combining knowledge-graph-guided retrieval, lexical-semantic retrieval, and source-linked generation for natural-language exploration of cultural heritage collections, instantiated on 81,852 SearchCulture records. It maps queries to structured catalogue relations and generates answers linked back to repository records. It demonstrates applied RAG over richly structured cultural data with an expert evaluation.

entry.title: Understanding Machine Taste: Aesthetic Agreement Across Foundation Models in K-pop

author.name: Kaishen Wang, Yucheng Pan, Xuehao Cui, Hanling Tian, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Using K-pop songs and music videos as a testbed, the authors characterize foundation model aesthetic preferences via pairwise ranking, finding stronger inter-model consensus in visual than audio evaluation and weak cross-modal alignment. They also examine how visual consensus relates to human popularity signals.

entry.title: Manifold Navigation Learning Using Recurrent Networks: Efficient Training Techniques

author.name: Sarah Harkins Dayton, Sathya Rengaswami, Vasileios Maroulas, David L. Boothe, Ioannis D. Schizas

entry.summary: Formalizes navigation on general manifolds as velocity-driven tracking and proposes a coordinate-chart-based framework where GRUs learn in Euclidean space, with predicted trajectories mapped to the manifold via an immersion function for geometrically consistent error computation. This avoids explicitly enforcing manifold constraints during training.

entry.title: Japanese Handwriting Generation Based on Human Preference Feedback Using Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Wakana Kuwata, Ryota Mibayashi, Masanori Tani, Hiroaki Ohshima

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for generating Japanese handwriting that aligns generative models with human stylistic preferences using Direct Preference Optimization. It addresses the inherent non-determinism of handwriting by defining and handling handwriting variability, distinguishing the task from deterministic font generation.

entry.title: Smartphone-Based, Field-Deployed AI Inspection System for Power Distribution Infrastructure

author.name: Sampath Balaji Masabathula (Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited, Andhra University College of Engineering, Visakhapatnam, India), Srija Vanapalli (Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited, Andhra University College of Engineering, Visakhapatnam, India), Gangadhar Kanchi (Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited), Sreenivasa Rao V. A. N (Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited), Vijaya Lalitha V (Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited), Sasank Chilamkurthy (Von Neumann AI)

entry.summary: This is a deployed industry-academic system from an Indian utility for smartphone-based AI inspection of power distribution infrastructure, combining image-quality validation with deep learning, monocular depth estimation, geometric analysis, and rule-based checks for pole lean, crossarm tilt, vegetation clearance risk, and transformer clearance. It demonstrates practical field deployment for geographically dispersed utility networks.

entry.title: Safety-Oriented Trajectory Ranking from BEV Perception Outputs

author.name: Leon Pohl, Martin Frauendorfer, Corinna Schmitt, Mirko Maehlisch

entry.summary: This paper presents a modular, interpretable pipeline that ranks candidate ego-vehicle trajectories using BEVFusion detections and map segmentations from nuScenes, prioritizing collision and walkway-violation avoidance over efficiency. It targets vehicular safety workflows, rapid prototyping, and human-in-the-loop validation rather than end-to-end autonomy. Its value is as a transparent, lightweight safety-checking component for autonomous driving stacks.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of a Collaborative Teleoperation Interface for Multi-Operator Multi-Robot Systems in Challenging Environments

author.name: Alperen Kenan, Juan Jos\'e Garc\'ia C\'ardenas, Adriana Tapus, Paul Bremner, Manuel Giuliani

entry.summary: The authors design and evaluate a shared-visualisation teleoperation interface intended to improve coordination, situational awareness, and task performance when multiple operators manage heterogeneous multi-robot teams in challenging environments. A comparative user study assesses whether the interface reduces the cognitive load and coordination friction of operator-to-operator communication.

entry.title: Distributed area coverage path planning subject to the inclusion of a headland path

author.name: Mogens Plessen

entry.summary: A deterministic method for multi-robot coverage path planning over non-convex areas with obstacles, machinery constraints, and headland path inclusion. The method handles working width, capacity limits, nonholonomic dynamics, and depot assignments, with discussion of globally optimal unconstrained depot scenarios. Relevant to agricultural and industrial field operations.

entry.title: Competitive Task Allocation with Temporal Proposal Windows and Improved Artificial Potential Fields for Dual-Arm Industrial Manipulation

author.name: Surya Prakash S. K, Bhuvan Narula, Jagannath Prasad Sahoo, Jayakumar VK, Praful Hambarde, Amit Shukla

entry.summary: This paper introduces a distance-based competitive task allocation framework for dual-arm industrial manipulation that integrates real-time vision, temporal proposal windows over five frames, dynamic reallocation, and improved artificial potential fields for collision-free motion. It targets more flexible collaborative automation than predetermined trajectory systems. The systems integration is the main contribution.

entry.title: One-Shot Learning for Double-Shot Latte Art: Adapting Cobot Pouring Skills with Dynamic Movement Primitives

author.name: Zain Khan, Victor Hernandez Moreno, Dinh Tung Le

entry.summary: The authors use one-shot learning from a single barista demonstration segmented into five phases, each encoded as a Cartesian Dynamic Movement Primitive, for a robot pouring latte art. Phase-based encoding reduces transition endpoint error 3.2-4.5x and shape error 2.7x versus a single-DMP baseline, and scales across cup sizes without re-demonstration. It is a charming, well-evaluated demonstration of DMP-based skill learning.

entry.title: Force Sensor-Based Picking Pattern Analysis and Two-Jaw Gripper Design for Cherry Tomato Robotic Harvesting in Greenhouse

author.name: Rajmeet Singh, Manveen Kaur, Yusuf Adamu, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: The authors capture six-axis force/torque signatures of human cherry-tomato picking patterns (gripping, twisting, lateral pulling) from 150 manual trials using a finger-mounted sensor, and use these data to design a bio-inspired compliant two-jaw gripper deployed on a mobile harvesting robot. The study quantifies the forces needed for gentle detachment of delicate fruit.

entry.title: Sensing via whole-body interactions with complex terrains: physical insights from robotic models

author.name: Chen Li

entry.summary: A perspective paper on how biologically guided robotic physical models can reveal how animals generate and use interaction-induced mechanical information (forces, deformations, vibrations) when moving over complex terrains. It argues robots can bridge the gap between sensory neurophysiology, biomechanics, and whole-body behavioral studies. The work connects robotics to neuromechanics research questions.

entry.title: Thoughts on alignment science vs. engineering

author.name: Leonard Dung

entry.summary: A conceptual post engaging with the distinction between alignment engineering (problem-driven interventions) and misalignment science (explanatory empirical understanding), arguing the latter occupies a useful intermediate level between current-model engineering and grand universal theories. The author acknowledges the piece is written quickly and is largely a framing exercise.

entry.title: OpenAI finds recording device in one of their offices

author.name: defun

entry.summary: A reproduced statement reporting that OpenAI discovered a hidden recording device in an office, used its own models to trace it to a specific employee, referred the matter to the FBI, and terminated the employee. The statement claims no evidence of model weight, source code, or customer data exfiltration and frames it as a demonstration of insider-threat security capabilities.

entry.title: China’s AI research is booming. Where is it headed?

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature news piece examining the rapid growth of AI research in China and analyzing the future direction of the country's research output. No article body text was provided, so the analysis is based on the title alone.

entry.title: A Hybrid Kinematic GCN and Elastic Transformer for Efficient Indian Sign Language Recognition

author.name: Pushp Garg, Himangshu Sarma, Mrinmoy Ghorai

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid architecture for Indian Sign Language recognition combining an entropy-driven SVD keyframe sampler, continuous dual positional encoding for irregular time gaps, and distance-aware kinematic graph plus elastic transformer components. It targets bimanual modeling under variable signing speeds and scarce large-vocabulary benchmarks.

entry.title: Dynamic Conflict Clustering with Lightweight Learning and Strategic Repair for Distributed Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Raziyeh Moghaddas, Fabio Caraffini

entry.summary: DCC-Incomplete is a repair-based solver for distributed constraint satisfaction problems that combines conflict-centered decomposition, structured coordination, strategic repair, and lightweight learning for stagnation recovery, reducing the broad peer-to-peer communication overhead of reactive solvers. It targets improved success on hard instances in multi-agent distributed decision-making.

entry.title: CIViC: Evidence Gates for Audio-Conditioned Visual Prediction on Proxy Tasks

author.name: Mengzhe Geng, Max W. Y. Lam, Yuewen Cao, Shoukang Hu, Jing Xu, Marc Tessier, Xu Li

entry.summary: Introduces CIViC, a four-gate protocol for verifying that audio-conditioned visual predictors actually use the intended audio information, linking interpretations to interventions, held-out task comparisons, and endpoint controls. The paper demonstrates the protocol on face-raster tests, synthetic audio mixtures, and SpeakerVid proxy tasks, finding in some settings that audio-trained fits are outperformed by constant-audio baselines.

entry.title: Support or Magnitude? Characterizing Neuron Relevance for Instruction Data Selection

author.name: Yifan Le

entry.summary: This work examines how neuron relevance should be characterized for model-internal instruction data selection, introducing Effective Relevance Support and Positive Relevance Magnitude criteria built on AttnLRP-guided attribution. The two characterizations produce distinct sample rankings despite shared signals, informing which selection strategy to prefer. It provides conceptual clarity for an increasingly popular data selection paradigm.

entry.title: Semantic Edge-Cloud Communication for Real-Time Urban Traffic Digital Twins

author.name: Murat Arda Onsu, Arman Dogru, Poonam Lohan, Burak Kantarci, Aisha Syed

entry.summary: This paper proposes semantic communication between edge surveillance cameras and cloud infrastructure to keep high-fidelity urban traffic digital twins synchronized in real time, supporting collision prediction, flow optimization, and scenario generation. It addresses bandwidth constraints by transmitting task-relevant semantic information rather than raw video. It matters for scalable smart-city traffic management systems.

entry.title: A Minimum Exact Disjunctive Basis for Two-Robot Solvability Profiles

author.name: Tsukasa Ninomiya, Shota Naito, Naoki Kitamura, Yuichi Sudo, Koichi Wada

entry.summary: This theory paper fully characterizes solvability profiles of tasks for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under variable disorientation, chirality, and rigid movement, across thirteen computational classes with a known quotient order. The authors prove every upset of the order is realizable and construct a minimum exact disjunctive basis of thirteen concrete tasks. It provides a complete combinatorial picture of which robot capabilities suffice for which tasks.

entry.title: ScienceBuddy-PV: A Verifier-Governed Recursive Improvement Protocol for Panvascular Intervention Research

author.name: Lingsen You, Yujun Guo, Xinyu Zhong, Zijie Feng, Wentong Wang, Li Shen, Junbo Ge

entry.summary: This paper adapts a recursive agent-improvement protocol to panvascular intervention research, specifying recursive harness optimization and outer-loop reinforcement learning but only auditing a fixed component on separate syntax and stenosis image tasks. It contributes structured scaffolding such as evidence ledgers, ontologies, and abstention contracts for self-improving research agents.

entry.title: Single-Sample Decoding of a Two-Layer Sound-Word Canvas Model for Thai Klon Pad

author.name: Worasait Suwannik

entry.summary: Presents a generator for Thai klon pad verse built on a masked language model (initialized from WangchanBERTa) over a fixed two-layer canvas enforcing rhyme, tone, and syllable constraints via hard masks, with single-sample decoding and no reranking. Evaluated against human verse on held-out topics using a frozen LLM judge, achieving 70.5% competitive quality.

entry.title: Multi-Horizon Explainable Queue Forecasting and Resource-Aware Decision Support for Intelligent Border Control Using LightGBM

author.name: Varvara Mama, Fani D. Christidi, Nikolaos C. Kapsalis, Anargyros T. Baklezos, Christos D. Nikolopoulos

entry.summary: The paper extends a multimodal queue-management framework with horizon-specific LightGBM regressors forecasting waiting times and queue lengths at 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes for border crossings, using lagged traffic, service, and staffing features. An operational decision-support layer turns forecasts into resource-aware recommendations. It is a solid applied systems contribution for a stochastic service-system setting.

entry.title: Towards Resilience: Slice-Driven Orchestration of Mobile IoMT in 6G-Edge-Continuum

author.name: Muhammad Zeeshan, Hafiz Faheem Shahid, Erkki Harjula
